Comments: MIXED BACTERIAL/ALGAE DERMATOPATHY WITH SEPSIS. This approximately 2.5-year-old dwarf Surinam toad had a slight decrease in food consumption over the last two weeks and was found dead in the morning. All other conspecifics in the tank appear normal. Necropsy revealed good body condition and fair postmortem condition. A focus of ulceration is present on the ventral mandibular region. Muscle underneath this lesion is hemorrhagic.
ENTERITIS. This male 3-year-old parakeet was found dead. It was apparently healthy. It was housed in an outdoor aviary. At necropsy there were two small hemorrhages on the surface of the skull.

ENTERITIS NEPHRITIS INANITION. This 10-year-old female viper has a history of inappetence. The animal was found dead. At necropsy serous atrophy of fat was identified within the coelom. A segment of intestine was distended and contained foul smelling green fluid.
ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old female lory was found ill and thin was brought to the hospital for examination and died. Gross necropsy revealed hemorrhagic small intestine.

UNDIFFERENTIATED ADENOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 7-year-old female meerkat had a large vascular mass identified at the root of the mesentery. The animal died following surgical exploration. At necropsy a 10 cm. in diameter mass of white tissue was present.

EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ARTERIOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RUMINORETICULITIS. This 9-year-old male greater kudu was immobilized for a hoof trim and died on recovery. Necropsy revealed petechiae in the mediastinum and no other abnormalities other than moderate cartilaginous defects of various sizes involving the articular surfaces of both carpi.

GRANULOMATOUS INFLAMMATION EPAXIAL REGION. This 15-year-old male captive bred tree python was euthanized due to abnormal mentation abnormal behavior and decreased activity. A mass 5 cm. in greatest dimension was present in the left epaxial muscles. The snake was euthanized and representative sections of the mass were submitted.

ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female rabbit had a one-week history of head tilt and rolling behavior and has no history of trauma. Examination revealed severe horizontal nystagmus and right-sided head tilt. Fenbendazole therapy was initiated and the animal appeared to stabilize but then head tilt developed again a few days later the rabbit assumed lateral recumbency with a large amount of ocular and nasal discharge and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the lungs serosanguineous fluid in the pericardium thick purulent urine in the urinary bladder full gastrointestinal tract some masses in the uterus and no gross lesions in the brain or ears.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This approximately 15-year/9-month-old female pochard was euthanized for humane reasons. It had a history of chronic lameness and was an old bird. At necropsy the heart was large. The kidney was granular appearing.

STRESS INANITION ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This female approximately 10-year-old fruit bat was humanely euthanized. This geriatric fruit bat was not competing well in the colony and was staying isolated. It appeared weak. At necropsy there was depletion of fat stores. There was alopecia on the back. There were superficial abrasions.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 3.5-year-old male common squirrel monkey was found dead by the keeper at morning check and had no prior medical history. Necropsy revealed foam in the trachea dark yellow clear fluid in the thoracic cavity wet and congested lungs pale myocardium some cloudy or serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen enlarged liver vertical tear around the intestine with hemorrhage around the tear and generalized lymph node enlargement.

ROUND CELL MALIGNANCY EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male colobus has a history of a right-sided facial swelling diagnosed as a malignant small cell neoplasm. Supportive care was administered with slight decrease in size of the facial swelling although the animal’s condition continued to progressively worsen and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified an unkempt haircoat dried diarrhea on the tail two masses on the right side of the face and jaw the largest 8 cm. in greatest dimension and the smallest 2 cm. in greatest dimension. Both masses were in the subcutis and did not invade the facial bones. The masses were solid firm and tan/gray with dark red streaking through portions of the larger mass. No other gross findings were observed.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOMA INSULINOMA. This 6-year-old female ferret has acute onset of hind limb weakness hypoglycemia and severe splenomegaly. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy mediastinal lymph nodes were enlarged. There was free clotted blood in the abdomen. Hepatic lobes were rounded. The spleen was enlarged with a bulging surface on the head and tail of the spleen which was heterogeneous on cut surface. The kidneys were small and pale.

LEUOENCEPHALOMALACIA AMYLOIDOSIS GASTRITIS STRESS. This 11-year-old female cheetah developed icterus renal failure inability to rise inappetence and central nervous system disease with dysphagia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The left hemisphere of the cerebral cortex had a focus of atrophy and dark yellow tissue surrounding the ventricle. The kidneys were small and hard with cortical atrophy. The liver was diffusely swollen and large. Tissues were icteric. Cystic structures were in both ovaries. A small mass was near the pancreatic duct possibly of enlarged lymph node. The mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Both adrenals were enlarged. Mucus was in the lumen of the stomach and the gastric mucosa appeared normal.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION EMACIATION. This 11-year-old female sloth was diagnosed two weeks earlier with open pyometra received supportive care and appeared to be doing well but then became lethargic and inappetent. Closed pyometra with ileus were diagnosed and an ovariohysterectomy was performed. The animal was lethargic for 36 hours after the procedure and then died. Necropsy revealed clean surgical sites and no abdominal effusion gas distended “rumen” pallor throughout the rumen mild hyperemia in the glandular portion of the stomach pale thin walled intestine and no other remarkable findings.
CHRONIC OSTEOARTHRITIS (SALMONELLA) INCLUSION BODY DISEASE. This 17-year-old boa had a three year history of spondylosis. The animal was euthanized and submitted fresh for necropsy.

DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS INANITION. This 17-year-old female tree boa has been inappetent since January. Physical examination blood work blood cultures and radiographs have all been normal. The animal was lethargic and showed vague neurologic signs on the day it was euthanized. At necropsy coelomic fat depots were absent. Numerous masses or granulomas were identified in the trachea and anterior lung.

TRAUMA SHOCK INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 10-year-old female ringed teal was found dead in the pool. At necropsy feathers were missing from the left side of the face and the underlying skin was reddened. Deep bruising was present in the musculature over the dorsal spine.

HEMIPENE HEMORRHAGE HEMORRHAGIC COLITIS RUATE STASIS. This 4-year-old male lizard presented in moribund condition. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy a fluctuant mass was present at the cloaca originating from the right hemipene. The liver was mottled pale to dark tan. A dilated segment of colon containing mucus was noted.

SHOCK HEMOSIDEROSIS ENTERITIS. This 1-year/5-month-old female stork was found dead on exhibit. It was found on the floor the day prior to death but was within the trees in the afternoon. At necropsy the stork was slightly thin.
DEGENERATIVE RENAL DISEASE ABOMASITIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female Tunis sheep had a history of chronic degenerative joint disease and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.
NA

NEPHROSCLEROSIS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA HYPERTENSION CATARACT EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male Amur leopard had a two week history of inappetence and weight loss and had been diagnosed the previous year with chronic renal disease. Recent blood work identified renal failure and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple subcutaneous lipomas and an irregular mass at the thoracic inlet that communicated with the left thyroid gland. The parathyroid glands were large and firm. Multiple small cystic lesions were present throughout the liver and a larger cyst was in the caudate lobe. Renal cortices were pale. Both adrenals were subjectively enlarged and firm and two masses were present in the medulla of the left adrenal.

STOMATITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 10-year-old male rattlesnake died unexpectedly with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition and fair postmortem condition. Ecchymoses are in the coelomic fat bodies. The kidneys are pale beige to white with prominent collecting ducts.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY FIBROSIS STEATITIS LEIOMYOMA ( UTERUS). This 27-year-old sea lion had a six month history of diarrhea and weight loss. The animal’s condition continued to decline despite treatment and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a calcified mass was noted in the cranial lung lobe. Two masses were noted in the uterus.

PAPILLARY NECROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS PACHYMENINGITIS AXONAL DEGENERATION (ROOT GANGLIA) BRONCHOALVEOLAR ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 23-year-old male African lion had a history of continued decline in health associated with difficulty walking urinary incontinence and scalding dermatitis on the hind legs testicle and prepuce. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Some drugs administered to this lion on a long-term basis include meloxicam flurbiprofen prednisolone diazepam and tramadol. Necropsy revealed minimal fat stores erosion or absence of the upper incisors biliary adenomas and hyperplasia rough to granular texture on articular surfaces of joints a thickened area at C6-C7 in the vertebral column two brown/yellow nodules in the subpleural region of the right pulmonary lobe a firm mass in the parenchyma of the lung two dark brown ulcerative lesions approximately one-half way down the esophagus a 3 cm. nodule on the diaphragm and a well demarcated white soft nodule in the liver.

1) Heart: chronic multifocal myocarditis 2) Stomach: perigastric mass Comments The myocardial masses are believed to be infectious in origin; either abscesses or granulomas; however; neoplasia is alos in the differential. The mass observed adjecent the stomach may also indicate infection in the abdominal cavity or neoplastic process. Histopathology and bacterial culture are pending; and the results will be included in the final report. 1) Lung: Moderate chronic caseogranulomatous pneumonia 2) Kidney: Focal chronic caseogranulomatous nephritis 3) Heart: Severe multifocal caseogranulomatous and fibrosing myocarditis Bacterial septicemia resulting in caseogranulomatous myocarditis; pneumonia and nephritis Comments: The histologic findings confirm our suspicions on gross necropsy of bacterial infection affecting the myocardium and other tissues. Acinetobacter; a gram negative rod; is the most likely agent to be causing the caseogranulomatous lesions seen. Staphylococcus infection is likely secondary. This completes the outstanding testing for this case.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY MILD SUBENDOCARDIAL LEFT VENTRICULAR WALL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male fruit bat had a history of congestive heart failure first noticed in August 2011. The animal was found on the floor of its exhibit breathing heavily. Radiographs confirmed cardiac disease and the bat was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition a focal chin abrasion cardiomegaly with left ventricular enlargement consolidation of the right middle pulmonary lobe tubular structures extending from the lateral sides of the bladder and absence of gonads due to previous castration.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS DYSECDYSIS. This 8-year-old snake had a history of constant shedding and skin lesions. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy areas of retained skin shed were present along the midbody and dorsal body. A serous cyst was identified anterior to the heart. Small areas of urate deposition were identified in the kidneys.

EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY PULMONARY ASPERGILLOSIS VASCULAR AMYLOIDOSIS. This approximately 24-year-old female flamingo had a one week history of debilitation from exertional myopathy. The bird was improving but became acutely weak with respiratory disease and died. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition bruising and white discoloration of skeletal muscles of the legs multifocal gray to green granulomas in the lungs focal serosal lesions in the small intestine that appeared to be transmural hemorrhage and injected vessels in the brain.

GASTRIC AND DUODENAL ULCERS PERITONITIS ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA ESOPHAGEAL CANDIDIASIS. This approximately 2-year-old female ferret was noted to have severe weight loss and inappetence with dark stools two days prior to death. Supportive care was administered but the ferret died. Necropsy revealed petechiae on the external surface of the left adrenal gland no distinction between the cortex and medulla in the right adrenal gland small thyroid glands a focus of dark pink discoloration in the caudal right lung lobe and pinpoint white spots in the lung yellow liver a 2 mm. cavitated region in the cranial pole of the left kidney and a similar cavitated lesion in the cranial pole. Petechiae were noted in the right kidney. A large blood clot was noted in the stomach and petechiae were in the duodenum. Raspberry jam-like material was in the distal jejunum and black tarry feces were in the colon. Amber fluid was in the abdomen and coagulated blood was in the thoracic inlet.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS AND PROTOZOAN ENTERITIS EMACIATION MELANOSIS AGED. This 14-year-old male leopard gecko was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy there was ingesta present within the stomach small intestine and large intestine. The liver was dark large and firm with diffuse white mottling. The overall body condition of this gecko was poor.

DISSEMINATED PROTOZOAN INFECTION POSSIBLE HEMOPARASITE. This approximately 1-year-old lorikeet developed an acute onset of dyspnea and lethargy with watery brown eliminations. The bird seemed normal the morning prior to death with good appetite. It declined over 11 hours despite supportive care with feeding subcutaneous fluids supplemental oxygen heat and humidity. The bird had an approximately 6% weight gain over the last four months. It is part of a flock of 47 other captive bred lorikeets sharing an aviary with two Tragopans two Turacos and two mandarin ducks. Two lorikeets died of aspergillosis approximately one year ago before corrections to the ventilation system were made. Necropsy revealed a moderately enlarged yellow/brown liver with rounded caudal margins and sharp cranial and lateral margins.

Whole body: Severe generalized edema. Severe thoracic and abdominal effusion. Pericardium: Moderate; diffuse; fibrinous pericarditis. Heart: Moderate; multifocal; fibrinous epicarditis. Colon: Colonic impaction. Bladder: Marked bladder distention. Forestomach: Moderate impaction. C3: Moderate; multifocal to coalescing; gastric ulceration. Lungs: Moderate; locally extensive; pulmonary congestion and consolidation. Comments The underlying cause of death could not be determined from gross examination. The severe generalized edema and thoracic and abdominal effusion may be due to underlying parasitism or other cause of protein loss. The impaction of the forestomach with distention of the intestines; colon; and bladder suggests a disturbance in normal gastrointestinal motility; possibly of neurologic origin. The fibrinous pericarditis; epicarditis and hemorrhagic lymph nodes may indicate systemic bacterial infection. Additional diagnostics including parasitology; bacteriology and histologic examination are pending and the results will be issued in the final report. Erin B. Howey; DVM Brain: Multifocal polioencephalomalacia. Heart: Severe diffuse fibrinous epicarditis; Moderate locally extensive myocardial degeneration with multifocal protozoal cysts. Liver: Severe; centrilobular to bridging; hepatic necrosis. Kidney: Multifocal membranous glomerulopathy; Moderate multifocal interstitial fibrosis; Mild multifocal renal tubular mineralization. Third compartment: Moderate multifocal mucosal erosion. Lymph node: Moderate to severe hemorrhage. Severe anemia. Polioencephalomalacia. Severe; centrilobular to bridging; hepatic necrosis. Comments The severe anemia noted in the clinical history is the most likely cause of many of the lesions observed grossly and histologically; however; an underlying cause of the anemia was not identified. The presence of an abundant amount of extramedullary hematopoiesis is a regenerative response to the anemia. Centrilobular necrosis within the liver is most likely due to hypoxia; secondary to the marked anemia. The polioencephalomalacia may be due to a thiamine deficiency or a hypoxic change. Thiamine deficiency can be a result of a thiamine deficient diet; decreased thiamine absorption; ingestion thiaminase containing plants or increased sulfur intake. Thiamine deficiency is difficult to definitively diagnose and is based on a combination of factors such as clinical neurologic signs; histopathological evidence; and testing of the environment and feed. The changes within the kidney can be contributed to the age of this animal and are not significant to the cause of death. The presence of numerous Giardia sp. as diagnosed through fecal examination may have contributed to this animals weight loss. The changes within the heart may be a hypoxic change as well; however; myocardial degeneration is often associated with Vitamin E and selenium deficiency in ruminants. Analysis for vitamin E and selenium deficiency is pending and the results will be issued in an addendum report. The abundant fibrin deposition on the epicardial and pericardial surfaces indicate an inflammatory response; however; no inciting organism was cultured. The protozoal cysts within myofibers are likely Sarcocystis sp. and are an incidental finding. Erin B. Howey; DVM \_ Comments This concludes the diagnostic testing for this case. Erin B. Howey; D

HEART FAILURE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ACUTE PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE ENTERITIS RENAL FIBROSIS INANITION. This 41-year-old male chimpanzee was found dead in the early evening without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy the right ventricle of the heart was extremely thin walled flaccid and enlarged. Several patchy cream colored foci were present within the left ventricle.

Hepatic lymphomas Salpingitis Avian Leukosis Complex (most likely Marek's disease) Comment: The cause of death in this chicken was due to liver tumors. The morphology and lack of bursal tumors suggest that the most likely cause for the tumors is Marek's disease. Unfortunately; based on the degree of post mortem degeneration in this bird; further testing would not be warranted to differentiate this from Avian Leukosis; another cause of lymphomas in chickens. No specific cause for the observed flock mortality could be determined from this submitted animal.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE ABDOMINAL CARCINOMA. This male 12-year-old impala was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic arthritis of the carpi and difficulty with ambulation. The impala was finally found leaning far off the right hip and rear limb and profoundly reluctant to move. Its condition seemed to get worse from prior months and the carpi were bilaterally more swollen than on previous observations. On palpation a caudal abdominal mass was palpable ventral in the pelvic canal. At necropsy the impala was thin. Subcutaneous fat reserves were present but reduced. The carpal joints were bilaterally swollen dorsally but when opened the joints did not release an increased amount of fluid or exudate. The synovium and ligaments surrounding the joints were fibrotic thickened and inflexible. Other forelimb and rear limb joints were not arthritic. The lumbosacral junction jutted dorsally and ventrally with bony texture. On radiographs vertebral spondylosis was noted and vertebral disarticulation was difficult. On exposure of the articular facettes of the lumbosacral junction and L3-4 there was substantial erosion eburnation and articular cartilage damage. There was a 7 cm. diameter nodular mass within the pelvic canal. On cut section the mass was granular and appeared green/gray. Cultures of lymph node liver lung and spleen were performed. Sections of liver lung kidneys and spleen were frozen for future use if needed.

INTESTINAL BACTERIAL ABSCESS EMACIATION. This 25-year-old male thick billed parrot received a West Nile virus vaccine ten days earlier and was moved to a permanent enclosure. It had an ongoing history of poor body condition with feather loss over the abdomen and thorax and continued re-injury of the skin over the keel. This condition was present when the bird was acquired and improved slightly by the time of death. Appetite was good and no signs of illness were noted prior to death. The bird was found dead in the enclosure. Necropsy revealed poor body condition with feather loss over the ventral and dorsal thorax and abdomen a scabbed abrasion over the length of the keel and no other gross abnormalities.

ACUTE THORACIC TRAUMA TRACHEOBRONCHIAL LYMPH NODE ABSCESS. This 9-year-old male zebra had been moved to a breeding hill on 3/9. It died spontaneously on 5/18. Breeding was observed but no offspring had been produced. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage within the wall of the trachea congestion and hemorrhage in the right lung mild thickening of the left AV valve moderate congestion in the spleen bilateral mucoid exudate in the kidneys and blood in the right nasal cavity.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female sheep had a history of severe chronic arthritis involving many joints with associated breakdown of the flexor tendons. The animal was also emaciated severely lame and could not ambulate well. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. On the morning of euthanasia the sheep had labored breathing. Necropsy revealed a small irregular mass in the liver dark thyroids poor delineation of the cortex and medulla of the adrenal possible thickening of the tricuspid valve atrophic uterus and possible ulceration in the pylorus.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS VACUOLAR MYELINOPATHY CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GASTRITIS. This 3-year-old female opossum had a history of posterior weakness. A firm enlarged cervical lymph node was also identified. Lymph node biopsy was performed and the animal was humanely euthanized two days following surgery due to worsening of clinical signs and poor prognosis. The lymph node biopsy revealed high grade malignant neoplasia likely lymphoma. At necropsy firm raised white foci were present in the spleen. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were also enlarged. Multifocal to coalescing white foci were present within the liver.

EUTHANSIA CYSTITIS. This captive bred 1.5-year-old male lizard was humanely euthanized. It had tetany of the front limbs and ventral flexion of the neck. It could not ambulate. It had not eaten anything of significance since June 2002. It regurgitated meals since that time. Medical treatment was attempted but the lizard continued to deteriorate.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS. This 18-year-old female peccary had a history of chronic lameness and arthritis. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy ascites and edema were noted.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA BACTERIAL RHINITIS AND LYMPHADENITIS. This 8-year-old female gerenuk was humanely euthanized due to exploratory laparotomy. The gerenuk had a history of chronic intermittent dystocia. It had a melengestrol acetate implant placed in March 2000. It was seen breeding with a male in June 2002. The abdomen had been increasing in size for the past two months. It had a history of a swollen right eye. There was purulent discharge from the right eye and from both nostrils. Radiographs showed fluid filled mass in the ventral abdomen with no fetus present. Exploratory laparotomy revealed severe pyometra with adhesions and extension to the liver. At necropsy the gerenuk was in fair to poor nutritional condition with no adipose tissue storage and reduced food in the digestive tract. The perineal area was stained with diarrhea. There were glandular secretions present on the hair around the tail and shoulders. There was a moderate amount of white purulent exudate present on the rostral nasal sinuses. The nasal choanae were filled with a white purulent to granulomatous exudate that extended to the caudal limits of the sinuses. There was pink foam present on the trachea. The dorsal lung fields were dark red congested and edematous but floated in formalin. The left lung fields were pink. There was approximately 10 ml. of clear yellow fluid in the pericardial sac. There were jet lesions present on the surface of the aorta as it leaves the heart. The aortic valves appeared thickened. There were no teeth present in the right maxilla. There were three premolar teeth present on the right mandible. The left maxilla and mandible had all teeth present. There were moderate areas of gingival recession. The liver appeared enlarged. The caudate process of the caudate lobe of the liver had areas of necrosis and hemorrhage. There were well-organized clots and adhesions on the caudal most surface. The ruminal papillae appeared blunted. The small and large intestines were compressed down in appearance. There was a mixture of diarrhea and formed fecal pellets in the large intestine. The body of the uterus was severely distended with 4.75 liters of tan purulent exudate. Both uterine horns were small but abnormal. The left uterine horn was approximately 10 cm. long and had fluid accumulated in cystic areas. The right uterine horn was approximately 5 cm. long and had a brown granular exudate present in it. The cranial most aspect of the uterus had thick blood clots present on the surface. There appeared to be a pinpoint hole in the luminal surface of the uterus below the blood clots. There were multiple white discrete oval masses present on the serosal surface of the uterus. The masses extended into the wall of the uterus. There were yellow/tan masses present in the wall of the uterus that were less discrete than the previously described masses. Both ovaries were small and inactive. The spleen was grossly enlarged. The adrenals appeared enlarged with prominent medullary areas. A melengestrol acetate implant was present in the muscle of the right shoulder. There was a thick capsule of reactive tissue surrounding the implant. There was an impression of generalized muscle atrophy of the muscles of the limbs and torso. The meningeal blood vessels were congested. Cultures of uterine exudate were performed. Culture of lung was performed. Culture of sinus exudate was performed. Mycobacterial cultures were performed. Sections of lung were frozen for future use if needed.
CHRONIC OOPHORITIS COELOMITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 9-year-old female turkey was found dead. At necropsy lungs were discolored black to green.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH SEPSIS STAPHYLOCOCCOSIS. This 2-year-old male scarlet ibis had no prior medical history at its previous institution or during a brief quarantine at the Phoenix Zoo although a preshipment exam did identify mild to moderate heterophilia and lymphocytosis. The bird died and necropsy revealed moderate fat stores good body condition other than mildly reduced pectoral muscling. The heart appeared subjectively enlarged and the right atrioventricular valve was covered in fibrinous easily removable yellow/tan adhesions. The liver had a tan/red mottled appearance and no other gross abnormalities were identified.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOMOCARCINOMA CARCINOMATOSIS HEPATIC METASTASIS PERITONITIS. This 18-year-old female jaguar had a several month history of ascites. The fluid was relatively high protein and contained neutrophils. Elevated bile acids neutrophilia and elevations of amylase and CPK were noted on blood work. Firm masses were present in the abdomen. The animal was found dead. At necropsy numerous cystic masses were identified within the liver.

IMPACTION EMACIATION. This 3-year-old female desert tortoise was found unresponsive possibly dead. Blood work revealed severe anemia leukopenia hypoproteinemia and hypoglycemia. Necropsy revealed no external lesions. Some mild stomatitis was noted and serous atrophy was present throughout the coelomic cavity. A large segment of the intestine contains much ingesta admixed with gravel and the mucosa was reddened.

SUSPECT ENTERIC CLOSTRIDIOSIS PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS. This 1-year/4-month-old female lory died. It was brought to the brooder lethargic and regurgitating. It was treated with fluids and medications. At necropsy the organs were very pale. The cardiac blood was light red and watery in appearance. The liver was enlarged and rounded. Kidney heart and brain West Nile virus testing.

ORAL ABSCESS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA INANITION. This 2-year-old male gerenuk had a history of chronic weight loss and oral abscesses. The animal lost the ability to prehend food. The animal was anesthetized and the abscess debrided. The animal regurgitated under anesthesia but did not seem to aspirate much material. Openmouthed breathing developed two days later and the animal died during hand restraint for fluid and antibiotic treatment. At necropsy the body was in poor condition with no internal fat stores. An abscess was present at the junction of the maxilla and mandible and extended to the hard palate. Caudal lung lobes were consolidated and mottled.

BOUT STRESS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA PITUITARY CYST. This 14-year-old male tiger ratsnake had a myxosarcoma excised from the left leg region in August (G13-3623). Excision was likely incomplete. The snake did well following the surgical procedure. The snake was noted to be in the early stage of the shed cycle and a few days later was found dead unexpectedly on the floor of the exhibit with its head under water in the pool. Necropsy revealed opaque gray spectacles but clear skin and a readily removed shed layer. The surgical site was healed. Some yellowish fat-like tissue was present in the deep intermuscular areas where the mass was excised. No other masses were identified. Fat stores were atrophic although muscle mass appeared moderate to good. Some mucus was in the oral cavity and choana. White opaque flecks and some yellow edema-like gelatinous material were on the serosal surfaces of the viscera. Eroded mucosa was noted in the stomach. The intestines were empty and dry. Intestinal villi became progressively more blunted towards the colon. The kidneys were swollen and speckled with urates and one multicystic lesion was buried in the parenchyma. The lung was edematous with gout or mineral in the walls. Multifocal spondylosis was noted along the ventral vertebra which generally was mild but was focally marked and irregular at the level of the liver.
adult. Weight: 3900.0 g.  Euthanased.  Suspect liver tumour and metastases to lungs and kidneys.  Pulmonary oedema.

CUTANEOUS FIBROSARCOMA CHRONIC UROCYSTITIS EUTHANSIA. This 13-year-old female gray wolf was evaluated for a wound on the tail and radiographs at the time revealed several small nodules throughout the pulmonary fields. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple firm white nodules in the lungs thickened bladder wall with purulent yellow fluid and a mass on the tail. Some black nodules were noted on the surface of the cranial mediastinum and one hilar lymph node had a darkened medulla.

EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA GLOMERULONEPHRITIS. This 5-year-old ferret had a suspected insulinoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the distal spleen had a hard raised nodule. A raised red to brown nodule was present in the pancreas.

SPLENIC HEMATOMA SPLENITIS NEPHRITIS. This 3-year-old female hedgehog had a history of anorexia and weight loss with marked anemia. The animal died during examination. At necropsy the animal was thin. A moderate amount of hemorrhagic fluid was present in the abdomen. The spleen was enlarged and firm. A 1 cm. in diameter red spherical structure was also noted in the abdomen.

BILATERAL CATARACTS UNILATERAL RETINAL DETACHMENT AND DEGENERATION WITH POSTERIOR SYNECHIA STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female screech owl had a long history of weakness and weight fluctuation and phthisis bulbi of many years duration. Low-grade uveitis was in the right eye. The bird had tested negative for Toxoplasma and recently had developed substantial alopecia. Skin biopsies suggested an underlying disease process. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified retinal scarring and lenticular opacity in the right eye and phthisis bulbi in the left eye. The heart was subjectively larger than expected. A small amount of pericardial fluid was noted. Congestion and/or hemorrhage were in the dorsal lung. The spleen seemed smaller than expected.

FAT ATROPHY HEAD TRAUMA SHOCK. This 1-year/3-month-old male tanager was found dead. It had been pulled out of ABC enclosure due to cagemate aggression. It was placed back into the ABC enclosure because the cage was needed for another bird. Cagemate aggression occurred again and the tanager was brought to the hospital and given oxygen and supportive treatment. At necropsy there was severe trauma to the head with no feathers on the head. There were hematomas on the head around the eyes and beak and underneath the lower beak. There were a few hematomas on the back of the head. There was a small amount of red tinged fluid in the oral cavity.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old male corn snake had severe ankylosis of the spine inappetence and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed spondylosis fragile pale kidneys with urate stasis dark liver and cachexia in the muscles.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS INANITION VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS. This 3-year/8-month-old male mynah died during postanesthetic recovery. This mynah had a history of losing weight and unusual vocalizations. It also had pronounced respiratory signs but no crackles or wheezes. CBC showed a mildly elevated hematocrit and chemistry panel showed hyperglycemia and mild hyperglobulinemia. The bird arrested while being radiographed and despite resuscitation attempts it died. At necropsy there were little fat stores. There appeared to be some hemorrhage within the calvaria over the left occipital region. Sections of liver were frozen for future use if needed.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) DYSTROPHIC MINERALIZATION ENTEROCOLITIS. This 3-year-old ewe had a history of chronic lameness. Recently radiographic evidence of intervertebral disc calcification and spondylosis were identified. Severe degenerative joint disease was identified in the elbows shoulders and stifles. The animal was humanely euthanized. Gross abnormalities were limited to the areas of spondylosis and degenerative joint disease.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS RHABDOMYOLYSIS CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS. This 5-year-old male pronghorn antelope was immobilized one day earlier for a hoof trim. No complications were noted during the procedure and the animal recovered normally. No regurgitation was observed. The animal developed progressive dyspnea the following day and arrested during attempts to intervene for diagnosis and treatment. Necropsy revealed a 1.5 cm. subcutaneous mass in the cervical area thick white material inside the mass (abscess) 1-2 liters of turbid yellow fluid in the thoracic cavity yellowish foam in the distal airways a 2 cm. focus of scarring on the dorsal surface of the left lung and a similar 4 cm. focus in the right lung. Two-thirds of the left caudal lung was dark pink. All sections of lung exuded yellow to reddish-brown fluid on cut surface. A small amount of pericardial edema was noted and the right ventricle was possibly slightly enlarged. A pinched-off possibly healed focus of trauma was in the right lobe of the liver. Some hemorrhage was noted on the surface of the adrenal. The kidneys had dark red to purple medulla. An 18 in. fibrous linear mass was in the lumen of the abomasum and did not appear to be obstructive (possible hair mat or digested cloth). Clotted blood was in the omentum.

NEPHROBLASTOMA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old budgerigar had a history of ataxia and lameness and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed decreased pectoral muscle mass and a large mass encompassing the left kidney and testicle. The mass had a necrotic core.

PROVENTRICULAR MACRORHABDIOSIS WITH TRANSFORMATION TO ADENOCARCINOMA. This 2-year-old budgerigar was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed thin body condition black loops of intestine and ulceration of the isthmus extending to the serosa. A wet mount showed very large rods consistent with Macrorhabdus ornithogaster.

TRAUMA ACUTE AND CHRONIC RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This approximately 25-year-old male bald eagle was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy identified a puncture wound on the dorsal surface of the thorax near the thoracolumbar junction to the right of the spine. The wound was associated with tissue necrosis and fly eggs. Affected muscle progressed caudally laterally and down into the thigh. The lung at the internal entrance of the puncture wound was normal. Samples of normal appearing pectoral muscle and darker congested muscle from the thigh are submitted.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS GASTRIC ULCER GOITER. This approximately 20-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy the snake appeared dehydrated. There were multiple yellow/gray non-adherent flakes at the cranial aspect of the lung. There was an ulcer present within the stomach. The liver was friable with multiple swellings. There were multiple white dots in the adrenal glands. There were severe adhesions between oviducts and ovaries with yellow/white flocculent material. Sections of heart lung liver and kidney were frozen for future use if needed.

EUTHANASIA PANCREATIC ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 9-year-old turkey hen presented with openmouthed breathing. Exam revealed fluid in the coelomic cavity. A large coelomic mass was identified on ultrasound. The animal was humanely euthanized.

ENDOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE SALPINGITIS ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 12-year-old female warthog was found dead. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the pericardial sac. A large quantity of straw colored fluid was present in the abdomen.
ENTERITIS INANITION. This 6-year-old female snake was found dead. At necropsy the lungs were edematous and pericardial effusion was noted. No other significant gross lesions were identified.

CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS EMACIATION INTESTINAL INTUSSUSCEPTION. This 5-year-old female greater kudu had a several month history of gradual weight loss and poor haircoat. Blood testing of a herdmate was suggestive of copper deficiency. This animal was placed on a high calorie diet with copper supplementation but its condition decompensated and following immobilization examination revealed dehydration and anemia in addition to a thin haircoat that epilated easily and alopecia with scabbed skin in the axillary regions. The animal recovered from anesthesia but never stood and was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed emaciation mild dental points on the arcades multiple mucosal ulcerations on the hard palate near the molars froth in the distal trachea and lower airways edema in the left lung and with the exception of diffuse marked acute congestion in the right lung. A moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid with a large clot was present in the pericardial sac and petechiae were noted in both ventricles and the atria with extension through the myocardium and into the endocardium. The liver was small and slightly firm and the gallbladder was filled with normal appearing bile. Crushed rocks were in the abomasum and a locally extensive focus of erythema was in the mucosa on the ventral aspect of the abomasum. Two focal mucosal hemorrhages were noted in the pylorus and blood-tinged liquid fecal material was in the ileum. The jejunum had a 12 in. intussusception with entrapment of the spiral colon and the surrounding jejunum was dark with mucosal hemorrhage. The affected spiral colon was congested and had petechiae. The mesentery near the affected bowel had petechiae and ecchymoses. The adrenals had petechiae in the cortices. Adipose tissue was atrophic and gelatinous. Muscle mass was reduced and the marrow in the femurs was gelatinous. Multiple ecchymoses were noted in the connective tissues surrounding the kidneys. Pleural and abdominal cavities contained a moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid.

PLACENTITIS VASCULITIS METRITIS. This 7-year-old female squirrel monkey was found dead in the morning with a live dry neonate clinging to her back. A significant amount of blood was present on both monkeys. Approximately 3-4 cm. of placenta was protruding from the vaginal area. This monkey had two prior pregnancies ending in live births with no apparent complications the most recently approximately one year ago. Necropsy revealed blood staining on the head face anal/genital area and tail 3-4 cm. of placenta with umbilical cord attached was protruding from the vagina and a large blood clot was on the distal end. The uterus was large and there was evidence of hemorrhage on the right side of the uterus. Placenta was still attached on the right side of the uterus. The tissue could be pulled away from the uterine wall with moderate traction. A ring of hemorrhage was noted in the cervical region with minimal tissue tearing. The left ventricular wall was subjectively thickened. A large amount of dark brown stained food material suggestive of ingested blood was present in the stomach. Dark brown-reddish fluid was in the duodenum and jejunum and normal colored feces were in the colon.

POSTSURGICAL CUTANEOUS THROMBI EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old captive bred fruit bat is one of several that developed necrosis of the wing webbing following anesthesia. The bat was spayed on 5/3 and the wing web necrosis was noted the following day. She was anesthetized and bled for blood culture and then euthanized for diagnostic necropsy. Both wing webs showed erythematous oval patches in the webbing between the elbows and digits. The wing webs were fixed in formalin in the extended position and the remainder of the necropsy showed no abnormalities.

SHOCK RENAL COCCIDIOSIS TRAUMA. This 1-year/9-month-old male kangaroo was found dead. It had crashed into a fence while getting into the barn. It was immobilized for castration. The procedure went well but the animal never recovered. At necropsy there was severe subcutaneous and muscular hemorrhage of the head and periosteum of the skull. There was pooling of blood. The left side of the head had extensive hemorrhage. There was moderate hemothorax. There was renal medullary hemorrhage/congestion. There was possible cerebral congestion. There was no hemorrhage in the brain.

DUCTUS DEFERENS LEIOMYOSARCOMA FIBROSARCOMA OF BODY WALL ENDOCRINE CARCINOMA OF UNDETERMINED LOCATION PANCREATIC ACINAR ADENOMA SEPSIS. This 22.5-year-old male rattlesnake had a recent history of inappetence decreased righting reflex and swollen coelom and died. Necropsy revealed a firm small white circular mass associated with a blood vessel 30 cm. down from the rostrum and adhered to the body wall. Surrounding the vessel and proceeding distally is some liver colored and shaped material that does not appear to be a part of the liver. The pericardium was thickened. Two nodular structures were noted in the liver. The left gonad was consumed by a mass to 3 cm. in greatest dimension that was attached to a large abdominal mass 8 cm. in greatest dimension. The right gonad appeared to be normal. The large mass attached to the left gonad appeared to be an enlarged section of oviduct that contained a degenerative slug. The contents of this tubular organ were similar to free contents in the coelomic cavity. Both kidneys were congested and had much white streaking. A small pea-sized mass was removed from cranial to the heart. Several cc’s of brown fibrotic cellular material was free in the coelomic cavity and was of unknown origin.

COLITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 2-year-old female rock hyrax died suddenly. An adult hyrax in an adjacent cage died recently with renal disease and degenerative cardiomyopathy (G99-1062). Necropsy of the animal of this report revealed dark discoloration of the duodenum and cecum and no other lesions.

SEPSIS ASPIRATION. This 2.5-year-old ornate horned frog had a previous episode one year earlier where it was found being swallowed by another horn frog. Its caudal half suffered partial digestion with digital loss on the hind legs and severe skin damage. It seemed to recover and was eating well after treatment. It was subsequently found dead in an off-exhibit tank. Necropsy revealed tan/brown kidneys multiple flat pale foci in the liver on the serosal surfaces and edematous lungs.

YOLK COELOMITIS TRAUMA/PREDATION. This 4-year-old female whistling duck was found dead following an apparent episode of predation in a stream. Necropsy revealed good nutritional status and most of the skin and muscle missing from the neck and base of the head. Severe hemorrhage was noted in the right body wall and medial to the right thigh. The lungs were bilaterally hemorrhagic. The ovary was active with multiple follicles in all stages of maturation but none ruptured. Multiple hemorrhages were surrounding the brain stem and brain.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS LARVAL CESTODIASIS. This 3.5-year-old alligator lizard had a history of scoliosis and kyphosis of one year’s duration and of unknown cause without bone changes in the radiographs. The lesions have progressed mildly since initially identified and the animal has had normal appetite and mobility. The lesions did not respond to antibiotic therapy. This animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed mildly thin body condition marked thoracic scoliosis and lumbar lordosis and a small puncture wound on the right caudal ventral abdomen with this lesion separated only by a thin membrane from the coelomic cavity. Hyperpigmentation was present in the coelomic lining. The ventricle was pale red/brown. The liver was enlarged pale tan and floated in formalin and multiple 0.5 mm. bulging white superficial nodules were present that extended into the parenchyma on cut surface. Multiple similar nodules were in the intestine. Skeletal muscle is pale throughout the body. The kidneys were tan with a brown/red speckled appearance.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA SEPTICEMIA. This approximately 9-year-old female snake was found dead on exhibit. At necropsy the snake was in good body condition. There were petechiae on the gingiva. There was an abscess in the soft tissue of the right palate. The lung was thick red and edematous. The tissue around the heart was edematous. There was a small amount of clear fluid in the pericardium. The pancreas was diffusely abscessed. The liver had multifocal small abscesses. There was a mild intussusception in the distal small intestine. The ovary was abscessed. The kidneys were slightly pale and edematous. There were small abscesses at the lobular junctions of the kidneys.

CARPAL TRAUMA RUMENITIS ABOMASITIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female gazelle had marked lameness associated with damage to the left front fetlock. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild degenerative changes in both carpal joints and degeneration of the left flexor tendons.

Liver: Mild; multifocal; granulomatous hepatitis (suspected; pending histopathology) Skin: Multifocal abscesses Stomach (C3): Mild; multifocal hemorrhage Right lung and kidney: Marked; diffuse hypostatic congestion Spleen: Moderate diffuse congestion Comments The above described and listed gross findings are not pathognomonic for any specific disease entity and may require further ancillary tests to determine the ultimate demise of this animal. Histopathology is pending and will be described in the final report; together with the results of the pending parasitology test on the feces. Samples of selected tissues were saved for additional tests if indicated by histopathology. Karla Fenton DVM; MS Skin: Moderate; focal; granulomatous dermatitis with intralesional foreign material Liver: Mild multifocal hepatitis; Locally extensive fatty degeneration (tension lipidosis) Intestine: Mild neutrophilic enteritis Spinal Cord: Mild myelin degeneration Open Comments Gross; histologic; and laboratory findings were largely nonspecific and were unable to identify a specific etiologic agent to explain the chronic weight loss and weakness. Parasitology identified few coccidial oocysts in the submitted well formed feces; however; these parasites were not identified in the sections of intestine examined microscopically. This may have been at least in part because of post-mortem loss of the lining epithelium. Diagnosis of clinically significant coccidiosis is based on clinical signs of diarrhea and often the demonstration of very large numbers of oocysts in the feces. These features were not present in this case. There was instead histologic evidence of mild neutrophilic enteritis; but the cause of it was not apparent. Advanced autolysis within the intestine greatly hampered critical evaluation of this tissue. There was histologic evidence of hepatitis; however; based on the mildness and very scattered distribution of this lesion; the significance towards the clinical signs of this animal is questionable. It is suspected that the focal area of fatty degeneration likely represents an area of ligament attachment to the liver and subsequent fatty change due to localized tension. As noted grossly; there was histologic evidence of a locally extensive area of dermatitis. These lesions likely formed in response to traumatically inoculated foreign material. Mild degenerative changes were noted within sections of the short segments of cranial cervical and lumbar spinal cord collected at necropsy. Although mild; these lesions could potentially explain the clinical signs of weakness.There was no gross or histologic evidence of the meningeal worm (Parelaphostrongylus tenuis); but lesions due to this parasite are focal and may not have been represented in the sections examined. Karla Fenton DVM; Open Comments The selenium (Se) level was slightly elevated in this animal. Several veterinary laboratories are reportedly finding significantly higher concentrations of Se (>12 ug/g dry weight) in llama and alpaca liver samples with no associated definable pathologic lesions. Use of newer feed supplements may result in higher liver and tissue Se concentrations. Further investigation is required to better define camelid Se requirements and toxicity levels. The Vitamin E level was slightly elevated in this animal; however; excess vitamin E is not considered harmful. Liver vitamin E concentration is a good indicator of dietary vitamin E intake. Nevertheless; hepatic vitamin E concentration is dynamic and the liver should be viewed as a very short-term vitamin E storage pool. There has been one documented report of vitamin E-related muscular disease in a llama; with musculoskeletal lesions similar to what is seen in other species; however; these lesions were related to a deficiency of vitamin E; which is the opposite of the result in this case. The copper (Cu) level was slightly decreased in this alpaca. Cu is often associated with anemia; altered hair coloration; impaired immune response; and poor growth; but usually in these cases the Cu levels are much lower than that observed in this animal. The iron (Fe) level was increased in this animal. The significance of this finding is undetermined because there is no report of iron toxicity in new world camelids. Karla Fenton DVM; MS

YOLK COELOMITIS VISCERAL GOUT INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This approximately 6-year-old female fowl was found dead. At necropsy there was hyperemia over the crop. There was bumblefoot on both legs. The lungs were very dark wet and heavy. There was abundant pericardial fat. The oviduct was thickened with congested vessels. The mucosal surface appeared irregular. There were necrotic follicles within the oviduct. The gizzard contained a large amount of grit. There were small black raised plaques found on the surface of the jejunum. The colon was very dilated. The liver appeared friable and autolytic. There was thick viscous orange fluid free in the coelomic cavity.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC CARCINOMA RENAL PAPILLARY ADENOCARCINOMA HEART FAILURE. This 13-year/9-month-old male pig was humanely euthanized. It had a history of weight loss anorexia depression and swelling at site of previous castration. Biopsy of the swelling on 1/17/01 revealed a diagnosis of undifferentiated carcinoma probable squamous cell carcinoma. The pig declined for the past several days. At necropsy the dentition was worn and some teeth were missing. The pig was thin and in poor body condition. There was a firm mass in the right scrotal inguinal area approximately 6-7 cm. in diameter. There was white foam in the trachea. There were blood clots in the cranial thoracic cavity. There was approximately 120 cc. of blood tinged straw colored fluid in the pericardial sac. The heart was slightly pale and flaccid. There was pulmonary edema. There was a lesion in the tip of the caudal right lung lobe. It was mottled multicolored and approximately 8 x 4 x 3 cm. It contained dark red opaque fluid on cut surface. There was dark red/black semisolid material in bronchi and bronchioles. There were two 3-5 mm. firm white round nodules in the ventral left caudal lung lobe. There were thin fibrinous blood clots throughout the abdominal cavity. There was a hematoma under the capsule of the left kidney. The right kidney had small blood clot in the pelvis and small blood clots seen in the vessels. There was a small soft white 3 mm. nodule in the medulla. There was a 5 x 3 cm. firm mottled red/black spherical mass attached to the left cranial adrenal gland by small cylindrical neck of tissue. There was a firm mottled red/black/tan mass 5 cm. in diameter found in the sublumbar region caudal to the right kidney. There was an irregular oval grayish-green 15 cm. x 10 x 10 cm. mass dorsal to the bladder that attached to the pelvic urethra. It was soft spongy and filled with air and green opaque fluid and covered with white connective tissue capsule. There was a yellow/white soft spongy irregular 10 x 6 x 6 cm. mass covered with a membrane attached to the dorsal bladder wall. Light yellow opaque suppurative looking fluid drained from the mass upon cutting the lumen. The bladder wall was thickened. There were pinpoint petechia in the mucosa of the jejunum and colon. There was a 24 x 16 x 4 cm. irregular multicolored mass extending from the midline at the rectum and penis to the mass seen externally in the scrotal region to the musculature of the proximal hind limb. Upon cut surface some areas appeared tan/gray soft and necrotic and in other areas appeared firm and multicolored with dark blood clots.

HYPOCALCEMIA BRONCHITIS. This 11-year-old female sheep died. It had a history of seizures from low blood calcium. It was on dietary supplementation. It had a cluster of eight seizures on 11/24. Blindness was noted postseizure. There were bilateral cataracts. At necropsy there were bilateral cataracts. There was white scarring in the heart. There was yellow fluid around the heart. The sheep was thin.

MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 10-year-old male meerkat died. It had a recent history of weakness but its appetite was good. It had weight loss (200 gm. in two years). At necropsy there was digesta within the intestine. There were no significant findings.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE OCULAR TRAUMA LINGUAL CANDIDIASIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 23-year-old male Jamaican fruit bat developed acute lethargy and difficulty breathing. Radiographs revealed consolidated lungs and soft tissue swelling in the abdomen. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the lungs sank in formalin. The liver was markedly enlarged and semifirm. The right eye had an opaque cornea and the teeth were worn.

ANEMIA. This male 1-year/3-month-old lorikeet died prior to night treatment for shock. At necropsy it was in good body condition. All organs were pale. The liver was bright yellow. The lungs were very pale. The gastrointestinal tract was pale and contained a large amount of black material.

EUTHANASIA HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS. This captive bred 13-year-old male chinchilla was humanely euthanized. It had a history of acting sluggish and had not eaten for a couple of days. It was found lying laterally and struggling to move. It had a thin body condition. The breathing was very labored with abdominal effort. At necropsy the lungs appeared shocky. The heart had a pitted surface on the left ventricle. The cecum was full. The stomach contained watery ingesta. Most of the small intestine was empty. The liver was pale tan.

BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS WITH YOLK COELOMITIS AND YOLK EMBOLISM PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS PULMONARY GRANULOMA PANCREATIC ACINAR ADENOMAS CHOLELITHIASIS. This 11-year-old female black tree monitor consumed food one day prior to death and had normal behavior noted prior to being found dead. Necropsy revealed excellent body and postmortem condition white mucoid egg material throughout the mesentery and coelomic organs pale liver with mottled red/purple spots and small white nodules on the surface. Ovaries were erythematous with multiple follicles of various sizes present. Multiple follicles were misshapen and had red/purple discoloration.

INTRASPECIES TRAUMA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE AVIAN MALARIA NEPHRITIS. This 20-year-old male penguin suffered intraspecies trauma. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed during treatment and resuscitation efforts were not successful. At necropsy pulmonary hemorrhage was noted.

MAMMARY GLAND FIBRO EPITHELIAL HYPERPLASIA OVARIAN CYST OVARIAN CYST SEPSIS POSTSURGICAL COMPLICATIONS. This 3.5-year-old female Virginia opossum had a 7 cm. pedunculated subcutaneous mass on the right side of the pouch that was surgically excised. The animal recovered from surgery with very little bleeding but then developed blood seepage from the incision site was monitored throughout the evening with no complications and was subsequently found dead a few hours later. Necropsy revealed a healing wound on the back attributed to self-trauma associated with acariasis. No other abnormalities were seen.

YOLK COELOMITIS ECTOPIC EGGS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 5-year-old female chicken was found dead. Necropsy revealed partially formed eggs in the coelomic cavity associated with yellow viscous material. A white substance was present on the surface of the liver the cranial surface of the coelomic cavity and extending to the pericardium.

EUTHANASIA OSTEITIS DEFORMANS SPONDYLOSIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 21-year-old female boa was euthanized due to severe spinal osteitis. At necropsy multiple areas of fusion were noted along the vertebral column.
NA

SHOCK ENDOGENOUS LIPID PNEUMONIA MYOCARDITIS. This approximately 3-year-old female opossum died three hours following recovery from anesthesia for orthopedic surgery of the right stifle joint. At necropsy the opossum was in good nutrition. The surgical site on the knee was clean and dry. The lungs were mottled dark pink to purple and were wet and heavy. There were numerous firm white nodules scattered throughout the lung fields. The right ventricle was somewhat flabby. There was considerable red foam within the stomach and areas of the gastric mucosa were hyperemic. There was a granular white substance within the body of the uterus.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male Nubian ibex was found two days prior to euthanasia in left lateral recumbency with its horn stuck under the stall door. Blood work revealed moderate azotemia. The animal did not improve with anti-inflammatory medication and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition cysts in the kidneys hemorrhage on the serosal surface of the colon some subcutaneous hemorrhage on the medial aspect of the left hock and no other remarkable findings.
EUTHANASIA. This greater than 1-year-old female rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of respiratory disease. At necropsy the heart was very pale. There was minimal body fat.

YOLK COELOMITIS SALPINGITIS BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS. This 14-year-old female whistling duck was found dead. At necropsy necrotic yolk material was present in the oviduct along with a fractured egg. The liver was enlarged and friable.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS (TRAUMA). This approximately 1-year-old lorikeet was found dead. It had been fine the day before. Necropsy revealed male gonad bright yellow to tan liver pale lungs serous fluid in the heart very little ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract blood in the proventriculus ventriculus and small intestine.

DISSEMINATED HIGH GRADE MALIGNANT ROUND CELL TUMOR. This 24-year-old female lemur had a one week history of poor appetite and occasional diarrhea associated with profound depression. Radiographs revealed multiple masses throughout the lungs liver mesentery and heart base. She had been previously diagnosed and treated for diabetes mellitus without incident. Necropsy revealed good body condition and multiple masses throughout the viscera.

EUTHANASIA CLOACAL PROLAPSE ENTERITIS RENAL GOUT INANITION. This 25-year-old male gopher snake suffered repeated prolapse of the distal GI tract. The animal was humanely euthanized due to advanced age and poor prognosis. At necropsy approximately 1.5 cm. of the colon was prolapsed through the vent. This tissue was swollen edematous and hemorrhagic. The distal GI tract was thickened and edematous. The kidney contained abundant urates. Some calcification and a large cyst were also noted in the kidneys.

EUTHANASIA ABDOMINAL TRAUMA GRANULOMATOUS STEATITIS HEPATOCELLULAR TOXIC CHANGE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 15-year-old male addax had a history of wasting arthritis and facial swelling of the right maxillary arcade associated with an abscess and poor dentition. The abscess was lanced and teeth were floated but the animal remained depressed over the next week and no fecal output was noted. Supportive care was administered but the animal became inappetent. Immobilization was performed for supportive care and following reversal the animal was not able to get back on its feet even with assistance. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed apparent serous change in the adipose tissue a fractured rib retroperitoneal hemorrhage some adhesions of the rumen to the body wall and cachexia.

SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 13-year-old female parrot was found dead on the ground in a large mixed species aviary. Necropsy revealed moderate autolysis enlarged thyroid glands edematous lungs and no other gross lesions.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 13-year-old male fruit bat suffered a fracture of the left wing. The digit was amputated; however the animal presented two days later with edema overlying the skull. Radiographs revealed lysis of the interphalangeal joints of the right pollux and radius. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy fluid was present in the pleural and peritoneal cavity. Marked cranial edema was noted. Hard white nodules were noted in the ribs. Cystic foci were noted in the kidneys.

PULMONARY SHOCK LOW GRADE SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION. This 16.5-year-old male roseate spoonbill was found in the morning soaked and the weather had been rain for 48 hours and was cold. The bird’s feathers appeared normal the previous day but waterproofing appeared to be absent in this bird and all other conspecifics the following morning. This bird was placed in holding but was found dead 30 minutes later. Necropsy revealed very good body condition no waterproofing dull gray material present on the barbules of the feathers thick gray waxy material on the interior and external surfaces of the distal rhamphotheca.
adult. Weight: 976.7 g.  Euthanasia. Poor condition. Dermatitus; chronic.Coelomic effusion. ?; chronic; suspect. Nodules; heart; lungs.

EUTHANASIA FEMORAL FRACTURE INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This 13-year/8-month-old female gazelle was humanely euthanized due to broken left leg. At necropsy there was a midshaft long oblique fracture of the left femur.

SHOCK BACTERIAL ENTERITIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 2-year-old male kangaroo had recently been treated for intestinal parasites. The animal was lethargic and inappetent and was found dead. At necropsy sections of stomach and intestine were dark purple and contained hemorrhagic material. The liver was yellow to tan.

PROVENTRICULAR ADENOCARCINOMA YOLK COELOMITIS. This 5-year-old chicken has a history of squamous cell carcinoma involving the tail that was excised in February of 2001 with no recurrence. In March 2002 it developed diarrhea and flagellates were detected in a fecal smear. Three days after treatment the bird was depressed lethargic pale and weak with profound anemia and atypical lymphocytes. It did not respond to therapy and died. Necropsy revealed fair body condition with pale comb and wattles pale skin good plumage good fat stores normal muscle mass petechiae on the serosal surfaces of the myocardium unclotted watery blood cloudy air sacs and pericardium congested lungs pale liver mottled spleen cyst involving the right kidney active ovaries and petechiae on the mucosal surfaces of the proventriculus duodenum and caeca.

METATARSAL FRACTURE. This 14-year-old female bighorn sheep was found recumbent and had a fracture of the metatarsal bone in the right rear leg. It had been hoof trimmed the previous day. Necropsy revealed multifocal red patches in the lung and pinpoint dark purple spots in the spleen.

ENTERITIS. This 8-year-old male rail was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the lower intestine and cloaca were filled with hemorrhagic fluid. E. coli and Enterococcus were cultured from the intestine.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK HEPATITIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 12-year-old female Bali mynah was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy there was a possible contusion on the skull and no other gross lesions.

BILIARY ABSCESSES CHOLESTASIS AMYLOIDOSIS LYMPHOCYTIC GASTRITIS. This 4-year-old male captive bred ferret had a two week history of illness died spontaneously and was refrigerated four hours prior to necropsy. During the quarantine period the animal developed mucoid diarrhea and inappetence. An exam on 7/27 found periodontal disease leukocytosis hypoglycemia azotemia inverted calcium-phosphorus ratio and Campylobacter in fecal cultures. The animal was treated accordingly but developed neurological signs and weakness with frank hematuria and tarry feces and died during a physical exam. Necropsy revealed partially atelectatic lungs with areas of congestion dilated right ventricle enlarged mandibular and mesenteric lymph nodes and spleen absence of numerous premolars frank blood in the esophagus tarry material in the stomach mucosal ulcers in the distal colon enlarged kidneys with serosal petechiae clotted blood in the renal pelvises sanguineous urine enlarged liver with irregular dark black/green depressions on the serosal surface purulent material in two areas on the diaphragmatic aspect of the left lobe and inspissated bile in the gall bladder.

MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 10-year-old female red panda had an episode of diarrhea and lateral recumbency in June responded well to supportive care and had inconclusive diagnostic tests. The animal improved clinically with intermittent episodes of vomiting but essentially normal appetite and attitude except when very hot. There was a plan to reevaluate the animal when it was moved for winter holding but the panda was found dead unexpectedly on exhibit. Necropsy revealed mottled white and purple areas on the serosa of the spleen red stripes on the inner left ventricular wall and papillary muscles 2 mm. white focus in one hepatic lobe that extended into the parenchyma hyperemic renal pelvises dark brown ovaries three irregular hyperemia plaque-like thickenings on the serosal surface of the distal jejunum enlarged mesenteric lymph node hyperemic proximal small intestinal mucosa generalized thickening and ropey texture to the gastrointestinal tract and a small amount of foam in the trachea.

SUSPECT LIVER LOBE TORSION STRESS LUTEOMA. This approximately 3-year/9-month-old female rabbit was found dead in its enclosure. This rabbit had several bouts of anorexia over the past several months from which she had fully recovered with conservative treatment. She was reported to be lethargic and not eating and was placed on Pedialyte which she drank on her own. At necropsy there were considerable amounts of clotted blood within the abdomen. The liver was tan and friable with one lobe covered in fibrin. The urinary bladder contained bloody urine. Both horns of the uterus contained small amounts of bloody fluid. There were two ulcerated areas in the gastric mucosa. The mucosa of the cecum was dark. The left lung was wet dark and heavy.

CIRRHOSIS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY HEMOABDOMEN. This male 10-year-old tamarin died. It had a history of some weight loss and hair loss. It was acting normal until 24 hours prior to death. At necropsy there was a large amount of hemorrhage noted in the abdomen. The liver was enlarged and nodular with several very defined lesions throughout the parenchyma (0.5-2 cm.). The liver was amorphous and tan in color and 100% of the liver was affected. There was a small well defined pale area in the dorsal cerebrum.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male wallaroo was found dead. The animal was treated for renal failure; however the animal’s condition failed to improve and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy erosions were noted in the gastric mucosa. Hemorrhage was present in the proximal small intestine. Kidneys were pale with foci of hemorrhage. A cyst was noted in the right kidney.

INTESTINAL INFARCTION PROBABLE VOLVULUS OR TORSION. This female 2-year-old kangaroo went off feed and became lethargic but had an active joey in the pouch. Three days prior to death she became recumbent and expelled the joey. Blood work revealed leukopenia and renal failure. The animal eventually developed mild seizure activity and expelled some necrotic appearing tissue from the vulva. The animal eventually died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and brown caked material on the caudal aspect of the tail head and rear end. Approximately 3 liters of red/brown fluid poured from the abdominal cavity when the body cavity was opened. The entire intestinal tract was hemorrhagic with petechiae and ecchymoses and ingesta were present in the large intestine. A section 30 cm. long of dead bowel was noted in the large intestine.

INTESTINAL AND URETERAL INCARCERATION POSTSURGICAL COMPLICATIONS. This 9-year-old female/spayed fruit bat was spayed two weeks earlier was checked one week after the spay and found to be clinically normal and was subsequently released to the exhibit. It was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed moderately distended and blue/purple discoloration of the intestine. A small portion of fat and connective tissue from the broad ligament was adhered to the ventral abdominal wall probably entrapped in the surgical closure. The intestinal tract became incarcerated in this piece of tissue. The left renal pelvis was dilated. The ovarian pedicle ligature was located caudal to the left kidney. It could not be determined if the ligation encompassed the ureter.

ARTHRITIS/DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female meerkat has a history of chronic spinal left shoulder and stifle joint disease with acute partial hind limb paresis that did not respond to rest and glucocorticoids. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large amount of ventral spondylosis in the spinal column and a narrow disc space at T6-7. Severe degenerative joint disease was in the left shoulder.

CHRONIC COELOMITIS WITH ADHESIONS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female Humboldt penguin had a history of congestive heart failure that had been reasonably well controlled the last year with various treatments. In the last two months respiration had become more labored body condition worsened and quality of life had decreased. Supportive care was administered with no effect and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed right-sided cardiac enlargement distended vena cava thickened mediastinal tissue at the base of the heart and at the cranial aspect of the keel and many adhesions in the viscera especially around the liver and gastrointestinal tract with a small amount of free fluid (previously severe ascites).
CHRONIC GINGIVITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old male African hedgehog has a two week history of a rostral mandibular mass and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

MYELINIC EDEMA AND AXONAL DEGENERATION SPINAL CORD. NEPHROSCLEROSIS POSSIBLE ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female opossum was euthanized for poor quality of life and was currently being treated with prednisolone. The animal had a history of ataxia and stumbling in the hind end. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a patch of mild alopecia on the dorsal trunk near the tail associated with some crusting lesions mild tartar cloudy eyes multiple coalescing pale lesions throughout the pulmonary lobes and one firm nodular lesion. The lungs were hyperpigmented. Foci of yellow discoloration were noted in the liver and ingesta were present throughout the alimentary tract. The renal medullas were yellow and both ureters were distended.

LYMPHOMA BACTERIAL PERITONITIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old vasectomized meerkat was the lone survivor from a group of four geriatric meerkats one of which succumbed to polioencephalomalacia the previous year. The meerkat of this report had a relatively unremarkable history aside from dental extractions and had reportedly been doing well until it presented in the morning with depression and dehydration. Examination revealed thin body condition and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified a large amount of white opaque flocculent fluid in the abdominal cavity and covering the serosal surface of the liver and spleen. Hay was in the stomach. Multiple firm nodules were within the jejunal mesentery and the pancreas was not observed. The heart was globoid and the left ventricle was hypertrophied. White streaking was in the medullary regions of both kidneys.

MAXILLARY ABSCESS EUTHANASIA EOSINOPHILIC GASTROENTERITIS. This approximately 4-year-old male red kangaroo has a history of tooth root abscesses and recently a piece of necrotic bone was removed from the left maxilla and the defect was surgically repaired. Recheck revealed failure of the surgical repair with no other option for fixing the defect. Due to the poor prognosis euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and a large lesion approximately 1 cm. in diameter on the left maxillary region just below the left eye. This wound communicated with the nasal cavity and into the oral cavity. In the oral cavity a 4 cm. defect was in the left side of the roof of the mouth corresponding to the area of necrotic maxillary bone that was previously removed. Nasal turbinates are exposed and easily seen through the oral cavity. Internal fat stores were atrophic and gelatinous.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA AMYLOIDOSIS ROUND CELL MALIGNANCY EUTHANSIA. This male black-footed ferret had arrived from the Front Royal Virginia facility 10 months earlier. One year ago the ferret had a history of acute hepatic disease following a dental procedure and responded to supportive care. While at the current facility it had a history of weight loss decreased appetite and increased renal values with poor response to supportive care and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a rounded heart with distended vena cava bilateral renomegaly small firm adrenals patches of reddening in the lungs and some patches of fibrous tissue in the lungs. An 8 mm. green thick nodule was attached below the urinary bladder by fibrous strand.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA MAMMARY GLAND FIBROADENOMAS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 3-year-old female rat has become inappetent and somnolent over the last two days and has rapidly growing mammary tumors and dyspnea. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.
EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY. This 3-year-old male fruit bat was found dead on exhibit with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no gross abnormalities.

XANTHOMATOSIS HYDRONEPHROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 10-year-old female goat had a one month history of decreased weight and blood work revealed renal disease that did not respond to aggressive therapy. Euthanasia was performed five days after treatment commenced for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed two liters of serosanguineous fluid around the tissues 250 cc. of urine in the urinary bladder fluid in the uterus a nodular firm fibrous mass in the region of the ovaries and lumbar lymph nodes enlarged kidneys with mild dilatation of the medullary tissue and absence of normal renal parenchyma in the right kidney which had marked fluid retention.

PARABRONCHIAL HEMORRHAGE DELETION OF ADIPOSE STORES. This 9-year-old female blue-crowned motmot had a history of air sac flukes and was found dead. At necropsy no flukes or other abnormalities were recorded.

CEREBRAL INFRACTION SUBCUTANEOUS ABSCESSES (SUSPECT INJECTION SITES). This 4-year-old male California sea lion had a three-week history of scrotal swelling edema of the left flipper anorexia and lethargy. The animal had multiple gastric ulcers noted on endoscopy and lost vision. The animal was anesthetized for diagnostics and arrested. At one year of age this animal had air bubbles in the cerebellum and has been abnormal neurologically.
