Postmortem brain MRI revealed one large and two small bubbles in the cerebellum and two areas of stroke a cataract a schwannoma and an arachnoid cyst. At necropsy there were multiple subcutaneous abscesses surrounded by skeletal muscle necrosis that were in regions of previous medication administration. Multiple lymph nodes were enlarged.

PERFORATING FOREIGN BODY WITH COELOMITIS YOLK COELOMITIS ASPERGILLUS GRANULOMA. This 5-year-old female rhea had a history of ataxia and respiratory distress prior to death. necropsy revealed erythema of the arytenoids mucopurulent saliva in the oral cavity erythema and erosions of the caudal oropharynx alopecia over the left flank cloudy air sacs a granuloma in the left cranial thoracic air sac and a green mucopurulent discharge in the left caudal thoracic air sac. The caudal tips of the lungs were green/gray and more firm than the cranial portions of the lung. A thin gelatinous region was present over the ventricles of the heart and red mottled tissue was noted at the right atrium. A firm torpedo-shaped abscess was noted in the liver adjacent to the ventriculus and a 2.5 in. nail was removed from the abscess and a tract was noted leading into the ventriculus. Adhesions were present between the liver and the ventriculus and omental adhesions were also noted to the ventriculus. A few granulomas were within the mesentery.

Right eye: Narrowing and descemetization of the ciliary cleft Segmental pre-iridal fibrovascular membrane with inferior ectropion uvea Lens luxation and moderate cortical cataractous change Inner to full thickness retinal atrophy; and segmental detachment Marked optic nerve atrophy; rarefaction; and gliosis Corneal edema; epithelial hyperplasia; parakeratosis; and fibrosis Focal staphyloma and fibrosis Comment Overall; the described histologic findings are consistent with chronic severe glaucoma; however; the exact cause of glaucoma is difficult to determine based on histologic findings. The ciliary cleft was diffusely narrowed; and endothelium and associated Descemet's membrane extended deep within the ciliary cleft. While it could be speculated that this contributed to glaucoma; this cannot be definitively confirmed as the singular cause of glaucoma. The ciliary cleft was otherwise not obstructed and there was no overt neoplastic population; evidence of active inflammatory process; or infectious agent within the examined sections. The focal peripheral area of corneal epithelial disruption and fibrosis dissecting under Descemet's membrane is of unknown significance; but likely represents a focus of scarring possibly related to prior corneal disease or trauma. Katie Barnes; DVM

AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION HEMOSIDEROSIS MACRORHABDIOSIS. This approximately 35- to 40-year-old flamingo was found in sternal recumbency at morning check and died within five minutes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition prominent keel no food in the proventriculus splenic enlargement thickened air sacs an inspissated mass possibly representing a cholelith or the gallbladder and absence of intracoelomic fat.

ANESTHETIC DEATH ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old female otter suffered cardiac arrest during recovery from anesthesia for routine health care. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. A male companion had a history of idiopathic bilateral nephrolithiasis and urolithiasis and also died in anesthetic recovery. At necropsy this animal had a grossly enlarged heart with pale tan to white streaks on the epicardium. Several small firm white foci were present in the lungs.

COELOMITIS CLOACAL ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female viper had a history of chronic cloacal disease. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy necrosis was identified adjacent to the cloaca. Abscessation with caseous material was present in the coelomic cavity.
PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE EUTHANASIA. This mouse is a 3-week-old weanling in an overcrowded cage. Ammonia toxicosis is suspected.
adult. Weight: 1402 g.  Euthanasia. Poor condition. Otitis; chronic. Nephritis; chronic. Tracheitis; haemorrhagic. Right ventricular hypertrophy. Atherosclerosis; suspect.

SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY/INFECTIOUS PROCESS GAS EMBOLI GOITER. This 13-year-old female pelican presented with a one-day history of illness received supportive care but died. Necropsy revealed mature cataract in the left eye thin body condition multiple cyst-like beads or granulomas scattered along the air sacs and body wall and a 2 cm. abscess in the right side of the body cavity. Air sacs were thickened thyroid glands were hypertrophied the epicardium was opaque the liver was swollen and reddened the right lobe of the liver was considerably larger than the left lobe multiple circular nonraised lesions were present along the hepatic serosal surface kidneys were symmetrical the spleen was markedly enlarged and congested and the oviduct was firm and contain inspissated material.
adult. Weight: 718.8 g.  Spondylosis thoracic spine. Arthritis left elbow.

GASTRITIS. This approximately 5-year-old male chinchilla died. It had a history of weakness ataxia labored breathing and poor righting reflex. Spinal trauma was suspected. Subcutaneous fluids and dexamethasone were administered. At necropsy the chinchilla was obese. The left lung was slightly cloudy. The gastric mucosa had patchy areas that were blackened. The liver was fatty and very friable.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS ADENITIS INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHRONIC KERATITIS. This 5-year-old female gecko had a history of mucopurulent ocular discharge and mineralization of the corneas. Swelling was noted caudal to the cloaca. The animal’s condition declined and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy mild weight loss was noted. Mucopurulent discharge was present in both eyes with opacity of the corneas. Scent glands were thickened and contained thick yellow exudate.

DROWNING. This male 1-year-old teal was found dead in wetlands exhibit. It had no previous history of problems. At necropsy there were lice present. The heart appeared mildly pale. There was frothy serosanguineous fluid in the lungs. There was moderate splenomegaly. The spleen was mottled on cut surface.

DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOUS INFLAMMATION MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This approximately 5-year-old male flying mouse completed quarantine on January 17th and was moved to the small mammal house with nine conspecifics. The animal was noted to be segregated from the group and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed poor nutritional condition hyperemia of the distal aspect of the distal tail prominent subcutaneous lymph nodes absence of abdominal fat stores marked splenomegaly mottled splenic capsule marked hepatomegaly and mesenteric and hilar lymphadenopathy. The right cranial lung lobe is consolidated and the intestine and pancreas appeared autolyzed.

SHOCK INTERSTITIAL NEPRHITIS RENAL CYSTS. This 1-year/10-month-old male dog was immobilized for annual examination and went into cardiovascular collapse during recovery. CPR was attempted but was not successful. At necropsy the dog was in good body condition. There were small 2-12 mm. multifocal cysts diffusely throughout both kidneys. There was a small twig in the fundus of the stomach.
SHOCK. This 8-year-old male duck was found dead at the bottom of the pool. At necropsy the heart was enlarged with thinning of the ventricular wall. The liver was enlarged dark purple and firm.

OOPHORITIS ENTERITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 2-year-old female spiny lizard had a history of bloody feces. Radiographs revealed multiple soft tissue masses in the caudal coelom. Blood work revealed marked heterophilia and azurophilia. Treatment was initiated with antibiotics and supportive care but the animal was found dead several days later. At necropsy the oral cavity contained a large quantity of tan material. The liver was pale and mottled. A small mass of pale green material was present in the large intestine. Numerous ovarian follicles were present which displaced the intestine and liver.

DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female saki presented with progressive polyarthropathy limited to the rear legs of five months duration. Joint fluid cultures have been negative. Supportive care was administered which relieved swelling but did not improve lameness. The animal had moderate leukocytosis and monocytosis and negative ANA and rickettsial titers. Marked neutrophilic inflammation with erythrophagocytosis was noted in the cytologic preparations of joint fluid. The animal subsequently developed enlarged abdominal lymph nodes. All known primate viral titers have been negative. Continued supportive care resulted in reduction and size of lymph nodes and lymph node biopsy (G13-2247) revealed histiocytic/neutrophilic lymphadenitis with microabscesses. Follow-up radiographs revealed bone abnormalities in the tibias although the animal was less painful and more stable. The animal then developed a sudden worsening of the lameness was sedated for bone biopsy and the biopsy procedure caused comminuted fracture of the tibia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple white raised firm lesions on the surface and in the parenchyma of the liver spleen kidney and pancreas. The tibia distal to the patellar ligament was fractured. The bone had abnormal gross architecture and was weak and broke irregularly. The wall of the stomach was swollen and edematous.

THYMOMA EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old male domestic goat presented with intermittent openmouthed breathing had a mildly increased respiratory rate compared to conspecifics and a large mass was visualized in the cranial thorax radiographically. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed some muscle wasting and abdominal enlargement 20 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity adhesions of the lungs pericardium and pleura some pulmonary atelectasis a 20 cm. variably necrotic and mottled mass containing clotted hemorrhagic fluid cranial and to the right of the heart and adhered to the pericardium. Apparent fat deposits were present throughout the mass which appeared somewhat lobulated. The heart was separated from the mass by a layer of fibrin or pericardium and was grossly normal with the exception of the right auricle which was pale and pitted.

VENTRICULAR ZYGOMYCOSIS. This 7-year-old male quail was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed thick tan liquid in the crop many seeds in the stomach thin tan fluid in the duodenum normal fecal material in the colon small tan liver mottled tan/red kidneys that are gritty on cut surface and desiccated eyes.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA HEPATIC CESTODIASIS. This 2-year-old female rate had a history of pneumonia and skin abrasions. Treatment was initiated however the animal later died. At necropsy lungs were firm and white to tan.

DYSTOCIA COELOMIC ADHESIONS BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS. This 13-year-old female chuckwalla had a five day history of dystocia and surgical correction was attempted. A large amount of adhesions to the ovaries liver and gastrointestinal tract were identified. The lizard recovered from surgery but was found dead the next morning. Necropsy revealed a pale liver that was diffusely mottled and a small pinpoint white nodule in the left lung.

INANITION RENAL GOUT SUSPECT MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 8-year/6-month-old male merganser died overnight. It presented the day prior to death ataxic and thin. It was treated with antibiotics. At necropsy the merganser was in poor body condition. There were numerous multifocal nodular lesions throughout all lung lobes that were more severe cranially. There were multifocal nodular lesions throughout all liver lobes. Frozen samples were collected for possible further testing.

NEUROPIL NECROSIS WITH HEMORRHAGE PROBABLE TRAUMA OR LOCALIZED VASCULAR DISTURBANCE INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE HISTIOCYTIC LYMPHADENITIS. This 3-year-old female domestic ferret has a history of chronic diarrhea and suspected inflammatory bowel disease. It developed acute neurologic disease and an MRI revealed a mass effect in the cranial cervical spine and possibly right temporal lobe. The animal developed opisthotonos and seizures and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed overweight condition macular crusting dermatitis along the tail and flanks three firm to cystic nodules in the pancreas up to 1 cm. in greatest dimension numerous prominent or enlarged jejunal and colonic lymph nodes a firm irregular mass of adipose tissue at the core of the mesenteric root slightly enlarged right adrenal gland compared to the left adrenal gland a focal red irregular intramedullary mass within the cervical spinal cord at C-1.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female hedgehog had a history of periodontal disease in all the dental arcades necessitating extraction of any molar/premolar teeth over the past year. It recently presented for inappetence and a 1 cm. ulcerated gingival mass was found on the left mandibular arcade. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

FIBROUS OSTEODYSTROPHY EUTHANASIA. This 6-week-old female hedgehog presented with unthriftiness and failure to grow in comparison to a sibling being approximately one-fifth the weight and size of its sibling. A curvature of the spine was noted on initial examination and radiographs revealed poor bone density throughout the skeleton with severe scoliosis and kyphosis. Congenital disease was considered likely and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed milk in the stomach and small intestines feces in the colon female reproductive tract pale kidneys moderate splenomegaly severe scoliosis to the left and kyphosis especially in the thoracic spine and less prominent in the lumbar spine. The long bones and bones of the skull were thin and fragile.

HEMORRHAGE MYOFIBER DEGENERATION SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS ULCERATIVE GLOSSITIS. This 12.5-year-old male zebra had an approximately eight hour history of facial trauma and moribund condition. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. A conspecific was found dead the previous day. Necropsy of this animal revealed white streaking on the serosal surface of the left ventricle petechiae on the serosal surfaces blood tinged fluid in the anterior portion of the digestive tract and multiple areas of petechiation or ecchymoses throughout the gut hemorrhage in the pancreas hemorrhage in the urinary bladder and hemorrhage at the corticomedullary junction of the kidneys.

GLOMERULONEPHRITIS THYMOMA ADRENAL ADENOMA INANITION. This 12-year 6-month-old male goat was found dead in its enclosure. It had a history of nonregenerative anemia. Recent kidney biopsy revealed a moderate mesangioproliferative glomerulonephritis. The goat was currently being treated for bloat. At necropsy there was a 3.5 x 3 in. pink alopecic lesion over the sternum. The corneas were slightly cloudy (OU). The lens was opaque (OU). The right atrioventricular and pulmonary valves had white mottled appearance. There was a large cystic mass (7 x 3.5 x 2 in.) found associated with the pericardium. The mass was very friable and yellow/white with nodular consistency. Both dorsal and ventral sacs of the rumen were fully distended with feed stuff. Fibrinous tags were present on the ruminal serosa. Mesenteric lymph nodes were large firm and white.

SEPTICEMIA GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS MYOCARDITIS COELOMITIS SPLENIC NECROSIS BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS. This greater than 22-year-old female milksnake was found dead. At necropsy the snake seemed to be in good body condition. The coelom was filled with approximately 30 cc. of thin serosanguineous fluid that contained a fair amount of white speckled flecked material. The coelomic cavity also contained multiple masses of different sizes. All were shaped in an elliptical manner ranging in size from 2-4 cm. long to 1-2 cm. wide. The masses were yellow to brown and appeared to have a gritty type pattern. On cut surface they were soft but held their shape and seemed to have concentric pattern. There was a mass present cranial to the heart base at the level of the distal trachea. The mass was tan with yellow specks and did not have concentric rings on cut surface. The splenopancreas was friable and had a mass. The gall bladder was enlarged and difficult to express on palpation.

EUTHANASIA LUMPY JAW RENAL CALCULI. This 6.5-year-old male wallaby was humanely euthanized due to severe “lumpy jaw”. This wallaby was originally diagnosed with tooth root abscesses and was administered antibiotics. There was some clinical improvement but subsequently became worse. At necropsy the wallaby was emaciated. There was bony lysis along the buccal aspect of the right mandible. There were tooth root abscesses of the three remaining right lower molars. There was mild ecchymosis at the pyloric area of the stomach on the luminal surface. There was mucosanguineous material with foul odor exuding toward the right middle lung lobe in the bronchus. The lungs were overall wet on cut section. The right submandibular lymph node was enlarged. There were renal calculi within the pelvis of the left kidney. Cultures of the mandibular abscess grew S. maltophilia. Cultures of lung grew Streptococcus viridans and Escherichia coli. Analysis of stone is pending.

EUTHANASIA ANEMIA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS INTESTINAL LEIOMYOSARCOMA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 12-year-old male jaguar had been under treatment for lameness. The animal became anorexic and anemic. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was pale tan. Marked emaciation was noted.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA PROBABLE CLOSTRIDIOSIS. This 3-year-old male lorikeet was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed moderate bruising and feather loss on the left side of the head. The liver was slightly enlarged with rounded edges and the spleen was approximately three times normal size hemorrhagic and friable. Small hemorrhages were noted in the lungs.

SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 7-year-old female lorikeet appeared to be normal in the morning but was then attacked by cagemates in the aviary and was presented dead. Necropsy revealed abrasions on the dorsal aspect of the skull little to no intracoelomic fat enlarged liver and spleen and dark red lungs.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female goat has a history of squamous cell carcinoma involving the right conjunctiva and vulva and recent signs of possible facial nerve abnormalities and a corneal ulcer in the right eye. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition flaking and scaling in the skin a 1 cm. raised mass present below the vulva mottled lungs abundant intracoelomic adipose tissue slight buccal points on the maxillary molars edematous and mucoid mesenteric lymph node firm masses within the wall of the urinary bladder clear fluid in the uterus with some pink discoloration of the mucosal surfaces of the uterus. A large hole was in the left rostral tentorium cerebelli and some pink tissue was associated with the brain in this region. A mucoid crust was on the surface of the right eye possibly subtended by a melting ulcer. Abscessed or caseous material was in the ventral periorbital region.

EPIDERMAL NECROSIS AND SLOUGHING. This 4-year-old male gecko had a three week history of a possible fungal skin infection with skin sloughing. Gross necropsy revealed no lesions other than the skin lesions.

DEGENERATIVE RENAL DISEASE VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS LINGUAL EPITHELIAL PLAQUES. This 10-year-old female snow leopard had been inappetent for three days was vomiting undigested food the first day and drinking excessively. Supportive care was administered. Necropsy revealed linear clusters of raised white papules on the cranial margins of the pulmonary lobes superficial linear ulcers in the left ventral aspect of the tongue many renal cysts and irregular mottled renal parenchyma.
adult. Weight: 349 g.  Mammary fibroadenoma.

BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS SEPTICEMIA. This 11-year/9-month-old female chuckwalla died. At necropsy the heart liver and lungs were very friable. The liver appeared to be enlarged with tiny discolored specks. The lungs were discolored. There was turbid fluid in the coelomic cavity. The stomach was empty. The left kidney was abnormal in color and size (large and friable). The left ovary had six mature eggs. One of the eggs was opened and the contents resembled a poached egg. The right ovary had small follicles. There were moderate amounts of fat stores.
AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7-year-old male sheep has a history of chronic weight loss with lethargy and acute pasty diarrhea. Necropsy revealed clear amber fluid in the chest cavity and pale kidneys.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS AND CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE BRIDGING PORTAL FIBROSIS. This approximately 11-year-old female raccoon had been deteriorating in activity level mentation status and behavior. Humane euthanasia was elected. Gross necropsy revealed a thin animal with diarrhea in the perianal area 100 ml. of clear to slightly opaque fluid in the abdomen pale kidneys firm tissue in the interventricular septum of the heart possible enlargement of the heart and a firm and gritty liver. The kidneys were also diffusely pale.

EMACIATION STRESS. LINGUAL CANDIDIASIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This approximately 2-month-old rabbit of unstated gender is in a reintroduction program. This rabbit and three others were included in a small mortality event. The rabbits had been captive born and raised and were placed in “hardening” pens approximately one month prior to death. Two animals were found dead on the same day. Traps were placed in the enclosure overnight and the following morning biologists found two dead rabbits in the traps. The water in the pen had become fetid and pelleted food left for the rabbits in the waterproof container had become moldy. Necropsy revealed emaciation food in the stomach reduced feces in the rectum that were small and hard absence of intra-abdominal fat and no other gross lesions.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA BILIARY AND RENAL CYSTS. This 6-year-old female ferret had a palpable fluid filled mass in the right cranial abdomen and mild hepatic enzyme elevations. It was found dead approximately one week later with no prior clinical signs of illness. Necropsy revealed two scabs on the right and left thorax behind the elbows enlargement of the heart spleen and liver. Multiple cystic fluid filled structures in the liver that contain serosanguineous fluid and varied in size from 2.5 mm. to 4 cm. in diameter. Multiple pinpoint orange foci were also detected in the hepatic parenchyma. The gastric serosa was hemorrhagic and the mucosa was thickened and hemorrhagic. The duodenal and proximal jejunal mucosa was reddened. The right kidney was thin walled and contained a cystic structure with serous fluid. The left kidney was thickened and had a pale pelvis. Two 0.25 cm. cyst-like structures were caudal to each kidney in the perirenal fat.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS OXALATE CRYSTALLURIA PULMONARY MINERALIZATION. This 18-year-old male leopard was lethargic and anorexic. The animal has a history of increasing BUN and creatinine. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were pale. Biliary cysts were noted in the liver.

EUTHANASIA INTERVETEBRAL DISK DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATIC NECROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 9-year-old female wallaby was found acutely down with hind limb paresis and ataxia. Vision loss was noted bilaterally. The animal was treated with steroids and supportive care for four days with little improvement in the neurologic status. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. At necropsy the lungs were congested with multiple areas of hemorrhage and atelectasis. The liver had a prominent reticular pattern with tan discoloration.  The spinal canal was compressed in the caudal thoracic and cranial lumbar regions. Foreign material consistent with disk material was present at T12-L1.

CRYPTOCOCCUS MEINGITIS ENCEPHALITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION. This 12-year-old female tamarin was anesthetized for contraceptive implant replacement. A canine tooth was avulsed during capture. Weight loss and aggression were noted and the animal was under treatment. The animal presented lethargic and dehydrated. Treatment was initiated; however seizures developed and the animal later died. At necropsy fat stores were reduced. The right liver was pale.

RENAL CELL CARCINOMA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA AND ADENOMYOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female African hunting dog arrived in quarantine from the Philadelphia Zoo and two days after release to exhibit was found severely dehydrated and moribund. Supportive care was administered during which time it was noted that the dog was neurologic. The dog initially responded to supportive care but then its condition deteriorated rapidly it developed renal failure and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed no fat and atrophy of muscle mass green bile in the stomach dark red/purple small and large intestinal mucosa black fecal material in the rectum multiple firm nodules in the pancreas a friable mottled red/tan mass in the cranial pole of the right kidney fluid-filled cyst in both ovaries irregularly shaped uterine horns with multiple variably-sized cystic structures in the mucosa and mucoid material in the lumina.

EUTHANASIA WEIGHT LOSS (CAUSE UNDETERMINED). This 2-year-old male leaf-tailed gecko has a history of continued weight loss despite treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed small fat pads in the caudal coelom mottled liver pale kidneys and no other abnormalities.

XANTHOMATOSIS DYSGERMINOMA BACTERIAL ABSCESS. This 13-year-old female gecko had a history of lethargy and weight loss and a mass was identified by ultrasound. Cytologic examination identified a neoplasm. Multiple masses were removed surgically and gout was noted during the surgical procedure. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed thin body condition white gritty material along ventral coelomic veins extending to the hepatic lobes and effacing approximately 50% of the lungs. Inspissated follicles were in the reproductive tract. The stomach contained cricket parts and the colon was moderately distended with fluid and ingesta. Adipose stores were atrophic.

EUTHANASIA BLEPHARITIS NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS. This 4-year-old female wallaby was under treatment for emaciation and lethargy. Approximately three weeks prior to death the animal’s face became swollen. Purulent material was noted in the left eye. The animal’s condition continued to decline despite antibiotic therapy. Serum chemistry revealed elevated CPK hypoglycemia hypocalcemia and elevated liver values. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated and had mucopurulent discharge in the left eye. There were adhesions of the heart to the body wall.

CARDIOMYOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This approximately 6-year-old male meerkat presented with acute dyspnea. Cardiac disease was suspected based on presentation radiographic and ultrasonographic findings. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a pale slightly rounded heart that was flaccid. The pericardium was adhered focally to the apex. A small amount of pericardial fluid was noted. The liver was possibly slightly enlarged. The left coxofemoral joint was malformed with abnormal acetabulum and no visible femoral head. Lungs were mottled and dark in some areas. Foamy material was in the trachea.

CONSPECIFIC TRAUMA. This 6-month-old male bighorn sheep had been attacked by a male bighorn sheep three days earlier. The following day it had blood in the urine and was lethargic and weak. It was found dead and necropsy revealed bruising throughout the caudal abdominal muscles fat and subcutaneous regions. Hemorrhage was in the wall of the bladder and the urine was bloody. Blood was present throughout the lungs. The kidneys were distended and the left ureter was partially torn.

POSTERIOR PARESIS POSSIBLE TOXIN EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female black footed ferret had a history of right hind limb paralysis and left hind limb paresis and radiographs and blood work revealed no abnormalities. The animal initially responded to glucocorticoids but the condition recurred and the patient deteriorated losing all motor function in both rear limbs and developing fecal incontinence and loss of deep pain. Elevated estradiol was noted in the serum. The animal began to self-mutilate its tail and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed diffuse bilateral alopecia on the caudal abdomen adequate body condition mild muscle atrophy of the rear limbs absence of the distal half of the tail 3 mm. umbilicated lesion in the cranial aspect of the cortex of the right kidney.

COLONIC IMPACTION ACUTE COLITIS INTESTINAL TREMATODIASIS. This 12-year-old male golden lion tamarin had a history of weight loss and IBD. The animal presented with inappetence and lethargy. A large quantity of feces was present in the colon. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy the animal was thin. No abdominal fat stores were identified. The distal colon contained a large quantity of fetid fecal material.

EUTHANASIA SARCOMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION. This 23-year-old male corn snake had a history of a sarcoma in the cervical region. The mass recurred and was enlarging and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a 0.5 cm. in diameter round mass was present at the level of C4-5. The mass appeared to be attached to the spine.

XANTHOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 15-year-old male leopard gecko has a history of progressive weight loss despite good appetite and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed five or six firm irregular white to yellow multilobulated masses ventral to the lungs and wrapped around the caudal vena cava. A scant amount of clear effusion was in the coelom and three irregular white/yellow masses were adhered to the left lateral and ventral body walls. The liver was mottled tan to dark brown the left ovary was mildly cystic. The right ovary was effaced by a 2 cm. ovoid firm yellow to brown mass.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA PODODERMATITIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS PHACOCLASTIC UVEITIS WITH KERATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 33-year-old female Humboldt penguin was euthanized due to development of a large pododermatitis lesion in the caudal plantar surface of the right foot. The bird also had degenerative joint disease in this right hock and was unable to extend the limb resulting in chronic pressure on the hock joint and caudal foot. The bird also had bilateral cataracts and a large corneal opacity in the right eye. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified exposed bone and necrosis associated with a tract in the hock joint. The stifle had a fused patella to the tibiotarsus. A large firm mass was on the caudal edge of the left lobe of the liver extending through the parenchyma. An additional firm polycystic mass was found in the medial portion of the left hepatic lobe. The ovary appeared inactive.

HEPATITIS AND MENINGOENCEPHALITIS. This 7.5-year-old male golden lion tamarin has a history of hyperbilirubinemia right-sided cardiac enlargement elevated hepatic enzymes and mild to moderate decrease in body weight. The animal was subsequently found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed icterus on all internal structures conjunctival and mucous membranes. Abdominal cavity had reduced fat stores and the liver was variably greenish in coloration with no apparent pattern of pigmentation. The parenchyma was subjectively mildly friable. The gallbladder could not be located. The stomach had a small focus of red discoloration. Some possible edema was noted in the ileum.

DERMATITIS AND DERMAL VASCULITIS BACTERIA OR YEAST-ASSOCIATED DERMATOPATHY SEPSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 6-year-old male fruit bat was found on the ground barely responsive and died in transport to the hospital. The bat had a history of wing web dermatitis two weeks earlier and biopsies identified chronic mixed-cell vasculitis with associated hyperplastic and ulcerative dermatitis (G14-4584). Necropsy revealed good body condition aside from multiple ulcerated skin lesions along the wing webs. The liver had a small pale region on the ventral aspect. No other abnormalities are noted.

MULTICENTRIC LYMPHOSARCOMA VISCERAL GOUT. This 1-year-old female chicken was found dead. It had an acute onset of left lameness on 8/3. It had some apparent stiffness in the hip or stifle joint but there were no obvious radiographic lesions. At necropsy the body condition was fair to thin. The feathers were stained on the ventrum with yellow/brown foul smelling liquid. The left leg was unable to be fully extended from the stifle and/or hip joint. There was an approximately 2 cm. focal dark brown discolored muscle on the right side of the keel. The pericardium was thick opaque and filled with thick flocculent yellow fluid. The myocardium was covered with white/yellow adherent material. The air sacs were uniformly thick opaque and adhered to the intestines and body wall. The lungs were red and congested with the left side darker and contained foamy yellow fluid when sectioned. The liver was friable. There were multiple pinpoint white foci throughout all lobes. The kidneys were uniformly pale and had multiple pinpoint white foci throughout. The spleen had multiple pinpoint white foci throughout. The serosal surface of the crop appeared hyperemic. The crop was filled with liquefied ingesta. There were loops of intestine adhered to air sacs. The ovary was active with multiple small follicles. The coelomic cavity was filled with yellowish opaque turbid fluid.

FACIAL CARCINOMA IRON STORAGE EUTHANASIA. This approximately 14-year-old female rock hyrax was euthanized due to declining quality of life over the last few days. Necropsy revealed good body condition and good postmortem condition no external wounds or scrapes calcification of the aortic valves congested lungs with some areas of dark purple discoloration and serous secretion on cut surface a 0.3 mm. yellow nodule on the intestine and another on the pancreas renal asymmetry with the left kidney smaller than the right and whitish cloudy urine in the urinary bladder.

LYMPHOMA. This 5-year-old female chinchilla has a history of weight loss decreased appetite loose stools lethargy and respiratory difficulty. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple masses in the lungs.

METABOLIC BONE DISEASE. This approximately 3-year/11-month-old female gecko was found dead. It was found with her tongue hanging out. She had been in declining condition for the past month. She has constantly laid eggs and was recently put on a calcium supplement. At necropsy the tail was lumpy. The gecko was getting ready to shed. The jaw was soft.

Whole body: Severe generalized edema. Severe thoracic and abdominal effusion. Pericardium: Moderate; diffuse; fibrinous pericarditis. Heart: Moderate; multifocal; fibrinous epicarditis. Colon: Colonic impaction. Bladder: Marked bladder distention. Forestomach: Moderate impaction. C3: Moderate; multifocal to coalescing; gastric ulceration. Lungs: Moderate; locally extensive; pulmonary congestion and consolidation. Comments The underlying cause of death could not be determined from gross examination. The severe generalized edema and thoracic and abdominal effusion may be due to underlying parasitism or other cause of protein loss. The impaction of the forestomach with distention of the intestines; colon; and bladder suggests a disturbance in normal gastrointestinal motility; possibly of neurologic origin. The fibrinous pericarditis; epicarditis and hemorrhagic lymph nodes may indicate systemic bacterial infection. Additional diagnostics including parasitology; bacteriology and histologic examination are pending and the results will be issued in the final report. Erin B. Howey; DVM Brain: Multifocal polioencephalomalacia. Heart: Severe diffuse fibrinous epicarditis; Moderate locally extensive myocardial degeneration with multifocal protozoal cysts. Liver: Severe; centrilobular to bridging; hepatic necrosis. Kidney: Multifocal membranous glomerulopathy; Moderate multifocal interstitial fibrosis; Mild multifocal renal tubular mineralization. Third compartment: Moderate multifocal mucosal erosion. Lymph node: Moderate to severe hemorrhage. Severe anemia. Polioencephalomalacia. Severe; centrilobular to bridging; hepatic necrosis. Comments The severe anemia noted in the clinical history is the most likely cause of many of the lesions observed grossly and histologically; however; an underlying cause of the anemia was not identified. The presence of an abundant amount of extramedullary hematopoiesis is a regenerative response to the anemia. Centrilobular necrosis within the liver is most likely due to hypoxia; secondary to the marked anemia. The polioencephalomalacia may be due to a thiamine deficiency or a hypoxic change. Thiamine deficiency can be a result of a thiamine deficient diet; decreased thiamine absorption; ingestion thiaminase containing plants or increased sulfur intake. Thiamine deficiency is difficult to definitively diagnose and is based on a combination of factors such as clinical neurologic signs; histopathological evidence; and testing of the environment and feed. The changes within the kidney can be contributed to the age of this animal and are not significant to the cause of death. The presence of numerous Giardia sp. as diagnosed through fecal examination may have contributed to this animals weight loss. The changes within the heart may be a hypoxic change as well; however; myocardial degeneration is often associated with Vitamin E and selenium deficiency in ruminants. Analysis for vitamin E and selenium deficiency is pending and the results will be issued in an addendum report. The abundant fibrin deposition on the epicardial and pericardial surfaces indicate an inflammatory response; however; no inciting organism was cultured. The protozoal cysts within myofibers are likely Sarcocystis sp. and are an incidental finding. Erin B. Howey; DVM \_ Comments This concludes the diagnostic testing for this case. Erin B. Howey; D

BACTERIAL ABSCESS WITH SEPSIS NEMATODIASIS OCHROBACTRUM. This 2.5-year-old waxy tree frog was being treated for a leg abscess associated with Ochrobactrum anthropi. The patient died while being treated. Necropsy revealed decreased body condition mottling in the region of the abscess but decreased size from previous evaluation clear yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity and absence of fat bodies.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS. This 8.5-year-old male sheep has a history of lameness. The animal was found down and was humanely euthanized. Abrasions and bruising were noted over the left hind limb with myiasis.

ENDOCARDITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CATARACT INANITION BACTERIAL MYOCARDITIS. This 17-year-old male teal had been under treatment for a possible infection. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the coelomic cavity contained opaque mucoid fluid. The liver was firm small and discolored pink.

GASTROENTERITIS GASTRIC FLAGELLATES PANCREATIC AND HEPATIC DUCTULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 6-year-old male wallaroo has a history of chronic weight loss clay-like soft stools and unthriftiness of three months duration. Serum chemistries revealed elevated hepatic enzymes and a fine needle aspirate of the liver revealed hepatic lipidosis (G11-5902). The animal died approximately one month later. Necropsy revealed a firm liver but with normal color size and shape. The bile duct appeared large with possible thickening of the wall. The intestines were distended with gas and some segments had focal or diffuse dark red coloring. One segment of the jejunum contained dark red feces.

BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 14-year-old male iguana had a history of intermittent episodes of hypercalcemia and elevated uric acid levels and pathologic fractures associated with metabolic bone disease that had been doing well for six months and was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed three firm white nodules free in the tracheal lumen inflated lungs atrophied right kidney and bilateral renal pallor.

UNIDENTIFIED APICOMPLEXAN PROTOZOAN INFECTION. This 3-year-old male meerkat had a history of progressive rear limb paralysis and was treated for three weeks with albendazole. The animal did not improve and was euthanized. There is a history of protozoan infection of conspecifics in the central nervous system. This animal was negative for toxoplasmosis and Neospora by serology.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS AND RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS SPIRILLIFORM GASTRITIS MYELOLIPOMAS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male cheetah had a history of chronic renal failure with depression and unwillingness to rise eat etc. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed chronic renal disease with small pale renal cortex and very irregular surface. The mucosa of the gastric fundus was thickened and some digested blood was present in the lumen. The animal was thin with severe muscle wasting. A fungal plaque was noted rostral to the left cerebral hemisphere in the sinus. The spleen had several white firm nodules to 0.5 cm. in greatest dimension. Adrenal glands were bilaterally enlarged.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS EGG YOLK COELOMITIS. This 5-year-old female chicken has been under treatment for crop stasis and laid an abnormal egg. The animal died spontaneously. At necropsy there were crop contents within the proximal trachea and serosal surfaces of intestinal organs were adhered to each other and multifocally dark red. A single abnormal egg was in the distal oviduct.
CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BACTERIAL HEPATITIS INANITION. This 3-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead and covered with mites. No significant findings were noted at necropsy.

INTESTINAL PERFORATION WITH ABSCESS FORMATION. This 10-year-old female Parma wallaby was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. The only medical history was some chronic tarsal arthritis. Necropsy revealed thickening of the tarsal joints decreased range of motion in the tarsal joints adequate adipose stores prominent thyroid glands subjectively thickened left ventricular wall 30 ml. of serosanguineous abdominal effusion liquid gastrointestinal contents and adhesion between the small intestine and colon at the root of the mesentery prominent mesenteric lymph nodes and possibly some purulent material in the mesentery at the focus of adhesion.

NASAL ADENOCARCINOMA SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA PORTAL ARTERIOLAR REDUPLICATION ADNEXAL GLANDULAR HYPERPLASIA AND ADENOMA BRAINSTEM ISCHEMIA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male African wild dog has a two week history of left-sided maxillary nasal mass with bone disruption and bone lysis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

SARCOCYSTOSIS VASCULITIS. This 7-year-old female lorikeet was attacked by other birds in the flock and isolated overnight. It was inappetent so was admitted to the hospital where antibiotic therapy was initiated. The bird died overnight. Necropsy revealed a yellow tinge to the tissues small foci of hemorrhage in the right pectoral muscle from an injection site clear fluid in the coelomic cavity enlarged liver and spleen hemorrhage and edema in the lungs and pale kidneys. Microscopic assessment of diff-quik stained impression smears showed intracytoplasmic inclusions suggestive of chlamydial infection.

CHRONIC OSTEOARTHRITIS VERTEBRAE MELANOSIS SPLENIC HEMANGIOMA CHRONIC FIBROSING GASTRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 26-year-old male boa has a history of osteitis deformans star gazing intermittent respiratory disease rib fractures cataracts and gaseous distention of the bowel. The snake also had a positive titer for paramyxovirus. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thickening of the duodenal mucosa irregular discolored vertebrae and cataracts.

DENTAL DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female prairie dog is one of several that were examined. This animal was noted to be thin and the upper incisors were missing. The lower incisors were severely overgrown. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition absence of incisors on the upper arcades and deep pockets in the gumline full of hay. A single small pedunculated nodule was present on the spleen and multiple small yellow plaques were on the omentum and within the stomach.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA PROBABLE YERSINIOSIS. This 10-year-old male bat was found dead on the floor of its cage with its mouth full of food. Necropsy revealed multiple coalescing 2 mm. yellow/white lesions throughout the liver and several in the spleen. The lungs were congested.

SUSPECT TOXIC HEPATOPATHY INTESTINAL BACTERIAL GRANULOMA. This female 12-year/1-month-old quail was found dead in exhibit. It had no premonitory clinical signs. At necropsy the bird had a distended lower abdomen with a bluish discoloration. There were droppings stuck around the vent and feathers. The lungs were hemorrhagic. There was ascites composed of yellow clear fluid. There was ileus in the middle intestine. There was intestinal stenosis caused by a granuloma. The granuloma was found in the lumen of the intestine and was well encapsulated.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL LUXATION. This 12-year-old male bat suffered a spinal luxation and fracture at the thoracolumbar junction. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the bat was obese. Displacement was noted in the vertebral column at the TL junction. Interphalangeal joints were swollen.

CARCINOMA WITH EXTENSION INTO CALVARIUM EUTHANASIA. This 19.5-year-old male mandrill had a recent history of stroke-like signs over the last 24 hours and a large brain mass was diagnosed by MRI. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed two large masses one inside the right occipital brain cavity with approximately 3 in. of bone missing due to bone lysis and a deep muscle mass in the occipital region. This animal also has a history of undifferentiated carcinoma excised off the right head region and moderate spondylosis.

ARTHRITIS EMACIATION RUMENITIS ABOMASITIS TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 18.5-year-old female gazelle had a deteriorating quality of life over a several week period and was found in sternal recumbency reluctant to get up or walk. Much laxity was noted in the joints of the front legs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and mild hemorrhagic appearance to the mucosa in the small intestine.

EUTHANASIA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This greater than 2-year-old female rat was humanely euthanized. It had a long history of dyspnea that would respond to antibiotics but retained a click sound when breathing. Cultures of the lung were performed.

TRAUMA MYOCARDIAL HEMORRHAGE RUMINAL HEMORRHAGE SHOCK INANITION. This 7-year-old male eland had a history of weight loss and arthritis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin. A wound was present extending from the skin into the thorax which contained food and hay. Similar material along with blood was present in the thorax. Herniation of the diaphragm with a loop of bowel was identified. Severe pulmonary hemorrhage was present.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 14-year-old female owl had a chronic history of difficulty perching. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy the liver was orange to brown.

EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS LEFT ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female ferret has a history of adrenal disease eosinophilia lethargy and poor quality of life. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mildly enlarged liver with blunted edges two dark masses in the right limb of the pancreas three-fold enlargement in the left adrenal gland.

NEPHROSIS HEMOLYSIS. This approximately 1-year/11-month-old male lory was found dead. It had a history of trauma that occurred during its initial quarantine and was unable to fly afterwards. It never fully recovered its ability to fly. Its feathers were in poor condition. Psittacine beak and feather disease and polyomavirus had been ruled out. At necropsy the eyes were sunken. The lory was dehydrated. The feathers were tattered. There was ingesta present within the proventriculus and gizzard and digesta present within the intestines.

TULAREMIA BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA PROBABLE PRIMARY PATHOGEN. This 3-year-old female golden lion tamarin presented with profound ataxia and died while being anesthetized for examination. Necropsy revealed thin body condition slightly pale and possibly hyperinsufflated lungs nodular enlarged spleen with white macronodules throughout the parenchyma reticulated pattern in the liver with mild to moderate blunting of the edges and slight yellow discoloration dark corticomedullary junction in the kidney and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA SUSPECT NEUROPATHY. This female greater than 6-year-old tree frog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of not being able to use its hind legs for the past month. It also stopped eating and was being force fed. It was also being treated with no clinical improvement. At necropsy there was a large amount of feces within the distal colon.

ASPERGILLOSIS SYSTEMIC LYMPHOCYTIC INFLAMMATION RENAL TREMATODIASIS. This 14-year-old tanager developed an acute onset of weakness received supportive care but subsequently died. Necropsy revealed adequate adipose stores mycotic plaques on the right pulmonary lobe inactive ovary and no other remarkable findings.

RUPTURED STOMACH SEPSIS. This 10-year-old male tiger was found dead in its indoor enclosure. It had been acting fine the past 48 hours. It had been found in right lateral recumbency under an elevated bench. Severe bloating and rigor mortis were present. Two small fecal boluses with frank blood were present in the exhibit behind the animal. Necropsy revealed good body condition. A ruptured stomach was noted along the greater curvature. Blood clots were adhered to the free edges of the serosal surface and five large blood clots were found in the abdominal cavity. Undigested food (27 lbs.) was dispersed throughout the abdominal cavity. The entire small intestinal tract was empty except for tan mucoid material lining mucosal surfaces. Lungs were dark red.
ROUND CELL NEOPLASM. This 6-year-old female buff-banded rail was found dead. At necropsy all hepatic lobes were very enlarged and had multifocal suspect abscesses throughout.
YOLK COELOMITIS. This female 4-year-old fulvous whistling duck was found dead. Necropsy revealed purulent debris in the coelomic cavity and a large necrotic focus in the ovarian region.

GASTRIC SPIROCHETOSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHRITIS SUSPECTED TO BE RELATED TO DIROFILARIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male Mexican wolf presented emaciated and in renal failure. The animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed poor body condition a nodule in the right thyroid gland three adult heartworms in the pulmonary artery dark purple gastric mucosa and plaques on the surface of the spleen.

BACTERIAL COLITIS WITH SEPSIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 2-year-old male lorikeet was found dead in the aviary in the morning and is the fifth lorikeet to have died in the last two weeks. Necropsy revealed feather loss on the head with associated erythema and trauma to the underlying skin lean body condition dried urates at the vent hemorrhage in the lungs friable liver serosal hemorrhage in the colon firm jejunum and hemorrhage around the cerebellum.

EPICARDITIS MYOCARDITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 9-year-old chicken was found dead. At necropsy the lungs were congested and had marked effusion. The heart was pale. The duodenum had a hemorrhagic mucosa. The reproductive tract contained two firm yellow objects.

BACTERIAL MICROABSCESSES YERSINIA-LIKE EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male ring-tailed lemur had a history of inappetence and slow deterioration that was not responding to medical therapy. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed copious translucent yellow-tinged fluid in the abdominal cavity multiple white raised nodules throughout the liver associated with mild hepatomegaly and two hepatic cysts. Bile was viscus. The left kidney was globoid and had a 1-2 mm. white fibrous streak at the junction of the cortex and medulla. The spleen contained numerous pale white raised nodules. The joints contained greenish-yellow fluid that was thickened. Marked synovial proliferation was noted but cartilage looked healthy.

ERYTHROPHAGOCYTOSIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS FOLLICULITIS. This 26-year-old female harbor seal has been on intensive treatment for hepatic disease and continued to deteriorate until it was found obtunded in the morning and dying shortly thereafter. The animal had elevated hepatic enzymes for several years that previously responded to Denamarin treatment. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a small corneal scar in the left thigh and a healed conjunctival flap in the right eye. Striated muscle was dark. Both mammary glands oozed thick light tan liquid consistent with milk. The liver was large friable and tan. Hepatic vessels were subjectively enlarged. The gastrohepatic lymph nodes were enlarged. The edges of the pancreas were darker than the rest of the pancreatic parenchyma resembling lymphoid tissue. The mucosa of the urinary bladder appeared thickened. The gastric mucosa had foci of hyperemia and some ulcers. The mucosa of the duodenum was thick. The colonic mucosa was thickened. The lungs had streaks of emphysema surrounded by slightly wet/heavy pulmonary parenchyma. Two small white plaques were on the serosal surface of the apex of the heart.

EUTHANASIA HEPATITIS MYOCARDITIS URATE STASIS. This 1-year-old chicken was euthanized due to chronic crop stasis and weight loss. At necropsy the crop was dilated and flaccid filled with ingesta. Other organs had no significant gross lesions.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA EOSINOPHILIC COLITIS. This 13-year/2-month-old male zebra was humanely euthanized. It got its foot caught in the fence and was hanging all night struggling. There was complete disarticulation of the left front pastern joint. There were multiple ligament and tendon ruptures. There were multiple lacerations and excoriations around the face left flank and left foreleg. The seminal vesicles were extremely large.

EMACIATION CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male parrot had a history of lethargy and inappetence of three days duration. Blood work revealed hypoproteinemia but no other abnormalities. Supportive care was administered but the bird was found dead. Necropsy revealed erosions in the mucosa of the proventriculus and a large amount of mucus present in the proventriculus. Yellow colored fluid was in the distal intestine and colon and some areas of hemorrhage were present throughout the intestine.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male budgerigar had a two day history of labored breathing fluffed appearance blue discoloration of the legs and feet thin body condition and decreased pectoral muscle mass. A large mass appeared to be distending the coelomic cavity. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple intracoelomic adhesions associated with the mass which appears to have originated from the right kidney.

CHRONIC GASTROENTEROCOLITIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA BILATERAL CHROMAFFIN CELL HYPERPLASIA. This 8-year-old female gerenuk has a history of ongoing diarrhea and unthriftiness with weight loss despite good appetite and energy level. It is one of several animals that have tested positive for Haemonchus and is being treated accordingly. This was the only animal that had diarrhea. Fecal exams had also been negative for other parasites Giardia Cryptosporidium and acid-fast bacteria. Fecal cultures grew two bile types of E. coli. Ruminal contents had normal appearing flora and pH. Blood work revealed hyperphosphatemia. This animal had been anesthetized for a diagnostic procedure that included surgical laparotomy and rigid endoscopy for biopsies of liver and small intestine. The animal had an uneventful anesthetic procedure and recovery but was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed poor nutritional status absence of adipose tissue hyperemia in the abomasal mucosa liquid digesta and feces in the lower alimentary tract and dark liquid digesta in the cecum. The hepatic parenchyma was mottled with small orange foci. Several dark islands of accessory splenic tissue were in the omentum and body wall. A fibrotic area was in the midbody of the uterus and several smaller glandular masses are associated with the lumen at this location. A larger glandular mass is in the uterine horn approximately 2 cm. in length.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE BACTERIAL COLITIS. This 14-year-old male tamarin has a recent history of acute respiratory distress that included fluid accumulation in the chest and the animal died while thoracocentesis was being attempted. Necropsy revealed edema in all tissues including the subcutis. The abdomen and chest were filled with blood-tinged fluid or hemorrhage. A scarred area was in the left kidney. The adrenals were large. The liver was firm. A large jelly-like clot was in the left thorax. The heart was enlarged and round with areas of hemorrhage in the pericardium. The lungs did not float in formalin. The thyroid was enlarged and multicolored. One testicle was considerably smaller than the other. Intestines had thickened areas of pink coloration possibly Peyer’s patches. Some free fibrin was noted in the abdomen.

EUTHANASIA ARTHROSIS RENAL CARCINOMA THYROID FOLLICULAR ADENOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA. This 13-year/4-month-old female warthog was humanely euthanized. It had severe arthritis. It had a history of slow moving and walking on its carpi. At necropsy there was callus and granulation tissue over the carpal joint on the lateral surface. On cut surface the joint surfaces were irregular and worn. There was a large 4 x 3 cm. abscess adhered to glandular tissue within the cervical region. On cut surface it was full of thin gray/tan granular liquid. Culture was performed. The stomach was very distended. Small intestine was hemorrhagic and purple to dark red/brown. The uterus was large and flaccid. It appeared hemorrhagic and purple to dark red/brown. It had two masses associated with it that were hard firm and white. One mass was at the uterine body and was 2 x 2 cm. and the other mass was at the caudal aspect of the cervix and was 5 x 7 cm. Both masses appeared fibrous in nature. The uterus contained multiple firm circular nodules within the uterine lining. The mucosal layer was red to pink and irregular on cut surface. The left kidney had a firm mass approximately 1 cm. in diameter that was raised in the cortex.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS PAPILLARY ADENOMA. This 11-year-old female fruit bat was hospitalized due to inability to fly and weight loss. The animal began to gain weight but was found dead unexpectedly. At gross necropsy the heart was larger than expected with thinning of the right ventricle. A large thyroid cyst was present in the right neck.

RENAL GOUT VISCERAL GOUT. This 5-year-old female chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy white powdery material was noted on the surface of the viscera. Kidneys were pale and gritty.

EUTHANASIA MESENTERIC INTESTINAL AND HEPATIC GRANULOMAS. This approximately 12-year-old female python was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed radiographically with complete fracture and luxation of the spinal vertebrae in the region of a kink. At necropsy there was a distinct kink and luxation noted approximately 30 cm. from the vent. On dissection a complete transverse fracture of the spinal vertebrae was noted with a large adherent 6-8 cm. diameter round mass that was comprised of dark red organized clotted material and cloudy brown exudate. This mass was cultured. There was also brown serous fluid in the coelomic cavity. The lungs appeared dark red and slightly thickened. The liver was slightly enlarged and dark red. This python had a history of a positive fecal culture for Mycobacterium avium and positive serology by IFA for Cryptosporidium.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS CAUSE OF DEATH UNDETERMINED. This is one of two 5-year-old female sibling meerkats housed indoors and in apparently good health. Their weights averaged just over 1 kg. Both appeared to be in good flesh with excellent appetites. They were found dead in a PCV connecting tunnel. There was no evidence of trauma or abrasions and both were in sleeping position next to each other. The carcasses were frozen prior to necropsy.
PNEUMONIA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA PANCREATIC HYPERPLASIA. This 9-year-old snake was found dead. Areas of intestinal intussusception were noted at necropsy.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS CUTANEOUS ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female/spayed fennec fox had a history of mildly elevated blood urea nitrogen in October 2011. In June 2012 the animal was lethargic with weakness and decreased appetite. Blood work revealed elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine. Supportive care was administered and radiographs revealed normal renal size and hepatomegaly. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to decline with elevated renal values. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed markedly thin body condition with moderate muscle wasting a single nodular firm cutaneous mass on the medial aspect of the left pelvic limb 1.5 cm. in diameter and at the level of the femoral diaphysis. The mass was mottled red/tan on cut surface. The heart was markedly enlarged compared to the size of the thoracic cavity occupying approximately two-thirds of the thoracic cavity. The caudal left pulmonary lobes were atelectatic. Approximately 2.5 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was in the pericardial sac. Moderate dental tartar and mild gingivitis were noted. The liver was diffusely red friable and had multiple raised tan to deep purple lesions over the surface of multiple lobes and margins of the lobes were rounded. Multiple round raised superficial masses that were cystic and filled with blood were present in the spleen. The urinary bladder was thickened.

ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BRONCHOPNEUMONIA HEPATITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 6.5-year-old female kangaroo was found dead. At necropsy the face was swollen and edematous with clotted blood at the nares. A 10 cm. pocket of dark gray to green fetid material was present over the occipital region. A 2 cm. in diameter blood filled lesion was present in the left caudal lung.

TRAUMA CHRONIC RUMENITIS CHRONIC ABOMASITIS AND ENTEROCOLITIS. This 3.5-year-old male southern gerenuk has a history of recent conspecific aggression and had a one-day history of lethargy with reluctance to move and was subsequently found dead in its stall. Necropsy revealed a hematoma over ribs #9-10 and #10-11 also on the left flank cranial to the thigh. A moderate amount of foam was in the trachea. Petechiae and bruising were noted in the soft tissues over the ribs on the right side and the left lung was congested. Multiple petechiae were at the base of the heart and within the myocardium. Hemorrhage was noted around the cervical spinal cord and cerebellum.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATION. This 1.5-year-old female black-tailed prairie dog was anesthetized to evaluate intermittent hematuria seen in the enclosure of the group in an attempt to identify the affected individual. This animal died unexpectedly under anesthesia. Necropsy was relatively unremarkable.

EUTHANASIA INTESTINAL LEIOMYOSARCOMA HEMATOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 7-year-old female prairie dog had a recent history of diarrhea and lethargy. The animal was in fair to poor body condition for the past several months. On physical exam an abdominal mass was identified. The animal was humanely euthanized due to age and intercurrent medical problems. At necropsy feces were pasted on the hindquarters and rear limbs. Uneven wear was noted in the cheek teeth. The right lung was dark pink and collapsed. Multiple pinpoint superficial white to tan raised lesions were present in the spleen. A 3 x 2 cm. round mass with a short peduncle was attached to the jejunum. On section the mass was homogeneous very dark red or black. Multiple firm tan to white nodules were present throughout the mesentery. Segmental aplasia was noted in the right uterine horn. The right kidney contained a 1.5 x 0.5 cm. black subcapsular mass.

LYMPHOSARCOMA. This greater than 7-year-old male sea lion died. It had been lethargic anorexic and coughing on and off for several weeks. It would not come off exhibit for diagnostics or treatment. It had a history of two strandings shot in the head and domoic acid exposure. It also had intermittent seizures before arriving at the zoo in December 2001. At necropsy there were two deep lacerations on the plantar aspect of the right rear flipper and a superficial laceration on the plantar aspect of the left rear flipper. There was mild dermatitis on the scrotum. There was a 10 cm. diameter firm raised nodular mass on the right side of the flank. Cut surface of the skin mass was mottled red/white and firm. The blubber layer was 11-13 cm. thick. There was a very large hematoma in the muscles medial to the right pectoral flipper. The lungs were wet and heavy. There were many 4-10 mm. white and red masses scattered throughout all lobes. The lungs were very edematous on cut surface. Mediastinal lymph nodes were very large. There was a 2 cm. firm red mass on the right side of the pericardium. There were 2-5 mm. firm masses (red and white) scattered throughout the heart. Similar masses were scattered throughout the mucosal surface of the esophagus. There were similar masses also on the omentum peritoneum in the liver on the serosal surface of the kidneys gall bladder and mucosal and serosal surfaces of all sections of bowel especially the colon. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. There was a 10 cm. circumferential mass in the distal colon. There were six 3-5 cm ulcerated nodules on the mucosal surface of the stomach. One nodule was submitted for culture. There were nodules present on the serosal surface of the urinary bladder.

EUTHANASIA INANITION ENTERITIS. This 7-year-old male rabbit had a history of tooth root disease and GI stasis. The animal’s condition declined despite treatment and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Minimal fat depots were present.

LYMPHOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 13-year-old male agouti was found cold and barely responsive. Supportive care was administered but the animal died a few hours later. Blood revealed renal disease. Necropsy revealed multiple masses in the stomach a mass in the proximal duodenum white masses in the pancreas multiple masses in the spleen pale liver cysts in the kidneys and some raised darker pigmented areas in the kidneys. The cranial bladder wall was thickened and the left testicle had a cystic cavity with orange fluid.
INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS HEPATITIS. This 3-year/6-month-old female parrot was found dead. At necropsy it was in good flesh. The small and large intestines were full of parasites.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 2-year-old male lory was found dead. Necropsy revealed ascites in the coelomic cavity inflammation and erythema in the duodenum and some gray patches on the serosal surfaces of the intestine.
adult. Weight: 306 g.  Euthanased.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 2-year-old female red kangaroo had a two day history of diarrhea. The joey was found outside its pouch yesterday and was dehydrated. The dam was anesthetized for physical examination and did not recover. Necropsy revealed flaccid pouch with one engorged teat. Mammary tissue was present and well developed with no evidence of infection. Petechiae were noted on the serosal surface of the heart. The jejunum and lungs were dark red.

NECK TRAUMA CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS. This 2-year-old female gazelle was noted to run into a fence and died before emergency treatment could be administered. This animal also ran into the fence one week earlier. Necropsy revealed two cervical fractures one at C2 and one at C4. C4 fracture is a slab fracture and C2 is a comminuted fracture that separated the body from the rest of the vertebra. Hemorrhage was noted around the soft tissues of C2 but not C4. Intestinal contents were present in the respiratory tract to the level of the terminal airways. A few pinpoint foci of ulceration were in the abomasum. Some hemorrhage was also noted in the myometrium of the left horn. The apex of the heart had a focus of pallor.

ENCEPHALITIS. This 2-year-old male coconut lorikeet presented with ataxia and head tilt. The bird initially stabilized but then developed an acute decline with torticollis and balance issues. The bird had been eating and maintaining weight. Other birds in the flock presented with similar clinical signs. Tests for zinc Chlamydophila West Nile virus avian paramyxovirus and avian influenza virus have all been negative. Several birds show mild to moderate Sarcocystis titers. There has been no response to treatment or supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a pale liver and large fat stores.

ACUTE CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS VASCULAR HYPERTROPHY CHRONIC COLITIS. This 37-year-old female lemur was found dead in the moat. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted in the right ear and both nares. An oval tail area was present on the serosa of the cecum.

SHOCK VENTRICULITIS. This approximately 22-year-old male flamingo died. The entire flock was captured and transported to the hospital for annual examination under anesthesia. This bird was very stressed during capture and restraint. Recovery from anesthesia was complete. When the bird was returned to the flock approximately 45 minutes after recovery from anesthesia he walked away from the keeper with no ataxia or disorientation. One minute later the keeper discovered the bird collapsed and nonresponsive. Upon arrival to the hospital the bird was intubated and CPR was attempted include manual ventilation and external compressions. Radiographs revealed a moderately to markedly enlarged cardiac silhouette. The lungs and air sacs appeared normal. At necropsy the bird was in good body condition. There was a moderate hematoma associated with the right jugular vein. There were several segments of the trachea that were gray to tan. There was no foamy fluid or hemorrhage in the tracheal lumen. The lungs were pink with scattered coalescing gray foci that extended into the parenchyma. The lungs were diffusely heavy wet and exuded pale pink foamy fluid on cut surface. Sections of lung floated in formalin. There was free serosanguineous fluid and coagulated blood in both cranial abdominal air sacs. There was 1-2 mm. of serous fluid filling but not tightly distending the pericardial sac. The epicardium appeared irregular with faint white streaking. The epicardial fat appeared edematous. The left atrioventricular valve had multiple smooth 1-2 mm. nodules. There was a fracture in the cranial dorsal part of the left and right liver lobes with adhered blood clots. The renal parenchyma was diffusely dark red.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA PULMONARY EDEMA AND CONGESTION. This 5-year/2-month-old female rabbit was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic ocular discharge. At necropsy the lungs were congested. There were two masses within the left uterine horn. One mass was 6 x 4 cm. and the other mass was 4 x 3 cm. in diameter. The masses completely involved the endometrium and myometrium but did not penetrate through the serosa.

GASTRIC ADENOCARCINOMA SMALL CELL LYMPHOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE CHOLELITHIASIS. This 6-year-old female ferret developed rapid weight loss and had a palpable mass in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen. The ferret also had low blood glucose. Exploratory surgery revealed a lesion in the stomach and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the lesion appeared to involve the pylorus and a possible lesion was also in the liver and lungs.

CHRONIC BACTERIAL PULMONARY ABSCESSES (TRUEPERELLA-LIKE) HYPERTROPHIC OSTEOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female red kangaroo had a history of pulmonary hypertrophic osteopathy that had been treated with various drugs but did not respond adequately and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed areas of alopecia on the tail proliferation on the surface of the metatarsal bone and right ulnar bone lobulated yellow masses in the left lung and no other remarkable gross findings.

HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS CECAL DIVERTICULUM EUTHANASIA. This approximately 6-year-old male pochard presented for coelomic distention. The animal was euthanized due to deteriorating clinical condition. Gross necropsy revealed a 5 in. diameter mass attached to the distal end of one caeca and adhered to the kidneys and testes. The mass contained abundant air and several firm fecal balls. The liver was firm and tan to yellow.

EMACIANTION (DAM) PRENATAL DEATH (FETI). This 12-year-old female ibex was found down in its pen and in shock. It died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed emaciation two fetuses in the placenta reddened lungs atrial petechiae thickened pericardium pale contracted spleen small kidneys with right unilateral irregularities hyperemic placenta thickened urinary bladder and a large ulcer on the upper palate. Serology was positive for leptospirosis.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS HEPATITIS SPLENITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 9-year-old male duck was thin and had an ulcerated mass in the right inguinal region. Radiographs revealed lysis of the femorotibial joints bilaterally. An aspirate of the mass revealed acid fast bacilli. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a 6 cm. subcutaneous mass and numerous smaller masses were present in the inguinal region. The liver was enlarged mottled and contained numerous granular foci.

EUTHANASIA MAMMARY FIBROADENOCARCINOMA CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS. This greater than 3-year-old female rat was humanely euthanized. It had a history of presumed mammary tumor that rapidly progressed in size. Other masses developed along the left and right mammary chain. At necropsy the rat was thin with a decreased muscle mass. There were two large distinct masses occurring in the right inguinal region. There were two masses in the left inguinal area. There was one mass over the sternum. The masses had a uniform appearance on cut surface and were light tan in color lobulated and granulated on cut surface. There were white very firm masses of varying size scattered throughout all of the inguinal and axillary masses. The lungs were mottled dark red to dark pink with multiple small white foci scattered across the serosal surface. Some of the foci extended into the parenchyma. The liver was dark red and soft. There was a small cyst present on the right ovary. The spleen was small and dark red. The kidneys were small. The cortex was dark red. There were small pale foci extending into the cortex on the left kidney. The medulla of both kidneys was diffusely pale.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA POSSIBLE SALMONELLOSIS. This 10-year-old male blue-crowned lory was found dead in its water bowl. It had a history of poor feather condition conspecific trauma and acid fast positive fecal stain in 2006. Necropsy revealed thin body condition absence of the majority of primary feathers on both wings all tail feathers and rough unkempt remaining feathers. Nails are long. No visible wounds are noted. Pale foci are in the right lung. The liver is grossly enlarged and occupies two-thirds of the coelomic cavity with rounded edges pinpoint pale foci throughout both lobes and friable parenchyma. The spleen is grossly enlarged and friable.

MYCOTIC DERMATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male panther chameleon had been treated for dermatitis and inanition. The lizard’s condition declined in spite of intensive therapy and appetite stimulation. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple ulcerative skin lesions along the trunk and some areas of darkly discolored skin not associated with active skin lesions. Fat stores were absent and serous atrophy of coelomic fat was noted. The liver was firm on cut surface. A 1 cm. long urate concretion was in the urodeum but not apparently associated with obstruction.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 2.5-year-old male hedgehog had a history of obesity intermittent hematuria and was found dead. Necropsy revealed enlarged right atrium bilateral adrenal gland enlargement mild hepatomegaly and mottled lungs that floated in formalin.

NEUROPIL NECROSIS WITH GLIOSIS. This 3-year-old female scarlet ibis had a history of neurologic signs that responded to therapy for two months. The bird was then found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed a yellow gelatinous area over the left hemisphere of the cerebrum.

FUNGAL PNEUMONIA BILIARY CYST RENAL GOUT CHRONIC KERATITIS. This 4-year-old male chameleon was being treated for emaciation and inappetence. At necropsy the right eye had corneal opacity. A large fluid filled cyst was present associated with the liver. Kidneys were firm with pinpoint white foci. The lung contained yellow mucoid material.
PULMONARY EDEMA BACTEREMIA. This 8-year-old glider was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA METABOLIC BONE DISEASE. This 7-year/1-month-old female gecko was humanely euthanized. It was a deformed animal which never behaved normally. It had a mandibular fracture on both sides possibly as a result of trauma. At necropsy the mandible was rubbery. The femur and tibia broke with a weak crack. There was ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract. There were white crystals around the heart and the heart was soft.

PROLIFERATIVE COLITIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female eland had gradual decline in body condition became emaciated had loose diarrhea for three years duration that did not respond to supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Numerous diagnostics were performed to determine the cause of the diarrhea but the condition remained idiopathic.
