Necropsy revealed emaciation sparse and brittle haircoat soiling of the tail perineum and rear legs with liquid diarrhea absence of fat stores skeletal muscle atrophy healed fracture of the left fourth rib absence of cavitary fat mildly to moderately enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes foam and aspirated food material in the trachea generalized pulmonary congestion mild nodular foci on the edges of the valve leaflets of the left and right AV valves mild to moderate periodontal disease thin walled enlarged rumen with light green frothy ingesta beaded and shortened ruminal papillae absence of formed stool in the distal intestine reddish nematodes in the cecum numerous raised soft somewhat nodular oval to oblong submucosal lesions in the spiral colon reddened colonic mucosa white glistening and bulging lesions corresponding to the nodules on cut surface and grossly normal descending colon and rectum. The right thyroid gland had a large cyst containing yellowish fluid and a small amount of glandular tissue on one wall of the cyst. Three smaller cysts are noted in the left thyroid. The left adrenal contains a small round white medullary mass.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATRIAL THROMBOSIS PASSIVE CONGESTION (LIVER) BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This 4-year-old hedgehog was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy moderate subcutaneous edema was noted. Serosanguineous fluid was present in the thorax. The heart was rounded with thickening of the left ventricle. Lungs were purple and reddened. One section sank in formalin.

RENAL CYST EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 7-year-old male/neutered ferret had a history of organomegaly and abdominal distention of two weeks duration. It had been on deslorelin for adrenal disease.

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male/neutered ferret was diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease and insulinoma approximately one year earlier and was managed with prednisolone omeprazole and a hypoallergenic diet. Over the past few weeks the ferret’s condition has slowly declined and more recently it developed a recurrent urinary tract infection with bilirubinuria. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting substantial adipose stores in the abdominal cavity small smooth pancreas with a red smooth lesion along the body absence of ingesta from the alimentary tract pale yellow liver and a firm consolidated lesion that extends through the parenchyma of one lobe. The kidneys were surrounded by a large amount of retroperitoneal fat and identification of the adrenal glands was difficult. The adrenals could not be located. A focus of alopecia was on the top of the head. Cataracts were bilateral.

INANITION PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA. This approximately 7-year/7-month-old male egret was found dead. At necropsy it was thin. The gall bladder was large. The intestines were empty. The air sacs were cloudy. The kidneys were pale.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 8-year-old male sheep was anesthetized with carfentanil and developed heart and respiratory arrest. Necropsy revealed multifocal purple lesions in the lungs of varying size. A moderate amount of fat was around the pericardium. The left and right ventricular walls seemed thickened.

GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS HYPERTROPHIC GASTRITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INANITION. This 5-year-old rattlesnake underwent gastroscopy due to a mid-coelomic swelling. The mucosa appeared abnormal and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the gastric mucosa was thickened and nodular.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA STEATITIS. This 1.5-year-old male mossy leaf-tailed gecko had a four week history of weight loss and decreased appetite. Nematode larvae and flagellates were noted in fecal examination. Supportive care was administered and two subsequent fecal examinations were negative for parasites. The gecko was subsequently found dead three days after treatment was discontinued with the tail avulsed and hemipenes exteriorized. Necropsy revealed thin body condition reddening of the ventral aspects of the rear legs mottled liver and identifiable intracoelomic fat.

EUTHANASIA ORAL FIBROSARCOMA. This greater than 10-year-old male snake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of poor body condition and swelling visible in the upper left maxilla for approximately two weeks. Radiographs indicated lysis of the left maxilla. At necropsy there was a mass surrounding the left maxilla. There were mummified eggs in the reproductive tract.

PROLIFERATIVE ESOPHAGITIS EUTHANSIA. This 13.5-year-old Dumeril’s ground boa is the third snake in the collection to show similar signs in the last three months. All have similar signs of lethargy poor muscle tone excessive esophageal mucous production and no response to various therapies. This snake was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed blood-tinged mucus in the esophagus rodent hair in the stomach and empty intestine with the exception of some normal fecal material in the colon.

ROUND CELL NEOPLASM UTERINE LEIOMYOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA SUPPURATIVE ENDOMETIRITIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION. This 14-year/6-month-old female warthog died. About 24-48 hours prior to death it seemed to be wobbly weak and possibly painful in the hindquarters. She was treated symptomatically. At necropsy the heart was slightly pale. Atrioventricular valves were thickened and irregular. The spleen was enlarged. There was a large mass 7-8 cm. in diameter with adhesions to the body wall and intestinal tract. There was hemorrhage in the spleen and body wall. There were multifocal areas of paintbrush hemorrhages and petechiae in both the small and large intestinal serosa. The uterus had multiple cysts along the serosa and within the wall of the uterus. There was a moderate amount of cream colored material in the body of the uterus. The left kidney had a 0.25 cm. diameter cyst on the cranial pole. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This greater than 7-year-old female ocellated turkey presented in thin body condition with weakness dyspnea and died during examination. Necropsy revealed large white firm caseous granulomas in multiple organs including the lungs air sacs liver and spleen. A conspecific died two months earlier under similar circumstances.

EUTHANASIA MYOSITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA BRONCHIOLO-ALVEOLAR HYPERPLASIA EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS. This 3.5-year-old male opossum has a history of progressive hind limb paresis and urine scald. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. At necropsy ulcers were present on the dorsal surfaces of both rear feet. Severe hind limb muscle atrophy was also noted. The lungs contained numerous pinpoint to 0.5 cm. diameter plaques. The liver contained numerous fluid filled cysts. The right cranial lobe contained a 2.5 x 1 cm. raised mass.

STEATITIS PNEUMONIA COLITIS SUSPECT HEAVY METAL TOXICOSIS. This greater than 4-year-old male caiman was found dead. It presented for anorexia and lethargy. Blood work was unremarkable. Radiographs suggested coin foreign bodies in the stomach. Endoscopy removed numerous hairballs but no coins. The caiman was treated with metronidazole and was force fed. Some stool was produced. The caiman became strong with feedings and was returned to the exhibit. At necropsy the caiman was in good condition. There were two lacerations at the left lateral aspect of the ventral scutes. There was an abrasion of the left upper eyelid. There were multifocal 0.5-3 cm. dark yellow to gold granular masses in the subcutis that sometimes coalesce to form sheets. There was a 5-8 mm. diameter lacy white epicardial lesion. There were multiple 2-4 mm. gold masses at the base of the heart. There were multiple 0.5-2 cm. firm tan masses adhered to the visceral pleura of the lungs. The lung parenchyma was dark to light gray with distinct delineation between the two colors. The light gray milky fluid was expressed from cut surface. There were 2-3 mm. yellow nodules on the dorsal pleural surface of the air sac. The liver was uniformly pale pink with sharp edges. The cranial ventral aspect contained two 1-2 cm. diameter firm pale yellow nodules that extended into the parenchyma. The stomach contained 3-5 rocks a dime a nickel and two pennies dated earlier than 1983. The caudal dorsal serosal surface was multifocally thickened with coalescing yellow nodules. Small and large intestinal lumen contained scant yellow mucoid material. The peri-intestinal tissue on the mesenteric aspect was completely effaced by firm coalescing yellow masses that had a cobblestone appearance on cut surface. The material extended into the mesentery and was 10-15 times the size of the contracted small intestine. Perirenal tissue was effaced by similar yellow material.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL GOUT MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SPLENIC HISTIOCYTOSIS MESENTERIC NEMATODIASIS. This 12-year-old male monitor had a prior history of elevated white blood cell count and possible ataxia or hind limb paresis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy marked renomegaly with urate stasis was noted. The myocardium had a localized area of pallor. Numerous 1 mm. pinpoint nodules were present in the serosa of the stomach. Advanced postmortem autolysis was also noted.

COLONIC IMPACTION BACTERIAL COLITIS WITH INTUSSUSCEPTION. This 2-year-old emerald tree boa had a history of mild cloacal prolapse and inability to defecate of several weeks duration. Examination revealed doughy material in the distal coelom and multiple attempts to flush the material were unsuccessful. Supportive care was administered and a contrast study was initiated. Some regurgitation and possible aspiration were suspected. The snake failed to pass feces overnight and died the following morning during physical exam. Necropsy revealed good body condition and an 8 cm. long swelling in the distal coelom immediately adjacent to the cloaca. Some inflamed cloacal tissue was prolapsed. An 8 cm. in length impaction of soft feces was in the colon. The distal cloaca was partially telescoped into the coprodeum. At the site of the impaction the mucosa was erythematous and inflamed.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY. This female greater than 3-year-old iguana died. It had chronic ulcerative skin disease. It had a large erosive granuloma ventral to the pubis. At necropsy the kidneys were very small.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY AND ARTERIOSCLEROSIS SUSPECTED LEPTOSPIROSIS SEPTICEMIA. This adult captive 21 year old Moustached Tamarin died after chronic illness. The tamarin had anemia dyspnea and alopecia over the back and tail. Necropsy findings were thickened gallbladder and renal infarcts. Kidney adrenal gland and liver are frozen for future use if needed.

PULMONARY MINERALIZATION LYMPHOSARCOMA DEGENERATIVE HETEROPHILS AND BACTERIA. This 13-month-old female chicken died spontaneously on 5/11/11. Necropsy revealed cachexia a dorsal cutaneous mass coelomic masses associated with the cloacal bursa and ovary multifocal areas of thickening in the caeca and ileum and caseous material within the oviduct.
NA

NEPHRITIS. This 9-year/1-month-old male toad was found dead in tank. It had no recent problems. The ventral chin and rear legs had red blotchy appearance. At necropsy the left forearm had a 1-2 mm. nodule under the skin. There was subcutaneous edema. There was ascites. There was a 2 cm. cystic structure in the region of the gall bladder/right liver lobe that was freely moveable on a tissue stalk with no apparent patent duct. The material in the cyst was yellow and gelatinous.

OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA PROLIFERATIVE PROVENTRICULITIS WITH NEMATODES (IN LUNG) EUTHANASIA. This 26-year-old female Inca tern presented for a distended coelom and weight loss. Endoscopy revealed adhesions and coelomic fluid and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 15 mm. mass in the region of the ovary associated with the adhesions opaque air sacs and severely congested right lung.

ACUTE SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 16-year-old male sea lion was doing well one hour prior to death. It was found in dorsal recumbency out of the water and unresponsive with a weak pulse agonal breathing and pale mucous membranes. The animal did not respond to resuscitation. Necropsy revealed no external wounds and an abundant fat layer. Lungs were wet on cut surface and dark red/purple discoloration was noted in the parenchyma. The larynx was hemorrhagic and the tonsils were enlarged. The spleen was enlarged and hemorrhagic. The right and left atrioventricular valves were extremely thickened. A small amount of hemorrhage was noted in the kidneys. The pancreas was gray and mottled. A mass of rope fibers and four small rocks were in the stomach and associated with gastric erosions and healed ulcers. Bruising of the skin and muscles on the cranial portion of the skull was noted.

CERVICAL MALFORMATION ESOPHAGEAL TRAUMA RHABDOMYOLYSIS EUTHANASIA THYROID ADENOMA. This 21-year-old female giraffe had a history of chronic weight loss despite supplemental increases in feed. Recently it had gone off feed and had no appetite or ingestion of food for two weeks. There was no response to treatment and the giraffe was euthanized. Necropsy revealed a flaccid heart with white streaks peracute aspiration a few areas of white scarring in the kidney and a small stone in the left kidney firm adhered pancreas multiple small blood filled ulcers in the abomasum and one large healed scarred ulcer in the abomasum small green/black tiny pebbles in the rumen and a bony mass on the fourth rib and ventral thoracic vertebrae 7-8. The neck had fusion of vertebrae 3-4 with a 45° angled malformation associated with the fusion. Other cervical vertebrae were twisted and curved toward the fused site.
HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE INANITION. This 14-year-old female milk snake was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

SEPSIS. This 8-year-old female captive bred golden lion tamarin died unexpectedly with no prior medical history. Necropsy revealed no evidence of trauma or disease except for the heart which had ventricular hypertrophy and decreased chamber size.

PROBABLE DROWNING. This 9-year-old female Inca tern was found floating in the pool after the pool had recently been filled. No abnormalities were noted in the flock prior to filling the exhibit pool. Necropsy revealed good body condition with no evidence of trauma. An active bumble lesion was present on the pad of the left foot. A 2 mm. polypoid cutaneous mass was present in the carpal area of the left wing. Frothy serosanguineous fluid was noted on cut surface of the left lung.

PANCREATIC ACINAR ADENOMA GINGIVAL NECROSIS ENDOCARDIOSIS EOSINOPHILLIC ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male raccoon had a history of a forepaw injury. The upper canine was broken and required extraction. Trauma to the maxillary bone occurred during the procedure. Elevations of renal and hepatic values developed the following week progressing to renal failure and free abdominal fluid. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the animal as obese. Bruising was noted over the sternum and ventral neck. Small areas of hemorrhage were noted in many tissues. A brown mass was noted at the heart base. Valves were roughened. Lungs were firm. The liver was enlarged and firm. A 2 cm. round mass was present in the pancreas. Necrotic tissue was identified adjacent to the forepaw injury.

ADENITIS (PREEN GLAND) ECTOPIC ADRENAL TISSUE SHOCK. This 16-year-old male ibis was brought indoors due to weather conditions and collapsed shortly after placement in the indoor holding area. The bird died en route to the hospital. At gross necropsy the meningeal vessels were congested and the coelom contained a large fat pad. A 1 mm. white to tan nodule was present on the surface of the left testicle. The myocardium was pale. A luxation was identified in the spinal column just anterior to the synsacrum; however no hemorrhage was associated with the lesion.

EMACIATION GASTRIC EROSION INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS (TICKS). This approximately 2- to 3-month-old rabbit was found dead in a humane trap while being prepared for release to the wild. The rabbit had been transferred to a different zoo one week earlier. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition with a few ticks in the integument. The stomach contained mucoid material but no ingesta. Formed feces were in the colon.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male slender-tailed meerkat has a six month history of renal disease and was involved in an outbreak of gastric impaction involving persimmon trichobezoars. Renal failure was discovered at that time and the animal has been monitored. The animal gained weight despite azotemia and was ambulating and acting well. The animal subsequently and unexpectedly was found depressed and stumbling inside its enclosure inappetent and examination revealed cysts in the kidneys and abnormal medullary architecture. Blood work revealed acute and chronic renal failure and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed congested wet lungs 8 mm. cyst in the right kidney and a 4 mm. cyst in the left kidney. The left kidney was smaller and shriveled on serosal surface and both kidneys were white to cream with subjectively enlarged renal pelvis. Numerous pinpoint petechiae were in the gastric mucosa and small brown fluid presumed to be digestive blood was in the lumen of the stomach. A small amount of feces were in the colon and cecum. Urine was clear in the urinary bladder.

CARDIOMYOPATHY LEUKOENCEPHALOMYELOPATHY PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY. This 34-year-old male gorilla died. It had a recent clinical disease characterized by heavy breathing when lying down. One month ago the gorilla had an acute increase in walking disability that was much worse on the hind left leg. The gorilla also had a history of edema that was treated with medication. The gorilla was found to have severe hypoalbuminemia anemia hypoproteinemia severe pleural effusion on the right side and abnormal nerve conduction of both hind legs that was worse on the right side (suggestive of disc disease around L4-L5). The gorilla did not recover completely from anesthesia and died later in the afternoon. At necropsy there was anasarca. The fat was firm yellow and watery. There were several gallons of yellow tinged bloody fluid within the thorax that was worse on the right side. There was abundant fluid in the lungs. The right lung was discolored (purple) with compression in some areas. The heart weighed 730 gm. The right ventricle appeared thin. There were white nodules noted on the lungs. The gall bladder was very large. The mucosa of the gall bladder appeared hemorrhagic. The liver was firm with purple mottling throughout. The abdomen was full of fluid. The pancreas was very rubbery and firm when cut. It was blue/purple. There were petechiae throughout the intestinal mucosa. There was small hemorrhage in the gastric mucosa. The adrenals were very thin. The right adrenal had multiple small round nodules on the outer surface. The jejunal-ileal junction had a firm white infiltrate in the serosa. The cecal mucosa appeared inflamed. There was an area of hemorrhage along the spine on the left side (T8-T9). A small square-shaped white firm mass was found in the vertebral space between the spinal cord and the vertebral wall.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 1-year-old male meerkat was found recumbent and nonresponsive and died shortly after. Several meerkats in the colony have died from toxoplasmosis. The animal initially presented depressed and ataxic with head tremors. It was treated with clindamycin tonazuril and carprofen. Its condition remained unchanged until the fourth day when it became more depressed with increased labored breathing and hypothermia. At necropsy there were adequate fat stores present in the abdominal cavity. The lungs were purple/red and wet. There were multiple round white lesions ranging from 1-3 mm. in diameter diffusely throughout the parenchyma. The heart was pale and had a globose shape. The liver was enlarged with blunted lobed edges. The surface was mottled pale and dark with a cobblestone-like pattern. The spleen was pale purple and contained a 2 mm. white round lesion on its surface that extended into the parenchyma. Cerebral vessels appeared prominent. Sections of lung and liver were frozen for future use if needed.

MENINGOENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female kangaroo has a two-month history of illness that includes episodes of decreased mentation and balancing. Blood work revealed thrombocytosis and no other abnormalities were detected. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to decline and developed clinical signs that included head pressing anisocoria and horizontal nystagmus. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified good body condition diffusely dark red lungs some bullae along the caudal margin of the left lung a small amount of light yellow clear urine and no other abnormalities.

DROWNED SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This approximately 19-year-old female California sea lion has had chronic eye issues and was treated with a combination of oral and topical medications. A few days prior to death the sea lion was exhibiting abnormal behavior that none of the keepers had observed before. The animal was observed eating snow around the exhibit and biting at the concrete. The animal was otherwise acting normal and eating well. The animal was subsequently found dead at the bottom of the pool in the morning. Necropsy revealed grossly normal eyes and area of ulceration or trauma on the right upper maxilla pale purple liver injected abdominal vascular enlarged vena cava and other vessels thick urinary bladder with a large firm mass on the uterine body measuring 9 cm. 002 in greatest dimension. Both ovaries were cystic and had dark areas on cut surface. The heart appeared subjectively enlarged. All pulmonary lobes were diffusely reddened.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA RENAL GOUT BACTERIAL ENTERITIS PANCREATITIS HEPATITIS. This 10-year-old male rattlesnake has a history of regurgitation and weight loss. Swelling was noted in the caudal coelom. The animal later died. At necropsy the kidneys were enlarged. White foci were noted in the intestine.

MAMMARY GLAND FIBROADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 1.5-year-old female roof rat was noted to have a mass in the ventral cervical region between the front legs. Over time the mass enlarged resulting in ambulatory problems and facial disfigurement. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA ATHEROSCLEROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 22-year-old male common marmoset was previously diagnosed with mammary gland adenocarcinoma one year earlier. The animal had gradually been losing weight and became inappetent over the last month could ambulate slowly and would only eat soft food until the last few days. The animal fell to the ground vocalizing and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a large rounded soft mass on the right thorax moderately rigid aorta large dark red liver with a granular appearance to the serosal surface pale tan pancreas and multinodular adrenals.

BILIARY CARCINOMA MYOCARDITIS. This 9-year-old male axolotl presented due to inability to submerge. The animal died shortly thereafter. At necropsy the liver contained a large yellow mass containing soft tissue and white granules of firm material. A small white mass was present on the ventricle of the heart.

FATTY LIVER OVIDUCTAL ADENOCARCINOMA BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA COLITIS. This approximately 29-year-old female boa constrictor was found dead. It had been anorexic for approximately 10 months. Keepers noted coughing and lethargy the day prior to death. At necropsy there were adequate fat stores. There was a tan colored frothy fluid within the mouth. Similar fluid was found within the lung. The lung appeared thickened and dark purple. The esophagus contained a mucoid material on the mucosa. The mucosa of the esophagus appeared to have ecchymoses proximal to the stomach. The small intestines were thickened uniformly and contained a thick mucoid material. The distal small intestine appeared ecchymotic. The colon contained three very soft fecal balls. The ovaries contained numerous follicles. The right ovary contained an inspissated follicle. The gall bladder was greatly enlarged. The thyroid appeared cystic.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA PULMONARY METASTATIC CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old female hedgehog has a long history of multiple tumors involving the mammary glands reproductive tract and most recently the maxilla. It had a history of weight loss and recent difficulty eating and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the right axilla and a small mass on the surface of the left lung. The liver was possibly enlarged.

ENDOMETRITIS PERITONITIS RETAINED PLACENTA GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS SHOCK. This 7-year-old female impala was under treatment for a suspected retained placenta. The animal’s condition declined and cardiopulmonary arrest ensued. At necropsy a large mass containing necrotic inspissated material is present in the uterine horn. Necrotic placental remnants are also present in the uterus.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS SALPINGITIS. This 5-year/10-month-old female Guam rail died. It lost 46 gms. of weight since the first of the year. It had been massively hounded and plucked by the male since the day prior to death. At necropsy there was diffuse traumatic feather loss. There was a large congealing mass in the caudal coelomic cavity around the oviduct. The mass contained white tubular material.

RHINITIS OTITIS CELLULITIS (HOCK) SEPSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 4-year-old female degu has a history of hair loss on the tail with scarring an open wound on the plantar surface of the left rear foot with associated lameness and subsequently developed difficulty breathing. Examination revealed a gas filled distended stomach some nasal crusting and developed cardiopulmonary arrest at the end of an anesthetic procedure (physical exam). The animal did not respond to resuscitation attempts. Necropsy revealed a cloudy blood-tinged nasal discharge hemorrhage in the lungs enlarged right adrenal gland severely enlarged left adrenal gland and a healing foot lesion.

UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 9-year-old female pygmy goat was found dead in the yard. The animal had been previously treated for pneumonia and a shoulder injury. At gross necropsy there was erosion of the articular surfaces of the left shoulder joint with periarticular fibrosis. Within the abdominal cavity there were numerous firm globoid masses from 2-8 mm. in diameter adherent to the peritoneum. The abdominal cavity contained a marked quantity of watery clear yellow fluid. The liver contained numerous firm white foci. The uterus was distended with mucoid to watery fluid.

MYCOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RIGHT VENTRICULAR DILATATION TUBULAR NEPHRITIS CANDIDIASIS (TONGUE). This 24-year-old male fruit bat was found dead. At necropsy the heart was enlarged and rounded. White material was present on the tongue and lips. Many teeth were missing.

TRACT FORMATION AND GLIOSIS BRAIN (PROBABLE BAYLISASCARIASIS) EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female wallaby had an eight week history of progressive neurologic signs. An exhibit mate had baylisascariasis (G12-4045). The animal of this report was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATRIAL THROMBOSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE RENAL MINERALIZATION WHITE MATTER VACUOLIZATION (WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME). This 4-year-old male hedgehog had a history of cardiomyopathy. Treatment was attempted; however the animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy white streaking was noted in the heart. The heart was enlarged and rounded. The tissue adjacent to the heart base was firm and yellow.
PREDATION. This 32-year-old female flamingo was found dead. It had been predated. At necropsy it was eviscerated.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male African hedgehog had an enucleation of the right eye in December 2012 due to anterior lens luxation and glaucoma. A right maxillary molar was easily extracted at the time of surgery. This animal subsequently developed a swelling on the right side of the maxillary arcade and a biopsy was consistent with squamous cell carcinoma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed prominent mandibular lymph nodes expansion and destruction of the right maxilla associated with a soft tissue mass.

EUTHANASIA PITUITARY ADENOMA CYSTIC BILIARY HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS BACTERIAL TRACHEITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 4-year-old female degu presented with weight loss and ataxia. Bilateral horizontal nystagmus head tremors and ataxia were noted. The animal was treated for head trauma and possible CNS infection. Mild improvement was noted over the next two days but then the animal’s condition rapidly declined. Dyspnea and openmouthed breathing developed and the animal became moribund. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. At necropsy ring-like round white foci with thinning of the mucosa was noted in the gastric wall. A large quantity of clotted blood was present over the cerebellum and brainstem.

PROTOZOAN ENCEPHALITIS. This 1.5-year-old female red panda had a two day history of left-sided head tilt and circling to the left with severe lethargy and anorexia. Blood culture CSF cytology and culture Toxoplasma serology and distemper PCR are pending. The animal’s condition rapidly declined and it was found nonambulatory with whole body tremors and anisocoria. Proprioceptive deficits are present in both hind limbs and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed congestion in the lungs and liver slightly enlarged cranial pole to the left kidney and no other gross abnormalities.
NA

RHABDOMYOLYSIS HYDROCEPHALUS NEPHROSCLEROSIS SALIVARY GLAND ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female opossum had a five-month history of a left sided thyroid mass and a one-month history of weakness or lameness in the hind limbs. The animal began to have intermittent anal prolapse when defecating. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

TYPHILITIS PERITONITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 6-year-old female capybara had a history of diarrhea. The animal developed an infection near the hock and was lame. The animal was found dead. At necropsy peritonitis with adhesions was present throughout the abdominal cavity. A multilobulated mass was present in the region of the cecum.

HEPATITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 7-year-old female meerkat died. It was a recent addition/arrival in January 2001. All laboratory work was normal at that time. It had a history of weight loss ataxia and cachexia. Lab work revealed elevated BUN AST and ALT. The rest was within normal limits. The meerkat was minimally responsive to fluids and antibiotics. At necropsy it weighed 500 gm. It was originally 780 gm. There was fibrin in the abdomen. There was fluid in the thorax and abdomen. The renal capsule was mottled. The heart was normal.

AMYLOIDOSIS VISCERAL GOUT HEPATIC NECROSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS BUMBLEFOOT EROSIVE VENTRICULITIS. This greater than 40-year-old male flamingo was found dead in its stall. It had been moved to a new exhibit three days prior to death. No clinical signs were noted the day of death. It was noted to be segregating itself from the flock and laying in sternal recumbency. It was weak and unable to rise. It had mild intentional head tremor. It had a slightly increased inspiratory effort and moderate respiratory click noted on auscultation. Emergency treatment was performed. At necropsy the flamingo had a moderate to good nutritional body condition. There was a small amount of green/black liquid present in the oral cavity. There was a 2 cm. in diameter swollen lesion on the plantar aspect of the left foot with a 1 cm. diameter area of superficial ulceration. There was moderate anthracosis within the lungs and air sacs. The blood vessels of the lower gastrointestinal tract and of the cerebrum were congested. The liver was moderately pale and friable. The kidneys were markedly enlarged and swollen. They were diffusely and bilaterally mottled white throughout. Tissues were submitted for submitted for West Nile virus testing.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC PLEURITIS. This 4-year-old snow leopard has a history of ovariohysterectomy followed one week later by jejunoscopy (bone foreign body) in April 2012 at a previous zoo. The animal represented in mid February for vomiting and decreased appetite and a mass was palpated in the gastrointestinal tract. Jejunoscopy was performed and a bone foreign body was removed. It was noted that the spleen had white fibrous web-like material on the capsular surface that was not easily removable or able to peel away. The animal presented a few days later with lethargy and had coughed up blood and by evening had become agonal and died. Necropsy revealed brown foul smelling effusion in the thorax and all pulmonary lobes were purple with consolidation and adhesions on the serosal surfaces. This animal also had an abnormality in the left eye.

CARDIOMYOPATHY PULMONARY ADENOMA. This 2-year-old female opossum was housed at BTM and used for education programs. The animal presented with partial anorexia of 48 hours duration and on exam was tachypneic and had a clear nasal discharge. The animal responded well to antibiotics and presented again with respiratory signs and declined rapidly over the next 48 hours. The animal became jaundiced had muffled right heart sounds dyspnea and a distended abdomen. A pleural effusion was detected radiographically accompanied by cardiomegaly elevated trachea and minimal air filled lung fields. Ascites was detected in the abdomen. Probable cardiac disease was diagnosed and the animal was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed thin body condition jaundice hepatomegaly ascites thoracic effusion pulmonary atelectasis multiple white foci on the parietal surface of the lung thin walled ventricles with dilated chambers.

ENCEPHALITIS HEPATITIS FATTY LIVER WEST NILE VIRUS INFECTION. This greater than 15-year-old female ibis was found dead. It was found in the flight cage in the afternoon. It had no previous clinical signs. At necropsy the ibis was in excellent nutritional condition with adequate muscling and moderate amount of fat stores. There was no evidence of mites. The heart had pale patches and streaks throughout the ventricular myocardium. The cloaca appeared thickened and edematous. The liver was severely enlarged and diffusely pale. It was friable. Sections of liver heart brain and kidney were submitted for West Nile virus testing. The bird was positive for WNV by PCR.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA URATE STASIS INANITION. This 3-year-old lizard had a history of conjunctivitis. The animal became inappetent and dehydrated and was under treatment. The animal was tube fed and regurgitated a small quantity. It was later found dead. At necropsy marked muscle wasting was noted. Food was present in the proximal trachea. A focal raised white lesion was present on the liver.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS PULMONARY FIBROSIS. This 19-year-old male jaguar has a three month history of anisocoria and chronic renal disease and an intermittent neurologic behavior. It has a six month history of weakness in the hind limbs. The cat also had a one day history of progressive neurologic signs and died prior to being euthanized.
NA

BAYLISASCARIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old rainbow lorikeet is part of an original group that presented with neurologic signs. This bird had been stabilized with medical therapy but neurologic signs did not substantially improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition with adequate fat stores. No gross lesions were seen.

XANTHOMATOSIS DISSECTING AORTIC ANEURYSM HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 8-year-old female leopard gecko was found dead and had no prior medical history. Necropsy revealed good body condition generalized pallor 6 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the coelom a central mass at the root of the mesentery that was firmly adhered to the ventral spinal column and connected to the liver and was dark purple with a granuloma in the center on cut surface. Many fibrous adhesions of the viscera were associated with the mass. The liver was enlarged yellow and soft mottled serosal surface and appeared necrotic on cut surface. Small white nodules were present on the surface of the liver in the adjacent mass. White nodules were noted at the base of the heart and pericardium. Both lungs were consolidated and contain white and yellow nodular tissues.

HEPATOPATHY POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS. This 13-year-old female Malayan tiger was receiving antibiotic therapy became icteric and died. Necropsy revealed generalized icterus some fibrinous mucosal lesions on the trachea two linear wall defects in the esophagus and thoracic area with associated intact mucosa pulmonary congestion in the down lung mild serosanguineous effusion in the thoracic cavity on the down side mild verrucous changes in the left atrioventricular valves few ecchymoses on both sides of the heart mild subpleural hemorrhages along the left ribs and under the vertebrae diffusely and severely demarcated lobulated pattern of pale yellow discoloration surrounded by congested zones with red perimeters in the liver a few 6 mm. in diameter pale nodules of pale yellow parenchyma suggesting hyperplasia thick walled gallbladder tortuous bile duct normal bile pale tan spots in the parenchyma of the pancreas plaque-like white thickenings in the capsule of the spleen and mild congestion in the parenchyma. Mild nodular thickening of the cortices of the adrenals deep cloudy yellow urine in the urinary bladder a large cavitated corpus luteum in the right ovary brown cloudy fluid in the stomach brown/black flocculent material adhered to the mucosa of the fundus no food in the alimentary tract and no feces.

COELOMITIS HEPATITIS. This 5-year-old lizard was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the liver was tan and friable. Multiple small white to tan granulomas were present in the coelomic cavity.

EUTHANASIA GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS GASTRITIS HEPATITIC LIPIDOSIS STEATITIS INANITION. This 6-year-old corn snake had been housed with a cryptosporidiosis positive rattlesnake. Regurgitation developed and marked weight loss ensued. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the snake was emaciated and pale. A coloboma was noted on the rostral portion of the iris of both eyes. The stomach was markedly enlarged due to mucosal thickening.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA SPERM GRANULOMA. This 5.5-year-old male kudu was anesthetized for a hoof trim. Anorexia and lethargy developed over the next few days and the animal was found down and tachypneic. The animal was found dead three days after the immobilization. At necropsy the pericardium was thickened and the epicardium was greenish-yellow. Hemorrhagic streaks were present in the myocardium. Fibrin tags covered the heart. The left ventricle was hemorrhagic with white plaques extending to the cut surface. The middle lobe of the left lung was gray/green and necrotic. The right lung was consolidated green and sank in formalin.

TRACHEITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ENTERITIS. This 14-year-old female colobus was recumbent and barely responsive. The animal was anesthetized for examination but initial workup was unrewarding. An exploratory surgery was performed. The animal regurgitated during anesthetic recovery and respiratory and cardiac arrest ensued. Resuscitation efforts were not successful. A blood culture taken at initial presentation revealed Bacillus sp. At necropsy the animal was thin. The left lung was markedly congested.

BLUE TONGUE INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS. This 4-month-old male pronghorn antelope had a one day history of lethargy developed disseminated intravascular coagulation and was found dead. Splenic tissue tested positive by PCR for blue tongue virus and negative for epizootic hemorrhagic disease virus. Necropsy identified bilateral inguinal bruising blood-tinged discharge from the nares areas of hemorrhage throughout the musculature of omentum and serosa red-tinged fluid in the pericardial sac and thorax multiple areas of hemorrhage in the epicardium and endocardium two firm dark red/brown nodules on the liver that did not extend into the parenchyma pale spleen a 2 cm. dark blue focus in the mucosa of the cecum and three smaller similar areas in the cecum and multiple pinpoint hemorrhages in the jejunum and proximal large intestine.

COLONIC AMEBIASIS WITH SEPSIS. This 17-year-old male Gila monster had a recent history of regurgitation and blood work obtained two weeks prior to death had moderate leukocytosis. Necropsy revealed decreased body condition adequate abdominal fat bodies diffusely pale tan kidneys with some streaking and no other gross abnormalities.

ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA ISLET ADENOMA APOCRINE GLAND ADENOMA (SKIN) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MYOCARDITIS. This 6-year-old male ferret had a history of a mass on the hind limb and near the anal region. The animal was humanely euthanized. A 1 cm. in diameter ulcerated mass was present on the left thigh. A large mass was present anterior to the left kidney.

MESENTERIC ABSCESS WITH DIC. This 7-year-old male red kangaroo has a history of partial anorexia with decreased activity and elevated white blood cell count with left shift. The animal appeared to be responding to therapy but was found dead. Necropsy revealed exsanguination into the abdominal cavity associated with a hemorrhagic mass at the root of the mesentery. Degenerative changes were noted in the liver some microabscesses or similar lesions were in the lung thrombosis was associated with the right atrioventricular valve and bilateral concretions were noted in the renal pelvises.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS FREEZE AND AUTOLYTIC ARTIFACT. This 2.5-year-old female nine-banded armadillo has a one week history of inappetence and no defecation. Abdominal exploratory surgery revealed gas in the alimentary tract and soft feces in the colon. An esophageal feeding tube was placed but the animal was found dead the following day. Necropsy revealed slight thickening of the pyloric outflow tract.

HEPATITIS. This approximately 5-year/3-month-old male duck was found dead on exhibit. There was no evidence of trauma. It had a previous history of pododermatitis. It was seen the night before behaving normally. Members of this flock have died with Mycobacterium avium. At necropsy the liver had a dark spot on one lobe. There was a dark 1 cm. focus on the spleen.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE HYPERTENSION CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS. This 13-year-old female tamarin recently was reported to be dyspneic with openmouthed breathing. The animal died and necropsy revealed a small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen and thorax pale and consolidated lungs subjectively enlarged heart worn teeth multiple pale foci in the serosa of the stomach that extend to the mucosa and no other abnormalities.

HEMOGLOBIN URIC NEPHROSIS SUBMASSIVE HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE LOW GRADE SEPSIS ACUTE PANCREATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male goat had recently been treated for colic but the patient’s signs progressed and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 60 ml. of dark yellow fluid in the abdominal cavity and 20 ml. of similar fluid in the thoracic cavity. Petechiae were noted and some pinpoint white chalky foci were noted in the adipose tissue adjacent to the pancreas and in the omentum. Lungs were dark red wet heavy and oozed white foam on cut surface. Pancreas was firm. Both adrenals were friable and had dark red medullae on cut surface. Multiple prominent lymph nodes were in the mesenteric root. The liver was firm tan and had focal areas of normal parenchyma. The jejunum had a segment that was thickened and had dark red/purple mucosa. The reticulum was edematous. The cecum was distended with gas and fluid.

SALIVARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS/HYDRONEPHROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female golden lion tamarin had a six week history of a large mass in the ventral neck region previously diagnosed as a salivary adenocarcinoma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes when the lesion recurred.

LYMPHOSARCOMA INANITION RENAL GOUT ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old female milksnake had a two week history of lethargy with a soft tissue mass in the midbody. The animal was later found dead. At necropsy fat depots were absent. A large cream colored mass was present in the mid coelom in the region of the splenopancreas. The lung was thickened and the liver was discolored olive green.
TOXOPLASMOSIS PROLIFERATIVE ENTEROCOLITIS. This 7-year-old female red kangaroo developed progressive ataxia of two weeks duration. Necropsy revealed weight loss and no other lesions.

GRANULOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old turkey is one of a group of eight specimens two of which died of mycobacteriosis. The remaining birds were euthanized. White granulomas were observed in multiple internal organs.

NECROTIZING MYOSITIS TRAUMA (PREDATION) EUTHANASIA. This 35-year-old male Chilean flamingo was attacked by a predator four days earlier. The wound was treated but progressed and necrosis occurred over a large part of the right caudal body and right leg. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

GERIATRIC ANIMAL WITH LEFT VENTRICULAR SUBENDOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 39-year-old captive bred male Chilean flamingo was found dead in the pool. Gross necropsy revealed mild streaking of the epicardium a 3 mm. thick right ventricular free wall fluid in the crop and distal esophagus bumblefoot lesions on the feet that do not appear infected excellent feather condition congestion in the pancreas a soft spleen dark kidneys and excellent to obese body condition.

BACTERIAL SEPSIS MENINGITIS. This greater than 31-year-old male American flamingo was acting lethargic and had bizarre behavior before becoming moribund and died en route to the hospital. Necropsy revealed severe cranial and cerebral hemorrhage.

ULCERATIVE COLITIS AND CLOACITIS YOLK COELOMITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female milksnake developed sudden onset of swelling in the caudal portion with complete paralysis below the level of the kidneys and no associated pain response. Exploratory celiotomy revealed multiple organ system involvement and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a tan “fatty” liver blood with the lower gastrointestinal tract associated with an ill-define mass or clot obstructing the coprodeum and associated urate impaction. Several degenerative follicles were dark and inspissated and much inflammation was in the adipose tissue and soft tissues at the level of the ovaries.

PULMONARY SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 6-year-old female lory has a history of sitting normally on its perch five minutes prior to dying and had no obvious injury or illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition moderately enlarged liver tear in the liver associated with a blood clot markedly enlarged spleen dark red lungs that sink in formalin and pale kidney.

GOUT MINERALIZATON. This greater than 12-year-old bull snake was euthanized. It had a partial obstruction of the jejunum due to jejunal thickening. This animal had been housed with bull snake #4121 (undifferentiated coelomic sarcoma). Necropsy of this snake revealed emaciation white irregular shaped structures ventral to the vertebrae in the mid-region of the snake. The material appeared purulent. Serous fluid was in the caudal coelomic cavity. The spleen was covered with multifocal pinpoint pale foci that extended through the parenchyma. Similar foci were in the liver. The mucosa of the duodenum was thickened and green. The jejunum was also thickened. About 20 cm. distal to the pylorus the jejunal lumen was narrowed almost to the point of total closure. Culture of the spinal lesions revealed Proteus sp.

Please see comments Comments There were no significant gross findings suggestive of a cause of death in this animal. Histology of the major organs are in progress; and findings will be included in the final report. Ong Chee Bing; BVSc Stomach: Severe; focal; gastric pyloric ulceration Kidney: Mild; diffuse; membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis; and mild multifocal neutrophilic interstitial nephritis Lung: Diffuse; chronic; moderate interstitial pneumonia; smooth muscle hyperplasia; and vascular arteriolar sclerosis Thyroid gland: Severe; bilateral thyroid atrophy Spleen: Lymphoid germinal center necrosis Comments Histological findings of gastric ulceration; splenic lympholysis are most likely stress related. The suspected glomerulonephritis was mild; and may be a variation of normal in this species. There was evidence of diffuse pulmonary interstitial change and smooth muscle hyperplasia; although the cause was not evident histologically. The fatty infiltration into pulmonary arteriole wall is indicative of arteriolar sclerosis; and possibility of antemortem hypertension was discussed. This differential could also explain the glomerular changes in the kidney.
