BACTERIAL CELLULITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE SPLENIC EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS. This 12-year-old female cotton-topped tamarin developed acute lethargy and lack of response and arrested while being examined. Resuscitation was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed good body condition although slight weight loss from previous exams. A 1 cm. skin wound associated with foul odor was distal to the base of the head and a large amount of green/black malodorous liquid was present within the wound. Extensive necrosis was present throughout the connective tissues in this region and extended to the ventral aspect of the neck. The left lungs were variably atelectatic. A thin rim of dark red tissue was on the right hepatic border and the liver appeared to be slightly enlarged. Several hyperemic foci were in the jejunum. The right adrenal gland was enlarged. The left adrenal gland could not be located. A dark red firm round lobulated mass was in the caudal abdomen between the kidneys extending distally to the level of the uterus but not attached to the uterus. One lobe of the mass was 2 cm. in diameter and the cranial aspect 1 cm. in diameter. Four adjacent spherical masses were also noted and on cut surfaces had a hemorrhagic appearance.
PNEUMONIA AIR SACCULITIS SHOCK. This 2-year-old parrot was found down with marked weight loss. The animal died during examination. At necropsy lungs were wet and heavy. The spleen was enlarged.

HEPATIC COPPER STORAGE BRONCHOGENIC ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male Navajo sheep had a history of hypoglycemia and suspected seizure. The sheep also had a pleural effusion inappetence and weight loss. This sheep is also of a phenotype with four horns and eyelid agenesis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed a large mass adhered to the cranial ventral chest wall covered in fibrous tissue and filled with soft brown smooth tissue. A pleural effusion was present in the thoracic cavity and the effusion was yellow and clear. Lungs were consolidated and atelectatic with patchy red coloration. The liver was pale small and had smooth parenchyma with sharp edges. Muscles were atrophic.
NA
HEPATITIS PANCREATITIS. This 3-year-old lorikeet was found down and died despite treatment. Recent mortalities have occurred in the flock due to West Nile virus. At necropsy the liver was streaked.

ATROPHIC RHINITIS ENCEPHALITIS AND HEPATITIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 4-year-old male rabbit had a history of intermittent mild respiratory disease of a few years duration and had been treated with antibiotics for three weeks. Two days after discontinuation of the antibiotics clinical signs worsened again. The animal was immobilized for evaluation of abnormal mastication ocular and nasal discharge with abnormal ear positioning but arrested while anesthetized and could not be resuscitated. Blood work at the time revealed mild leukocytosis and radiographs revealed mild elongation of all premolars molars and mandibular incisors. Necropsy revealed dark red firm lungs that did not float in formalin complete destruction of the right nasal turbinates and right nasal passage partial bone lysis of the cribriform plate on the right side pinpoint foci of brown/black coloration throughout the meninges of the cortex purulent exudate in the right external ear canal and thickening of the left and right tympanic bullae with luminal purulent discharge in the bullae.

WEST NILE VIRUS ENTERITIS HEPATIC AND PANCREATIC NECROSIS. This 5-year/7-month-old male lory died. It was admitted to the hospital for treatment of suspected flock outbreak of Salmonella. This bird was quiet lethargic and fluffed for several days. AST was 1124 CK was 1137 and there was hyperglobulinemia. The bird improved but then deteriorated rapidly. Thus far three of thirty birds in the flock are positive by PCR for Salmonella. At necropsy the lorikeet was in good body condition. The choanal papillae were severely blunted. There was bruising of the right mandibular skin and along the right side of the neck. There was clotted blood present along the entire length of the right jugular vein. The liver was enlarged with rounded edges. It was diffusely mottled tan to pale red with prominent vascular pattern. The kidneys were mildly pale.

HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS INTESTINAL AMYLOIDOSIS ENTERITIS. This 19-year-old male swan was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy air sacs were thickened and cloudy. A small quantity of clear yellow/tan fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. The liver was firm and white to tan. The cecum was distended with clotted blood.
adult.  Haemorrhagic neck muscles.  Cranial haemorrhage.  Possible rodenticide poisoning +/- trauma.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS WITH GOUT PORTAL HEPATITIS AND INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This greater than 14-year-old cattle egret had a decrease in its appetite over a two day period and became lethargic. The bird was treated with supportive care but was found dead the following day. Necropsy revealed a decrease in pectoral musculature hepatomegaly and no other findings.

LYMPHOMA TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male mandrill was euthanized due to weight loss dehydration inappetence and cutaneous lymphoma. Necropsy revealed multiple ulcerated cutaneous nodules in the inguinal region polycystic accessory gland in the pelvic canal multinodular liver with multiple small yellow to white foci on the capsular surface and occasionally within the parenchyma white nodules in the parenchyma of the lungs enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes a multinodular soft white mass in the submandibular region enlarged left thyroid thickening of the meninges along the midline fractured lower left premolar and pale kidneys.
NEPHRITIS ABOMASITIS BACTERIAL RUMENITIS THYROID ADENOMA. This captive bred 13-year-old female addra died. Necropsy report to follow.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA. This greater than 3-year-old male rat died unexpectedly. It had normal appetite and behavior during the day then apparently fell over and died. It had a recent abscess caudal to the left external ear that resolved and no remnant abscess was noted. Necropsy revealed an isolated lesion on the surface of the liver some darkening of the small intestine and possibly some darkening of the atrial appendage of the heart. Possible abnormal periorbital tissue was noted behind the left eye and a possible clot was noted around the circle of Willis.

MYCOTIC VASCULITIS. This 7-year-old male coconut lorikeet presented with ataxia and trauma to the skin of the head attributed to conspecific aggression. The bird stabilized and wounds were healing but then it presented with a left wing droop and significant swelling of the left pectoral muscle with no bone trauma noted radiographically. Supportive care was administered and the wing droop and pectoral swelling resolved although pectoral muscle was sunken and irregular. The bird had been eating and acting normally but suddenly declined with lethargy weakness and inappetence. The bird died despite supportive care. Other birds in the flock presented with similar clinical signs but no wing droop or muscle concerns. Tests for zinc Chlamydophila West Nile virus avian paramyxovirus and avian influenza virus have all been negative in various birds. Several birds show mild to moderate Sarcocystis titers. This bird was treated accordingly for sarcocystosis but died. Necropsy revealed pale green rubbery left pectoral muscle pale liver with capsular fibrosis pale kidneys and no other abnormalities.

EMACIATION. This 6.5-year-old male rhinoceros viper has a history of respiratory infections and the last episode resolved three months earlier. The snake developed a one-month history of inappetence and was found dead on exhibit with no other clinical signs of illness or injury. Necropsy revealed thin body condition prominent dorsal spinous processes male reproductive tract and some possible old fractured ribs. No adipose stores were identified.

Coelomic cavity: Mesothelial proliferation with yolk aggregates (suggestive of yolk coelomitis) Liver: Moderate melanomacrophage center hyperplasia Comments The histologic findings were most consistent with a florid mesothelial proliferation within the coelomic cavity and covering the surface of multiple coelomic organs. The presence of yolk associated with the areas of mesothelial proliferation was suggestive of an underlying yolk coelomitis. Yolk coelomitis is a well-recognized problem and a significant cause of death in captive adult female lizards; particularly Fiji Island Iguanas (see Stacy et al; J Zoo Wildl Med. 2008 Jun;39(2):161-9.Yolk coelomitis in Fiji Island banded iguanas (Brachylophus fasciatus).The proliferative mesothelial cell population was considered to be a reactive response to free intracoelomic yolk based on the signalment (mature female). The basis for the florid mesothelial response is not known; however it is thought to be influenced by the volume of yolk present ant the chronicity of coelomitis. Jennifer Lamoureux; D

ASPIRATION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS MILD CARDIAC DISEASE BALANTIDIUM COLITIS. This male approximately 17-year-old gorilla was immobilized for tooth repair/implant and yearly physical exam but aspirated during induction and died in recovery. At necropsy this gorilla was in good hydration. There was a 4.5 in. x 3 in. area of hemorrhage on the lateral caudal aspect next to the umbilicus and an area of skin hemorrhage within the left inguinal region. Mucous membranes were pale gray. There was severe pulmonary edema of all lobes. There was emphysema in the cranial and left mediastinum. Stomach jejunum duodenum and ileum contain air and ingesta as well as partially digested matter. The stomach also had extensive aerophagia.
NA

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS HEMOSIDEROSIS INANITION. This 34-year-old male flamingo was humanely euthanized. It had a two to three month history of a swollen tibiotarsal joint. At necropsy there was septic arthritis. No other gross lesions were found.

EMACIATION HEPATIC GLYCOGENOSIS URINARY BLADDER HEMORRHAGE. This 16-year-old female Seba’s short-tailed bat was removed from exhibit for difficulty flying. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the animal was in thin nutritional and muscular condition. There was a small amount of free fluid within the caudal aspect of the abdomen. The heart was subjectively enlarged. There was dark red fluid within the lumen of the urinary bladder.

CHRONIC ENTERITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 14-year-old male/neutered squirrel monkey had a history of weight loss anemia mildly elevated hepatic enzymes and radiographic evidence of diffuse intestinal disease. The animal also had mild spondylosis. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed absence of body fat mildly dilated and mildly thickened intestines and no other abnormalities.
BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 7-year-old female red lory died and necropsy revealed hepatomegaly with yellow discoloration and dilated intestines with ulcers.
See elephant paper

ULCERATIVE PODODERMATITIS LOW-GRADE SEPSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male turkey had a long history of degenerative joint disease and bumblefoot. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed several filarid worms in the small intestine and no other abnormalities.

PANCREATITIS ABDOMINAL AND THROACIC TRAUMA. This 4.5-year-old female meercat was found dead with no prior clinical signs. Necropsy revealed very good nutritional status with large amount of adipose. A bruised area with hair loss approximately 5 mm. in diameter was over the left pelvic area. The cranial left lung lobe was approximately 90% torn in half. A blood clot extended from this lung lobe around the apex of the heart. The lungs were mottled purple/pink. Periodontal disease was moderate. The abdomen contained approximately 90 ml. of pink blood that upon clotting formed a thick lipid layer on the surface of the clot. The spleen was severed in half with a large blood clot extending from the cut surfaces. The left liver lobes had a macerated/crushed appearance and were friable in these areas. The pancreas was crushed and in an early stage of necrosis. Multiple firm white masses were present in the caudal body of the pancreas. A large amount of food was in the stomach.  A few small pale areas were present in the cortex of the kidneys. A culture of small intestine was positive for Salmonella.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS DROWNED. This 14-year-old female meerkat was found dead in the moat around the exhibit. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of white/pink froth in the trachea. Kidneys were bilaterally small and pale tan. Some pelvic ectasia was noted on cut surface of the kidneys.

EMACIATION VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE CHOLESTASIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS VASCULITIS AND HYPERTENSION. This 18-year-old male Bali mynah died. Necropsy revealed pale gray koilin layer with no bile staining and multifocal dark discoloration and degeneration of the koilin layer. Mild hepatic enlargement was noted and the pancreas was pale.

YOLK COELOMITIS ECTOPIC EGG MICROGRANULOMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female duck presented with a distended coelom and diagnostics indicated yolk coelomitis. Surgery was performed to lavage and extract yolks but was discontinued and the bird was euthanized while anesthetized due to compartmentalization and extensive adhesions in the coelom. Rare diplococci were seen on presurgical cytology but no growth was obtained from cultures.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS ENTERITIS. This greater than 25-year-old male flamingo died. The flock had been transferred to a new enclosure due to construction. The bird was presented alive for processing and had a web hematoma of the right pes. It was transferred and seemed initially to stabilize but then became weak and despite support became agonal shortly thereafter. At necropsy the flamingo was in adequate body condition. The right pes had a mildly turgid swelling in the interdigital web of digits #2-3. When incised the area contained a 2 cm. diameter hematoma and unclotted blood. The right digit #2 had a proximal luxation that appeared healed. Sections of liver and small intestine were frozen for future use if needed.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA (DENTAL DISEASE). This 14-year-old male Bennett’s wallaby had six days of inappetence and has historically had dental disease and coccidioidomycosis. Radiographs also identified a bone lesion in the left proximal humerus and hyperechoic nodules through the liver. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation bruising and edema at the right elbow 2-4 mm. firm white round nodules throughout the pulmonary lobes calcification of the connection to the bronchi and enlarged firm perihilar lymph nodes. Heart muscle was subjectively thin. Multiple 2-4 mm. white round firm nodules were present throughout the hepatic parenchyma. Similar nodules were present throughout the splenic parenchyma. The right adrenal gland was calcified. The left humerus was irregular.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 23-year-old female squirrel monkey was noted to have a macerated arm in the morning presumably inflicted by a kinkajou in an adjacent cage. Severe bite wounds and multiple fractures were present in the wrist and elbow. Amputation was planned but the monkey developed cardiac arrest and could not be resuscitated near the end of the surgical procedure. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with alopecia at the tip of the tail mild atrophy of skeletal muscle and body fat multiple bite wounds in the humeral region of the right arm pulmonary edema some gray speckling of the lungs some irregular roughening of the aorta and yellow discoloration of the intimal surfaces a few soft choleliths in the gallbladder tan/white streaking of the medullary crests of the kidney markedly enlarged vagina and cervix with thickened walls and normal uterus active ovaries and poor dentition.

COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE COELOMITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 11-year-old male monitor had a two day history of inappetence and died while being examined. At necropsy a cystic mass was present on the gall bladder. The liver was enlarged. Free fluid was present in the coelomic cavity.

COMPLETE NECROSIS OF FAT BODIES (POSSIBLE INFARCTION). This 14-month-old female captive bred frog died spontaneously and was refrigerated 24 hours prior to death. The animal had no prior medical history and was found dead. Necropsy revealed possible fat necrosis.

AORTIC MINERALIZATION GASTRIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 26-year-old female sloth had a several day history of inappetence. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the heart was dilated and rounded. Many vessels are mineralized.

CHOLELITHIASIS CHOLECYSTITIS PANCREATIC DUCTULAR ADENITIS AND PANCREATITIS XANTHOGRANULOMATOUS PANNICULITIS EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old female lemur had been diagnosed with nonobstructive gallstones five years earlier was on supportive care for the choleliths but had developed a recent decline in appetite and demeanor did not respond to supportive care and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Neck masses had been aspirated and revealed mixed inflammation and mesenchymal cell proliferation and biopsies revealed Cryptococcus-like organisms in these lesions. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with three dermal masses on the back of the neck dorsal to the vertebrae flank region and left side the largest the flank lesion and up to 7 cm. in greatest dimension. Adipose stores were abundant. The common bile duct was bulbus dilated and tortuous with multiple outpouchings and thickened walls. Two large stones are present in the duct. The liver had several dilated ducts. Multiple pinpoint black foci were in the spleen. Multiple depressed areas were in the left kidney and the pelvis of the right kidney was dilated. Generalized muscle atrophy was noted.
NA

RENAL AND ARTICULAR GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old female cockatiel had a history of elevated uric acid levels and poor body condition. It received supportive care and improved with uric acid levels returning to normal. After discharge the bird lost weight and uric acid levels again elevated. No improvement was noted with additional supportive care and the condition progressed to include lameness or disuse of the right foot. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a large amount of adhesion between the body wall and ventral gastrointestinal tract outpouching or distention of the cloaca filled with thick colorless fluid and fecal material congested gastrointestinal vasculature and lungs pale pink and mottled kidneys and white pasty material within the left hock joint and along the tendon sheath of the third digit.
ENTERITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 3-year-old male red lory was found dead. At gross necropsy the GI tract was hyperemic and the liver was mildly enlarged and friable.

EUTHANASIA RENAL FIBROSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY INTESTINAL LEIOMYOMA. This 26-year/6-month-old female polar bear was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed with renal disease in 2002. It had been on a renal diet since that time. She recently started vomiting. She was immobilized to assess her condition. Renal values had increased dramatically. There were lesions around the vulva (cutaneous myiasis). She was also anemic. At necropsy there were raised white 1.5 x 1.5 in. firm circular lesions in the caudal lung lobe. There were multifocal 1-3 mm. firm white nodular lesions in the lung parenchyma. There were multifocal depressed dark areas in the lungs especially at the periphery. There were 1-2 mm. round raised firm nodules on the periphery of the left atrioventricular valve. There was a raised granular pink peripheral lesion of the right auricle. There were a few 3-5 cm. linear ulcerations in the distal small intestinal tract. There were nodules palpated on the serosal surface of the small intestine. There was a 2 cm. round depressed lesion in the stomach. There were a few 1 mm. round firm white lesions in the left kidney. Both kidneys appeared pale and had yellow/brown discoloration.

SUPPURATIVE HEPATITIS SYSTEMIC HEMOSIDEROSIS REGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 16-year-old male tamarin had a history of chronic illness suspected peripheral vestibular disease. The animal had nonpositioned horizontal nystagmus. Necropsy revealed a dark cobblestone appearance to the liver and hard yellow deposits surrounding the pancreas.

SEPSIS MESENTERIC CESTODIASIS. This 10-year-old male rock rattlesnake had been housed with another snake that had been euthanized due to suspected spinal fracture. The snake of this report was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed slightly yellow kidneys petechiae in the intestines dry fecal crusty material on the vent one drop of green liquid feces in the distal colon and one or two drops of yellow gastric contents in the stomach.

EUTHANASIA SUSPECT PORTOSYSTEMIC SHUNT SUSPECT HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY ENTERITIS LYMPHADENITIS. This male 1-year-old raccoon was humanely euthanized after being found obtunded/recumbent in the train station. It was alert but was unable to move. At necropsy there were no external or internal lesions. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. The gastrointestinal tract was completely empty.

CERVICAL SARCOMA (BODY WALL) EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male Florida kingsnake developed an open raw mass over the caudal aspect of the left side of the head following a shed. The lesion continued to progress and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large subcutaneous mass caudal to the left side of the head (previously diagnosed as a sarcoma). The mass had been debrided twice and recurred both times within several weeks. The tissues around the mass have become increasingly inflamed and necrotic.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS STAPHYLOCOCCOSIS GRANULOMATOUS GLOSSITIS BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 17-year-old male penguin had a three-month history of stridor and a yellow necrotic plaque was noted on the tongue that partially occluded the glottis. A biopsy identified mycobacteriosis (G14-5429) although this organism was not cultured. The lesions had begun to resolve with supportive care. The animal then presented with bleeding from the mouth and lethargy with anemia and some minor bleeding on the soles of the feet. The animal was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed abrasions on the ventral aspect of the left foot adequate adipose stores petechiae on the serosal surface of the thoracic girdle and thickening of the coelomic lining in this region enlarged spleen thickened air sacs with multiple small white plaques blood filled lungs petechiae on the epicardium and endocardium slightly enlarged left ventricle a 2 cm. mass on the dorsal caudal aspect of the tongue 4-5 granuloma-like objects in the proximal esophagus and petechiae on the mucosal surface of the esophagus small intestine and large intestine a 3 cm. mass encircling the distal aspect of the colon diffuse hepatomegaly patent gallbladder and petechiae on the serosal surfaces of the kidneys.

NEPHROBLASTOMA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANSIA. This approximately 10-year-old male budgerigar was found laying flat on the cage floor with its face down and was alert and willing to bite but had problems gripping with its foot. Respiratory rate was increased. Eyes were dilated and the bird had trouble keeping its balance when walking in the incubator. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged left kidney and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA RENAL MINERALIZATION HEPATOPATHY. This approximately 12-year-old female lorikeet was humanely euthanized. At necropsy it was very thin with a prominent keel. It had poor feather condition. Approximately 95% of the lung lobes were dark gray to black. There were multifocal nodules throughout the lung parenchyma. The liver occupied 70% of the coelomic cavity. It had rounded edges and multifocal patches of light discoloration on the edges. The pancreas was smaller than expected. Caudal intestines were dark blue to black. The kidneys were slightly friable.

RUPTURED EGG YOLK COELOMITIS AND YOLK EMBOLISM. This 5-year-old female was found limp on the ground during morning check and was dead on arrival at the health center. Necropsy revealed bilateral pulmonary congestion and active ovary.

HYDROMETRA THYMOMA TRAUMA RHABDOMYOLYSIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female goat had a one week history of injury to the right hind limb suspected to be related to the stifle or stifle ligament. Supportive care was administered but pain control was inadequate and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed age-related muscle wasting adequate fat stores severely enlarged and fluid filled uterus filling approximately one-third of the space of the abdominal cavity straw colored fluid with yellowish debris within the uterus and hardened yellow cotyledons ruptured ligament of the femoral head on the right hip large amount of hemorrhage present within the surrounding tissues of the right hip severe arthritic changes to both hips and multiple other joints and sclerotic and lytic appearing areas around most of the circumference of the femoral neck of the right hip.

TRAUMATIC MANDIBULAR CELLULITIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male bat had a history of falling in the exhibit and had sustained multiple injuries to the chin and nose resulting in degloving injuries with granulation tissue formation. The nares were stenotic and the bat was an openmouthed breather. After concurrent weight loss over the past few months and a fracture to the distal phalanx the bat was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. In addition to the previously described lesions no other gross lesions were seen.

RENAL GOUT GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS VASCULAR AMYLOIDOSIS PANCREATITIS HEPATITIS ENTERITIS MYCOTIC DERMATITIS PROVENTRICULAR MINEALIZATION HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 30-year-old male flamingo was found dead. At necropsy gout was noted on the epicardium. The liver was mottled pale and friable. Kidneys were enlarged and contained gouty tophi.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHRONIC CYSTITIS MYCOTIC RHINITIS PNEUMONIA DYSGERMINOMA (OVARY) GASTRIC MINERALIZAITON MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 17-year-old female snow leopard had a history of chronic renal disease and hematuria. No response was seen with treatment and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the ribs were noted to be soft and pliable. The left ovary was markedly enlarged and contained hemorrhagic fluid. Granular white material was present in the urinary bladder. The stomach contained multiple small firm nodular masses. An abscess was identified in the lung. A black to green mass containing purulent material was present in the left nasal sinus. Dark discoloration was noted over the cerebrum and cerebellum.

CHROMOBLASTOMYCOSIS RENAL MICROSPORIDIOSIS. This approximately 19-year-old female marine toad died during treatment. It had been treated for skin ulcers on the ventrum with both sulfadiazine topically and enrofloxacin orally. The lesions improved with this treatment. Oral antibiotics were discontinued. Two days later the toad presented with severe ulceration and hyperemia of the dorsum and hind legs. At necropsy there were multifocal ulcers of the dorsum and hind legs. There were multiple healed ulcers in the ventrum. There were multifocal pinpoint hemorrhagic foci on the hind legs. There were multiple 3-5 mm. diameter tan nodules between the skin and the coelomic lining. There was horizontal central corneal opacity bilaterally. There were white streaks on the epicardium of the ventricle. There were multifocal pinpoint to 2 mm. diameter dark gray nodules with pale yellow centers present on the surface of the lungs. The liver was diffusely dark gray to black. There were multiple 2-7 mm. cysts in the right kidney. There were two 1-2 mm. diameter pale yellow nodules in the parenchyma of the left kidney. Both kidneys had yellow streaks throughout the parenchyma. The stomach had multiple pale yellow to gray nodules in the pyloric mesentery and in the pylorus. The gastric mucosa was dark pink. There were multifocal pinpoint red mucosal lesions in the large intestine and rectum. The urinary bladder had multiple yellow to gray nodules on the serosal surface.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA CHRONIC HEPATITIS. This 5-year-old female gerenuk was found dead. The animal recently arrived from another institution. At necropsy lungs were collapsed with adhesions to the parietal pleura. Multiple bullae were present in the lung lobes. Consolidated foci were also present that sank in formalin.

CARDIOMYOPATHY ESOPHAGITIS STRESS. This greater than 2-year-old female hedgehog died. At necropsy there was severe subcutaneous fat. There was hemorrhage within the thorax and lungs. There was renal cortical hemorrhage.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION. This 4-year-old female snake was euthanized due to extensive fusion of the spinal column. At necropsy the only significant gross lesion was the presence of multiple areas of spinal fusion and malalignment of the spinal column.

EUTHANASIA PULMONARY EDEMA HISTIOCYTIC PNEUMONIA NEPHRITIS URATE STASIS. This 6-year-old male zebra finch had feather loss on the back. This bird had often been seen on the floor of the cage with labored breathing. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy the right lung was dark red and did not float in formalin. Kidneys contained abundant urates.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This approximately 1-year/2-month-old lory of unknown gender was found dead. At necropsy the bird was thin. It was missing its right eye. The skin and muscle over the coelom were thickened moist and edematous. There was fluid present in the coelom. The pericardial sac contained 0.3 cc. of serosanguineous fluid. The lung on the left side contained a yellow to tan lesion that was 0.5 cm. wide and ran the length of the dorsal surface of the lung. The yellowish material seemed to be purulent. Culture of the material was done. The spleen appeared pale. The gastrointestinal tract appeared slightly redder than normal.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2-year-old female degu had weight loss intermittent diarrhea and lethargy for approximately two months. The animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition alopecia in multiple sites minimal fat stores left kidney larger than right kidney and marked enlargement of the adrenal glands with the left larger than the right.
adult. Weight: 356 g.  Euthanased.  Mass; suspect neoplasia.  Pulmonary collapse.
PERITONITIS HEPATITIS. This 6.5-year-old female meerkat was found down and died despite treatment. At necropsy a large quantity of straw colored fluid and fibrin were present in the abdominal cavity.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE AMYLOIDOSIS STRESS. This 5-year-old male northern pintail was examined for preshipment and blood draw and had a transponder placed in the breast muscle. The bird was released to the kennel and died. Necropsy revealed good body condition a moderate amount of serous fluid in the pericardial sac multiple pale streaks in the epicardium that extend into the myocardium near the apex and minimal dark fluid in the trachea.

ASPIRATION CHRONIC YOLK COELOMITIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 5.5-year-old female bantam chicken was noted to be clinically healthy at the time of routine preshipment examination. The keeper staff had performed a nail trim one day prior to death and death is presumed to be due to hypovolemic shock secondary to hemorrhage from the nail trim. Necropsy revealed dried blood on the feet and feathers along the sternum and good body condition. No visceral abnormalities were noted.

ADENOMATOUS PROLIFERATIVE PROVENTRICULITIS INANITION. This approximately 5-year-old rainbow lory of undetermined gender was found down on the floor of its enclosure and was presented to the hospital in shock and died during resuscitation attempts. This flock has a history of Dispharynx spiralis infection that has been treated with Levamisole. At necropsy this lory was thin. There were numerous superficial wounds on the head. There was hemorrhage on the tongue. The right leg had a healed fracture. The liver and kidneys were pale tan. The proventriculus was completely prolapsed into the ventriculus and was adhered. The mucosa of the proventriculus was thickened and there were numerous small worms protruding from the mucosa. The colon was hyperemic.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS CASEATING ABSCESS CERVICAL REGION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 1-year-old male tree kangaroo had been previously diagnosed with Mycobacterium avian complex from a ventral mid cervical mass. The mass can be resected but the animal died during anesthesia. Necropsy revealed a 3.5 cm. mass in the subcutis in close proximity to the right submandibular salivary gland that contained exudative material on cut surface. Approximately 30 cc. of straw-colored transudative fluid was in the abdomen. One abdominal mesenteric lymph node was pale yellow. Lungs were congested. The right salivary gland was hypertrophied.
adult. Weight: 828 g.  Open. Evidence of poor/lack of preeming and cleaning beak. Mild atherosclerosis. Old age. Mild nodular thickening of L AV valve. Cloacal fluid?.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male bighorn sheep had a chronic history of forelimb and neck tremors perceived neck pain and lameness. The sheep was treated with painkillers and gabapentin. Keepers noticed recently that urination had been scant and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed spondylosis and mineralized discs in the cervical and lumbar spine arthritis in both carpi a previous right horn partial amputation a mild amount of white foam in the bronchioles excessive pericardial fat excessive intra-abdominal fat reddened descending duodenum reddened bladder mucosa mild erosions of articular cartilage and bone in the left carpus.

ANESTHETIC DEATH SHOCK. This 20-year-old male river otter died under anesthesia for dental work. At necropsy fibrin tags were noted on the serosa of abdominal organs.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC PROVENTRICULITIS UNILATERAL FACIAL SINUSITIS. This 8-year-old budgerigar was found dead in its enclosure and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed asymmetry in the nares and irregularities to the surface of the cere ventral to the left naris. A 2.5 cm. mass was located in the central caudal coelomic space displaying the ventriculus in other organs cranially and was round hemorrhagic and had a fluctuant component. A 2 mm. perforation was in the ventral wall of the fluctuant component and this was associated with clotted blood. A large blood clot extended from the perforation into the coelomic space. The mass appeared to be arising from the caudal pole of the left kidney. A small amount of patchy green discoloration was in the right lobe of the liver.

NONSUPPURATIVE MENINGOENCEPHALITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE CATARACT SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS STRESS. This 41.5-year-old two-toed sloth had been immobilized for routine physical exam one week earlier was slow to recover but did well while anesthetized. The animal had been seen on the ground over the past week which was considered abnormal behavior. Physical exam revealed thin body condition and a gingival/tooth abscess that was drained. The animal subsequently died. Necropsy revealed male reproductive tract large urinary bladder that was difficult to express no obvious uroliths or other plugs and the urine flowed normally after initial expression. Multiple tan colored oval to round masses were near the colon resembling lymph nodes. Kidneys were small and on cut surface were grossly normal. The stomach had erythemic and irregular chambers but no obvious ulcers. The lining of the colon was reddened. Jejunal lymph nodes were long and flat. Some slightly pink fluid was in the pericardial sac that clotted in the syringe. The left ventricle was thickened compared to the right which was thin and small. Turbinates were dark green/brown.

SPONDYLOSIS. This captive bred 19-year-old male jaguar had a four year history of chronic intermittent rear limb weakness associated with spondylosis of the lumbar vertebrae. Minimal response to treatment with analgesic and anti-inflammatory drugs was observed and the cat was euthanized.
adult. Weight: 5160.0 g.  Degenerative joint disease of the left stifle.

INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS PYELONEPHRITIS CYSTITIS. This greater than 13-year-old female sloth was found dead in exhibit. It had a three day duration of lethargy and decreased appetite. At necropsy the sloth was in thin body condition but was not emaciated. The animal was very dehydrated. The heart was small. Skull films prior to necropsy showed no evidence of dental disease. There were lots of ingesta in the stomach. There were also hair and rocks in the stomach. At the junction of the nonglandular and glandular portion of the stomach was a large rock. A third section of stomach was compact and filled with sand and small rocks. The pancreas was yellow. The liver was gray/brown with an enhanced lobular pattern and the edges were rounded. There was black along the edges. The spleen was small. The right kidney had fluid in it and was very small. The left kidney had a bumpy cortex. The bladder was very thickened and was filled with a malodorous chunky purulent material that was collected for culture and cytology.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR RUMINORETICULITIS SEPSIS POSSIBLE HYPERESTROGENISM FIBROUS OSTEODYSTROPHY. This 11-year-old female greater kudu had a two week history of bilateral swelling in the fetlock regions of the hind legs. Radiographs showed calcified tendons and soft tissue swelling. Fine needle aspirate revealed neutrophils in the joint fluid. The animal also had a vulvar discharge. The animal recovered uneventfully from anesthesia but was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed petechiae in the heart a 2 cm. pedunculated and lobulated mass in the rumen associated with some gastroliths an ulcer in the abomasum enlarged lymph nodes enlarged cystic right ovary hemorrhagic and viscous fluid in the right and left intertarsal joints and discolored and calcified hind limb tendons.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT EMACIATION METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA (PROBABLY RENAL). This 15-year-old male ratsnake was found listless with a barely detectable heartbeat. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe emaciation early shed cloudy spectacles web-like material covering the pericardial sac and surface of the ventricle subjectively thickened ventricle friable and pale green liver multiple flat black spots on the gallbladder white areas on the surface of the kidneys empty alimentary tract erythema in the duodenal mucosa and absence of fat stores. The ventral aspects of the vertebrae were irregular and some were larger than normal.

CHRONIC ENTERITIS INTESTINAL PERFORATION PERITONITIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA AMYLOIDOSIS. This 16-year-old female cheetah had a two week history of diarrhea anorexia and elevated white blood cell count with left shift elevated total bilirubin and decreased hematocrit with elevated reticulocyte count. Acute renal failure developed and the cheetah died while being anesthetized for treatment. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a yellow tinge to all subcutaneous tissues pale muscles a large amount of blood in the abdominal cavity partially clotted fibrinous adhesions in the abdominal cavity a hiatal hernia in the diaphragm with approximately 4 cm. of the proximal stomach protruding into the thoracic cavity hemorrhages throughout the parenchyma of the liver a few small white foci in the spleen partially consolidated lungs that have thick yellow/white mucoid purulent material on cut surface mesenteric adhesions around a previous intestinal anastomosis site swollen kidneys with pale streaking of the medulla multiple parovarian cysts around each ovary small cyst in the left thyroid a 5 cm. dark mass in the area of the right adrenal and no obvious normal right adrenal.

CHORNIC GASTRITIS AND HEPATITIS POSSIBLY BACTERIAL EARLY VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male captive bred cheetah had a one year history of illness and was euthanized. The animal was diagnosed with liver disease in September/98 based on clinical signs and increased liver values in blood work. Veno-occlusive disease is suspected. The animal also had a “grade 3” Helicobacter infection (as per Dr. Linda Munson) based on a biopsy in September 1998. This animal is from a litter in which one of the siblings died of a herpesvirus infection (cheetah #1221 Ft. Worth Zoo/G96-0008). Necropsy revealed a tan enlarged liver enlarged gall bladder a miliary white pattern throughout the lung multiple white firm foci in the splenic parenchyma gastric hemorrhages and foci of gastric ulceration.

EUTHANASIA SKIN TRAUMA DERMATITIS CANDIDA SP. STOMATITIS NEPHRITIS. This 10-year-old female fruit bat was entangled in a glue trap. Necrosis of the wing web ensued and the animal was humanely euthanized.

BACTERIAL CHOLECYSTITIS PERITONITIS ENTERITIS. This 1-year-old male hedgehog was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy diarrheic feces were noted in the perineum. A caseated firm nodular mass was present adjacent to the liver.

BACTE4RIUAL CLOCAL DERMATITIS AND CLOACITIS EMACIATION. This approximately 2-year-old tern was found in a weakened condition and died later that evening in spite of supportive care. The bird had eaten a large fish earlier that morning. The bird had been shipped to the zoo four days prior to death and flight time was prolonged due to mechanical difficulties. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with ingesta in the intestines and cloaca. The cloaca was covered with petechiae externally. The mucosa appeared hemorrhagic with an ulcer on the margin at the opening of the coprodeum.

GLOMERULONEPHRITIS HYPERTENSION STROKE. This 9-year-old female goat was examined due to partial inappetence and depression of 16 hours duration. While being restrained for examination the animal developed clusters of focal motor seizures involving the left side of the face. The animal became progressively obtunded weak and ataxic received supportive care but died within 45 min. Blood work at the time of death revealed severe azotemia. Necropsy revealed petechiae throughout the renal cortices and along the coronary arteries. Pale streaks were in the ventricular free walls the hemorrhagic area was on the surface of the right cerebrum along the midline at the caudal end of the frontal lobe. A 2 cm. void was noted in the parenchyma of the brain corresponding to the focus of discoloration and overlying the void was some gray hemorrhagic tissue.
LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 5-year-old male chicken was euthanized due to progressive onset of neurologic signs and weight loss. At necropsy a small quantity of purulent material was present within the lung.

POSTANESTHETIC DEATH STOMATITIS NEPHRITIS. This 8-year/7-month-old female gazelle never fully recovered after reversal of anesthesia. It had developed left facial swelling around the maxillary cheek teeth that was first noted on 4/29/03. Treatment with penicillin for suspected tooth root abscess was initiated. The facial swelling did not respond to treatment. On day 8 of treatment the gazelle developed nonweight bearing lameness on the left rear leg. Radiography revealed a simple oblique fracture of the midshaft femur. Oral exam revealed enlarged left maxillary alveolar bone with mobility of molars #2 3 and 4. Radiographs revealed lysis of the left third maxillary bone and lysis of the alveolar bone surrounding the left maxillary molars #2-5. The left femur was plated. There was severe swelling and laceration of the muscles of the left thigh. At necropsy there was normal fat. The left femur was severely swollen. All femoral muscles were swollen edematous and hemorrhagic. Several of the muscle bellies were torn. Molars #2-4 were missing from the left maxilla. There was purulent material adhered to the alveolar bone. There were petechiae on the epicardium. The epicardium was streaked white and pale pink. There were several ecchymoses and petechiae on the left ventricular endocardium. The right lung was red heavy and exuded hemorrhagic fluid on cut surface. There was a 3 x 5 cm. suspected ulcer in the omasum. There was pinpoint mucosal hyperemia in the cecum and colon. There were multifocal raised firm 1-3 mm. diameter light pink nodules in the hepatic parenchyma. The liver was friable. There was red streaking of the cortex and medulla of the kidneys. Both adrenals were friable. Half of one adrenal was dark purple. The left uterine horn was larger than the right uterine horn.

1. Trachea: Peritracheal cellulitis; myositis and chondritis; pyogranulomatous and necrotizing; regional; marked; chronic 2. Oral cavity: Stomatitis; pyogranulomatous and necrotizing; focal; marked; chronic 3. Lungs: Pneumonia; pyogranulomatous and necrotizing; multifocal; marked; chronic 4. Brain: Meningoencephalitis; lymphoplasmacytic; neutrophilic; and histiocytic; multifocal; mild 5. Brain: Few quiescent protozoal cysts (Toxoplasma gondii; presumptive) 6. Liver: Hepatitis; portal; suppurative and lymphohistiocytic; moderate; chronic 7. Adrenal gland: Hemorrhage; cortical; marked Comment: Cause of death in this wallaby was due to severe peritracheal pyogranulomatous inflammation that led to secondary pneumonia and sepsis. Bacterial infection is a probable cause; including bacteria such as Nocardia/Actinomyces/Fusobacterium. The source of infection could have been due to migrating foreign material like ingesta; leading to secondary bacterial infection. Hepatitis; meningoencephalitis; and adrenal hemorrhage were presumably due to sepsis. Few quiescent protozoal cysts (likely Toxoplasma gondii) were also present within the brain; but were likely incidental. There was no tissue reaction or inflammation suggesting widespread protozoal infection in this case. No infectious organisms were noted in necrotic lesions; however special stains (Gram; acid-fast) are pending. Amended Diagnosis: Lungs: Pneumonia; pyogranulomatous and necrotizing; multifocal; marked; chronic with intralesional Gram-positive cocci and Gram-negative coccobacilli Comment: Sections of lung had numerous extracellular mixed Gram positive and negative bacteria within pyogranulomas. No acid-fast positive organisms were observed

GLIOSIS AND TRACTOR FORMATION (BRAIN) CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old male lorikeet initially presented with ataxia but improved with treatment although the condition never fully resolved. A second recurrence of worsening ataxia developed in September and the bird remained stable with mild ataxia until being found in dorsal recumbency on the bottom of the cage. The bird was hospitalized for several days and received supportive care but due to lack of clinical improvement and persistent inability to right itself the bird was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA PNEUMONIA NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male cotton-topped tamarin had a history of recurrent diarrhea and substantial weight loss of a few months duration and examination identified an intestinal mass. Supportive care was administered with suboptimal response and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation palpable vertebrae in the back markedly reduced gluteal tissue and markedly distended abdomen. Approximately 3 ml. of straw-colored fluid was in the abdomen. The intestine was dilated proximal to the ileocecal junction and contained green feces. A palpable hard thickened valve wall was noted in the ileocecal valve region causing marked luminal narrowing. The wall of the cecum was hard and white. Approximately one-third of two pulmonary lobes one on each side were white and firm.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT INTESTINAL LIPIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old lorikeet is the cagemate to a lorikeet that died from disseminated protozoan infection (G06-4959). The bird recently developed renal failure and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA AND SEPSIS RENAL TUBULAR GOUT EMACIATION. This approximately 17-year-old female milk snake was hospitalized for poor muscle tone anorexia urate spotting and hematochezia. The snake died while being force fed. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous swellings cranial to the heart that were associated with fluid administration and cardiocentesis. Lungs were congested and contained large clots. Kidneys have evidence of gout. Ovaries appeared abnormal with no developing eggs and hematomas of varying age present. Overall body condition was thin.

PENMATE TRAUMA. This approximately 4-year-old female leopard was found dead in its stall with apparent fight wounds from the male. Necropsy revealed erythematous skin and possible punctures in the laryngeal/cervical region with associated hemorrhage. Some bruising was also noted along the torso. Hemorrhage was present in the muscles of the ventral cervical region near the larynx. A moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the abdominal cavity. Erythema was in the lungs and a loss of integrity in the cartilaginous tissue of the trachea and larynx was noted. Areas of macerated muscle and disarticulated larynx and trachea were present. A moderate to marked amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the heart and hemorrhage was noted in the epicardium and myocardium. Some possible erosions were noted in the stomach and areas of erythema were present in the small intestine.

EUTHANASIA FATTY LIVER COLITIS ENTERIC COCCIDIOSIS GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This greater than 1-year-old male rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It regurgitated a juvenile rat on 11/24. The snake was weak and had lost 500 gm. since December 1 2002. At necropsy there was hemorrhage in the lungs. The heart seemed flaccid. The liver was light tan and very rubbery. The gastric wall felt thickened and somewhat rubbery. The spleen appeared small.

CILIATE COLITIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 34-year-old female macaque had a history of lethargy and respiratory problems was depressed and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple renal cysts in both kidneys biliary cysts in the liver foamy fluid in the lung and a circular yellow lesion on the mucosal aspect of the colon approximately 1 cm. in greatest dimension.

THYMOMA DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) POSSIBLE LAMINAR NECROSIS/ISCHEMIA RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 17-year-old female pygmy goat had a history of degenerative arthritis and intrathoracic thymoma. It had a one day history of vestibular disease did not respond to supportive care and died overnight. Necropsy revealed an old infarct in the left kidney congestion of the adrenal glands bilateral nuclear sclerosis muscle wasting and severe arthritis in almost all limb joints.

YOLK COELOMITIS SEPSIS. This 21-year-old female lizard laid six eggs the week prior to death while in reptile holding. The keeper reported that the lizard appeared to be trying to lay more eggs in the afternoon and was found dead later that day. Necropsy revealed no external abnormalities fibrinous material and adhesions throughout the coelomic cavity and a small amount of clear fluid around the heart and lungs. The lungs were congested but floated in formalin. The liver was large with an irregular surface and purulent to caseous material on the surface. The oviduct contained multiple soft eggs in various stages of development ranging from 3-9 cm. in diameter.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS VACUOLAR DEGENERATION. This 10-year-old fox has a history of chronic renal and liver disease. The animal was found down with seizures. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. At necropsy the liver was friable and finely nodular. The kidneys were small tan and pitted.

Mass (intrauterine; per history): Teratoma Comment The histologic composition of disorganized proliferative structures representing at least two germ cell layers supported the diagnosis of teratoma. Based on the relatively well-differentiated cell features and minimal atypia; as well as on the history of a localized mass without invasion/metastasis; the teratoma was interpreted as benign. Teratomas most commonly arise in gonadal tissues (ovaries and testes); and have only rarely been reported to arise spontaneously in the uterus of mice. There was no associated originating organ tissue in the examined section to confirm a uterine source; and based on the common incidence of teratomas in the ovary versus the rarity of teratomas in the uterus; review of the gross findings at necropsy may be prudent to confirm that the lesions did not represent an ovarian mass encroaching on the uterus. Regardless; teratomas are neoplasms composed of two or more germ tissue layers (endoderm; mesoderm; ectoderm); which are most often benign and can occur in any site of the body. Although a pregnancy-related tumor was also considered; such tumors were not supported histologically: there was no evidence of placental structures (e.g.; yolk sac membranes or trophoblastic cells); nor fetal anatomic compartmentalization. Reference: Ogata K et al. Well-differentiated teratoma in a mouse uterus. Toxicol Pathol 2011 39:901-904. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology)

RHABDOMYOLYSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 24-year-old female California sea lion was anesthetized for bilateral cataract removal and developed severe bradycardia and cardiac arrhythmias during the first lensectomy. The animal responded to multiple treatments with epinephrine. Approximately 2.5 hours after reversal the animal became unarousable and mentation and ambulation were markedly abnormal. The animal proceeded to develop respiratory and cardiac arrest that initially responded to epinephrine but the animal eventually expired after approximately 20 minutes of CPR. The animal appeared to go into rigor very quickly (during CPR). Necropsy revealed good body condition multiple superficial wounds associated with repetitive swimming in the indoor pool purple left lung mucoid discharge in the proximal trachea distal to the glottis small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the pericardial sac congested liver bright unilateral ovarian cysts congestion in the stomach multiple uterine masses and some cysts in the thyroid.

RENAL GOUT EPICARDIAL GOUT MYOCARDIAL MINERALIZATION. This 4.5-year-old male basilisk was found in moribund condition. Treatment was initiated; however the animal died a short time later. At necropsy a large quantity of hemorrhage was present within the coelomic cavity. Marked urate deposition was present on the heart. Kidneys were bilaterally firm enlarged and contained abundant urates.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE RIGHT ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This approximately 8-year-old female ferret had a history of insulinoma and cardiomegaly was receiving long-term supportive care and was found dead. Necropsy revealed bilateral thinning haircoat over the dorsal midline and sides bluish discoloration of the teat region decreased muscle mass bilateral pulmonary congestion marked thickening of the left side of the heart splenic congestion and enlargement multiple foci of nodularity in the pancreas and bilaterally congested kidneys.

PENMATE TRAUMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male saki monkey was injured by a howler monkey during introductions four days earlier. The animal presented for abnormal ambulation with a hunched appearance and moving slowly. Examination revealed a large necrotic wound extending from the right caudal most rib to the ileum. The wound exposed the abdominal cavity and the right kidney was attached only by blood vessels in the ureter. The greater omentum was injected and partially filling the void in the body wall. Most of the epaxial muscles along the wound were necrotic and debrided during surgery. A small hole in the diaphragm was subsequently discovered and the animal was euthanized due to its age and poor prognosis for return to a reasonable quality of life. Necropsy revealed congestion or contusions in both kidneys. The entire ventral abdominal wall is severely contused.

CAPTURE-RELATED CARDIOVASCULAR SHOCK CLOACITIS. This 8-year 4-month-old female tammar wallaby was found dead. It was caught up for nuflor injection without apparent problem restrained holding base of tail and covered with blanket injection given blanket removed and animal was on side convulsing. The wallaby was brought to VCC and died. It had a history of cloacitis. This was the second case of a severely necrotizing inflammation of the urogenital sinus seen at the zoo. At necropsy there were a few mild ulcers within the cloaca. Multiple organisms were cultured from cloacal swab.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE POSSIBLE ANEMIA. This 9- to 10-year-old burrowing owl was diagnosed two years earlier with a heart murmur characterized as tricuspid regurgitation. Supportive care was administered with no improvement thus the cardiac medication was discontinued. The animal has done poorly since diagnosis with waxing and waning episodes of poor appetite bilateral wing droop dilated pupils sitting on its hocks with a fluffed appearance and head bobbing. One week earlier the animal had split its upper beak and subsequently became progressively weaker and fluffed with occasional head bobbing and poor body condition. Numerous feather mites were seen. The animal was hospitalized for assisted feeding and was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed numerous feather mites minimal muscles over the keel few visible fat stores wet heavy lungs with serosanguineous fluid a few 1-2 mm. tan foci in the air sacs overall cardiac enlargement with dilatation of the right ventricle splitting of the keratin on the upper beak mostly empty gastrointestinal tract and slightly enlarged and friable liver.
BACTERIAL ENTERITIS (PROBABLY CLOSTRIDIUM) IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 2-year-old female was found dead. Necropsy revealed subdural hemorrhage pale lungs and bloody liquid in the alimentary tract.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 17.5-year-old male Amur leopard had a one week history of lethargy and inappetence. Diagnostic workup identified renal failure and radiographically the kidneys were small. Supportive care was administered but with no improvement and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple foci of red/dark discoloration of the lungs multiple cysts filled with serosanguineous fluid in all of the hepatic lobes small cystic yellow kidneys full urinary bladder and no other remarkable findings.

NEPHRITIS. This 8-year/2-month-old female ibis was found dead on ground in exhibit. At necropsy it was in fair body condition. The left ovary was large and filled with a yellow creamy material. The heart was large. The right ventricular free wall was 2 mm. the center wall was 3 mm. and the left ventricular free wall was 8 mm. There was hemorrhage on the skull at an area of the left temporal region.
adult. Weight: 664 g.  Euthansed.  Pancreatic tumour.  Hepatitis and hepatic tumour (metastases?).  Alopecia.  Skin wounds.  Chronic kidney disease.  Poor condition.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS FLAGELLATED PROZOAL ENTERITIS RENAL GOUT INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old male gecko was found dead. There is a recent history of weight loss. At necropsy the animal was thin and dehydrated. Little lung tissue was identified. Kidneys contained a large quantity of urates.

GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 52.5-year-old female American flamingo presented for lethargy and acute lameness and had currently been managed for right lateral collateral ligament rupture of the tarsometatarsal joint with bandages and metal hinges applied. The patient presented for acute nonweight bearing lameness of both pelvic limbs with lethargy and inability to maintain normal posture. The patient was able to flex and extend the tarsometatarsal joints when supported but was unable to extend the left digits and kept the toes contracted. The patient died while anesthetized for radiographs. Blood work revealed elevated serum AST and CK elevated uric acid level inverse calcium:phosphorus ratio hyperkalemia elevated white blood cell count and mild anemia. Necropsy identified bilaterally yellow kidneys with diffuse pale tan/yellow mineralized nodules. Food was in the proventriculus and crop. The dorsal right pulmonary lobe was black on the serosal surface and slightly firm. The left heart ventricle appeared subjectively thickened with decreased luminal volume. The right tarsometatarsal joint had increased medial laxity and had partial rupture of the lateral collateral ligament. The tendon located on the caudal lateral aspect adjacent to the right tarsometatarsal joint had a focus of dark red discoloration. Foci of red discoloration were also noted on the caudal aspect of the right metatarsal bone. Some periarticular fibrosis was in the right lateral collateral ligament.

OSTEOMYELITIS WITH SPONDYLOSIS AND SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old male rattlesnake has a long history of spondylosis and was inappetent for several months and recently unable to right itself when found on its back. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe spondylosis and spinal deformity. The liver was dark and the kidneys were mottled.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 8-year-old female red kangaroo had a three day history of labored breathing and lethargy. At gross necropsy there was cloudy yellow fluid in the thoracic cavity. The right lung had severe necrotizing pneumonia. The left kidney was yellow with hemorrhages throughout the medulla.

OOPHORITIS SALPINGITIS SHOCK. This 20-year-old female ibis had labored breathing and coelomic distention. The animal was egg bound. The bird died despite treatment. At necropsy the cloaca was distended with four collapsed and necrotic eggs.

HISTIOCYTIC PNEUMONIA MYELITIS INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS ENTERITIS ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 10-year-old male chicken was used as a blood donor for another bird. At the end of the procedure the animal developed cardiopulmonary arrest; however resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy mild muscle wasting was noted. Congestion and petechial hemorrhages were present in the GI tract. Lungs were congested hemorrhagic and sank in formalin.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS EMACIATION PINEAL GLAND HYPERPLASIA/ADENOMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY NEPHROSCLEROSIS ISCHEMIC BRAIN LESION. This 16-year-old female Grévy’s zebra was diagnosed clinically with hyperadrenocorticism and was treated accordingly. The animal also developed lameness and received nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The anti-inflammatory drugs were slowly discontinued and the animal subsequently developed diarrhea and lethargy. Clostridium perfringens endotoxin A was identified in fecal exam. The zebra was anesthetized for treatment and arrested during recovery. Necropsy revealed active ovarian follicles sand in the stomach and distal alimentary tract but no obvious impactions serosal adhesions on the stomach and abnormal appearing adrenal glands that had a “glandular appearance”. A small mass was present on midline sectioning of the brain that did not appear to be adhered to any structures. The pituitary gland was dark and possibly enlarged. The lungs were heavy and dark.

TRICHOBEZOAR ENTERITIS CESTODIASIS. This 5-year-old female rabbit was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy frothy serosanguineous fluid was present in the trachea and nostrils. The lungs were congested and wet. The duodenum has a 1 cm. firm trichobezoar causing marked ulceration of the mucosa. Throughout the mesentery there were numerous 0.5 to 0.75 cm. clear cystic structures.

CARDIOMYOPATHY PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE RENAL GOUT RENAL CELL ADENOMA. This 15-year-old female spoonbill was found dead. It had a history of lameness on the right leg the week prior to death. Swelling was present on the right pes and leg up to the hock joint. The bird was treated topically with DMSO on the leg for two days and the swelling was reduced. The bird was also started on oral Banamine but it died the next day. At necropsy the bird was in fair body condition but had no fat stores in the coelomic cavity. There were prominent bumblefoot lesions present centrally on the right pes. There were yellow streaks in/on the epicardium. Ingesta was present in the gizzard and digesta was present in the intestines. Kidneys were pale and yellow with multiple pinpoint nodules.

AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC GASTRITIS. This 5-year-old female ferret had a long history of chronic renal failure and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed severe pulmonary congestion and the lungs sink in formalin. A 1 mm. yellow nodule is in the right medial lobe of the liver. The spleen was larger and darker than normal. The small intestine had reddened serosa and mucosa and the colon was diffusely reddened. The kidneys were bilaterally misshapen firm and asymmetrical.
adult. Weight: 246.2 g.  Euthanasia. Cause of neurological signs undetermined.

CARDIAC STEATOSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old male Houdan chicken was found dead. The weather had been particularly hot the past several days. The animal had some iris changes in the left eye in the past couple of weeks. At necropsy the lungs were reddened there was excessive adipose and the liver was enlarged and yellow.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 1-year/4-month-old male lory was found dead two hours after being placed in howdy cage. It was pulled from exhibit due to a bleeding toenail. At necropsy the liver was mildly enlarged and light brown/reddish-brown and mottled. The lungs were very pale. Sections of small intestine were very pale. There were multifocal light pink raised full thickness plaque-like lesions 1-3 mm. in diameter in the midjejunum.

EMACIATION ERYTHROID DYSPLASIA PANCREATIC ATROPHY STRESS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 11-year-old male koala had been acquired in February 2014 with a history of having been at several other institutions and having been treated for weight loss bloating nonspecific pruritus and grumpy attitude attributed to hepatobiliary disease and possible enteritis. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to lose weight recently becoming more precipitous in this regard. Additionally the animal had flaccid abdominal distention and marked anemia. Bone marrow examination identified myeloid dysplasia and ultrasound examination identified a dilated common bile duct and gallbladder. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to lose weight despite moderate appetite and anemia persisted. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This koala had tested negative for koala retrovirus-B although koala retrovirus-A status had not been recorded in the medical notes. Necropsy revealed cachexia generalized organ pallor and severe atrophy of the pancreas. Lymph nodes were small or unremarkable. The right cranial pulmonary lobe had an opaque capsule and a similar focus was also noted dorsally on a caudal lobe. Feces were pelleted and digesta was relatively normal throughout the entire alimentary tract. The common bile duct was dilated but patent. The bile is almost colorless and watery. The liver was dark or black with slightly diffuse granular lobular surface. The spleen was small and pale. Urinary bladder contained normal appearing urine. The prostate was symmetrical but somewhat thick with some reddening around the urethra. The pancreas was markedly atrophic.

TRAUMA. This 3-year-old female bat was part of a group scheduled to be shipped to another zoo. The entire group was in a holding stall until shipment and all had been examined prior to shipment. No apparent complications were associated with the examination. This bat was found dead two days after the procedure. Necropsy revealed good body condition good hydration hemoclips in the location of previously resected ovaries empty stomach scant feces in the colon and rectum.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ISLET ADENOMAS (PANCREAS) ENDOGENOUS LIPID PNEUMONIA. This 15-year-old male jaguar had a 10 day history of neurologic signs including vestibular and cerebellar signs. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was humanely euthanized due to lack of response to therapy. At necropsy the hepatic surface was finely nodular. A biliary cyst was present in one lobe of the liver. Scattered hard foci were present in the lung. The cerebellum and brainstem appeared asymmetrical and markedly congested.

TRAUMA HEPATIC MICROGRANULOMAS. This 9-year-old female Inca tern was noted to have a mass hanging from the ventral body wall when it was flying and this was thought to be a prolapsed cloaca. The animal was captured and examined and the mass was determined to be a laceration through the body wall with extrusion of the mesenteric fat and intestine. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed extensive coelomic adhesions associated with the laceration and desiccation/necrosis of exposed tissues.

CARDIOMYOPATHY CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE. This approximately 3-year-old female hedgehog died during an education program. At necropsy there were areas of the lung that were dark red to purple and firm. The heart appeared rounded but the ratio of the right ventricle to the left ventricular wall thickness appeared normal. The cervix and uterine horns appeared fibrous. There were wood chip pieces in the stomach. There were feces in the colon. There were two white 1 cm. diameter masses on either side of the ventral neck.

AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 3-year-old female black-footed ferret presented with anorexia lethargy and dehydration. Blood work revealed renal azotemia and elevated hepatic enzymes and bilirubin. The ferret failed to respond to treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed jaundice pitting and red streaking of the kidneys sludged bile in the gall bladder and serosal congestion of the intestine.

EUTHANASIA ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA INTERVERTEBRAL DISC DISEASE. This approximately 6-year-old male hedgehog was humanely euthanized. It was recently obtained and while getting quarantine examination proliferation of the gum was noticed. The gum lesions had become progressively worse. Previous biopsy suggested squamous cell carcinoma. The pinna had crusty thickened texture. The skin was flaky and thickened on the dorsum. At necropsy the right side of the maxilla was grossly distended. The lingual and labial surfaces showed extensive proliferation of the mucosa. The right eye was exophthalmic and pushed caudally by a mass. There was a large pocket of macerated tissue on the ventral side of the mass. There was a 3 mm. area of granular texture in the upper right maxillary soft palate rostral to the glottis. There was a segment of spine that had two small hard 0.5 mm. protrusions.

EUTHANASIA CARDIOMYOPATHY PITUITARY ADENOMA GLOMERULAR DISEASE. This 1-year-old female rat was humanely euthanized. It was in quarantine for education. It was treated for mites. It became unstable with walking as well as dehydrated. It also had respiratory distress and was euthanized.

EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS SPINAL ARTHRITIS SPLENIC HEMATOMA. This 15-year-old skink had been under treatment for hind limb paresis. The animal was unable to urinate or defecate and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the distal GI tract was packed with feces. Spondylosis was noted at the pelvis along with a possible fracture of the tail.

EUTHANASIA RUPTURED URETER CHRONIC URETERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS STEATITIS. This 8-year/2-month-old neutered female dog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of ovariohysterectomy 10 days prior to death. It recovered well but was anorexic. Exploratory laparotomy revealed numerous adhesions of the fat and surrounding tissues in the abdomen. There was a large area of fat necrosis near the pelvic canal where the fat was removed to allow access to the cervix during ovariohysterectomy. The necrosis of that area extended dorsally and involved the left ureter. The ureter was dilated and ruptured. At necropsy the dog was thin. There were numerous adhesions in the abdominal cavity from fat surrounding the surgical sites. Both kidneys had massive renal cysts involving the whole of each kidney. The liver was pale yellow and friable.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA INSPISSATED EDEMA CHRONIC HEMORRHAGE (GREAT VESSELS AND EPICARDIUM) EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female corn snake had been diagnosed in February 2015 with renal adenomas. Supportive care was administered with no improvement and euthanasia was performed when the animal became inappetent and quality of life was compromised.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE PULMONARY ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male opossum had a history of paresis and dermatitis and had been on prednisolone for eight days. The animal’s condition deteriorated and it had dyspnea and inability to move. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA URATE STASIS SHOCK. This 6-year-old chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the lungs were filled with blood. The liver and spleen were enlarged. Approximately 30 ml. of clear fluid were present in the caudal coelomic cavity with numerous adhesions. The walls of the small intestine were thickened and the lumen contained gelatinous material. The caeca were enlarged and discolored.

INANITION SEPTICEMIA. This 2-year/2-month-old lory of undetermined gender was found dead on a howdy cage covered with ants. At necropsy the lory was thin with a body condition of 2. The spleen was large and pale. The liver was large and dark red to brown. The gastrointestinal tract contained some hemorrhagic material. The lungs were red. There was trauma to the left occipital and temporal region. Fecals were negative.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL GOUT CHRONIC OOPHORITIS INANITION. This 14-year-old monitor has a history of elevations of uric acid and was humanely euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy the liver contained a 1 mm. white mass.

SPINAL CORD DEGENERATION ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS MUSCLE ATROPHY ENCEPHALITOZOON-LIKE LESIONS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male/castrated rabbit had a one-year history of progressive mobility issues and diarrhea when vegetables were fed. The rabbit was unable to groom himself due to cervical immobility associated with ankylosing spondylosis and had an inability to use its left rear limb. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified pitted kidneys poor spinal mobility and contracture of the hamstrings. Formed stool was in the colon.

EUTHANASIA FRACTURED LEG. This 1-year-old female warthog had been anesthetized for preshipment exam a few days earlier was isolated in a stall but did jump up the wall once prior to induction and was noted to be holding the left hind limb while going down. Recovery was prolonged from anesthesia and the animal did not walk or stand much the next 24 hours. When the animal did walk it had severe lameness with a drooped hock and marked swelling of the left tarsal joint. The animal was allowed several days to fully recover from the anesthetic event and began eating again was then re-anesthetized for evaluation of the limb injury. Radiographs and palpation revealed an avulsion fracture of the epiphysis of the tuber calcaneus at the attachment of the gastrocnemius tendon. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition with adequate adipose stores some abrasions on the skin of the carpi and plantar aspect of the left hock over the lips where the tusk protrude and on the nose. Lungs were edematous and congested with variable atelectasis the spleen was congested the spleen had a small serosal bleb on the antimesenteric border at midbody the kidneys were congested and had streaks of pallor through the cortex and medulla the mucosa of the stomach was congested hay and bits of produce were in the lumen of the stomach the duodenum was markedly congested in the proximal aspect the ovaries were inactive the urinary bladder was empty the left tarsal region was enlarged and thickened due to hemorrhage edema and fibrosis. The epiphysis of the tuber calcaneus was avulsed with retraction of the gastrocnemius tendon and over flexion of the joint. The intervening space between the fracture fragments was filled with an organized blood clot. Some blood-tinged effusion was in the joint.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK PROBABLE HYPERTHERMIA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female guanaco was found weak and unsteady on a hot afternoon. The following day the animal was moribund. It responded initially to supportive care but then declined rapidly and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 8-year-old female rabbit presented with mandibular swelling presumed to represent a dental abscess. The animal was anesthetized and radiographs revealed severe right mandibular bony lysis and molar malocclusion. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the rabbit had poor body condition with minimal abdominal and subcutaneous fat stores. A large abscess extended from the right mandible and extended adjacent to all mandibular cheek teeth. This was filled with caseous purulent material. The right caudal lung lobe had a 1 x 0.5 cm. white area. Uterine horns were dilated and contained cysts filled with mucoid clear or brown fluid.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 9-year-old female bat was found dead. At necropsy a large blood clot was present adjacent to the liver and intestine. Adipose tissue stores were absent. Marked tooth wear was noted. Lungs were congested. The heart had pale foci within the myocardium. The GI tract was devoid of ingesta.

ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA PYOMETRA PANCREATIC DUCT CARCINOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA ALVEOLAR BONE LOSS. This approximately 10-year-old female meerkat presented with ataxia and decreased appetite on June 29 2011. The meerkat was diagnosed with mandibular osteolysis at the root apex of both canine teeth and pyometra. The animal underwent ovariohysterectomy premolar extraction and aggressive treatment but died spontaneously.
