Gross necropsy revealed fair body condition dental extraction sites filled with clotted blood pulmonary edema pale areas in the liver mediastinal emphysema petechiation of the gastric mucosa intact sutures on the ovarian pedicles and uterine stump a blood clot near the left ovarian pedicle and petechiation of the urinary bladder mucosa.

INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS ENTERITIS MYOCARDITIS. This 2-month-old black footed ferret was found dead. At necropsy the heart was globoid. The left ventricular free wall is mildly thickened. A pale fusiform mass was adherent to the endocardium of the right ventricle. Other tissues examined were grossly normal.

DUODENAL HAIRBALL IMPACTION DUODENITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 8-year-old rabbit was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed a diaphragmatic hernia bruising of the duodenum and a hairball in the duodenum with hemorrhage and congestion around it.

MAMMARY GLAND FIBROADENOMA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 2-year-old female rat presented for a mass removal. The mass had been progressively enlarging. During excision biopsy procedures the animal arrested and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed a 5 cm. mass in the left thoracic wall dark red lungs some foci of white discoloration in the lungs and active ovaries.

PHTHISIS BULBI EUTHANASIA GINGIVAL HYPERPLASIA AND INFLAMMATION. This 17-year-old male black tree monitor has chronic loss of appetite nodules in the oral cavity and recently regurgitated food. The animal had was believed to have exposure to lead and serum lead level was 0.1 ppm. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was a granuloma in the right maxillary gingiva. The right eye was collapsed and shrunken.

EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL ARTHRITIS INANITION. This 8-year-old male copperhead was euthanized due to lethargy inappetence and a history of spinal fusion. At necropsy multiple areas of spinal fusion were identified. Other internal organs had no significant gross lesions.
TRAUMA. This approximately 3-year-old male budgerigar was accidentally stepped on by a visitor to the zoo. Necropsy revealed massive internal injuries with associated hemorrhage.
BACTERIAL ENTERITIS INANITION. This 6-year-old snake was found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin. The mucosa of the stomach was hyperemic.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE WITH LEFT-SIDED CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY CATARACT HELICOBACTER-ASSOCIATED GASTRITIS. This 28-year-old mandrill of unknown sex was reluctant to move and was unresponsive to NSAIDS and other analgesics. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy cartilage of all major joints was eburnated to eroded with thickened and variably mineralized joint capsules. There was also bridging of the vertebral bodies. Additionally the liver was pale tan.
adult. Weight: 232 g.  Euthanasia. Pyelonephritis. Lung congestion.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) THYROID ADENOMA. This 16.5-year-old female Thomson’s gazelle had a chronic history of severe osteoarthritis involving multiple joints with ankylosis of the stifles. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The kidneys seemed small at necropsy.

TRAUMA. This greater than 1-year-old female lory died. It was new to the collection in September 2002. It was missing its right foot. At necropsy there was abdominal herniation with secondary external trauma that extended into the coelomic cavity. There was serosal hemorrhage on multiple sections of intestine.
MYOCARDITIS SHOCK. This 20-year-old female ibis was treated for lethargy and weight loss and later died. At necropsy the animal was thin. Pale streaks were present in the myocardium.

CHRONIC COLITIS EMACIATION STRESS SEPSIS. This 10-year-old male Inca tern presented with lethargy and weight loss of two weeks duration and blood work was nondiagnostic. Laparoscopic biopsies revealed focal heterophilic hepatitis and mild renal tubular mineralization with normal air sac. The bird was unable to use its right leg after laparoscopic exam although the surgical approach was from the left flank. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed emaciation congestion of the dorsal lungs and possible hemorrhage around the nerves in the right leg that did not appear to be associated with the previously obtained renal biopsy.

AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female black-footed ferret had a history of a “broken back” and has had chronic renal disease since 2010. Ultrasound revealed multiple hepatic cysts. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized muscle atrophy and thin body condition multiple foci of bright red coloration in the lungs resembling hemorrhage on cut surface hematoma along the right cranial vena cava moderate generalized periodontal disease with gingivitis two large hepatic cysts in the right hepatic lobe enlarged and congested spleen irregular kidneys with pale cortices and thickening across the intervertebral joints in the mid thoracic spine.

PERITONEAL HEMATOMA (PRESUMPTIVE) HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old female hedgehog had a history of inappetence and weight loss. The animal was found dead. Severe autolysis was noted at necropsy. A mass was present in the cranial abdomen.

AORTIC RUPTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 27-year-old female ibis has a recent history of lethargy and inappetence. At necropsy the bird was thin. Marked pododermatitis was noted. A large blood clot was present adherent to the aorta and hemorrhage was noted in the lungs and coelomic cavity.

INTUSSUSCEPTION ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC HEPATIC THROMBOSIS. This 13-year-old male Malayan tiger developed vomiting and bloody diarrhea three days after physical examination. Evaluation revealed azotemia and intestinal torsion necessitating removal of four feet of necrotic jejunum was administered and recovery from anesthesia was prolonged although the animal did eat and urinate. The tiger declined 72 days after surgery was immobilized again for treatment was slow to recover and was found dead the following morning on a “pig board”. Necropsy revealed thin body condition absence of abdominal fat intact surgical site pale kidneys with irregular pelvises and all tissues warm to the touch.

OTITIS INTERNA GASTRIC CANDIASIS. This 2.5-year-old male kangaroo was unable to stand without assistance. The animal was under treatment with antibiotics and fluids. At necropsy marked weight loss was noted. The bone adjacent to the left ear canal was filled with purulent material. Culture of this material revealed Klebsiella pneumoniae. Multifocal black foci were identified in the mucosa of the pylorus.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE STRESS POSSIBLE TRAUMA. This 5-year-old female green tree python was found dead on exhibit in the morning. Necropsy revealed good body condition no signs of trauma reddened lung no food in the alimentary tract and adequate adipose stores.

SPLENIC TORSION. This 6-year-old female pig had a two-day history of lethargy and inappetence prior to death and previous history of inappetence and lethargy three months prior to death that resolved over a few days interval. This animal was slow to come in from pasture 24 hours prior to death. Treatment was initiated for bloat or colic and a few hours prior to death the animal had foul smelling yellow nasal discharge and gaseous bloat from recumbency. The animal vomited a large amount of foul smelling yellow liquid prior to death and also had seizure-like activity just prior to respiratory and cardiac arrest. Necropsy revealed good body condition slightly pale mucous membranes a 6 cm. bruise on the ventral neck region foam in the trachea pink/purple atelectatic lungs that float in formalin hemorrhage in the diaphragm on both thoracic and abdominal sides hemorrhage within the ventral abdominal wall and 3-4 liters of frank blood in the abdominal cavity with associated fibrin adhesions tan pale liver friable hyperplastic spleen and numerous nodules of clotted blood throughout the mesentery around the spleen yellow fluid and sand in the stomach and intestine fecal material in the spiral colon tan kidneys and full bladder and focal hemorrhage/thickening of the bladder wall with clay-like debris in the lumen of the bladder.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS SEPTICEMIA ORAL FIBROSARCOMA INTUSSUSCEPTION. This approximately 16-year-old female python was found dead in its enclosure. It had a history of being off feed for two months. It had laid fertile and infertile eggs all with fungus and the eggs were discarded. The python also had a history of a submandibular mass that was diagnosed as an oral fibrosarcoma (G99-1506). At necropsy the lungs contained mucoid yellow/orange discharge bilaterally. There was greenish-black fluid within the coelomic cavity. There was an old nodular lesion on the ventral mouth and a caseous nodule inside the mouth on the right side. The large intestine contained urates that were very hard and large. The colon was necrotic and hemorrhagic with pedunculated masses from the mucosa. There was mild intussusception near the cloaca. There was a stricture mid colon with possible impacted urates. The spleen contained microabscesses. Overall there was atrophy of fat bodies. Sections of liver lung kidney heart reproductive tract and small and large intestine were frozen for future use if needed. Cultures of lung were performed.

CIRRHOSIS/IRON STORAGE DISEASE HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS TO LUNG EUTHANASIA. This 30-year-old female lemur had a history of diarrhea reluctance to move weakness in the rear limbs and poor appetite. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed ascites cachexia hepatic tumor and metastatic tumor in the lungs.

TRAUMA (GORE WOUNDS) SEPSIS AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male eland had been examined one day earlier for preshipment. The following morning the animal had what appeared to be superficial wounds on the dorsum and was shipped to a separate holding area. About 10-15 min. later the animal was recumbent with a horn stuck under the door and feet in the air unable to stand. The animal was pulled sternally and supported but became weak and depressed and incognizant. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal also has a previous history of severe diarrhea and weight loss approximately one month earlier and was thin at the time of euthanasia. Necropsy revealed a gore wound in the right cranial abdomen and over the tuber coxae with a third gore wound noted on the caudal back. Two superficial wounds were noted on the right rear and a fair amount of bruising was located dorsal to the puncture wounds. Minimal fat stores were identified. Ventral thoracic tissues were hyperemic and fluids were in the subcutis of the prescapular area. Bruising was noted on the serosal surface of the rumen beneath a region of the gore wound. The spleen was pale. Ruminal contents were in the trachea (possibly postmortem) a small amount of foam was in the main stem bronchi the lungs were congested and edematous and rumen contents were in the bronchi. Approximately 50 ml. of clear yellow pericardial effusion was noted and a small amount of fat was present around the coronary vessels. Ruminal contents were dry and the mucosal lining was sloughing (possibly postmortem change). Black linear ulcerations were in the abomasum. The puncture wound in the right abdomen was full thickness but did not penetrate the gut.

GASTRIC DILATATION/VOLVULUS CHRONIC GASTROENTERITIS RUPTURED BILE DUCT RENAL TUBULAR ANISOKARYOSIS. This 9-year-old male red wolf was noted to have abdominal distention during annual physical exam. One episode of bloody diarrhea was detected when the animal recovered and the wolf was reluctant to move around the enclosure. The animal progressed to shock with profuse bloody diarrhea and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified a gas-filled dilated stomach with purplish discoloration extending from the fundus through the body to the pylorus. Petechiae and ecchymoses were present. A moderate amount of foamy viscous fluid was in the lumen. Spleen was enlarged with a rent in the splenic body that appeared to be associated with folding or torsion and the parenchyma was dark purple. The liver had multiple large gray/firm nodules at the hilar region. The nodules had a firm fibrous capsule and contained brown grainy thick material. Alcaligenes faecalis was cultured from the nodules. The small intestine was distended and discolored purple with petechiae along the serosal surfaces. Free blood was in the coelomic cavity.

INFLAMMATORY PSEUDOMEMBRANE (PROBABLY GUT ORIGIN) MILD PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS. This 3.5-year-old male Gila monster had been flipping over onto its back and was inappetent. It received supportive care but was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed dark red pulmonary fields some emphysema multiple areas of hemorrhage brownish serosanguineous fluid oozing from the eyes when the brain cavity was opened.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS POSSIBLE DEATH FROM POOR NUTRITIONAL CONDITION. This approximately 2-year-old male lovebird appeared to be in good health and was recently released from quarantine. The bird was found dead. Gross necropsy revealed possible bruising on the side of the head involving bone but not the skin bruising of the ventral aspect of the left and right lungs and no adipose tissue present.

PERIRENAL HEMANGIOSARCOMA. This 14-year-old female dog had an approximately one-week history associated with lacerations attributed to conspecific aggression in the enclosure. The animal received supportive care but developed frank blood in the rectum and a painful abdomen with progressive weakness and lethargy. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an irregularly shaped mass with indistinct margins and multiple areas of red discoloration in the right kidney. The omentum was dark yellow and multiple black firm round to ovoid masses were present throughout the omentum. The liver was diffusely tan. The heart seemed large. A large amount of blood was in the abdominal cavity.

MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION EPICARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS ENDARTERITIS ARTERIAL MINERALIZATION HEPATITIS. This 13-year-old male snake had a history of heart disease. The animal was found dead after eating and regurgitating a mouse. At necropsy three masses of clotted blood were identified adjacent to the heart. Vessels posterior to the heart were markedly enlarged and tortuous. The liver was firm and contained a large fluid filled cyst on the distal end.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION. This 14-year-old male ibex was found down and minimally responsive. The animal has a history of chronic osteoarthritis and marked weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the lower arcades of teeth were markedly worn. Osteoarthritis was noted in all major joints.

A 28-year old reproductive female chimpanzee was found screaming abnormally on the morning of 8-18-15. When moved into a stall; the chimpanzee attempted to use a stall prop to steady herself but then fell into recumbency and died. The chimpanzee died 15 minutes after the abnormal behavior was noted. This chimpanzee had a history of mitral valve prolapse and mitral regurgitation; which was diagnosed in 2013. A 54 kg-female chimpanzee was necropsied on 8-18-15. Autolysis was mild and there were adequate visceral fat stores; body condition was 6/9. The oral mucous membranes were dark blue/purple. In the heart; white streaks were present throughout the myocardium and the right ventricle was dilated. The heart weighed 279.5 g. The 1/3 middle of the left lung lobe was partially depressed; dark purple; and less well aerated than the surrounding lung tissue. The liver; kidney; and spleen were all dark red in color and oozed blood upon cut surfaces. The mucosal surface of the middle 1/3 of the jejunum was covered in discrete multifocal 1-2 mm dark red areas. The stomach contained a grey mucoid substance with black flecks. The duodenum and oral jejunum contained a grey mucoid digesta. A yellow mucoid digesta was found within the aboral jejunum and ileum. The large intestine contained green liquid digesta with fibrous material. The mucosal surface of the urinary bladder was diffusely reddened. The urinary bladder contained 10 ml of creamy yellow fluid. All other organs were grossly unremarkable. Heart: Myocardial degeneration and cardiomyopathy (suspected) Lung(s): Partial atelectasis (suspected) Jejunum: Segmental multifocal petechiae and ecchymoses Comments: The heart was not examined in detail during necropsy; but has been fixed whole and the valves will be examined further during trimming after fixation. Considering the history and the gross abnormalities noted in the heart; we strongly suspect an underlying cardiomyopathy as the primary cause of the described clinical signs; diagnosis is pending histology. Heart (left atrioventricular valvular leaflets): Mild endocardiosis Representative sections of brain; pituitary; heart; lung; liver; trachea; esophagus; liver; gallbladder; spleen; pancreas; kidney; adrenal; thyroid; eye; tongue; stomach; intestine; and urinary bladder are examined. PENDING HEART SECTIONS Alveolar spaces in sections of lung contain moderate amounts of edema fluid; free red blood cells; and moderate numbers of foamy macrophages containing intracytoplasmic brown hemosiderin pigment. The alveolar septa are expanded by congested capillaries. Throughout the liver there is mild centrilobular congestion. Diffusely; hepatocytes contain moderate amounts of intracytoplasmic brown granular lipofuscin pigment. In both kidneys; there is mild; diffuse; segmental; membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis. Affected glomeruli are hypercellular; the basement membranes of the glomerular tufts and of Bowman's capsule are mildly thickened and hypereosinophilic; and rarely there is synechiation of glomerular tufts to Bowman's capsules. In addition; there is rare; multifocal; mild interstitial fibrosis. Diffusely throughout the adrenal cortex; epithelial cells in all zones contain abundant intracytoplasmic brown granular lipofuscin pigment and moderate amounts of variably sized; distinct vacuoles. Multifocally; there is mild cortical dysplasia characterized by karyomegalic cells and mild disorganization of the zona glomerulosa and fasciculata. Throughout the brainstem; there are moderate numbers of astrocytes characterized by pyknotic nuclei and and abundant cytoplasm composed of homogenous; eosinophilic; amorphous; and paucicellular material; presumed to be amyloid. In the sagittally bisected globe; there is minimal peripheral cortical cataractous change including formation of bladder cells. No other remarkable lesions are observed. Heart: Moderate; multifocal; myocardial degeneration; fibrosis; and adipocyte infiltration Lung: Moderate pulmonary congestion; edema; and alveolar histiocytosis Liver: Moderate centrilobular congestion Kidney: Mild; diffuse; segmental membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis; rare multifocal interstitial fibrosis Adrenal: Cortical lipofuscinosis; and mild multifocal dysplasia Brainstem: Astrocytic amyloid deposition? Chronic heart disease Comments The changes in the heart were present in all sections but most prominent in the right ventricular free wall and regions adjacent to the atrioventricular and aortic valves. The changes in the lung and liver are likely secondary to the cardiac changes. There was also evidence of mild renal disease and adrenal dysplasia; which likely did not contribute to clinical disease. The significance and cause of the eosinophilic material within astrocytes is unknown; but negative staining for congo red makes amyloid deposition less likely. This completes all testing for this case. Katie Barnes; DVM

COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE GOITER ARTERIOSCLEROSIS CHOLELITHIASIS CUTANEOUS FIBROSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 26-year-old female ring-tailed lemur has a history of chronic hepatic enzyme elevations. The animal had bilateral cataract surgery in December 2014. A mass has been seen on the chest at multiple locations. The lemur recently has an inability to raise its tail had progressive weight loss and deterioration and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified thin body condition multiple soft tissue masses on the chest possible mild sclerosis and narrowing of disk spaces in the tail mottled pink/red lungs mottled pancreas surrounded by excessive connective tissue gallstones adhesions around the liver and gallbladder small spleen small amount of clear fluid in the uterus healed dorsal incisions from cataract surgery mild to moderate muscle wasting and no other gross abnormalities.

AUTOLYZED TISSUE. This 4-year-old toad was found dead on exhibit under a fiberglass rock. Necropsy revealed autolysis coelomic distention many follicles on the ovaries and edematous hyperemic intestine.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 16-year-old female lemur had been off food for a few weeks but was improving slowly and eating normally. The animal developed a one day history of lethargy and died. Necropsy revealed a large circumscribed area in the caudal abdomen with thickening and infiltration of all organs and tissues.

COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS. This approximately 39-year-old female chimpanzee was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy the abdomen was bloated. The mucous membranes were pale. The vulvar tissue was swollen and pale. There was blood coming out of the nose. The pleural cavity contained cloudy fluid. Nasal passages and trachea contained blood. There was a large blood clot within the air sac on the left side of the neck. The right air sac was normal. The left lung was adhered to the diaphragm. The adhesion was adjacent to an enlarged white lymph node. The left lung was atelectatic congested and had multiple firm white necrotic areas. The caudal region of the right lung was atelectatic and congested. The cranial part was emphysematous. There was a large empty walled off abscess at the hilar region. There was vegetative endocarditis on the left atrioventricular valve. There was cloudy pericardial effusion. The omentum was thickened yellow and had numerous vessels. It was adhered to all abdominal organs and the body cavity. The peritoneal cavity contained cloudy white fluid. The esophagus had a small full thickness ulcer. The stomach had a full thickness ulcer in the mid greater curvature. The edges were rounded not irregular and appeared to have tried to seal over an attached necrotic abscess material. There was ingesta present within the stomach. There was fresh blood within the proximal small intestine. There was an ulcer with rounded edges within the large intestine. The spleen was extremely contracted and wrinkled. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and white. The right kidney was firm and had loss of architecture. Both ureters were enlarged. There was mild mucometra. Overall there were minimal fat stores. Sections of lung kidney liver heart plasma spleen mesenteric lymph nodes uterus brain axillary and inguinal lymph nodes stomach and gastrointestinal tract were frozen for future use if needed.

Lungs: Diffuse interstitial pneumonia; Miliary nodular infiltrate Comments: The findings on gross necropsy suggest that the pulmonary lesions were the cause of death. The disseminated pattern within the lungs; and the texture of the lesions leads to the differential diagnoses of neoplasia or bacterial or fungal granulomas. Final diagnosis is pending histopathology; bacteriology and virology. David Needle; DVM Lung - Bronchoalveolar adenocarcinoma Kidney - Glomerulonephritis; membranoproliferative; mild; Nephritis; interstitial; lymphoplasmacytic; mild. Bronchoalveolar adenocarcinoma Comments: The histopathologic changes are consistent with a malignant neoplasm of epithelial origin and bronchoalveolar epithelial differentiation. The location of the neoplastic cells and their organization in secretory units supported by a thin stroma are characteristic of a bronchoalveolar adenocarcinoma. In domesticated dogs; this neoplasm metastasizes within the lungs; to distant lobes via the lymphatics; as is likely the case for the intravascular metastasis seen in the distant lung lobes; histologically. This tumor may also metastasize to extra-pulmonary sites including lymph nodes; bone marrow and the brain; however; in this case no metastsis to other tissues was found. The rare E. coli isolated from the lung are considered post-mortem contaminants. The renal changes would not be uncommon for a domestic dog of similar age to this wolf. This completes the outstanding testing for this case. David Needle; D

COELOMITIS STRESS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS AND POSSIBLE AMYLOIDOSIS INTESTINAL DEHISCENCE EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female green tree python has a history of intestinal obstruction and fecalith extraction one week earlier. During a recheck examination the snake opened its mouth and began fasciculating. Shortly thereafter the snake arrested and was subsequently euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a pale liver that floated in formalin gas in the colon and partially dehisced enterotomy site but no apparent leakage or inflammation on the coelomic lining.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 7-year-old female red lory is one of several in this collection that have died over the last two weeks. Necropsy revealed pale lesions suggestive of ulceration in the alimentary tract with some hepatomegaly and pale foci in the parenchyma.

PULMONARY EDEMA HEPATIC NECROSIS. This 7-year-old lory was hospitalized for treatment for suspected clostridial enteritis. The bird was later found dead. At gross necropsy all air sacs were opaque and lungs were filled with foamy fluid and were firm. The liver was pale rounded and friable.

INTESTINAL PERFORATION WITH PERITONITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male meerkat was the subject of conspecific aggression in recent months resulting in at least one facial abscess that healed well. The animal developed a week episode of abnormal behavior including separation from the group accompanied by aggression from younger males and females. Examination revealed depression shaking behavior and head held down. Multiple small superficial wounds were present over the front legs and tail. The animal did not respond well to supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. In addition to skin lesions necropsy identified a broken left maxillary and right mandibular canine and general wear on the premolars and molars severe bruising around the caudal coelom mild congestion in the lungs and a 2 cm. in diameter mass at the lateral edge of the right hepatic lobe. The distal jejunum just proximal to the colonic junction was distended with uniform fecal material that appeared obstructive and may have perforated.

LEIOMYOSARCOMA (COELOMIC CAVITY) EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS. This 6-year-old budgie was fluffed and weak with increased respiratory rate. The animal later died. At necropsy the animal was thin. An irregular tan mass was present in the coelomic cavity.

CARCINOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA HEPATIC BACTERIAL ABSCESS. This greater than 8-year-old female domestic sheep was anesthetized for exploratory laparotomy due to persistent stranguria weight loss and history of uterine pathology in other sheep in the herd. Surgery revealed nodular masses throughout the serosal surfaces of the abdominal cavity and on the internal body wall. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

ESOPHAGEAL STRICTURE ESOPHAGITIS GASTRITIS NEURONAL INCLUSIONS (INCLUSION BODY DISEASE PRESUMPTIVE). This 15-year-old female boa had a history of weight loss and intermittent regurgitation. The animal presented in agonal condition and died. At necropsy the esophagus was markedly dilated and friable and contained decaying ingesta. A narrowing or constriction of the distal esophagus was noted; however the lumen remained patent.
UROLITHIASIS BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS AND SEPTICEMIA. This 3-year-old frog had been lethargic soaking and not eating for about one week. It died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed autolyzed tissues.

ACUTE SHOCK ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 19-year-old female captive bred polar bear was immobilized for transfer to another zoo. The animal was administered a reversal agent and appeared to be recovering normal when she abruptly stopped breathing. CPR and resuscitative drugs were administered with no success. The bear had been in good health prior to immobilization with the exception of allergic dermatitis which appeared to be resolving. The bear was administered banamine and penicillin during the procedure. At necropsy the alimentary tract appeared reddened.

EUTHANASIA DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS. This 7-year-old female rattlesnake had a history of a coelomic mass which was surgically removed and was histologically consistent with a granuloma. The mass has recurred and several new masses have developed caudal to the original mass. Surgical resection was attempted but the masses were found to be too invasive for resection. The snake was euthanized. At gross necropsy masses were adherent to the body wall along the vertebral column and surrounded several ribs. Small firm masses were protruding from the wall of the lung. Numerous small brown nodules were present on the serosa of the GI tract.

EUTHANASIA NECROTIZING TYPHLITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) COLONIC IMPACTION ENTERITIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS XANTHOMA. This 5-year-old female gecko was euthanized following surgery for a cecal and colonic impaction.

COMMINUTED SPINAL FRACTURE EMACIATION NECROULCERATIVE ENTEROCOLITIS. This 10-year-old female Mexican lance-headed rattlesnake had a history of acute regurgitation severe spondylosis and was found dead. Necropsy revealed the animal to be in thin body condition with severe regions of spinal fusion.

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR OSTEOMYELITIS STOMATITIS INANITION MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 5-year/2-month-old female kangaroo was humanely euthanized. It had advancing mandibular osteomyelitis. It had three procedures to debride the chronic mouth and lingual infection. It had a partial tongue amputation due to necrosis. Radiographs revealed advancing osteomyelitis with tooth root lysis. The animal had deteriorated in body condition despite eating well. At necropsy there was severe mandibular osteomyelitis. The soft tissue infection was mostly healed. There were no fat stores evident. The stomach was full of food.

SYSTEMIC AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male Speke’s gazelle had been in declining health and was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed pale atrophic kidneys thin abomasal mucosa enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes with edema hemorrhagic congested lungs atrophic liver and enlarged adrenals.

EPIDERMAL ULCERATION RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS LOW-GRADE SEPSIS SUBOPTIMAL AQUATIC ENVIRONMENT (ELEVATED TEMPERATURE). This 6.5-year-old male axolotl recently developed inappetence and dermal lesions responded to supportive care but then presented for bloat and a necrotic tail tip. The animal had changed colors and was completely white. Coelomocentesis removed 30 ml. of transudate. Additional supportive care was administered. More recently this animal experienced elevated water temperatures due to a malfunction in the building and presented with dyspnea and fluid distention in the coelom. The mucous layer was sloughing and the animal was barely responsive. Supportive care was administered but the axolotl was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed dark pigment along the dorsum and tail region clear fluid in the coelomic cavity dark mottled liver enlarged spleen yellow pigment in the kidneys and no other abnormalities.
adult. Weight: 1230.0 g.  Possible heart failure.

TRAUMATIC FRACTURES EUTHANASIA. This 3-month-old male peninsular pronghorn antelope fractured its proximal left metatarsal bone which was reduced with an external fixator. Overnight the animal fractured the same bone approximately 2 in. below the original fracture. Four external pins had migrated out. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Aside from the left fracture five bone lesions ranging from 1.5 to 2 cm. in greatest dimension were noted along five ribs midway along the bone and only on the left ribcage (same side of the leg fracture).

adult. Weight: 550 g.  Euthanased.  Ventricular hypertrophy.  Atherosclerosis.  Suspect congestive heart failure.  Pulmonary emphysema - localised collapse.  Chronic hepatopathy.  Missing and broken teeth.

RHINITIS OSTEOMYELITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 1.5-year-old female wallaby was found dead. At necropsy there was marked swelling and purulent discharge within the left naris and nasal cavity. Lungs were markedly congested.

BRONCHOALVEOLAR CARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS TO LYMPH NODE CONSPECIFIC TRAUMA. This 14.5-year-old female giant eland had been reportedly sparring with another female and was observed to have been pushed over the moat edge landing on its rump. After this episode it had lameness depression and partial inappetence. It had been treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and a sedative and was found dead in the morning in its holding pen. Necropsy revealed multiple fractures of the coccygeal vertebrae and pelvis one of the fractures perforating the jejunum with associated fibrinous peritonitis. A few large lung masses and an enlarged mediastinal lymph node were also noted.

EUTHANASIA ARTHROSIS ARTICULAR AMYLOIDOSIS. This 10-year/11-month-old female merganser was humanely euthanized. Two weeks prior it had been diagnosed with arthritis in the right hock along with cataracts in both eyes. It did not show any improvement after treatment. At necropsy the heart was enlarged. The adrenals were green/brown. The ovaries were inactive. The cartilage of the tibiotarsal/tarsometatarsal joint appeared normal. Sections of lung kidney heart liver spleen and intestines were frozen for future use if needed.

BACTERIAL VENTRICULITIS. This 3-year-old female budgerigar had a three-day history of fluffed appearance with weight loss was isolated determined to be a female based on cere color and subsequently died. Necropsy identified decreased pectoral muscle mass dehydration and a small circular lesion in one pulmonary lobe.

CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female polar bear was euthanized due to chronic renal disease. At necropsy the animal was thin with reduced body fat depots. The spleen was previously fractured and healed with marked omental adhesions on the fractured ends. The stomach contained numerous stones. The intestine contained hemorrhagic contents with foci of ulceration in the duodenum jejunum and colon. Kidneys were pale with foci of fibrosis.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE LEUKEMIA INCLUSION BODY DISEASE. This approximately 15-year-old male boa constrictor was found dead in the afternoon. Necropsy revealed yellow-tinged fluid in the abdomen and pericardium and some blood was clotted around the heart admixed with fibrin and adhesions. The heart had a divot in the muscle deep into the organ with possible rupture. The ventricle was thickened with very little opened space. The heart was discolored pale tan/yellow and covered in clotted blood and fibrin. An increased numbers of vessels were present in the heart base. The gallbladder was enlarged. Multiple variably-sized lobulated masses were attached to the gastrointestinal tract and were firm and varied in color. A possible mass or pancreatic tissue was present.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ISLET CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 19.5-year-old tamarin had been hospitalized due to illness associated with elevated hepatic and renal values and continued to decline. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a dark pigmented area on the skin of the chest multiple clear firm but easily moveable masses beneath this region some black pigmentation on the underside of the skin brown discoloration of the heart irregular cardiac surfaces tortuous bile duct two small gallstones in the bile duct pale gastrointestinal tract multiple enlarged mesenteric and jejunal lymph nodes irregular renal surfaces and pallor in the parenchyma patchy areas of red discoloration in the mucosa of the urinary bladder and no other abnormalities.

HEPATIC FIBROSIS RENAL GOUT PNEUMONIA. This 4-year-old female lizard had a previous history of tail trauma which healed without incident. The skin became opaque approximately one week prior to death. The animal was found dead. At necropsy coelomic fat pads were absent. The liver was markedly enlarged brown and firm.

EUTHANASIA OSTEITIS DEFORMANS SARCOMA (SKELETAL MUSCLE) URATE STASIS. This 17-year-old male corn snake had a history of scoliosis and chronic weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized. Arthritis and scoliosis were noted throughout the spinal column. Small nodular white foci were present in the kidneys.

INTRACOELOMIC ABSCESS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 28-year-old female Chilean flamingo was noted to be separated from the flock not especially unusual behavior for this bird. It was found dead on exhibit two days later in sternal recumbency. Necropsy revealed thin body condition scant tan clear fluid in the pericardium some small flat yellow plaques throughout the air sacs gray discoloration of the left caudal pulmonary lobe yellow firm nodules throughout the mesentery a firm convoluted mass beneath the gastrointestinal tract containing rubbery yellow material. On cut surface this material had concentric rings that peeled apart easily. Beneath the lesion was a normal appearing ovary. The kidneys were yellow and friable.
CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND PORTAL HEPATITIS TRAUMA. This 35-year-old male Chilean flamingo died. Necropsy revealed absence of the head open coelom and absence of the heart.

PREMATURE PLACENTAL SEPARATION UTERINE RUPTURE WITH PERITONITIS. This 12-year-old female golden lion tamarin had been acting normal the previous day. It was immobilized and pregnancy was confirmed. Blood work was within normal limits. Supportive care was administered and recovery was uneventful. The animal was found dead the following morning in its exhibit. Necropsy revealed a male fetus free in the abdominal cavity and a rupture in the cranial dorsal aspect of the uterus 4-5 ml. of sanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity possible bilateral renal enlargement.
INANITION. This 1-year-old male tree monitor was found dead. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS BACTERIAL HEPATIC ABSCESSES. This 22-year-old female guanaco was found deceased. The animal had been eating up until the time of death. The guanaco was found in its usual spot and did not appear to have struggled at all prior to death. This animal had a three-year history of food accumulation in the left cheek pouch. In September 2014 a supernumerary molar was extracted from the right mandible. Food continued to accumulate after the procedure but lessened in frequency and severity. The animal had appeared to be thinning and was being trained for awake weight checks. Necropsy revealed thin body condition having lost 15 kg. from the previous year. A chronic superficial wound was over the left hip. Some cataract or nuclear sclerosis was seen in both eyes. A small fibrin strand extended from the iris in the anterior chamber of the left eye. Wavemouth was noted in the right dentition and a large food bolus was in the left buckle cavity. Some postmortem condition of the right pulmonary field was noted and both pulmonary fields had evidence of white precipitate-like material on the pulmonary surface. Serous atrophy of fat was in the coronary grooves. Degenerative changes were mild in the heart valves. The liver was small and had multifocal petechiae throughout the parenchyma. Multiple foci of small tan discoloration were also noted and the liver felt firm on cut surface. The spleen was contracted and the capsule of the spleen was thicker than the parenchyma. Normal ingesta of grass-like material was in the pseudorumen a moderate amount of ingesta was in the intestinal tract no cavitary fat stores were identified and no other remarkable findings were identified.

ACUTE BACTERIAL CLOACITIS TAIL TRAUMA (AUTOTOMY). This greater than 2-year-old gecko died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed that the tail was fractured off of the body. The intestinal tract was dark and hemorrhagic. No other gross lesions were detected.

OBESE PREGNANCY TOXEMIA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CESAREAN SECTION. This 8-year-old goat was extremely obese and had been treated for pregnancy toxemia for the previous two days. A Cesarean section was performed due to deteriorating condition of the dam. She stopped breathing and could not be resuscitated during closure of the abdominal wall and removal of three fetuses. Necropsy revealed obesity pale soft kidneys pale fatty heart and edematous lungs. Approximately 2 liters of serous fluid was drained from the abdominal cavity during the C-section. The spleen has slightly increased granularity. Blood clots were detected in the right uterine horn where the placenta had been removed during the C-section. The right horn was partially invaginated (from pulling placental membranes). Adrenals were friable.

NEMATODE ASSOCIATED GRANULOMATOSIS CHOLELITHIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male golden lion tamarin had a three year history of intermittent loose stools and thin or poor body condition. The animal had been immobilized multiple times for examination and blood collection and abdominal ultrasound evaluation identified distended gallbladder and bile duct but no stones were observed. The animal had moderate hyperbilirubinemia and significantly elevated bile acids and GGT. Supportive care was administered for hepatic disease and for occult blood in the feces. Recently the animal appeared depressed and examination revealed dehydration and a firm swelling in the abdominal cavity. Exploratory surgery revealed a 1 cm. mass and multiple smaller masses in the mesentery adjacent to the ileum. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition no adipose store reserves rounded hepatic margins and a lobular pattern in the hepatic parenchyma a tortuous and distended bile duct a moderate amount of opaque colored material in the biliary tract a nodule in the duodenum interpreted as duodenal papillae multiple green nodules in the pancreas a 1 cm. firm white homogeneous mass in the mesentery adjacent to the ileum and multiple masses of similar color and consistency along the antimesenteric portion of the ileum. The masses were homogeneous on cut surface. The mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Multiple defects were along the corticomedullary junction within the left kidney suspected of a cyst. There was bulge on the dorsal aspect of the left renal pelvis and multiple cysts on the serosal surface of both kidneys. Some black linear streaking was in the medullary region of both kidneys.

INTRATHORACIC ENDOCRINE TUMOR NEPHROSCLEROSIS POLIONCEPHALOMALACIA EUTHANASIA. This 11-month-old male meerkat presented with a history of seizures left head tilt and knuckling of the right carpus. Examination revealed nystagmus dehydration and apparent blindness with circling to the left. Supportive care was administered and blood work revealed renal and/or hepatic disease. The animal never fully recovered from anesthesia and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a rounded heart petechiae in the stomach and small intestine distended cecum and no other gross abnormalities.

UTERINE HEMANGIOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female golden lion tamarin developed an acute onset of lethargy pallor and hemoabdomen. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a solid lobular uterus with numerous nodules.
PRESUMPTIVE TRAUMA PULMONARY SHOCK. This 4-year-old male fruit bat was found dead floating in the pool. Gross necropsy revealed subcutaneous hemorrhage in the lower jaw and no other gross lesions.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE ENTERITIS ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS. This 5-year-old male sugar glider was found down and nonresponsive. Large gas pockets were noted in the GI tract on radiographs. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed during anesthesia. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy multiple ulcerations were noted in the stomach. The intestine was hemorrhagic.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS TUBULAR PROTEINOSIS ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old female opossum had generalized edema and conjunctival edema for the past several months. Serum chemistry revealed chronic renal disease. Sloughing of the tail skin was identified recently and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the lungs were dark purple and filled with blood and fluid. The right kidney was pitted and scarred.

THYMOMA PYLORIC LIPOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA RUMENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male pygmy goat presented with a severely distended abdomen and emaciation with pale mucous membranes. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed serosanguineous fluid around the lungs markedly enlarged mediastinal lymph node serosanguineous pericardial effusion with mild thickening on both sides of the heart and an enlarged area in the outflow tract of the abomasum constricting the lumen. The adrenal glands appeared bilaterally enlarged.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS INANITION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CYSTIC RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS ABOMASITIS. This 12-year-old female impala was euthanized due to multiple problems including osteoarthritis renomegaly with renal cysts spondylosis and cachexia. At necropsy the animal was in poor nutritional condition. A 7 cm. in diameter spherical mass was present in the liver. Kidneys were enlarged with multiple cysts. The urinary bladder contained hemorrhagic urine. Both tarsi and the left elbow were severely affected by arthritis with marked osteophyte production.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE DIC. This 17.5-year-old female cotton-topped tamarin was found dead in the morning and had been clinically normal the previous day. Necropsy revealed low weight but fair body condition. An MGA implant was in the subcutis between the shoulders pale foci were in the liver the stomach was empty possible adhesions were noted between the bowel loops the right adrenal had a dark mass and no other abnormalities were noted. All tissues appeared autolyzed.

GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS RHINITIS FACIAL CELLULITIS PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old fer-de-lance tested positive for cryptosporidia while in quarantine and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

BACTERIAL COLITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 25-year-old male beaded lizard had been lethargic for several days and also inappetent. Mucoid enteropathy had been observed and the lizard had bilateral hind limb paresis. It was found dead at morning check. This lizard tested positive for adenovirus by PCR and negative for Cryptosporidium by PCR. Necropsy revealed serosanguineous fluid in the coelomic cavity a perforated ulcer in at least three sites of the large intestine petechiae on the serosal aspects of the intestine and in the coelomic cavities a focus of pallor on the proximal small intestine edema in the subcutis of the left rear leg roughened surface to the articular cartilage of the right femoral head and multiple fibrin tags on serosal surfaces of the coelomic viscera.

TRACHEAL TRAUMA (INTUBATION) PULMONARY SHOCK. This 19.5-year-old male scarlet ibis was hospitalized for a hip luxation and recovered from reduction surgery. The bird subsequently died. Necropsy revealed a pressure sore on the pad of the left foot. Small scrapes and cuts were on the toes. A large air pocket was under the skin in the region of the neck. Pectoral muscle was dark. A hard object was in the trachea. Fat stores were good. A small nodule was in the trachea surrounded by a membrane.

EUTHANASIA PNEUMONIA ARTHRITIS. This 16.5-year-old female gazelle was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic arthritis weight loss and pneumonia. At necropsy the gazelle was in fair to good nutritional condition. There were multiple small black masses on the skin of the legs. The spine was curved dorsally. Radiographically there were multiple thoracic vertebrae involved. The deflection of the spine was almost at a 90° angle. The accessory lung lobe was dark purple and sections sank in 10% formalin. The right lung lobes were congested and ventral portions of the lung lobes were purple. The caudal lung lobes were pushed dorsally into the space created by the deflection of the spine. The heart appeared grossly enlarged with a thickened left ventricle. The aortic valve leaflets appeared thickened. The liver appeared grossly enlarged. There was a 5 mm. long polyp present in the small intestine. The kidneys were congested with blood. There were multiple 5 mm. long polyps in the uterine body. Three scapular lymph nodes were enlarged and pale pink. There were two large hemorrhagic lymph nodes at the thoracic inlet. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were enlarged and congested. The mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Adrenal glands were enlarged. There were bilateral lenticular opacities. Sections of lung were submitted for culture. Sections of lymph node were submitted for mycobacterial culture. Liver kidney heart and brain submitted for West Nile virus testing.

Compartment 3: C3 Impaction Esophagus: Multifocal mucosal ulcers Peritoneal; thoracic; and pericardial cavities: Tricavitary effusion Liver: Hepatic lipidosis Subcutis of neck; dorsal thorax: Petechial hemorrhage Pericardium; endocardium; mediastinum: Petechial hemorrhage Lungs: Focal pulmonary consolidation Lip commissures: Bilateral proliferative dermatitis Comment The most striking gross findings were impacted ingesta in C3 and contraction of the aboral small intestine with nearly no intestinal content. The pathogenesis of this lesion is unknown. Negative energy balance likely contributed to hepatic lipid accumulation. The body cavitary effusions appeared transudative. Hemorrhages in the thorax and neck regions may represent terminal (agonal) changes. Lesions will be further evaluated histologically and ancillary testing for parasitology as well as bacterial cultures of the lung and liver are underway. The results of complete histologic evaluation and ancillary tests will be included in the final report. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology) Lung: Mild multifocal suppurative bronchopneumonia with intralesional plant material Liver: Marked diffuse hepatic lipidosis and mild suppurative peridochitis Glandular stomach (C3): Small inestine: Mild lymphocytic and eosinophilic enteritis Skin: Moderate regional epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis with multifocal epidermal erosion; serocellular crusting; and mild superficial perivascular dermatitis C3 impaction with mild gastritis and enteritis; marked hepatic lipidosis; and perimortem aspiration pneumonia Comment The complete necropsy findings revealed C3 impaction; severe hepatic lipidosis; multifocal hemorrhage; and evidence of perimortem aspiration. A combination of factors likely contributed to the animals' illness; and perimortem aspiration may have contributed to worsening clinical picture and demise. The cutaneous lesions reported clinically consisted of proliferative epidermis with multifocal erosion and crusting. In addition to the clinically suspected differential of Orf (Contagious Ecthyma; Contagious Viral Pustular Dermatitis); another top differential is Idiopathic Nasal/Perioral Hyperkeratotic Dermatosis (also known as Munge); a relatively common condition in young alpacas and llamas for which the inciting cause is unknown. If desired based on herd or human health concerns; PCR testing for parapoxvirus (the inciting agent of Orf) could be pursued to further investigate the cutaneous lesion. Otherwise; this report concludes diagnostic testing in this case. Tissues will be retained for at least three weeks from the date of necropsy should further investigation be desired. CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old female lorikeet had a less than one day history of illness and died. The bird was found on the floor of its exhibit with a minor wound on one toe. It developed seizure and death within two hours. Necropsy revealed splenomegaly.
VISCERAL LARVAL MIGRANS. This 1-year-old female gecko was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed pale heart and mottled tan/red liver.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEMATODIASIS RUMINORETICULITIS LINGUAL CANDIDIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female giraffe has a history of limb lameness and has a 3-month-old calf. The giraffe was observed falling down on exhibit and became laterally recumbent and weak. Supportive care was administered and the animal improved over the next several hours was eating and drinking water but was still weak and unable to hold its head up without support. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild degenerative changes in the right shoulder and right coxofemoral joint approximately 500 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen small amount of omental fat a firm tubular linear region 9 cm. long in the adipose multiple pale foci that coalesced on the serosal surface of the liver dehydrated ruminal contents bland mucosal architecture in the reticulum congested abomasal mucosa thickening of the pyloric region possibly increased mucus in the lumen of the colon small cyst in the medulla of the left kidney and pale streaks in the parenchyma of the right kidney empty urinary bladder with some congestion in the mucosa wide adrenal cortex with pale streaks and a single cyst in the medulla of the right adrenal small thickened uterus with some congestion in the mucosa and three or four tan foci on the mucosal surface near the cervix a small cyst in the left ovary 50 ml. of serosanguineous pericardial fluid pale streaked myocardium with areas of adhesions on the right ventricular serosal surface and soft lumbar spinal cord (compared to the cervical spinal cord).

ARTHRITIS CATARACT HEMANGIOMA RENAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old male duck had a foreign body in the bill which upon closer examination under anesthesia appeared to be cornified papilloma-like growths. Three years later this bird’s legs were reported to have turned out and the patient was unable to walk on land and swims abnormally. Blepharospasm was noted in the eyes and the right eye had an ulcer. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. mass in the left inguinal region and similar masses in the mesentery eburnation on the condyles of the stifle joint white striations on the serosal surface of the liver a 2 mm. white circular lesion on the serosal surface of the kidney and symmetrical testicle.

RENAL GRANULOMAS RHABDOMYOLYSIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION AND NECROSIS. This 5-year-old female toad was found dead at the bottom of its tank. It was being treated with piperacillin and enrofloxacin. At necropsy there were several clear cysts within the liver. The lungs were foamy. There was grittiness to the kidneys.

BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female rattlesnake had been inappetent for months and had progressive neurologic problems that included stiffness head tilt and drift righting problems neck deformity and spondylosis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed inspissated yolk follicles coelomic effusion dark tan/brown liver spondylosis and edema in the body and tail.

OVOSTASIS ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 20-year-old female duck had a history of weight loss cataracts and chronic arthritis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a large quantity of hemorrhage was noted in the coelomic cavity. The oviduct contained a partially formed retained ovum.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7-year-old female pintail had a history of weight loss and lethargy and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the bird was thin. The right hepatic lobe was enlarged. Some foci of hemorrhage were noted adjacent to this lobe.

DISSEMINATED BACTERIAL INFECTION FLAGELLATE ENTERITIS. This 3-year-old male panther chameleon presented in thin body condition and dehydration and initially responded to supportive care but then continued to lose weight and died over a two week period. Necropsy revealed emaciation firm kidneys and pulmonary edema.

OCULAR TRAUMA CATARACT CARCINOMA IN SITU ANGIOMATOSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS HEPATITIS AND NEPHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 15-year-old female pochard had a history of blindness cataract in the left eye and possible ocular infection. The bird also had a swelling along the left mandible from which frank blood was aspirated. Examination revealed yellow pedunculated and raised nodules along the right wing that contained a malodorous serosanguineous exudate. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an adhesion of the nictitating membrane of the right eye to the right cornea. A focal white circular nonraised lesion was in the liver and female reproductive tract was identified.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE BACTERIAL GASTRITIS. This 17-year/9-month-old male kangaroo was humanely euthanized. It was hospitalized with azotemia lethargy and regurgitation. It had minimal response to treatment. At necropsy both kidneys had multiple pale streaks on the capsular surface. There were multiple ulcerations in the pyloric region of the stomach. There were multiple pale nodules in the spleen. There was diffuse congestion in the lungs with evidence of aspiration. There were multifocal firm nodules in the trachea. A swab of gastric ulcer was submitted for culture.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS PULMONARY SHOCK NECROTIZING HEPATITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 4.5-year-old male bobwhite quail was noted three days earlier to have swollen tarsi. Radiographs revealed osteophytes and mineralization of the extensor tendons. The bird developed cardiac arrest during recovery and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed pale pectoral muscles.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This 1-year-old western pygmy rattlesnake has been an aggressive eater since birth but over the past 3-4 months its passion for food has slowed. No other clinical abnormalities had been noted and the snake was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed no external lesions. Kidneys were subjectively pale.

EMACIATION CHRONIC RUMENITIS AND ENTEROCOLITIS. This 8-month-old giant eland is from a dam that died when the calf was 3-4 months old.  The calf had been stunted and doing poorly since that time and was one-half the size of similar aged calves. It was found down and agonal near a large fallen tree in its enclosure after a hurricane. It died shortly thereafter before medical care could be administered. No external signs of trauma were noted. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with generalized muscle atrophy and 2-300 ml. of clear golden fluid in the peritoneal cavity. No cavitary fat stores were observed. Both lungs were dark red. The rumen was large for the age of the calf and contained normal appearing ingesta. The ruminal papillae were sparse shortened and beaded. Two or three small erosions were on the pyloric mucosa and a moderate number of whipworms were in the caecal mucosa. Formed pelleted stool was in the descending colon and rectum. The liver seemed small.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS INANITION HEMOSIDEROSIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 18-year-old female lemur had a history of elevated hepatic and renal enzymes. The animal also has chronic severe arthritis. Appetite and activity declined dramatically and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the kidneys were small irregular and pale.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE COLLOID GOITER. This greater than 5-year -old male toad was humanely euthanized. The entire group of five animals was culled to screen for mycobacteriosis. Historically they were in contact with an animal that was suspect for tuberculosis based on histopathology. Tissue was submitted for mycobacterial culture.

TRAUMA SHOCK PULMONARY FIBROSIS AIR SACCULITIS. This 10-year-old female chicken had a recent history of respiratory difficulty was treated and recently released. This animal was found dead with her foot entangled in cage wire. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted over the skull and calvarium. A mass of white purulent material was present in the left cranial air sac. Liver and heart were mottled.
GRANULOMATOUS ENTERITIS PNEUMONIA. This 6-year-old male boa had a history of behavior abnormalities and was found dead. At necropsy thick white plaques were noted in the intestinal lumen.

INTUSSUSCEPTION CARDIOMYOPATHY FATTY LIVER. This 12-year/8-month-old female chinchilla died. It was found very lethargic and unable to walk. There was blood on the cloaca. At necropsy the liver was fatty and friable. It was enlarged and had rounded edges. It was pale tan to pink and mottled. The kidneys were pale pink. The right kidney had a few pinpoint scarred areas. The cortex had streaking on cut surface. The stomach was full of food. The lungs were very congested. Cloudy white fluid leaked from the lungs on cut section. The left lung was mottled. There was dilatation of the right side of the heart. The left ventricular free wall was 3 mm. and the right ventricular free wall was 1 mm. There were three distinct areas of intussusception spanning a 6 cm. length of descending colon. Each was between 1 and 1.5 cm. in length and arranged in a linear array in the affected colonic segment. The affected areas of intestine were dark red and hemorrhagic.

OCULAR SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CEREBRAL METASTASIS PULMONARY METASTASIS ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 4-year-old male hedgehog had a history of conjunctivitis and endophthalmia. Enucleation was performed; however the animal’s condition declined rapidly following surgery. The animal was found dead. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted in the axilla. A firm white mass containing purulent material was present in the inguinal region. Clotted blood was present in the stomach. Melena was noted in the colon. Irregular masses were noted adjacent to the urinary bladder.

TRAUMA RHABDOMYOLYSIS POSSIBLY TETANUS EUTHANASIA. This 5.5-year-old male capybara had developed lameness and discomfort of a few weeks duration attributed to conspecific aggression. Currently there is an additional capybara in this group that is sick. Supportive care was administered and the animal appeared to be responding but then deteriorated over a one-day interval and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed many healing wounds over the body and head a few minor fresh skin ulcerations attributed to recumbency in the last 24 hours. The mouth had a sour smell foam was at the bifurcation of the trachea the lungs were congested and edematous especially the middle and caudal pulmonary lobes the gallbladder was distended with bile the stomach contained bile but was otherwise empty the cecum contained much green ingesta some pallor was in the skeletal muscles severe spondylosis was noted (radiographically) and no other abnormalities were noted.

GRANULOMATOUS INFLAMMATION EPAXIAL REGION. This 15-year-old male captive bred python was found writhing. Examination revealed profound depression with abnormal posture muddy mucous membranes and a long firm subcutaneous mass along the left side of the epaxial muscles. The biopsy submitted from the flank revealed granulomatous inflammation. The snake did not respond well to supportive therapy and was euthanized. Necropsy revealed good body condition and a sutured surgical site 42 cm. from the head on the left side.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female chicken had a one-year history of oral plaques which progressively worsened. Biopsy identified squamous cell carcinoma and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed swelling of the right commissure large plaques of necrotic tissue in the mouth along the upper and lower right side extending into the choana and down to the glottis. The ovary was active with numerous follicles of various size and a soft-shelled egg was present in the oviduct.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 7.5-year-old male common wallaroo presented for examination and treatment one day prior to death. The animal was thin weak and dehydrated and had seizures and possible circling behavior prior to death. Necropsy revealed severe atrophy of fat pale right kidney and prominent mesenteric lymph nodes.

TRAUMa. This 6-year/5-month-old male lemur was found dead near its shelter on island. It had a history of having a routine exam several weeks earlier. The keeper noted the lemur to be moving slowly many days afterwards. It had accepted food normally earlier that day. At necropsy there were large fat deposits surrounding all major organs. The right heart was thickened and dilated. Ingesta was present in the stomach that appeared to be from browsing on the island and not prepared diet. The right leg thigh muscles were full of hemorrhage and several large blood clots were present. Sections of spleen liver heart lung kidney skeletal muscle brain skin stomach with contents eye and right leg muscle were frozen for future use if needed.

EUTHANASIA MAMMARY CARCINOMA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA INANITION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 15-year/3-month-old female tamarin was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed with mammary neoplasia on 8/21/01 based on biopsies examined by Northwest ZooPath (G01-3652). There was histologic evidence suggestive of lymphatic invasion at time of diagnosis. The tamarin initially responded to treatment and supportive care for secondary bacterial infection as well as dietary and housing modifications. The size of the lesion at time of diagnosis prohibited surgical excision of the ulcerated neoplastic region. Postmortem radiographs compared to previous films demonstrated soft tissue densities in lung fields and ventral spondylosis of thoracic and lumbar vertebrae. Mites were observed on the extremities at time of final examination. Fecal examination revealed pinworms and strongyles. At necropsy the tamarin was thin with decreased muscle mass and no subcutaneous or body cavity fat stores. There was alopecia of the tail and dorsum. There was heavy dental tartar and moderate gingivitis. There was approximately 4.5 ml. of clear yellow fluid in the thoracic cavity. There was an ulcerated lesion from underneath the left axilla to just the right axilla and extended from the xyphoid process to just cranial to the thoracic inlet. The lesion was tightly adhered where it was in contact with the underlying ribcage and sternum. The lesion extended underneath the scapula dissecting between muscles. There were multiple small flat tan foci located subcutaneous along the ventral cervical region adjacent to the trachea and esophagus. The left lung was diffusely hard and mottled dark red to purple with firm white coalescing areas that extended into the parenchyma. The serosal surface contained multiple small bulla and pinpoint areas of petechiation. The gall bladder was enlarged and the common bile duct was distended and appeared tortuous. The bile was very thick and viscous. The kidneys appeared enlarged pale and were firm on cut surface. The left adrenal appeared larger than the right.
GASTRIC RUPTURE (GROSS DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK. This 7-year-old male rabbit was found dead. At gross necropsy the stomach was ruptured with ingesta free within the abdomen.

ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MILD ENTERITIS PORTAL HEPATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old male Chilean flamingo had a history of chronic lameness with intermittent exacerbation of the right intertarsal joint. Exam and radiographs confirmed chronic osteoarthritis with progressive bony changes and decreased flexion. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged spleen swollen right intertarsal joint and a 1 cm. region of hemorrhage in the lateral soft tissue. The proximal lateral edge of the tibiotarsus is irregular.
adult. Weight: 1234 g.  Euthanased.  Obesity.  Pulmonary congestion +/- oedema.  Splenomegaly.  Suspect hepatic lipidosis.

INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS SHOCK. This 2-month-old black footed ferret was found dead. Other littermates were diagnosed with coccidiosis. The group was under treatment with sulfadimethoxine. At necropsy the carcass was dehydrated and wet fecal material was pasted around the anus. Intestines were pale and contained gas and a small quantity of pale ingesta.

INTESTINAL HEMORRHAGE ANEMIA. This 2-year-old female lorikeet was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition uniformly yellow/tan liver tar-like consistency to the lining of the mucosa of the proventriculus and ventriculus. Kidneys were pale brown and female reproductive tract was identified.

LYMPHOBLASTIC LYMPHOSARCOMA MENINGITIS SPLENITIS HEPATITIS INANITION. This 18-year-old male kingsnake presented with head tilt and abnormal posture. Treatment was initiated. Blood work showed lymphocytosis with circulating lymphoblasts. The animal later died. At necropsy the liver was enlarged and light red in color. Contour was coarsely nodular. White foci were present in the kidney.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 11-year-old male python presented for lethargy and inappetence. Blood work revealed marked elevation in white blood cell count total protein globulins and AST. White blood cells had morphologic abnormalities and biliverdinemia was identified. Neoplasia or systemic infectious disease was suspected. The snake died and necropsy revealed numerous firm masses under the skin along the dorsum and on cut surface the masses contained thick white chalky material. Similar material was present throughout the subcutis when the skin was reflected. Abundant adipose stores were identified in the coelom. The liver was swollen and firm. Digested blood and rodent skeletons were present in the stomach (last fed one month earlier). The colon contained a large amount of hard fecal material. Both kidneys were firm and ureters were subjectively distended and slightly filled with urates.

GASTRIC ULCERS SEPSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS EMACIATION. This 5-year-old male giant eland had recently been moved for possible shipment. The eland appeared fine in late afternoon and was eating normally. Blood work identified marked leukocytosis with left shift hypoglycemia and elevated blood urea nitrogen creatinine and phosphorus. The animal improved only minimally with supportive care and died the next morning. Necropsy revealed fair to poor body condition with generalized muscle atrophy absence of subcutaneous adipose stores and mild subcutaneous edema in the ventral thorax. The muscles of the rear limbs have pale areas and streaking. Mild accumulation of clear golden fluid is in the peritoneal cavity and cavitary fat stores are absent. A few old fibrous adhesions from the abdominal wall to the rumen are noted. A few old fibrous adhesions were present between the visceral and parietal pleura. One gastric lymph node was enlarged with multiple presumptive granulomas. The spleen was contracted and small. A small amount of ruminal contents were in the trachea. Both lungs were congested with the right lung worse than the left. All dental arcades showed moderate gingival loss and periodontal disease. The rumen appeared larger than expected and was thin walled. Ruminal contents were liquid and ruminal papillae appeared shortened and blunted. Multiple large linear hemorrhagic ulcers were present in the fundic portion of the abomasum. The gastrointestinal contents from the stomach were dark. Formed stool was in the distal colon and rectum. The entire intestinal tract was grossly normal.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. EUTHANASIA INTESTINAL LYMPHOSARCOMA ULCERATIVE ENTERITIS. This 23-year-old female guanaco presented with severe lethargy and anorexia. The animal was humanely euthanized. This 5-year-old female chinchilla had a five day history of complications associated with a skin avulsion and self-injury following the original surgical repair. Diagnosis (es): 1. Thoracic cavity (pleura): Mesothelioma 2. Lungs: Endogenous lipid pneumonia; focal; mild 3. Lungs: Bronchiolitis; suppurative; multifocal; subacute; minimal 4. Lungs: Pulmonary edema; multifocal; minimal 5. Lungs: Smooth muscle hyperplasia; multifocal; moderate 6. Arteries (myocardial; pulmonary): Arteriosclerosis; mild to moderate 7. Heart: Valvular endocardiosis; focal; mild to moderate 8. Heart: Myocardial interstitial fibrosis; multifocal; mild 9. Kidney: Tubulointerstitial nephritis; lymphoplasmacytic; multifocal; mild; chronic 10. Adrenal glands: Nodular cortical hyperplasia; bilateral; multifocal; moderate 11. Lymph node: Anthracosis; multifocal; moderate 12. Lymph node: Hemorrhage; focal; mild 13. Thyroid gland: Follicular cyst; focal Comment: The most significant finding in this animal was mesothelioma of the thoracic pleura; corresponding with the firm nodules noted on gross necropsy (per history). This neoplasm was closely associated with the periosteal surface of the ribs. Mesothelioma is a commonly diagnosed neoplasm of both the pleura and peritoneum in in zoo felids. Tubulointerstitial nephritis was mild in this case; and is also a common finding in zoo felids. In one section of lung; there was minimal neutrophilic bronchiolitis and pulmonary edema. The green appearance of the lymph nodes noted in the thoracic cavity were due to anthracosis; commonly found in the tracheobronchial lymph nodes. One lymph node; as described grossly (per history) had a small amount of hemorrhage; or was draining a region of hemorrhage; but histologic findings were mild. The nodules described adjacent to one adrenal gland (per history) may have been the nodular cortical hyperplasia found histologically. Remaining lesions were considered age-related or mild; incidental findings; such as valvular endocardiosis and arteriosclerosis. Myocardial fibrosis was mild and limited to one section of heart adjacent to a valve.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS EROSIVE GASTRITIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANASIA. Lung (1/2 sections): Acute necrohemorrhagic pneumonia with myriad intralesional bacteria Heart; left ventricle: Focal mild necrotizing myocarditis Liver: Diffuse moderate to marked hepatocellular fatty degeneration (hepatic lipidosis) Gallbladder: Multifocal moderate lymphocytic cholecystitis Stomach: Multifocal mild lymphocytic gastritis Small intestine: Intraluminal hemorrhage and bacteria Comment The lung lesions in this ferret are comparable to those observed in animals with acute to peracute fatal pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa; extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli or; although the morphology of the bacteria is not coccoid; possibly Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus. A Gram stain is pending to further characterize the intralesional bacteria. The result of this stain will be reported in an addendum. Hepatic lipidosis is indicative of negative energy balance. The cause of the mild focal myocarditis and the chronic cholecystitis are undetermined. Chronic lymphocytic gastritis in ferrets is typically associated with Helicobacter mustelae infection; although no bacteria were evident in the section of stomach examined. One of the sections of intestine contained blood as observed at necropsy. It is undetermined whether the intraluminal bacteria in this section represent overgrowth of the intestinal flora and/or the same bacteria as noted in the lung. A Gram stain was requested on this section as well; in an attempt to further characterize also these bacteria.

1. Pharynx: Severe necrotizing pharyngitis with peripharyngeal abscess formation and associated lymphadenitis 2. Lung: Severe focally extensive bilateral bronchopneumonia 3. Adrenal: Enlarged adrenal medulla - pending histologic evaluation Comment The gross findings indicated severe pharyngitis and bronchopneumonia. Such pharyngeal lesions are most commonly associated with trauma from foreign objects. The pattern of findings suggested extension of infection from the pharynx to the lung by inhalation. Bacterial cultures on both pharynx and lung are underway; suspected agents include Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes and Fusobacterium necrophorum infection. Qualitative fecal culture has also been submitted for screening. Results of ancillary tests and complete histologic examination will be included in the final report. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Patholog Pharynx: Severe regionally extensive chronic pharyngeal/peripharyngeal abscess Lymph node: Severe chronic granulating and granulomatous lymphadenitis with multifocal necrosis/suppuration Lung: Severe multifocal aspiration pneumonia Adrenal gland: Multifocal cortical hyperplasia Severe chronic pharyngitis and peripharyngeal abscess formation with associated lymphadenitis and severe secondary aspiration pneumonia Comment The gross and histologic findings indicated severe pharyngeal inflammation with abscess formation; regional lymphadenitis; and aspiration pneumonia. Bacterial cultures indicated Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes as the primary infectious agent with the other isolates being likely secondary contaminants. Focal trauma likely contributed to development of the pharyngeal lesion which progressed to aspiration pneumonia. Bacterial culture of the lung is pending and those results will be released in an addendum report. Intestinal parasitism appeared incidental in this case; but evaluation of the antihelminthic regiment may be warranted and ongoing parasitism may herald antihelminthic resistance. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology) Isolation of Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes from the lung further supported extension of infection from the pharyngeal lesion to the lung. The other isolated agents may represent contaminants; although some; such as Pasteurella species; may also have contributed to pulmonary pathology. This report concludes diagnostic testing in this case; tissues will be held for at least three weeks from the day of necropsy should further investigation be desired. Please refer to the final necropsy report for diagnosis and complete case comments. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology)

ABOMASAL AND COLONIC NEMATODIASIS RUMINORETICULITIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female gerenuk had chronic arthritis that worsened due to changes in the weather.
