VISCERAL LARVAL MIGRANS METASTRONGYLES (POSSIBLE ANGIOSTRONGYLUS-PARASTRONGYLUS SP. This approximately 7-year-old female golden lion tamarin was found in a corner of a mixed species exhibit where a prehensile porcupine was usually located. The animal had died by late afternoon. No prior signs of illness were noted. Necropsy revealed a quill embedded in the skin of the left temporal region that did not deeply penetrate tissues. An MGA implant was present along the subcutaneous region of the dorsum. Ecchymoses or bruising was along the medial aspect of the left stifle and smaller ecchymoses were on the distal aspect of the left femur and along the ventral aspect of the left and right body walls. Hemorrhage was present around the left renal capsule and the corticomedullary junction was not well demarcated for either kidney. Multiple green/black stones or slugs were within the gallbladder the liver had a lobular pattern and a blood clot was present along the serosal surface of the left side of the liver. Petechiae were on the mucosa of the gastrointestinal tract and the stomach contained a 0.5 cm. raised erythematous nodule. A similar lesion was in the cecum. The pancreas and distal small intestine were palpably firm and mesenteric lymph nodes appeared enlarged. Hemorrhage was present along the left cerebral hemisphere. The calvarium was red.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 12-year-old male golden lion tamarin had a one day period of illness and died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and dehydration enlargement of the right popliteal lymph node and an intussusception at the ileocolic junction. Loose stool/diarrhea was noted.

MENIGITIS VASCULITIS PNEUMONIA. This 5-year/8-month-old female red panda died. It went into cardiopulmonary arrest for a second time and despite extensive resuscitation attempts it was unresponsive. The animal had been worked up on 2/15 because of keeper complaints of acting abnormally. The keeper noted episodes of anxiety then depression. Workup revealed no problems. On 2/27 keepers noted an acute onset of serous nasal discharge blepharospasm O.S. and sneezing. On 3/1 she was found down in the enclosure. At necropsy there was obesity. There were fleas noted along the face. The cranial and middle lung lobes had patchy contusions. The stomach was empty. The duodenum appeared to be thickened. The colon was thickened along the descending portion.

CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS SEPSIS EMACIATION. This 11-month-old male giant eland had a history of watery diarrhea and had received treatment accordingly. The animal responded but the condition developed again sometime after treatment was discontinued. Subsequent blood work showed marked left shift hypoglycemia and azotemia. An elevated strongyle count was noted in fecal exam and Giardia cysts were also identified. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead. Similarly affected animals have also had fecal cultures that revealed Campylobacter jejuni and a parvovirus has been seen by electron microscopy of feces. Testing for Neorickettsia risticii on whole blood was negative. Heart blood and feces have been submitted for culture and negative stained electron microscopy from feces is pending. Necropsy of this animal identified thin body condition absence of adipose stores small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen prominent abdominal lymph nodes mottled lungs foam in the trachea and main stem bronchi and moderate to large amount of watery foul smelling material in the small intestine cecum and colon. Adhesions of the pancreas to hepatic vessels and gastrointestinal tract were noted and the parenchyma was firmer than normal.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE IRON STORAGE DISEASE GASTRIC PERFORATION. This 10-year-old female rock hyrax was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed a perforation in the fundus with adhesions of the omentum. The perforation appeared chronic. Tapeworms were in multiple areas of the small intestine and one cyst-like lesion was in the liver. The liver was orange tinged. The heart had an adhered blood clot in an atrium and the heart was pale pink to white on cut surface. A small cyst-like structure was on the tip of one of the right pulmonary lobes. Cecum had six mineral-like liths in the lumen which broke apart with digital pressure.
adult. Weight: 91000.0 g.  Poor dentition; Cystic endometrial hyperplasia; periodontal disease.

EMACIATION IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 19.5-year-old male Bali mynah was found down in the atrium and was easily captured. Supportive care was administered and it was noted that puncture wounds were on the left side of the face and a firm grape-sized swelling was under a puncture on the left side of the neck near the head. Some lacerations were noted on the toes near the metatarsus. In spite of supportive care the bird died the following day and necropsy identified a large focus of hemorrhage at the base of the skull instability at the atlantooccipital joint hemorrhage above the left eye orbit under the cranial pole of the left liver and in the right pectoral muscle.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male quail presented fluffed and lethargic and blood work indicated inflammation. Supportive care was administered but the patient did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. There is a history of mycobacteriosis in this group. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a 4 mm. nodule at the apex of the heart congested lungs and no other gross abnormalities.

GASTRIC IMPACTION SEPSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 12-year-old male meerkat was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed a gastric impaction comprised of fibrous material and possibly digested blood.

EUTHANASIA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE MILD PORTAL HEPATITIS. This 13-year-old male red panda was found laterally recumbent wet and shivering at the bottom of the moat. Examination was consistent with acute and chronic renal failure and the animal was euthanized. At necropsy the spleen had multifocal hemorrhage and the kidneys had multiple small cysts throughout the parenchyma.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS POSSIBLE RENAL DYSPLASIA. This 2-year-old female rabbit was found in lateral recumbency. Necropsy revealed thin body condition no evidence of malocclusion or dental problems gas and red tinged fluid in the large intestine possible adrenal and renal enlargement.

DIC RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS FREE COELOMIC YOLK. This 4-year-old gecko was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed white liquid material in the neck region eggs without shells of varying sizes in the oviduct and possible parasites in the stomach.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 14-year-old agouti had a history of inappetence and lethargy. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy cystic changes were noted in the kidneys. Cystic calculi were noted in the urinary bladder.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC THYROID CARCINOMA UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 31-year-old female ring-tailed lemur developed an acute onset of respiratory difficulty and radiographs revealed general loss of detail and fluid in the chest. Three round masses were seen near the heart by ultrasound and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed enlarged pendulous vulva cataracts serosanguineous fluid in both sides of the chest generous adipose tissue in the abdominal cavity and ventral abdominal fat stores mottled darkly colored lungs atelectasis of the right lung three round soft tissue densities that were pendulous independent of one another and near the heart base interpreted as atelectatic lung thickened pericardial sac dark purple/brown spleen with a 1 cm. mass at one pole brown liver with scattered nodules the largest nodule 1 cm. in greatest dimension a whitish pseudomembrane on the lining of some of the gastric rugae tiny cysts in the ovaries indistinct lumen in the uterus and a 1 cm. cyst on one side and areas of previous cysts in both kidneys on cut surface.

ARTHRITIS C-CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old male jaguar had multiple health issues that included thyroid abnormalities a mass in the cranial chest associated with elevation of the trachea glaucoma and severe osteoarthritis. It had become splayed over the last two days and was unable to ambulate appropriately in the rear legs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the esophagus that contained caseous material. Age-related changes were noted in the liver spleen and kidneys. Ingesta was noted in the digestive tract and the urinary bladder was full.

PULMONARY SHOCK CRYPTOCOCCOSIS GONGYLONEMIASIS THALAMIC PLAQUES. This 20-year-old male squirrel monkey was found dead. The animal was clinically normal the previous day. Necropsy revealed good body condition mildly reddened lungs and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA ISCHEMIC SKIN LESION ENCEPHALITIS PENTASTOME EGGS RENAL TREMATODIASIS. This greater than 2-year-old ratsnake had two hard body ticks removed from the skin in December 2011. In March 2012 it fractured its premaxillary bone had a retained shed and necrotic tissue plug on the rostra head this lesion believed to be associated with frequent striking at the terrarium glass. In August 2012 it was diagnosed with cutaneous acariasis. It had a recent history of weight loss decreased body condition and inappetence and was subsequently found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and wasting of the epaxial muscles an incomplete patchy shed over the head and proximal third of the body multiple abrasions on the dorsal scales mild ventral patchy erythema moderate pulmonary congestion mild atrophy of fat a mucopurulent discharge within the choana and oral cavity and mildly reddened and thickened intestinal mucosa.

THYMOMA HEPATICMETASTASIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 16-year-old female gazelle had a history of shifting leg lameness on the front limbs. Poor conformation of the hooves and hoof overgrowth were noted. The animal was anesthetized and a small abscess was present in the left front hoof. The lameness continued to worsen despite treatment. Radiographs revealed a mass within the cranial thorax. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a cataract was present in the right eye. A 12 cm. in diameter firm mass was present anterior to the heart. A large firm white to tan mass was present in the liver near the gall bladder. Smaller nodules were present in other hepatic lobes. Some of these masses contained purulent material. A large infarct was noted in the right kidney. Mild to moderate cartilage loss and osteophyte proliferation were noted in the left front fetlock.

AMYLOIDOSIS CATARACT ULCERATIVE KERATITIS EUTHANASIA. This geriatric Chilean flamingo was at least 50 years old blind in the left eye and was the victim of conspecific aggression. The right eye developed a corneal ulcer attributed to trauma that was slow to heal and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed congested lungs and no other abnormalities.

MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHRITIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female cottontop tamarin had a 3.5 week history of lethargy with associated increase in blood glucose.

EUTHANASIA GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY PULMONARY CHOLESTEROL GRANULOMAS VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE LINGUAL PAPILLOMAS. This 17-year/8-month-old male snow leopard was humanely euthanized. It had a chronic history of hip dysplasia and arthritis. It had a recent history of anorexia and vomiting. Blood work one week prior to death showed renal failure. At necropsy the snow leopard had thin musculature and fair subcutaneous fat stores. There were small irregular 1-4 mm. nodules present in the lungs that were numerous. The kidneys appeared slightly small. There were small raised nodules on the ventral surface of the tongue. The liver capsule was slightly thickened. Sections of tongue nodule were saved in ultra low freezer. Half of the brain was saved frozen and half was sent in formalin to Dr. Munson.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE UROGENTITAL SARCOMA WITH METASTASIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 23-year-old female ring-tailed lemur was euthanized. It had a history of polycystic kidneys. The keeper noted the lemur was less active over a few day period with decreased appetite. On the day of euthanasia “Fluffy” would not eat. At necropsy there was a large abdominal mass that measured approximately 6 cm. x 2 cm. The mass appeared to contain the reproductive tract urinary bladder and lower gastrointestinal tract.

TRAUMA LOW-GRADE SEPSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND HEPATITIS. This 27-year-old male Chilean flamingo was traumatized by a predator and was unable to rise. It received supportive care that included a sling but was found dead the morning after supportive care was administered. Necropsy revealed good body condition a large wound on the dorsum slightly enlarged spleen small gravel in the ventriculus empty small intestine adequate adipose stores male reproductive tract a fracture in the spine at the level of the external wound and no other gross abnormalities.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 9-year-old female meerkat was found dead on exhibit in the afternoon with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed subjectively enlarged liver with rounded edges a 4 cm. section of mid jejunum with darkened serosal pigmentation hemorrhage in the lumen of the intestine reddening of the mucosa throughout the jejunum and no other abnormalities.

AIR SACCULITIS MYOSITIS PNEUMONIA ENCEPHALITIS. This 5-year-old lorikeet has a history of inability to fly. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the bird was thin. Adhesions were noted between the heart and body wall. Hemorrhages were noted in the air sacs. A yellow granuloma was also present in the right cranial air sac. Liver was yellow to tan and friable.

JOINT TRAUMA SEPTIC JOINT SEPSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 5-year-old female golden lion tamarin incurred conspecific aggression with significant injury to the left calcaneus. The wound was exacerbated by self-trauma and developed septic arthritis involving the tarsus. The animal self-amputated its foot and during anesthesia to repair the other damage the animal died. Necropsy revealed an enlarged left inguinal lymph node and the node was gelatinous. The left iliofemoral lymph node was enlarged and had a cystic appearance. Both kidneys were pale. No other abnormalities were noted.

ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female chicken was found lethargic and in respiratory distress. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy approximately 40 cc. of reddish serous fluid were present throughout the coelomic cavity and numerous red round nodules ranging from 1-10 cm. were present in the caudal coelom.

XANTHOMATOSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 8-year-old female meerkat is from a group in which penmate aggression had been observed. The animal was found dead. Necropsy revealed a lesion in the ventral abdomen scars on the dorsum of the nose hemorrhage in the abdomen two masses distal to the pancreas and the mesentery of the small intestine with one associated with hemorrhage and one with a gelatinous core. Brown granular material was on the dorsum of the cerebellum.

YOLK COELOMITIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS HEPATITIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION. This 5-year-old female duck was found dead under a bush in the water. At necropsy the abdomen was distended with firm masses. Two large caseated masses were present adjacent to the oviduct and intestine. The oviduct was distended and contained abnormal yolk material.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS SOFT TISSUES DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE. This 16-year-old female palm viper has a history of excessive shedding and blood work one month earlier revealed elevated uric acid. Supportive care was administered but the snake died. Radiographic evidence of proliferative spinal osteopathy was noted. Necropsy revealed congestion of the stomach and lungs.

ATYPICAL ROUND CELL INFILTRATE PROBABLE LYMPHOMA; BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This approximately 30-year-old male Burmese python had recently been found dead in its exhibit. It had no prior history of illness other than one episode of retained spectacles in May of 2004. Three nights of no supplemental heat and temperature approximately 55°F occurred approximately one month prior to death. A partially decomposed and possibly regurgitated rabbit carcass was found in the animal’s exhibit after its death. Necropsy revealed adequate body fat and multiple firm brown nodules up to 5 mm. in diameter in the caudal coelomic region. Approximately 200 ml. of light green viscous fluid was in the caudal coelom. Some tan masses were noted throughout the renal parenchyma. Some hemorrhagic fluid was in the pericardial sac. A 3 mm. in diameter mass was on the heart valve.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female snow leopard had a recent history of doing poorly with associated hematuria acute hind limb weakness and chronic renal disease. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large amount of subcutaneous and intra-abdominal fat. The ribs and sternum were easily cut with a scalpel. The femoral head were arthritic. Carbon deposits were noted throughout the lungs and emphysema was noted in the nondependent lung. The heart was small and pale and the right ventricle was flabby. The intimal surface of the aorta was reddened and the wall of the right ventricle was thin. Both thyroid glands were 5 cm. in length but symmetrical. The pancreas appeared enlarged pink and had abnormal texture and color with deposits throughout the parenchyma. Numerous nodules were noted and no normal appearing pancreas was recognized. The liver was nodular fibrous and exuded pasty thick red material on cut surface. The right kidney had a thickened capsule that was mildly adherent and was mottled yellow/brown on cut surface. Possible hemorrhage was at the corticomedullary junction and the medulla was red/tan. Multiple concretions were in the renal pelvis and ureter. Structures radiating through the medulla had fibrous or mineral texture. The left kidney had a brown degenerative cortex and the corticomedullary junction was hemorrhagic. The medulla appeared inflamed or necrotic. The renal pelvis was packed with mineral deposits. The urinary bladder was thick fibrotic and the distal portion was black and possibly necrotic. Red/gray thick/dense pasty material was in the urinary bladder.

1. Kidney: Renal carcinoma 2. Kidney: Interstitial nephritis; lymphocytic; multifocal; mild; chronic 3. Kidney: Renal gout; multifocal; mild; chronic 4. Skeletal muscle: Myositis; granulomatous and heterophilic; regional; marked; chronic 5. Heart: Arteriosclerosis; multifocal; moderate; chronic 6. Heart: Interstitial fibrosis; perivascular; multifocal; mild; chronic Comment: This animal had histologic lesions in multiple organs that may have contributed to the clinical signs noted. In the submitted history; drowning was suspected (the animal was found dead in the pool with a claw stuck in the pool grate); and could be considered as a possible cause of death. Renal lesions noted grossly were consistent with renal carcinoma. Other renal lesions included interstitial nephritis and renal gout. Granulomatous and heteriophilic myositis was present in one section of skeletal muscle. No intralesional infectious organisms were observed; however bacterial infection is a plausible differential diagnosis; possibly induced by regional skeletal muscle trauma. Cardiac lesions included moderate arteriosclerosis and perivascular fibrosis; both considered age-related findings - no inflammation was observed in the heart. West Nile virus and heavy metal toxicity screening were pending (per history); and immunohistochemistry for West Nile virus is also available upon request.

INTERVERTEBRAL DISK DEGENERATION LUMBAR SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male captive bred African pygmy hedgehog was euthanized for acute hind limb paralysis. Radiographs revealed arthritis in the lumbar spine.

Haired skin (x2): See comments Comments The histopathologic findings for both masses in this case are suggestive of soft tissue spindle cell sarcomas; for which the top differential for both masses is a fibrosarcoma. While the neoplastic cells were well-differentiated; they were noted to be densely cellular and dissecting between collagen and skeletal muscle bundles (suggestive of more infiltrative behavior; thus the malignant diagnosis). Soft tissue sarcomas have been reported in Capybaras; although it would appear that cutaneous soft tissue sarcomas have not; however; soft tissue sarcomas have been frequently reported in rodents in general. Complete excision could not be confirmed for either mass; as neoplastic cells extended to the examined margins. Stephanie French; DVM; MS

ERYTHROID CONSUMPTIVE ANOMALY CHRONIC PANCREATITIS ASPIRATION ADNEXAL GLAND TUMORS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female dog had surgical repair of the left knee several days earlier became inappetent and never completely recovered from the procedure developing severe melena and was found moribund. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Blood work identified renal compromise and anemia. Necropsy revealed generalized pallor blood in the thorax melena and some lesions along the gastrointestinal tract and urinary bladder the bladder also thickened. The adrenals were friable and the liver was large congested and pale. The heart had possible hypertrophy of the ventricular wall. Adnexal tumors were extensive in the skin adipose tissue was icteric bruising was present in the ventral ribcage the pancreas is granular and the thymus had a possible nodular tumor or fatty remnants. The thyroid was pale.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA OBESITY. This 3-year-old female opossum was noted to eat her normal morning diet and had feces in her enclosure. There had been some loss of locomotion according to the keepers. The animal was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed multiple irregular nodules distributed throughout the mesentery bladder wall uterine body diaphragm kidney and intestinal walls. The liver had a 1 in. diameter round mass with normal appearing hepatic parenchyma on cut surface. An irregular brown mass was attached to the right ovary and a 4 mm. mass was in one lobe of the lung.

EUTHANASIA EPIDERMITIS PERIOSTEITIS. This 1-year/11-month-old male rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of extreme weakness and lethargy. It had become progressively worse since birth. It also had abnormal movement. No gross lesions were noted.

APOCRINE GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS TO LYMPH NODE. This 9-year-old male African painted dog has a mass in the right cervical area to 14 cm. in greatest dimension. The mass had an excellent blood supply and was encapsulated and appeared to be glandular. Separate masses were present dorsal to the original mass but upon dissection these appeared to be contiguous with the primary mass. A small string of nodular masses were in the adipose tissue and connective tissue extending from the mass to the jugular furrow and thoracic inlet and these were also removed as they had a similar appearance to the primary mass.
TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female gray wolf was euthanized due to trauma. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 17-year-old male corn snake had a recent history of a biopsy of a bony lesion. The animal was found with its teeth caught in its own skin and the snake died prior to treatment. No significant gross changes were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS GRANULOMATOUS COELOMITIS HEPATIC MELANOSIS INANITION MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA. This approximately 20-year-old snake had a history of chronic weight loss and sloughing of the skin. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. Scales were sloughing from the dermis with patchy foci of hemorrhage. Multiple 2-3 mm. in diameter masses were present in the tracheal mucosa. Similar masses were present in the lung and esophagus.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS SHOCK EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male peccary had a previous diagnosis of Leydig cell tumors diagnosed in August 2004. The animal recently has developed marked azotemia and isosthenuria. The animal was found down and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the kidneys contained numerous cysts bilaterally. The cortex was markedly thin and numerous cysts ranging from 2-5 mm. in diameter were present throughout the renal parenchyma.

EUTHANASIA ENDOCARDIOSIS PORTAL HEPATITIS. This approximately 2-year/11-month-old female hedgehog was humanely euthanized due to frequent seizures and weight loss. At necropsy ample fat stores were present. There was possibly slight cardiomegaly. There was possibly hepatomegaly. The liver had a mottled appearance. Sections of liver and brain were frozen for future use if needed.

HISTORICAL TRAUMATIC VERTEBRAL FRACTURES WITH ACUTE PULMONARY CONGESTION. This approximately 7-year-old captive bred female gerenuk was found dead on August 10 2013. The animal was found on the ground within four feet of a tree and fence. Gross necropsy revealed that the first cervical vertebra was shattered and the second cervical vertebra was fractured in multiple places. Three Trichuris were found in the cecum. The animal also had a midgestational fetus in the left uterine horn. The kidneys were congested and there was an area of pallor on the liver. The lungs were also congested.

ASPERGILLOSIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 18-year-old male thick billed parrot was found dead on the ground. The bird had been healthy and active and was rearing a chick. The bird was potentially exposed to Mycobacterium avium. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with minimal adipose stores. All air sacs were infiltrated by granulomas resembling aspergillosis.

THYMIC LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male African wild dog presented with dyspnea and radiographs revealed pleural effusion. Two liters of fluid were removed from the thoracic cavity and a mass was subsequently visualized cranial to the heart. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal has had a history of mild nonprogressive right head tilt for 2-3 months and also a cruciate tear that required surgical correction. The dog also had dental disease with multiple root canals. Necropsy revealed 1-2 liters of hemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity a 14 cm. tan/white mass incorporating the aorta and great vessels cranial to the heart extending from the thoracic inlet to the base of the heart and invading the soft tissues surrounding the first few ribs. The right cranial pulmonary lobe was adhered to the mass. Free-floating fibrinous debris was in the thoracic cavity. The right lung was dark red congested and sank in formalin. The duodenal mucosa was diffusely red/purple.

SEPTICEMIA VACUOLAR HEPATOPAHTY SEPTIC SHOCK. This 9-year-old female wallaby had respiratory dyspnea one day prior to death. It had a healthy joey about weaning age. At necropsy the lungs appeared very dark and congested. The wallaby was in good body condition.
GUNSHOT TRAUMA. This 1- to 2-year-old female Bengal tiger was found dead along a road in Dallas. Necropsy revealed multiple gunshot wounds.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS ADVANCED POSTMORTEM AUTOLYSIS. This 8-year-old male wolf was found dead. At necropsy extensive areas of subcutaneous hemorrhage and subcutaneous emphysema were noted. Serosanguineous fluid was present in the body openings. A large quantity of gas was present in the peritoneum. Marked emphysema was noted in the liver spleen and testes. Marked autolysis was noted in multiple tissues.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 8-year-old male Gray’s monitor was found dead. It had a chronic history of illness and was receiving supportive care. Clinical signs prior to death included swelling of the caudal left eye occasional flaccid tongue inappetence depression obtunded clinical appearance weakness and blood work consistent with chronic inflammation. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. area of scarring in the skin over the left eye swelling on the left side of the mouth caudal to the vomeronasal gland openings edema around the trachea thick white rubbery tissue adhered to the heart and associated with white deposits on the surface papillae lining the mucosa of the intestine empty cecum fine white streaks in the trachea and few pinpoint white foci in the spleen.
