CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA OTITIS MEDIA MENINGITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 1.5-year-old male rat has a history of chronic dental problems with abnormalities in the incisors. The rat became progressively weak with generalized neurologic signs that did not respond to treatment. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an abscess at the base of the skull likely from the right upper incisor tooth root with involvement of the sinus retrobulbar area and possibly the base of the brain.

EUTHANASIA NUTRITIONAL BONE DISEASE. This 11-month-old smoky jungle frog of undetermined gender was euthanized. This jungle frog had a history of severe skeletal deformities noted on radiographs and xero radiograph with significant clinical signs. Photographs were obtained during gross necropsy. At necropsy the thighs appeared shortened and bulbous. Hemorrhage was noted within the hip joints.

BACTERIAL ENTERTIIS CAMPYLOBACTERIOSIS SHOCK. This 8-month-old male squirrel monkey was lethargic and found dead the following day. At necropsy the small and large intestines contained a large quantity of hemorrhagic fluid. Cultures revealed a heavy growth of Campylobacter sp.

CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 6-year-old female Gaboon viper had a history of frequent regurgitation tested negative for cryptosporidiosis and had no other significant medical history. Necropsy revealed good postmortem and body condition some scale necrosis on the ventrum some discoloration around the cloaca ovarian slugs diffuse reddening on the caudal serosa of the stomach and duodenum large amounts of watery fecal material in the colon and no other remarkable abnormalities.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS PERFORATING INTESTINAL ULCER ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS THYROID ADENOMAS CIRRHOSIS RIGHT-SIDED CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female snow leopard had a history of chronic hematuria of several years duration and had been treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for 1.5 years prior to death. During routine health exam in November 2012 the animal was cachectic dehydrated and had renal azotemia with bacterial cystitis. Antibiotic therapy was initiated but compliance was poor and the cat represented with dull mentation lethargy and inappetence. Evaluation revealed marked dehydration renal azotemia anemia and leukocytosis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with palpable pelvis and spine normal haircoat no papilloma lesions identified muscle atrophy depleted fat stores 1-2 liters of purulent effusion in the abdominal cavity enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes diffusely nodular liver a pale firm focus in one lobe of the pancreas a full thickness perforation of the small intestine pale renal medullary regions a 1.5 cm. diameter cyst in one ovary polycystic thyroids enlarged parathyroids an no other gross abnormalities.

HEPATITIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS INANITION. This 5-year-old male tamarin had a history of diabetes mellitus which had initially been well regulated. Recently glucosuria was identified. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the liver was swollen and diffusely orange. Kidneys were swollen and contained scant hemorrhage in the perirenal tissues.

SEVERE INTESTINAL MURAL EDEMA. This 10-year-old captive bred female chuckwalla presented in November 2010 with acute hind limb paresis and atrophy of the muscles of the hind limbs. No radiographic abnormalities were identified. The animal was treated supportively but was found dead on March 21 2011. Hematology prior to death revealed leukopenia with toxic heterophils. Gross necropsy revealed severe enlargement of the distal small intestine and colon with an extremely edematous intestinal wall and hemorrhagic mucosa. Several necrotic eggs were also found in the coelom.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA ENDOCARDITIS SPLENITIS MENINGEAL HEMORRHAGE INANITION. This 16-year-old male corn snake had a history of weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the heart was enlarged. Blood was present in the oral cavity and trachea and the lungs were wet and congested.
MODERATE HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This approximately 3-year-old rock dove was found dead. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition.

EUTHANASIA CARDIOMYOPATHY MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY DERMAL CARCINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 17-year-old female panda was humanely euthanized. It was an aged animal that became acutely morbid. At necropsy it had many old age changes including cystic thyroids ovaries oviducts and lymph nodes. There was abundant fat. The liver was cirrhotic. The spleen was enlarged and oozed blood into the abdominal cavity. There was a lesion in the left ventricle.

METASTATIC SARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male milksnake was diagnosed with a spindle cell sarcoma of the body wall in October 2013 (G13-4583). The tumor was not resectable and the snake was routinely monitored for quality of life. When the snake became inappetent and masses were noted to have significantly enlarged euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed two dorsal body masses two-thirds of the way down the bottom and no other external findings. A firm white mass was noted caudal to the heart the liver was enlarged firm and covered in a thick white capsule and contained multiple white firm foci throughout the parenchyma. One area of the proximal small intestine was subjectively thickened. Multiple white masses were present throughout the renal parenchyma.

CHOLECYSTITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 13-year-old male ringed teal was found dead in the pond. Necropsy revealed fat deposits around the coronary arteries and apex of the heart possible cardiac enlargement pale lungs with thin clear air sacs a 2 cm. white thick structure with green/gray fluid and black mineralized material in the area of the gallbladder and no apparently healthy gallbladder present. This tissue was adhered to many of the intracoelomic organs. Multiple diffuse areas of muscle pallor were noted.

EUTHANASIA GILOSIS (BRAINSTEM) SHOCK. This 2-year-old female rat was inappetent and had a history of weight loss. The animal presented with labored breathing and proprioceptive deficits in the hind limbs. The animal was anesthetized for radiographs. Seizures developed following anesthesia and the animal was humanely euthanized.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female red kangaroo was being treated for mammary tumors but was refractory to the chemotherapy and further tumor growth was noted. The animal became unsteady on its feet in the morning and was unable to ambulate. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition several small masses inside the pouch all less than 1.5 cm. in diameter. Larger masses were palpable deep to the pouch. In the tissue deep to the cranial left quadrant of the pouch was a mass to 4 cm. in greatest dimension and deep to the left quadrant was a 2 cm. mass. Centrally deep to the pouch was a 6 cm. mass and the right superficial scapular lymph node was markedly enlarged to approximately 6 cm. in greatest dimension. On cut surface the node had areas of necrosis and what appeared to be tumor metastasis. The spleen was enlarged and had two pale masses up to 1 cm. in greatest dimension. The liver had approximately two dozen small masses up to 1.5 cm. in diameter. Three masses were present on the ventral aspect of the lumbar vertebrae two of which appeared to be metastatic foci and the third perhaps a lymph node. Four masses were noted on the pleural side of the diaphragm up to 1.5 cm. in greatest dimension. The lungs were riddled with metastases too numerous to count and up to 0.5 cm. in greatest dimension. A pale mass was in the wall of the right ventricle to 1 cm. in greatest dimension.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 15-year-old male sheep had a history of bad teeth acute fever and increased respiratory effort some regurgitation and was found dead. Necropsy revealed a twisted abomasum and hyperemic/necrotic rumen with associated rumenitis. Possible right displaced abomasum was noted.

EUTHANASIA POX DERMATITIS RENAL CHOLESTEATOMA. This 5-year/9-month-old male prairie chicken was humanely euthanized. It had a large lesion on the right side of the neck that resembled a pox lesion. The lesion was getting larger. At necropsy the left portion of the coelomic cavity had a large purulent area approximately 1 cm. in diameter. Culture and sensitivity were performed. There was a lesion on the right kidney approximately 1 cm. and brown and composed of brown granular material. There was a 1.5 cm. lesion on the right surgical area.

HYPERSENSITIVITY DERMATITIS. This 27-year-old female polar bear had a 1.5 year history of renal disease and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The bear began vomiting a few days prior to immobilization and euthanasia. Ulceration was noted in the gastrointestinal tract and pale kidneys were seen. The animal’s haircoat was in excellent condition and skin is submitted for comparison to conspecifics on the premises that have skin problems.

CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION LUNG; SYSTEMIC NONSUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION (ENCEPHALITOZOON-LIKE) AXONAL DEGENERATION. This 10-year-old male rabbit had a history of rear limb lameness of four months duration that was slowly progressive and eventually developed to acute paralysis of the rear limbs which necessitated humane euthanasia. Necropsy revealed good nutritional status with moderate adipose tissue stores and a large amount of food throughout the digestive tract. The lungs were congested. Feces were matted around the perineal area and under the tail. Meningeal blood vessels were congested.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC OOPHORITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 9-year-old monitor presented with severe lethargy. Rib fractures were identified radiographically. CBC revealed marked anemia. Treatment was initiated; however the animal died the following day. At necropsy mild pulmonary edema was noted. Bruising was noted in the muscle of the dorsal lumbar region and right femoral region. Massive hemorrhage was noted in the caudal coelomic cavity.

CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA (MYCOBACTERIAL SCREEN). This approximately 5-year-old male turkey is from a group of eight specimens two of which died with mycobacteriosis. The remaining birds were euthanized. This bird had white granulomas in the spleen.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female black footed ferret had a 3-4 day history of inappetence lethargy hematochezia and conjunctivitis and had been anesthetized one day prior to death for diagnostic work. A fecal parasite exam revealed coccidia. The animal was minimally responsive on the day of euthanasia. This ferret also has a chronic history of microphthalmia and early cataract formation. Necropsy revealed a multiloculated cystic structure in the right medial lobe of the liver. The spleen was subjectively enlarged. Yellowish liquid was present throughout the small intestine and hematochezia was noted in the large intestine. Kidneys bilaterally were small misshapen and had irregular margins and loss of normal architecture on cut surface. Capsules were adhered.

DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female meerkat has a history of intervertebral disk disease involving the cervical and lumbar vertebrae and possibly some deformity in the sacral vertebrae. The meerkat has given birth to multiple pups. She had alopecia on the ventral tail due to poor ambulation and tail dragging. Muscle atrophy and weight loss have been noted.

RENAL MINERALIZATION CYSTIC CALCULUS. This female greater than 2-year-old tree frog was found dead in its enclosure. This frog had a history of lethargy with decreased appetite. It was force fed one adult cricket the day prior to death. It was also given Emeraid. At necropsy there was brownish cloudy fluid within the coelom. Culture was done of the fluid. The gall bladder was distended with slightly blood-tinged bile. There was a 3 x 4 mm. yellow concretion within the urinary bladder. Both kidneys were red and engorged.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS GOUT SCALE FOLD DERMATITIS. This 11-year-old male rhinoceros snake died. Necropsy revealed multiple round dark red lesions on various scales throughout the dorsum and ventrum three intact sutured sites on the dorsum from previous skin punch biopsies retained epidermis noted between the scales generalized throughout the body and multiple round tan to white raised smooth soft to firm lesions on the liver up to 0.5 cm. in diameter which had a caseous core on cut surface and extended into the hepatic parenchyma. Both kidneys were dark red with mottled white precipitates throughout the parenchyma.

DUCK VIRUS ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female white-faced whistling duck was one of six fulvous whistling ducks that were found dead. Mortality due to duck virus enteritis has reached 90% in the fulvous whistling ducks. This bird was vaccinated for DVE three days prior to death. The bird was found lethargic on exhibit and had neurologic signs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed petechiae on the surfaces of the heart a diphtheritic membrane on the surface of the cloaca enlarged hemorrhagic liver hemorrhagic follicles in the ovary enlarged spleen petechiae in the pancreas and congestion of the meningeal blood vessels.
SHOCK TRAUMA. This 9-year-old male ruddy duck was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed opaque air sacs.

METASTATIC ENDOCRINE CARCINOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 19.5-year-old female river otter had a history of intermittent lameness and arthritis mild nephrolithiasis degenerative joint disease and chronic dermatitis (G14-1560). The animal presented with acute hind limb paresis that progressed to complete paralysis over 24 hours with no deep pain response. Several disk spaces at the thoracolumbar spine showed compression and spondylosis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition with mild dental calculus and no other external abnormalities. Three 2 mm. irregular nephroliths were in the left kidney and several 1 mm. nephroliths were present in the right kidney. Renal cysts were present in both kidneys. Multiple masses were present in the right uterine horn. The cranial mass was 0.5 cm. firm and white on cut surface. The caudal mass was 0.75 cm. and consistent with pasty green material. Three disk spaces had significant spondylosis and appeared to bulge into the spinal canal at T13-L3 although the spinal cord was grossly within normal limits.

EUTHANASIA CATARACT RETINAL DEGENERATION HEPATITIS MENINGEAL HEMORRHAGE. This 5-year-old male owl had a one month history of neurologic signs which was not responsive to treatments. A mature cataract was present in the left eye. The animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy adipose tissue depots were absent. A mature cataract was present in the left lens. An early cataract was present in the right lens. A small yellow area was present at the opening of the left tympanic area. The cervical vertebrae were hyperextended and could not be reduced. The liver was markedly congested.

ADENOCARCINOMA (LIVER AIR SAC) ANESTHETIC DEATH PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 5-year-old female chicken had a history of weight loss and lethargy. A large quantity of straw colored fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Surgery revealed numerous developing follicles with adhesions throughout the coelomic cavity. The animal died during surgery. At necropsy consolidated yellow foci were present throughout the lung. White foci were present in the liver. Fibrosis was noted adjacent to the proventriculus ventriculus intestine and ovary.

CATARACTS GLAUCOMA ANTERIOR UVEITIS NEUROENDOCRINE CARCINOMA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 11-year-old male call duck had a chronically occurring ulcer in the left eye. The animal was anesthetized and died spontaneously. The animal was resuscitated once and subsequently died. At necropsy the coelomic cavity contained a large space-occupying mass with a smaller mass caudal to the larger mass. The origin of the mass was not determined. The cardiac valve had a single small white nodule. The ventral surface of the liver had a blood clot and fracture (cardiopulmonary resuscitation artifact). The eyes had hypermature cataracts in both eyes and a healing corneal ulcer in the left eye.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 4-year-old female hedgehog was euthanized due to declining condition. The animal has a history of intermittent diarrhea vomiting and melena. At necropsy the animal was thin. The gastric mucosa contained an area of ulceration. The wall of the colon appeared thickened. The right lung was consolidated.

RETINAL DEGENERATION DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE BRONCHOALVEOLAR ADENOCARCINOMA DIGITAL SARCOMA NERVE SHEATH TUMORS MYELINIC EDEMA AND LAMINAR NECROSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS GLOSSITIS. This 21-year-old male African lion has a history of chronic renal disease maxillary canine extraction a firm mass on the dorsal aspect of the front right paw and a firm swelling on the lateral aspect of the left stifle. A pedunculated mass was in the left neck. The animal was immobilized for a second dental extraction and a punch biopsy was obtained of the paw mass which had radiographic evidence of bone lysis associated with the lateral aspect of P1-P2. Four hours into the anesthetic procedure the animal had evidence of hyperkalemia and acidosis received supportive care and the procedures were completed without complications. The animal showed evidence of initial recovery with tongue movement and swallowing behavior but when extubated he progressed to coma of approximately 24 hours. The animal then attempted sternal position when stimulated and had evidence of elevated hepatic enzymes and dehydration. Supportive therapy was continued but at 36 hours post anesthesia the animal developed respiratory dyspnea and died. Necropsy revealed adequate subcutaneous and intra-abdominal fat stores. White granular material was near the left elbow resembling gout. Some hard feces were in the terminal colon. Parathyroids were enlarged. Reddening was noted at the corticomedullary junction of the kidneys and 50 cc. of dark brown to red fluid was in the urinary bladder. Some of the hepatic lobes had pallor. A cystic lobulated mass was attached to the liver in the vicinity of the gallbladder and contained one liter of clear amber-colored fluid. The interior wall of the mass was reticulated. Some additional somewhat smaller but similar masses were also present throughout the liver. One of the main stem bronchi had luminal thick fibrous material. The pulmonary parenchyma was dark red and the lungs floated in formalin. Cartilage erosion was noted centrally in the articular surfaces of both hips.

ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS DIABETES MELLITUS ESOPHAGEAL CANDIDIASIS HEPATITIS WITH SEPSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 16-year-old male mandrill was found dead in its holding enclosure. The animal was being treated for pneumonia and anemia and also had been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. It initially showed some improvement but days prior to expiring became more lethargic and inappetent. Necropsy revealed purulent fluid in the abdominal cavity and a mild to moderate amount of fluid in the pleural space. The liver was enlarged with blunted margins and caseous material was present within and adhered to the gall bladder with fistulas or openings extending into the peritoneal cavity. The lungs were congested and the kidneys were edematous. Hemorrhage was in the pancreas.

PROLAPSED DISK DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female Arabian oryx was euthanized due to advanced gait abnormalities and evidence of intervertebral disk luxation at T13-L1. Caudal myelography showed a narrowing of the ventral dye column at this location. Necropsy revealed moderately obese body condition subcutaneous hemorrhage spanning the entire left metatarsus and degenerative joint disease.

NEPHROLITHIASIS URINARY TRACT OBSTRUCTION DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male/castrated goat presented with mild lethargy and partial inappetence of one day’s duration. Examination revealed a turgid urinary bladder with severe hematuria. This goat had a long history of recurrent urinary tract obstruction attributed to cystic calculi blocking the urethra and multiple surgical procedures had been performed for this problem. The goat also had severe degenerative joint disease with poor quality of life. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy a 5 mm. long brown peanut-shaped calculus was distal to the brim of the pelvis and numerous cystic calculi similar in appearance were in the urethra. These calculi ranged from fine sand to 10 mm. in length. Both lungs were congested and multiple joints had severe capsular thickening and dull cartilage.
AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT INTRANUCLEAR ISLET INCLUSIONS. This 17-year-old male swan was found dead. Necropsy revealed emaciation a friable liver and renomegaly.
BACTEREMIA. This 10-year-old male tentacled snake was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy marked postmortem autolysis was noted. Multiple pale foci were noted in the liver.
PULMONARY EDEMA PULMONAR HEMORRHAGE SHOCK BACTEREMIA. This 6-year-old male hyrax was found dead. At necropsy the animal was obese. The lungs were collapsed and congested.

TRACT FORMATION WITH GLIOSIS AND AXONAL DEGENERATION (PROBABLE BAYLISASCARIASIS) EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old female wallaroo has a 1-2 day history of lethargy falling over and ataxia. Examination revealed no obvious abnormalities but the animal did not recover from anesthesia and after two hours had fixed and dilated pupils and was stargazing. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.
BACTERIAL SPLENITIS HEPATITIS ENTERITIS. This 4.5-year-old female pochard was found dead in the exhibit pool. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.
GRANULOMATOUS ENTERITIS INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 6-year-old alligator lizard was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the liver was pale.

HYPERPLASTIC GOITER EUTHANASIA. This approximately 12-year-old male chuckwalla had a history of treatment from unconfirmed systemic and skin fungal infection in 2011. The animal has been requiring supportive care since that time. The animal would become dyspneic with minimal handling and had enlargement of both sides of the ventral neck of uncertain cause. Because of deteriorating clinical condition and weight loss euthanasia was elected. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition bilateral mandibular enlargement due to glandular and cystic structures containing greenish-yellow gelatinous material a yellow focus in the left hepatic lobe two stellate lesions on the right hepatic lobe white punctate foci on the margin of the urinary bladder and enlarged adrenal glands.
NA

XANTHOMATOSIS ARTICULAR GOUT GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS GRANULOMATOUS DERMATITIS. This 14-year-old female gecko was under treatment for a chronic facial abscess and hypocalcemia. The animal appeared opaque and was unresponsive the following day. The animal later died. At necropsy the body was thin and dehydrated. Swelling was noted over the right maxilla. A chronic abscess was present ventral and caudal to the right eye. White masses were present in the lungs. Multiple 2-3 mm. in diameter white masses were present in the liver. A large mottled white and tan mass was present in the serosa adjacent to the liver. Joints contained caseous white material (articular gout).

RHABDOMYOLYSIS POSSIBLE IDIOSYNCRATIC DRUG REACTION. This greater than 4-year-old female domestic rabbit had routine examination (with no anesthesia) and a rabies vaccine. The animal was returned to its holding space but developed trouble standing. The animal was dead upon return to the hospital. CPR was attempted but without results. Necropsy revealed ruptured stomach (possibly associated with CPR) and mild bleeding at the blood draw location but no other lesions. The heart was subjectively smaller than expected.

MENINGIOMA (FOREBRAIN) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS MENINGEAL HEMORRHAGE RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS. This 13-year-old female kudu has a history of intermittent seizures over the past four months occurring approximately every three weeks. An MRI of the skull was performed under anesthesia and a forebrain lesion was identified. Cardiopulmonary arrest occurred during anesthetic recovery and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy the animal was moderately thin. There were three small foci of purulent debris within the bronchi. The pericardial sac contained 50 ml. of serosanguineous fluid and approximately 300 ml. of hemorrhagic fluid in the peritoneal cavity. Extensive hemorrhage was present within the calvarium and adjacent to the brain brainstem and spinal cord. A semi firm mass was present in the forebrain and adjacent brain tissue was friable.

BACTERIAL COLITIS HEPATITIS PNEUMONIA. This 9-year-old toad has a history of lethargy and regurgitation. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the large intestine was enlarged and hemorrhagic and contained fetid fluid and debris.

AMYLOIDOSIS PODODERMATITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS CHRONIC HEPATITIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 28-year-old female Caribbean flamingo was found down and unable to stand. The animal died in hand prior to attempted treatment. At necropsy there was bilateral pododermatitis renal discoloration to pale orange and a free egg in the coelom.

CELLULITIS SUSPECT SEPTIC SHOCK GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This approximately 4-year-old male addax was found dead. It was found down in its stall the day prior to death semiresponsive. It was treated with fluids and antibiotics. Blood work showed severe leukopenia with elevated renal values. Physical exam revealed a cellulitis type reaction along the jugular furrow. Supportive care and antibiotics were continued. At necropsy there was severe necrotizing cellulitis from the left mid abdomen to the intramandibular space. The area over the left ribs contained the most severe cellulitis with multiple walled off pockets (approximately 5 cm. diameter) of brown purulent material. The lungs were hemorrhagic with petechia. The spleen was fibrotic with a thickened capsule. There were good amounts of abdominal fat. Both adrenal glands were enlarged and markedly hemorrhagic.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC RENAL AND HEPATIC DISEASE HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA STRESS EMACIATION. This 7-year-old male sugar glider was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple yellow nodules throughout the hepatic parenchyma and no other gross abnormalities.

YOLK COELOMITIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS SHOCK. This 5-year-old female wood duck was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the animal was in good body condition. The peritoneum was thickened and discolored yellow. A large quantity of yellow fluid and pasty material were present within the coelomic cavity. Several large yolk filled ovarian follicles were identified.

EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA ADRENAL CARCINOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS LYMPHANGIECTASIA EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS RENAL MINERALIZATION GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 8-year-old female ferret had a history of insulinoma cardiomegaly and adrenalectomy. Lymphangiectasia was noted during the adrenal surgery. The animal presented with extreme lethargy. Treatment was initiated; however seizures developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a small scabbed area was present on the ventrum. The right thyroid was enlarged. Spleen was markedly enlarged.
adult. Weight: 135500.0 g.  Died post anaesthetic.  Haemorrhagic cystitis +/- bladder rupture.  Bloody peritoneal effusion.  Pleural effusion.  Prostatic oedema.

PLEURAL ADHESIONS PULMOLNARY ABSCESSES ANTLER FIBROPAPILLOMA. This 8-year-old male reindeer was castrated in December 2008 and has shown nonspecific clinical signs of weight loss intermittent decreased appetite and occasional coughing following castration. The reindeer recently developed acute coughing and severe nasal hemorrhage resulting in death. There is also a history of a viral papilloma involving the right antler shovel. Necropsy revealed severe bilateral nasal hemorrhaging a blood clot in the lumen of the larynx caudal to the glottis and a blood clot in the lumen of the trachea. The bronchi and bronchioles were filled with blood clots. The lungs were congested with multiple tan/brown masses up to 2 cm. in diameter and numerous adhesions of the entire lung to the pleura. Five thoracic masses were noted in the cranial ventral thoracic cavity attached to the lungs by adhesions but not involving the pulmonary parenchyma. The largest mass was 10 cm. in diameter. The perihilar lymph nodes were soft and contain tan/brown material.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS WITH SEPSIS. This greater than 4-year-old male lorikeet had a fluffed and lethargic appearance in the morning received supportive care but died three days after initial presentation. It is the 16th death in this flock in the past month generally associated with bacterial enteritis. Necropsy identified emaciation good plumage congested lungs congested small intestinal mucosa hemorrhagic fluid in the jejunum dark stool in the distal colon generalized muscle wasting some coalescing foci of hemorrhage on the dorsal skull bone and no other abnormalities.

CARDIOMYOPATHY DERMATITIS PERIOSTEITIS. This 6-year/3-month-old female fruit bat was found dead. It had a history of edema and ulceration of both thumbs several months ago. This resolved spontaneously. More recently the bat developed edema and ulceration of a portion of the left wing web between digits #3-4. The lesions almost had the appearance of a chemical or thermal burn. The skin lesions appeared to be resolving although focal hemorrhage has persisted in the wing web. The bat was noted to be acting strangely 48 hours prior to death. At necropsy there was an area of skin in the left wing that had a number of small foci of hemorrhage in the area that previously had edema and ulceration. These lesions have largely resolved. The abdomen contained about 0.5 ml. of blood tinged fluid and a culture was obtained. The thorax contained a large amount of clear yellow fluid admixed with fibrin clots. The liver was large dark and mottled with rounded edges. Both lungs were congested and partially collapsed. Pieces of lung floated in formalin. The heart was enlarged and rounder in shape than normal. The left ventricle was thin walled and dilated. There was a thin white band on the surface of the right atrium. There appeared to be a well organized thrombus in the right ventricle with extension into the right pulmonary artery. The adrenals were about 3 mm. in diameter.

CHRONIC OOPHORITIS OVARIAN CYSTS SHOCK. This 2-year-old hen presented with distention of the coelom and fecal staining at the cloaca. Multiple cysts were found on ultrasound. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple thin-walled fluid-filled cysts were present throughout the coelom.
adult.  Euthanasia. Repeat prolapsed rectum.

BACTERIAL INGLUVITIS GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS HISTIOCYTIC MYOCARDITIS CELLULITIS. This 23-year-old male bittern was found moribund and died despite emergency treatment. At necropsy the body was thin. Yellow to green caseous material was present surrounding a dilated esophagus which was filled with putrid ingesta. A 2 cm. in diameter firm dark red to purple mass was present in the right inguinal region. The liver was moderately enlarged and contained numerous white foci.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC OVARIAN PAPILLARY CYSTADENOCARCINOMA. This 15-year/2-month-old female jaguar was humanely euthanized. It had a history of vomiting and anorexia over the last three days. It also was weak. At necropsy there were firm mammary masses in the left side of the abdomen. There was approximately 50 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity. The abdominal surface of the diaphragm and omentum were seeded with neoplastic tissue. The uterus and ovaries were completely infiltrated with neoplastic tissue. Both ovaries were cystic. There was abscess formation in large tumorous sections of the uterine horns. The left horn was adhered to the omentum. The urinary bladder was slightly thickened in one area. The right kidney was markedly swollen and congested. The left kidney contained multiple cysts. The middle lobe of the liver was completely infiltrated with neoplastic tissue. The pancreas was firm and dark. There was a 3 x 3 cm. round mass cranial to the right kidney that appeared almost caseous on cut section. The stomach was thickened and had an ulcer. The stomach contained only bile. The duodenum was thickened and the mucosa was reddened. There was a hard lemon-sized mass that appeared to originate from the root of the mesentery behind the descending colon against the dorsal body wall. The lungs were diffusely infiltrated with small white nodules.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female goat was euthanized for degenerative joint disease. The goat had a cystic mass in the mammary tissue. No other gross lesions were seen. This animal had been treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS HISTIOCYTIC ENTERITIS AND SPLENITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND ESOPHAGITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7-year-old male quail was found in moribund condition and died en route to the hospital. It had no prior health issues. Necropsy revealed good body condition three small hemorrhages on the calvarium behind the left eye and hemorrhage around the brain mottled tan/red and slightly friable liver seeds in the crop ingesta in the stomach and normal feces in the intestine.

PROLIFERATIVE DERMATITIS ACANTHOCEPHALIASIS RENAL TREMATODIASIS ENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female duck was found stumbling and falling over with every step and examination revealed depression and disorientation with labored breathing and frequent sneezing. Supportive care was administered but the bird’s condition did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mottled pigmentation of the feet legs and bill cornified papilliferous growths on the bottom of both feet mainly in the webbing contraction of the webbing and gnarled bent middle toes on both feet. Multifocal roughening and ulceration with slightly raised yellowish nodules are present on the maxillary bill near the left naris and the adjacent nasal mucosa is reddened and appears raw. Mucoid vomit is in the oral cavity and nasal passages. Oral mucous membranes are pale. A few pinpoint raised white foci in the liver are noted prominent gray spots were in the kidney. Both ventricles of the heart appeared dilated and the heart appeared enlarged with some fine white streaking in the myocardium of the left ventricle and thickening of the aortic valves at their attachment to the endocardium. Lungs were congested. Acanthocephalans were in the distal half of the small intestine. The pancreas was congested.

VENTRICULAR ULCER SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 42-year-old male thick-billed parrot had an acute onset of lethargy and dehydration. Five months prior to this the animal had dental extractions. The animal continued to decline and was euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin there were injected vessels on the surface of the crop and there was a small amount of reddening on the mucosal surface of the small intestine.

UTERIN LEIOMYOSARCOMA WITH METASTASES HEPATIC ADENOCARCINOMA (PRESUMED CHOLANGIOCELLULAR CARCINOMA). This approximately 18-year-old female Seba’s short-tailed bat died (it is not stated if this animal died spontaneously or was euthanized). At necropsy the liver was discolored with a pale firm mass in the central lobe. The uterus was enlarged with a mass in the uterine body. The stomach had multiple pinpoint regions of reddening on the mucosa.

ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS LYMPHONODULAR HYPERPLASIA SALPINGITIS WITH INTRA COELOMIC YOLK MATERIAL EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female domestic chicken had a 2-3 week history of being slightly off and this condition worsened on the day of exam. The bird had no prior medical history other than chronic bilateral pododermatitis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes when physical examination revealed an occlusive caseous yellow mass in the oral cavity. Necropsy also revealed a mass in the caudal coelomic cavity attached to the reproductive tract that on cut surface resembled egg-like material.

PANCREATIC ATROPHY/FIBROSIS BACTERIAL TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female cheetah had a history of chronic weight loss and poor appetite with abnormal feces. She had been receiving digestive enzymes in her food for suspected exocrine pancreatic insufficiency. The cat had a poor haircoat inattention and apparent cognitive difficulties. The cat deteriorated rapidly developing tremors vomiting and weakness and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The cat had a long history of hematuria and the etiology was never fully understood. Necropsy revealed surprisingly good fat body stores but generalized muscle atrophy dry ungroomed haircoat tacky mucous membranes marked tartar buildup on the carnassials enlarged parathyroids at the cranial poles of each thyroid numerous small white linear subpleural plaques over the lungs a thin jagged capsular sac in the liver marked atrophy of the pancreas and apparent cysts in the pancreas a single ascarid in the proximal duodenum mild congestion and erythema on the mucosa of the urinary bladder deep red shrunken kidneys with coalescing areas of yellow/tan pallor in the subcapsular cortex streaks and granular material on cut surface of the kidneys marked papillary necrosis with loss of a large portion of the tissue bilaterally without hydronephrosis sludgy tan mucoid material in the pelvis of each kidney a small greenish urolith or inspissated necrotic tissue in the pelvis of the right kidney some irregular brown/yellow streaking of the cortex of the adrenal and a few 4-6 mm. in diameter pink/white nodules in the parenchyma of the spleen.

DROWNING CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ENTERIC COCCIDIOSIS. This 11-year/11-month-old female gazelle was seen alive in the yard 30 minutes before she was found dead in a pool. At necropsy there was foamy serosanguineous fluid coming from the nose and mouth. The left thyroid gland was normal and the right could not be located (possible removal during biopsy G98-2070). The lungs were wet and heavy with exudate on cut surface. There were two small adhesions to the thoracic pleura from the right cranioventral lung lobe. There was 4-5 mm. firm white raised area on the right ventricular wall near the base of the heart. There appeared to be jet lesions on the left pulmonary artery. The kidneys were small and bumpy.

HEPATITIS MYOCARDITIS URATE STASIS. This 1-year-old female junglefowl was found lethargic with bright yellow urates. The animal died within an hour. At necropsy a large blood clot was present within the coelomic cavity which was adherent to the coelomic wall. The liver was reticulated with numerous nodules. Two large cavitated areas were present in the right lobe of the liver. Kidneys were pale yellow.
INANITION. This 10-month-old female frog was found dead. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS PARATHYROID ADENOMA. This 13.5-year-old female North American wood duck had a history of weight loss and was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed phthisis bulbi of the right eye associated with dried yellow exudate. The kidneys were diffusely pale.

SHOCK RENAL GOUT. This 2-year/1-month-old female lory was found caught in a drainpipe and died despite emergency treatment. At necropsy the bird was thin. There was a large amount of hemorrhage in the left temporal region of the calvaria. The ureters were full of urates.

STREPTOCOCCOSIS BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 4-year-old male cheetah had a history of decreased appetite decreased urination and decreased fecal output was anesthetized one day prior to death for examination and then returned to its exhibit where it had a normal recovery. It was found dead in the morning. Blood spots and small pools of blood were in the exhibit and blood was on the penis. This animal was used for promotional purposes lived in a kennel type enclosure with a small yard and with a littermate adjacent to four other cheetahs. This animal and its exhibit mate had not left the ground for greater than two years and were always cared for by the same staff. The remaining cheetahs are healthy. Blood work revealed possible hepatic disease with elevations in serum ALT AST GGT and total bilirubin. White blood cell count was slightly elevated and had band cells. Necropsy revealed moderate body fat and marked icterus. The liver was swollen with rounded margins and friable on cut surface. Hemorrhage was in the urinary bladder. There were 25 ml. of blood-tinged fluid in the pericardial sac. The lungs were congested and the adrenal glands appeared to be enlarged.

EUTHANSIA SARCOMA. This 16-year/10-month-old female oryx was found down with pale gums hematocrit of 25% and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the oryx was in poor body condition. The abomasal mucosa was discolored dark purple. Mesenteric lymph nodes were grossly enlarged as were the iliac lymph nodes. There was a large firm nondiscrete mass along the ventral surface of the spinal column. The mass was off-white to yellow and appeared to have some lymph node-like tissue involved. The kidneys were pale beneath the capsules.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ADRENAL VACUOLIZATION. This 16-year-old female chinchilla had decreased fecal output for several days. Supportive care and treatment were initiated; however the animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. Blood work revealed evidence of renal compromise and anemia. Kidneys were irregular and finely nodular. The cecum was distended with pasty ingesta.

ISLET AND ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMAS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE WITH FLAGELLATED PROTOZOA CATARACT AND POSSIBLE GLAUCOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old ferret had a history of adrenal disease with deslorelin implant and an insulinoma managed with prednisolone. The ferret also had complete cataracts and was blind. It had a recent history of progressive hair loss and diarrhea. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe muscle wasting and potbellied appearance alopecia over the cervical right dorsal and ventral regions and thin remaining coat marked intrathoracic fat congested lungs small amount of intra-abdominal fat reddened gastric mucosa with luminal black mucus hepatomegaly three firm nodules in the pancreas and adhesion to the duodenum red/purple spleen reddening of several mesenteric lymph nodes firm round irregular yellow to red left adrenal gland bilateral cataracts and a 2.5 cm. irregular flat white tissue adhered to the right proximal ribcage.

PNEUMONIA ENDOMETRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS. This 2-year-old female rat was found dead. The animal has a recent history of pneumonia. At necropsy lungs were mottled. Hemorrhage was noted within the GI tract.

SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 26-year-old male cockatoo is from a group in which there is a history of sarcocystosis at a bird show and three psittacine deaths. This bird had been quieter and losing weight and was found dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition slightly enlarged spleen and liver food in the proventriculus and ventriculus and the lungs floated in formalin.

THYMIC SARCOMA PROBABLE LEIOMYOSARCOMA PULMONARY SHOCK. This 14-year-old female tamarin was found dead on exhibit. It was diagnosed one month earlier with dilated cardiomyopathy and treated accordingly. Two days prior to death keepers had noted respiratory difficulty and decreased activity in the heat. When examined in the enclosure the animal had abdominal breathing with increased respiratory rate but still was eating well and active. Necropsy revealed pleural effusion pericardial effusion 5 cc. of serous fluid grossly normal heart a mass cranial to the heart at the tracheal bifurcation that was mottled pale and dark and approximately 4 cm. in greatest dimension. The mass compressed the right lung and the left lung was pushed caudally. The mass was cystic and contained approximately 10 cc. of yellow fluid. The liver appeared slightly enlarged and had a nodular surface.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 30-year-old female tortoise was found dead unexpectedly and had no prior history of illness. It typically would hide in the exhibit so may have been dead longer than one day. Necropsy revealed large numbers of maggots between the carapace and plastron and necrosis of the shell surrounding the tail. Free-floating urates were in the coelom and cylindrical clear gel-like material was free-floating in the coelom. Mineral deposits were noted in the kidney and in the heart. The liver was friable. The bladder was adhered to the plastron and contained patches of erythematous mucosa. The pancreas was firm and palpated like plastic.

ADRENAL CARCINOMA EMACIATION HEPATIC MELANOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male ground boa had a history of intracoelomic neoplasia and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the caudal coelom cranial to the kidneys. The mass was triangular and 11 cm. in greatest dimension soft and appeared fatty except for some firm tissue in the cranial pole. The mass was cavitated on cut surface and contained clotted blood or scar tissue. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) DEGENERATIVE NEUROPATHY (RESEMBLING WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME) RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 5.5-year-old female hedgehog had a one-week history of rear limb ataxia. Examination revealed severe spondylosis with loss of disc space and obscured intervertebral foramina. The hedgehog also had severe periodontal disease resulting in extraction of nearly all teeth. This animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged right adrenal gland and the previously described dental and spinal lesions.

ULCERATIVE PODODERMATITIS AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT. This 24-year-old male flamingo was found down in its enclosure was being medically treated for a severe bumblefoot lesion and was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed severe pododermatitis involving both feet possibly mottled spleen adequate adipose stores tan kidneys with white granules throughout the parenchyma and endocardiosis on a heart valve.

GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION PORTAL FIBROSIS. This 13-year-old male marmoset had a history of weight loss and possible hepatic disease in 2009. It was clinically normal for the next two years. The animal was missing for 24 hours then was found deceased. Gross necropsy revealed no significant findings and food in the stomach and intestines.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This greater than 26-year-old female lizard was found dead in its enclosure. It was very old and had lost most of its body condition. It was being force fed for approximately one week. At necropsy the lizard was emaciated. The coelomic contents were autolyzed. The kidneys were gritty with lots of urate deposits.

CHLAMYDIA-LIKE BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS. This 9-year-old male chuckwalla had been hospitalized for multiple limb swellings. This animal had been in an exhibit in which a Uromastyx died previously and in which another chuckwalla is currently ill. A fracture of the mandibular symphysis was noted in January 2003. The animal also had chronic luxation of the left carpus and tarsus that was radiographically stable. The mandibular symphysis had a radiolucent region at the rostral aspect and this lesion was stable. The chuckwalla was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed good body condition with no evidence of trauma autolyzed tissues congestion in the liver mildly mottled spleen pigment on the serosal surface of the kidneys and pale renal parenchyma on cut surface a 5 mm. subcutaneous swelling along the right dorsal antebrachium that contained mucoid material when incised and chronic luxation of the left carpus and tarsus with no associated soft tissue swelling.

ECTOPIC EGG ENTERITIS AND COELOMITIS. This 7-year-old female rock dove had a several day history of hospitalization for acute weight loss and being found in recumbency. The animal appeared to be improving and tube feedings were reduced. The bird suddenly declined became fluffed and had crop stasis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed crusting above the left eye thin body condition food in the crop a 4 cm. green plaque on the right breast muscle mottled yellow liver a tubular structure that was dilated and had thick fibrin contents (possibly gastrointestinal tract).

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS INTESTINAL AMYLOIDOSIS INANITION. This 13-year-old female gazelle was found laterally recumbent and paddling. The animal was humanely euthanized. The animal had a recent history of leukopenia azotemia and elevated hepatic enzymes. At necropsy the kidneys were small pale and irregular. Urine specific gravity was low (1.005).

MYONECROSIS ENTERITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS HEPATIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 13-year-old female giraffe was found down with the forelimbs splayed. Blood work revealed low calcium and markedly elevated CPK. Treatment was initiated including raising the animal with a sling. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy areas of edema were present near the junctions of the legs and body. Liquid rumen contents were present in the trachea and esophagus. Urine was dark. Erosion of the femoral condyle with exposure of subchondral bone was noted in the stifle.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS MYONECROSIS MYOFIBROSIS HEPATITIS ESOPHAGITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS SHOCK. This 36-year-old female flamingo was recently treated for wing droop and possible aspergillosis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy great vessels in the left shoulder region were hard (arteriosclerosis). The liver was enlarged. A midcervical vertebra was fractured while straightening the neck. Muscles of the distal humerus were dark orange and soft.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female snow leopard had a history of inappetence lethargy vomiting and was noted to be laying in the rain and unaware of its surroundings. The leopard was also noted to be standing over water but not drinking. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and red tinged urine was noted during the procedure. The animal was currently being treated for a presumptive urinary tract infection. Necropsy revealed decreased muscling but abundant subcutaneous and abdominal fat tacky tissues a 1.5 cm. dark irregular mass attached to the ventral skin surface of the right mammary nipple pale muscles small rare adhesions between the omentum and ventral and lateral abdominal walls small rare adhesions between the liver and omentum areas of linear dark discoloration in the cranial mediastinum a few small focal serosal plaques scattered over the pulmonary surface that did not extend into the pulmonary parenchyma small liver with sharp borders and firm parenchyma on cut surface mottled serosa a single 1.5 cm. depression in the hepatic capsule containing a firm tan/yellow concretion mottled and erythemic serosa on the urinary bladder moderate amount of dark red urine in the urinary bladder small firm kidneys with reduced cortex and irregular corticomedullary junction and hemorrhagic mucosal surface of the stomach extending from the cardia to just above the pylorus.

EPIDERMAL PLAQUE DIC NEPHROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 22-year-old male Gila monster had been treated for one year for crusting dermatitis on the sides of the feet and ear. Cultures revealed Ochrabactrum anthropi. Previous biopsy revealed fungus but cultures were unsuccessful. Multiple antibiotics and antifungal drugs did not change the appearance of the skin. The lizard died and necropsy revealed black spots in the liver and urate and crystals in the urinary bladder.

EUTHANASIA HEPATITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS UVEITIS ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA. This 17-year-old female jaguar had a several week history of weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy multiple small nodules were present in the peritoneum. Lungs were edematous. Papillary carcinoma had been diagnosed approximately one year prior to death.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 4-year-old female rat presented with increased weakness and ataxia and slight increase in respiratory effort. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes since this rat was at the upper limit of its lifespan. It is from a group in which bronchopneumonia has been a problem.

EUTHANASIA MULTICENTRIC LYMPHOMA ADRENAL CARCINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC GASTRITIS. This approximately 6-year-old female ferret was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed with lymphoma via fine needle aspirate of a splenic mass. It was treated with prednisone for approximately one month with initial improvement and then progressively declined. There was also a history of progressive lethargy and weight loss. At necropsy there was little subcutaneous fat. Perirenal fat remained. The left atrium was small firm and pale. The left ventricle contained multiple pale firm raised streaks. The right ventricle was dilated with nearly 90% of the myocardium replaced by firm pale tissue. There was moderate colorless slightly cloudy pericardial fluid. There were countless 0.5-2 mm. white possibly umbilicated masses that extended from the surface to the parenchyma of the lung. There were 1-2 ml. of serosanguineous fluid free in the peritoneum. There were multiple 2-5 mm. yellow firm masses in the liver that extended from the serosa through the parenchyma. The spleen contained two firm pale masses in the head. The tail of the spleen was replaced by a 4 cm. diameter firm pale mass. The capsule over this mass was ruptured and there was omentum attached to the underlying spleen. All mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Some were dark and some were white on cut section. There were multiple 0.5-5 mm. firm pale raised nodules in the kidneys that extended into the parenchyma.

ANESTHETIC/HANDLING COMPLICATIONS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY TRAUMA RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS IRON STORAGE SEPSIS. This 8-year-old female southern gerenuk died during a diagnostic procedure. Blood work showed severe azotemia and hypokalemia. Necropsy revealed moderate pulmonary atelectasis enlarged liver with a triangular white mass roughened gray/white peritoneal surface on the liver rumen and diaphragm mottled purple/red kidneys healing fractures on four adjacent ribs on the left chest wall and swollen right tarsus with a possible abscess on the medial surface.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC ENDOMETRIAL CARCINOMA PORTAL HEPATITIS ENTERITIS. This 8-year-old female Dutch rabbit was hospitalized for respiratory distress. The animal had minimal improvement with treatment and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal was spayed in 2015 and diagnosed with endometrial carcinoma. At necropsy large masses were identified within the right and left pulmonary lobes and in the dorsal thoracic body wall. Hilar lymph nodes were enlarged. There was a chronic diaphragmatic hernia.

1. Pharynx: Severe necrotizing pharyngitis with peripharyngeal abscess formation and associated lymphadenitis 2. Lung: Severe focally extensive bilateral bronchopneumonia 3. Adrenal: Enlarged adrenal medulla - pending histologic evaluation Comment The gross findings indicated severe pharyngitis and bronchopneumonia. Such pharyngeal lesions are most commonly associated with trauma from foreign objects. The pattern of findings suggested extension of infection from the pharynx to the lung by inhalation. Bacterial cultures on both pharynx and lung are underway; suspected agents include Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes and Fusobacterium necrophorum infection. Qualitative fecal culture has also been submitted for screening. Results of ancillary tests and complete histologic examination will be included in the final report. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Patholog Pharynx: Severe regionally extensive chronic pharyngeal/peripharyngeal abscess Lymph node: Severe chronic granulating and granulomatous lymphadenitis with multifocal necrosis/suppuration Lung: Severe multifocal aspiration pneumonia Adrenal gland: Multifocal cortical hyperplasia Severe chronic pharyngitis and peripharyngeal abscess formation with associated lymphadenitis and severe secondary aspiration pneumonia Comment The gross and histologic findings indicated severe pharyngeal inflammation with abscess formation; regional lymphadenitis; and aspiration pneumonia. Bacterial cultures indicated Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes as the primary infectious agent with the other isolates being likely secondary contaminants. Focal trauma likely contributed to development of the pharyngeal lesion which progressed to aspiration pneumonia. Bacterial culture of the lung is pending and those results will be released in an addendum report. Intestinal parasitism appeared incidental in this case; but evaluation of the antihelminthic regiment may be warranted and ongoing parasitism may herald antihelminthic resistance. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology) Isolation of Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes from the lung further supported extension of infection from the pharyngeal lesion to the lung. The other isolated agents may represent contaminants; although some; such as Pasteurella species; may also have contributed to pulmonary pathology. This report concludes diagnostic testing in this case; tissues will be held for at least three weeks from the day of necropsy should further investigation be desired. Please refer to the final necropsy report for diagnosis and complete case comments. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology)

This chimpanzee died following prolonged seizures. A 68.04 kg; male chimpanzee was necropsied on 8/31/16. Autolysis was mild. The animal was shaved over the chest; and there was a indwelling catheter in the cephalic vein over the left forearm. The chest circumference at the level of nipples was 103 cm. The width across the back at the level of axilla was 41 cm. The abdominal circumference at the level of umbilicus was 87 cm. The skin fold thickness at dorsum at the level of lower ribs was 1.5 cm. There were scant amounts of fat over throat sac; and the depth of abdominal fat was 1 cm. There were moderate amounts of visceral fat; and the overall body condition score was 4/9. There was a 2.5cm; wedge shaped; defect in the right pinna which was covered by smooth intact skin. There were numerous pale white; linear; irregularly bordered scars over the skin of the distal extremities. The distal ends of the second digit of right upper limb and the 5th digit of the left upper limb including P2 and P3 of these digits were absent and the blunted ends of the shortened digits were covered by smooth intact skin. There were 1-3cm in maximum dimension; open; sharply demcarcated; irregularly shaped skin wounds over the first digit of the left foot; the distal tip of the third digit of the right foot; and between the first and the second digits of the right foot. The upper left second incisor was missing; and there was marked gingival recession at the buccal aspect of the first upper incisors. All canine teeth were fractured and the root canals had been filled with epoxy. The dorsal two thirds of the lungs were dark ret to black; rubbery; and wet. The heart weighed 449.45 g and had a circumference of 30 cm at the coronary groove. The circumference of the right atrioventricular (AV) valve was 14.1 cm; and the circumference of the left AV valve was 10.6 cm. The pulmonic valve circumference was 7.2 cm; and the aortic valve circumference was 5.7 cm. The cerebrospinal fluid was slightly cloudy and contained scant flocculent; pale white t Lung: Acute extensive pulmonary hemorrhage and congestion Brain: Suspected meningitis Comments: Given the increased turbidity of the cerebrospinal fluid; meningitis is of concern. Changes within the external portions of the brain were minimal. Further gross evaluation of the brain including assessment of internal structures is pending fixation in formalin. The hemorrhage and congestion in the lung likely reflect pulmonary contusion associated with aggressive attempts at cardiopulmonary resuscitation. A final report is currently pending bacterial culture of the CSF and histopathologic examination. Amit Kumar; DVM; MS; PhD Representative sections of cerebrum; cerebellum; heart; spinal cord; trachea; tongue; diaphragm; liver; lung; gall bladder; kidney; spleen; lymph node; adrenal gland; thyroid; pancreas; small intestine; large intestine; skin; nipple; eye; and bone marrow were examined. Along the dorsal aspect of the frontal lobe of the right cerebral hemisphere and affecting the grey and white matter; there was a regionally extensive area of necrosis and hemorrhage associated with fibrinoid vasculitis; vascular thrombosis; and intralesional amoebal trophozoites and rare cysts. In this region; the neuropil was extensively replaced by hemorrhage; fibrin; necrotic debris and variable infiltrates of gitter cells and neutrophils. Dense fibrin often obscured the walls of vessels. Scattered throughout the necrotic neuropil and concentrated around vessels; there were numerous 35-75 um in diameter; variably shaped amoebal trophozoites that had abundant stippled eosinophilic cytoplasm and small eosinophilic nuclei with a single large karyosome. Intermixed with trophozoites in central regions of hemorrhage; there were rare cysts that were spherical; 20-40 um in diameter; and that had a thick refractile wall. The overlying meninges were moderately expanded by flocculent proteinaceous fluid and marked perivascular and scattered infiltrates of neutrophils and fewer histiocytes. There were regionally extensive regions of moderate interstitial fibrosis and myofiber atrophy; hypertrophy; disarray and/or degeneration throughout all portions of the myocardium of the ventricular free walls; interventicular septum; and atria; but most severely affecting the right ventricular free wall. Dense mature interstitial fibrosis and interstitial accumulations of well differentiated adipocytes extended deep into the myocardium where they dissected between and occasionally individualized myofibers; often disrupting the normal regular arrangement of myofibers. In affected regions; myofibers had moderate varia Brain: Acute necrohemorrhagic meningoencephalitis with intralesional amoeba Heart: Multifocal moderate to marked myocardial degeneration and necrosis and multifocal myofiber disarray with associated myocardial fibrosis Kidney: Chronic diffuse and segmental membranoproliferative glomerulopathy Chronic mild multifocal lymphoplasmacytic interstitial nephritis Liver: Chronic lymphoplasmacytic periportal hepatitis Pancreas: Chronic inter- and intralobular fibrosis and multifocal hyperplasia Large intestine: Segmental chronic lymphoplasmacytic colitis Lung: Peracute regionally extensive intraalveolar hemorrhage and pulmonary edema (pulmonary contusions) Encephalitic amoebiasis Cardiomyopathy Comments: The amoebic encephalitis in this case likely represents an environmental acquired infection. The most common species associated with encephalitis include Naegleria fowleri; Balamuthia mandrillaris; and Acanthamoeba species. Cardiomyopathy is common in aged chimpanzees. While this lesion was incidental in this case; there was evidence of abnormalities in cardiovascular performance in the form of degenerative changes in arteries and arterioles. Changes in the glomeruli and renal interstitium represent chronic changes likely associated with age; chronic cardiovascular compromise; and/or chronic antigenic stimulation. The changes in the pancreas suggest that this animal have previous episodes of pancreatitis resulting in the degree of fibrosis and nodular hyperplasia seen at the time of death. The colitis and periportal hepatitis are chronic incidental findings. The acute hemorrhage and edema in the lungs are consistent with contusions associated with aggressive attempts at resuscitation. Please note that numerous sections of heart were taken as per SSP protocols by our zoo species expert; Dr. Dalen Agnew; and that details regarding such sectioning can be made available from him. Amit Kumar; DVM; MS; PhD

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA NECROTIZING PANCREATITIS THYROID ADENOMA ACINAR CELL HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 18.5-year-old male tiger has a history of elevated renal enzymes cataracts fractured lower left canine and intermittent diarrhea or soft stools. More recently it has a history of vomiting and inappetence with blood coming from the nose. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a left-sided dorsal diaphragmatic hernia with smoothed edge margins along the entire circumference and the hernia contained stomach spleen small intestine and omentum. The spleen had multiple 4 mm. white to pale yellow nodules on its surface. Lungs were atelectatic with dark purple discoloration and multiple pale white to yellow 4 mm. nodules distributed throughout the pulmonary lobes. Adhesions of the stomach to the diaphragmatic wall were noted and ulceration was present throughout the stomach esophagus small intestine and large intestine. The small intestine and proximal large intestine were diffusely thickened and had multiple large hemorrhages along and in-between the intestinal wall layers. Large clumps of hair matted feces were in the distal colon. The renal medullae were bilaterally thickened and diffusely pale. The renal cortices were pale and cystic. A 0.5 cm. free-floating mineralized mass was in the right renal pelvis.

HEAD TRAUMA. This approximately 3-year/7-month-old male wallaby died as treatment was administered. It presented for quarantine on 1/31/02. It had sustained mild facial injuries at loading at originating institution. It sustained trauma to the facial rostral region on 2/2. At necropsy there was blood present around the rostrum and oral cavity. The maxilla was fractured transversely at the level of the mid palatine region and was noticeably moveable. There was marked crepitus present in the region of the sinuses as the maxilla was moved during postmortem examination. The left anterior dental arcade was fractured at the base of the teeth along the maxilla. The left lower incisor was fractured transversely at its base adjacent to the gingiva. There were moderate fat stores present. Bilaterally the lungs were red and had increased density to the parenchyma. There was hemorrhage present in the airways and the lungs oozed on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL SPONDYLOSIS MYELOPATHY. This 9-year-old female meerkat was euthanized due to progressive central nervous system signs which were unresponsive to treatment. At necropsy fusion and spondylosis were identified in the cervical thoracic and lumbar vertebrae. Other organs were grossly within normal limits.

PERITONEAL FIBROSARCOMA. This 3-year/8-month-old female capybara died. It had been treated for possible scurvy and had significant improvement. It was gaining weight the past two months. There was also no evidence of any lameness. At necropsy there were multiple white masses along the intestinal tract (5x7 cm. to 2x3 cm.). The masses were very firm and almost fibrous on cut section. One mass compressed and constricted the intestinal lumen which appeared to have resulted in impeded flow of digesta. There was moderate fat and muscling. The lungs had multiple 1-2 cm. pale tan/white foci. The liver had one lobule with rounded edges and white streaking on the serosa and cut surface. The stomach contained 1 to 1.5 liter of liquid ingesta. The lower gastrointestinal tract was empty. There were multiple areas of hemorrhage along the small and large intestine. The kidneys were congested.

DIC SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS. This 1.5-year-old male common squirrel monkey presented with sudden onset of severe lethargy and moderate ataxia. Physical examination was unremarkable except for mild hypothermia. Radiographs showed increased opacity in the caudal lung fields. Antibiotics were administered and the animal showed minimal improvement prior to being found dead late in the night. Blood work revealed elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine with mild anemia. Necropsy revealed no external lesions and good body condition. The right caudal lung lobes oozed foamy white material on cut surface. Small areas of hemorrhage were noted on the dorsum corresponding to the location of subcutaneous fluid administration. Aerobic and anaerobic cultures of liver kidney and lung revealed no growth.

TRAUMA CERVICAL FRACTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 1-year-old male kangaroo was found dead. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted in the nostrils and oral cavity. A fracture was identified radiographically at C2. Hemorrhagic fluid was present in the thoracic cavity. The liver was orange to brown and friable.

CORONAVIRUS INFECTION EROSIVE ENTEROCOLITIS WITH SEPSIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 4.5-year-old female giant eland is from a group with diarrhea. This animal had a two-day history of diarrhea and body condition declined rapidly. Supportive care was administered but the animal died during the initial procedure. Necropsy revealed scant mucoid brown diarrhea with flecks of fresh blood in the rectum.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA GOUT PULMONARY PENTASTOMIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 35-year-old female Gila monster has a history of a mass effect in the coelom and exploratory surgery identified a mass that incorporated the kidney. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 9 cm. irregular firm mass originating from the cranial pole of the left kidney. On cut surface the mass had a granular appearance and pale yellow gritty material. Several large vascular structures coursed through the mass. The left kidney was enlarged compared to the right kidney and both kidneys contained pale firm gritty nodules throughout the parenchyma. The liver was slightly enlarged friable and pale yellow with firm gritty nodules scattered throughout the parenchyma. The gallbladder was distended with bile. Both lungs contained pale yellow firm gritty nodules. Hemorrhage was in the spleen and pancreas. Both ovaries had multiple small follicles in various stages of development and the left ovary contained a firm dark brown to purple soft mass at the medial aspect.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MESENTERIC MINERALIZATION RENAL MINERALIZATION ABOMASITIS INSULINOMA. This 13-year-old female sheep has a history of chronic arthritis and weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy a firm tan nodule was present in the pancreas. A mineralized pink to tan mass was present in the mesentery.

GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 9-year-old male snake had been undergoing treatment for illness of unknown origin and appeared to be having problems moving its tail region. The snake died and necropsy revealed thin body condition and dehydration.

ENTERITIS. This 8-year-old female kangaroo was found dead. The animal had been under treatment for dehydration and anorexia. At necropsy marked enteritis of the duodenum and jejunum were noted with marked edema of the pancreas.

BACTERIAL TRACHEITIS RENAL GOUT DERMATITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 31-year-old male macaw had a history of dyspnea. The animal was anesthetized; however cardiopulmonary arrest ensued and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. Radiographs revealed narrowing of the tracheal lumen. At necropsy the skin of the legs was devoid of feathers and had scabbed foci. The left kidney contained multiple cysts.

SEPSIS NECROTIZING PANCREATITIS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS. This greater than 17-year-old male Matamata presented in moribund condition and had no prior signs of illness. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed partial depletion of fat stores fluid in the larynx and lungs fluid in all coelomic compartments and in the pericardial sac. The liver is fibrotic and several cystic lesions are on the lobes. Approximately 30 small stones are in the stomach. The gastrointestinal tract seems to have thicker walls in some areas than is expected. Male gonads are identified. Kidneys are pale and pancreas was yellow and firm.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE AMYLOIDOSIS. This 3-year-old male pygmy marmoset presented for dyspnea weakness and cyanosis and had severe pleural and abdominal effusions. The condition responded to drainage and supportive care and the marmoset lived approximately one month then died after developing the same effusions. Necropsy revealed dilated heart and enlarged liver.

EUTHANSIA HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY COLLOID GOITER BACTERIAL GRANULOMA ESOPHAGITIS. This female greater than 15-year-old rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of CNS signs with poor prognosis. At necropsy there was hemorrhagic pneumonia. There was mucus on the esophageal mucosa. There were inactive ova in the uterus.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS SEPSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE. This 4-year-old male black-footed ferret died and necropsy revealed hemorrhagic pleural fluid and hemorrhagic pneumonia especially severe in the cranial/dorsal pulmonary fields. The left cranial portion of the left hepatic lobe had a 1 cm. cystic area. Both kidneys were pale with irregular serosal surfaces and a possible infarct or hemorrhage in the cortex.

NEPHROTOXICOSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS EUTHANASIA. This 10.5-year-old meerkat was in quarantine and showed no evidence of illness until 24 hours prior to death. The animal had been immobilized and noted to have severe azotemia with elevated creatinine blood urea nitrogen and potassium. No obvious urinary blockage was noted supportive care was administered to no effect and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a loose necrotic left upper canine pale kidneys adequate adipose stores bilaterally congested lungs and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS MYOCARDITIS. This 11-year-old male python was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a 0.5 cm. in diameter soft white structure was present in the atrium. Lungs were edematous. Urate stasis was noted in the kidney.

PNEUMONIA PULMONARY THROMBOSIS BACTERIAL EPICARDITIS SHOCK. This 15-year-old female tree kangaroo was weak and inappetent. The animal was treated but died overnight.  At necropsy the lungs were dark and congested and contained fibrinous material on the pleura. One lung contained firm white well demarcated masses. A possible area of vegetative endocarditis was noted on the mitral valve.

VASCULAR NECROSIS WITH HEMORRHAGE EROSIVE PROVENTRICULITIS. This 12-year-old male whistling duck had been hospitalized for weakness ataxia weight loss and anemia and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed generalized pallor serosanguineous fluid in the coelom two small foci of hemorrhage on the surface of the heart attributed to resuscitation efforts blood-tinged fluid in the lung minimal digesta in the alimentary tract and tan/green soft and friable liver.

EUTHANASIA EMACIATION DENTAL PROBLEMS. This 12-year-old female warthog had been anesthetized three days earlier for examination due to weight loss and losing food out of the mouth. Examination revealed cachexia enlarged urinary bladder hypothermia and dental problems resulting in upper premolar #2 cutting into the oral mucous membrane. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed cachexia bilateral nephropathy apparent myopathy in the hindquarters pancreatic mass mild endocardiosis intestinal intussusception and severe distention of the urinary bladder.

BACTERIAL SIALOADENITIS EMACIATION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 6-year-old female gerenuk had a history of alopecia and unthrifty body condition. The animal had been eating and acting normally 24 hours prior to death although body condition had been poor. The animal was found recumbent in the morning swaying its head and projecting its ears caudally. It became agonal shortly thereafter. Blood work revealed low ionized calcium metabolic alkalosis and hyperkalemia. The group had recently been treated with anthelmintic drugs. Necropsy revealed a small area of pigmentation on the meninges caudal to the diencephalon prominent left-sided submandibular lymph nodes and several areas of abscessation extending down the left side of the neck 15 ml. of yellowish pericardial fluid small amount of frothy material in the carina hemorrhage on the serosal surface of the abdomen multiple petechiae in the pylorus slight blunting of the ruminal papilla edematous and hemorrhagic pancreas dark small intestine fresh blood on the surface of pellets in the cecum adhesion of some of the cecal pellets to the mucosal surface a 2.5 cm. cyst in the left ovary hemorrhage in the joint capsule distal to the patella of the right stifle and hyperpigmentation and alopecia in the skin.

YOLK COELOMITIS TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female duck presented after having been found in a beaver den on exhibit. The bird had a distended coelom and hemorrhagic fluid flowed freely from the trachea. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed yolk coelomitis and multiple hematomas with rib fractures and hepatic fractures. The oviduct and most of the ovary had been removed approximately one year earlier due to dystocia.

COLONIC AMEBIASIS. This approximately 5-year-old ratsnake regurgitated on 2/24 after a musk turtle tried to bite the snake on the head. The animal died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed fluid filled lungs pale yellow liver and a fibrinonecrotic membrane in the distal colon.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA UTERINE ABSCESS/PYOMETRA. This 3-year-old female rat has a history of increased dyspnea over the last several weeks and also has had a history of several mammary mass removals. The rat was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 2 cm. in diameter mass in the right abdomen and multiple white flat raised firm plaques and masses in the uterine horns. The right ovary had a 2 cm. in diameter cyst and the left ovary had a 0.5 cm. in diameter cyst. The lungs are diffusely infiltrated in all lobes with pinpoint to coalescing tan circular lesions that leaked purulent liquid on cut surface. The heart was mildly globoid.

EMACIATION COLONIC NEMATODIASIS.
