This 1-year-old male eland was in poor condition and had been moved to the corral area to be in the company of an additional female that subsequently died two days later. This patient was found recumbent in the enclosure by the keepers. Necropsy revealed poor body condition of several weeks duration absence of adipose stores decreased muscle mass congestion in the lungs foam in the trachea numerous Trichuris in the cecum and at the ileocecocolic junction mild congestion in the liver small testes and some black pigmentation in the right adrenal. Both adrenals appeared to have slightly thickened cortex.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE AND RENAL DISEASE PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female river otter was being treated for cardiac disease for one year. The animal’s appetite had declined and it had weight loss and bilateral cataracts. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed areas of decreased fur density but otherwise good pelt some tartar buildup fair to thin body condition tacky abdominal surfaces no appreciable fat stores several small linear black structures in the cranial mediastinum generalized cardiac enlargement with loss of cardiac muscle tone and enlargement of the great vessels wet and edematous lungs that appeared enlarged mottled and pale enlarged liver with mottled parenchyma and bilateral cataracts.

LYMPHOMA. This greater than 1-year-old female rat was determined to have a large abdominal mass at surgery had recovered from anesthesia but then died. Necropsy revealed a large poorly demarcated mass in the region of the pancreas obliterating the normal tissue. A second mass was noted between the stomach and spleen and the omentum had a nodular appearance. The cranial pulmonary lobe was tan and friable.

TAIL MUTILATION EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female sugar glider chewed off its tail within a 24 hour period. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A conspecific recently developed central nervous system disease associated with a brain abscess.
HEAD TRAUMA BACTERIAL SINUSITIS. This 7-year-old cockatiel of undetermined gender was found dead during the morning cleaning. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the cerebellar region.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATION CHRONIC CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE HYPERTENSION NEPHROSCLEROSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS. This 14-year-old male tiger had a history of intermittent vomiting and soft stool of four months duration with associated weight loss decreased foot intake and no weight gain over a four month interval. While anesthetized for examination the animal unexpectedly arrested and died. This cat also had anesthetic complications two years earlier due to high potassium values. Blood work at the time of death revealed elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine but normal potassium values. Necropsy revealed thin body condition in the rear quarters few white 2-3 mm. foci on the surface and in the parenchyma of the lungs ulceration and petechiae in the stomach bile staining in the pyloric and antral regions of the stomach grass sticks and leaves in the small intestine two 6-8 cm. thin-walled areas in the colon a modified transudate in the abdominal cavity some scarring in the mesentery larger than expected kidneys with loss of corticomedullary architecture and a 4 cm. cyst in the right kidney.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS STRESS. This 10-year/6-month-old male dog was humanely euthanized. It had a one week history of lethargy and depression combined with partial anorexia. Radiographs revealed a very large heart with marked tracheal elevation. The lungs were at 25% capacity. There was ascites. Ultrasound showed marked dilation of the right side of the heart and some pericardial effusion. There was a possible mass associated with the right atrium. The liver was enlarged with rounded edges. Chemistry panel revealed mild azotemia and increased LDH. A peritoneal tap had an inflammatory exudate. The dog did not respond to treatment. At necropsy the dog was in fair body condition. There were numerous nodules in the lungs that were 3-30 mm. dark red raised and sometimes cystic with blood. Others contained solid and dark red material on cut surface. One area of the lung (right) had marked consolidation. The heart was very enlarged with multiple coalescing dark red nodules around the base of the heart cranial and caudal. The pericardium was adhered to the heart in many places. There was moderate pericardial effusion with dark red clear fluid. There were multiple smaller coalescing nodules around the heart both at the base and apex. There was a very large mass associated with the cranial aspect of the right side of the heart (120 x 200 mm.) which was very friable and vascular and extended from the apex to around the base of the heart. There was mild hyperemia in the renal medulla. The duodenal mucosa was hyperemic. The liver was enlarged with prominent rounded margins. There were some fibrin tags attached. There was an area of marked fibrosis between lobes. There were two mass lesions noted (15 x 45 mm. and 5 x 15 mm.) located in the parenchyma. On cut section they were mottled dark red.

CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 6-year-old male wallaroo was found caught in a tree. The animal was immobilized and treated with fluids and antibiotics. The animal was later found dead. At necropsy the lungs were congested the liver was dark red and the kidneys were pale.

PERINEAL HERNIA HEPATIC GRANULOMAS (TREMATODE OVA) EUTHANASIA. This approximately 22-year-old guanaco had been in poor body condition for the last six months prior to death. The animal had a left perineal hernia and painful arthritis. Euthanasia was elected. Necropsy revealed thin body condition spondylosis of the cervical vertebrae multiple absent teeth easily reduced hernia pinpoint white firm lesions throughout the hepatic parenchyma and thickened adrenal cortices.

EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 29-year-old male green tree python underwent exploratory surgery for an intracoelomic mass. This animal had arthritis and possible neurologic disease or weakness. During surgery the mass was found to be an obstructed gallbladder. Visually the animal was thin and had fragile skin. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was possible obstruction of urine.

MYOCARDITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 12-year-old male bat was found dead. At necropsy mild hemorrhage was present in the thorax and abdomen. The liver was enlarged and appeared lipidotic.

CHOLELITHIASIS CHOLECYSTITIS PERITONITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA LINGUAL CANDIDIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 28.5-year-old male lemur had a 3-4 week history of illness with elevated white blood cell count and abnormal electrolyte levels. The animal developed moderate anemia and was receiving supportive care but would return to abnormal status when treatment was discontinued. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple enlarged firm areas in the pancreas adhesions of the pancreas duodenum and liver light brown liver with much bile staining roughened parenchyma on cut surface and vague masses. The gallbladder and bile duct were dilated. Kidneys had roughened surfaces and were pale on cut surface. The lungs were congested and adhered to the body wall.
ADRENAL CYSTS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 20-year-old female guanaco was euthanized. Nodules were present in both lung fields.

CHRONIC CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE LOW-GRADE SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male hedgehog had been inappetent for two days and had a proptosed eye. It also had difficulty breathing and bubbles from the nose. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

TRAUMA ENTERITIS ENDOMETRIAL CYSTS. This 14-year-old gazelle was found dead during morning rounds with no external injuries. At gross necropsy a large hematoma was identified in the retroperitoneal tissues surrounding the kidney.

CARCINOMATOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE AND RENAL DISEASE BILATERAL PHEOCHROMOCYTOMAS BRONCHITIS. This 32-year-old female California sea lion had a history of chronic pulmonary disease and debilitation. The animal’s condition continued to deteriorate despite supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed miliary nodules throughout the lungs thoracic effusion consolidation of the left upper lung and bronchioles thick discolored mucus in the bronchi of the consolidated lung large heart with large conus at great vessel outflow tract ascites pale liver with thickened and nodular gallbladder.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ESOPHAGEAL CANDIDIASIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CATARACT AND RETINAL DEGENERATION ISLET FIBROSIS OR AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old male koala had been diagnosed with a heart murmur weight loss and reduced appetite. It had not responded to several weeks of treatment and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified no external lesions. Teeth were worn and multiple raised yellow lesions were in the laryngeal region and within the esophagus some nodules were in the right atrioventricular valve a firm white region was present in the right pulmonary lobe the left pulmonary lobes were collapsed and osteoarthrosis was present within the shoulder stifle and hip joints.

TRAUMA (LUXATED JOINT) RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS (MYOGLOBIN NEPHROSIS) ATHEROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS CLOACAL PROLAPSE. This 9-year-old male cattle egret had been examined for gray discoloration of the right foot. The foot appeared functional and the bird was moved to off-exhibit holding. While there the bird developed an apparent luxation of the right metacarpal phalangeal joint which was stabilized with a splint. Three days later the bird was found dead. Necropsy revealed a prolapsed and necrotic cloaca and luxation of the wing joint. The koilin layer came off of the ventriculus easily during necropsy. This bird had been treated for two months with an oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug.

CHRONIC TYPHLOCOLITIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS DIC. This 8.5-year-old male ring-tailed lemur had a 2- to 3-year history of anterior lens luxation had a lens removal and was treated with eyedrops for corneal damage. The animal had been healthy until the last few months where it developed evidence of chronic renal disease with elevated white blood cell counts and toxic neutrophils. Supportive care was administered but the animal became weak hypothermic marked pitting edema in the left leg anemia hypoproteinemia and hyperglycemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes when the animal became agonal. In addition to the leg swelling the corresponding inguinal lymph node was enlarged. Adipose stores were adequate. Multiple small cysts were in the left kidney and one large cyst was in the right kidney. The adrenal glands were asymmetrical with the right twice as large as the left. A mass was on one end of the spleen. Multiple nondiscrete masses were present throughout the hepatic parenchyma. Much blood and blood clots were present in the connective tissues of the left leg and a blood clot and/or mass were in the region of the inguinal lymph node.

METASTATIC HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA. This approximately 11-year-old fruit bat had no history of prior disease although it had lost 8 gm. in the last month. The bat died and necropsy revealed thin body condition a small amount of straw colored transparent pleural effusion diffusely congested lungs with dark red mottling subjectively enlarged heart and scant amount of serosanguineous peritoneal fluid. The liver appeared enlarged and firm and the right and caudate lobes were nodular and irregular. Several 2 mm. tan cystic structures were in the spleen.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 9-year-old saki was found dead. The animal had been normal the day before. Approximately 1.5 months earlier she was treated by a referring veterinarian for depression lethargy and rubbing her rear end. Necropsy revealed congested lungs 8 ml. of clear fluid in the pleural cavity some dark pink discoloration in the jejunum and ileum an enlarged mesenteric lymph node and ingesta throughout the alimentary tract.

EUTHANASIA PLEURITIS PERITONITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 45-year-old female gorilla had a two week history of partial anorexia lethargy and exercise intolerance. This progressed to lateral recumbency with severe dyspnea. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy severe myocardial fibrosis and dilation of the ventricles was identified. Approximately 10 cc. of pericardial fluid were present. A large quantity of yellow tinged pleural fluid with fibrin was present. The dorsal abdominal wall contained a 20-30 cm. chronic abscess with adhesions. Adhesions were identified between the jejunum and colon with a large quantity of purulent exudate. Two large hard masses were identified in the left mammary gland.

AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 4-year-old female quail was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed possibly thickened air sacs dark lungs a white film coating the surface of the heart adhesions of the coelomic contents full crop pale enlarged liver dark enlarged spleen dark colon and pale enlarged kidneys.
METABOLIC NONE DISEASE PULMONARY EDEMA ATELECTASIS. This less than 1-year-old male bat was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy there was autolysis of the brain. The lungs were congested.

BACTERIAL COELOMIC ABSCESS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA CYSTITIS. This approximately 7-year-old female tree frog was found dead. At necropsy it had a 3 cm. diameter sized stone in the lower gastrointestinal tract.

ABSCESS PARALUMBAR SOFT TISSUES. This 6-year-old female reindeer had a one day history of lameness. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed an abscess on the left side of the caudal lumbar vertebra. Medial claw separation from the sole was noted on the left rear leg.

EUTHANASIA DEGERNERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINCAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC RUMENITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS HEPATITIS INANITION. This 16-year-old female eland had a history of chronic lameness and arthritis. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy marked weight loss and muscle wasting were noted. Marked erosion of cartilage was noted in the forelimbs.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC KERATITIS BLINDNESS SHOCK. This 18-year-old male duck had a history of rupture of the eye and enucleation. Scarring was noted in the contralateral eye. Neurologic signs developed and the animal was humanely euthanized.

YERSINIOSIS. This 3-year-old female black and white ruffed lemur was found dead unexpectedly on exhibit. This lemur was lowest in the social hierarchy within this group. Keepers noted no unusual behaviors or changes in appetite prior to death. Campylobacter has been cultured in this group recently and the entire group is currently undergoing treatment. Necropsy of this animal revealed minimal fat stores and abscesses present throughout the liver and cecum.

EUTHANASIA BILIARY CYSTADENOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA HEPATIC FIBROSIS CHOLECYSTITIS HEPATITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 16-year-old male lemur had a history of chronic GI problems. Masses and cysts were identified within the liver and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was coarsely nodular and contained numerous cysts. An inspissated brown mass of material was present in the gallbladder. A 3 cm. in diameter mass was present in the spleen.

ENTEROLITH CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 7-year-old female rock hyrax was hospitalized due to weakness and lethargy. The animal responded partially to supportive care but was found dead. Necropsy revealed dental disease distended colon and cecum a hard multiprojected mass at the junction of the caeca small intestine and colon with areas of the projections causing ulceration of the mucosa. Serosal surfaces have fibrin-like deposits and straw colored ascites was in the coelomic cavity. Apparent mineralization was noted around the oviducts.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 14-year-old female rattlesnake had a one-month history of caudal coelomic swelling and passed one irregular slug. Imaging identified several ovoid masses in the caudal coelom but no fetuses. Several other slugs were passed with water soaking but a general soft tissue swelling persisted and exploratory surgery revealed irregular ovaries which were excised. The snake died one week later and multiple white small spots were noted in the liver at necropsy.
TRAUMA RHABDOMYOLYSIS PULMONARY HYPOPERFUSION. This 39-year-old male flamingo was found dead. Necropsy revealed trauma attributed to predation.

EMACIATION NEPHROSCLEROSIS BRUCELLA ISOLATE. This 2-year-old tree frog has a history of gradual weight loss increased time sitting on the ground darkening skin color and is from a colony with intestinal nematodiasis and brucellosis. Examination revealed depression thin body condition dark green discoloration of the dorsal surface and no other abnormalities. Supportive care was administered but the frog died. Necropsy revealed 1.5-2 ml. of orange-colored coelomic fluid a white substance in the gastrointestinal tract interpreted as a dewormer (Panacur) and no other abnormalities. Culture of the heart and liver identified scant growth of Brucella sp most closely resembling Brucella inopinata although sequencing was consistent with a new species. No anaerobes were cultured. Chryseobacterium indologenes was also cultured from coelomic fluid.

THYROIDITIS PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS). This 16-year-old male cheetah had a history of cystitis and progressive neurologic signs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified a 3 cm. cyst in the pancreas a cobblestone appearance to the mucosa of the urinary bladder and a 3 cm. red raised mucosal focus and no other abnormalities.

ARTHRITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 6-year-old female wood duck was euthanized due to chronic sinusitis and multiple joint swellings. Previous biopsies from the sinus revealed chronic dermatitis and adenitis of the paranasal gland. Necropsy revealed fair nutritional condition a granulomatous exudate in the left nares and enlarged opening of the right nares. Lungs were mottled the liver was enlarged the kidneys were enlarged and tan the spleen was enlarged and both legs were mildly edematous from the hip to the hock with fluctuant swellings in the hock joints. Clear thick fluid was present in one of the hock joints.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS GASTROENTERITIS PANCREATITIS. This 22-year-old female snow leopard had a history of chronic arthritis. A wound developed on the hind end with fly strike. The animal became unable to rise and walk and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy muscle wasting was noted over the hind limbs and hips. Hair was matted with dirt and urine over the back half of the body. A large fluid filled cyst surrounded the left ovary.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIA DISEASE BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MILD IRON STORAGE DISEASE SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This greater than 25-year-old male fruit bat was found dead. At necropsy the animal was in fair nutritional condition and intra-abdominal testes were small.

FRACTURED LEG EUTHANASIA. This captive bred 5-year-old female addra gazelle was euthanized. It had been lame for two weeks and was sedated for radiographs. She likely broke her left humerus when she went down. Surgical repair was attempted but the bone kept splintering as screw holes were attempted to be drilled. Repair could not be completed. Exploration of the scapulohumeral joint revealed luxation with much soft tissue damage and granulation tissue. There was also fracture of the humeral head.

SUPPURATIVE GASTRITIS WITH VASCULITIS VASCULAR RUPTURE AND HEMORRHAGE. This 3-year-old male rock hyrax died spontaneously and had no recent medical history. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage and extravasation of blood along the lesser curvature of the stomach. A large amount of clotted blood was present in the lumen of the stomach. The first compartment of the stomach contained multifocal white raised areas varying in size within the lumen. The right lung was congested. The jejunum contained blood tinged clear fluid.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GASTRITIS MYELOLIPOMA BRONCHITIS. This 13-year-old male cheetah was euthanized due to chronic renal failure. At necropsy the animal was thin with marked muscle wasting and dehydration. The kidneys were small irregular and pale. The spleen contained multifocal 1 mm. to 1 cm. round raised firm cream colored nodules. The gastric mucosa was eroded with foci of pink raised tissue.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE PASSIVE CONGESTION PROLIFERATIVE PNEUMONIA. This 24-year-old female Dumeril’s ground boa was being treated for a respiratory tract infection and was not eating on its own. The animal died and necropsy revealed green mucus with white flecks throughout the trachea hyperemic lungs with white or tan plaques nodules in the splenopancreas and areas of white discoloration in the epicardium.

ENDOCARDIOSIS CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS GRANULOMATOSIS PANCREATIC TUMOR CATARACT EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female puff adder was found unresponsive and had no prior medical concerns. CPR was attempted with no response and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.
Weight: 7800.0 g.  Euthanased. Missing and chipped teeth. Oronasal fistula. Mineralised arteries.

SHOCK STRESS PERIPARTURIENT DEATH URINARY BLADDER EDEMA. This approximately 2-year-old female rabbit was found dead after giving birth to two juveniles. Necropsy revealed two additional kits in the uterus a moderately large blood clot in the uterus and no other abnormalities.

CHRONIC INTERSTITAL NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female goat was euthanized due to chronic anemia and arthritis. At necropsy general loss of body condition was noted. Fibrotic foci were present in the heart and arteriosclerosis was noted in the great vessels. Severe erosion of articular cartilage was present in the joints.

AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL GOUT BACTERIAL TENDONITIS AND ARTHRITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS VALVULAR ENDOCARDITIS. This approximately 7-year-old captive bred female pintail died. It presented with mild limping for two days. It became more severe and was examined. The tarsometatarsal joint was swollen and warm with some crepitus and pain when manipulated. Treatment was initiated. At necropsy there was hemorrhage around the right corner of the mandible that seemed to originate from the jugular. There was extensive bruising over the right side of the neck and head that extended halfway down the neck from the base of the skull. There was slight bruising over the left leg muscle. The right tarsometatarsal joint contained thick white material and was swollen. The joint was very inflamed. There were petechia on the pericardium and epicardium. The kidneys appeared slightly pale with urates. The jejunum and duodenum had petechiae throughout.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS AMYLOIDOSIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 21-year-old male sea lion had a one year history of progressive renal failure associated with progressive weight loss cataracts and elevated blood urea nitrogen. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed dark red moist lungs gray/red discoloration in the tracheal mucosa firm kidneys with concave depressions. Renal failure.

FATTY INFILTRATION OF THE HEART OBESITY. This approximately 20-year-old female bald eagle died suddenly. CPR was unsuccessful. Earlier in the day the animal had fallen off its perch and had gone to the hospital minimally responsive and cyanotic. At necropsy the left ventricular free wall and septum were markedly thickened. The serosal surface of the liver had pale multifocal lesions. A 2 mm. cyst-like lesion was present in the parenchyma of the liver. The lungs were congested.

PULMONARY EDEMA AND CONGESTION SHOCK. This 11-year/2-month-old female wallaby died. This animal had a history of not eating the day prior to death and had not eaten its medication. It was being treated for myiasis in the hospital. It had an abscess on its tail. At necropsy there was generalized pulmonary edema. There was a mineralized focus within the left lung. There were blood clots throughout the abdominal cavity. There were multifocal white foci throughout the liver. There were multifocal renal cysts.

AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATIC BILIARY CYSTS WITH ABSCESS FORMATION AND CHOLELITHIASIS ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female black-footed ferret has a history of chronic renal disease and a 48-hour history of lethargy and inappetence with elevated renal values that did not respond to treatment. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition hairless mass on the ventral mandible pale pink lungs with small white to very pale pink multifocal circular to oval lesions mottled pale tan to pale red liver with multiple cysts containing clear to pale yellow gelatinous or liquid fluid empty small intestine and pale tan mottled irregular kidneys.

SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AND LYMPHONODULAR HYPERPLASIA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS (FOOT NECROSIS). This 1.5-year-old female chicken has a history of a necrotic digit presumably due to avascular necrosis and amputation was performed under general anesthesia. The bird arrested during the anesthetic procedure and could not be resuscitated. The animal had been treated with several antibiotics and anti-inflammatory drugs since the time of the injury. Other chickens in the collection have died and display respiratory difficulties after being handled. Necropsy revealed necrotic tissue over the metatarsal pad and at the ends of all the digits and digits #1 and 2 were no longer present. The lungs were dark red and firm. Soft white plaque-like structures were present diffusely throughout both lungs and both lungs were filled with serous fluid. Kidneys were mildly pale bilaterally.

SARCOCYSTOSIS BILIARY TREMATODIASIS EMACIATION. This 8-year-old female pygmy falcon was submitted with no history. At necropsy feathers on the ventrum are matted and greasy and feathers around the vent were pasted with dry urates. Body condition was poor and the keel was prominent. A single pale focus was on the distal margin of the left liver lobe and a large amount of urates were in the urodeum.
HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS PULMONARY SHOCK. This 3-year-old male teal was found dead. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

INANITION FUNGAL GASTRITIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 2-year-old male zebra died. It was recumbent for several days. It ate well. It was mentally obtunded. At necropsy there was gastrointestinal ulceration especially of the stomach.

EUTHANASIA MUSCULAR HEMORRHAGE AND HEMATOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOCARDIOSISHEPATITIS NEPHRITIS INANITION. This 26.5-year-old male zebra was humanely euthanized. It was found acutely down in the stall and not able to stand or use rear legs. The left rear leg appeared to collapse under the zebra every time it tried to stand. A cerebrovascular incident was suspected. At necropsy the zebra was in fair to poor nutritional condition. There were no adipose tissue stores present and there was evidence of serous atrophy of fat around the heart and kidneys. There were multiple skin abrasions present on the body. There was mild separation of the hoof wall at the toe of both front feet. The left rear hoof wall had areas of separation at the lateral and medial bars. There was approximately 120 ml. of clear yellow fluid within the pericardial sac. The heart was grossly enlarged and globoid in shape with a thickened left ventricle and a dilated right ventricle. There were pale areas of muscle on the surface of the left ventricle. There was a white band of connective tissue present in the wall of the left ventricle. The left atrioventricular and aortic valves were thickened with multiple small nodules. There was a thin blood clot arising from one of the nodular masses on a leaflet of the aortic valve. There were jet lesions present on the surface of the aorta. The teeth had a classic “waveform” pattern of wear. There was an oral-nasal fistula just medial to the lingual surface of the left maxillary first and second premolar teeth. There were approximately four liters of clear yellow fluid within the abdomen. The liver appeared enlarged. There was a mild gastric ulcer present on the glandular surface of the stomach. The surfaces of the kidneys were pitted. The epididymides were firm. The secondary sex glands were very large. There were multiple small firm masses present within the subcutaneous tissue around the prepuce. The inguinal lymph nodes were enlarged and surrounded by gelatinous material. The tracheobronchial lymph nodes were black. The adrenal glands had multiple small green nodules primarily present within the cortex. There was bilateral severe hemorrhage present in the gluteal muscles and the muscles caudal to the coxofemoral joint. Multiple joints opened had varying degrees of severity of osteoarthritis.

GASTRITIS COLITIS PULMONARY EDEMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 3-year-old male rabbit had a history of significant weight loss and was found dead. At gross necropsy adipose tissue stores appeared depleted. The mandibular molars were severely worn. Lungs were mottled and firm.

PITUITARY TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old rat had a recent decrease in weight appetite and activity and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The rat had small amounts of blood on her fur and on the paper of the cage recently. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. fluid-filled cystic mass cranial to the left kidney.

VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS HEMOCHROMATOSIS BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS. This female approximately 2-year-old lory was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy the liver was diffusely swollen and copper. The spleen was enlarged grayish-pink and friable. Both kidneys are mottled white/pink. The proventriculus contains several 0.5 mm. white nematodes within its lumen (Dispharynx?).

CARDIAC NECROSIS THYROID FOLLICULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 15-year-old female tree kangaroo was anesthetized for tail tip amputation due to exposure of bone and cartilage. Recovery was uneventful but the animal was found down in exhibit shortly thereafter and died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed a flabby thin walled right heart. Stomach was distended with gas.

SALPINGITIS YOLK COELOMITIS SEPSIS. This greater than 17-year-old female black swan was found dead in its enclosure. It had a history of left leg lameness of 1.5 years. The left wing was noted to be drooping. There was surgical excision of a callus on the left foot. The swan became progressively weak and anorexic and was tube fed for six days along with antibiotic administration. At necropsy the air sacs were thickened and cloudy. The entire intestinal tract was adhered to itself and air sacs. The liver was congested tan and enlarged. The spleen was pale. The coelom contained a granuloma with necrotic egg material within and two noncalcified eggs within the uterus. There were multifocal white spots in the kidneys.

IRON STORAGE DISEASE EMACIATION STRESS BACTERIAL OSTEOARTHRITIS. This 12-year-old female mynah had been undergoing treatment for a trauma-related injury to the left pectoral muscle attributed to self-mutilation and also restricted paresis of the left leg. Surgery was performed to release the skin stricture of the left stifle. The wounds had healed but the bird died 24 hours after being returned to its enclosure. Reintroduction to the enclosure and mate reported to be uneventful. The bird had been on long-term haloperidol treatment. Necropsy revealed absence of feathers over the majority of the keel and ventral coelom thin body condition and completely healed incision over the left stifle. The spleen was small and pale. The left stifle joint was thickened and a large flap of cartilage was present over the cranial stifle.

PROVENTRICULITIS HEPATITIS SUBCUTANOUS HEMATOMA. This 17-year-old female duck had a history of weight loss. The animal was weak and depressed. The duck was found dead. At necropsy the liver was small and discolored brown. Cysts were present in the pancreas. A firm white nodule was present in the neck presumed to represent a parasite. The cecum was impacted with sand.

DUCK VIRAL ENTERITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS FLAGELLATE ENTERITIS HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE LYMPHOID NECROSIS. This 5-year-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy the body was in good nutritional condition and there was generalized vascular congestion. The esophagus intestine and colon contained foul smelling brown fluid.

EUTHANASIA SEPTIC ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) PNEUMONIA GASTRITIS. This 2-year-old female red kangaroo had a history of foot abscess which was under treatment for oral antibiotics. The distal portion of the foot developed a vascular necrosis which was treated with aggressive wound care; however the soft tissue continued to slough from the distal foot and fracture of the metatarsal phalangeal joint ensued. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy the right lung lobe was completely consolidated and contained bright green purulent material. Similar purulent material was present throughout the foot and metatarsal phalangeal joint.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED. This 7.5-year-old male cockatiel presented for acute blood loss and lethargy and had a large amount of clotted blood around the beak. The bird received emergency medications and died within five hours. Necropsy revealed contusions on the maxilla and nares hemorrhage in the nasal cavity and autolyzed viscera.

AXONAL DEGENERATION ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 17-year-old male African lion had a history of mobility problems of two years duration with reluctance to climb stairs some ataxia and apparent clumsiness. The animal also had some problems with constipation but otherwise remained in good health. Two weeks prior to euthanasia the animal began to deteriorate substantially with stumbling and misstepping mobility problems. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition moderately distended but patent gallbladder apparent confluence of the gallbladder with the hepatic lobe with associated cavitations and some mild hyperemia was in the gastric mucosa. Postmortem radiographs identified severe bridging discospondylosis from C3-T2 and most severe at C4-T1. Prosection of the spinal column revealed no overt compression of the spinal cord in these regions although the canal was narrowed by proliferative bone.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY OLD CERVICAL ABSCESS. This 9-month-old male capybara had a prolonged recovery from castration surgery and developed signs of rhabdomyolysis. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed a firm swelling in the ventral laryngeal area and a 4 cm. mass in the subcutis ventral to the larynx containing thick white material with a firm capsule surrounded by fibrosis and petechiation. The lesion does not communicate with the tooth roots. White pale streaking of the muscles was noted in all skeletal muscle regions. White foamy material was in the trachea. The lungs were diffusely red/purple. The adrenals appeared moderately enlarged particularly the cortices.

GRANULOMATOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION. This 20-year-old female penguin had a history of weight loss and regurgitation since late November 2015. Examination identified elevated white blood cell count and multiple areas of increased density in the left lung. The liver was possibly enlarged. Supportive care was administered but the patient died. Necropsy revealed clear fluid in the lungs and air sacs (found in the pool) two 1.5 cm. in diameter granulomas in the left lung and a large firm white/yellow granuloma in the left posterior thoracic air sac with multiple smaller orange plaques in the air sacs. Pinpoint black discoloration was on the serosal surface of the gastrointestinal tract and multiple orange plaques were in the mesentery. The liver was enlarged mottled green/brown and had multiple white 2-4 mm. in diameter nodules throughout the parenchyma. The ovary was black.

LOW-GRADE SEPSIS PROBABLE TYPHLITIS (AUTOLYZED TISSUE). This 25-day-old male rabbit had been removed from the mother’s care the previous day and was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed plant material in the stomach and upper gastrointestinal tract dark cecum full of dark pasty material and evidence of diarrhea in the distal gastrointestinal tract.

EUTHANASIA PERIOCULAR ABSCESS MENIGITIS PNEUMONIA NEPHRITIS MYELIN VACUOLIZATION. This 8-year-old female sugar glider has a history of suborbital abscesses. Ataxia developed and the animal was euthanized. At necropsy purulent discharge was present in both eyes. The lungs were consolidated. Liver was enlarged and kidneys were pale.
SEPTICEMIA. This approximately 7-year-old male chuckwalla died. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

AMYLOIDOSIS ARTICULAR AND VISCERAL GOUT MYCOBACTERIOSIS BUMBLEFOOT PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE INANITION. This male 5-year/1-month-old duck was found dead. Previous blood work noted an elevated CPK and uric acid. It had been pulled from exhibit as a companion to another duck undergoing treatment. Approximately one week following removal from the exhibit this duck demonstrated acute onset of lethargy presumed ataxia reluctance to move and decreased appetite. The duck would not eat and was being tube fed. Antibiotics analgesics topical treatments thermal and nutritional support were initiated. At necropsy the duck was thin and had a prominent keel. There were multiple plantar cracks and lesions resembling pododermatitis present along both feet. There was a small adhesion present between the ventral distal aspect of the ventriculus and the coelomic body wall. Both kidneys appeared pale and swollen. The pancreas appeared pale. The pericardium was dotted by multiple small white nodules which were gritty on palpation.

BACTERIAL COLITIS SEPSIS DEHYDRATION. This 9.5-year-old male Mexican beaded lizard was lying on its side taken to holding and found dead. At necropsy there was a small amount of fibrin within the distal coelom overlying the distal colon. The lungs were congested. There were moderate uric acid tophi in the kidneys bilaterally.

ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS COLITIS WITH SYNCYTIA POSTANESTHETIC RECOVERY COMPLICATIONS. This 5-year-old male rock hyrax was found dead a short while after recovering from anesthesia. The animal had been examined to assess an extraction site from a previous tooth removal. Necropsy revealed a reddened raised lesion to 2 cm. in diameter on the left lobe of the liver and a small red focus cranial and medial to it suggestive of hemorrhages or hematomas. The glandular portion of the stomach was proliferative.

GRANULOMATOSIS BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 13.5-year-old female tentacled snake was a reproductively active animal and had been apparently healthy until the day it was found dead. The snake was found agonal in the tank with blood coming from its mouth. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the oral cavity trachea and lungs. A large number of unfertilized ova were in the oviduct. The mucosa of the caudal oviduct appeared inflamed. Two possible nematode-like parasites were found in the coelom and one was found in the mucosa of the stomach.

RUPTURE BILIARY CYSTADENOMA PERITONITIS AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 7-year-old male black footed ferret had an acute onset of anorexia depression and weakness and was reluctant to move into a restraint cage when prodded. The ferret tilts side to side. It appeared to be normal the day before. Surgery revealed peritonitis and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed approximately 4 ml. of cloudy brown abdominal effusion enlarged spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes discolored dark tan omentum petechiae on the perirenal fat and cysts in the kidneys.

VISCERAL GOUT FATTY LIVER. This approximately 8-year/6-month-old female copperhead was found dead. It had a positive serology test for Cryptosporidium in September 2002 but negative on fecal IFA. At necropsy there were miliary to 2 mm. in diameter white nodules scattered throughout the splenopancreas. Intestinal serosal blood vessels were congested. The gall bladder was distended. There was white streaking (urate deposits) on the surface of the liver and pericardium. The liver was enlarged and pale. There was a 5 mm. round cystic nodule cranial to the heart. There was cloudy mucoid material within the esophagus stomach and upper small intestine. The lungs appeared dark red and congested.

EUTHANASIA MILD SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION (POSSIBLE PARASITISM) SALPINGITIS (POSSIBLY BACTERIAL) RENAL GOUT CENTRAL NERVIOUS SYSTEM DISEASE (ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED--BRAIN NOT SUBMITTED). This approximately 20-year-old female screech owl had recently become less responsive and had difficulty perching with a head tilt to the left. Blood work revealed hyperphosphatemia and hyperuricacidemia with mild leukocytosis. The bird was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed renomegaly and hepatomegaly with possible visceral gout.

LYMPH PROLIFERATIVE DISEASE PROBABLE MAREKS DISEASE. This 1-year-old female chicken was found dead in the morning and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity mottled yellow/red kidneys and no other findings.

EUTHANASIA SALMONELLOSIS OSTEOMYELITIS HEMIPENE IMPACTION. This 10-year-old male snake was euthanized. Histologically multiple areas of boney thickening were noted in the spinal column. Salmonella sp. was cultured from heart blood at necropsy.

STOMATITIS AND FACIAL CELLULITIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male rat presented in poor body condition with poor porphyrin stained wet hair on the face. A lesion in the rostral palate that entered the sinus cavity absent right upper incisor malaligned left upper incisor moderately overgrown lower incisors and no other abnormalities externally. The liver was small kidneys were dark red and lungs were diffusely tan to red. No abscesses were seen in the lungs.

MULTICENTRIC LYMPHOSARCOMA. This approximately 5-year/10-month-old male viper died. It had a history of not eating in the past two months. At necropsy there were abundant adipose stores. There was a small amount of blood tinged fluid present in the caudal portion of the air sac. The intestines adipose tissue and some of the other abdominal organs were adhered together in a single mass of tissue. On cut section there were relatively few tissues that were recognizable. There were scattered small hemorrhages in the liver and multiple small white dots. The lung wall was thickened edematous and hemorrhagic. There was a thick mucoid hemorrhagic exudate present in small and large clumps in the lung and in the caudal trachea. There was blood tinged pericardial fluid in a greater than normal quantity. There was an area of hemorrhage visible on the heart that extended through the entire myocardium to the endocardium. Cultures of lung grew presumptive Salmonella and Providencia alcalifaciens.

HEPATIC MEDULLOBLASTOMA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old axolotl had a large nonresectable hepatic mass noted during exploratory celiotomy and was euthanized while anesthetized. Necropsy revealed two white spots from previous injuries to the skin. A 5 cm. heterogeneous mass was in the middle of the liver. The mass was tan to gray with small white grainy nodules throughout. The surrounding hepatic tissue appeared normal. On cut surface the entire parenchyma of the liver appeared abnormal with areas of necrosis and purulent material. The stomach was empty.

ENCEPHALOMYELITIS AXONAL DEGENERATION POSSIBLE VIRAL INCLUSIONS DISSEMINATED MYCOTIC INFECTION. This 10-year-old female red panda had a few month history of difficulty walking and apparent ataxia associated with spondylosis of L6-S1. Supportive care included antibiotics and various anti-inflammatory drugs. Urine and cerebrospinal fluid tests for distemper were negative. Serology for coonhound paralysis and West Nile virus are pending. The animal became moribund over time did not respond to supportive care and died. Pyelonephritis several nodules in the lungs a glandular bilobed mass cranial to the heart interpreted as thymus and apparent cirrhosis of the liver were noted at necropsy.

SPINAL CORD DEGENERATION PROBABLE CERVICAL TRAUMA RHABDOMYOLYSIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS PERITONITIS POSSIBLE RUPTURED URINARY BLADDER OR GASTRIC ULCER. This 7-month-old male gazelle had arrived 2.5 days earlier from a different zoo unloaded into the stall with no problems but then jumped straight upward and thereafter was unable to stand or walk. Examination revealed a minor chip fracture in the right ilium and elevated hepatic and muscle enzymes. The animal received aggressive treatment for myopathy and possible nerve paralysis was observed standing for brief periods of time each day but did not regain mobility and remained weak. The animal did not eat voluntarily and had stopped taking food from keepers although mentation remained normal. The animal was not holding its head up and developed an ocular lesion in the right eye. The animal subsequently died and blood work at the time of death revealed acute renal failure elevated muscle and hepatic enzymes moderate hypoglycemia mild hyperglobulinemia and hyperkalemia. Necropsy revealed no signs of trauma or injury a minor wound on the right lateral hock (occurred during unloading from trailer) fibrinous adhesions of the diaphragm liver rumen and spleen and no gross lesions in the musculoskeletal system or central nervous system.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC CARCINOMA MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 19-year/4-month-old male tree kangaroo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of elevated hepatic enzyme values. Its condition had not significantly improved and it had many problems. At necropsy the body condition was fair. Both feet had pododermatitis on the weight bear surfaces with loss of skin. There were black 3 mm. to 2 cm. areas of discoloration over on the ventral side of the tail vertebrae. There was loss of mobility of many of the joints. There was approximately 10 cc. of straw colored fluid within the pericardial sac. The liver had variably sized 2 mm. to 2 cm. discolored masses that continued into the parenchyma. Approximately one-fifth of the liver was affected. The adrenal glands appeared enlarged.

EUTHANASIA CANNON BONE FRACTURE. This 26-year/2-month-old female giraffe was humanely euthanized. It developed a sudden fractured cannon bone. The fracture was compound displaced and open. At necropsy there were some areas of hyperkeratosis noted on the body. There was lateral deviation of the left rear foot. The skin was open over the fetlock joint. There was hyperkeratosis in the groin and inguinal regions. There was a compound fracture of the right rear cannon bone distally. There were many small bone fragments present. The kidneys had some scarring and some cysts.

ISLET CELL TUMOR HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female/spayed ferret was diagnosed with insulinoma nine months earlier and had been well managed on oral prednisolone. It presented for rapid weight loss despite normal appetite of three weeks duration with elevated hepatic values and hypoglycemia. Supportive care was administered but the animal’s condition continued to decline and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition. The liver was diffusely yellow/tan. A 2 mm. nodule was in the pancreas. The spleen seemed small for the species.
CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This 1-year-old desert tortoise was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed anasarca and congested lungs. The bile was fluid filled and distended.

CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 17-year-old female tamarin presented with weakness poor gum color shock moderate dyspnea with manual restraint heart murmur and mild arrhythmia. Supportive care was administered but the animal died overnight. Necropsy revealed thin body condition pale lungs enlarged right atria pale color in the liver large adrenals and a moderate amount of blood in the stomach.

BACTERIAL TENOSYNOVITIS OF THE HOCK WITH AVASCULAR NECROSIS OF DISTAL LEG EUTHANASIA. This greater than 13-year-old male spoonbill developed acute onset of lameness of the left leg with swelling of the left hock. Aspirates of the swelling are consistent with inflammation and cultures were negative. The bird did not respond to anti-inflammatory drugs and topical DMSO. Lameness eventually developed in the right leg with swelling of the right leg from the stifle distally and moderate swelling of the left hock persisted. Aspirate of the right hock and foot yielded an inflammatory exudate and cultures were negative. Antibiotic therapy was instituted. Swelling decreased slightly and the foot developed large vesicular type lesions. Eventually the medial vein of the right leg became swollen and black. The right leg approximately 2 cm. distal to the hock was purple and cold. Vascular compromise was suspected. Due to continued deterioration the bird was euthanized. Necropsy revealed fair nutritional status multiple small black spots in the lungs and surrounding air sacs hepatic and splenic enlargement swelling of the left hock with clear fluid in the subcutaneous tissues around the hock joint but normal appearing joint surfaces. The right hock was swollen more than the left with similar fluid present in the subcutaneous tissues. The right leg distal to the hock was dark purple and black in some areas. A line of demarcation existed between healthy and abnormal tissue in the skin over the right tarsal/metatarsal bone approximately 2 cm. distal to the right hock.

CHRONIC MYOCARDIAL AND RENAL FIBROSIS. This 20-year-old female squirrel monkey presented with weakness debilitation hypothermia and thin body condition and appeared to be dehydrated. Supportive care was administered and ultrasound the following day revealed small choleliths in the thickened gastrointestinal tract. The monkey died later that morning. Necropsy revealed red blisters in the cecum and appendix and a nutmeg liver.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY MENINGEAL ARTERIOSCLEROSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS MESANGIOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY PANCREATIC ACINAR CELL ADENOMA. This 25-year-old female tamarin died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed thin body condition modified transudate in the abdomen and thorax lymphadenopathy mediastinal mass __ diffuse infiltrative disease in the lung with areas of hemorrhage dilated left ventricle large pancreatic tumor (photo submitted) advanced dental wear.

PYOMETRA SEPSIS POSTSURGICAL COMPLICATIONS. This 7-year-old female African hunting dog developed an acute onset of lethargy and inappetence. Pyometra was diagnosed and ovariohysterectomy was performed. Approximately three hours after the surgery the dog developed cardiopulmonary arrest and died despite resuscitation attempts. Necropsy revealed fair to good body condition a large amount of clotted and unclotted blood in the abdomen primarily in the mesentery and around the kidneys absence of right ovarian pedicle and sutures rust/red colored fluid in the duodenum and abundant internal fat stores.

SEPTIC SKELETAL MYOSITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS. This 12-year-old female Bali mynah presented on March 4 2011 for not using its right foot normally. The bird became apneic and died during anesthesia for workup. Gross necropsy revealed a wound present on the proximal and mid-tibiotarsal diaphysis with approximately 4 mm. of exposed bone. Internal organ pallor was also noted.

INTESTINAL INFARCTION ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 23-year-old female zebra had a one day history of signs of colic. The animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy the jejunum was discolored dark purple and necrotic. An area of jejunum was entrapped in the mesentery with compromise of blood flow.

PULMONARY EDEMA HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This 6-year/2-month-old male bittern died. It was attacked by a royal starling on 1/9/2001. It was on antibiotics for several days. It was seen regurgitating on 1/13. At necropsy the lungs were dark. There was possibly aspiration of blood or chronic congestion. There were very abundant fat stores. The kidneys were pale.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION UREMIC PNEUMONITIS UREMIC GASTRITIS INANITION. This 18-year-old female sloth was under treatment for renal disease. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the left kidney was dark firm and showed white scarring in the renal pelvis. The right kidney was enlarged and contained a dilated ureter containing several renal calculi. Renal parenchyma was markedly atrophied due to hydronephrosis. Firm nodules were present in the right lung. A mass of firm tissue was identified between the spleen and stomach suspected to represent a chronic abscess.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE RENAL AND HEPATIC CYSTS. This 7-year-old female chicken was found dead in the morning with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed fair body condition and good postmortem condition slight discoloration of the liver and a soft dark red mass to 3 cm. in greatest dimension located near the left kidney.

ANAPHYLACTIC SHOCK LUETOMA. This 8-year/5-month-old female llama seizured and died three hours after vaccination. During examination this llama became extremely stressed and began to salivate excessively and cough intermittently. The lungs auscultated normally at examination and 30 min. after vaccination. The llama settled down and stopped salivating and coughing. At necropsy there was adequate subcutaneous and intra-abdominal fat. There was frothy hemorrhagic fluid in the lumen of the trachea. There was no food material in the lumen of the trachea. The lungs were diffusely wet and heavy. There was exudative hemorrhagic foam on cut surface of the lungs. There was hemorrhagic fluid in the pleural space.

EUTHANASIA MULTICENTRIC BRONCHOALVEOLAR ADENOMA CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This male greater than 3-year-old opossum was humanely euthanized due to paraparesis. At necropsy the opossum had poor body muscling but substantial fat deposits. The skin on the tail was dry and mildly ulcerated on the left lateral side. The pulmonary parenchyma was mottled collapsed and congested. The caudal edges of the caudal lung lobes had yellow 5-8 mm. in diameter foci that were solid on cut section. The gastrointestinal tract contained substantial gastric and intestinal contents. There was a 5 mm. in diameter white nodule in the mucosa of the caudal body of the stomach. The liver had a 10x15 mm. in diameter hepatic cyst on the right lateral lobe. The gall bladder was full of bile. The renal parenchyma had a granular subcapsular appearance. The spleen contained a 1 cm. in diameter yellow caseous nodule. The costochondral junctions were mottled and poorly mineralized. The scapula appeared essentially hollow on cut section and poorly mineralized. Antemortem radiographs showed an area of lumbar vertebral spondylosis. The stifle hock and elbow joints seemed to lack mineralization or were eburnated (polished red/pink appearance). Sections of costochondral junction were frozen for future use if needed.

EUTHANASIA CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM DISEASE. This 5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of unsteady gait and occasionally dragging its hind legs especially the left rear leg. The animal had been on prednisolone which seemed to help for a while although the disease progressed and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed weight loss pale hepatic lobes enlarged gallbladder filled with liquid approximately 2 ml. of blood in the thorax (possible euthanasia artifact) pale edges to the pulmonary lobes and no other remarkable findings.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 5-year-old male rabbit had an 18 hour history of inappetence followed by weakness and poorly responsive behavior. The animal became laterally recumbent and died. Prior to death the animal was noted to be overconditioned with a packed cell volume of 24% and blood smears that contained large numbers of very degenerative cells. Necropsy revealed multiple hemorrhages in the lungs approximately 4 ml. of fluid in the thoracic cavity extensive fat reserves a white multilobular firm to hard mass with central cystic cavities filled with clear fluid along the margin of one lobe of liver and a second but similar smaller mass was in an adjacent lobe. The stomach had food but the small intestine and rectum were empty.
adult. Weight: 212.6 g.  Euthanaised. Open.

EUTHANIZED FOR CHRONIC ARTHRITIS PURULENT SIALOADENITIS. This 21-year-old female giraffe was euthanized on June 25 2012 for acute lameness related to severe ringbone of the left forelimb that was no longer responsive to pain medications. Gross necropsy revealed dark brown fluid in the uterus degenerative changes of the cartilage of the joints mild inflammation of the intestinal tract a chronic jaw abscess that appeared to be originating from the salivary gland pus in the salivary gland skin thickening on the caudal elbow and crusting dermatitis over the caudal dorsum.

BACTERIAL/YOLK COELOMITIS. This 2.5-year-old basilisk was found dead on display with no signs of illness prior to death. Necropsy revealed fibrous adhesions throughout the coelomic cavity hemorrhagic lungs and intestines pale spleen and possibly some yolk-like material in the coelom.
adult. Weight: 445 g.  Hepatitis and congestive heart failure.

SUPPURATIVE MENINGOENCELHALITIS HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA EUTHANASIA LISTERIOSIS. This 5-year-old prairie dog presented with marked lethargy and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed obesity a 5 cm. growth on the ventral surface of the liver within the parenchyma and rising above the surface capsule consolidation of the right lung and dark vasculature on the meninges of the brain.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA RENAL METASTASIS ABDOMINAL HEMORRHAGE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 11-year-old female capybara was found dead. At necropsy the liver was discolored friable and contained masses which extend to the omentum body wall and diaphragm. Hemorrhage was noted within the abdomen originating from the liver.

TRAUMA TRACHEAL HEMORRHAGE TRACHEITIS AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATITIS. This 33-year-old male flamingo was examined for a firm raised area of granulation tissue on the carpus. The animal was found dead. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted in the pectoral muscle. Cervical vertebrae C5-6 were dislocated. The trachea was transected.

CAPTURE MYOPATHY MYONECROSIS MYOGLOBINURIA SHOCK. This 15-year-old female oryx was immobilized for an in zoo transfer. The animal was found down three days following the immobilization and was treated with supportive care but was found dead two days later. At necropsy the right lung lobe was congested and hemorrhagic. Clear brown urine was present in the urinary bladder. A five-month-old fetus was present in the uterus.

EUTHANASIA PERITONITIS ENTERITIS GASTRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VACUOLAR DEGENERATION. This 4-year-old male ferret had a history of anorexia weight loss and lethargy. The animal presented acutely with bile peritonitis. Laparotomy revealed enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes and severe peritonitis. Lymph node cytology was consistent with lymphoma and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the anterior mediastinum was expanded by pale pink to tan soft tissue. The abdomen contained 10 ml. of flocculent yellow/tan fluid. The jejunum had a 4 cm. length of thickened wall consisting of firm yellow/white tissue. A pinpoint perforation was identified within the jejunum. The spleen contained a 1 mm. in diameter raised firm white nodule.

HEPATIC PARASITE TRACT WITH HEMATOMA FORMATION AND HEMOCOELOM. This 5.5-year-old female motmot was found down in the water and appeared to have aspirated a large amount of water. Necropsy revealed a fractured liver but no external evidence of trauma.

EUTHANSIA LYMPHOSARCOMA ADRENAL CARCINOMA. This approximately 15.5-year-old neutered male addax was humanely euthanized. It had a history of progressive weakness and thinning of body condition. It stayed from herdmates and was frequently observed lying down. Physical exam revealed a thin condition with severe muscle atrophy. The abdomen appeared mildly distended. Auscultation revealed a 4 out of 5 mitral valve murmur that could be felt through the chest. At necropsy both horns were broken off from previous fights. The mucous membranes were pale. Teeth had several sharp points. The gastrointestinal lymph nodes appeared enlarged. There was diffuse muscle atrophy. The left ventricular wall appeared slightly enlarged. The mediastinum was full of straw colored fluid. The thoracic cavity was full of straw colored fluid. There was a large white nodular mass extending from the diaphragm caudally along the aorta. The mass seemed to follow the path of the abdominal aorta and was impinging on the aorta. It had completely occluded the renal artery on the left side. The caudal portion of the aorta was approximately 50% occluded by compression from the mass. There was no evidence of intravascular invasion by the mass. Some areas of atelectasis were noted in the right lung. The liver appeared small fibrotic and had small white nodules. The left kidney appeared totally encapsulated by the mass and the left renal artery was completely occluded from compression by the mass. The renal capsule is very thickened and irregular. The left kidney was completely necrotic.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDER. This greater than 14-year-old boa developed an abnormal growth and body swelling that had previously been diagnosed as a spindle cell tumor. The mass had resolved but then recurred two months ago. The animal was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed a firm coelom 15 cm. cranial to the subcutaneous mass. An intracoelomic mass occupied the entire coelom and encased all of the coelomic organs from the level of the heart to the liver. The mass was firm and white. Abundant intracoelomic fat stores were noted. A few 2 cm. in diameter white firm masses were in the parenchyma and on the surface of the liver. The gallbladder was large and distended and a 2 cm. mass was in the parenchyma of one kidney.

MYELOLIPOMA IN SPINAL CANAL. EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male Thomson’s gazelle was noted to be sitting upright but alert but struggling to stand. Physical exam and radiographs revealed no apparent spinal or skeletal abnormalities. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Gross necropsy revealed a 1 x 0.5 cm. raised mottled tan and purple mass within the spinal canal at T8. The spinal cord in this region was grossly normal. No other lesions were noted.

EUTHANASIA LUMPY JAW INANITION THRUSH RENAL CALCULI. This 9-year-old female wallaby was humanely euthanized. It had chronic lumpy jaw syndrome and complications. It presented for evaluation of acute weight loss lethargy and anorexia. It was placed on intensive therapy with IV fluids antibiotics and anti-inflammatories. There was short-term improvement with multiple relapses. Her condition continued to deteriorate. At necropsy the wallaby was in poor nutritional condition with no adipose stores and generalized muscle atrophy. There was a large amount of food in the digestive tract. There was a mass present in the intermandibular space. The mass was filled with a thick green purulent exudate. The bone of the rostral mandible was infected with multiple small pieces of bone present. The lungs were mottled purple/red. The heart was enlarged and flaccid. The left ventricle appeared dilated. Aortic valves were thickened. The surface of the aorta had vertical lines. The surface of the distal esophagus was covered with a pseudomembrane. Sections of sacculated stomach were covered with a pseudomembrane. There were ulcers present on the surface of the distal stomach. The liver appeared grossly enlarged and there were three small firm white masses present on the surface. There were multiple small white masses 2-3 mm. in diameter in the mesentery. There was a small yellow cystic mass attached to the mesentery. The right kidney was approximately 3x larger than the left. The right renal pelvis appeared dilated. The right ureter was 2-3x larger in diameter than the left. There was an area of the distal right ureter that was constricted and appeared fibrotic. The left kidney was small and pale with some areas that appeared to be infarcted. The left renal pelvis was dilated and there were yellow/green uroliths (approximately 5 mm. in diameter) present. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were enlarged and black/red. The mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. The inguinal lymph nodes were enlarged and there was one with a small calcified center. The thyroids were enlarged and cystic. The adrenals were enlarged and had prominent medullary areas. Cultures of intermandibular abscess were performed. The urolith was submitted for analysis.

CHRONIC CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE PITUITARY ADENOMA TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female Hill wallaroo had a less than 24 hour history of labored breathing that did not respond to supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. It is from a group in which toxoplasmosis has been diagnosed. Necropsy revealed pulmonary edema multiple foci of discoloration in the hepatic lobes firm kidneys with reduced cortex and irregular corticomedullary junction pinpoint ulcerations in the pylorus inactive ovaries a tan mass in the lateral pelvic canal attached to the distal reproductive tract by two linear soft tissue structures that are patent to the reproductive tract and to the mass which is torsed along the lateral linear soft tissue structure and four rotations are present. The torsed tissue incorporated the mesentery and vessels; mesentery and soft tissue associated with the torsion was dark purple.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS HYDRONEPHROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 7.5-year-old male domestic rabbit had a history of chronic bilateral inner ear infection and renal disease and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a subjectively enlarged heart renal asymmetry with the right twice as large as the left and slightly lumpy with tan discoloration of the capsule. The liver was shrunken. Subcutaneous edema was noted. Caseous material was in both tympanic bullae.

UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA SUPPUREATIVE ENDOMETRITIS. This 2-year-old female hedgehog had a history of anorexia and hematuria. The animal was found dead one day following anesthesia for examination. At necropsy a 3 cm. mass was present in the uterine body.

BACTERIAL GASTRITIS INANITION. This 4-year-old male rattlesnake had a history of regurgitation and tested positive for Cryptosporidium sp. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the kidneys were pale.
NA

PODODERMATITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS PUSTULAR RUMENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female addra gazelle developed a necrotizing interdigital wound on the right front foot supportive care was administered and despite intensive treatment the wound progressed to involve P1-P2 joints of both toes with subluxation and septic arthritis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed gravid uterus at approximately one-half to two-thirds gestation. The right foot from just above the fetlock distally is swollen with loss of support structure between the toes. The medial collateral ligaments of P1-P2 joints of both toes are disrupted and toes easily subluxate at the joint. Yellowish purulent exudate is expressed from both P1 and P2 joints of the right front foot. Small stores of cavitary fat were observed. The lungs were congested and had froth in the airways. Frothy rumen ingesta was noted. The liver was friable and moderately congested. A 2 kg. normal midterm fetus was in the right uterine horn.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE GASTRIC EROSION CUTANEOUS PAPILLARY CYSTADENOMAS. This approximately 26-year-old female California sea lion has a history of mammary gland cystadenoma and mammary gland lobular hyperplasia (G03-0651). Over time additional masses have developed on both flanks. The sea lion also has had an abnormal gait in the hind end since July 2009 described as “a little stiff”. Over the last two weeks the sea lion developed marked weight loss with decreased appetite and decreased willingness to participate in trained behaviors. A three day history of lethargy and anorexia followed the animal became dehydrated and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy yellow purulent liquid was noted when the skin was incised on the ventral abdomen. The aortic base appeared to be dilated and the brachiocephalic trunk also appeared subjectively enlarged. Multiple miliary masses were present in all areas of the lung. All of the skin masses had a similar appearance with yellow purulent fluid in cystic cavities. The adrenal glands appeared subjectively enlarged.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY PROVENTRICULITIS YEAST DERMATITIS. This 5-year-old female rainbow lorikeet presented with coelomic distention associated with ascites and blood work revealed anemia heterophilia hypoalbuminemia hypoglobulinemia hypocholesterolemia and elevated CPK. Due to high prevalence of hepatopathy in this flock end stage hepatic disease was suspected. The bird died following exploratory laparotomy (just prior to euthanasia). Necropsy revealed ascites and intracoelomic adhesions (hepatic biopsy is 2004). Mucosal folds of the distal esophagus and proximal proventricular region appeared thickened and the liver was small lumpy pale brown and firm on cut surface. Parathyroid gland was hypertrophied. Lungs were congested.

GRANULOMATOUS NECROTIZING OSTEOARTHRITIS WITH DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE AND ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male rattlesnake has a history of chronic fusion of the spine with difficulty moving and shedding. The snake was identified coiled on its back and could not right itself and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Aside from the spinal lesions no gross abnormalities were noted.

EUTHANASIA COLONIC IMPACTION CHRONIC COLITIS. This 13-year-old male frog had prior histories of colonic impactions. These had been treated with surgical removal of the impaction. Following the most recent surgery and six months prior to death no feces have been passed. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the colon was markedly distended and adhered to the ventral body wall.

CHROMOMYCOSIS PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS WITH CESTODES RENAL GRANULOMAS HERMAPHRODITE. This 9-year-old marine toad died. Necropsy revealed fair postmortem condition thin body condition and dehydrated body condition. No gross lesions were noted.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL GLOSSITIS RUMINAL ULCER STEATITIS. This 7-year-old female gazelle was humanely euthanized. It had been immobilized for examination for lethargy flank swelling and reduced appetite. During examination of the oral cavity a large 5 x 8 cm. area of dorsal tongue was affected by a caseous white malodorous lesion. At necropsy there was a 3 cm. diameter ulcer within the wall of the rumen. It appeared to have perforated. There were fibrinous adhesions to the omentum. There was a thickened area of the tracheal wall. The gastrointestinal tract was empty. There was hay within the rumen omasum abomasum and reticulum. There was mild hydrometra.

SUPPURATIVE MYOCARDITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE. This 50-year-old female gorilla developed acute weight loss dry skin and poor haircoat approximately three months earlier despite excellent appetite and behavior. The cause could not be determined. The animal was anemic and supportive care was administered. In the last 2-3 days the condition rapidly declined with poor appetite slow mobility and the gorilla was found dead in its nest box in the morning. Necropsy revealed dry flaky skin coarse haircoat thin body condition muscle atrophy absence of left eye (previous enucleation) clotted blood in the oral cavity absence of several upper and lower incisors and worn remaining teeth. A mild clear yellow pericardial effusion was noted. The apex of the pericardium was adhered to the diaphragm. Marked serous atrophy was noted around the heart. In the abdomen there were 200 ml. of clear yellow fluid associated with marked serous atrophy of fat and numerous adhesions of the viscera to the abdominal wall. A markedly firm thickened area of the abdominal wall in the midline at the umbilicus was 5 cm. in greatest dimension and associated with surgical mesh from a previous abdominal hernia repair. The hepatic parenchyma was slightly firm on cut surface but normal color and architecture. The uterine wall was diffusely thickened. Both kidneys were slightly pitted and had a cobblestone appearance on the serosal surface. The left adrenal gland was thin and on cut surface the cortex was thin and black. The right adrenal gland was grossly normal.

INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA MYOSITIS EPICARDITIS. This female 3-year-old bat was found dead in enclosure. At necropsy there was alopecia. There was hepatomegaly and cardiomegaly. The bat had been recently moved to a new enclosure.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRTIONAL STATUS SEVERE COELOMITIS OF UNDETERMINED ETIOLOGY RENAL GOUT. This 5-year-old male common moorhen was found dead on the ground in its exhibit. There was an electrical box with exposed wires in the enclosure and a poison bait box just outside the exhibit. At necropsy there was bilateral pododermatitis. The coelom was distended with brown-tinged flocculent fluid that had fibrin. The heart was subjectively enlarged. The lungs were congested. The serosa of the intestines was reddened with engorged vessels. A large fluid-filled cyst occupied approximately half of the left hepatic lobe.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE/TRAUMA HEPATIC MICROGRANULOMAS IRON STORAGE. This 4-year-old male lory was observed flying in the aviary 15-20 minutes prior to death and acting strange. The bird died en route to the hospital. Necropsy revealed a small dark liver and small tan spleen.

COLONIC ABSCESS HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC PANCREATIC FIBROSIS AND ACUTE PANCREATITIS. This 9-year-old female rock hyrax delivered an apparently healthy infant on 4/19. The animal was eating well until 4/22 when it became laterally recumbent and died. Necropsy revealed small yellow nodules in the mesentery enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes adrenal and spleen enlarged liver with rounded edges petechiae on the uterus right horn enlargement sanguineous exudate in both horns and the body pale kidneys hemorrhagic duodenal mucosa hemorrhage in the cecal mucosa thickened distal colon.

DIABETES MELLITUS EMPHYSEMATOUS GASTRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA GONGYLONEMIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 28.5-year-old female lemur has a one year history of progressive weight loss but is otherwise bright alert and ambulating well. The animal also had a history of diabetes mellitus. The animal developed a cutaneous callused and excoriated at the base of the tail and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 4 cm. spherical mass on one lobe of the liver and the mass was cavitated on cut surface. Kidneys were mottled and pitted and apparent firm fat infiltrated the pancreas.

MUCOID ENTEROPATHY WITH PERFORATING ULCER. This approximately 6-month-old male rabbit died spontaneously three days after having been moved to another exhibit for the winter. Necropsy revealed severe cecal impaction with fecal material colon full of mucus and perforation of the bowel at the ileocecal-cecal junction. The pyloric region of the stomach appeared thickened and the liver was congested. The stomach and the ileocecal region are submitted.

GRANULOMATOSIS. This 8-month-old lorikeet has a history of progressive neurological disease and currently was being treated with prednisolone. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition.

ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION RENAL INCLUSIONS DIC EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male hedgehog had a history of weight loss associated with a lesion in the maxilla. Hind limb paresis was also noted.

PROBABLE CARDIAC DISEASE ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 20-year-old male North American river otter had a five year history of spinal arthritis and suspected allergic dermatitis. Supportive care was administered that included Adequan meloxicam and cyclosporine. It had a two day history of increased lethargy straining to urinate or defecate with normal appetite. It developed severe ventral edema on day #2. It was anesthetized for exam and the urinary bladder was extremely distended but with no evidence of crystalluria. During anesthesia cardiac arrest occurred and the animal could not be revived. Necropsy revealed good body condition severe subcutaneous edema moderate light yellow peritoneal fluid severe distention of the urinary bladder mottled liver moderately distended right ventricular wall few 1-2 mm. flat white lesions in the lungs edematous lungs thin brown fluid in the trachea and multiple cracks and abrasions on the plantar surfaces of all feet.
SHOCK MYOCARDIAL STEATOSIS OBESITY. This 2-year-old neutered male rabbit was found dead. At necropsy large deposits of fat were present in the coelomic cavity and epicardium. The lungs were mottled.

PULMONARY SHOCK STRESS CEPHALIC VASCULAR MINERALIZATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 11-year-old female rainbow lorikeet had a history of chronic hepatopathy (G10-2427) and neurologic signs. The bird had been on a high vitamin A diet from 2003-2008 and the hepatopathy is believed to have a dietary component. In recent months this bird exhibited seizures and worsening central nervous system signs that responded to lactulose therapy. The bird was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed cloacal distention poor feather condition and a mottled liver.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE BACTERIAL CHOLANGITIS MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old female ringtail lemur had been moving slowly and was being picked on by new females in the exhibit. With hand feeding the animal gained weight. It was found recumbent and moribund with hypoglycemia and elevated blood urea nitrogen and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

ENCEPHALOMYELOPATHY. This 12-year-old male African lion has a 1.5 week history of ataxia that responded to high dose steroids but then recurred when the drug was tapered. Radiographs of the cervical spine were unremarkable. Necropsy revealed good body condition and some cystic structures in the liver. The spleen was enlarged with rounded borders.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old four-toed hedgehog presented for ataxia. A sibling presented with the same clinical signs and the sibling was euthanized.
