That animal was diagnosed with wobbly hedgehog syndrome. The animal of this report had been monitored since January and was euthanized due to progression of signs and declining quality of life. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting and decreased body condition absence of most of the dentition due to previous periodontal disease hyperkeratosis on the pinnae and no other grossly visible lesions.

CASEOUS LYMPHADENITIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 2-year-old male goat was recently treated for caseous lymphadenitis. The abscessed areas had scabbed over. The animal had been sedated for elective vasectomy and died while anesthetized. Necropsy revealed green-tinged fluid and hay in the oral cavity a small scab on the right cranial lateral neck and multiple small abscesses in the mandibular lymph nodes and omental lymph nodes. Frothy fluid was in the trachea to the level of the carina and a small amount of yellow-tinged fluid was within the main stem bronchi. Multiple adhesions from the lungs to the thoracic walls were noted. The left lung was hemorrhagic and atelectasis was in the right cranial and middle pulmonary lobes. The pericardial sac had 6-8 ml. of red-tinged fluid. Brownish-red fluid was in the proximal gastrointestinal tract and the mucosa was reddened. Petechiae were on the mucosa of the urinary bladder at the apex and in the neck. A large amount of intra-abdominal fat was noted.

TRAUMA LEFT-SIDED CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE. This 22-year-old male Rodriguez flying fox had a minor abrasion on its left thumb that appeared to be healing well but was found dead two weeks later. At necropsy the distal phalanges had arthritic changes multiple pinpoint holes were in the patagium there was a fractured dislocation of the left thumb the lungs are congested the teeth were very worn few pinpoint yellow nodules were on the surface of the liver and kidneys were subjectively pale.

CLOSTIRDIAL ENTERITIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS URATE NEPHROSIS. This greater than 1-year-old female lory died. It was found down with labored respirations to the point of almost agonal. Subcutaneous fluids were administered. At necropsy there were areas of hyperemia along the intestinal tract. There were very liquid gastrointestinal contents. There was a small amount of pasty material at the vent.

LYMPHOBLASTIC LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 1-year-old male rat had progressive posterior paresis and paralysis. The animal died under anesthesia. At necropsy a large quantity of hemorrhagic fluid was present in the abdomen and thorax. Masses were present in the hilus of the liver cranial thorax and spleen. Masses with associated hemorrhage were identified adjacent to the intestine and within the mesentery.

YOLK COELOMITIS. This 9-year-old female chicken had a history of weight loss and was depressed and lethargic. Examination revealed cyanotic wattles clear fluid in the oral cavity and thin body condition. White blood cell count was markedly elevated as were uric acid glucose and phosphorus. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was later found dead. Gross necropsy revealed yolk peritonitis with numerous adhesions and large friable kidneys.

SHOCK SEPTICEMIA POST SURGICAL COMPLICATIONS. This 6-year/10-month-old neutered male wallaby went into cardiac arrest postoperatively and was unsuccessfully resuscitated. The keepers reported seeing some mucus in the left eye on July 3rd. On July 4th there was exophthalmos of the left eye and scleral injection. Enucleation surgery of the left eye was performed on July 5th. Prior to the surgery there was mild exophthalmos of the right eye. The wallaby remained stable throughout the surgery but went into cardiac arrest postoperatively. At necropsy there was a 2 x 1.5 cm. bruise on the ventral midline of the abdomen. There is hemorrhage between the skin and the skull bilaterally. There is a bruise on the left ventral body wall that is 5 cm. in diameter. There is hemorrhage within the muscles of the rear limbs. The tissues around the left eye appeared swollen. The right eye was exophthalmic and the sclera was injected. There was hemorrhage behind the eye. The trachea was full of frothy bloody fluid. There were petechial hemorrhages on the epicardium. The right ventricle was flabby and possibly dilated. The tricuspid valve appeared thickened at the edge. The lungs were bilaterally dark red. On section a frothy bloody fluid oozed from bronchi. There were petechia and ecchymoses on the serosa. and mucosal surfaces of the stomach. There are petechia and ecchymoses on the serosal and mucosal surfaces of the small and large intestine.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT. This 15-year-old female corn snake had a several month history of lethargy and inappetence and a small abscess on two scales was treated and did not return. The snake’s white blood cell count was elevated and it was on antibiotics. The snake was found dead. Necropsy revealed decreased muscle condition erosion and desiccation of a scale in the right midbody multiple 1.5 cm. tan masses in the liver urate accumulations in the kidneys subcapsular hemorrhage and necrosis in the spleen and no other abnormalities.

PULMONARY AND LYMPH NODE ABSCESSES DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS PERIDONTAL DISEASE NEPHROLITHIASIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 34-year-old female reticulated giraffe had a history of multiple chronic medical problems and was found down in the moat struggling. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple abrasions over the dorsal pelvis and multiple abrasions and scrapes along the body. The pleural surface of the lungs was irregular and roughened and multiple discolored areas ranging from gray to white were present extending into the parenchyma. Multiple cavitations were noted on the dorsal aspects of both lung lobes and these were filled with green purulent to caseous exudate and some of these cavitations were surrounded by firm connective tissue. Multiple raised plaques were present on the surface of the aorta. All teeth were moderately worn down with deep gingival pockets that extend to bone around the left third maxillary and left third mandibular premolars. A deep pocket of bone loss was present around the tooth roots of the first maxillary molar tooth. The tooth was loose and attached to the bone only at the rostral border. Some areas of mucosal irritation and possible ulceration were noted in the abomasum and some adult Trichuris were noted in the cecum. The liver was grossly enlarged with rounded edges. Multiple old infarcts were in the kidneys and multiple stones ranging from 5-6 mm. in diameter were present in the kidneys primarily within the renal calices. A fine layer of crystalline material was on the surface of the urinary bladder. The spleen was grossly enlarged. The tracheobronchial lymph nodes at the tracheal bifurcation were large firm and black and the prescapular lymph was enlarged. Signs of bruising and myopathy were in the large muscle bellies of the down legs. All joints showed signs of moderate to severe arthritis ranging from mild osteophytes to complete articular cartilage erosion.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA METASTATIC FOCUS TO LUNG PANCREATIC ADENOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 19-year-old female ring-tailed lemur had a history of a hepatic mass and was found dead. Necropsy revealed a hepatic mass and several small masses in the lung.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA LYMPHADENITIS GASTRIC EROSION RENAL COCCIDIOSIS. This 2-year/7-month-old neutered male kangaroo was found dead in stall. It was admitted for treatment of a severe laceration of the left wrist. The wound was cleaned and repaired two days prior to death. The animal was bright alert responsive and was moving well. It was not bothered by the sutures and began taking oral antibiotics the day prior to death. At necropsy the wound was minimally swollen with a small amount of mucopurulent discharge. The left cranial ventral lung lobe was dark purple and heavy. There was a sharp line of demarcation between normal and affected lung. There were scattered 2-3 mm. masses in the right cranial ventral lung lobe. There was a 10 cm. ulcer in the distal stomach just before the pylorus. A 30 cm. length of small intestine was very dark and there was a mild twist at the root of the mesentery that did not appear tied enough to compromise blood supply.

EMACIATION EUTHANASIA (HIND LIMB ATAXIA). This 6-year-old male hedgehog developed ascending paralysis of the hind legs. The condition did not respond to supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thickened and enlarged seminal vesicles.
OOPHORITIS INANITION. This 12-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant lesions were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA ENDOMETIRTIS BRONCHIECTASIS CHRONIC PNEUMONIA TRACHEITIS RHINITIS MYCOPLASMOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE). This 1-year-old female rat was euthanized due to a coelomic mass and vaginal bleeding. At necropsy a large white mass was present at the base of the uterine horns. The liver and kidneys were pale. Lungs contained nodules in the right middle lobes. The right tympanic bulla was filled with caseous purulent material.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA TRAUMATIC TRACHEITIS ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS. This 7-year-old male rabbit had a history of upper respiratory problems after undergoing anesthesia for a foot abscess. The rabbit began acting lethargic and had increased abdominal effort in its breathing pattern. Radiographs revealed an interstitial or alveolar pattern and narrowing of the trachea. The rabbit’s condition deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed patchy alopecia over the front limbs calcified aorta especially in the aortic curve two small fluid-filled cysts attached to the proximal large intestine multiple pale foci in the right cranial pulmonary lobe that oozed fluid on cut surface an irregularity in the trachea 3 cm. proximal to the bifurcation with an associated artificial bifurcation and puncture of the mucosa on the left artificial bifurcation. The renal pelvises were mildly dilated.

RUMENITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 14-year-old female sheep had a history of lethargy and inappetence. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was pale gray. Hemorrhages were noted in the GI tract.

SHOCK POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS GRANULOMATOUS PARABRONCHITIS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS. This 19-year-old female parrot was found dead in its nest box with no prior signs of illness. Both thick-billed parrots were found dead but ground birds in the same exhibit were normal. No husbandry or environmental changes have been made except that this bird was fed a small amount of avocado prior to death. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. area of hemorrhage on the dorsal caudal aspect of the skull not associated with hemorrhage on the inner surface of the skull or in the brain. A small amount of ingesta including corn and chopped greens were in the crop and proventriculus. The caudal intestine and colon had dark purple coloration to the serosa and intestinal contents and feces were normal color with no evidence of hemorrhage or blood.

CLOSTRIDIOSIS PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS SARCOCYSTOSIS (SKELETAL MUSCLE) GAS EMBOLI EMACIATION. This greater than 4-year-old female lorikeet presented one week earlier with acute lethargy and weight loss received supportive care for enterocolitis based on previous flock culture results and histopathology results appeared to stabilize but was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed lean body condition extensive hemorrhage in the left and right caudal pulmonary lobes moderate pulmonary edema pale liver empty proventriculus and ventriculus pale duodenum dilated and mottled jejunum dark stools normal colon pale spleen pale thyroid glands slightly larger left thyroid gland compared to the right thyroid gland pale kidneys focal hemorrhage within the dorsal skull bone a moderate amount of clear serous fluid and fibrinous strands in the coelomic cavity and moderate edema in all tissues.

SALMONELLOSIS EMACIATION. This 8-year-old male captive bred lorikeet was found dead. The bird had a history of problems gripping with its right foot and held its foot at a several lateral angle. Necropsy revealed enlarged atria and a hemorrhagic lesion at the apex of the heart. The liver was mildly enlarged and mottled with few tan lesions.

MUCOCUTANEOUS CARCINOMA BILIARY TUMOR NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female leopard had a one-year history of poor appetite and lethargy had been diagnosed with chronic renal disease and hypertension one year earlier and was being treated for the hypertension. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large verrucous hepatic mass and firm remaining hepatic parenchyma with a prominent surface reticular pattern. The left thyroid was cystic and a portion of the thyroid and parathyroid were white. The left anal gland was enlarged and firm. The hypophysis appeared enlarged and was easily displaced from its fossa.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS SPLENITIS TUBULAR NEPHRITIS MYCOCARDIAL STEATOSIS. This 9-year-old chicken was lethargic and emaciated with increased respiratory effort. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the crop contained a large mass of straw and feathers. The ventricles were distended and thin walled. The liver contained numerous firm nodules ranging from 2-15 mm. in diameter.

SUSPECT INTESTINAL TORSION HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This 10-year-old male tortoise was found dead. At necropsy the liver was pale and friable. The coelom was full of serosanguineous fluid with digesta. The pylorus to the cecum was black thin walled. There was rupture of the proximal cecum.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENTERITIS NEPHRITIS. This 8-year-old female kangaroo developed an ocular lesion and pitting edema of the face. The animal had bradycardia and was hypothermic. Radiographically the heart was enlarged with thinning of the ventricular free walls. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy the proximal intestine was hemorrhagic.
EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 27-year-old female owl presented nonresponsive with weight loss and anemia. The animal was humanely euthanized.

PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA NEPHROSCLEROSIS REPEAT LEG FRACTURES EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male cheetah has a history of degenerative arthritis involving a foreleg. Arthrodesis of the carpus was performed but the animal subsequently fractured the radius and ulna proximal to the plate. This fracture was repaired and the cheetah subsequently fractured the humerus of the same leg. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild cataract formation a granular patch on the pleural surface of the dorsocaudal lung field where it meets the diaphragm and no other gross lesions.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE TRACHEAL HEMORRHAGE ACINAR CELL ADENOMA STRESS. This 18-year-old male tree boa was found dead. Necropsy revealed ventral erythema and erythema in the oral and cloacal mucosa. The splenopancreas was firm and mottled and muscle atrophy was noted. This animal had a history of panhypoproteinemia periods of inappetence and anemia. The animal also had a history of stomatitis.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE RENAL GOUT. This 11-year-old male African pygmy falcon was lethargic. It is not stated if it was found dead or euthanized. At necropsy multiple deposits were seen throughout the coelomic cavity and the air sacs were thickened.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA HEPATITIS. This 5-year/5-month-old male capybara was humanely euthanized. It was attacked by a female tapir and sustained extensive injuries. At necropsy there was severe multiple traumatic wounds to much of the dorsum and sides. There were numerous closed and open surface and subcutaneous wounds. There is multifocal hemorrhage within the intercostal musculature as well as the thoracic and abdominal walls. There were deep muscle tears over the right side extending full thickness. There was bilateral pulmonary congestion.
EUTHANASIA TRAUMA SHOCK. This 16-year-old female fruit bat suffered comminuted fractures of the tibia and wounds over the wings. The animal was humanely euthanized.

CHRONIC RENAL AND CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female golden lion tamarin has a history of chronic renal disease with associated anemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE BILIARY CYSTS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female cottontop tamarin had been diagnosed with lymphoma and continued to accumulate thoracic and abdominal fluid despite treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed yellow tinged fluid in the abdomen blood tinged fluid in the thoracic cavity white discolored liver with vesicles over the edges and throughout the body of all lobes similar structures around the liver near the pancreas and in the mesentery pale white gallbladder enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes firm kidneys enlarged nodular adrenal glands areas of discolored fat a white infiltrate in the spleen roundish heart firm lungs that floated in formalin and a few cysts in the ovaries.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS PYOMETRA MYOCARDITIS EOSINOPHILIC GRANULOMA RENAL LEIOMYOMA. This 16.5-year-old female Sumatran tiger had a one week history of inappetence and lethargy and urinalysis revealed blood and degenerative neutrophils. Supportive care was administered and compliance was good but small drops of blood were noted from the vulva. Follow-up exam revealed pyometra and ovariohysterectomy was performed. The tiger arrested during closure of the surgical excision and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed normal amounts of adipose tissue hemorrhage on the mucosal surface of the stomach hemorrhage on the mucosal surfaces of the jejunum and colon melena in the lumen of the intestine abscess in the cranial pole of the left kidney thickened urinary bladder with cloudy urine and no other abnormalities.

BACTERIAL AND AMOEBIC COLITIS SEPTICEMIA HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This approximately 1-year-old tortoise of undetermined gender died. At necropsy there was a small amount of pinkish fluid within the coelomic cavity. All organs appeared pale especially the lungs liver and heart. The stomach and small intestine were devoid of ingesta/digesta. The large intestine had a portion which was hemorrhagic and contained large amounts of sand.

GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION CHOLELITHIASIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 25-year-old female American flamingo was found down on its nest and had no other recent medical history. Necropsy revealed a large proliferative and semiulcerated mass to 2 cm. in diameter involving the left metatarsal pad which did not appear to involve the joint. White pinpoint material was noted over the pericardium and myocardium. Ovaries were large and active although some appeared atretic. The kidneys had urate stasis.

MILD HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 9.5-year-old Matamata has a several month history of anorexia following a move to a temporary holding facility during exhibit renovation. The other turtle in the same holding tank is eating well. The turtle is being tube fed to maintain its weight. Blood work revealed no abnormalities and no endoparasites have been detected. Supportive care was administered with no response. Endoscopic biopsies of the kidney and liver are submitted.
HEPATITIS PLEURITIS. This 4-year-old toad was found bloated and was dead the following day. No significant lesions were identified at necropsy.

CHRONIC CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE MINERALIZATION PULMONARY ABSCESSES BILATERAL THYROID TUMORS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE. This 17-year-old female domestic sheep developed a history of weight loss and stiff gait in all limbs and was being treated for degenerative joint disease. The sheep also had a high pitch diastolic ejection murmur and age-related dental wear. The sheep also had a purulent bilateral nasal discharge also seen in several goats at the facility. The sheep died unexpectedly and necropsy revealed green/brown discoloration of the frontal lobes of the cerebrum and some hepatic abscesses granulomas in the lung pyometra and arthritis.

HEPATIC FIBROSIS BILIARY CYSTS CHRONIC PNEUMONIA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 7-year-old male rabbit had a history of weight loss and urine scald. A mass was palpated in the abdomen. The animal was humanely euthanized. Cystic structures were present throughout the liver.

CHRONIC CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE PULMONARY CRYPTOCOCCOSIS. This 14-year-old male cheetah had a history of congestive heart failure of approximately one year’s duration and also had lymphoplasmacytic gastritis diagnosed in January 2014. A penmate died in January due to chylothorax associated with myocardial fibrosis. The cat of this report had intermittent vomiting inappetence and lethargy between January and March. Blood work revealed markedly elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine and no fluid in the chest or abdomen. Supportive care was administered which improved the azotemia for a few days but the animal’s condition continued to deteriorate and it died while sedated for treatment and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed opaque white fluid filling the thoracic cavity in the pleural space. Cytology suggested the presence of chyle. Lungs were edematous. The left ventricle was mildly thickened. Moderate erythema was noted around the fundus. Hepatic margins were rounded and white streaks were present in the parenchyma. Four focal nodules were present on the spleen. Marked erythema was in the proximal duodenum. Kidneys were bilaterally shrunken and irregular with notable loss of cortical mass and calcification of the cortices.

PROLIFERATIVE ESOPHAGITIS TRACHEITIS AND PNEUMONIA. This 28-year-old male ground boa presented with excess mucous secretion in the oral cavity approximately one month earlier. The snake was housed with two male offspring that also had similar clinical signs that included weakness lethargy and excessive oral mucus. The animals had been maintained in the same husbandry conditions for the past eight years with no major changes. The snakes had tested negative for paramyxovirus and inclusion body disease. Blood work was unremarkable and culture grew E. coli. Several antibiotics have been administered to this snake over the last month with no clinical improvement. Due to the lack of clinical response and concurrent illness of the two other snakes euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes regarding this snake. Necropsy identified moderate amounts of thick cream-colored mucus throughout the esophagus and stomach and congested vasculature on the serosal surface of the small intestine with thickened and edematous layers. The large intestine contained bile and a small amount of fecal and urate material. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

SEPSIS COLITIS. This 31-year-old Matamata had a two day history of illness that included gurgling respiratory sounds. Supportive care was administered but the animal died two days after treatment was initiated. Necropsy revealed wet heavy lungs and liquid and foam in the airways.

PROLAPSED UTERUS. This 12-year-old female tamarin died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed abundant fat stores pale liver serosal white spots that did not extend into the hepatic parenchyma inverted prolapsed uterus with endometrial tissue exposed outside the vagina and increased vessel diameter in the right cortex (site?).

EPIMYOCARDITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS SUSPECT SEPTICEMIA. This 6-year-old male meerkat arrived in quarantine about one month prior to death. It had a history of mandibular abscess at the previous zoo but appeared to have resolved. The animal was being introduced to other meerkats with contact through mesh. The meerkat spent a lot of time pacing. It was found dead. At necropsy the liver appeared enlarged although the margins were still sharp. The heart appeared enlarged. There was a poorly demarcated area of the left ventricle that appeared pale. There were vegetative valvular lesions within the left atrioventricular valve.

EUTHANASIA RENAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION BILIARY ADENOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 7-year-old male domestic rabbit was hospitalized due to increased respiratory effort. Treatment was initiated; however the animal failed to improve. Blood work revealed acute renal failure and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. The upper incisors were worn to the gumline. The aorta was calcified. Multiple white cystic masses were present throughout the liver.

SEVERE INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS AND GLOMERULONEPHRITIS POSSIBLE LEPTOSPIROSIS PERITONITIS. This 12-year-old female mustache tamarin was found dead in its enclosure. It had a recent history of abdominal distention dyspnea hepatomegaly and jaundice. It had a recent tail amputation surgery and liver and skin biopsy in conjunction with an ovariohysterectomy. A adenocarcinoma (G99-0097) was noted histologically. Recent clinical pathologic data included hypoproteinemia uremia increased creatinine and monocytosis. At necropsy the thoracic cavity contained approximately 5 ml. of pink clear fluid. There were small yellow nodules on the atrioventricular valve. There was approximately 5 ml. of straw pink fluid within the abdominal cavity. There was no digesta present within the stomach. The descending colon was adhered to the urinary bladder and left abdominal wall. The liver was large congested firm and had rounded edges. The spleen was contracted. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. The urinary bladder was adhered to the descending colon and vagina. The kidneys had irregular small cysts in the cortex. The gall bladder was thickened and irregular with adhesions to the body wall.

SHOCK PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE ALVEOLAR HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 5.5-year-old female otter was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the right ventricle was dilated. Lungs were collapsed and contained frothy material.

BACTERIAL OOPHRITIS PULMONARY EDEMA AND HEMORRHAGE FATTY LIVER ACUTE ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This female approximately 6.5-year-old anole died during recovery from surgery. It underwent surgery to remove a malpositioned egg. It had a history of extremely elevated white blood cell count and lethargy. At necropsy there was a cricket wound on the dorsal aspect of the tail approximately 2 cm. from the tip. The stomach was full of food. There was an inspissated egg present in the right oviduct that measured 12 x 9 mm. The surgical site of the left oviduct appeared normal. The lungs were wet heavy and did not float in formalin.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS PYLORIC ABSCESS. This 21-year-old male colobus was found dead unexpectedly in the morning and had no history of illness. It had previously been diagnosed with a tricuspid regurgitation with right atrial and right ventricular enlargement in 2010 but no treatment was commenced. Necropsy revealed severely thickened right heart grossly normal heart valves and no other abnormalities.

EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female goat had a three month history of weight loss leukocytosis (eosinophilia) anemia hypoproteinemia hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia. Johne’s serology and culture were negative. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond well. Exploratory surgery was performed and no abnormalities were noted. The goat was euthanized during the surgical procedure for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild congestion in the left lung a large amount of foamy fluid in the trachea adequate internal fat stores and no gross abnormalities.

ASPERGILLOSIS MALARIA. This male 7-year/3-month-old tern died shortly after physical exam. This tern was tachypneic and dyspneic. At necropsy the coelomic cavity was filled with 1.5-2.0 ml. of unclotted bloody fluid. The spleen and liver were markedly enlarged. The pericardial sac was filled with 8+ ml. of yellow tinged serous fluid. The myocardium appeared pale. The lungs were dark red slightly mottled and mostly consolidated. The air sacs appeared cloudy.

INANITION RENAL GOUT VENTRICULAR IMPACTION. This 3-year/1-month-old female prairie chicken died. At necropsy the bird was emaciated. The crop was full of pellets. The ventriculus was impacted with fibrous grass material. There was aspiration pneumonia. There was cecal impaction. The pectoral muscle was edematous and hemorrhagic. There was ileus of the large bowel. The kidneys were dark and congested.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS TREMATODIASIS CAPILLARIASIS EMACIATION. This 17.5-year-old North American wood duck was hospitalized for supportive care. A large liver was suspected but the animal seemed to improve and was returned to the exhibit and found dead later that day. Necropsy revealed jelly-like material in the coelom enlarged liver with a cyst-like structure in the center and multiple white lesions throughout the remaining portions of the hepatic parenchyma also with a few cyst-like structures and opaque yellow/red structure resembling air sac on the right side of the coelom.

ANAPLASTIC MALIGNANCY NEPHROSCLEROSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 18.5-year-old male lemur had a recent history of labored breathing and lethargy but was difficult to capture. Eventually the animal was successfully transported to the hospital and upon arrival was dyspneic and had a large abdominal component to its breathing. Labored breathing persisted despite a rest period so medical intervention was initiated. The animal was anesthetized and examined. The lemur was obese with harsh cardiac sounds and arrested while anesthetized and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed consolidated lungs that filled the entire right side of the thorax obscuring the heart a pocket of hemorrhage and purulent material in the right lung congestion in the left lung hemorrhage in the abdominal cavity a focus of dark discoloration in the spleen otherwise pale splenic parenchyma smaller than expected pancreas that contained a firm nodule hemorrhage present along the perirenal areas and multiple cysts throughout the renal parenchyma.

SHOCK RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 1-year-old female cottontop tamarin is from a group that died shortly after arrival following a long road trip. Necropsy revealed minimal intra-abdominal fat minimal ingesta and feces in the lower gastrointestinal tract empty stomach congested lungs and a small amount of serohemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity.

1. Heart; lung; liver; skeletal muscle; proventriculus: Intravascular (intracellular) and intraendothelial protozoal organisms. 2. Aorta: Focal vacuolar degeneration and mineralization suggestive of an early atherosclerotic lesion. 3. Renal arteries; heart based arteries: Locally extensive mineralization 4. Testes: Tubular degeneration and interstitial fibrosis 5. Adrenal gland: Moderate to marked cortical hyperplasia 6. Esophagus: Focally extensive esophagitis. 7. Ventriculus: Severe; locally extensive; serosal to focally transmural; necrotizing ventriculitis. Comments: The numerous protozoal organisms noted in multiple organs are consistent with blood parasites. The genus and species of these organisms can not be determined from histopathologic examination. Possibilities include Plasmodium spp.; Haemoproteus spp.; and Leucocytozoon spp. The lesions noted in the gastrointestinal organs; specifically the ventriculus; are consistent with the reported gross finding of a foreign body (wire) perforation at the junction of the proventriculus and ventriculus. The exact cause of death could not be determined from histopathologic examination of these tissues; however; it is possible that the large number of blood parasites in this bird caused severe debilitation

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOCARDIOSIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 23-year/7-month-old female lemur was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the lemur was in thin body condition. There were several pea-sized nodules found throughout the lung lobes. The trachea seemed very firm. The spleen had a mottled capsule. The liver contained a tumor that was 479 gm. A small portion of nontumorous liver was identified and was extremely dark on cut section. Most of the liver was consumed by the tumor. It was highly nodular and most areas appeared necrotic. The stomach was extremely thickened. There was emphysema of the caudal 25% of the stomach to the level of the pylorus. The secretory portion of the stomach was slightly hemorrhagic. The jejunum appeared mildly hemorrhagic.

SEPSIS. This 3.5-year-old female lemur had a brief history of depression and died. Necropsy revealed multiple 2 mm. foci scattered throughout the hepatic parenchyma. Approximately 3 cc. of fluid was in the left thoracic cavity.  The spleen had multiple light pink foci. The lungs were hemorrhagic. Culture was not obtained.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female sugar glider had a history of substantial weight loss and a mass involving the caudal ventral region. Cytologic examination revealed suppurative inflammation but necrotic mammary tumor was suspected. Supportive care was administered with no changes in the size of the mass. The mass subsequently ruptured and a large lesion developed lateral to the pouch. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy findings included infiltration of the entire pouch extending nearly the complete width of the abdomen and on cut surface multiple small pockets of purulent material were present within the mass.

SHOCK. This approximately 3-year-old snake was found dead unexpectedly. It had eaten normally two days earlier. Necropsy revealed a fecal impaction in the lower large intestine yellow/brown discoloration of the liver and hyperemic small intestines.
SHOCK PULMONARY EDEMA INANITION. This 8-year-old female bat was found dead in the exhibit pool. At necropsy the lungs were mottled dark red.

The results will be released in a forthcoming final report as soon as results are available. Ian N. Moore; DVM Multiple organs: Lymphosarcoma with multifocal metastatic foci Cecum: Intestinal nematodiasis Lymphosarcoma Comments: The neoplastic cells infiltrates were histologically consistent with lymphosarcoma which is a malignant round cell neoplasm that commonly metastasizes to multiple organs; as in this case; and can account for this animal's death. Lymphosarcoma in avian species (specifically chickens) has often been associated with vial infections; including Herpes virus (Marek's disease) and Retroviruses (Avian leukosis). Mareks' disease has been associated with lymphosarcoma and a transient unilateral limb paralysis; which in combination with the provided history; may indicate and underlying viral infection and may warrant further evaluation of other birds/flock on the premises. The submission of other affected (live) individuals for necropsy and testing may aid in identification of an etiologic agent. Close continued monitoring of other birds is recommended. The pending laboratory tests will be released in a forthcoming addendum report as soon as results are available. Ian N. INANITION COLITIS RETICULITIS. This 2-year-old male gerenuk has a history of chronic diarrhea and weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy severe muscle atrophy was present. Marked serous atrophy of fat was also noted. Mesenteric lymph nodes were markedly enlarged.

STOMATITIS OOPHORITIS. This 6-year-old female lizard had a history of conjunctivitis and respiratory difficulty. Treatment had been provided with minimal response. The animal later died. At necropsy the animal was thin.

ASPIRATED WATER (POSSIBLY DROWNED) MILD MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 20-year-old male ibis died. No prior signs of illness were noted. Necropsy revealed an elongated and conical shaped heart a moderate amount of adipose stores at the cranial aspect of the heart rounded hepatic margins on the cranial aspect of the liver and no other remarkable findings.

ABDOMINAL ADHESIONS ACUTE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS PULMONARY THROMBOSIS. This greater than 7-year-old female sheep had a history of hypoglycemia with elevated blood urea nitrogen. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed several liters of straw colored slightly viscous fluid in the abdominal cavity and a 10 cm. in diameter solid mass in the midabdomen.

Autolysis in all organs is at least mild; and autolysis in sections of intestine is moderate. The abomasum is characterized by multifocal regions of severe mucosal hemorrhage and congestion; often in association with necrosis and mucosal ulceration. The mucosa and submucosa is infiltrated by numerous scattered neutrophils; lymphocytes as well as multifocal aggregates of cocci and large; rod-shaped bacteria. Mucosal surfaces are lined by a moderate quantity of luminal necrotic debris; red blood cells; and additional bacterial aggregates mixed with fibrous plant material. The rumen; small intestine; and colon contain similarly dilated vessels within the muscularis and serosa; occasional small regions of hemorrhage; and mild to moderate infiltration by lymphocytes and plasma cells. Additional multifocal hemorrhage and congestion is identified within numerous tissues. The cerebrum is moderately congested and contains multifocal regions of perivascular hemorrhage. Within the lung; individual lobules comprising 20% of examined pulmonary sections are diffusely hemorrhagic with infiltration by moderate numbers of neutrophils. Remaining pulmonary parenchyma and tracheal mucosa is characterized by marked congestion and edema. There is moderate panlobular congestion within the liver; and periportal parenchyma is dissected by small numbers of lymphocytes and plasma cells. Centrilobular hepatocytes frequently demonstrate cellular swelling and indistinct intracytoplasmic vacuoles (glycogen accumulation); with a small quantity of cell lysis and admixed cellular debris. There is severe congestion diffusely within the spleen and multifocally within the renal cortex and medu Abomasum: Severe multifocal necrohemorrhagic abomasitis with intralesional bacteria Rumen; intestine; cerebrum; lung; liver; spleen; kidney; adrenal; bone marrow: Widespread moderate to severe congestion and hemorrhage Liver: Centrilobular hepatocellular degeneration and necrosis Skeletal muscle: Multifocal Sarcocystis tissue cysts Clostridial abomasitis with multisystemic congestion and hemorrhage (see comments) Comments:Histopathologic findings; supported by ancillary test results; are suggestive of Clostridium perfringens type A infection. CHRONIC BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ACUTE MESENTERIC TORSION. This 9-year-old male/castrated kangaroo was found dead unexpectedly in the evening. Necropsy revealed good body condition with no external lesions. The abdomen was distended and the small intestines were hemorrhagic and distended with areas of necrosis. A counterclockwise intestinal torsion was noted involving the proximal aspect of the small intestine.

INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA WITH CARCINOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old female rat presented with lethargy and bloated appearance and was limp. Muscle wasting was identified. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed ascites muscle wasting white firm foci in the left lung multilobular and firm lymphatic channels in the mesentery extending along the intestinal tract and connected to the spleen and liver.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female black-tailed prairie dog was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (G13-3141). No evidence of metastasis was noted at the time. The animal had lost 20% of its body weight in three weeks. Abnormal teeth were trimmed and the diet was changed to small pellets. The prairie dog became more lethargic and inappetent and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition worn cheek teeth sharp points on the buccal aspects of the mandibular first premolars cataracts in both eyes dark lungs that contained red foamy fluid on cut surface enlarged right side of the heart rounded hepatic margins a yellow/tan focus in the parenchyma that extends through all hepatic lobes distended gallbladder a small amount of fluid in the stomach multiple firm boluses of food in the duodenum irregularly surfaced kidneys with parenchymal pallor a cyst in the cortex of the right kidney and a few 1 mm. blood filled cystic structures in the right uterine horn.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 6-year-old female red kangaroo had an approximately five day history of dyspnea one day history of lethargy and inappetence and radiographic evidence of pneumonia. A mob mate died five days prior to this one and histopathology confirmed toxoplasmosis. Necropsy of this case revealed a moderate amount of straw colored fluid in the pericardial sac moderate amount of pleural fluid and areas of pallor in the lungs. The intestines were distended.

EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION INTESTINAL LYMPHOSARCOMA HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS BILIARY CYST. This 33-year-old female lemur was euthanized due to poor condition and spondylosis. At necropsy fusion of the spine and marked muscle atrophy were noted. A moderate quantity of straw colored fluid was present in the pleural cavity. Cataracts were present bilaterally. A large abscess was present in the ascending colon which contained ingesta and gravel. Adhesions were present to adjacent internal organs.

BACTERIAL RHINITIS OSTEOMYELITIS OTITIS MYELIN VACUOLIZATION. This 5-year-old male hedgehog had been treated for chronic otitis externa. Multidrug resistant Proteus sp. was cultured. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a raised pigmented lesion was present near the tip of the right ear. The right ear canal was moderately stenotic and erythematous and contained purulent material. A small amount of serosanguineous fluid was present in the abdomen. Miliary white foci were present in the liver and lung.
See elephant paper

METRITIS. This 5-year/6-month-old female fruit bat had no premonitory clinical signs. At necropsy there was some localized bruising on the leading edge of the right wing. The carcass was covered in ants. Autolysis was present. There was minimal adipose tissue. There was bloody fluid in the abdomen. The molars were very worn. The liver was slightly pale. The right horn of the uterus was enlarged and contained a mass of reddish friable tissue that was not connected to the uterus. The wall of the right uterine horn seemed thickened.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 37-year-old male Gila monster presented with weakness pallor and openmouthed breathing and had previously been eating and active. Examination revealed dehydration moribund condition and agonal respirations. A soft mass was palpable in the caudal coelom. The animal was judged to have 30% weight loss for the age and gender. Euthanasia was prepared but the animal died before the full dose could be administered. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dehydration enlarged and cystic testes clear fluid within the testicular cyst prominent vas deferens and small left kidney that was tan mottled and firm on cut surface. The right kidney was incorporated into a dark red friable mass 6 cm. in greatest dimension that contained multiple pinpoint white/yellow granular foci. The liver was friable on cut surface with pale foci scattered over the capsular surface. The pancreas was firm and hard on cut surface.

EMACIATION. This approximately 4-year-old toad was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed fair to poor postmortem condition no external lesions female gonad empty stomach and small intestine and autolyzed viscera.

SEPSIS HEAD TRAUMA. This approximately 3-year-old male lorikeet died spontaneously and was refrigerated 36 hours prior to necropsy. The bird fell from its perch after possibly fighting with a cagemate. It presented with decreased mental alertness and favoring the right leg. It did not respond to supportive therapy.

COLITIS CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. This 18-year/7-month-old female tamarin was found dead in its exhibit. It had no clinical signs prior to death. At necropsy it was in good body condition. There was bilaterally symmetrical alopecia on the right and left lateral forehead and dorsal aspect of the distal tail. The spleen appeared congested. The left ventricular free wall measured 2.5 mm. and the right measured 1 mm. The interventricular septum measured 3 mm. Several teeth were missing. There was moderate staining and mild tartar. One liver lobe was difficult to cut and slightly pale.

GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS BACTEREMIA BACTERIAL COELOMITIS INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 3-year-old snake was treated with ivermectin and developed abnormal behavior two days later. The animal was flaccid and lethargic. Treatment was initiated with some improvement; however the animal was later found dead. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL RHINITIS SUSPECT SEPTICEMIA. This 5-year/2-month-old female wallaby was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. This wallaby presented the day prior to death with lethargy and snotty nose. It was started on antibiotics. It was found in shock the next morning and despite supportive care continued to deteriorate. At necropsy the wallaby was obese. There was bloody mucopurulent discharge in both nostrils. The right nasal turbinates were very hyperemic and friable. The glottis was very edematous and there appeared to be purulent material in a small pocket near the choanal opening. The trachea was hyperemic. The lungs had several dark areas that bled on cut surface but were in general within normal limits. There were several 0.5-1 cm. ulcers in the gastric mucosa. The intestines were mildly distended with gas. The adrenal glands were large. Deep culture of the right nostril grew moderate Escherichia coli. A CBC at presentation showed marked left shift with bacteria in monocytes.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE SHOCK GASTRIC EROSION RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This approximately 6-year-old female rabbit initially presented with hypothermia and lethargy received supportive care and appeared to improved was released from the hospital but supportive care was continued and the rabbit appeared to recover. It was subsequently found dead unexpected. Necropsy revealed a large amount of clear light yellow fluid in the abdominal and thoracic cavities friable and mottled liver and no other abnormalities.

LARGE BOWEL RUPTURE MYOPATHY INANITION. This 5-year-old male meerkat was found dead in its enclosure. It had been treated for sinus infection and also gastric distention with constipation. At necropsy there was peritonitis and rupture of the large bowel. There was severe gastric dilatation with food. The small intestine only contained gas. Feces were soft and there was no foreign body within the gastrointestinal tract. There has been a history of toxoplasmosis within the colony.

EUTHANASIA CHOLECYSTITIS PORTAL HEPATITIS PANCREATITIS MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY CARDIOMYOPATHY WEST NILE VIRUS. This 23-year/5-month-old tamarin was humanely euthanized. It had a previous history of a stroke but recovered. It always retained some neurologic sequelae that required it to be maintained in a special off exhibit holding area. Recently the tamarin presented for left rear lameness. A healed femoral fracture and decreased bone density were identified on radiographs. Approximately one week later the animal presented for acute lameness of the left front leg and radiographs identified closed fractures of the left humerus and tibia. The tamarin was icteric. At necropsy the tamarin was thin. There were no subcutaneous or abdominal fat stores noted. The serosal and mucosal surfaces all appeared icteric. There was a small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity. The gall bladder appeared as a mass of pale brown to yellow tissue along the caudal surface of the liver. There were palpable multiple nodules which appeared almost cystic that were adhered to the root of the mesentery. The hepatic bile duct contained small soft friable concretions that crumbled easily. The liver appeared slightly enlarged dark red to brown and had sharp borders. It bulged slightly on cut surface. The parenchyma was firm on excision. Both kidneys appeared icteric. There were cysts noted in both kidneys. The stomach and intestines were empty. There were small round firm pale white to yellow nodules present along the serosal surface of the proximal duodenum. Both lobes of the thyroid gland appeared enlarged.

AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL GOUT BACTERIAL VENTRICULITIS BACTERIAL CHOLECYSTITIS GLOSSITIS BUMBLEFOOT. This 21-year-old female flamingo died en route to hospital. The keepers found the flamingo down. It had a history of decreased alertness weakness and segregation from the flock earlier in the month. Treatment was performed. Radiographs revealed granular osteopetrosis of the ulnas and tibiotarsi. At necropsy the flamingo was in good nutritional condition with adequate muscling and ample fat stores. There were several active pododermatitic lesions on both feet. There were multifocal pinpoint white foci on several of the thoracic and abdominal air sacs. There were several areas of petechiae on the epicardial surface. There was diffuse melanosis of all serosal surfaces. There were several ulcerative plaques noted on the tongue. The mid to caudal esophagus had multifocal pinpoint white foci. There was bile stained ingesta from the distal esophagus to the intestine. The colonic mucosa appeared mildly hyperemic. There was moderate to severe hepatomegaly. The kidneys were pale and markedly enlarged. There were several irregularly shaped discolored ovarian follicles one of which was very dark and hemorrhagic. Culture of the follicle was performed. There was mild to moderate cortical thickening of the nonpneumatic long bones.

EUTHANASIA MASTITIS ENTEROCOLITIS CAPRINE ARTHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS. This approximately 6-year-old female goat was humanely euthanized. It was suspected of having caprine arthritis encephalitis. It had a history of decreased alertness decreased activity hyperthermia weight loss mastitis and localized swelling of the carpus. Treatment was initiated. The udders were very hard and had white chunks that were coming from the teat. At necropsy the mammary glands were very firm. One area oozed milk and purulent material in the gland. There was serous fluid in the pericardial sac. The pancreas was pink to red. There were some adhesions of the lungs to the pleura. Abdominal lymph nodes were enlarged. The bladder wall was thickened. There were small protuberances on the edge of the spleen.

EMACIATION. This approximately 13-year-old male Nigerian dwarf goat was found dead. At necropsy the epicardium mesentery and kidneys were surrounded by gelatinous material. The liver had two white foci.

ACUTE BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA AND AMYLOIDOSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS UNDIFFERENTIATED SARCOMA FROM HOCK (BIOPSY DIAGNOSIS). This 30-year-old male swan was found dead in its pool. It have been on “retirement” for several months because of chronic lameness related to tendon/synovial neoplasia at the left hock joint. Necropsy revealed good body condition but with little fat reserve and advanced autolysis. Both central pads of each pes were covered with large chronic bumbles. The left tarsal joint was thicker compared to the right but grossly the structures around each hock joint were comparable (antemortem biopsies revealed sarcoma of the joint/tendon structures). The right lung was pale pink and contained large amounts of embolic fluid. The left ventricular wall of the heart had a focus of pallor that appeared limited to the epicardium. The pulmonary artery contained several foci of thickened intimal plaques at the split of the main branches as did the aorta at the first major branch. No ingesta was detected in the gastrointestinal tract and a large amount of bile stained sand was in the ventriculus. A diphtheritic membrane was on the mucosal surface of the jejunum and duodenal loop. Refractile crystals were detected near a cystic duct suggestive of cholelithiasis. Kidneys contained multiple white nodules resembling gout tophi.

ENTERITIS HEPATITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male tree kangaroo has a history of weight loss and intermittent diarrhea. Serum chemistry suggested hepatic lipidosis. The animal failed to respond to supportive care and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large ulcer was identified at the base of the tail. The animal was emaciated. The foregut contained a large quantity of watery sour smelling ingesta. The liver was enlarged with accentuation of the reticular pattern.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE RENAL CYSTS CHRONIC RUMENITIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL) EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female Speke’s gazelle had a recent onset of lameness with pain inappetence and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cavernous cyst-like lesions in the kidneys swelling around the accessory carpal bone of the left front foot severe degenerative joint disease detected radiographically in the fetlocks and some cysts in the right ovary.

HYPERKERATOTIC FOLLICULITIS (POSSIBLE DYSPLASIA) FLAGELLATE COLITIS NONSUPPURATIVE ENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female banded rail was normal for the first couple of years of her life had a history of a leg fracture which healed with treatment and no other problems. Approximately one year ago her plumage began to thin and she developed abnormal stunted feathers and plugged follicles. A biopsy at that time revealed bacterial dermatitis but the bird did not respond to antibiotic therapy. Various other forms of supportive care were also administered but with no improvement. No change was noted with a molt and additional biopsies revealed bacterial dermatitis (G11-1977) and circovirus testing was negative. The bird failed to respond to antibiotic therapy or other supportive care and became completely bald. A course of steroid therapy was administered and a few stunted feathers emerged from the head and body but the majority of the follicles remain plugged and the legs and body were hyperkeratotic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized plugging of follicles or empty follicles swelling of the wings due to obstipated primary and secondary follicles hyperkeratosis of the legs and feet bumblefoot on her right foot dermatitis involving the eyelids and ears adequate fat stores a single greenish-yellow granulomatous plaque in the periphery of the left lung inactive ovary and symmetrical adrenals.

SAND IMPACTION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 5-year-old male wallaby was found down. The animal was treated with fluids and antibiotics but later died. At necropsy no fat stores were noted. A moderate amount of clear yellow fluid was present in the abdominal cavity. Pale streaks were noted on the ventricular wall of the heart. The stomach contained a large quantity of sand and an 8 x 4 cm. phytobezoar. A heavy growth of Campylobacter sp. was isolated from a perimortem fecal sample.

DROWNING TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 4-year-old male wallaby was found dead in pond in exhibit. It had been previously healthy. It had a history of low platelets. At necropsy the liver was small. The intestines were hyperemic. There was bone loss in the jaw. There were two possible wounds found in the pericardium and pulmonary artery.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS RENAL GOUT ENTERITIS. This 13-year-old male rhea developed severe left rear limb lameness approximately one week prior to euthanasia. The animal responded to initial therapy but suffered trauma from a cagemate Patagonian hare which required suturing of the right hind limb including the medial metatarsal vein. The animal could stand with assistance but the condition rapidly deteriorated to recumbency and inability to hold the head up. The animal was humanely euthanized.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS RENAL TUBULAR SYNCYTIA RETROVIRUS. This approximately 9-year-old female colobus monkey had a one day history of thin body condition and hypothermia. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not recover from anesthesia. Necropsy revealed congestion and mottling of the lungs food in the alimentary tract dark red jejunum enlarged and mottled adrenal glands and friable spleen.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS TAIL INFRACT EUTHANASIA. This approximately 20-year-old gecko presented for chronic weight loss and inappetence. Supportive care was administered with minimal improvement. Approximately 3 cm. of the distal tail became necrotic and two days later the lizard was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. In addition to the necrotic tail necropsy revealed thin body condition a 1 cm. focus of black discoloration on the dorsum of the tail and a distinct black demarcation in the muscle of the tail in which no bone was noted distal to the demarcation.

CYSTITIS ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA FATTY LIVER THYROID CHOLESTEATOMA. This captive bred 18-year-old female snow leopard died. She had a recent history of partial anorexia and lethargy. She had an ulcerated lesion over the lateral aspect of the right metatarsus. Radiographs revealed degenerative joint disease of the left coxofemoral joint and loss of the intervertebral space with osteophyte formation at L3-L4. There was whole body muscle atrophy. Treatment was initiated. Cystitis was diagnosed on clinical pathology and urinalysis. At necropsy there was an ulcerated wound on the skin area from the left hind hock. There were a few small hard nodules palpated in the lungs that ranged in size from pinpoint to 2 mm. in diameter. There were areas of emphysema in the caudal lung lobes. The right ventricle had a ratio close to 1:5 of the right to left ventricles. The left ventricular wall appeared thickened. There were fibrin tags on the surface of the liver. There was a white capsular line visible on the edges of the lobes. The liver appeared fatty. There were fibrous adhesions of the jejunum to the dorsal peritoneum. The right kidney had a few dark flakes of material in the renal pelvis. The bladder was filled with purulent material. The wall was thickened. The surface of the spleen had white raised irregular substance on the capsule. There was no articular cartilage within the left hip. The head of the femur was almost absent and the neck was greatly thickened. There was a fragment of cartilage in the joint capsule. The right lobe of the thyroid gland was irregular in appearance and had a 2 mm. diameter cyst at the cranial end. The left lobe had two cysts present.

ENTERITIS WITH NEMATODES GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA WITH PARASITE EGGS. This 7-year-old male monitor lizard had a rectal prolapse noted one day earlier. The animal was otherwise normal. The tissue appeared necrotic but was lubricated and replaced in the coelom. The animal was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed generous adipose stores and good body condition. The rectum was prolapsed 2 cm. and was dry and discolored yellow. Both kidneys were enlarged and extended 2 cm. beyond the pelvic brim into the coelom. No other abnormalities were noted.

ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS PERITONITIS ANESTHETIC DEATH VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY. This 12-year-old female red panda had a history of anorexia. Radiographs reveal gas and food in the stomach and loss of abdominal detail. The animal presented sternally recumbent and in shock. Abdominal exploratory revealed a large quantity of brown fluid in the abdomen with a perforation in the pylorus. Tissues were resected; however cardiac arrest ensued and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. The resected portion of the pylorus was thickened tan to black with pinpoint black to brown foci. At necropsy the distal GI tract contained black to green pasty contents which was positive for occult blood. The liver was copper colored and finely nodular with several small clear foci on the surface.

TRAUMATIC FACIAL CELLULITIS SEPSIS. This approximately 1-year-old female rat incurred severe facial trauma due to conspecific aggression and had been treated accordingly but was found dead. Necropsy revealed a 0.5 cm. facial defect on the left side and the tissue surrounding the defect smelled necrotic. The wound did not extend to the oral cavity.

TRAUMA PROVENTRICULAR ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATOPATHY. This 3-year-old male captive bred whistling tree duck was found dead. It was attacked by a marabou stork. There were severe contusions to the cranial half of the neck. The brain and skull were grossly unremarkable. The rest of the body at necropsy was grossly unremarkable.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE HYPERTENSION GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS. This 24-year-old female squirrel monkey had a history of degenerative joint disease involving the left coxofemoral joint and a one day history of weakness and thin body condition. The monkey subsequently died and necropsy revealed irregular contours to the renal surfaces two raised fluid-filled cysts in the left kidney multiple small raised fluid-filled cysts in the right ovary a large cervix and no other remarkable findings.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS CESTODIASIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS EMACIATION GERIATRIC. This 22-year-old python was submitted with no history. The snake died and necropsy identified a large area of dermatitis on the left dorsolateral aspect approximately 9 in. in length in the caudal third of the body. The skin in this area was dry and friable and a copious amount of subcutaneous hemorrhage was present. Three sutured incisions were present in areas of the skin from previous biopsies and these appear to be healing well. Slight asymmetry was noted in the mandibular musculature with the left side more prominent than the right. A serosanguineous pericardial effusion of approximately 20 ml. was noted. The atrioventricular valve was slightly thickened. The caudal vessels on the left side lateral to the vent were dilated. The dilated vessels were connected to a sac-like structure bilaterally and lateral to the vent. In this region in the subcutis was a large collection of presumed parasite larvae. Multiple firm nodules were present throughout the pulmonary parenchyma. An undigested rat was in the distal esophagus. Multiple small cystic structures were present throughout the liver. The gallbladder was large. The reproductive tract could not be identified due to severe inflammation in the caudal coelomic cavity. The kidneys were dark with a smooth serosal surface. Fine deposits were present over the coelomic membranes in this region. Firm granulomatous masses were attached to membranes in the caudal coelomic cavity and pale cream-colored filamentous structures were attached to the subcutaneous tissues or were floating free in the coelomic fluid. Approximately 60 ml. of ascites were noted.

BACTERIAL MYOCARDITIS BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS INANITION. This 7-year-old female duck died within 45 minutes after presentation. The duck was observed to be limping the evening prior to death but it was otherwise alert and active. It was found in the night enclosure in the morning cold nonresponsive and dyspneic. It was brought to VCC and placed in warm cage. The duck was given 1 mg. of dexamethasone IM 20 cc. LRS with 2.5% dextrose sub-q. The duck was extremely weak but was able to hold its head up. At necropsy the duck was in thin body condition. It had a prominent keel. There was fecal staining around the vent. There was gravel present in the ventriculus. There was a small amount of tan feed material in the proventriculus. There were scant feces present in the large intestine and coprodeum. The ovary was yellow and approximately 8 x 4 mm. The distal oviduct and uterus appeared thickened and contained small amount of caseous material.

INTRACOELOMIC ABSCESS WITH BACTERIA BRAIN ABSCESS. This 4-year-old female green junglefowl was being treated for weakness and labored breathing with lethargy and was also being treated for hookworms (Capillaria?). The bird died and necropsy revealed thickening of the abdominal and caudal thoracic air sacs dark red liver and tame necrotic ovum off of the left ovary near the junction of the proventriculus and ventriculus.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ABOMASITIS. This 17-year-old female gazelle was noted to be stiff and had acute swelling of the fetlocks. At examination there was crepitus of both carpi. Radiographically degenerative joint changes were noted in the stifles and severe spondylosis of the vertebral column was noted. The animal was humanely euthanized due to advanced age and severe degenerative joint disease. At necropsy the animal was in poor body condition. The rumen contained a 3 cm. in diameter tricholith. Marked degenerative joint changes were present in most joints and were most severe in the stifles and carpi.
BACTERIALPYELONEPHRITIS AND SEPTICEMIA UROLITHIASIS. This 2-year-old tree frog was not eating and had become thin. Necropsy revealed no gross lesions.

PULMONARY PENTASTOMIASIS GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS SEPSIS EMACIATION. This 4-year-old Matamata was a recent donation that was still in quarantine. It had severe ulcerative skin disease and was found dead. It had not eaten while in quarantine but had gained some weight attributed to an effusion in the coelom. Mixed gram-negative bacteria were cultured. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond. Necropsy revealed an effusion in the coelom reddened lungs and ulcers in the skin and shell.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 2.5-year-old male budgerigar was found on the ground weak and off balance by a visitor was examined and appeared to be alert and responsive but weak and ataxic. Respirations were rapid and the vent was pasty. Supportive care was administered but the bird was found later on tossing its head lifting its wings and unable to stand without rolling backwards. The bird subsequently died. Necropsy revealed good external condition and no gross visceral lesions.

HEAD TRAUMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 9-year-old female rainbow lorikeet was found dead. This bird is from a flock in which there is a history of hepatopathy presumably due to dietary hypervitaminosis A. This bird had been exposed to a high vitamin A diet for several years although the diet was changed in 2008. Necropsy revealed good body condition some bruising on the face around the beak and eyes and on the crown of the head mottled yellow small liver and no other abnormalities.

HEPATIC FIBROSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 9-year-old male lorikeet had a history of weight loss and was under treatment with metronidazole. The bird was found dead. At necropsy the bird was extremely thin. Bruising was present on the right side of the head.

EUTHANASIA GINGIVITIS ENTERITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 10-year-old male gazelle was humanely euthanized due to disseminated neoplasia. At necropsy chronic conjunctivitis with gingival recession was noted. Marked congestion and erythema were noted throughout the small intestine with accumulation of hemorrhagic material in the lumen.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE CLOACAL IMPACTION. This 17.5-year-old male Bali mynah was found on the floor of the forest bird trail in midday on its back with ants on its body. It was placed in an incubator but died within an hour just prior to treatment being administered. Necropsy revealed a swollen and crusted vent containing urates and feces. Remodeling of the intervertebral spaces of the lumbar spinal area was obtained. Fat stores were scant. A granuloma-like swelling was noted near the caudal slit of the glottis. The right subclavian branch of the aorta was dilated. The right thyroid was slightly larger than the left.

EUTHANASIA DERMATITIS OSTEOMYELITIS METABOLIC BONE DISEASE POSSIBLE RICKETTSIAL DISEASE AND POSSIBLE RENAL MYXOSPORIDIOSIS. This greater than 1-year-old female ornate horned frog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of a swollen left leg that had circular ulcerative lesions on the dorsal and ventral left tibia. The stifle joint was swollen. Radiographs showed fracture of the right tibia and left ulna. At necropsy there were ulcers on the right front leg and left rear leg. The liver was pale tan/yellow and mottled. All bones were very soft and cut easily with a scalpel. There were white granular masses adjacent to the spinal column. There was scoliosis of the spinal column.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE MYCOBACTERIOSIS ULCERATIVE PROVENTRICULITIS. This approximately 3-year-old male budgerigar was found dead. It had been moving slowly a few minutes before. The animal had been found on the ground with labored breathing that morning. Necropsy revealed fecal matter caked around the vent a moderately enlarged liver and no other gross abnormalities.

PROLIFERATIVE TRACHEITIS AND PNUMONIA. This approximately 10-year-old female diamond python has a history of being loosely coiled and did not appear to be well. The animal was treated for pneumonia but died. Necropsy revealed blood in the trachea lungs and air sacs enlarged heart ingesta in the stomach digesta in the intestines a small red mass in the right oviduct active ovaries and overall good body condition.

MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA DERMAL FIBROSARCOMA. This spayed female 15.5-year-old wolf had two masses excised during recent surgery. The mass on the left medial foreleg was proximal to the carpus. It was first noted 10 months ago. It has gradually enlarged. Approximately one week ago it ulcerated exposing a portion of its surface. The leg mass easily dissected away from the skin. The cut surface was white. It had both fibrous and fatty-like components to it. The mammary gland was excised (2nd gland in the right mammary chain). It was approximately 2.5 x 3.5 in. in size. It was multilobulated and when cut there were several cystic structures that exuded a dark red to brown serous fluid. There was a mass in the right axillary region that was aspirated but not excised. Two large well defined masses were noted on thoracic radiographs. The larger of the masses was noted three years ago when the animal was spayed.
BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS. This 7-year-old male falcon was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the lungs were hemorrhagic and the liver was mottled.

FRACTURED FEMUR SEPSIS FETAL DEATH EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2-year-old female pregnant gazelle incurred a flank laceration one week earlier associated with trauma from a conspecific male. Supportive care was administered but partial dehiscence occurred with associated subcutaneous emphysema and lameness on that side. While being anesthetized for treatment a femur was fractured repaired with a plate and pin but abnormal alignment and reluctance to stand was noted during an episode of dystocia. A nonviable fawn was delivered and fracture failure was confirmed radiographically. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an autolyzed fetus that was normally formed at late but not term third trimester. Marked pitting edema was in the right rear leg and a bloody discharge was in the vulva. Much bruising was noted in the leg and body wall. Herniated fat was in the cranial ventral left abdomen and fibrinous debris and dead space were present deep to the left flank laceration repair. The femoral pin had backed out 5 cm. and the locking plate was moderately bent with complete dislodgement of the femoral screws and fracture of the femoral neck. Red discoloration was along the ridges of the omasal folds and multiple foci of red discoloration were in the abomasum. The spleen was moderately enlarged. The adrenals were enlarged and the left adrenal had local hemorrhage.

TRAUMA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE BACTERIAL AIR SACCULITIS. This 5-year-old male rhea was found bleeding from a wound in the neck. The animal later died. Exsanguination and muscle necrosis were noted at necropsy. A large mass of black gritty material was present at the thoracic inlet.

GRANULOMATOUS DERMATITIS BACTERIAL ORCHITIS SHOCK. This 12-year-old male copperhead was found dead without premonitory signs. Blood was present on the enclosure walls. At necropsy the oral cavity had foci of hemorrhage. Kidneys were swollen and pale.
EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL OSTEOMYELITIS. This 10-year-old male rattlesnake was euthanized. The animal had a mass along the spine correlating with areas of spinal deformity and bony proliferation.

INANITION URATE STASIS. This 9-year-old female turtle was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a 5 x 5 x 1 cm. rock was present in the oral cavity covered with mucus. All internal organs were pale and edematous. Gelatinous yellow fluid was present in the coelomic cavity and 20 ml. of clear yellow fluid were present in the pericardial sac. Testes were identified at necropsy.

COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE MYOCARDITIS HEPATITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA PULMONARY EDEMA. This 7-year-oldl male lorikeet was found dead. At necropsy the pectoral muscles were pale tan to yellow. Blood was present in the abdomen. A large blood clot was present at the end of a 1 cm. in diameter mass adjacent to the ventriculus. The liver was pale yellow to tan. Severe hemorrhage and edema were noted in the lung.
See elephant paper

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ATHEROSCLEROSIS ISLET CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old female marmoset had a long history of a thyroid cyst. The animal went into acute cardiac failure 24 hours prior to death which did not respond to drainage and Lasix. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thoracic pericardial and abdominal blood tinged effusions cardiomegaly hepatomegaly and congested liver. The aorta appeared sclerotic the lungs were wet and the thyroid mass appeared to be a cyst.
CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This male approximately 5-year-old captive bred African hedgehog was found dead. At necropsy it appeared to be in poor nutritional condition.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male hedgehog presented in moribund condition with blood in its mouth. The animal was ataxic inappetent and depressed and had lost 80 gm. in two weeks. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dark purple heart (euthanasia) a blood clot in the lumen of the stomach that was adhered to the mucosa numerous small foci of black discoloration in the mucosa of the stomach dark black fluid in the lumen of the duodenum pale kidneys and some areas of black discoloration in the parenchyma of the spleen.

MACROHABDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old male budgerigar was being treated for weight loss and macrorhabdiosis. It was found on the floor of the holding facility and was unable to stand. Eyes were fixed and dilated. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed reduced pectoral muscle mass prominent keel darkly discolored terminal intestine and minimal food or feces throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

EMACIATION EUTHANASIA AMYLOID-LIKE MATERIAL OSTEOARTHRITIS. This approximately 20-year-old male timber rattlesnake presented for suspected musculoskeletal disease with loss of righting reflex and inappetence. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thickened gastric walls urates in the distal cloaca a large amount of thick green fluid in the gallbladder mottled kidneys with pinpoint light yellow areas consistent with urate tophi male gonad palpably thickened spinal foci and diffusely pale pink spleen.

DENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 3-year-old female Virginia opossum was euthanized for unspecified regions. At necropsy the animal was overweight. Multiple discrete firm white nodules were found in the parenchyma of all pulmonary lobes. A large mass was within the right hepatic lobe. The colon had mucosal white pinpoint plaques. The left adrenal gland was approximately three times larger than the right.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS BRONCHIECTASIS CHRONIC BRONCHOINTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA LEIOMYOSARCOMA (UNDETERMINED LOCATION)POLIONCEPHALOMALACIA. This 18-year-old female tiger has an eight month history of abnormal behavior with mild disorientation confusion with routine procedures and failure to recognize keepers. This condition progressed to dementia weight loss and failure to recognize food. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA STOMATITIS GINGIVITIS MALOCCLUSION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 9-year-old male bighorn was immobilized for hoof trimming. Diminished fat reserves were noted at this time. Hyperkeratosis was present adjacent to the hooves. The animal was humanely euthanized the following week. At necropsy severe dental malocclusion with loss of maxillary teeth and lower incisors was noted.

EXHIBIT ENTRAPMENT EMACIATION DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 16-year-old female motmot was found dead on its nest and had an orange plastic twine caught around the lower bill and stuck to the nest. Necropsy revealed that the twine entrapment was associated with fracture of 1.5 cm. of the rhinotheca. The bird was in good body condition with some dirty and caked feathers and a possible bruise on the right ventral abdomen. The left lung was mottled and congested. The intestines were dark. Kidneys were prominent and pale tan.
adult. Weight: 643 g.  Bumble foot/ euthanasia.

EUTHANASIA FEMORAL FRACTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 16-year-old female gazelle suffered a fracture of the distal half of the femur and femoral condyle. The animal was humanely euthanized. No other significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 21-year-old female squirrel monkey was anesthetized for a preshipment examination and died approximately 10 minutes after anesthetic recovery. At necropsy the heart was pale and the liver contained innumerable cysts throughout the tissue. The kidneys were pale and firm.
RENAL MINERALIZATION NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS. This 9-year-old female fruit bat was found dead. At necropsy swelling was noted in the lower lip.

CHRONIC HEPATIC DISEASE SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA. This 6-year-old female lorikeet presented with lethargy and weight loss and evaluation revealed no specific diagnosis. The bird was being treated empirically due to the history of liver disease in the lorikeet flock. The bird was doing well but then presented with severe seizures. Supportive care was administered but the bird was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed cachexia congestion in the skull and mild hepatomegaly.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS CAUSE OF DEATH UNDETERMINED. This 9-year-old female milksnake was taken on an outreach program that took place outdoors on an extremely hot and humid day. The snake became lethargic and was warm to touch and died en route to the hospital. There appeared to be a mark across the bridge of the nose and the head was tilted to the left.
