Trauma during the trip is suspected. Radiographs were unremarkable.

CONSPECIFIC AGGRESSION CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 4-year-old male Speke’s gazelle was found dead in its enclosure and had no prior signs of illness. Trauma from a conspecific is suspected. Necropsy revealed multiple contusions over the right and left flanks a puncture wound in the ventral abdomen some areas of extensive subcutaneous hemorrhage over the dorsum substantial intraperitoneal hemorrhage in the left lateral abdominal quadrant bruising on the serosal surface of the right and left ventricle congested left lung (down side) ingesta in the rumen congestion and bruising over the serosal surface of one portion of the rumen and also in the wall of the abomasum.

LYMPHOMA/LYMPHOCYTIC LEUKEMIA. This 4-year-old male degu was found in lateral recumbency with respiratory distress and had been clinically normal the previous day. Examination revealed dehydration gas in the intestines and the animal died shortly after recovering from anesthesia. Necropsy identified thin body condition partially collapsed lungs ingesta in the stomach white granular material in the gallbladder pink/bright red spleen large amount of gas distention in the small intestine and possibly some hemorrhage in the intestine with segmental plication. The cecum had a large amount of firm fecal material and little stool was in the colon. The kidneys were pale. Degenerative joint disease was noted in the stifles.

ENDOMETRITIS ATELECTASIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 9-year-old female chinchilla had a history of weight loss. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy engorged vessels were noted over the uterine horns. The uterus contained cloudy fluid. Lungs were mottled.

HEAD TRAUMA EOSINOPHILIC ENTEROCOLITIS. This 1-year-old male zebra was found down in its enclosure and died shortly thereafter. It had some skin abrasions on the head. Postmortem cervical radiographs showed abnormalities in the third vertebra. At necropsy the dorsal portion of the cerebellum was discolored purple/gray.

MAMMARY GLAND ABSCESS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA OMASAL ULCERS RUMINORETICULITIS. This 10-year-old female gazelle has had numerous offspring in succession and calved in early November. After a few weeks she stopped allowing the calf to nurse and developed a draining abscess in the mammary gland. Treatment compliance was poor and was administered by dart at irregular intervals until the drainage site appeared to heal. The animal was eating well and regained condition by early December but the animal’s condition again deteriorated and she was found dead in her holding pen. Necropsy revealed mild Haemonchus infection in the abomasum bilateral adrenal gland enlargement an abscess in the left mammary gland and chronic mastitis severe unilateral bronchopneumonia ulcerative omasitis and chronic ruminoreticulitis.

LYMPHOMA (ANGIOTROPIC) EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old ferret was diagnosed by fine needle aspirate cytology of a thoracic mass with multicentric lymphoma. The ferret presented with labored breathing exercise intolerance and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple enlarged lymph nodes especially sublumbar mediastinal hilar and sternal lymph nodes. The left adrenal gland was larger than the right. The lungs were mottled with multifocal pallor. A 2 cm. nodule was at the tail of the spleen.

PENMATE TRAUMA SEPSIS. This 2.5-year-old slender-tailed meerkat had a 24 hour history of hypothermia and lethargy three days after introduction to the group. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed abundant abdominal fat and multiple puncture or bite wounds over the rump.

INTUSSUSEPTION WITH BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 8-year-old male capybara presented with a one day history of anorexia lethargy and bloody discharge from the rectum. A firm mass was noted on the lateral aspect of P-2 digit #4 right front foot. The animal had a mast cell tumor removed two years earlier. The animal also had a history of intermittent soft stools for 1.5 years and flagellates were occasionally noted in fecal examination. The digital mass was debulked but the animal died during the anesthetic procedure. Necropsy revealed a red/purple jejunum and a small amount of clear red fluid in the abdominal cavity. A telescoping mass approximately 13.25 in. long was in the distal intestine.

ENTERIC MYCOBACTERIOSIS (PROBABY M. AVIUM OR M. PARATUBERCULOSIS). This greater than 10-year-old female chinchilla had a two month history of illness characterized by wasting with terminal neurological signs. The animal was euthanized for humane reasons.

EUTHANASIA CHOLECYSTITIS CHOLANGITIS PERITONITIS. This 7-year-old male tamarin had a large quantity of bile tinged fluid in the abdomen along with hypersegmented neutrophils. Surgery revealed a friable liver lobe. The animal was humanely euthanized.

EUTHANASIA RHINITIS SINUSITIS TRACHEITIS BRONCHITIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This approximately 2-year/3-month-old female rat was humanely euthanized. It had hyphema noted in the right eye in September 2003. It was treated unsuccessfully with topical steroids and systemic antibiotics. The rat developed slight buphthalmia in October 2003. Radiographs of the skull were unremarkable. The animal developed respiratory distress on January 4th but was unresponsive to supportive care. At necropsy the footpads on both hind limbs had small ulcerations on the heels. There was severe hyphema within the right eye and possible superficial corneal ulceration at the medial commissure. There was a mature cataract OS. There was a several millimeter pocket of eroded bone at the area of the most caudal maxillary molar on the right side of the oral cavity. The brain had a 1-2 mm. area of discolored tissue at the most cranial aspect of the cortex on the midline. The tissue overlying the nasal turbinates appeared hyphemic. The bone dorsal to the nasal turbinates seemed brittle and appeared thin on radiographs. The liver had several 1 mm. areas of hemorrhage.

FOCAL CEREBRAL MALACIA CEREBELLAR VACUOLATION SUSPECTED THIAMINE DEFICIENCY LEAD TOXICOSIS. This 3-year-old captive bred male black and white ruffed lemur presented with seizures in December 2010. The animal was being managed with phenobarbital. The animal was found down on March 31 2011 with a fractured maxilla and hard palate and was euthanized due to the poor prognosis. The brain was submitted whole in case of a pathologic lesion missed on MRI or at necropsy.

SHOCK STRESS. This 1-year-old female cottontop tamarin is one of several that died while in quarantine shortly after a long road trip. Necropsy revealed adequate abdominal fat minimal gastric contents minimal ingesta and feces congested lungs and a small amount of serohemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA INTERSTITIAL CELL TUMOR PANCREATITIS PERIOTONITIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 26-year 1-month-old male polar bear was humanely euthanized. It had developed acute lethargy and inappetence. It did not respond to any supportive care. At necropsy there was degenerative joint disease within the right hip joint. There was approximately 1 qt. of bloody cloudy fluid within the abdomen. An anterior mediastinal lymph node was enlarged. There was cloudy brown mucoid fluid coming out of the right naris. This fluid extended into the nasal cavity and the caudal portion of the nasal sinus. The tongue had a small 0.3 cm. diameter mass. The pancreas had an abscess-like mass. A mesenteric lymph node was enlarged. Throughout the liver there were variably sized masses. Some of the masses were white with a starburst pattern of fibrous tissue. Some of the other masses had a more tissue consistency with necrotic centers. About 60% of the liver was affected. One testicle had a mass within it that contained a necrotic center. Sections of heart lung spleen liver stomach small intestine large intestine kidney and urinary bladder were frozen for future use if needed.

TRAUMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS EMACIATION. This 17-year-old female Bali mynah was found dead. The male had been chasing this bird lately and she had been missing feathers around her neck. There was also some new feather loss on the head. Necropsy revealed good body condition blood in the mouth absence of the distal phallus of digit #3 on the left foot pale white spleen 1 cm. clear cyst in the caudal left coelom not associated with the ovary and hemorrhagic areas on the skull with no abnormalities in the brain.

Sections of a cervical mass were composed of sheets and nodules of large epithelial cells; with plentiful palely basophilic cytoplasm; moderate anisocytosis and anisokaryosis; 1 to 3 nucleoli; and a low mitotic index of 1-3 mitoses per high power field; consistent with a salivary carcinoma. Scattered throughout the mass were low numbers of salivary ducts. There were scattered areas of parenchymal necrosis; and these areas contained low to moderate numbers of neutrophils. Sections of brain; heart; lung; liver; kidney; spleen; adrenal; pancreas; stomach; small intestines; colon; and skeletal muscle were morphologically normal. Salivary gland: carcinoma with necrosis and secondary suppurative inflammation Salivary gland carcinoma Comments: Salivary gland tumors are relatively common in mice; more common in some transgenic strains. The fact that this tumor was outgrowing its blood supply led to areas of necrosis and secondary inflammation. However; the few mixed bacteria isolated supports this as secondary infection rather than a primary abscess as was initially suspected upon gross necropsy. No metastases were found in any other tissue examined. This completes all diagnostic testing for this case.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC CYSTITIS URINARY BLADDER MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS. This 11-year-old male meerkat had a recent history of difficulty walking and swelling of the abdomen. The animal was unable to urinate. Due to advanced age the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were firm and pale.

AUTOLYZED TISSUE. This 16-year-old male corn snake had a four month history of weight loss regurgitation and dysecdysis. A previous gastric wash was negative for cryptosporidia by PCR. A gastric biopsy was obtained but the snake died two days later. Radiographs revealed some abnormalities in the air sacs and lungs. Necropsy revealed fluid in the lungs. The thyroid appeared enlarged and there was a 90° kink in the trachea.

SEPSIS. This 1.5-year-old male junglefowl was clinically normal the previous evening had been actively displaying recently and was found dead on the ground along the netting in the aviary the following morning. Necropsy identified fly egg deposition in the plumage fresh bruising over the right shoulder region and over both stifles and thighs some bruising around the neck adequate pectoral mass and abundant body fat congestion and hemorrhage in the lungs mildly enlarged spleen with congestion and some possible hemorrhage slightly smaller than expected pancreas active testicles and no other gross findings.

TRAUMA SHOCK ENTERITIS. This 7-year-old male kangaroo was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy there was hemorrhage in the muscles of the ventral neck and laxity of the atlantooccipital joint; however no fractures of the cervical vertebrae were identified grossly or radiographically. There was a 4 cm. area of hemorrhage in the right lung and a small subdural hematoma.

Ovarian adenocarcinoma Ovarian adenocarcinoma Comment The cause of death in this bird was due to ovarian adenocarcinoma; a tumor of the ovary. This condition is not contagious and should not be the cause of death in other birds in your flock. This report confirms our conversation and concludes our communication concerning this case. If you have additional questions; feel free to contact me at 517-353-3701.

FETLOCK TRAUMA ASPIRATION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS RUMINORETICULITIS COLITIS. This 8-year-old female gerenuk developed front fetlock hyperextension and was anesthetized to splint the leg. The animal regurgitated shortly after intubation and a large amount of ruminal content was noted. Antibiotics were initiated while the animal was anesthetized. After immobilization the animal was observed openmouthed breathing and although no crackles or wheezes were ausculted aspiration pneumonia was suspected. This animal was found dead in the corral the following morning. Necropsy revealed extensive bruising from mid cannon bone to fetlocks of both front limbs swelling of the fetlocks mild clear subcutaneous effusion a partial tear of the distal aspect of the flexor tendons at the level of the fetlocks partial tears in the annular ligament on both sides and clear fluid from the lacerated regions. The sesamoid bones were loosely affixed and were easily freed from their connective tissues. Circumferential tracheal ulceration and petechiae were noted caudal to the larynx. Some additional areas of petechiation were in the tracheal mucosa caudal to this region approximately 10 cm. cranial to the bronchial bifurcation and another 20 cm. cranial to the bronchial bifurcation. No food material was seen in the lumen. The right pulmonary lobe was consolidated firm and oozed blood on cut surface. A moderate amount of fluid was in the esophagus and three diverticula were present in the proximal duodenum approximately 5 cm. distal to the abomasum. The left kidney was smaller than the right firmer and irregularly shaped. A 1.64 kg. fetus was in the uterus.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA STRESS. This approximately 8-year-old female chuckwalla was humanely euthanized. This chuckwalla had a history of dehydration and not eating well. It had a very high white blood cell count (60000) with 80% lymphocytes. An exploratory laparotomy was performed and revealed fluid within the coelomic cavity an enlarged spleen and an enlarged liver. At necropsy there were minimal adipose stores. The heart was slightly enlarged. There was splenomegaly and hepatomegaly. The liver had rounded edges and several 1-3 mm. red circular lesions. The anterior colon was distended with gas and a small amount of fecal material.

Open Comment: The cause of this alpaca's reported neurologic signs could not be determined upon gross necropsy alone. There were no pathologic lesions noted within the meninges or brain. Sections from the brain have been sent for rabies testing; and the results of the rabies test will be released in an addendum report. Pending negative rabies results; additional saved tissues may be sent for further microbiologic testing. Histologic evaluation of tissues is in progress and results will be issued in a final report. Barbie J. Gadsden; DVM Brain: rabies negative Comment: Histologic evaluation of tissues is in progress and results will be issued in a final report. Barbie J. Gadsden; DVM Cerebrum: Marked multifocal acute laminar cortical necrosis with cerebral edema Liver: Mild multifocal to coalescing nonsuppurative periportal hepatitis with biliary hyperplasia and bridging fibrosis; mild hepatic lipidosis Polioencephalomalacia Comment: The histologic lesions observed in the brain are consistent with a diagnosis of polioencephalomalacia. This condition may be due to sodium ion toxicosis; or decreased amount of thiamine (as a result of thiaminase containing plant; a defect in thiamine metabolism; or inadequate dietary thiamine). The exact pathogenesis remains unclear; but it is often amenable to thiamine supplementation in the early stages. The exact cause of the liver lesions are undetermined at this time; special stains are in progress to further characterize the pigment within hepatocytes. Results will be issued in an addendum report. Barbie J. Gadsden; DVM

GASTRIC ADENOCARCINOMA WITH CARCINOMATOSIS AND METASTASIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 55-year-old female lowland gorilla was one of the oldest captive gorillas on record. This geriatric gorilla had experienced a bout of paresis which responded to glucocorticoid therapy but the gorilla became inappetent with progression to anorexia and decreased fluid consumption when weaned off of prednisolone. Diagnostic procedures identified a large mass and mucosal erosion adjacent to and occluding the gastroesophageal opening. Thoracic radiographs revealed poor ventilation and air bronchograms in the right lung. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed pleural and peritoneal effusion pulmonary congestion and anthracosis arteriosclerosis and osteoarthritis conjunctival masses gastric neoplasia and ulceration hepatic neoplasia dental attrition tooth loss cardiac disease uterine neoplasia mesenteric neoplasia splenic necrosis renal cortical cysts and lenticular opacities. Complete necropsy information is on file.
TRAUMA POSSIBLY DROWNED. This 37-year-old female Caribbean flamingo was found dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition and fair postmortem condition. No other abnormalities were noted.

TRAUMA SHOCK. This 6-year-old female fruit bat was found dead on the floor of its exhibit. At necropsy the intestines were distended with large amounts of gas. There was a complete open laterally displaced fracture of the right ulna and radius surrounded by a moderate amount of hemorrhage. There were also two pinpoint areas of abraded skin lateral to the fracture site.

SPINAL CORD TRAUMA SUBOPITMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS BACTERIAL DUODENITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 10-year-old male African hunting dog vomited a whole rabbit three days earlier and keepers noted that the animal appeared hunched and had diarrhea. The animal became wobbly in the rear legs with a wide based stance but was alert responsive and appeared to be passing normal stools one day prior to being found in lateral recumbency with splayed rear legs. The animal was minimally responsive pale cold and dehydrated. An attempt at supportive care was unsuccessful and the animal died. Necropsy revealed dehydration thin body condition multiple pressure sores multiple tan raised irregular lesions in the lung mottled adrenals ulcer in the proximal duodenum diffusely thickened intestine multiple yellow foci on the serosal surface of the liver and dark kidneys.
NA

INTESTINAL TORSION. This 7-year-old male addax died. It was immobilized for MGA implant and Haloperidol for possible herd introduction. It had a rocky recovery and circled in the stall. It bloodied its nose against the wall as it circled. The addax quieted down in the evening and spent most of the next day getting up and down but showed interest in food. At necropsy the addax was in good body condition. The surgical site appeared to be free of infection. The implant was intact. There were petechiae and ecchymoses along the ventral surface of the lumbar musculature. There was emphysema present in the musculature. The ventricles of the heart appeared slightly thickened. The lungs had bilateral areas of cranial atelectasis. There was a torsion in the gastrointestinal tract. The omentum was twisted around a significant portion of the small and large intestines with the intestinal loops cranial to the torsion appearing to be pink in color and the loops caudal to the torsion appearing dark purple. There was a large amount of solid ingesta in the reticulum and rumen. The ruminal papillae looked flattened in appearance. The ingesta in the omasum and abomasum was liquid diarrhea. The liver had multifocal areas of dark discoloration. The spleen was small and a white pale blue.
PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 10-year-old male tern was found dead in the water. At necropsy the heart was pale and the liver was firm.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA PUSTULAR DERMATITIS AND FOLLICULITIS CERUMINOUS GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA THROID FOLLICULAR CYSTADENOMA CATARACT OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 11.5-year-old male fennec fox had a history of chronic skin disease and otitis externa glaucoma and osteoarthritis. The fox has also had a history of self-mutilation and recently mutilated the toenails of the hind legs with increased digging behavior in the last few weeks and injuries to the toe pads. Supportive care was administered with no response and substantial deterioration of quality of life. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized alopecia and lichenification dried blood on the front limbs and a torn toe pad in the left front digit. Debris was in the external ear canal and a polyp occupied a large portion of the external ear canal of the right ear. Distal to the polyp was a large amount of debris and the tympanum was ruptured. Several missing incisors were noted. Petechiae were noted over the ventral thorax in the subcutis. The right thyroid was larger than the left and both had small cystic structures. Multifocal soft nodules were in the liver. Numerous nodules were in the pancreas. The left eye was not present and the lens of the right eye was cloudy and friable. The right elbow joint had proliferative changes and osteophytes. Similar findings were in the right hock.
SEPSIS. This 3-year-old male gecko was found dead. Necropsy revealed an enlarged liver.

HYPERTHERMIA INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This approximately 2-year-old male degu participated in an out-of-zoo program. It had been held in a shaded area for 30 minutes when a staff member noted that the animal appeared to be in distress. The animal was moved to an air-conditioned space indoors but was dead by the time a veterinarian arrived. Necropsy revealed pulmonary congestion hepatic congestion and hemorrhage in the intestine.

ENTERITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS NEPHROPATHY. This 3-year-old male wallaby had a history of coccidiosis and gingivitis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the mucous membranes and skin were icteric. The gall bladder contained inspissated bile. The liver was enlarged.

EXUBERANT HEMATOPOIESIS AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 9-year-old female pygmy marmoset was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed plump kidneys and no other gross abnormalities. Blood work obtained three days prior to death revealed elevated white blood cell count with left shift regenerative anemia and severe elevation in blood urea nitrogen creatinine and phosphorus. Pyelonephritis was suspected.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This approximately 5-year-old beaded lizard was found dead in its enclosure and had been inappetent for two weeks. The animal was housed with a conspecific that died suddenly approximately 1-2 weeks earlier. That lizard had hemorrhagic necrotizing enteritis. Necropsy of the lizard of this report revealed mottled and congested liver that was gritty on cut surface hemorrhage in the mucosa of the stomach hemorrhage in the intestine urate stasis and large follicles in the ovaries (three of which contain granulomas).
EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL OSTEOMYELITIS HEPATITIS. This 11-year-old rattlesnake was euthanized due to multiple swellings along the spine. At necropsy several areas along the spine appeared fused.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA (UTERUS DIAPHRAGM). This 11-year-old ewe had a history of chronic forelimb lameness and arthritis. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy osteophytes were noted in the elbow and stifles. The uterus was distended with brown fluid. Firm pink masses were present in the uterine wall.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA RENAL TUBULAR PROTEINOSIS SHOCK. This 8.5-year-old female duck presented with lameness and was found to have two broken legs. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large hematoma was noted in the thigh associated with a fracture of the head of the left femur. There was also a fracture of the distal right femur with associated soft tissue injury. Multiple small white foci were present in the kidneys.

INTESTINAL INTUSSUSCEPTION BACTERIAL ENTERITIS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS CEREBRAL TOXOPLASMOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male kangaroo has been repeatedly treated for toxoplasmosis. The animal’s condition declined and anorexia developed. The animal was humanely euthanized due to lack of response to therapy. At necropsy the cecum was hemorrhagic. An intussusception with necrosis is noted in the duodenum with foci of perforation of the wall and leakage of intestinal contents into the abdominal cavity.

SEPTIC PERITONITIS RUMINAL ACIDOSIS WITH FUNGAL INVASION ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 6-year-old female pronghorn had a four-day history of anorexia and lethargy. The animal was anesthetized for evaluation and died under anesthesia. At necropsy there was approximately 1 liter of abdominal effusion fibrinous serositis ruminal distention with suspect partial volvulus enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes no ingesta in the caudal portion of the GI tract and a region of duodenum that was darkly discolored with multiple adhesions to the mesentery and surrounding structures.

CHRONIC HEMORRHAGE AND INFLAMMATION IN DEEP DERMAL ADIPOSE EUTHANASIA. This captive bred male axolotl was euthanized on December 26 2015. The cause for euthanasia was not indicated. The animal’s age was 7 years and nine months. Gross necropsy revealed gray to blue hepatic lobes possible ovaries present and lungs that did not float in formalin but were grossly unremarkable.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA PANCREATITIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS DIABETES MELLITUS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION AND OSSIFYING PACHYMENINGITIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male cheetah has a history of chronic medical issues. It had cryptococcal meningitis and pulmonary lesions in 2004 gradually recovering with treatment over one year. The animal has also developed a hind limb swagger suggesting proprioceptive deficit and keratous tail abnormality resulting in tail trauma (bumping along the ground). The animal gradually developed urinary incontinence with recurrent dermatitis from urine scald and also with skin necrosis that suggested a possible underlying neurovascular abnormality. The cat also had evidence of recurrent obstipation progressing to mild megacolon. For several years it had moderate azotemia and would receive subcutaneous fluid administration. It had recurrent bouts of urinary tract infections and silicone urolithiasis. In the last month the animal developed diabetes mellitus and became abruptly depressed vomited melanic material several times overnight and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an open granulation bed on one side of the proximal tail. Muscle was somewhat orange/copper. A 1.5 cm. encapsulated abscess is in the region of the shoulders corresponding to fluid infusion sites. Body fat is abundant. Nuclear sclerosis is in both eyes. The oral cavity contained melanic vomit on the mucous membranes and around the teeth. The right frontal sinus was filled with mucus gelatinous material and some greenish suppurative exudate. The brain was adhered to the ventral surface of the skull around the hypothalamus and along the cranial brainstem associated with opacified granular whitish plaques overlying the brain. Multiple white firm crispy plaques overlie the spinal cord and caudal nerve roots under the dura and these plaques fused to form a nearly rigid opaque white thin tube around the caudal equina. Areas of bronchiectasis were in the lungs. Some pinpoint tan/white subpleural spots were noted. The liver was bright yellow and blotchy red with a prominent lobular pattern and miliary white speckles throughout the parenchyma. A few small cysts were also noted. The common bile duct was somewhat tortuous but otherwise normal. The pancreas was speckled with tiny nodules throughout the lobes and a larger multiloculated cyst and some surrounding white opacification and thinning of the parenchymal/peritoneal lining were noted. On cut surface an abscess filled with white/green suppurative exudate was at the center of the cystic lesion. The lymph nodes at the root of the mesentery around the pancreas were edematous. The spleen was enlarged with numerous coalescing white masses throughout the parenchyma. A single daughter spleen was in the mesentery at one pole which also contained a white mass. Melena coated the mucosa of the stomach. The gastric walls were edematous. Firm-ish fecal material was in the colon. Anal sacs were dilated and filled with tan flocculent sour smelling exudate. The wall of the anal sac appeared mineralized. The kidneys were congested. The urinary bladder was empty. A sludge of sand was in the neck of the urinary bladder cranial to the prostate. The adrenals were congested.
MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MYOCARDITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS PNEUMONIA. This 2-year-old male opossum was found dead. At necropsy the liver was firm and mottled. Firm white plaques were noted on the lungs.

RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 7.5-year-old female impala had a history of loose stool lethargy azotemia and was receiving supportive care. When the animal was restrained for blood collection it developed a seizure and died. Necropsy revealed good body condition swollen and congested lungs pleural effusion severe arteriosclerosis in the great vessels pericardial effusion multiple areas of fibrosis or infarction along the surface of the heart a flabby right ventricular wall congestion in the cecum and jejunum and swollen kidneys that are pale and grainy on cut surface but with congested medullae.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS GOUT. This 20-year-old female Burmese python had a history of progressive weight loss over several years with dysecdysis inappetence presumptive renal failure and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed dysecdysis retained eye caps and firm small kidneys.

ENTERITIS ASPRIATION. This 6-year-old female colobus presented depressed anorexic and hypothermic. The animal was immobilized for diagnostic workup. Depression worsened following recovery from anesthesia. The animal became anuric regurgitated and died while being manually restrained. At gross necropsy gastric contents were identified and aspirated into the deepest portions of the respiratory tract. Kidneys were smaller than expected and the bladder was empty.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 13-year-old male Humboldt penguin had presented three years earlier for dyspnea and plaques were noted in the trachea. PCR was positive for Mycobacterium sp. and cultures were negative for fungi. Supportive care was administered for almost a year and signs resolved but then returned in January 2015. Radiographs revealed markedly consolidated left lung and air sac. Endoscopy identified plaques in the left trachea. Supportive care was administered but the animal’s appetite and activity level continued to decline. An esophagostomy tube was placed but the bird continued to regurgitate medications and food and was found dead two days later. Necropsy revealed thin body condition green stained urates on the feet and perineal region muscle atrophy a few fat stores vomitus in the oral cavity caseous or purulent material in the left trachea and obliteration of both pulmonary fields due to infiltrates of small granulomas. A 7 cm. pseudomembranous lesion overlaid the left lung and all air sacs were thickened and had adhesions and multiple fine white plaques. A 4 cm. pseudomembranous granuloma was cranial and overlying the heart at the level of the thoracic inlet. The stomach was markedly dilated and the esophagus at the site of the enterotomy tube placement had a 2 cm. opening with leakage of food attributed to regurgitation and vomiting. The liver was enlarged but otherwise grossly normal. The kidneys appeared to be bilaterally inflamed.

AMYLOIDOSIS VISCERAL GOUT ENTERITIS PORTAL HEPATITIS. This greater than 20-year-old female flamingo was found dead. It was segregated somewhat from the group in the morning. It was later found unable to stand and was brought to the hospital. It was depressed and exhibited head tremors. It was given supportive therapy. Treatment was initiated. Blood work revealed hypoglycemia elevated CK and uric acid. At necropsy the bird was in thin body condition. There was a large blood clot present on the right side of the thoracic cavity. The pericardium and epicardium had a white chalky appearance. There was pink colored fluid in the pericardial space. The surfaces of the hepatic lobes had white chalky appearance. On cut section the parenchyma was yellow/brown and friable. The kidneys were diffusely covered with less than 1 mm. in diameter yellow round lesions. The intestinal mucosa had patchy red lesions throughout its length. The hock joints contained a pink discharge with a granular appearance. Tissues were submitted for West Nile virus testing.

ANESTHETIC DEATH PULMONARY SHOCK MINERALIZED GRANULOMA TRAUMA. This 3-year and 9-month-old castrated male capybara had trauma several weeks prior to death from conspecifics. Ten days prior to death the animal had surgery and wound management from conspecific trauma. The animal was on antibiotics and developed severe watery diarrhea and inappetence. The animal was anesthetized for evaluation and died. At necropsy there were multiple skin wounds some of which had caseous exudate. There was a small amount of ascites. The cecum and colon had red foci. Colonic contents were watery. The retroperitoneal region had a large greater than 8 cm. gelatinous whitish mass. This mass corresponded to a pale region in the skeletal muscle that corresponded to a cutaneous wound.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOCARDIOSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 21-year-old female colobus had no recent medical history. It had been examined two days earlier for routine checkup dental prophy and vaccines and had been administered penicillin for gingivitis. It was observed to be clinically normal in the morning and was found dead later in the morning. Necropsy revealed nodular thickenings of the left atrioventricular valve some ecchymoses on the serosal surface of the stomach and no other abnormalities.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA CELLULITIS HEPATITIS LYMPHADENITIS INANITION. This 4-year-old female wallaby was treated for cutaneous Cuterebra. The wound failed to heal and the animal was separated from the mob and was treated with antibiotics. The animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the skin wound contained gray caseated material. Numerous calculi were present in the right kidney. The right lung contained numerous abscesses.

RENAL GOUT OSTEOMYELITIS SPONDYLOSIS FIBROSARCOMA (MUSCLE) INTRAMUSCULAR FIBROSIS. This 11-year-old python had been under treatment for a septicemia with little improvement. Proliferation and collapse of vertebrae were noted radiographically. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy inspissated material was noted in the coelomic wall. Bony proliferations were noted throughout the spine.
PARASITIC GASTRITIS ENTERITIS. This 7-year-old toad was found dead. At necropsy abundant dark orange fluid was present in the coelomic cavity.

MUSCLE NECROSIS AND HEMORRHAGE (POSSIBLE ENVENOMATION) RUPTURED YOLK FOLLICLE SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 10-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed multiple subcutaneous hemorrhagic regions.

WING TRAUMA XANTHOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS URATE STASIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male scarlet ibis is from a group in which mycobacteriosis has been identified. Two of these birds were found recumbent with wounds on the wings and were euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy vegetative lesions were on the heart valves and the proventriculus was empty. Ingesta were in the intestines. Male reproductive tract was identified.

AMYLOIDOSIS DIC BACTERIAL EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male black footed ferret has a history of chronic renal failure and was maintained on a renal diet. Supportive care was periodically administered. The ferret stopped responding to treatment and developed bleeding from the mouth and gastrointestinal tract and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage around the kidneys and in the skin where subcutaneous fluids were administered. Hemorrhage was also present in the soft tissue structures in the mediastinum and a small amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the thoracic cavity. The heart appeared mildly enlarged on the left side. A small amount of serosanguineous fluid was free in the abdomen and multiple areas of hemorrhage were noted in the fat bodies and omentum. Retroperitoneal hemorrhage was prominent. Kidneys were symmetrical and small. Fresh blood was in the oral cavity in the region of the esophagus and some apparent ulcers were noted in the stomach and esophagus. Coffee ground appearance to the substrate in the stomach was also noted. The liver had multiple cystic structures and the gallbladder contained thick hemorrhagic fluid. Urine was red.

NECROTIZING HEPATITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 1-year-old female saki was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed areas of alopecia on the hips and knees but no evidence of cutaneous inflammation. The heart is abnormally globoid.

Whole body - Emaciation Bone marrow - Serous atrophy of fat Pericardium; Peritoneum - Bicavitary serous effusion Lungs - Moderate bronchopneumonia C1; C2 - Multifocal; chronic ulceration C3 - Multifocal erosion and congestion; with intralesional Haemonchus contortus Small and large intestine - Multifocal enterocolitis; suspected Comments: The findings on necropsy are various; encompassing chronic nutritional deficiency [emaciation; serous atrophy of fat] and their sequela [effusion]; infectious disease [bronchopneumonia; Haemonchus contortus]; and chronic inflammatory/infectious disease [stomach ulcers]. It is possible that the Haemonchus contortus infection could be at the heart of the nutritional deficiency; which led to subsequent immune suppression resulting in the observed infectious lesions. The chronic ulceration of the nonglandular stomach are possibly evidence of such a chain of events that occurred in one of the reported previous episodes of emaciation. A final report is pending histopathology; bacteriology; and parasitology. David Needle; DVM C1 - Chronic ulceration C3; duodenum - Mild; chronic; lymphoplasmacytic and histiocytic gastritis and duodenitis Lung: Mild; multifocal BALT hyperplasia; mild multifocal interstitial pneumonia; and mild; multifocal alveolar histiocytosis Heart - Mild; diffuse; lymphoplasmacytic; and histiocytic interstitial myocarditis Kidney: Multifocal moderate to severe neutrophilic and lymphocytic vasculitis Tongue: Multifocal epithelial erosion and mineralization; with adherent bacteria Colon: Mild; multifocal lymphoplasmacytic colitis; with mild; perivascular to interstitial chronic active serositis Haemonchiasis and Coccidiosis Emaciation; with hypoproteinemia leading to abdominal and pericardial effusion; and serous atrophy of fat Renal vasculitis Interstitial pneumonia and myocarditis Comments The findings on gross examination; bacteriology; parasitology and histopathology are listed in order of purported pathogenesis. These findings reveal evidence of ongoing parasitism; and emaciation. This led to chronic lesions of glossitis; foregut ulceration; gastroenteritis; and colitis. The acute lesions are renal vasculitis; interstitial pneumonia; and myocarditis; all of which indicate septicemia [blood borne bacteria]. The most likely order of events in this case is longstanding parasitism combined with the metabolic demands of parturition and lactation leading to a significant negative calorie balance. Prolonged caloric debt lead to decreased total body protein; with decreased blood albumin resulting in loss of fluid into the abdominal cavity and the pericardial sac [effusion]. Immunosuppression occurred secondary to this prolonged illness and protein loss; and bacteria were able to access the blood stream; through the oral; foregut lesions; or the lungs. The lesions in the kidney; lung and heart are the microscopic evidence of disseminated / blood borne bacteria. The severe serous atrophy of fat reported in the femur and the pericardium suggest that at this point; it was unlikely that increasing feed would have been sufficient to return this animal to health. David Needle; DVM

HEPATIC LACERATION. This 9-year-old male Rodriquez fruit bat was found dead in rigor mortis within the exhibit. At gross necropsy there were numerous blood clots on the liver and covering the abdominal viscera. A 1 cm. tear was present in the capsule of the liver.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS INANITION. This 8-year-old toad was being hibernated. The animal was found dead. At necropsy lungs were congested. The liver was small. Numerous developing ova were present in the ovary.

LYMPHOMA AMYLOIDOSIS. This greater than 5-year-old female quail was found dead in a walkthrough aviary lying on its back with fecal matter crusted on the vent. Necropsy revealed good body condition some thickening of the coelomic lining in the right caudal ventral abdomen adhered to the ventral most aspect of the liver and to a small section of the intestines. A small brown granulomatous lesion was attached to the coelomic lining on the left caudal dorsal aspect. Crop and ventriculus were distended with ingesta the liver was enlarged and mottled pink to red with some black discoloration around the edges and some small abscess or nodules were noted throughout the parenchyma.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE TRACHEITIS THYROID ADENOMA. This 20-year-old female wallaroo was laterally recumbent and showed mild nasal discharge. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy arthritic changes were noted in the right shoulder. The heart was enlarged with thinning of the right ventricle.

HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS PULMONARY EDEMA SHOCK. This 6.5-year-old male parrot was found dead near the Plexiglas. At necropsy a large quantity of fat was present in the abdominal cavity. The spleen was enlarged. Lungs were wet heavy and dark.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GASTRIC MINERALIZATION AORTIC MINERALIZATION ATHEROSCLEROSIS PULMONARY MINERALIZATION CHRONC ENTERITIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 22-year-old male sloth had a history of polydipsia and weight loss. Azotemia and leukocytosis were noted on blood work. The animal has ulcerative lesions in the oral mucosa and had been treated with antibiotics. The presented severely dehydrated and poorly responsive. The animal was humanely euthanized. Kidneys had pale areas in the cortices.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old corn snake had a mass in the lower abdominal region and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed three focal lesions to 2 mm. in size and white in the liver multiple white lesions in the lung about 1 mm. in size and an oval shaped 6 cm. long mass with a necrotic center in the gonadal region.

TRAUMA INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA (PROBABLE SEPSIS). This 3-year-old tiger was attacked by a cagemate five days earlier and treated with prednisolone for neurological injuries. It was found recumbent and did not recover from gas anesthesia. Necropsy revealed multiple skin lacerations and abrasions. The lungs were infiltrated with firm to hard encapsulated nodules of varying size from pinpoint to 2 mm. in diameter. Hair and grass were in the stomach and few punctate hemorrhages were noted. Digesta was present in the alimentary tract.

MALIGNANT THYMOMA WITH METASTASES FUNGAL PNEUMONIA OBESITY. This female 2-year-old prairie dog was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed no external abnormalities. A 4 to 5 cm. firm tan mass was located in the cranial mediastinum and appeared to extend into the thoracic inlet. Two similar masses 3 cm. in diameter were detected in the thoracic inlet. The left caudal lung lobe had a 1 cm. white/yellow nodular plaque on the pleural surface and both caudal lung lobes were consolidated. The left ventricular free wall was thick. The liver had an increased lobular pattern and was pale with multiple yellow foci. The omentum and mesentery contained a large amount of adipose tissue. A 3 cm. spherical mass was present on the left kidney at the renal pelvis and the mass was dark red on cut surface. No other abnormalities were detected in the abdominal tissues.

MYOPATHY RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS PANCREATITIS ILEOTYPHILITIS. This 5-year-old female gazelle was submitted with no history. Necropsy revealed abundant fat stores edema in the subcutis small areas of atelectasis in the pulmonary lobes hemorrhage in the ventral mandible fibrosis and possible calcification in the pancreas enlarged lymph nodes around the pancreas tarry contents in the cecum and ileum petechiae on the serosal surfaces of these tissues hemorrhage on the mucosa dark brown urine and hemorrhage in the cervical and neck muscle.
NA

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA NEPHROPATHY INANITION. This 12-year-old female Matamata turtle became anorectic approximately five days prior to death. On physical exam white foamy material was present in the nose and mouth. The animal was moved from the exhibit and treated with antibiotics. The discharge resolved and appetite returned; however the animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy the gall bladder was enlarged with adhesions to the adjacent liver lobes. Other tissues had no significant gross changes.

BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13.5-year-old male pygmy goat has a history of depressed appetite for one month. Recent blood work identified elevations in hepatic enzymes and blood urea nitrogen. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified several liters of ascites and pleural effusion. The liver was thickened and had multiple white nodules. Some of the nodules coalesced.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA PHECHROMOCYTOMA. This 18.5-year-old female Thomson’s gazelle has a history of chronic arthritis and difficulty standing even with pain medication. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed marked cartilaginous wear with synovitis osteoproliferation and capsular thickening. A 6 cm. dark red mass was anterior to the left kidney.

COLONIC DILATATION WITH COLITIS AND TRANSFORMATION TO LYMPHOMA BACTERIAL CHOLECYSTITIS WITH SEPSIS. This approximately 10-year-old female tree monitor had a cloacal mast cells excised five months earlier and since the surgical procedure has had poor appetite and food consumption with substantial weight loss. Blood work has been within normal limits. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition severely distended colon containing soft ingesta displacement of the intestine and stomach cranially and dorsally and moderate erythema but no ulcerations in the colonic mucosa.

DUCK VIRUS ENTERITIS BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA BUMBLEFOOT. This 6-year-old male fulvous whistling duck died shortly after treatment and blood collection. It is one of seven fulvous whistling ducks presented from the river exhibit one morning. Four were dead and three were alive. All three live birds died either en route to the hospital or shortly after treatment. Five birds were dead in the same exhibit the previous day. These deaths constitute approximately one-third of the fulvous whistling duck population in the large outdoor exhibit that contains multiple bird species. No other bird species are affected at this time. Necropsy of this bird revealed good nutritional status but little food or digested food in the gastrointestinal tract. Mild bumblefoot lesions were on both feet. A moderate amount of clear fluid drained from the mouth. The right lung lobe had an area of hemorrhage at the caudal dorsal aspect and the air sacs had clear fluid. Approximately 1 ml. of clear fluid was in the pericardial sac. A moderate amount of clear fluid distended the crop and was present in the esophagus proventriculus and ventriculus. Hemorrhages were on the serosal surface of the caeca and distal small intestine and the lumina of the caeca were filled with caseous plugs. The liver was enlarged with hemorrhages on the surface and there were two areas of hemorrhage with a “bull’s-eye” type appearance on the surface of the liver. The kidneys were pale the testes were large and there was seasonal reproductive hypertrophy. The spleen was approximately twice normal size and multiple petechial hemorrhages were noted on the surface of the pancreas. Meningeal blood vessels were congested.

CHRONIC LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC AND HYPERPLASTIC CHOLECYSTITIS AND CHOLANGITIS ADENOMATOUS PANCREATIC LOBULAR HYPERPLASIA LYMPH NODE CHOLESTEROL GRANULOMA EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male lemur had been previously hospitalized for chronic hepatic disease and poor appetite. Because the animal was continuing to do poorly and regularly refused food and medications elective euthanasia was performed. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition with moderate depot adipose present a pale and enlarged liver with multifocal raised nodules that were paler brown in the surrounding parenchyma oozing of light green to white flocculent fluid from the cut surface of the liver distention of the intrahepatic bile ducts marked distention of the gallbladder and associated bile ducts a thickened gallbladder wall with numerous cystic chambers a 10 x 10 mm. nodular firm yellow mass in the abdominal mesenteric fat caudal to the stomach approximately 30 petechiae in the jejunal mucosa a 6 x 7 mm. mass in the mediastinal adipose cranial to the heart that was firm and yellow and filling of the distal trachea and bronchi with yellow flocculent mucopurulent discharge and pink frothy fluid. The lungs were also diffusely congested and dark red.

HEPATIC BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA CRUSTING EPIDERMITIS URATE STASIS LINGUAL GRANULOMA. This 12-year-old male rattlesnake had a history of weight loss and was not doing well. The snake subsequently died and necropsy revealed adequate body condition and fair postmortem condition ecchymoses and desiccation noted in the ventral scutes. The pancreas was firm and mottled brown and white. The spleen was dark purple. The kidneys were pale with prominently visible collecting ducts and a 1 cm. in diameter beige focus was in the liver.

TRAUMA ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS PENMATE AGGRESSION. This 9-year-old male rail was found in the flight cage on the ground and was inappetent. The bird was nervous in the presence of the keepers. The bird had lost several grams in the previous two days and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a full thickness wound on the caudal aspect of the maxillary beak bruising on the back and on the dorsal aspects of the wings with associated petechiae feather loss is noted along the back where the bruising had occurred and a full thickness defect in the skin was noted in the back covered by a scab. Similar lesions were noted over the base of the neck. The left lateral toenail was avulsed. Caudal air sacs were slightly opaque and cranial air sacs were moderately opaque. A small plaque was on the keel at the level of the heart. The distal portion of the aorta was firm. The spleen was slightly enlarged with a small white mass in the caudal aspect. The liver was diffusely mottled and tan with areas of hemorrhage. The pancreas was pale with congested vessels. Some hemorrhage was in the caudal aspect of the left lobe. The kidneys were enlarged at the cranial pole. Small foci of hemorrhage were in the skull and two indentations were noted in the skull.

MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION URATE STASIS COLLOID GOITER. This 20-year-old male rattlesnake was found dead. At necropsy the kidneys showed evidence of renal gout. The thyroid gland was markedly enlarged. The myocardium was diffusely tan.

INANITION RENAL GOUT URATE STASIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS CUTANEOUS HEMANGIOMA. This 4-year-old duck was found dead frozen in the ice. At necropsy the bird was emaciated. A 1 cm. in diameter irregular round purple mass was present on the right side of the head. A large quantity of sand was present in the ventriculus. Marked congestion was noted throughout all tissues. Kidneys were swollen firm and pale.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA PULMONARY EDEMA SHOCK HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ENTERITIS. This 8-year-old female wallaby had two episodes of upper respiratory infection. The animal was recently found moribund and died. The animal is from a group which was positive for wallaby retrovirus. At necropsy lungs were reddened and edematous. The liver contained numerous yellow pinpoint lesions.

FRACTURED VERTEBRA EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male black-footed ferret presented with lethargy and decreased appetence three days earlier. The ferret received supportive care but declined and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The ferret had been unable to move its hind limbs and was unwilling to ambulate. Necropsy revealed good body condition mild alopecia with thinning of the fur over the left thorax right thorax and the abdomen and a 2 mm. scab on the right metatarsal pad. Mild hemorrhage was in the epaxial muscles cranial and dorsal to a fractured spinous process of the fifth thoracic vertebra. The tips of the canine teeth were worn or broken off moderate tartar was present on the buccal aspects of the molars very little food material was in the alimentary tract and scant stools were identified in the colon. The urinary bladder was full and a wedge-shaped defect was in the cortex of the left kidney. This lesion was dimpled and pale. On cut surface the defect extended to the medulla. The right kidney contained one small focus of pallor in the medulla. Dark gray/black miliary coloration was on the dorsal aspect of the spinal cord corresponding to T5 vertebrae.

AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION ASCENDING BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS EGG YOLK COELOMITIS. This 52-year-old female Caribbean flamingo was found down and died spontaneously. At necropsy the kidneys were pale. There was a ruptured egg yolk around the distal cloaca. The spleen was enlarged.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS TUBULAR MINERALIZATION MYOCARDIAL MINERALIZATION GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS SHOCK. This 10-year-old meerkat was lethargic ataxic and possible retching. The animal could not be removed from exhibit for examination and was found dead several days later. The animal has a history of chronic renal disease. At necropsy the body was markedly autolyzed. The left kidney contained a fluid filled capsule.

ACUTE SHOCK. This 21-day-old male cottontail rabbit is from a conservation breeding program. The animal was found out of the enclosure on the ground at morning check in. No evidence of trauma was noted and no gross abnormalities were seen at necropsy. Hay was present in the stomach and gastrointestinal contents were normal.

SEPSIS COLITIS RECTAL PROLAPSE PERIODONTAL DISEASE. This 11-year-old male eyelash palm viper had a history of rectal prolapse occurring six months ago and one week prior to death. The animal was found to have a foul odor from the vent and was lethargic. Blood work indicated sepsis. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed abundant intracoelomic fat stores hemorrhage in the trachea and lung pinpoint white foci in the liver and left kidney thickened distal rectum with dry yellow proliferative mucosa and some submucosal hemorrhage. The fat surrounding the gonad contained several small firm yellow nodules that oozed yellow thick material on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS AND WASTING (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HYPERSENSITIVITY DERMATITIS. This 13-year-old female addax had a roughened haircoat and generalized pruritus for several years attributed to fly bite allergy or some other form of hypersensitivity. There has been some minor trauma from conspecifics and a few miscellaneous subcutaneous abscesses one dystocia and a postpartum uterine infection. Over the last 6-8 months the animal gradually lost condition and developed generalized muscle atrophy and a gaunt appearance. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of body fat soft tissue enlargements on both carpi minimal degenerative arthritic changes in the stifles and hips good dental condition for the animal’s age mildly cystic thyroids pulmonary and froth in the trachea mildly edematous and yellowed or atrophied pancreas contracted spleen a few small cortices of the kidneys inactive ovaries a few small firm nodules in the wall of the uterus variable morphology in the villi of the rumen depending on the location some sand in the abomasum no parasites observed in the alimentary tract and no other remarkable findings.

SARCOMA (SKIN) HEPATITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 11-year-old male owl presented for dyspnea. The animal was emaciated and clear fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. A prominent systolic heart murmur was ausculted. The animal was humanely euthanized due to multiple medical problems. At necropsy a large mass was present in the cervical region near the shoulder and a smaller mass in the right cervical region. The intestines contained brown to dark red mucus and were congested. Liver was enlarged and mottled tan. A 1 cm. in diameter tan mass was present in one lobe.

MALIGNANT THYMOMA CEREBELLAR HEMORRHAGE EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old neutered male rabbit was euthanized following the acute onset of a head tilt and radiographic evidence of a cranial thoracic mass and opacities in the entire lung fields. Gross necropsy revealed two subcutaneous skin masses approximately 20 ml. of pink thoracic fluid a cranial mediastinal mass that was adhered to the chest wall pinpoint white nodules in the lungs a distended gallbladder and irregular hepatic margins.

EUTHANASIA INANITIN HEPATIC FIBROSIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 11-year-old male viper had a history of weight loss and regurgitation. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was humanely euthanized due to continued decline in condition. At necropsy multifocal irregular tan nodules were present throughout the liver.

SEPSIS SCLEROSING COELOMITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 5-year-old male masked bobwhite quail was found dead in the morning with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed no evidence of trauma dark purple lungs and thin body condition. A large amount of clear fluid was in the crop.
adult.  Metabolic disease. Presumed metabolic disease.

FLEA INFESTATION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HYPERTENSION BRONCHIOLOALVEOLAR HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR VACUOLAR DEGENERATION. This 2-year-old female opossum had a history of severe flea infestation. The animal was treated topically. The animal was found dead several days later. At necropsy the liver was mottled white and pink and was firm. A large trichobezoar was present in the stomach along with numerous roundworms.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMA ORAL CAVITY. This 5-year-old lizard had a one week history of lethargy and inappetence associated with a large mass in the right lower oral cavity that was dorsally ulcerated. The mass deflected the tongue to the left side of the mouth. A fecal acid-fast stain was negative. Supportive care was administered but the lizard did not respond and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This lizard shared an exhibit with a Gila monster that was diagnosed with cryptosporidiosis. Necropsy of the lizard revealed a 1 cm. firm mass in the right oral cavity deflecting the tongue to the left side. The central dorsal area of the mass is ulcerated. When squeezed a small amount of caseous exudate was present. The mass is fleshy in color with a necrotic center.

INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 2-month-old ferret was found dead. Coccidiosis was recently identified in this litter. The animal was treated with Alban. At necropsy the body was dehydrated. Scant pasty yellow contents were present in the large intestine.

EUTHANASIA THYMIC LYMPHOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL CYSTS ATELECTASIS. This 14-year-old female lemur was euthanized due to lethargy and a space occupying mass in the thorax. At necropsy blood was present in the thorax. A large mass of adipose-like tissue was present in the anterior mediastinum.

Cause of death uncertain at this time; gross findings most suggestive of severe ulcerative dermatitis; please see comments Comments: Gross findings within the skin are severe and are likely a contributory factor to death. Scotch tape test for ectoparasites on both mice did not reveal organisms. Final diagnoses are pending histologic findings; bacteriology; and mycology. Molly H. Seavey; DVM M Mouse A: Haired skin: Severe chronic locally extensive ulcerative dermatitis with bacterial colonization; serocellular crusts; and squamous dysplasia Liver: Moderate to severe random multifocal to coalescing hepatic necrosis with centrilobular vacuolation and mononuclear aggregates Liver; spleen; lung: Moderate to marked extramedullary hematopoiesis Mouse B: Haired skin: Severe chronic locally extensive ulcerative dermatitis with bacterial colonization and serocellular crusts; and skeletal muscle fibrosis Liver; spleen: Marked extramedullary hematopoiesis Mouse A: Suggestive of sepsis; bacterial dermatitis Mouse B: Bacterial dermatitis Comments: The cutaneous lesions are similar between the two mice. Staphylococcus xylosus has been identified as a cause of dermatitis and an opportunistic pathogen in laboratory mice. Other isolates are likely secondary contributors or environmental contaminants. Histologic findings for Mouse A are suggestive of a systemic septicemia. Bacterial culture of the liver is in progress. Results will be released in an addendum report. Molly H. Seavey; DVM M See comments Comments: Additional findings do not alter original diagnosis. An ulcerative dermatitis has been reported mice with a strain B6 background. It is unclear from the history provided if these mice can be categorized as such. Concerning the hepatic necrosis observed in the single mouse; a bacteriologic etiology was not identified. Although no indices of viral etiology (inclusion bodies; syncytial cells) were observed; virologic screening may be warranted if these mice and newly acquired mice are not routinely surveyed. MYCOTIC DERMATITIS INANITION. This 2-year-old female pit viper was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy dermatitis was noted in the ventral scales.

TRAUMA SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female kangaroo had a one day history of lameness on the right rear limb and was unable to climb and had been inappetent. Examination revealed a mildly displaced transverse fracture of the #6 lumbar vertebral body. All of the vertebrae of the lumbar spine were bridged by severe ankylosing spondylosis. Euthanasia was performed due to age and severity of the lesion. Gross postmortem exam showed extensive contusions in the lumbar spinal flexors free clotted blood in the abdominal cavity adhesions of the renal capsules to the parenchyma and a thin flaccid right ventricular free wall.

AMYLOIDOSIS PYELONEPHRITIS CHOLECYSTITIS. This 4-year-old female black-footed ferret had a four day history of lethargy and inappetence. Blood work revealed end stage renal failure and protein losing nephropathy. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK BACTERIAL SPLENITIS. This 1-year-old rat had been treated for an upper respiratory infection. The animal was found dead. At necropsy lungs were consolidated and red. Hemorrhage was noted in the small intestine.

PANCREATIC FIBROSIS EMACIATION. This 5-year-old male red lory presented to the hospital showing ataxia and general neurological signs and died within an hour. Necropsy revealed fair to thin body condition no adipose stores and large tan spleen.

DISSEMINATED INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED; TRAUMA. This 4-year-old male rainbow lory was found dead after being placed in the clinic under a heat lamp. The night keeper reported wounds to the head. Necropsy revealed multiple bite wounds to the head and wings a pale friable liver and no other abnormalities.

PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA. This greater than 12-year-old male lorikeet was found dead in a puddle. It had no recent signs of illness and the flock has had no signs of illness. Necropsy revealed some ulcerated foci on the left foot and lateral tarsal region and tan rounded liver.

BACTERIAL SPLENITIS AND PERITONITIS SUSPECT SEPTICEMIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This approximately 4-year-old female marmoset was found dead. It may have vomited the night prior to death. It has a history of enlarged liver and nucleated red blood cells in circulation. At necropsy the lungs were congested. There was ingesta in the stomach and digesta in intestines. The colon was empty. Peyer’s patches were darkened. The liver was enlarged and had rounded edges. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. The spleen was large hard and had an irregular surface. Adrenal glands were large. Thyroids were small.

CHRONIC MYOSITIS. This greater than 2-year-old male toad died. This toad was extremely lethargic and had nose rub that worsened in the past two days. The nostrils appeared to be covered by erythematous rub that seemed to be creating difficulty in breathing causing gurgling sounds and gulping for air. The toes were also worse with exposed bone. The ventrum was red and there were multiple red 1 mm. bumps on the body. The toad had been tube fed a few times in the past week. At necropsy the stomach contained a small amount of ingesta. There was a small nematode embedded in the omentum between stomach and pancreas. The caudal large intestine was extremely dilated and thinned and contained a large amount of ingesta.
adult. Weight: 385.8 g.  Euthanasia.

EMACIATION STRESS GASTRIC AND INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 14-month-old male giraffe had a history of intestinal nematodiasis (strongyles and whipworms) and anemia that required a transfusion. The animal became laterally recumbent and unresponsive during the transfusion process developed cardiopulmonary arrest and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed good body condition 4 liters of straw-colored fluid in the thoracic cavity and 6 liters of similar fluid in the abdominal cavity. The liver was mottled. Aspirated gastric contents were present in the lungs. Numerous Haemonchus organisms were in the abomasum and associated with ulceration of the mucosa.

BACTERIAL/FLAGELLATE ASSOCIATED ENTERITIS AND GASTRITIS SEPSIS OSTEOMYELITIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male rattlesnake was examined for severe lethargy and examination revealed limp body condition dehydration atrophied muscle and an agonal breathing pattern. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed prominent dorsal spinous processes slightly thickened gastric wall granulomas in the duodenum and no other gross abnormalities.

EMACIATION. This 5-year-old female green-naped lory was transferred along with a flock of several other lories from the holding area to the lory landing on the day before. The bird was found dead and necropsy revealed no significant findings.

POSSIBLE IVERMECTIN TOXICOSIS. This 11-month-old female pit viper developed paralysis after internal parasite treatment with ivermectin. The dose was apparently within therapeutic boundaries. The animal developed ascending paralysis two days after treatment and did not recover. Necropsy revealed no gross lesions.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS CIRRHOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old male rattlesnake was found moribund in the morning with a slow heartbeat and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had been diagnosed with a melanoma in the skin in February 2012 (G12-0736) and a squamous cell carcinoma in the cloacal mucosa in July 2012 (G12-3346). Necropsy revealed good body condition irregular ventral rim to the vent with marked ulceration and tissue proliferation an old scar on the left body wall with previous mass removal (melanoma) and the lungs were congested. The liver had diffuse congestion and occasional circular pale areas. A 1 cm. focus of thick pale necrotic tissue was present along the dorsal wall of the distal colon contiguous with the vent lesion. The kidneys were diffusely pale and enlarged with multiple pale nodules 1-3 mm. in size. Both ureters were dilated and contained orange-colored urates.

EUTHANASIA RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS GLOSSITIS ENTERITIS CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS. This 6-year/7-month-old male ferret was humanely euthanized. It was an aged ferret that had been declining in appetite and body condition over the past few months. At necropsy the ferret was in poor body condition. It had cachexia. There were minimal to no fat stores. There was a hemorrhagic soft tissue structure noted cranial to the heart. There were multifocal tan foci on the surface of the lungs. The heart appeared enlarged. There was a tan clot within the ventricles. There was some firm mineralized material firmly attached to the aortic wall. The teeth had moderate tartar. One lobe of the liver had cystic structures. The kidneys were very pale and tough to cut. The renal pelvis of the right kidney was dilated.

TRAUMA SHOCK ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 2-year-old male bat was found with its hind leg trapped under a log. A distal tibial fracture was identified. Cardiopulmonary arrest ensued and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy a closed fracture of the distal right tibia was identified. The animal was obese.

LYMPHOMA LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE. This 11-year-old male fruit bat was found dead with no previous medical history. At necropsy there was some free fluid in the thorax and hepatic pallor. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and red discoloration was noted on the diaphragm colon and in mesenteric adipose.

RIGHT OVIDUCT CYST ATHEROSCLEROSIS OVARIAN ADENOCARCINOMA INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS (ASCARIDS) EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female chicken presented with inappetence and lethargy a distended coelom containing a large amount of fluid received supportive care but did not eat on its own developed crop stasis that impeded gavage feeding and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed moderate crop distention thick layer of intracoelomic fat two thin-walled 7-8 cm. cystic structures present cranial to the cloaca in the location of the right oviduct one cyst containing 30 ml. of clear colorless fluid with the other containing 20 ml. of clear fluid with red/brown flocculent debris.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA RENAL COCCIDIOSIS. This 10-year-old female red-necked wallaby has a five day history of inappetence. Supportive care was administered but the animal became uncoordinated and died. Necropsy revealed thin greenish-tinged mucopurulent material at the base of the brain that grew Escherichia coli. No ingesta were noted except fur in the stomach.

CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK LOW-GRADE SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION. This 6.5-year-old female tamarin died. Necropsy revealed no external lesions scant foam in the nares congested lungs much cavitary fat enlarged spleen and no other gross abnormalities.

DUCK VIRAL ENTERITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 9-year-old male duck was found weak and was dead on arrival at the hospital. At necropsy the animal was in good body condition and frank blood was noted in the coelomic cavity. Generalized vascular congestion was present throughout all internal organs. The esophagus intestine and colon contained foul smelling brown liquid. The intestinal mucosa was hemorrhagic.

EMACIATION. This 4-year-old male fruit bat was observed by a keeper to drop from its perch and appeared to have died during this episode. No prior signs of illness were noted in this bat. Necropsy revealed an empty gastrointestinal tract and pale myocardium.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 3-year-old male degu was noted in the morning to be lethargic did not eat its food overnight had liquid diarrhea received supportive care but died later in the afternoon. Necropsy revealed green liquid material in the intestine good body condition and no other abnormalities.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS SHOCK ULCERATIVE GLOSSITIS. This 14-year-old male zebra is one of two that died over a 24 hour period. There was evidence of blood on the floor and no evidence of trauma to the gates or wall. Blood was in the snow along a linear route from the barn to where the zebra was found. The zebra had a broken tooth and the upper lip was cut. Necropsy revealed pulmonary congestion.

DIABETES MELLITUS ISLET CELL VACUOLAR DEGENERATION AND FIBROSIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female rock hyrax had been treated the past few years for diabetes. It had a chronic cardiac murmur and more recently developed an arrhythmia. Ascites from congestive heart failure was noted and radiographs revealed pulmonary edema. The animal presented almost comatose and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large amount of clear yellow fluid in the abdomen a free-floating piece of necrotic liver in the abdomen some fluid in the thoracic cavity enlarged liver with multiple large nodules a stone in the common bile duct pulmonary congestion thickened left atrioventricular valve enlarged left ventricle slightly raised plaques and streaks on the aorta small dark but otherwise normal pancreas and thin renal cortices.

EMACIATION RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 15-year-old male giraffe had a history of intermittent regurgitation and nonspecific gastrointestinal problems. It had received treatment daily the past few weeks for suspected chronic ruminal acidosis. The animal was found dead and necropsy revealed good body condition and good postmortem condition. Adipose stores were markedly atrophic. Food material was in the bronchi. Adipose stores in the abdomen were markedly atrophic. A large irregularly shaped ruminal lith was present up to 25 cm. in greatest dimension and was easily broken apart. The lith was made of feed small pebbles sand and mineral concretions. Mild overgrowth was noted on the medial claws of the front feet.
adult. Weight: 2084 g.  Euthanasia. Poor body condition. Pulmonary congestions plus/minus collapaes; suspect aganol.
CIRRHOSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS PULMONARY SHOCK. This 11-year-old male corn snake had been overheated during a shed cycle and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed no gross lesions.

EUTHANASIA NECK TRAUMA. This 11-year-old female oryx was humanely euthanized due to severe neck injury. At necropsy the oryx was in good body condition. There was substantial pulmonary edema and froth in the trachea. Some areas of the cranial intestine were congested to almost hemorrhagic. The right patella was luxated laterally and there was hemorrhagic synovial fluid in the left fore fetlock and carpus. The cervical area was contused in the epaxial muscles at the occipital atlas and axis. There was frank hemorrhage in this area. The atlantoaxial joint essentially fell open without any assistance and the right ligaments were disrupted to allow a 1 cm. lateral deviation of the joint and spinal cord. The cranial surface of the axis and caudal surface of the atlas were roughened and appeared “fractured” apart and no dens could be palpated. The meninges were congested. The space around the cord was filled with clotted blood from the occiput to the atlas. Sections of liver lung heart lymph nodes and spleen were frozen for future use if needed.
