UNDIFFERENTIATED SARCOMA (LIVER TESTIS COELOM) HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS MELANOSIS RENAL GOUT RENAL MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 37-year-old male skink had a history of conjunctivitis and declining condition. The animal was found dead despite treatment. At necropsy a large quantity of serosanguineous fluid was present in the coelom along with gelatinous masses. The liver contained multifocal and coalescing white to tan nodules. A focal cavitated mass was present in the testis.

DERMATOPHYTOSIS TRAUMA (PROBABLY DROWNED) CHRONIC GASTROENTEROCOLITIS EPIDERMAL PLAQUE. This 2-year-old male sea lion was recently obtained from a rehabilitation facility on the Pacific Coast. The animal was undersized for its age. Necropsy revealed healed scars on the hind flippers and left front flipper early eruption of permanent teeth generalized lymph node enlargement in the thorax and abdomen four esophageal diverticula that appeared to represent healed foci of ulceration white foam in the lung and trachea larger than expected portal vein mottled pancreas and no other abnormalities.

TOXOPLASMOSIS LUTEOMA. This 9-year-old female red kangaroo had an approximately 1.5 week history of dyspnea with partial anorexia and lethargy. She was observed to have increased dyspnea and was spending more time in lateral recumbency shortly before death. She had been treated with clindamycin for one week. Lasix and ceftazidime were administered on the day of death. Necropsy of this case revealed a mild amount of red tinged fluid in the nostrils congested lungs erosions on the gastric mucosa reddened jejunum and reddened pancreas.

CHOLECYSTITIS PERITONITIS SEPSIS RENAL CYSTS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This approximately 12.5-year-old male warthog had a history of intermittent weight loss that would resolve as the food was increased. The day prior to death the animal became lethargic inappetent and was unwilling to stand or ambulate. Examination revealed a ventral abdominal mass and gas distended loops of intestine. Blood work revealed elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen. The animal did not improve with clinical support and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a modified transudate in the abdominal cavity (60 ml.) multiple cysts throughout each kidney with most of the cysts containing translucent fluid and minimal normal appearing renal parenchyma adhesions in the jejunum colon and body wall an enlarged cystic thyroid containing dark brown fluid and no apparently normal thyroid parenchyma.

CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 13-year/11-month-old male tamarin died. It was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy in March 2002 and had been maintained on daily aspirin and enalapril. Pulmonary edema pleural fluid and ascites were not noted during 2002 exams. The tamarin presented with an acute onset of dyspnea anorexia and lethargy on January 21st and died during anesthetic induction to facilitate examination. The tamarin had a history of intermittent alopecia. Mites were noted in the tail skin of this tamarin’s sibling. At necropsy the tamarin was in good body condition. The dorsal aspect of the tail was thinly haired. The skin on the ventral neck/chest region was thickened and greasy. There were normal fat stores present. There was 2.5 ml. of blood tinged ascites. There was 12 ml. of blood tinged pleural fluid in the right hemithorax and 15 ml. of blood tinged pleural fluid within the left hemithorax. The lungs were mottled atelectatic and congested. The heart was enlarged. The left ventricle was thin walled and dilated. The left ventricular free wall measured 3 mm. the right ventricular free wall measured 1 mm. and the interventricular septum measured 2 mm. The heart weighed 6 gm. The teeth had moderate tartar. The liver was congested. The gall bladder contained some firm gritty bile sludge. The renal medullas of both kidneys contained some small cysts.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA (STAPHYLOCOCCAL-LIKE) CATARACT. This 42-year-old female Chilean flamingo presented for inappetence weight loss and mild lameness. Blood work revealed leukocytosis with heterophilia and toxic change with severe monocytosis mild hyperproteinemia and mild hyperglobulinemia. Serum AST and CK were moderately elevated. Supportive care was administered but the bird worsened during the day was unable to stand developed labored respiration and became hypothermic. The bird died while being treated. Necropsy revealed absence of internal fat stores a large amount of muscle necrosis in the medial left thigh in a region of subcutaneous fluid administration small to moderately-sized multifocal orange mottled areas in some parts of the liver large and mostly abnormal orange pulpy tissue in the spleen some mild adhesions of the intestines pancreas and spleen liquid ingesta in the intestine grit and a small piece of metal in the ventriculus and inactive ovary.

BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS WITH PATHOLOGIC FRACTURE. This 16-year-old female palm viper had a history of dysecdysis spondylosis and intermittent inappetence and had been spending more time on the bottom of the enclosure. The snake was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed poor to fair body condition a midbody vertebral fracture was palpable and firm bone proliferation was noted in the middle third of the spine.

DISSEMINATED HETEROPHILIC TO GRANULOMATOUS INFLAMMATION OSTEOARTHRITIS. This 11-year-old female corn snake was noted a few days earlier to have a sluggish righting reflex and had missed the previous four feedings. The snake had lost over 100 gm. in nine months. Supportive care was administered and radiographs revealed several areas of bony proliferation along the spine. The snake died and necropsy revealed a 5 mm. white mass in the parenchyma of the cranial liver. Some 1 mm. white lesions were noted in the kidneys. The animal was in thin body condition.

HEPATITIS CIRCULATING LEUKOCYTOSIS MYOSITIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 18-year-old male copperhead was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy the liver was enlarged and friable with numerous pinpoint white foci.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS GRANULOMATOUS PREITONITIS HEPATITIS PNEUMONIA AND LYMPHADENITIS. This approximately 12-year/2-month-old female jaguar was found dead. It had a recent history of lethargy and lack of appetite associated with abdominal enlargement due to fluid accumulation. It was taken to surgery and the majority of the greater omentum was removed due to involvement with an infiltrative mass of tissue. A biopsy indicated that this was granulomatous inflammation. Surgery to remove the fluid and mass did not result in any improvement and the animal deteriorated over the next few days. The white blood cell count was 32000 and rose to 56000 with a left shift the day prior to death. At necropsy the abdomen had been shaved and there was a 30 cm. long midline surgical incision that started at the xiphoid process and extended caudally. The incision had been sutured closed and all layers of closure appeared to be intact. There were several small decubital ulcers present on the elbows and tarsal joints. There were several hundred milliliters of clear yellow fluid within body cavities. There were several well organized blood clots adhered to the serosal surfaces of abdominal viscera. The thoracic cavity contained 50-100 ml. of clear yellow fluid. The liver was slightly pale and had rounded edges. One lobe contained multiple abscesses ranging from few millimeters to 1 cm. in diameter. The right lung was moist and congested. The left lung contained a number of small 2-5 mm. firm nodules. Both lungs were slightly adhered to a small caseous mass in the ventral midline of the thoracic cavity. There were small abscesses visible around the main mass. Tapeworms were present in the small intestine. The colon was filled with hard dry fecal material.
DERMATITIS MYOSITIS SHOCK. This 6-year-old male bat presented with acute onset of dyspnea. The animal later died. At necropsy the lungs were congested.

GUNSHOT WOUND CARDIAC FIBROSIS MILD HEPATITIS (POSITIVE SEROLOGY FOR HEPATITIS A OR HEPATITIS B) EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male/neutered captive bred chimpanzee was euthanized and refrigerated 52 hours prior to necropsy. The animal developed severe cerebral and spinal cord injuries resulting from a shotgun wound. The exit wound was located at approximately the level of cervical vertebra #6 on the left side. Pellets traveled through the thoracic and abdominal cavities. Two chimpanzees were shot during an attack on employees and were subsequently euthanized. This animal had an IgG antibody response to Hepatitis A virus.

URATE STASIS EXPOSURE (PRESUMPTIVE). This 3-year-old lorikeet was found dead. A small amount of hemorrhage was noted at necropsy on the right side of the skull and cerebellum. Marked urate stasis was present in the kidneys.

LISTERIOSIS SUPPURATIVE MENINGOENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male straw-colored fruit bat had a one-day history of moribund condition with hypoglycemia dehydration and azotemia. Supportive care was administered but resulted in cranial dependent edema. The bat became comatose and completely unresponsive and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy showed white/tan foci throughout the liver and pale renal cortices.

MYCOTIC DERMATITIS EUTHANASIA PYLORIC GASTRITIS PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS. This 8-year-old male bullsnake had a history of skin lesions since October 2010 and was being treated with antibiotics. The snake also intermittently had episodes of “shaking”. A large mass near the cloaca was aspirated and round cells with criteria of malignancy were identified and the snake was humanely euthanized. Necropsy revealed a 1.2 cm raised ulcerated mass on the ventral body wall just cranial to the cloaca involving the skin and underlying musculature. A raised area was present on the ventrum approximately one-half of the body length and another area cranial to this on the right dorsal aspect of the body. Both of the masses were in the skin and subcutaneous tissue but did not penetrate the body wall. A darkened rough area of necrosis was noted within the smaller ventral mass. Pulmonary tissue was moist and floated in formalin.

CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION FATTY LIVER. This approximately 2-year/7-month-old male hedgehog was found dead in the morning. The keepers reported that the animal was fairly active the day before and ate some of the regular diet. The hedgehog was being treated for respiratory disease (increased respiratory depth and rate decreased appetite and activity). It seemed to improve with antibiotic therapy but became more severe again and the antibiotic was changed. The animal seemed to improve but was found dead two days later. At necropsy the hedgehog was in good body condition. The liver was enlarged pale yellow and floating in formalin.

LYMPHOMA BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT UROLITHIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 43-year-old male beaded lizard has been inappetent with muscle wasting for some time and then appeared to be refusing water and became lethargic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed lesions throughout the liver and renal disease possibly gout.

AMYLOIDOSIS ENTERITIS INANITION. This 8-year-old male pygmy marmoset was found moribund. Approximately 30% weight loss was noted over the past nine months. At necropsy the kidneys were enlarged. Abdominal and subcutaneous fat depots were absent.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE COLLAGEN NEVUS RENAL GOUT. This 9-year-old male quail had a left leg lameness. The leg was swollen and radiographs revealed osteophyte proliferation adjacent to the joints. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the kidneys were tan to gray.

HEPATITIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS. This 13-year-old male timber rattlesnake had a history of inactivity. Osteolytic and osteoproliferative lesions were noted in the midbody vertebrae. At necropsy the liver had firm irregular brown foci.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA RHABDOMYOLYSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This approximately 8-month-old rat is from a rat rescue facility and was in quarantine. It had previously been treated for lower respiratory tract disease. It died unexpectedly while anesthetized for an ovariectomy. The patient had been unstable throughout the entire procedure. Necropsy revealed bilateral pulmonary congestion.

CIRRHOSIS. This greater than 3-year-old female/spayed iguana has a history of elevated serum protein and phosphorus and decreased levels of uric acid and calcium. The animal also had a history of chronic abscess with anorexia and weight loss. Necropsy revealed enlarged kidneys and small white hepatic nodule.

EUTHANASIA CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 9-year/6-month-old male goat was humanely euthanized. It had a history of anorexia and progressive weight loss since the beginning of February 2003. The goat did not respond to treatment with antibiotics antiparasitics vitamins minerals and rumen transfaunation. The goat remained lethargic and weak. Exploratory laparotomy was performed. Ascites suspected microhepatica and edematous omental fat were all noted. At necropsy there was moderate to severe generalized seborrhea especially on the trunk. There was a 1.5 x 1 cm. healing wound on the left midthorax just lateral to the spine. The omental fat appeared edematous. The adrenal gland was cystic. The cortex and medulla were obliterated by cysts. The cysts contained a small amount of clear fluid. The liver appeared small and had pale white streaks on the capsular surface. On cut surface there were white streaks and a 2 x 1 cm. area of the right middle lung lobe. The liver lobe had a nutmeg appearance on cut surface. There was a moderate amount of gas and a large amount of ruminal fluid present. The abomasum was distended with firm partially digested ingesta. The duodenal mucosa appeared hyperemic. The distal ileum and cecum were filled with firm fecal balls. The dorsal two-thirds of both caudal lung lobes were hyperemic. There were 24 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the pericardial sac. Both kidneys had few 0.5-1 mm. subcapsular cysts. The left stifle had a partially eroded articular cartilage.

EUTHANASIA BILIARY CYSTADENOMA RENAL PAPILLARY CYSTADENOMA NEUROENDOCRINE TUMOR. This 14-year-old male leopard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of weakness in the hind end and had infected dewclaws bilaterally. At necropsy there was a 3 cm. scar in the area of the right shoulder. The left salivary gland was mildly enlarged. The thyroid was slightly enlarged. The right ventricular wall was thin. The lung lobes were pink with occasional 0.5 cm. white nodule. The liver was mottled red to dark brown with circular cystic nodules of various size that were filled with clear fluid and yellow bile fluid. Both kidneys were small with the right kidney smaller than the left. The caudal pole of the left kidney had a 3 cm. cyst filled with clear fluid.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA AND SCENT GLAND ASSOCIATED CELLULITIS ENDOCARDIOSIS WITH EPICARDIAL ADHESIONS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 10-year-old female copperhead was found dead with no recent medical problems. The snake appeared active the day before. There was a recent history of surgery to the tail for impacted scent glands. The snake also had a history of lipemia and green serum. Necropsy revealed bilateral swelling of the tail caudal to the vent. Two areas of scabbing in the previous incision site were noted. All internal tissues around the scent gland were bruised and there appeared to be cellulitis in the proximal aspects of the tail distal to the cloaca. Fat pads appeared adequate. Numerous white structures were present throughout the lung. Some areas of the lung were dark red and some were bright red. Lesions were noted on the outside surface of the heart. A pale area was noted in the spleen and the pancreas seems slightly pale and thickened. The liver was mottled pale and fatty and had a rough external texture. Streaking was noted throughout both kidneys.

Coelomic cavity: Mesothelial proliferation with yolk aggregates (suggestive of yolk coelomitis) Liver: Moderate melanomacrophage center hyperplasia Comments The histologic findings were most consistent with a florid mesothelial proliferation within the coelomic cavity and covering the surface of multiple coelomic organs. The presence of yolk associated with the areas of mesothelial proliferation was suggestive of an underlying yolk coelomitis. Yolk coelomitis is a well-recognized problem and a significant cause of death in captive adult female lizards; particularly Fiji Island Iguanas (see Stacy et al; J Zoo Wildl Med. 2008 Jun;39(2):161-9.Yolk coelomitis in Fiji Island banded iguanas (Brachylophus fasciatus).The proliferative mesothelial cell population was considered to be a reactive response to free intracoelomic yolk based on the signalment (mature female). The basis for the florid mesothelial response is not known; however it is thought to be influenced by the volume of yolk present ant the chronicity of coelomitis. Jennifer Lamoureux; D

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE BACTERIAL PYELONEPHRITIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male warthog presented with rapid weight loss over a three week period coinciding with a significant drop in environmental temperatures. Dietary increases were implemented but weight loss continued. Thirty-six hours prior to death the animal presented with acute paresis and was having difficulty standing up. The animal developed cardiac arrest while being examined. Necropsy revealed larger than expected urinary bladder that was difficult to express. Multiple small stones that were dark brown to black were found. Stones were in the urethra proximal to the pelvic flexure.

Uterus: Moderate cystic endometrial hyperplasia; adenomyosis; moderate mucometra; and moderate suppurative endometritis Ovaries: Multiple corpora lutea and follicles Cervix and vagina: Moderate squamous metaplasia with severe ulcerative vaginitis Comment: The most severe inflammation was in the area of the vagina. The uterine lesions were less inflammatory; but there was prominent adenomyosis and neutrophils largely contained within the endometrial stroma. A specific cause for the severe vaginitis was not apparent. Uterine lesions are common in big cats which are cycling and do not conceive or which are treated with some contraceptives. Interestingly; the endometrial epithelium in this animal was not typical of a diestral or progestational epithelium; but more suggestive of an estrogenic stimluation. Similarly; the marked keratinization and squamous metaplasia of the cervix was more suggestive of an estrogenic stimulus. Follicle were prominent; but it is difficult to ascertain whether they were long-standing or not in a necropsy sample. Adrenal or other hormonally active neoplasia might also be a source of estrogen. Intromission may also be a cause of vaginitis; though no sperm were seen in any sections. This animal's tissue and data will be a part of the AZA Reproductive Health Surveillance Program

TOXOPLASMOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female red kangaroo had a one week history of anorexia lethargy dyspnea and ataxia and was treated with antibiotics. Prior to death the kangaroo had increased dyspnea and was in lateral recumbency and unable to rise. Radiographs revealed a mildly enlarged heart and ultrasound revealed a mild amount of pericardial fluid. The kangaroo became stressed when supplemental oxygen was discontinued and developed respiratory arrest. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mottled dark lungs straw colored fluid in the pleural cavity reddened pancreas pericardial effusion and a gastric ulcer.

LYMPHOMA CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA URINARY NEMATODIASIS (TRICHOSOMOIDES CRASSICAUDA) EUTHANASIA. This 9-month-old female rat presented with acute dyspnea radiographs identified a thoracic mass and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 3 cm. brown firm mass associated with the right and left caudal pulmonary lobes.

ENTERITIS HEPATITIS SHOCK. This 15-year-old male parrot was recently introduced to the free flight aviary. The bird suffered some intraspecies aggression and was treated for minor wounds. The animal was found dead the following morning. At necropsy the bird was thin with no internal fat stores. Numerous superficial wounds were present on the right wing.

NORMAL REPRODUCTIVE TRACT. This 5-year-old female greater kudu had a several month history of gradual weight loss and poor haircoat. Blood testing of a herdmate was suggestive of copper deficiency. This animal was placed on a high calorie diet with copper supplementation but its condition decompensated and following immobilization examination revealed dehydration and anemia in addition to a thin haircoat that epilated easily and alopecia with scabbed skin in the axillary regions. The animal recovered from anesthesia but never stood and was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed emaciation mild dental points on the arcades multiple mucosal ulcerations on the hard palate near the molars froth in the distal trachea and lower airways edema in the left lung and with the exception of diffuse marked acute congestion in the right lung. A moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid with a large clot was present in the pericardial sac and petechiae were noted in both ventricles and the atria with extension through the myocardium and into the endocardium. The liver was small and slightly firm and the gallbladder was filled with normal appearing bile. Crushed rocks were in the abomasum and a locally extensive focus of erythema was in the mucosa on the ventral aspect of the abomasum. Two focal mucosal hemorrhages were noted in the pylorus and blood-tinged liquid fecal material was in the ileum. The jejunum had a 12 in. intussusception with entrapment of the spiral colon and the surrounding jejunum was dark with mucosal hemorrhage. The affected spiral colon was congested and had petechiae. The mesentery near the affected bowel had petechiae and ecchymoses. The adrenals had petechiae in the cortices. Adipose tissue was atrophic and gelatinous. Muscle mass was reduced and the marrow in the femurs was gelatinous. Multiple ecchymoses were noted in the connective tissues surrounding the kidneys. Pleural and abdominal cavities contained a moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC PULMONARY PASSIVE CONGESTION. This 13-year-old male golden lion tamarin was diagnosed with renal disease in August 2008. This condition was associated with progressive azotemia weight loss and poor body condition. Two days of hospitalization and supportive therapy were administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed poor condition with absence of fat slightly enlarged adrenal glands rough kidneys with cysts moderate dental disease and erosive plaques in the oral and lingual mucosa.

ASPERGILLOSIS ECTOPIC EGG BACTERIAL DERMATITIS. This 14-year-old female Humboldt penguin presented two weeks earlier with lethargy inappetence weight loss marked leukocytosis and a negative Aspergillus galactomannan test. Radiographs revealed respiratory disease and Aspergillus sp. was cultured from a tracheal wash. Supportive care was administered but regurgitation developed the bird became progressively weaker and was found dead. Necropsy revealed regurgitated material in the upper trachea numerous circular white foci throughout the lungs green spore-like growth in the air sacs a 3 cm. oval free-floating rubbery mass in the caudal coelom and small follicles in the ovary.

HERNIA WITH INTRALESIONAL ABSCESS/ECTOPIC EGG EUTHANASIA. This approximately 36-year-old female Chilean flamingo had a history of prolapsed cloaca and a mass on the abdomen on the inside of the right leg region. The bird had a history of dystocia and a right-sided flank hernia that contained gas and soft tissue densities. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a hernia of the body wall on the right side sealed with inflammatory tissue extending through the right rear limb fossa into the subcutaneous space over the proximal medial tibiotarsal bone. The capsule contains a small amount of dark red flocculent material and a full-sized necrotic egg. The uterus contains a full-sized but thin-walled egg that cannot be expressed manually and the distal uterus is dark purple swollen and edematous. A small yolk is present in the proximal uterus. The cloaca is prolapsed exterior to the body wall with no entrapment of the ureters or distal colon. The ureters are distended with urates.

CATARACT. This 14-year-old male leiothrix had a history of mature cataract in the left eye with associated blepharospasm. The animal died while being restrained for euthanasia. Necropsy revealed a diffusely yellow liver.

RENAL GOUT NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 13-year-old male chuckwalla had a short duration of anorexia and weight loss and blood work revealed renal disease. The body was inadvertently frozen prior to necropsy. At necropsy the kidneys were grossly enlarged.

BACTERIAL STOMATITIS/GLOSSITIS/SIALOADENITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA/DIC. This approximately 27-year-old male saki presented with progressive dyspnea due to swelling of the tongue face and laryngeal region. The animal became agonal and died despite therapy. Necropsy revealed bruising of the inguinal regions marked swelling of the throat and ventral mandibular region and soft tissues of the face dark yellow larynx with congested vessels irregular arytenoids congested lungs concentrically enlarged heart visceral congestion marked swelling of the tongue necrosis of the palatine mucosa ulcers on the tongue and white tracts and nodules involving the tongue and mandibular muscle.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female meerkat is the last of a group of 12 established over 10 years ago. This animal had been slowing down losing weight and showing general signs of geriatric decline. More recently she was lethargic and had increased respiratory rate and effort. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed edema in the subcutis along the trunk. A small amount of fluid was in the abdomen. The thorax is filled with approximately 15-20 cc. of straw-colored fluid and minimal fat stores were noted. The heart was enlarged and yellow material was in the coronary arteries. Speckled throughout the lungs there are 1-2 mm. yellow nodules noted. The lungs were deep red to purple. Both adrenal glands appeared enlarged. The left kidney had dark discoloration at the caudal pole. The ovaries were quiescent. A 1.5 cm. firm tan spherical mass was in the wall of the uterus.

EUTHANASIA SPINDLE CELL SARCOMA MYOCARDIAL STEATITIS METRITIS PULMONARY EDEMA GINGIVITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 13.5-year-old female snow leopard had a history of a rapidly enlarging mass on the side of the face. The animal was humanely euthanized. A prior biopsy (G05-1941) revealed a low grade spindle cell sarcoma. At necropsy a 10.5 x 8.0 x 9.0 cm. mass extended from the ventral aspect of the orbit through the zygomatic arch and into the oral cavity. The maxillary premolars and molars had deep periodontal pockets extending into the retro-orbital tissue. The right nasal passage was partially occluded by the mass. Submandibular lymph nodes were bilaterally enlarged. A sequestrum of necrotic bone was present within the zygomatic arch. The mass appeared to invade the facial and trigeminal nerves and parotid duct. The mass extended to but did not appear to cross the cribriform plate. Lungs contained pinpoint to 0.5 cm. in diameter white to tan nodules in the caudal lobes.

CUTANEOUS MALIGNANT ROUND CELL TUMOR CHRONIC DERMATITIS ENCEPHALITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS. This 4-year-old male rabbit had been previously diagnosed with a malignant round cell tumor of the skin. Lesions recently recurred and the animal was anesthetized for a skin biopsy. The rabbit suffered cardiac arrest under isoflurane anesthesia. At gross necropsy the animal was thin and had multiple crusted and proliferative lesions in the skin between the scapulae right shoulder and inguinal area. The lungs were congested hemorrhagic and sank in formalin.

EUTHANASIA INANITION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS ENDOMETRITIS. This 16-year-old female bighorn was euthanized due to chronic weight loss and dental disease. At necropsy the animal was in very poor body condition with no subcutaneous or abdominal adipose tissue stores. Adhesions were present between the lung lobes and parietal pleura. Arteriosclerosis was noted in the great vessels. Marked dental attrition and tooth loss was present. Severe arthritis was present in the stifles and other joints. A large gelatinous mass was present in the lumen of the uterus.

NECROTIZING PROVENTRICULITIS. This 5-year-old male rhea died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed hemorrhagic clots in multiple areas of the intestines a dry chest cavity and abdominal cavity small amount of yellow pericardial fluid small liver lobes an oval abscess-like mass in the distal proventriculus with fistulas hyperemic kidney and lungs.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS INANITION. This 9-year-old snake recently underwent surgery for an abscessed gallbladder. Progressive anemia later developed and the animal was found dead. At necropsy muscles were pale. A firm pedunculated mass was present in the lung.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS DISSEMINATED INFLAMMATION (PROBABLE TOXOPLASMOSIS). This approximately 2-year-old female red kangaroo had been acquired from another zoo in March of 2011. Upon arrival she was noted to have a joey in the pouch. The joey had only recently emerged permanently from the pouch but was still nursing. The dam was noted to develop seizure-like episodes and was found dead by the time the keeper arrived at the exhibit. Necropsy revealed minimal fat stores and serous atrophy of remaining fat. All inguinal mammary and peripheral lymph nodes are enlarged and edematous. Mild bilateral serous pleural effusion and marked pericardial effusion were noted. Froth was in the trachea and both lungs were markedly edematous and failed to collapse. Diffuse fine white spotting was noted throughout the lungs and across the pleura. A single brown umbilicated lesion was present under the pleural surface on the medial edge of one lung lobe. Several short linear mineralized raised plaques are in the aorta and pulmonary artery near the valvular attachments. The brain was grossly swollen with flattening of the gyri and some mild herniation of the cerebellum through the foramen. The liver had some irregular pale tan patches of variable size and many of the hepatic vessels were dilated. The pyloric mucosa had some hemorrhage. A few small reddened or blackened areas in the small intestine were also noted. The kidneys were reddened and had tiny white foci in the cortex below the capsular surface. Numerous visceral lymph nodes were enlarged and edematous.

Liver: Multifocal to coalescing; hepatocellular carcinoma (presumptive) Rectum: Rectal prolapse Whole body: Icterus Comments: The cause of death of this animal is euthanasia. The most significant lesion is multiple nodules within the liver; which it is uncertain whether these nodules represent chronic inflammation or neoplastic process of the liver. Given the history of the background of the animal; infections with enterohepatic Helicobacter species (EHS) should be considered. In various mouse strains; infections with Helicobacter spp. are associated with inflammatory bowel disease; chronic hepatitis; and liver tumors. Histopathological examination of major internal organs is in progress; results will be released in the final report. Tuddow Thaiwong; DVM; PhD Liver: Carcinoma Lung: Multifocal metastatic carcinoma Skin at the left flank: Carcinoma Kidney: Mild pigmented nephropathy; Mild multifocal regenerative nephropathy Penis: Paraphimosis Metastatic carcinoma Paraphimosis Comment The most significant lesions in this animal are carcinomas within the liver; lung and skin at the left flank. Given the history of this mouse as part of a xenograft study of neoplastic cells; the presence of carcinoma may represent the proliferation of the injected neoplastic cells that are part of the xenograft study. Severe invasion of carcinoma within the liver likely led to hepatic failure and icterus. Helicobacter sp. infection could not be confirmed based on special staining. A test with higher sensitivity such as PCR detection is recommended to rule out an enterohepatic Helicobacter infection. Re-examination of the mouse revealed the previously diagnosed rectal prolapse to actually be paraphimosis. This is considered an indicidental finding in this case. Tuddow Thaiwong; DVM; PhD

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male pronghorn has had a steady decline over the past nine days with progressive lethargy anorexia fever and respiratory distress. The animal was given supportive therapy and antibiotics and was euthanized due to grave prognosis. At necropsy there was a small abrasion on the right dorsum petechiation of the epicardium small vegetative lesions on the atrioventricular valves portal effusion severe fibrinous adhesions throughout the thorax food material within the bronchi and necrosis of one of the pulmonary lobes.

Liver: Severe chronic necrotizing and suppurative hepatitis with granulation tissue and bile duct hyperplasia Ovaries: Bilateral cystic rete ovarii Uterus: Cystic endometrial hyperplasia; Endometrial carcinoma Comment: A cause of the hepatitis is not evident in the sections examined; however; bacterial culture of liver would be recommended if tissue is still in hand. A possible hepatic carcinoma underlying the inflammation cannot be ruled out in this case either; though this seems less likely. The ovarian tumors are common in guinea pigs; however; the uterine tumor is more unusual. This neoplasm does not appear to have metastasized at the time of necropsy.

GASTRIC ULCERATION GASTRIC VASCULOPATHY ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male tree kangaroo had a recent history of lethargy inappetence and possible renal disease. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed enlargement of the right heart small kidneys and gastric ulceration.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION GRANULOMATOUS PYLORIC GASTRITIS AND PORTAL HEPATITIS. This 6.5-year-old male rabbit was found dead in the morning. It had 2-3 days of subtle standoffish behavior. Necropsy identified a few points on the lingual aspect of the mandibular cheek teeth large tympanic stomach to 0.5 cm. thick at the pylorus mottled brown lungs and flocculent debris.

This 5-year-old male alpaca presented to MSU VMC on 4/15/2015 for pain and labored breathing after being found lateral that morning. Physical exam indicated decreased lung sounds ventrally on the left side; no gut sounds; and a firm; bloated abdomen. Exploratory abdominal surgery revealed a large gas- and ingesta-filled C1 compartment of the stomach. Excessive ingesta was removed surgically. Postoperatively; the animal's condition deteriorated; with the development of significant bilateral pleural effusion and diarrhea. The animal died on the evening of 4/15; and was submitted for necropsy on 4/17. Additional history is on file at DCPAH. An 81-kg male alpaca was examined on 4/17/2015. Autolysis was moderate. The animal had adequate subcutaneous and visceral fat stores and an overall body condition of 5/9. There were bilateral chest tubes and nasal cannulas. A closed ventral midline abdominal surgical incision extended 13 cm cranial and 7 cm caudal to the umbilicus. There was 1L of watery; translucent; serosanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity that had a urine-like smell; but the urogenital tract was intact. The thoracic cavity contained 500 mL of similar fluid with strands of free-floating fibrin. There were multifocal; random; pinpoint to 5-mm diameter petechiae and ecchymoses on the parietal pleura; visceral pleura; and epicardial surface along the coronary groove and the interventricular septum. The C1 compartment of the stomach was gas distended and had a 10-cm; linear; closed surgical incision along the left ventrolateral wall. The mucosal surface of C3 had numerous 2- to 5-mm diameter; white to tan; firm nodules and multifocal random petechia and ecchymoses; of which the largest measured 1 cm in diameter. The liver had an enhanced lobular pattern; and multiple (approximately 10) white to tan; firm nodules were multifocally randomly scattered throughout the liver parenchyma. The mucosal surface of the larynx was diffusely dark red. The esophagus contained a green to brown; 10-cm long; fairly formed but moist; dark green brown trichobezoar at the level of the tracheal carina. The esophageal mucosa in this region was diffusely dark red. No other significant lesions were observed. Whole body: hydroabdomen and hydrothorax/pleuritis; multifocal pleural and epicardial hemorrhages C3 stomach: multifocal mucosal nodules liver: multifocal nodules esophagus: trichobezoar; with associated mucosal hyperemia and hemorrhage Comments The hemorrhages and pleuritis are suggestive of septicemia. The noted firm nodules in the C3 stomach and liver are likely due to parasites. A final report is pending complete histologic evaluation; fecal parasite analysis; and aerobic culture of the liver and lungs. Erica Noland; DVM; MS Sections of brain; lung; trachea; thyroid gland; heart; spleen; liver; kidney; adrenal gland; stomach; intestine; and tongue are examined. There are multifocal; large organizing fibrin thrombi within hepatic; pulmonary; and esophageal blood vessels. In the liver; there is regionally extensive capsular and parenchymal fibrosis; with scattered multifocal hemorrhage. Thrombosed vessels are surrounded by variably dense rims of fibrosis. There are abundant intracytoplasmic accumulations of rhodanine- positive; coarse granular material within large numbers of primarily centrilobular to midzonal hepatocytes. There are multifocal centrilobular to random foci of hepatocellular necrosis admixed with small to moderate numbers of histiocytes containing rhodanine-positive granular material; lymphocytes; plasma cells; and fewer neutrophils. Perioportal and centrilobular regions are multifocally mildly expanded by similar cellular infiltrates. There is mild bile duct hyperplasia. The hepatic parenchyma is focally expanded by a region of mineralization associated with varying amounts of fibrosis and moderate numbers of macrophages. Similar foci of dystrophic mineralization are focally to multifocally present within the splenic parenchyma; the submucosa of C3; and the intestines; associated with various amounts of fibrosis and small to moderate numbers of macrophages. In the kidney; there are multifocal wedge-shaped areas of renal cortical coagulative necrosis characterized by hypereosinophilic tubular epithelial cells with fragmented nuclei (karyorrhexis). These regions are outlined peripherally by moderate congestion. Adjacent intact tubules multifocally contain bright eosinophilic proteinaceous material. The capsular surface is focally lined by plump reactive mesothelial cells and there are moderate aggregates of infiltrating lymphocytes. The lungs are mildly diffusely congested and alveolar spaces multifocally contain small numbers of histiocytes. The pleural surface is lined by Liver: Chronic fibrosing hepatitis; marked centrilobular to midzonal copper accumulation; mild bile duct hyperplasia; hepatic thrombosis; and multifocal dystrophic mineralization Kidney: Acute to peracute renal infarctions; multifocal tubular proteinosis; and lymphocytic serositis/peritonitis Lung: Focal pulmonary thrombus; mild alveolar histiocytosis; and pleural fibrosis Esophagus: Locally extensive transmural hemorrhage and edema Spleen/C3/Intestines: Multifocal dystrophic mineralization Chronic fibrosing hepatocellular necrosis and hepatitis; and multiorgan fibrin thrombi Comments The multifocal thrombosis is suggestive of disseminated intravascular coagulation; which may be related to chronic liver disease. The findings in the liver are both severe and chronic; and may be due to copper toxicosis; as suggested by excessive staining for copper in histologic sections. Quantification of the hepatic copper level is pending to confirm this; and an addendum report will be issued when results are available. The noted ischemic changes (i.e.; infarcts) in the kidney are likely due to thrombi not captured in the planes of sections examined. Thus; these renal lesions may also be associated with DIC. Effusions in both the thoracic and abdominal cavities may have been due to hypoproteinemia associated with liver disease; although total solids were apparently not low until after intravenous fluids administration. The multifocal dystrophic mineralization is consistent with old parasitic cysts. These foci are all similar in terms of chronicity--i.e.; similar degrees of fibrosis; mineralization; and mild macrophage infiltration; but with a lack of apparent parasites; suggesting the animal was treated for an infestation at one time. The locally extensive hemorrhage seen in the esophagus grossly and histologically was possibly associated with the trichobezoar identified at necropsy. Erica Noland; DVM; MS Copper-associated hepatitis Comments The quantitative copper amount of 525.05 ug/g dw in this case is consistent with copper toxicosis . A level this high is consistent with excessive dietary intake. Consultation with a veterinary nutritionist is recommended to address appropriate feeding for the remaining animals in the herd. There are several references to copper toxicosis in camelids in the published literature; including: Copper poisoning in four llamas. 1989. J Am Vet Med Assoc 195(7): 987-989. Erica Noland; DVM; MS
MANGEMENT EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 19-year-old male copperhead was euthanized due to contact with a Cryptosporidium positive animal. At necropsy kidneys were white to tan.
INANITION VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS ENTERITIS. This 12-year/8-month-old female ibis died. At necropsy it was emaciated. The spleen was small and pale.

PREDATION PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 5-year-old male mot mot was recently hospitalized and had been released into the aviary the previous day. The animal was found dead. At necropsy evidence of predation was noted with loss of skin and muscle from the right pectoral region and right leg. The abdominal cavity was exposed and some internal organs are missing.

OVIDUCTAL ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC SALPINGITIS COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 4-year-old female budgie died during restraint for a beak trim. At necropsy excessive fat depots were noted in the subcutis and abdomen. Frank blood was noted in the abdominal cavity. Multiple pale foci were present in the liver. The uterus was dilated and contained hemorrhagic fluid. A firm mass was present in the proximal uterus.

COELOMITIS TRAUMA (RAPTOR ATTACK). This 6-year-old pigeon was training when a hawk flew in and made contact with the pigeon. Necropsy revealed good postmortem condition a small wound on the right side of the neck a 4 cm. clot surrounding the trachea adequate adipose stores in the coelomic cavity prominent follicular activity in the ovary and no other gross abnormalities.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female bighorn sheep had a two-week history of coughing that progressed to openmouthed breathing. The animal was immobilized for therapy and on recovery had become severely dyspneic received supplemental oxygen but eventually was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Radiographs had revealed a bronchointerstitial pattern that seemed less severe than the clinical signs. Necropsy revealed good body condition a few abrasions in the skin a small amount of pleural fluid reddened cranial half of the tracheal mucosa and some fluid in the trachea dark discoloration of the right lung and the medial left lung which were palpably consolidated mild cardiac pallor and a mild amount of straw-colored free abdominal fluid. Hemorrhage was noted focally within the pancreas. The animal was pregnant with a female fetus and the amnion sac had multiple 4 mm. yellow generalized “lesions”.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA ANESTHETIC DEATH ENTERIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 24-year-old male black and white ruffed lemur was anesthetized for examination of lethargy anemia and a midabdominal mass. The animal died during anesthetic recovery. At necropsy the liver was multinodular with nodules up to 10 cm. in diameter. Similar nodules were observed in the mesentery and omentum with the largest omental nodule being 10 cm. with a region of rupture. The testicles were multifocally effaced by nodules similar to those seen in the liver and omentum.
Weight: 1700.0 g.  Euthanased. Poor condition. Dehydration. Hepatic congestion. Intususceptions. Sexually active. Alopecia on tail base (self inflicted?).

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS HEMOCROMATOSIS PSEUDOHERMAPHRODITISM. This 19-year-old male lemur was found dead. It presented lethargic the day prior to death. It was transported to the hospital and sedated for workup. It was noted to be about 8% dehydrated. Blood work revealed leukopenia hyperphosphatemia and glucosemia. Blood culture was taken. The lemur recovered from sedation but died overnight. At necropsy the lemur was in thin body condition with no fat deposits. The right maxillary canine was broken at the gingiva and had a deeply exposed root canal. There were nodular growths on the tricuspid valve. The lungs appeared wet. There was approximately 25 ml. of turbid viscous yellow fluid in the abdominal cavity. The serosa of stomach and intestines had multiple petechiae. There were multiple black pinpoint foci in intestinal mucosa. The liver was pale and there was fibrin attached to the capsule. The scrotal sac contained pus that had leaked from the abdominal cavity along the inguinal canals. The testes appeared smaller than in prior physical exams and were not firm but somewhat yielding on palpation. Dorsal to the urinary bladder there was a bicornuate tubular organ that appeared identical to female reproductive tract without ovaries. Sections of heart lung liver kidney spleen and peritoneal fluid were submitted for culture. Sections of heart liver and skeletal muscle were sent to the SSP pathologist. Sections of heart lung liver kidney and spleen were frozen for future use if needed.

HYPERTROPHIC GASTRITIS CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS BACTERIAL GASTRITIS. This 12-year-old male boa was found dead. At necropsy kidneys were pale with urate deposits. The stomach was markedly thickened with prominent rugae.

EUTHANASIA EPITHELIAL THYMOMA. This 15-year-old female bighorn was euthanized due to chronic dyspnea and the presence of a large mass in the left thorax identified radiographically. At necropsy approximately 60 cc. of serosanguineous fluid was present in the left hemithorax. The right cranial lung lobe was collapsed and purple. A 20 x 8 x 8 cm. lobulated cystic mass was present in the left cranial hemithorax. This mass displaces the right lung and heart and there were numerous adhesions to the pleura and adjacent lung lobes.

EUTHANASIA HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA PULMONARY EDEMA FLAGELLATED PROTOZOONOSIS. This 11.5-year-old female wallaby has a history of toxoplasmosis dental disease weight loss and ataxia. Recent examination showed marked anemia and ultrasonographic abnormalities in the spleen liver and left kidney. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy bilateral cataracts were noted. The spleen was enlarged and irregularly nodular. The lungs were edematous and sank in formalin. The middle liver lobe had a rounded friable center.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA UNILATERAL OTITIS MEDIA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 1-year-old female rat developed a chronic left head tilt and chronic respiratory disease received supportive care until the condition worsened and dyspnea prompted euthanasia for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a mucoid discharge multiple nodules containing mucus in the lungs and some mottled brown regions in the left lung rounded hepatic margins left ear bulla enlarged and discolored compared to the right with light green pasty material within the lumen of the left bulla.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ARTERIOSCLEROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 14-year-old male warthog was found dead. The animal had a history of weight loss and examination revealed systolic heart murmur cardiomegaly and subjectively dilated heart walls with decreased contractility. Cardiac treatments were initiated and the warthog gained some weight but would show periodic and transient inappetence and lethargy. The animal died shortly after being returned to its stall and fed for the evening. Necropsy revealed thin body condition approximately 500 ml. of clear straw-colored ascites in the abdominal cavity atrophic adipose stores the right naris partially occluded by ventrally deviated right tusk some streaky pallor in the epicardium and generalized cardiomegaly with substantially dilated and flabby left auricle and atrium moderate endocardiosis in the left atrioventricular valve and mild endocardiosis in the right atrioventricular valve absence of a pulp chamber in the right tusk (in radiographic images) worn incisors uneven wear in the molars congested liver dark pancreas digesta in the alimentary tract several cysts on the capsular surface of the right kidney mild renal asymmetry with the left kidney slightly smaller than the right and more rounded in shape. A 12 cm. cyst was noted in the caudal aspect of the left kidney which ruptured when the kidney was incised.
INANITION CUTANEOUS ABSCESS. This 8-month-old gecko was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy the long bones were pliable and fat deposits were not identified.

GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA BACTERIAL ESOPHAGITIS SEPTICEMIA COLITIS INANITION. This 12-year/3-month-old female boa was found dead. It had been pulled off exhibit on 3/27. It was thin and not eating. It was soaked in warm water. Two fecaliths were removed. At necropsy the boa was in thin to poor body condition. There were numerous 10-20 small 1-2 mm. tan raised foci on the serosal surface of the lung. Cultures of lung were performed. There was tan ingesta in the esophagus at the level of the heart. There was mild esophagitis with petechia. The stomach was empty. The colon contained a 2.5 cm. fecalith adhered to the mucosal surface. The gall bladder was full. There were minimal to nonexistent fat stores.

AMEBIASIS. This 3.5-year-old female Gila monster is the third of this species to die in the last three months. Necropsy revealed a pale liver three large follicles and several small reddened areas of the mucosa in the stomach.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS URATE STASIS. This 18-year-old wood duck of undetermined gender is one of five birds that died in a two-day period. One bird was obviously a traumatic episode and the other was possibly mycobacteriosis. Necropsy revealed thickened air sacs granulomas in the lungs and spleen and no other gross abnormalities.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS. This 7-year-old female sugar glider had been losing weight despite addition of more food. The glider was returned to the male the previous night and no aggression was observed. The animal was subsequently found dead. Necropsy identified somewhat thin body condition blood around the pouch two small masses protruding from the pouch pale liver and lungs congestion in the dorsal aspect of the right cranial pulmonary lobe extension of the pouch masses into the abdominal cavity and no other abnormalities.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This greater than 4-year-old female lemur had been anesthetized for eight minutes had poor muscle relaxation arrested and could not be recovered. Necropsy revealed little to no fat around the heart or in the omentum and no other gross lesions.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS NODULAR HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA LYMPHADENOPATHY ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 7-year-old female ferret was euthanized due to a suspected insulinoma and poor quality of life. At necropsy lymph nodes were enlarged and edematous. Kidneys had a finely nodular capsular surface.
juvenile. Weight: 8.6 g.  Open.  Poor condition.

CARDIOMYOPATHY CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE AMYLOIDOSIS BRONCHOPNEUMIA CESTODIASIS PANCREATIC ISLET FIBROSIS. This approximately 6-year/9-month-old male hyrax died. It presented the day prior to death as profoundly lethargic and thin. Treatment was administered. At necropsy the hyrax was cachectic. There was no subcutaneous fat present. The muscles masses were reduced. There was no intra-abdominal fat. There were two pie-shaped areas present on the right margin of the liver. They possessed arcs of 3-4 mm. and were a pale pink/brown. The liver had some cestodes in the sinuses of hepatic vessels. The ventral and lateral aspects of both lungs were firm. The tissue had a fibrous consistency and was red/brown. The pancreas seemed atrophic. Some of the tissue was relatively firm. There were cestodes associated with the pancreas. There may have been cavitation to the tissue in which the cestodes were present. Cestodes were also noted in portions of the duodenum.

BACTERIAL THYPHLITIS. This 4-month-old female rat was found minimally responsive and hypothermic. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy firm irregular nodules were present in the cecum.
NEPHRITIS GRANULOMATOUS AIR SACCULITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 4.5-year-old female duck was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

MACRORHABDUS PROVENTRICULAR GLAND DYSPLASIA BACTERIAL GRANULOMAS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITION EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old male budgie has a history of regurgitation lethargy and weight loss and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was muscle wasting and reddening of the esophagus and proventriculus.

TOXOPLASMOSIS STEATITIS. This 3-year-old male meerkat was found dead while under treatment for pneumonia. It had a history of being slightly off. One meerkat from the group died several days earlier from toxoplasmosis. There were mild equilibrium problems and was treated with clindamycin. At necropsy it was in good body condition. The lungs were purple wet and mottled with multiple pinpoint to 5 mm. firm white lesions. Lung tissue sank in 10% formalin. The heart appeared grossly enlarged with a small amount of fluid in the pericardial space. The liver had a mottled pattern. There was a layer of thick clear mucus on the mucosa of the stomach and duodenum. A small amount of stool was present in the large bowel. There was callous formation present at an old fracture site of the left femur. Lung was submitted for culture. Lung liver heart and brain were submitted for West Nile virus testing. Impression smears of brain and lung were performed. Brain kidney lung and liver were frozen for future use if needed.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS PNEUMONIA URATE STASIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS INANITION. This 19-year-old male monitor had a history of increasing lethargy. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the left kidney was enlarged and adherent to the body wall. The liver was small and firm.

GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male black-footed ferret had a one-month history of inappetence weight loss polyuria and polydyspnea. Renal values have been elevated for one year. A tooth extraction was performed three months ago. The animal developed renal failure one week ago received supportive care did not respond and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed renal asymmetry with the left greater than the right pitting and discoloration proximally enlargement of the left adrenal gland and segmentation into three fragments and multiple hepatic cysts.

PROVENTRICULAR DILATATION DISEASE. This 10-year-old male hyacinth macaw had a two week history of lethargy depression and increased water intake. The bird died and necropsy revealed a large amount of ingesta in the proventriculus and ventriculus.
Euthanasia; cataract right eye; dehydration.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE IDIOPATHIC SEIZURE DISORDER INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS PROBABLE PULMONARY MITES EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old female baboon had a history of chronic seizures of nine months duration. Medicinal compliance was irregular and seizures increased in frequency. Ten days prior to death the animal had a dog sitting posture and difficulty ambulating. Hind leg paresis worsened the animal did not respond well to treatment and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition bright yellow adipose tissue and some clear multifocal bullae throughout the pulmonary fields. A few small clear cysts were in the hepatic lobes. The mesentery was focally adhered to the serosal surface of the uterus which was enlarged and firm on palpation occupying approximately 95% of the pelvic inlet. The bladder was firmly adhered to the uterus. On cut surface the uterine mucosa appeared markedly hyperplastic with an attenuated luminal tract.

ULCERATIVE ENTERIIS SUSPECT SEPSIS. This 1-year and 8-month-old male black-tailed prairie dog was found dead. At necropsy there are several excoriations on the tail. Abdominal fat was scant. A right cranial pulmonary lobe was dark red. There was an intussusception without associated inflammation within one section of jejunum.
adult. Weight: 3530 g.  Visceral gout.  Splenitis.  Hepatomegaly.  Renomegaly.  Pulmonary congestion.

AMYLOIDOSIS INTESTINAL ACANTHOCEPHALIDS INANITION. This approximately 5-year/7-month-old female duck was found dead in its enclosure. It had a history of slow continuous weight loss of undetermined cause. At necropsy there was little subcutaneous fat. There was minimal wasting of the pectoral muscles. There were numerous small helminths within the small intestine. These worms were partially embedded in the wall of the intestine and were difficult to extract. Under the microscope the anterior end of this helminth was covered with small spines (acanthocephalan). The liver appeared enlarged and friable. The edges were slightly rounded. The kidneys were pale.

TRAUMA DROWNED CATARACT ESOPHAGITIS. This 8-year-old female Bali mynah was found dead in the pond with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed waterlogged body no fluid in the oral cavity or nares good body condition adequate abdominal fat stores yellow tinge to the fat subjectively enlarged great vessels diffusely pale yellow mottled liver and hepatomegaly and mottled pink spleen with splenomegaly.

GRANULOMATOUS DERMATITIS VASCULAR NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male brown pelican has a history of suspected fungal infection and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged spleen pale kidneys darkened intestine and recurrence of oral masses at previous surgical sites.

SPONDYLOSIS MEDULLARY FIBROSIS AND BONE RESORPTION PANCREATIC GRANULOMA EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male snake had a history of chronic weight loss inappetence abnormal movement and regurgitation. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with little epaxial musculature bilateral cataracts teeth in the oral cavity worn to the gingiva a 1.5 cm. round yellow cystic structure at the base of the heart several 2-5 mm. round green firm masses on the surface of the liver spondylosis involving approximately 70% of the vertebral column and no other abnormalities.

SHOCK STRESS PRESUMED HEMORRHAGE GRANULOCYTIC ENDOPHTHALMITIS. This 14-year-old male roseate spoonbill was found listless after a large rainstorm. The animal died at the initiation of treatment. At necropsy the animal had damage to the left eye superficial abrasion on the keel slight opacity to the air sacs slight reddening to the intestinal tract slight enlargement to the kidneys and subjective thinning of the heart walls.

INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS ENTERITIS GRANULOMATOUS NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS. This 7-year-old male alligator lizard had a two day history of lethargy and was found dead. At necropsy the lungs were hemorrhagic and contained purulent material.

GOUT SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION EROSIVE VENTRICULUS WITH CLOSTRIDIUM-LIKE BACTERIA. This 15-year-old female penguin initially presented with inappetence and weight loss and blood work revealed leukocytosis and Aspergillus titers were suggestive of infection. The bird had been treated with itraconazole after being moved to a temporary holding facility for exhibit repairs. A scheduled recheck showed severe weight loss with severe uricacidemia but resolution of leukocytosis. The bird presented acutely dyspneic one day following a recheck examination and died in the oxygen cage shortly after presentation. Necropsy revealed pale kidneys and numerous small flat gray plaques in the right abdominal air sac. A relative small accumulation of tenacious mucoid material was in the larynx and there were what appeared to be two small ulcers in the ventriculus.

ANEMIA COAGULOPATHY CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE. This 4-year-old lorikeet was found dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition with no signs of trauma. The viscera were pale the proventriculus was distended with soft liquid black/brown material and the wall of the proventriculus was thin.
NEPHROSCLEROSIS ARTERITIS NODOSA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old male Norway rat was euthanized due to advanced degenerative joint disease.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS ENTRAPMENT COCCIDIOSIS CESTODIASIS LINGUAL PAPILLOMA. This 3.5-year-old female rabbit had been released into predatory proof hardening pen earlier in the fall and this animal was subsequently found deceased in a live trap. The hind limbs of the rabbit were sticking through the mesh of the cage and wounds were visible in the inguinal area. Necropsy revealed thin body condition luxated right coxofemoral joint several 1 mm. white foci on the pleural surface that extend into the lung on cut surface several 3-4 mm. white nodules in the mesentery prominent dark brown mesenteric lymph nodes mucosal reddening in the stomach and a small amount of mucoid ingesta in the stomach. Normal feces were in the colon.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE BILATERAL RETINAL DEGENERATION AND DETACHMENT LINGUAL FIBROSARCOMA MAMMARY AND PULMONARY TUMORS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female Virginia opossum was being treated for several months for cardiorespiratory disease and had a grade IV heart murmur. The opossum also had an ulcerated tongue mass that was progressing (hyperplastic stomatitis G14-5668). Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 0.5 cm. mass present on the right side of the nose multiple small cystic masses in the skin of the pouch in the region of the mammary gland slightly enlarged right ventricular chamber dark discoloration and loss of bone integrity in the caudal nasal turbinates a few small cream-colored masses in the pulmonary parenchyma multiple pinpoint light-colored lesions in the parenchyma of the liver and a few small cystic areas in both ovaries.

GOUT AXONAL DEGENERATION EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female green tree python had problems with chronic colonic impaction and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a markedly distended gallbladder markedly distended colon (filled with gas) multiple coalescing green to black areas on the mucosal surface a 2-3 cm. irregularly shaped tan to white stone in the caudal portion of the colon many abnormal bone curvatures in the spine and multiple tan to white botryoid areas in both kidneys.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE CORD COMPRESSION UROCYSTITS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male meerkat presented one day prior to death with a distended colon and urinary bladder. The bladder was catheterized and yielded hemorrhagic urine with minimal bacteria or white blood cells noted. Blood work revealed mildly elevated blood urea nitrogen creatinine and potassium but otherwise was within normal limits. This animal had previous received treatment for severe thoracolumbar spondylosis and right coxofemoral arthritis. Minimal changes were noted overnight and the bladder was again severely distended the following day. Urine could be expressed with digital pressure but no voluntary urine or feces were passed. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition and good postmortem condition. The bladder was distended with dark yellow translucent urine the mucosa was purple multiple discrete mildly raised circular dark purple to black lesions up to 3 mm. in diameter covered the entire mucosal surface. The colon was moderately distended with firm feces that filled the majority of the pelvic inlet and mild reddening was in the colonic mucosa. A focus of white discoloration was in the right kidney approximately 1 cm. in greatest dimension. Moderate roughening of the right femoral head was noted and severe spondylosis and fusion of the lumbar vertebrae were present.

METABOLIC BONE DISEASE RHINITIS. This captive bred female greater than 1-year-old frog was one of several frogs that died from the same enclosure. Some of the frogs exhibited neurologic signs prior to death. The only husbandry change recently made involved a change from dechlorinated water to regular tap water after the first three frogs died. After the 4th and this frog died the drinking water was replaced with dechlorinated water again. At necropsy the ventral abdomen and legs were erythematous. The leg muscles were thick but softer than normal. The spleen appeared hemorrhagic. There were multifocal ecchymotic hemorrhages on the liver. The kidneys were bilaterally swollen and hemorrhagic. The bladder was empty.

BUMBLEFOOT AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 26-year-old female flamingo was found dead on exhibit with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed probable amyloid in the kidneys bumblefoot darkened lungs and gut full gallbladder and cystic follicles in the reproductive tract.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EPICARDIAL FIBROSIS THYROID ADENOMATOUS HYPERPLASIA. This 16-year-old male sheep was euthanized due to chronic arthritis. At necropsy white streaks were present in the myocardium. Small nodules were identified on the surface of the spleen. The kidney had irregular foci of scarring. Degenerative changes were noted in the joints.

EMACIATION STRESS. This 7-month-old female captive bred red panda had a one day history of illness and died spontaneously. She had been the smallest panda of the litter and was noted to be thin approximately ten days prior to death. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the stomach and intestines normal stool in the distal colon no subcutaneous fat thin body condition and pale mucous membranes.

EUTHANASIA RENAL LEPTOSPIROSIS CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 3-year-old female rock hyrax was humanely euthanized. It had acute renal failure that was nonresponsive to treatment. The rock hyrax had a markedly elevated Leptospira grippo titer (1:51200) seven days prior to euthanasia. At necropsy the hyrax was in moderate nutritional body condition. There was mild thoracic subcutaneous edema and marked abdominal distention. There were multifocal 2-3 mm. flat dermal lesions on the ventrum. The abdomen contained approximately 250 ml. of serosanguineous fluid. The thorax contained approximately 50 ml. of straw colored fluid. Cultures and fluid analysis were done. There were multifocal 2 mm. to 1.5 cm. irregularly shaped firm white/tan structures embedded in the mesentery and omentum. The trachea and bronchi contained a moderate amount of clear fluid. The lungs were edematous and oozed hemorrhagic fluid on cut section. There were moderate amounts of straw colored pericardial effusion. There was vascular congestion of the entire gastrointestinal tract. There was distention of the cecum and large intestine. The uterus was firm and irregularly thickened. It had multiple small cysts on the serosal surface. The endometrium was thickened and hemorrhagic. The lumen contained a small amount of turbid hemorrhagic fluid. The adrenals were bilaterally enlarged.

SEIZURE DISORDER EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male squirrel monkey had a history of seizures. An MRI performed six months prior to death revealed no abnormalities. Seizures were well controlled with high doses of phenobarbital and zonisamide but social problems in the group of seven squirrel monkeys resulted in frequent injury and the animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple scabs and scars from previous injuries and no other gross lesions.

According to the history provided; this 6.5-year-old; male Chinchilla died on 12/8/16 after traveling in a van to an educational event. The animal had been previously healthy. A screech owl in the van was also found dead; but all other animals were unaffected. Additional history is on file. A 545.2-g male Chinchilla was submitted to the DCPAH for necropsy on 12/9/16. Autolysis was mild. There was abundant subcutaneous and visceral fat; and body condition score was 7/9. The oral mucous membranes and sclerae were diffusely pale pink. The lungs were multifocally patchy dark red to light pink; and all lung sections floated in formalin fixative. The liver diffusely exhibited a centrilobular pattern. The stomach contained small amounts of green semisolid material. The small intestines contained small amounts of light green liquid. There were 50-60 formed fecal pellets within the distal colon. The cecum was filled with small amounts of dark green semisolid material. There were no other significant gross necropsy findings. No significant gross lesions Comment: The cause of death of this Chinchilla is unknown based on gross necropsy alone. Appropriate tissues have been saved for further testing or other ancillary testing prove warranted. Histopathologic examination of major organs is in progress; and results will be released in a final report. Wallaya Manatchaiworakul; DVM Representative sections of cerebrum; cerebellum; heart; lung; spleen; small intestine; large intestine; kidney; liver; pancreas; lymph node; urinary bladder; tongue and bone marrow were examined. Autolysis in all organs was mild to moderate. In the heart; there was mild multifocal myocyte degeneration characterized by swelling of some myocytes; atrophy of others; and occasional loss of cross-striations. In occasional areas; there was loss of myocytes and replacement with thin trabeculae of fibrous tissue; causing mild expansion of the interstitium. In sections of lung; there was multifocal congestion; perivascular interstitial edema and mild peribronchiolar lymphoid hyperplasia. Multifocally; there were small aggregates of lymphocytes and plasma cells surrounding small and medium-sized arteries. In some areas; alveolar spaces contained small numbers of histiocytes and strands of fibrin. Hepatocytes were mildly vacuolated throughout the liver. Multiple areas of the liver were mildly congested. There were no other lesions in the sections of other organs examined. 1) Heart: Focal; minimal to mild myocardial degeneration; atrophy; and interstitial fibrosis 2) Lung: Multifocal pulmonary congestion; perivascular interstitial edema Please see Comments Comments: Although there was mild myocardial degeneration and interstitial fibrosis; the significance of this finding is uncertain. The pulmonary congestion appears to be acute; and may be related to stress or may be linked to heart disease. There was no microscopic evidence of an infectious etiology or a significant inflammatory process. No further diagnostic testing is pending for this case. Wallaya Manatchaiworakul; DVM

SCLEROSING PERITONITIS AND LYMPHADENITIS UROCYSTITIS. This 9-year-old male bat was hospitalized for two weeks to receive supportive care for emaciation. The bat had a fair appetite but failed to gain weight and had soft and reduced fecal production. The animal was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed emaciation moderate dental wear congested gingiva mottled and congested liver cream-colored fluid within the lumen of the stomach and small intestine plicated intestines from the duodenum to the colon surrounding a 1 cm. firm cream to white mass at the root of the mesentery and multiple 1 mm. firm cream nodules were present along the mesenteric border of the intestine. The kidneys were pale.

EUTHANASIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS STRESS EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS. This 6-year-old female hedgehog was humanely euthanized. It had not been eating and had lost approximately 50% of its body weight. It was not responding to treatment.

COLONIC GRAVEL IMPACTION SEPSIS. This 46-year-old male desert tortoise was found dead on exhibit with no prior signs of illness. There is a history of gravel ingestion in the exhibit. This animal had been treated monthly to assist passage of gravel. Postmortem radiographs revealed a large amount of gravel in the intestine. Necropsy revealed absence of intracoelomic fat pulpy liver dark lungs yellow subcapsular material in the kidneys congested bladder wall and food in the stomach. The wall of the large intestine was congested and hemorrhagic in areas of gravel impaction.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS HEAD TRAUMA. This 1-year-old male gerenuk ran into a wall at the end of the day fractured the right horn at the base and had severe ocular damage with neurologic signs and was in lateral recumbency. Supportive care was administered with slight improvement and then deteriorated. A large subcutaneous swelling was noted at the top of the head. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large urinary bladder containing dark urine congested lungs with free blood in the thorax two fractures over the top of the right eye socket a 0.5 cm. linear fracture and a 1.5 cm. wedge fracture displaced ventrally into the back of the eye from the horn growth plate and adjacent bone. A 6 cm. blood clot was found in the subcutis of the top of the head. The back of the right eye was macerated. Some edema was in the upper one-half of the neck.

ASPERGILLOSIS. This 15-year-old male ringed teal was found dead and had no prior history of illness. Necropsy revealed numerous copepods on the surface of the body and adequate body condition. The right lung was gray and the left lung was obliterated by mycotic granulomas. A similar granuloma was present ventral to the kidneys. Male reproductive tract was identified.

CHRONIC AIR SACCULITIS PROVENTRICULITIS SHOCK. This 16-year-old male teal was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy cataracts were present in both eyes. The liver was enlarged nodular and firm.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS SEPTIC SHOCK. This approximately 6-year-old female python was found dead in its enclosure. It was noted to have abdominal distention and was believed to be “yolking up”. At necropsy the caudal coelomic cavity was distended due to fluid retention. The stomach was devoid of ingesta. There was no digesta present within the small intestine. The kidneys and ureters were distended with urates. The genital tract contained many lumps and within the caudal coelomic cavity was adhered together and contained pockets of fibrinous adhesions with clear fluid and liquid necrotic debris. Overall the carcass appeared dehydrated. Sections of kidney were frozen for future use if needed.

PULMONARY TUMORS ISLET CELL TUMOR PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA BILATERAL GLAUCOMA CORNEAL DYSGENESIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 14-year-old female Polish rabbit had multiple longstanding medical issues and a recent decrease in appetite and weight loss. The animal had a palpable reproductive mass and cystic mammary gland changes ocular issues that included cataracts corneal ulcers chronic ocular discharge and enlarged glands in the eyelids and a presumed gastrolith or urolith were also being monitored radiographically. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a dry discharge around the eyes mature cataracts a 0.5 cm. scar in the left cornea and a smaller scar in the right cornea. The eyelids were thickened. Mild diffuse edema was in the lungs and multiple firm tan nodules were noted throughout the pulmonary parenchyma. The heart was globoid and had a 4 mm. pale region on the epicardium of the apex of the left ventricle. Nodular changes were in the left and right atrioventricular valves and a small tan nodule was noted along the vena cava near the right adrenal gland. The liver had multiple cystic structures throughout the parenchyma and along the dorsal caudal border of the liver. Multiple 2 mm. in diameter tan regions were noted throughout the hepatic parenchyma. A 2 cm. long thick white band of tissue was present within the cecum along the mesenteric side. The stomach was filled with normal ingesta but the distal gastric contents were mildly dry and compact. Intestinal contents appeared normal. Kidneys were diffusely pale. The right ovary was enlarged and pink. No normal follicular structure was seen. The left ovary was enlarged and firm. A 1.5 cm. cyst was present on the proximal vaginal wall. All mammary glands were enlarged. Brownish-yellow fluid was noted on cut surface of the mammary tissue. An old fracture was in the right radius and ulna. A 1.5 cm. mineralized structure was adhered to the dorsal surface of the distal vagina (between the colon and vagina. Two similar smaller structures were noted in the omentum caudal to the stomach.
MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VASCULAR ECTASIA RENAL HEMORRHAGE. This 9-year-old female bat was found dead. At necropsy the liver was markedly enlarged but otherwise normal.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PARATHYROID ADENOMA LEIOMYOMA (SKIN) NODULAR HEPATIC HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 19-year-old female potbellied pig had a history of chronic arthritis and neoplasia in the perianal region. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy round firm masses were present adjacent to the anus. Marked tooth wear was noted. A 9 cm. round raised mass was present in the liver. A pedunculated mass containing gritty white material was present on the spleen. Kidneys were pitted and pale. Marked erosions were noted in multiple joints.

PODODERMATITIS AMYLOIDOSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATITIS OSTEOMYELITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 30-year-old female flamingo was found dead in the flamingo pool. At necropsy the animal was in poor nutritional condition with minimal adipose tissue depots and little food in the digestive tract. Moderate bumblefoot lesions were present on both footpads. Ulcerated skin was overlying the hocks which may have penetrated to the underlying tendon. The heart had prominent dilation of the left ventricle with thickening of the left A/V valve. Multiple raised yellow plaques were present on the surface of the aorta.
