CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS EMACIATION ASPIRATION. This 8-year-old male giant eland was found dead in its enclosure in the morning. The animal had a long history of intermittent and then continuous diarrhea with wasting developing in 2009. Coronavirus was seen by electron microscopy in the stool but since that time no further pathogens or causes for the diarrhea could be found. Numerous attempts at treatment were made with little success. Necropsy revealed cachexia diarrhea atrophy of muscle thin blood organ pallor ruminal distention with villous atrophy pulmonary congestion bilateral myopathy involving the adductor muscles mesenteric lymphadenomegaly abdominal and pericardial effusions small liver and atrophy of fat.

SARCOCYSTOSIS. This approximately 2.5-year-old violet-necked lory was found dead and is from a building in which several lories and turacos have recently died. Necropsy of this bird revealed an enlarged spleen.

EUTHANASIA FIBROSARCOMA (MUSCLE) URATE STASIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 8-year-old female pit viper had a history of chronic weight loss and a tumor on the cervical spine. The animal was humanely euthanized.

CHRONIC ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS. This 17-year-old female ibex had a history of chronic lameness and was scheduled for euthanasia but was found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin. Both carpi were hyperextended.

INANITION METASTATIC MINERALIZATION VISCERAL GOUT. This 6-year/7-month-old female whistling duck was found dead in its enclosure. It had a history of being found depressed lethargic and had weight loss. It was given supportive care but subsequently died. At necropsy there was little to no body fat and slight muscling. There were white plaques noted on the abdominal air sac. The lungs were diffusely congested. The proventriculus had serosal white stippling. The kidneys were pale tan and had a firm granular consistency.
NA

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female lory presented with depression and lethargy of eight weeks duration received supportive care but developed neurologic signs that suggested peripheral vestibular syndrome. Blood work revealed leukocytosis elevated hepatic enzymes and bile acids and low protein and albumin. The bird developed ataxia and a pronounced head tilt and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified a yellow friable liver with rounded edges and enlarged bile ducts. The heart was subjectively enlarged.
CERVICAL FRACTURE SHOCK. This 1-year-old male gerenuk ran into a fence. The animal suffered a cervical fracture and died. At necropsy fracture of distal C1 with luxation of C1-2 was identified.

SYSTEMIC AMYLOIDOSIS RELATED TO BUMBLEFOOT HOCK INJURY AND INFECTION. This approximately 16-year-old male flamingo had a history of chronic left hock injury with a methicillin resistant Staphylococcus cultured from a hock aspirate. The bird deteriorated and died spontaneously despite supportive care and antibiotic therapy. Gross necropsy revealed pectoral muscle atrophy an orange and waxy liver and spleen hemorrhage in the keel and right pectoral muscle bumblefoot and chronic hock arthritis and tenosynovitis with clots of fibrinonecrotic debris and tissue necrosis.

UROLITHIASIS OBSTRUCTION HYDRONEPHROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male pygmy goat had a history of dysuria with distended bladder and radiodense areas in the urethra at the point of the pelvic outlet and in the distal urethral process. A urinary catheter could not be passed. Attempts at perineal urethrostomy were unsuccessful and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild right-sided hydronephrosis and marked left-sided hydronephrosis. Stones were noted in the renal glomeruli bladder and urethra. The bladder wall was markedly inflamed. Lungs were congested.

HEPATOCELLULAR LIPIDOSIS. This 4-year-old female prairie dog was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy pinpoint to 1 mm. white spots were present in the liver. The liver floated in formalin. Alopecia was noted over the inguinal area.

RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 5.5-year-old female black-footed ferret arrived at the zoo one month earlier and had a history of mammary cancer with ovariectomy performed in January of 2016 at the previous facility. Two weeks prior to death recurrent mammary tumor and renal failure were diagnosed. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed enlarged kidneys with dark infarct-like lesions and cortical spaces. Lungs were dark red. Uterus was intact. The heart was enlarged (intracardiac euthanasia needle).

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS GLOMERULAR LIPIDOSIS ENTEROCOLITIS. This 3-year/9-month-old female toad was humanely euthanized. The entire group of five animals was culled to screen for mycobacteriosis. Historically they were in contact with an animal that was suspect for tuberculosis based on histopathology. Tissues were submitted for mycobacterial culture.

EMACIATION. This approximately 4-year-old male screech owl was found dead. It had seemed lethargic a few days prior to death. It was eating but had lost 20 gm. over a two day period. The carcass appeared to have been frozen prior to necropsy. The pancreas appeared inflamed but no other gross abnormalities were detected.

AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female black-footed ferret had a history of inappetence weight loss and chronic renal disease. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition crusts present on the distal aspect of the tail tip little intra-abdominal fat empty stomach aside from some black granular material several cystic regions in the liver filled with what appeared to be bile slightly reddened pancreas pale tan kidney with areas of infarction slightly mottled pancreas and no other abnormalities.
EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL OSTEOARTHROSIS. This greater than 2-year-old female rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It had diffuse spinal fusing.

ASPERGILLOSIS PNEUMONIA AIR SACCULITIS HEPATITIS ESOPHAGEAL CAPILLARIASIS PROVENTRICULITIS BACTERIAL RHINITIS INANITION. This 6-year-old male duck was found dead. The animal was thin. At necropsy a featherless patch was noted on the mid dorsum with a small abrasion at the center. A red nematode was identified in the trachea. Caudal thoracic air sac was thickened with yellow caseous material and fungal mattes. Multiple white nodules were present in the lung.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS GRANULOMATOUS PARABRONCHITIS. This 10-year-old female motmot was apparently normal in the morning and was found dead an hour later. Necropsy revealed no obvious abnormalities.

POLYCYSTIC KIDNEYS. This approximately 1-year-old male junglefowl was found dead on the grounds. It was a free roaming bird. At necropsy there was deep bruise of the right pectoral muscle. The air sacs appeared cloudy. The right lung was congested. The spleen was enlarged and congested. The parathyroid glands appeared enlarged. The jejunal mucosa was hemorrhagic. The kidneys were enlarged congested and granular.

ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA (MYCOBACTERIA SCREEN). This approximately 5-year-old ocellated turkey is one of a group of eight two of which died with lesions typical of mycobacteriosis. The remaining birds were euthanized. This bird had no gross lesions.

TOOTH ROT ABSCESS WITH MENINGITIS. This 7-year-old female wallaby had a history of tooth root abscess received supportive care but deteriorated and examination revealed a retrobulbar abscess with draining tract from the caudal maxilla. The animal recovered from anesthesia but remained in lateral recumbency and died 10 hours later. Necropsy revealed decreased body condition with minimal adipose stores some areas of alopecia over the shoulder and hip a 5 mm. deep circumferential lesion in the right caudal maxilla containing yellow purulent material and this lesion communicates with the retrobulbar space. Exophthalmos was noted in the right eye. Purulent material was in the retrobulbar space and yellow/green purulent discharge was in the spinal cavity distal to the cerebellum and ventral to the medulla oblongata.

AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male black footed ferret became inappetent three days prior to death. Examination revealed a large necrotic and infected sublingual mass presumed to be the cause of the inappetence. Biopsy revealed necrosis infection and inflammation but no evidence of neoplasia. The patient remained inappetent and then developed acute renal failure. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At the time of euthanasia the sublingual mass was almost completely resolved. Necropsy revealed generalized edema of the head neck and submandibular region abdominal distention mild jaundice small wound on the top of the nose with dried blood present small amount of serosanguineous fluid within the thoracic cavity serous atrophy of fat diffusely congested lungs two small dark red gelatinous clots in the pericardial sac a large amount of serosanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity a small amount of abnormal tissue in the sublingual mucosa and a small red lesion at the tip of the tongue several cystic lesions in the liver that contained fluid pinpoint red foci on the serosa at various levels of the intestine especially at the junction of the stomach and duodenum diffusely reddened intestinal mucosa and bilaterally mottled and darkened kidneys that were irregular in shape and had foci of red discoloration in areas of indentation.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE ANGIOSARCOMA VISCERAL GOUT NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 15-year-old female gopher snake was acutely unresponsive with uric acid greater than 70. The animal received supportive care but did not respond and was euthanized within two days. At necropsy there were white deposits on the cut surface and luminal surface of the trachea lung liver cardiac valve oviduct and kidneys.

GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA INANITION HEPATIC FIBROMA. This 17-year-old female tree boa was euthanized due to a large coelomic mass and declining condition. At necropsy the liver contained a 1 cm. in diameter mass.

MALIGNANT SEMINOMA SUSPECTED PSEUDO HERMAPHRODITISM WITH UTERINE HYPOPLASIA. This approximately 9-year-old male rabbit was reported to be in lateral recumbency tachypneic and making high-pitched vocalizations. The animal died spontaneously. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition serosanguineous fluid in the thorax adhesion of the pericardium to the sternum and left ribcage white nodules throughout the lungs plaques on the vena cava serous fluid in the abdomen a friable liver and an ambiguous reproductive tract. The animal had a retained testicle removed previously. Gross necropsy revealed the animal had a penis and two empty scrotal spaces. Bilateral rudimentary ovaries were present with the left larger than the right. The oviducts uterus and cervix were markedly reduced in size. The right ovary was in the inguinal canal and the left ovary was in a normal location.

SHOCK PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 7-year-old female bat was found dead a few minutes after being manually restrained to place a transponder chip. No significant abnormalities were identified at necropsy.

NECROTIZING STOMATITIS. This 4-year-old snake was found stuck in an exhibit prop one day earlier and was extricated. The snake had apparently injured its back and there was a kink in the body and no feeling or movement in the caudal two-thirds of the snake. It was found dead at morning check. Necropsy revealed no obvious kinks in the vertebral column and no swelling above or below the specific point of entrapment. No palpable abnormalities were noted. No radiographic evidence of fracture or dislocation was noted. The snake was in good condition with adequate body fat and muscle mass a seed-shaped tan/white focus in the ventricular muscle pale and small thyroid blotchy red/tan liver deeply congested lymphoid patches in the esophagus some dryish/cheesy material in some segments of the intestine large testes and congested kidneys.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA FRACTURE. This 11-year/1-month-old female duck was humanely euthanized due to poor condition and prognosis. At necropsy it had a corneal defect of the right eye. There was a small defect in the calvaria that was dorsal just off of the midline on the left side. There was an associated hole in the left cerebrum.

EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL FRACTURE VERTEBRAL OSTEOARTHROSIS RENAL GOUT HEPATITIS. This greater than 8-year-old male snake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of bad shed. Attempts to restrain the corn snake resulted in fracture. The spine was fused in a curve. At necropsy 50-80% of the spine had fused (osteoarthrosis) with fracture of the spine about 75% down the vertebral column.
CESTODIASIS NEMATODIASIS ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 11-year-old male snake failed to recover from anesthesia for exploratory surgery. At necropsy the left kidney was gray and granular.

AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 5-year-old male/neutered ferret has a six-month history of polyuria and polydipsia occasional inappetence and renal failure. The animal developed a five-day history of inappetence reluctance to drink and reduced urine output and blood work revealed an elevated creatinine level. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged right kidney small left kidney and dark patches in the lungs.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male tamarin was being managed for chronic elevations in hepatic enzymes. A previous biopsy (G13-3319) identified moderate vacuolar hepatopathy. Approximately one week after the biopsy the animal developed lethargy that initially responded to supportive care but then the animal developed marked depression with gaseous distention of the bowel and abrupt drop in hematocrit. The animal died while anesthetized prior to exploratory laparotomy. Necropsy revealed no external abnormalities bilaterally enlarged cervical lymph nodes normal appearing biopsy site in the liver mildly dilated and tortuous bile duct intussusceptions in the jejunum and ileum and a possible perforation at the proximal end of the intussusception of the ileum. A small perforation was in the large intestine. No coelomic fluid or evidence of inflammatory process was associated with either perforation (possibly postmortem).

EUTHANASIA (SEIZURE DISORDER) MENINGITIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE PULMONARY ALVEOLAR ADENOCARCINOMA. This 17-year-old male cougar had been at the zoo eleven years with no major health problems. It then developed a one year history of progressive hind limb weakness and a four month history of intermittent grand mal seizures. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mineralization in the lungs a peripheral thickened nodule in the left lung fluid distention in the left kidney and fragmentation of the spleen.

LYMPHOMA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA SEPSIS CHRONIC RENAL AND CARDIAC DISEASE. This 3-year-old female roof rat was noted to have overgrown incisors and while anesthetized for dental work splenomegaly was noted. A few days later the animal was reluctant to eat and was ataxic and subsequently was found dead. Necropsy revealed a 2-3 mm. wound on the right side associated with some hemorrhage under the skin an enlarged liver with multiple pale nodules a single white raised area on the serosal surface of the jejunum a 2 mm. cyst in the right horn of the uterus a 3 mm. mass present under the cyst markedly enlarged spleen and thin body condition.

CHRONIC GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. This approximately 18-year-old female cotton topped tamarin died spontaneously. Gross necropsy revealed a small amount of peritoneal effusion pinpoint lesions on the lungs a pale liver a thickened gallbladder a cystic lesion on the liver a large ovary with a hemorrhagic capsule that was sloughed and paste-like on cut section and appeared to surround the left kidney a pale and fibrous right kidney adhesion of the left kidney to the GI tract and a firm and fibrous uterus.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This greater than 3-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead. At necropsy it was thin and edematous. The liver was mildly mottled. The ovaries contained follicles with yellow purulent material.

GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS BACTERIAL GASTRITIS COELOMITIS. This 2-year-old female toad had been moved to warm holding two weeks prior to death. The animal was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a mild quantity of fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Liver was mottled tan.

HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 10-year-old female fruit bat was found down. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was found down the following day and later died despite supportive care. At necropsy a large quantity of blood was noted overlying the cerebrum.

EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA. This 11-year-old male prairie dog had a history of chronic spondylosis and poor mobility. The animal became lethargic anemic and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was obese. Approximately 2 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was present in the pleural cavity. Lungs were edematous.

DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS HEPATOCELLULAR NEOPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female fruit bat was found lying on a large branch in poor body condition and with multiple large abrasions and degloving injuries along the entire ventral surface resembling friction wounds (dragging). Radiographs identified a possible fracture in the spine at the thoracolumbar junction and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition several full-thickness skin abrasions along the ventral thorax abdomen chin and wrists and no gross visceral lesions.

GRANULOMATOUS COELOMITIS ESOPHAGITIS OOPHORITIS URATE STASIS INANITION. This 13-year-old female corn snake has a history of inappetence and a mass caudal to the heart. Exploratory surgery revealed a caseous abscess and multiple smaller abscesses. The larger abscess was removed. The animal was found dead a short time after anesthetic recovery. At necropsy several caseous abscesses were identified caudal to the heart and near the esophagus. Kidneys contained urate deposits.

Diarrhea Heart: Mild right ventricular hypertrophy Kidney: Multifocal renal cortical cysts Comments The exact cause of death in this animal remains undetermined. There is evidence of diarrhea; which is a very common clinical problem of captive primates. There are many infectious and non-infectious causes of diarrhea in primates: bacteria; viruses and parasites; neoplasia; stress; diet; food hypersensitivity; and amyloidosis. Multiple sites in the small and large intestine will be examined histologically. The cystic lesions in the kidney are likely incidental findings. The cause of the cardiac enlargement and the clinical significance of this finding remains unknown at this time. Histopathology is pending; the results will be released in a final report. Jennifer Lamoureux; DVM Intestine: Moderately severe acute neutrophilic enteritis; multifocal submucosal pyogranulomas Heart: Moderate pyogranulomatous myocarditis Kidney: Moderate chronic lymphoplasmacytic interstitial nephritis; Multifocal; bilateral renal cysts Liver: Focal capsular fibrosis with bile ductular hyperplasia and mild lymphoplasmacytic inflammation; Moderate diffuse hemosiderosis Acute enteritis Myocarditis Chronic interstitial nephritis Multifocal renal cysts Hepatic hemosiderosis Comments The findings within the small intestine were considered moderately severe and were most consistent with a bacterial infection. Bacterial culture and susceptibility is pending; the results will be released in an addendum report. Jennifer Lamoureux; DVM Please see comments Comments The exact cause of death could not be definitively determined. Gram stain did not indicate the presence of bacterial organisms within the pyogranulomas of the small intestine although there were large numbers of gram positive rods within the intestinal lumen. The clinical significance of this findings is not clear; these organisms may represent antemortem or postmortem bacterial (presumably Clostridia sp.) overgrowth. The isolated strains of E.coli are considered to represent the normal resident bacterial flora; as these organisms tested negative for virulence factors. Further; Salmonella; Shigella; or Yersinia sp. were no isolated from the intestine. Jennifer Lamoureux; D

VISCERAL GOUT TRACHEAL FUNGAL GRANULOMA. This 10-year-old female bittern died one week after treatment. It had a history of probable trauma. It was unable to extend its right wing. Premortem blood work showed elevated renal values. The bird appeared to respond to supportive treatment. At necropsy there were white mineral-like deposits over the serosa of the kidneys and liver extending into the parenchyma. The pericardium and heart muscle also contained similar deposits. There was a gray/green irregularly shaped mineralized mass noted at and distal to the tracheal bifurcation. There was decreased pectoral muscle mass.
NA
BRAIN STEM XANTHOMAS MELANOSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 9-year-old Nelson’s milksnake died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with no evidence of fat stores.

NONSUPPURATIVE ENCEPHALITIS. This 11-year-old male boa was housed in a mixed species exhibit consisting of venomous and nonvenomous snakes. The snake was clinically normal the previous day and was found dead in the morning following a brief period of lethargy and inability to right itself. An Amazon tree boa was found dead unexpectedly in the exhibit one week earlier. Necropsy of that snake identified a hemorrhagic lung and no other abnormalities. Both snakes were in good body condition and had been eating regularly. Necropsy findings for the rainbow boa included good condition no obvious wounds or puncture marks dark red cranial lung pinpoint reddened foci in the mucosa of the stomach adequate adipose stores and male reproductive tract.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL AMYLODOSIS RENAL MINERALIZATION VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE GASTRITIS MYELOLIPOMAS BRANCHIAL CYSTS. This 11.5-year-old male cheetah was anesthetized for a dental procedure. Physical exam revealed mild muscle atrophy in the hind limbs. Ultrasonographic abnormalities were noted in the liver spleen and kidney. Biopsy samples were taken of the liver stomach and duodenum. The stomach showed areas of plaques or fungal infection on endoscopy. The animal suffered respiratory and cardiac arrest during anesthetic recovery and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy focal areas of hypertrophy and hemorrhage were identified in the stomach. The lungs were pale. Multiple nodular foci were identified throughout the spleen. The liver was dark brown. A large blood clot was identified adjacent to the liver.
adult. Weight: 176.9 g.  Disseminated caseous material: suspect articular gout.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male meerkat had a recent history of lethargy inappetence decreased body condition and poor coat quality. A large hepatic mass was diagnosed radiographically and was palpable. Radiographs also revealed spondylosis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with a mildly dull haircoat and multiple tan round lesions with focal atelectasis in the right cranial and middle pulmonary lobes with nodules 0.2-0.4 cm. in diameter. A 0.5 cm. raised firm nodule on the ventral aspect adjacent to the gallbladder in the right medial lobe of the liver and a 6 cm. mass in the quadrate lobe. The left adrenal gland was enlarged compared to the right adrenal gland.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS ASPIRATION EUTHANASIA. This 13.5-year-old female sheep had been retired from exhibit three years earlier due to severe arthritis and previously was diagnosed with renal failure although current blood work did not support renal failure. The sheep had an unthrifty appearance. Recently it was reported to be recumbent with labored breathing and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation swollen left hock with a 13 cm. cyst-like lesion containing clear or serous fluid and exuberant fibrous tissue in the left hock. Marked cartilaginous wear was on multiple joint surfaces. No other major gross findings were noted.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7-year-old female black footed ferret had a previous history of renal disease hepatic cysts and intermittent diarrhea. The animal was recently treated with antibiotics for hemorrhagic diarrhea and some improvement was noted. The appetite returned to normal. One day prior to death the animal had a recurrent episode of formed stool and hemorrhagic mucus. The ferret died while anesthetized for fluid support and blood work. Necropsy revealed good body condition multiple cystic masses throughout all lobes especially on the edge of the right lobe slightly rounded heart and possibly thin right ventricular wall. Thickening of the left ventricular free wall some indentations in both kidneys at the poles and granularity in the medulla mucus in the stomach and throughout the alimentary tract slightly thickened small intestine and no other abnormalities.

ADVENTITIAL VASCULITIS HISTIOCYTIC LYMPHADENITIS AND SPLENITIS. This 4-year-old female gazelle had a recent history of necrotizing stomatitis. Supportive care was administered but after a few weeks of treatment the animal aborted a fetus. The placenta and umbilicus were attached to the fetus but the fetus was autolyzed. Minimal discharge from the vulva was noted and a small amount that was present resolved within a week. The patient improved the mouth lesions resolved and the animal recovered uneventfully. Three days after being released back to the herd this animal became lethargic weak and hyperthermic with a tense abdomen and straining. Pinging was ausculted over the left cranial abdominal region and some sloshing was noted within the rumen. While being examined the animal became agonal and died. Necropsy revealed small foci of hemorrhage in the spinalis muscles attributed to drug injections. Multiple areas of pallor were in the skeletal muscle of the hind legs. A small amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the thoracic cavity. A single cervical lymph node was slightly enlarged and diffusely reddened. The left lung was pale and the right lung was congested. A small amount of foam was in the trachea. The left ventricle was possibly hypertrophied. The rumen was distended with fluid froth and ingesta. Fluid content was greater than normal and this was seen throughout the gastrointestinal tract to the level of the ileocecocolic junction. Serosal vasculature of the rumen was congested. Some of the ruminal papillae were blunted and areas of hyperemia were in the mucosa. The left horn of the uterus was grossly larger than the right and cotyledon attachment sites were still visible on the mucosal surface of the left uterine horn. Several major meningeal blood vessels were congested. No other abnormalities were noted.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE GOUT. This 4-year-old male waxy tree frog was found lethargic and discolored. The animal had some fluid accumulation. The animal died spontaneously. Animals from this collection have a history of Brucella inopinata-like organisms. At necropsy the animal was thin and there was approximately 1 ml. of dark red fluid in the coelomic cavity.

SHOCK. This 11-month-old female parrot went into respiratory arrest approximately 2 minutes into examination. It was being examined for quarantine. It then went into cardiac arrest despite placing it on oxygen. It was given emergency treatment but did not respond. The bird had 2 gm. weight loss over the past 10 days but was most recently eating well and active. At necropsy the bird was in good condition. It was in the midst of regrowing tail feathers and some contour feathers on its head. The crop was full. The proventriculus and ventriculus contained seeds. There was hemorrhage around the medulla and cranial cervical spinal cord area.

SUPPURATIVE MENINGITIS AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male black-footed ferret was being treated for prednisolone for suspected inflammatory bowel disease and had been doing well and gaining weight over the last few months. The animal had been partially inappetent over the last few days was found in the morning minimally responsive laterally recumbent and in respiratory distress. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition improvement in fat stores and muscle quality since last exam and a darkly pigmented small mass on the medial aspect of the right ear pinna that was 3 mm. in dimension and apparently filled with blood. Lungs were darkened in multiple locations especially on the down side of the body. The right heart appeared mildly dilated and subjectively enlarged. A moderate amount of clear to straw colored fluid was in the abdominal cavity. Multiple cystic areas were in the liver and some swelling or reddening of the pancreas was noted around the pancreatic ducts. A short focus of deep purple discoloration was noted in the caudal aspect of the duodenum. A few divots were noted in the cortical surface of the right kidney. Some bruising was noted in the dorsal meninges of the brain.

OSMOREGULATORY DISTURBANCE PROLIFERATION OF RESPIRATORY EPITHELIUM STRESS. This greater than 2-year-old toad is from a group where there has been on ongoing problem. This toad was pulled off exhibit with the rest but only had a nose rub with no other visible lesions. The animal died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed multiple areas of diffuse reddening on the ventral surfaces especially cranial abdomen and legs. A large amount of dark yellow subcutaneous fluid had collected in the rear legs and caudal abdomen; otherwise the toad appeared to be in good body condition and had good amount of fat stores. Some dark yellow fluid was noted in the body cavity and clear yellow fluid was in the pericardial sac. The heart muscle was dark red soft flabby and slightly friable. Intestines were reddened.

CHRONIC TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS WITH   PROTEINURIA MAMMARY FIBROADENOMA. This approximately 2-year-old female roof rat had a large mass ventral to the right forelimb that was interfering with ambulation. The rat was euthanized. Gross necropsy confirmed the presence of a soft tissue mass ventral to the right forelimb and a second soft tissue mass along the ventral midline of the thorax. Adhesions were also noted between the left lung and thoracic wall and were interpreted to be the result of intracardiac injection for euthanasia.

EUTHANASIA ENCEPHALITIS SPINAL HEMORRHAGE MYOCARDITIS INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS PANCREATIC FIBROSIS THYROID HYPERPLASIA ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA. This 17-year-old male tiger had a history of seizures. The animal was humanely euthanized due to lack of response to therapy. Radiographs revealed collapse of the disk spaces and spondylosis throughout the cervical and thoracic spine. At necropsy marked bridging spondylosis was present in these areas. Pale streaking was noted in the heart. Marked congestion was noted in the renal medulla. The thyroids contained various fluid filled cysts.

EUTHANASIA GINGIVITIS BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS KERATITIS. This 12-year-old female kangaroo had a history of depression and recumbency. Minimal response was noted to supportive care. Surgery revealed ileus and congestion of mesenteric vessels. The animal was humanely euthanized due to abnormal clotting. At necropsy edema and hemorrhage were noted adjacent to the surgical incisions. The left eye had scarring of the cornea with neovascularization. A large quantity of hemorrhagic fluid was present in the abdomen. Lungs were hemorrhagic with marked edema. Ulcers were noted in the stomach. Severe dilation of the intestine with liquid green ingesta was noted.

INCONCLUSIVE CYTOLOGY. VENTRA ASPECT OF VERTEBRAE. This 17-year-old male ratsnake had a one year history of weight loss with associated bridging spondylosis on the ventral aspects of the vertebral processes. A hepatic biopsy identified hepatic fibrosis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed three focal pale tan lesions up to 2.5 cm. in diameter in the liver muscle wasting was severe and proliferative bone lesions were on the ventrum of the spinal column. Ankylosing lesions were between the last third and middle third of the body. Culture is obtained from one of these lesions.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA. This 7-year/7-month-old male ibex was humanely euthanized. It had sustained a fractured left femur and right tibia from a dart injury. At necropsy the proximal portion of the left femur and the midshaft of the tibia were fractured.

ZYMBALS GLAND CARCINOMA LYMPHOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female rat developed a mass in the face that extended deep into the bone and mandible and into the horizontal ear canal. An attempt to resect the mass was unsuccessful and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. firm mass ventral to the ear and caudal lateral to the mandible that occluded the horizontal and vertical ear canal and on cut surface was gray with a caseous exudate. The mass extended deep into the mandible.

EMACIATION STRESS CHRONIC ENTERITIS ACUTE BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 13-year-old male ibis did not compete well in the flighted flock had lost weight and condition and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed cachexia absence of fat rough cardiac valves bright red lungs small liver gravel in the ventriculus compact brown gut contents in the intestine and hemorrhages in the upper side of the cranial cavity and behind both orbits.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 10-year-old female meerkat showed signs of ataxia and abnormal behavior. The animal was found dead the following day. Serum chemistry reveals renal failure. At necropsy mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Small white foci were scattered throughout the lungs. The kidneys were small and finely nodular. The left ventricle of the heart was markedly thickened.

ATELECTASIS PULMONARY FIBROSIS BRONCHIOALVEOLAR HYPERPLASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK OOPHORITIS. This 11-year-old female meerkat was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy some hemorrhage was present in the oral cavity and gingiva. A large quantity of cloudy white fluid was present in the pleural cavity. Numerous white nodules were present in the lung. Some sections of lung sank in formalin. The heart was rounded with thickened walls. The liver contained numerous large nodules.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL ENTERITIS SUSPECT YERSINIOSIS PERITONITIS AMYLOIDOSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 5-year/2-month-old male marmoset was humanely euthanized. It presented down and comatose. At necropsy there was diffuse hepatomegaly. There was a parenchymal abscess and granulomas. Mesenteric lymph nodes were severely enlarged.

ESOPHAGEAL TRAUMA STRESS BILIARY CYSTIC HYPERPLASIA. This 11.5-year-old female cottontop tamarin was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy identified tan/brown areas in the liver throughout multiple lobes. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

PERITONEAL HEMANGIOSARCOMA DERMATITIS. This 12-year-old female dog died. On 12/3 it was immobilized for evaluation of left leg lameness and left stifle draining tracts. On 12/23 the dog had a 1-2 day history of vomiting. It was observed in the run as ataxic and wobbly with unusual tremors especially of the head. She was markedly hypothermic. At necropsy there were multiple skin lesions on the different limbs. The lateral aspects of both hocks were ulcerated. The left stifle had three small open wounds cranial laterally. There was an ulceration on the medial aspect and the caudal aspect of the hind leg had an ulceration that was 2 cm. in diameter and surrounded by alopecia. The left axillary lymph node appeared caseous and granular. The left caudal lung lobe had multiple pinpoint raised white foci each 2 mm. or less in diameter. The pancreas had multifocal raised white nodules throughout the parenchyma. The liver had a small approximately 5 cm. region of pale mottling. Both kidneys had a bumpy appearance. On cross section the left kidney had pale areas within the cortex. The bladder mucosa appeared mildly hyperemic. Two dark black/red masses up to 4 cm. in diameter were noted in the fat tissue ventral to the bladder. The masses on cross section had white foci interspersed throughout. The intestinal mucosa from the duodenum to the descending colon appeared thickened.

VISCERAL GOUT GASTRITIS COLITIS. This greater than 5-year-old male caiman was found dead. It had been anorexic since October 2002. The caiman was hospitalized. Radiographs revealed coins in the stomach that were removed via endoscopy. Blood screening revealed elevated copper levels. The caiman was treated with D-penicillamine and antibiotics and was force fed fish. The caiman greatly improved and was returned to the exhibit. A few days after hospital discharge the caiman was discovered morbid and was again hospitalized and treated. It had minimal response to therapy. Repeat blood work revealed severely elevated uric acid. At necropsy there were several erosions of the osteoderm. There were thick crusts over the wounds on the palmar and plantar surfaces of all feet. Digit #5 of both front feet was shortened with exposed phalanx. The pericardium was filled with 6 ml. of chalky white fluid. Approximately 90% of the epicardium was covered with chalky white deposits. The pulmonary parenchyma had increased clear foamy fluid within airways. The liver was brown/gray with a prominent sinusoidal pattern. There were pinpoint white foci scattered over the serosa and throughout the parenchyma of the liver. There were pinpoint white foci scattered over the renal serosa and there were white gritty streaks throughout the parenchyma.

CENTRAL NEUROATHY AND AXONOPATHY LEIOMYOSARCOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 7-year-old female guinea hog was previously diagnosed with multiple melanomas. One month prior to death the animal had a neurologic episode (ie decreased response to external stimuli rhythmic chewing and ear twitching for approximately 45 minutes). On the day of death the animal had a more severe neurologic episode (ie weakness and decreased responsiveness) and was euthanized (per clinician email). She was routinely vaccinated for rabies leptospirosis tetanus and erysipelas. At necropsy there were multiple superficial abrasions. The animal had an approximately 10 in. in diameter spherical mass in the left uterine horn. The endometrium of both uterine horns was cystic. There was approximately 100 ml. of fluid in the abdominal cavity. Two unknown structures were identified in the lumbar region.

CHRONIC NEPHROPATHY. This 13-year/4-month-old female duck died. It was reported to be staying huddled in the corner and was not eating or walking. At necropsy the kidneys were pale (likely renal gout). The left kidney had a small circular white area (possible microgranulomas).

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 7-year/7-month-old male rhea died the day after it was immobilized for a neck injury. At necropsy there was food material present in the mouth. There was bruising in the soft palate. There were adequate fat stores present in the coelomic cavity. The spleen was purple on one end.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 23-year-old male hyacinth macaw had a one day history of weakness and inability to stand but still eating. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Six days earlier this bird was moved to a new holding facility with galvanized wire and some zinc anticorrosive spray flaking from the wire. Blood work prior to death revealed leukocytosis with heterophilia slight anemia hypoproteinemia hyperphosphatemia and hyperuricemia. Necropsy revealed white sludgy material in the subpericardial region and ventral serosal surfaces. Both kidneys were pale swollen and had a firm rubbery consistency on cut surface. Urates were present throughout the kidneys. The proximal intestinal wall was congested and bloody contents were in the lumen.

This 23.5-g mouse was submitted in adequate hydration and fair nutritional states; and was necropsied on 10/23/15. There were no external abnormalities except that the abdomen appeared bloated. The thoracic cavity contained approximately 1 mL of clear; red tinged fluid. The thymus was enlarged (1.25x1.5x0.5 cm); and mostly tan with mottled dark red areas. The liver was enlarged; with rounded lobe edges; was slightly friable; and was diffusely light brown red. The spleen was markedly enlarged; measuring 4.0x1.0x0.5 cm; it was diffusely dark red except for an irregularly shaped; 5x3-mm; tan area on the capsular surface which extended about 1 mm into the splenic parenchyma. The stomach contained a 10x5-mm; white; clearly demarcated area on the greater curvature of the serosa and at this site; the stomach was adhered to the liver. No other significant lesions were observed grossly. 1) Liver: Hepatomegaly 2) Spleen: Splenomegaly 3) Thymus: Thymokesis Comments: The abdominal distension and firmness noted in this mouse was probably due to marked enlargement of liver and spleen. Persistence (and possible enlargement) of the thymus was also noted. Neoplasia is suspected (e.g.; lymphoma). Histopathology of these tissues should be able to shed some light on the cause of death of this animal and will be released as a final report. Rahul B. Dange; DVM; PhD Sections of brain; heart; liver; kidney; spleen; adrenal glands; intestines; and lymph node were examined. Within the section of liver; the hepatic parenchyma was diffusely effaced and replaced by a proliferation of a poorly circumscribed monomorphic neoplastic round cell population. The neoplastic cells were large; arranged in sheets; and were supported by delicate fibrovascular stroma. The neoplastic cells had distinct cell borders; and scant to moderate amounts of eosinophilic cytoplasm. Anisokaryosis was mild to moderate. The nuclei were round; finely stippled to vesiculate and contained 1-2 prominent nucleoli. There were 30 mitoses in 10 HPF. The microscopic architecture of spleen and lymph node was entirely replaced and effaced by large aggregates of similar neoplastic cells. In the kidneys; there was multifocal perivascular infiltration of a similar population of neoplastic round cells; which replaced and effaced many renal tubules. Within the surrounding area; renal tubules were ectatic and contained eosinophilic homogenous proteinaceous fluid. In addition; within the brain; there was a focal area of perivascular infiltration of numerous neoplastic round cells. No other significant lesions were observed. Liver; spleen; kidneys; brain; and lymph node: malignant round cell neoplasm consistent with disseminated lymphoma Disseminated lymphoma Comments The microscopic lesions in this mouse were suggestive of a disseminated lymphoma. As is often the case in mice; this lymphoma was widely disseminated throughout the body affecting spleen; kidney; and liver. No further testing is currently pending. Rahul B Dange; DVM;PhD
DERMATITIS WITH SCARRING AND DEMODECTIC MITES. This 23-year-old female captive bred gorilla had two cutaneous masses.

LYMPHOSARCOMA BACTERIAL AND SAPROLEGNIAL DERMATITIS. This 5-year/7-month-old female axolotl died. It had a leg wound that cultured a light growth of Aeromonas sp. At necropsy there was a superficial wound on the left rear leg with a fungal mat. There was a traumatic wound on the left side of the face. The stomach appeared thickened and felt stiff.

CRYPTOCOCCOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male sugar glider had a 10 day history of head tilt and difficulty maintaining its balance. This condition worsened despite supportive care. Radiographs revealed a fracture in the most proximal aspect of the right humerus but the bone appeared lytic and sclerotic. A previously amputated left forelimb is also in this animal’s history but the cause is not stated. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple variably sized masses in the lung and thickening of the proximal aspect of the right humerus. A fracture is visible in the humeral head.

CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA CHOLECYSTITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS COLITIS. This 29-year-old female polar bear underwent gastrotomy to remove a foreign body. Bowel resection and anastomosis was also performed at this time. The animal’s recovery was slow and prolonged and the animal was found dead the following day. This bear has a prior history of chronic cholangiohepatitis. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA (CAE-LIKE) AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old male/castrated goat developed intermittent episodes of lethargy and inappetence seven years ago and has being doing poorly since maintaining poor body condition. Episodes have been more severe and closer together in the last year and had been severe in the past three weeks. Blood work revealed leukocytosis and supportive care was administered. The goat improved briefly but then relapsed and lost a great deal of weight rapidly. The goat collapsed on exhibit and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The goat also had developed carpal arthritis and tested negative for CAE although other goats in the group have tested positive. The goat was receiving meloxicam for the arthritis. Necropsy revealed cachexia numerous enlarged lymph nodes and nodules in the lung near the hilus.

AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION HEMOSIDEROSIS PORTAL HEPATITIS BUMBLEFOOT (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This approximately 17-year-old Chilean flamingo is from a flock that has been kept inside due to winter temperatures. This animal was found dead in the water with no prior history of illness and it is the second animal to have died in the flock over the last 6-8 weeks. There is current breeding within the flock. Necropsy revealed moderately severe pododermatitis with ulceration and fibrous tissue along the metatarsal pads. The brachiocephalic vessels appeared firmer than expected and the spleen was enlarged and had pink friable parenchyma. Hemorrhage and water were present in the right lung and some pale white streaking was noted in the kidneys.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL COLITIS FIBRINOUS PNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENCEPHALITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOSITIS TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 5-year-old female lemur presented with lethargy and partial anorexia. Encephalomyocarditis virus has been seen in several lemurs in this collection. Radiographically the heart was mildly enlarged. Treatment was initiated with initial improvement. The animal was immobilized for a recheck exam; however acute respiratory distress ensued and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the right atrium was dilated. The left ventricle was thickened. Lungs showed pulmonary edema. The liver was enlarged pale and friable. The bile duct was dilated and tortuous. A blood smear revealed intracellular parasites possibly malarial organisms.

INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS PANCREATIC NECROSIS PROBABLE WEST NILE VIRUS INFECTION. This 6-year-old lorikeet presented after being picked up off the ground by keepers. Supportive care was administered but the bird died 15 min. later following a seizure. There is a history of West Nile virus mortality in the flock. Necropsy revealed good body condition and splenomegaly.

ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS REACTIVE SYSTEMIC AMYLOIDOSIS CUTANEOUS ABSCESS. This 22.5-year-old female tiger was diagnosed four years earlier with cutaneous hemangiosarcoma. For the past few months it was noted that this animal was losing weight and was draining from a malodorous mass. Radiographs revealed possible metastasis in the lungs and a possible mass in the caudal abdomen. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cystic ovaries multiple firm masses in both uterine horns multiple small white firm nodules throughout the lungs small kidneys with irregular surfaces and pale parenchyma thick pancreas with multiple firm nodules thick duodenum with multiple firm masses a few enlarged jejunal lymph nodes and irregular slightly friable liver.

MILD MENINGOENCEPHALITIS AND ERYTHROPHAGOCYTOSIS. This 2-year-old male red panda had been observed on the ground and unresponsive a few minutes after being observed as normal. Resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed fair body condition with prominent ribs and hips little abdominal or pericardial fat and no external signs of trauma. No bruising or fractures were noted. Approximately 40 cc. of straw colored fluid was in the peritoneal cavity. The stomach was filled with plant material and the distal half of the stomach seemed firm on palpation but when opened the material within fell apart easily and did not seem impacted. The material had a strong smell of fermentation. Bright green material was in the proximal stomach that appeared to have been recently eaten and there was similar chewed bright green material present on the right side of the mouth as if regurgitated after recumbent. Normal appearing ingesta was present throughout the gastrointestinal tract and well formed stool was in the colon.

SEPTICEMIA BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This approximately 4-year-old female tree monitor was found dead in pool. This exhibit was next to an exhibit where three sanzinia died within one week of another. The male tree monitor in this exhibit died two days later. At necropsy there were large fat bodies. The retroperitoneal space contained yellow gelatinous fluid. The liver was long large and elongate. It had a slight variegated pattern. There was ingesta in the colon.

ISLET CELL CARCINOMA CORTICAL ADENOMA NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION GLIOSIS SPONGIFORM CHANGE INFLAMMATORY BOWEL PORTAL HEPATITIS. This 6-year-old female captive bred ferret had a three day history of illness that included neurological signs and the animal was euthanized. Necropsy revealed a renal cyst.

CALVARIAL OSTEOBLASTIC OSTEOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male screech owl had an extensive mass on the head. Radiographs and fine needle aspiration were consistent with sarcoma. The owl was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed a 2x3 cm. irregular mass on the rostral aspect of the cranium and a smaller 1 cm. round mass caudal to it on the left side with diffuse thickening of soft tissue around the left ear and narrowing of the ear canal. The larger rostral mass had areas of hemorrhage. Hemorrhage was apparent throughout the cephalic air sac of the cranium. No other abnormalities were noted grossly.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 15-year-old female sheep was euthanized due to chronic degenerative joint disease. At necropsy there was moderate loss of muscle mass and severe degenerative joint disease identified.

CARDIOMYOPATHY GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY HEPATOPATHY HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATIC CARCINOMA HEPATITIS. This approximately 31-year-old male lemur was found dead. It was recently hospitalized with leukocytosis and uremia. It was treated symptomatically and improved. It was returned to the exhibit and was found dead. At necropsy there was a small amount of bloody fluid in the thoracic cavity. The distal trachea and main stem bronchi appeared calcified. There was right heart enlargement (ventricle) with pale areas in the myocardium. There was a small amount of bloody fluid in the abdominal cavity. There were numerous adhesions. The liver was darkly discolored with large areas of cysts and necrosis. It appeared neoplastic. There were adhesions to the diaphragm and serosal surface of the peritoneal cavity. The spleen was enlarged. There was no obvious body fat. Sections of spleen heart and liver were frozen for future use if needed.

SEPSIS. This 6-year-old female zebra died spontaneously and was refrigerated two hours prior to necropsy. The zebra had a dystocia overnight while delivering a large dead foal on September 1 1996. A 10 cm. rectal/vaginal fistula resulted and was treated with standing immobilizations to allow flushing every 72 hours for two weeks. On 11/96 the defect was surgically repaired. The zebra had been on mineral oil three days prior to surgery to soften stools and mineral oil was continued postoperatively. A standing immobilization was used on December 12th and December 13th to help void feces around the repair (the zebra did not defecate on her own after surgery). December 13th 45 minutes after the procedure the zebra was observed to run into the wall of the stall twice lose footing and fall. She remained down the second time and stopped breathing a few minutes later. Rectal palpation after death revealed a palpated gas filled cecum on the ventral aspect of the colon. Necropsy revealed excellent body condition with the surgical repair intact and healing. Abrasions were on both brows of the forehead. The brain had slight haziness of the dura and hemorrhagic vessels on the right frontal lobe and left dorsal cerebrum. The cecum and left and right ventral colon were distended with gas. The mucosal lining of the stomach was hemorrhagic and the mucosa was possibly disrupted. The stomach contained oil with ingesta. The liver was pale and petechial hemorrhages were on the surface of the lung that extended into the parenchyma. The airways contained ingesta suggesting terminal aspiration. The heart was pale and had hemorrhages along the coronary vessels and around the valves.
UROLITHIASIS. This greater than 4-year-old male beaded lizard was found dead and is one of a group of three that had vomited. Necropsy revealed emaciation and generalized autolysis.

BACTERIAL PODODERMATITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS STRESS CHOLELITHIASIS RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male turkey was being treated for abnormalities in the right foot. The condition initially responded but then progressed. Recently the bird was being reevaluated for an abnormality in the left middle digit. One day prior to euthanasia the bird presented with recumbency wet body condition and was unable to stand. Medical treatment was initiated with no response overnight. Further evaluation revealed a reduction in pain response in the foot and no effort to stand and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a clot in the vena cava at the level of the femoral or renal vein liquid ingesta in the caeca empty crop proventriculus and ventriculus multiple superficial abrasions and crusts on the keel and flank skin mottled pancreas swollen middle toe of the left foot and thick brown fluid throughout the length of the toe. Much soft tissue swelling is in the foot extending to digit #4 in the right foot and mineralized hock extensor tendons. The left caudal kidney had a 1 cm. focus of pallor along the lateral margin. The cranial pole showed thickening in the area near the bifurcation of the vena cava. The left testicle was pale and the right testicle was gray/brown.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS THYROID FOLLICULAR CYSTADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female otter presented with a caudal abdominal abscess in March 2013 subsequently presented with right rear leg lameness associated with an open lesion on the leg received supportive care until an additional lesion was observed in the caudal abdomen. This lesion communicated with the abdomen and what appeared to be a necrotic tumor in the musculature of the ventral abdomen extending into the right leg. Cytology revealed numerous spindle cells and inflammatory cells and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition much weight loss a cavity in the caudal abdomen extending through the muscle deep to the peritoneum surrounded by a firm mass that extended between the rear legs and the mass was 14 cm. in greatest dimension. A second smaller opening in the skin was present in the caudal aspect of the right thigh. Numerous pinpoint white lesions were in the parenchyma of the lung and these had a gritty texture. The bladder wall was thickened and nodules were on the interior and exterior surface of the bladder. Both ureters were distended and thickened. An enlarged firm lymph node was adjacent to the colon. A mass was in the caudal ventral abdominal musculature and skin extended into the right leg and wrapped around the pelvis to incorporate the musculature around the caudal lumbar vertebra. The mass was firm and solid on cut surface with a few areas of necrotic tissue. The musculature of the right thigh had a moth-eaten appearance.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PERICARDITIS HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 15-year-old female tamarin appeared disoriented in the morning and was found dead later in the cage. At necropsy purulent material was present in the thorax. The pericardium was fibrous.

OVARIAN SARCOMA BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old female Gila monster had a history of declining health bloat and inappetence. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 35 cc. of green-tinged fluid in the coelomic cavity with some yellow flocculent material a large mass incorporating multiple ovarian follicles in various stages of development clear fluid on cut surface of the mass multiple red/brown circular areas in the liver gray discoloration of digits #1-4 on the left rear foot and devitalization of digit #3 of the left rear foot.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ENDOMETRITIS SEPSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 6-year-old female capybara developed cardiopulmonary arrest while recovering from a lengthy orthopedic surgery. Necropsy revealed foam and regurgitated material in the trachea multiple cystic structures in the external aspect of the uterus hemorrhage on the dorsal aspect of the abdominal wall in the subcutaneous tissues a spherical cyst in the left kidney to 1 cm. in greatest dimension and at least seven nodular dark areas in the lumen of the uterine horns.

THYMOMA RUMINORETICULITIS ABOMASITIS ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 7.5-year-old female pygmy goat had an 8 x 12 cm. thoracic mass restricting respiration and gastrointestinal function. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATITIS YOLK COELOMITIS. This 4-year-old female lorikeet presented with dyspnea and abdominal distention. Radiographs revealed hepatomegaly and a liver biopsy showed hepatic lipidosis. The animal had been treated; however its condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was enlarged friable and light brown to tan.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old female four-toed hedgehog was noted to be in lateral recumbency and did not want to get up. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not significantly improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal had been treated for an abscess on the foot and cutaneous acariasis. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with decreased fat and muscle mass and enlarged right front foot. Kidneys were enlarged and firm. Alimentary tract was empty.

EUTHANASIA INTESTINAL LYMPHOSARCOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 10-year-old male capybara has a history of weight loss and diarrhea. A large abdominal mass was palpated. Exploratory laparotomy revealed an intestinal mass and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large mass was present in the jejunum and smaller masses were present within the mesentery.

AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old male black-footed ferret had a history of inappetence and bloody diarrhea renal failure and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition yellow liquid fecal staining around the perineum lack of skin turgor 2.5 ml. of translucent red/orange free fluid in the thoracic cavity a yellow dry discharge from the nares marked congestion of the right caudal dorsal pulmonary fields and the right cranial ventral pulmonary field as well as tan/brown mottling of the right cranial ventral pulmonary field. Hematoma formation was noted around the left and right cranial vena cava (venipuncture). One milliliter of orange free fluid was in the abdomen and abdominal fat stores appeared adequate. All four canines were fractured and moderate dental tartar was noted on the maxillary premolars and molars. The liver was congested and had a cystic lesion on the right middle lobe. Yellow mucoid luminal contents were in the small intestine and marked reddening of the mucosal surface was noted. Yellow mucoid luminal contents were also noted in the large intestine with reddening of the mucosal surfaces. Kidneys were diffusely pale tan to red and multiple subcapsular foci of red depressions were noted.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 11-year-old male turkey was captive bred and had no prior health concerns. It was submitted for physical examination and was found dead in its carrier. Necropsy revealed unilateral cerebral hemorrhage left ventricular hypertrophy and fibrosis atherosclerosis in the great vessels adequate fat stores and muscling diffusely congested lungs food in the gastrointestinal tract and no other gross abnormalities.

FLAGELLATE COLITIS OOPHORITIS EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female beaded lizard had become lethargic and inappetent with associated weight loss and had defecated mucoid material on several occasions sometimes with blood. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed white punctate foci on the liver.

AMYLOIDOSIS URATE STASIS PROVENTRICULAR MINERALIZATION. This 20-year-old male flamingo was found dead. At necropsy ulceration was noted on the feet. The tarsal joint was swollen. Caseous material was present in the joint space.

Whole body: Emaciation Kidneys: Mild to moderate; chronic interstitial nephritis Uterus: Endometrial cyst (incidental finding) Liver: Mild; multifocal; white foci. Comments: The underlying cause of the reported clinical signs was not evident from gross examination. The gross lesions in the kidney are most suggestive of chronic interstitial nephritis which may represent an aging change. Multiple organs contained foci of suspected calcification which may be an incidental lesion or may represent an underlying chronic disease process. The white foci within the liver were very small and nonspecific. Histopathology to further characterize these gross lesions is in progress; along with fecal analysis. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAMAnatomic pathology resident Cerebrum: Focal glial nodule with neutrophilic inflammation Lungs: 1. Multifocal subpleural and parenchymal foam cell foci 2. Mild; multifocal anthracosis Liver 1. Multifocal hepatic lipidosis 2. Multifocal; centrilobular to random; acute hepatocellular degeneration and necrosis Kidney (unilateral): Severe; locally extensive; suppurative nephritis with intralesional bacteria Kidney (unilateral): Moderate; multifocal; chronic interstitial nephritis with fibrosis and multifocal glomerulosclerosis Intestine: Mild coccidiasis Uterus: Focal endometrial hemorrhagic cyst Kidney: Unilateral severe bacterial nephritis Kidney: Moderate chronic interstitial nephritis Liver: 1. Multifocal hepatic lipidosis; 2. Multifocal; moderate hepatocellular degeneration Lung: 1. Multifocal; subpleural foam cell foci; 2. Multifocal anthracosis Intestine: Mild coccidiasis Comments: This animal has several significant lesions that are difficult to relate to one another and may represent concurrent but unconnected processes. Most significantly; there is a severe bacterial nephritis in one kidney. It could not be determined whether this arose by an ascending (from the urinary tract) or hematogenous (from the blood) route. No other tissue appears affected and there is no evidence of infection in the uterus. Although this renal infection appears severe enough to have some clinical impact; there still appears to be a fair amount of unaffected renal tissue remaining. Additionally; it is difficult to correlate this lesion with the clinical history of abdominal effusion. The opposite kidney has chronic changes supportive of chronic interstitial nephritis. The liver lesion is unusual. Hepatic lipidosis is not uncommon in post-parturition ruminants; however the distribution is often more diffuse. The cause for the liver degeneration is unknown. The foam cell foci in the lung are likely incidental findings possibly related to previous parasite migration. Coccidia are identified histologically and by fecal evaluation. Coccidiasis in adult alpacas is rarely clinically significant unless present in high numbers. Special stains are in process on the liver and kidney sections to determine if bacteria are present in small numbers in the liver and to attempt identification of the bacteria in the kidney. These results will be released as an addendum report. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAM Anatomic pathology reside See previous reports Comments: Although kidney was not available for culture; the bacteria observed in kidney tissue sections were gram negative rods and could be coliforms; which were isolated in high numbers from other tissues (liver; abdominal fluid; lungs). Although cultures must be interpreted with caution due to the state of the animal at necropsy; it is possible that bacterial septicemia (bacterial infection spread through the blood) could account for the lesion in the kidney; the abdominal fluid; and the poor general state of the animal. The types of bacteria isolated from tissues in this animal are all considered commensals (normal inhabitants of body sites such as the intestinal tract and skin) or are ubiquitous in the environment. Bacterial septicemia with these types of bacteria is usually secondary to other processes such as post-partum infections; wound infections/abscess; or opportunistic spread from a local site of infection (mastitis; pneumonia; etc...). A precise pathogenesis and definitive confirmation of bacterial septicemia is not possible in this case. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAMAnatomic pathology resident

TRAUMA BACTERIAL ENTERITIS URATE STASIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 6-year-old female pintail was found dead. At necropsy liver and kidneys were pale. Hemorrhage was identified adjacent to the stifle and body wall.
EUTHANASIA CARDIOMYOPATHY GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 14-year/2-month-old male tree kangaroo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of mycotic onychitis.

ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATITIS PNEUMONIA. This 9-year-old female chicken had been treated with diuretics for several months due to fluid accumulation in the coelom. The bird became lethargic and was moved to the hospital and died overnight. At necropsy the animal was in poor body condition with marked atrophy of pectoral muscles. No adipose tissue was identified in the subcutis. The coelomic cavity contained numerous ovarian follicles. The liver was small and contained a single white 3 mm. in diameter mass in the parenchyma. Similar white foci were present within the lung serosa of the digestive tract and kidney.

EMACIATION STRESS. This 1-year-old female rat was noted two days earlier to be apparently healthy except for a mild amount of weight loss. The animal was subsequently found dead with no premonitory signs. Necropsy revealed thin to good body condition with frank blood expressed from the bladder and some pinpoint petechiae in the mucosa of the stomach associated with digested blood.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA PORTAL HEPATITIS. This approximately 9-year/2-month-old male turkey was humanely euthanized. It was found agonal at the barn. The hyoid apparatus appeared displaced. Trauma was suspected. At necropsy the turkey was in thin body condition. The hyoid was protruding from under the skin on the right side. The right hyoid was displaced. The muscles and tendons in the area appeared damaged. There was hemorrhage present under the skin in the area. Both lungs appeared congested and hemorrhagic. The air sacs were moderately thickened. The entire length of the gastrointestinal tract had a dark green discoloration. Both kidneys were dark green. The liver was mottled and had multiple 1-4 mm. purple/black areas of discoloration. The fat deposits were bright yellow.

SPLENITIS SUSPECT SEPTICEMIA MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION ENDOCARDIOSIS. This approximately 9-year-old male otter died. It had a three week history of intermittent lethargy and decreased appetite. Physical exam revealed a right retropharyngeal abscess that communicated to the right second lower molar alveolus. At necropsy the body condition was good. There were bilateral retropharyngeal abscesses with purulent draining tracts extending rostrally to the caudal mandible. Culture results are pending.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA PULMONARY LYMPHOMA. This 15-month-old female rat had a recent history of weight loss and had previously been obese. It had a few hour history of dyspnea that did not respond to oxygen and was associated with an intrathoracic mass detected by radiography and ultrasound. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition and white rounded nodules in left and right lungs with some containing caseated debris. Only the left caudal pulmonary lobe appeared normal.

CLOACAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female whistling duck had a history of mild pododermatitis but no other medical concerns. It was found lethargic in the morning hiding under vegetation in the exhibit. Examination revealed a firm thickened mass involving the caudal dorsal vent region and a large number of fly eggs and larvae were present around the cloaca and tail base. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition good postmortem condition a 1 cm. focus in the caudal/dorsal ventral margin of the vent that was abnormally thickened and firm with mild erosions at the mucocutaneous border. Fly eggs and larvae were present adhered to the vent margin and the tail base. Feather lice were present on the head and in the cervical plumage. The firm cloacal tissue extended deep to the dorsal border of the cloaca. On cut surface the tissue was white/tan with areas of caseous necrosis.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMAS SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 15.5-year-old male kingsnake had a history of spinal lesions and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified full body swelling to 10 cm. cranial to the vent fused spinal vertebrae enlarged right kidney bilateral cataracts and no other gross lesions.

PNEUMONIA BACTERIAL ENTERITIS SUSPECT DROWNING. This approximately 11-year-old male python was found dead. It had been placed in a soak bath. The python was reportedly not eating recently and having respiratory wheezes. At necropsy it had retained shed on the head. The lungs were severely hemorrhagic and thickened with cream colored plaques. Mucous membranes were pale. There was ingesta in the stomach and digesta in the small and large intestines. The liver was mottled. Sections of liver lung heart and kidney were frozen for future use if needed.

SYSTEMIC LOW GRADE INFLAMMATION PROBABLE ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old female rabbit had been unable to properly consume night feces which subsequently stuck to the fur and caused cutaneous irritation. The condition worsened and treatment was no longer providing comfort. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A large amount of brown urine was noted in the urinary bladder the kidneys were pitted and had multiple infarcts and no other abnormalities were noted.

CHRONIC JOINT DISEASE AND BACTERIAL CELLULITIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE AMYLOIDOSIS ASPIRATION EMACIATION. This approximately 12-year-old male greater kudu was found dead one day after being immobilized with carfentanil/zylazine for lameness. One day prior to death blood work revealed azotemia. It had a history of left front limb lameness with arthritis in the metacarpal joints bilateral carpi swelling with abscesses in the right carpus and cellulitis/edema above the left carpus. An old abscess was on the right hind hock that appeared to be walled off. Necropsy revealed congested and darkened lungs and white streaks in the heart. The vertebrae appeared to be very brittle and were easily cut with a knife.

CATARACTS CUTANEOUS MYXOSARCOMA HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female mouse had three subcutaneous masses that rapidly appeared in less than one week. The mouse was also geriatric with a right eye cataract and was euthanized.

FIBROSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old snake has a history of a large firm midbody swelling attributed to fibroplasia associated with fractured ribs. A fine needle aspirate from the site suggested sarcoma and the lesion was nonresectable. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

DEGENERATIVE LEUKOENCEPHALOMYELOPATHY CONSISTENT WITH WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME FIBRILLAR ASTROCYTOMA. This captive bred 4-year-old female hedgehog had progressive loss of motor control on the hind limbs over the past year. The hind limbs also appeared dark in color frequently. The animal was euthanized.

PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS. This 6-year-old male quail was found dead. Necropsy revealed a hematoma in the liver and free blood in the coelom pulmonary congestion and arthritis in the right tarsus. Feathers were missing from the top of the head.

BRONCHOINTERSITIAL PNEUMONIA SKELETAL MUSCLE HEMORRHAGTE SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 3.5-year-old male wallaroo had a one month history of illness became moribund and was euthanized. Blood work prior to euthanasia indicated dehydration or renal failure and radiographs reveal generalized lung disease. Necropsy revealed thin body condition bloody foam in the trachea consolidated lung 250 ml. of bloody fluid in the abdominal cavity an abdominal mass in the region of the cecum and a tubular mass resembling a diverticulum in the intestine.

HEPATITIS URATE STASIS INANITION. This 3-year-old female rail was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a large quantity of straw-colored fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Adhesions were present within the coelom.

DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE MILD NEPHRITIS AND HEPATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old female rabbit had a several month history of reluctance to groom and ataxia. Radiographs revealed two intervertebral disk disease lesions at T13-L1 and L1-L2. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition ingesta and feces in the gastrointestinal tract and retroperitoneal fat present.

ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS MYOSITIS HISTIOCYTIC COELOMITIS RENAL GOUT. This 19-year-old gecko has a history of pododermatitis and weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy swelling was noted on the right metacarpus with ulceration of the palmar and plantar surfaces of several feet. The coelomic cavity contained a large quantity of serosanguinous fluid. White material was present on the capsular surface of the liver. White masses were present in the coelomic cavity and adjacent to the oviduct.

Skin: Vascular malformation Comments: The described histomorphologic changes are most consistent with a vascular malformation; such as a vascular hamartoma. Vascular hamartomas are benign developmental malformations. In some forms; proliferative vessels may dissect locally into adjacent stroma. The described changes extend to the deep margins; therefore; excision cannot be confirmed. Monitoring of the site for recurrence may be warranted. Colleen F. Monahan; DVM

RENAL GOUT CLOACITIS. This captive bred 1-year-old female lovebird was found dead on exhibit. It had no previous signs of illness. Another lovebird that died last year may have had Baylisascaris infection. At necropsy the lovebird was in slightly thin body condition.
adult.  Euthanasia. Multifocal deposits; suspect cholesterol. Intracranial mass; suspect cholesterol granuloma.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS EMACIATION GRANULOMATOSIS INTESTINAL PARASITISM (NEMATODES AND CESTODES) CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK STRESS. This 10-year-old female swan was found in moribund condition in the evening and had been clinically normal three hours earlier. Examination revealed sand in the gastrointestinal tract and the animal arrested while a catheter was being placed. Attempts to resuscitate were unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with minimal fat stores areas of hemorrhage in the lungs sand in the proventriculus and ventriculus green discoloration in one segment of the small intestine adjacent to the gallbladder mildly distended cloaca multiple 3-5 mm. white nodules in the liver and a 7 mm. cyst on the dorsal aspect of the left kidney that contained a white structure resembling a parasite.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 4-year-old female lorikeet is from a flock in which there has been a recent increase in mortality. Most birds present moribund with respiratory distress. This bird was seen falling off its perch in the morning and lying laterally recumbent on the floor was moribund upon admission to the hospital received supportive care but died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed thin body condition no external lesions empty crop multiple variably-sized areas of tan discoloration on the surface and throughout the parenchyma of the liver hyperemia and gas distended intestine and no other gross abnormalities.

AMYLOIDOSIS GASTROENTERITIS HELICOBACTER EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male black-footed ferret was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes following a history of renal failure that did not respond to supportive care. Necropsy revealed prominent hips and ribs normal fat stores fractured upper canines and bilaterally enlarged kidneys.

EUTHANASIA DIABETES ISLET ATROPHY HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ENTERITIS. This 14-year-old female chinchilla had a history of polyuria and polydipsia. The animal was hyperglycemic with ketonuria and glucosuria. The animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC GASTRITIS WITH CYSTS ENTERITIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This male 17-year-old lemur was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic vomiting and mucoid feces for approximately four years. It had been treated for inflammatory bowel disease with prednisolone for some time and showed some improvement but still showed intermittent vomiting on a cyclical schedule. Laparotomy was performed due to nonspecific findings. Surgical exploration revealed severe gastric lesions and a poor prognosis. At necropsy there was an emphysematous nodule on the ventral gastric surface that incorporated the omentum and was surrounded by numerous tortuous blood vessels.
