There was a focal perforating ulcer and transmural emphysema in the stomach especially near the nodule and pylorus. There was coffee ground material within the stomach. There were large amounts of mucus throughout the gastrointestinal tract. The lungs were congested and atelectatic. The gall bladder seemed thin and emphysematous. There was a reticular pattern on the renal serosal surfaces.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZAITON BIBROUS OSTEODYSTROPHY INIATION. This greater than 2-year-old female hedgehog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of being treated for possible pulmonary fungal infection based upon clinical signs radiograph results and results of recently deceased exhibitmates. At necropsy there were increased amounts of fluid within the thoracic cavity. The lungs were solid bilaterally and crunchy. Aorta and other great vessels appeared calcified and were brittle. The epicardium and myocardium had white streaks. There were increased amounts of fluid within the abdominal cavity. There were moderate white streaks throughout the stomach with hardening of the tissue. The liver was pale. The thyroids were enlarged. The adrenals were enlarged. The kidneys were pale and edematous with white flecks and blotchy hemorrhage. The bones were brittle. Lung was submitted for bacterial and fungal cultures.
MYOCARDIAL HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 1-year-old female teal was found dead in the water. At necropsy petechial and ecchymotic hemorrhages were noted on the heart.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS OSTEOARTHRITIS GRANULOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female rattlesnake had abnormal caterpillar-like movements in the caudal two-thirds of the body suggesting neurologic disease and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an aggregate of irregular masses cranial to the thyroid gray and approximately 1 cm. in total length. Another gray irregularly shaped mass approximately 4 cm. in diameter was caudal to the thyroid and cranial to the heart. A moderate to large amount of yellow clear fluid was in the coelomic cavity. The kidneys were smaller than expected. Multiple ovarian cysts filled with clear fluid were in the reproductive tract and multiple atretic or degenerative follicles were present. Two osteoproliferative areas were observed in the caudal half of the spinal column.

Cause of death uncertain at this time. Please see comments. Comments: No definitive cause of death could be determined based on the gross examination. Final diagnosis is pending microscopic examination. Molly H. Seavey; DVM M Please see comments Comments: PAS; Acid Fast; and Warthin Starry was negative for infectious organisms. Bacterial culture of intestine revealed E. coli which is typical in an adult ferret. This case is in the process of being reviewed by a mustelid specialist-pathologist. As previously explained; the infiltrating cells observed in multiple organs are of round cell lineage. Our primary differentials at this time include lymphocytic neoplasia; histiocytic neoplasia; or a severe systemic lymphohistiocytic inflammation due to an uknown cause. Further information will be released upon availability. Molly H. Seavey; DVM MPH

INANITION OSTEOMYELITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PANCREATIC HYPERPLASIA. This 9-year-old female viper had a history of inappetence and bridging spondylosis in the midbody. A wound was noted on the ventrum following an episode in which the cage substrate was thrown to one side of the exhibit. The animal died before treatment could be initiated. At necropsy the animal was thin. A large quantity of clear yellow fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. A 1.5 cm. in diameter wound was present in the ventrum. Proliferations of bony material were present in two areas of the vertebral column. Caseous material exuded from the proliferative material on section. The pancreas was firm and adherent to the bile duct with occlusion of the bile duct.

SARCOCYSTOSIS ASPERGILLOSIS EMACIATION. This 13-year-old male pygmy falcon was noted to have eaten well the previous day and was acting normally. It had a one day history of lethargy and weight loss received supportive care but was found dead the following morning. Heat stress is suspected. Necropsy revealed thin body condition absence of coelomic fat adhesion of the ventriculus to the peritoneum empty proventriculus and ventriculus a small amount of black gut contents hemorrhagic lungs and dark kidneys.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HEMOCHROMATOSIS CHOLECYSTITIS. This approximately 34-year-old male lemur was humanely euthanized. It had a history of renal disease that initially responded to intensive care. He also had a tooth root abscess. At necropsy the lemur was in poor body condition with protruding hips spine etc. There was edema in the subcutaneous space ventrally and in the inguinal area. There was a dermal abscess at the tail base (2 mm. diameter). There were 42 ml. of blood tinged fluid in the abdominal cavity. There was approximately 60 ml. of straw colored fluid in the left pleural space and 40 ml. in the right pleural space. The lungs were decreased in size. The lung surface was white and on cut surface the lungs were markedly atelectatic. There was an apical abscess of the right cuspid tooth. The liver appeared swollen and the edges were possibly rounded. The gall bladder was tubular. Both kidneys were pale and fibrotic. There were two cysts protruding from the cortical surface of the right kidney. On cut surface the cysts leaked brown thick fluid.
adult. Weight: 310 g.  Euthanased.  Fibrous mass surrounding microchip.  Pulmonary congestion suspect euthanasia artefact.

PULMONARY CONGESTION AND HEMORRHAGE SUSPECT SHOCK HEPATITIS. This approximately 1-year/2-month-old male snake was found dead in its enclosure. The animal had been removed from quarantine status due to management decisions requiring movement to a new location before quarantine could be completed. At necropsy the lungs were slightly hyperemic. The animal was in good body condition.

EUTHANSIA CEREBRAL EDEMA CEREBRAL NECROSIS GASTRIC EROSIONS FATTY LIVER. This 9-year/10-month-old female wallaroo was humanely euthanized. It was found in the morning lying laterally and was comatose. It had minimal response to stimuli and pupils were fixed and dilated. The wallaroo was anesthetized the day prior to death for physical examination and contraceptive implant placement. Induction was relatively smooth. Reversal drug was administered half intravenously and half intramuscular but the wallaroo could never completely rise. The intramuscular atipamezole was repeated along with dexamethasone later that day. The wallaroo became easily exhausted during attempts to stand. The animal could never coordinate itself or find the strength to stand or get sternal. The forelimbs particularly seemed to be quite paretic. The animal declined overnight and was humanely euthanized the next morning. At necropsy the body condition was good. The muscles were largely normal except for some multifocal hemorrhagic areas in the forelimbs likely secondary to intramuscular injections. There were abundant fat stores present. The left (downside) lung lobes were congested. The heart seemed generally enlarged. The forestomach was full of ingesta. The urinary bladder had some petechia on the mucosa. The adrenal glands were bilaterally very pale. Bacterial culture of the liver was performed. Sections of liver kidney spleen lung and skeletal muscle were frozen for future use if needed.

SEVERE DENTAL DISEASE SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION EUTHANASIA CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. This 19-year-old female bighorn sheep had been losing weight and was found laterally recumbent. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was abundant feed material packed in both right and left cheeks. There was severe wavemouth. The right maxillary molar #2 was broken off at the gumline with a sharp point. The tooth root was infected. The left maxillary molar tooth was loose and infected at the tooth root as well. Kidneys were mildly decreased in size. There was an infarct of the left kidney. The urinary bladder had an irregular mucosal wall. The right adrenal cortex appeared mildly enlarged. Some fluid was noted upon sectioning the lungs.

HEMOGLOBIN CRYSTALLIZATION POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS. This approximately 5-year-old female tentacled snake was found dead on exhibit along with a tankmate. Necropsy revealed some active follicles in the ovary and some brown plaques on the liver that extended into the parenchyma.
BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS THYROID MINERALIZATION. This 17-year-old female penguin was found dead. At necropsy lungs were firm and partially sank in formalin.

FOCAL PULMONARY FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 4-year-old male rooster was euthanized following a seven day history of lethargy weakness and decreased responsiveness. The bird was also exhibiting neurologic signs and did not respond to any treatments. Gross necropsy revealed subcutaneous hemorrhage over the left thorax extending toward the wing.

SUPPURATIVE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA SUPPURATIVE PODODERMATITIS/CELLULITIS PROBABLE ASPIRATION. This 6-year-old female kangaroo developed acute onset of swelling of the right rear limb distal to the hock shortly after tropical storm Fay. Supportive care was administered but necrosis of the toe developed necessitating amputation of P3 and P2. Supportive care was administered but the lesion progressed necessitating amputation of part of P1. The condition seemed to be responding to therapy but the kangaroo developed unexpected respiratory problems a seizure and died. Necropsy revealed thick hemopurulent material occluding the left naris bulging of the diaphragm into the abdominal cavity which deflated after puncturing the diaphragm liquefactive necrosis and adhesions of the cranial lung lobes caseous abscesses in the caudal lung lobes and probable injection reactions in the left semitendinosus muscle.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 8-year-old male rabbit died shortly after having its nails clipped. It had no previous signs of illness. Necropsy revealed adequate body condition. Approximately 30-40 ml. of pink fluid was in the thoracic cavity.

MULTICENTRIC RENAL CELL ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL GOUT GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This approximately 9-year-old male milksnake was found dead on second check. It had a history of regurgitation hypercalcemia hyperphosphatemia polyuria weight loss dehydration heterophilia monocytosis basophilia hyperkalemia and emaciation. It had three palpable masses in its caudal one-third of the coelomic cavity. Radiographs revealed the masses as soft tissue density. At necropsy two bilateral cream colored soft oval structures were the hemipenises should have been located. The gall bladder was severely distended. Both kidneys contained large masses that invaded their stroma. These masses ranged greatly in size from pinpoint to about 1 cm. in diameter. They appeared to have a pink background matrix with mineralized granulomas throughout. The masses corresponded to the palpable masses felt antemortem. There was severe muscle atrophy present throughout the carcass.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS ADHESIONS AMYLOIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE. This 6-year-old male ferret had been inappetent the previous night had abnormal behavior the following morning characterized by abnormal mentation and also had a dried discharge that occluded the nares. The animal was ataxic and arrested while anesthetized for examination. Necropsy revealed good body condition calculus on all teeth worn teeth mildly enlarged heart pitted kidney with white streaks extending into the medulla reddened duodenum and colon absence of ingesta in the stomach and no other abnormalities.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 22-year-old female cockatoo was found moribund and died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed fair body condition ulcerative dermatitis on the left patagium 1-2 cc. of white opaque fluid in the pericardium and semiopaque pericardial membrane. The surface of the liver was white and opaque. The kidneys were swollen and pale.

FATTY LIVER. This approximately 1-year-old female gecko was found dead in its cage. It had a recent history of trauma from a fight with a male gecko. It was noted to be egg bound and was given supportive care and recovered nicely. At necropsy there was hemorrhage within the coelomic cavity. There were calcium stores within endolymphatic sacs. The liver was enlarged. One egg was found. The gecko was molting.

EUTHANASIA ORONASAL FISTULA PYOGRANULOMATOUS DERMATITIS AND CELLULITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PULMONARY EDEMA ENCEPHALITIS. This 8-year-old female wallaby presented 10 days prior to death with chronic nasal discharge and anorexia. Multiple ulcers of the palate were identified. The animal was treated with pharyngostomy tube IV fluids and antibiotics. The animal was sedated to change the IV lines and pneumonia was discovered. Two oronasal fistulas were present. Abscesses were also noted in the tooth roots. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. At necropsy the animal was in poor nutritional condition with no adipose tissue stores. Nasal sinuses were filled with firm yellow exudate. Similar material was present in the right bronchus. The right lung lobes were dark purple and sank in formalin. The lung and pericardium were covered with fibrin. The heart was rounded and pale tan. Small masses were present on the edges of the aortic valve and within the ascending aorta. A large quantity of clear yellow fluid was present in the peritoneal cavity. Marked fibrous tissue reaction was noted at the pharyngostomy tube site and involving the right thyroid gland.

OSMOREGULATORY DISTURBANCE VESICULAR DERMATOPATHY GRANULOMATOSIS STRESS. This greater than 2-year-old toad was treated prophylactically for saprolegniosis due to recent death of a nonclinical frog. All five had nose rubs of varying degrees. This was not a problem prior to placement in the Gunnite exhibit. One frog had exposed bone and one had a moderately severe nose rub. Treatment for the saprolegniosis included malachite green baths and Silvadene ointment. No specific lesions or problems were detected in this particular individual which died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed slight nose rub ventral redness and petechiation and slight redness between the toes. A small amount of subcutaneous fluid was noted ventrally. The frog was otherwise in good body condition with a few small fat bodies present. Lungs were slightly hyperinflated. A large nematode parasite was found detached to the serosal layer of the stomach and proximal small intestine. Stomach had normal ingesta. No parasites were found within the gastrointestinal tract.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS DIC IRON STORAGE DISEASE ANESTHETIC COMPLICATION DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE. This 44-year-old male gorilla had a particularly severe episode of cervical pain and immobility due to longstanding spinal problems. Supportive care was administered but response was poor and cardiopulmonary arrest occurred during sedation for manipulation and fluid administration. Necropsy revealed good body condition and a 35 cm. area of sloughed skin on the dorsal thorax with associated hyperemic dermis. Three 1 mm. white/tan masses clustered together are present on the left inferior conjunctiva. Approximately one liter of serosanguineous fluid is in the pleural cavity and the lungs bilaterally are atelectatic. Multiple black deposits are present at the periphery of all lung lobes. The heart is moderately flaccid and some arteriosclerotic plaques are noted on the great vessels extending to the peripheral arteries. The upper left canine tooth is missing and excessive wear and moderate tartar are associated with the remaining teeth. A small firm gingival mass is noted. The liver is cobblestone in appearance with an irregular contour to the edges. Multiple mineralized areas are noted. The gall bladder is markedly distended and contains several choleliths. Gray striations are in both kidneys. Several lymph nodes are hemorrhagic and friable. The adrenals are enlarged friable and hemorrhagic especially the right adrenal. The pancreas has multiple petechiae. Degenerative joint disease is noted in the right shoulder both stifles and the cervical and lumbar vertebrae. Mild rotational deformity and lateral deviation of the lumbar spine is noted. Numerous areas of narrowing of the cervical and lumbar spinal canal are noted and most intervertebral discs are brittle yellow/tan and friable.

MELANOMA NERVE SHEATH TUMOR HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA. This 10-year-old male sugar glider had a two month history of ataxia and proprioceptive deficits in the hind limbs a circumscribed pigmented tumor on the right side of the nasal planum amber colored fluid in the lungs consolidation of the pulmonary parenchyma and dark discoloration of the lungs.

SHOCK DROWNING. This 17-year-old male scarlet ibis was found dead in the exhibit pool. At necropsy the GI tract was filled with normal ingesta. Several small cysts were present in the kidney. Fluid was present in the lungs.

MANDIBULAR ABSCESS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS ENTERITIS MYOCARDIAL INCLUSIONS. This 10-year-old male rock hyrax was under treatment for an abscess located in the left mandibular area and for severe emaciation. The animal was later found dead. At necropsy in addition to the mandibular abscess there were multiple areas of the intestine that were noted to contain 1-2 mm. pale foci.

SHOCK POSSIBLE HYPERTHERMIA BLADDER NEMATODES TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS BRONCHIOLITIS. This 1-year-old female/spayed dumbo rat had been transported with two conspecifics in the same crate to a program. When the staff at the program arrived one hour later all rats were dead. No urine or feces were found in the crate suggesting that the rats died shortly after the trip had started. The rats may have been put too close to a heat duct. Necropsy revealed normal ingesta in the stomach congested lungs that oozed blood on cut surface and advanced autolysis.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 20-year-old penguin had been treated for three years with cardiac disease and had recent decompensation. The animal subsequently died. Necropsy revealed good postmortem condition enlarged heart markedly enlarged ascending and descending vena cava a small fungal plaque in the trachea at the syrinx and no other abnormalities. This animal had presumptive West Nile virus infection three years earlier based on rising titer and clinical signs.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT MULTICENTRIC RENAL ADENOMA GRANULOMATOUS DERMATITIS. This female greater than 16-year-old spoonbill was found dead. It was separated from the flock on 12/12 for lameness (2-3/5). On exam the right pes was slightly edematous. The body condition and appetite appeared adequate. The bird was started on Banamine. Postmortem radiographs demonstrated cranial pole swelling of the kidneys. At necropsy the spoonbill was thinner than when examined a week ago. No substantial fat reserves were noted intracoelomically. There were small bumbles present and mild inflammation on the lateral and medial digits of both pes. Air sacs were lightly dusted with uric acid deposits. Pericardial sac was deeply coated in uric acid deposits. The coelomic viscera were also lightly dusted with uric acid deposits. The proventriculus was empty but the gizzard contained a notable amount of ingesta. The kidneys were pale and greatly swollen cranially. They are moderately swollen for the remainder of the parenchyma. The ovary was quiescent.

COLITIS URATE STASIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 15-year-old female owl had a several day history of anorexia with no response to treatment. The animal later died. At necropsy the cloaca was distended with gritty malodorous feces and a large fecalith.

MEDIASTINAL THYMOMA COLLOID GOITER CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 12.5-year-old male goat was anesthetized for dental treatment; however tachycardia and apnea developed under anesthesia; however the eyes became fixed and dilated and minimal responsiveness to painful stimuli was noted. Emergency treatment was unsuccessful and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy marked wave mouth was noted with missing lower premolars. A 10-12 cm. in diameter mass was present in the thoracic cavity cranial to the heart. Severe arthritic lesions were noted in the stifles.

PULMONARY EDEMA STRESS HEPATOPATHY. This approximately 13-year-old male bull snake was found dead in its enclosure. It had no history of illness. It had experienced weight loss of 300 gm. since release from quarantine in August of 1988. At necropsy the snake was in adequate nutritional condition. Sections of spleen liver lungs and heart were frozen for future use if needed.

BACTERIAL UROCYSTITIS SEPSIS/DIC POSSIBLE BLADDER DENERVATION. This 1-year-old male meerkat was noted to have mildly abnormal ambulation and posture in the pelvic limbs since birth and was unable to sit up on rear legs. A congenital spinal or pelvic malformation or neurologic condition was suspected but not confirmed. In the past month keepers noted mild progression of abnormal gait but good appetite. The animal was subsequently found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed good body condition reddish fluid staining the perineum and ventrum a skin flap and an ulcerated area on the skin of the scrotum/perineum. The urinary bladder was markedly distended and the entire serosal and mucosal surfaces were dark red to purple. The contents were dark red with few small blood clots. A catheter passed without obstruction from the trigone through the entire urethra.

ISLET CELL TUMORS INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS ISLET VACUOLAR DEGENERATION DIABETES MELLITUS EUTHANASIA GLUCAGON MA INSULINOMA. This 7-year-old male ferret had a history of insulinoma and adrenal disease that was managed medically. It recently developed nonspecific gastrointestinal signs that resolved with supportive care although hepatic enzymes gradually elevated over the past month. The animal subsequently presented with lethargy weakness and decreased appetite and blood work revealed continued elevation of hepatic values and marked hyperglycemia. Urinalysis revealed ketonuria glucosuria bilirubinuria and casts. Prednisolone therapy was discontinued and glucose dropped to within the 300 range. Ultrasound revealed a suspected mass near the cranial aspect of the spleen and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachexia three distinct nodules in the pancreas enlarged firm left adrenal and dark right adrenal that was hard to find thickened gallbladder with gelatinous bile and patent bile duct a 2 cm. mass in mid cranial spleen with normal capsular color but pale core brown/orange colored urine with bilirubinuria trace protein glucose and blood marked mesenteric and mediastinal fat deposits and multiple 3-5 mm. discrete areas of red/brown discoloration in the fat surrounding the stomach believed to be gastric lymph nodes.

SUSPECT TRAUMA. This 19-year-old female Madagascar tree boa was found dead without any known clinical signs. At necropsy the liver was mottled and slightly gray. There was abundant fluid within the pericardial sac. Six well-developed offspring were in the uterus and two macerated sacs were cranial to the well-developed offspring. There was a hematoma in the caudal dorsal aspect of the coelom.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male lemur had a history of chronic renal disease and was found lethargic on exhibit. The animal was minimally responsive had lost 30% of its body weight over the last six months and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed small pale pitted kidneys and dilatation of the right renal pelvis.
PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA CATARACTS. This 14.5-year-old female Jamaican fruit bat was found dead in its enclosure and had no prior signs of illness. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 10-year-old female frog was found dead in its pool with no prior medical history. The keeper noted a heavy deposit on the eyes. Breeding had been observed but no offspring were produced. Necropsy revealed edema of the subcutis and white discoloration of the lower eyelid. The coelomic cavity was filled with dark brown to red fluid. The liver was black. The ovary was present and inactive. The skin had multiple plaque-like dermal masses that were symmetrically placed on either side of the fore and hind limbs and which may have been normal structures.

TRAUMA RHABDOMYOLYSIS POSTSURGICAL COMPLICATIONS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female gazelle was noted to be acutely lame on its left rear limb at closing was evaluated the following day and determined to have dislocation of the left stifle and destruction of both cruciates and collateral ligaments. Surgical repair was performed that day but the animal was found recumbent the next morning with a fractured left tibia and destruction of the stifle repair. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild overconditioning marked swelling and bruising at the surgical site swollen limb distal to the site crepitation in the joint marked pulmonary congestion adhesion of the right lung to the thoracic wall in two locations a large amount of adipose in the mediastinum congestion in the liver and enlargement of both uterine horns and a small fetus with associated placenta in the right horn large areas of clotted blood throughout the left thigh muscles and within the soft tissues of the distal left rear limb with complete fracture of the left tibial crest and associated displacement.

TRAUMA PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS. This adult (greater than 1 year) male parrot was found dead on exhibit. It was seen eating and taking care of chicks. Three finches were introduced into the exhibit recently. At necropsy all internal organs were autolyzed. The proventriculus was grossly enlarged and thickened. Small approximately 2 mm. white coiled nematode was found within the proventricular lumen. The liver was soft and friable. There were several white miliary foci surrounded by a ring of inflammation and hemorrhage noted within the wall of the jejunum.

FIBRINOUS EPIMYOCARDITIS BRONCHOINTERSTITAL PNEUMONIA CHRONIC MYOCARDITIS AND PORTAL HEPATITIS OVARIAN LEIOMYOSARCOMA. This 1-year-old female rabbit had been eating well and behaving normally prior to being found unexpectedly dead. Necropsy revealed numerous small white foci throughout the lung pericardium and epicardium and a large amount of clear fluid in the pericardium. A 2 cm firm white mass was in the perihilar region and the mass is homogeneous on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA FOR FACIAL INFECTION (HEAD NOT SUBMITTED). This greater than 3-year-old rattlesnake had a history of swollen pits with chronic infection that spread to the facial area and did not respond to therapeutics. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed old crusting lesions around the eyes sensory pits and head. A granular/tubular pattern was in both kidneys and straw colored fluid was in the coelomic cavity.

NECROTIZING MYOCARDITIS WITH GANGLIONEURITIS. This 22-year-old female Humboldt Penguin had a one-month history of illness that included open mouth breathing holding the wings abnormally and weak positive Aspergillus titer. Blood films did not reveal hemoparasites. Supportive care was administered with initial improvement followed by deterioration with progressive leukocytosis. The bird became sternally recumbent with open-mouth breathing and pulmonary congestion and was inappetent for two days prior to being found dead. Necropsy revealed pulmonary consolidation with hemorrhage cloudy air sacs and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA MYOSITIS PULMONARY ABSCESS LYMPHADENITIS RENAL CYST. This 14-year-old female sheep had a history of lameness and was recently observed with mandibular edema dyspnea and anorexia. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large quantity of intra-abdominal and intrathoracic fat was present. There was evidence of chronic arthritis in the femoral head and acetabulum. A large area of necrosis was identified adjacent to the left mandibular salivary gland extending to the retrobulbar area. The right caudal lung lobe was mottled and blunted. Two 3 cm. in diameter masses were palpable in the lung lobes. On sectioning they contained purulent material. The left kidney contained a 3 mm. firm white raised mass.

EUTHANASIA RENAL GOUT RENAL ADENOMA BILIARY CYSTS VISCERAL GOUT. This 17-year-old milk snake had a history of a mass in the caudal abdomen. Celiotomy revealed neoplasia within the kidneys and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were irregular and enlarged with foci of yellow to white material. Irregular fluid filled structures were present in the liver. A soft yellow nodule was present in the gastric mucosa.

INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ENTERITIS. This 4-year-old female monitor was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a granuloma was noted on the spleen. Flattened yellow structures were free within the coelom.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS HEART AND BRAIN (FREEZE ARTIFACT). This is one of two 5-year-old female sibling meerkats housed indoors and in apparently good health. Their weights averaged just over 1 kg. Both appeared to be in good flesh with excellent appetites. They were found dead in a PCV connecting tunnel. There was no evidence of trauma or abrasions and both were in sleeping position next to each other. The carcasses were frozen prior to necropsy.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE IRON STORAGE EMACIATION EUTHANSIA. This 15-year-old naked mole rat was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified multiple yellow foci in the liver a cyst in the right kidney to 1 cm. in greatest dimension pale discoloration of the cranial aspect of the spleen and no other gross abnormalities.

GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old blue tongued skink presented for lethargy and inability to ambulate effectively. The front limbs and right rear limbs showed severely decreased function and a persistent position of the ventral side. The animal was born with marked spinal deformities. Pale soft tissue swellings were visible along the ventral aspects of the limbs. One of the swellings on the left ventral stifle was lanced and expressed material that was chalky and white resembling uric acid crystals by light microscopy. Visceral and articular gout was suspected and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple subcutaneous pale regions on all limbs covering the dependent surfaces especially near the joints. Small multifocal raised subcutaneous plaques were in the skin beneath the mandible and along the ventral thorax and abdomen. The animal also had marked kyphosis of the pelvis lordosis of the lumbar spine and scoliosis of the caudal vertebrae. A mild hemorrhagic pericardial effusion was noted. The stomach contained serous foamy fluid. The colon was distended with feces. A 1.5 cm. concretion was noted in the urinary bladder. Both kidneys were markedly enlarged and diffusely infiltrated with white chalky plaques covering 99% of the serosa and extending into the renal cortex on cut surface. Similar material was found in the pelvic canal. Small nodules of white chalky material were in the mediastinal tissues of the cranial thorax.

TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA CHRONIC CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male/neutered tiger had lost 20 kg. since last time it was weighed in October 2011. The tiger does not eat well and is mostly hand fed. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a firm mass adjacent to the trigone of the urinary bladder that is 3.5 cm. in greatest dimension. The right kidney was polycystic. Multiple small nodular areas were in the left atrioventricular valve leaflet resembling endocardiosis.

AMYLOIDOSIS INANITION. This 3-year/7-month-old male marmoset was found dead. Recently the family group was moved from their large enclosure to a smaller cage so that the large enclosure could be cleaned. The next day this male and a baby were found dead. At necropsy there was ingesta present in the stomach and digesta present in the small and large intestine.

GRANULOMATOUS AIR SACCULITIS STEATITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK MYOCARDIAL STEATOSIS. This 9-year-old female chicken was lethargic. The animal has a recent history of weight loss. Examination revealed a loss of deep pain response. Respiratory and cardiac arrest ensued. At necropsy the animal was thin with a prominent keel. The colon contained a large yellow/white mass. Numerous 0.5-1.5 cm. in diameter masses were present in the mesentery.

EUTHANASIA INTRASPECIES TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 5-year-old male mole rat had bite wounds and had been under treatment. The feet became swollen and had abscesses with exposure of the underlying bone. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy purulent material was noted in the left front and right rear feet with necrosis of the digit on the right foot.
HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 10-year-old female tern was found dead. At necropsy the liver was markedly enlarged.

PROLIFERATIVE ENTEROCOLITIS CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female giant eland had been thin for some time. Supportive care initially was administered four years earlier. The animal had evidence of mild anemia leukocytosis with left shift and hypoalbuminemia at that time and has never fully recovered after the event but did produce a calf. Recently this animal has developed diarrhea with marked weight loss received supportive care and also had anemia leukocytosis with left shift and hypoalbuminemia. The animal responded partially to supportive care but has remained noticeably thin despite good appetite. The animal developed an episode of diarrhea of one week’s duration and fecal examination revealed moderate elevation in strongyle egg count. The animal was separated from the herd received supportive care but did not noticeably improve despite good appetite. The animal was found head pressing in a corner and unable to stand without balancing. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed absence of adipose generalized pallor 300 ml. of clear fluid in the abdominal cavity serous atrophy of fat around the heart and gastrointestinal tract markedly enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinal and gastric regions generalized organ pallor regurgitated material in the trachea a large amount of frothy material and liquid in the rumen slightly rounded papillae and no apparent fiber mat. Multiple areas of hyperemia and pigmentation were in the abomasum as well as some healed ulcers. No active ulcers were seen. Fluid was in the small intestine. The cecum was diffusely reddened but with minimal parasites noted. Soft formed feces were in the large intestine. The liver seemed small.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY IRON STORAGE DISEASE DIC. This 26-year-old female lemur was found dead laying on its left side with its right foot gripped on the cage front. Necropsy revealed food in the stomach pale mottled liver and no other gross lesions.

CHRONIC SYNOVITIS AIR SACCULITIS AMYLOIDOSIS URATE STASIS INTRAMUSCULAR HEMORRHAGE. This 17-year-old female flamingo was under treatment for septicemia and arthritis. Blood work revealed severe hyperuricemia. At necropsy swelling was noted over the tarsus. Friable tissue was present beneath the pectoral muscle. Firm masses were noted in the axilla extending to the deep pectorals and humerus. Tan nodules were noted in the air sacs.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA. This 14-year/5-month-old female impala was humanely euthanized. It had fallen trying to get a drink in front of exhibit. It stumbled and fell several times getting off exhibit. At necropsy there were abrasions through the skin and into muscles above both elbow joints. The 3rd and 4th cheek teeth on the maxilla had hypertrophy of the gingiva of the labial surface. There was a lot of impacted hay in areas of both right and left mandible. The right uterine horn was enlarged. There was arthritis and spondylosis. There was a 3 cm. irregularly shaped hard rubbery substance in the rumen.

MYELOLIPOMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This female 7-year-old captive bred lovebird was found dead. It fell abruptly from perch and was presented dead to the hospital. It had no premonitory clinical signs noted. At necropsy the liver was moderately enlarged and diffusely pale. It floated in formalin. There was a slight cobblestone texture to the hepatic surface. On cut section the liver was homogeneously pale. The ovary was cystic. There was a 1.5 x 1 cm. pale tan encapsulated mass associated with the right kidney or adrenal gland. The ischiatic nerve associated vessels and the right ureter were stretched ventrally and medially around the mass. Tissues were submitted for West Nile virus testing.

NECK TRAUMA. This 1-year-old male captive bred gerenuk ran into a fence or tree on its exhibit and dislocated its neck. The animal is from a barn that has been under quarantine for bovine tuberculosis. Necropsy revealed good nutritional state with moderate fat stores. The lungs were congested with blood. A large area of hemorrhage was in the musculature of the cranial cervical region. A complete dislocation was detected between C1-C2 and the caudal aspect of the lateral transverse process was fractured bilaterally. The rostral portion of the dorsal spinous process of C2 was fractured from the underlying bone. All lymph nodes appeared larger than expected but were grossly normal on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 21-year-old chinchilla has a recent history of severe weight loss and lethargy. Marked elevations in BUN glucose and phosphorus were noted on blood work and marked scoliosis and degenerative joint disease were identified radiographically. Given the advanced age of this animal it was humanely euthanized. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA AMYLOIDOSIS INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS. This greater than 1-year-old black-footed ferret presented in moribund condition and died while anesthetized for examination. The ferret previously was diagnosed with coccidiosis and was being treated. Blood work at the time of examination revealed severe elevations in serum CK phosphorus calcium blood urea nitrogen and creatinine. The animal had been recently acquired (two months earlier). Necropsy revealed dehydration generalized petechiae and no other abnormalities.

BACTERIAL HRINITIS SEPTICEMIA INANITION. This 13-year/9-month-old male duck died. It had a history of left leg lameness and granuloma removed from the right naris on 4/6. It was swimming in the quarantine pool with difficulty. It also had recent weight loss of 100 gm. It was found floating dead in the pool. It had been treated with enrofloxacin for seven days. At necropsy the keel was prominent and the duck was in thin body condition. There were small tannish-white plaques on all air sacs. The gall bladder was distended. There was approximately 1 ml. of pericardial effusion. The heart was grossly enlarged by approximately 30%. The right external naris was deformed. Approximately 2 cm. of the bill was missing around the naris. There was a caseous tan material present in the deformed area. There was ingesta in the crop. The ventriculus was full of seed and grit. The proventriculus was empty. All joints of the left leg were examined and appeared grossly normal.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL ARTHRITIS INTERVERTEBRAL DISK DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS ENDOMETRITIS. This 13-year-old female goat was euthanized due to neurologic dysfunction and spinal arthritis. At necropsy the animal was thin. Irregular bony proliferations were noted in the cervical vertebrae with disk protrusion between C1 and C5. Heart valves had nodular foci of fibrosis.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 10-year-old female bighorn sheep suffered an acute fracture of the left femur. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a midshaft transverse femoral fracture was identified in the left leg. No other significant lesions were identified at necropsy.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS EMACIATION. This greater than 4-year-old male frog died spontaneously and was refrigerated three hours prior to necropsy. The frog had been relocated to a new facility on three separate occasions and apparently had not been eating well. Necropsy revealed emaciation myocardial hemorrhage and ulceration on the feet.
adult. Weight: 787.6 g.  Euth. Chr.diabetes. Poor cond'n. Chr.dermatitis; tail. Missing distal digits. Hepatitis? Pulm.oedema (agonal?). Myocardial pallor. Polycystic kidneys. Renal nodule.

URATE STASIS AND RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male duck had been spending much time out of the water and lying down which is abnormal for this species. Lameness was observed when the duck walked. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed some mild cracks in the right third digit some calluses in the left foot osteophytes on the medial and lateral aspects of the left stifle some 3 mm. pale foci in the right caudal hepatic lobe and no other gross abnormalities.

1. Kidney: Renal carcinoma 2. Kidney: Interstitial nephritis; lymphocytic; multifocal; mild; chronic 3. Kidney: Renal gout; multifocal; mild; chronic 4. Skeletal muscle: Myositis; granulomatous and heterophilic; regional; marked; chronic 5. Heart: Arteriosclerosis; multifocal; moderate; chronic 6. Heart: Interstitial fibrosis; perivascular; multifocal; mild; chronic Comment: This animal had histologic lesions in multiple organs that may have contributed to the clinical signs noted. In the submitted history; drowning was suspected (the animal was found dead in the pool with a claw stuck in the pool grate); and could be considered as a possible cause of death. Renal lesions noted grossly were consistent with renal carcinoma. Other renal lesions included interstitial nephritis and renal gout. Granulomatous and heteriophilic myositis was present in one section of skeletal muscle. No intralesional infectious organisms were observed; however bacterial infection is a plausible differential diagnosis; possibly induced by regional skeletal muscle trauma. Cardiac lesions included moderate arteriosclerosis and perivascular fibrosis; both considered age-related findings - no inflammation was observed in the heart. West Nile virus and heavy metal toxicity screening were pending (per history); and immunohistochemistry for West Nile virus is also available upon request.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 4-year-old female ring-tailed lemur is the second lemur from this collection to die in the last few weeks. The lemur was sick for approximately one week prior to death. Necropsy revealed blood in the thorax adhesion of the heart to the left thoracic wall with fibrin and consolidated lung that sinks in formalin. Aerobic cultures were obtained.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS INANITION. This approximately 19-year-old male lory was found dead. At necropsy it was emaciated. There was severe granulomatous splenitis and hepatitis. There was mucoid exudate in the lung. There were possible mucoid granulomas in the proximal small intestine. Sections of spleen and liver were frozen for future use if needed.

EUTHANASIA NASAL ADENOCARCINOMAHEPATITIS GASTRITIS GLUMERULONEPHROPATHY LEFT SIDED HEART FAILURE. This 30-year-old male lemur was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic nasal discharge. Nasal tissue cytology revealed possible bacterial and/or fungal infection. The lemur developed respiratory distress. Further examination revealed blockage of the right nasal passage by a tissue mass.

EUTHANASIA BILATERAL CATARACTS BILATERAL RETINAL SEPARATION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS GASTRITIS. This 6-year-old female mandrill had a hypermature cataract in the left eye and a developing cataract in the right eye. Acute blindness developed one week prior to euthanasia. Bilateral detached retinas were identified by ultrasound and an electroretinogram determined that both eyes were nonvisual. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy in addition to the ocular lesions identified above there was a small quantity of serosanguineous fluid in the pericardium. Numerous cysts were present in the kidney.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female meerkat had a two year history of progressive thoracolumbar scoliosis and bridging vertebral arthritis. Pain management was accomplished with a chronic course of tramadol and meloxicam. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes and no gross lesions were noted other than the skeletal lesions.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA (SPLEEN LIVER) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 3-year-old female ferret had a mass in the spleen. Masses were also identified in the thorax. The animal’s condition was declining and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multifocal to coalescing white nodules were present throughout the spleen and liver.

CHRONIC EPICARDITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOCARDIOSIS CARDIAC FAILURE ENDOCRINE CARCINOMA C-CELL ADENOMA EMACIATION. This 20-year-old female sea lion presented with perineal edema which progressed to generalized ventral peripheral edema and the animal was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed bilateral cysts in the thyroid glands marked peripheral ventral edema marked fibrinous ascites marked pleural effusion marked fibrinous pericardial effusion marked fibrinous epicarditis severe endocardiosis pulmonary congestion and edema cachexia generalized lymph node enlargement systemic congestion and nodules in the uterus.

MILD VASCULAR MINERALIZATION GASTRIC CESTODIASIS POSSIBLE DEATH RELATED TO EGG LAYING. This 5-year-old female basilisk lizard was found dead on exhibit. Gross necropsy revealed tail regrowth from the mid portion of the tail and multiple shelled ova in both oviducts with one egg visible at the level of the cloaca.

MESOTHELIOMA (LUNG THORAX) BILIARY CYST HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 18-year-old male lion died under anesthesia. At necropsy several liters of serosanguineous fluid were present in the pleural cavity. Numerous proliferative masses were present on the pleura diaphragm and lungs. The liver contained globular cyst-like masses containing serous fluid. The GI tract was diffusely thickened and firm and contained hemorrhagic and mucoid material.

HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS PROVENTRICULAR AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC ARTHRITIS PHTHISIS BULBI. This 54-year-old male flamingo suffered a fracture of the distal humerus and radius during a hailstorm. The fractures had been healing; however left leg lameness and hock swelling developed. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was found dead. At necropsy the bird was thin. Calluses were present adjacent to the fracture sites. Erosion of the articular cartilage was noted in the hock joint. The mucosa of the GI tract was hemorrhagic. White foci were noted on the heart and kidney.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS SUSPECT ENTERIC CLOSTRIDIOSIS ESOPHAGEAL CAPILLARIASIS COELOMITIS. This 3-year/1-month-old female prairie chicken died. At necropsy it was thin. The large intestine had multifocal raised plaques on the mucosal surface.

XANTHOMATOSIS OOPHORITIS KERATITIS. This 10-year-old female anole presented with masses in the conjunctiva and corneal opacities. Xanthomatosis was noted on biopsy of the conjunctival mass. The animal became anorexic and showed weight loss presumably due to blindness. Elevations of phosphorus and uric acid were also noted. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy marked corneal opacity was noted. Several small round structures were identified in the coelomic cavity containing tan material.

TRAUMA STRESS CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK. This 2.5-year-old male tanager was acquired as a young bird in 2012 and had recently been moved to a new aviary. The bird had been observed behaving normally and eating in its new surroundings but was found dead on the ground unexpectedly in the morning. Necropsy revealed good body condition with adequate fat stores slightly enlarged and swollen liver marked multifocal hemorrhage or congestion in the calvaria congestion on the subdural surfaces of the brain and tenacious mucus in the oral cavity.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA COLONIC LEIOMYOMA PITUITARY AND ADRENAL MEDULLARY HYPERPLASIA ADRENAL CORTICAL ATROPHY EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male kangaroo had a history of squamous cell carcinoma involving the right mandibular ramus and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed poor body condition with much weight loss despite good appetite. An 8 cm. mass involved the mandible. Areas of consolidated pulmonary parenchyma were noted in both lungs primarily on pleural surfaces. The great vessels had sclerotic change. An 8 cm. mass was associated with the serosal surface of the colon that on cut surface resembled an inspissated abscess. Multiple cystic structures are present within the parenchyma of the liver up to 6.5 cm. in greatest dimension all of which were filled with bile.

DIC ULCERATIVE COLITIS GRANULOMATOUS STEATITIS SEPSIS. This greater than 1-year-old male rock hyrax had a one day history of reluctance to move with associated diarrhea. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed a rounded heart with petechiae reddened right lung atelectasis dark large intestine and a hard mass surrounding the testicle. Mesenteric lymph nodes were firm.

UNDIFFERENTIATED CARCINOMA PULMONARY SHOCK INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 3-year-old pygmy hedgehog was found with vaginal hemorrhage. A large firm mass was palpated in the caudal abdomen. The animal was treated with supportive care but was found dead the following morning. At necropsy the abdominal cavity was filled with serosanguineous fluid. There was a 4-5 cm. diameter red friable mass in the abdominal cavity. The mass appeared to arise from the uterus but was adherent to the intestinal tract and omentum.

TRAUMA. This 26-year-old male Inca tern was noted to be favoring its left leg and examination revealed instability in the left stifle due to fracture or joint luxation. Marked bruising and some bleeding of the left carpus were also noted but no apparent fracture at this location. A sling was applied to the leg but the bird was found deceased the following morning. Necropsy revealed abrasions and bruising over the left wing and marked bruising and hemorrhage extending from the caudal half to the left pectoral muscle to the stifle joint. The tendons around the stifle were completely severed and the stifle was subluxated. The spleen was diffusely pale.
MYOPATHY. This female approximately 9-month-old snake was found dead in its enclosure. It was eating and behaving normally. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

VASCULITIS AND HISTIOCYTIC INFLAMMATION. This 3-year-old intact female dama gazelle had a recent history of multiple medical issues including a swelling of the left mandible with associated tooth root abscess and mandibular osteomyelitis. Supportive care was administered and the dam calved with no discernable complications. The calf was healthy and normal. Following parturition a few weeks later the dam was noted to have a heavy burden of strongyle ova and then developed ventral edema. The animal had become slightly hyperthermic which resolved shortly after restraint. Blood work at this time revealed marked leukopenia and moderate thrombocytopenia. One week later leukopenia with regenerative left shift was identified thrombocyte count had slightly improved and elevations were noted in serum AST. A few days later the ventral edema had recurred but then resolved the next day. Follow-up blood work identified moderate anemia and severe thrombocytopenia with further elevations of serum AST. The patient subsequently became severely lethargic and unable to stand with hypothermia pallor and profound weakness. Streams of desiccated blood were noted from injection sites the previous day. Shortly after examination the patient became agonal and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin light blood multiple ecchymoses throughout the subcutis over the body a focus of darkened bone corresponding with the mandibular osteomyelitis reddened lymph nodes abundant fibrous adhesions in the cranial pulmonary lobes numerous foci of hemorrhage throughout the costal and medial surfaces of the lungs petechiae in the heart and throughout the alimentary tract and asymmetry in the uterine horns the right horn larger and lighter than the left horn.

JUMPY JAW EUTHANASIA. This 7-year/7-month-old female wallaroo was humanely euthanized. It was noted to have had a mass on the jaw and weakness. Physical exam and radiographs revealed bony erosions associated with a mass on the upper mandible with loss of root of the first molar. The lesions were typical of lumpy jaw or necrobacillosis. Aerobic and anaerobic cultures were taken of the abscess. At necropsy the molar teeth had a significant amount of tartar particularly the first lower left molar which was loose. No parasites were seen within the intestinal tract. A spherical mass of sebaceous material with a thin membrane of approximately 4 cm. in diameter was in the subcutaneous tissue dorsal to the rectum. There were multiple small (1 cm. to 4 cm.) nodules throughout the lungs that were filled with green purulent material. The left mandible had a severe area of bony enlargement centrally for approximately 50% of its length that was surrounded by fibrous connective tissue. On cut section the center of the enlargement had many pockets of green purulent material. The mandibular bone was soft and eroded.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE. This 4-year-old female budgerigar was found dead. Necropsy revealed a large blood clot in the abdomen that appeared to originate from the liver. The liver was soft and friable. Lumps were noted on the pancreas.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HISTIOCYTIC LYMPHADENOPATHY PNEUMOCONIOSIS EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS. This 13-year-old male leopard has been under treatment for arthritis. Recently the animal became inappetent and unwilling to drink. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy a plastic bag was present in the stomach. Fluid filled cysts were present in all liver lobes and white nodules were present on the pancreas. Marked muscle atrophy was noted.

LYMPHOMA PULMONARY SMOOTH MUSCLE HYPERTROPHY NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male leopard has a 6-7 week history of chronic vomiting and inappetence. Endoscopy identified mild ulceration in the lower esophagus multiple small raised lesions in the gastric mucosa two larger firm masses near the pyloric sphincter and unremarkable duodenum. Biopsies were obtained of the pyloric masses. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy identified two firm nodules on the caudal lobe of the liver a gray multilobulated firm mass on the margin of the left lateral hepatic lobe and multiple small lumps on the gastric mucosa with two more pronounced masses in the regions of the biopsies. The jejunum and ileum were reddened.

CARDIOMYOPATHY VENTRICULAR THROMBUS EUTHANASIA. This 1.5-year-old male Virginia opossum had a history of severe malformation of the coxofemoral joint and chronic degenerative joint disease for which it was receiving supportive care. The animal abruptly developed apparent thoracic disease with exercise intolerance a pounding heart weakness and inappetence and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 50-60 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the thorax and 20-30 ml. in the abdomen. The right ventricle appeared larger than the left. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

THYMOMA BACTERIAL ESOPHAGITIS HEPATITIS URATE STASIS RENAL TUBULAR MINERALIZATION. This 11-year-old owl underwent surgery for a subcutaneous mass in the cervical region. The animal was found dead the following weak. At necropsy the bird was thin. A large necrotic ulcer was present in the esophagus with caseous material.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 11.5-year-old female domestic goat was found recumbent and dyspneic with bottle jaw and brisket edema. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachexia ascites thin heart walls nodular fatty and exudative miliary granules encasing the heart and scattered throughout the mediastinum. Ovaries were enlarged and cystic with possible ovarian tumor. Pancreas was small and fatty. Kidneys were small. The adrenals were possibly enlarged. Fibrosis and possible inflammation were noted in the mammary glands.

EUTHANASIA MULTISYSTEMIC GRANULOMATOUS DISEASE DERMATITIS CELLULITIS INANITION. This greater than 7-year-old female mantella was humanely euthanized. It had a history of being extremely distended. Over 1.5 cm. of air was aspirated.

PRESUMED HEMANGIOSARCOMA ISLET CELL TUMOR LYMPHONODULAR HYPERPLASIA IN THE SPLEEN ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA NEPHROSCLEROSIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS CARDIAC LIPOMATOIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female gray wolf had a long-term history of receiving meloxicam for suspected arthritis. The animal began knuckling and was ataxic in both pelvic limbs. Radiographs were suspicious for mineralized discs. Blood work revealed azotemia. The animal continued to lose weight was hyporexic and was euthanized. At necropsy there were small firm areas in all pulmonary lobes the spleen had two masses the gastric mucosa was erythematous with focal ulceration the duodenum was erythematous a small mass was in the pancreas the kidneys were pale with an irregular surface and a large mass was overlying the caudal aorta just cranial to the pelvis.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 13-year-old male ringed teal was found dead. This bird has a history of swollen uropygial gland which responded to Baytril. At gross necropsy the uropygial glands contained thick yellow exudate. Otherwise the bird had no significant gross lesions.

INTERRENAL CELL ADENOMA SEPSIS. This 13.5-year-old female copperhead has a several month history of inappetence. Examination revealed a palpable soft tissue mass in the caudal coelom and a lytic lesion in the right ribs at about the level of the heart. Exploratory surgery was performed to evaluate the mass in the caudal coelom and the animal never fully recovered from anesthesia. Necropsy revealed good body condition wrinkled skin in the area of the rib lysis serosanguineous fluid expressed from the lung and trachea a 1 cm. yellow colored cystic region in the liver enlarged gallbladder and a 2 cm. in diameter firm irregular tan hemorrhagic mass arising from the junction of the proximal third and caudal two-thirds of the right kidney. The caudal portion of the right kidney was infiltrated with smaller irregular tan masses some of which appeared cystic. The left kidney had a similar infiltrate of tan lesions throughout the parenchyma. A region of bone loss in the ribs and thoracic wall on the right side adjacent to the heart was noted. Within this region there were several irregularly shaped abscesses that exuded tan paste-like exudate on cut surface. A moderate amount of serous fluid was free in the caudal coelom.

DROWNING. This approximately 4-year/3-month-old female snake was found dead in tank. At necropsy the eyes were opaque. The skin came off easily in a normal shed. The lungs were wet. There was considerable pericardial fluid. There was digested food in the stomach. The ovaries had follicles in various stages of development. The kidneys were very pale. There was a moderate amount of coelomic fat.
BACTERIAL VENTRICULITIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 1-year-old tanager was found down. The animal was under treatment but later died. At necropsy the organs were pale.

GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA COELOMITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 9-year-old female green tree monitor had a history of chronic weight loss cachexia and dehydration. A coelomic effusion was noted several months prior to death which was characterized as an acellular serous effusion. At gross necropsy the animal was emaciated and had evidence of stomatitis adjacent to the left maxilla. The liver was mottled yellow/tan and enlarged. There was a spherical yellow to green mass in the mid abdomen dorsal to the stomach approximately 1 cm. in diameter. The mass was lamellated on section. Granulomas were present within the lung and mesentery.

EUTHANASIA MESENTERIC TORSION SHOCK. This 4-year-old male wolf was immobilized for semen collection. Recovery was normal; however several hours later the animal was depressed and unresponsive. Exploratory laparotomy was performed for suspected gastric torsion which revealed mesenteric root torsion with extensive damage to the GI tract and spleen. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the small intestine cecum and proximal large intestine were displaced cranially anterior to the stomach. The spleen was markedly enlarged and caudal to the stomach. The root of the mesentery was hemorrhagic. Petechial and ecchymotic hemorrhages were noted on the stomach. The stomach contained a large quantity of dark red fluid. Similar fluid was present in the GI tract. Dark red to orange urine was present in the urinary bladder.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS STROKE EUTHANASIA. This approximately 40-year-old male thick billed parrot had a history of bilateral cataracts and corneal lesions in the right eye. It also has a five year history of stroke-like neurologic episodes. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

JOINT TRAUMA CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS WITH FLAGELLATES SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female ruddy duck had a three day history of lethargy with reduced response to keepers. The bird had loss of body condition and depression. The bird also had a history of arthritis and lameness in the right limb. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed decreased muscling over the pectoral region an effusion in the right stifle joint osteoarthritis in the stifle articulation and no other abnormalities.

ULCERATIVE STOMATITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS DENTAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male goat has a history of oral food impaction that worsened despite treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with good internal fat stores oral diverticula packed with ingesta with extension into the soft tissues caudal to the left eye uneven tooth wear gingival recession and root exposure and a small red left adrenal gland.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE IMMOBILIZATION COMPLICATIONS ENTERITIS AND ABOMASITIS. This 6-year-old male reticulated giraffe was sedated for repair of the hoof wall on the right front foot. While in the chute the animal collapsed and died. CPR was attempted but was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed possible enlargement of the thyroid glands and adrenal glands severe rotational deformity and flexor contracture of the right front leg conical heart with prominent apex and possible hypertrophy of the ventricular muscle.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS. This 4-year-old male degu presented with severe respiratory distress. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy fibrinous adhesions were noted between the lung and pleura.

CHRONIC RENAL DISESE EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male Sumatran tiger has a history or progressive chronic renal disease and liver disease with anemia. A blood transfusion was administered two days prior to euthanasia.

ISLET CELL TUMOR ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 5.5-year-old female ferret was diagnosed with an insulinoma in February 2015 and was receiving prednisolone. The animal began losing weight although blood glucose was normal. There was a mild elevation in hepatic parameters. Supportive care was administered and ultrasound then identified a section of thickened intestine. Additional treatment resulted in some improvement but continued weight loss. The animal subsequently presented in the morning moribund with low blood glucose and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachexia a small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen coffee ground blood clots around the stomach and pancreas blood in the stomach and ulceration of the gastric mucosa large dark right adrenal gland normal sized left adrenal gland with firm parenchyma no specific lesions in the pancreas and evidence of digested blood in multiple segments of the intestine.

STRESS EPIDERMAL NECROSIS POSSIBLE PAINT TOXICOSIS. This 3-year-old green tree python had historically been used to participate in animal painting. Acrylic paint was inadvertently used instead of the usual water-based paint and the paint could not be removed from skin. This animal had begun to shed and was assisted by a volunteer. A manager noted bruising on the ventrum later in the afternoon and the next morning the animal was found dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition and several regions of irregular medium blue coloration on the body attributed to ecdysis or bruising in the underlying muscle. Two 1 cm. streaks of red paint were present at the caudal aspect of the animal. The gonad was small and could not be further identified.

CEREBRAL GANGLIONEUROMA EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old male hedgehog had a history of presumed allergy associated respiratory signs with watery nasal discharge sneezing and a chapped upper lip. Supportive care was administered and the animal appeared to respond. The hedgehog subsequently developed a brief period of inappetence and depression that responded to antibiotics after which the signs returned and accompanied by a head tilt and ataxia with significant paraparesis. Supportive care was administered and the animal improved to almost normal status in the next few days but then became depressed had hypersalivation weakness and was unable to walk. The animal became quadriplegic obtunded and possibly blind and could not swallow. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed adequate fat stores a small intradermal nodule on the right shoulder dry flaky skin around the quills a single pinpoint tan focus in the parenchyma of the liver a single red focus buried in the parenchyma of one lobe of the pancreas engorged enlarged spleen mostly empty alimentary tract a few submucosal white slightly linear raised areas in the esophagus congested lungs herniation of the cerebellum through the foramen magnum flattened and herniated brainstem and an ill-defined mass-like enlargement of the left olfactory lobe of the cerebrum with distortion of the normal contours and compression across the midline.

Euthanized (for soft tissue sarcoma previously diagnosed) Kidney: Multifocal severe glomerulosclerosis; proteinosis; and mild glomerulonephritis Liver: Mild hemosiderosis Lung: Mild multifocal granulomatous pneumonia with lipid (endogenous lipid pneumonia) Small intestine: Mild multifocal crypt ectasia Ovary: Cystic rete ovarii; ovarian lipidosis; follicular exhaustion Uterus: Moderate endometrial atrophy; arteriolar hyalinization Comment: These changes are all common in geriatric patients and none were clinically significant; though the renal lesions were likely progressive and would have continued to develop leading to decreased renal function. The reproductive organs have been archived in the Reproductive Health Surveillance program.

EMACIATION GLOSSAL CANDIDIASIS MACRORHABDIOSIS. This approximately 9-year-old female cockatiel had feather loss around the neck and was morbid with severe emaciation and died. At necropsy there was a large granuloma in the left lung. Some intestinal loops were reddened and the kidneys were pale.

PUSTULAR RUMENITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 3-year-old female southern gerenuk was found dead on exhibit in the morning and had been clinically normal the prior evening. A conspecific died due to acute systemic shock the previous day. Necropsy findings in the animal of this report identified hyperemia and petechiae in various tissues.

SHOCK OVARIAN FOLLICULAR RETENTION AND FOLLICULAR STASIS. This greater than 10-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead. The snake was in fair body condition. The body was very soft on palpation. There were multiple firm lumps throughout the body. At necropsy the ova were large firm and formed. There were multiple ova present throughout the salpinx.

BILARY ADENOCARCINOMA. This 9-year-old male rabbit had clinical signs of pasteurellosis and had been treated for two months for this condition. The animal was euthanized due to persistence of the disease. A 1 cm. white fibrous mass was detected in the caudal liver lobe and the spleen was small.

SEPSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION NEPHROSCLEROSIS POSSIBLE HYPERVITAMINOSIS D (BONE). This 9-year-old male two-toed sloth was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed poor body condition a moderate amount of diarrhea around the perineum a firm raised growth along the gingival surface of both mandibular canines soft cartilage along the left femoral head gelatinous thyroids thick and fibrous mediastinum gelatinous clots in the oracles and ventricles globoid heart thin walled right ventricle multiple roughened plaques above the aortic valves that extended into the aorta firm aorta and several other firm vessels absence of adipose stores two-toned serosal surface of the left kidney gritty urate-like material in the pelvis of the left kidney pale renal parenchyma a focus of white discoloration in the medulla of the right kidney urine in the urinary bladder thickened pyloric mucosa ulceration of the pylorus mottled serosal surface of the liver white discoloration on the serosal surface of the liver a white nonraised lesion extending into the parenchyma on cut surface of the liver and male reproductive tract.

CARINAL ABSCESS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 5-year-old male fruit bat had developed an abscess on its had and appeared to be doing well with treatment but was found dead unexpected. Necropsy revealed an abscess on the rostrum and when removed a deep hole was noted in the sinus. The sinus was discolored brown. A small bone growth was noted on the back of the skull. Lungs were congested.

EXUDATIVE EPIDERMITIS COLITIS FATTY LIVER. This 9-month-old female boa was found dead. It was admitted to the zoo hospital for quarantine on Dec. 6 2000 with another snake. The cagemate was found dead in the morning approximately one week prior to this snake’s death. Neither snake ate during quarantine. This snake was tube fed with feline clinicare. The mucous membranes were white when the animal was tubed. It regurgitated a small amount of formula when placed in its cage but appeared BAR. At necropsy there was small 5-10 mm. black discoloration on the dermis of the left cranial one-third of the snake. The lung was white. The heart was small and pale. The kidneys were tan. The liver was tan. There was a large amount of bile staining along the small intestines and coelomic lining. The cloaca had a small amount of urates. The pancreas was erythematous. When the cranium was incised there was a moderate amount of clear fluid.

YOLK SACCULITIS OSTEOMYELITIS WITH PATHOLOGIC FRACTURE AND SPINAL CORD NECROSIS. This 7-month-old rattlesnake was in quarantine and was found dead. It had not eaten since arrival. Necropsy revealed atrophied muscle pallor in the coelomic cavity and coelomic viscera moderately enlarged gallbladder empty alimentary tract aside from some liquid material in the terminal colon.

DISSEMINATED INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS PROBABLY VIRAL. This 6.5-year-old female hooded merganser was found dead in its food bowl. Necropsy revealed normal GI contents a small area of hyperemia on the proventricular mucosa mildly enlarged heart and yellow streaking in the muscle.

EUTHANASIA GLOMERULONEPHRITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 5-month-old ferret was nonresponsive and weak and was euthanized. At gross necropsy the kidneys had a band of pallor at the corticomedullary junction and one kidney had a 4 mm. cortical cyst.

CHRONIC ENTERITIS BACTERIAL HEPATITIS LYMPHADENITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 20-year-old male lemur underwent exploratory laparotomy following four days of lethargy and no fecal production. Numerous adhesions and dilation of the bile duct were noted on laparotomy. No peristalsis was noted in the intestine during surgery. The animal recovered uneventfully postoperatively but was found dead the following day. At necropsy enlargement of mediastinal lymph nodes was noted.

BACTERIAL HEPATIC ABSCESSES EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old male colobus seems slightly less active and responsive and within 24 hours was comatose. Exploratory surgery revealed multiple large hepatic abscesses and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified atrophy of fat clear yellow fluid with fibrin clots in the abdominal cavity large liver with fibrous adhesions in the mesentery to the mesentery colon and gastric wall. Multiple masses are in the liver up to 8 cm. in greatest dimension. Purulent material was in the center of the masses and white tissue infiltrated the liver around these structures. The right lung was collapsed and the right bronchus was occluded with aspirated gastric contents. The left lung was edematous.

LAMINITIS SOLE ABSCESS EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female Grévy’s zebra had a 2.5 month history of laminitis that progressed to abscess in the right front foot in which a sequestrum eventually formed. The sequestrum was removed surgically and postoperatively the foot became severely infected with eventual hoof wall separation. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This zebra had received numerous doses of Banamine phenylbutazone and omeprazole over the last few months.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 24-year-old male ibis was found in the exhibit stream wet and shivering. The animal was warmed but died a short time later. At necropsy the GI tract was devoid of ingesta.

CHRONIC CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE OVER HYDRATION EMACIATION. This 19-year-old female straw-colored fruit bat had a less than one day history of illness that included being found on the bottom of its cage unresponsive and hypothermic. Supportive care was administered but the animal died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed 11.5 ml. of straw-colored clear fluid in the peritoneal cavity thickened right ventricular wall and slightly dilated left ventricle pale digestive tract pale stomach absence of the glandular/nonglandular gastric demarcation fluid-filled lungs with purple discoloration a large lymph node in the cranial ventral cervical region pale edges on the spleen bilaterally darkly speckled kidneys with mildly dilated renal pelvis and prominent vasculature and possibly abnormal caudal dorsal vasculature. The liver was wet filled with fluid friable and mottled.

BACTERIAL HEPATITIS SEUSPECT SEPTICEMIA PULMONARY EDEMA. This 3-year-old male captive bred chinchilla was found dead in exhibit. It was in good health and had no signs of injury. At necropsy the liver was mottled and had rounded edges. The stomach was enlarged and gaseous. There was a large amount of liquid food material in the stomach. The serosa was slightly hemorrhagic. The gall bladder contained inspissated bile.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS PUSTULAR RUMENITIS. This 4-year-old female gerenuk was found recumbent in the evening and had been clinically normal that afternoon. Blood work identified hypovolemic shock hypocalcemia azotemia and hyperkalemia. The animal died while anesthetized for exam. Necropsy revealed good body condition hemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity hyperemia in blood vessels throughout the mucosa of the trachea and multiple pinpoint black foci and consolidation throughout the lungs. Petechiae were present throughout the cardiovascular system and a hemorrhagic effusion was in the abdomen. The mucosa of the abomasum was reddened. The liver was friable. The mesenteric lymph nodes were prominent. The small intestine was congested and edematous. The central nervous system was congested.

INTESTINAL DISPLACEMENT EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female Parma wallaby had a one week history of inappetence gastrointestinal disease with gas severely reduced fecal output and possible neurologic disease or weakness. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed adequate intra-abdominal fat stores gas distention in the stomach and intestinal tract reddened duodenum dark red thick duodenal contents moderate splenomegaly and no other abnormalities.

DIABETES MELLITUS ISLET CELL VACUOLAR DEGENERATION PANCREATITIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female domestic ferret was diagnosed with insulinoma in 2009 and had been managed with prednisolone since. The ferret also has clinical signs suggestive of adrenal disease but this was not substantiated with blood work. The ferret developed a one week history of lethargy hyperglycemia ketonuria and glucosuria. A midabdominal mass was palpated. Insulin was administered and glucose level returned to level over a two day period. The ferret’s condition subsequently worsened developing diarrhea and partial rectal prolapse and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation fecal staining around the rectum and tail generalized alopecia multiple dark mottled areas on the skin of the legs attributed to hematoma formation associated with venipuncture dark red right caudal and right middle lung lobes moderate periodontal disease digested blood in the stomach trichobezoar in the stomach a 3 cm. mass in the mesentery adjacent to the stomach resembling adipose tissue pale liver large spleen multiple firm round masses in the mesentery adjacent to the jejunum. The right adrenal gland appeared grossly normal and the left adrenal gland could not be located.

EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA HEPATITIS ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA. This 7-year-old male ferret developed seizures and hypoglycemic episodes. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the spleen was markedly enlarged and contained a small soft nodule. A firm mass was present within the pancreas. Small white foci were present in the liver.

UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA WITH CARCINOMATOSIS AND METASTASIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS ASPIRATION. This 12-year-old female sheep had been acting inappetent and lethargic and had a slightly distended abdomen. Blood work was unremarkable. A gastric tube was passed which did not yield free gas and 250 ml. of mineral oil were administered. The animal was found dead the following day. Necropsy revealed a 4 cm. firm subcutaneous mass dorsal to the left scapula. Both lungs were congested and contain serosanguineous fluid and cranial sections of both lungs do not float in formalin.
