In the abdomen were 3-4 liters of straw-colored fluid. The liver was small and pale tan to yellow. Several 1 cm. white firm nodules were in the hepatic parenchyma and some smaller nodules were scattered on the abdominal side of the diaphragm on the internal abdominal wall and on the serosal surface of the rumen. Both horns of the uterus were distended and filled with mucus. A 1 cm. firm white nodule was present in the right uterine horn similar to the nodules in the liver.

ASPERGILLOSIS MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS HEPATITIS ADRENAL AMYLOIDOSIS. This 19-year-old male flamingo was found down. The animal was placed in a sling and treated; however it later died. At necropsy dark green plaques were noted in the mucosa of the trachea. Caseous nodules were present in the lungs.

EUTHANASIA WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME. This 5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of abnormal hind end gait with intermittent weakness and paresis with suspected arthritis and had received steroid therapy. There is a recent history of severe progressive weight gain. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes during an acute episode of hind limb weakness. Necropsy revealed obesity a large amount of subcutaneous and serosal yellow adipose tissue some pallor in the liver prominent biliary ducts thickened white medullary regions in the kidneys and multiple pale fibrotic focal lesions on serosal surfaces of the kidneys slightly enlarged heart urine filled urinary bladder slightly enlarged cranial cervical lymph nodes and no arthritis was seen.

ACUTE PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old female monitor had a history of lethargy and weakness. Blood work revealed anemia and hypoproteinemia. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy the left lung was consolidated and contained clotted blood. The liver was diffusely tan. Small blood clots were present in the stomach and intestine.

TUBULAR NEPHRITIS CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC FIBROSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS ENTERITIS. This 42-year-old female gorilla had a recent history of intermittent coughing and respiratory difficulties. The animal was found nonresponsive and later died. At necropsy adhesions were noted throughout the abdomen. Cardiac valves were nodular and irregular. Adrenal glands were enlarged with prominent medulla. A nodule was present in the uterus. Marked pulmonary edema was noted.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS. This 3.5-year-old female tammar wallaby was found dead in its enclosure. This is the second wallaby to be found dead unexpectedly in the last few months. Necropsy revealed obesity dark red lungs some green discoloration in the colon and no other gross abnormalities.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS SALPINGITIS. This 1-year-old female lorikeet was found dead. Necropsy revealed liquid substance in the gastrointestinal tract and numerous petechiae and ecchymoses in the mesentery. Some hemorrhage was present in the jejunal folds. The liver was light brown to tan with some petechiae and the spleen was pale brown. The kidneys were slightly lighter and firmer than normal.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 5-year-old male squirrel had a history of mandibular trauma and chronically overgrown incisors. The animal recently developed anorexia and lethargy which were unresponsive to treatment. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the liver appeared fatty. The animal had recently been fed an unidentified flowering plant as enrichment.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS AND MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS PERICARDIAL EFFUSION AND CHRONIC SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION. This 2-year-old female pigeon developed a swollen foot in its first summer after hatching (1996) which eventually resolved. The following year the bird wouldn’t load into the crate with other pigeons and appeared overweight lethargic and unwilling to walk. Slight labored breathing was noted shortly before death. Necropsy revealed no body fat serous fluid in the coelomic cavity and pericardial sac wet lungs and tail heart and breast muscle.

PROVENTRICULAR ADENOCARCINOMA MACRORHABDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male budgerigar had been a weak flyer with a poor appetite left leg weakness and caked cloaca. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed seed in the crop and no gross lesions.

DISSEMINATED INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS PROBABLE TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 15-year-old male ring-tailed lemur had decreased activity and appetite with loose stool beginning 8/1. The animal became jaundiced and dyspneic over the course of treatment and died. Necropsy revealed generalized icterus mildly enlarged lymph nodes large amount of thick yellow fluid in the thoracic cavity moderate amount of yellow fluid in the pericardium petechiae in the heart atelectasis in the lungs a large amount of yellow fluid in the abdominal cavity and nutmeg liver.

HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY FAT ATROPHY BUMBLEFOOT. This approximately 28-year-old female swan was found dead. The bird had been acting normal and eating well. At recent annual examination the bird was found to have a low total protein and anemia. At necropsy the head and neck were not present. There was evidence of scavenging on the muscle tissue on the left pectoral muscle. The cloacal area was also opened and the intestinal tract was severed and removed cranial to the cloaca. Both feet had severe pododermatitis on the heels. The overall body condition was thin. The air sacs felt thickened. There were diffuse pinpoint black foci throughout the lungs on the pericardial sac and extending down the tissues covering the abdominal viscera. The ventriculus was packed with grit. There were mildly hyperemic 1 mm. in diameter areas in the proventriculus. The kidneys appeared hyperemic and friable ventrally and pale dorsally. The liver had several pinpoint white lesions that were not raised.

GERIATRIC EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old female squirrel monkey had become cachectic with elevated blood urea nitrogen and elevated hepatic values and could not concentrate urine. The animal developed vomiting behavior with poor appetite and depression hunched appearance and the appearance of pain. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachexia absence of adipose stores hunched posture a small amount of free fluid in the thoracic cavity fluid within the parenchyma with associated cobblestone appearance to the lung yellow discoloration around the great vessels on the heart surface yellow tinged atrophic fat in the cavities a small amount of milky ingesta in the stomach rounded hepatic margins mottled hepatic parenchyma with yellow discoloration small thin spleen bloody fluid in the duodenum atrophied left kidney with abnormal architecture absence of the ovaries and uterus a smooth brown surface to the central nervous system and atrophied muscles.
MALARIA. This female approximately 2-year-old tern was found dead in pool of exhibit. At necropsy it was slightly thin. The hepatic edges were slightly rounded. The spleen was enlarged.

THYMOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male goat had a 10-day history of weakness inappetence and lethargy. Blood work revealed regenerative anemia thoracic radiographs identified a cranial mediastinal mass and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified an 8 cm. mass cranial to the heart base. On cut surface the mass was encapsulated and had white to tan creamy soft tissue and green to yellow gelatinous tissue and some yellow fluid was also noted. Approximately 15 ml. of fluid were in the thoracic cavity. Fibrous material was present along the edges of the caudal pulmonary lobes. Much adipose was in the abdominal cavity and the adipose was firm.

EUTHANASIA PULMONARY GRANULOMATOSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INANITION HEPATIC FIBROSIS STOMATITIS. This 16-year-old female gecko had a history of neurologic signs including stargazing head tilt and circling. The signs progressively worsened and the animal was humanely euthanized.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE THYMOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male goat had a history of chronic rectal polyps and clumped feces. It had been treated for infectious polyarthritis and vestibular disease as a kid. It tested negative for CAE. It was euthanized after one month of severe inappetence wasting and electrolyte derangements that did not respond to supportive care. Necropsy revealed marked muscle wasting alopecia and lichenification over the sternum thin right ventricular free wall periodontal disease gravel and grit in the reticulum grit and fluid in the rumen plant material in the abomasum caseous lymph nodes found in the cervical periprostatic and colonic regions erythematous intestinal mucosa and thin intestinal walls pale kidneys and thickened sternebra.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA MYOSITIS CONJUNCTIVITIS. This male greater than 20-year-old flamingo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of corneal rupture and enucleation. Lacrimal gland adenocarcinoma was found. Radiation treatment was done at TUSVM for four weeks. The flamingo was returned to the zoo and integrated back into the flock. It was keeping good weight but was somewhat aloof from the flock. It seemed a little disoriented from time to time. It had a high titer to West Nile virus during screening in the summer. It was found acutely sternal on exhibit. It appeared weak and could not hold its head up. It had decreased mentation. It was treated with supportive care. The flamingo remained recumbent and was not eating. There was no change in its status. At necropsy there was severe bruising on the lower one-third of the neck. There was muscle tissue hemorrhage that was edematous and purple-green. There was possible luxation of the cervical vertebrae. The pancreas had several pinpoint red foci on the surface.

SARCOCYSTOSIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS MENINGITIS. This 3-year-old lorikeet was found with dyspnea was manually restrained for treatment and developed respiratory failure. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy there was moderate subcutaneous edema and marked air sac edema. The liver was enlarged mottled and pale. The spleen was markedly enlarged and spherical. The lungs were edematous.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EPITHELIAL INCLUSION CYSTS CHRONIC DERMATITIS. This 17-year-old male giraffe had a history of overgrown hooves nerve injury to the hind leg and onset of lameness on the right foreleg. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy swelling was noted in the right ankle joint. Joint fluid was cloudy. Overgrowth of claws with abscessation was noted in the front and rear left foot.

HEMANGIOSARCOMA GASTRIC AND DUODENAL PERFORATING ULCERS PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male gray wolf had a three month history of inappetence lethargy and weight loss and supportive care included antibiotics nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and prednisolone. It was subsequently found recumbent and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Postmortem radiographs revealed pinpoint radiodense foci in the lungs. Necropsy revealed duodenal and pyloric full thickness perforations red masses in the mesentery and spleen cysts in the liver and apparent cachexia.

CHRONIC SKIN ULCER. This 2-year/1-month-old snake of undetermined gender was found dead. It had a history of a chronic wound on the rostrum. It was treated with Pipercilin for the past two months. The lesion was healing slowly but was progressing. At necropsy there was a chronic healing wound on the rostrum that was granulated. The ventricle was pale.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 2.5-year-old female Grévy’s zebra had no previous history. During preshipment examination a firm swelling was noted over the cranial left maxillary region and complicated crown fractures were identified. Diastemas were also present and moderate sharp enamel points. Dental prophy was performed and no evidence of periapical abscess formation was associated with the fractured teeth. The bony swelling was thought to be related to inflammation. Supportive care was administered during and after recovery from anesthesia but the animal was found dead during morning rounds 11 days after the procedure. Necropsy identified good body condition pressed dirt in the coat on the down side a firm swelling of bone over the cranial left maxilla just lateral to the nasal bridge a moderate amount of bruising along the dorsal and caudal left ribs without fractures a mild amount of subcutaneous edema along the ventral left abdomen a focal round subcutaneous swelling in the left base of the neck resembling an organized hematoma a moderate amount of serosanguineous thoracic effusion a moderate amount of brown/pink turbid abdominal effusion with abundant bacteria and white blood cell fibrin strands along the omentum and overlying peritoneal lining multiple petechiae in the jejunal lymph nodes rounded and congested spleen diffusely congested and heavy lungs numerous petechiae along the coronary vessels normal appearing feed material and fecal material in the gastrointestinal tract purple omentum marked diffuse serosal hyperemia of the jejunum multiple regions of hyperemia on the serosa of the ileum and cecum necrosis of the proximal portion of the right ventral colon petechiae in the mucosa of the ventral left colon and congested pancreas.

SUSPECT HEAD TRAUMA INANITION. This female 9-year-old fruit bat was found dead in its cage. It was found dead along with three other bats. This bat was caught up with other free flight bats in the tropical forest for routine physical exam. It was in holding for 24-48 hours. At necropsy there were multiple superficial abrasions with scabs and blood present on the joints of the first digits bilaterally. There were multiple white spots scattered across the surface of both wings. There was no visible cutaneous or visceral fat. The heart appeared enlarged grossly. The left ventricular wall was grossly thickened in comparison to the right ventricular wall thickness. The peritoneal and visceral surfaces had white linear structures that appeared slightly organized on the peritoneum and more random and scattered throughout the viscera and diaphragm. Mesenteric lymph nodes were tan and grossly prominent/enlarged. The caudal cerebrum and cerebellum had regions of hemorrhage that were more prominent on the left side.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS SEPTICEMIA INANITION. This approximately 6-year-old female lory was found dead. It had a history of polydipsia followed by regurgitation and production of watery stools of one day duration. The bird was also noted to be slightly off and lethargic. A fecal sample was collected and analysis was within normal limits. Radiographs revealed increased opacity of the right cranial air sac. Regurgitation occurred during anesthesia with the possibility of aspiration. After anesthetic recovery the bird appeared alert and responsive but was exhibiting an expiratory effort. At necropsy the lory was thin. There was a 5-6 mm. diameter contusion on the right pectoral muscle. The liver had what appeared to be fracture of the right cranial lobe. The lungs were centrally red and congested. The crop contained a small amount of watery contents as did the proventriculus and ventriculus.

EUTHANASIA ENTERITIS LYMPHADENITIS OVARIAN CYST. This 20-year-old female otter had a large mass in the caudal abdomen. Exploratory surgery revealed a cystic ovary and thickening of the jejunum and local nodes. Cytology was suggestive of lymphoid neoplasia and the animal was humanely euthanized.
SHOCK. This 1-year-old female kangaroo was found dead in the yard. Mature cataracts were present in both eyes. No other significant gross necropsy findings were identified.

WING TRAUMA HEPATOTOXICOSIS EUTHANASIA CATARACTS WITH UNILATERAL GLAUCOMA. This approximately 19-year-old female Bali mynah had reduced activity and poor quality of life and ongoing tissue damage to the wing with loss of flight and blindness in one eye. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed decreased feather quality cachexia and a circular soft tissue lesion medial to the left elbow (this area traumatized by the bird historically). Decreased range of motion was in the left elbow associated with contraction of the patagial tendon. Foci of gray discoloration are present in the heart and lung and in adjacent skeletal muscle.

INANITION TRAUMA. This approximately 2.5-year-old captive bred male lorikeet was found dead hanging in the branches. At necropsy there was bruising and trauma to the skin of the upper face and cere. There was bruising on the top of the head. There was bruising in three spots on the skull. There was blood in the mouth. There was a penetrating wound over the left radius and ulna with the skin degloved. There was bruising from the wrist to the right elbow. There was blood in the esophagus and crop.

According to the history provided; this 32-year-old intact male cockatoo had history of balanced issues and was known to fall from perching in the morning. The animal was found unresponsive. After CPR; blood was noted within the mouth. There was no change in location; food or water and no recent medications. Other signs of injury were not observed. Previously; the animal was eating and drinking normally. A 342.98 g intact male cockatoo with metal leg ring labeled CSC 410 on the right leg was present to the MSU-VDL for complete necropsy on 08/31/17. Autolysis was mild to moderate. Animal was in poor to fair nutritional status with increased prominence of sternal bone (Keel); slightly less than normal pectoral muscle mass (atrophy); and lack of visceral adipose store and an overall body condition score of 4/9. Within the cloanal slit; there was scant bright red mucoid material. The lumen of cranial 7 cm of trachea contained scant amounts bright red fluid and there was 1 cm cyclical dark red clot within lumen of the cranial esophagus. In region of coelomic inlet; there was approximately 2X1.5 cm dark red gelatinous clot that extended to adjacent left cervical muscle up to 1 cm. The clavicular and thoracic air sacs contained scant amount of bright red fluid. There were no other significant findings. Choanal slit; trachea; esophagus; lungs; and cranial portion of the coelom: Multifocal hemorrhage Comments All described findings are most consistent with trauma. Histopathologic examination is currently pending. Results will be issued in the final report. Tanit Kasantikul; D Representative sections of brain; lung; heart; tongue; esophagus; proventriculus; ventriculus; small and large intestine; liver; pancreas; kidneys; adrenal gland; testicle; and eyes are examined. Within the sections of lung; lumens of several large airways are diffusely replaced by pools of extravasated free erythrocytes and there is lack of erythrocytes within alveolar capillaries throughout the lung. Within the section of heart; the tunica media of occasional small to medium coronary arteries is moderately thickened by irregularly arranged hypertrophic/hyperplastic smooth muscle and has a focal mineralization in one focus. In region of aortic artery; the elastic medial stroma of the vessel is separated by variable amounts of basophilic flocculent myxomatous material and moderate numbers of discrete open vacuoles laden histiocytes. There is a foci of mineralized osseous metaplasia noted within subintimal stroma of aortic vessel in one area. Within the section of liver; hepatocytes diffusely contain abundant finely granular cytoplasm. The section of pancreas has a focus of ectatically distended pancreatic duct containing abundant amounts of brightly eosinophilic secretory material. There are no other significant findings; histologically. Lung: Severe extensive pulmonary hemorrhage and alveolar interstitial depletion of erythrocytes Heart: Mild multifocal osseous metaplasia Aorta: Severe arthrosclerosis Severe extensive pulmonary hemorrhage Aortic arthrosclerosis Comments The principle finding in this case is severe extensive pulmonary hemorrhage; however the exact mechanism cannot be definitively determined. Changes of aortic artery suggest underlying arthrosclerosis. Aortic atherosclerosis is a common aging change in parrots particularly those with high fat diets. Rupture of such blood vessels can result in hemocoelom. Further examination of aorta is on process. Results will be released as an addendum. Tanit Kasantikul; D

DEGENERATIVE MYOPATHY. This 5-year-old male brown pelican had elevated muscle enzymes and was weak and lethargic. The animal was treated for myopathy and died spontaneously. This animal has a history of domoic acid toxicity with mild neurological signs. At necropsy pectoral and leg muscles were pale.

ASPIRATION. This approximately 1-year/2-month-old male lorikeet was anesthetized with isoflurane for examination and blood drawing for quarantine testing during which it stopped breathing regurgitated and despite resuscitation attempts died. At necropsy the distal one-third of the wing and tail feathers were damaged (likely due to self-mutilation). There was good body condition. There was white runny paste in the thoracic trachea 0.5 cm. above the bifurcation (probable feed material). The lungs had multifocal areas of congestion/atelectasis bilaterally. The liver had large multifocal pale areas. The crop was full of feed material similar in appearance to the substance found in the trachea.

NASAL ADENOCARCINOMA FIBROUS POLYP ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male sheep had a history of epistaxis and nasal discharge. Polyps were identified via endoscopy. Recently the left eye was bulging. At necropsy masses were present in the sinus adjacent to the left eye. The dorsal sinus was filled with thick brown mucus.

RENAL DYSPLASIA PANCREATIC ACINAR HYPOPLASIA OR APLASIA INTESTINAL MUCOSAL ATROPHY EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female tamarin has a history of chronic weight loss with intermittent diarrhea and inappetence and was subsequently euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 14-year-old male tree boa was found crushed to death between a tree limb and the cement rockwork. At necropsy frank blood was present in the oral cavity. Radiographs revealed crushing lesions in approximately five vertebrae.

SEPTIC COELOMITIS AND CELLULITIS. This 13-year-old female parrot was found dead. It was part of a group of thick billed parrots with recent deaths. The first death was due to Salmonella arizonae in last year’s chick. A breeding pair died within several weeks of each other. The female had positive West Nile virus antigen and necrotizing hepatitis. This animal and her mate were moved to the AMC approximately two weeks ago due to mosquito load and Salmonella risk in exhibit. Both animals had been doing well. About 48 hours prior to presentation this animal was noted to be slightly fluffed but perked up considerably the following day. Regurgitation of water was noted. Radiographs showed a dilated proventriculus with a large gas pattern in the proventricular area. Anesthesia and endoscopic examination showed a slightly hyperemic proventricular mucosa with prominent mucosal vasculature. There was food material in the crop and proventriculus which impeded further evaluation. Samples of proventricular material were taken for evaluation. The animal appeared lethargic and fluffed after anesthesia but responded to supportive care and fluids. At necropsy the bird was moderately thin. The upper thoracic tissues appeared inflamed especially at the heart base. There were a few small blood clots present in this area. The air sacs in this area were tightly adhered to the organs and there was brown thick fibrous tissue that had to be dissected to fully visualize and remove the distal esophagus and trachea. The musculature underlying these affected areas was dark brown. The heart appeared pale on the serosal surface. There were petechiae at the heart base. On cut surface the endocardium was brick red. The crop contained abundant feed material. Approximately 10 mm. proximal to the proventriculus the esophagus appeared dark brown and very friable. There was a diffuse demarcation between the abnormal and normal tissue. Within this region there was a small full thickness tear on the dorsal aspect. The tissue around the tear was dark brown. The proventriculus was greatly distended with feed material and was hyperemic along the mucosal surface. The lungs in the inflamed areas were markedly hemorrhagic at their borders with some dark necrotic areas present where the lungs contacted the affected trachea and esophagus. Dark brown fluid oozed from cut surface of these affected lungs areas. The cranial thoracic air sacs were bilaterally inflamed thickened and opaque. The liver was slightly enlarged with sharp borders. There were pale tan/yellow areas at the cranial aspect. Both kidneys were diffusely pale.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS FRACTURED BEAK GRANULOMATOUS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA EUTHANSIA. This 19-year-old male Humboldt penguin fractured its distal lower beak three weeks earlier. Radiographs revealed a circular radial lucency at the fracture site. The site was repaired surgically and the patient had been tolerating the repair but then refractured the site on the day of euthanasia. Radiographs revealed enlargement of the focus of radiolucency extending beyond the proximal pin with associated instability. Necropsy revealed adhesion of the right air sac to the liver (previous surgery) hemorrhagic lungs previous described beak lesion with associated softening of the surrounding tissues at the fracture site pale liver with multiple 1-3 mm. white round nodules and no other gross abnormalities.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA ADENOMA AND HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male fennec fox has a history of hepatic neoplasia (G12-5605) and had been doing well until recently. It developed a seizure one week prior to euthanasia had mildly elevated hepatic enzymes and a palpable mass was noted in the region of the liver. The animal became unable to use its rear legs but was otherwise alert. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 10 cm. lobulated hepatic tumor and smaller tubules in other lobes. No other lesions were seen and no thrombus was seen in the descending aorta. The spleen was enlarged soft and attributed to euthanasia.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 6-year-old female lorikeet was found wet and minimally responsive in the morning. Supportive care was administered but the bird died within an hour of presentation. Necropsy revealed thin body condition wet and rough plumage multiple fresh skin wounds on the head from conspecifics a large area of skin on the dorsal cranium that was dry and yellow. The choanal slit was enlarged and had blunted papillae. Congestion was in the lungs. The liver was congested. Minimal food material was in the proventriculus and ventriculus. The intestinal tract contained foul-smelling yellow-colored fecal material. The jejunum was enlarged and had vascular congestion on the serosal surface. Large areas of yellow fibrinous debris were noted on the mucosal surface. The spleen was mildly enlarged. Blood was pooled around the pituitary gland.

HEMOLYSIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 9-year-old male pygmy goat has a several year history of polyuria and polydyspnea and has had recent episodes of stranguria and red/pink urine. The goat died and necropsy revealed no evidence of stones or sand in the urinary bladder hemolyzed serum and pigmenturia. Straw-colored fluid was in the bronchi. The right lung was mottled and heavy. A hematoma was in the left jugular groove. Minimal straw-colored fluid was in the abdominal cavity. Some dark brown to black stellate lesions were in the abomasum. The pancreas was reddened. Reddened fluid was in the lumen of the small intestine and stool was in the colon. A 3 mm. raised circular white lesion was on the bladder wall. Urine was pink to red tinged and no obvious obstructions were seen in the lower urinary tract. Some dark discoloration was on the surface of the kidney.

EMACIATION SHOCK PROBABLY DROWNED. This 1-year-old male agouti was found in the pond with blood coming from the nose. Necropsy revealed thin body condition pink froth in the trachea wet heavy and mottled lungs and empty stomach aside from a small amount of what appeared digested blood. Some possible intraluminal blood was in the small intestine. Male reproductive tract was identified. The adrenal glands were prominent.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA LYMPHOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 2-year-old male rat had a long history of chronic pneumonia that improved on long-term antibiotics but with eventual increased respiratory difficulty and apparent embolic tissue loss at the tail tip and at the ends of the toes. Due to progressive lesions and weight loss euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed consolidation of the lungs especially the left lung with abscessation and firm enlargement and rigidity. The liver was congested and the thyroids appeared enlarged. The adrenal glands were asymmetrical with the left larger than the right.

ACUTE SHOCK POSSIBLE HYPERTHERMIA. This approximately 9-month-old female desert tortoise was confiscated and had a history of metabolic bone disease. It was responding well to treatment and gaining weight but was found dead unexpectedly two hours after a blood draw. The animal was bloated and felt hot to touch. Necropsy revealed a large amount of coelomic fluid pale muscles cellulitis involving the back legs fluid in the lungs pale kidneys urates in the kidneys and digesta/dirt in the cecum and colon.

ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS PROBABLE TRAUMA LINGUAL CANDIDIASIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 13-year-old female Jamaican fruit bat was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed good body condition with mild muscle atrophy abrasions on the carpal joints reddened and mottled lungs that floated in formalin and no other abnormalities.

ARTHRITIS AND CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) OBESITY DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female African lion had a history of chronic osteoarthritis with progressive hind limb ataxia. The animal developed a possible cerebral episode on 12/6 with transient head tilt and circling. The animal’s condition did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had a sebaceous carcinoma removed from the right upper eyelid in June 2014. Necropsy revealed obese body condition unkempt haircoat pulmonary congestion mineralization of the aortic valve cusps and the ascending aorta dark striations on the mucosal surface of the pylorus three large masses in the right hepatic lobe and two smaller masses that were cystic containing dark brown clear fluid. No other abnormalities were noted.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS AND TAMPONADE. This approximately 37-year-old male American flamingo had been normal in the morning and was receiving diuretic treatment for chronic facial swelling. The bird died unexpectedly with minimal stress and resuscitation was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed a large clot found around the heart. The liver was large.

MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION AND FIBROSIS ENDOCARDIOSIS DISSEMINATED INTRAVASCULAR COAGULOPATHY UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA SPLENITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS. This approximately 36-year/6-month-old female gorilla died. At necropsy there was 2 x 1.5 cm. subcutaneous mass just to the left of the midline of the mandible which appeared to be a lipoma. It did not communicate with the dentition. There was abundant subcutaneous fat. There was some edema in the subcutaneous tissues. The marrow of the right femur appeared light brown and slightly fatty. There were multiple adhesions in the pleural and peritoneal cavities. There was blood tinged straw colored fluid free in the thoracic cavity. There was a 3.3 x 3.3 x 3.5 cm. mass in the midbody of the spleen that was solid and tumor-like. The lungs had multifocal atelectasis congestion and edema. There were blood clots in the pulmonary arteries. The apex of the heart was slightly rounded. The left ventricular wall thickness was 1.5 cm. and the right ventricular thickness was 0.4 cm. Several teeth were missing. Remaining teeth had associated gingival recession and some were loose. The liver had very rounded edges and appeared enlarged. There were few blood filled masses in the left right and caudate lobes of the liver that ranged from 0.5 to 1 cm. in diameter. There was a mucosal cyst in the duodenum that collapsed when it was incised. The small intestine was segmentally hemorrhagic. The kidneys had severe bilateral pyelonephritis with the right being more involved than the left. The kidneys were bilaterally swollen. The capsule of both kidneys stripped off with difficulty. The right kidney had abscesses within the upper and lower pole. Two abscesses of the right kidney were submitted for culture. The left kidney had two areas of chronic infection with scarring of the upper pole and upper to middle pole. In the left kidney the inflammation was mainly on the posterior aspect. On cut surface there were abscesses in both kidneys with extensive abscessation of the right kidney. There were abscesses in the cortex. The abscesses in the right kidney ranged from 1.5 cm. to 2 cm. in diameter. The ureters were dilated. There was a uterine mass that completely filled the pelvic inlet and appeared to be impinging on the ureters. The uterine cavity was distorted by multiple fibroids the largest being 5 cm. in diameter. The entire reproductive tract was covered by dense adhesions. There was a 3 x 3.5 x 3 cm. solid mass attached to the pelvic mass by adhesions.

HEMOCHROMATOSIS MESENCHYMAL TUMOR MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This approximately 5-year-old female tanager was humanely euthanized. It had a continuous elevated white blood cell count that was not responsive to any treatments. Acid fast stains of liver spleen and intestine were performed. At necropsy the air sacs were slightly cloudy. The cranial lungs were black congested and contained a clear foamy fluid. The liver had a copper colored mottling. The ventral surface was blanched gray as was the surface of the heart. Intestinal wall seemed thickened.

TRAUMA EMACIATION. This 10-year-old male pygmy goat had been slowly losing weight over time but appeared to be in good health the day prior to being found dead. It had abnormal stool due to coccidiosis that resolved eventually several months prior to death. It was on a joint supplement for arthritis and was also being treated for urinary crystal prophylaxis. The goat was known to play rough with a much larger goat in the exhibit and had been knocked off its feet recently. Postmortem radiographs revealed segmental gas accumulation in the gastrointestinal tract. Necropsy revealed slightly overgrown hooves bilateral focal pulmonary congestion old scars in the liver excessive wear in the upper and lower dental arcades with areas of nonfunctional surface for chewing loose incisors excessive gingival recession dry rumen contents increased rumen particle size and no other abnormalities.

MENINGOENCEPHALITIS PROBABLE COXIELLOSIS. This 7.5-year-old female rainbow lorikeet was being treated for progressive rear limb paresis and paralysis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged mottled dark red/pale liver. The bird was in slightly thin body condition.

PULMONARY SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 7-year-old female rainbow lorikeet had a history of fluffed appearance and lethargy and had been in the hospital for two weeks with no improvement. It was found dead. Necropsy revealed a yellow tinge to the subcutis thin body condition edematous viscera congested lungs and hepatosplenomegaly.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY SEPSIS. This 18-year-old male cottontop tamarin had been acting mildly lethargic but appeared to be alert; although a short time after examination the animal displayed acute collapse and died during transport to the hospital. The animal appeared to develop rigor mortis at an accelerated rate during transport. There was a report of blood in the feces in the exhibit. Necropsy revealed red material suggestive of hemorrhage in the lumen of the jejunum.

DEGENERATIVE HEPATOPATHY MALASSEZIA-LIKE DERMATITIS GRANULOMATOUS GLOSSITIS HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 6-year-old male lorikeet presented with a distended coelom and orthopnea. Evaluation revealed marked ascites and hypoalbuminemia and end stage hepatic disease was suspected. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed normal plumage and integument hemorrhagic lungs straw colored ascites in the coelomic cavity thickened and opaque air sacs enlarged heart and pale mottling in the liver.

IRON STORAGE DISEASE WITH CHRONIC HEPATIC PANCREATIC AND CARDIAC LESIONS. This 11-year-old male ruffed lemur died spontaneously following a few day history of pleural effusion. Necropsy revealed bilateral pleural effusion chronic dermatitis bilateral pulmonary atelectasis unilateral pulmonary emphysema atrophy of adipose tissue and cirrhotic liver.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS AND YOLK COELOMITIS GAS EMBOLI. This 2-year-old female junglefowl was found moribund in the morning and died in transit to the hospital. It was clinically normal the previous day. Necropsy revealed adhesions in the coelomic cavity that encased the entire gastrointestinal tract. Lungs were darker than normal.

AUTOLYSIS PROBABLE CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 1-year-old male lory died. Necropsy revealed predation of the right side of the head an enlarged pale rounded liver hemorrhagic duodenum and thickened mucosa in the proventriculus.

INTESTINAL LEIOMYOMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMAS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female warthog had a chronic history of arthritis and dropped fetlocks. Supportive care had been administered periodically. The warthog had a one day history of progressive weakness and was found recumbent in the morning and unable to stand. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed no external injuries scant pericardial effusion mildly globoid heart worn and loose molars and incisors rough and irregular spleen and a 6 cm. round asymmetrical and nonobstructive mass in the ileum with adhesions to the cecum and proximal large intestine that on cut surface had yellow to purple to green discoloration. A small fistula communicated the mass to the large bowel. The endometrium was cystic and the left kidney had a 5 cm. round cortical mass that distorted the surface that was yellow and firm on cut surface with some areas of purple/black mottling. Two similar cortical masses were found on the right kidney.

NECROTIZING MYOCARDITIS PROBABLE EMC. This 18-year-old mandrill had a brief period of inappetence with apparent vomiting. The mandrill was lethargic and was found recumbent with labored breathing. The mandrill was dead upon arrival at the hospital. Necropsy revealed a small umbilical hernia a small dermal mass on the nasal planum red foam in the trachea purple/red lungs 60 ml. of clear yellow fluid in the chest 40 ml. of clear yellow fluid in the pericardial sac pale streaks throughout the myocardium 100 ml. of clear yellow fluid in the abdominal cavity grossly enlarged liver with fibrin strands on the capsular surface enlarged spleen hemorrhagic tracheobronchial lymph nodes a hemorrhagic mass in the cranial abdomen in the area where the pancreas should be and apparent pancreatic tissue in the center of the mass.

CHRONIC MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS AND HEPATOPATHY. This 18-year-old rattlesnake reportedly was not doing well had not moved around much had recently lost body condition and was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed reddened ventrum empty stomach grit in the gallbladder admixed with bile serous fluid in the colon admixed with digesta and dark tan and granular kidneys.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS/TRAUMA EUTHANASIA ACUTE AND CHRONIC RUMENITIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 14-year-old female giant eland had a two day history of unwillingness to rise and has a history of severe lameness in the rear secondary to old hip and stifle injuries. Generalized body condition was poor and continued to worsen and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an absence of adipose tissue blunting of the ruminal papillae with areas of fibrosis severe atony and dilatation of the rumen a 1 cm. intraparenchymal fluid-filled cyst in the liver small kidneys with thinning of the cortices a 5 cm. cystic structure adjacent to one ovary and no other abnormalities.

AMEBIASIS SEPSIS PULMONARY NEMATODIASIS EPICARDIAL FIBROSIS AND HEMOSIDEROSIS. This approximately 6-year-old female Gaboon viper had a history of enlarged retained left spectacle that necessitated periodic lancing. A conspecific died eight days earlier. The snake of this report died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed fluid in the oral cavity and esophagus petechiae in the stomach and markedly enlarged colon filled with luminal necrotic material.

A 3-year-old; neutered male ferret was submitted for necropsy on 1/20/16. The animal was euthanized on 1/19; but no clinical history was provided. A 1.06-kg ferret was presented to DCPAH for complete necropsy on 01/20/16. There was mild postmortem autolysis. The animal was thin (BCS = 3/9); and eyes were mildly sunken into their orbits; indicating dehydration. The buccal mucosa was red in thin linear segments at the junction with the gingiva of the maxilla and the mandible. All lung lobes were mottled red and purple; except at the peripheral lobe edges; which were pink. The heart was rounded externally; and the left ventricular free wall was 7-8 mm thick; while the right ventricular free wall was 1-2 mm thick. The spleen enlarged (12x4x0.3-0.5 cm); dark purple; and rather firm. The diaphragmatic capsular surface of the right lobe; near the gall bladder; contained a slightly raised; round; 2-mm diameter; white nodule. There was a 8x5x2-mm; bilobed; pedunculated; firm mass attached to the center of the mesentery. There were no other significant gross findings. Heart: left ventricular myocardial hypertrophy (presumptive) Lungs: diffuse pulmonary congestion Spleen: splenomegaly Comment: Thickening of the left ventricular myocardium and splenomegaly were the most prominent gross findings. If there is indeed left ventricular hypertrophy/cardiomyopathy; then the apparent pulmonary congestion may indicate left-sided heart failure. Splenic enlargement may be due to euthanasia; but the spleen did not seem overly congested; as is typical with euthanasia. Lymphoma is a possibility. Histopathologic examination of major organs will hopefully determine the nature of these lesions; results will be issued in the final report. Tanit Kasantikul; DVM Sections of brain; lung; trachea; liver; heart; omental mass; kidney; small intestine; pancreas; tongue; and spleen are examined. Within the section of the heart; there is mild to moderate fibrosis within the myocardium. Scattered cardiac myocytes; including those within areas of fibrosis; are various sizes; with various staining affinities. Occasional myocytes have pyknotic nuclei and/or are hypertrophied. In the lung; many alveoli and bronchioles contain eosinophilic; homogenous; proteinaceous fluid. Multifocally; the alveolar septa are markedly congested. There is an increased prominence of peribronchial and perivascular lymphoid aggregates. Staining of lung sections with Prussian blue reveals rare individual; and small aggregates of hemosiderin-laden macrophages within alveolar spaces. The tracheal cartilage is mostly replaced by deeply basophilic; granular material (mineralization). The splenic architecture is obscured because of marked congestion of the red pulp; and multiple lymphoid folllicles have expansion of marginal zones; while maintaining their polarity. Within the liver; sinusoids are expanded by erythrocytes (congestion); especially centrilobularly. Staining of the liver with Prussian blue reveals iron pigments in many hepatocytes and fewer macrophages. Small aggregates of lymphocytes surround bile ducts in multiple portal tracts. In the sections of kidney; scattered renal tubules are distended by homogeneous; eosinophiic material and are lined by attenuated epithelial cells. A representative section containing the omental mass described grossly indicates that the mass is well circumscribed; and is well differentiated adipocytes arranged in dense sheets and separated by delicate collagenous stroma. These neoplastic cells have distinct cell borders; abundant clear vacuolar cytoplasm and periphery displaced hyperchromatic nuclei. Anisokaryosis is minimal. Mitotic figures are rare with 0-1 per 10 high power fields. The bone marrow specimen is s Heart: moderate multifocal myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis Lung: moderate pulmonary edema; mild hemosiderosis Liver: moderate diffuse congestion; mild hemosiderosis Omentum: lipoma Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy Comment: Gross and histologic findings are suggestive of heart disease due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Pulmonary edema; along the presence of hemosiderin-laden macrophages (heart failure cells) in alveoli; suggests left-sided heart failure; and centrilobular hepatic congestion and hemosiderosis is compatible with right-sided heart failure. Splenic congestion is most likely due to euthanasia. The small omental mass appeared to be a lipoma; a benign neoplasm of adipocyte origin. This completes all diagnostic testing for this case. Tanit Kasantikul; DVM

PENMATE TRAUMA SYSTEMIC GRANULOMATOUS INFLAMMATION. This 4-year-old male lory had a history of traumatic shock and a bite wound and was not able to grasp with its left foot. No fractures were detected radiographically. The bird died spontaneously in spite of supportive therapy. Other lorries have been observed attacking this bird in the morning. Necropsy revealed blood in the ventral abdominal feathers and feathers pulling off at the base of the head around the beak and on the back and both wings. The skin on both legs appeared red and blood was in the mouth. Subcutaneous hemorrhage was detected on the neck. Subcutaneous emphysema and hemorrhage were detected on the ventral caudal abdomen. Evidence of trauma to the neck back on the right side and right leg were most obvious. Also damage to both wings with possible penetrating wounds were noted. The lungs appeared congested.

EUTHANASIA VALVULAR FIBROSIS CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE PULMONARY ATELECTASIS GASTRITIS SPLENITIS. This 12.5-year-old male African hunting dog has a history of chronic heart failure. The animal was humanely euthanized due to progression of clinical signs. At necropsy the animal was thin. Straw colored fluid was present in the abdomen and thorax. Hilar lymph nodes were prominent. The right heart was enlarged. Mineralized masses were present in the right atrium. Nodular thickening of the mitral and tricuspid valves was also noted. Severe spondylosis was present in the thoracic spine.

EUTHANASIA TYPHLITIS PERITONITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PANCREATIC FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS INANITION. This 12-year-old female hyrax presented emaciated and dehydrated. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple pale nodules were present in the serosa of the stomach. Fibrin tags were present in the abdomen. Pale nodular foci were present on the left AV valve. A 1 cm. in diameter spherical mass was present in the anterior uterus. Enteroliths were present in the cecum with ulceration of the mucosa.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 6-year-old female ferret was under treatment for adrenal gland enlargement. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and mitral regurgitation developed recently and diuretic treatment was initiated. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy a multinodular mass was present in the right adrenal gland. The ventricular walls of the heart were thickened. There was moderate pulmonary edema and fluid within the caudal one-third of the trachea. The left kidney was approximately 20% larger than the right.

PITUITARY ADENOMA AND CORTICAL LAMINAR SPONGIFORM CHANGE EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old female domestic rat was euthanized due to declining condition that included weakness ataxia and emaciation. The animal had lost weight and appeared to be dehydrated. Necropsy revealed a soft tissue mass on the ventral aspect of the brainstem. No other gross lesions were seen.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male hedgehog has a history of chronic progression of central nervous system signs. The left leg had become nonfunctional and the right leg had some deficits. The patient had started chewing on its rear feet so both legs had been bandaged to allow for healing. The animal had removed its bandage overnight and excoriated leg bounds to the level of tendons and bone with only one digit remaining. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified adequate adipose stores that were tinted orange substantial soft tissue wounds to both hind feet possibly enlarged heart and no other gross abnormalities.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT VERTEBRAL MALFORMATIONS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male skink was born with marked vertebral defects in the lumbar and tail region (kyphosis and scoliosis). The animal lost weight in October 2013 and failed to gain weight despite dietary adjustments and hand feeding. It became inappetent developed paresis in the right front and right rear limbs and blood work revealed elevated uric acid and leukocytosis. Supportive care was administered but the animal’s condition worsened and it was found moribund with markedly elevated uric acid levels. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The lizard is from a clutch in which similar vertebral defects were noted in siblings that also died of gout. Necropsy revealed multiple white plaques on the scales of the ventral rostral mandible and ventral cranial cervical area. An undulating appearance to the tail and spine was noted. Diffuse mineralization was apparent on the ventral aspect of the pericardium. A small hemorrhage was in the right caudal lung and the lungs were congested. Multiple pinpoint lesions were present throughout the parenchyma of the liver and on the serosal surface. The spleen was pale. The testes were symmetrical. Gritty material congealed into a disk was present in the urinary bladder. The kidneys were bilaterally enlarged and had white discoloration and an irregular surface. Palpable thickening of the right elbow and right stifle with associated decreased flexion was also noted. Fat bodies were large.

Heart: Moderate multifocal myodegeneration; fibrosis; and necrosis Heart: Arteriolar mural dissection and hemorrhage Kidney: Moderate multifocal suppurative tubulitis; mild membranous glomerulonephritis; pelvic tubular atrophy Cecum; small intestine: Intussusception with mural hemorrhage and necrosis Large intestine; cecum: Mild lymphoplasmacytic typhlocolitis Pancreas: Mild nodular exocrine hyperplasia; zymogen depletion Tongue: Mild chronic glossitis Comment: The most important finding in this animal was its heart disease which likely underlies the animal's increasing debilitation. Tubulitis and typhlocolitis suggest that there was also some degree of secondary immune compromise. The other lesions reflected its debilitation more than an other condition

Lungs: Diffuse interstitial pneumonia; Miliary nodular infiltrate Comments: The findings on gross necropsy suggest that the pulmonary lesions were the cause of death. The disseminated pattern within the lungs; and the texture of the lesions leads to the differential diagnoses of neoplasia or bacterial or fungal granulomas. Final diagnosis is pending histopathology; bacteriology and virology. David Needle; DVM Lung - Bronchoalveolar adenocarcinoma Kidney - Glomerulonephritis; membranoproliferative; mild; Nephritis; interstitial; lymphoplasmacytic; mild. Bronchoalveolar adenocarcinoma Comments: The histopathologic changes are consistent with a malignant neoplasm of epithelial origin and bronchoalveolar epithelial differentiation. The location of the neoplastic cells and their organization in secretory units supported by a thin stroma are characteristic of a bronchoalveolar adenocarcinoma. In domesticated dogs; this neoplasm metastasizes within the lungs; to distant lobes via the lymphatics; as is likely the case for the intravascular metastasis seen in the distant lung lobes; histologically. This tumor may also metastasize to extra-pulmonary sites including lymph nodes; bone marrow and the brain; however; in this case no metastsis to other tissues was found. The rare E. coli isolated from the lung are considered post-mortem contaminants. The renal changes would not be uncommon for a domestic dog of similar age to this wolf. This completes the outstanding testing for this case. David Needle; D

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA. This 10-year-old rhea was attacked by stray dogs in the exhibit. The bird was euthanized due to severe injuries. At gross necropsy numerous lacerations puncture wounds and one 6 x 5 x 3 cm. area of skin and muscle was missing. The right wing was traumatically amputated at the carpus. There was also a tear in the caudal thoracic air sacs with displacement of the liver proventriculus ventriculus and part of the intestine into the thoracic cavity.

NECROSUPPURATIVE LYMPHADENITIS SPLENITIS HEPATITIS. This 1-year-old female tamarin was found dead in the incubator. Necropsy revealed an intussusception in the ileum approximately 4 cm. of which was telescoped into the distal aspects of the gut. The lesion was easily reduced and a total of 8 cm. of dark purple ileum appeared to be affected. Lymph nodes in the omentum were prominent. The spleen had yellow nodules. This animal had a possible seizure and fell one day earlier.
BRONCHOPNEUMONIA KOILIN DEGENERATION VENTRICULITIS HEPATITIS. This 1.5-year-old female ibis died along with two cagemates. At necropsy blood was noted within the ventriculus and small intestine.

ANKYLOSING CERVICAL SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EMACIATION ANEMIA. This 20-year-old female black swan was found dead in the lagoon. The bird had a history of cervical scoliosis and kyphosis since it was a chick due to trauma from a raccoon. Necropsy revealed decreased body condition kyphosis and scoliosis involving the cervical vertebra from C6-C11 and a firm swelling at each of the affected intervertebral joints with no associated range of motion in the joints. There were 5 ml. of thin straw-colored pericardial fluid and no epicardial fat was seen. A small amount of gelatinous tissue was at the atrioventricular junction. Several foci of edematous tissue were in the fascia on the internal surface of the keel bone. A 1.5 cm. tan irregular tissue was at the cranial lobe of the right kidney in the region of the adrenal gland. Grit and sand were in the ventriculus.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA CHRONIC GASTROENTEROCOLITIS PAPILLOMAS. This 22-year-old male colobus monkey had a history of proliferative gingival hyperplasia necessitating extraction of some teeth. Remaining teeth were lost. Gingival lesions were subsequently considered minimal. The animal had significant weight loss and eventually was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed papillomatous growths on the gingiva around the left maxillary canine region and on the outside surface of the upper lip to the right of the midline. The epicardial surface had areas of white streaking and an adhered clot in the right atrium.

BACTERIAL STOMATITIS OSTEOMYELITIS HEPATITIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION. This 13-year-old female mynah had a prior wing injury and was unable to fly. The bird was found dead. At necropsy body condition was poor. A caseous mass was identified in the oral cavity. Straw-colored fluid was present in the coelom. The liver was markedly enlarged and friable.

RUPTURED AORTA. This 19-year-old male flamingo died unexpectedly with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed a 0.5 cm. long split in the right aorta and a large blood clot surrounding the heart and extending into the cervical air sacs and trachea.

BACTERIAL COLITIS AND SEPSIS (PROBABLE SALMONELLOSIS) BILIARY HYPERPLASIA (PROBABLE TREMATODIASIS). This 29-year-old male cockatoo was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed poor body condition absence of fat stores a 1.5 cm. length of necrotic large intestine and adhesion between the lesion and the adjoining loop of bowel watery ingesta and feces in the small intestine and a swollen and congested liver.

ANESTHETIC RELATED DEATH AMYLOIDOSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY INANITION. This 14-year/1-month-old male pygmy marmoset did not recover from anesthesia. It had a history of recent tail amputation that initially healed well but began to develop necrotic tissue. The tail became cold to touch. The marmoset was anesthetized for further amputation and subsequently died. At necropsy the marmoset was emaciated and had no fat stores present. The kidneys and adrenals appeared large. There was concentric hypertrophy of the left ventricle. There were mitral plaques and right ventricular eccentric hypertrophy.
adult. Weight: 3100.0 g.  Died after GA for ovariectomy.  Subcutaneous oedema and icnreased body cavity fluids.  Chronic coelomic/repro tract adhesions.

SHOCK PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 7-year-old female bat died a few minutes after being manually restrained to place a transponder chip. At necropsy the lungs were hemorrhagic with a small quantity of blood free within the thorax.

TRAUMA PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS ESOPHAGEAL NEMATODIASIS. This greater than 5-year-old female prairie chicken died an hour after being found. It appeared to have a broken neck. At necropsy the left wing had the distal end missing and was traumatized. There was fresh blood present. The pancreas was erythematous and possibly edematous. There was a gray infiltrative lesion in the left lung. Tissues were submitted for West Nile virus testing.
adult.  Euthanasia; Osteoporosis; Chronic; Multiplejoints; nodule.mass peritonium; Pulmonary emphasema; pleurisy; suspect.

SUSPECT WEST NILE VIRUS. This captive bred 2-year-old female lory was found dead. Heart and kidney were submitted for West Nile virus testing. There is a history of West Nile virus in five other lories from the collection. At necropsy the head appeared dry. The body was very damp. The air sacs were clear. The spleen was enlarged. The proventriculus appeared very thin but not dilated. The gizzard was not dilated but the muscular wall appeared thin.

ENDOCARDIOSIS CARDIOPULMONARY FAILURE METASTATIC COMPLICATIONS. This 6-year-old male polar bear had an approximately one week history of lethargy and periods of openmouthed breathing with respiratory effort. The animal was immobilized for examination developed cardiac arrest and could not be revived. Necropsy revealed approximately two liters of serous fluid in the thoracic cavity and lesser fluid in the pericardial sac. The right ventricular free wall was thinner than expected. Ventral edema was noted in the subcutis of the thoracic and abdominal regions.

BACTERIAL PLEUROPNEUMONIA EMACIATION. This 7-month-old female captive bred kudu died spontaneously after a 24 hour history of illness. The animal had no prior health problems but was observed to have poor body condition and regurgitation of rumen fluid 24 hours prior to death. The animal died within ten hours of immobilization despite fluid and antibiotic therapy. Moderate numbers of Haemonchus/Trichostrongylus sp. ova were present on fecal examination and the calcium/phosphorus ratio at the time of the calf’s death was inverse (7.4 and 9.7 mg/dl respectively). Heavy growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa was isolated from the lung. The dam of this calf had a history of mandibular fibrous osteodystrophy. Necropsy revealed emaciation necrotic anterior lungs fracture of the right rostral mandible.

AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS OXALATE NEPHROSIS. This 13-year-old female armadillo had been inappetent for 24 hours and was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed dried blood on the shell around the anus and tail blood in the vaginal tract inactive ovaries multiple small variably-sized bumps on the exterior of the kidneys and firm renal parenchyma blood in the caudal abdomen hemorrhage on the serosa of the urinary bladder clotted blood in the cranial colon and distal small intestine reddened intestine corresponding to the clotted blood white discoloration in the heart and no other abnormalities.

LYMPHOMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This approximately 7-year-old female hedgehog had been donated as an adult and had uncertain history prior to being acquired. The hedgehog had a history at the zoo of multifocal red dermal nodules reported as some form of hypersensitivity (G12-5939). This animal developed diarrhea two months prior to euthanasia. Clostridial bacilli were seen in stained smears. Supportive care was administered but the animal developed a sudden onset of reduced appetite and feces changed from green to mucoid. The animal continued to lose weight despite treatment became anorectic but remained alert. Exploratory surgery revealed a large spleen and enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes large tonsils and a prominent lobular pattern in the liver. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed crusting and erosions around the commissures of the lips worn dentition prominent tonsils larger than expected thyroids adequate adipose stores and body condition congested lungs euthanasia artifact in the heart prominent lobular color pattern in the liver and a few scattered pinpoint white foci in the parenchyma markedly enlarged and congested spleen with prominent gray foci throughout the parenchyma red/white streaks in the kidneys prominent adrenals mucus and fresh blood is noted in multiple segments of the alimentary tract and some bile stained mucus is in the rectum mesenteric lymph nodes are enlarged and reddened and the uterus is plump with a thick wall and empty lumen. Several parovarian cysts are noted.
ENTERITIS MYOCARDITIS. This 12-year-old male duck was found dead in the nest box. At necropsy the distal GI tract contained dark watery stool.

PAPILLOMAS GASTRITIS SIV. This 19-year/1-month-old female mandrill was humanely euthanized. It was SIV positive. It was noted to have swelling for about 1.5 weeks around the oral cavity. At necropsy the animal was obese. There were one dozen wart-like growths around the eyes. There were several papillomatous growths over the periodontal surface and tongue. The tongue was swollen. The gingiva had proliferative lesions. Only the very distal tops of the canine teeth were exposed as were the very back molars. Proliferative lesions covered all of the teeth. There were multiple raised red nodules near the pylorus. The cecum was distended with a large amount of plant material. The colon appeared to have some segments where the wall was thickened. The liver was dark with some rounded edges. The cranial lobes had a tan blotchy appearance. The uterine wall was very thick and hard.

CARDIOMYOPATHY AND ATHEROSCLEROSIS RENAL GOUT ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY. This approximately 18-year-old female parrot had a history of weight loss and poor feather condition. The bird died spontaneously and necropsy revealed thin body condition with atrophy of feathers and skin over the pectoral region. The heart was pale with areas of hemorrhage. Pinpoint foci of hemorrhage were in the pancreas. The lungs were bilaterally adhered to the thoracic wall.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS CATARACT. This 17-year-old female pronghorn presented with severe arthritis. Neurologic and vestibular signs were noted and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy arthritis was noted in the distal joints.
TRAUMA. This 8-month-old blue spiny lizard of undetermined sex was found crushed under a rock. At necropsy there was blood in the abdomen. Cryptosporidiosis is known to be in this exhibit.

RENAL FIBROSIS VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY EROSIVE GASTRITIS. This 13-year-old male snow leopard was found morbid two weeks into quarantine and died. It was hypothermic. The white blood cell count was 64000 BUN was 157 mg/dl and creatinine was 8.6 mg/dl. At necropsy there were multifocal pinpoint to 2 mm. smooth dark areas on the surface of the liver. There were depressed irregular areas 2-3 cm. in diameter on the gastric mucosa. The areas were dark red. Meningeal vessels were engorged. The adrenal cortex was thin. The leopard had no evidence of weight loss.

EUTHANASIA MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA PULMONARY METASTASIS THYROID HYPERPLASIA. This 3-year-old female hedgehog presented with a mass in the subcutis. Anorexia and dyspnea developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large mass was associated with the right mammary gland and had focal abscesses. Lungs contained large numbers of firm tan nodules. Similar nodules were present in the liver. The right uterine horn contained tan to white material.

EMACIATION SEPTICEMIA RENAL TUBULAR PIGMENT DEPOSITION. This 5-year-old female captive bred pygmy goat died spontaneously and was refrigerated 96 hours prior to necropsy. The bird presented in lateral recumbency with pale mucous membranes nystagmus opisthotonos hematuria and hypothermia. The animal was treated with supportive therapy but died two hours later. Necropsy revealed diffusely hemorrhagic lungs.

TRAUMA TREMATODIASIS CESTODIASIS. This 2.5-year-old male tanager had been moved from its enclosure in the morning to holding was subsequently found on the ground breathing but unresponsive and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed a pinpoint abrasion on the medial right carpus substantial subcutaneous fat stores moderate to substantial fat stores in the coelom dark red muscles several foci of black discoloration along the serosal surface of the liver prominent testicles and no other grossly remarkable findings.

MYELOGENOUS LEUKEMIA SEPSIS STEATITIS FIBROSING GASTRITIS. This greater than 5-year-old female gaboon viper was found dead on exhibit with its mouth open. Necropsy revealed a 2 in. in diameter skin lesion on the right side of the body resembling a bite wound and a few white plaques were noted on the outer surface of one lung. One kidney had some white/tan discoloration internally. Many noncalcified egg yolks were noted.

EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA. This 13-year-old female snow leopard had a history of weight loss. An oral mass was found on examination with markedly enlarged submandibular lymph nodes. A fine needle aspirate revealed neoplastic squamous cells. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large mass was present in the left oral cavity beneath the tongue. The left submandibular lymph node was markedly enlarged with pockets of purulent material.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE. This 33-year-old female baboon had an approximately one year history of deteriorating mobility due to generalized arthritis. The animal had become inappetent and lethargic and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed weight loss poor hind limb muscle tone multiple 1-4 cm. cystic structures in the liver severe spinal fusion with spondylosis and severe arthritis in both stifles.

ENDOCARDITIS ENCEPHALITIS NEPHRITIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS INANITION. This 9-year-old female duck was unable to use its hind leg. Severe weight loss and myiasis was noted. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was found dead. At necropsy the bird was emaciated. Severe pericardial effusion was present. Kidney and spleen were pale.

PULMONARY ABSCESSES RENAL COCCIDIOSIS MASTITIS. This 3-year-old female wallaby was being treated for a pulmonary abscess appeared to be improving but then suddenly seizured and died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and obliteration of the middle and caudal right pulmonary lobes by a large abscess in each lobe. The myocardium was enlarged but relatively thin walled.

FUNGAL DERMATITIS. This greater than 1-year-old toad of undetermined gender was humanely euthanized. It had severe dermatitis over the dorsum. There appeared to be dysecdysis with necrotic skin attached to the underlying immature skin. The toad was thin.

CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS BACTERIAL/FLAGELLATE/ADENOVIRUS ENTERITIS YOLK COELOMITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 5-year-old corn snake had a history of regurgitation weight loss abnormal fecals and decreased appetite. It has been in quarantine for seven months. Cryptosporidium was identified in a fecal sample and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition adequate intracoelomic adipose tissue mildly thickened gastric mucosa mottled liver enlarged gallbladder irregular splenopancreas with possible granulomas some small unshelled eggs in the oviducts with irregular firm hard mineralized material within the lumen of the oviduct and no other remarkable findings.

TOXIC HEPATOPATHY. This greater than 8-year-old female lorikeet was found acutely down on its back on floor of aviary. The bird was reportedly on its back for a short time the day prior but quickly normalized. This time the lorikeet could be easily picked up and was moved to a brooder. The bird was wobbly and dyspneic. Trauma or cagemate aggression was not suspected. The bird did not stabilize with oxygen therapy and was found dead a few hours later prior to examination. Special request for pathologist please comment on all tissues submitted particularly brain and liver (see photo). At necropsy the animal was in good body condition with normal integument and plumage. The liver was enlarged and mottled and there was a small focus of hemorrhage on the calvarium; however this did not correspond with a meningeal or cerebral lesion. Brain appears normal.
