EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (ORAL CAVITY LUNG LYMPH NODE). This 10-year-old female snow leopard had a history of oral squamous cell carcinoma and recent inappetence. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the firm mass was present in the intermandibular region. Another firm mass was present ventral to the tongue. Lytic areas were identified in the left mandible.

PROBABLE TRAUMA (HYPOTHERMIA) STRESS INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS MESENTERIC. This 4.5-year-old female New England cottontail rabbit was released into a predator-proof hardening pen earlier in the fall and during routine trapping for surveillance this animal was found deceased in the live trap. The trap had been hidden in the brush overnight temperatures were below freezing and the biologists were concerned that hypothermia may have contributed to death. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and no evidence of wounds or scavenger activity. Several parasite cysts were in the mesentery and some 1 mm. foci of hemorrhage were in the gastric mucosa.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS SEVERE MESENTERIC FIBROSIS WITH INTESTINAL ADHESION AND PANCREATIC ATROPHY. This approximately 9-year-old captive bred female junglefowl was found unresponsive in the morning. The bird died during anesthesia for euthanasia. The bird had been treated previously for sour crop. Gross necropsy revealed a large mass in the reproductive tract with sclerosis and fluid and one abnormal small egg in the oviduct. Massive adhesions were present binding the reproductive and GI tracts.

MACRORHABDIOSIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 7.5-year-old male budgerigar had recently been treated for macrorhabdiosis but continued to lose weight. The bird was noted to be mobbed by other birds and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE SARCOMA GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This greater than 5-year-old female sheep was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic weight loss. A large abdominal mass was detected on abdominal ultrasound. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a large reproductive tumor. A foreign body was also noted in the rumen on radiographs. The sheep also had anemia. At necropsy the duodenal mucosa was darkly erythemic. There was a 6 x 6 cm. foreign body found in the rumen. The foreign body was very petrified but may be a small ball of tin foil. The right lung lobes were very dark and congested ventrally. There was a very large reproductive mass. The mass in the remaining tract weighed 1.2 kg. The mass was roughly spherical white to green and fibrous with necrotic areas. It appeared to originate in the left uterine horn. The remaining uterine horns were turgid with serous green/yellow fluid.
MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS HEPATITIS. This 15-year-old male egret was found dead. At necropsy white streaks were present on the heart.

EUTHANASIA METABOLIC BONE DISEASE HEPATIC FUNGAL GRANULOMA. This 7-month-old gecko of undetermined gender was humanely euthanized. It had a history of osteomalacia. The mandible was ventrally folded on itself exposing the tongue and mucous membranes. The maxilla was flexible. At necropsy the mandible folded ventrally on itself and was very flexible. It was easy to cut through the leg bones. The liver was pale yellow. The gecko was about ready to shed. The lungs had a mottled appearance.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL GOUT CHRONIC OOPHORITIS HISTIOCYTIC HEPATITIS. This 22-year-old female corn snake has a recent history of inappetence and progressive paresis. Radiographs show a localized lesion in the spine. The animal was found dead. At necropsy hemorrhage and bloody fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Small white foci were present in the kidneys.

SHOCK PULMONARY EDEMA ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 5.5-year-old male macaque had been anesthetized for examination contraceptive implants and TB testing. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed during anesthetic recovery and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy lungs were hyperemic and edematous. Fluid was present in the trachea.

MYONECROSIS MYOSITIS SPONDYLOSI EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male wood duck presented with head tilt. Radiographs revealed bridging spondylosis in the cervical spine. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition failed to improve and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy atrophy of fat depots and muscle was noted. Fusion was noted in the cervical vertebrae. A firm white mass was present adjacent to the small intestine.

ORAL CANDIDIASIS TRAUMA. This 5-year-old male Jamaican fruit bat was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed periocular hemorrhage an abrasion on the mandible good teeth condition petechial hemorrhages in the liver pale spleen pale kidneys with focal hemorrhages bright adrenal glands pink calvarium and male reproductive tract.
RENAL GOUT HEPATITIS. This 27-year-old female flamingo was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy small plaques were noted in the air sacs. Kidneys were firm and gritty.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATITIS. LYMPHADENITIS. This 11-year-old female fruit bat presented with abdominal effusion. Masses were noted in the liver on ultrasound. Exploratory laparotomy revealed multiple hepatic masses as well as nodules in the intestine and mesentery. The animal was humanely euthanized.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS TOXIC HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old male peafowl had advanced arthritis and chronic debilitation and was unable to rise for two days having lost use of the left foot. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe arthritis in all joints of the legs and feet and cachexia.

MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA CATARACT. This 4-year-old python had a history of seasonal respiratory tract infections following the cool down breeding hibernation. This year the situation recurred again resulting in pneumonia and possible sepsis. The snake was hospitalized and treated but continues to decline and died. Necropsy revealed empty stomach moderate amount of fecal material in the colon erythematous ventral scales some with dry or necrotic edges otherwise good body condition white chalky materials throughout the subcutis and musculature purple/red thickened right lung with plaques of dense brown/green purulent material on the luminal surface normal left lung and opaque lenses.
adult. Weight: 729.3 g.  Euth. Chr.diabetes. Poor cond'n. Ankylosis; tail. Hepatitis? Pulm.oedema (agonal?).

EMACIATION STRESS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 32-year-old male green tree python was found dead in the soaking chamber. The snake had not eaten but had been opaque prior to being found dead. The snake had been losing condition and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic reasons. Necropsy identified cachexia and some blood in the glottis.

TRAUMATIC FRACTURE CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS AND ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 10-year-old male black and white ruffed lemur is clinically normal although flattened yellow areas were noted in the pyloric mucosa during endoscopic exam.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 9-year-old male rattlesnake had a history of spinal fusion. The animal was found dead. At necropsy large sections of the spinal column were fused and rigid.

INANITION ENTERITIS URINARY BLADDER NEMATODIASIS. This 6.5-year-old male otter was found semicomatose and unable to use the hind limbs. The animal was dehydrated and thin. The animal died before treatment could be initiated. At necropsy the jejunal mucosa appeared roughened. GI contents were hemorrhagic.

DISSEMINATED INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED. This 5-year-old male lory was found dead. There has been a recent cagemate death and one remaining bird from the group is being housed in the clinic for observation. A history of sarcocystosis and enteritis is present in the flock. Necropsy of this bird revealed dehydration and scant fat stores.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL STOMATITIS PULMONARY GRANULOMAS. This 13-year-old female was found nonresponsive on the floor of its enclosure and no heartbeat could be determined. Necropsy revealed dehydration and emaciation a small amount of pericardial effusion and white material in the pericardial sac multiple lesions in the oral cavity involving the right maxillary arcade the tip of the snout and soft palate. Multiple nodules to 1 mm. in greatest dimension were in the lungs and air sacs that were hard and calcified. Multiple immature follicles were in the ovaries and some maturing eggs were noted.

PULMONARY ABSCESSES DISSEMINATED YEAST INFECTION (PROBABLE HISTOPLASMOSIS) CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS THYROID ADENOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS FIV. This approximately 15-year-old female snow leopard is positive for FIV and was diagnosed with chronic renal failure 18 months ago. She has been managed biweekly with subcutaneous fluids and daily calcitriol administration and has maintained good quality of life. One week ago keepers noted mucoid nasal discharge and visual examination revealed severe loss of body condition weakness labored breathing and decrease in appetite. The cat was moved to an indoor location and offered larger quantities of diet. She was treated with fluids and antibiotics but her condition deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation ulcers on the tongue and soft palate collapsed left lung lobes firm nodules and large cavitations containing fibrotic tissue with walled off pockets in the lungs thickening of the mitral valve slightly icteric appearing liver thick bile with sludge in the gall bladder a red raised area in the stomach ingesta in the small intestine and colon enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes enlarged pale kidneys large stones in the renal pelvises thickening of the urinary bladder.
EUTHANASIA TRAUMA CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 23-year-old female flamingo suffered a fracture of the right tibiotarsus and was euthanized. A raised white mass was noted on the apex of the heart.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This approximately 6-year-old male hedgehog was found dead. At necropsy there was jaundice in the sclera skin and subcutaneous fat layer. There was a large amount of subcutaneous fat present in the ventral abdomen. There was possible pulmonary congestion. The liver appeared unusually small.

SURGICAL/ANETHTHETIC COMPLICATION HETERAKIS STRESS. This 4-year-old male captive bred turkey was received in quarantine on 6/7 was examined with routine liver biopsy on 6/23 and died on 6/24. Complications during the liver biopsy included puncture of the gall bladder cardiac arrest with successful resuscitation and prolonged recovery. Necropsy revealed ascites and hemorrhage in the abdomen generalized mild peritonitis multiple granulomas in the cecum hemorrhage in the right kidney and bilateral pulmonary edema.
NA

OSTEITITIS DEFORMANS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION. This 13-year-old male rattlesnake had a prior history of poor shedding and anorexia. The animal was found dead. At necropsy multiple areas of spinal fusion were noted. White streaking was present within the kidneys.
adult. Weight: 1200.0 g.  Pulmonary haemorrhage and oedema; suspect agonal.  Suspect convulsing.  Trauma to nostrils.  ?Swollen brain.

SHOCK EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS DYSTOCIA. This 5-year-old female tamarin delivered two stillborn fetuses following prolonged labor. The animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy marked bruising and hemorrhage were present in the ventral abdomen and vulva. Pinpoint foci of pallor were present in the heart. The right lung had foci of consolidation. The uterus was enlarged with hemorrhage on the surface and interior.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS TYPHLOCOLITIS COLLAGEN NEVUS. This 10-year-old female tiger had a one week history of anorexia lethargy and abdominal pain. The animal was anesthetized for examination but remained obtunded for approximately 16 hours following anesthesia and was euthanized.
SHOCK POSTMORTEM AUTOLYSIS. This 1-year-old male lory was found dead. At necropsy gelatinous subcutaneous tissue was noted over the pectoral area. No other significant gross lesions were identified.

UROLITHIASIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HYDRONEPHROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS. This 6-year-old female kangaroo was found dead. At necropsy mild effusion was present in the thorax. The left kidney showed severe hydronephrosis. A brown/green calculus was adherent to the mucosa of the distal ureter. A smaller urolith was present in the right ureter.
ENTERITIS ESOPHAGITIS INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS SHOCK. This 5-year-old chicken was found dead in the stall. At necropsy the GI contents were foul smelling; otherwise there were no gross lesions.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS PROVENTICULAR NEMATODIASIS. This 2-year-old female captive bred lory died spontaneously with no prior clinical signs. Necropsy revealed a large clot in the stomach and many 2-3 mm. white curly worms embedded in the proventriculus. Hemorrhage was detected in the large intestine and the liver was mottled.

SALMONELLOSIS MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 15-year-old female timber rattlesnake was found dead with no prior signs of illness other than a two week history of inappetence considered normal for the species and season. Necropsy revealed no skin or oral cavity lesions. The liver was mottled and had multiple cystic structures and paler foci throughout the parenchyma. The cranial portion of the right ovary was adhered to the gastrointestinal tract by a 4x5 cm. irregular mass containing flocculent tan/brown fluid and some areas of organized hemorrhagic debris.

TRACHEITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PANCREATITIS INANITION. This 14-year-old boa was under treatment for severe stomatitis and pneumonia and was found dead. At necropsy the animal was in early shed. The lungs were congested and contained mucopurulent material. Similar material was present throughout the trachea.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS DENTAL ATTRITION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC ENTERITIS ARTERIAL MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 16-year-old female oryx was in poor body condition and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy severe dental attrition was noted in all dental arcades. All joints showed severe arthritis. Cysts were present in both ovaries. Marked arteriosclerosis was present in the heart.

EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) COLITIS CYSTITIS. This 11-year-old male meerkat presented with obstipation. Severe osteoarthritis of the stifles and ankylosing spondylosis was also present. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the distal colon was distended with feces. The urinary bladder was also markedly distended. An oblong green mass was present in the connective tissue adjacent to the esophagus.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS LEIOMYOSARCOMA EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old male budgerigar was found recumbent in its food pan was easily captured fell to its side when placed in a crate and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a mass effect within the body cavity and dorsal aspect of the tail base and a 1 cm. mass within the body cavity effacing the liver. Both masses had firm white consistency.

AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT BUMBLEFOOT RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 26-year-old female flamingo had been separated in the flock for a month and had been hospitalized with several others for treatment of chronic bumblefoot. The bird also had chronic elbow enlargement and drooping of the left wing. The bird lost weight during treatment became recumbent and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed old hemorrhage in the caudal right thigh muscles body wall and pelvis and a focus of hemorrhage and necrosis in the caudal right thigh resembling an injection site. Other muscles seemed atrophied but otherwise normal. Adipose stores were atrophic in some areas the aortic and left atrioventricular valves were thickened and gnarled and a pinpoint white/yellow focus was in one hepatic lobe. The gallbladder was markedly distended with thick dark green bile the spleen was mildly enlarged and slightly waxy the kidneys were speckled with retained urates and bile was in the proventriculus and ventriculus.

EUTHANASIA RENAL GOUT ENDOCARDIOSIS TESTICULAR CYSTS COELOMITIS ADRENALITIS. This approximately 17-year-old male kingsnake was humanely euthanized. It had a long history of intermittent cranial edema and periodically enlarging coelomic cyst. It also had periodic subcutaneous and skin abscesses. It had progressive weakness and distal tail paralysis. It also had distal gastrointestinal tract impaction and elevated resting respiratory rate. At necropsy the animal was thin with decreased muscle mass. There was a moderate amount of clear yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity. There were multiple large cysts in the distal half of the coelomic cavity. The cysts contained clear fluid. The heart appeared grossly distended. The heart muscle appeared flabby. There were several focal areas of hemorrhage in the lung tissue surrounding the heart (euthanasia artifact). The gall bladder appeared distended and contained viscous bile. The distal stomach and pyloric region appeared thickened and very firm. The distal colon was moderately distended with feces. Both kidneys were diffusely mottled and ranged from dark brown to light tan. There were multiple tan nodules varying in size scattered throughout the serosa and parenchyma. The renal capsule appeared thickened. The parenchyma appeared firm on cut surface. The right eye contained a corneal or spectacular scar. There appeared to be cataractous changes in the left eye.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE GANGLIONEUROMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 25-year-old female California sea lion had a history of chronic partial inappetence and had received a miscalculated medetomidine dose during induction (5x normal dose). The animal did well while anesthetized despite the high dose of medetomidine. Atipamezole was also administered at a higher dose to reverse the medetomidine. The sea lion then developed tremors and muscle spasms and did not recover to normal responsiveness. Supportive care was administered and tremors subsidized in approximately three hours but mentation continued to decline and cardiorespiratory arrest developed later in the evening. CPR was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed fair to good body condition and good carcass condition. A single 0.5 cm. skin nodule was on the right side of the neck and no other external lesions were noted. Adipose tissue was 5 in. at the pectoral region and multiple mustard-colored yellow nodules with paste-like consistency and up to 2 cm. in diameter were present in the subcutaneous adipose tissue. A large amount of free fluid was in the thoracic cavity and this was not detected during premortem examinations. Straw to orange-colored clear to slightly cloudy fluid was noted. Mild bruising was in the mucosa of the trachea. The lungs were diffusely dark pink to red. The mitral valve had thickening at the margins. The stomach had 15 small white nodules on the mucosal surface. Some patchy pale areas were in the left kidney. Several small nodules were on the surface and in the surrounding tissue of the right adrenal. The spleen was pale. A possible lymph node was prominent and adhered to the vena cava on the right side cranial to the adrenal. A 2 cm. cyst was noted in the uterus.

SUSPECT SHOCK PULMONARY EDEMA. This 10-year-old female fruit bat was found dead. It had been recently trapped and transferred to holding pen for physical examination. At necropsy there were some small white areas of depigmentation on the wings. There was one small (1 mm.) hole near the tip of the right wing. The caudal right lung lobe appeared adhered to the rib cage. There was an area of hemorrhage on the left side of the thoracic cavity that extended from the thoracic inlet to the diaphragm. The heart appeared enlarged relative to body size and the left ventricle appeared hypertrophied. There was no ingesta in the stomach. The liver appeared enlarged and autolytic. The spleen appeared mildly enlarged. The urinary bladder was full.

PULMONARY NEMATODIASIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS ULCERATIVE ENTERITIS MYOCARDITIS INANITION. This 6-year-old toad was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE CARCINOMA LEIOMYOSARCO9MA HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS. This 15-year-old female pig was found laterally recumbent. Examination revealed a large intra-abdominal mass. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the peritoneal cavity contained dark brown to red fluid. The uterus was markedly dilated and contained similar fluid. A 3 cm. diameter circular mass was present in the left horn. A 16 in. diameter solid mass was present at the root of the mesentery. The mass was white. A smaller tan mass was present in the left lobe of the kidney. Hemorrhage was noted in the right pleural cavity probably secondary to euthanasia.

IRON STORAGE DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION SEPSIS. This 5-year-old female naked mole rat presented for distention of the abdomen and also had a nasal discharge with increased respiratory rate suggestive of respiratory infection. Radiographs revealed gas in the gastrointestinal tract. The animal was treated with antibiotics but died one week after presentation. Necropsy revealed a large amount of gas in the gastrointestinal tract pale kidneys and no other abnormalities.

1. Mandible; left side: Focal; chronic-active; osteomyelitis with bony proliferation and associated submandibular lymphadenitis. 2. Jejunum: Locally extensive hyperemia and intraluminal hemorrhage. 3. Esophagus: Multifocal to coalescing ulcerative esophagitis. 4. Colon: Trichuriasis. 5. Heart: Multifocal epicardial petechia. 6. Liver: Diffuse pallor. COMMENTS: The exact cause of this animals death was not determined by postmortem examination. The sharp surface of the teeth and the focal mandibular lesion would have caused pain and difficulty in mastication; and are the most likely cause for the episodes of not eating reported in the history. It is possible that bacteria from the mandibular abscess entered the blood and caused a septicemia/endotoxemia. The multiple foci of petechia and hyperemia noted within multiple tissues are suggestive of such a septicemia. Bacterial culture and histopathology to investigate this possibility are in progress. Additional diagnostic testing (including fecal examination for additional enteric parasites) is in progress in an attempt to define the cause of death of this animal. Results will be released in a final report. Ebony Gilbreath; DVM 1. Liver: Bile duct hyperplasia and bridging fibrosis; Hepatic lipidosis. 2. Bone: Multifocal chronic necrosuppurative osteomyelitis; mandible. 3. Lymph node; submandibular: Diffuse necrotizing lymphadenitis. 4. Colon: Coccidiosis. 5. Esophagus: Focal ulcer with bacterial colonization. 6. Heart: Multifocal; mild myocardial degeneration. 7. Lung: Patchy alveolar edema with mild to alveolar histiocytosis. 8. Kidney: Mild membranous glomerulopathy. 1. Liver: Hepatic lipidosis and chronic hepatotopathy. 2. Enteric coccidiosis and trichuriasis. 3. Mandible: Focal chronic abscess. COMMENTS: The cause of death in this animal is likely multifactorial. The hepatic lipidosis may have resulted from lack of energy and malnutrition from the combined effects of lactation; anorexia due to the mandibular abscess; and enteric parasitism. The bile duct proliferation and fibrosis in the liver are indicative of a previous or chronic hepatic insult. A definitive cause of this lesion cannot be determined but some possibilities include a previous enteric infection; bile duct obstruction; or ingestion of hepatotoxic plants. There is no evidence of an overall systemic inflammatory/infectious disease process in this animal. A cause for the esophageal ulceration was not evident histologically. This may be secondary to ingestion of rough feed due to difficulty in mastication. BVD infection is also a consideration; though there are no other lesions suggestive of BVD infection. Testing for BVDV and vitamin E and selenium status is in progress. Results will be included in an addendum repot. Ebony Gilbreath; DVM BVDV not detected. Vitamin E levels above normal Selenium levels marginally low COMMENTS: If supplementation of vitamin E and/or selenium was given shortly before death; these values do not likely represent the true status of this animal or the herd. Excess vitamin E is not toxic. Ebony Gilbreath; DVM\_

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 14-year-old male ibex was euthanized due to chronic arthritis and poor mobility. At necropsy excessive tooth wear was noted. Marked osteoarthritis was noted in most joints with cartilage erosion and osteophyte proliferation.

ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS CHOLECYSTITIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA ATYPICAL LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA (SPLEEN AND LYMPH NODES). This 4-year-old male ferret presented for acute onset hematochezia/tarry feces. Profuse melena developed and the animal was treated for shock and hemorrhage but was found dead within six hours. Necropsy revealed fair to poor nutritional status a large blood clot in the stomach ulcers on the mucosal surface of the stomach three large ulcers on the mucosal surface of the duodenum just beyond the pylorus congestion of the small and large intestines mottled orange/yellow liver with hepatomegaly distended gall bladder with thickened wall and bile duct large cystic structure on the cranial aspect of the left kidney splenic enlargement absence of the left adrenal (previously removed surgically) and normal right adrenal. Swabs of gastric mucosa were submitted for Helicobacter isolation.
adult. Weight: 855 g.  Euthanased.  Multiple tumours; suspect mammary.

BACTERIAL PLEUROPNEUMONIA AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male ferret developed acute renal failure with diarrhea inappetence and weakness. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Prior to euthanasia the animal had severe azotemia hyperphosphatemia hypocalcemia hypokalemia hyponatremia normal red blood cell count and isosthenuria. Necropsy identified 5-10 ml. of creamy yellow to pink free fluid in the thoracic cavity a white raised circular lesion on the surface of the left lung that extended into the parenchyma areas of white discoloration on the surface of the heart near the left auricle gray ingesta in pieces of bedding material in the stomach fractures of the maxillary canines rounded hepatic margins prominent mottled kidneys a blood clot in the urinary bladder and good body condition.

EUTHANASIA PERITONITIS NEPHROSIS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 22-year/6-month-old female polar bear was humanely euthanized. It had a history of being sick for over two weeks. She presented with lethargy and inappetence that after immobilization was attributed to septicemia. She had been on Baytril for almost one week orally and benzipen therapy was also added. The polar bear initially improved and then deteriorated. A second workup revealed renal failure. She did not respond to fluid therapy. At necropsy the haircoat was poor. The body condition was fair. There was a small pustule on the right rear foot dorsally that exuded pus when squeezed. There was muscle wasting evident. A pocket of pus was discovered within the epaxial muscles. The muscle tissue was necrotic and soft in that area. The abdominal cavity was filled with approximately 5 gal. of yellow turbulent material containing fibrin strands and pus. The thoracic cavity contained about 0.5 gal. of similar fluid. The spleen was enlarged and engorged with blood. The lower aspect of the lungs was congested with blood. The omentum was discolored necrotic and covered with purulent fibrinous strands. The intestines were discolored red and contained scant bile stained material. The stomach contained a few dozen grapes and some mucus. The pancreas was soft and friable. The kidneys were slightly pale in appearance. The adrenals were pale.

VALVULAR ENDOCARDITIS ENDARTERITIS RENAL FIBROSIS. This 13-year-old male red wolf stopped eating approximately two days prior to death. The animal seemed normal otherwise. The wolf was found dead. At gross necropsy the heart had foci of perivascular hemorrhage on the left ventricle and a large hemorrhage covering the right atrium. Segments of intestine were congested to hemorrhagic with mucosal edema. The left kidney was enlarged and very soft.

RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS WITH KARYOMEGALY ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS. This 10-year-old male axolotl was found dead. It was being treated for fungal infection based on gill cytology. The animal appeared to respond well to saltwater baths and no visible fungal growth was noted but the animal subsequently died. Necropsy revealed absence of the left gill set and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL SPONDYLOSIS OSTEOMYELITIS AXONAL DEGENERATION ESOPHAGEAL MINERALIZATION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL FIBROSIS COLONIC DILATATION. This 15-year-old male snake was euthanized due to weight loss inactivity and an enlarging bony mass over the vertebral bodies. At necropsy a 3 mm. in diameter lesion with a central opening was present on the ventral aspect of a larger bony mass (2 x 3 cm.). No other significant gross lesions were identified.
adult. Weight: 571.5 g.  Open; kidney failure (blood work?); diarrhea.

METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE. This 12-year-old female agouti was found dead. At necropsy the body condition was fair. The animal appeared bloated. There was a large mass palpable in the caudal abdomen. There was a creamy white to tan discharge present from the vulva. There was alopecia present on the medial aspects of both carpi. There was hard firm swelling approximately 3 x 2 x 2 cm. on the right hock. There was a large amount of yellow to orange to tan/brown fluid filling the entire abdominal cavity. The fluid contained multiple specks of white material. There was a large 12 x 8 x 6 cm. mass in the uterine body that contained clear fluid. The mass was vacuolated and contained thick white caseous material. The horns contained multiple hard raised masses. The ovaries were abnormal. The left ovary was small 1 x 0.5 cm. and firm brown/green on cut surface. It contained white material. The right ovary was large and firm and contained white caseous material. It was 1.5 x 3 cm. long. The spleen was dark red to brown with one demarcated white/yellow firm nodule in the pale portion. Both kidneys were large 5 x 3 cm. and firm. The right lung was pale with multiple areas of hemorrhage. There was a large firm white to tan 2 x 1 cm. nodule on the distal surface of the caudal lung lobe. The left lung was dark red. The heart was 5 x 3.5 cm. The pericardium contained 5 cc of clear fluid.

FIBROSARCOMA COELOMIC CAVITY WITH METASTASIS TO LIVER AND HEART EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old female captive bred boa has had a three month history of inappetence three week history of retained shed and development of a midbody swelling on 4/6. Radiographs revealed a soft tissue mass ventral to the spinal column approximately one-third of the way down the body from the head. Gaseous distention of the intestinal tract was noted in this area. Necropsy revealed a firm domed shaped mass associated with the spinal column and ribs. A partially digested rodent was in the small intestine just distal to the spinal lesion and normal appearing feces and urates were in the distal colon. Five or six focal circular firm tan nodules of varying size were on the hepatic surface and extended into the parenchyma on cut surface.

NASAL ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male cheetah has a history of nasal adenocarcinoma. The animal was treated for awhile but deteriorated and was euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation approximately 4000 cc. of translucent clear fluid in the abdomen and approximately 150 cc. of serosanguineous to brown fluid in the thoracic cavity. Multiple light and dark masses were in the spleen. A 4 cm. in diameter mass was in the nasal sinus. The liver had a 4 cm. circumscribed mass with a light tan appearance. The pancreas was firm and irregular and contained a fluid filled cyst.

EUTHANASIA INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 17-year-old spayed female mountain lion was humanely euthanized due to degenerative joint disease. At necropsy there was spondylosis/masses on the thoracic spinal bodies.

RENAL INTERSTITIAL FIBROSIS NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 13-year-old chinchilla was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy the liver was mottled with accentuation of the lobular architecture. Kidneys were noted to be very small and irregular with severe pitting.
GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA EPICARDITIS. This 4-year-old male viper was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA AND FIBROSIS EMACIATION THYROID SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA. This 10-year-old male giant eland had a history of chronic emaciation with intermittent diarrhea and rough haircoat of one year’s duration. According to the history provided; this 9-year-old female alpaca was found down the evening of 10/15/17 and was taken to MSU VMC after failing to respond to treatment with banamine; baytril; ivermectin; and dexamethasone. On presentation at MSU; she was recumbent; unresponsive; hypothermic; tachycardic; and was breathing agonally. Ocular examination revealed an absent pupillary light response OS and positional nystagmus. Supportive treatment was unsuccessful; and she died on 10/17/17 and was submitted for necropsy and rabies testing the same day. An 87-kg female alpaca was necropsied 10/17/17. Autolysis was mild. An indwelling venous catheter was present in the right jugular vein. There was scant subcutaneous and visceral fat; and the animal had an overall body condition score of 3/9. The subcutaneous tissues over the mandible; inner thighs; and ventral abdomen were expanded by pale yellow gelatinous edema. There was red-tinged serous fluid in the peritoneum (300 mL) and thoracic cavity (80 mL). The pericardium contained approximately 5 mL of clear yellow thin fluid admixed with few white strands of fibrin. There were 10-15 0.3-0.5-cm irregular white foci in the left ventricular myocardium in the region of the aortic outflow tract. The lungs were mottled pink to dark red; wet; and oozed red serous fluid on cut section. Clusters of pinpoint to 1-mm diameter white round foci were scattered throughout the pleural surface of the right and left caudal lung lobes; consistent with endogenous lipid pneumonia. The cortex of the right kidney contained a focal 1-cm cyst. The jejunum contained dark red watery fluid digesta. There were formed fecal pellets in the colon. There were no other significant gross lesions. Body as a whole: Ventral subcutaneous edema Peritoneum; Thoracic cavity; Pericardium: Tricavitary effusion Lungs: Pulmonary edema; Multifocal subpleural lipogranulomas Kidney: Focal renal cortical cyst Open Comments: This alpaca had significant tricavitary effusion and edema for which the inciting cause was unclear. Such effusion and edema commonly form secondary to endoparasitism in alpacas and other small ruminants; however; no parasites were seen on gross examination. The endogenous lipid pneumonia and renal cyst are considered incidental findings in this case. Histopathologic examination of tissues and results will be released in a final report. Rabies testing results will be released in a separate report. Michelle Magagna; DVM Brain: rabies negative Comments: Histopathologic examination of tissues and additional diagnostic testing is pending. Results will be released in a final report. Michelle Magagna; DVM Representative sections of brain; trachea; lung; tongue; heart; thymus; spleen; liver; kidney; adrenal gland; pituitary gland; pancreas; thyroid gland; urinary bladder; skeletal muscle; esophagus; stomach; small intestine; and large intestine were examined. Autolysis was mild. The myocardium of the left ventricle contained multifocal locally extensive areas of myofiber necrosis and mineralization. Necrotic myofibers were characterized by hypereosinophilia; sarcolemmic clumping; loss of cross-striations; fragmentation; and nuclear pyknosis. Additionally within this region; there were occasional foci of fibrosis that variably separated and individualized myofibers. In sections of liver; the majority of centrilobular and midzonal hepatocytes contained a single large discrete lipid vacuole or multiple smaller lipid vacuoles; consistent with macro- and microvacuolar degeneration. Within the renal cortex; there were few focal aggregates of dilated tubules lined by attenuated cuboidal epithelium with increased cytoplasmic basophilia; consistent with tubular regeneration. Dilated tubules occasionally contained intraluminal eosinophilic proteinaceous fluid; and were variably surrounded by increased amounts of interstitial fibrosis. In one section; the renal cortex and medulla were regionally compressed by an expansile; well-demarcated cyst lined by flattened rectangular epithelial cells and surrounded by a thin fibrous capsule. Few tubules in the cortex and medulla were focally mineralized. In the lung; bronchiole-associated lymphoid tissue was multifocally mildly prominent and occasionally contained aggregates of foamy; vacuolated macrophages with intracytoplasmic brown; crystalline pigment. Few small aggregates of similar macrophages were scattered throughout the subpleural pulmonary interstitium. Alveolar septa were diffusely congested. Moderate numbers of eosinophils were scattered throughout the superficial and deep lamina propria of the small intestine. There were Heart; left ventricle: Multifocal myocardial necrosis; mineralization; and fibrosis Liver: Centrilobular to midzonal vacuolar degeneration Kidney: Multifocal tubular regeneration; Focal renal cyst; Mild multifocal tubular mineralization Lung: Mild BALT hyperplasia and pneumoconiosis Suspect nutritional cardiomyopathy Comments: The histologic lesions in the heart are most suggestive of a nutritional myopathy; such as is commonly seen with vitamin E/selenium deficiency. The grossly observed effusion and edema likely developed secondary to heart failure. The vacuolar degeneration in the liver was thought to represent hypoxic change resulting from terminal cardiac shock. The remainder of the lesions represent subclinical processes or incidental findings. Qualitative fecal analysis and liver vitamin E levels and trace mineral analysis are pending. Results will be reported as an addendum. Michelle Magagna; DVM Liver trace mineral analysis : Mildly elevated selenium (3.83 ug/g; reference interval 1-3 ug/g) Liver vitamin E levels: 316.18 ug/g Comments: While vitamin E and selenium appeared to be mildly elevated; these values are most suggestive of recent supplementation and likely do not reflect long-standing; established vitamin E/selenium levels in this alpaca. The histologic the histologic lesions in the heart remain consistent with white muscle disease; caused by vitamin E/selenium deficiency. This completes all diagnostic testing for this case. Michelle Magagna; DVM

Rabbits A-E: mild to moderate hepatic lipidosis Rabbits A-E: moderate to marked gastric distension; and possible impaction Rabbit C: Moderate; diffuse icterus Multifocal subcutaneous hemorrhages Mild pericardial effusion Comments: Based on the gross finding of abundant doughy material in the stomachs of all examined rabbits; as well as the history of several days of anorexia; a syndrome known as Gastric Stasis Syndrome is a possible differential. This syndrome is common in rabbits; and is characterized clinically by anorexia; decreased water consumption; decreased stool production; and a stomach filled with dough-like contents. It is often associated with a high carbohydrate / low fiber diet; stress; lack of exercise; and occasionally ingestion of hair. These factors cause a decrease in gastric motility and an absorption of the fluid from the ingesta. When the ingesta becomes dry; it can no longer pass easily through the digestive tract. Hepatic lipidosis; as observed in these rabbits; can develop secondarily and quickly as the animals are in negative energy balance; and try to mobilize energy from fat stores. The hepatic changes are often the cause of death in these animals. Feeding the rabbits a diet high in fiber has been shown to prevent the syndrome. Rehydration of the animal and stomach contents are helpful in restoring gastric motility. Reference: Jenkins; J. R. 2004 Gastric Stasis Syndrome. in Ferrets; Rabbits; and Rodents: Clinical Medicine and Surgery. 2nd Edition. K. E. Quesenberry and J. W. Carpenter. Joy Gary; DVM Rabbit A: Liver: Moderate; chronic active periportal hepatitis with portal and periportal fibrosis; bile duct hyperplasia; and mild; multifocal hepatocellular necrosis Cecum: Pinworm infestation Rabbit B: Liver: Submassive periportal hepatocellular necrosis and hemorrhage with bile duct hyperplasia Cecum: Pinworm infestation Rabbit C: Liver: Massive hepatocellular necrosis with bile duct hyperplasia Small Intestine: Regional; chronic granulomatous enteritis with necrosis and intralesional short bacterial rods Rabbits D and E: Liver: Submassive hepatocellular necrosis and hemorrhage with bile duct hyperplasia Lung: Moderate; lymphocytic and neutrophilic interstitial pneumonia All rabbits: Various stages of periportal hepatocellular necrosis (acute to subacute to chronic active); with bile duct hyperplasia; rabbit calicivirus infection Rabbits A and B: Pinworm infestation Rabbit C: Regional; chronic granulomatous enteritis with necrosis and intralesional short bacterial rods Rabbit D and E: Moderate; lymphocytic and neutrophilic interstitial pneumonia Comments: Rabbit caliciviruses include Rabbit Hemorrhagic Disease Virus; Michigan Rabbit Calicivirus; European Brown Hare Syndrome Virus; and non-pathogenic rabbit calicivirus. Only four outbreaks of Rabbit Hemorrhagic Disease Virus have been reported in the United States since 2000; and it is considered a foreign animal disease with the potential for significant mortality and economic impact. Michigan Rabbit Calicivirus was first seen in Michigan in 2001; with a case fatality rate of 32. 5%. These two viruses can have similar histologic and clinical features; though the Michigan Rabbit Calicivirus is less virulent. Because of the potential that these rabbits may have a foreign animal disease; the USDA and Ohio and Michigan state veterinarians have been contacted to further investigate this case. Reference: Novel Calicivirus Identified in Rabbits; Michigan; USA. Ingrid L. Bergin; Annabel G. Wise; Steven R. Bolin; Thomas P. Mullaney; Matti Kiupel; and Roger K. Maes. Emerging Infectious Diseases. www.cdc.gov/eid. Vol. 15; No. 12; December 2009. Joy Gary; DVM

EUTHANASIA PANCREATIC ACINAR ADENOMA HYDROPIC HEPATOTPATHY SUSPECT STRESS. This male approximately 15-year-old otter was humanely euthanized. It had a history of decreased activity lethargy and anorexia. It also had a history of mature cataracts OU and severe dental disease. Skull radiographs confirmed a tooth root abscess of the left upper carnassial tooth. Abdominal exploratory revealed no obvious masses or obstructions. The intestines were hyperemic. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and there were white nodules in the pancreas and liver which were biopsied. The kidneys were also biopsied. Biopsy results indicated pancreatic acinar adenoma multiple liver hepatomas with fatty change and lymphangiectasia of the lymph node. At necropsy the otter was thin with sunken eyes. There was inflammation around the area of the abdominal incision. There were adhesions of the mesentery to the pancreas and surrounding the intestines and kidneys. The pancreas had multiple firm white/pink nodules throughout its parenchyma. There were multiple 1-3 mm. white nodules throughout all liver lobes. There was a 2 cm. cyst in the left liver lobe. The mitral valve leaflets were slightly thickened. Both cranial ventral lung lobes were dark and had a few white firm nodules. The right caudal lung lobe was also dark.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS CARDIOMYOPATHY CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 7-year/10-month-old female rock hyrax arrested when netted. It was noted to have increased respiration effort on 5/7. Catch-up attempt was done 5/8. The rock hyrax was unresponsive to CPR. At necropsy the lungs had pale pink appearance with melanotic foci visible on the surfaces. The thoracic cavity was filled with a large amount of clear serosanguineous fluid. The heart had a rounded appearance. The ventricles had similar wall thickness. There was a foreign body found within the post gastric sacculation. The foreign body was about 6 in. long and felt like a segment of a cotton mop head. The hyrax was in thin body condition.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GASTRIC MINERALIZATION. This 18-year-old male tiger has a history of decreasing activity appetite and weight. Renal failure was recently diagnosed. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was very thin. An overgrown nail was present on the forefoot growing into the footpad. The pad was necrotic. Consolidation of the lungs was noted. Dilation of the renal pelvis was present in the left kidney. The right kidney was not identified. Right testicle was also not identified.

ANAPLASTIC INTESTINAL SARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female Gila monster was diagnosed with yolk coelomitis during exploratory surgery and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a small amount of pericardial fluid a granuloma within the membranes at the level of the transition from small intestine to large intestine mottled liver multiple masses throughout the reproductive tract resembling inspissated yolk material and similar material is in the coelomic cavity. The right kidney was pale and contained whitish deposits on its surface. Salmonella sp. was cultured.

SUSPECT TRAUMA. This 11-month-old male meerkat was found dead in holding. It was an apparently healthy animal. At necropsy there was blood within the abdomen. There was a laceration on the liver and a wound on the abdominal wall. The meerkat may have fallen from the top of the cage to the floor.

CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE INANITION. This 2-year/8-month-old female capybara was found dead. It had been noted to have weight loss over the few days prior to death. The diet was increased since this female was nursing five pups. It had been observed to be eating. At necropsy the animal was thin with obvious muscle loss over the hips and pelvis. There were no significant adipose stores present. There was generalized muscle wasting. There were numerous white areas ranging in size from a few millimeters to 1 cm. in diameter on the surface of the liver that did not appear to involve the parenchyma beneath the capsule. The hepatic parenchyma was congested. The spleen was small and had some focal fibrosis of the capsule. The stomach contained a large amount of ingesta and there was digesta along the entire intestinal tract. The bladder contained a small amount of clear urine. The uterus and ovaries were congested. The adrenal glands were larger than expected. There was a 2 cm. diameter area of hemorrhage inside the brain case just ventral to the brain stem. The pituitary gland was larger than expected.

EUTHANASIA GASTRITIS WITH CRYPTOSPORIDIA. This 2-year-old male tree boa tested positive for cryptosporidiosis and was euthanized. At necropsy the animal had a body condition score of 2/5. The spleen was pale and small. Stomach appeared hyperemic with small white masses noted in a row in one area. Lots of abdominal fat was present caudal to the stomach but none was present cranial to the stomach.

ANESTHETIC DEATH POSSIBLE SEPSIS OR CONSUMPTIVE ERYTHROID DISORDER. This 2-year-old male captive bred impala was bred and maintained in a large enclosure with minimal human interaction but was easily frightened while in quarantine. The animal was immobilized for quarantine examination and died within 15 minutes of drug administration. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no external signs of trauma. Petechiae were detected on the dorsal surfaces of the lungs and both kidneys were darkened.

TRAUMA MYCOBACTERIOSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC ABSCESS DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS. This 8-year-old male lovebird presented with dyspnea and lethargy. A superficial wound was noted on the left wing. The animal was under treatment with mild improvement. The bird escaped from the cage during treatment and flew into a glass window. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy a large quantity of intracranial hemorrhage was noted. The left lobe of the liver was nearly completely effaced by a large yellow mass. Similar smaller masses were identified in the adjacent liver lobes. The caudal aspect of the left lung was sharply demarcated by a dark line separating yellow friable tissue from normal pulmonary tissue.

MYOCARDITIS HEPATITIS PERITONITIS BACTERIAL ENCEPHALITIS. This 9-year-old male tamarin had a four day history of weakness and collapsing. Examination revealed mild regenerative anemia and a possible retroperitoneal mass. Treatment was instituted; however the animal was found dead. At necropsy there was marked weight loss with minimal intra-abdominal fat. The trachea contained blood tinged fluid and all lung lobes were firm and dark red. Mild abdominal effusion containing macrophages and neutrophils was present. Kidneys were enlarged soft and mottled.

AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 10-year-old female rock dove presented one week earlier with lethargy and decreased appetite and green feces. Cardiac murmur was auscultated. Blood work identified mild heterophilia and mild hyperuricemia. Supportive care was administered but the bird declined rapidly one week into the treatment protocol. The cardiac murmur persisted and the bird died shortly after arriving at the hospital. Necropsy revealed firm rubbery great vessels thickened ventricular muscle reddened lungs pale white spleen and kidneys mildly enlarged kidneys and dark green watery feces.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA RENAL BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This greater than 19-year-old female rattlesnake became moribund and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple white nodules throughout the lung circular demarcation in the pancreas pale granular liver and white spots on the kidneys.

AMEBIASIS. This 3-year-old male Gila monster was found dead on display. It had refused its last food but had no other indication of health problems. Necropsy revealed a pale and mottled liver congested lungs and a small amount of ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract. Male reproductive tract was identified.

CATARACT GRANULOMATOUS VENTRICULITIS AND ENTERITIS WITH FLAGELLATES SEGMENTAL BACTERIAL ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old turkey had enucleation of the right eye due to cataract formation and glaucoma. Within two weeks the other eye developed the same disease and became nonvisual. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition numerous healing skin wounds over the face neck and body. Mild hyperemia was in the right caudal turbinates. A mucus plug was in the caudal pharynx. The cecum was mildly erythematous on the mucosal surface. Complete cataract was in the left eye. The keel was mildly curved.

TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS WITH COCCIDIA STRESS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male green tree python had been inappetent for three months and recently had been doing poorly. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation with lateral compression concave ventrum and skin pulled upward between the right and left ribs. Valve leaflets were white and translucent and several 1 mm. round firm yellowish nodules were present in the lung. Some hard desiccated masses of fecal material are present in the distal alimentary tract and the rest of the alimentary tract was empty. The kidneys were symmetrical but with slightly irregular serosal surfaces.

SEMINOMA POSSIBLE HERMAPHRODITE. This 21-year-old eastern blue-tongued skink has a history of gingivitis and was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the coelomic cavity occupying approximately 80% of the coelomic space. Pulmonary lobes were collapsed and compressed cranially. The liver was dark green and compressed cranially against the coelomic wall. The pylorus and duodenum felt firm and thickened. Three to four focal discrete slightly raised white nodular structures were in the mesentery. The mass appeared to arise from the reproductive tract and was cystic containing approximately 90 ml. of clear yellow proteinaceous fluid. Several smaller structures were present on the surface of the mass and also filled with fluid. The inner surface of the mass was white with thickened areas and occasionally irregular raised small white bumps.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS RETENTION OF SHED RENAL ADENOCARCINOMA GOUT NEPHROSCLEROSIS SUSPECT LOW-GRADE THYROID NEOPLASIA. This approximately 7-year-old male milk snake had a malignant melanoma removed 1.5 years prior to death. For approximately one year prior to death the animal had poor skin condition with decreased shed frequency and an enlarged thyroid (presumed hyperthyroidism) based on a thyroid panel. The animal did not improve despite treatment and due to quality of life concerns was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the skin had abundant retained shed there were minimal fat stores the kidneys were mottled with multiple nodules the thyroid was subjectively enlarged and the spectacles were retained.

EUTHANASIA RENAL MINERALIZATION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 10-year-old male gerenuk presented with weight loss and blood work revealed hepatic disease. The animal’s condition continued to decline despite treatment and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Marked muscle wasting and fat atrophy were noted. Small areas of fibrosis with pericardial effusions were present in the heart.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS EUTHANASIA. This female 5-year-old ibex was euthanized. Necropsy revealed reduced fat stores small kidneys and spleen rounded liver margins and a second or third trimester calf in the right uterine horn. A member of the herd was positive for leptospirosis.

BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS AND SEPSIS INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS CLOACAL FLAGELLATES METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 2.5-year-old female reunion chameleon was presented in moribund condition with agonal breaths. Supportive care was administered but the lizard did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The lizard had reproductive problems over the last month with deposition of slugs and then egg binding. Necropsy revealed a mass in the coelom in the region of the adrenal or ovary.

DISSEMINATED CRYPTOCOCCOSIS. This 4-year-old male captive bred baboon has a history of multicentric nodules throughout the skin and oral mucous membranes. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. In addition to the nodules necropsy revealed generalized enlargement of lymph nodes and irregular spleen.

PHTHISIS BULBI HEAD TRAUMA. This 8-year-old male fruit bat was found dead at midmorning. Necropsy revealed a collapsed right eye and a 9 mm. focus of hemorrhage over the caudal left cerebrum associated with the meninges.

CHRONIC HEPATOTOXICOSIS TERMINAL BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 14-month-old male llama had been a poor doer with “failure to thrive” syndrome. The animal developed diarrhea and lethargy and was found dead the following day. Necropsy revealed petechiae in the atria dermal and scleral injection serous pleural and peritoneal fluid foamy tracheal/bronchial exudate hemorrhagic mesenteric lymphadenopathy inflamed intestinal mucosa.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This greater than 1-year-old nine-banded armadillo died. The animal presented to the clinic in lateral recumbency with dyspnea. Necropsy revealed a porcupine spine in the left axillary region congested lungs and enlarged right heart with white streaks.

URATE STASIS EPICARDIAL GOUT BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 11-year-old male duck had a history of renal disease and possible hepatic disease diagnosed by blood work. The animal also has a history of severe degenerative osteoarthritis. The bird was found dead. At necropsy marked enlargement of the right hock and stifle with mineralization of the tendons was identified. White matter was present on the pericardium (gout).

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male emerald tree boa had a history of a large swelling in the caudal half o the animal and examination identified a large mass. At surgery the mass was determined to be originating from one of the kidneys. The other kidney was smaller than expected. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition a laterally angled right maxillary fang abundant intracoelomic fat stores fecal material and urates in the caudal gastrointestinal tract and an 8 cm. mass filled with cystic structures that had clear to straw-colored liquid in the kidney. The tissue bulged on cut surface was tan and had diffuse pinpoint white gritty material. The other kidney was small. A cyst was noted in the cranial portion of the identified testicle.

SEPSIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS CORTICAL ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA. This 6.5-year-old male ferret had a two-day history of inappetence and lethargy. The ferret also had a one-day history of melena. Supportive care was administered but the ferret became lethargic and unresponsive. The animal died while restrained for a blood draw and CPR was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple absent or fractured teeth and much wear in the remaining teeth. Watery mucoid feces were on the perineum. The lungs were congested and approximately 5 ml. of serosanguineous fluid were in the thoracic cavity. In the abdomen there were 15 ml. of red/brown opaque fluid and the mesentery and peritoneum are hyperemic. The right medial hepatic lobe contained an abscess and the left medial lobe contained a blood-filled mass. A tan nodule was in the same lobe. Some pitting was on the surface of both kidneys. The serosa of the gastrointestinal tract was hyperemic.

EUTHANASIA INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 6-year-old female viper was euthanized due to chronic weight loss and anorexia. The animal had been bitten by a gaboon viper approximately one year prior to death.

TRAUMA STRESS. This 11-year-old female lorikeet had been attacked by conspecifics. The bird was found on the ground and died in transport to the hospital. Necropsy identified good body condition absence of cervical contour feathers trauma in the dorsal elbow regions and on the top of the head hemorrhage in the caudal aspect of the left cerebral hemisphere adjacent to the cerebellum and no other abnormalities.
juvenile. Weight: 2100.0 g.  Euthanased.  Open.  Clinical signs.

AMYLOIDOSIS ASPIRATION PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old ferret developed acute renal failure after a three day history of poor appetite. The ferret did not respond to supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dehydration good body condition and good coat with the exception of mild barbering along the tail tip. The right ventricle appeared slightly dilated and the left ventricle appeared thickened. A small cluster of parenchymal cysts was in the right lateral lobe of the liver. The colon contained dark black to green pasty stool. The kidneys were pale with poor corticomedullary distinction and multiple cortical infarcts were present in the right kidney. A few teeth were fractured.

EUTHANASIA CELLULITIS MYOSITIS METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 18-year-old female impala had a history of jaw swelling. Severe arthritis was present in the left rear limb. The animal was humanely euthanized due to continued decline in condition. At necropsy swelling was noted over the shoulder and forelimb along with fetid fluid. Serosanguineous effusion was noted in the pericardium. Firm nodules were present in the uterus. Irregular white nodules were noted in the liver kidneys and lung.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR LIPIDOSIS HEPATITIS SHOCK. This 5-year-old male meerkat had a one week history of seizures. Examination revealed enlarged kidneys with white cells on urinalysis. Seizures developed a short time following anesthesia and the animal failed to regain consciousness and was humanely euthanized. Animals recently ingested a large volume of acorns.

TRAUMA MENINGEAL HEMORRHAGE PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 1-year-old male impala was immobilized for transport but anesthetic recovery was slow and the animal was unable to stand. Symptomatic treatment was instituted; however the animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy a white area was present at the apex of the heart. Instability was noted over vertebrae C4-C5. Moderate hemorrhage was noted in the adjacent muscle and bruising was present in the spinal cord. The articular surfaces of the vertebral bodies were roughened and irregular.

FATTY LIVER HEPATIC NECROSIS DERMATITIS. This greater than 1-year-old female lory was found dead. At necropsy the right eye was missing. It had a body condition of 3+. The left leg had a large amount of skin missing from the foot at digits #2 3 and 4. The dorsal aspect of the digits had no skin. The liver was large and dark brown to black. The lungs were dark red to black. The gastrointestinal tract contained red/brown ingesta. The small intestine was slightly hemorrhagic.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old Bali mynah had been unable to fly since its arrival at the facility in 2010. In recent months body condition and mobility were steadily declining until the bird was found in agonal condition and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting and atherosclerosis and no other lesions.

HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS PNEUMONIA PUMONARY PROTOZOONOSIS (SARCOCYSTITIS SP. PRESUMPTIVE). This 6-year-old female quail was found dead. At necropsy caseous material was noted in the nares. Pale foci were noted in the liver. The lungs were dark red.

THYMOMA (LYMPHOID VARIANT) CAVERNOUS HEMANGIOMA (LIVER) ALVEOLAR HISTIOCYTOSIS. This 19-year-old female red panda had a history of a mediastinal mass. The animal recently presented with severe dyspnea. The animal was euthanized due to radiographic evidence of enlargement of the mediastinal mass and poor condition. At necropsy the animal was thin. The cornea was ruptured in the right eye. A 12 cm. x 8 cm. light yellow cavitated mass was present adherent to the great vessels. A large quantity of fluid was present in the abdomen. Liver was enlarged and firm.

NECROBACILLOSIS. This 5-year-old female wallaroo had a history of cervical disc disease that responded to anti-inflammatory therapy. The animal developed tongue lesions and could not eat or drink and radiographs revealed an increased density in the left caudal lung lobe. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS GRANULOMATOSIS METASTATIC MELANOMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old frog developed multiple lumps on its limbs and pelvic region had a decreased appetite enlargement of the left eye possibly associated with a mass in the eyelid radiographic evidence of disarticulated and effaced joints and lightly mineralized nodules in the soft tissues around the joints. Culture of aspirated fluid from the pelvic lumps revealed Aeromonas and Pseudomonas sp. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous edema serous coelomic effusion asymmetry of all limbs with associated nodule formation and joint deformation nodules in the left pelvic notch enlargement of the left eyelid and irregularities over the head and scapular region. On cut surface the nodules of the limbs and pelvis had thick cystic masses. Affected joints included the shoulder hip stifle tarsus elbow and carpus. Yellowish or bloody turbid thick fluid was noted on cut surfaces of the masses that resembled synovial fluid. The masses had thick fibrous capsules and ranged in size from a few millimeters to one centimeter. The liver is slightly greenish. The stomach and intestines were relatively empty and no parasites were observed. Chalk sacs lining the vertebra contain a large amount of white material but are not enlarged or ruptured. Some irregular mineral or bony material is on the ventral aspects of the scapulae.

SEPSIS AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT. This 16-year-old female duck had no recent abnormalities in appetite. A few days prior to death the duck was seen in a different area of the aviary which was considered unusual and was found on the ground next to the waterfowl covered in ants. Necropsy revealed thin body condition ants on the carcass a decreased amount of adipose tissue in the coelomic cavity bile distended gallbladder yellow-tinged fluid in the crop empty proventriculus and ventriculus and watery feces in the distal colon. Autolysis was moderate.
XANTHOMATOSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 10-year-old male gecko was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the animal was thin. The left hepatic lobe was enlarged.

CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS SPLENITIS. This 5-year-old neutered male rabbit had a history of facial paralysis and respiratory problems. Both resolved with treatment. The animal was found seizuring and died prior to treatment. At necropsy lungs were firm and mottled.

EUTHANASIA MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY SUSPECT ASPIRATION. This approximately 9-year/1-month-old neutered female puma was humanely euthanized. She recently had a tooth root abscess which needed treatment. Blood work indicated possible early stages of renal disease. At necropsy there was a 1.5 cm. round scab on the right side of the muzzle where the abscess had formerly been. There was some congestion of the lungs. There was a 0.5 cm. erosion on the buccal side of the left mandibular carnassial tooth and a 0.5 cm. erosion 2 cm. rostral to the frenulum on the tongue. There was a broken right maxillary canine. There were 3-4 cm. long slender worms in the proximal jejunum/distal duodenum.

BRAN SENILE ATROPHY SPLENIC GRANULOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male whistling duck had an acute history of severe neurologic disease. The duck was also losing weight and was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed fair to good body condition bilateral bumblefoot thickened air sacs friable myocardium and liquid ingesta within the proximal gastrointestinal tract.

LYMPHOSARCOMA MYCOBACTERIOSIS DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS INANITION. This 9-year-old male lovebird was found down with a large soft tissue mass over the right pectoral region. The animal was scheduled for euthanasia but died before the procedure could be performed. At necropsy marked pectoral muscle wasting was present. A 2.5 x 2.1 x 1 cm. in diameter round mass was present in the right pectoral region. This mass had a central yellow core. The liver was white nodular and firm.
INANITION SHOCK. This 6-year-old female fruit bat was found dead. There is a history of recent weight loss. At necropsy no abnormalities were noted except for poor body condition.

OVARIAN AND BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMAS LEIOMYOSARCOMA LYMPHOMA BRONCHIOLITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female opossum had a history of poor appetite and lethargy of one week’s duration. Examination identified a palpably enlarged and nodular liver and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed much cavitary fat but minimal subcutaneous fat a small amount of bloody free fluid in the abdomen multiple irregular white lesions scattered throughout both lungs markedly enlarged firm and nodular liver and many of the nodules were whitish/cream and of varying sizes. One whitish lesion up to 4 mm. in greatest dimension was in the spleen. The pancreas was dark and possibly nodular. The mesentery was markedly congested especially near the liver. The uterine mucosa was possibly hyperplastic. Liquid contents were in the stomach. The small intestinal wall was reddened and the lumen contained liquid contents. The large intestine was mildly congested. The cecum was impacted with semifirm ingesta. An old healed perforation was in the left cornea.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old male budgerigar had a history of a large body cavity tumor that affected its ability to fly move around and breathe. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized hepatic enlargement.

EUTHANASIA FEMORAL FRACTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BACTERIAL BRONCHONEUMONIA BRONCHIOLITIS PULMONARY EDEMA SHOCK. This 17-year-old male had a history of arthrosis of the left forelimb. The animal was found down and unable to stand. The animal was treated with supportive care but was later humanely euthanized. At necropsy subcutaneous fluid accumulation and emphysema were noted. Marked pulmonary congestion and several apical abscesses were noted. The right femur was fractured with associated soft tissue trauma.
BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MYCOPLASMOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE). This 2-year-old male rat was euthanized due to lower respiratory disease. At necropsy lungs appeared normal.
SHOCK INANITION UVEITIS. This 4-year-old screech owl was found dead. The animal has a history of chronic neurologic disease. At necropsy minimal fat depots were noted.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY ACUTE AND CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female meerkat was a new arrival in quarantine that developed an acute onset of weakness. Lab work indicated renal failure that did not respond to supportive therapy and the animal was euthanized for humane reasons.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE HEPATOPATHY PYLORIC ULCER PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 28.5-year-old lemur had an approximately one year history of hepatomegaly. Previous biopsies suggested neoplasia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a few nodules up to 3 mm. in greatest dimension in the omentum dark red/pink lungs with approximately ten scattered dark black/green nodules on the surface 1 cm. cyst in the region of the left adrenal gland multiple areas of cyst formation rounding of the parenchyma and raised nodular foci in the liver a 3 cm. fluid filled cyst in the left ovary and subjectively small dark red kidneys.

ISLET CELL TUMOR HYPOGLYCEMIA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female sheep has a history of severe weight loss that was rapidly progressive over one week prior to euthanasia. It had acute episodes of weakness trembling and seizure-like activity that increased in frequency several days prior to euthanasia. The sheep did not respond to supportive care and developed apparent blindness 36 hours prior to euthanasia. The sheep had persistent hypoglycemia and mildly persistent hypomagnesaemia levels although a mineral block was used in the unit. Necropsy identified muscle atrophy adequate adipose stores a coin-shaped firm omental mass approximately 2.5 cm. in greatest dimension containing crumbly yellow material on cut surface some subcutaneous and muscle bruising over the left lateral ribcage associated with a fractured caudal rib clotted blood in several bronchi a few small dark specks over the serosal pulmonary surface enlarged firm reddened pancreas and several small pale nodules scattered throughout the parenchyma.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male scarlet-chested parrot was found hanging from a stick with complete disarticulation of the tibiotarsal-tarsometatarsal joint and significant soft tissue trauma. The bird was euthanized. In addition to trauma gross necropsy also revealed thin body condition.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS NEPHROLITHIASIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ENCEPHALITIS PNEUMONIA. This 5-year-old female rabbit has a history of weight loss head tilt and ataxia. Renal calculi were present bilaterally. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Muscle wasting was noted over the hind limbs and epaxial muscles. A large quantity of fluid was present in the abdomen. Firm nodules were present in the lung. Kidneys were pale and irregular with dilation of the renal pelvis and numerous calculi.

AMYLOIDOSIS. This 17-year-old female flamingo had a history of a “hitch” in the left leg and had been on stall rest with conspecifics for the past few days. It was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed no external wounds good body condition empty alimentary tract swollen grainy kidneys active ovaries two large follicles containing inspissated material a 3 cm. globoid structure in the region of the ovarian tissue that resembled spleen friable liver osteophytes on the medial surface of both tibiotarsal bones and no other abnormalities.
BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA HEPATIC HEMATOMA. This 3-year-old female chicken underwent surgery for oviduct removal. The animal died one week postoperatively. At necropsy the bird was thin.

SUSPECT IMPACT. This 8-year-old male leopard gecko was found dead. At necropsy there was fecal staining around the cloaca. The liver was orange with multifocal black mottling. The intestines were erythematous. The colon was purple and distended with sand and fecal material.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS. This 6-year-old male chicken had a history of diarrhea which was not responsive to antibiotic therapy. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple pinpoint white foci were present in the right atrial epicardium and coronary groove.

PYELONEPHRITIS ORCHITIS INANITION. This greater than 2-year-old male tree frog was found dead. It was previously diagnosed with cystic uroliths and substantial weight loss. The urolith was surgically removed. The frog failed to resume eating. The surgical site dehisced. The frog was treated symptomatically. At necropsy the frog appeared dehydrated despite fluid administration. There was fluid in the coelomic cavity. There was a cricket in the stomach. There was cricket further along in the digestive tract from force-feeding. There was possible obstipation of the large intestine. The liver was extremely green. The frog was emaciated.

SHOCK OPTIC NEURITIS. This approximately 6-year 7-month-old male kangaroo died. It had a history of circling to the left. It then began to start pacing in the stall and banging its head on the left side of its face on the wall. It began bleeding out of its nose especially on the left side. There was swelling evident on the left side of the muzzle. It was not using its right front leg well. It was breathing heavy. Treatment was initiated but the kangaroo died. At necropsy the right eye has a central ventral opacity present in the anterior chamber. The kangaroo was in good body condition. The kidneys were small.

CAUSE OF DEATH UNDETERMINED POSSIBLY TRAUMA. This 13-year-old male Rodriguez fruit bat was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Another bat from the same group died in a similar fashion two weeks earlier. This bat had a history of tibial fracture that required multiple procedures. Necropsy revealed lean body condition few minor wounds on the legs and wings resembling insect bites and no other abnormalities.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male cheetah had a history of chronic renal disease that recently worsened substantially. The animal became inappetent and was vomiting and examination revealed dehydration and severe azotemia. The cat improved after fluid therapy but lethargy and inappetence returned a week later. The animal was sedated for subcutaneous fluid administration which went well but then the cat began vomiting 45 min. after reversal. The animal then developed harsh respiratory sounds 1.5 hrs. after reversal. Aspiration pneumonia was suspected and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Ovarian neoplasm Salpingitis Comment: The most likely cause of ovarian neoplasm is either an ovarian stromal tumor or infiltration by lymphocytes associated with the avian leukosis complex (avian leukosis and Marek Microscopic examination of the ovarian mass revealed the presence of large numbers of longitudinal and cross sections of tubules lined with a medium to tall columnar epithelium and a single basal nucleus with moderate amounts of eosinophilic granular cytoplasm. In some areas the epithelium formed papillae. The epithelium was supported by a thin fibrovascular stroma. Another cystic structure at the thoracic inlet consisted of cysts both empty and some with fine eosinophilic granules that were lined by a thin; flattened epithelium. There was a thin fibrous stroma surrounding the cysts. Ovarian serous carcinoma Goiter; cystic Salpingitis Comment: The gross and microscopic alterations within this chicken were consistent with ovarian serous carcinoma and cystic goiter. Both conditions are not thought to be related to avian leukosis complex as written earlier. The most likely cause of death would be due to salpingitis.
