Whole body - Emaciation Bone marrow - Serous atrophy of fat Pericardium; Peritoneum - Bicavitary serous effusion Lungs - Moderate bronchopneumonia C1; C2 - Multifocal; chronic ulceration C3 - Multifocal erosion and congestion; with intralesional Haemonchus contortus Small and large intestine - Multifocal enterocolitis; suspected Comments: The findings on necropsy are various; encompassing chronic nutritional deficiency [emaciation; serous atrophy of fat] and their sequela [effusion]; infectious disease [bronchopneumonia; Haemonchus contortus]; and chronic inflammatory/infectious disease [stomach ulcers]. It is possible that the Haemonchus contortus infection could be at the heart of the nutritional deficiency; which led to subsequent immune suppression resulting in the observed infectious lesions. The chronic ulceration of the nonglandular stomach are possibly evidence of such a chain of events that occurred in one of the reported previous episodes of emaciation. A final report is pending histopathology; bacteriology; and parasitology. David Needle; DVM C1 - Chronic ulceration C3; duodenum - Mild; chronic; lymphoplasmacytic and histiocytic gastritis and duodenitis Lung: Mild; multifocal BALT hyperplasia; mild multifocal interstitial pneumonia; and mild; multifocal alveolar histiocytosis Heart - Mild; diffuse; lymphoplasmacytic; and histiocytic interstitial myocarditis Kidney: Multifocal moderate to severe neutrophilic and lymphocytic vasculitis Tongue: Multifocal epithelial erosion and mineralization; with adherent bacteria Colon: Mild; multifocal lymphoplasmacytic colitis; with mild; perivascular to interstitial chronic active serositis Haemonchiasis and Coccidiosis Emaciation; with hypoproteinemia leading to abdominal and pericardial effusion; and serous atrophy of fat Renal vasculitis Interstitial pneumonia and myocarditis Comments The findings on gross examination; bacteriology; parasitology and histopathology are listed in order of purported pathogenesis. These findings reveal evidence of ongoing parasitism; and emaciation. This led to chronic lesions of glossitis; foregut ulceration; gastroenteritis; and colitis. The acute lesions are renal vasculitis; interstitial pneumonia; and myocarditis; all of which indicate septicemia [blood borne bacteria]. The most likely order of events in this case is longstanding parasitism combined with the metabolic demands of parturition and lactation leading to a significant negative calorie balance. Prolonged caloric debt lead to decreased total body protein; with decreased blood albumin resulting in loss of fluid into the abdominal cavity and the pericardial sac [effusion]. Immunosuppression occurred secondary to this prolonged illness and protein loss; and bacteria were able to access the blood stream; through the oral; foregut lesions; or the lungs. The lesions in the kidney; lung and heart are the microscopic evidence of disseminated / blood borne bacteria. The severe serous atrophy of fat reported in the femur and the pericardium suggest that at this point; it was unlikely that increasing feed would have been sufficient to return this animal to health. David Needle; DVM

Whole body: Severe generalized edema. Severe thoracic and abdominal effusion. Pericardium: Moderate; diffuse; fibrinous pericarditis. Heart: Moderate; multifocal; fibrinous epicarditis. Colon: Colonic impaction. Bladder: Marked bladder distention. Forestomach: Moderate impaction. C3: Moderate; multifocal to coalescing; gastric ulceration. Lungs: Moderate; locally extensive; pulmonary congestion and consolidation. Comments The underlying cause of death could not be determined from gross examination. The severe generalized edema and thoracic and abdominal effusion may be due to underlying parasitism or other cause of protein loss. The impaction of the forestomach with distention of the intestines; colon; and bladder suggests a disturbance in normal gastrointestinal motility; possibly of neurologic origin. The fibrinous pericarditis; epicarditis and hemorrhagic lymph nodes may indicate systemic bacterial infection. Additional diagnostics including parasitology; bacteriology and histologic examination are pending and the results will be issued in the final report. Erin B. Howey; DVM Brain: Multifocal polioencephalomalacia. Heart: Severe diffuse fibrinous epicarditis; Moderate locally extensive myocardial degeneration with multifocal protozoal cysts. Liver: Severe; centrilobular to bridging; hepatic necrosis. Kidney: Multifocal membranous glomerulopathy; Moderate multifocal interstitial fibrosis; Mild multifocal renal tubular mineralization. Third compartment: Moderate multifocal mucosal erosion. Lymph node: Moderate to severe hemorrhage. Severe anemia. Polioencephalomalacia. Severe; centrilobular to bridging; hepatic necrosis. Comments The severe anemia noted in the clinical history is the most likely cause of many of the lesions observed grossly and histologically; however; an underlying cause of the anemia was not identified. The presence of an abundant amount of extramedullary hematopoiesis is a regenerative response to the anemia. Centrilobular necrosis within the liver is most likely due to hypoxia; secondary to the marked anemia. The polioencephalomalacia may be due to a thiamine deficiency or a hypoxic change. Thiamine deficiency can be a result of a thiamine deficient diet; decreased thiamine absorption; ingestion thiaminase containing plants or increased sulfur intake. Thiamine deficiency is difficult to definitively diagnose and is based on a combination of factors such as clinical neurologic signs; histopathological evidence; and testing of the environment and feed. The changes within the kidney can be contributed to the age of this animal and are not significant to the cause of death. The presence of numerous Giardia sp. as diagnosed through fecal examination may have contributed to this animals weight loss. The changes within the heart may be a hypoxic change as well; however; myocardial degeneration is often associated with Vitamin E and selenium deficiency in ruminants. Analysis for vitamin E and selenium deficiency is pending and the results will be issued in an addendum report. The abundant fibrin deposition on the epicardial and pericardial surfaces indicate an inflammatory response; however; no inciting organism was cultured. The protozoal cysts within myofibers are likely Sarcocystis sp. and are an incidental finding. Erin B. Howey; DVM \_ Comments This concludes the diagnostic testing for this case. Erin B. Howey; D

Stomach: Marked lymphoplasmacytic gastritis and Helicobacter spp colonization Kidney: Moderate chronic multifocal to global membranous glomerulopathy; Moderate multifocal lymphoplasmacytic glomerulonephritis with interstitial fibrosis; Mild multifocal tubular degeneration and proteinosis Spleen: Feline systemic mastocytosis Anal sac: Modified sebaceous epithelioma Lung: Multifocal foam cell foci Skeletal muscle: Multifocal intramuscular sarcosystosis Liver: Locally-extensive hepatic telangiectasia Comments: The most significant lesions in this animal were severe gastritis and chronic renal disease. In captive cheetah populations; a severe gastritis associated with Helicobacter spp. infection is a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Given the severity of the lesion in the stomach; this lesion could be a main contributor to the clinical presentation of this animal. The changes in the kidney including the membranous changes in the glomeruli and the interstitial lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates are suggestive of chronic renal disease; however; the clinical significance of these changes is unclear based on histologic examination alone as there no obvious histologic evidence of chronic uremic changes observed in other tissues. There were multiple studies showed that many cheetahs develop glomerulopathy secondary to gastritis that can progress to renal failure; a leading cause of death among captive cheetahs. There was no microscopic lesion in the brain that could explain multiple episodes of seizure; however; given the poor body condition and chronic renal disease; there was a possibility of hypoglycemic seizure or uremic encephalopathy in this case. The histopathologic findings of the mass over the anal sac were consistent with modified sebaceous epithelioma; resembling hepatoid gland epithelioma in dogs. MYCOTIC FACIAL CELLULITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS EPIMYOCARDITIS. This 8-year-old female timber rattlesnake was hospitalized after being found out of its den in the winter. Mycotic and bacterial dermatitis was diagnosed by biopsy (G13-0164) and culture/PCR showed Cryptococcus surugaensis. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to lose weight and developed a mass in the cranial third of the coelom at the level of the heart. Supportive care was continued but the animal died. Necropsy revealed distortion of the rostral maxillary region due to dermatitis around the eyes and pit organs. A 4 cm. swelling is present at the level of the heart. The esophagus was full of liquid tube feeding diet and the gastrointestinal tract caudal to the heart had scant amounts of similar material. The heart was enlarged pale yellow tan and had thickened walls. Pericardial sac was thickened tan and adhered to the gastrointestinal tract and body wall. A clear yellow pericardial effusion was noted.

EUTHANASIA ASTROCYTOMA. This 2-year-old male rat had a history of seizures and was euthanized. At gross necropsy the left cerebrum was discolored and a small 1-2 mm. mass was located just rostral to the cerebellum on the dorsal midline.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS WITH COELOMITIS HISTIOCYTIC ENTERITIS. This 6-year-old female black-capped lory was found dead in the morning holding onto the mesh in its enclosure. There have been numerous recent deaths in this flock due to bacterial enteritis. Necropsy revealed pulmonary edema congestion in the proventriculus cachexia and congestion in the intestine.

ACUTE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS AND PULMONARY CONGESTION (POSSIBLE TOXIN EXPOSURE OR ENDOTOXEMIA). This 2.5-year-old female degu was lethargic unresponsive and hypothermic and was found dead. The animal had hypoproteinemia and hypersegmented neutrophils with left shift. Necropsy revealed congested lungs pale myocardium enlarged adrenals pale and friable liver pale kidneys discolored uterus.

COELOMIC CARCINOMA PROBALE LIVER ORIGIN. This 11-year/11-month-old male burrowing owl was found dead in its enclosure. It was noted to be depressed and lethargic on the day before it died. It was given fluids antibiotics and steroids and was placed in an incubator for additional heat. At necropsy there was a semisoft pale pink 4 cm. x 1.5 cm. x 1.5 cm. coelomic mass within the left caudal quadrant overlying the left kidney. The kidneys were similar pale pink color. Sections of mass were frozen for future use if needed.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS METABOLIC BONE DISEASE EPICARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 4-year-old frog was under treatment for metabolic bone disease. Radiographs revealed severe bone loss in the pelvis and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the bones of the limbs were deformed but adequately mineralized. The coelomic cavity contained a large quantity of flocculent pink fluid. Lymph sacs also contained a large quantity of similar fluid. The liver was pale tan and floated in formalin.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE LOBAR HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old spayed female rabbit had a history of weight loss intermittent arrhythmia cardiomegaly and polyuria with urine scald alopecia flaking dermatitis and cataracts. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 2 mm. white/tan smooth round nodule on the surface of the left caudal pulmonary lobe a mild serosanguineous effusion around the liver and cranial abdomen enlarged congested irregular liver with prominent reticular pattern a 2 cm. long ovoid mass present within the mesenteric fat resembling an enlarged lymph node iris atrophy with dystrophic pupils immature anterior cataracts focal anterior synechiae with blue coloration in the left eye generalized thin body condition and alopecia.

UTERINE HEMORRHAGE POSSIBLE HYPERPLASIA AUTOLYZED TISSUE. This approximately 12.5-year-old female bat had a one day history of lethargy and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed reddened lungs and globoid enlarged uterus.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 6-year-old male sheep had a recent history of weight loss. The animal was found down. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition deteriorated and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was very thin. A firm nodule was present in the caudal right lung. A large quantity of fluid was present in the abdomen. Multiple masses were present adherent to all pleural and serosal surfaces. Numerous masses were present in the liver frequently with necrotic centers. A mass was present in the lumen of the ileum with occlusion of the lumen.

EUTHANASIA HEPATITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 13-year-old penguin was euthanized due to severe CNS signs which were nonresponsive to treatment. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted over the cerebellum and left cerebral hemisphere.

DEGENERATIVE MYELOPATHY DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS BILIARY CYSTADENOMA IN LIVER. This approximately 17-year-old female milksnake was found dead unexpectedly after an 11 day history of sporadic muscle paralysis from being trapped under a rock. The cranial 40% and distal 10% of the body had normal movement but the caudal 50% in-between these two sections had no muscle movement. The snake seemed to be improving with supportive care and anti-inflammatory therapy but was found dead. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition possible popping of the vertebral column when palpated pockets of gas in the intestine and caseous material caudal to the vent.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This greater than 5-year-old male anole has a several-day history of lethargy the thigh muscles seemed swollen and supportive care was administered. The lizard died overnight. Necropsy revealed dark liver pale kidneys good nutritional status and no other abnormalities.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS PYELONEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male golden lion tamarin had a history of a recent fall and then some weakness. More recently it was diagnosed with chronic renal failure unsteadiness and problems with the right leg. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an abscess or mass in the upper right palate behind the right canine tooth sparse hair and thin skin over the entire body emaciation hard white dermal mass in the skin of the upper left chest near the midline edematous dark lungs fluid in the thoracic cavity small bumps on the outer surface of the heart in two areas enlarged heart and pallor in the heart muscle (possible euthanasia artifact) irregular splenic surface large glands in the ventral neck enlarged and tortuous bile duct grainy liver pale pancreas and irregular kidneys with distended renal pelvis.

RENAL GOUT HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS HEPATITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 4-year-old female alligator lizard had been cooled since November and was being warmed up for approximately the past 10 days. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the oviduct contained several cystic areas. The left kidney was smaller than the right. Eyes were sunken. Mites were identified adjacent to the mouth.

CHLAMYDIOSIS BACTERIAL/FLAGELLATE ENTERITIS HEPATIC GRANULOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male gopher snake (stated as geriatric?) is from a group in which one conspecific was diagnosed with Cryptosporidium. The snake of this report was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. diameter nodule in connective tissue cranial to the heart containing yellow gelatinous transparent material. The small and large intestines were possibly thickened.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE MILD CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female goat had a history of chronic lameness involving the left hock. Radiographs revealed lysis and new bone formation. Range of motion was much decreased in the affected joint. The goat had been managed with pain medication until lameness developed in the left front limb and radiographs identified new bone formation in the olecranon. The goat became refractory to intensified pain management and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified abundant fat stores ankylosis of the left hock and irregular articular surface and associated new bone formation and bone lysis. The articular surface of the olecranon had a mildly irregular surface.

AVIAN POX MULTIFOCAL YEAST INFECTION EMACIATION BONE MARROW AND SPLENIC HYOPCELLULARITY. This 4-year-old male bobwhite quail had a history of an oral plaque dyspnea proliferative toe and hock lesions and weight loss. The quail died spontaneously despite supportive care and treatment. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition two raised white to yellow skin lesions over the keel proliferative ulcerative lesions on the right third digit on the hock complete obstruction of the choana by oral plaques oral plaques at both commissures under the tongue and around the glottis a mottled liver pale kidneys and large testes.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE OBESITY INTRA-ABDOMINAL ABSCESS (ACTINOMYCES-LIKE) EUTHANSIA. This 17-year-old reindeer had a history of declining health and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed degenerative arthritis in front and back legs flattened right adrenal gland granular lymph node in the omentum a 5 mm. round pale lesion in the liver thickened leaflets on the atrioventricular valves clear fluid in the uterus and a longitudinal fracture of the left mandibular molar #3.

LYMPHOMA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA UNIDENTIFIED ENDOCRINE TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male goat had a history of regurgitation and inappetence attributed to toxic plant ingestion received supportive care for suspected esophagitis and ulceration developed hematuria and inappetence appeared to improve with analgesia but continued to lose weight. The goat’s hematocrit dropped to 10% and ruminal motility was minimal. Euthanasia was performed seven weeks after the clinical presentation. Necropsy revealed miliary white lesion on the serosal surface of the liver especially near the diaphragm and associated with omental adhesions prominent mesenteric lymph nodes atrophied muscle and wet heavy lungs that contained a large amount of clear fluid on cut surface.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS OBESITY CATARACT. This 18-year-old male flying fox was found dead on the exhibit floor and had been refrigerated four days prior to necropsy. Some yellow/tan mottling of the renal cortices was noted. No other gross lesions were identified.

EMACIATION PULMONARY ABSCESSES CHRONIC ENTERITIS ABOMASITIS RUMENITIS SIALOADENITIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY (TREMATODIASIS-LIKE). This 11-year-old male gerenuk had been treated numerous times in the past for diarrhea and for high parasite counts and old injury to the medial claw of the left thoracic limb resulted in chronic abnormal hoof growth. The animal has had intermittently increasing renal values and hypoalbuminemia since 2009 and general appearance of the body has declined since May 2015. Recently this animal developed a swollen periorbital gland and lethargy. Two weeks earlier the animal had been moved to an isolated barn area due to cold temperatures. Since the move its appetite has been reduced and no other changes were reported. On presentation the animal was weak and ataxic with knuckling on the right front limb. The gerenuk was in poor condition hypothermic mildly bloated and seemed uncomfortable with abdominal palpation. Supportive care was administered but two hours after treatment the animal was found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dull haircoat that epilated easily crusting and scarring over the points of the hips abnormally thickened medial claw on the left thoracic limb prominent periorbital scent glands marked muscle atrophy subcutaneous edema over the scapula and extending ventrally toward the midline pitting edema along the length of the right antebrachium marked arthritic change in several joints spondylosis callous formation in mid diaphysis of the fourth and ninth right ribs white fibrinous material covering the surfaces of the rumen peritoneal diaphragm surface and splenic capsule prominent tracheobronchial lymph nodes congested rib marks along the left lung consolidation of the right cranial and middle lobes with associated coalescing masses up to 4 cm. in greatest dimension that were minimally encapsulated and white and some of the larger masses had a depressed center. The right middle lobe was adhered to the pericardial sac at the same location as a multilobulated pale mass. A wavemouth appearance was noted in the cheek teeth and several cheek teeth were loose. Congestion was noted over the ventral lateral surface of the ventral lateral rumen. Ruminal papillae were subjectively blunted and a slightly sour smell was in the ruminal contents. The mucosal surface of the body of the abomasum was purple and the rugal folds were thickened edematous and contained too numerous to count pinpoint erosions. Thin white thread-like nematodes were present in the abomasum. The proximal duodenum and several segments of the jejunum were congested. The liver was congested with brown borders and the gallbladder was moderately distended. Kidneys were dark purple and the surface is mildly pitted and poor corticomedullary distinction was noted. The left cornea was covered in dirt and an axial corneal ulcer to 0.5 cm. was noted in the cornea.

CENTRAL AXONOPATHY ESOPHAGEAL CANDIDIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 21.5-year-old male mandrill had a one-month history of hemiparesis on the left side followed by knuckling in both front and rear left limbs. Eventually the animal developed mild ataxia in both rear limbs. The animal had increased weakness and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy was relatively unremarkable.

BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA WITH WIDESPREAD METASTASIS CHOLELITHIASIS LYMPH NODE ABSCESS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old ring-tailed lemur has a history of decreased appetite and lethargy and its condition declined despite treatments. Severe pleural and peritoneal effusion was identified and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 150 ml. of red-tinged clear pleural effusion 150-200 ml. of dark brown clear fluid in the peritoneal space many small white round masses throughout the mesentery and omentum and many adhesions especially around the cranial aspect of the liver gallbladder and pancreas. The liver had a 1-2 cm. white firm mass in the cranial aspect and some smaller 1-2 mm. masses throughout the parenchyma. Many stones were in the biliary tract the largest 6 mm. in greatest dimension and the bile duct was distended and tortuous but patent. A 2 mm. white mass was present on the edge of the spleen. Nuclear sclerosis was noted in the eyes and muscle wasting was noted along the dorsum.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA. This 1.5-year-old female rat has a 10 day history of progressive respiratory distress that did not respond to treatment. Necropsy revealed an abscess in the right caudal lung lobe and a cobblestone appearance to the rest of the lung lobes.

EUTHANASIA. This female approximately 6-year-old wolf was humanely euthanized due to multiple problems including behavioral and health issues. At necropsy the wolf was in good body condition. There was a callus on the left ulna from a previous fracture. The left and right pinnal tips had small bulbous masses probably from fly-strike. The left lower canine was the only canine tooth remaining. The upper incisors were worn with gingival hyperplasia caudal to the incisors. There were very prominent lymphatic vessels within the abdominal cavity and thoracic cavity. The spleen exhibited approximately 20% capsular fibrosis. The mucosal surface of the duodenum was slightly hemorrhagic. The mucosal surface of the urinary bladder appeared slightly hemorrhagic.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA GASTRITIS INTESTINAL HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 5-year-old female hyrax has a chronic history of poor condition and a prior diagnosis of hepatic and intestinal hemosiderosis. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the body was thin with marked wasting of fat depots. The right caudal lung lobe sank in formalin. There was marked dilation and thinning of the right ventricle.
CHRONIC NEPHRITIS SHOCK. This 11-year-old female duck presented with abnormal posture. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

CLOACAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male Madagascar tree boa developed a swelling of the cloaca that progressed to involve the hemipenis. This lesion was diagnosed as a tail abscess that has been poorly responsive to treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified active shed cycle opaque spectacles good muscle condition some mild streaking in the kidneys moderate swelling at the opening of the left hemipenis no involvement of the associated scant glands or skeletal supports for the claspers a granulation bed and necrotic tract that extends lateral and dorsal to the cloaca and no other gross abnormalities.

RENAL VENEOUS THROMBOSIS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION VASCULAR MINERALIZATION. This 13-year-old female marmoset arrived in quarantine from another institution. The animal had a history of vaginal bleeding or hematuria. Ovariohysterectomy was performed. Postoperatively the animal became bloated and was found dead one week later. At necropsy most teeth were missing. The abdomen contained a small quantity of cloudy flocculent fluid. The right renal vessel was ligated and dilated proximal to the kidney. Erythema and roughening were noted in the urinary bladder.

HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This approximately 33-year-old male flamingo was found down and died on the way to the hospital. The bird had been in good condition and acting normally. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition adequate feather condition amputation of the right wing at the proximal humerus a darkly pigmented dermal layer that may be normal for this species adequate musculature and possible discoloration of some extra-abdominal musculature.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS MINERALIZATION HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 11-month-old female agouti was found dead. Necropsy revealed no external lesions. The gall bladder was full but not distended with bile. The liver appeared to be normal in size and color except for some pseudomelanosis along the edges that were in contact with the intestinal tract during the postmortem period. The stomach and small intestine had an unusual configuration with thickened pylorus and proximal small intestine. The large intestine was congested and had blood contents.

SEGMENTAL NECROTIZING BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATOCELLUALAR HEMOSIDEROSIS INTESTINAL CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This 20-year-old male flamingo was noted to be lethargic and anorexic and died shortly after venipuncture. Necropsy revealed poor body condition good feather condition possible hemorrhage in the cloaca (swab) hematoma over the right jugular vein small spherical pale area in the spleen at one pole pink fat on serosal surfaces and no other remarkable findings.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA INANITION. This 4-year-old male ferret had a 3-4 week history of inappetence following treatment for a tooth abscess. Evidence of renal insufficiency was noted on blood work. At necropsy one kidney was enlarged and discolored. The other kidney was small.

EUTHANASIA LIPOFUSCINOSIS CEREBRAL GLIOSIS. This female greater than 12-year-old owl was humanely euthanized. It had a one month duration of illness. It had ataxia and was unable to perch. It used its left wing as a crutch. It was West Nile virus negative. Chemistry panel and CBC were normal. X-rays were within normal limits. It had no response to seven day treatment with Baytril and Depo-medrol. At necropsy the lungs and air sacs were clear. The spleen was very small.

RENAL GOUT EPICARDIAL GOUT MYOCARDIAL MINERALIZATION. This 2-year-old female lizard was found dead. At necropsy a large quantity of pericardial fluid was present. The liver was mottled tan and red. Kidneys were enlarged firm and gritty.

EMACIATION STRESS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old desert tortoise had a one week history of weakness and inappetence with thin body condition after coming out of hibernation. Supportive care was administered and it was noted that the animal had limb edema and soft scutes anemia hypoproteinemia and high blood urea nitrogen. Radiographs revealed gravel and gas in the intestine but no evidence of obstruction in a contrast study. Endoscopy revealed a large volume of fluid in the coelomic cavity and white soft material floating free in the fluid. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation absence of intracoelomic fat a large volume of brown clear fluid and white soft flocculent material resembling urates in the coelomic cavity. Lungs are mildly congested. The liver was slightly mottled. A moderate amount of gravel and ingesta was in the descending colon and much gas was in the intestine proximal to the gravel. The urinary bladder was massively distended extending to the heart and had a thin wall. The bladder contained a large amount of white soft flocculent material.

TRANSMURAL ULCERATIVE AND NECROTIZING COLITIS PERITONITIS SPLENIC INFRACT SEPSIS. This 2-year-old female wallaby was found recumbent in its enclosure in the morning received supportive care but died within 48 hours of hospitalization. Necropsy revealed unclotted dark blood throughout the abdominal cavity malodorous abdominal cavity dark purple lungs multiple areas of hemorrhage or ulceration in the mucosa of the colon possibly enlarged liver enlarged spleen with irregular borders and white/purple mottling and reddening of the serosal surface of the uterus.

DROWNING MYOCARDITIS ENTERITIS PROVENTRICULITIS. This approximately 25-year/5-month-old male ibis was found dead in water below island perch. It had possible neck trauma. It had lost greater than 200 gm. of weight since its last weighing three months ago. At necropsy there was approximately 10 ml. of clear fluid within the caudal air sacs.

POSTPARTURIENT SUPPURATIVE METRITIS (RETAINED PLACENTA). This 14-year-old female captive bred kudu had a less than one week history of illness and died spontaneously. The animal was found dead in its pool. It had a history of retained placenta for 4-5 days postpartum and was showing discomfort and vaginal discharge. The calf was doing fine and developing well. Necropsy revealed white foam in the trachea petechiae around the mammary glands inner thigh and ventral side of the tail thickened and reddened edges to the tricuspid and bicuspid valves multiple cortical infarctions in the kidney multiple petechiae in the gastrointestinal tract congested liver and abomasum and multiple abomasal ulcers. The right thyroid was twice the size of the left thyroid and had large cysts that collapsed when opened.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS CHOLANGITIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old female Virginia opossum had been diagnosed with spondylosis several months earlier and was treated with anti-inflammatory drug therapy. The animal developed reduced ability to ambulate over time and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a slightly pendulous mass resembling a lipoma a dark black dermal mass bilaterally symmetrical alopecia a splenic mass containing desiccated white material and a cystic mass on the pancreas.

NEPHRITIS AND PORTAL HEPATITIS (POSSIBLE ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male/neutered rabbit was diagnosed with a thymoma and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition low fat stores and a small mass effect adjacent to the heart.

CARDIOMYOPATHY HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 6-year-old female hyrax was humanely euthanized. It had undergone anesthesia for workup. It was not defecating at all. Its body condition had declined substantially. It was bleeding from the mouth but the cause was undetermined. There were no visible lacerations or broken teeth. At necropsy the hyrax was emaciated and had poor hydration status. The liver was uniformly mottled. Needle aspirate cytology of the liver revealed golden stained granules characteristic of iron storage disease. The gastrointestinal tract was packed full of ingesta from the stomach distally. The adrenals were markedly enlarged. The liver was uniformly mottled with golden yellow background. The left kidney had subcapsular bruising.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 8-year-old male lorikeet was found fluffed and lethargic in the morning received supportive care but was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition alopecia on the dorsum of the head fresh hemorrhage in the lumen of the cloaca congested lungs enlarged and mottled liver mucoid gray/yellow liquid in the cranial portion of the gastrointestinal tract and clotted blood in the lower portion of the gastrointestinal tract dark purple to black spleen mild asymmetry in the thyroids with the left slightly larger than the right generalized muscle wasting and petechiae in the dorsal calvarium.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS INANITION. This 17-year-old male snow leopard was under treatment for chronic arthritis and renal disease. The animal’s condition rapidly declined with marked weight loss. Due to poor quality of life the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was markedly thin. Renal cortices were pale yellow. Some thinning of the articular surfaces was noted in some joints.

STRESS ANEMIA. This 6-year-old male rainbow lorikeet was found on the ground in the morning with conspecifics attacking it. Supportive care was administered and the animal appeared to partially respond but had its head down and was mildly ataxic. The animal was found dead a short time later. Necropsy revealed cloudy air sacs pale lungs subjectively thickened left ventricle dilated proventriculus containing dark brown mucoid ingesta pale kidneys and male reproductive tract.

INTESTINAL TREMATODIASIS EMACIATION MYOCARDIAL FRBORSIS POSTSURGICAL ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This greater than 7-year-old male dwarf caiman had surgery to repair a corneal laceration and associated iris prolapse but the animal did not recover fully from the anesthetic procedure and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed a few tissues that could not be identified but resembled avian spleen and possibly atrophic fat body.

INANITION ENTERITIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 1 year/7-month-old male marmoset died. It had a history of repeated fights with cagemates. It presented twice for hypoglycemia and nonresponsiveness. It had diarrhea just prior to death. At necropsy there was a chronic scabbed wound present on the bottom of the right heel. The marmoset was in fair body condition. No fat stores were evident. Both lungs were diffusely mottled pink and white.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION ATHEROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old male western cattle egret had proprioceptive defects of the right foot with absent withdrawal. Due to poor prognosis and quality of life concerns the animal was euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin the great vessel had arteriosclerosis the right kidney had two cysts and was smaller than the left kidney and there was a large cyst in the omentum.

TRAUMA. This 292 gm. 5-year-old female pigeon was not loading for the show was pulled and felt thin. It was placed in a separate enclosure with food and water overnight and was found dead in the morning with trauma to the right side of the head. The body was partially pulled out of the enclosure. Significant necropsy findings include good postmortem condition and adequate nutritional status with a body condition score of four out of nine. On the right side of the head there was a large defect of missing bone from the skull and the calvarium was empty. There were bite marks on the exposed bone. Soft tissue trauma extended for 2 cm. along the cervical region. The liver was mottled orange/brown and the parenchyma was extremely soft. The kidneys were dark red and smooth with no abnormalities but did not fill the entire pelvic space and was subjectively small.

PROLIFERATIVE BRONCHOINTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA LIKELY VIRAL. This 6-month-old male cheetah had a history of dyspnea and intermittent cough of one week’s duration progressing to tachypnea with abdominal effort. A sibling presented with similar cough that responded to antibiotic therapy. Both cheetahs were housed with a similarly-aged domestic dog that was clinically normal. The cheetah of this report received supportive care but its condition deteriorated rapidly and it developed cardiopulmonary arrest while anesthetized for radiographs. The cat could not be resuscitated. Blood work at the time of death revealed a marked increase in LDH and no other abnormalities. Necropsy revealed good hydration status copious amounts of intra-abdominal adipose tissue clear trachea some bruising in the trachea 8 cm. from the glottis and diffusely dark purple lungs a few sections of which sank in formalin. A moderate amount of pale streaking was present along the myocardium and the right ventricle appeared dilated and flabby. A 4 cm. clot/fabric foreign body was in the pylorus of the stomach and some pseudomembranous plaques were present on the mucosa of the duodenum and jejunum.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS (PROBABLE MYCOBACTERIOSIS) AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT. This approximately 5-year-old female whistling duck presented with weakness inability to use legs and a fractured left ulna. Radiography revealed a markedly enlarged cardiohepatic silhouette and mid diaphyseal fracture of the left ulna. The white blood cell count was 49000. The animal was treated appeared to be responding but was found dead one hour later. Necropsy revealed purulent material in the right stifle numerous white coalescing nodules in the liver tan firm and gritty kidneys a thickened area on the right side of the calvarium. A touch preparation of liver was positive for acid fast organisms. Culture is pending.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female squirrel monkey was nursing a 6-month-old juvenile at the time of death. The monkey was noted to be depressed and inactive two days prior to death and examination revealed weight loss icterus and bilirubinuria. When the animal became comatose euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized icterus enlarged orange liver serous atrophy of fat and possible vegetative lesions of the aortic valve.

This 4-year-old female red lory was found lethargic on the ground in the lory landing exhibit.  It was placed in a warm incubator and given subcutaneous fluids.  The bird died soon thereafter.  Necropsy revealed no food in the crop and little food throughout the gastrointestinal tract.  The liver was enlarged and pale.

ACUTE SHOCK PROBABLE HYPERTHERMIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old male captive bred squirrel monkey may have become overheated in a malfunctioning incubator. Necropsy revealed pale yellow liver with dark red to black irregularly shaped foci. The animal was a positive TB reactor.

TRAUMA. This 3-year/5-month-old male bittern was found dead in caiman water. It had no recent health history. This exhibit has had birds positive for Mycobacterium avium. At necropsy this animal was in good body condition. The tail feathers were all broken off. There was a 2 mm. bruise on the left side of the skull. There was considerable hemorrhage around the liver with a focal fracture in the distal left lobe.

PYODERMA VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS RENAL ADENOMATOSIS. This 10- to 20-year-old female rhea has a history of chronic keratinaceous masses involving the legs and feet. The masses occasionally would fall off or were traumatized by the bird or by conspecifics. This bird was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed nodular masses on the aortic and pulmonary valves. No other birds in the exhibit are affected.

VENTRICULAR ADENOCARCINOMA WITH CARCINOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male Humboldt penguin has a history of chronic weight loss and regurgitation and numerous gastric biopsies identified ulceration hemorrhage and necrosis. The patient would partially respond to supportive care but then rapidly declined in body condition over the last two days and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Endoscopy had identified hemorrhage in the gastrointestinal tract and blood work revealed severe anemia and hypoproteinemia. Necropsy identified multiple white fibrous masses along the coelomic cavity in the area of the costochondral junction and severely thickened and fibrous stomach with ulceration and luminal blood. The stomach was adhered to the gallbladder. Small intestines were filled with blood. The gallbladder was contiguous with a cystic structure that incorporated the intestines. The liver was pale orange with multiple round white nodules. Many adhesions were in the coelomic cavity. The kidneys were enlarged and pale.

URINARY BLADDER OBSTRUCTION RUPTURED URINARY BLADDER FOREIGN BODY PERITONITIS SEPSIS EUTHANSIA. This 10-year-old female rabbit had a two day history of urinary obstruction. Exploratory surgery revealed peritonitis and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed clotted serum in all cavities.

BACTERIAL COLITIS CONSTIPATION URATE STASIS AND METASTATIC MINERALIZATION HEPATOCELLULAR AND RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMAS. This 16-year-old male Gila monster presented for inappetence and lethargy and examination revealed fecal impaction in the colon. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond to therapy although the animal’s condition did not progress while being treated. A colonic surgical procedure was performed to eliminate the obstruction and a biopsy of the colonic wall was unremarkable. Following the surgical procedure the animal began passing small amounts of fecal material and rodent hair from previous meals but remained weak and lethargic with no interest in eating. The lizard was found dead. Necropsy revealed male reproductive tract autolysis in the coelomic tissues white streaks on the surface of the kidneys white cloudy fluid on cut surface of the kidneys a large amount of rodent hair and formula in the stomach and no other abnormalities.

FATTY LIVER CUTANEOUS ROUND CELL TUMOR HEPATOPATHY. This 6-year-old male hedgehog died. It had a history of a lump on the chin/dewlap area that was diagnosed as nonsuppurative inflammation. At necropsy this is an obese hedgehog with no external abnormalities. There is a 1 cm. nodule in the anterior mandibular region with a firm capsule and hemorrhagic center. The lung liver heart kidney and intestinal tract are friable and all show evidence of postmortem autolysis.

GRANULOMATOSIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE AXONAL DEGENERATION ENDOCARDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male copperhead was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified adequate adipose stores an abnormality in the cranial portion of the spine and grossly normal appearing stomach although a gastric biopsy identified Cryptosporidium (G10-1975).

ULCERATIVE DISSECTING ESOPHAGITIS POSSIBLE AMYLOIDOSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 15-year-old male kingsnake had a one month duration of a large mass in the cranial body cavity caudal to the head. Fine needle aspirate revealed dark concentrated blood. The mass continued to proliferate and displace the ribs on the right side and deviated the trachea ventrally. MRI identified a capsule around the mass. The mass was associated with a region of scale separation in the skin. The mass was surgically resected but the snake arrested during recovery. Necropsy revealed tacky tissues adequate pale yellow adipose tissue remnants of the capsule from the mass in the cervical region and some pale yellow mineralized areas on the intimal surface of the capsule. The lungs were firm. A 1 mm. pinpoint black focus was on the cranial aspect of the liver. The esophagus was adhered to the mass in the cervical region. The stomach had prominent mucosal folds. The kidneys were smaller than expected.

METASTATIC MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA INTESTINAL LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female tiger had a history of inappetence intestinal parasitism (ascarids) soft stools with traces of fresh blood lethargy and mammary masses. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had responded poorly to prednisolone and metronidazole therapy. It had also come in contact with a human creating a wound that necessitated isolation (rabies quarantine). The animal was euthanized when the mammary masses were discovered. Necropsy revealed multiple masses in the mammary chains subcutaneous edema in the left inguinal area a large amount of free blood in the abdomen and too many to count irregular pale nodular masses in the right ovary liver and mesenteric lymph nodes. Multiple pale circular and coalescing lesions were present throughout the lungs and a cavitated mass was in the liver which contained fluid. The splenic capsule had a roughened appearance. An ulcerated area was in the wall of the jejunum approximately 1 cm. in length.
NORMAL HEAD. This greater than 9-year-old female lizard was euthanized due to yolk coelomitis (G12-1356). The head is submitted.

YOLK COELOMITIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 2-year-old female chameleon had been under treatment for weight loss and abdominal distention. The animal later died. At necropsy the coelom was distended with inspissated ova and fibrin. A large cholelith was noted in the gallbladder.

EUTHANASIA TOXOPLASMOSIS. This approximately 6-month-old female meerkat was humanely euthanized. This juvenile was found lethargic and stumbling on exhibit. She had an altered mental status and had difficulty supporting herself. She was brought to the hospital and treated for toxoplasmosis since two other meerkats had recently died with acute toxoplasmosis after presenting with neurologic signs. The meerkat responded well to injectable clindamycin and trimethoprim sulfa and was eating well and ambulating better. On 9/28 a keeper reported the meerkat had fallen during handling but appeared fine immediately after. Late in the afternoon however the animal was ataxic and lethargic. It was treated for head trauma. Vision was impaired and she was unable to eat on her own. After two weeks she was still unable to eat without keeper assistance. It appeared that she was unable to see or hear and possibly unable to smell or taste. She showed no clear direction in her movement around the incubator. A neurologist performed an exam and the prognosis was poor. At necropsy the animal was in good body condition. The liver contained pinpoint white lesions on the surface and throughout the parenchyma. The spleen was enlarged and contained white pinpoint nodules throughout the parenchyma. Both kidneys appeared dark and very vascularized. Heart kidney liver and lung were frozen for West Nile virus infection. Liver lung and kidney were frozen.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE PULMONARY ADENOCARCINOMA TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 13-year-old female rabbit had a history of occasional urine scalds poor body condition bilateral conjunctivitis ataxia and polyuria/polydipsia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 5 cm. white firm heterogeneous mass in the right caudal pulmonary lobe and approximately three 5 mm. white nodules in the other lobes. A small white nodule was in the left caudal lobe of the liver. A 1.5 cm. cyst was at the cranial pole of the right kidney.

CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS SHOCK PULMONARY FIBROSIS HEMORRHAGIC ENTERITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 7-year-old male meerkat had an acute onset of lethargy and weakness. BUN was elevated. Treatment was initiated however the animal was found down and bleeding from the anus. The animal later died. At necropsy the kidneys were firm and pale yellow. The heart was flaccid with thin walls. A large quantity of yellow serous fluid was present in the thoracic cavity. The small intestine colon and stomach contained hemorrhagic contents. Ulcers were noted in the gastric lining.

ENTERITIS (POSSIBLE PRESSURE NECROSIS) HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS MILD PNEUMOCONIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2.01 kg 25-year-old female rainbow boa was being treated for chronic constipation of 2 months duration. A suspect mass was seen on radiographs. Exploratory surgery showed no mass but left coprodeum appeared thicker than the right. One region of the intestinal serosa appeared bruised with the mucosal surface irritated and thin. The animal was euthanized due to poor prognosis. Submitter reported that the splenopancreas appeared very rounded and irregular in color slightly pink on one side.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION. This 7-year-old male quail was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed emaciation pulmonary congestion empty proventriculus and ventriculus ingesta and fecal material in the intestinal tract and orange/yellow mottled liver. Spleen was mildly pale.

EUTHANASIA ENCEPHALITIS RENAL MYXOSPORIDIOSIS. This 5-year-old male wallaby was humanely euthanized due to chronic lumpy jaw. It had ongoing purulent discharge from a draining tract and bloody proliferation associated with the rostral mandible. At necropsy there was extensive bony proliferation on the lateral aspects of the mandible. There was a purulent discharge from a persistent draining tract present in the central aspect of the rostral mandible. Teeth were worn but there were no areas of necrosis or abscess. The spleen had areas of opacity and fibrosis.

BILATERAL RETINAL DEGENERATION ARTERIOSCLEROSIS WITH EARLY DISSECTION EUTHANASIA. This approximately 40-year-old western lowland gorilla has had visual defects for several years with the eyes mostly looking up and to the left and has had several years of dementia. The gorilla also has several years of intermittent loose to watery stools that responded less to increased paper intake for fiber. The animal also had mild cardiac disease. Three months ago this animal was breeding with a younger female and following this episode seemed stiff in the neck and right shoulder. There is some concern for intervertebral disc disease and the animal received glucocorticoids but mobility steadily declined in the last few months. The gorilla also developed abdominal enlargement with malodorous eructation and flatulence. The gorilla was weak in the hips when walking and sometimes dragged the feet to the point of wearing down his toenails. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes although the animal died under anesthesia before the euthanasia solution could be administered. Necropsy identified a 58 in. in diameter umbilical hernia containing adipose tissue. The tips of the toenails were worn down and muscle atrophy was evident over the stifles tibia shoulders spine and hips. Adequate subcutaneous fat stores were identified and abdominal fat stores were prominent. Adipose tissue in the chest was hanging from the inside of the ribs and a large mass of fat surrounded the heart. The gastrointestinal tract and omentum were adhered to the abdominal body wall especially along the dorsum and lateral coelom. A single cream-colored material was free in the tracheal carina in one bronchus. The lungs had some raised purple nodules the largest 2 cm. in greatest dimension and one of which had a creamy center. Dark pinpoint foci were present throughout the lungs. The spleen was oblong with a narrow tail and five or six scattered lighter areas were in the parenchyma on cut surface. The pancreas was thick and nodular. The liver had rounded margins and was smooth and homogeneous. Most sections of the intestine were filled with gas and the entire tract was filled with digesta and ingesta. The stomach had patches of cream-colored pseudomembrane that could be wiped off. A few areas of pinpoint reddening were noted in the stomach and the gastric contents had a strong fermenting odor. The duodenum and part of the jejunum were covered in a cream to yellow pseudomembrane which in some areas was very thick. Petechiae were in the mucosa of the duodenum. The mid to distal duodenum and the jejunum had vertical congested purple lines. The cecum had dark purple mucosa. The feces were green and soft.

HYPERTHERMIA. This 4-year-old female wallaby was found dead in the early evening. It was apparently healthy. The environmental temperature exceeded 100° that day. At necropsy there was dark colored blood running from the nose. The lungs and kidneys were dark and congested. The serosal surface of the intestines appeared hyperemic. Some of the tissues appeared autolyzed. The animal was obese.

Abdominal mass: Traumatized adipose (Granulomatous panniculitis) Urinary bladder: Chronic cystitis with urolithiasis Comment: The cause of the abdominal distension was not apparent; however; the mass was most likely the nodule of adipose tissue dissected by macrophages and fibrous connective tissue; most compatible with traumatic insult to the adipose. The urinary bladder appeared chronically irritated based on the degree of squamous metaplasia of the lining and the chronic inflammation. While very unlikely; an acid fast stain is pending to rule out a mycobacterial infection of the adipose tissue.

GLOSSITIS LINGUAL PAPILLOMA MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION AND NECROSIS VALVULAR DYSPLASIA. This 1-year/30-day-old female leopard died. It had a history of lethargy and being off feed for approximately one day. Keepers noted wounds on the lower rear limbs and thought that the queen may have inflicted them on the cub. The cat suddenly became acutely ill recumbent agonal and died. Chemistry revealed BUN=99 creatinine=23.6 AST=438 ALT=153 phosphorus=18.9 and total bilirubin=4.7. At necropsy the leopard was in good body condition and may have actually been overweight. There was bilateral superficial ulcerative dermatitis on the lateral aspects of the rear hocks. There was symmetrical bilateral defects in the cartilage of the coxofemoral joint. There were multifocal superficial ulcers on the mid region of the dorsum of the tongue (0.25 cm. in diameter). There was a 2 mm. white nodule noted on the right lateral surface of the tongue. The parents have a history of oral papillomas. The pericardium contained approximately 50 ml. of clear yellow fluid that cytologically was of low cellularity consisting primarily of macrophages with occasional neutrophils. The right atrioventricular valve appeared thickened along its edges. The gall bladder was distended and tortuous with very viscous bile. The bile was cultured and was negative for growth. There was a small amount of ingesta mixed with hair in the stomach. There was a small amount of normal feces present in the colon. The kidneys appeared edematous. There were two small cysts noted in the cortex of the right kidney. The bladder contained concentrated urine. The right thyroid appeared hemorrhagic and measured 1 x 2 cm. and was slightly larger than the left. The ventricles of the brain appeared slightly enlarged.

INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 9-year/1-month-old female bat was found dead. It presented the day prior to death on the floor of the exhibit. The animal was strong and vigorous but cold and wet. The skin appeared hyperemic. It ate well overnight. At necropsy the animal appeared to be in good body condition. There was a small amount of dried black feces present in the perineal region.

SHOCK SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA. This 8-year-old female river otter had a history of weight loss alopecia mild leukocytosis and anemia and elevated hepatic enzymes. Supportive care was administered and the animal gained weight and behavior seemed normal. The skin condition continued to progress and included hyperpigmentation and apparent pruritus. Prednisone treatment was initiated for the skin condition. One week later the animal became weak and lethargic and blood work revealed hyperglycemia hypokalemia hypophosphatemia and metabolic acidosis with normal hepatic enzymes. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed good body condition white particulate matter floating in the urine distention of the urinary bladder foam in the bronchi multiple pinpoint white spots on the dorsal aspect of the left and right lung lobes and medial aspect of the left caudal lung lobe. Two small fractures were in the spleen but without associated hemorrhage. The gallbladder was distended. Microscopic examination of urine showed numerous motile bacteria.

EUTHANASIA CUTANEOUS ABSCESS BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MYCOTIC BRONCHOPNEUMONIA INANITION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 14-year-old female gazelle has a five month history of recurrent abscesses on the thigh. Treatment included placement of antibiotic impregnated beads into the abscessed pockets. The animal was found down and unable to rise. Treatment continued however the animal was again found down and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin with scant fat depots. Several abscessed sites containing purulent material were present in the thighs. A firm mass was present in the skin of the neck. Marked crepitation and suppurative synovitis were identified in several joints. Lungs had several adhesions to the body wall and contained white round firm lesions. A firm round green nodule was present adherent to the thorax. The liver contained numerous 1-2 mm. white foci and was friable.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA POSSIBLE SALMONELLOSIS. This 18-year-old female hyacinth macaw presented with an acute onset of inappetence and depression and died. Necropsy revealed multiple lesions throughout the liver and gastrointestinal tract and the lesions resemble yellow/tan plaques.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS EMACIATION RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 6-year-old female gerenuk had been losing weight for several months survived a severe bout of diarrhea and gastrointestinal blood loss two months ago recovered and then developed diarrhea again with anemia in September. The animal did not respond to treatment lost weight and was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed dehydration emaciation agonal regurgitation absence of fat stores muscle wasting mild to moderate osteoarthritis in the left coxofemoral joint a small amount of serosanguineous peritoneal fluid contracted spleen mild generalized pulmonary congestion 200 ml. of serosanguineous pericardial fluid an oval white depressed lesion 7 mm. in greatest dimension on the right ventricle and three round white depressed lesions on the left ventricular apex. The forestomachs and abomasum were relatively empty and the pyloric portion of the abomasum was congested or irritated. A few Trichuris nematodes were attached to the cecal mucosa formed stool was in the rectum and multiple small calculi were present within the left renal pelvis.
PULMONARY EDEMA SHOCK HEPATITIS. This 12-year-old ibis was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy lungs were tan and wet.

AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female captive bred ferret had a two day history of inappetence and severe azotemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed consolidation of the left lung a translucent cystic structure on one lobe of the liver enlarged and roughened kidneys and atrophy of the muscular system.
EUTHANASIA DISEASE SCREEN. This 16-week-old female mouse is from an overcrowded cage and ammonia toxicosis is suspected.

EUTHANASIA DERMATITIS. This greater than 1-year-old male lory was humanely euthanized. It had a history of rigid limbs and clenched toes secondary to trauma. Prognosis was poor. The bird was eating and appeared well hydrated. Dexamethasone intramuscularly was given. At necropsy the lory was in good body condition. The liver was light tan and almost cobblestone in appearance.

MYCOTIC RHINITIS WITH SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male giraffe had a two day history of epistaxis which progressed to include labored respiratory pattern weakness and leg tremors with eventual collapse to lateral recumbency. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed petechiae and ecchymoses between the muscle bellies of the base of the neck the apex of the left ventricle and the endocardial surface of the heart. Similar hemorrhages were in the cranial aspect of the abomasum and in the lungs. Froth was present throughout the trachea. Multiple white nodular lesions were present on the caudal aspect of the liver resembling fibrosis.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS YOLK COELOMITIS OOPHORITIS SALPINGITIS. This 7-year-old female pygmy falcon was found on the floor of the exhibit and possibly egg bound. The coelomic cavity was distended and soft. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy fibrinous adhesions were present throughout the coelomic cavity. The oviduct was distended with dark red to purple discoloration proximal to the cloaca.

EUTHANASIA ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA. This 10-year-old female fruit bat had a large mass on the left side of the face. Aspiration suggested a follicular cyst; however radiographs revealed bony involvement. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis and rapid progression of the mass. At necropsy the mass was found to invade the maxillary bone and impinge on numerous teeth.

EUTHANASIA MAXILLARY SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA FATTY LIVER. This greater than 15-year-old female monitor was humanely euthanized due to squamous cell carcinoma. There was a prior history (1998) of being egg-bound which was resolved after surgery. At that time a mass was noted on the right maxilla and was biopsied. A diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma was made. Despite incomplete removal of the mass the lizard continued to thrive and was overall healthy. Three weeks ago the right maxilla (commissure area) became notably enlarged and the lizard became partially anorexic. Repeated biopsy diagnosed return of a rapidly growing squamous cell carcinoma as well as a schwannoma of the body wall. The monitor continued to decline in body condition. At necropsy there was poor body muscling but substantial to normal fat deposits. The right maxilla at the commissure had a 2 mm. area of ulceration where the squamous cell carcinoma had been located. The maxillary soft tissue and bone at this site was also notably thickened. The pericardial sac contained 0.5 ml. of turbid yellow fluid. The gastrointestinal tract contained a partially digested mouse in the stomach. The liver was completely pale and mottled with pinpoint dark spots. The gall bladder contained thickened granular bile.

TRAUMA EMACIATION LOW GRADE SEPSIS IRON STORAGE. This 10-year-old female Bali mynah had a leg injury after being attacked by an exhbitmate. Necropsy revealed dark red confluent irregular zones in the calvarium.

EUTHANASIA DERMATITIS PNEUMONIA PERITONITIS HEPATCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS GINGIVITIS INANITION. This 17-year-old male bat has a several week history of declining condition with labored breathing. Wing webs were deteriorating with numerous holes. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy miliary holes were present in the wing webs and scattered gray foci were present. Small masses were present within the thoracic cavity.

PULMONARY ABSCESS EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old female rat presented for labored breathing lethargy and inappetence. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of fluid in the thoracic cavity replacement of the left lung with an abscess and similar abscess-like material in the right lung.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This approximately 5-year-old female red kangaroo was hospitalized for treatment of pneumonia of 2-3 days duration. The animal died. Necropsy revealed serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen wet and heavy lungs with fluid in the thoracic cavity and some streaking on the serosal surface of the heart.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DIESASE PROCESS. This 10-month-old male lorikeet had been laying on its keel resting and was found dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition congested lungs ecchymoses in the spleen and prominent intracoelomic veins.

INANITION GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY COLITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA SUSPECT STRESS. This male 9-month-old marmoset died two days after presentation. It was initially found down in the cage and was brought to AH emaciated weak and minimally responsive. It was treated with supportive care and seemed to be responding. It had evidence of diarrhea on the anus. Fecal swab was negative for parasites. At necropsy the marmoset was emaciated. There was no fat present. There was ingesta present in the stomach. There was a small number of petechia in the distal small intestine.

Liver and spleen: Severe; diffuse hepatosplenomegaly Kidneys: Mild; diffuse renal pallor and renomegaly Thymus: Diffuse enlargement Mesenteric lymph node: Lymphadenomegaly Comments The post mortem findings of marked hepatosplenomegaly and multiple lymph node enlargement are suggestive of multicentric lymphoma. Histopathology of the collected organs are currently in progress; and findings will be included in the final report. Ong Chee Bing; BV Multicentric Lymphoma Lymphoma Comments The necropsy and microscopic findings in this case is consistent with a multicentric lymphoma with involvement of the liver; lungs; spleen; kidney; intestine; thymus; bone marrow and lymph node. Ong Chee Bing; BVSc

NEPHROSCLEROSIS TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male snow leopard had a history of thin body condition ascarid infection and gingivitis. Blood work revealed elevations in blood urea nitrogen and creatinine the animal became inappetent received supportive care but eventually was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed erosion on the left femoral head areas of pale streaking on the capsular surface of the liver irregular contour with pale streaking of the medulla in the right kidney pale streaking in the medulla and small cysts in the left kidney abnormal color of the adrenal cortex.

DIC. This 1-year-old female rock hyrax was found dead in the morning. There had been no obvious change in appetite or behavior. A small amount of blood was on a rock near the body and the animal was found under a platform on the ground. Necropsy revealed good body condition with intra-abdominal fat stores food in the stomach and no gross abnormalities.

METASTATIC CHONDROSARCOMA COLLOID GOITER GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male corn snake had a history of weight loss and cataracts and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple areas of mineralization in the urinary tract and bilateral lens opacity with muscle atrophy.

EUTHANASIA SHOCK DERMATITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 7-year-old male gecko presented with ulcerations on the ventral digits. Treatment was initiated; however the animal failed to improve and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy ulcerative dermatitis was noted on the plantar surface of the digits. Tan patches were noted in the kidneys.

CONSPECIFIC AGGRESSION SEPSIS/DIC. This 8-year-old female lemur had been attacked by the father. Sixty lacerations were present throughout the body and a partial toe amputation was noted. Surgery was performed to correct the lacerations and the animal is receiving supportive care. Two days after the surgical procedure the animal became minimally responsive and dyspneic and died within a few hours. Necropsy revealed dark purple hemorrhage on the serosal surface of the left kidney.

GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY SUSPECT HYPOTHYROIDISM MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This captive bred 23-year-old male polar bear died. It had a history of hemangioma on the left elbow on 6/1. Since then it had lost weight and had been regurgitating coughing and choking when eating. T3 and T4 values were much lower than the other two polar bears. Urinalysis at necropsy revealed moderate blood trace ketones 2+ protein and granular casts 1-5 red blood cells and 0-3 white blood cells in the sediment. Cultures of liver intestine and urine were performed. At necropsy there were minimal fat stores. There were no fat stores on the coronary groove of the heart. The lungs were congested. There was blood tinged fluid in the pericardial sac. The abdominal wall musculature was gray. The right lobe of the thyroid gland appeared slightly longer and darker than the left lobe. There was a substantial amount of bloody fluid in abdominal cavity. All liver lobes were enlarged with rounded edges. The right lobe was very enlarged. The surface was mottled. The gall bladder was orange. Some areas of the gastric mucosa were very pale and other areas were hemorrhagic. The intestines were distended with gas. The serosa had large areas of blotchy hemorrhage. The mucosa appeared dark gray and hemorrhagic. The pancreas appeared almost black in color. Submandibular lymph nodes were enlarged. The left side had blackened areas. Axillary lymph node was enlarged and had a fibrous texture when cut. It was not homogeneous in color. Some areas appeared very blackened in color. There was one cystic area on the left side of the lymph node. The left inguinal lymph node was enlarged on cut section and appeared very mottled. Other lymph nodes in the body were blackened.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA ORAL PAPILLOMA. This 8-year-old male/castrated red kangaroo had a three-week history of weight loss and regurgitation. Regurgitation occurred several times a day when attempting to eat. The animal had an interest in food but became increasingly weaker. Blood work revealed mildly elevated total bilirubin and mild dehydration. A Toxoplasma titer obtained ten days earlier was 400. A conspecific had died a month earlier due to chronic bronchopneumonia and acute gastrointestinal torsion. The animal of this report died before further diagnostics could be performed. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous emphysema and edema along the lateral thorax in regions of fluid administration little to no subcutaneous fat mildly distended gallbladder filled with bile severe distention of the stomach with tension at the root of the mesentery but no evidence of torsion strangulation or devitalized tissue narrow and diffusely thickened pylorus gas in the small intestine and entrapment of the distal colon through the mesentery with formed feces distal and proximal to the entrapment and with no associated discoloration of the tissues.
AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT BACTERIAL ENTERITIS STRESS. This 24.5-year-old male flamingo was found splayed on the ground in its pen. Necropsy revealed swollen kidneys.

ENTERITIS PORTAL HEPATITIS. This approximately 6-year/1-month-old male lory was found dead. This bird was housed in an outdoor lorikeet exhibit where guests can feed the birds. On 8/11 two rainbow lorikeets were found dead with obvious evidence of trauma. This bird was the dominant bird in the group. It had been hiding and resting a lot since 8/11. On 8/13 it was noted to be lethargic and weak. He was admitted to the veterinary hospital. Radiographs revealed hepatomegaly. The bird was treated. There was an outbreak of Salmonella in this flock at this time last year. The bird declined rapidly exhibited extreme weakness tachypnea with tail bobbing and watery urates/stools. Five additional birds have been hospitalized for nonspecific signs of illness such as lethargy and fluffing. CBC’s have revealed heterophilia and some birds went as high as 55000. Chemistry panels have revealed icterus and elevated AST and CK. This bird also had elevated LDH and cholesterol. At necropsy the body condition was good to slightly over condition. There was hemorrhage in the right pectoral musculature. The left pectoral musculature had pale streaks. The choanal papillae were blunted. There was mucoid debris in the oral cavity. There were small longitudinal hemorrhages in the trachea. There was very subtle white streaking on the epicardial surface. There were multifocal pinpoint serosal hemorrhages of the small and large intestine. There was a circumferential band of pinpoint hemorrhage just proximal to the cloacal sphincter. The liver was diffusely enlarged and the serosal surface was coarsely mottled dark red to yellow/green. On cut surface the parenchyma was diffusely yellow/green. There was bruising of the caudal and dorsal surfaces of the calvaria. There were multifocal hemorrhages in the dorsal surface of the cerebrum and the ventral surface of the cerebellum.

EUTHANASIA POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION. This approximately 10-year-old neutered female otter was humanely euthanized. It was immobilized the day prior to death for seizures. The seizures were minimally responsive to medical therapy. The otter had a previous history of polycystic kidney disease and vaginal infection. At necropsy the otter was in good body condition. The spleen was dark but normal in size and texture. There was a soft tissue density in the right ventricle that occupied 60% of the luminal volume and was attached to the caudal region. There were severe bilateral polycystic kidneys.

SHOCK MYOCARDIAL HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS MYELINIC EDEMA (CEREBELLUM). This 7-year-old male chicken presented with profound neurologic signs including ataxia and torticollis. Treatment was initiated; however the animal died several days later. At necropsy foci of bruising were noted in the skin. The liver was moderately enlarged. The crop was markedly distended with ingesta.

ACUTE HEMORRHAGE PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 3.5-year-old male duck was a new arrival that was in quarantine for two weeks prior to death. It was found dead in an exhibit pool. Necropsy revealed congestion of the liver and lungs and no other abnormalities.
DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 30-year-old male captive bred squirrel monkey had a seven day history of illness and was euthanized for humane reasons and diagnostic purposes.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE PANCREATIC FIBROSIS DISSEMINATED YEAST INFECTION IRON STORAGE BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA IRIS MELANOMA. This 8.5-year-old male rock hyrax had previously been diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy. It was noted to have bloody fluid in the mouth and was lethargic and found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition good postmortem condition minimal fat stores mild congestion in the right medial hepatic lobe firm dark right medial and left cranial pulmonary lobes that sank in formalin. Remaining lungs were pink and floated. Foam was in the main stem bronchi. A small amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the pleural cavity. Numerous foci of fibrin deposition are on the surface of the epicardium. Multiple areas of slightly pale myocardium are on the left and right ventricles especially towards the apex.

EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MEDIASTINAL THYMOMA MAMMARY DUCTAL ADENOMA BILIARY CYST HEPATITIS BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA STOMATITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 23-year-old female lion had been gradually losing condition; however rapid deterioration was noted over the three days prior to death. The animal became inappetent with episodes of vomiting wasting of the muscles of the hind limbs and hind limb ataxia. The animal was humanely euthanized. A large tumor was identified in the mediastinum. Variably sized cysts were present in the liver. The abdomen contained a large quantity of bright yellow fluid. Purulent material was noted in the lungs.
