Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter were cultured. There was little response to aggressive therapy. At necropsy there was a 5 to 6 cm. cavity extending from the last maxillary cheek tooth to the midzygomatic arch and behind the right eye. The maxillary bone and zygomatic arch were soft and fractured easily.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 12-year-old female Matamata had been seen on land frequently prior to death but was found floating. At gross necropsy the uterus was enlarged and numerous retained ova were present in the coelomic cavity. The body had marked ventral erythema and was autolyzed.

ASPIRATION EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male cockatiel recently completed a course of treatment for sinusitis. ADRENAL ADENOMA (PROBABLE CORTICAL ORIGIN) EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female bat could not fly and was hanging improperly. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and no other gross lesions.

Necropsy revealed proteinaceous fluid aspirate with low cellularity thin body condition perianal staining and erythema alopecia at the tail tip a 1 cm. firm subcutaneous mass on the dorsum of the tail dried white discharge bilaterally in the nares congestion of all pulmonary lobes 300 ml. of transparent and translucent straw-colored fluid free in the abdomen multiple fibrinous adhesions on the abdominal viscera mild dental attrition a 3.5 cm. pale yellow to white nodular cystic hepatic mass covered in fibrinous tags involving the left lateral hepatic lobe and a small hepatic cyst at the hilus on the left medial lobe. EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS INANITION ABOMASITIS. This 11-year-old male gazelle presented in obtunded condition. GASTRIC PERFORATION PERITONITIS GASTRITIS PLEURITIS. This 2-year-old female rat had a history of weight loss and possible polydipsia. The animal was found dead. This 2-year-old; male guinea pig died around 3 a.m. on 11/16/16; after a 1-day illness characterized by lethargy; anorexia; acting painful; not drinking; and not passing stool. This is the third guinea pig the owner has lost over the past year with the same symptoms. Recycled paper pellets are used for bedding; and samples of bedding and feed were submitted; along with the animal for necropsy. T A 1.15-kg guinea pig was submitted to DCPAH for necropsy on 11/17/16. There was severe postmortem autolysis. There were scant amounts of subcutaneous and visceral fat stores with overall body condition score of 3/9. Dried yellow crusty debris was noted bilaterally in the external ear canals. There was dried yellow crusty fecal material on the skin surrounding the anus.The lungs were mottled red and dark red diffusely (congestion); but were of normal consistency on palpation. The urinary bladder was distended to a diameter of approximately 2.5 cm; and was mottled dark gray and red on its serosal surface. Urine could not be expressed through the penile urethra when digital pressure was applied to the bladder. The bladder was filled with opaque dark red; watery urine; but neither sand nor uroliths were found. The portions of the vesicular glands nearest to the bladder also contained red; watery fluid. No other gross lesions observed. Urinary bladder: severe diffuse hemorrhagic cystitis; with apparent urinary obstruction Lungs: severe diffuse pulmonary congestion Comments Although no stone or sand-like crystals were found in the urinary tract; the red (hemorrhagic) nature of this cavy's urinary bladder suggests a diagnosis of urolithiasis (stone formation; with possible blockage of urine flow); which is relatively common in adult male and female guinea pigs. The condition is of uncertain cause; but may be associated with clinical signs such as lethargy; anorexia; and pain. The stones (or calculi) are typically composed of calcium salts; so that a diet low in calcium (limited alfalfa and calcium-rich greens) is often recommended. Histopathology; bacterial culture of urine; and fecal examination for parasites (for the sake of ruling out parasites as a problem for the rest of the animals in the group) are pending; and results will be released in the final report. Amit Kumar; DVM; MS; PhD Representative routinely stained sections of brain; heart; lung; kidney; liver; urinary bladder; spleen; lymph node; adrenal gland; intestine; and vesicular glands were examined. The lungs were diffusely congested; with areas of alveolar collapse (atelectasis). In many areas; there was diffuse alveolar edema with moderate infiltrates of alveolar macrophages and fewer degenerate neutrophils. The alveolar walls were thickened with accumulation of fibrin and infiltrates of mononuclear inflammatory cells. The section of the urinary bladder had segmental to diffuse mucosal epithelial necrosis with infiltrates of neutrophils. The underlying muscular layer was also infiltrated by neutrophils; lymphocytes; and fewer plasma cells. Multifocally; there was degeneration of the musculature as well. Diffusely; hepatocytes contained discrete; clear; intracytoplasmic vacuoles. Portal areas had mild infiltrates of neutrophils and fewer mononuclear cells. There was an increased in number and prominence of Kupffer cells in hepatic sinusoids. Section of kidney had mild multifocal interstitial infiltrates of lymphocytes. In few areas; the tubules were lined by degenerative; attenuated epithelium and contained small numbers of neutrophils. The myocardium had small to moderate; multifocal infiltrates of neutrophils and lymphocytes between myofibers. In few areas; cardiac myocytes were shrunken; with hypereosinophilic sarcoplasm (atrophy). In very few areas; myocyte sarcoplasm contained fine; purple granules; suggestive of mineralization. The section of the spleen had moderate red pulp depletion with few infiltrates of neutrophils. No other significant lesions were found. Urinary bladder: Severe suppurative; necrotizing; and hemorrhagic cystitis Kidney: Chronic active tubulointerstitial nephritis Lung: Mild diffuse interstitial pneumonia and pulmonary edema Heart: Mild to moderate multifocal myocarditis with focal myocyte atrophy and degeneration Spleen: Mild suppurative splenitis Severe cystitis and septicemia Comments: The histopathological examination was most consistent with severe cystitis due to any underlying bacterial infection with later septicemic spread to other organs; as evidenced by inflammation in kidneys; lungs; heart; and spleen. The specific cause of the cystitis is uncertain; as relatively small numbers of several types of bacteria were cultured from various organs. Cystitis is a common problem in guinea pigs; with females more susceptible than males. The problem may be managed by diet (as mentioned in the preliminary report) and/or by improved sanitation and hygiene. Amit Kumar; DVM; MS; PhD

SEPSIS. This 13-year-old female gorilla has a history of iliopsoasitis. It has been under treatment for a prolonged period of time. Recently the area had become infected with a methocillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Despite treatment the gorilla became acutely lethargic and anorectic and quickly developed septic shock. Necropsy revealed 60 ml. of clear yellow fluid in the peritoneal cavity 20 ml. of clear red tinged fluid in the pleural cavity 5-6 ml. of clear red tinged fluid in the pericardial cavity a blood clot approximately 9 cm. in greatest dimension was in the cranial mediastinum (transfusion) swollen liver with rounded edges and purple mottling swollen soft spleen ecchymoses in the urinary bladder and no other abnormalities.

Jet lesions were noted in the left atrium. A 3 cm. in diameter mass was present in the cortex of the left kidney and a smaller mass in the right kidney.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA. The animal was found acutely lateral and nonresponsive in the morning and was dead on arrival at the hospital. Necropsy revealed good body and postmortem condition transparent yellow fluid in the thoracic and abdominal cavities (greater than 60 ml. total). The liver was dark purple with multiple pale white circular lesions up to 2 mm. in greatest dimension. The surface was roughened and irregular. The heart was moderately enlarged and flaccid. A single section of jejunum approximately 6 cm. in length was dark purple. No erosions or perforations were noted and normal ingesta was present throughout the alimentary tract.

ACUTE SHOCK POSSIBLE DIC/ENDOTOXEMIA. Necropsy revealed bilaterally hemorrhagic lung parenchyma and no other lesions. A large amount of abdominal adipose tissue was noted.

FATTY LIVER DIC SUSPECT SEPTICEMIA. This 2-year/3-month-old scarlet ibis of unknown gender was found on the ground lethargic in its exhibit and died moments later. At necropsy there was marked hepatomegaly splenomegaly and renomegaly.

TRAUMA ARTICULAR GOUT (CLINICAL DIAGNOSES) URATE STASIS SHOCK. This 12-year-old male duck had a one day history of lethargy and lameness. Swelling of the tarsometatarsal joints and tibiotarsal joints were noted bilaterally. The animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy the animal was thin. A small raised nodule was present in the right kidney. Articular surfaces and joint capsules contained white viscous exudate. Moderate osteoarthritis was noted in the left stifle. A healed malunion was noted in the right humerus.

EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY HYPERTHERMIA RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 12-year-old male gazelle was noted to be sitting in sternal recumbency during the night and was found dead in the morning. This animal had recently been trailered and was reportedly openmouthed breathing. The animal was ataxic while walking down the hallway entered a stall and collapsed on its right side. The animal received supportive care for suspected hyperthermia and exertional myopathy (temperature 107.2°F) but subsequently died. Necropsy revealed absence of all lower incisors hemorrhage along the epicardium and myocardium of the left ventricle and right auricle dark heavy lungs that floated in formalin hemorrhage and bruising along the left lobe of the liver dry ruminal contents nematodes in the cecum melena in the small intestine much blood in the spleen on cut surface white striations in the renal pelvis and mottling of the serosal surfaces of the kidney and multiple regions of dark colored musculature along the limbs.

MAXILLARY FRACTURE EUTHANASIA. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Prior to euthanasia it was noted that the mandibular fracture was healed but the maxillary fracture was not healed.

AIR SAC ENTRAPMENT ANEMIA INTRACOELOMIC NEUROMA HEPATIC CYSTS CHRONIC SALPINGITIS. This 25-year-old female cockatoo had a hepatic mass. Endoscopy revealed blood filled cystic structures. INTERRENAL CELL CARCINOMA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 8-year-old female chicken had a history of continuous weight loss was immobilized for examination and died while immobilized for exam. CHRONIC DEGENERATIVE RENAL AND CARDIAC DISEASE COLONIC ULCER WITH INTUSSUSCEPTION GRANULOMATOSIS ASPIRATION MYCOBACTERIOSIS. TRAUMA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (VERTEBRAE) EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male goat was found unexpectedly in sternal recumbency and unable to stand with cervical proximal dorsal and bilateral front limb swelling. A year earlier this animal was evaluated with right limb lameness which over time developed to weakness and paresis with muscle wasting. Radiographs identified a cervical spinal lesion. The goat was also being treated for lumbar pain and weakness. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Postmortem radiographs confirmed the cervical spinal lesion but did not identify a lumbar lesion. Necropsy revealed edema throughout the cervical proximal dorsal and both front limbs with mild crepitus (emphysema). A superficial scab was present over the proximal sternum to 4 cm. in greatest dimension and appeared to be confined to the skin. Extensive subcutaneous and cavitary fat stores were noted. A 15 cm. longitudinal stretch of hemorrhage was in the subcutis and fat layer along the dorsal lumbar region. Deep to this region was an organized hematoma within the dorsal aspects of the longissimus dorsi. The hematoma was 5 cm. in greatest dimension. The hematoma appeared to originate from a possible rupture in the muscle serosa in this region. The right front limb musculature was diffusely atrophied especially those muscles of the shoulder region. Both dorsal and ventral musculature was affected. Atrophied muscles were pale red to pink with flecks of yellow.

This bird was found dead in the morning and no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition food in the alimentary tract and no gross lesions.

EUTHANASIA ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA. This captive bred female approximately 13-year-old tiger was humanely euthanized. It had a six month duration of illness. Surgery was performed and the animal appeared to be recovering; however its condition declined several days later and the animal died during treatment. At necropsy the animal was thin and dehydrated. A large quantity of straw colored fluid and fibrin was present in the thorax. The lower esophagus was perforated with necrotic material and fibrin.

1. Stomach and small intestine: Gastric distention associated with pyloric impaction and absent small intestinal digesta 2. Whole body: Absent adipose stores and dehydration 3. Skin: Multifocal chronic ulcerative and crusting dermatitis Comment The most striking gross finding was gastric distention with packed ingesta at the pyloric region and absent small intestinal digesta. This pattern of findings supports gastric impaction as the likely cause of death. The animal was also in thin body condition without apparent adipose stores. No lesions were found in the pulmonary system. The results of complete histologic examination will be released in the final report. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology) Stomach: Mild to moderate diffuse lymphocytic gastritis and focal suppurative gastritis Haired skin: Marked multifocal ulcerative and crusting dermatitis Periocular tissue: Serous atrophy of adipose tissue Tongue: Multifocal protozoal cysts Gastric outflow obstruction Emaciation Ulcerative and crusting dermatitis Comment The complete necropsy findings in this case indicated severe emaciation with concurrent complete gastric outflow obstruction. Functional impairment of digestion due to obstruction of food passage to to the intestine likely contributed to loss of body condition. Crusting dematitis -===========. As in many species; protozoal cysts appeared to be an incidental finding. This concludes diagnostic testing in this case; tissues will be saved for at least three weeks from the date of necropsy if additional evaluation is desired.

FIBRINOPURULENT CELLULITIS SALPINGITIS AND PERITONITIS. This 29-year-old female western lowland gorilla had a history of chronic degenerative joint disease in multiple joints a subcutaneous mass hypercholesterolemia and demodectic mange. Several days prior to death she was observed to be frequently recumbent and reluctant to move. She was being treated with multiple drugs including carprofen tramadol amikacin penicillin cephalexin and Lixotinic. On the day of her death she vomited a large amount of food. Gross necropsy revealed yellow opaque peritoneal fluid dark red nodular structures dorsal to the esophagus friable liver edema in the left femoral region between muscles dark gray/green caudal femoral muscle with a foul odor on incision necrotic muscle tissue in the caudal aspect of the femur multifocal peritoneal adhesions and cysts in both ovaries.

CLOACAL PERFORATION AND COELOMITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS WITH HEPATIC MICROGRANULOMA. This approximately 1-year-old male scarlet-chested parrot died one day after normal preshipment exam. The bird formed a hematoma on the leg prior to death. Necropsy revealed a mild hematoma over the left jugular vein mild splenic enlargement mild amount of fluid in the coelomic cavity moderate amount of urates in the caudal abdomen and what appeared to be a ruptured cloaca. The liver was mildly mottled.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 18-year-old male hyacinth macaw was noted to be weak with abnormal behavior and mucus in the mouth in the late morning and had no prior signs of illness. While examined the animal developed respiratory difficulties arrested and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy identified brown discoloration in the caudal aspect of the right lung and the ventral aspect of the left lung a few yellowish plaques in the air sacs petechiae on mucosal surfaces of the gastrointestinal tract a greenish pseudomembrane overlying the mucosa of the small intestine and proximal large intestine a whitish-pink pseudomembrane overlying the mucosa of the distal large intestine prominent vasculature on the serosal surfaces of the intestines widespread 2-4 mm. in diameter masses throughout the gastrointestinal tract wall a few 2mm. white to yellow masses in the parenchyma of the liver and male reproductive tract. Cytology of the hepatic mass is identified diplobacilli and chains of cocci.

ENTERITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS MYOCARDIAL STERATOSIS. This 4-year-old female chicken was anesthetized for physical exam. Respiratory and cardiac arrest rapidly developed and the animal died despite resuscitation efforts. At necropsy the animal was obese with excessive fat depots within the coelomic cavity. There was a collection of caseous material in a blind pouch between digits #3 and 4 of the hind limb. The cardiac muscle was pale. Lungs were congested.

BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS ASCITES MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS INANITION. This 19-year-old toad has a history of weight increase with no change in diet or appetite. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Kidneys were firm.

TRAUMA PARAMYXOVIRUS. This 13-year/3-month-old female mandrill never recovered from anesthesia and died overnight. It gave birth to a weak fetus. There was hemorrhage after birth. The fetus was pulled and resuscitated but eventually died. The dam seemed to be doing okay despite a large amount of blood loss. She was found down that night. Shock therapy was administered. At necropsy the abdomen was very distended. The dorsal surface of the lungs had a moderate number of raised gray nodules. The heart was pale. The abdominal cavity contained a large amount of light yellow to clear fluid. There was ingesta present within the stomach and digesta present within the intestines. The liver was very pale. There was a large vaginal tear in the left vaginal wall near the cervix. The uterus had some hemorrhage within the cavity but it appeared normal postmortem. There was a moderate amount of hemorrhage in the connective tissue surrounding the proximal portion of the uterus as well as the cervix. The uterine vessels appeared to be damaged on the left side of the uterus.
TRAUMA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 3-year-old female parrot was found dead. At necropsy a small area of hemorrhage was present on the right side of the skull and brain.

BACTERIAL TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS PULMONARY AND INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS CUTANEOUS MINERALIZATION. This 4-year-old female giant marine toad had been treated for a full-thickness skin wound in May of 2012 on the ventral sternum. The wound was circular and 1 cm. in diameter. Initially the wound healed following debridement and suturing but reopened a month later. The lesion subsequently dehisced and reopened again in August. A third procedure to close the wound was performed and the patient recovered uneventfully from surgery but was found dead in its enclosure the following morning. The toad had lost 150 gm. Other toads in the exhibit have a history of nematode infection. At necropsy the skin sutures and stints were in place with no signs of hemorrhage and no gross abnormalities were noted.

FRACTURED LEG EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old male lorikeet was found in the morning with a fractured leg and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. There is a history of bornavirus infection in the flock. This bird tested positive for bornavirus. Necropsy revealed mild intracranial hemorrhage and a complete transverse simple distal metaphyseal fracture of the left tibiotarsus with associated soft tissue swelling and hemorrhage.

AMEBIASIS. This 6-year-old lizard was found dead on exhibit and has been housed with another beaded lizard. The lizard had not eaten for 2-3 weeks but this was not unusual and it had no other signs of illness. Necropsy revealed generalized congestion and patchy hemorrhage on serosal surfaces an orange liver with multiple areas of congestion blood stained frothy fluid in the esophagus stomach and intestine and caseous contents in the caudal intestine. Some large follicles were present in the ovaries.
adult. Weight: 216.7 g.  Euthanasia. Consolidated lungs. Suspect fibrotic change in liver. Suspect neoplasia left ear. Thin body condition.

EUTHANASIA OOPHORITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA RENAL GOUT. This approximately 12-year/3-month-old female kingsnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of left nephrectomy in March 2003 for a neoplastic mass. The snake appeared to do well postsurgery. Several abdominal masses became palpable in August 2003. The masses were confirmed radiographically. Exploratory surgery performed on September 29th revealed multiple masses in the liver. At necropsy the snake was in overall good body condition. The liver contained four distinct masses that were the same color as the normal appearing hepatic tissue. The masses were firm. At the cranial end of the liver were two masses approximately 4 cm. in diameter and 0.5 cm. in diameter respectively. The other two masses were at the caudal end of the liver and measured 1 cm. and 0.5 cm. in diameter. There were multiple ovarian follicles in various stages of development. There were two masses near the follicles that were each approximately 2 cm. long and 2-3 mm. in diameter. The masses were green/yellow and necrotic. On cut surface a small amount of creamy white/yellow material was expressed.

MANAGEMENT EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 9-year-old female rattlesnake was in contact with Cryptosporidium sp. positive animals and was humanely euthanized. Subjectively the rugal folds of the gastric mucosa appeared thickened.

CARDIOMYOPATHY AND SADDLE THROMBUS PARATHYROID OF C CELL ADENOMA AND ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA. This 7-year-old female leopard had no prior history of medical problems until one month prior to physical examination when weight loss had been observed. At physical exam seizures occurred during induction and recovery and sedation was prolonged. Twelve hours prior to death the cat developed rear limb paralysis and some of the rear digits were absent. The rear limbs were cold and no femoral pulses could be detected. The cat died within six hours of initiation of therapy for saddle thrombus secondary to dilatative cardiomyopathy. Necropsy revealed thin body condition absence of the third phalanx of digits 2 and 3 of the right rear foot and absence of the digital pads of digits 3 and 4 of the left rear foot. All of these tissues were white with no evidence of hemorrhage. Musculature of the rear limbs was pale. A large volume of yellow/brown serous fluid filled the abdominal cavity and approximately 60 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was in the thoracic cavity. Petechiae were detected on the mucosal surface of the distal trachea. The lungs were edematous with rounded borders and some lobes were darkened and congested but floated in formalin. The pericardium and mediastinal tissues were thickened and gelatinous. The right ventricle of the heart was greatly enlarged and thin walled enough that the ventricular wall could be folded over on itself. A 2 cm. in greatest dimension irregularly shaped fibrin mass was present in the right ventricle at the right atrioventricular valve. Another fibrin mass was present in the caudal aorta approximately 5 cm. proximal to the bifurcation. This mass conformed exactly to the vessels of the distal aorta and had apparently moved proximally due to therapy or postmortem change. (Submitted gross photographs of the opened heart revealed that the clinically described thrombus is present at the left atrioventricular valve and the left ventricle has marked thinning of the ventricular wall and marked luminal dilatation.) The digits of the right rear foot were present within the lumen of the stomach. A 1 cm. red focus was present on the serosal surface of the distal colon. Bacterial culture was obtained from the cardiac thrombus. Plasma taurine levels = 198 nmol/ml (normal domestic cat range 60-120 nmols).

LYMPHOCYTIC LEUKEMIA AND LYMPHOMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA AMYLOID-LIKE SUBSTANCE SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female California kingsnake had developed profound lymphocytosis (300000 total white blood cell count) 96% lymphocytes and slightly elevated uric acid level. Palpable coelomic masses were identified and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 3 cm. granular yellow solid mass in the left kidney and a 2 cm. solid mass in the intestinal wall. This snake was in thin body condition.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA MAMMARY GLAND ADENOMAS AND FIBROSARCOMA. This 2-year-old female rat had a history of mammary masses and was having difficulty standing and was rolling on one side with labored breathing. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

METASTATIC GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA MAMMARY GLAND LOBULAR HYPERPLASIA HYPERTENSION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS POLYCYSTIC DISEASE. This 18-year-old male potbelly pig was anesthetized for removal of mammary masses. The pig was difficult to intubate and during recovery from anesthesia the pig arrested and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed a mass in the right adrenal gland bilateral masses in the mammary chain bilateral carpal osteoarthritis multiple cysts in the kidney emphysema in the larynx a mass adjacent to the larynx several small masses in the liver pulmonary edema and emphysema and masses in the spleen.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOGENOUS LIPID PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS. This 17-year-old male snow leopard had an acute onset of lethargy and anorexia. Marked elevations in BUN and creatinine were identified. The animal was treated with fluids; however its condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were firm with pale cortices. Intestines contained dark brown to black liquid material.

BACTERIAL PLEURITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 2-year-old black-footed ferret had a 48-hour history of inappetence lethargy and weakness. Examination revealed labored breathing with wheezing and muffled heart sounds. Ultrasound examination revealed substantial consolidation and pleural effusion and the animal died while anesthetized. Necropsy revealed bacteria in cytologic examinations of thoracic fluid and many degenerative neutrophils. Approximately 15 ml. of serosanguineous fluid were interspersed with small white amorphous fibrin clots in the thoracic cavity. A tan mass with mottled black discoloration is noted along the central aspect of the mediastinum from the thoracic inlet to the diaphragm approximately 10 cm. in length and varying in width up to 2.5 cm. with the thickest region cranial to the heart. The mass was intimately associated with the trachea esophagus and great vessels. The right lung was dark red and the left lung was bright pink and mottled. Single small infarcts were seen in both kidneys.

MESANGIOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ATHEROSCLEROSIS GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old female squirrel monkey had a four day history of illness and died. Blood work prior to death revealed renal failure.

ACUTE SHOCK. This 2-year-old male rainbow lorikeet was observed by a keeper to go down and die and much fluid from the crop was emitted as the bird died. Necropsy revealed no evidence of trauma a cystic area in the left testicle red to pink and mildly hemorrhagic small intestine.

TRAUMA. This 15-year-old female Swainson’s lorikeet was found dead with no prior signs of illness. The bird had been previously examined due to poor body condition score but was otherwise healthy. Necropsy revealed a pale liver with severe hepatomegaly prominent pale streaking through the pectoral muscles and hemorrhage or congestion in the skull around the foramen magnum.

BACTERIAL AIR SACCULITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS OSTEOMYELITIS. This 26-year-old female swan was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the animal was thin. A fatty mass was present invading the dorsal keel and compressing the heart. The lung was congested and sank in formalin.

EMACIATION STRESS. This 5-week-old New England cottontail rabbit is from a captive breeding program. It had been transferred to a hardening pen to acclimate to natural temperature and light cycles and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed mucus in the stomach pinpoint gastric ulcers absence of intra-abdominal adipose and poor body condition. A conspecific had died within 24 hours of this rabbit.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS TUBULAR PROTEINOSIS GLOMERULOSCERLOSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA DERMATITIS. This 18-year-old red panda was weak and shaking. The animal was humanely euthanized due to geriatric condition. At necropsy an area of hair loss was present over the thoracolumbar region. Lungs appeared hemorrhagic. Present in the pericardium are 3 ml. of straw colored fluid. Renal cortices appeared pale and firm.
