METASTATIC MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 30.5-year-old female ring-tailed lemur had been diagnosed with mammary gland adenocarcinoma in January 2009 and also in 2013 (G09-0477 G13-0035). Routine examination in June 2013 identified multiple pulmonary masses noted by radiograph and ultrasound. The animal recently presented with dyspnea and refused food. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cataracts in both eyes a 1 cm. in diameter firm mass palpable in the left cranial mammary region multiple small nodules palpable in the right cranial mammary region numerous firm tan-colored masses of various shapes and sizes throughout the pulmonary parenchyma some endocardiosis in the left and right atrioventricular valves some tan discoloration of the duodenum at the opening of the bile duct a 2 cm. tan firm mass in the omentum at the cranial aspect of the greater curvature of the stomach a second smaller mass with similar appearance near the duodenum and pancreas. Cystic changes were in the left arm of the pancreas. Multiple red nodules were present on the dorsal surface of the spleen the kidneys were bilaterally congested and a circular mass was in the serosa of the right kidney. Multiple firm tan-white nodules were present throughout the pleural cavity and 75 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was in the left pleural cavity. A 2 cm. firm mass was present on the ventral aspect of the right femoral artery distal to the aortic bifurcation and no other abnormalities.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA HARD PALATE. This 11-year-old male capybara was previously diagnosed with an oral lesion that was suspicious for a squamous cell carcinoma. In the last week of life the capybara developed bilateral sporadic epistaxis with progressive respiratory distress and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. A flat 6.5 cm. in greatest dimension mass that was tan and brown was attached to the hard and soft palate. The mass infiltrated into the fibrous and osseous tissues of the hard palate and on the nasopharyngeal side of the palate one large firm red nodule extended dorsally. The palate was otherwise thickened and irregular. On cut surface the middle of the mass was white homogeneous and firm.

AUTOLYSIS. This 2-year-old female Madagascar day gecko was found dead. At necropsy there was a small amount of berry-like material in the mouth and the throat region seemed swollen. All tissues were severely autolyzed making it difficult to determine their origin.

CHRONIC GASTROENTEROCOLITIS AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This female 7.5-year-old gerenuk developed a distended hypermotile rumen and became severely wasted over a five month period in spite of good appetite and normal pelleted feces. The animal did not improve with supportive care and a surgical exploratory that did not identify the cause. The animal became recumbent several days after the surgical procedure and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation rough haircoat generalized muscle atrophy and absence of fat stores. Adhesions at surgical sites were noted but with no associated obstructions and no adhesions elsewhere. One mesenteric lymph node was enlarged. The rumen contained foamy soft material with grade variation of fibrin and liquid content. Reduced villous development was noted in the mucosa reticular cells were shallow and the omasum had normal appearing contents. Scattered shallow ulcers or erosions are present in the mucosa of the fundus and pylorus and the pylorus had a mild cobble irregularity to the mucosa. The duodenal mucosa was mildly thickened and cobbled. No parasites were identified. The mucosa of the gallbladder was slightly hyperplastic and cystic. An abnormal extension of the bone of the nuchal crest was noted 2-3 cm. caudal to the plane of the foramen magnum and the sella tursica appeared abnormally deep although the pituitary appeared grossly normal. The right cranial ventral pulmonary lobe was atelectatic and consolidated. Plant material and mucous exudate were noted in the trachea and in the right main stem bronchus and small airways of the right cranial lung.

PARAMYXOVIRUS INFECTION RENAL GRANULOMAS. This female approximately 8-year-old green tree python was found dead in its enclosure. It had a recent history of gurgling but physical exam at that time was unremarkable. Culture grew Alcaligenes xylosoxidans Citrobacter freundii and Morganella morganii. At necropsy there was severe pneumonia with purulent flocculent material within the trachea and lungs. The lungs were dark red and consolidated. There were multiple 1-2 mm. in diameter abscess/granulomas adjacent to the esophagus and small intestine. There are multifocal areas of 1 mm. in diameter grape-like clusters throughout the kidney. There was an apparent encysted nematode found along the small intestine.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS AND NECROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS TRAUMATIC FRACTURE WITH OSTEOMYELITIS. This 17-year-old male Rodriguez flying fox was found dead. It had no prior clinical problems. Necropsy revealed swellings along the phalanges of digits #3 and 4 of the left wing and an open fracture of the third phalange digit #3 of the right wing. Lungs had patchy congestion.

TERMINAL SEPSIS ASCENDING AORTA ATHEROSCLEROSIS EMACIATION. This 31-year-old male thick-billed parrot was recently hospitalized for a traumatic wound to the upper eyelid. The bird was anesthetized twice for surgical repair and debridement of necrotic tissue. The bird appeared to be doing well but was found dead in the cage. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition dehydration a 2 cm. scab on the proximal keel a granulating surgical wound by the right eye a scab above the left eye hemorrhage within the skull a puncture wound into the skull a small white opacity on the left AV valve an enlarged liver with hemorrhages an mildly enlarged spleen yeast within the proventriculus and abundant ingesta in the proventriculus and ventriculus.

ACUTE PULMONARY SHOCK CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 20-year-old female pygmy falcon was found dead unexpectedly. It had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed large amounts of adipose tissue in the coelomic cavity some pinpoint mucoid plaques on the air sacs ingesta in the alimentary tract and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA SHELL ULCERS SHELL NECROSIS GASTRIC NEMATODES. This greater than 3-year-old female matamata was humanely euthanized. This turtle was housed in a small fiberglass tank on public display. The tank was well lit and had a gravel substrate. The turtle presented on 12/2/02 with a pale peeling plastron and peeling keratin scutes on the right and left marginal carapace. The ventral thighs were also pale with loss/wear of the warty tubercles normally more prominent in this species. The skin on the ventral neck was bright red. Cultures of the lesion revealed a few different gram negative bacteria. The turtle was treated and then moved to a different exhibit to join a group of unaffected matamatas housed off exhibit. At recheck the skin where it attached under the bony carapace had peeled away leading to exposure of the soft tissues underneath the carapace. One of the lesions on the carapace where there was bone exposure revealed a totally avascular section of bone even after scraping through the bone. At necropsy the turtle was cachectic. There was no darkly pigmented keratinized scute material present on the bridge plastron or marginal carapace. These areas were very pale and denuded with multifocal areas of exposed bone. The keratinized scutes remaining on the carapace were easily peeled away with a fingernail. The skin was pale and easily pulled away from bony attachments on the shell. The ventral neck skin was bright red. The ventral thighs were pale. Skeletal muscle was very pale. There were minimal subcutaneous intracoelomic fat stores present. The coelomic cavity was very wet. There was a focal group of what appeared to be encapsulated coiled nematodes fixed to the gastric serosa. The liver was frozen for future use if needed.

1. Kidney: Renal carcinoma 2. Kidney: Interstitial nephritis; lymphocytic; multifocal; mild; chronic 3. Kidney: Renal gout; multifocal; mild; chronic 4. Skeletal muscle: Myositis; granulomatous and heterophilic; regional; marked; chronic 5. Heart: Arteriosclerosis; multifocal; moderate; chronic 6. Heart: Interstitial fibrosis; perivascular; multifocal; mild; chronic Comment: This animal had histologic lesions in multiple organs that may have contributed to the clinical signs noted. In the submitted history; drowning was suspected (the animal was found dead in the pool with a claw stuck in the pool grate); and could be considered as a possible cause of death. Renal lesions noted grossly were consistent with renal carcinoma. Other renal lesions included interstitial nephritis and renal gout. Granulomatous and heteriophilic myositis was present in one section of skeletal muscle. No intralesional infectious organisms were observed; however bacterial infection is a plausible differential diagnosis; possibly induced by regional skeletal muscle trauma. Cardiac lesions included moderate arteriosclerosis and perivascular fibrosis; both considered age-related findings - no inflammation was observed in the heart. West Nile virus and heavy metal toxicity screening were pending (per history); and immunohistochemistry for West Nile virus is also available upon request.
LIPOSARCOMA. This 8-year-old female lemur had a prior diagnosis of an inoperable abdominal liposarcoma. The animal was humanely euthanized.

EUTHANASIA STRESS ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA THYROID HYPERPLASIA. This 12.5-year-old male tiger had an acute onset of repeated vomiting. Radiographs suggested volvulus and gastric dilatation and the animal was humanely euthanized. Necropsy revealed a focal mural cyst in the duodenum and moderate gaseous distention of the stomach. The stomach was not otherwise anatomically displaced and gastric volvulus could not be documented.

HEAD TRAUMA ULCERATIVE FACIAL CELLULITIS. This 11-year-old spayed female straw colored fruit bat was found dead on the exhibit floor in the morning one week after routine examinations were performed on the colony. The bat was spayed years ago and had chronic mandibular skin avulsion with rostral mandibular subcutaneous tissue exposure of many years duration. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy other than the rostral mandibular exposure.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) NEPHROSCLEROSIS AMYLOIDOSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 15.5-year-old male gerenuk had outlived its teeth and lost many of them requiring special attention regarding the diet. The animal also had chronic stiffness in the rear limbs and back and chronic lameness in the forelimbs associated with bone proliferation and partial fusion across the pastern joints. The animal initially improved with anti-inflammatory drug therapy and laser applications but then became less responsive and was lame most of the time on the left front limb. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dry dusty haircoat moderate generalized muscle atrophy modest body fat degenerative arthritic changes in the hip joints long rear hooves spondylosis in the lumbosacral region degenerative changes in both shoulders overgrown front hooves with medial curling of the right toe and excessive extension of the distal interphalangeal joint. Both lateral pasterns have bone proliferation on the abaxial sides restricting range of motion. Dental condition is poor with severe wavemouth. The eyes have mild nuclear sclerosis with ragged pupillary margins. The lungs have peripheral hyperinflated margins and a 6 cm. subpleural bulla is in the center of the left caudal pulmonary lobe. The bulla is directly across from the healed rib fracture. A few old healed fractured ribs and some uneven bone/cartilage enlargement of multiple costochondral junctions and sternebral joints are also noted. Severe discrete foci of fibrosis are present within the myocardium of each ventricle. Numerous fibrous tags are on the abdominal surface of the diaphragm at points of contact with the spleen and rumen. Some mild serosal fibrosis and numerous pinpoint white or tan foci are present throughout the parenchyma of the liver. Several 4-5 mm. in diameter gallstones are in the lumen of the gallbladder. The kidneys have markedly granular cut surface the parenchyma bulges on cut surface and is heavily streaked red and white. A few scattered small cysts are in the renal parenchyma and a few tiny sand-like uroliths are in one section of kidney but not in either pelvis. The villous surface of the rumen is uneven but otherwise normal. One whipworm is observed in the cecal mucosa.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA WITH ABSCESS FORMATION CHRONIC RENAL ABSCESS. This 5-year-old male wallaby had been examined six months earlier for chronic weight loss despite good appetite and at that time pneumonia was diagnosed in the right caudal pulmonary lobe. Supportive care was administered and the animal improved. Three weeks prior to death dental disease was noted and extractions were performed. An opacity was present in the right cranial ventral lung. The day prior to death the animal presented with acute tachypnea and inappetence. Severe right pulmonary opacity was noted radiographically. Treatment was initiated but the wallaby died the following evening. Necropsy identified thin body condition translucent fluid in the thoracic cavity multiple adhesions between the right lateral pulmonary lobes and body wall purple discoloration of the right lung multiple firm nodules throughout the lung dark brown material on cut surface of the lung and an encapsulated focus of purulent material in the right caudal lung. No normal pulmonary tissue was observed. The left lungs were dark purple with multiple light brown nodules in the cranial lobe. Gas was present in the jejunum normal ingesta were in the stomach and no other abnormalities were noted. No abnormalities were noted in the tooth extraction sites.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This greater than 12-year-old male gecko died. it was being treated since late June for a skin ulcer near the cloaca. The wound was healing and topical treatment had stopped. The gecko had been separated in a bucket so stress may have been a factor. At necropsy the gecko was in thin body condition. There was a small skin ulcer (less than 0.5 cm.) just anterior to the cloacal opening that did not extend into the muscle layers. The lungs were red and wet. The liver was friable and autolytic. All intestines were uniformly red to black. The stomach was white.

CERVICAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA THYROID ADENOMA PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA SUBAORTIC STENOSIS ENDOCARDIOSIS. This 18-year-old male snow leopard was a geriatric animal with a previous history of thyroid carcinoma removed in March 1995. The animal had a history of periodontal disease. Previous echocardiograms revealed mild subaortic stenosis mild mitral valve regurgitation and slight left atrial enlargement. The animal had previous problems with intermittent ulcerative granulomatous dermatitis of the tip of the prepuce. It had recently been observed coughing and gagging and stopped breathing shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed excessive adipose tissue multiple large cavitated masses on the right lateral aspect of the trachea subaortic stenosis balloon dilatation of the aorta of the outflow tract a small jet lesion on the mural surface of the aorta mild endocardiosis of left and right atrioventricular valves absence of teeth adhesions of the distal esophagus to the trachea three nematodes in the stomach hyperemia of the gastric and intestinal mucosa a cyst containing green fluid in one lobe of the liver pitted kidneys a raised white plaque on the mucosal surface of the urinary bladder ulceration of the prepuce black tracheobronchial lymph nodes and pitting/eburnation of the articular surfaces of the coxofemoral joints.

HYALINE GLOMERULOPATHY WITH PROTEIN LOSING NEPHROPATHY. This 4-year-old female ferret has a history of intermittent inappetence and dehydration and died in the hospital. Necropsy revealed approximately 8 ml. of serosanguineous thoracic fluid consolidated lungs enlarged left adrenal multiple hepatic cysts gas distended intestines irregular kidneys and an 8 mm. mass caudal to the left kidney.

EUTHANASIA MALOCCLUSION TOOTH ROOT ABSCESS TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This approximately 9-year-old male rabbit was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic dental problems and malocclusion. It also had cataracts. It was diagnosed with severe tooth root abscessation that would have required extensive surgical repair. At necropsy there was malocclusion and fracture of the lower right incisor. There was overgrowth of the lower left incisor. There were two firm 1-2 cm. swellings just cranial to the angle of the jaw ventrally that were associated with a fistulous tract leading from the right incisor and right first molar. There was purulent discharge also evident around the lower right first molar which was also overgrown. There was white caseous purulent discharge present in the swellings under the jaw. There was bilateral cataract.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMAS MICROGRANULOMATOSIS HEPATITIS AND PERIVASCULITIS POSSIBLE ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS CARDIAC FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 3-year-old rabbit has had mammary gland adenocarcinomas excised twice in the last 12 months and has two more suspected tumors in the right ventral neck and axilla. The right ventral neck mass has a purulent necrotic center that is draining. Cytology is consistent with a carcinoma. The rabbit was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed patchy congestion in the lung large amount of internal fat and no other abnormalities aside from the previously described masses.

DIC BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 5-year-old female lemur was found dead in its nest box. The animal was found curled in the fetal position with its head in opisthotonos. Necropsy revealed a mesenteric torsion with food in the stomach and feces in the colon.

COCCIDIOSIS. This 8-week-old female black-footed ferret was found dead in its enclosure in the morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition some reddening around the vessels connected to the heart enlarged heart apparent extra vessels connecting the lungs to the heart particularly around the area of the right atrium congestion and increased tortuosity of the vessels around the heart subjectively enlarged liver mild lymph node enlargement in the colon possible inflammation in the small and large intestines petechiae on the surfaces of the kidney mildly enlarged and rounded right kidney a 2 mm. white smooth region in the medulla of the right kidney and a similar white region in the left kidney.

COELOMIC SOFT TISSUE SARCOMA XANTHOMATOSIS COELOMIC BACTERIAL GRANULOMA. This 7-year-old female anole had a history of emaciation weakness and dehydration. The animal was treated several days with antibiotics but died in the hospital. Necropsy revealed emaciation. Two large masses were in the coelomic cavity effacing most of the other organs. One mass was fibrous and white; the second mass was fluctuant and filled with what appeared to be yolk.

BILATERAL CATARACTS SPINAL DEFORMITY (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old female python had a two week history of lethargy and abnormal posture with a corkscrew position at midsection. The animal had been inappetent for four months. Examination revealed obstipation dehydration good body condition vertebral deformity in the midsection with high normal uric acid level anemia and negative blood culture. Supportive care was administered with no improvement and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed empty stomach hard cast in the large intestine bilateral cataracts with the left more prominent than the right and bilious fluid in the caudal coelom in two separate compartments.
NA

HEMANGIOSARCOMA HEMOABDOMEN CONSPECIFIC AGGRESSION EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female African wild dog was introduced into an enclosure with two males two weeks prior. The animal sustained multiple bite wounds from the males on exhibit. The animal became lethargic inappetent and was reluctant to move remaining in sternal recumbency. Examination revealed pale mucous membranes anemia slightly distended abdomen and multiple brown masses along the ventral midline up to 5 cm. in greatest dimension. Abdominocentesis identified frank blood in the abdomen. Radiographs revealed stacking of the intestines peritoneal fluid and multiple round masses. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes after 700 ml. of blood were sectioned from the abdomen during surgery. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple lacerations over the body a 5 cm. firm intradermal mass on the dorsum over the lumbar vertebrae pinpoint black foci in the lungs possibly thickened left ventricular free wall multiple black circular masses attached to the abdominal wall a 1 cm. focus of pallor in the spleen multiple black masses throughout the omentum that oozed blood on cut surfaces a fluctuant mass attached to the caudal pole of the right kidney bruising associated with lacerations and no other gross findings.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE ATHEROSCLEROSIS AORTIC DEGENERATION WITH EARLY ANEYRYSM FORMATION UTERINE LEIOMYOMA. This 35-year-old female chimpanzee was found dead in her nest. Necropsy revealed few adhesions in the abdominal and pleural cavities some degenerative arthritis in the left stifle endocardiosis on the left atrioventricular valve and multiple fibrous masses in the uterus.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOCARDITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 11-year-old male capybara had a history of chronic weight loss and lameness. The animal was anesthetized for physical exam. Neurologic signs developed during recovery and the animal later died. At necropsy a large mass was present in the right axilla. Smaller masses were present in the skin adjacent to the spine.

CARDIOMYOPATHY WITH THROMBOSIS DIC. This 12-year-old male warthog presented with acute onset of lethargy and partial anorexia. The animal exhibited dull mentation and was reluctant to stand unless poked. Ambulation was coordinated when the animal did stand. The animal also had a prominent systolic heart murmur. Necropsy revealed ample adipose stores numerous hematomas throughout the abdominal cavity hemorrhage in the diaphragm hemorrhagic and edematous lymph nodes frank blood in the pericardial sac and a large clot that surrounds the entire heart hepatic laceration with blood clot and few nodular foci in the kidneys. The penmate also died with similar gross lesions.

TRAUMA HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 16-year-old male naked mole rat was recently introduced to the colony and had significant trauma. The animal had abundant wounds received supportive care over three days but died spontaneously. At necropsy there were multiple lacerations of the dorsum and skull. There were multiple bruises on all limbs the thorax and the pelvis. Free blood was on all limbs the thorax and the pelvis. Free blood was present in the cranial thorax.

METASTATIC PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA UTERINE LEIOMYOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female river otter had become acutely lethargic with increased respiratory effort would lay laterally (unusual for this animal) and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had no previous medical history. Necropsy revealed thin body condition fractured upper canines a moderate amount of yellow/brown-tinged clear fluid in the abdominal cavity subjectively enlarged spleen with darkened sharp borders and areas of hemorrhage pale kidneys with a few renal cysts a mass effect in the left ovary and multiple firm cauliflower-like masses of varying sizes within the abdomen along the walls within the mesentery and also along the thoracic walls and throughout the pulmonary parenchyma. A similar mass was present at the heart base and thick white striations were noted on the wall of the pericardium and the pericardium was thickened.

PARATHYROID TUMORS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male jaguar had a history of chronic hypercalcemia and was diagnosed with a parathyroid adenocarcinoma which had been removed four weeks prior to euthanasia. The cat subsequently developed severe azotemia that did not resolve and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition muscle wasting over the hips and thighs pale tan renal parenchyma thick renal capsule miliary white inclusions in the parenchyma of the kidneys subjectively enlarged adrenal glands cavitated right adrenal medullary region distended gallbladder and tortuous distended bile duct and thickened biliary papilla in the duodenal mucosa.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA WITH METAPLASIA TO LUNG EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old female prairie dog had a history of chronic weight loss and thin body condition requiring assisted feeding. Two masses were identified in the abdominal cavity. The animal also had Giardia and a fecal exam. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a thickened and irregular liver and a 3 x 3 x 2 mm. cystic mass on the caudal left lobe that was yellow. Several masses up to 2 mm. in greatest dimension were in the right caudal lung lobes and another mass was in the mediastinum. A 2 mm. mass was at the root of the mesentery and a 4 mm. mass was in the left kidney. Minimal abdominal fat was noted.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOMETRIOSIS UTERINE LEIOMYOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 57-year-old chimpanzee had a history of declining quality of life. Radiographs revealed osteophyte formation and other musculoskeletal changes. The animal was nonambulatory following anesthetic recovery and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy excess thoracic fat depots were noted. Severe arthritis was noted in the stifles.

SEPTICEMIA MYOCARDITIS AND DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE MESANGIOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY PULMONARY CARCINOMA. This 9-year-old female cotton headed tamarin died shortly after emergency therapy. It had been reported the day before to have been not acting right may be in labor shivering depressed and lethargic. Blood was drawn for CBC and chemistry panel. The tamarin was treated symptomatically. It had lordosis from a previous fracture. At necropsy there was increased pericardial fluid. There was no ingesta present within the stomach or small intestine. The liver was pale brown. Mesenteric lymph nodes were edematous. Samples of brain liver and kidney have been frozen for future use if needed.

MACRORHABDIOSIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS HEPATIC MICROGRANULOMAS URATE STASIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 10-year-old male budgerigar was in poor condition with weight loss and regurgitation despite treatment and supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Radiographs were suggestive of a coelomic mass. Necropsy revealed atrophied pectoral muscles thickened coelomic membranes intestines pushed laterally by the ventriculus with moderately enlarged proventriculus several small gray nodules scattered over the proximal surface of the left lung seed material in the crop and ventriculus and absence of ingesta or fecal material in the intestine.

RENAL NEMATODIASIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 1.5-year-old male tanager was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy overly abundant internal fat stores were present in the coelomic cavity and thoracic inlet. The GI tract was devoid of ingesta. The right liver lobe was swollen and pale.
PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 3-year-old male ibis was found dead. At necropsy hemorrhage was present in the pectoral muscles within the trachea and beneath the calvarium.

RENAL GOUT CHRONIC NEPHRITIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION. This 11-year-old male viper was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a large area of hemorrhage was noted beneath the skin. Caseous and necrotic masses were present associated with the kidney. Mineralization was noted in the aorta.

EUTHANASIA SUPPURATIVE NEPHRITIS PERITONITIS ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA OVOTESTIS. This 27-year-old female tree kangaroo had a history of declining quality of life and it was humanely euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy areas of joint erosion and arthritis were noted in multiple joints. The GI tract contained firm trichobezoars and mineralized material. The kidneys contained multiple raised yellow firm plaques extending into the parenchyma.

CRYPT ABSCESSES MULTIPLE TISSUE EUTHANASIA. This 5-month-old Rocky Mountain bighorn sheep had a history of lethargy and had been hospitalized for a week receiving supportive care. The animal had become very lethargic and could not stand and had been soaked in urine. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple areas of hemorrhage within the adductor muscle of the right rear leg pitting edema in the right hock multiple pale areas in the liver and pale nodular lesions in the spleen resembling abscesses. Abscesses were also noted in the wall of the cecum. The lungs were edematous and a small amount of straw-colored fluid was present in the thoracic cavity that included a fibrin clot. Mesenteric lymph node was enlarged and had nodular pale lesions.

ALVEOLAR PROTEINOSIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 8-year-old female sugar glider was found on the bottom of the cage in the morning and died shortly thereafter. It has a history of mass/pouch removal several years earlier. Necropsy revealed a small amount of blood in the nares yellow/white nodules encompassing most of the pulmonary parenchyma a 1 cm. nodule in the right lateral hepatic lobe and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA. This female 2-month-old tamarin had been apparently healthy. Its sibling was found dead one day before. Necropsy revealed a wet perineum thin walled bowel with gaseous distention and sections of hemorrhagic enteritis in the small intestine.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE VACUOLAR DEGENERATION INANITION. This 9-year-old meerkat was found dead. The animal had been under treatment for seizures. At necropsy a large quantity of soil and debris was present in the oral cavity. The liver contained numerous pinpoint white foci. The central areas of both lungs were dark and wet.

POX CANDIDA DISPHARYNX COCCIDIA AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old male bobwhite quail developed oral plaques and a proliferative lesion on the right foot and a lesion under the right eye and also had a history of weight loss. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A wet mount of crop contents identified yeasts. This animal had previously had toe necrosis requiring amputation. Necropsy revealed nasal discharge with white plaque covering the choana pale brown right side of the heart several white plaques within the oral cavity around the glottis and esophagus and the crop mucosa was thickened. Two 4 mm. pale foci were on the ventral surface of the liver. The adrenals were enlarged. Both eyes had some discharge.

VISCERAL GOUT HETEROPHILIC MESANGIOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY. This approximately 6-year-old male green tree monitor was found dead on exhibit. Gross necropsy revealed fine crystalline debris throughout the coelom ascites and a tan liver.

INTESTINAL INFARCTION PULMONARY EDEMA AND CONGESTION RENAL CALCULI. This 4.5-year-old female wallaby was found dead in early morning. It was originally worked up for a preshipment exam on 5/27. An 8 cm. diameter round mineralized mass was found by palpation and radiographs. A percutaneous biopsy of the mass submitted for culture was positive for acid fast organisms. Exploratory surgery was performed on 6/4 and the mass was discovered to be an abscessed mesenteric lymph node containing many large blood vessels. The mass was removed and submitted to Northwest ZooPath for histopathology and NVSL for mycobacterial culture. The wallaby recovered from surgery but slept most of the following day and did not eat. She died overnight. At necropsy the wallaby was in good body condition. Surgical incision of the abdominal wall was intact. The lungs were diffusely congested. The heart appeared grossly normal with no evidence of endocardiosis. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were enlarged. Both kidneys had concretions at the renal pelvises. A portion of the small bowel was transmurally black. Adipose tissue around the surgical site appeared necrotic. The bladder mucosa was bruised at the site from the apex to the base. Cultures of lung liver lymph nodes kidney and adrenal gland were submitted to NVSL. Renal calculi were submitted for analysis and the stone was analyzed as 100% calcium carbonate.

BILE DUCT ADENOCARCINOMA THYROID FOLLICULAR ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 34.5-year-old male ring-tailed lemur developed a seizure a few months earlier and never seemed to completely recover. The animal had a one week history of collapse and an associated laceration of the finger. The finger was repaired and blood work at the time revealed hyperbilirubinemia. A mass was palpable in the cranial abdomen. The animal slowly declined thereafter and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mature cataracts fusion of the lumbar spine small kidneys with normal appearing parenchyma multiple punctate white foci throughout the liver a firm white mass adhered to the stomach proximal duodenum and liver in the region of the pancreas. On cut surface the mass had a necrotic center and 30 ml. of yellow-tinged fluid was in the abdomen. The stomach was empty and scant feces were in the intestine. The gallbladder and bile duct were enlarged and three small dark stones were at the terminus of the bile duct. White firm foci were scattered throughout both lungs. Pericardial fluid was normal in amount and a 23 mm. mass was in the area of the right thyroid gland.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS DERMATOPHYTOSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 7-year-old male/castrated ferret had a history of chronic adrenal disease and a deslorelin implant placed two months earlier. An insulinoma was managed clinically. The ferret had chronic atelectasis of the cranial segment of the left cranial pulmonary lobe and chronic progressive dermatitis or pyoderma of the face and tail. A resected sebaceous epithelioma of the second digit was also performed in January 2012. The ferret had morbid obesity weakness and may have been immunosuppressed. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

LEUKOENCEPHALOMYELOPATHY (WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME). This 4-year-old male hedgehog was found moribund and died before examination. Necropsy revealed ulcerated areas of the stomach and no other gross lesions.

ACUTE AND CHRONIC ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 11-year-old female Speke’s gazelle had a seven-day history of illness and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed consolidated cranial pulmonary lobes with multiple 15 mm. in diameter cavitated and thick walled abscesses. Remaining pulmonary parenchyma was congested. The cranial pole of the left kidney was cystic. The papillary areas of both kidneys were pale and had prominent white streaks. The uterus was flaccid and contained mucoid fluid. A 45 mm. long male fetus was in the right horn.

EUTHANASIA FROSTBITE. This male 2-year-old teal was humanely euthanized. It had a history of severe frostbite one week prior to death. Both feet were affected. It had lost 14% of its body weight over the past eight months. Blood work demonstrated anemia and mild leukocytosis. Treatment was begun. The teal continued to worsen. At necropsy the teal was thin. It had a prominent keel. Two-thirds of both feet were affected by frostbite. The heart had significant bulging of the right ventricle and atrium. The right ventricular wall was thin. The liver was slightly pale.

SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 1-year-old female lorikeet was found dead in its cage with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition and plumage and no external signs of trauma. The lungs were diffusely dark red and firm and sank in formalin. Female gonad was identified.

MULTI ORGAN DYSFUNCTION SYNDROME AND POSSIBLE TRANSFUSION REACTION INJURY. This 8-year-old male ring-tailed lemur was immobilized approximately one month prior to death with multiple lacerations due to aggression in the group. After immobilization he became lethargic approximately one week later and was minimally responsive to Clavamox with a temperature of 104.5°. The animal became anemic at 26-28%. He was administered multiple medications including fluids metronidazole ceftazidime and famotidine intravenously. His face became swollen within a day and he was given steroids and Benadryl for presumed hypersensitivity reaction. Facial swelling improved and antibiotics were stopped. His hematocrit was still low and a blood transfusion was performed. He was restarted on metronidazole as he had frank blood in the stool. He continued to be lethargic and died spontaneously. At necropsy there was a small amount of clear pleural effusion and the lungs seemed wet.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 4-year-old male whistling duck had been hospitalized for emaciation and responded partially to antibiotic therapy but then died. Necropsy revealed cachexia thin-walled myocardium multiple white foci throughout the liver mottled white/pink spleen and thickened yellow air sacs. DNA probes identified Mycobacterium avium in the liver.

CIRRHOSIS CARDIOMYOPATHY HEMOCHROMATOSIS. This 6-year/1-month-old female fruit bat was found dead. It was brought to the hospital for lethargy and abnormal behavior. It appeared to be improving. At necropsy the abdominal cavity contained about 5 ml. of clear straw colored fluid. The fluid was negative for bacterial growth on aerobic culture. The ammonia level in the fluid was greater than 1000 µmol/l. The liver was slightly enlarged and covered with nodules of varying size from 2-10 mm. On cut surface the nodules consisted of pale soft tissue that had displaced the normal parenchyma. There was some congestion of both cranial lung lobes. There was ingesta present in the gastrointestinal tract but the stomach was empty.
HEPATITIS. This 9-year-old male lory was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the internal organs appeared pale.
PORTAL HEPATITIS SPLENITIS. This female 12-year/8-month-old whistling duck died. At necropsy there was severe splenic hypertrophy.

POLYP VAGINA. This greater than 3-year-old female opossum presented with vaginal hemorrhage obesity and rear limb ataxia and was euthanized. A dark red pedunculated mass approximately 2 cm. in diameter was on the mucosal surface of the left vagina. Multiple cystic structures were present on the mucosal surface of the right uterus.

CHRONICNEPHRITIS BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS CHRONIC HEPATITIS MYELIN DEGENERATION. This 4-year-old female hedgehog had a history of vaginal hemorrhage. Acute neurologic signs were also noted. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy the left kidney was enlarged and irregular. Serosanguineous fluid and clotted blood were noted in the medulla along with small ureteroliths. The bladder contained hemorrhagic fluid.

EUTHANASIA ATYPICAL PULMONARY AND HEPATIC HISTIOCYTIC INFILTRATE RUMINORETICULITIS. This greater than 14-year-old male sheep had arthritis and was geriatric. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large hard nodule between the lungs containing white chalky material. No other abnormalities were noted.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old male chameleon had a history of anorexia and lethargy. Treatment was initiated; however no improvement was noted and the animal was found dead. At necropsy the liver was large and firm. Kidneys were mottled red and gray. Lungs appeared hemorrhagic and contained small abscesses.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS EMACIATION MALASSEZIA DERMATOPATHY. This 18-year-old male parrot was being monitored for a ruptured cervical air sac that occurred five days prior to death. On the morning of death the animal appeared off and lethargic and was isolated for supportive care. The animal was found dead two hours later. This bird had a history of chronic severe feather picking and was featherless except for the flight feathers. The animal also had bilateral carpal abrasions and scabs on the shoulders and arthritis in the carpal joints. The bird had tested negative for circovirus polyoma Pacheco’s disease and Chlamydophila. Necropsy revealed fair to thin body condition chronic nonhealing wounds over the wing joints and keel subcutaneous emphysema in the right thoracic and inguinal area dark red to purple pectoral muscles slightly opaque air sacs thyroid asymmetry with the left larger than the right empty crop but ingesta throughout the gastrointestinal tract slightly enlarged kidneys fecal material in the cloaca and no other gross findings.

SEPSIS. This 8-year-old female ring-tailed lemur developed an acute onset of lethargy and inappetence after presenting earlier in the week with diarrhea. The animal died and necropsy revealed congested lungs hemorrhagic foci in the skeletal muscle particularly around the periocular facial and cervical regions white/tan foci on the liver and spleen hyperemic intestinal loops and multiple infarcts in the kidneys.

AMYLOIDOSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY PERITONITIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 10-year-old female marmoset was found dead on exhibit. It had no weight loss since its TB test in November 2003. At necropsy there were fibrinopurulent strands on the surface of the liver and within the abdominal cavity. The liver appeared enlarged and friable. The stomach and intestines were devoid of parasites.

EUTHANASIA INANITION ENTERITIS NEPHROSIS BILIARY CYSTADENOMA. This 13-year-old female capybara had a chronic history of loose stool weight loss alopecia and lameness. The animal had been under treatment for metronidazole for flagellate overgrowth. The animal was humanely euthanized due to progression of clinical signs. At necropsy the capybara was thin with marked alopecia. A small pedunculated mass was present in the left axilla. The heart was pale with foci of fibrosis. The thyroid glands were enlarged and filled with thick mucoid material. Multiple areas of the lower GI tract had thickening of the mucosa. Ulceration and fibrin were present on much of the lower GI tract. The gall bladder was distended and contained many small fluid filled cystic structures. The adrenal glands were large and pale. The elbows and stifle showed roughening of the articular surfaces.

THYMOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12.5-year-old female sheep had a two week history of weight loss and a two day history of bloat for which it received treatment. The animal was depressed dehydrated and a large mass was present in the ventral neck region. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a mass in the thoracic inlet to 30 cm. in greatest dimension that was somewhat squash shaped with a wide base and narrower dorsal portion. Serosanguineous fluid was in the nares. All four hooves were moderately overgrown. Approximately 300 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was in the pleural space. The lungs were congested and had much foam. The trachea also contained foam. A 3 cm. pale lesion was on the caudal right and left pulmonary lobes resembling scar tissue. Adhesions to the thoracic wall were also noted in the cranial right pulmonary lobe. The right heart appeared mildly enlarged with a slight bulge in the right ventricle. A 9 cm. nodular firm mass was in the thorax at the level of the thoracic inlet communicating with the mass at the external aspect of the thoracic inlet. The thoracic mass on cut surface had a fluid filled cavity containing serosanguineous fluid. The mass was centrally necrotic. Multiple small dark brown/purple firm nodules were within the mass.

BACTERIAL SINUSITIS SEPSIS EMACIATION. This 1.5-year-old female chameleon arrived into the collection for a nutritional study and was a control animal. She deposited three clutches of eggs during the study. She had been treated with calcium supplements and fluids for a presumed calcium imbalance after an episode of presumed hypocalcemia. The animal died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed thin body condition darkened skin and a slightly raised nodular focus of white discoloration in the nares associated with erosion of the sinus and a luminal yellow exudate. The gall bladder was filled with reddish heavy sediment. The kidneys were pale yellow but not gritty.

SPINAL OSTEOMYELITIS AND SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old male Utah milksnake had a history of spinal disease and was euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed vertebral stiffness and skin lesions.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 14-year/6-month-old female gazelle was humanely euthanized. It had prior bouts of respiratory disease that appeared to respond to antibiotic treatment. Blood work one day prior to death revealed hypoalbuminemia hyperproteinemia hypoglycemia hypocholesterolemia elevated BUN elevated creatinine and hyperglobulinemia. The gazelle was unresponsive to treatment. At necropsy there was an abrasion on the left lateral hind leg at the level of the fetlock joint. There was an erythematous area at the level of the left medial fetlock on the left hind leg. There was a 13 x 7 cm. hairless area on the right side of the middle third of the neck at the level of the jugular vein. There was red tinged fluid (1 ml.) on the ventral aspect of the vulva. The vulvar lumen appeared to be increased in diameter about 1-2 mm. The caudal ventral portion of the lung was noted to be firm and consolidated with multifocal purple/brown areas. There was a 7 x 3 cm. area of fibrin adhered to the ventral lateral right cranial lung lobe. This area of fibrin was adhered to the parietal pleura of the ventral aspect of the chest cavity. The ventral aspect of the caudal lung lobe was fully adhered to the diaphragm. There was an 8 x 6 cm. area of erythema on the right lung that was adhered. The cranial ventral right lung surface contained white purulent material that encompassed approximately 20% of the right lung lobes. The caudal dorsal aspect of the caudal right lung lobe was diffusely emphysematous. Approximately 30% of the ventral aspect of the left cranial lung was focally light purple firm and had fibrin along the ventral margin. There were variably sized firm circular raised nodules on the ventral luminal surface of the trachea.

BILATERAL PEDAL AMPUTATION DUE TO BACTERIAL AND FUNGAL DERMATITIS POSTSURGICAL EUTHANASIA. This approximately 4-year-old alligator lizard presented for swollen front feet with sloughing of the digits suspected to be due to vascular compromise and necrosis secondary to dysecdysis. The distal forelimbs were amputated. Although the tissue appeared healthy the amputation sites dehisced and the animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed the amputation sites along the antebrachia were not well opposed but tissue appeared viable erythema on the plantar aspect of the left rear foot abraded scales and erythema on the ventral aspect of the tail a blood clot in the esophagus that have occurred during pithing and a yellow liver.

EUTHANASIA INANITION ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old female otter was humanely euthanized. It had a history of inflammatory bowel disease over the last two years. It was unresponsive to various treatments. She was starting to have trouble getting around her exhibit on several occasions almost could not get out of the pool. She was immobilized for physical exam and radiographs and on examination the body was found to be completely devoid of fat with very little muscle tissue. Her mucous membranes were tacky and pale. At necropsy there were no fat stores. There was little muscle mass. There was no ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract despite having been fed that morning. The kidneys were slightly small.

FRACTURED PELVIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female sheep had a history of ataxia and radiographs revealed severe bilateral pelvic fracture cranial to the acetabulums. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed congested lungs hemorrhage in the retroperitoneal space especially on the left side and in the caudal/ventral abdomen.

COLONIC LEIOMYOSARCOMA HEPATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA RENAL GOUT. This 18-year-old male snake was treated for obstipation two days prior to death. The animal was found dead. At necropsy an oblong mass was present adjacent to the caudal intestine and fecal accumulation in the GI tract anterior to the mass. Gouty tophi were noted in the kidneys.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED. This 6-year-old male red kangaroo was found dead in the barn in sternal recumbency with splayed legs and black tarry stool. The animal had normal appetite and behavior the previous day. Necropsy revealed advanced autolysis. The abdomen contained approximately 500 ml. of free fluid. Macerated plant material was in the stomach.

CHRONIC COLITIS WITH SEPSIS EMACIATION GLOMERULOPATHY NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 10-year-old female cottontop tamarin presented with dehydration emaciation depression weakness and hypothermia. Supportive care was administered and the animal appeared to respond. It developed a seizure of one minute duration two days into treatment. Diarrhea was in the cage and Campylobacter was isolated from feces. The animal continued to do poorly and died. Necropsy revealed food in the stomach and portions of the small intestines and formed stool in the colon.

IRON STORAGE ANEMIA CHRONIC COELOMITIS. This 19-year-old male roseate spoonbill was found dead on the ground with no other history. Necropsy revealed thin body condition pale heart and lungs and a small soft egg-like material inside the ventriculus.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA VASCULITIS (GALL BLADDER) NEPHROSIS. This 5-year/9-month-old female kudu died despite resuscitation attempts. On 5/28 the kudu was started with carfentanyln xylezine for MGA implant replacement. She regurgitated on the trip to the veterinary hospital from the plane stall where she was immobilized. Throughout the procedure she maintained low oxygen saturation readings. She recovered normally and appeared normal the next day. About 1/2 hour after darting for treatment of possible aspiration complications she presented with increased respiration and dyspnea as well as hyperesthesia slight opisthotonos and a knuckled over front leg fetlock. Chemistry panel results revealed severe hypomagnesaemia. Treatment was initiated but with no improvement. At necropsy there were petechiae on the spleen duodenum gall bladder and endocardium. The gall bladder had a dark serosal surface. The kidney had a range of contours to the surface of it. There were large areas of ischemia noted throughout the kidney. There was a low corticomedullary surface area noted. The aortic valve had bony mineralization at the base of the valve. There was subcutaneous emphysema noted. The lungs had distinct segmentation of heavy red areas bordering normal pink parenchyma in cranioventral portions. Remaining lung parenchyma was heavy and congested. A small amount of frothy yellow/green foam was noted in the trachea and primary bronchi and culture was taken.

ASPERGILLOSIS ENDOCRINE TUMOR (UNDETERMINED LOCATION) INGLUVITIS WITH INCLUSIONS. This 41-year-old male hyacinth macaw was notably normal in the morning and found dead two hours later unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed edema and serous atrophy in the caudal neck and ventral regions a large cavitated mass at the left cranial kidney extending to involve the ventriculus proventriculus and caudal left lung with associated severe adhesions.

EUTHANASIA CARCINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PULMONARY MINERALIZATION. This 10-year-old female armadillo had a mass removed approximately one week prior to death. The animal was euthanized. At gross necropsy the lungs had numerous small nodules.

NEPHROLITHIASIS UROLITHIASIS RUPTURED URETER EUTHANASIA. This 5.5-year-old male sheep went through quarantine in August 2012 was apparently healthy but then developed urethral calculi and obstruction one month later. Calculi were removed surgically but the urethra remained blocked after surgery. Attempts to dissolve the calculi were unsuccessful and perineal urethrostomy could not be performed due to inability to locate the urethra. The urethra distal to the pelvis appeared to be ruptured. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a dilated and thickened 6 in. section of the urethra distal to the pelvis and muscle surrounding the urethra was inflamed with a purulent mucoid discharge. Muscle appeared to be in various stages of necrosis. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

METABOLIC BONE DISEASE INTESTINAL BACTERIAL ABSCESS EUTHANASIA. This 1- to 2-year-old female gecko had a six month history of calcium homeostasis problems and was diagnosed while in quarantine with hypocalcemia. It was treated with oral calcium and ultraviolet light and bone density improved. The diet was modified and the animal was placed on exhibit. It had a history of egg laying but was noted to be lethargic with a swollen pelvis and radiographs revealed severe loss of bone density and calcification of the thyroid and parathyroid. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

NEPHRITIS COELOMITIS HEPATOPATHY. This 19-year/7-month-old female frog was found dead. It was in declining condition. At necropsy it was bloated and edematous. The coelomic cavity contained clear fluid with streaks of black. The liver was black and extremely friable. It appeared to be encased in a fibrous sheet of tissue on the left side with adhesions to the heart and sternum.

HEPATOPATHY INTESTINAL LEIOMYOSARCOMA MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION. This greater than 15-year-old male gecko died. It had been under medical treatment for over one month. It had necrotic skin an elevated white blood cell count (70000) and loss of considerable amount of weight. The gecko’s condition was deteriorating despite supportive care. At necropsy the stomach was empty. There was ulcerated skin on the right rear foot. There were several necrotic toes. The tail appeared almost healed.

INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWL DISEASE. This 7-year-old male ferret was previously diagnosed with an insulinoma in March. A splenectomy was also performed at that time. A hepatic biopsy performed at that time was within normal limits. Medical management was unsuccessful and blood glucose remained uncontrolled. The ferret became anemic and increasingly lethargic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple white nodules throughout the liver and a single firm 5 mm. mass. The stomach and duodenum were adhered to the previous surgical site. A 3 mm. cyst was in the left kidney and a 1 mm. cyst was in the right kidney.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE MULTICENTRIC BRONCHIOLOALVEOLAR ADENOMA THYROID ADENOCARCINOMA MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 3-year-old male opossum was humanely euthanized. It had a history of rear limb ataxia that was first noted in January 2002. The ataxia progressed to rear limb paresis over the past eight months. Radiographs showed bilateral coxofemoral joint luxation with progressive degenerative joint disease. Postmortem radiographs showed severe bilateral coxofemoral degenerative joint disease and degeneration of both femoral heads. At necropsy the opossum was obese. There were multifocal firm yellow 1-5 mm. nodules throughout all lung lobes. There were several 2-3 mm. clear fluid filled cysts within the liver. There were several 7-8 cm. white tapeworms in the jejunum. There was a single 4-5 cm. white nematode in the caudal esophagus. The joint capsules of both coxofemoral joints were thickened. There was severe eburnation of the articular cartilage of both coxofemoral joints. Both femoral heads and acetabula were flattened.

SHOCK STRESS INTESTINAL SEROSAL GRANULOMA NEPHROSIS. This 10-year-old male wolf died shortly after being found with abdominal distention. It had been immobilized for routine examination and had a normal recovery. Approximately one hour later the animal was introduced to a new wolf. This animal became very stressed and at midday the temperature approached 90°. The animal was observed drinking large quantities of water prior to death. At necropsy there was severe gaseous distention of the stomach with some liquid contents but no detectable torsion or volvulus. The serosal surfaces of all viscera were diffusely hyperemic with ecchymoses. The spleen was greatly enlarged and congested.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL CYSTS BILIARY CYSTS. This 8-year-old neutered male ferret was under treatment for hepatopathy. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy numerous cysts were present within the liver.

EUTHANASIA MALIGNANT MELANOMA (LIVER) ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS HEPATITIS. This 16-year-old female penguin had papillary inguinal masses. A cagemate had similar masses which later progressed to malignant melanoma. An exploratory laparotomy was performed and the animal was euthanized intraoperatively due to dissemination of melanotic neoplastic lesions. At necropsy multiple foci of hyperkeratosis and black discoloration were noted in the right inguinal region. The liver contained numerous large masses replacing much of the normal hepatic parenchyma. Lesions were firm and dark.

NONSUPPURATIVE ENCEPHALITIS LUMPY JAW (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This male approximately 2-year-old King Island wallaby died. It had a history of right-sided facial swelling and abscessation since January of 1999. It was surgically explored several times and treated with antibiotics. Cultures of the abscess grew Enterobacter. Significant weight loss was noted since the onset of the problem. At necropsy this wallaby was in poor nutritional condition with prominent spinous processes and pelvic bones being palpable. The face was swollen around the right eye with a purulent discharged adhered to the lower medial canthus and several healing incisions present from surgical explorations and tooth extraction. Subcutaneous tissues in this region are markedly thickened with fibrous connective tissue and contain loops of suture material. Small amounts of more purulent material were present within the conjunctival and retrobulbar spaces. There was an apparent connection from the retrobulbar space to the socket of the extracted upper molar tooth. The tooth socket contained a large clot mixed with food material and pus. The dorsal aspect of the zygomatic arch that forms part of the orbital rim was thickened with adherent fibrous connective tissue. All internal organs are grossly unremarkable.

PORTOSYSTEMIC SHUNT HYPERTENSION PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male tiger was diagnosed with an extrahepatic portosystemic shunt and hepatic encephalopathy in October 2010. Supportive care was administered and a band was surgically placed for gradual attenuation of the aberrant vessel resulting in initial improvement of clinical signs of hepatic encephalopathy although signs returned over the next six months. A second procedure was performed with deployment of an intravascular plug and at this time right-sided cardiac hypertrophy pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary thromboembolism were detected. Supportive care was administered but the tiger developed ascites two weeks after the procedure. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The cat had been administered aspirin and sildenafil. Necropsy revealed multiple firm white nodules associated with blood vessels in the liver. The right atrium and ventricle appeared thin walled. The testes were hypoplastic. The left eye appeared to contain a cataract.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND HEPATIC DISEASE. This greater than 10-year-old male iguana was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed small kidneys and an enlarged and mottled liver.

EUTHANASIA SYSTEMIC SHOCK INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS RENAL CYSTS. This 21-year-old female squirrel monkey was found lethargic with a left head tilt. Clear serous discharge was noted from the left ear. The animal was treated with fluids and antibiotics but was later found in agonal condition and was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy the kidneys were slightly irregular in shape and the uterus was thickened.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE THYROID ADENOMA PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA GASTRIC ULCERS. This 20-year/10-month-old male jaguar was humanely euthanized due to chronic renal failure. It had a history of chronic renal disease fusion of the lumbar vertebrae and joint pain responsive to glucosamine/chondroitin administration. Several months prior to euthanasia there was decreased appetite with increased lethargy and some difficulty maneuvering in the environment. It became totally anorexic one week prior to euthanasia. Four days prior to onset of anorexia the animal was immobilized for evaluation. It was severely dehydrated had weight loss and continuous urine dripping from the penis. Lab results showed elevation in BUN and creatinine. Fluid and supportive care were administered. Episode of vomiting occurred. At necropsy the jaguar was extremely thin and had a poor haircoat. There was decreased muscle mass. There was a circumscribed area of cartilage loss present along the lateral aspect of the left coxofemoral joint. There were two circumscribed firm masses on the right thyroid. The left adrenal was large firm and irregular in shape. Retroperitoneal tissue behind this gland was black and discolored. The liver contained a large cystic structure along the right ventral border (4 x 3 in.). There were several small cysts scattered throughout the liver. The liver was firm on cut surface with sharp edges. The bile duct was distended and tortuous. Both kidneys had thin firm cortices hemorrhagic irregular corticomedullary junctions and thickened renal capsules. There was redundant yellow tissue in the renal pelvis. The bladder mucosa was thickened irregular and had diffuse areas of hemorrhage. The gastric mucosa contained multiple areas of hemorrhage some with areas of ulceration. The lesions extended into the proximal duodenum. The lesions appeared more severe in the body and pyloric region of the stomach. Several of the ulcers appeared deep. There was a black circumscribed lesion present in the musculature of the left ventricular free wall. The lesion oozed dark blood on cut surface. There was prominent lens opacity bilaterally.

INTRASPECIES TRAUMA MYOCARDIAL HEMORRHAGE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 2-year-old male tamarin suffered trauma from cagemates. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy multiple bite wounds were present over the face neck abdomen and left hind limb.

PLEURAL ABSCESS WITH SEPSIS. This 7-year-old female golden lion tamarin ad a one day history of weakness and labored respiration. Examination revealed opaque thoracic cavity with malodorous fluid aspirated from the left side pleural space and fluid also aspirated from the right pleural space. Pyothorax was suspected and the patient died shortly after recovery. The patient had given birth to twins five weeks earlier which are still alive. Necropsy revealed absence of subcutaneous fat and minimal abdominal fat. The mammary gland was lactating. The lungs were collapsed and a small amount of fluid was in the pleural space of the right lung. A mottled and encapsulated large yellow gelatinous mass filled the entire left pleural space with associated mediastinal involvement.

SPINDLE CELL SARCOMA CHEST WALL EUTHANASIA. This 1.5-year-old female roof rat has had a declining quality of life due to a large mass on her side but with no other prior medical history. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 7 cm. mass in the right thoracic wall caudal to the left shoulder and forelimb. On cut surface the mass was yellow to white and appeared to be well encapsulated. No other abnormalities were noted.

HEPATIC MELANOMA SYSTEMIC NONSUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male Humboldt penguin has a history of weight loss and regurgitation with a firm irregular soft tissue mass and elevated hepatic enzymes. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a nonresectable cystic hepatic mass affecting multiple hepatic lobes and associated with severe compression of the stomach and intestines and the bird was subsequently euthanized. Necropsy revealed a hyperkeratotic mass in the inner inguinal area bilaterally two 2 cm. in diameter black masses in the right lung lobe one 1 cm. black mass in the left lung lobe and multiple coalescing black masses throughout the liver. A 4 cm. white mass was in the area of the gall bladder.

BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS AND SALPINGITIS XANTHOMATOSIS GOUT. This 16-year-old female Standing’s day gecko was reported to have completed a heavy shed one day earlier and was found poorly responsive the following morning. Supportive care was administered but the animal died an hour later. Necropsy revealed partially retained shed on the distal phalanges.

MYCOTIC PROVENTRICULITIS. This 3-year-old male finch was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy whitish mottling was present over most of the epicardium. The ventriculus contained 0.5 to 1 cm. in diameter round white to yellow masses.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA STEATITIS. This captive bred 2-year-old male ferret was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. It was diagnosed with multicentric lymphosarcoma. It had done well until it developed posterior paresis and paralysis on 8/23rd. At necropsy the ferret was in good body condition. There were multifocal white 1-3 mm. nonraised lesions on the surface of all lung lobes. All lung lobes were collapsed and discolored in an uneven pattern from dark red to pale pink. The spleen was absent. There was multicentric lymphadenopathy. Adrenal glands were slightly enlarged.

EPIMYOCARDITIS PERITONITIS AND MENINGITIS. This approximately 2-year-old female squirrel monkey developed an acute onset of lethargy and died. Necropsy revealed pyothorax and free fluid in the thoracic cavity with possible purulent material in the pericardial sac.

SEMINOMA SERTOLI CELL TUMOR. This 9.5-year-old male pintail duck had been partially blinded a few years earlier due to an eye injury and had not been able to maintain good condition in the aviary. Recently excessive discharge was noted from the blind eye and the eyelids were crusted closed. It was found dead in the pool one day after being examined. Necropsy revealed a large oval smooth mass filling the coelom and displacing the organs cranially and laterally and appears to replace the right testes. On cut surface the mass had irregular glandular-like nodules compressed together and encapsulated. A few areas of hemorrhage were noted in the mass. The liver was atrophic. The proventriculus was thin and irregular with slightly raised black spots on the surface but no parasites observed grossly. A gnarled bunch of enlarged tubules is on the left side of the cloaca in the pelvis suggesting obstructed or hyperplastic epididymis. The left testis is small and irregular with a small black nodule on the capsular surface.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA WITH SEPTICEMIA LEFT SIDED CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY SPLENIC AND OVARIAN GRANULOMAS PREVIOUS LUNG WORM INFECTION EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female llama had a history of chronic weight loss and coughing which became productive in August 1999. It had been positive for lungworms in January of 1999 and treated accordingly. Due to worsening of clinical signs stumbling and depression the animal was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed numerous abscesses throughout the lungs dark red mucous membranes endocardiosis involving the right and left atrioventricular valves and a firm nodule in the spleen that was adhered to the visceral surface and 1 cm. in greatest dimension. On cut surface the nodule was hollow with a thick friable brown lining. The liver was mildly enlarged petechiae were on the uterine mucosa and right auricular serosa. Hemorrhage was detected in the mucosa of C-3 in the small intestine and the mediastinal lymph node was enlarged and inflamed. Arytenoids were inflamed.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA COLONIC NEMATODIASIS. This 14-year/10-month-old male baboon was found dead. It had a history of occasional anorexia and vomiting for approximately one year. There is a history of positive fecals for whipworms in the group. This baboon was treated with repeated doses of ivermectin last fall and winter. The baboon became anorectic and was found collapsed. He died within 30 minutes prior to receiving any treatments. At necropsy the gastrointestinal tract was empty with the exception of some fecal material within the cecum and colon. No parasites were seen. There was congestion of the mesentery of the large bowel. The colon appeared normal. The pancreas was firm and chalky white colored. A mass was present within the area of the distal end of the pancreas bile duct and small intestine. It was Ping-Pong ball sized. Necrotic areas were present. No bile stones were seen. The heart had some fatty streaks. The liver was swollen.

EUTHANASIA CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS CHOLECYSTITIS PANCREATITIS. This 12-year/2-month-old female kangaroo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of liver disease. It did not respond to treatment and supportive care. Biopsy of the liver revealed severe generalized cirrhosis and severe biliary obstruction. At necropsy there was jaundice. The kangaroo was thin. There was red/brown fluid noted in the peritoneal cavity. The serosal surfaces of the intestines were jaundiced and injected. The splenic edges were rough and ragged. The liver was friable with sharp edges. On cut surface the liver appeared normal. There was a 1 cm. focal firm slightly pale lesion noted on the liver’s surface. The gall bladder was 11-12 cm. in diameter and contained a postsurgical clot and red/brown bile. The common bile duct was dilated and tortuous. As the bile duct entered the duodenum it became extremely thickened. The pancreas was firm nodular and pale. The stomach was gas filled and bloated. There were multiple 5 mm. ulcerative lesions at the pylorus and a 6 cm. focal circular reddened area at the pylorus.

ANAL SAC ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male black-footed ferret had a history of chronic cataract in the left eye. Multiple tooth root abscesses digital amputation in 2009 root canals of the left canines and a ruptured right anal sac gland associated with a round cell tumor. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition inspissated secretions and swelling with fistula formation involving the anal sac region multiple cystic lesions in the liver splenomegaly and white streaking through the medulla of the kidney.

ROUND CELL MALIGNANCY HISTIOCYTIC OR MYELOID EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female corn snake was noted to have a small wound on the ventrum and by the next day the area was swollen. Biopsy results identified a round cell tumor and over the next four weeks the mass tripled in size to involve more of the coelom and the snake became inappetent. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed absence of ingesta in the alimentary tract female reproductive tract with inactive follicles and two masses adhered to the body wall.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HEMANGIOSARCOMA STRESS. This 22-year/9-month-old male leopard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of grand mal seizure while on exhibit and had a history of hemangioma on the left hock increased BUN increased creatinine cardiac murmur and cataract. At necropsy the liver was firmer than normal and had multiple serous fluid filled cysts of varying diameter throughout the parenchyma. The articular cartilage was completely eroded away on the distal radius and opposing carpal bones. The distal medial tibia had a serosanguineous fluid filled cyst beneath the skin.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK INANITION HEPATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA HEPATITIS. This 14-year-old male duck was found dead. The animal has a history of a recent infection of the uropygial gland but had otherwise been healthy. At necropsy a dark red to brown nodular mass was present in the liver.

Liver: Severe acute massive hepatopathy and focal necrosis. Lung: Mild pulmonary fibrosis Massive hepatopathy (please see comments) Comments: Pulmonary findings are not significant in the cause of death and are likely related to aging. Aeromonas veronii biovar sobria is a ubiquitous pathogen found in aquatic environments and is implicated in cases of diarrhea in humans and diseases of fish. The pathogenesis; pathogenic mechanism; and virulence factors responsible for infection in different species are not well understood; and the significance of the bacteria in this case without microscopic pathology is questionable. Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) cause hepatotoxicity by disorganization of hepatocytes leading to necrosis; apoptosis; and perisinusoidal hemorrhage; frequently; individual or small groups of hepatocytes are affected; rather than zonal necrosis. The hepatopathy as demonstrated in this case likely preceeded massive hepatic necrosis. Cyanobacteria toxicosis is a primarily differential; however; definitive diagnosis is pending additional diagnostic testing to be completed at another diagnostic laboratory. Additional results will be addressed in a future addendum. Kristy A. Mietelka; DVM Negative for cyanide toxicity Comments:The toxicologic assay for cyanide did not detect this chemical in submitted liver samples. Stomach contents and liver have been sent to the California Animal Health and Food Safety Laboratory System for Anatoxin-A and Microcystins (for microscopic algae detection; i.e. Blue Green Algae). Additional results will be sent to you directly from CAHFS. Kristy A. Mietelka; DVM Negative for cyanobacteria toxins Comments: While the toxicology analysis performed at California Animal Health and Food Safety Laboratory System did not detect microcystins or anatoxin-a in the submitted sample of stomach contents; the hepatopathy as demonstrated in this case is consistent with cyanobacteria toxicosis. Degradation of the toxins or very low content of toxins within the sample may lead to no detection. Death due to anatoxin-a fast-death factor found in some blooms is also a consideration in this case; however; these deaths usually follow collapse; prostration; and hyperesthesia; and are typically devoid of any specific lesions. This concludes diagnostic testing for this case. Kristy A. Mietelka; D

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEPATITIS URATE STASIS. This 2-year-old male lory was found down and being traumatized by other birds. The animal died despite treatment. At necropsy the serosa of the proximal duodenum was hemorrhagic.
SUPPURATIVE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA WITH SEPSIS. This 13-year-old male fruit bat arrived in quarantine June 20 2008 and was found dead on August 4 2008. Necropsy revealed no obvious abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIA NAD NEMATODAL GRANULOMAS. This greater than 7-year-old male lizard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of not doing well and had lost weight and was extremely thin. It was not eating as much as it had been despite hand feeding efforts. At necropsy the entire coelomic cavity was riddled with 2-3 mm. round yellow lesions identical to those seen with mycobacteriosis. The largest numbers of lesions were seen in the area of the lungs and large intestine. There were more lesions on the serosal surface of the gastrointestinal tract than the mucosal surface. Some of the lesions were mucosal in origin. All organs were affected. Sections of lung were submitted for culture.

ASPERGILLOSIS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 15-year-old bald eagle presented for dyspnea and was subsequently isolated from a collection of four other nonreleasable eagles. Culture revealed bacteria and treatment was initiated but the bird died three days later. Necropsy revealed a purulent granuloma in the right distal lung lobe enlarged heart mottled lungs and kidney and a nodular growth next to the left testis.
adult.  Euth. Chr.arthritis. Gen.cong'n. Chr.gastritis. Local atherosclerosis. Chr.dermatitis; distal limbs. Hep.cyst. Salivary gland nodule.

PYLORIC ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA. This 15.5-year-old peafowl had been losing weight and not doing well for one month. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a freely moveable subcutaneous mass below the left caudal portion of the keel generalized swelling of the left foot opaque air sacs enlarged ventriculus at its distal end and a perforation in the body wall. The liver was pale and multiple cystic lesions were present. The pericardial sac was thickened.
ENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA PNEUMONIA. This approximately 14-year-old male tree boa had a history of chronic anorexia and lethargy and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

TESTICULAR AND THYMIC NEOPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male boa had a history of a large swelling in the caudal third of the coelom associated with hemorrhage in the skin and underlying subcutis overlying the lesion. A moderate amount of free-floating orange/brown-colored fluid was present in the coelom. A 16 cm. pedunculated mass was exteriorized and appeared to be directly adhered to a large vessel possibly the vena cava in an area adjacent to the adrenal gland. Urate-like material was found along the serosal surface of the mass. Attempts to resect the mass were unsuccessful and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal also had some hemorrhaging in the oral cavity associated with intubation. Necropsy revealed a 2.5 cm. globoid heterogeneous mass at the level of the thyroid gland abundant adipose stores empty stomach ingesta throughout the intestine a 16 cm. cystic heterogeneous pedunculated mass from an undetermined location normal kidneys and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA COLONIC ADENOCARCINOMA. This 9-year-old corn snake had a history of scant fecal production. The animal recently presented with cloacal swelling which was treated topically; however the cloacal mass continued to enlarge. Exploratory surgery revealed that the mass replaced much of the cloaca and could not be resected. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy necrosis of the skin was present adjacent to the mass. Fecal material was present throughout the colon. The colon was partially obstructed by a firm friable pink mass.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA. This approximately 8-year-old male budgerigar had recently been noted in thin body condition and subsequently was found dead. Necropsy revealed a dark red/brown irregular firm mass in the caudal coelomic cavity emanating from the kidney.

HISTIOCYTIC ENCEPHALITIS MYELITIS HEPATITIS. This 6-year-old axolotl had a recent history of traumatic digit amputation; however these wounds were healing.
