The animal began spinning and swimming in a tight circle in the tank. The animal was treated with antibiotics and a saltwater soak but was later found dead. No significant gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR OSTEOMA OSTEOMYELITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC PLEURITIS. This 11-year-old female kudu has a one year history of mandibular swelling. The animal was humanely euthanized due to progression of the mass lesion. At necropsy a 4-5 in. in diameter bony mass was present near the ramus of the right mandible. The mass contained purulent discharge and necrotic tissue. The lungs contained two well circumscribed nodules in the right lung.

AMYLOIDOSIS COLLOID GOITER PANCREATITIS. This 5-year-old female black-footed ferret had a 7-10 day history of illness and responded in a suboptimal fashion to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

ENCEPHALITIS LYMPHOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female koala had a one-month history of abnormal behavior and was found on the floor in lateral recumbency and comatose hypothermic and hypoglycemic. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to decline and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 3-5 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the pericardial sac a focus of pale discoloration in the pulmonary lobe mildly thickened left and right ventricles and a bite wound behind the ear.

BILATERAL RHINITIS MICROGRANULOMATOSIS CLOACAL PROLAPSE. This 3-year-old male gecko has a history of retained shed on the hind limb recurrent cloacal prolapse and deterioration following reduction of the cloacal prolapse. The animal appeared to recover fully from anesthesia but then rapidly deteriorated and died. Necropsy revealed blood-tinged fluid around the lungs and trachea adequate placement and retention of colonic stay sutures associated with the prolapse reduction yellow mottled liver and some scarring in the skull attributed to previous osteomyelitis.

PULMONARY EDEMA CONGESTION; SUSPECT SHOCK; SUSPECT BLOAT. This neutered male 4-year/6-month-old goat was found dead in the barn. The keepers noted that this goat did not eat its grain earlier in the day and that it was a little lethargic in the afternoon. At necropsy the goat was bloated and had rumen fluid coming out of its mouth and nose. The goat was quite fat. The sclera were injected OU. There was abundant ingesta within the rumen. Several areas of ruminal mucosa were sloughing. The duodenal mucosa was hyperemic and the contents were blood tinged. There was soft stool in the spiral colon and no stool in distal colon. The serosa of the urinary bladder had petechial hemorrhages but the mucosa appeared normal. The lungs were pink and had a small amount of fluid on cut surface. There were three white streaks on the right ventricular epicardium.

ULCERATIVE AND HETEROPHILIC TRACHEITIS DUE TO POSSIBLE TRACHEAL CONGENITAL ABNORMALITY. This approximately 25-year-old male flamingo was part of a small group hospitalized during a roundup for treatment of bumblefoot. The bird was exhibiting gurgling noises when caught and during hospitalization. Radiographs revealed a long cervical trachea that formed a loop over the sternum before entering the thorax. Gross necropsy revealed muscle atrophy minimal body fat stores pododermatitis redundant length of the cervical trachea with mucoid exudates and mucosal reddening in the segment of the trachea and mild urate retention in the kidneys.

CERVICAL VERTEBRAL JOINT DISEASE WITH CORD COMPRESSION EUTHANASIA CNS SIGNS. This 4-year-old male quail had an inability to stand after flapping around and being on its back. It had been eating and defecating normally and did not respond to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed pulmonary congestion white milky material in the coelomic cavity food in the crop ingesta in the proventriculus and ventriculus and normal digesta in the intestine. The left hepatic lobe was enlarged and had multiple mottled foci that involved the capsule and the superficial parenchyma.

RUPTURED ATRIUM HEMOPERICARDIUM. This 30-year-old female bald eagle was found weak and on the ground in the afternoon. Physical examination revealed thin body condition and dehydration. A loud parasystolic murmur was identified. Radiographs revealed an enlarged heart and elevated white blood cell count. The bird died a few minutes after subcutaneous fluids were administered. Necropsy revealed thin body condition hemopericardium originating from the base of the right atrium and no other abnormalities.

FIBROSARCOMA RENAL GOUT DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS. This 28-year-old male rattlesnake was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a 1.5 x 1 cm. oval mass was present beneath the skin near an area of prior cyst removal. A cystic mass was present anterior to the heart. The liver contained numerous small nodules. Kidneys had gross lesions consistent with renal gout.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This greater than 8-year-old female red lory was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition bilaterally congested lungs thickened and mildly opaque air sacs tan spleen friable liver and congested intestine.

DEGENERATIVE INTERVERTEBRAL DISC DISEASE PITUITARY ADENOMA THYROID HYPERPLASIA STRESS RESPONSE MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULOPATHY SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA COLONIC NEMATODIASIS. This 3-year-old male domestic rat had chronic weight loss and declining hind limb function. The animal was euthanized for quality of life concerns. At necropsy the spleen was firm and the pituitary gland was enlarged and dark purple.

ISLET ADENOMA ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL) NEUROECTODERMAL TUMORS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old female tiger had a few year history of azotemia and intermittent hematuria some muscle atrophy and unkempt haircoat. The cat also had occasional wheezing. The cat developed a few week history of precipitous decline with weakness in the rear limbs polydipsia and plantigrade walk. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed matted haircoat a reddened nodule in the skin along the margin of the right ear tip a small reddened nodule in the mucosa of the right lower lip tartar on the canines overgrown claws on the rear feet muscle atrophy but abundant fat stores a mild yellow tinge to most tissues mild arthritis in moist joints spondylosis on some of the vertebrae in the thoracic and lumbar regions some adhesions in the abdomen a few small foci of hemorrhage in the liver mottled nodular adrenal cortices some tan or white foci in the pancreas and a small red nodule in the parenchyma near the pole of the splenic lobe cloudy fatty urine four small irregular stones in one fold of the urinary bladder red/white streaking of both kidneys with bloody defects in the renal crests numerous scars in the cortices of the kidneys prominent glomeruli on cut surface of the kidney a few uroliths in one kidney enlarged thyroids with variably-sized cysts some red streaking and possible fibrosis in the myocardium verrucous changes in the left atrioventricular and aortic valves some cartilaginous hardening in the bronchi and bronchioles and some areas of atelectasis in the lobes and moderate numbers of semifirm raised white subpleural foci.

OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA CUTANEOUS MELANOMA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 13-year-old female mountain boa had been evaluated three years earlier for stomatitis and increased respiratory noise which resolved with antibiotic therapy. Gelatinous material cytologically suggestive of inflammation from the intestinal or reproductive tract was found in the exhibit in March 2011 and evaluation confirmed a solid homogeneous mass in the mid coelomic cavity dehydration underweight body condition shed stage and blood work suggestive of sepsis and dehydration or renal disease. Cytology of the mass revealed inflammation fibroplasia and possibly well-differentiated carcinoma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and a 9 cm. mass was present caudal to the gallbladder and terminus of the air sac. The caudal aspect of the mass terminated in the uterus which appeared to be enlarged flaccid and erythemic at this junction. The lumen appeared patent and contained gelatinous material resembling that which was found in the exhibit. Ovary was not identified. On cut surface the mass had a heterogeneous appearance with areas of dark brown/yellow chalky material and tan or pale gray tissue and areas of reddening. The gallbladder was intimately attached to the mass at the caudal aspect and the liver contained multiple gray/tan focal masses scattered throughout the parenchyma some with a cystic quality. The alimentary tract was empty with the exception of a normal fecal mass.

MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION. This greater than 5-year-old female bat died before euthanasia could be performed. The bat presented for generalized weakness and increased respiratory rate. Radiographs revealed a large globoid heart. Frothy white discharge was noted from the nares. The bat initially responded to oxygen and thermal support but relapsed. At necropsy the bat was in moderate body condition. There was a small amount of dried blood present at the external nares. The heart appeared large and rounded. The lungs were bright pink with a small amount of white froth on cut surface. The stomach and intestines were distended with gas.
STOMATITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS EUTHANSIA. This 8-year-old male wallaroo has a history of necrobacillosis involving the mandible and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

METABOLIC BONE DISEASE INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2-year-old gecko had a history of severe metabolic bone disease with spinal collapse and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed collapsed thoracic spine severely hypocalcified bones a rubbery jaw and inactive ovaries.

PROBABLE TRAUMA AUTOLYZED TISSUES. This 26-year-old male turtle had a traumatic episode several weeks earlier and was subsequently found dead in the pool and may have died a day prior to necropsy. Necropsy revealed autolyzed tissue.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS AND YOLK COELOMITIS AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS AND CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS. This approximately 31-year-old female American flamingo was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy there was no active pododermatitis. The liver was pale and friable. There was active ovary and pale streaks in the myocardium.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS STRESS. This male 17-year-old tiger was humanely euthanized due to pharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Biopsy diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma 5/25/02. It had been doing well up until six days before euthanasia. At that time the tiger refused to come into holding or to eat. At necropsy the liver was dark with fine black streaks. It was not enlarged. There was a large amount of mucus in the stomach. The primary tumor in the oral cavity had enlarged extending from the dorsolateral pharynx ventrally to around the epiglottis and base of the tongue. It was very necrotic. The spleen was enlarged. There were some areas of scarring on the capsule. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and firm. Bronchial mesenteric and prescapular lymph nodes appeared reactive. The adrenal surface appeared nodular.

TRAUMA (DROWNED) NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 9-year-old male meerkat fell and hit its head landing in the water and died shortly thereafter. The animal had no previous health issues. Necropsy revealed wet carcass a small amount of blood-tinged fluid in the nose white renal pelvises pale heart congested lungs and no other abnormalities.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MAMMARY FIBROADENOMA. This 1-year-old rat had a mass in the thoracic cavity removed approximately two months prior to death. Multiple masses occurred at the thoracic inlet and a large space occupying mass was present within the thoracic cavity radiographically. At necropsy the body condition was fair to poor. Lice were present on the hair shafts. Generalized muscle wasting was noted. The entire right lung was replaced by multiple coalescing caseous abscesses. Similar masses effaced much of the left lung.

EMACIATION AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 20-year-old male swan was alive in the morning but then found dead in the pond in the afternoon. It had no other history. Necropsy revealed no external signs of trauma moderate bumblefoot on both feet and no visceral lesions.
CHRONIC RUMINITIS ADHESIONS. This 5-year-old gerenuk died acutely. Necropsy revealed renal hemorrhage peritonitis and petechiae on the serosal surfaces.

PULMONARY AND COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE PROBABLE TRAUMA AIR EMBOLI ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 13.5-year-old female blue crowned motmot had a three-day history of dyspnea and also had poor feather quality and short feathers. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed abnormal appearing appendicular skeleton and no other gross abnormalities.

INANITION FIBROUS OSTEODYSTROPHY RENAL GOUT. This 6.5-year-old female day gecko has a history of gradual weight loss over the past 10 months. Radiographs revealed poor bone quality. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the animal was dehydrated and had trauma to the toes.

HEPATIC ABSCESS CATARACTS ABDOMINAL ADHESIONS DEGENERATIVE JOINT. CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 30-year-old male colobus had a one-week history of diarrhea and declining quality of life associated with osteoarthritis in the vertebral column and femurs. Teeth were worn with associated halitosis and gingivitis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed poor body condition with fecal matter matted over the tail and perineal region spinal deformities limited range of motion in the stifles bilateral cataracts absence of adipose stores numerous adhesions of the viscera in the abdominal cavity enlarged flabby heart with a focus of dark discoloration in the right ventricular serosa a firm tan homogeneous mass within the right atrial lumen arising from the endocardial surface numerous small white firm nodules in the lung up to 2 mm. in greatest dimension numerous firm white/pale tan nodules scattered throughout the liver multiple cysts in the kidneys a firm tan nodule within the fascia adjacent to the epididymis a cyst at the ventral apex of the urinary bladder containing gelatinous yellow fluid and the cyst did not communicate with the bladder lumen. A diverticulum was present in the distal stomach or proximal duodenum and contained a firm tan intramural nodule to 5 cm. in greatest dimension within the wall.

LYMPHOMA INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 3-year-old female silky bantam chicken was found dead in the morning. The bird had a history of weight loss and occasional diarrhea and recently had been treated for feather lice. Necropsy revealed emaciation with minimal fat deposits poor feather coat mildly enlarged liver with rounded edges and pale tan parenchyma and no other abnormalities. Food material was in the crop proventriculus and ventriculus.

SCHISTOSOMIASIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This approximately 13-year-old male black swan was found in recumbency and weak and was unable to hold its head up. Abrasions were noted on its toes. It was struggling to exit the cement pond. A similar episode was noted last winter that responded to supportive care. The bird died and necropsy revealed good body condition a moderate amount of thick saliva in the mouth and an enlarged thin-walled right atrium. Blood work prior to death was unremarkable.

POSTSURGICAL DEATH BACTERIAL ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS. This 25-year-old female cockatoo died postsurgery while still on the table. There was a history of a chronic wound on the breast. Surgery was done to remove the mass. The cockatoo’s respiratory rate slowed but the heart rate continued for one hour with Dopram and epinephrine. Despite attempts respirations could not be revived. At necropsy there was hemorrhage around the heart. The ovary was dark. The heart was thin.

DEGENERATIVE VASCULAR RENAL JOINT AND LENTICULAR DISEASE ENDOMETRITIS PANCREATIC ATROPHY RETROVIRUS INFECTION EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female koala had a history of successful breeding that resulted in multiple nonviable or shortly lived joeys prior to her arrival at Zoo Miami in 2007. The koala was suspected to be in early stages of retroviral-induced leukemia/lymphoma in 2009. The animal was in thin body condition so supplemental nutrition was offered daily in addition to supportive care that included anti-inflammatory drugs for osteoarthritis. In 2013 the koala developed intermittent periods of inappetence weight loss and low fecal output. Supportive care was administered during these episodes. In April 2015 an antiviral drug was administered for two months but the koala became leukopenic so the medication was discontinued. The koala failed to respond to supportive treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition light yellow colored ridge within the tracheal lumen congested right lung a 2 cm. region of white discoloration along the cranial aspect of the right lung roughened texture to the epicardial surface of the right ventricle proliferative tricuspid valve that was granular and thickened white nonraised foci on the serosal surface of the kidneys a focus of dark discoloration in the right renal medulla and a darkened area around the left renal pelvis. The adrenal glands were small. An ectopic spleen was identified. The right acetabulum was rough and erosion was present along both femoral heads. White semitransparent fluid was within the uterus. Klebsiella pneumoniae was cultured from the fluid in the uterus. A eucalyptus gruel was in the stomach and the pylorus was thickened.

EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA TRICHOEPITHELIOMA. This 6-year-old polecat was euthanized due to poor body condition. A necropsy a 3 x 4 mm. mass was present in the caudal lobe of the pancreas. Several white nodules were present on the left lung. A 1 cm. proliferative mass was present on the left side of the neck.

METASTATIC MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA WITH CHYLOTHROAX EUTHANASIA. This female 16-year-old puma had a mammary gland adenocarcinoma removed on 2/19/97. The animal presented with dyspnea and chylothorax. A mediastinal mass was detected and the cat was euthanized. Necropsy revealed severe thoracic disease with over 6 liters of chylous fluid removed from the chest. A large mediastinal mass was present. The serosal surface of the small intestine was dotted with nodules.

GOUT BACTERIAL OSTEOARTHRITIS. This approximately 16-year-old male wood duck was humanely euthanized. It had a history of bilateral cataracts swollen tarsometatarsal phalangeal joints and bumblefoot. Radiographs revealed severe bony destruction of the tarsometatarsal bone and proximal phalanges of the right foot. At necropsy there was white caseous material protruding from the right plantar surface. Two smaller similar lesions were present on the distal phalanges of the right and left feet. There was severe bilateral enlargement of both kidneys. The kidneys were mottled with areas of pallor. A 1 cm. cyst was present at the cranial pole of the right kidney. The right tarsometatarsal phalangeal joint was enlarged with white cream colored caseous material infiltrated around all tendons. Other soft tissue and bone structures. The left tarsometatarsal phalangeal joint had similar but less dramatic lesions.

PULMONARY SHOCK ASPIRATED GASTRIC CONTENTS. This approximately 3-year-old female agouti had no medical problems was anesthetized for annual exam and arrested while anesthetized shortly after a rabies vaccine was administered. Necropsy revealed good body condition and good postmortem condition mottling of the lungs attributed to CPR and no other gross lesions.

SEMINOMA CEREBELLAR MICROGRANULOMAS (RESEMBLING TREMATODE EGGS) EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male whistling duck presented for acute lameness and incoordination. Examination revealed ataxia and stumbling or falling over when attempting to step. Blood work was within normal limits. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition good feather condition a pinion in the right wing corneal opacity in the left eye pale liver pale kidneys and a firm mottle highly vascular 6 cm. space-occupying mass in the left cranial dorsal coelomic cavity.

BUMBLEFOOT GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS. This 40-year-old female flamingo was found dead. Necropsy identified white chalky material on the pericardial surface grit ingesta and digesta in the gastrointestinal tract chronic pododermatitis on both digits #4 dark caudal lungs black specks in the distal trachea and firm kidneys with white coloration throughout the parenchyma.

HEPATITIS ANEMIA. This male approximately 22-year-old tern died about 30 min. after treatment. It was being treated for bleeding bumbles. At necropsy there was severe anemia (CBC). The kidneys and pancreas were pale. The hepatic parenchyma was spotted pale.

RENAL CARCINOMA GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS ORAN SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA ATYPICAL MAST CELL INFILTRATE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION NEPHROSCLEROSIS CARDIAC FAILURE. This 4.5-year-old female hedgehog was examined for weight loss associated with loose teeth and periodontal disease. The hedgehog had pronounced hind limb ataxia. Radiographs revealed congestion of the right cranial pulmonary lobe and mineralization in the location of the cardiac silhouette. Supportive care was administered but the animal died the following day. Necropsy revealed mildly hyperplastic gingiva thin body condition three or four focal dark purple areas within the parenchyma of both lungs white streaks in the serosa of the heart enlarged and lobulated kidneys with numerous cystic structures and no other gross lesions.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS. This 24-year-old male ring-tailed lemur was found in thin body condition at annual examination in November 2011. Laboratory testing was within normal limits at that time. The animal developed stiffness in its hind limbs and was treated with meloxicam. The animal did well until December 29th when it presented with acute lethargy inappetence and tremoring. While immobilized the lemur developed acute cardiopulmonary arrest and could not be completely resuscitated. All laboratory values obtained prior to death were normal. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a large amount of blood tinged froth throughout the airways bilateral edema in the lungs and a small focal white concretion in the right lung. Multiple petechiae were on the serosal surface of the liver and the parenchyma diffusely was congested. The gallbladder had multiple yellow stones up to 5 mm. in diameter. Some erythema was noted on the fundic mucosa and duodenal mucosa. The left adrenal gland was larger than the right and contained a focus of hemorrhage. Tonsils were bilaterally enlarged. Marked osteophyte formation was noted in both stifle joints. A small amount of straw-colored fluid was in the abdominal cavity. Bilateral cataracts were noted.

NEMATODIASIS CYSTITIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 1-year-old female rat presented hypothermic and moribund. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy lungs were congested. Irregular pale foci were noted in the liver.

SUSPECT DROWNING. This female approximately 12-year-old bat was found dead in the tapir’s pool. This bat had a history of tendonitis of the right mid proximal ulna and bilateral loss of cortices within the distal ulna. She was also found to have hypocalcemia with a calcium/phosphorus imbalance. The calcium/phosphorus imbalance was chronic. At necropsy there was loss of body condition. There was alopecia on the ventral neck. The nose had an approximately 1 cm. scrape and the chin was peeled down. There was scarred muscle covering most of the chin but a small opening was probed on the right side which scraped down to the bone. There was foam within both nostrils. No subcutaneous fat was noted. The trachea contained a large amount of foam. The lungs were pink and soft. Sections of lung floated in formalin. The left chamber of the heart was much thicker than the right. There was some pericardial sac fat.

EPIDERMAL NECROSIS SAPROLEGNIA. This 5-month-old toad is one of two that were moved to a new tank and both were found dead with no prior signs of illness other than some acute skin lesion development. Necropsy identified multiple raised skin lesions on the dorsum up to 3 mm. in greatest dimension.

EUTHANASIA HEPATIC GRANULOMAS GLOMERULAR LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year/9-month-old female toad was humanely euthanized. The entire group of five animals was culled to screen for mycobacteriosis. Historically they were in contact with an animal that was suspect for tuberculosis based on histopathology. Tissues were submitted for mycobacterial culture.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 1-year-old female mouse is from a colony with a sneezing problem. Generally this condition is improved with treatment although the mouse of this report continued to sneeze. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

PERFORATED BOWEL SCLEROSING PERITONITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 6-month-old warthog arrived healthy but soon developed aspiration pneumonia which resolved with treatment. The animal became impacted with feces one month ago necessitating enterotomy. A second enterotomy was performed a few days later due to impaction of hay. The animal passed little feces in the following two weeks and a barium series confirmed lack of gut motility despite use of kinetic drugs. An additional exploratory surgery identified a large dilated loop of spiral colon and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed pulmonary congestion and edema attributed to postmortem hydration. The colon was dilated from the ileum to the rectum. Luminal food material was sticky but soft. Several nodules were on the surface of the duodenum and the serosal surface was disrupted and abnormal. Mesenteric vessels were engorged and mesenteric lymph nodes were larger than expected. Fibrous nodules were within the spleen. The bladder had a hemorrhagic focus on the cranial ventral surface.

BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS YOLK COELOMITIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female chuckwalla was being treated for retention of shelled eggs. Surgical exploratory revealed retained uterine eggs preovulatory follicular stasis postovulatory yolk retention free yolks encapsulated within the coelomic cavity uterine rupture coelomitis and coelomic fluid. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy in addition to the previously described findings the liver was enlarged mottled friable and had multiple 1-2 mm. yellow nodules scattered throughout the parenchyma. A dark red 2 cm. firm was on the caudal hepatic border. The liver was adhered to the coelomic wall in multiple locations. Adhesions of the uterus to the body wall were also noted. The lungs sank in formalin.

GASTRIC CARCINOMA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male pronghorn antelope had a history of weakness emaciation and dehydration with muscle wasting and had been inappetent for four days prior to immobilization. Ultrasound identified free fluid with clots of fibrin in the abdomen and irregular liver with flocculent debris in the right cardiac chambers. Blood work identified azotemia hyperlactatemia and mixed metabolic and respiratory acidosis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed food particles in the trachea and in the cranial bronchi. A few 1 cm. white nodules on the accessory pulmonary lobe and left cranial pulmonary lobe that were white and soft on cut surface. A thin layer of tissue was found directly below the atrioventricular valve and entwined around the papillary muscles and approximately 100 ml. of red fluid and clotted blood were in the ventral abdominal cavity and retroperitoneal space around the left kidney. A small amount of yellow gelatinous fluid was present around both kidneys. A full thickness nodular white to tan to black mass was found along the floor of the rumen omasum-abomasal orifice and along the caudal wall of the omasum the lesion approximately 25 cm. in greatest dimension. The ruminal papillae in this region are hardened elongated and crusted. A white nodule was in the liver.

SEMINOMA EMACIATION OSTEOARTHRITIS NECROULCERATIVE DERMATITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 10-year-old male white leghorn chicken has a history of losing weight and falling over. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the air sacs were thickened. There was some yellow discoloration of the left pulmonary lobe. The right testis was slightly larger than the left. There was a synovial cyst adjacent to the left metatarsus.
adult. Weight: 1102 g.  Blood in mouth.  Killed by female.
SEPTICEMIA INANITION. This 10-year-old male axolotl had a history of abnormal posture when swimming. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the coelomic cavity contained cloudy fluid.

OBESITY. This approximately 9-year-old female Polish chicken had a history of obesity but no other medical problems. The animal was found dead. Gross necropsy revealed obesity autolysis erythematous skin around the face and vent a focal puncture wound over the left hip possibly due to postmortem predation ingesta in the crop red and black discoloration of the liver and an active reproductive tract.

ASPIRATION. This 12-year-old male chinchilla developed progressively worsening dental disease necessitating multiple tooth trims. After the most recent trim the chinchilla experienced rapid weight loss and sudden onset of respiratory difficulty. Supportive care was administered but the animal became agonal and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

CHRONIC ENTERITIS WITH BACTERIAL OVERGROWTH PERITONITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 3-month-old female ferret had a history of chronic diarrhea and weight loss and fecal culture was positive for Clostridium sp. It had received supportive care but continued to decline and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed lean body condition with some hair loss and erythema on the cranial half of the tail. The lungs are bright red and floated in formalin. Multiple white nodules were in the parenchyma. The liver was firm mottled red brown and yellow and some multiple white pinpoint nodules were present. Digested blood strands were on the mucosal surface of the stomach and various areas in the intestines were dark purple on the mucosal surface. Lymph nodes in the jejunal region and mesentery were enlarged and the spleen was large firm and dark purple.

RENAL COCCIDIOSIS EUTHANASIA (CNS SIGNS). This 4-year-old female Parma wallaby had an eight week history of progressive neurologic signs and a conspecific was diagnosed with baylisascariasis (G12-4045). Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.
ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA HEPATIC GLYCOGENOSIS VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY. This 8.5-year-old male sugar glider was found dead. At necropsy the liver was large and heterogeneous.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 8-year-old male corn snake was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed good body condition. The snake had been clinically normal although had refused its last four feedings. Necropsy revealed partial prolapse of the right hemipenis good body condition with adequate adipose stores numerous white to tan 1-3 mm. nodules on the serosal surfaces of the lung and the nodules had viscous tan to yellow exudate on cut surface. The stomach contained green to tan malodorous fluid and formed fecal material was in the colon. Multiple pinpoint white nodules were present throughout the body kidneys and liver.
MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA ASPERGILLOSIS HEPATITIS SHOCK. This 24-year-old male bittern was found dead. At necropsy numerous 2-4 mm. white foci were present in the thoracic air sacs and lungs.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA (CAR BACILLUS-LIKE) EUTHANSIA. This 4-year-old female domestic rat had a history of chronic respiratory disease dyspnea and did not respond to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bilateral pulmonary consolidation the left side worse than the right. Multiple firm nodules were in the caudal left lung. Some mild streaking was in the myocardium. Some petechiae were on the serosal surface of the colon.

SYSTEMIC AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC RENAL FAILURE WITH RENAL GOUT SOFT TISSUE MINERALIZATION. This approximately 22-year-old female flamingo was found dead. Gross necropsy revealed pectoral muscle atrophy minimal body fat stores bilateral bumblefoot verrucous endocardiosis of the left AV valves an empty gastrointestinal tract and diffuse renal gout.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE CARDIOMYOPATHY FATTY LIVER. This 6-year-old female hedgehog was found dead in its enclosure. It had a brief history of right front leg lameness. Radiographs were unremarkable. It was given supportive care for several days but did not respond to treatment and instead became more lethargic. At necropsy the kidneys were large. There was some feed material within the stomach. The urinary bladder was full of urine. The gastrointestinal tract contained some tarry dark green stool.

PARVOVIRAL ENTERITIS. This 12-week-old female captive bred Mexican wolf had a 2-3 day history of illness and died. It is from a litter of 10 pups. All pups were vaccinated at eight weeks of age and treated for parasites (ivermectin and topical flea prevention product). The pups were revaccinated at 12 weeks of age with the same products. The pups then developed loose stool/diarrhea with depression and two died. All pups were lethargic dehydrated and most had profuse hemorrhagic diarrhea. Blood work revealed profound leukopenia with toxic change. Fecal exams revealed coccidia. Necropsy of this pup revealed poor nutritional status with thin body condition and no recognizable fat stores. The intestines were autolyzed but contained watery pale green colored fluid.

CIRRHOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male meerkat was diagnosed with severe hepatobiliary disease one year earlier with cholestasis and elevated serum ALP GGT and hyperbilirubinemia. The animal also had decreased hepatic function (hypoglycemia hypoalbuminemia and hypocholesterolemia). Bile acids were severely elevated. The animal remained clinically healthy and in good body condition for the following eight months but over the last several weeks its appetite and body weight have declined and it presented one day earlier with lethargy vomiting and hind limb ataxia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified thin body condition moderate dental wear on all arcades and absence of the fourth cheek tooth on the left maxilla the first cheek tooth on the left mandible and the left mandibular canine tooth. The right mandibular canine tooth was fractured. The heart was globoid. Lungs were diffusely congested. The liver was firm multinodular mottled red to golden brown and had rounded lobar margins. Thick yellow material was in the gallbladder. The spleen was diffusely enlarged.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ACUTE TRAUMA PYODERMA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 16.5-year-old Jamaican fruit bat was found dead at morning check and had no prior history of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no gross abnormalities other than possible hepatomegaly.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA CHROMOMYCOSIS CORNEAL HYPERPIGMENTATION AND CATARACT. This approximately 15-year-old smoky jungle frog was found dead. It had a history of weight loss and ocular pigmentation. Necropsy revealed pigmented and clouded corneas thin body condition and a small white tag on the ventral surface of the liver.

UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female sheep had a two-week history of decreased appetite and a two-day history of increased weakness with episodes of decreased mental awareness progressing to tremors and head pressing with bruxism. Necropsy revealed muscle atrophy over the back and pelvis a large amount of straw-colored free fluid in the abdomen and thorax white granular or nodular lesions on the serosal surface of the liver spleen rumen and stomach large grainy sublumbar lymph node dark congested dependent pulmonary lobes white granular lesions on the mucosal surface of the omasum and liver and bilaterally gnarled and enlarged ovaries with fluid-filled uterus. The pancreas was not grossly recognized.

DROWNING. This 5-year/7-month-old male duck was found drowned in drain. At necropsy it was in good body condition. All feathers were soaked. The coelom was full of blood. There were large amounts of thick hemorrhage present. There was a very small amount of abdominal fat present. There was a small amount of food in the digestive tract. The lungs were dark red. The liver was friable. The kidneys were small.

EUTHANASIA ADENOCARCINOMA PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 7-year-old chicken had a history of ascites. Withdrawn from the coelomic cavity was 55 cc. of yellow tinged fluid approximately one week prior to death. Due to continuing decline in condition the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the bird was in very poor body condition with marked muscle wasting. Fecal material was matted around the vent. A large mass was present in the caudal coelom adherent to the duodenum jejunum colon spleen and ovary.

EUTHANASIA DENTAL WEAR HEPATITIC LIPIDOSIS. This 13-year-old male sheep was euthanized due to its advanced age loss of vision and severe dental wear. At necropsy uneven wear of the molars and premolars were extremely worn.

EUTHANASIA RUMINAL ACIDOSIS PRESUMPTIVE PARASITIC ENTEROCOLITIS SPERM GRANULOMA. This 11-year-old male greater kudu has a chronic history of degenerative joint disease and arthritis which has been medically managed. The animal is having difficulty rising due to arthritis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was arthritis in all joints of the limbs as well as bilateral hygromas on carpi. There are arterial plaques and jet lesions present along the great arteries of the heart.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS CATARACTS PLEURITIS PANCREATITIS ENTERITIS. This 15-year-old male sheep was euthanized due to poor quality of life. The animal has a history of arthritis and cataracts. At necropsy variably sized abscesses were present in the lung and adjacent to the heart. Round masses were present adjacent to the duodenum. White foci were present in the heart.

TRAUMA BACTERIAL SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male emperor tamarin was moved to a new enclosure at which point he became nonweight bearing lame on his leg due to trauma and severe myositis. Amputation was performed and the animal steadily lost weight and had a single episode of dark colored diarrhea. Examination revealed necrotic tissue and multiple openings at the amputation site. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy multiple abscesses were noted at the amputation site. The third digit of the left hand was partially nonviable. The lungs and heart were coated in a thick plaque-like material. The liver has a white focus.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE. This 33-year-old male ibis was being fed when it died. It had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed hydrocoelom pale liver with rounded edges raised areas on the hepatic parenchyma that were lighter in color than the rest of the parenchyma on cut surface pale kidneys yellow fat in the coelom food in the gastrointestinal tract thickened air sacs with numerous white rounded plaques around the pericardial sac pale streaks in the heart and dense lungs.
ROUND CELL NEOPLASIA. This 2-year-old female house mouse was found dead. At necropsy the liver was enlarged mottled and discolored. The GI tract was distended with gas.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH SYSTEMIC ABSCESSES THYROID FOLLICULAR CARCINOMA. This 4.5-year-old hedgehog presented for routine examination with no clinical signs reported by the keepers. Examination revealed thin body condition with weight loss since the last examination. Blood work revealed marked leukocytosis with left shift and elevated renal values. The animal continued to decline despite antibiotic therapy and died when anesthetized for repeat evaluation. Necropsy revealed thin body condition. A 1 cm. area of pasty purulent material was in the right upper abdomen closely associated with the liver. Gastrointestinal adhesions were present in this region. Mesenteric lymph nodes were prominent. The left seminal vesicle was larger and firmer than the right seminal vesicle. The lungs had multiple pinpoint dark red foci throughout all lobes.

EUTHANASIA NEMATODAL COLITIS. This 8-year-old male corn snake was humanely euthanized. It had been housed with a cryptosporidial positive snake. This snake was positive serologically. At necropsy there were adequate adipose stores. The lungs floated in formalin.

EUTHANASIA PERIOPHTHALMITIS MULTIORGAN GRANULOMAS. This approximately 10-year-old male snake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic swelling around the left eye. There was fluid accumulation behind the spectacle. It was unresponsive to treatment. At necropsy there was swelling of the left eye. The left periocular region was swollen and edematous. The left speculum was cloudy with an inflamed red area visible at the previous incision site. There was clear fluid accumulation between the spectacle and cornea. The left maxillary region appeared partially distended. There were good coelomic fat stores present.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL COELOMITIS AND COLITIS INANITION HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This 17-year-old female python was humanely euthanized. It had a history of anorexia since August 2000 and swelling cranial to the vent. Radiographs revealed radiodense material at and cranial to the distention. Barium was administered and it did not pass by this material. An enterotomy was performed on 11/2/00. Firm stools were removed from three enterotomy sites. The snake recovered from the surgery but still did not eat when reacclimated at the reptile house in December. The python was force fed small items but did not pass any stools. Another barium series was performed 1/8/01 and again the barium stopped at the radiodense material which was at the site of the previous enterotomy. It was suspected there might be damage to the intestine (e.g. neural). At necropsy the python was thin and had no intracoelomic fat stores. The liver had multiple raised cystic structures that varied from 0.5 to 10 mm. in diameter and contained clear fluid. The intestine was adhered to the abdominal wall at the previous surgery site. The intestine was teased away from the adhesion and a 5 mm. round ulcerated lesion on the serosa was evident. The adhesion side of the body wall contained firm material. Large firm stools were present in the intestine at the adhesion. Cranial to the vent the intestinal and reproductive tracts appeared edematous. There were multiple broken ribs present at or cranial to the surgical site. There were multiple soft red amorphous masses and firm dark red/brown granuloma-like lesions present throughout the mesentery.

FEMORAL RHABDOMYOSARCOMA SUPPURATIVE PROSTATITIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male Egyptian bat had lost 25% of its body weight in the past year. It presented with hypothermia in a moribund condition and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed remodeling of the right femoral neck and proximal femur. The bones of the skull and mandible were soft and easily cut with a scalpel. The left eye was phthisical.

HYPERPLASTIC GOITER BACTERIAL DERMATITIS EMACIATION. This approximately 27-year-old male hyacinth macaw developed severe dermatitis following West Nile virus vaccine in March 2004. The bird had been previously healthy. Skin biopsies were obtained on 3/15 and at that time dermatitis extended from the axillary region over the pectoral region and anterior legs but was not present on the abdomen head posterior legs or dorsum. The bird was found dead six days later. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dermatitis mottled liver and an apparent fracture in the hepatic parenchyma.

EUTHANASIA INANITION BILE STASIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA ENTERITIS. This 8-year-old female sheep has a history of chronic weight loss and inappetence. The animal has been treated with supportive care; however weight loss and inappetence continued. Due to lack of response to therapy the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin with marked muscle wasting although moderate quantities of fat were present in the abdominal cavity. A small quantity of serous fluid was present in the abdomen. Teeth were worn with numerous points. The liver was pale and friable. The rumen contained a 5 mm. firm raised mass on the mucosa. The pancreas was dark and contained a firm round dark mass. The urinary bladder contained foci of hemorrhage. Kidneys contained multifocal irregular pale foci. Mammary glands were dilated and contained clear yellow fluid with numerous black flecks.

SHOCK DIC POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS. This 1-year-old male Surinam toad had inconsistent appetite over the last week and spending a lot of time at the top of the tank. It was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed adequate fat stores slight constriction near the pylorus and no other abnormalities noted.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) LOW GRADE SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male bat was unable to perch with the other bats and had age-related degenerative joint disease with associated abrasion of two interphalangeal joints and exposure and luxation of the joints. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.
EUTHANASIA GASTRITIS. This 12-year-old male sheep was aged and had arthritis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. No abnormalities were noted at necropsy.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE LOW-GRADE SEPSIS. This 11.5-year-old male meerkat was noted to be unresponsive and was dead upon arrival at the hospital. It had a history of slow anesthetic recoveries. Necropsy revealed mild dehydration enlarged heart enlarged auricles moderate pulmonary congestion an enlarged liver with rounded and blunt edges enlarged left adrenal gland and food throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 12-year-old rattlesnake had been regurgitating food and had tested positive for Cryptosporidium. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed white streaks in the kidneys enlarged spleen enlarged thyroid gland and adequate fat stores.

ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 9-year-old female screech owl has a chronic history of arthritis and blindness. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was severe arthritis within the shoulder girdles (not submitted) and the liver was subjectively enlarged.

EUTHANASIA CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE INANITION. This 6-year-old male meerkat was humanely euthanized. There was a recent death of an older companion. Within 3-5 days this meerkat became weak and had onset of neurologic signs. It also developed weight loss despite good appetite. The previous case (G00-1863) had degenerative myopathy. There was recent diet analysis for vitamin E/selenium levels.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS LYMPHOMA THYROID ADENOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female tiger had a history of chronic renal disease eventually necessitating euthanasia. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and decreased muscle mass mottled pale liver pitting and white discoloration on the capsular surface of the spleen bilateral thyroid cysts moderate to severe thickening of the entire gastrointestinal tract with areas of superficial erosion or ulceration in the gastric mucosa green particulate matter in the renal pelvises bilateral lenticular opacities and no other abnormalities.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA THYMOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female goat had a history of an adenoma involving the mammary gland that continued to fill with fluid. The animal became inappetent and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the right flank region. An additional mass was present above the heart in the thorax.

HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATIC NECROSIS SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 11-year-old female bat was hospitalized for leukopenia anemia and hypoproteinemia. The animal’s condition gradually improved and the animal was returned to the exhibit. It was found dead several days later. At necropsy the animal was thin with minimal body fat. The liver contained a pale tan to pink area in one lobe. Kidneys were pale.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE UROCYSTITIS. This 10-year-old female rock hyrax was found dead in holding. It had a history of trichofolliculoma on the right forearm that had been excised several months earlier with clean margins. Necropsy revealed 30 ml. of translucent straw-colored fluid in the thoracic cavity 3-5 ml. of translucent straw-colored fluid in the pericardial sac subjectively thickened left auricle foamy liquid in the trachea and primary bronchi four 1-2 mm. tan raised nodules on the surface of the right adrenal gland and some petechiae in the mucosa of the urinary bladder.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOSARCOMA (VETEBRA SPINAL CORD) ATELECTASIS PULMONARY FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 6-year-old male hedgehog presented with congestive heart failure and was under treatment. Hind limb ataxia was also noted. This progressed to severe proprioceptive deficits in the hind limbs and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy minimal fat depots were noted. A small hard white mass was present along the ventral thoracic vertebrae.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old lorikeet was clinically healthy one day prior to death and then developed severe respiratory distress and died despite aggressive supportive care. Blood work revealed renal failure and hepatic disease. The bird is from a flock in which an unidentified protozoan infection has been diagnosed. Necropsy revealed pulmonary edema urate stasis in the kidney and plaques on the serosa.

OVIDUCTAL ADENOCARCINOMA WITH CARCINOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female bantam chicken had a one day history of lethargy coelomic distention and reduced fecal and urate production. The bird was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed light brown watery fluid in the coelom and numerous coalescing white firm masses involving the air sacs pericardium left hepatic lobe duodenum mesentery intestinal serosa and renal capsules. The oviduct also contained a dark red to pink mass and a firm white to tan mass.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA VASCULITIS INTESTINAL HEMORRHAGE ABDOMINAL ADHESIONS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 2-year-old female mouse developed respiratory difficulties with squinty eyes received supportive care but did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The mouse had a significant amount of blood in the stool at the time of euthanasia.

EUTHANASIA ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA SPLENIC HEMATOMA. This 5-year-old male ferret had a history of an abdominal mass. The animal was humanely euthanized after an exploratory laparotomy revealed a large irregular mass extending from the spleen with presumed metastatic lesions anterior to the right kidney.

UTERINE AND BRONCHIOLAR GLANDULAR HYPERPLASIA IRON STORAGE DISEASE PYOMETRA. This greater than 5-year-old female Seba’s fruit bat was found down in its exhibit weak and tremoring. With supportive care it gradually improved over the next four days but was unable to fly. Radiographs revealed poor abdominal contrast. No fractures were noted. Lethargy increased appetite decreased and the animal was found dead six days after the initial presentation. Necropsy revealed a bruised appearance to the heart enlarged kidneys and uterine enlargement.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 2-year-old male sugar glider was found dead on the bottom of the enclosure near the food bowl. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of amber-colored fluid in the peritoneal cavity adhesion of the liver to the diaphragm and no other abnormalities.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 9.5-year-old male Jamaican fruit bat was found on the ground nonresponsive and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition absence of hair over most of the body with only a small amount of pelage present on the limbs and face. Scant abdominal fat was noted and several white plaques were noted on the colon. The liver was mottled with several small white masses throughout the parenchyma.
adult. Weight: 4100.0 g.  Euth. Hydroperitoneum; thorax & p/cardium. Pulm.congestion & oedema. Splenomegaly. Mesenteric LN nodule.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS EMACIATION PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA CHRONIC ABOMASITIS AND ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old female gerenuk had given birth to a dummy calf two weeks prior to death and the calf died shortly after parturition. Parturition had been uneventful and the dam consumed the placenta. The dam had chronic thin body condition since arrival in quarantine since October 2012 but had no other abnormalities noted. Diarrhea had been observed but resolved with no further intervention. Six days prior to death moderate bloat was noted. The animal was tubed and gas and green/brown fluid were removed. The following day the animal became sternally recumbent and could not stand and when lifted made no attempt to bear weight on the limbs. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond had markedly elevated CK and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition good postmortem condition prominent vertebral processes and pelvic bones and absence of intra-abdominal and mesenteric adipose tissue. The abdomen was distended with a moderate amount of red transparent fluid identified as a modified transudate. The rumen was distended with froth and feed material. The fetal membrane were lodged in the reticular/ruminal opening partially obstructing the opening and a moderate amount of edema was present in the epaxial and proximal muscles in the hind limbs. Multiple regions of pale pink muscle were present in the femoral and gluteal muscle bundles. A moderate amount of transparent pericardial fluid was present and the heart was grossly within normal limits. The renal pelvis bilaterally was dilated. A mild amount of mucoid dark brown discharge was present in the uterine body and horns.

METASTATIC CYSTADENOCARCINOMA SPLENIC THROMBOSIS CENTRILOBULAR HEPATIC NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 15-year-old female jaguar was diagnosed with a cystadenocarcinoma following ovariohysterectomy. At surgery cysts were widespread throughout the abdominal cavity. The animal was treated with piroxicam and asymptomatic until having severe abdominal distention two weeks prior to euthanasia. At necropsy there were three liters of hemorrhagic fluid with many blood clots throughout the abdomen splenomegaly with two raised foci and several breaks in the splenic capsule with associated blood clots numerous fluid-filled cysts throughout the abdomen and adhered to the diaphragm omentum musculature and serosal surfaces of the intestines and multifocal lymphadenomegaly.
ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS SPLENITIS. This 1-year-old male lorikeet died during treatment. Necropsy revealed yellow material within airways. Lungs sank in formalin.

EUTHANASIA INANITION CHRONIC ENTERITIS GASTRITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 22-year-old male llama has a history of chronic weight loss and inappetence. The animal was humanely euthanized due to lack of response to therapy. At necropsy body condition was poor. The GI tract contained a large quantity of ingesta. Several walled off pieces of green food material were present within the diverticula of the forestomachs. A thickened area was noted in the stomach. A 2 cm. in diameter red nodule was present in the small intestinal lumen.

ANESTHETIC DEATH BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MAMMARY ADENOMA SHOCK. This 2-year-old rat was anesthetized for removal of a mass. Respiratory arrest developed under anesthesia and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy a 2 x 3 cm. well circumscribed mass was present over the left thorax. Lungs were hemorrhagic and contained a 1 cm. in diameter mass containing purulent white discharge.

LYMPHOSARCOMA (SPLEEN LIVER MENINGES) SPLENIC HEMORRHAGE NEPHRITIS INNITION OSTEITIS DEFORMANS BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS. This 10-year-old female viper was being transported to off exhibit holding began tremoring and openmouthed gaping. The animal became nonresponsive and died. The animal has a history of abnormal head movements which had resolved. It also tested positive for paramyxovirus. At necropsy a large quantity of blood was present in the caudal coelomic cavity. The spleen was enlarged and friable.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 7-year/8-month-old male rattlesnake died. It had a history of not eating over about three months. It also had a history of lethargy. At necropsy there was granulomatous hepatitis pneumonia tracheitis and splenitis. The lungs were congested and hemorrhagic. Sections of lung liver trachea and spleen were frozen for future use if needed. Rule out mycobacteriosis.

TRAUMA SHOCK MYOCARDIAL PROTOZOONOSIS LEUCOCYTOZOON-LIKE ORGANISM. This 2-year-old female tanager was found dead. At gross necropsy the right tarsometatarsus and the left humerus were fractured. Feathers were missing from the head and there was associated bruising and skin abrasions at this site. The left lower beak was fractured. A large area of hemorrhage was present on the dorsocranial aspect of the liver. Lungs were filled with blood.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 21-year-old male scarlet ibis was found dead in its cage two days after a routine exam. Blood work was within normal limits. Necropsy revealed a large flabby heart. E. coli was isolated from serous fluid in the coelomic cavity. The liver was founded.

EUTHANASIA NONSUPPURATIVE ENCEPHALITIS CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS. This 16-year-old male Dumeril’s ground boa has a seven month history of neurologic signs. Two weeks prior to euthanasia the snake became opaque and frequently was found upside-down. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed obesity late stage ecdysis and ingesta in the stomach.

INTRACOELOMIC ABSCESS WITH OOPHORITIS AND SALPINGITIS. This 9-year-old female rail presented with a distended abdomen and was having difficulty walking. A large mass was palpated in the coelomic cavity. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed a 6 cm. mass adhered to several points in the coelom with associated displacement of the liver and intestines. On cut surface the mass was laminated and appeared to contain yolk material.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK URATE STASIS. This 8-year-old turtle is part of a group which are inappetent and showing weight loss. The animal presented with bleeding from the oral cavity and died the following day. At necropsy the lungs were hemorrhagic.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL OSTEOPATHY (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATITIS SPLENITIS GRANULMATOUS COELOMITIS INANITION. This 11-year-old male rattlesnake was euthanized due to chronic spinal fusion and inappetence. At necropsy the animal was emaciated and marked areas of spondylosis were noted in the spine.

EUTHANASIA BILIARY CYSTS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 4-year-old female ferret had a recent history of weight loss and lethargy. The animal was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy the pancreas was enlarged and had several dark nodules. A 1 cm. firm granular mass was present in the area of the right adrenal gland.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS DISSEMINATED HISTIOCYTIC INFLAMMATION EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female Tamar wallaby developed severe respiratory disease and had bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed marked weight loss thin body condition adhesions of the lung to the thoracic wall a mass in the mediastinum effacement of the majority of the pulmonary parenchyma with pale white to brown solid tissue type infiltrates a small amount of peritoneal fat multiple 2-3 mm. pale nodules on the surface of the liver several nodules up to 5 mm. in diameter in the parenchyma of the spleen enlarged kidneys replaced by white soft tissue infiltrates and bilateral mature cataracts.

EROSIVE TYPHLITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 9-month-old male rock hyrax was found moribund in its exhibit and died while being examined. Blood work revealed hypoglycemia and examination revealed low body temperature. Necropsy revealed an area of hemorrhage in the gastric wall gas in the alimentary tract and normal feces in the colon. The pancreas appeared normal although possibly small.

AMYLOIDOSIS PULMONARY MINERALIZATION RENAL GOUT INANITION. This greater than 17-year-old female flamingo died. It was noted to be limping and was placed in a barn prior to death. At necropsy there was severe diffuse renal gout. There was renomegaly. There was severe meningeal congestion. There was splenomegaly. There was clotted blood on the ventral hepatic peritoneal membrane. The lung fields were discolored bilaterally and had severe hemorrhage in the parenchyma and airways.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA. This 13-year-old female call duck presented for listing to the left the previous day appeared normal on clinical exam aside from lean body condition and slight lameness in the right leg. The following day the bird was acting weaker and was found dead the following day. Necropsy revealed lean body condition normal plumage and no external lesions. White specks were present throughout the coelomic cavity on all serosal surfaces and kidneys were large and swollen. Lungs were brown/red heavy and wet.

Lung (1/2 sections): Acute necrohemorrhagic pneumonia with myriad intralesional bacteria Heart; left ventricle: Focal mild necrotizing myocarditis Liver: Diffuse moderate to marked hepatocellular fatty degeneration (hepatic lipidosis) Gallbladder: Multifocal moderate lymphocytic cholecystitis Stomach: Multifocal mild lymphocytic gastritis Small intestine: Intraluminal hemorrhage and bacteria Comment The lung lesions in this ferret are comparable to those observed in animals with acute to peracute fatal pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa; extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli or; although the morphology of the bacteria is not coccoid; possibly Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus. A Gram stain is pending to further characterize the intralesional bacteria. The result of this stain will be reported in an addendum. Hepatic lipidosis is indicative of negative energy balance. The cause of the mild focal myocarditis and the chronic cholecystitis are undetermined. Chronic lymphocytic gastritis in ferrets is typically associated with Helicobacter mustelae infection; although no bacteria were evident in the section of stomach examined. One of the sections of intestine contained blood as observed at necropsy. It is undetermined whether the intraluminal bacteria in this section represent overgrowth of the intestinal flora and/or the same bacteria as noted in the lung. A Gram stain was requested on this section as well; in an attempt to further characterize also these bacteria. Gram stain: - Lung: Intralesional Gram negative bacteria - Small intestine: Mixed intraluminal bacteria Comment The result of the Gram stain of the lung is consistent with the previously suspected Gram-negative bacterial pneumonia. Considering that this is a mustelid; infection with Pseudomonas sp. is considered most likely; but other possibly pathogens include E. coli; Klebsiella pneumoniae and Bordetella bronchiseptica. In the small intestine; there were mixed bacteria within the lumen; some of which may have represented the same bacteria noted in the lung. Culture would be needed to determine the exact causative agent of the pneumonia and whether it may have been present also in the intestine.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CORONARY MEDIAL HYPERTROPHY CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL TUBULAR MINERALIZATION. This 6-year-old female wallaroo was found down. Blood work revealed anemia and inflammatory leukogram. The animal was treated with supportive care but was found dead. At necropsy the left ventricular wall was thickened. Focal areas of hemorrhage were present within the lung. The proximal duodenum appeared hemorrhagic.

ESOPHAGEAL NERVE SHEATH TUMOR DEGENERATIVE JOINT CARDIOPULMONARY AND RENAL DISEASE. This 30-year-old female colobus has a history of osteoarthritis of both sacroiliac joints with osteophytes in the proximal femur and bilateral stifle arthritis elbow arthritis and osteophytes in the tarsi and carpi. Arthritis is also present with fusion in the vertebral column with loss of disc space. Radiographic evidence of fibrosis in the lungs is also noted. Teeth were loose with associated gingival recession. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified some muscle atrophy adequate fat stores bilateral cataracts multiple white firm nodules throughout the lung a 4 cm. intramural esophageal mass proximal to the thoracic inlet enlarged and hyperemic duodenum a dark black ovoid mass joined to the serosal surface of the proximal small intestine by a small stalk whipworms in the gastric lumen small kidneys with reduced cortex and pitted serosal surface uniformly thickened and enlarged uterine body uniformly thickened and reddened pancreas and previously stated arthritic lesions.

SYSTEMIC ANTIGENIC STIMULATION CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION OVARIAN YOLK EMBOLISM. This 17-year-old female spoonbill was found on the ground lethargic. The bird was moved to an isolette and was found dead later in the morning. The bird had no prior medical history. Necropsy revealed no evidence of trauma active folliculogenesis and hemorrhage in the cerebrum and subdural meninges. A 3 cm. long stick was lodged in the left caudal pelvic inlet with no obvious entry wound and no associated scar tissue. A large bruise was present on the skull extending through the bone.

MYCOTIC AIR SACCULITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE ATHEROSCLEROSIS GRANULOMATOUS AIR SACCULITIS. This 23-year-old male Humboldt penguin has a history of progressive exercise intolerance and increased respiratory effort over one year’s duration. Radiographs revealed an enlarged cardiac silhouette and cardiac ultrasound was difficult to obtain due to anatomy but the septum appeared thinned. The bird subsequently died. Necropsy revealed granulomas in the respiratory tract and at the base of the heart.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS CONSPECIFIC TRAUMA. This 2-year-old female rainbow lorikeet had been displaced by two larger chattering lories but no obvious aggression was noted. The bird was found dead on the floor of the exhibit. Necropsy revealed good body condition but severe feather loss with bruising and hemorrhage over the lateral and ventral head. The left eye globe was ruptured. The rostral one-third of the tongue is completely shredded and there is moderate oral hemorrhage. A left distal mandibular fracture with associated hematoma was noted. Mild hepatomegaly and severe splenomegaly were also noted.

EUTHANASIA DYSGERMINOMA HEPATITIS PERITONITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 20-year-old female lemur was weak and ataxic. The animal’s condition continued to decline. A large firm mass was identified in the anterior abdomen. Elevations were noted in BUN bilirubin and phosphorus. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin with poor muscle mass. A lobulated mass was present adherent to the kidneys spleen and pancreas. Metastases were noted to the esophagus and diaphragm.

LOW GRADE SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION ACUTE PULMONARY SHOCK ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS IRON STORAGE DISEASE CYTOLOGY. This 10.5-year-old female Bali mynah had a one day history of not using its right leg. Physical examination the following day did not reveal an obvious fracture. The mynah arrested during the anesthetic procedure following an episode of regurgitation. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed a prominent liver prominent mottled spleen and mild hemorrhage in the meninges.
NEPHRITIS FILARIASIS INANITION ENTERITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 11-year-old male Gila monster was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy multiple nodular foci were present on the liver.

SEMINOMA HEPATITIS. This 6-year-old male lory was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy areas of feather loss were noted over the pectoral region and legs (feather picking). Moderate atrophy of the pectoral muscles was also present. A large white lobulated mass was present in the coelomic cavity.
NA

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA HYPERSENSITIVITY DERMATITIS OBESITY. This 8.5-year-old male oryx regurgitated while anesthetized for preshipment exam and was believed to have aspirated. The animal coughed before standing following recovery remained depressed the rest of the day but was sternally recumbent and alert at first check in the morning. The animal was found dead a few hours later. Necropsy revealed obesity chronic dermatitis over the dorsal midline in the rump area and semilinear patches of alopecia and crusting hyperkeratosis. The tip of the tail had lost some hair and had a hyperkeratotic surface. A few chronic incisor fractures were noted. The trachea was irregularly reddened and had some hemorrhages in the mucosa and some superficial erosions. The right lung had red/gray consolidation of the cranial ventral half with ruminal material filling the bronchioles deep into the parenchyma and a small amount of tan/white purulent-looking exudate in some of the parabronchiolar areas. The caudal half of the right lung and all portions of the left lung were congested and edematous. Some gelatinous or greasy material is in the interstitial areas of the pancreas. The adrenals had marked cortical hemorrhage and possibly some associated hematomas. A few trichobezoars were in the abomasum.

MYCOTIC LYMPHADENITIS LYMPH NODE ABSCESS. This 10-year-old male antelope had a two month history of progressive hind end and forelimb ataxia with limping and muscle wasting. Blood work revealed elevated CPK and elevated serum zinc. Radiographs were unremarkable. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and revealed emphysematous lungs thick left heart and bony fibrous nodules at the back wall of the thorax near the vena cava.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS CHOLECYSTITIS. This greater than 8-year-old female lizard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of lethargy for the last several months. At necropsy the gall bladder was firm and inspissated. Culture was taken of the gall bladder. There were numerous inspissated ova. There was a firm 1 cm. mass present in the coelom. Culture was sent for suspect mycobacteriosis.

CIRRHOSIS BILIARY CYSTADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old male black and white ruffed lemur had been off feed for a few days and had elevated serum GGT. A palpable mass was noted in the cranial abdomen that appeared to be cavitated and cystic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EMACIATION DRAINING TRACT WITH FOREIGN MATERIAL. This 4-year-old male greater kudu was received and housed with a conspecific. The animal continued to lose weight the entire time it was housed at this facility with a conspecific. The animal was anesthetized for feeding tube placement and was found dead two days later. The animal had a dislocated left shoulder at necropsy. Additionally there was a focal abomasal ulcer with congestion and suspect pseudomembranes on the colon and transverse colon.

ENTERITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 15-year-old female lory has a history of bloody stool. The animal is under treatment for trimethoprim sulfa. At necropsy the intestines were hemorrhagic with dark red/brown contents.
HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS. This 6-year-old lizard was found dead. At necropsy the liver was pale.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 10-year-old male lorikeet was found dead in its food bowl. Necropsy revealed trauma to the head trachea and tongue good body condition orange tint to the muscle and opaque plaques on the serosal surfaces of the viscera.

RUPTURED DISK EUTHANASIA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA THYROID SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA. This 2-year-old female addax had a history of running into a fence two weeks earlier breaking off the horn at the base. The horn was removed and treated without incident. The following day the addax developed swelling at the region of C4-5 became inappetent and when treated became laterally recumbent and could not rise. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Radiographs obtained prior to necropsy revealed fracture of the dorsal and lateral spinous processes of C4 as well as some erosive damage to the articular surface of the vertebral body. Prosection revealed rupture of the disk between C3 and C4 with cranial articulation of C4.

BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA BACTERIAL GASTRITIS HEPATITIS RENAL GOUT INTESTINAL MINERALIZATION. This 11-year-old male corn snake had a mass in the coelom. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the snake was thin. The anterior liver had an 8 cm. in diameter mass containing friable tissue with necrosis in the center.

THYROID ADENOCARCINOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS ENTERITIS INTRAOPERATIVE DEATH. This 13-year-old male tamarin had a thyroid mass. The mass suddenly enlarged and became ulcerated with purulent discharge. Surgical excision was attempted; however the mass was adherent to underlying tissues. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed and the animal died. At necropsy an irregular multilobulated mass with areas of necrosis was present associated with the right thyroid gland. The contralateral gland was larger than normal. The liver was mottled red and orange. Pancreas was firm and nodular.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE OLD RIB FRACTURES IMPLANT SITE REACTION SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONALS STATUS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male fruit bat had a two-week history of weakness and blood work identified hyperphosphatemia. The bat was treated with meloxicam but failed to improve and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified nodules and thickening of some of the ribs. Digits and other bones were normal. A scirrhous reaction was present around a transponder site.

PNEUMOCONIOSIS WITH PARENCHYMAL ATROPHY ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 4.5-year-old female chicken has a two year history of reproductive disease and a previous obstruction of the oviduct was removed surgically but has been recurring. The bird has experienced weight loss over the last three months and was sedated for a full exam but did not recover from anesthesia. Necropsy revealed severely congested lungs did not float in formalin and impaction in the oviduct with associated coelomitis.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY HEPATOCELLULAR TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 29-year-old male lemur had a recent history of lethargy and moribund condition. While receiving supportive care it was noted that the animal had an abdominal mass and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed roughened internal aortic surface and large abdominal mass that did not appear to be associated with the liver but encompassed the right kidney. The mass had a thick capsule and friable dark red material on cut surface.

PULMONARY ABSCESS POOR DENTITION ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) UROGENITAL INFLAMMATION VASCULITIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male reindeer initially presented with lameness involving three legs. Subsequently the reindeer developed coughing and dyspnea and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed abscessation in a lung field. One of the upper left cheek teeth was displaced and severe periodontal disease was noted.

CARDIOMYOPATHY ENDOGENOUS LIPID PNEUMONIA TRUE HERMAPHRODITISM. This female approximately 3-year-old opossum was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy the foot pads were thickened and had numerous sores especially the right foot. There was yellow mottling throughout the lung parenchyma. There was free serosanguineous within the pleural cavity. There was foamy exudate within pulmonary airways. There was a thick mass with fibrous yellow strands within the atrium. The left adrenal gland was enlarged. There was approximately 10-15 ml. of hazy orange peritoneal fluid. The liver was very enlarged pale and had a prominent reticular pattern. The opossum was possibly a hermaphrodite. There was normal uterus but appeared to have seminal vesicles and a bifurcated penis.
NA

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE MYELINIC EDEMA AND AXONAL DEGENERATION POSTOPERATIVE PERITONITIS. This 12-year-old male capybara has a history of liquid diarrhea of one year’s duration and also some mild ataxia in the rear limbs. No etiologic agents could be associated with the diarrhea. Endoscopic mucosal biopsies were obtained but the endoscope perforated the colon so laparotomy was performed to repair the perforation. The animal recovered from the procedure but died overnight. Necropsy revealed fair body condition and a 2 cm. in diameter firm round nonhaired mass rising from the surface of the skin over the left elbow and on cut surface was tan/yellow. Brown opaque malodorous fluid was free in the abdomen and no open perforation sites were seen. The suture sites from the surgical procedure were intact. The hepatic parenchyma was friable.

EUTHANASIA ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA ATELECTASIS VACUOLAR DEGENERATION. This 10-year-old female bat was found on the floor of the exhibit. The animal was isolated but began self-trauma of the left wing. The abdomen was distended and contained a firm mass on palpation. Frank blood was noted in the feces and a fecal occult blood test was positive. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. At necropsy the uterus was markedly enlarged and filled with brownish cloudy fluid. Polypoid masses protrude into the uterine lumen.

EUTHANASIA NEUROENDOCRINE CARCINOMA (THROAX ABDOMEN) HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS INANITION. This 24-year-old male ring-tailed lemur was euthanized due to the presence of a large mass in the anterior thorax. Another large mass was present in the anterior two-thirds of the abdomen. At necropsy marked tooth wear was noted. A 3 in. diameter mass was present caudal to the liver and stomach. Many adhesions were present to the adjacent intestine and left kidney. The mass was firm and dark red on section. Small cystic masses were present on the margin of the left liver lobe. A small concretion was present in the gall bladder. A 2 in. diameter firm red mass was present in the anterior thorax which displaced the heart caudally.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE SPINAL TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male naked mole rat incurred a traumatic fracture or luxation of the lumbar spine with associated hind limb paralysis.
