An abrasion was also noted on the left flank with bruising around the site of the injury. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hemoabdomen and hemothorax.

AMYLOIDOSIS SEPSIS PODODERMATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male ringed teal had a chronic history of neurological disease that included unsteadiness and inability to swing. It had done well on soft substrate in a shallow pool for several months but two days prior to euthanasia had progressively worsened. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. It had been treated in the past with antiparasitic drugs with no change in neurologic signs. Necropsy revealed an infected right digit #1.

SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 1-year-old female parakeet was apparently healthy prior to being found dead. It was housed in a flight cage in an outdoor aviary. It is the first in a series of peracute avian deaths in this exhibit. Necropsy revealed dark hemorrhagic lungs.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA WITH ENDOTOXEMIA CATARACT. This 7-year-old male captive bred wallaby had a 48 hour history of illness died spontaneously and was refrigerated 24 hours prior to necropsy. The animal presented with depression and coughed up blood on day 2. The animal developed a seizure approximately 30 seconds prior to cardiac arrest. The wallaby had a history of chronic head tilt following a previous episode of toxoplasmosis. Necropsy revealed severe hemorrhagic pneumonia and cataract.

FRACTURED FEMUR EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male antelope had a fractured femur and was euthanized. A comminuted spiral fracture of the right femur was noted and associated with severe muscle damage. All organs were grossly normal.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS RENAL GOUT BACTERIAL VENTRICULITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 11-year-old male burrowing owl has a history of a chronic mass above the left eye but was otherwise normal and died unexpectedly. The animal was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed a mass on the left superior eyelid. Some opaque flat plaques in the air sacs resembling adipose tissue abundant intracoelomic fat minimal gastric contents mottled liver dark ingesta in the small intestine mottled kidneys and no other remarkable findings.

ULCERATIVE DIGITAL CELLULITIS ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA THYROID ANOMALY (POSSIBLE GOITER) EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female Jamaican fruit bat was found on the floor of the exhibit hypothermic and minimally responsive with bruising on the rostral ventral mandible and leading wing edges. Several interphalangeal joints have decreased range of motion. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS. This 25-year-old male ring-tailed lemur has a history of chronic hepatopathy with normal bile acids and enzymes but with acute inflammatory hepatitis episodes in the past that have responded to antibiotics. The animal has also had multiple fractures believed to be traumatic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed an unusual large auricle or appendage attached to the heart.

GRANULOMATOSIS GOUT. This 6-year-old male green tree monitor had no recent medical problems other than a preference for crickets in the diet over the last seven days. The animal was found dead. Necropsy revealed a mild amount of serosanguineous and tenacious fluid in the pharynx empty alimentary tract prominent fat pads mottled pale purple spleen 4 ml. of orange clear colored fluid cranial to the left kidney and firm kidneys with white miliary striations.

MYELOGENOUS LEUKEMIA AND MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE. This approximately 3-year-old female African hedgehog had a three day history of inappetence with diarrhea and green-tinged urine. Examination revealed icterus splenomegaly severely elevated hepatic enzymes severe leukocytosis and neutrophilia (approximately 85% neutrophils). Exploratory laparotomy was performed in an attempt to exteriorize the spleen and the organ split in half. The animal arrested during surgery and could not be revived. Necropsy revealed icteric mucous membranes and viscera 1 mm. black nodule in the lungs diffusely thickened liver with rounded edges and diffuse green mottling throughout the parenchyma friable spleen green staining kidneys greenish staining gastrointestinal tract and 1 cm. firm white mass in the uterus attached to a stalk in the uterine horn.

CIRRHOSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION. This 18-year-old female rattlesnake had a two year history of ascites and subcutaneous edema that did not respond to supportive care and the cause could not be determined. The snake continued to have a good appetite until it was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous edema in the lateral body wall cranial to the vent and bilaterally over the ventral head and neck some blood in the oral cavity a large amount of clear fluid in all coelomic spaces moderate amount of clear pericardial fluid a mild amount of subcapsular clear fluid in the liver a large amount of intraluminal fluid in the colon a cobblestone pale brown appearance to the liver multiple active ovarian follicles a single mottled pink mass in the left adrenal gland 1.5 cm. in greatest dimension and moderate to heavy white streaking in the kidneys.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE SEPSIS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS EMACIATION. This 3-year-old female pygmy marmoset presented one week earlier for lethargy and a swollen face. Trauma was identified and several teeth were extracted. The animal received supportive care but deteriorated and died. Necropsy revealed ascites pleural and pericardial effusions peritonitis with adhesions loose molars in the upper left dental arcade hard feces in the intestine and colon possible rupture of the intestine just cranial to the cecum bilaterally pale kidneys and subjectively enlarged adrenal glands. Some possible petechiae were noted over the brainstem and cerebrum.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA MATURE CATARACTS ABOMASITIS. This 7-year-old female gazelle had a several-year history of hypocalcemia. The animal had been repeated treated for endoparasites. Bilateral cataracts were noted. Serum calcium levels were normalized by daily calcium injections; however these were discontinued and calcium levels continued to decline. The animal was found down stuporous and had an open rostral mandibular fracture. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy a 1 x 0.5 cm. ovoid cystic structure was present anterior to the left thyroid gland presumed to represent an enlarged parathyroid. Bilateral mature cataracts were noted. In addition to the mandibular fracture closed fractures were noted in the right first two ribs. A large blood clot was noted adjacent to the right hepatic lobe.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 5-year-old female pronghorn antelope presented with pitting ventral edema low albumin and weight loss but had normal appetite. Numerous fecal exams acid-fast stains Johne’s PCR test and cultures were negative. The animal had resolution of edema one year ago and albumin had increased then decreased repeatedly during the last two years. This animal received a number of different antimicrobials and antiparasitic drugs and feces would vary from normal to soft. Four days prior to death the antelope seemed quieter than normal and other pronghorn in the same herd also were eating less and their exhibit was covered with fallen oak leaves and on the day of death the animal was up with the herd in the morning was sitting sternally just before lunch and was found lateral and died at 2 PM. Necropsy identified no evidence of trauma slightly reduced body condition no palpable subcutaneous fluid buildup or emphysema hemorrhagic fluid resembling urine in the caudal end of the animal normal oral cavity and good teeth. The thoracic cavity was normal except for a 1.25 cm. focus near the apex of the heart that was paler than the rest of the myocardium. No ascites were noted in the abdominal cavity. The entire abdominal cavity had an orange/yellow appearance the duodenum was subjectively thickened the ileum was slightly thickened numerous diverticula were noted with loss of mucosal surface and persistence of possibly only the serosal surfaces in the jejunum. Some raised nodules were also noted in the jejunum.

MILD MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male wild turkey had a history of chronic lameness that did not respond to pain medications and antibiotics or stall rest and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Prior to euthanasia the patient had increased laxity in the left digit #3 tarsometatarsal-phalangeal joint and a dislocated right digit #3. Necropsy revealed fair body condition swollen kidneys especially the caudal pole of the right kidney and joint surfaces were grossly normal.
adult. Weight: 71.9 g.  Open.  Suspect drowned.  Hepatomegaly.

VACUOLAR NEUROPATHY (WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME) NEPHROSCLEROSIS CARDIAC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION THYROID ADENOCARCINOMA METASTATIC ABDOMINAL CARCINOMA. This 3.5-year-old male hedgehog has a several week history of progressive spasticity and problems using the rear limbs with inability to right itself or to ambulate. The animal became progressively weaker and unstable and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. This condition did not respond to supportive care including assisted feedings and vitamin E supplementation. At necropsy the right thyroid was darkened the left lung had caudal discoloration and the caudal brain was more fragile than normal. An apparent tumor was in the lower urinary or reproductive tract.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA FACIAL TISSUES EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female Mexican wolf had a one-week history of reverse sneezing. One day prior to death the animal was found lethargic inappetent and wheezing. Examination revealed an oronasal mass involving the palate enlargement of the left mandibular lymph node inflammation of the sclera and slight proptosis and elevated third eyelid. A CT scan with contrast revealed a mass in the right nasal cavity with bone destruction. This animal also has a history of calcinosis circumscripta on the paw and recently had a litter of pups six months prior to death. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed that the mass invaded the right maxillary cavity and sinuses extending from the canine to the eye and into the orbit.

MYELINIC EDEMA (BRAIN AND CORD) STRESS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS HEPATIC AND RENAL PIGMENT DEPOSITION. This 5-year-old female wood duck had been observed swimming “off kilter” with its right side facing down. The bird appeared to have right leg paresis when walking and would fall towards the right side. Mild to moderate pododermatitis was present but no other abnormalities were noted during examination. Supportive care was administered but the bird was observed falling over on its back. Blood work revealed anemia and a strongly positive Aspergillus titer. Sarcocystis falcatula titer was also moderately positive. The bird failed to improve over the next few weeks and laparoscopic exploratory examination was performed. The bird died during recovery from this procedure. Necropsy revealed thin body condition enlargements along the plantar aspects of both metatarsal pads and digits but no ulceration pinioned left wing some white striations in the epicardium a 3 mm. region of white discoloration along the left endocardial surface near the interventricular septum adipose in the coronary groove hemorrhage in both pulmonary lobes multiple round tan lesions on the serosal surface of the liver that did not extend into the hepatic parenchyma and a freely moveable lumbar vertebra (possible postmortem).

CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS SEPSIS DIABETES MELLITUS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 10-year-old male cotton-headed tamarin has a history of apparent diabetes mellitus with anemia. It presented immobile with a head tremor and was unable to stand. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition empty stomach multiple masses in the mesentery and enlarged kidneys.

PERIPHERAL AXONOPATHY POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE PNEUMONIA ENTEROCOLITIS. This 1-year/11-month-old frog of undetermined gender died. It was under treatment for swelling and nonuse of front legs. At necropsy the skin on the right side of the dorsal abdomen had a 1.5 x 0.2 cm. bruise. There was 3.5 cc. of clear fluid in the coelomic cavity. The gastrointestinal tract was empty except for the colon which contained firm feces. The stomach appeared firm and swollen. The wall of the stomach seemed thickened. Both kidneys were diffusely nodular with clear cyst-like structures. On section the noncystic portions of the kidney were uniform in color. The kidneys may have been larger than normal.

Uterus: Moderate cystic endometrial hyperplasia; adenomyosis; moderate mucometra; and moderate suppurative endometritis Ovaries: Multiple corpora lutea and follicles Cervix and vagina: Moderate squamous metaplasia with severe ulcerative vaginitis Comment: The most severe inflammation was in the area of the vagina. The uterine lesions were less inflammatory; but there was prominent adenomyosis and neutrophils largely contained within the endometrial stroma. A specific cause for the severe vaginitis was not apparent. Uterine lesions are common in big cats which are cycling and do not conceive or which are treated with some contraceptives. Interestingly; the endometrial epithelium in this animal was not typical of a diestral or progestational epithelium; but more suggestive of an estrogenic stimluation. Similarly; the marked keratinization and squamous metaplasia of the cervix was more suggestive of an estrogenic stimulus. Follicle were prominent; but it is difficult to ascertain whether they were long-standing or not in a necropsy sample. Adrenal or other hormonally active neoplasia might also be a source of estrogen. Intromission may also be a cause of vaginitis; though no sperm were seen in any sections. This animal's tissue and data will be a part of the AZA Reproductive Health Surveillance Program

OSTEOMYELITIS GLOSSITIS. This 1-year-old female chameleon was found on the cage floor. The animal has a recent history of maxillary abscess. At necropsy the abscess was present extending to the maxilla. A small mass was identified on the tongue. Marked postmortem autolysis was noted.

EUTHANASIA LEUKOENCEPHALOMALACIA PERITONITIS EXOCRINE PANCREATIC HYPERPLASIA. This 15-year-old male otter was humanely euthanized. This otter had a history of decreased activity for several weeks. It later became polydyspneic and continued to be anorexic. Antibiotics were administered with some improvement in activity level and appetite. Several weeks later the otter again became anorexic and lethargic. There was marked chemosis +/- prolapse of the third eyelid. The otter had mature cataracts OU and the left eye had marked chemosis of the third eyelid moderate mucopurulent ocular discharge and mild corneal edema. The otter also had severe dental disease and the left upper carnassial and right lower canine were extracted. The sockets and abscess pocket were flushed with dilute chlorhexidine solution and packed with gel foam. Thoracic radiographs revealed consolidation and air bronchograms in the area of the right middle lung lobe. Skull radiographs confirmed tooth root abscess of the left upper carnassial tooth. Antibiotics and supportive care were administered. The otter was slow to recover from anesthesia. Over a several day period the otter continued to be lethargic and anorexic and abdominal exploratory surgery was performed. No obvious masses or obstructions were seen. The intestines were hyperemic mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and there were white nodules in the pancreas and liver that were biopsied. Biopsy results indicated pancreatic acinar adenoma multiple liver hepatomas with fatty change lymphangiectasia and no significant kidney lesions. Postabdominal exploration the otter continued to be lethargic and anorexic and was euthanized. At necropsy the otter was thin and had sunken eyes. Inflammation was noted around the area of the abdominal incision both internally and externally. There were adhesions of mesentery to the pancreas and surrounding intestines and kidneys. There was yellow cloudy fluid present at the biopsy sites. The pancreas had multiple firm white/pink nodules throughout its parenchyma. There were multiple 1-3 mm. white nodules throughout all liver lobes. There was a 2 cm. cyst in the left liver lobe. The mitral valve leaflets were slightly thickened. Both cranioventral lung lobes were dark and had white firm nodules. The right caudal lung lobe was also darkened.

MANDIBULAR OSTEOMYELITIS WITH OSTEOMYELITIS WITH ASPIRATION HEPATOMA EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female captive bred Bennett’s wallaby was euthanized following a one week history of decreased appetite and swelling of the left mandible. Radiographs revealed a severe osteomyelitis. At necropsy there were large amounts of green purulent rancid material within the soft tissues and bone surrounding the left mandible and within the mandibular bone. There was a 5 cm. x 3 cm. firm tan loculated mass within the liver.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PULMONARY ABSCESSES GASTRIC ABSCESS SEPSIS EMACIATION ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS. This 15-year-old female warthog was found recumbent and could not rise. The previous day she had been on exhibit and doing relatively well. The animal died approximately 10 min. after first detected in lateral recumbency. The warthog had been on a quality of life watch due to ataxia lack of appetite and weight loss. Two days prior to death she had exhibited more energy and appetite than in previous weeks. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with prominent ribs and pelvis minor abrasions over several bony protuberances at least one liter of blood-tinged fluid in the abdomen 100 ml. of straw-colored pericardial fluid in the thoracic cavities partially calcified or gritty thyroid gland numerous cysts in the left kidney and three firm white 2 mm. masses beneath the capsule of the right kidney. The liver had a nutmeg appearance with rounded margins. Some white mottling and gritty texture was noted in the spleen. Too many cysts to count were in the endometrium of the uterus and cysts were also in the infundibula. The edges of the lungs were heavy wet and had numerous tan firm masses up to 3 cm. in greatest dimension. Numerous ulcers were in the gastric mucosa. The mucosa of the cecum colon and rectum was edematous. Numerous firm tan nodules were on the right atrioventricular valve leaflets and numerous hemorrhages were on the endocardium of the right ventricle. Serous atrophy of fat was noted in the cardiac groove.

FRACTURE SHOCK ANESTHETIC DEATH CROP CANDIDIASIS BACTERIAL FOLLICULITIS. This 10-year-old male cockatiel had been undergoing treatment for self-trauma in the axillary region. The animal became nonweight bearing on the left hind limb. The animal was anesthetized and oblique mid-diaphyseal fracture was identified that was associated with an abscess. The fracture was also associated with two small puncture wounds. The animal arrested under anesthesia. At necropsy there was hemorrhage in the thoracic cavity suspected to be from resuscitation efforts. There were swelling bruising and erythema around the left tarsometatarsus with caseous material extruding from the lesion.

CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA HEPATITIS INANITION. This greater than 6-year-old female teal died. It had a history of treatment for possible chlamydiosis in 1998 and possible frostbite in January 2000. At necropsy the bird was thin with moderate to severe pectoral musculature wasting. The eyes were sunken and dehydrated. There was free blood present in the abdominal cavity and a large blood clot was present on the anterior surface of the left liver lobe. The liver was pale severely enlarged and had multiple masses in all lobes.

MENINGIOMA PAPILLOMATOSIS ERYTHROID CONSUMPTIVE ANOMALY EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female snow leopard has a two month history of neurologic signs with more recent loss of appetite and lethargy exercise intolerance and reduced activity levels. The animal did not respond to supportive care continued to decline and radiographs revealed a possible abnormality in the brain. The animal had a hematocrit of 10% or less and was severely dehydrated and constipated. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed abundant adipose tissue yellow liver with small round bumps pale kidneys two or three small clumped scarred areas of tissue in the lungs much fluid in the pericardium possibly enlarged thyroid small white bumps under the tongue and along the mucosa of the throat and a small round firm nodule seen in the center of the brain. Green/brown mucosa was noted at the dorsal caudal edge of the turbinates with associated brown exudate.

HISTIOCYTIC HEPATITIS XANTHOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 16.5-year-old female gecko began passing blood from the cloaca. A mass was identified in the coelomic cavity. The animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy a large pale mass was present in the liver.

COELOMITIS CLOACITIS OOPHORITIS. This 2-year-old female parrot was found dead. At necropsy a partially calcified eggshell was noted in the caudal coelom. Urate stasis was noted in the ureter and kidney.

TRAUMA ANESTHETIC DEATH MIGRATING NEMATODES. This 7-year-old female crocodile monitor sustained trauma from a conspecific male. She had abundant lacerations including full thickness lacerations on her ventrum with prolapse of coelomic tissues. She was anesthetized for surgical repair of her lacerations and never regained consciousness despite approximately seven hours of ventilation following anesthesia. At necropsy she was in good body condition. Numerous wounds were identified most of which were full thickness. A focal area of intestines was dark red.

EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (ORAL CAVITY LYMPH NODE LUNG) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 17-year-old female tiger had a prior history of mammary adenocarcinoma and chronic lymphoplasmacytic colitis. Recently a soft tissue mass was identified on the soft palate identified as a squamous cell carcinoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large mass with necrotic material was present effacing the soft palate and caudal oral cavity and tongue. Nodular masses were present within the lung and a cervical lymph node.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA STRESS. This greater than 16-year-old female horn frog shed normally on 7/31 but then became bloated and minimally responsive on 8/1 and was found dead that evening. Blood work showed a BUN=102.5 mg/dl and calcium less than 5 mg/dl albumin 0.8 gm/dl. Necropsy revealed hepatomegaly pale cardiac muscle a large amount of subcutaneous edema free serosanguineous fluid in the coelomic cavity renomegaly inflamed small intestinal mucosa.

CHRONIC COLITIS WITH SCARRING ACUTE ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 26-year-old female python became impacted and died before surgery could be performed. Necropsy revealed a pseudodiverticulum and possible incomplete perforation at the point of impaction and some old ovarian follicles. The liver was irregular and possibly neoplastic.

PARASITIC AND BACTERIAL GRANULOMAS. This female 3-year/11-month-old toad was found dead in its enclosure. The toad had not eaten in three weeks. Its front toes were worn off on the rocks. At necropsy the toad was emaciated. There was exposed bone on the toes. There were possible ectopic eggs or nematode granulomas over the serosal surfaces. There were large cranial lung lobe abscesses in the right lung.

INTESTINAL PERFORATION/IMPACTION GASTRIC EROSIONS SEPSIS. This 5-year-old male capybara was found dead. It was clinically normal on the same day. Necropsy revealed a puncture wound to 4 cm. wide in the ventral mandible superficial abrasions on both flanks froth in the trachea small ulcers in the mucosa of the stomach a focus of red discoloration in the duodenal flexure that is sharply demarcated from remaining intestine. The mucosa in this area is eroded and surrounded by fibrin. A hard bolus of food is in the lumen of the intestine at this location. Fibrin is present on multiple hepatic lobes and the gallbladder is severely distended with bile.
SHOCK DROWNING. This 2-year-old male bat was found dead in the exhibit pool. At necropsy a small wound was noted in the skin overlying the skull. Hemorrhagic fluid was noted in the thoracic cavity.

NECROTIZING LARYNGITIS SEPSIS GLOMERULONEPHRITIS OBESITY CHOLELITHIASIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 8.5-year-old male golden lion tamarin died unexpectedly and had no recent illness or problems. The animal had been active in the morning and was found dead at midmorning check. This animal had normal appetite and behavior prior to death. Necropsy revealed some nodularity in the pancreas gastric distention but no evidence of obstruction. A plug of digesta in the cecum with no associated perforation prominent veins on the surface of the cerebrum and possible enlargement or congestion of the liver.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS SPINDLE CELL SARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old female rattlesnake had a history of flaccid paresis of the caudal half of the body and associated with distention of the colon. More recently it developed neurologic signs that manifested as behavioral abnormalities and also some subcutaneous edema was noted. Salmonella cholerasuis arizonae was cultured from the blood and treatment was initiated but with no improvement and worsening of the subcutaneous edema. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a pocket of subcutaneous fluid beneath the mandibles and the fluid was cloudy and slightly blood tinged. The caudal half of the coelom was flaccid and distended with a palpable fluid wave and cloudy blood-tinged subcutaneous fluid was present around the tail. Abundant adipose stores are present. A large amount of straw-colored fluid was within the coelomic cavity. The fluid clotted when the body cavity was opened. The thyroid glands were small round and firm. The right gland was dark blue and the left gland was cystic and clear. The heart muscle was diffusely pale with some red streaking. The pericardial sac contains similar straw-colored fluid as in the coelom. A single scar or infarct was present along the right border of the liver. The stomach was empty. A round white smooth firm mass was present within the mesentery adjacent to the pylorus. The colon contained normal formed fecal and urate material. The ovaries were inactive. Each ovary contained a small yellow irregular mass towards the cranial aspect and a round purple mass was on the left oviduct that was filled with blood when cut. Both kidneys had white streaks throughout the parenchyma.

PULMONARY EDEMA DUE TO SUSPECTED LEFT-SIDED CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY EUTHANASIA. This approximately 9-year-old female prairie dog had a history of corneal ulceration and exophthalmos in the left eye. The animal was treated with tarsorrhaphy and extraction of two premolars on the left maxilla. The animal became inappetent dyspneic and was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed subcutaneous edema a large blood clot in the chest cavity a thickened right caudal pulmonary lobe miliary white spots throughout the liver pale and tan kidneys and abundant fat stores.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 14-year-old female cottontop tamarin had an exploratory laparotomy approximately four months prior to death. This revealed neoplasia in the right ovary. The animal had been normal since the time of surgery. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. A large mass was present anterior to the left kidney. Abdominal fat bodies were absent.

HYPERKERATOSIS SKIN. This 9-year-old female fox had a cutaneous neoplasia in the perineal and inguinal areas. Chemotherapeutics had been used; however lameness and progression of lesions were noted and the animal was humanely euthanized.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE THYROID FOLLICULAR CYSTIC ECTASIA. This 20-year-old male red panda was being treated for distal tail necrosis and had two amputations done. The animal had recently displayed significant hind limb weakness without proprioceptive deficits and also had poor appetite. It had received three daily oral doses of meloxicam recently with no response. Its clinical condition deteriorated slowly and radiographs revealed possible reduced disk space at T10-T11. Blood work revealed low calcium and mild anemia. A chronic lesion of the proximal coccygeal vertebra had progressed to bony proliferation and possible fusion of two adjacent vertebrae. The tail tip had become necrotic again. The animal had significant weight loss and had been treated with high doses of dexamethasone for 24 hours with no improvement had become unable to stand up empty its bladder or eat. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with muscle mass atrophy absence of several teeth necrotic tail tip bilaterally enlarged and cystic thyroid glands containing brownish fluid spotty black pigmentation on the surface of the pulmonary lobes bile distended gallbladder moderate amount of ingesta and fecal material in the alimentary tract urine distended bladder several small to moderately-sized cortical cysts in the left kidney and many small to large cortical cysts in the right kidney.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL PLEUROPNEUMONIA. This male 8-year-old wallaby was humanely euthanized. It was noted to have a white discharge from the right nostril and both eyes were tearing excessively. Physical exam revealed weight loss. Blood work was positive for Toxoplasma anemia elevated hepatic values and metabolic alkalosis. Treatment was initiated but the wallaby continued to decline. Recheck blood work revealed little improvement. At necropsy the wallaby was emaciated. All ribs and vertebrae were visible. There were patches of matted fur on the ventrum and rear end. There was evidence of ocular discharge bilaterally. There was very little muscle mass and no fat stores present. The heart was large and flabbier than expected. Both ventricular walls were thin. All lung lobes had multifocal nodules some of which were cystic and some were granulomatous. The liver was enlarged with uneven edges and appeared white in many areas. There were small granulomas on cut surface. The spleen was grossly enlarged and mottled purple/white. The mesenteric lymph nodes appeared reactive.

DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION EU. This 21-year-old male collared peccary had a hemilaminectomy performed on the left side of L5-L6 due to chronic degenerative joint disease. A large amount of chronic disk material was removed. The animal was initially stable but started to decline in use of its hind limbs necessitating euthanasia approximately two weeks later. Necropsy revealed mildly thin body condition healed incision site with no evidence of drainage mild congestion in the right lung early cataract formation a seroma in the region of the hemilaminectomy site and bilaterally luxated patellas.

THYMOMA HYPERSENSITIVITY DERMATITIS EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male goat has a previous history of hypersensitivity dermatitis and a recent history of excised hemangiosarcoma in the perirenal area. It recently has tested serologically positive for Mycobacterium paratuberculosis and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a mass in the mediastinum.

VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC UROCYSTITIS EUTHANASIA. This 20.5-year-old female snow leopard had a history of chronic renal failure and intermittent episodes of cystitis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation matted and unkempt haircoat tacky subcutis congestion of the right lung perimortem aspiration in the trachea moderate mitral valve endocardiosis nodular marbled liver with a 2 cm. in diameter mineralized lesion on the edge of one lobe small kidneys with hemorrhagic streaking on cut surface and a few gold calculi in the pelvis of one kidney and congestion of this kidney. Both ovaries had cysts and the uterus was quiescent. One caudal mammary gland was firm and darkly pigmented. One thyroid was identified and the associated parathyroid was prominent.

TOOTH ROOT ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE AMYLOIDOSIS TRAUMA. This 6-year-old male meerkat was anesthetized the previous day for a large subcutaneous swelling of the left maxilla identified as a tooth root abscess. Dental extraction of the left maxillary premolar #2 was performed. The animal has a history of azotemia. The animal was normal following the procedure eating well and interactive but was found dead the next morning. Necropsy revealed good body condition some purulent discharge in a wound from the medial canthus of the left eye with a mild amount of swelling. Scant food material was in the dental extraction site. A clot associated with a linear fissure was on the surface of the liver and one lobe contained a 1 cm. dark red raised mass. A large amount of food material was in the stomach. The heart had a moderately thin right ventricular free wall and a moderately to severely thickened left ventricle.

AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION GOUT BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 19-year-old male flamingo was found dead on the ground in the morning. The remainder of the flock was clinically normal. Necropsy identified no evidence of trauma good body condition and good postmortem condition. Adequate adipose stores were noted in the coelom and ingesta were in the alimentary tract. No gross lesions were identified.

ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS PITUITARY HYPERPLASIA OR ADENOMA BILATERAL RETINAL DEGENERATION UNILATERAL GLAUCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male rabbit presented with ataxia and weakness in the front legs had some circling behavior first to the left and then to the right and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed adrenal asymmetry with the left larger than the right pale streaking in the left kidney one punctate focus observed on the capsular surface of the liver multiple white foci in the right lung and to a lesser extent in the left lung pale areas on the superior and inferior aspect of the iris of the left eye a corneal scar in the right eye and no other gross lesions.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female meerkat continued to lose weight in spite of various diet options and treats. It had a poor attitude and body condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal also had a seizure disorder and a several month history of head tilt and severe ataxia with vestibular symptoms.

TRAUMATIC LEG FRACTURE CATARACT MILD ENCEPHALITIS HEPATIC INFRACT. This 22-year-old female bat was found on the floor of the exhibit with an apparent broken leg and examination revealed a complete compound fracture of the tibia and fibula of the right leg. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This is the second bat in a week to develop a fracture and a third who has sustained an injury from falling. Necropsy revealed an open fracture of the right leg with bone extending through in two places. The carcass was obese. Miliary pale foci were in the liver. The adrenal glands were subjectively enlarged. A 1.5 cm. mass was adhered to the costal arch and also adhered to the intestine and liver. The mass was white encapsulated and with adipose tissue surrounding it. The mass had a caseous core.

SUPPURATIVE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MYCOPLASMOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 2-year-old male rat was emaciated and developed dyspnea. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. The caudal lung lobes were consolidated dark purple and small. A 3 x 3 x 4 mm. rounded dark red to purple mass was present on the aorta distal to the renal arteries.

OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA. This 2.5-year-old female chicken presented with acute onset of lethargy weight loss and decreased appetite. Radiographs revealed a distended coelom with free fluid. The chicken was found dead in its hospital cage. Necropsy revealed thin body condition fair postmortem condition markedly distended coelom 100 ml. of thin brown/orange colored fluid in the coelom and 8 cm. yellow/tan free-floating mass in the mid coelom yellow pasty material with a layered appearance on the cut surface of the mass markedly thickened air sac membranes and visceral surfaces with areas of nodularity 1 mm. white circular flat lesion on the capsular surface of the liver many adhesions of the gastrointestinal tract and coelomic viscera thickened intestinal walls with adhered intestinal loops many small ovarian follicles adhered to the coelomic viscera and spleen and pancreas could not be located due to the adhesions.

IRON STORAGE DISEASE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 2-year-old female Egyptian fruit bat had a five day history of abnormal behavior and location in the enclosure and had not been eating well. It subsequently died and necropsy revealed thin body condition a wound in the lower lip and slightly large liver with normal color but lobulated firm and slightly friable. The lungs had bubbles at the edges.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old female polar bear has a three week history of degenerative neurological signs and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severely thickened left ventricular wall. Kidneys were bilaterally moderately enlarged. The kidneys appeared fibrous in consistency.

HEPATIC RUPTURE DERMAL ULCERATION FROM LEG BAND. This approximately 10-year-old female scarlet ibis was found dead approximately one hour after feeding. Gross necropsy revealed erosion of a plastic leg band into the dermis and tendon with proliferation of tissue around the band pulmonary hemorrhage a large blood clot attached to the liver a smaller blood clot near the left kidney a 1 cm. fracture in the left hepatic lobe a pale liver and congested dorsal cerebral blood vessels.
PRESUMPTIVE TRAUMA SHOCK. This 4-year-old female bat was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

LYMPHOCYTIC GASTROENTERITIS LYMPHADENITIS EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS RENAL CYST. This 4-year-old female ferret was recently donated to the zoo. Multiple mast cell tumors were previously excised. The animal presented with marked weight loss and collapse. Treatment was initiated; however the animal became hyperthermic and died despite supportive care. At necropsy the animal was thin. The heart was rounded. The liver was pale and contained multiple white raised lesions.

TESTICULAR ATROPHY MESANGIAL GLOMERULOPATHY VISCERAL GOUT SOFT TISSUE MINERALIZATION. This 12-year-old male Sinaloan milk snake had a history of lethargy decreased appetite and elevated uric acid. The animal was found dead on March 12 2011. Gross necropsy revealed poor body condition white material on the surfaces of most viscera crystalline material and small white foci on the kidneys brown malodorous thick material in the cloaca and a small right gonad.
NA
CHRONIC POSTERIOR UVEITIS RETINAL SEPARATION ENTERITIS. This 13-year-old male leiothrix was humanely euthanized due to age chronic atrophy of the right eye and declining quality of life.

UROGENITAL CARCINOMA (PENIS) OCULAR TRAUMA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This approximately 14-year-old male California sea lion had a five day history of lethargy inappetence and reluctance to move. Blood results revealed elevated serum calcium and low sodium and chloride. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond. Follow-up blood work revealed markedly elevated white blood cell count and elevated serum calcium total protein globulin blood urea nitrogen and creatine. Neoplasia was suspected and the animal was anesthetized for examination but developed respiratory arrest and died. Necropsy revealed a slug from a .22 rifle on the dorsal cervical midline in the subcutaneous tissues reduced intra-abdominal adipose tissue dark brown sclera in the left eye with the globe rotated ventrally hazy cornea and a 3 mm. oval hole in the center. The right eye cornea was normally positioned but no anterior structures were visible and opaque blue discoloration was noted. The lungs bilaterally had scattered large cream-colored nodules up to 2 cm. in greatest dimension. Numerous parabronchial lymph nodes had caseous centers. The mediastinum was filled with small white nodules. Some areas of fibrosis were in the myocardium attributed to aging. A prominent venous hepatic sinus was noted just caudal to the liver. The sublumbar lymph nodes were markedly enlarged (up to 16 cm. in greatest dimension) these lymph nodes reaching into the pelvic canal and caudal to the kidneys. On cut surface the nodes were pale yellow and appeared caseous or fibrous. The pancreas was yellow/tan and semifirm. The gallbladder contained dark green fluid. Testicles were symmetrical. Soft tissues of the mid to distal penis were ulcerated red raised and had some areas of white roughened or thickened texture. The left kidney was congested and dark purple compared to the right kidney. A 3 mm. pink mass was in the mid cortex of one kidney.

RENAL ADENOCARCINOMA PERITONEAL FIBROSARCOMA WITH RENAL LYMPH NODE METASTASIS. This approximately 15-year-old male warthog was euthanized. It had a history of weight loss of about six month duration. It has had an extremely pendulous abdomen suggestive of tumor for about three weeks. At time of euthanasia the warthog had trouble getting up and showed extreme muscle wasting with very prominent ribs scapulas pelvis and spine. The appetite had remained good to ravenous throughout. At necropsy the entire body was emaciated with generalized muscle wasting. The abdomen was pendulous and tense with one large swelling 6 in. in diameter ventrally. There were moderate amounts of clear pericardial effusion. There was a large abscess subcutaneously on the ventral abdomen that contained large amounts of white pus and firm white tissue. Within the actual cavity was one extremely large mass approximately 14 lb. that contained a large amount of pus and more firm white tissue. The mass was partially adhered to the stomach wall and the spleen was entirely adhered to the mass. Two separate masses were found both oval in shape and about 4 in. in diameter. Both masses consisted of a capsule with a hollow center and easily separated lining. One mass was adhered to the proximal duodenum and had a very firm somewhat mineralized consistency. The second mass was adhered to the ileum and had a more fleshy consistency. Several smaller kidney shaped fleshy masses were also found adhered to different portions of the abdomen. The pancreas was firm pink and lobulated. Both kidneys were flecked with small white spots. Both kidneys contained multiple fluid filled cysts varying from about 0.1 in. to 0.5 in. Both kidneys also contained a number of firm white masses on the surface varying from 0.2 to 0.5 in. that were not raised. The right adrenal gland was relatively enlarged about 2 in. in length and 0.5 in. in diameter and had multiple cysts within the parenchyma. Aerobic and anaerobic cultures of purulent material were submitted.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 5.5-year-old female meerkat had a 10 day history of lethargy and radiographs revealed an enlarged heart. The animal was found dead in the water in the late afternoon. Necropsy revealed wet spongy lungs that floated in formalin enlarged spleen enlarged adrenals with red cortex a large amount of fluid in the stomach sparse fat stores increased amount of clear pleural fluid excessive amount of yellow/orange colored abdominal fluid enlarged liver with rounded edges enlarged and rounded heart and equally wide ventricular walls.

HEPATITIS DERMAL BACTERIAL GRANULOMA NEPHROSIS. This male approximately 7-year-old duck was found dead in children’s zoo duck pond. At necropsy there was a cutaneous mass at the right elbow joint (1.5 cm. diameter). There was poor muscle mass. The mucous membranes were pale yellow. The liver was markedly enlarged firm and mottled gray/brown-red/brown. The kidneys were gray/brown and mildly enlarged. There were white plaques on the external trachea at the syrinx. Sections of brain and kidney were frozen for future use if needed.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS INANITION. This 11-year/1-month-old male Guam rail was found dead in aviary. At necropsy it was in good body condition with normal plumage. The carcass was moderately autolyzed. The metatarsal pads on both feet had a central crust. There was some hyperkeratosis on the digits. There were multiple small nodular structures adjacent to the ribs that became evident after the lungs were removed. The spleen was pale. The lungs were bilaterally hyperemic. There were some small multifocal white plaques on the left abdominal air sac. The liver was slightly larger than expected. The right testis was twice as large as the left. Sections of liver were frozen for future use if needed. Cytology of liver was done.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS PROBABLY TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 5.5-year-old female ring-tailed lemur was being treated for presumed toxoplasmosis gradually deteriorated despite intensive treatment developed gas bloat that became life threatening and died during surgery. Necropsy revealed good body condition icterus mucous membranes consolidated lungs that did not float in formalin multiple irregular white to yellow foci in the bronchi bruising proximal to the base of the heart congested liver icteric omentum ecchymoses in the stomach multiple 1-2 mm. round to oval white to yellow raised firm lesions with irregular margins throughout the wall of the small intestine cecum colon and rectum. The mesenteric lymph node was enlarged. The descending colon in the area proximal to the rectum had gray/white discoloration. A mesenteric lymph node at the root of the mesentery was 5 cm. long 1 cm. wide yellow and firm. The spleen had multiple 0.5 mm. irregular pale areas on cut surface. Several pale striations were in the right thyroid gland. The left kidney had pale 3 mm. round foci and the right kidney had a 2 mm. depression in the cortex.

EUTHANASIA INGLUVITIS TRACHEITIS GLOSSITIS PROVENTRICULITIS CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. This greater than 5-year-old female junglefowl was humanely euthanized. This animal had been treated for suspected oral pox based on previous biopsy. Although the pox was slowly resolving with repeated radiocautery application to affected area the bird developed other problems including crop stasis diarrhea and weight loss. At necropsy there were yellow plaque-like lesions around the inside of the glottis. The lesions were limited to this area. The coelomic cavity was filled with green watery fluid resembling bile. The right liver lobe was enlarged green stained and nodular. The cut surface of the liver revealed multiple 2 mm. masses and a fibrous base to the entire lobe. The crop was filled with a very foul smelling material that also contained food items.

EUTHANSIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY CHRONIC PERITONITIS. This 6-year-old female hedgehog was humanely euthanized. It presented with a decreased appetite and hard abdomen. She was immobilized and worked up. The firm abdomen was caused by a large volume of blood tinged ascites. The fluid was sent for cytology and culture and the cytology revealed a moderate modified transudate with no evidence of infection/inflammation or neoplasia. The culture did not grow any bacteria. Exploratory surgery was done and about 140 cc. of blood tinged fluid was removed from the abdominal cavity. The only significant finding at necropsy was a smaller than expected liver and several renal cysts. A course of antibiotics was started but her condition continued to worsen. At necropsy the lungs were congested. There was euthanasia artifact in the heart. The liver appeared small for the body size. The kidneys appeared pale and had several cystic areas and a shallow cortex. The body was in good condition.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS CATARACT EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old duck was evaluated for lameness and decreased activity level of nine days duration. Examination revealed severe degenerative joint disease involving the right stifle and moderate to severe degenerative joint disease in the left stifle right intertarsal joint with lateral subluxation of the tibiotarsus. Supportive care was administered with initial improvement but then no further improvement and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition callus on the ventral keel with a 2 cm. mass on the cranial margin of the keel scant fat stores globoid enlarged spleen dark tan nodules throughout the parenchyma of the kidneys with associated urate stasis quiescent ovaries and the associated joint changes.

CHRONIC HETEROPHILIC AIR SACCULITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS HEPATITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 4.5-year-old turkey has had a swollen hock for several days. Labored respirations and lethargy were noted. Following a physical examination the bird was tachypneic. A moderate amount of fluid drained from the mouth. The bird was found dead. At necropsy there were 15 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the coelom. Mucopurulent exudate was present around the extensor tendon sheath of the hock. The liver was enlarged and had multifocal yellow discolorations.

GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old rattlesnake was euthanized due to chronic illness. Cryptosporidium has been noted on gastric wash. At necropsy gastric hyperplasia was present. The liver was pale yellow.

XANTHOMATOSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA INANITION. This 15-year-old female gecko was found dead. The animal had been under treatment with antibiotics and fluids. At necropsy white nodular masses were present throughout the coelomic cavity. The animal was thin.

EUTHANASIA HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA HYPERTROPHIC OSTEOPATHY. This male greater than 15-year-old lizard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of histiocytic sarcoma. Localized swelling of the left front limb was confirmed. At necropsy the left forelimb varied in swelling. All long bones were thickened with areas of exostosis. There were 2-3 mm. diameter white nodules within the wall of the heart ventricle.

EUTHANSIA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA STRESS. This 16-year-old female ibex was humanely euthanized due to advanced age and deteriorating condition. This animal was lethargic and anorexic over the past two days. It was straining to urinate frequently. At necropsy the ibex was in fair body condition. The uterus was markedly distended and contained about 8 liters of clear fluid. The right ovary contained some growing follicles and an old corpus luteum. The left ovary was small. The uterus cervix and oviducts were edematous. There were severe erosions of the femoral condyles of the right hind stifle joint. There were minimal erosions on the left stifle joint. There were erosions evident on the left front carpal joint. Sections of lung liver kidney and lymph nodes were frozen for future use if needed.

CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA LOW-GRADE SEPSIS. This 44-year-old male chimpanzee had a recent and ongoing history of neurologic signs and an extensive history of bite wounds that would periodically receive supportive care. Eight months prior to death the animal began holding its head at an angle with a very small head tremor. Two large maxillary fractures extended from the incisors to the molars on the left maxilla and these were removed surgically. Four months prior to death the animal was observed pressing its left jaw with its hand dropping food from its mouth and persistence of the head tremor with associated weight loss. More bone fragments were removed the jaw pressing was stopped but tremors increased in intensity. No other signs were observed. The animal was treated for Parkinson’s-like disorder with temporary regression of the tremors followed by relapse. The dose was manipulated several times but was no longer effective and the animal developed abdominal swelling followed by preputial scrotal and leg swelling. MRI of the head revealed no significant findings. Severe ascites and a hepatic mass were identified by CT scan. Thoracic ultrasound revealed severe thoracic effusion and moderate regurgitation of the right atrioventricular valve. One liter of transudative fluid was removed from each cavity and no growth was observed from culture of these fluids. Supportive care for heart failure was administered but the animal died three days later. Necropsy revealed thin body condition well healed maxillary fracture site moderate amount of transudative fluid in the abdominal and thoracic cavities fibrinous adhesions throughout the thoracic and abdominal cavities adhesions between the heart and the pericardial sac enlarged right atrium a clot or thrombus adhered to the right atrioventricular valve mass in the liver adjacent to but not invading the bile duct that was necrotic on cut surface a large fluid-filled cyst directly below the mass containing yellow transparent fluid and no other abnormalities.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA PROVENTRICULAR MACRORHABDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 8-year-old budgerigar was found on the floor and was easy to catch. It had lost weight had droopy wings and heavy respirations. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed decreased pectoral muscle mass a 1 cm. firm white ovoid mass in the region of the testicle and no other abnormalities.

RENAL GOUT SPONDYLOSIS AND AXONAL DEGERNERATION BILIARY HYPERPLASIA AND HEPATIC FIBROSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 13-year-old female rattlesnake presented one year prior to euthanasia for poor writhing reflex and inflexibility of the vertebral column. Ankylosing spondylosis was demonstrated in mid-body vertebrae to account for the inflexibility. The snake presented three weeks prior to euthanasia for regurgitation and similar skeletal problems and subsequent decline in body condition. Euthanasia was requested. Necropsy revealed spondylosis in the mid thoracic region empty alimentary tract and approximately 20 ml. of clear yellow jelled fluid in the caudal coelomic cavity. The kidneys were pale and engorged with visible urates.

EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA. This 2-year-old female rat was euthanized due to an upper respiratory infection which was unresponsive to antibiotics. At gross necropsy a soft tissue mass was associated with the left mandible and the incisors were broken and maloccluded.

INANITION ENCEPHALITIS ENTERITIS PANCREATITIS. This 1-year/2-month-old male lory was found dead. It had no premonitory clinical signs. At necropsy there was a small patch of feathers missing from the left side of the cranium. There was dried food on the beak and both feet. No fat stores were present in the body cavities. There was very little ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract. The meningeal vessels were congested and there were areas of small hemorrhage adjacent to the vessels.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 10-year-old male wallaroo had a history of weight loss. The animal was sedated to move to a new exhibit and anesthetic recovery was uneventful. Serum chemistry revealed renal disease and the animal became lethargic depressed and was found dead. At necropsy no significant gross lesions were identified.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ACUTE CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK STRESS. This approximately 10-year-old male captive bred kudu had a two day history of illness and died spontaneously. The animal had been inappetent and developed bloat on day #2. Blood work revealed neutrophilia and azotemia. It did not respond to therapy. Necropsy revealed severe enteritis with abomasal ulcers and friable bumpy masses in the right ventricle. Lungs were heavy and moist. Petechiae were present on many of the serosal surfaces. Approximately one liter of watery red fluid was in the thorax.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE/NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 18-month-old male was apparently healthy prior to being found dead. This group of animals includes three males and environmental temperatures have been low. There is possibly competition for food and shelter. Keepers have been adding bedding to the shelter which consists of hay from a hay barn which is occasionally inhabited by feral cats. Necropsy revealed severe serous atrophy of fat in the thoracic and abdominal cavities prominent adrenal glands and a small amount of watery ingesta in the forestomach.

NEPHROPATHY FATTY LIVER HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 11-year/10-month-old male owl was found in its enclosure. It had a recent history of decreased alertness and suspected CNS disease. At necropsy the owl was in good body condition. The liver was friable red to copper and mottled with rounded edges. The kidneys were very pale tan and enlarged. There was a cyst on the caudal part of the right kidney.

Coelomic cavity: Mesothelial proliferation with yolk aggregates (suggestive of yolk coelomitis) Liver: Moderate melanomacrophage center hyperplasia Comments The histologic findings were most consistent with a florid mesothelial proliferation within the coelomic cavity and covering the surface of multiple coelomic organs. The presence of yolk associated with the areas of mesothelial proliferation was suggestive of an underlying yolk coelomitis. Yolk coelomitis is a well-recognized problem and a significant cause of death in captive adult female lizards; particularly Fiji Island Iguanas (see Stacy et al; J Zoo Wildl Med. 2008 Jun;39(2):161-9.Yolk coelomitis in Fiji Island banded iguanas (Brachylophus fasciatus).The proliferative mesothelial cell population was considered to be a reactive response to free intracoelomic yolk based on the signalment (mature female). The basis for the florid mesothelial response is not known; however it is thought to be influenced by the volume of yolk present ant the chronicity of coelomitis. Jennifer Lamoureux; D

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE MENINGOENCEPHALITIS. This 4-year-old male red panda was reportedly within normal limits in the morning and was found dead in the afternoon. The animal had a positive occult heartworm test in April 2004 but subsequent tests at other labs were negative. In May 2004 the animal was worked up for cardiac enlargement and possible cardiomyopathy. The animal had an abdominal modified transudate. The animal has been healthy throughout this time with occasional episodes of loose stool. The stool was within normal limits prior to death. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no external abnormalities. The right ventricle of the heart is possibly mildly dilated. No parasites are seen in the heart or lungs.

EUTHANASIA BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL CYSTS. This 24-year-old male lemur presented with weakness depression and vomiting. A large mass was identified in the anterior abdomen. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy an 8 x 5 cm. firm round mass was present in the middle hepatic lobe. Fluid filled cysts were noted adjacent to the left kidney.

MAXILLARY SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female Grévy’s zebra had a history of a mass in the right axilla and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 15 cm. in length maxillary tumor that on cut surface had cartilaginous texture. Abscesses were present dorsal to the dental arcade and hay was packed into a penetrating wound caudal to the incisors on the right side. Proliferative bone had penetrated through the gums at this site. The caudal sulcus of the nasal passage had a coating of dry white material. One ovary was 50% larger than the other and the large ovary had a cystic structure filled with yellow clear gelatinous material. A soft tan mass to 5 cm. in length was also noted. A 1 cm. yellow mass was in the smaller ovary. Both kidneys had cysts 1-3 cm. in diameter some of which were filled with viscous flocculent material.

SHOCK PROBABLE HEAD TRAUMA. This 16-year-old female reticulated giraffe had no prior history of illness and appeared to be in good health. When it was called in for the night it slipped going down a hill to the barn. The animal fell into lateral recumbency tried to get up once or twice and could not. After a few attempts to rise the giraffe remained lateral. The veterinarian arrived within eight minutes of the fall and pronounced the animal dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition congested lungs adequate fat stores a ruminal lith 6-8 cm. in diameter active ovarian follicles some hemorrhage around the base of the cerebellum and in the white matter throughout the brain and pale hind limb musculature.

SPINAL CORD DEGENERATION TOXIC HEPATOPATHY DYSBIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male European rabbit had a few week history of ataxia possible vision problems large wounds in the hind end received supportive care and appeared to improve but then became stressed during blood collection with labored breathing trembling and an increase in severity of neurologic signs. The rabbit tested negative for Encephalitozoon. The animal failed to respond fully to treatment and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed some free fluid in the abdomen fluid-filled and edematous gastrointestinal tract a small amount of pericardial fluid and no other findings.

TRAUMA COELOMIC HEOMRRHAGE INTRAMUSCULAR HEMORRHAGE INANITION. This 14-year-old male kingsnake recently escaped from its enclosure and was missing for several weeks. The animal was recovered on grounds and was treated for wounds ataxia and a lack of righting reflect but later died. At necropsy scale damage and wounds were noted over the ventrum. An area of hemorrhage was noted in the liver. The kidneys contained white streaks.

SMALL CELL LYMPHOMA PULMONARY ADENOCARCINOMA EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 17.5-year-old male North American river otter had been losing weight for several months and had lost approximately 50% of its body weight. Supportive care was administered the animal appeared to be eating but continued to lose body weight and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation with muscle atrophy minimal to no adipose stores pulmonary congestion pale pancreas large mesenteric lymph node enlarged right adrenal gland compared to the left adrenal gland multiple foci of pallor in the liver adhesion of the right adrenal gland to the vena cava mineralization in the spleen a small amount of purulent discharge in the pylorus and multiple dark masses noted around the tracheobronchial region. Multiple nodules were in all pulmonary lobes up to 10 mm. in greatest dimension.
See elephant paper

SEPSIS DIC. This 2-year-old female Gaboon viper was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the skin where ulcers or blisters were present. The pancreas and spleen were firm and difficult to cut. The stomach was pale white. Blood tinged fluid was around the reproductive tract and kidneys and petechiae were in some of the organs. The kidneys were discolored yellow to orange and covered in thick mucus.

RENAL AND ARTICULAR GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old frilled lizard was noted to have swollen stifle joints attributed to gout although this diagnosis was not confirmed. The animal recently declined and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Clutchmates are all clinically normal. Necropsy revealed bilateral swelling of the stifle joints the right more severe than the left. Both femurs were broken with little effort. Male reproductive tract was identified. Kidneys appear to have severe gout. Both tarsi had gout.

METASTATIC CHONDROSARCOMA VERTEBRAL SPINDLE CELL SARCOMA ADRENAL TUMOR ISLET CELL TUMOR RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA PROLIFERATIVE DUODENITIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male gopher snake had been previously diagnosed with a spinal chondrosarcoma (G14-5974). The snake also developed a renal mass identified at the time. The chondrosarcoma recurred and the snake became increasingly lethargic with poor muscle tone to the caudal half of the body. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an additional spinal mass cranial to the first mass on the coelomic sign of the spine and ribs. A renal mass was confirmed. The liver contained a 10 mm. and several 5 mm. masses in the parenchyma.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE ATHEROSCLEROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 19-year-old female Humboldt penguin was found dead on the bottom of the penguin pool and had been seen alive one hour earlier. The bird was currently molting and had no significant prior clinical issues. Necropsy revealed serosanguineous coelomic fluid thickened coelomic air sacs and inactive ovaries.

EUTHANASIA RENAL MYXOSPORIDIOSIS. This male 4-year-old wallaby was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic lumpy jaw infection severe bilateral arthritis of the hocks and suspected coagulopathy. At necropsy there was bony callous formation on the left mandible. Upon sectioning of the liver spleen and heart it was apparent that the blood had not clotted adequately and easily poured from the organs. The lungs appeared red and mottled/hemorrhagic. The stomach was full of food material. In the distal colon there were fecal pellets and a moderate amount of blood.

THRYOID ADENOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATIC CESTODIASIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 18-year-old ewe exhibited frothing in the nose and mouth collapsed and died. At necropsy the heart was pale and brown with white streaks. Liver was friable and contained a parasitic cyst. A large mass was present near the thyroid.

COELOMIC SARCOMA GOUT BACTERIAL SEPSIS. This 13-year-old male bull snake had weight loss and anorexia of approximately one year’s duration and regurgitation over the last few months prior to death. The snake died spontaneously and necropsy revealed emaciation and masses in the fat body and liver. The pericardium epicardium and kidney were mineralized.

Whole body - Emaciation Bone marrow - Serous atrophy of fat Pericardium; Peritoneum - Bicavitary serous effusion Lungs - Moderate bronchopneumonia C1; C2 - Multifocal; chronic ulceration C3 - Multifocal erosion and congestion; with intralesional Haemonchus contortus Small and large intestine - Multifocal enterocolitis; suspected Comments: The findings on necropsy are various; encompassing chronic nutritional deficiency [emaciation; serous atrophy of fat] and their sequela [effusion]; infectious disease [bronchopneumonia; Haemonchus contortus]; and chronic inflammatory/infectious disease [stomach ulcers]. It is possible that the Haemonchus contortus infection could be at the heart of the nutritional deficiency; which led to subsequent immune suppression resulting in the observed infectious lesions. The chronic ulceration of the nonglandular stomach are possibly evidence of such a chain of events that occurred in one of the reported previous episodes of emaciation. A final report is pending histopathology; bacteriology; and parasitology. David Needle; DVM C1 - Chronic ulceration C3; duodenum - Mild; chronic; lymphoplasmacytic and histiocytic gastritis and duodenitis Lung: Mild; multifocal BALT hyperplasia; mild multifocal interstitial pneumonia; and mild; multifocal alveolar histiocytosis Heart - Mild; diffuse; lymphoplasmacytic; and histiocytic interstitial myocarditis Kidney: Multifocal moderate to severe neutrophilic and lymphocytic vasculitis Tongue: Multifocal epithelial erosion and mineralization; with adherent bacteria Colon: Mild; multifocal lymphoplasmacytic colitis; with mild; perivascular to interstitial chronic active serositis Haemonchiasis and Coccidiosis Emaciation; with hypoproteinemia leading to abdominal and pericardial effusion; and serous atrophy of fat Renal vasculitis Interstitial pneumonia and myocarditis Comments The findings on gross examination; bacteriology; parasitology and histopathology are listed in order of purported pathogenesis. These findings reveal evidence of ongoing parasitism; and emaciation. This led to chronic lesions of glossitis; foregut ulceration; gastroenteritis; and colitis. The acute lesions are renal vasculitis; interstitial pneumonia; and myocarditis; all of which indicate septicemia [blood borne bacteria]. The most likely order of events in this case is longstanding parasitism combined with the metabolic demands of parturition and lactation leading to a significant negative calorie balance. Prolonged caloric debt lead to decreased total body protein; with decreased blood albumin resulting in loss of fluid into the abdominal cavity and the pericardial sac [effusion]. Immunosuppression occurred secondary to this prolonged illness and protein loss; and bacteria were able to access the blood stream; through the oral; foregut lesions; or the lungs. The lesions in the kidney; lung and heart are the microscopic evidence of disseminated / blood borne bacteria. The severe serous atrophy of fat reported in the femur and the pericardium suggest that at this point; it was unlikely that increasing feed would have been sufficient to return this animal to health. David Needle; DVM

PROBABLE TRAUMA (EXPOSURE) LOW GRADE SYSTEMIC ANTIGENIC STIMULATION. This 5-year-old male bobwhite quail was found dead on exhibit. A major winter storm had occurred the previous night. The bird had a chronic history of deformed beak that required aggressive trimming. Necropsy revealed overweight body condition wet feathers deformed beak with markedly thickened rhinotheca and no gross lesions in the viscera.
ACUTE PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 2-year-old female lory was found dead. Necropsy revealed blood on the surface of the right air sac and slight feather loss on the head.

HEPATIC GLYCOGENOSIS AND LIPIDOSIS FOCAL HEPATIC NECROSIS RENAL TUBULAR VACUOLATION EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female Rodriguez bat presented with a chronic open luxation of the right stifle joint. Surgical repair was attempted but the bat was euthanized. In addition to the right stifle injury gross necropsy revealed that the liver was stippled with pinpoint tan foci throughout.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA SEPSIS HEPATOPATHY WITH PIECEMEAL NECROSIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male red kangaroo has a history of dental problems three years earlier. Recently two kangaroos at the facility died of toxoplasmosis. Examination of this kangaroo revealed decreased muscle mass gastric bloat and dehydration. Supportive care was administered but the animal became agonal over a 12 hour period and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed consolidation and abscess formation in both lungs and gastric dilatation.

PULMONARY ASPERGILLOSIS MICROFILAREMIA TRAUMA. This approximately 3-year-old male blue crowned mot-mot had been introduced to the aviary and was found dead. Necropsy revealed fracture of the left lower beak skin lacerations and broken or missing feathers. The sternum was fractured and a puncture and associated fracture of the hard palate was also noted. A large blood clot was in the cranial liver and within the pericardial sac. A large amount of aspirated blood was in the lungs. A tear or laceration was in the right ventricular wall close to the outflow tract. The adrenal glands were larger than expected.

COELOMITIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 12-year/9-month-old female rail died. It had a recent history of ascites decreased activity and dyspnea. Liver failure and iron storage disease were suspected. Fluid analysis of the coelomic fluid showed modified pyogranulomatous peritonitis. At necropsy there was slightly cloudy straw colored fluid in the coelom. The liver had a rough surface. Sections of lung kidney small intestine and liver were frozen for future use if needed.

BACTERIAL COELOMIC ABSCESS. This 7-year/8-month-old female anole died. It had a history of lethargy. At necropsy the anole was emaciated and dehydrated. It was in poor body condition. There was a large mass that encompassed the caudal coelom. All organs were pale. There were no fat pads evident. There was a 1.8x2.2 cm. mass in the caudal coelom. There was another 2x1.5 cm. mass present in the caudal coelom. The masses were firm and tan to gray and well adhered to the body wall. The ovary appeared to be small and normal in size and shape without active follicles. Both kidneys were brown.

METASTATIC CHONDROSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male Florida pinesnake had a subcutaneous abscess removed three months earlier. There was radiographic evidence of osteomyelitis in the ribs and spine which progressively worsened resulting in rupture of the vertebral column and subsequent euthanasia. Necropsy revealed multiple masses in the lung cranial aspect of the heart liver and spine.

BILIARY CYSTADENOMA RENAL CELL ADENOCARCINOMA BACTERIAL AND FUNGAL DERMATITIS. This 11-year-old female milk snake had a history of anorexia weight loss and dysecdysis for the past three months. At necropsy there was a white starburst pattern of discoloration under the scales. The cranial lobe of the liver was beige on cut surface and cross section. There was a 5 x 5 mm. white lesion on the surface and cut section of the kidney.

CECAL ABSCESS HUMERAL ABSCESS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female red kangaroo was geriatric and had been moving slower in the last few weeks. The kangaroo had a long-term history of a cystic bone lesion in the left humeral head. On the morning of euthanasia the kangaroo presented with acute severe colic. Necropsy revealed unshed fur over the dorsum mattes over the anterior chest thin body condition with minimal subcutaneous fat some mesenteric and abdominal fat mild pericardial effusion pale left renal cortex a 12 cm. subcutaneous lipoma over the enlarged left humeral head a 6 cm. caseous mass extending into the medullary cavity of the bone distorting the scapulohumeral joint of the left leg enlarged and abscessed cecum adhesion of the abscess to the body wall and the colon with associated outflow obstruction and pus on cut surface normal fecal pellets proximal to the obstruction enlarged spleen and mottled adrenals.

AMELONITIC MELANOMA. This 10-year-old anole had a limb amputated approximately three months prior to death due to amelanotic melanoma. The animal was found dead. At necropsy masses were present in the lung and pale foci were present in the liver and kidney.

METASTIC SARCOMA BACTERIAL DERMATITIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 39-year-old female hyacinth macaw was down had a head tilt was unable to stand and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal has a previous history of a recurrent feather follicle mass on the left shoulder that was diagnosed as anaplastic sarcoma. Recent blood work had anemia low albumin and high uric acid. At necropsy the animal was in thin nutritional status had a small liver had a nodule in the lung had swelling in the region of the left shoulder (previous tumor area) subjective swelling of the midbrain a mass in the region of the ovary and chronic cataracts.

METASTATIC CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11.5-year-old male domestic rabbit has had an overall decrease in comfort level and general decline in appetite and activity levels and developed an acute onset of hematuria and renal failure. The rabbit also developed conjunctivitis in the left eye that responded to treatment. The rabbit had bilateral cataracts. Recently the rabbit developed a seizure and had hind limb paresis and spinal arthritis was identified. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed atrophied muscle prominent skeletal projections decreased range of motion in the hips scant fat stores mature cataracts and no other abnormalities.

EMACIATION PERFORATING VENTRICULAR ULCER BACTERIAL INGLUVITIS AND INGLUVIAL CELLULITIS. This 3.5-year-old male pygmy falcon has a history of severe dermatitis involving the beak and oral commissure and a few small scabbed lesions on the feet. The cause has not been determined. Keratin on the lower beak had slowly been growing back. The bird became acutely weak with coelomic distention and died within 12 hours of presentation. Necropsy revealed thin body condition poor feather condition urates adhered to the vent area keratin of the lower beak growing but incomplete three small brown foci of discoloration on the dorsal right foot markedly distended gizzard filled with dry impacted fur possibly enlarged right auricle and some urate stasis.

SYSTEMIC VASCULITIS SUSPECT SEPTICEMIA/ENDOTOXEMIA. This 9.5-year-old male addax died after having seizures. It had a history of fighting with another addax and had many previous injuries. At necropsy the right horn was broken. There was some black tissue around the tail amputation site. There was minimal subcutaneous adipose tissue. There were two areas of hemorrhage on the right caudal lateral abdomen. There were petechia on the epicardial surface of the heart. There was a moderate amount of yellow pericardial fluid. The right auricular appendage was irregular with areas of dark red firm tissue on the surface. There were 4+ liters of clear yellow fluid with fibrin clots in the thoracic cavity. The lungs were atelectatic and had multiple areas of dark purple friable parenchyma along the edges. The bladder was full and difficult to express. The right kidney had subcapsular bruising. On cut section both kidneys were dark brown. There was approximately 4 liters of clear yellow fluid in the abdominal cavity. There were areas of hemorrhage on the ruminal surface that ranged in size from 1-8 cm. The rumen was moderately filled with green ingesta. There were areas of mucosal hemorrhage in the abomasum. The small intestine had diffuse serosal hemorrhage throughout. It was very friable. There were bloody mucous luminal contents. The cecal mucosa was covered with areas of hemorrhage and dark firm nodules present on the mucosa. There was a single loose piece of grass adhered to the mesentery near the spiral colon. There were multiple areas of mesenteric hemorrhage and adhesions throughout the abdomen. The colon was very friable and had what appeared to be shavings embedded on the serosal surface at the most caudal aspect of the colon. The spleen was gray and fibrous. The liver was small. The gall bladder was distended with hemorrhage. CBC revealed toxic neutrophils abnormal lymphocytes and monocytes. Abdominal fluid had occasional red blood cells and bacteria. Thoracic fluid had occasional red blood cells.

NEUROENDOCRINE PANCREATIC TUMOR MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULOPATHY CIRRHOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year and 9-month-old male domestic rat was found unresponsive tachycardic and tachypneic. The animal likely had a seizure overnight and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

BRAINS STEM ABSCESS EUTHANASIA.
