This 6-year-old female sugar glider had a history of ataxia that progressed to muscle tremors and hemiparesis on the right side with the right front being more severely affected. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes and had lost 15% of its body weight by the time of euthanasia although was still eating. Necropsy revealed ulcers on three of four feet and an enlarged brown liver.
adult. Weight: 740 g.  Granulomatosis. Hapatitus; splenitis and coelomitis - avian TB or neoplasia. Bumblefoot. Ascites.

BACTERIAL TUBULOINTERSITITIAL NEPHRITIS CHRONIC UROCYSTITIS SEPSIS. This 1-year-old female captive bred hyrax appeared clinically normal a few hours prior to death. The animal was found nonresponsive in lateral recumbency and was dead on arrival at the clinic. Necropsy revealed a few petechiae in the epaxial muscles and shoulder muscles.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 13.5-year-old female kudu was found down in the stall with a compound fracture of the olecranon. Due to the severity of injury and the poor prognosis for recovery the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy in addition to the olecranon fracture there was a comminuted fracture of the right acetabulum ileum and extensive soft tissue hemorrhage and subcutaneous edema in the right flank and right inguinal area.

SARCOCYSTOSIS PULMONARY EDEMA HEPATITIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION NEPHRITIS. This 7-month-old male lorikeet was found dead. The animal was being introduced to the group. No significant findings were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA INANITION PERIPORTAL HEPATITIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA RUMENITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 17-year-old female gazelle was euthanized due to emaciated condition and progressive weight loss. At necropsy the liver was friable and contained miliary white foci. The colon was dilated and thin walled.

EMACIATION INTESTINAL ULCERATION/IMPACTION. This 8-year-old female tentacled snake had recently become inappetent for two weeks with hypoglycemia and possible sepsis. Supportive care was administered but the snake was found dead. Necropsy revealed a small amount of fluid in the lung dried food in the esophagus and stomach and possibly some blood in the bolus of food although the mucosa was unremarkable. The proximal one-half of the intestine had a 1 cm. full circumferential section that was ulcerated. Adipose stores were atrophic.

BACTERIAL OSTEOARTHRITIS DYSECDYSIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female rattlesnake has a history of skin lesions and was treated accordingly but subsequently developed neurologic signs and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EXERTIONAL RHABDOMYOLYSIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female oryx was reported to be thin and separated from the herd three days prior to death. Blood work revealed elevations in liver and muscle enzymes. Soft tissue damage was detected in the distal limbs. Recovery from sedatives was slow and the animal remained sternally recumbent. Blood values from sedation indicated a profound rise in muscle enzymes. She became laterally recumbent and was euthanized. Necropsy revealed thin body condition but with some residual fat reserves. The muscles of the shoulders were pale and several large sections contained dry mealy tissue. Petechiae were detected in the nerve plexuses. The lungs oozed frothy sanguineous fluid. The abomasum contained three small ulcerations at the pyloric sphincter.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY DEGENERATIVE RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA (MYCOPLASMOSIS). This 2-year-old female rat had a history of intermittent respiratory signs received supportive care but presented in respiratory distress that did not resolve with supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified thin body condition dark purple cranial left lung and multiple pinpoint white foci throughout the right cranial pulmonary lobe. The kidneys were enlarged and pale.

BACTERIAL TRACHEITIS WITH SEPSIS MYHOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 14-year-old female Boelen’s python presented with pneumonia sinusitis and stomatitis. Supportive care was administered but the animal died approximately one week later. Necropsy revealed good body condition thickened reddened and congested lungs and air sacs and inactive ovaries.

CIRRHOSIS GRANULOMATOSIS CESTODIASIS. This 7-year-old female alligator lizard was found dead in the morning. This lizard was thought to be gravid although this was not confirmed at necropsy. Postmortem findings included hepatomegaly firm yellow liver several noncalcified eggs resembling slugs in the coelomic cavity and well vascularized oviduct.

INANITION MYCOBACTERIOSIS ADRENALITIS PNEUMONITIS HEPATITIS. This 17-year-old duck of undetermined gender was found dead in rainforest exhibit pool. At necropsy there was a 0.1x0.1 cm. white mass on the serosal surface of the right liver lobe. The gall bladder was large and distended with bile. The gizzard contained gravel. There was a 0.5x0.5 cm. creamy white colored mass on the serosal surface of the proximal jejunum. The cloaca was prolapsed. There was a swollen tarsometatarsal joint with a wound on the dorsal surface of the left leg. There was a blister on the web between toe #2 and #3. Both feet had abrasions on the plantar surfaces on the distal end of P3 of toes #2 3 and 4 with extremely abraded toenails.

OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA COELOMIC HERNIA EUTHANASIA ENTERITIS WITH FLAGELLATES. This 12-year-old female Rhode Island white chicken developed a large hernia in the coelomic walls a consequence of complications during egg laying. Surgical correction was attempted but failed. The bird had done well for three years but recently had been traumatizing the skin over the hernia and the skin had been getting thinner. The staff noticed a quantity of fat protruding through a hole in the hernia today progressing to intestinal prolapse through the defect. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A segment of the small intestine was adhered to the coelomic surface of the skin of the hernia and no other gross lesions were noted. This bird is part of a large flock of chickens and all the other chickens in the flock have previously died of complications associated with Marek’s disease.

MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY ATHEROSCLEROSIS AORTIC ANEURYSM MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION AND FIBROSIS LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE. This 16-year/4-month-old male tamarin died. It was hospitalized for therapy associated with renal disease and gingivitis. At necropsy the liver was large and light red/brown with a reticular pattern. There were lesions on the ascending/descending aorta with thickening and possible calcification of the wall. There were associated areas of aneurysm. There was possible moderate dilatation of the left ventricle. The kidneys were pale with dilated renal pelvis. The pancreas appeared lightly inflamed and edematous.
HEPATIC MELANOMACROPHAGE HYPERPLASIA. This 5-year-old golden mantella was found dead on February 8 2011. Gross necropsy revealed no significant lesions.
MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA AIR SACCULITIS ASPERGILLOSIS. This 3-year-old female rail was found dead. At necropsy a granuloma with fungal hyphae was identified in the lung.

ENCEPHALITIS PROBABLE WEST NILE VIRUS INFECTION. This 6.5-year-old lorikeet presented on the ground with ataxia and there is a recent history of West Nile virus mortality in the flock. Supplemental heat was provided but the bird died and necropsy revealed a yellow/orange mottled liver.

CHYTRIDIOMYCOSIS. This approximately 8-year/9-month-old female toad died. It was found upside-down on exhibit unable to right itself. It had a brown/pink patch on the belly that looked abnormal. At necropsy there was a large 2 in. in diameter patch on the abdomen that was brown and easily removed. The skin underneath was pink with many vessels. There were similar patches on both front and rear feet. The left front foot was especially bad. There were many preovulatory eggs present.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 12-year-old lory had not been acting normally for approximately one week and was found dead in a howdy cage on the lorikeet landing. Necropsy revealed multiple ulcerations and perforations in the intestine digested material in the coelomic cavity a pale focus in the liver darkened left lung and air sacculitis.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE PANCREATIC FIBROSIS IRIS MELANOMA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 5-year-old male rock hyrax was sedated for blood collection recovered well in its crate but then developed an abnormal respiratory pattern and hiccups. The animal then arrested twice in which case resuscitation efforts were successful the first time but not the second time. This animal had a deslorelin implant for aggression control. Necropsy revealed adequate adipose stores marked atrophy of the testes shrunken spleen and no other abnormalities.

HEPATIC BACTERIAL GRANULOMAS SEPTICEMIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS COELOMITIS ORAL PERIPHERAL NERVE SHEATH TUMOR. This 10-year-old captive bred male monitor died. It had a one month duration of illness consisting of decreased appetite. On the day prior to death the lizard was seen drinking a large quantity of water and then immediately regurgitated it. At necropsy there were five focal ovoid dark patches on the ventral tail (0.2-0.5 cm. in diameter). There were adequate fat pads. The right foot was missing digits #3 and 4. The upper left rostral palate had a firm white 2 mm. mass. There was mild gingivitis. The mass was firm and white on cut surface. The surface of the liver was mottled. There were two large 0.8 cm. cavitating abscesses in the hepatic parenchyma that contained large amounts of caseous material. There was a fluid filled cyst attached to the liver. There was moderate ascites. There was clear amber fluid in the coelomic cavity. The kidneys were dark brown with white streaks. Culture of the liver was performed.

PERFORATED CROP/ESOPHAGITIS COELOMITIS. This 1-year-old male lorikeet was hospitalized for lethargy and received supportive care but became weak and dyspneic and died. This is the ninth lorikeet in the flock that has died in the last two weeks. The flock has a recent history of clostridial infection. Necropsy revealed thin body condition thickened pericardium with a small amount of straw-colored pericardial effusion darkened lungs viscous yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity and a fibrinous exudate on serosal surface of the proventriculus and small intestines. The distal colon was diffusely congested and contained dark formed fecal material.
MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 18-year-old female monkey died acutely. At necropsy lungs were congested. Foam was present in the trachea. The heart was rounded with petechial hemorrhages.

PANCREATIC ADENOCARCINOMA THYROID FOLLICULAR CYSTADENOMA GRANULOMATOUS CERVICAL CELLULITIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old male tree boa had been doing poorly for some time with inappetence and thin body condition. A previous biopsy (G11-5491) identified dysecdysis hepatic melanosis and acute hemorrhage in the lung the latter attributed to biopsy artifact. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a prominent spine darkly colored scales on the dorsum hyperkeratosis and corneal edema in both eyes lipid dystrophy in the right eye keratitis in the left eye a 1 cm. semisoft yellow tissue in the layers of the esophagus and trachea proximal to the heart dark red lungs irregularly nodular splenopancreas dark brown to black liver dark green fluid in the gallbladder and dark purple kidneys with urate lines and some hemorrhage in the mucosa of the left ureter.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARIDAL FIBROSIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 11-year-old female meerkat had a distended abdomen due to distention of the urinary bladder. The animal also has a history of chronic renal disease and arthritis. The animal was humanely euthanized due to advanced age and declining condition. At necropsy several teeth were fractured. The bladder contained approximately 300 ml. of pale yellow fluid. No obstruction was noted in the urethra. Kidneys were pale yellow and firm. Several cyst-like structures were present in the liver. A pale yellow focus was present in one lung.

SPLENIC LIPOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 25-year-old female guanaco had progressive difficulty in walking due to osteoarthritis associated with aging. The animal was euthanized due to decreasing quality of life. Gross necropsy confirmed the presence of arthritis. In addition multiple splenic nodules were identified.

OOPHORITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 22-year-old female skink was found moribund on exhibit and later died. At necropsy the ovaries contained numerous follicles with inspissated yolk and were hyperemic. Kidneys were pale and gritty.

GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS HYPERTROPHIC GASTRITIS BACTERIAL GASTRITIS PANCREATIC ACINAR DEGENERATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 4-year-old male rattlesnake had a history of chronic regurgitation and abdominal swelling. At necropsy marked swelling of the stomach with mucosal hypertrophy and erythema was noted. The kidneys also had numerous white streaks.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS AUTOLYZED TISSUE. This less than 1-year-old female python had a history of difficulty eating and refused its last two meals. Keepers report that this animal has never looked healthy. The animal died and necropsy revealed petechiae on the ventrum white plaques on the pleura extending from the caudal liver to the kidneys small plaques within the air sac membrane white nodules involving several ribs in the mid coelom region that are hard on cut surface and autolysis of the caudal aspect of the snake.

EUTHANASIA LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE GINGIVITIS. This greater than 4-year-old female hedgehog was humanely euthanized. It had been under long-term treatment for gingivitis. At necropsy the hedgehog was in good body condition. The heart appeared enlarged. The large intestine was full of feces. The uterus was thicker than expected. There was thickened tissue around the trachea anterior to the heart.

DUODENAL PERFORATION PERITONITIS. This greater than 2-year-old female mouse presented in thin body condition with dehydration and a large soft palpable abdominal mass. Aspiration of the mass was unsuccessful. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a dilated stomach and proximal duodenum associated with foreign body obstruction and gastrointestinal leakage. The obstruction appeared to be rodent chow.

CHOLESTASIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS SPHEROIDS IN PITUITARY. This 9-year-old female red kangaroo had a 2.5 day history of lethargy and inappetence with associated neurological signs. Blood work revealed leukocytosis and neutrophilia with left shift hyperbilirubinemia and increased hepatic enzymes with azotemia. The red kangaroo was found dead and necropsy revealed fair body condition with minimal internal fat stores a 5 cm. necrotic oral ulcer on the right upper lip white plaques throughout the liver lobes and a mild amount of fecal material in the large intestine.

ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA OVARIAN FIBROLEIOMYOMA EOSINOPHILIC COLITIS. In July 2007 this 25-year-old female zebra had some hind end lameness/gait abnormalities. Her stride in the left hind leg was greater than the right. The severity progressed to the point that she had trouble lying down properly and would actually fall down instead. She would then to struggle to stand up again. Treatment with NSAIDS and Cosequin did not improve her condition. Vitamin E was also supplemented. In mid April 2011 this animal began to drop hay and lose weight. The animal was examined in May. Hoof trim was performed. A small proliferative lesion was noted on the gingiva surrounding the middle cheek teeth in the upper right arcade at that time. The animal improved a little after the procedure but then continued to have difficulty prehending food. She began to have unilateral nasal discharge on the right side and then bleeding into her mouth on occasion. In early July another workup was performed. The proliferative lesion was much more extensive than the previous exam. Through a defect in the lesion a communication between the oral cavity and sinus was found. Biopsy results showed squamous cell carcinoma. When the severity of oral bleeding increased euthanasia was elected. Note the animal was contracepted repeatedly with PZP.  At necropsy the animal was in fair body condition with adequate fat stores around the heart. The oral mass was extensive and the lesion spanned approximately 4 in. long and 2 in. wide (including the teeth) by 1-2 in. deep extending up into the lateral sinus. There was a communication from the oral cavity to the sinus. Necrotic tissue and clotted blood was present at the site. On the upper right arcade all teeth but premolar #1 were loose. No gross evidence of metastasis to the abdominal thoracic cavities. The right ovary was about 25 to 50% larger than the left. On cut section a reddish-brown mass approximately 3 cm. in diameter was present centrally. There was mild to moderate clear yellow abdominal fluid present. A muscle belly on the medial aspect of both upper hind legs (most likely sartorius but possibly pectineus or gracilis) felt very firm. Samples of these muscle bellies as well as more normal appearing muscle were obtained as were sections of sciatic nerve. There were no other significant gross findings.

CARCINOMATOSIS LIKELY OVIDUCT ORIGIN RENAL APLASIA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 6-year-old female chicken was found dead unexpectedly and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed hydrocoelom with approximately one liter of clear slightly blood-tinged fluid in the coelomic cavity. The oviduct was thickened and had fibrin-like strands throughout most of the oviduct. The intestine and addendum had multiple small round masses that were firm and solid on cut surface. The spleen was pale. There was no evidence of a left kidney in this bird.

ROUND CELL NEOPLASIA HEART FAILURE. This 5-year-old male degu had weight loss muscle wasting arthritis and alopecia. Additionally this animal had ataxia and left-sided head tilt. At necropsy there was muscle wasting mottling of the lungs subjective cardiomegaly mottling of the spleen and a tube-like organ associated with the testicles and the urinary bladder. The right kidney had multiple cysts.

HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA (KIDNEY LIVER INTESTINE SPLEEN) RENAL GOUT VISCERAL GOUT. This 25-year-old boa had a history of renal disease. The animal died despite treatment. At necropsy raised white masses were present throughout the liver. Caseous white foci were present in the lung. A large mass was present in the intestine and smaller foci were present in the kidneys.

TRAUMA HEPATITIS NEPHROSIS. This 2-year-old male lory died. It was found caught in the netting of the exhibit hanging upside-down and being picked on by the other birds. It was very shocky when it was brought to the hospital. It was cold and the leg was injured. Treatment was initiated. At necropsy the skin over the lateral aspect of the left leg had been abraded from the stifle to the foot. The left stifle joint seemed very loose. The air sacs were clear and dry. The spleen appeared enlarged and pale. The crop mucosa appeared red. There was no food in the crop. The gizzard was empty.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS AND NONSUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION. This 6-year-old male/castrated rabbit presented for partial inappetence and respiratory infection received supportive care but then developed rear limb weakness and partial inappetence worsened. Radiographs identified lysis of L2 vertebral body and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed coalescing white 1-3 mm. nodules in the kidneys thick and white aortic outflow tract a cluster of punctate 1 mm. lytic foci in the dorsal calvarium prominent adrenals a 2-3 mm. organizing hematoma in the thoracic inlet (venipuncture site) and compression of the spine through the cranial lumbar area.

INCLUSION BODY DISEASE. This approximately 10-year-old boa had a several month history of weight loss and inappetence. Initial blood results revealed hyperuricemia. Supportive care was administered but hyperuricemia persisted and elevated creatine kinase levels with panhypoproteinemia were noted. Skin began to tear and slough with accumulation of fluid in the subcutaneous spaces. The patient failed to respond to antibiotic therapy and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed detached skin from the underlying skeletal muscle involving two-thirds of the body. Yellow tinged fluid was in the coelomic cavity and a 2 mm. irregular white nodule was noted presumed to be parathyroid gland. Lungs were dark and mottled.

DYSECDYSIS WITH BACTERIAL/MYCOTIC DERMATITIS CATARACT HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This greater than 10-year-old male gecko had a history of chronic skin lesions and ulcers and a biopsy indicated squamous cell carcinoma. This gecko’s condition had continued to worsen and it was no longer eating on its own. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed minimal fat stores erosions and ulcers on the ventral surface of the front and back feet many ulcers and erythema involving the skin on the ventrum multiple areas of tan colored tissue in the liver and empty alimentary tract.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE OVARIAN FOLLICULAR RUPTURE. This 10-month/15-day-old female finch died. It was seen nest building quite a bit in recent months but there was no history of eggs being laid since the group of hatchlings late last year. At necropsy there was normal pectoral muscle mass. The crop was full of seeds. There were several small follicles present and two larger follicles present. There was yolk protein present in the coelomic cavity. There was ingesta and feces in the intestines. There was a 1 cm. unshelled egg yolk present halfway down the oviduct. The right lung appeared congested.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 4-year-old male prairie dog had a history of several months of intermittent dyspnea. Some improvement was seen initially with antibiotic treatment; however the condition recurred accompanied by nasal discharge. The animal became increasingly lethargic and depressed and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy dried discharge was noted at the external right nares. The liver was moderately enlarged.

BILIARY CYSTADENOCARCINOMA PANCREATIC ISLET TUMOR ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA CYSTIC MUCINOUS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA ADENOCARCINOMA WITH OSSEOUS METAPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 8.5-year-old female ferret has a history of an insulinoma and adrenal disease for which it was treated with prednisolone and deslorelin. Additionally the animal had an abdominal mass and multiple resected skin masses (mast cell tumors peripheral nerve sheath tumor sebaceous epithelioma). The animal was euthanized for lethargy ataxia and weakness. At necropsy there was alopecia surrounding the area of resected skin masses. The opening for the left eye was smaller than for the right. A soft 4 mm. mass was identified on the serosal surface of the trachea distal to the thyroid. The lungs had multiple less than 1 mm. white foci throughout all pulmonary lobes. The gastric mucosa was brown to black. The liver had approximately five 1 mm. brown foci scattered throughout the lobes. Additionally the liver had approximately two 2 mm. in diameter white foci in two of the lobes and a large cystic 3x6 cm. multilobulated mass attached to the serosal surface of the hepatic parenchyma by a stalk. The gallbladder was multinodular and contained brown to red fluid. Two firm approximately 1-2 mm. in diameter masses were identified in the pancreas. Lymph nodes were prominent.

PNEUMOCONIOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE PNEUMOCONIOSIS URATE STASIS. This greater than 12-year-old female burrowing owl was found in the morning recumbent and with dyspnea received supportive care but died a few minutes later. Necropsy revealed clear fluid ascites in the coelom moderate hepatomegaly congested lungs filled with fluid and cardiomegaly. An additional owl in the exhibit is clinically normal.

ENCEPHALITIS UVEITIS ENDOCRINE TUMOR. This 8-year-old Gray’s monitor had a one-day history of acute neurologic signs walking in circles and holding its mouth open. The lizard subsequently died. Necropsy revealed discoloration in the fascia above the liver over a 0.25 cm. lesion in the liver. Kidneys were dark brown to green. The mucosa of the upper palate had small red petechiae. A 2 cm. blood clot was noted above the palate under the eye and brain.
CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old male lory was found dead. Necropsy revealed curdled nectar in the crop and a reddened intestine.

VERTEBRAL SPINDLE CELL TUMOR SERTOLI TUMOR. This 19.5-year-old female corn snake was noted to have a small hard nodule noted along the spine roughly one-fifth of the way down the body and apparently attached to the spinal process. It also had a history of regurgitation weakness and weight loss. A second mass subsequently developed behind the right rib several inches behind the head. The snake received supportive care but subsequently died. Necropsy revealed a mass in the dorsal spinous process of the vertebra associated with swelling cranial to the heart and no other abnormalities.

RENAL GOUT FATTY LIVER. This greater than 10-year-old male rattlesnake died. It was anorexic for the past month. It regurgitated its diet last month. It has lost 25% of its weight since last March. At necropsy there were no fat stores observed. The upper esophagus had a small remnant of regurgitated food. The liver was friable. The first section of intestine next to the stomach had a macerated appearance. The same was also noted in the section by the coprodeum. The kidneys were engulfed with gouty tophi. There were large masses bilaterally. The cranial part of the kidney had purulent exudate.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS. This 25-year-old female squirrel monkey has a recent history of lethargy. Examination revealed elevations of BUN and the animal was treated with fluids. This resulted in moderate improvement in the animal’s condition; however the animal was found dead. At necropsy the heart was rounded in contour.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 23-year-old female addax had been immobilized for a suspected caudal ventral wound. Examination revealed a large mammary mass that was ulcerated and colonized by maggots. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed that the mass involved the entire mammary gland and that multiple masses were present throughout the lungs. The uterine body was firm and thickened.

SUBDURAL HEMORRHAGE HEAD TRAUMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS EMACIATION PYELONEPHRITIS. This 11-year-old male Linné’s two-toed sloth was acting abnormally overnight and in the morning was on the ground and unresponsive. CPR was attempted and was unsuccessful. The animal has a previous history of watery diarrhea for the last few weeks. At necropsy the lungs had small numbers of emphysematous bulla the tricuspid valve was slightly roughened the glandular mucosa of the stomach had a focal ulcer the urinary bladder wall was thickened and the medulla of the kidneys was hyperemic.

TRAUMA PROBABLE DROWNING. This 2-year-old male Inca tern was found floating in the pool after the pool had recently been filled. No abnormalities were noted in the flock prior to filling the exhibit pool. Necropsy revealed good body condition and frothy serous fluid on cut surface of the right lung.

SARCOCYSTOSIS INANITION. This 4-year-old male pygmy falcon was treated in the hospital for weight loss and dyspnea. Although initial improvement was noted the animal’s condition gradually declined and the bird was found dead. At gross necropsy all internal organs were congested.

NEURONAL LIPOFUSCINOSIS GERIATRIC HEMOSIDEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old screech owl had a one-month history of intermittent inappetence and fluctuating weight and a persistent weak grip of the right foot that improved slightly when the animal started eating again but never normalized. The bird was found face down in its enclosure but quickly recovered when approached. The bird became inappetent received supportive care but again was found face down several times per day responding appropriately when approached. Radiographs revealed increased opacity in the region of the lungs and a possible coelomic enlargement. When the animal became completely inappetent euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dark syrinx mature cataract in the right eye dark lungs rigid pericardial apex irregular coelomic fat mottled liver and no other abnormalities.

PARAVERTEBRAL MINERALIZATION FOCAL PNEUMONIA INANITION. This greater than 3-year-old male tree frog was found dead. It presented two days prior to death for behavior change and ventral hyperemia. The frog was treated with enrofloxacin orally and LRS0.45% NaCL/2.5% dextrose 1:1 topically. On day 2 the frog presented for extreme lethargy and coelomic distention. Radiographs revealed retracted lung fields and extensive fluid opacity in the coelom. Coelomiccentesis revealed a poorly cellular transudate. Injectable amikacin was initiated. On day 3 the frog appeared greatly improved in attitude. Repeat radiographs revealed expanded lung fields and progressive ascites. At necropsy there was multifocal hyperemia of the ventrum and hind legs. There were three 1-2 mm. in diameter yellow/gray nodules on the surface of the right lung. There was a large volume of clear fluid filling the coelomic cavity. The small intestine was intussuscepted into the stomach but there was no apparent devitalized tissue. The entire length of the large intestine was distended with compact fecal material. This material was expelled manually from the anus with great difficulty. There were multifocal 1 mm. in diameter soft white paravertebral masses at the base of nerve roots. The masses were radiopaque.

EUTHANASIA ARTEROSCLEROSIS ARTERIAL MINERALIZATION ENCEPHALITIS MENINGEAL MINERALIZATION CHRONIC ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 34-year-old female polar bear developed hind limb ataxia. This improved with treatment. The animal had been under treatment for chronic osteoarthritis. The animal was found down and unable to rise and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. A firm region was noted in the iliac artery. Multiple small cysts were present in the liver. Osteophytes and cartilage erosion were noted in the stifle. Bony masses were present along the ribs. A disk protrusion was noted intervertebral disk space L5-6.

ACUTE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA LIKELY ASPIRATION. This 3-year-old male captive bred macaque died spontaneously and was refrigerated 24 hours prior to necropsy. The animal was found on the floor in comatose condition and has a history of lead exposure. Serum lead level is pending. Necropsy revealed yellow meager subcutaneous adipose pulmonary atelectasis enlarged spleen and enlargement of the mesenteric lymph nodes.
INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS SHOCK. This 2-month-old male ferret was found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin. Minimal fat depots were present. The GI tract was nearly devoid of ingesta.

INTESTINAL POLYP ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 18-year-old male chuckwalla was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy fat depots were markedly reduced. A large calculus was present in the urinary bladder.

CUTANEOUS ABSCESS SEPSIS CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE CATARACT. This 20-year-old male golden lion tamarin had a history of thin body condition and alopecia over the dorsum and tail. The animal had a deeply ulcerated abscess on the midline of the dorsum that did not improve with antibiotics. The animal was a suspected diabetic. When anesthetized to check the wound the animal died and resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed no internal or subcutaneous fat a thin walled shallow pouch caudal to the cartilage on the ventral aspect of the glottis (which may have entrapped the tracheal tube) mottled liver multicystic large structure with whitish clear walls in the liver originating from the gallbladder region and containing slightly cloudy green fluid. The pancreas appeared thickened. An intussusception was in the small intestine with no associated intestinal necrosis and the intestine was reddened caudal to the intussusception. Moderate bruising was in the cranium.

BACTERIAL HEPATITIS SPLENITIS MYOCARDITIS. This 9-month-old male chameleon had been very restless and then became depressed and anorexic for two days prior to death. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy the liver contained yellowish foci. Kidneys also contained multiple white foci.

BACTERIAL SPLENITIS SEPTICEMIA INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA MENINGITIS. This 1-year/9-month-old female tamarin was found dead in nest box at AM check. It had no previous medical history. It was noted to be alert and active at the PM check. At necropsy there were abundant fat stores. The spleen was slightly enlarged. The liver was greatly enlarged dark red and had rounded borders. Both kidneys were enlarged dark red and appeared swollen on cut surface. The proximal GI tract contained no feed material or ingesta. The distal one-third of the cecum was darkly discolored. Sections of kidney liver spleen heart lung and skeletal muscle were frozen for future use if needed.

INTESTINAL LYMPHOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS (INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE-LIKE) HEMANGIOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male Mexican wolf has a history of lymphoma diagnosed by surgical biopsy of the jejunum. It had developed suspected weight loss and gastrointestinal obstruction prior to the diagnosis and had received treatment. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified pale pulmonary parenchyma a mild amount of serous pericardial fluid absence of pericardial fat a moderate amount of hemorrhagic fluid in the abdominal cavity a constricted region in the pylorus rounded hepatic margins prominent pancreas small spleen with a serosal nodule numerous prominent lymph nodes gas distended small intestine multiple constricted and thickened regions in the small intestine hemorrhagic feces in the large intestine contracted urinary bladder symmetrical testes and muscle atrophy.

INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA SPLENIC AND HEPATIC LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old ferret had a history of lethargy diarrhea polydipsia and weight loss. The ferret also had a history of long-term splenomegaly. The ferret eventually became anemic with continued weight loss and ultrasound revealed hyperechoic areas in the spleen. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation splenomegaly miliary foci in the liver nodules in the pancreas and a mass in the mesenteric root.
HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS NODULAR HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 12-year-old male fruit bat fell from the mesh and died. At necropsy the liver was enlarged and firm.

EUTHANASIA CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA PANCREATIC EXOCRINE HYPERPLASIA. This approximately 7-year-old captive bred female ferret was humanely euthanized. It had a history of suspected adrenal disease and insulinoma.

SHOCK RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 1-year-old female warthog was found dead inside the barn at morning check in right lateral recumbency. No abnormal behavior was noted prior to death and no external trauma was apparent. A small amount of blood was present below the right naris and some white foam was in the left naris. Necropsy findings included bilateral pulmonary hemorrhage and congestion presumptive bilateral hemorrhage in the atria presumptive bilateral hemorrhage in the endocardium congestion in the liver cervical trauma and possible focal spinal cord inflammation.

IRON STORAGE DISEASE CIRRHOSIS. This 5-year-old lorikeet became stressed and shocky following collection of a blood sample. It was treated but never recovered and died a few hours later. Necropsy revealed presumptive hepatic cirrhosis.

EUTHANASIA ENTEROCOLITIS. This 10-year-old female fox was humanely euthanized. It had a history of intermittent diarrhea. It presented with abdominal pain. It had no signs of improvement over two days.

EMACIATION LOW-GRADE SEPSIS ENTERITIS. This 2-month-old New England cottontail rabbit is in a reintroduction program. This rabbit and three others were included in a small mortality event. The rabbits had been captive born and raised and were placed in “hardening” pens approximately one month prior to death. Two animals were found dead on the same day. Traps were placed in the enclosure overnight and the following morning biologists found two dead rabbits in the traps. The water in the pen had become fetid and pelleted food left for the rabbits in the waterproof container had become moldy. Necropsy revealed fair to good body condition empty stomach duodenum and ileum normal feces in the cecum and colon slightly reduced intracoelomic fat and no other gross lesions.

FRACTURED CALCANEUS EUTHANASIA. This 3-month-old male pronghorn antelope developed right rear lameness after playing in the yard and radiographs revealed fracture of the right calcanean tuberosity and tuber calcaneus. Euthanasia was performed due to historical poor success rate in repair of this fracture. Necropsy revealed swollen and edematous tissue in the right hock region abundant retroperitoneal fat dependent congestion a single fracture of a calcanean tuberosity in the right leg moderate to severe hemorrhage in this region and swelling of the surrounding soft tissue due to edema. Several other pronghorns around the same time have had problems with lameness and two have sustained fractures during play.

PULMONARY VASCULITIS PULMONARY BACTERIAL ABSCESS FATTY LIVER. This 3.5-year-old female wallaby was found dead. It was hospitalized two weeks prior to death for treatment of a severe eye injury/infection. The animal appeared to respond well to treatment and was returned to holding area where it was housed with 10 other wallabies. It was found dead the next morning. Several of the apparently healthy wallabies have tested positive for wallaby retrovirus. This particular animal had not been tested. At necropsy there was hemorrhage around the mouth and nose. The lungs were severely congested. There was blood in the trachea. The liver was pale tan and floated in formalin. There were abundant fat stores grossly.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 6-year-old female squirrel monkey had a history of seizures and was being treated with antiseizure medications. It was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed bruising on the palms and fingertips of the hands blood in the oral cavity subcutaneous hemorrhage over the skull. Diffuse congestion of the lungs dilated and gas filled stomach grossly enlarged liver with a mottled appearance soft pancreas generalized lymphadenomegaly petechiae in the cecum soft kidneys and possibly enlarged pineal gland.

PULMONARY EDEMA AND CONGESTION. This female 10.5-year-old fruit bat was found dead in its cage. It was recently trapped in preparation for physical exam. There was no history of trauma poor appetite or decreased activity. At necropsy there were mild abrasions on the first digits of both wings. There were no palpable fractures. There was mild generalized hyperemia to the lungs. There was frothy serosanguineous fluid noted on cut section of the lungs. Similar frothy fluid was present in the trachea.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA. This 6-year-old female prairie chicken was found dead. At necropsy the bird was thin. Thick yellow plaques were present in the air sacs and the lungs were dark purple. Several foci of caseous necrosis were present in the lungs.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY NEPHROSCLEROSIS THYROID HYPERPLASIA AND ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old male lemur had been ill for less than one day and under anesthesia had arrested several times. Radiographs revealed fluid in the chest and a large heart with loss of detail in the abdominal cavity. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed pleural effusion gelatinous material in the right and left hemithorax collapsed lungs small nodules in tissue at the heart base thickened pericardial sac and markedly dilated right kidney with numerous cysts.

Spleen - Mild; multifocal extramedullary hematopoiesis Pancreas - Islet cell adenoma Lymph node - Sinus histiocytosis and erythrocytosis; with intrasinusoidal poorly differentiated cell colonization Comments The splenic tissue is histologically unremarkable. The pancreatic neoplasm is a benign neuroendocrine neoplasm arising from the islet of Langerhans. The designation of an adenoma in the ferret is made based on small size; and lack of perceived invasion. The majority of islet cell tumors in ferrets are beta cell tumors that can secrete insulin. Such neoplasms are most commonly diagnosed between 4 and 5 years of age; though they are often seen as incidental findings during necropsy. Distant metastasis is rare. The findings in the lymph node are notable; but not specific. The population of cells within the sinusoids is poorly differentiated. Differential diagnoses include mast cells; lymphocytes; and epithelial cells. Further histochemical testing is in progress; the results of which will be released in an addendum report. David Needle; D

FRACTURED ANTEBRACHIUM ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 15-month-old tamarin of undetermined gender incurred a fracture of the ulna and radius which was surgically repaired but during the procedure the animal arrested and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed hemoabdomen with clotted and unclotted blood firm heart with thick ventricles and atria and no other abnormalities.

LYMPHOMA PARATHYROID ADENOMA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 15-year-old male Amur tiger has a history of inflammatory bowel disease and degenerative arthritis. It had been receiving prednisolone for one year. It received one dose of ketoprofen on the day of death. Blood work prior to death revealed marked anemia nucleated red blood cells in peripheral blood mild left shift in neutrophils moderate hyperphosphatemia and azotemia high normal creatinine and mild elevations in total bilirubin sodium and potassium. Physical examination revealed mild cataract formation and epulis-like gingival growth and a subcutaneous mass in the caudal left axillary region. Both inguinal lymph nodes were markedly enlarged. Ultrasound revealed free abdominal fluid. The animal developed arrhythmia during the anesthetic procedure and did not recover. Necropsy revealed generalized lymphadenomegaly palpable firm masses in the parenchyma of the lung thickened intestinal walls splenomegaly with rupture and associated hemoabdomen pinpoint raised white masses on the mucosal surface of the urinary bladder and a fluid filled cystic region in the right thyroid gland.

STRESS PULMONARY AND HEPATIC FIBROSIS NEPHROLITHIASIS. This 21-year-old male timber rattlesnake was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed one piece of pine straw in the cranial portion of the esophagus with a small amount of sand. Male reproductive tract was identified.
adult. Weight: 2250 g.  Euthanased.  Thoracoperitoneal mass.  Suspect metastases in pleura and lung.  Pneumothorax.  Pulmonary atelectasis.

GOUT. This 10.5-year-old female cockatiel was found dead in the morning in the treatment room incubator. It had been found on the ground unable to fly and had difficulty walking. Examination revealed dull mentation emaciation and dehydration. Multiple small masses were present on the metatarsal and phalangeal joints of both limbs. Supportive care was administered. Necropsy revealed congested lungs pinpoint white foci on the pericardium liquid red/brown contents in the intestinal tract and diffusely white/tan kidneys.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female koala developed dyspnea and 360 cc. of fluid were removed from the chest. No growth was obtained when the fluid was cultured. The animal subsequently again became dyspneic and more fluid was removed from the pleural cavity. The animal subsequently became dyspneic again and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 108 cc. of yellow-tinged fluid in the left side of the chest and 140 cc. of fluid from the right side. Lungs were atelectatic. Sections of lung did not float in formalin. The mediastinum was enlarged and a mass was present in the mediastinum. The liver had a miliary pattern on cut surface and a 5 cm. firm white mesenteric mass was noted. A small amount of clear fluid was in the abdomen.
adult. Weight: 3.7 g.  Severe clavicular air saculitis.  Presumed aspergilosis.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This 12-year-old male captive bred African lion had a history of acute pulmonary illness of three days duration. The animal was treated with fluids antibiotics and amphotericin B but was found dead on June 19 2011. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition serosanguineous fluid draining from the nose and oral cavity serosanguineous pleural effusion with adhesions between the lungs and thoracic walls serosanguineous fluid in the trachea and bronchi edematous and mottled lungs with serosanguineous fluid within small airways small nodules throughout the pulmonary parenchyma serosanguineous pericardial effusion pyloric ulceration a mottled and nutmeg-colored liver hemorrhagic lymph nodes hemorrhagic renal cortices and hemorrhagic adrenal and thyroid glands.

LEG TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 27-year-old female Chilean flamingo was found bleeding on exhibit and unable to bear weight on its right leg. A clean laceration the width of the lateral hock and into the joint with bone exposure and complete severance of the lateral ligament was identified and no stability was in the joint. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.
TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 7-year-old male snake was found dead and trapped in a filter in the exhibit tank. At necropsy dried blood was present on the anterior portion of the body.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS. This 4-year-old female tammar wallaby was found dead in its enclosure with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition a moderate amount of foul smelling exudate of peritoneal effusion petechiae on the serosal surfaces in multiple organs minor hemorrhage in the dorsal sclera of the right eye a small amount of blood in the nasal passages and mouth some petechiae on the epicardium dark lungs a small amount of ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract and no other gross abnormalities.

SHOCK DERMATITIS COLITIS. This 8-year-old male addax was found dead in the yard. It was sitting sternal and appeared alert the night before. it had been immobilized the day prior to death to check MCF status. Initial heart rhythm was erratic but was stabilized during the 20 min. procedure. The animal recovered quickly and was reported to be doing fine afterwards. At necropsy the entire tracheal mucosa was hemorrhagic. There was petechia and ecchymosis on the mucosal surface of the abomasum and duodenum. The heart contained fibrinous material adhered to the chordae tendineae of the left atrioventricular valve.

CARPAL ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INTRASPECIES TRAUMA HEPATIC FIBROSIS RENAL PROTEINOSIS. This 12-year-old male capybara was found dead. At necropsy an abscess with a draining tract was noted on the left carpus.

PULMONARY ABSCESSES ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 12-year-old male California sea lion had a two week history of respiratory distress and died while anesthetized for examination. Necropsy revealed dark skeletal muscle pyothorax and multifocal pulmonary abscessation.

ENTERITIS. This 1-year-old lory presented with suspected clostridial enteritis. The animal was treated with supportive care; however it was found dead the following day. At necropsy yellow fluid was present throughout the GI tract.

BACTERIAL GASTRITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS. This 12.5-year-old female cheetah had a history of chronic gastritis and colitis. The animal has a history of feline coronavirus positive immunostaining of intestine and colon. Lymphoplasmacytic gastritis and numerous spiral bacteria were identified on gastric biopsies. At necropsy the animal was emaciated with marked muscle wasting. Multiple firm white nodules were present in the spleen. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Several cystic areas were present throughout the liver. The stomach had extensive foci of fibrosis. The small intestine had a segmental area of marked thickening.
adult. Weight: 78.4 g.  Air sacculitis; suspect aspergillosis.  Focal coelomitis and hepatitis.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 4-year-old female squirrel monkey appeared normal in the afternoon and was found dead one hour later. Necropsy revealed foam in the nostrils and in the oral cavity congested and mottled lungs an apparent ulcer on the serosal surface of the jejunum and enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes.
INANITION SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 6-year-old male fruit bat was found dead. At necropsy the body condition was poor and there was no external evidence of trauma.

CHRONIC ARTHRITIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 16-year-old female flamingo was found dead. At necropsy a 3 mm. in diameter mass was present in the spleen. White foci were present on the heart. Joints were swollen and contained pasty white material.

TOXOPLASMOSIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 1-year-old male red kangaroo is from a mob in which there have been multiple losses due to toxoplasmosis. Only two males remain in the mob. This animal had a one day history of respiratory distress was treated for toxoplasmosis but died the following day. Necropsy revealed multiple pale foci in all lung lobes red/purple mottling of the lungs grayish-white foci in the pleura of the mediastinum and enlargement of the intrathoracic and omental lymph nodes. Abundant translucent straw-colored fluid was in the abdominal cavity and intestinal loops had congested vessels.

Small intestine: Luminal foreign body Liver: Diffuse hepatic lipidosis (presumptive) Lung: Multifocal pulmonary foci/nodules Pancreas: Focal pancreatic plaque Right adrenal gland: Focal adrenal nodule Comments: The most important gross necropsy finding was the small intestinal foreign body; which appeared to a fragment of rubber tubing. There appeared to be intestinal obstruction due to the foreign body; as the small intestine adoral to the object was distended with gas. Intestinal obstruction due to foreign body ingestion is a very common syndrome in ferrets. The presumed hepatic lipidosis supports the history of the animal being off-feed; and this may have contributed to its illness and its demise. The nature of the nodules described in the lungs; pancreas; and adrenal gland is uncertain; but histopathologic examination should help determine their nature. Histopathologic examination of all major tissues is in progress; and results will be released in the final report. Katriya Chankow; DVM severe diffuse hepatocellular lipidosis mild hepatic hemosiderosis; and moderate splenic hemosiderosis multinodular adrenocortical hyperplasia small intestinal foreign body hepatic lipidosis Comment: Small intestinal obstruction due to the rubber foreign body probably led to this ferret going off-feed; and hepatic lipidosis subsequently developed. This metabolic liver disease may have compounded the animal's illness and led to its death. The nodules in the adrenal gland were determined to be foci of cortical hyperplasia; and the white foci in the lungs apparently were areas of lipid-laden macrophages in subpleural alveoli; both were incidental findings in this case. The dark brown to red area described grossly near the head of the pancreas was apparently a mesenteric lymph node. This concludes diagnostic testing for this case. Katriya Chankow; DVM

GASTRIC IMPACTION SEPSIS. This 6-year-old female slender-tailed meerkat is one of several in the collection that have presented with gastric obstructions. This animal subsequently died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a palpable mass in the stomach hard black firm somewhat fibrous mass filling the lumen of the stomach black debris on the surface of the stomach and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL GOUT BUMBLEFOOT HEMOSIDEROSIS. This greater than 35-year-old male Chilean flamingo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of deterioration of health due to age-related multiorgan failure. At necropsy the flamingo was in poor nutritional state with no adipose tissue storages and little food within the digestive tract. There were multiple small black ectoparasites present on the feathers. The old pinion site on the left wing was ulcerated with a thick bed of granulation tissue and a few abnormally formed feathers. There were large chronic bumblefoot lesions on both feet. The lungs and air sacs were covered with a fine black particulate matter. The heart was enlarged with a flaccid right ventricle and thickened right ventricle. The aortic valve and left atrioventricular valve were thickened. There were jet lesions and multiple raised orange plaques on the surface of the aorta starting at the base of the heart and extending down to the kidneys. There was a section of mid abdominal aorta that was firm and presumed mineralized. The liver appeared grossly enlarged. The kidneys were enlarged tan and had multiple small white spots. The spleen and adrenal glands were enlarged. The left hock joint had a moderate soft tissue swelling that on cut section exuded a yellow/white thick material.
Weight: 270 g.  Euthanased. Subcutaneous mass; suspect benign tumour.
HEAD TRAUMA PULMONARY SHOCK ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 15-year-old male fruit bat was found dead on the exhibit floor. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no gross lesions or evidence of trauma.

MESOTHELIOMA EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female jaguar presented with abdominal distention due to ascites in October. Fluid analysis indicated a modified transudate and blood work revealed elevations in serum ALT. An ultrasound exam revealed thickened and nodular mesentery suggestive of carcinomatosis. Supportive care was administered but the animal’s condition deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed adequate fat stores several liters of serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen with floating fibrin-like material and a similar effusion present in the pleural spaces. Serosal surfaces are lined by pale material. Lungs had patchy atelectasis and congestion a small amount of pericardial effusion was noted and the mediastinum attached to the pericardium was thickened and nodular. Valves had mild endocardiosis and wall thicknesses seemed within normal limits. The mesentery was thickened and nodular and intestines were hyperemic and plicated. The liver had a rough surface and was mottled on cut surface resembling a nutmeg appearance. Kidneys had pale medullary streaking. Ovaries were quiescent and one uterine horn was slightly thicker in a short segment than the contralateral horn and this section contained some mucoid material.

RENAL GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION AMYLOIDOSIS. This 24-year-old female flamingo was found down. At necropsy the animal was thin and markedly dehydrated. The animal later died. At necropsy white deposits were present on the surface of the epicardium. Kidneys contained pinpoint white foci throughout the serosal and cut surfaces.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS GRANULOMATOSIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female rainbow lorikeet has a history of chronic left wing droop no response to medication and multiple radiolucent lesions in the bones of the appendicular skeleton. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The liver was extremely enlarged with rounded edges and multiple punctate white foci were scattered throughout the parenchyma. An abscess was noted at the end of the distal left ulna.

SHOCK ENTEIRTIS NEPHRITIS. This 3.5-year-old female panda was found nonresponsive in the exhibit. The animal later died. At necropsy the stomach contained dark green ingesta. No significant gross lesions were identified in other tissues.
INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION SHOCK. This 11-year-old female owl was found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin. Kidneys were mottled.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 6-year-old male agouti was found recumbent and unable to ambulate in the morning. A perch had fallen at some point in the night but it is unknown if these events were related. Examination revealed that the animal was in shock but could paddle its front limbs. No withdrawal or voluntary movement was noted in the hind limbs. No radiographic lesions were observed. Supportive care was administered but the animal died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed a minor cut on the plantar surface of the central digit of the right hind foot minor erythema and excoriations medially on the distal forearms a few minor areas of presumptive calcification in the lungs beige kidneys with irregular surfaces associated with abnormalities in the cortices on cut surface.

PULMONARY EDEMA AND CONGESTION SUSPECT DROWNING TRAUMA STRESS RESPONSE INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ABOMASITIS. This 14-year/1-month-old female gazelle was found dead in the pool. At necropsy there were abrasions noted on both carpi with blood on the surrounding haircoat. There was an approximately 1 cm. laceration just ventral to the mandibular incisor at the junction of the gingiva and buccal mucosa. The lungs were diffusely congested. The left lung had several adhesions. There was a 4 cm. scar-like lesion present. There was a 1 x 0.5 cm. plaque in the caudal portion of the lung. The pericardial fat was very firm and solid. Both kidneys were irregular shaped and appeared to have undergone a significant amount of renal degeneration with healing via scar formation. On cut section some areas of the cortex appeared to be virtually absent due to marked scarring. There was a 2 x 1 cm. triangular lesion in the liver. There was marked hemorrhage in the pancreas.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS NODULAR HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 12-year-old male fox has a history of renal failure and osteoarthritis. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. A soft pendulous mass was present in the skin of the ventral tail. Vertebral spondylosis was noted radiographically. The liver was yellow to brown and contained a large dark mass in the right lateral lobe.

EUTHANASIA OVARIAN CARCINOMA URATE STASIS ENTERITIS. This 10-year-old chicken has a history of unilateral lameness and weight loss over a one month period. The animal was anesthetized for laparoscopy and a large nodular tumor was identified within the coelomic cavity. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a 6 x 3 cm. nodular mass was present on the ovary. Kidneys were pale mottled and enlarged.

ENTEROCOLITIS. This 10-month-old female capybara presented with lethargy and depression received supportive care but later was found in lateral recumbency with heavy breathing severe gastric dilatation and a gas-filled intestinal tract. The animal’s attitude and condition improved mildly when the alimentary tract was decompressed but it was subsequently found dead two hours later. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with minimal subcutaneous fat stores bilaterally congested lungs digested food stuffs in the stomach and duodenum gas-filled ileum and colon with reddened serosal surface and hemorrhage on the mucosal surface cloudy urine and enlarged adrenal glands.

Liver: suggestive of mild; multifocal hepatopathy Open COMMENTS: The pale foci within the liver may be caused by uneven blood pooling postmortem; and will require histopathology to confirm. A cause for the neurologic signs was not determined on gross examination. Previous clinical pathology from 12/13/08 indicated a calcium: phosphorus ratio imbalance (0.9:1.0). Nutritional inadequacies; such as seen with all seed diets; should be considered as a cause for hypocalcemia and neurologic signs in this case. Selective tissue have been placed on hold; and histopathology is pending. A final report will follow. Danielle Desjardins; D Testicular atrophy; bilateral; diffuse. Moderate; bilateral parathyroid hyperplasia. Mild; multifocal pulmonary anthrocosis? mild heterophilic tracheitis and bronchitis. Mild to moderate; multifocal random hepatocellular necrosis with mild heterophilic hepatitis and vacuolar degeneration. \_ Adrenal lesions have been described in a high percentage of birds on postmortem examination; however a clinical diagnosis of naturally occuring hypoadrenocorticism has not been documented in birds. It is possible the adrenal cortical degeneration may have contributed to anorexia; weakness and lethargy secondary to decreased glucocorticoid production. In addition; the cerebral edema identified within the brain may have been caused by electrolyte abnormalities; which may have been related to a deficiency in mineralcoritcoids from the adrenal cortex. The parathyroid gland hyperplasia in combination with the calcium:phosporous imbalance may be secondary to a diet which was high in phosphrous and low in calcium and vitamin D. All seed diets; fruits and most vegtables are low in calcium. High fat seeds; such as sunflowers; may interfere with calcium uptake. It is important to note that in nutritional secodnary hyperparathyroidism; serum caclium levels may be low to normal; despite clinical signs of weakness; seizures; etc. Ultimately; the proximate cause of death in this bird was most likely acute liver failure. A culture of the liver has been submitted to investigate the possibility of a terminal bacterial septicemia. An association between these findings and the findings in the brain and adrenal gland has not been determined. (See previous report) Danielle Desjardins; D Comments:(see previous final report) Danielle Desjardins; D

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 4-year-old male hedgehog (00-0133-51BF) was euthanized following a less than one day history of diarrhea. Physical exam had revealed a heart murmur moist lung sounds and a palpable mass in the abdomen. Necropsy revealed good body condition and a bilobed relatively large prostate gland. Lungs were red and wet. The heart was globoid.

CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE ISLET CELL TUMOR CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female ferret had been previously diagnosed with adrenal disease. The ferret also had chronic diarrhea and azotemia and had been on prednisolone for several months. On the day of presentation the ferret was noted to have lost significant weight and found in a possible seizure-like state. Examination revealed right side deviated opisthotonos. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a moderately enlarged spleen a firm mass in the area of the right adrenal gland small mass on the pancreas degenerative changes in the kidneys and no other abnormalities.

LARGE CELL LYMPHOMA. This 9-month-old domestic house mouse was found dead without previous clinical illness. At necropsy the right side of the chest was occupied by a large thoracic mass. Additionally the right ureter with associated 4 mm. in diameter tan mass is noted.

ENDOMETRIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female mandrill had a history of chronic mensis-related pain depression and lethargy. Examination revealed a large caudal abdominal mass with cystic areas and possible bowel entrapment with associated peritoneal fluid. Exploratory laparotomy revealed hemoabdomen peritonitis omental inflammation disfiguring and fibrotic changes within the uterus with several adhesions and entrapment of the urinary bladder and cecum and displacement and compression of the rectum.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA WITH ABSCESSES. This 12-year-old female bighorn sheep had a three month history of coughing and died. Necropsy revealed multiple areas of nodularity and caseous material in the lungs with adhesions to the body wall.

TRACHEAL TRAUMA ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS PAPILLOMA. This 17-year-old female mandrill had been immobilized for routine annual exam. Intubation was difficult and blood was seen after the animal was extubated. Two to three days later the animal developed increased upper airway sounds and was re-immobilized for respiratory distress and openmouthed breathing. Supportive care was administered the animal recovered but upper airway noise persisted although was much improved. The animal was stable for three days but then deteriorated. Immobilization was performed and a mass was identified at the opening of the trachea. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple small skin scabs obesity reddened firm uterus lipoma in the left inguinal area diffusely mottled liver congested and consolidated left middle and caudal pulmonary lobes foam in the trachea and lungs on cut surface a 1.4 cm. multinodular mass at the opening of the trachea and multiple red foci in the pancreas.

BACATERIAL SALPINGITIS WITH INVOLUTED EGG POSSIBLE EXPOSURE TO HEPATOTOXINS. This 8-year-old female quail died spontaneously and was refrigerated 24 hours prior to necropsy. The quail presented inactive and fluffed with a large amount of feces adhered to the cloaca. Radiographs indicated a mass in the left abdominal cavity. Necropsy revealed a poorly calcified egg mass in the reproductive tract and a yellow/tan exudate in the lungs on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS STRESS. This 2.5-year-old male budgerigar was lethargic and restrained for examination at which point he began breathing laboriously and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE. This 20-year-old male snow leopard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic progressive renal failure with elevation of BUN and creatinine. It had polyuria polydipsia and weight loss. At necropsy the liver had a large 8 x 6 cm. clear fluid filled sac. The kidneys were pale and small with gritty material in the pelvis. The thyroid and parathyroid glands had multiple clear cysts that were 3-8 mm. in diameter.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL GOUT SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male Mexican black kingsnake presented for a large coelomic mass. At surgery the mass was arising from the kidney and severely compressing the colon. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy a cyst was in the liver. The colon was compressed and contained abundant hard fecal material. The caudal half of the left kidney was markedly enlarged by firm gritty and white material. The cranial half of the left kidney was subjectively within normal limits and the right kidney was unremarkable.

NUTRITIONAL BONE DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 9-month-old smoky jungle frog of undetermined gender was found dead. This jungle frog and another largest youngster from the same clutch displayed neurologic signs simultaneously. The signs consisted of ataxia weakness an inability to use or coordinate hind limbs. At necropsy there were no obvious external lesions. The liver appeared somewhat small.

EUTHANASIA VACUOLAR DEGENERATION (MYELIN) WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME. This 4-year-old male hedgehog was euthanized due to ataxia and weight loss. At necropsy spondylosis was noted in the thoracic vertebrae.

SCROTAL ABSCESS SEPSIS. This 2-year-old male Navajo sheep developed an acute onset of ataxia which progressed to seizures and cardiopulmonary arrest. This animal was castrated three weeks earlier and the surgical site healed poorly. An additional surgery was performed two weeks prior to death and tested for scirrhous cord. Necropsy revealed excessive fat stores a small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity froth in the trachea and bronchi emphysema in the right cranial pulmonary lobe some petechiae on the auricles of the heart firm fat deposits around the cardiac vessels that cracked when palpated a small amount of pericardial fluid a small amount of serosanguineous free fluid and a large amount of fat in the abdominal cavity a laceration on the inside of the lower lip reddened mottled pancreas irregular texture on the spleen full urinary bladder thickened scrotal tissue with necrotic white/green solid center to both sides of the scrotum and enlarged regional lymph nodes generalized lymphadenomegaly white/yellow fluid in a prescapular lymph node on cut surface and multiple reddened lymph nodes.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOMYELITIS. This 11-year-old male corn snake had a history of tail amputation. Enlargement of the stump was diagnosed as a vascular anomaly or hemangioma. Repeated episodes of hemorrhage occurred and the animal was euthanized. At necropsy a large fluctuant mass was present at the amputation site.

YOLK COELOMITIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 4-year-old female chicken was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed thin body condition mottling of the hepatic lobes pale heart large clot in the aorta large amount of fat surrounding the heart small clots in the lungs a large amount of yellow material resembling fat or yolk covering the ventriculus and intestines tightly adhered to the dorsal body wall surrounded by yellow material resembling fat. The cloaca was prolapsed.
NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 10-year-old male axolotl was found dead. At necropsy no gross lesions were identified; however the body was markedly autolyzed.

Liver (necropsy specimen): Well differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma; biliary cystadenoma; glycogen accumulation Liver (surgical specimen): Pelioid hepatocellular carcinoma; glycogen accumulation Adrenal gland: Cortical hyperplasia Kidney: Moderate multifocal membranous glomerulonephritis; multifocal glomerulosclerosis; multifocal interstitial nephritis Pancreas: Nodular hyperplasia Barbie J. Gadsden; DVM Adrenal gland: Moderate cortical hyperplasia Pancreas: Islet cell vacuolation Comment: No distinct adrenal mass was observed within sections of adrenal gland. EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS. This 5-year-old male corn snake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of severe spondylosis with sclerosis throughout the spine noted on radiographs. It also had a history of weight loss although it was eating. It had loose abnormal stool. Its diet consisted of mice. It was housed alone. At necropsy there was severe sclerosis of the lumbar and sacral vertebrae. The muscles appeared pale. There was adequate fat within the coelomic cavity. The spleen was black. The liver appeared mottled. The pancreas appeared mottled and had a soft texture. The kidneys appeared slightly mottled. The thyroid gland was somewhat cystic.

CHROMOBLASTOMYCOSIS. This male 4-year/2-month-old frog was humanely euthanized. It was found sitting out in the open the day prior to death. It was found barely moving the morning of death. At necropsy there was a lesion through the skin and musculature on the left forearm. The heart was pale. The right liver lobe had numerous white pinpoint foci throughout the parenchyma.

CHRONIC RENAL AND CARDIAC DISEASE HYPERKALEMIA POLYCYTHEMIA ADRENAL MEDULLARY HYPERPLASIA EMACIATION. This adult female prairie dog had a packed cell volume of 70% increased respiratory effort and frequent focal seizures of approximately 3.5 months duration. Potassium levels were markedly elevated. Necropsy revealed diffuse bright red parietal lung surface brown visceral lung surface dark brown myocardium and approximately 7 cc. of serosanguineous abdominal fluid. Two approximately 0.5 cm. diameter yellow nodules were detected one in the peritoneum and one in the abdomen.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT LYMPHOCYTIC ADRENALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old boa has a history of respiratory difficulty stomatitis and central nervous system signs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed diffusely hyperemic lungs tan fibrinous material and foam on the mucosal surface of the trachea and tan colored fibrin beneath the capsular surface of the liver. Osseous proliferation was noted in the vertebrae.

RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 2.5-year-old female rat had a three-month history of cataracts and intermittent glaucoma or exophthalmia. There is a familial history of heart disease. The rat subsequently died and necropsy revealed an enlarged heart and blood in the thorax and an abnormal appearing reproductive tract.

PROLAPSED HEMIPENES CIRRHOSIS SEPSIS. This 10-year-old male palm viper had a three week history of swelling in the caudal third of the body and cytology revealed septic inflammation and Pseudomonas aeruginosa and E. coli were cultured. Blood work revealed leukopenia and anemia and chemistry values were within normal limits. Supportive care was administered but the animal subsequently prolapsed both hemipenes and the tissue could not be reduced manually. The patient died before surgery could be performed. Necropsy revealed irritation or redness of the fat bodies where the aspirate was obtained pale kidneys with urate crystals on the ventral surfaces pale heart with very little blood in the lumina and no other abnormalities.

EMACIATION DERMATITIS. This approximately 10-year-old female leiothrix was found on the ground and had an overgrown beak that had punctured the skin. Supportive care was administered but the bird became more and more lethargic laying on its side and unable to hold its head up. The bird died a few minutes later. Necropsy revealed no abnormalities other than the lesion in the neck created by the beak.

PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS BACTERIAL VENTRICULITIS ENTERITIS HEPATITIS ESOPHAGITIS PNEUMONIA. This 3-year-old female lorikeet was found dead. The collection has a history of hepatopathy possibly due to vitamin A toxicosis. At necropsy the liver contained pinpoint white to yellow foci.

CARDIAC MYCOTIC THROMBOEMBOLISM GRANULOMATOSIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 11.5-year-old lorikeet was found dead unexpectedly at mid morning. It had been clinically normal earlier in the day. There have been no problems with this animal or within the flock. Necropsy revealed a firm mass in the left atrium extending slightly into the right atrium and right ventricle. The mass peeled from the heart easily and had a white capsule and caseous material in the center. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

EUTHANASIA STOMATITIS PNEUMONITIS FATTY LIVER. This greater than 9-year-old male python was humanely euthanized. It had a history of not doing right chronic stomatitis and respiratory symptoms. Culture of the mouth grew Pseudomonas Enterococcus Providencia and Burkholderia. At necropsy the oral cavity was erythematous and had granulomas. The python was very thin with little fat stores. The lungs were hyperemic.
NA

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS AND SEPSIS HEPATIC AND MESENTERIC NEMATODE GRANULOMAS. This greater than 3-year-old male toad had been a poor eater over the last few months and had not eaten in the last two weeks. The toad died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed a 2 mm. in diameter ulcerated plaque on the skin of the mid dorsal region little coelomic fat stores and no contents in the gastrointestinal tract. The mesentery contained numerous yellowish-orange granulomas.

DERMAL XANTHOMATOSIS DERMATITIS MYOCARDITIS INTERSTIAL PNEUMONIA URATE STASIS MUCOSAL MINERALIZATION. This 13-year-old copperhead was found dead. At necropsy a deep skin wound was noted in the anterior one-third of the body. The kidney contained miliary white foci. Moderate ascites was noted in the coelomic cavity.

MASSIVE HEPATIC NECROSIS POSSIBLE MICROCYSTIN TOXICOSIS. This 7-month-old male river otter had a two day history of lethargy and died. Necropsy revealed severe generalized icterus friable liver endocardial hemorrhages near the heart valves yellow brain bilateral hematomas in the angle of the mandible subcutaneous hemorrhages in areas of venipuncture severe epiglottal swelling.

CARDIOMYOPATHY PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This female 9-year-old fruit bat was found dead in its cage. It was found dead along with three other bats. This bat was caught up with other free flight bats in the tropical forest for routine physical exam. It was in holding for 24-48 hours. At necropsy there were 4-5 white spots in the web of left wing. There were no visible cutaneous or visceral fat stores. The left lung had adhesions to the parietal pleura with two small areas of hemorrhage in the middle and caudal lobes. There was free blood in the thoracic cavity on the left side. The heart was slightly rounded and on cut section the left ventricle wall appeared greatly thickened and the right ventricular wall was small. There was slight subdural hemorrhage over the frontal sinuses.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA HEPATOMA PULMONARY ADENOMA. This 15-year-old female impala had hind limb lameness for several months which had recently worsened such that the left rear legs was minimally weight bearing. The animal was immobilized and the left tarsus was determined to be severely affected with hemorrhagic osteoarthritis and had restricted extension. Recovery from anesthesia was slow and poor and the animal was found in lateral recumbency overnight. Euthanasia was performed the following morning for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed approximately 150 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the peritoneal cavity several 3-6 mm. masses on the surface of the lungs and a linear chain of black raised lesions on the surface of the left middle lung lobe. Several 3-7 mm. vascular masses were noted on the serosal surface of the left renal artery. A 3 x 3 x 2 cm. mass was in the liver approximately 2 cm. from the bile duct the gall bladder was distended with black fluid and the wall of the gall bladder was hemorrhagic. Multiple cysts were noted in both uterine horns and the left kidney had a large cyst on the cranial pole. Degenerative changes were noted in the left tarsal joint.

TRAUMA GASTROENTERITIS RENAL COCCIDIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2.5-year-old male wallaby was humanely euthanized. It was found on exhibit with the left leg caught in a rope. It was immobilized. No fractures were palpated. The stifle demonstrated bilateral laxity. Radiographs revealed a small tear in the cranial aspect of the tibial crest. The condition became much worse over the next 24 hours and was euthanized. This wallaby had a history of periodic decreased appetite. No recent Toxoplasma titers have been run. The dentistry was performed 2.5 months ago the appetite became consistently better but episodes of decreased appetite have been increasing again recently. At necropsy there were no gross lesions except for a circumferential abrasion just distal to the left tarsus. There was marked lateral to medial laxity at the left stifle. Internally there was mild thickening of the edges of the leaflets of the mitral valve. The contents of the stomach were mostly grass. The colon contained normal stool.
