The urine was cloudy with mucoid clots. A sample was saved for urinalysis. The pancreas was hemorrhagic.
HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 1.5-year-old gecko was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy puncture wounds were identified in the base of the tail with marked muscle wasting.

PULMONARY ASPERGILLOSIS EMACIATION MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This greater than 6-year-old female tanager presented with head tremors and lack of balance control. The bird had weight loss and melena. The animal received supportive care but died. Necropsy revealed a large ovoid heart enlarged kidneys and an enlarged liver with a rough protuberance in the main lobe.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 14-year-old male bat had decreased mobility for 1-2 months received supportive care and was isolated to a smaller cage for medicating and to prevent long falls. The bat was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed dark patches of discoloration in the heart lung and kidney bloated intestines yellow/brown liver with dark discoloration at the margins and normal appearing trachea.

INANTION RENAL GOUT PULMONARY EDEMA. This 10-year/11-month-old female gallinule was found dead. It was noted that the food was not touched from the previous evening or morning diet. This animal had a previous left toe amputation with biopsy results indicating chronic necrotizing cellulitis osteomyelitis and fracture. Approximately one week prior to death the animal presented with lameness and plantar skin cracks on the right foot. The lesions were debrided treated and the animal was pulled off exhibit. Clinical improvement was noted. Several days prior to death the animal broke down in the left limb and was unable to stand or walk. The animal died several hours following recheck examination. At necropsy the gallinule was thin with a prominent keel. There was mild pasting of urates around the vent. The previous surgical sites were within normal limits. The liver was mildly enlarged but with sharp edges dark red to brown and very friable. The gall bladder was distended. The spleen was moderately large slightly swollen and pale pink. The kidneys were pale tan and cranial poles appeared slightly enlarged. The distal 0.5 cm. of bowel is thickened.

CHRONIC CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION. This 21-yeary-old female chinchilla died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed congested lungs a nutmeg appearance to the liver a large yellow clot in the vena cava and no other abnormalities.

HIGH-GRADE LYMPHOMA PYLORUS. This 17-year-old female llama had a 3-4 week history of diarrhea that had progressively worsened and the animal was not responding to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a soft mass in the spleen of similar consistency as the adjacent splenic parenchyma. A large mass was present in the region of the duodenum and associated with perforation of the bowel.

END-STAGE RENAL DISEASE NEPHROSCLEROSIS NECROTIZING STEATITIS MAMMARY HYPERPLASIA/ADENOMA APOCRINE GLAND ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female African hunting dog had a history of inappetence and weight loss of approximately one month’s duration. Supportive care was administered but the animal became azotemic did not respond to fluid therapy and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation worn teeth a nodular mass in the area of the left caudal abdominal mammary gland to 3 cm. in greatest dimension that had been present for a year with no growth. Areas of palpable nodules were also noted in the inguinal and right caudal mammary chain but also did not appear to be enlarged. Multiple various sized firm masses were present along the dorsum in the cervical region and proximal shoulder region. Multiple firm nodules were present throughout the pulmonary lobes. Mild thickening of the mitral valve was noted. The kidneys were pale with an irregular cortical surface. Muscles were atrophied. A few small foci of white discoloration were on serosal surfaces of the abdominal organs.
adult. Weight: 314 g.  Euthanased.  Pulmonary congeestion.  Tumour - suspect mammary.

GRANULOMATOUS MYOCARDITIS HEPATITIS BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS PNEUMONIA SPLENITIS. This 4-year-old chameleon has a history of nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism and had been treated with little improvement. Coelomic transudate developed and the animal’s condition continued to decline despite treatment. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy two 1 mm. in diameter gray to pink masses were present on the tail base. A large quantity of viscous serosanguineous fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Multiple white raised masses were present in the liver. Similar masses were present in the lung. The right side of the heart was replaced by pale yellow to white fibrous tissue. The left kidney was enlarged and nearly completely replaced by yellow to white tissue.

YOLK COELOMITIS WITH ADHESIONS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS. This 7-year-old female chicken had a surgery in April and June for retention of several eggs in the coelom. In April 18 eggs were removed and 17 in June. A deslorelin implant was placed after surgery in April. At three month recheck no further eggs had been produced and a six month recheck revealed egg production had restarted. The eggs were removed again and a leuprolide injection was administered. One week later the patient was found moribund and an additional surgery identified yolk coelomitis. This bird had been receiving meloxicam and an antibiotic but died. Necropsy revealed mild erythema of plucked skin warm coelomic contents (after three hours of refrigeration) eight eggs in the coelom four of which were deflated and one intact egg in the uterus. No patency could be traced from the position of the egg to the coprodeum. Several adhesions were noted. The body wall was markedly reddened and large quantities of intracoelomic fat were seen. The colon and small intestine were mildly thickened and reddened. The lungs were consolidated and reddened solid gelatinous yolk material was attached to the right kidney the liver was yellow and pink with a friable texture and marked reddening was present around the openings in the vent. The right ureter was dilated.

EUTHANASIA INANITION GASTRITIS. This greater than 12-year-old female tree boa was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic weight loss and anorexia. At necropsy there were three old retained necrotic ova. The boa was very emaciated. There were very little to no fat stores present. There were three hemorrhagic stalk-like masses in the stomach at the cardiac sphincter.

Kidney: focal cortical cyst Ovary: paraovarian cyst Thoracic cavity: moderate pleural effusion Comments: Overall findings were highly suggestive of hypoproteinemia and poor body condition. Hypoproteinemia is often associated with severe parasitism; however parasites were not observed during the necropsy. Histopathology; virology; bacteriology; nutrition; and parasitology is in progress. Cyst found in the kidney and adjacent to the ovary were incidental findings and were unassociated with the cause of this animal's demise. Schantel A. Hayes; DVM Liver: severe; centrilobular to midzonal necrosis Heart: minimal myofiber degeneration with numerous intracellular protozoa (Sarcocyst) Kidney: multifocal mild interstitial fibrosis with multifocal tubular mineralization Stomach: moderate crypt hyperplasia Comments: The primary cause for hepatic lesions could not be determined histologically however; lesions may represent anemia or acute cardiovascular collapse (heart failure). Another differential is vitamin E and selenium deficiency. To rule out this etiology; liver has been submitted to nutrition. A supplemental report will be released when results are available. Changes in the heart were minimal. There were large numbers of Sarcocyst within myofibers. This finding is generally incidental however; large numbers may impede cardiac conduction and cause cardiovascular compromise. There was no evidence of parasites in sections of stomach or intestine examined however; many coccidial oocyst and trichostrongyles were found in feces submitted to parasitology. The parasite load may have contributed to the long history of diarrhea. Schantel A. Hayes; DVM

DISSEMINATED SARCOMA PNEUMONIA RUMINORETICULITIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female gazelle was being treated for suspected pneumonia that did not respond. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed completely consolidated left lung and numerous masses within the left lung a purulent exudate in the pleural space adhesions of the left lung to the diaphragm and thoracic wall normal right lung and yellow gritty masses along the maxillary and mandibular gingiva. Numerous white masses of varying size were in the pancreas and on the serosal surfaces of the colon and mesentery. A small cystic structure was noted in the left kidney and corticomedullary architecture was indistinct. Abomasal mucosa was mottled and slightly hyperemic and normal feces were in the large intestine.

Skin: Vascular malformation Comments: The described histomorphologic changes are most consistent with a vascular malformation; such as a vascular hamartoma. Vascular hamartomas are benign developmental malformations. In some forms; proliferative vessels may dissect locally into adjacent stroma. The described changes extend to the deep margins; therefore; excision cannot be confirmed. Monitoring of the site for recurrence may be warranted. Colleen F. Monahan; DVM

METASTATIC UTERINE ADENOCARCINOOMA BLASTOMYCOSIS BALANTIDIUM ATHEROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 43-year-old female gorilla has a several year history of reproductive bleeding and trials with various medical therapies. In March 2008 an ovariohysterectomy was performed and adenocarcinoma with carcinomatosis and lymphatic invasion was noted. She recovered from surgery and did well until her last three months. Ultrasound revealed masses in her abdominal body wall and near her aorta as well as lymph nodes around the great vessels in her abdominal cavity. A Tru-cut biopsy of a mass in the body wall revealed carcinoma. Progesterone therapy and dexamethasone as well as other supportive care were administered but the gorilla lost 80 lbs. over a three month period and developed marked peripheral edema. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized edema especially of the arms legs and feet. A total of four liters of fluid was removed from the abdomen thorax and subcutaneous tissues of the limbs (combined). Several red/purple body wall masses were noted on the ventral midline. Skin of the external right mandible had a chronic abscess with pale gray fluid. Diffuse black lesions were on the surface and extended into the parenchyma of the lungs resembling anthracosis. Nodules up to 1.5 cm. in greatest dimension were present throughout the pulmonary parenchyma and on the surface. A few tiny palpable nodules were on the heart valves and some scarring was noted in the epicardium especially at the apex. Multiple foci of possible necrosis were in the hepatic lobes and some scarring was noted on the capsular surface. A small amount of milk could be expressed from both mammary glands. The kidneys were symmetrical dark red and had deep fissures on the cortex that gave them a mottled irregular appearance. A moderate amount of scarring was present throughout the medulla more on the right than left.
HEPATITIS SPLENITIS PNEUMONIA. This 11-year-old male pintail had a history of weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a cataract was present in the left eye.
NA

SEGMENTAL BACTERIAL ENTERITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION CHRONIC EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS MARKED BILIARY HYPERPLASIA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATION. This 4-year-old female red kangaroo had blood work that indicated renal disease and the animal died during anesthesia to place a jugular catheter for fluid therapy. Necropsy revealed atrophic pale and possibly fibrotic kidneys lymphoid stimulation in the spleen thickened gall bladder wall meningeal congestion gastric ulceration digested blood sand and hair in the alimentary tract possible increased intraocular pressure pale streaked myocardium and epicardium.

END STAGE RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old female ring-tailed lemur had a history of weight loss and progressive renal disease. The lemur was found in lateral recumbency on the exhibit floor and blood work revealed renal failure. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition small and misshapen kidneys.

MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA PODODERMATITIS ENTERITIS RENAL GOUT. This 8-year-old male whistling duck was found dead in the pool without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy water was present in the air sacs and coelomic cavity. Multiple small yellow masses were present within the abdominal air sacs. Jet lesions were identified in the ascending aorta.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS HYPERTENSION CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE GASTRITIS. This female 19-year-old mandrill died. It was positive for SIV. It had swelling of the left eye and hyphema. There was proptosis of the left eye. There was wound on the back. At necropsy there were several superficial bite wounds over the head right arm and perianal area. There was chronic pneumonia with numerous consolidated areas. There was lots of fatty tissue in abdominal cavity with adhesions between organs. The liver was slightly friable.

LYMPH NODE ABSCESS RUMINORETICULITIS ENTEROCOLITIS. This 3.5-year-old male gerenuk had been acquired as a yearling and at that time was noted to be small and underdeveloped for its age compared to conspecifics that were age matched. The animal subsequently developed normally and sired four calves only one of which has survived beyond a few days of age. This animal subsequently was noted to be ataxic and had difficulty standing up from sternal recumbency with a base-wide stance and is swaying hypermetric gait with the rear limbs. Radiographs of the vertebral column and head revealed some well-defined radiolucent areas in a couple of the cervical vertebrae and possibly alignment or other issues with the caudal cervical vertebra. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A primate mycobacterial stat-pack test was positive on two different occasions. Atypical mycobacteriosis has been diagnosed in a conspecific from the facility. Necropsy revealed locally extensive fibrinous peritonitis over the surface of the diaphragm liver spleen and portions of the abdominal wall where these tissues were in contact with each other. An enlarged caudal cervical lymph node contained an abscess comprised of green/white pasty material. A large cavitated lesion with a suppurative exudate was present within an enlarged lateral process of C3 on the right side and a smaller similar focus was present in the dorsal lateral wall of C4. The vertebral body of C6 was entirely “hollowed out” and filled with similar exudate and this lesion was associated with compression of the spinal cord.

Lungs: Mild; multifocal bronchiolar and bronchial epithelial hypertrophy. Comment: The described changes in the bronchial and bronchiolar epithelium are mild and nonspecific. This may indicate reactive hyperplasia secondary to irritation higher in the respiratory tract or may be within the spectrum of normal for this strain. Serology and /or histology of the dead pups may provide more specific information with respect to the cause of death. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; ACLAM

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION ATHEROSCLEROSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION HEPATOMA BILIARY CYSTADENOMA PYELONEPHRITIS NEUTROPHILIC CYSTITIS EUTHANASIA. This 32-year-old two-toed sloth was lethargic for the past few weeks and blood work revealed renal disease. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the kidneys had an irregular subcapsular surface and mottling as well as small cysts. The liver had an irregular red mass on the caudal edge of one lobe. Additionally two roughly spherical greenish masses were identified on the capsular surfaces of the liver. One of the coronary vessels was rigid. The interior surface of the aorta was roughened. The urinary bladder was thickened.

PROLIFERATIVE AND EXFOLIATIVE ESOPHAGITIS RHINITIS AND STOMATITIS. This 13.5-year-old male boa has a prolonged history of gastrointestinal and respiratory disease that has not responded to various medications. All three boas in this group have acquired the disease. Previous histologic examinations have identified esophagitis tracheitis and pneumonia. This snake died and necropsy revealed dehydration fair fat body presentation voluminous quantity of free yellow-tinged fluid throughout the coelom excessive pericardial fluid and thickened and mucous-filled lungs dilated esophagus especially in the cervical region empty gastrointestinal tract engorged gallbladder firm and slightly mottled liver urate stasis in the kidneys and prominent dilatation of the major vessels.

GASTRIC SPIRILLIFORM BACTERIA METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male lion had been lethargic with inconsistent appetite and attitude and did not train well. One month earlier the animal was diagnosed with probable pulmonary metastasis and the liver was cystic with possible neoplastic disease. The animal eats better on pain medication and other supportive care but then developed a cough was immobilized to obtain a hepatic biopsy and at that time it was detected that the lungs had metastatic lesions and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple nodules throughout the lungs a 12 cm. cavitated tumor containing red fluid in the liver and numerous cysts in the liver. Some 1 cm. nodules were on the pancreas. Several intestinal lymph nodes were enlarged. Both kidneys were redder than expected. The right eye had a soft bump where the iris meets the sclera. This eye had been swollen and had higher pressure when palpated compared to the left eye.

HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA (LIVER LUNG SPLEEN HEART) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 11.5-year-old lion had a history of declining health over the past month. A basal cell carcinoma had been removed from the right front leg one week previously. Local lymph nodes were also enlarged. The enlarged lymph node was surgically removed; however the animal’s recovery from anesthesia was poor and it was found dead 36 hours postoperatively. At necropsy several masses were present in the mediastinum. Numerous 1-3 mm. in diameter white foci were present in the liver. Some larger masses were also present with foci of necrosis. Similar masses were also identified within the spleen lungs heart and gastric lymph nodes.
SHOCK INTESTINAL IMPACTION (GROSS DIAGNOSIS). This 6-year-old female sloth was found dead. At necropsy multiple wood fibers and ingesta were present in the duodenum.

HEPATITIS PROTOZOAL COLITIS (GIARDIASIS) COELOMITIS AIR SACCULITIS BONE MARROW HYPOPLASIA. This 10-year-old female chicken was emaciated anemic and lethargic. The animal was transfused but its condition declined rapidly and later found dead. At necropsy the spleen was enlarged and pale.

PANCREATIC EXOCRINE ATROPHY BLOAT EMPHYSEMATOUS GASTRITIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old female squirrel monkey was found recumbent and had been clinically normal the previous day. It had a previous history of abdominal/subcutaneous abscess with rupture ovarian granulosa cell tumors (hysterectomy in 2009) and intermittent diarrhea that was treated with pancreatic enzymes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition small amount of free thoracic fluid reddened lungs moderate amount of free bloody fluid many adhesions severely distended stomach discolored deep red to purple with emphysematous walls possible adhesions of the proximal duodenum and pyloric region of the stomach ingesta in the intestines and thin body condition. The pancreas could not be identified.

INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old female rattlesnake was euthanized due to chronic regurgitation and failure to gain weight. At necropsy the gastric mucosa was hypertrophied. The liver was pale yellow.

URETERAL TREMATODIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female ocellated turkey had a chronic inability to stand was down on its hocks and had ulcerated hock lesions. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. No gross lesions typical of mycobacteriosis or aspergillosis were seen but these have been diagnosed in conspecifics.

TRACHEAL EDEMA TRACHEAL HEMORRHAGE EPITHELIAL HYPERPLASIA SHOCK. This 6-year-old female duck presented with dyspnea. Tracheoscopy revealed occlusion of the main stem bronchi by thick mucoid to hemorrhagic material. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the tracheal mucosa was red. Syrinx and main stem bronchi were filled with thick mucoid material.

DYSTOCIA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ENTERITIS HEPATITIS SPLENITIS. This 4-year-old female squirrel monkey was pregnant and expected to deliver soon. The animal was suddenly found dead. At necropsy a small quantity of blood was present in the perineum. A large fully developed female fetus was present in the uterus. A second placenta was identified within the uterus with a small firm brownish disc adjacent to it possibly an early fetal death of a fraternal twin. The head of the fetus appeared to be too large to fit into the pelvic canal.

LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC MENINGOENCEPHALIITS EUTHANASIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 9-year-old male coconut lorikeet came from a flock with a history of Baylisascaris infection. The animal developed a mild head tilt that progressed over the next 11 days despite treatment and the animal was euthanized.

GRANULOMATOUS MEDIASTINITIS PNEUMONIA AND LYMPHADENITIS POSSIBLE MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 15-year-old male tree kangaroo was reportedly lethargic and had a swollen face/jaw of less than one day duration. Physical examination revealed depression decreased lung sounds edema in the face legs scrotum and abdominal ascites. The animal developed respiratory cardiac failure shortly thereafter and did not respond to emergency treatment. Necropsy revealed moderate body condition the previously described edema and ascites worn teeth edematous lymph nodes thoracic effusion adhesion of the lung pleura to the thoracic wall multiple caseous nodules within the parenchyma of the lung and mediastinum. The left atrium was completely occluded with granulomatous masses and the right atrium had similar lesions to a lesser degree.

PULMONARY ASPERGILLOSIS VASCULAR AMYLOIDOSIS EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY. This approximately 18-year-old female flamingo had a one week history of debilitation from exertional myopathy. The bird was being maintained in a sling. The bird became acutely dyspneic and died. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition bruising of muscles in multiple sites multifocal white to gray nodules throughout both lungs and a mottled spleen.

MALIGNANT ROUND CELL TUMOR (PROBABLY INTESTINAL ORIGIN) FAT NECROSIS GASTRIC ENDOCRINE CARCINOMA. A mass was removed from the intestine of this 16-year-old female California kingsnake and the intestine was anastomosed. The animal died the next day. The mass had been causing visible distention and at surgery a reddish-purple oval mass was attached to the intestine. At necropsy pronounced biliverdin pigment was at the tip of the cecum or other portion of the gut. This mass did not seem connected to the intestine and was a dark color. A small purple mass was noted near the ovaries and multiple soft yellow masses were adhered to the body wall. The anastomosis was intact with no signs of leakage.

Cause of death uncertain at this time; please see comments Comments: Gross findings are nonspecific and severe autolysis may preclude a final diagnosis for cause of death. The most severe gross changes were observed within the liver. Final diagnosis is pending histologic findings. Additional tissues have been saved for further diagnostics if they are indicated. Molly H. Seavey; DVM M Liver; small intestine; adrenal gland: Chronic multifocal mineralized granulomas Heart: Multifocal myofiber degeneration Brainstem: Multifocal lipofuscinosis Kidney: Mild to moderate interstitial congestion Possible septicemia or parasite migration; see comments Comments: Histologic findings of well-defined areas of necrosis are most suggestive of a migrating parasite (trematode; cysticercus; etc.) and/or bacterial infection (Corynebacterium spp; Actinomyces (Arcanobacter) pyogenes; Fusobacterium spp. etc.) Marked autolysis precludes optimal histologic examination and a definitive cause of the lesion is uncertain. There was no evidence of positive acid fast bacteria (e.g. tuberculosis) within the sections examined. Myocardial fibrosis and lipofuscinosis represent chronic age-related changes. In this case; the locally extensive increase in fibrosis may have resulted in cardiac electroconduction abnormalities and may have been a contributing cause to sudden death. The coccidial oocysts recovered from the feces of this alpaca indicate some parasitism is present. Vitamin E and Selenium levels and bacterial culture of the liver is pending and will be released in an addendum. Molly H. Seavey; DVM MPH Possible septicemia or parasite migration; see comments Comments: Further findings do not alter original diagnosis. Molly H. Seavey; DVM MPH

HYPOVOLEMIC SHOCK MYELOLIPOMA VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY SUSPECT TRAUMA. This 6.5-year-old female Fischer’s lovebird was found dead. At necropsy there were multiple follicles of various sizes in the urogenital system and a large amount of hemorrhage in the thoracic cavity.
adult. Weight: 661 g.  Chronic salpingitis +/- coelomitis.  Dehydration.  Cloacal impaction: faecoliths and uroliths.  Impacted preen gland.  Digit luxation.  Trauma to boady wall.

FATTY LIVER FOLLICULAR STASIS AND DEGENERATION. This approximately 28-year-old female beaded lizard was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy there was severe postmortem autolysis. It had been dead for several days. The carcass was thin.

ISLET CELL CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE. This approximately 20-year-old female mountain lion was seen walking stiffly in the rear for one day and it was found deceased in its enclosure the following morning. It had tested positive for microfilaria Cytauxzoon felis and feline immunodeficiency virus nine years earlier. It is listed as a Texas cougar (Puma concolor). Necropsy revealed decreased muscle mass heavy flea burden maggots in the oral cavity degloving of the proximal tail and ventral tail base and perianal region with severe maggot infestation dry tissues generalized pallor small irregular kidneys with multiple cysts in the cortical parenchyma bilateral hypertrophy of the adrenals maggot infestation of the oral and nasal passages and moderate fat deposition in the falciform omental and mesenteric regions.

INTESTINAL LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female hedgehog had a history of decreased appetite hematuria and lethargy and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large jejunal mass and a smaller mass in small intestinal tissue with firm masses at the mesenteric root. The liver was tan with rounded margins. Radiographic evidence of a stone was present in the kidney.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BACTERIAL ENTERITIS EMACIATION. This 15-year-old pochard was found dead in the water. It had a history of lameness in the left leg and was nearly blind. Necropsy revealed consolidation of the left lung and degenerative changes in the left tarsal joint.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH DIC PROBABLE CLOSTRIDIAL INFECTION. This female 8-year-old duck was found sitting on its nest and appeared very weak. It died during treatment. Necropsy revealed petechial hemorrhages over the epicardium free blood in the coelomic cavity and a 1 cm. band of hemorrhage over the serosal surface of the liver extending into the underlying hepatic parenchyma.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS DROWNED MICROGRANULOMATOSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS WITH CILIATES. This approximately 17-year-old blue-tongued skink was found at the bottom of the pool. Necropsy revealed thousands of variably-sized cysts with serous fluid within the left and right ovaries. The right ovary was 4-5 in. in length and irregular and appeared to be adhered to the liver by a white mottled firm structure. A similar mottled white nodular structure was associated with the right caudal border of the liver. Food was present in the stomach.

PIGMENTARY NEPHROSIS LOW GRADE SEPSIS EMACIATION. This 6-year-old male pygmy goat had recent evaluation for weakness became acutely lethargic and hypothermic and with hind limb paresis. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous edema in the brisket region 20 ml. of straw-colored fluid in the peritoneum blunting of the ruminal papillae a small amount of sand in the reticulum some possible ulcers in the distal abomasum some pale streaking in the medulla of the left kidney petechiae on the mucosal surface of the trachea a small amount of clear straw-colored fluid in the pericardium thickened adrenal cortex and pale right adrenal medulla.

ECTOPIC EGG EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old turkey was geriatric and inappetent and had minimal response to supportive care. Blood work was within normal limits. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

TRAUMA SHOCK. This 9-year-old female duck was found dead in the pool. Three ducklings were also found on the pool. At necropsy hemorrhage was present adjacent to the left eye and within the oral cavity. Extensive hemorrhage was noted within the skull.

CONJUNCTIVAL AND NASAL GLAND SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA CONSISTENT WITH HYPOVITAMINOSIS A. This approximately 5-year-old male spiny lizard was found moribund and was euthanized. The animal was being treated for possible hypovitaminosis A. Gross necropsy revealed fair body condition swelling of the mandibular soft tissues a chronic corneal scar OS pulmonary congestion and adequate fat bodies within the coelom. A digested mealworm was present in the stomach and another was present within the pharyngeal area.

ARTICULAR GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female frilled lizard had a history of chronic articular gout and was receiving supportive care until quality of life deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dark mottled liver multiple creamish deposits in many joints small kidneys and no other abnormalities.

BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA BACTERIAL HEPATITIS. This 10-year-old male rattlesnake had a mass presumably associated with the liver. The animal was found dead. At necropsy an 8-10 cm. pale yellow multilobular mass was present in the liver. Multiple smaller nodules were present throughout the liver.

GUNSHOT WOUND EUTHANASIA LYMPHOCYTIC MYOCARIDITIS HEPATITIS B VIRUS INFECTION. This 28-year-old male captive bred chimpanzee received gunshot wounds following an attack on a human. The animal was subsequently euthanized. This animal tested positive for hepatitis B surface antibody. Necropsy revealed gunshot wounds to the upper right arm and right side of the face a shattered right maxilla missing premolars #3 and 4 shattered left maxilla a transverse fracture of the hard palate.

ANTERIOR UVEITIS KERATITIS RENAL GOUT GLOMERULAR FIBROSIS RHINITIS. This 9-year-old snake had a history of chronic enlargement of the left orbit and retained spectacles. The spectacle was removed and the animal was held out of water on moist paper towels and was treated with fluids and antibiotics. The animal died approximately one week after surgery. At necropsy foci of discoloration were noted in the scales. Corneal edema was noted in the left eye. A torn membrane was present deep to the orbit.

GRANULOMATOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS PANCREATIC FIBROSIS. This 11-year-old male hooded merganser has a history of heart murmur of 1.5 years duration. No treatment was administered to avoid stress. This bird was found lethargic and in an abnormal position in holding and died while transported to the hospital. The bird had lost substantial weight in the last six months. Necropsy revealed moderately severe subacute lesions on the bottom of the feet attributed to being housed indoors for two weeks due to an outdoor predation problem. The spleen was small but diffusely granulomatous. The right side of the heart was moderately enlarged. The liver had approximately 10% affected with small tan nodular lesions.

BACTERIAL/FOREIGN BODY COELOMITIS INTESTINAL PERFORATION SEPSIS. This 25-year-old male Chilean flamingo was noted to be a little slow in the flock the previous day and was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed congestion in one part of the right lung mild inflammation in the air sacs mild reddening of the serosal surface of the intestine and mucosal surface of some sections of the intestine liquid ingesta in the alimentary tract and congestion in the meninges.
EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS INANITION. This 13-year-old male duck was lethargic and very thin. Osteoarthritis was noted in the stifle. The animal was humanely euthanized.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS NEURONAL LIPOFUSCINOSIS. This greater than 5-year-old leothrix has always had good plumage but could not fly well. It may have been attacked by exhibit mates. Necropsy revealed right eye cere and 95% of both beaks missing with hemorrhage in the remaining tissues of the head. The spleen was markedly enlarged and the liver was mottled and friable. The cloaca was prolapsed. The cranial portions of both lungs were red and depressed.
HEPATITIS ENTERITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This 2-year-old female lory was treated for lethargy and was found dead shortly thereafter. At necropsy the liver was mottled.

ACUTE BACTERIAL ENTERITIS POSSIBLE CLOSTRIDIUM EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female chicken is from a flock that developed acute hemorrhagic enteritis with crop stasis and weakness. This bird was euthanized for humane reasons and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed splenomegaly friable liver gray meninges aspiration hemorrhagic intestines and egg binding. This group of birds was fed marigold flowers at the onset of signs. Brain and kidney have been submitted for WNV testing.

UROGENITAL CARCINOMA ISLET CELL TUMOR RUPTURED PANCREATIC DUCT WITH PERITONITIS AND PACREATITIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 26.5-year-old female California sea lion had a full-week history of decreased mobility and a CT scan revealed enlargement of the prescapular lymph nodes mesenteric lymph node mineralization a mass in the caudal left mammary gland severe bilateral hip arthropathy with subluxation of both hips and poor response to supportive care. Visual deficits associated with ocular disease were also present. The animal became inappetent and had signs of severe pain and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1.5 cm. cyst-like structure on the serosal surface of the left thyroid pale yellow mucoid discharge from the left bronchus multiple pinpoint nodules in the right cranial pulmonary lobe multiple cyst-like structures in both kidneys hepatomegaly with rounded edges opaque capsule and multiple 1-3 mm. tan lesions throughout the parenchyma. The mucosal surface of the gallbladder was diffusely thickened but with normal appearing bile a 2 cm. in diameter mass on the distal aspect of the pancreas a 1 cm. red dark mass with tan caseous core on the serosal surface of the jejunum congested mesenteric vasculature a 2 cm. multinodular mass on the serosal surface of the proximal duodenum and slightly cloudy straw-colored abdominal fluid. The axillary lymph nodes had caseous debris on cut surface and multiple mesenteric lymph nodes were larger than normal. The eyes had luxated mature cataracts and granulation tissue in the corneas.
adult. Weight: 246 g.  Otitis media. Rat respiratory disease complex; otitis media.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEART FAILURE RENAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS INANITION. This 11-year-old female wallaroo had generalized subcutaneous edema. Thoracic auscultation revealed a grade IV-V out of VI systolic murmur with an irregular arrhythmia and harsh respiratory sounds. Thoracic ultrasound revealed marked right heart dilatation with tricuspid regurgitation (right heart failure). The animal was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy there was marked subcutaneous edema thoracic effusion and ascites. The liver was small and firm with a cobblestone texture. The heart was enlarged and had a 3 cm. diameter circular lesion near the apex in the interventricular septum which was mottled and translucent. Atria were enlarged and thin walled.

RENAL GOUT PNEUMONIA DIGIT NECROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This approximately 9-year-old male cockatiel died. It had a history of showing less ability to walk on right foot. It also had lost weight. The right foot was swollen and the animal demonstrated high limb pain. It regurgitated gavaged feedings. It was nonweight bearing on the legs and sat with its tail in the air. Treatment was initiated. At necropsy the crop was full of gavage from recent tube feeding. The pectoral musculature had bruises due to injections. The right front third toe was swollen and appeared necrotic at the end of the amputated toe. The kidneys appeared enlarged and swollen.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female meerkat was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes when its response to anti-inflammatory drug therapy for degenerative joint disease diminished. Necropsy revealed severe arthritic changes in the elbows and stifles and decreased range of motion. The kidneys had white mottling. The spleen had pale mottling. A lobulated hepatic mass was on the right side of the abdomen and a pale focus was in the gall bladder. The tail tip was enlarged with chronic ulceration.

AIR SAC GRANULOMA PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE HEAD TRAUMA MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA. This approximately 7-year-old male lory had a history of being on the floor of the aviary most of the time. The bird was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed enlarged heart pale liver and severe pulmonary congestion.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK POSSIBLE ANAPHYLAXIS OR TOXICOSIS. This 10.5-year-old male California sea lion was found dead floating in the pool. The animal had eaten normally in the morning feeding and had been behaving normally at that time. The animal had been treated with ivermectin as a routine heartworm preventative and had shown no adverse reactions to ivermectin in the past. Necropsy revealed frothy blood tinged discharge in both nares bite marks on both rear flippers (postmortem) swollen edematous and tightly closed larynx frothy fluid in the trachea and laryngeal region frothy blood tinged fluid on cut surface of the lungs and no other significant findings.

SHOCK STRESS. This 4-year/2-month-old female otter was found dead. It had been received from shipment the evening prior to death. The shipping crate was metal with burlap covering the vents. There was dried blood on the cage floor and walls. The mammal curator thought the otter might have overheated. Fecal smear and floatation were negative for parasites; however there were 4+ red blood cells present. At necropsy the otter was in good condition. There was mild to moderate dental tartar. The mucous membranes appeared hyperemic. There was foul smelling blood tinged mucus at the perineum. The skeletal musculature was hyperemic/dark red/brown. The lungs appeared diffusely reddened. The mitral valve leaflet edges appeared slightly thickened. The diaphragm was dark red/brown. The spleen was mottled purple/red and contracted. There were bilateral multifocal red 1 mm. diameter foci in the adrenal glands. The gastric mucosa was gray and there were 10-12 cc. of watery gray fluid in the stomach. The intestinal serosa had multiple red foci. The mucosal surface of the intestine was hemorrhagic and there was a significant amount of blood tinged mucus present in the entire length of the intestine. No ingesta was present in the intestinal tract. Several mesenteric lymph nodes appeared enlarged. The meningeal vasculature of the brain appeared engorged. Sections of intestine stomach intestinal contents lung liver brain spleen kidney and heart were frozen for future use if needed.
TRAUMA RENAL CYST PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 8-year-old male quail entered the meerkat exhibit and was killed. At necropsy extensive trauma was noted over the wings legs neck and abdomen.

EUTHANASIA FAT ATROPHY ANEMIA. This 10-year/5-month-old female giraffe was humanely euthanized. It had an ongoing history of epistaxis. It had a recent history of anemia and declining blood cell parameters. Infectious disease was ruled out. At necropsy there was pericardial effusion. There was scarring on the serosal surface of the heart. The lymph nodes were enlarged within the abdominal cavity. There was fluid within the abdomen.
ENTERITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 12-year-old male lory had a history of lethargy and inappetence and was found dead. At necropsy the intestine appeared hemorrhagic.

EMACIATION RHABDOMYOLYSIS CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS. This 9-year-old female gerenuk had a severe bout of diarrhea and melena from 6/11-6/15 becoming anemic hypoproteinemic and leukopenic during this period. Supportive care was administered and the condition resolved. The animal appeared to be gaining weight and was doing well but on 8/29 developed watery diarrhea without melena. The animal quickly became anemic and hypoproteinemic again dropped weight quickly and despite intensive care the condition progressed and the animal died. No parasites or other pathogens were ever identified. Necropsy revealed cachexia fecal soiling on the tail and perineum complete absence of adipose stores tacky serosal surfaces approximately 800 ml. of clear yellowish fluid in the peritoneal cavity and approximately 200 ml. of similar fluid in the thoracic cavity small and contracted spleen foam in the airways congested lungs dark red left caudal and middle lungs edema in all pulmonary lobes mild nodularity in the mitral valve leaflets periodontal disease with missing teeth frothy contents in the forestomachs liquid digesta in the small intestine and large intestine small liver and bile distended gallbladder.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS WITH GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS HEPATIC RENAL AND SPLENIC LIPIDOSIS. This 10-year-old female cockatiel was alive in the morning found on the floor 30 minutes later was unresponsive and died in hand. Weight was down approximately 16 gm. but the bird had no abnormal behavior or clinical signs prior to death. Necropsy revealed pale tan kidneys.
CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 18-month-old male lory was found dead. At necropsy a 2 cm. section of intestine appeared necrotic and friable.
adult.  Euth. Chr.osteoarthritis?.

SCLEROSING PERITONITIS PROBABLE INTESTINAL PERFORATION EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female warthog had a history of intermittent constipation lethargy and inappetence that would typically resolve with mineral oil and analgesics. Recently the animal had partial inappetence lethargy and scant feces which did not improve with conservative treatment. A mass was noted in the ileocecocolic junction and exploratory laparotomy revealed multiple masses in the mesentery of the spiral colon and a large mass at the ileocecocolic junction. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The mass at the ileocecocolic junction was 14 cm. in diameter adhered to the gastrointestinal tract and difficult to dissect. Several sections were obtained. The mass had a 6 cm. in diameter hemorrhagic area in the center surrounded by fibrous tissue. Multiple masses of hard fat were also noted throughout the mesentery of the spiral colon.

CHOLESTASIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS AND GOUT ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS EMACIATION. This 23-year-old female duck had been lame on the right leg for three days. No fractures were seen radiographically and the animal was treated for soft tissue trauma with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The bird appeared to be responding but then presented with depression dyspnea and tachypnea. Radiographs revealed abnormal gastrointestinal and ingesta patterns in the distal coelom and elevated blood ureic acid was noted. The bird died during anesthetic recovery. Necropsy revealed a 3 cm. round dilated structure arising from the vent that was filled with feces and readily extruded from the vent. The urodeum was distended with clear pale urine and scant urates. The kidneys were small tan and friable. The lungs were hyperemia.

EUTHANASIA HEPATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 17-year-old captive bred male cougar was humanely euthanized. It had a history of ataxia in the hind limbs. It had general debilitation. It was on prednisone therapy for five days. It also had anorexia. At necropsy there was anthracosis in the lungs. The spleen was enlarged and had rounded borders. The adrenal glands were prominent/enlarged. The liver was enlarged and had firm multiple disseminated nodular masses. The liver was mottled red/gray.

EPICARDIAL FIBROSIS PERICARDIAL FIBROSIS INANITION PENTASTOME COELOMITIS. This 4-year-old female rattlesnake had a history of cardiac dilatation. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the atria were dilated. Two pentastome parasites were present in the coelomic cavity.

LYMPHOMA ECTOPIC EGG EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female chicken presented with a distended coelomic cavity and had no prior signs of illness. Ultrasound revealed a large ovoid spleen and blood work revealed hyperglobulinemia leukocytosis and mild anemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes when endoscopy revealed a soft tissue mass associated with organ displacement. Necropsy revealed numerous pinpoint white nodules throughout the liver and a large mass in one lobe with a cauliflower appearance. The spleen was massively enlarged and pale pink. Cystic structures were noted throughout the oviduct.

EMACIATION NEPHRITIS. This 1-month-old male rabbit was recently weaned and was found dead by keepers. It is part of a group that has recently been observed with diarrhea so had been treated accordingly. Necropsy revealed diarrhea around the caudal hind limbs and a superficial scrape on the left stifle. Body condition was thin. No ingesta was in the stomach and a 2 mm. circular thickened lesion in the fundic region was sampled. The small intestine was distended with thin yellow fluid. Abnormally small formed feces were in the rectum and colon. Cecal contents were more liquid than typical. No parasites were seen in fecal exams.

END STAGE RENAL DISEASE INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS CYTOLOGY. This 14-year-old male dart frog was found dead. The keeper noted that the animal had appeared larger than normal over the last few days. Reportedly the frog was still eating. Necropsy revealed generalized bloat in the body but no swelling of the limbs. Approximately 0.4 ml. of fluid were aspirated from the left side of the coelomic cavity. The liver was congested and had a 0.5 mm. tan nodule on the ventral caudal surface to the left of the midline. Female reproductive tract was identified. Lungs floated in formalin.

CYSTITIS NEPHRITIS PERITONITIS. This 3-year-old male sugar glider had a several week history of dysuria and lethargy. Urine culture revealed Pseudomonas which was resistant to numerous antibiotics. Ultrasound indicated possible urolithiasis. An abdominal exploratory was performed but no uroliths were found. Biopsy indicated chronic cystitis. Approximately one week post surgery the animal became suddenly lethargic and died several hours later. At necropsy yellow fibrous material was present in the subcutis adjacent to the surgical incision. A large quantity of yellow cloudy fluid was present in the abdominal cavity. Numerous adhesions were present adjacent to the urinary bladder.

ACUTE SHOCK CHRONIC PROVENTRICULITIS. This 3-year-old female lory was found seizuring in its exhibit. Emergency therapy was administered but the bird did not respond and died. Necropsy revealed nectar in the crop female gonad slightly enlarged spleen plant material and fluid in the proventriculus and plant material in the ventriculus hemorrhagic material in the duodenum and jejunum and subdural hemorrhage in the temporal region.

EUTHANASIA MULTICENTRIC LYMPHOSARCOMA. This approximately 3-year-old male polecat was humanely euthanized. It had a history of a large abdominal mass thin body condition and dermatitis. Thoracic auscultation revealed decreased lung sounds on the left side and inspiratory dyspnea. Thoracic radiographs revealed a possible mediastinal mass tracheal elevation pulmonary infiltrates and enlargement of the bronchial lymph nodes. There was a large mass at the root of the mesentery on abdominal radiographs. At necropsy there was a 7 cm. abdominal mass. There were metastatic nodules on the surface of the kidney spleen and liver. There was a large mediastinal mass. There were metastatic nodules in the pulmonary parenchyma.

PRESUMED MAST CELL TUMOR PULMONARY CARCINOMA HEPATOMA BILIARY CYSTIC DILATION NEUROENDOCRINE CARCINOMA PRESUMED FOLLICULAR INFUNDIBULAR ACANTHOMA. This 3.5-year-old female Virginia opossum was suspected to have hypothyroidism six months prior to death and a liposarcoma three months prior to death. A few weeks prior to death the animal became anorexic and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was an approximately 2 cm. firm subcutaneous nodule of the left knee and approximately 4 cm. soft nodule on the lateral aspect of the abdominal wall. There were spherical 1-2 cm. in diameter nodules distributed throughout the pulmonary parenchyma. There were five roundworms in the stomach. The abdominal cavity had a large bilobed tumor attached to the mesenteric fat. The spleen had an approximately 1 cm. spherical nodule in the cranial aspect. The liver had multiple firm nodules in the parenchyma including several which are cystic.

FATTY LIVER OVARIAN ADENOCARCINOMA. This approximately 14-year-old female boa died. It presented five months prior to death with swelling in the distal coelom. There was a mass that progressively enlarged. Radiographs were inconclusive. Ultrasound revealed a heterogeneous mass that was very vascular. Cytology from fluid aspirated from the mass resulted in numerous erythrocytes and fewer heterophils and macrophages. At necropsy the mucosa of the oral cavity was pale. The stomach contained food remnants. There was a mesovarium mass that was 12 x 6 cm. A thin fibrovascular tunic enveloped it. Approximately 40% of the contents of the mass were viscous thick bloody fluid. The rest of the mass was very vascular friable soft tissue.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY FIBROSIS ENTERITIS COLITIS BALANTIDIASIS PLEURITIS. This approximately 41-year-old male gorilla had a history of congestive heart failure pericardial peritoneal and thoracic effusion and marked subcutaneous edema. A prior pulmonary thrombus resulted in destruction of the right caudal lung lobe. At necropsy the thorax contained a large quantity of fluid. The trachea contained blood tinged foam. The left lung was edematous with many adhesions to the thoracic wall. The right lung was approximately one-half the normal size with extensive adhesions to the parietal pleura. There was a 2.5 cm. in diameter nodule containing greenish-yellow fluid and a 4 cm. in diameter fluid filled nodule also in the right lung. The abdominal cavity contained a large amount of straw colored fluid. The left kidney contained small tan nodules in the subcapsular area extending into the cortex. The liver was coarsely nodular with accentuation of the reticular pattern.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS RENAL TUBULAR URATE STASIS. This 5-year-old male blue-tongued skink was being treated for renal disease weight loss and inappetence and was being tube fed. It had regurgitated fluid after feeding the previous day and was found dead in the tank the following day. Necropsy revealed shedding red discoloration on the scales of the ventrum copious amount of food material in the coelom a perforation in the caudal third of the esophagus friable tissue in the region of the perforation and enlarged gritty kidneys.

EUTHANASIA INANITION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS THYROID FOLLICULAR HYPERPLASIA LEIOMYOMA (UTERUS). This 13-year-old female chinchilla has a history of weight loss despite treatment. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the body was extremely thin. Liver was pale. Kidneys were asymmetrical. A 1 cm. firm white mass was present in the uterus.
RENAL MINERALIZATION HEPATIC MELANOSIS INANITION. This 11-year-old gecko had a history of chronic weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized.

RENAL MYXOSPORIDIOSIS MICROSPORIDIOSIS. This greater than 1-year-old male horned frog was found dead in its enclosure. It was being kept separate from the female. It had been in a breeding situation but no offspring were produced. There was no abnormal behavior prior to death. An exhibitmate died with renal myxosporidiosis. At necropsy the lungs were red/black bilaterally and floated in formalin. The heart was congested. The liver was diffusely tan with mottled pinpoint brown areas.

SHOCK MAMMARY CARCINOMA. This captive bred female 11-year-old wallaroo died. The day prior to death it was found down with respiratory compromise dyspnea hypothermia and bloody oral and nasal discharge. Antibiotics fluid and supportive care were administered. Blood work revealed hypokalemia hematocrit of 54% and increased segmented and band neutrophils. At necropsy there were ample fat stores. The lungs were congested. The distal colon had a focal circumscribed lesion with a darkened center and yellow halo surrounding (5 x 4 mm.). There was approximately 20 ml. of bloody fluid in the abdominal cavity. The surface of the right and left kidneys appeared congested and friable. Mesenteric lymph node was enlarged and solid cream colored. The mammary gland felt nodular and fibrotic.
DUODENAL POLYP MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ECTOPIC SPLEEN. This 25-year-old neutered male llama was found dead. At necropsy two polypoid masses were noted in the proximal small intestine.

MALIGNANT NEUROENDOCRINE TUMOR(PROBABLE PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA) UTERINE LEIOMYOMA ENDOMETRITIS GASTRITIS. This 16-year-old female captive bred lion was euthanized following detection of disseminated neoplasia during exploratory laparotomy.

EUTHANASIA MAMMARY FIBROADENOCARCINOMA BRONCHITIS ENDOMETRITIS. This greater than 2-year-old female rat was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed with possible right mammary adenocarcinoma approximately three weeks prior to euthanasia. At necropsy the rat was in good body condition. There was a large lobulated well vascularized mass varying from light white to tan located subcutaneously along the right lateral abdomen and right inguinal area. The mass was in close proximity to the structures of the femoral triangle. There was an isolated serosal granuloma with associated cyst along the lateral edge of a loop of jejunum. The right uterine horn was greatly enlarged and was located in the left abdominal cavity ventral to the left uterine horn. No torsion was identified. The right uterine horn was dark pink to red. Dark blood could be observed within it just cranial to the cervix and blood was expressed from the vaginal cavity by pressing on the right uterine horn. The left uterine horn appeared normal in size and color. Vasculature to both horns was greatly enlarged. The right uterine horn contained a large pink semifirm mass that filled most of the entire horn and was attached to the ventral mucosa of the horn approximately midway in the horn. There were multiple firm yellow plaques present along the serosal surface of both lungs and on section extended into the parenchyma. The lesions varied from 1-5 mm. and varied in shape.

POSSIBLE VERTEBRAL TRAUMA ACUTE SHOCK ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 21-year-old female sea lion developed an acute onset of hind limb paresis. Following administration of the sedative she developed possible seizure activity and eventually developed respiratory arrest and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed good body condition dark red lungs that sank in formalin moderately thickened heart valves congestion of the stomach segmental dilatation of the small intestine and reddening of the mucosa.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ATHEROSCLEROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION ANESTHETIC DEATH. This approximately 13-year-old male meerkat presented two days earlier with a 2-3 day history of inappetence and lethargy. It appeared to have labored breathing on presentation and physical examination showed diffuse muscle atrophy hypothermia and labored breathing and radiographs revealed fluid in the thorax and abdomen. The meerkat died while anesthetized. Necropsy revealed pulmonary edema and fibrosis a firm yellow/brown mass in the left auricular region renal fibrosis enlarged adrenals and enlarged symmetrical prostate.

NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION PROBABLE WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME THYROID ADENOMA. This 5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of chronic abnormal hind end gait with intermittent weakness paresis and suspected arthritis. Steroid therapy was administered. The animal also has a history of severe progressive weight gain. Euthanasia was performed following an acute episode of hind limb weakness. Necropsy revealed overconditioned body a large amount of subcutaneous and serosal yellow adipose firm liver with multifocal pallor or streaking large biliary ducts both medullary cavities of the kidneys were thickened and white and multiple pale and fibrotic foci were on the serosal surface of the kidneys. The heart was slightly enlarged. The bladder was large and filled with fluid. The cranial cervical lymph nodes bilaterally were slightly enlarged.

UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE) ENCEPHALITIS CHRONC NEHRITIS HEPATITIS. This 6-year-old female rabbit had episodes of hemorrhage in the perineum. Uterine neoplasia was suspected. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed under anesthesia and the animal died despite resuscitation efforts. At necropsy a small quantity of frank blood was present in the abdomen. The liver was yellow. A 4.5 x 2 cm. mass was present in the left uterine horn.
BRONCHOPNEUMONIA BACTEREMIA INANITION. This 22-year-old milk snake was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy lungs were congested.

ENTERIC NEMATODIASIS. This 2-year/5-month-old female parrot died. At necropsy the small and large intestines were filled with large white stringy material (parasites). The back was bare of feathers. There were dirt and pebbles caked on the head. The body was in poor condition (emaciated).

AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL GOUT BACTERIAL ENTERITIS BUMBLEFOOT. This greater than 26-year-old male flamingo was found dead. This animal was reported to be thin on 5/22. At necropsy the bird was notably wasted in body condition across pectoral muscles. Both pes had notable chronic bumble lesions present the right pes centrally and the left pes on digit #4 along the interphalangeal joints. Ectoparasites were noted on the primaries of both wings. There was notable pneumoconiosis in the lungs. The atrioventricular valves were somewhat nodular on both sides but especially on the left. The gall bladder was largely distended with heavily viscous bile. The liver was greatly enlarged and had a waxy appearance on cut section. The renal parenchyma was golden yellow swollen and granular on cut section. The spleen was enlarged and had a waxy appearance. Sections of spleen and brain were frozen for future use if needed.

ULCERATIVE LARYNGITIS WITH INFRACTION PROBABLE ENDOTOXEMIA. This 12-year-old female ring-tailed lemur had some bleeding from her oral cavity noted during routine physical exam presumed to be from biting her tongue during capture. No lesion was found but the bleeding stopped and the mouth was cleaned out prior to recovery. Intubation was difficult so the animal was anesthetized for a facemask. Visual examination of the epiglottis was normal but during intubation attempts it was noted that the laryngeal membranes did not move much when breathing. The animal recovered from anesthesia with slight increase in respiratory noise but no apparent respiratory effort. Supportive care was administered but the animal died two days later. Necropsy revealed swelling around the larynx.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 15-year-old female chinchilla has a history of heart disease and weight loss. Examination revealed hypocalcemia hyperphosphatemia and azotemia. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were small and irregular.

ANESTHETIC DEATH MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 9-year-old female jaguar had intermittent episodes of diarrhea. The animal was anesthetized for examination; however cardiopulmonary arrest ensued. Resuscitation efforts were successful; however the animal later died. At necropsy the caudal margins of the lungs were consolidated. The gastric mucosa was thickened and brownish fluid was present in the lumen. Cyst-like structures were present on the ovary.

ENDOCRINE CARCINOMA WITH INTESTINAL PERFORATION GRANULOMATOUS BRONCHIOLITIS. This 8-year-old male karakul sheep had a history of depression apparent pain and inappetence. Supportive care was administered and the sheep appeared to respond but then rapidly deteriorated. Necropsy revealed septic peritonitis associated with rupture of the gastrointestinal tract. This sheep had a previous history of possible intestinal tract disease that had responded to therapy.
EUTHANASIA INSULINOMA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE ENTERITIS. This 6-year-old male ferret has a history of suspected insulinoma. Gross necropsy findings were not provided.

THYMOMA OBESITY. This 6-year-old male rabbit was found dead unexpectedly in its enclosure with no prior signs of illness other than chronic dacryocystitis that had improved substantially with antibiotics and nasal lacrimal flushing. Necropsy revealed overweight body condition 40 ml. of serosanguineous fluid with fibrin in the thoracic cavity and a 6 cm. necrotic and reddened mass with serosanguineous fluid pockets and purulent debris in the thoracic cavity. The mass was ventral to the heart and compressed the heart and lungs. The lungs were atelectatic and mottled. The mass incorporated the pericardium but the heart was grossly normal. Approximately 20 ml. of reddened fluid was in the abdominal cavity. Digesta was in the alimentary tract.

GRANULOMATOUS CHONDRITIS (RIB) RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 8.5-year-old female black-footed ferret had a one week history of pelvic limb paresis and one month history of progressive decline in mobility activity and appetite. The ferret was previously diagnosed with polyuria and polydyspnea attributed to renal failure. A gastric foreign body surgery was performed on this animal in 2010 and it was ovariohysterectomized in 2011 due to prolonged estrus and inappetence. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition moderate thoracic fat moderate atelectasis of the dorsal portions of the pulmonary lobes moderate abdominal and perirenal fat stores multiple hepatic cysts marked enlargement of the spleen with blue/black discoloration formed feces in the distal colon and rectum bilateral renal atrophy with roughened appearance mild enlargement of the left adrenal gland and no other abnormalities.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS TUBULAR DILATION AND DEGENERATION MESENTERIC GRANULOMAS WITH NEMATODES. This 283 gm. 4.5-year-old female Surinam toad was seen acting normal in the morning but was found dead at the end of the day. Significant findings at necropsy included severe coelomic distention with serosanguineous fluid and abundant follicles on both ovaries that occasionally showed congested vessels along the surface. There were approximately one dozen pinpoint round yellow granulomas attached to the serosal surfaces of the intestinal tract spread out along its entire length.

EMACIATION STRESS METABOLIC BONE DISEASE CALCINOSIS CIRCUMSCRIPTA. This 1-month-old rabbit is from a group in which the dam died two weeks earlier from bacterial typhlocolitis (G15-2053). The kit was subsequently raised by an experienced rabbit rehabilitator and appeared to be doing well until being found dead. No signs of illness were noted prior to death. Necropsy revealed good body condition food in the stomach and normal digested material in all sections of the alimentary tract.

EUTHANASIA RETICULOENDOTHELIOSIS VIRUS INFECTION. This 3-year/6-month-old male prairie chicken was humanely euthanized. It was positive for reticuloendotheliosis virus. At necropsy no gross lesions were noted. Sections of kidney heart and brain were collected for West Nile virus testing.

CEREBELLAR PEDUNCLE MYELIN DEGENERATION ACUTE ASPIRATION. This 3-year-old female lorikeet had a several week history of lethargy anorexia ataxia and suspected polydipsia. Blood work revealed cachexia heterophilia and possible hypoalbuminemia. The bird was being treated with gavage feeding of Emeraid omnivore and enrofloxacin. The bird experienced a seizure-like episode during gavage and possibly aspirated. Gross necropsy revealed emaciation food in the mouth and crop congested and edematous lungs a thin walled ventriculus that was possibly dilated and a 10x5 mm. oval area of pale tissue in the rostral and ventral left cerebral hemisphere. There is a concern for bornavirus.

EUTHANASIA CATARACTS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) URATE STASIS INANITION. This 19-year-old male owl was euthanized due to weight loss and cataracts. At necropsy the animal was thin and hypermature cataracts were identified bilaterally.

EUTHANASIA STRESS TRAUMA. This 19-year-old male blue crowned motmot was found dead in the adjacent enclosure with abundant trauma (presumably caused by an agouti). The animal was euthanized due to severe extent of injuries. At necropsy there were lacerations on the keel a puncture wound on the left sternum fracture of the sternum penetrating lesions into the coelomic cavity multifocal carpal fractures with avulsion and crushing of the skull and rhinotheca.
LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 1-year-old male chicken died during physical exam. At necropsy the lungs were dark red and the liver was enlarged firm and pale.

TRAUMA STRESS PULMONARY EDEMA SHOCK. This 4-year-old male bat died two hours after emergency admittance to the hospital. It had been moved from exhibit for renovations and was noted to be banging itself around the new holding area. The next day it was found on the ground collapsed. It was given supportive care but died. At necropsy there was a small 6 mm. abrasion on the left leg. There were multiple small patches of depigmentation diffusely throughout the wing webs. The left kidney had a small 1 mm. capsular cyst near the renal pelvis. Both adrenal glands appeared prominent. The right lung lobe appeared dark red with almost black areas. The thoracic cavity contained a mild amount of hemorrhage. Sections of heart and liver were frozen for future use (nutritional analysis).

VERTEBRAL DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA EMACIATION EPICARDIAL MELANOMA. This 14-year-old male crocodile monitor was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes secondary to marked vertebral fusion and bony proliferation. At necropsy there were several firm nodules on the skin. The heart had thickening of the atrioventricular valves. There was marked bony proliferation throughout the spine.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 10-month-old female rainbow lorikeet was found down on the ground and died the following morning. Necropsy revealed a yellow/brown liver dark and hemorrhagic intestines and hemorrhage around the dorsal calvarium.

PANCREATIC ACINAR CELL ADENOCARCINOMA AND ADENOMA HEPATOCELLULAR NODULAR HYPERPLASIA AND BILIARY ADENOMA PULMONARY ADENOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 1-year-old male slender-tailed meerkat had a history of mandibular fistula that resulted in multiple tooth extractions. Supportive care was administered for a cervical abscess ten years earlier that grew Clostridium perfringens. The meerkat had a pancreatic mass removed in 2011 described as an acinar cell tubular adenoma (G11-2698). This animal presented to the hospital in 2013 for being ataxic. Two conspecifics had developed neurologic signs and were subsequently diagnosed with polioencephalomalacia. This animal responded to B vitamins and dextrose although another mass was palpated in the abdomen at this time. Excision biopsies of these masses were pancreatic acinar cell adenoma and pancreatic acinar cell adenocarcinoma (G13-1638). This animal subsequently developed a seizure received supportive care and was in the process of being reintroduced to a younger group of meerkats when it started mutilating its tail. Two amputations were required to heal the surgical site. The meerkat was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed fair body condition healed amputation site at the tail absence of multiple teeth adequate adipose stores possible parathyroid lesion or thyroid lesion in the left thyroid a raised round light colored lesion in the left lung multiple large nodules within the pancreas a few yellow raised nodules in the liver some white streaking in the renal pelvis and no other abnormalities.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE ROCK INGESTION RUMINORETICULITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 27-year-old female giraffe was being monitored for quality of life for several months due to progressively worsening osteoarthritis and chronic weight loss. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed matted hair that exfoliated easily on the right dorsal thorax and flakiness in the underlying skin recessed gingiva with exposed roots white froth and green fluid in the tracheal lumen multiple dark foci in the parenchyma of the lungs marked thickening of the left ventricular free wall calcified and immobile aortic valve jet lesions on the proximal aorta calcified and immobile left chordae tendinea and calcification of the left atrioventricular valve. The liver had rounded edges and multiple pinpoint white areas in the parenchyma. Numerous rocks were in the rumen. The reticulum was completely filled with rocks with areas of mucosal ulceration. The abomasum was half filled with rocks and multiple areas of shallow mucosal ulceration were noted. Multifocal mucosal thickenings or nodules of various sizes were also noted and were more diffuse and concentrated near the pylorus and the pylorus contained a 3 cm. soft tissue swelling. Numerous variably-sized soft tissue nodules were on the mucosal surface of the proximal duodenum. Ecchymoses were noted in the mucosa of the colon. Multiple white depressions were present on the serosal surfaces of the kidneys. Small cystic structures were within the myometrium of the uterine horns and both horns had areas of mucosal erosion and hyperemia. Several large firm masses containing projections of soft tissue were noted at the entrance to the cervix. A small urolith was in the urinary bladder and the mucosal surface was mottled and hyperemic. Osteophytes were prominent on the femoral head and no cartilage was noted on the weight bearing surface of the acetabular joint or femoral head. Minor erosions and loss of cartilage were noted in the remaining joints.
ENDOCARDIOSIS HEPATITIS. This less than 1-year-old female Bali mynah had not been seen for two days and was found dead under a plant. Necropsy revealed tissue autolysis.

DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA. This 18-year-old female Siberian tiger had a two week history of illness died spontaneously and was refrigerated 19 hours prior to necropsy. This animal was immobilized on 2/3 for biannual preventative health examination. No abnormalities were detected during examination. The animal recovered well from anesthesia but remained partially anorexic until 2/16. On this date the animal was released from its inside holding area back onto exhibit. The animal was weak in its hind limbs for the next few days but was beginning to eat an increased amount of food daily. On 2/18/99 the animal appeared active and alert throughout the morning and ate 4 lb. of meat. At approximately 5:30 PM the night keeper staff noted the animal was in sternal recumbency and vomiting white foam. The animal later became tachypneic and at approximately 7:30 PM the animal expired on exhibit. Necropsy revealed good body condition and good haircoat and markedly distended abdomen. Approximately 400 ml. of light brown colored malodorous fluid was present in the thoracic and abdominal cavity. The spleen was congested and mildly enlarged along the caudal pole. The lungs were bilaterally collapsed and congested. A 4 in. rent was noted in the diaphragm dorsal to the esophageal hiatus. Stomach spleen majority of the small intestine pancreas and cranial aspect of the right medial liver lobe were herniated into the left thoracic cavity. The stomach was bloated and contained a large quantity of digested meat. The herniated small intestine was diffusely congested and mildly discolored. The small intestine contained digested food material. The distal portion of the large intestine contained hard formed fecal material. The liver was diffusely congested and the herniated portion of the pancreas was congested. The urinary bladder mucosa contained multiple ecchymoses. The ovaries and mesovarium were congested.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS SPINAL FRACTURE EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female carpet python had been inappetent for over a year. Evaluation identified spinal changes and no other abnormalities. The animal was hospitalized for several weeks and appeared more alert at discharge but remained inappetent and was subsequently found on the ground. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a palpable step and lateral shift to the spine approximately 25% down the length of the body fluctuant caudal coelom filled with fluid and palpable masses in the caudal coelom. Abundant adipose stores were noted and 20 ml. of straw-colored fluid were in the subcutis of the caudal body. A large quantity of appropriately digested food was in the caudal gastrointestinal tract and small quantities of urates were in the caudal gastrointestinal tract. A spinal fracture was identified.

EUTHANASIA EMACIATION ESOPHAGITIS. This 6-year-old male banded rock rattlesnake had an approximately year-long history of neurologic disease. He was not able to feed or right himself. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

RENAL AND TESTICULAR LIPOFUSCINOSIS TESTICULAR ATROPHY URINARY BLADDER DISTENTION AND ATTENUATION. This approximately 49-year-old male desert tortoise died spontaneously on August 13th. Necropsy on August 14th revealed thin body condition feces around the vent and a large urinary bladder adhered to the shell and containing 1.15 liters of urine and gray to white granular material a thin urinary bladder wall no coelomic fat distention of the cecum and colon and hyperemic gastrointestinal tract abundant grit and gravel in the cecum and colon admixed with ingesta and autolysis of the brain.

CLOACAL POLYP DUODENAL SMOOTH MUSCLE HYPERTROPHY UNILATERAL NEPHROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old female green iguana had a history of chronic weight loss hyperuricacidemia and anemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified severe muscle loss moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid in the coelom dark plum-colored liver firm focal nodule on the duodenum small and firm right kidney bilaterally darkened kidneys with absence of perirenal fat a 5 mm. pale area in the ventricle eburnation on the left femoral head osteophytes on the left humeral condyle and copious tenacious joint fluid.

CERVICAL TRAUMA RUMENITIS. This 2.5-year-old female greater kudu was found dead in the yard close to the fence. It has a history of tooth root abscesses and extractions (G06-1139). Necropsy revealed good body condition. Musculature overlying the third and fourth cervical vertebrae was extensively hemorrhagic and multiple fractures and instability were noted in cervical vertebra #4. The right hemimandible was enlarged midshaft in the location previously affected by tooth root abscesses. No teeth are present in this location. Hemorrhage was noted surrounding the spinal cord.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS AND SEPSIS POSSIBLE FECAL OBSTRUCTION. This 3-year-old male wallaby (black #52 white) was found dead. Necropsy revealed a fecal pellet impacted and partially adhered to the mucosa of the small intestine. The wall adjacent to this area was friable and dark red. The lungs were diffusely red. The intestinal site was cultured.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA PULMONARY LYMPHOMA. This approximately 1-year-old male rat has a history of chronic respiratory disease with recent decompensation. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed abscesses throughout the lungs.

CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE BACTERIAL URINARY TRACT INFECTION. This 37-year-old female chimpanzee has a history of cardiac disease diagnosed one year prior to death that was treated with propranolol and enalapril. Several months prior to death the animal had a grade IV heart murmur. The animal had increased signs of exercise intolerance cough pale mucous membranes and severe lethargy. Emergency examination revealed a two-fold increase in BNP. The animal died 24 hours after examination. The animal also had a previous history of amputation of the right arm due to luxation of the elbow. At necropsy there was abundant pleural and abdominal effusion as well as subcutaneous edema. Mucous membranes were pale. The heart had 24 ml. of pericardial effusion and weighed 443 gm. The entire heart was submitted to the Great Ape Heart Project. Gastric vessels were injected on the mucosal and serosal surfaces. The liver and spleen were enlarged. Kidneys were mottled and hemorrhagic with a cobblestone texture. The mucosal surface of the urinary bladder was hemorrhagic. The uterine body was slightly thickened. There was mild atherosclerosis of the meningeal vessels.

INTESTINAL PERFORATION PERITONITIS MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 14-year-old male polar bear was found dead. At necropsy there was a large amount of malodorous red flocculent fluid free within the abdomen. The serosal surfaces of the intestines were reddened. There was fibrin deposition on the omentum and peritoneum. There was an approximately 2 cm. in diameter perforation in the distal duodenum. There was a foreign body (winter fleece glove) located proximal to this site. The gall bladder was distended and thin walled. The spleen was gray/green on the surface. The intestinal lymph nodes were dark green. The pancreas was severely inflamed. The liver was green/gray discolored on the surface but normal on cut surface.

CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 20-year-old female rock python has recurrent episodes of pneumonia. Signs resolve with antibiotic treatment based on culture results but then the condition recurs.
