During the most recent episode the snake was noted to be thin and producing large amounts of exudate from the trachea. The snake was hospitalized for treatment but was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed thin body condition reddened oral mucous membranes reddened scales on the ventrum thickened and foamy cranial lung with strands of viscous tan exudate and multiple cystic follicles and slugs were in the reproductive tract.

ENTERITIS MENINGOENCEPHALITIS INANITION. This greater than 3-year-old male lory died. It had a history of not being able to fly. It had been treated since November without improvement. Psittacine beak and feather disease and Chlamydia have been negative during the last testing. The bird had been losing weight over the past month. The skin had sloughed in several areas. At necropsy the bird was thin. It had significant weight loss. Its body condition was 1. There were several large well circumscribed areas of dark scabbing and discoloration over the left shoulder right wing left foot (digit) and right foot (digit). The liver was large firm and had several black foci. The dura mater was firm and difficult to break down.

BACTERIAL/YOLK COELOMITIS SYSTEMIC NONSUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION. This 4-year-old rock dove was found dead in the morning and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed slightly underweight body condition no skin on the dorsal aspect of the head a 3 cm. long ulcerated skin lesion on the left lateral abdomen multiple pinpoint red spots on the surface of the pancreas yolk in the coelom and no other abnormalities.

SEPTICEMIA MYOCARDITIS ENTERITIS. This female 4-year/2-month-old toad was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy the cloaca was swollen and edematous. The skin was erythematous. There was serohemorrhagic fluid within the coelomic cavity. There was little coelomic fat. The entire small intestine was consolidated and hemorrhagic including the mesentery.

EUTHANASIA THYMOMA CHYLOTHROAX. This 16-year/1-month-old male lemur was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chylothorax. It was immobilized on two occasions for evaluation and thoracocentesis with drainage of moderate transudate. The lemur presented with severe dyspnea on the day of euthanasia. At necropsy the lemur was very obese. Fat stores were very excessive subcutaneously in the mesentery etc. There was a small mediastinal mass palpated in the fat that was dark red. There were 200-300 ml. of modified white transudate in the thoracic cavity. The lungs were severely atelectatic and collapsed. The lungs were congested. The liver appeared hemosiderotic grossly. It had a sheen with dark areas. The right kidney had a cystic structure on the cortex. There was mild congestion of the brain. There was mild pancreatitis.

TOOTH ROOT ABSCESS/PERIODONTAL DISESE BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA AND SEPSIS. This 10-year-old male captive bred wallaby (tattoo #12) was found very weak and died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed generalized alopecia on the tail a tooth root abscess between the second and third molars obesity pulmonary abscesses and a mottled liver.

SEPSIS PULMONARY SHOCK. This 12-year-old male California sea lion has a history of regurgitation. The animal became disoriented coughed white foamy fluid became unresponsive and stopped breathing. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the intestinal wall slightly dark lungs slightly reddened mesenteric lymph node a fibrin clot in the pericardial sac mild reddening of the esophagus adjacent to the heart a distinct nodule in the pancreas bile in the duodenum and minimal adipose stores.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS PARATHYROID ADENOMA POSSIBLE HEART BASED TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 11.5-year-old female Amur leopard had been previously diagnosed by biopsy with atypical mycobacteriosis involving the ventral abdominal wall. Supportive care was administered but the condition continued to progress and involved the entire right abdomen thorax and axillary region. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed extension of the inflammation and draining tracts through the wall of the abdomen and enlargement of the dermal lymph nodes. The right thyroid contained a central round nodule approximately 5 mm. in diameter. The right lung lobes were entirely atelectatic and the left lung lobes were multifocally congested. The cortex of the adrenals was thin. The liver was mottled. Heart valves were thickened and a possible abscess was in the intima of the pulmonary trunk.

MALIGNANT HEMANGIOSARCOMA INVOLVING INTESTINE LUNG LIVER HEART. This female blue-tongued skink was 12 years old and weighed 500g. There was progressive weight loss over six months with anorexia and lethargy. Blood work revealed a leukocytosis (40.0) that was partially resolved with enrofloxacin and ceftazidime treatment. Fluids were administered and baby food offered by syringe. The final decision for humane euthanasia was based on the continued decline in condition and poor prognosis for return to health.

SEPTICEMIA. This approximately 14-year-old female boa was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic anorexia. It had been force fed since last October. It had both an adenocarcinoma associated with the bowel wall and a granuloma removed. It had colonic atony dilatation and gas distention. At necropsy there was a large hemorrhagic unorganized mass in the fat just cranial to the vent and dorsal to the colon. The mass felt firm but rubbery and had a lacy appearance. The mass was approximately 4-5 cm. in length and 1-2 cm. in diameter. The fat it was contained in was necrotic. There was also a very large amount of gas in the coelomic cavity entrapped around the fat in the caudal third of the body. The gas was accompanied with approximately 30 ml. of brown translucent fluid. There were very little fat deposits in the rest of the body. There was a small oval mass that was flat and dark red and firmly adhered to the body wall about 20 cm. cranial to the vent. It had a smooth surface and may have actually been outside of the coelomic cavity. There was a well organized encapsulated mass in the coelomic fat approximately 25 cm. cranial to the vent. The mass was surrounded by a few ml. of turgid salmon colored fluid. The mass had rounded borders a smooth surface dark red to purple and was homogeneous on cross section. The pericardial sac was thickened. There was an unorganized mass that conformed to the shape of the heart and pericardium within the pericardial sac. The epicardial surface was thickened gray and edematous.

HEPATITIS SPLENITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA AIR SACCULITIS NEPHRITIS. This 5-year-old female chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the bird was thin. Serosanguineous fluid was present throughout the coelom and pericardial sac. Gelatinous material was identified covering the viscera. The liver was enlarged with multifocal and coalescing white to yellow foci. Similar foci were present in the spleen.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE. This 8.5-year-old male budgerigar had trouble flying and had droopy wings and a fatty lipoma on the chest. The bird was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a large amount of seed in the crop adhesions throughout the coelom lesions in the liver enlarged spleen and a lesion in the lung.
adult. Weight: 658.9 g.  Emaciation. Gastric bloat. Focal pulmonary haemorrhage. Bruising caudal thorax. Trauma; suspect. Atherosclerosis.

Diagnosis (es): 1. Thoracic cavity (pleura): Mesothelioma 2. Lungs: Endogenous lipid pneumonia; focal; mild 3. Lungs: Bronchiolitis; suppurative; multifocal; subacute; minimal 4. Lungs: Pulmonary edema; multifocal; minimal 5. Lungs: Smooth muscle hyperplasia; multifocal; moderate 6. Arteries (myocardial; pulmonary): Arteriosclerosis; mild to moderate 7. Heart: Valvular endocardiosis; focal; mild to moderate 8. Heart: Myocardial interstitial fibrosis; multifocal; mild 9. Kidney: Tubulointerstitial nephritis; lymphoplasmacytic; multifocal; mild; chronic 10. Adrenal glands: Nodular cortical hyperplasia; bilateral; multifocal; moderate 11. Lymph node: Anthracosis; multifocal; moderate 12. Lymph node: Hemorrhage; focal; mild 13. Thyroid gland: Follicular cyst; focal Comment: The most significant finding in this animal was mesothelioma of the thoracic pleura; corresponding with the firm nodules noted on gross necropsy (per history). This neoplasm was closely associated with the periosteal surface of the ribs. Mesothelioma is a commonly diagnosed neoplasm of both the pleura and peritoneum in in zoo felids. Tubulointerstitial nephritis was mild in this case; and is also a common finding in zoo felids. In one section of lung; there was minimal neutrophilic bronchiolitis and pulmonary edema. The green appearance of the lymph nodes noted in the thoracic cavity were due to anthracosis; commonly found in the tracheobronchial lymph nodes. One lymph node; as described grossly (per history) had a small amount of hemorrhage; or was draining a region of hemorrhage; but histologic findings were mild. The nodules described adjacent to one adrenal gland (per history) may have been the nodular cortical hyperplasia found histologically. Remaining lesions were considered age-related or mild; incidental findings; such as valvular endocardiosis and arteriosclerosis. Myocardial fibrosis was mild and limited to one section of heart adjacent to a valve.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOMYELITIS SYNOVITIS DERMATITIS. This 11-year-old gallinule had difficulty walking and marked swelling of the metatarsal joint. The animal was humanely euthanized due to chronic suppurative arthritis. At necropsy the metatarsus contained white to yellow thick fluid.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION CATARACT WITH RETINAL DEGENERATION (GLAUCOMA) RIGHT-SIDED CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old male opossum developed chronic mobility problems in the hind end and had chronic severe bilateral cataracts. The animal improved briefly with supportive care that included nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and corticosteroids but its condition subsequently deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed spondylosis in the lumbar spine and bilateral cataracts.

ASPIRATION DISSEMINATED NONSUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION (PROBABLE MALARIA) POSITIVE TREATMENT EFFECT. This 1.5-year-old male Inca tern had a history of lethargy and anemia and was being treated for malaria. The bird died and necropsy revealed feces on the vent moderate body condition and thin blood.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male sugar glider was found late in the morning minimally responsive and dehydrated and had a previous history of an eye ulcer that resolved. The animal had been eating drinking and behaving normally according to the keepers. Examination revealed severe hypothermia and dehydration with bradycardia some crusting dermatitis at the tip of the right ear reflecting a nonhealing wound a palpable mass in the abdomen and the animal developed cardiopulmonary arrest while anesthetized. The animal was recovered but due to the poor prognosis euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed marked hepatic enlargement with effacement by pale yellow to white nodules. A 2 cm. mass was in the right caudal lobe of the same consistency and color as the rest of the liver. A small amount of coagulated blood was in the abdomen (from fine needle aspirate). The proximal gastrointestinal tract was empty. Formed feces were in the colon.

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR OSTEOMYELITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ENTERITIS. This 15-year-old female kangaroo had recently had the remaining two molars of the right lower dental arcade extracted. Immediate postsurgical condition was good; however now the animal has difficulty chewing and poor appetite. Examination revealed one remaining molar is loose and a large mass was present on the right mandible which contained purulent material. Due to the animal’s deteriorating condition complete loss of teeth and poor quality of life the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the heart was rounded and flaccid.

BUMBLEFOOT AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION BACTERIAL ENTERITIS EMACIATION. This greater than 32-year-old male flamingo is from a flock in which there were some mortalities associated with catching the birds for examination. One bird fractured its neck and one bird had a capture myopathy. The bird of this report had been handled in a similar fashion a few months earlier with no problems. It had no clinical signs prior to being found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed multiple blackened areas on the serosal surface of the trachea tan flaked material on the pericardium and epicardium and a focal tan lesion in the endocardium of the right ventricle. Some hemorrhage is noted in the liver. The proventriculus and ventriculus were devoid of digesta and the ventriculus contained coarse sand. Digesta was in the intestine. The spleen was granular. The kidneys were dark and had a granite-like appearance. Severe pododermatitis was present on both feet.

FUNGAL SEPTICEMIA CHRONIC UROCYSTITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE CATARACT. This 20-year-old female snow leopard had a one year history of declining condition due to renal disease spondylosis and chronic urinary tract infections. Hind end weakness had worsened dramatically in the last month and was not responding to medication. The cat’s appetite had been irregular and medications could not be delivered. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed purulent exudate from the nares absence of most of the upper right premolars and molars urine staining of the back end approximately 500 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen substantial intra-abdominal fat flocculent urine (Pseudomonas aeruginosa cultured) cloudy fluid in the right renal pelvis mottled cecum containing red pasty material 200 ml. of clear fluid in the thorax and a possible premortem thrombus 1 cm. in diameter wrapped around the papillary muscles in the left ventricle. The thyroids were asymmetrical with the left larger than the right and the left parathyroid was 3x larger than the right. A wart-like growth was on the back of the neck.

TIBIAL PLATEAU OSTEOARTHRITIS PANCREATIC ISLET CELL HYPERPLASIA. This approximately 19-year-old male fruit bat has had a long history of multiple digital bone fractures bone infections and ulcerative skin lesions. The animal also has degenerative arthritis and possible fluorosis. The bat was found with his right wing caught in the mesh and comatose. The bat arrested and died during treatment. Gross necropsy revealed an enlarged mottled liver severe arthritis of the wrists and stifles hemorrhage in the colon and a flabby right atrium.

JAW TRAUMA. ASPIRATION SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female Speke’s gazelle was immobilized in December for examination reportedly acting abnormally. A recent mandibular fracture had been healing well. Other animals in the exhibit have been partially eaten by coyotes. The jaw fracture was attributed to a coyote attack. More recently the animal had been losing weight was inappetent doing poorly and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with dehydration light-colored mucous membranes thin renal cortices with hyperemia foci resembling granulomas in the cranial lungs and possibly in the region of the thymus. The right caudal mandible had a moderately-sized mass to 2.5 cm. in greatest dimension in the area of the previous fracture.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 2-year-old red kangaroo died unexpectedly and appeared normal that morning. Storms were present the previous evening and nightshade had been found in the exhibit earlier in the week. Necropsy revealed fluid accumulation in the chest and abdomen and from the nares.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS GRANULOMATOUS COELOMITIS NEPHRITIS PNEUMONIA. This 8-year-old male toad has a history of weight loss and poor appetite. Treatment was initiated but the animal later died. At necropsy coelomic fat pads were depleted. The liver was dark and had fibrinous adhesions to the body wall. Fibrinous adhesions were also present between loops of intestine.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA PHARYNGITIS GLOSSITIS. This 3-year-old female chicken was found dead with a history of 18% weight loss over the past 3-4 weeks. At gross necropsy the body was very thin. The oral cavity contained ingesta. There was a 0.5 x 0.5 x 0.5 cm. mass protruding from the dorsal pharynx with a similar fibrous lesion in the tongue where the mass contacted.

SHOCK STRESS. This 12-year-old male cottontop tamarin is from a group in which there have been several losses following a long road trip. The animal of this report was the patriarch of the group. Necropsy revealed an adequate amount of intra-abdominal fat monkey chow and carrots in the stomach gas in the lower gastrointestinal tract ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract mildly enlarged heart pale liver congested lungs and a small amount of serohemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS STEATITIS SHOCK. This 4-year-old male prairie dog was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the liver was pale. A well circumscribed 2 cm. x 3 mm. irregular abdominal mass was present in the mesenteric fat.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS WEST NILE VIRUS. This 3-year-old female lorikeet was separated from the flock yesterday evening due to poor flying ability but otherwise looked alert and active and was eating well. It was found down on the ground in the morning. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no external wounds. The hepatic lobes have a central area of pallor. No other gross abnormalities are seen.

CHRONIC PROLIFERATIVE PROVENTRICULITIS AND ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old budgerigar had a history of weight loss and was a poor flyer. It was found laying in its food pan and had a weak grip in both feet. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachexia thickening of the intestinal loops and no other visible lesions.

EUTHANASIA GRANULOMATOUS COELOMITIS PNEUMONIA VASCULAR HYPERTROPHY. This 8-year-old duck had a several day history of ataxia and weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy minimal fat depots were present. The left ventricular wall was thickened. Air sacs were opaque and contained multiple plaques.

ACUTE SHOCK NECROTIZING STEATITIS CHOLESTASIS AND BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 10-year-old female wallaroo was found dead within its exhibit. The carcass was refrigerated for 24 hours prior to necropsy. At necropsy there were abundant focal plaques throughout the abdominal adipose tissue. There were hemorrhages and ecchymoses throughout the mesentery. The intestinal mucosa was severely congested as was the serosa of the cecum and large intestine. The large intestinal contents were normal.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA POSSIBLE FETAL DEATH. This 14-year-old sheep had been off food for one day and had secluded herself in the afternoon. The sheep had heavy breathing and was lethargic and responsive to stimuli. The sheep was unsteady when forced to walk and died within two hours. Necropsy revealed a small amount of yellow effusion in the thoracic cavity ruminal fluid and hay in the nasal cavity trachea and bronchi hemorrhagic mucosa lining the trachea consolidated cranial pulmonary lobes congested caudal pulmonary lobes pinpoint hemorrhages over the right epicardium severe premolar and molar attrition some possible dark plastic within the rumen some erythema around the pylorus a gravid uterus with a 3-month-old fetus and mild mammary development with colostrum.

LYMPHOMA PARATHYROID ADENOMA ISLET CELL TUMOR. This 28.5-year-old female California sea lion had a history of inappetence and bloating of three days duration developed an enlarged abdomen had two tonic-clonic seizures the last of which was associated with entering the pool. The animal was retrieved but apneic and barely responsive with no audible heartbeat. Supportive care and resuscitation attempts were initiated but the animal could not be resuscitated. Necropsy identified copious mildly opaque straw-colored fluid in the abdomen and copious serosanguineous clear fluid in the thorax. A moderate amount of sanguineous fluid was in the pericardium admixed with clots and some white caseous material. The heart was misshapen and elongated with an irregular epicardium. Mild endocardiosis was in the mitral valve. The lungs were purple the aorta and vena cava were enlarged and cavernous the spleen was contracted the liver was pale purple and the dorsal serosal surface had corrugated leaflets. The entire intestinal tract was empty and firm. Several abdominal lymph nodes were black/tan on cut surface. The adrenals had a markedly thin outer cortex with occasional small nodules. The kidneys were mottled purple/tan and a single cortical cyst was noted. Several palpable nodules were in the pancreas. The brain had clear fluid on the surface. Some cysts and follicles were in the ovaries. The tonsils were cystic and contained clear fluid. A lens was missing from the left eye (previous surgery).

EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS CHRONIC ARTHRITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA. This 17-year-old female wolf was euthanized due to severe spondylosis arthritis and declining condition. At necropsy decreased muscle mass was noted over the hind limbs and hips. White nodules were noted in the lung and a raised mass was present in the spleen.

ENDOCARDITIS MYOCARDITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA CHRONIC GASTRITIS ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS ULCERATIVE COLITIS. This 1-year-old female cheetah was found dead. A heart murmur had been ausculted during a quarantine exam; however the animal’s activity and appetite were normal. Recently the animal became inappetent and lethargic corresponding with high temperatures. Examination at that time revealed bronchointerstitial pattern in the lungs and persistence of the heart murmur. Treatment was initiated; however melena developed. The animal was later found dead. At necropsy the left nostril contained thick purulent material. A moderate quantity of straw colored fluid was present in the thoracic cavity. Foamy white to yellow purulent material was present on sections of the lung. A yellow thickened plaque was present in the myocardium of the left ventricle. The aortic valve contained a large vegetative lesion. The stomach contained several erosions in the fundus. The distal colon contained black pasty feces. The left kidney contained an infarcted area.

SPINAL STENOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female sheep had a several year history of slowly progressing spinal stenosis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting over the back and rear end. Cataracts were noted.

EUTHANASIA ADENOCARCINOMA PROVENTRICULITIS. This 5-year-old female chicken was under treatment for suspected egg yolk peritonitis and presented with severe ascites. An exploratory laparotomy was performed and the bird was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy multiple neoplastic growths of varying size shape and color were present in the coelomic cavity. The pancreas was nearly completely effaced by nodular growths.

ENTERITIS ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS URATE STASIS INAITION. This 19-year-old female boa was euthanized for weight loss spondylosis and anemia. At necropsy an area of swelling was present 60 cm. cranial to the vent with areas of necrosis in the scale. The liver was diffusely nodular.

Pancreas: Islet carcinoma Liver; mesenteric lymph node: Metastatic carcinoma Kidney: Membranous glomerulopathy; ectatic glomeruli; glomerular sclerosis; tubular degeneration and necrosis; granular casts; and segmental medullary mineralization Eyes: Multifocal iris cysts Duodenum; jejunum; ileum colon: Mild; diffuse; lymphoplasmacytic enterocolitis. Comments: The carcinoma within the pancreas is consistent with neuroendocrine origin. Islet cell tumors can secrete various hormones such as insulin; gastrin; somatostatin; etc. Thus; the clinical signs they cause depend on the hormone; or hormones; that they secrete. Immunohistochemical labeling can be performed to determine hormone expression in this tumor; if desired. The hepatic and lymph node metastases appear to be neuroendocrine in origin; but this cannot be confirmed from routine histopathology. Immunohistochemical staining is available for an additional cost to further investigate the origin of these tumors; this testing can be performed on the submitted tissues. The renal changes show chronic glomerular changes as well as acute tubular disease. The deep medullary/renal papillary necrosis may be evidence of an adverse drug reaction; such as due to NSAID therapy. The iris cysts are an incidental finding; as they are small; and there is no evidence of occlusion of the iridocorneal angle. The enterocolitis does not extend into the submucosa and there is no change within the alimentary epithelium; as such the clinical relevance of these lesions is likely minimal. David Needle; DVM. Normal Stomach Comments: There were reports of mutlifocal white nodules in the gastric mucosa on necropsy. These lesions were not evident after formalin fixation and there was no histologic evidence of disease within the stomach. David Needle; DVM

RENAL AND ARTICULAR GOUT OBESITY NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old female blue tongued skink was born with severe congenital lordosis of the thoracolumbar spine and scoliosis of the coccygeal vertebrae. The animal presented with multiple pale subcutaneous swellings on all limbs and aspiration confirmed the presence of uric acid crystals. Another lizard from the same clutch with similar congenital malformations and uric acid deposits was recently euthanized due to severe renal disease. Euthanasia of this animal was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition several white foci in the skin and subcutaneous white swellings around the limbs ingesta and fecal material in the alimentary tract pale firm kidneys with accumulated urates active folliculogenesis and large fat bodies.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY. This female 8-month-old opossum was found dead. It had not consumed its entire diet the day before but otherwise had appeared normal. Necropsy revealed no external lesions good adipose stores a small amount of bloody fluid and fibrin tags on the serosal surfaces of the abdomen and a large amount of clear yellow fluid with fibrin in the thoracic cavity. The liver was enlarged and mottled with congestion and a nutmeg appearance. Both lungs were partially collapsed. The heart was enlarged rounded and occupied a large percentage of the thoracic cavity. The left ventricular chamber was very dilated. Adrenal glands were larger than expected but grossly normal.

EUTHANASIA PODODERMATITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) RENAL GOUT COELOMITIS INANITION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL MINERALIZATION AIR SACCULITIS. This 36-year-old female eagle has a history of degenerative arthritis in the feet. Recent blood work revealed elevated uric acid. Purulent discharge was noted in the digit and treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition declined progressing to recumbency. The animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin with scant fat depots. The right lung contained a round metal fragment consistent with lead shot. Adjacent lung was grossly normal. Dark flat encapsulated material was present in the caudal air sac. The left ventricle was markedly thickened with nodular lesions on the AV valve. Kidneys were enlarged and irregular with cysts containing clear fluid. Mucopurulent discharge was present in the joints of the feet and stifle.

PERFORATED CROP. This 10-year-old lorikeet was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed good body condition and a 5 mm. round scab on the right neck. This lesion connected to a granuloma that was adhered to the inside of the esophagus and neck musculature. The granuloma contained yellow firm material and mineral deposits. The liver was yellow and friable. The right abdominal air sac was adhered to the organs and had a yellow thickened appearance.

EUTHANASIA LEPTOSPIROSIS (PRESUMPTIVE) NEPHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR DISSOCIATION METASTATIC CALCIFICATION. This 4-month-old male wolf was found icteric weak and thin. There was elevation of Leptospira sp. titer. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the pancreas was yellow firm and nodular. The lungs had firm dark red areas throughout all lobes. The liver was yellow. Kidneys were enlarged and yellow with pronounced congestion at the corticomedullary junction. Hemorrhage was noted on the mucosal surface of the duodenum.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE UROCYSTITIS. This 18-year-old mole rat died. Necropsy revealed dehydration congestion in the right pulmonary lobes and a mild amount of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity.
CHRONIC TUBULOINTERSITIAL NEPHRITIS GASTRIC MINERALIZATION SHOCK. This 9-year-old female sloth was found dead. At gross necropsy the kidneys contained calculi and the lungs appeared heavy.

EUTHANASIA MALIGNANT ROUND CELL TUMOR SKIN; ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 1.5-year-old female hedgehog presented with a large skin mass on the dorsal thorax. Examination revealed multiple small skin masses and subcutaneous masses. The hedgehog was humanely euthanized. At necropsy round subcutaneous masses of varying sizes were present throughout the skin. Masses were tan to red and firm. A 0.5 cm. in diameter firm tan mass was present in the mediastinum. A second mass was present at the left thoracic inlet. The left kidney also contained tan round masses.

PYELONEPHRITIS BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS HEPATIC NECROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 6-year-old male chinchilla was hospitalized for lethargy and anorexia. Renal failure was diagnosed and treatment was instituted; however the animal later died. At necropsy fat depots were absent. A smooth hard white mass was present in the liver. The heart showed marked dilation of the right ventricle with thinning of the wall and thickening of the left ventricular free wall. The right kidney was pale tan and contained numerous pale foci in the cortex.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME MYELOLIPOMAS ENDOMETRIAL STROMAL CELL SARCOMA LEIOMYOSARCOMA HYPERKERATOTIC DERMATITIS. This 2-year-old female African hedgehog had been hospitalized for four days with neurologic disease that includes falling to one side and reduced mentation. The animal continued to eat in the hospital but did not improve despite treatment. A second animal was found at the same time with similar signs but less severe. There is no history of exposure to toxins although both of these animals are used for educational programs. Necropsy revealed large blood clots in the thoracic cavity. A large tumor mass approximately 1 cm. in greatest dimension was found on the cranial aspect of the liver. The mass was firm to hard with areas of central necrosis. The mass extended into the parenchyma of the liver. A second smaller tumor was on the lobe of the liver that was resting close to the duodenum and cardia of the stomach. This tumor was smooth and round. The right horn of the uterus had what appeared to be chronic pyometra. The spleen was very large and congested.
NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 9-month-old female snake died. There was no recent history of problems. At necropsy follicles were present.

RENAL GOUT BILIARY HYPERPLASIA HEPATIC FIBROSIS INANITION. This 20-year-old male milksnake had a history of gaping. Endoscopy of the lung revealed widespread tracheal collapse. Anesthetic recovery was prolonged and the animal was found dead. At necropsy the kidneys contained numerous white foci.

FACIAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA WITH CHOLANGITIS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female red kangaroo had previous enucleation of the left eye and biopsy of periorbital tissue indicated squamous cell carcinoma. Swelling of the periorbital tissue continued and a large amount of purulent material continued to drain from the upper palpebrae nose and mouth. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. On external examination much swelling was noted in the left side of the face and purulent material was expressed from the left orbit. Purulent material also is present in the left naris and mouth. A large periorbital diffuse mass is present on the left side with a necrotic purulent center. The mass infiltrates the conchae and occludes the meatuses. The orbital bone is friable and easily cut with a blade. The lungs are completely adhered to the diaphragm. Multiple pulmonary bullae are present in the right caudal lung lobe. The pericardial sac is adhered to the sternum and miliary nodules are present on the mitral valve. The liver is small and contains multiple white hard nodules. The spleen is small with irregular margins.

ENTERITIS NEPHRITIS HEPATIC NECROSIS SHOCK. This 6-year-old male gazelle was immobilized for a hoof trim but never fully recovered and was found dead. At necropsy the lungs were congested. The abomasum was hemorrhagic and contained focal ulcers in the mucosa. The jejunum and duodenum were also hemorrhagic. Dark red urine was present in the urinary bladder.

EUTHANASIA FIBROSARCOMA. This 22-year-old male skink had a history of progressive anorexia lethargy and depression. Blood work revealed a chronic inflammatory process. The animal was treated with fluids and antibiotics but was humanely euthanized due to poor clinical response and poor prognosis. At gross necropsy approximately 40 cc. of serosanguineous fluid was present. There was a firm white irregularly shaped mass measuring 6.5 x 3 x 2.3 cm. adjacent to the right lung. The mass was tightly adherent to the surrounding connective tissue.  Also two bilaterally symmetrical soft red masses were present within the subcutaneous tissue of the ventral coelom.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE BILATERAL PHEOCHROMOCYTOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 16.5-year-old female whitewater had a one year history of dilated cardiomyopathy and ultrasonic evidence of adrenal disease mineralized pancreas and renal atrophy. The bird was treated with yearly implants of melatonin responded well but then developed acute collapse had poorly detectable pulse in the legs suggestive of a saddle thrombus and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 7-year-old warthog had a history of chronic lameness which had been treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. He animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy no significant lesions were identified within the internal organs. Moderate degenerative joint disease was present in the head of the right femur and severe degeneration was noted in the left humerus.

STOMATITIS. This female 6.5-year-old turkey was found dead in morning. The bird seemed fine the night before at closing. A preventative treatment with metronidazole for Trichomonas was completed about a month ago. At necropsy there was abrasion of the left wing edge 6 cm. long that was scabbed over. There was mucus in the choanal slit. The feet had calluses and the nails were very long and growing at an angle. Internally there was a very large amount of adipose tissue. The spleen was friable and pale. The right lobe of the liver had pale streaks along the surface. The liver seemed friable. The ovary had developing ova at different stages. The lungs were dark and friable. The vessels of the heart seemed very thick. The heart was pale and the walls seemed thick. This was a turkey pox suspect.
EUTHANASIA METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 18-year-old chuckwalla was humanely euthanized. It had a history of anorexia and dehydration. The kidneys were firm and mineralized. The gonads were firm.
PREDATION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 13-year-old male duck was found dead with evidence of predation. The neck was severed. No other abnormalities were noted at necropsy.

PERITONITIS WITH ADHESIONS PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male golden lion tamarin had a three day history of lethargy and inappetence. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a globoid heart with thin-walled ventricles congested lungs large fibrinous adhesion of the right abdominal wall to the right kidney gastrointestinal tract and serosal surfaces of the cecum and transverse colon large cystic gallbladder partially adhered to the serosal surfaces of the liver and gastrointestinal tract fibrin tags on the serosal surfaces of the small intestine white exudate in the center of the prostate hypertrophied adrenal glands and cerebral congestion.

EUTHANASIA HEPATIC FIBROSIS RENAL GOUT NEPHRITIS. This 23-year-old corn snake had a history of regurgitation and bilateral cataracts. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy hemorrhagic foci were noted in the GI tract.

Biliary Tree: Severe biliary ectasia and possible hypertrophy Liver: Moderate focal adhesion of the left caudal liver lobe to the stomach and omentum; Multifocal; white discolorations on the serosal surface of the left lateral liver lobe Kidney: Multifocal cortico-medullary cysts Spine: Traumatic fracture at the level of L4 and L5 Comment The brain appeared grossly normal. There is evidence of a disease process in the liver and biliary tracts; the tortuous bile duct seen via MRI was visualized on necropsy. The adhesions of the left caudal liver lobe and the white discolorations may be due to migrating parasites. A more definitive diagnosis may be possible when additional results from histopathology are available. Stephanie French; DVM; MS 1)Kidney: Mild glomerulonephritis 2)Gallbladder: Moderate chronic-active choledochitis with fibrosis 3)Pancreas: Mild ductular hyperplasia 4)Liver: Mild centrilobular hepatopathy Moderate choledochitis Mild glomerulonephritis Comment The inflammation; hyperplasia; and fibrosis seen in the ducts of the gallbladder; the pancreas; and in the region of the duodenal papilla are consistent with chronic inflammatory disease. The inflammation likely started at the level of the outlet of the pancreatic and bile duct and then became an ascending process up into the pancreatic and bile ducts. No inciting cause was noted; histologically. Multiple sections of the brain were reviewed; but no abnormalities that would explain this lemur's history of seizures could be found. The regions of satellitosis and lipofuscin can be attributed to the age of this lemur. The lesions in the kidney can be attributed to chronic antigenic stimulation. The hepatic degeneration can be secondary to heart failure (chronic passive congestion) or generalized hypoxia. Stephanie French; DVM; MS

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS HEPATITIS CESTODIASIS. This 9-year-old female rabbit had acute onset of dyspnea. The animal died shortly thereafter. At necropsy a cystic mass was present in the right caudal lung lobe.

ACUTE NEPHROSIS LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE. This 12-year-old male chinchilla was found dead. It had surgery on its tail 10 days prior to death. The day prior to death the fecals were noted to be smaller and a different color (light brown). The chinchilla was eating smaller amounts of food. At necropsy the right lung lobes were red wet and heavy. There was a large amount of light brown ingesta in the stomach and throughout the gastrointestinal tract. The bladder was slightly full.

EUTHANASIA GRANULOMATOUS NEPHRITIS MESENTERIC GRANULOMAS INANITION. This 1-year/10-month-old female frog was humanely euthanized. It was unable to right itself and had no improvement over a three week period. At necropsy there was good muscle mass. The stomach and intestines contained partially digested cricket bodies. The colon was distended with firm fecal material containing digested crickets.

CHRONIC CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE NEMATODIASIS BALANTIDIUM COLITIS EMACIATION. This 38-year-old female western gorilla had an 8-10 day history of dry cough that became wet in the past 48 hours. The animal died and necropsy revealed arthritic stifle and femoral joints straw colored fluid in the thorax and chest cobblestone liver swelling of the pharynx swelling and thickening of the retroperitoneal area associated with an elongated thrombus and areas of necrosis and capsular thickening in the kidneys.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL RHINITIS AND MENINGITIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 3-year/6-month-old male ferret was humanely euthanized. It presented with anorexia weight loss lethargy and brown tinged foam around the mouth. Fecals were negative for coccidia and cryptosporidia. Blood work revealed toxic changes to the neutrophils. The ferret did not respond to fluid therapy antimicrobials and Alban and became worse. At necropsy the ferret was thin. The spleen was larger than expected. The lungs were congested. Within the oral cavity there was a 1 x 1 mm. rent in the soft palate on the left side. There was purulent exudate in the rent.

SHOCK BACTEREMIA BACTERIAL HEPATITIS SPLENITIS ADRENAL HEMORRHAGE. This 9-year-old male squirrel monkey was found dead in an outside exhibit without premonitory signs. At necropsy some foci in the lungs were dark and the liver had a prominent reticular pattern.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS KILLED BY CONSPECIFIC. This approximately 6-year-old male Malayan tiger was killed on exhibit by a conspecific. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition excellent coat condition puncture wounds on either side of the larynx and trachea with lacerations on the dorsal neck blood-tinged fluid in the lumen of the trachea and pinpoint black specks on the surface of the lungs.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This 8.5-year-old female green junglefowl died (not stated if spontaneous or was euthanized). At necropsy there was green fluid and an abscess of an organ with moderate autolysis.

EUTHANASIA CHOLESTEROL GRANULOMA EPICARDIAL FIBROSIS HEMATOMA. This 20-year-old male tree boa had a history of neurologic signs for the past five years. A kidney was removed approximately one year prior to death due to adrenal adenocarcinoma. The animal was found on the floor of the exhibit and did not respond to external stimuli. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a small dark purple mass was identified anterior to the splenopancreas. Approximately 8 cc. of serosanguineous fluid was present within the caudal coelomic cavity.

BRONCHOALVEOLAR ADENOCARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE CHRONIC CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS RETROPERITONEAL HEMATOMA. This approximately 18-year-old male mountain lion had a history of chronic spondylosis and reduced mobility in the elbows. The animal may have had leptospirosis several years earlier. Recently the cat has developed weakening in the rear quarters attributed to spondylosis with progressive muscle atrophy in the hind limbs. Routine evaluation revealed a solitary pulmonary mass several years earlier. Five days prior to death the animal presented with lethargy and unwillingness to rise. The animal was inappetent over this time. A possible retroperitoneal mass was identified supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond developed respiratory problems and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a modest amount of pericardial fluid a large mass involving the caudal vena cava and abdominal portion of the aorta at the mediocranial pole of the right kidney in the region of the adrenal gland. The mass contacted and appeared to be invading the wall of the vena cava and possibly aorta. The left parathyroid gland was enlarged compared to the right. Marked roughening and osteophyte production was noted on the humeral epicondyles on both sides. Less severe lesions were on the olecranon process. Minimal erosions or roughness of joint surfaces were noted in other joints. A 4 cm. mass was in the medial aspect of the right cranial pulmonary lobe. Some possible calcification of airways was noted in the pulmonary parenchyma. The right kidney had hemorrhage under the capsule at the cranial pole which was adhered to the right lobe of the liver and to the diaphragm. Retroperitoneal fat was discolored and adhered to the body wall.

NECROTIZING DERMATITIS STRESS AND HEPATOPATHY. This less than 1-year-old male fruit bat died. It had been neutered three weeks prior to presentation. At necropsy there was necrosis and bone exposure of the distal phalanges and webbing of the left wing. There was serosanguineous fluid within the thoracic cavity.

CEREBELLAR NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS OBESE. This approximately 1.5-year-old male rainbow lorikeet had been attacked by cagemates and the right wing was damaged in October 2006. The lorikeet was isolated for a while and was eventually reunited with the flock. In December the bird presented with ataxia and a history of being attacked by flockmates. The bird was isolated but ataxia did not resolve. Exam revealed dull plumage absolute monocytosis elevated serum AST and CPK nephromegaly and preponderance of gram negative bacteria in crop and cloacal cytology. One day following the exam the bird developed a severe head tilt to the left which resulted in rolling. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL GOUT PROVENTRICULAR MINERALIZATION CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND PORTAL HEPATITIS. This approximately 10-year-old female swan had a one day history of depression diarrhea and fever. White blood cell count was mildly elevated and uric acid levels were elevated. The bird was mildly dehydrated. During examination the bird regurgitated brown fluid. Fluid therapy was administered but the bird became dyspneic and died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed a vegetative lesion on the heart valves pallor in the liver mottled kidneys and areas of purple discoloration in the lungs.

MESENTERIC TORSION (PROBABLE TRAUMA) CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA AND HEPATIC FIBROSIS (POSSIBLE CARDIAC ANOMALY). This 8-month-old male opossum was raised as a juvenile after its mother was killed. The animal has always been smaller than its sibling. While in quarantine the animal had gagging episodes while swallowing. This animal developed respiratory arrest while anesthetized for quarantine examination but recovered. The animal gained weight after leaving quarantine but remained small compared to normal opossums and a sibling. On the day of presentation this animal was quiet had difficulty standing in the afternoon and was in lateral recumbency upon admission to the hospital. Examination revealed pallor and the opossum died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed a 360° torsion around the base of the mesentery with necrosis of part of the mesenteric tissues. All loops of small intestine were substantially distended with gas.

SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AMYLOIDOSIS SPLENIC RUPTURE INTERNAL EXSANGUINATION. This 19-year-old male Chilean flamingo was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed abundant orange fat clotted blood in the coelom pale liver with areas of hemorrhage a pea-sized firm mass embedded in the hepatic lobe a baseball-sized spleen that had ruptured at the cranial end and a clot was present at the rupture site.

- Whole body: Emaciation with serous atrophy of fat - Cecum and colon: Severe; multifocal to coalescing; ulcerative and hemorrhagic typhlocolitis - Glandular stomach: Multifocal erosive/ulcerative gastritis - Urinary bladder: Multifocal erosive cystitis Comment The most striking gross necropsy finding was severe inflammatory disease of the large intestine. Possible causes for this type of lesion include salmonellosis. Samples are on hold for additional testing; but no ancillary testing will be pursued until the requested rabies test results are returned from the Michigan Department of Community Health. Tissue lesions; including changes in the brain; will be further assessed by histologic examination. The rabies test results will be released as soon as they are available; and the findings of complete histologic examination and ancillary testing will be included in the final report. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Patholog

SEPSIS. This 4-year-old female boa had been doing well with no signs of illness was eating well and had eaten one day prior to being found dead. There is a history of Cryptosporidium in other animals of this species in the same area. Necropsy revealed no signs of trauma diffusely pale liver hemorrhage in the lungs a rat in the stomach and feces in the colon.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT RENAL CARDIAC AND HEPATIC DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS AXONAL DEGENERATION EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old snake had a one year history of chronic weight loss. Radiographs revealed bridging proliferative bone growths ventral to the vertebral processes on at least 33 cm. of the body. A previous hepatic biopsy identified hepatic fibrosis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe muscle wasting in addition to the proliferative bone lesions. The stomach and intestine were mildly corrugated.

BACTERIAL URINARY TRACT INFECTION BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This 5-year-old captive bred male Mexican bighorn sheep had a history of stranguria in September 2010 that appeared to resolve with oral antibiotics. In March 2011 the animal showed signs of illness and weakness and fell from a butte. The sheep was found deceased approximately five days after the onset of signs. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition frothy fluid within the trachea and bronchi heavy lungs with discolored and mottled margins a mottled serosal surface of the heart abundant dark yellowish fluid in the abdominal cavity bright red and inflamed abomasal mucosa a bright red pancreas possible petechiation of the intestinal mucosa a diffusely dark red urinary bladder that cannot be expressed manually a urethral urolith severe ureteral distention and enlarged kidneys.

BAYLISASCARIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male parrot developed severe neurologic impairment and did not respond to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Small hematomas were noted along the wing veins attributed to previous venipuncture. No other gross lesions were reported.

Pancreas: Islet carcinoma Liver; mesenteric lymph node: Metastatic carcinoma Kidney: Membranous glomerulopathy; ectatic glomeruli; glomerular sclerosis; tubular degeneration and necrosis; granular casts; and segmental medullary mineralization Eyes: Multifocal iris cysts Duodenum; jejunum; ileum colon: Mild; diffuse; lymphoplasmacytic enterocolitis. Comments: The carcinoma within the pancreas is consistent with neuroendocrine origin. Islet cell tumors can secrete various hormones such as insulin; gastrin; somatostatin; etc. Thus; the clinical signs they cause depend on the hormone; or hormones; that they secrete. Immunohistochemical labeling can be performed to determine hormone expression in this tumor; if desired. The hepatic and lymph node metastases appear to be neuroendocrine in origin; but this cannot be confirmed from routine histopathology. Immunohistochemical staining is available for an additional cost to further investigate the origin of these tumors; this testing can be performed on the submitted tissues. The renal changes show chronic glomerular changes as well as acute tubular disease. The deep medullary/renal papillary necrosis may be evidence of an adverse drug reaction; such as due to NSAID therapy. The iris cysts are an incidental finding; as they are small; and there is no evidence of occlusion of the iridocorneal angle. The enterocolitis does not extend into the submucosa and there is no change within the alimentary epithelium; as such the clinical relevance of these lesions is likely minimal. David Needle; DVM. Normal Stomach Comments: There were reports of mutlifocal white nodules in the gastric mucosa on necropsy. These lesions were not evident after formalin fixation and there was no histologic evidence of disease within the stomach. David Needle; DVM

YOLK COELOMITIS PROBABLE SEPSIS. This 2.5-year-old female domestic chicken presented for illness and a distended coelom and died overnight. Necropsy revealed extensive yolk in the coelom with associated inflammatory response. Food was in the mouth and upper trachea.

VALVULAR FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 15-year-old female pygmy goat had a history of acute dyspnea. The animal died prior to treatment. At necropsy moderate pleural effusion was noted in the thorax. Lungs were edematous. A focal tan nodule was present in the right lung. Cystic nodules were noted on the mitral and aortic valves.

PULMONARY CONGESTION PNEUMOCONIOSIS URATE STASIS. This 2-year-old male finch presented as fluffed lethargic and dyspneic. The animal was treated with oxygen antibiotics and dextrose but was found dead two hours later. At necropsy hemorrhage was present within the interclavicular air sac. The liver contained foci of yellow/tan discoloration.

CERVICAL ENDOCRINE CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female warthog has a history of a cervical mass that had recently grown. The animal had become inappetent with minimal stool output lethargy and upper airway noise. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large mineralized and encapsulated mass in the thoracic cavity that was tan and mottled on cut surface a mild amount of frothy material in the trachea a mild amount of fluid on cut surfaces of the lungs gas distension in the small intestine cysts in the ovaries and uterus old fracture in the right rear leg and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA HEART FAILURE CHRONIC PLEUROPNEUMONIA. This approximately 3-year-old male gorilla was humanely euthanized. It had a six month history of Pseudomonas pneumonia secondary to chlorine gas poisoning. It began to develop right heart failure. At necropsy there was serosanguineous pleural effusion bilaterally. There was pleuritis on the right side with substantial adhesions of the right lung to the diaphragm and between lung lobes. There were adhesions between the left lung lobes. The trachea was erythematous with hemorrhage and softening of the trachea at the intubation bulb site. The right lung lobes were small and green. There was a frank abscess with an adhesion to the diaphragm. The left lung lobes were dark and irregular. The right ventricular wall was thickened. There were 3 liters of yellow effusion in the abdominal cavity. There was a yeast infection on the tongue. There were esophageal erosions. There were small amounts of ingesta present in the stomach and a piece of plastic. Peyer’s patches were prominent. There was a large amount of digesta present in the large intestine. The mucosa was hemorrhagic. The liver was enlarged and mottled with rounded edges. There were good fat stores and moderate muscle atrophy.

TRAUMA HEPATITIS. This 15-year-old male tern was found dead in the pond. At necropsy the right humerus was fractured and the right elbow was dislocated. Fracture was also noted in the tibiotarsus. Hemorrhages were present adjacent to the fracture sites.

OSTEOARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male rattlesnake had a history of proliferative osteoarthritis and Salmonella sp. was cultured from blood. This animal had recently become nonmobile and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified hardened ribs and spine in a large midsection of the vertebral column.

RENAL GOUT BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 10.5-year-old male quail had a history of corneal opacity and left leg lameness. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the lungs were congested and hemorrhagic and the coelomic cavity contained viscous sanguineous fluid. The pancreas contained a 2 mm. diameter cyst.

FRACTURED SPINE EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male ibis was found in the morning unable to use its legs and had no prior medical history. Deep pain responses could not be elicited from the legs. Radiography revealed a midthoracic spinal fracture with compression of the spinal cord. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Aside from the fracture no gross lesions were noted and the bird was in good body condition.

RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS PERFORATING ULCER SEPSIS. This 7-year-old male meerkat developed acute depression and neurologic disease with paralysis aggression foaming at the mouth and weakness. Supportive care was administered but the animal died overnight. Necropsy revealed injected blood vessels in the brain and no other abnormalities. The animal was obese.

MYOCARDIAL INFRACT PULMONARY HYPERTENSION CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE POSSIBLE MICROSPORIDIOSIS. This 9-year-old male domestic rabbit had a routine physical exam on 2/26 and was within normal limits. Blood work was within normal limits as well. It was found dead during morning rounds on 3/20. Necropsy revealed no gross lesions.

FUNGAL TRACHEITIS PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS RENAL GOUT. This 6-year/7-month-old male boa died. It was being treated for pneumonia for the past few months. It was housed with a ground boa that died of a protozoan pneumonia and this boa also started showing signs of pneumonia about the time the other snake did. The boa was treated for several weeks with metronidazole and antibiotics and then was switched to itraconazole when fungal hyphae were recovered in a lung wash. At necropsy the boa was in good nutritional condition. All tissues were slightly dry and tacky. The spleen may have been slightly enlarged. The vestigial lung was filled with a thick yellow purulent fluid. The main lung wall was thickened edematous and congested. The surface of the lung was covered with a layer of clear mucus. The mucus was thick and completely covered the normal reticular pattern giving the interior surface of the lung a smooth glistening appearance. Impression smears of the lung reveal fungal hyphae. There was a small amount of bloody fluid in the pericardial sac. The folds in the stomach were prominent.

EUTHANASIA PITUITARY ADENOMA MAMMARY HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS UTERINE LEIOMYOMA ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA OVARIAN CYST DERMATITIS. This 9.5-year-old female goat has a history of abdominal distention and inappropriate lactation. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the pituitary gland was enlarged. A multilobular cystic mass was present on the proximal wall of the urinary bladder. A firm mass was present in the body of the uterus.

Intestine: Moderately severe acute neutrophilic enteritis; multifocal submucosal pyogranulomas Heart: Moderate pyogranulomatous myocarditis Kidney: Moderate chronic lymphoplasmacytic interstitial nephritis; Multifocal; bilateral renal cysts Liver: Focal capsular fibrosis with bile ductular hyperplasia and mild lymphoplasmacytic inflammation; Moderate diffuse hemosiderosis Please see comments Comments The exact cause of death could not be definitively determined. Gram stain did not indicate the presence of bacterial organisms within the pyogranulomas of the small intestine although there were large numbers of gram positive rods within the intestinal lumen. The clinical significance of this findings is not clear; these organisms may represent antemortem or postmortem bacterial (presumably Clostridia sp.) overgrowth. The isolated strains of E.coli are considered to represent the normal resident bacterial flora; as these organisms tested negative for virulence factors. Further; Salmonella; Shigella; or Yersinia sp. were no isolated from the intestine. Jennifer Lamoureux; D

YOLK COELOMITIS BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA OOPHORITIS. This 9-year-old female rattlesnake had been out of hibernation for over a week and had not been fed or completely warmed up. It had a history of active reproductive behavior. The snake was found dead and necropsy revealed good body condition blood present around the cloaca much ovarian development and free yolk in the oviduct.

CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS URINARY CALCULI GASTRIC MINERALIZATION INANITON. This 9-year-old sloth was lethargic anorexic weak and was treated with antibiotics steroids and subcutaneous fluids. The animal’s condition continued to decline and the animal died later that day. At gross necropsy urinary calculi were present within the right renal pelvis and purulent material was present in the right ureter. The lining of the urinary bladder was black.

PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS CECAL NEMATODIASIS RUMENITIS WITH PAPILLOMAS RHABDOMYOLYSIS RENAL TUBULAR MINERALIZATION AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7.5-year-old female southern gerenuk is from a herd in which there have been dietary alterations and overgrown hooves. This animal was found collapsed in the exhibit a few days after the animals were treated for the hoof problem dewormed and had blood draws. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed tacky internal organs with a dark blue to purple tint. The rumen was filled with green fluid and little fibrous material. Multiple coalescing dark red to black foci were on the mucosal surface resembling bleeding ulcers. Dark red fluid filled contents were noted in the duodenum and the rumen.

LYMPHOMA HEPATIC GRANULOMATOSIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male rattlesnake had a history of caudal body paralysis and swelling with a prominent dorsal spine and severe concavity of the ventral body with poor muscle tone. Palpable masses were noted in the caudal half of the body. Radiographs revealed numerous fractured ribs on both sides of the caudal half of the body. Necropsy revealed wet lungs and enlarged liver with multiple white masses that are 0.5 cm. in diameter throughout the liver ovary uterus and kidney. A mass located distal to the gallbladder was adhered to the serosal surface of the adjacent intestine.

OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS TO LIVER ECTOPIC EGG AND YOLK COELOMITIS. This 7-year-old female domestic chicken was seen with feather mites pasting of feces and urates around the vent and a pronounced keel. The bird fell backwards when trying to walk and was slow to right itself when falling over. A hard mass was felt in the coelomic cavity and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large amount of feces and urates around the vent and numerous arthropods crawling over the entire body. A massive yolk mass was noted around the oviduct. The liver contained numerous white nodules. The gall bladder was distended with dark yellow fluid. A free-floating mass of gelatinous material was noted in the coelomic cavity.

EUTHANASIA IMPACTION CYSTITIS. This 7-year/1-month-old female rock hyrax was humanely euthanized. It had a history of decreased alertness foreign body and intervertebral disc disease. At necropsy there was fecal matter present free in the abdominal cavity. There was extensive serosal hemorrhage present on the bowel bladder uterine horns and mesentery. There was a small hole in the large colon. The surface of the large colon was very thin and hemorrhagic. There was a large amount of feces firmly impacted in the rectum. The diameter of the rectum was approximately 5-6 cm. The proximal portion of the large bowel was very large and full of fecal material some of which was firm. The caeca were full of dry somewhat impacted feces and had areas of mucosal hemorrhage. The stomach was very dilated with air and a large amount of food. The left kidney was larger than the right which had a slight fibrous appearance. The renal pelvises were large and full of viscous fluid.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS CESTODIASIS FLAGELLATES AND CRYPTOSPORIDIA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 3-year-old monitor was euthanized when PCR results indicated Cryptosporidium infection. Necropsy revealed thin body condition decreased muscle mass fat bodies in the coelom thickened gastric wall absence of ingesta in the intestine male reproductive tract and ectoparasites (mites).

EUTHANASIA THYMOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 11-year-old male goat had a history of anorexia and lethargy with distention of the abdomen. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition failed to improve. A mass was identified at the heart base (thymoma presumptive). The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Erosion was noted in the joint cartilage. A lobulated pale tan mass was present anterior to the heart. The mass contained gelatinous material. A firm white area was present in the heart. The abomasum was distended with fluid.

PULMONARY GRANULOMA FATTY LIVER. This 1-year/3-month-old boa was found dead. Its cagemate from a different container was swarmed by ants and died one day last week. This animal appeared normal and ate two mice but was then found dead. Both snakes have been poor eaters and have not grown well since arrival. At necropsy there was food material from the mice in the stomach and lower intestine. The jejunum appeared thickened. The lungs appeared mildly erythematous. There were few firm white nodules present in the lungs. The liver was pale and firm. The spleen was pale.

BILATERAL THYROID ADENOMAS CHRONIC COELOMITIS. This 6-year-old female chicken presented with depression and coelomic distention presumed to be reproductive tract disease. Supportive care was administered and the bird improved for a while but then became weak and unable to stand. Supportive care again was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition ovoid masses in the thoracic inlet cranial and dorsal to the heart approximately 3 cm. in length. Each mass on cut surface had a yellowish cystic structure and a reddish cystic structure and some consolidated soft tissue. A large blood clot was present on the surface of the liver. Hemorrhage was noted on the serosal surfaces of the intestine. The oviduct had multiple cavitated areas containing clotted blood. The cranial oviduct contained multiple inspissated egg yolks.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 18-year-old marine toad had radiographic lesions in the joints of all four legs. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the great vessels were irregular. Pale foci were present in the liver.
EUTHANASIA RETINAL SEPARATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 2-year-old female basilisk had a history of chronic ocular disease. The animal was humanely euthanized.
PNEUMONIA. This 4-month-old male elephant shrew was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy fat depots were absent.

INTRASPECIES TRAUMA EPICARDIAL HEMORRHAGE PULMONARY EDEMA HEPATITIS. This 10-month-old lorikeet suffered trauma from cagemates. Wounds were surgically repaired; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy lacerations were present over the dorsum. Hemorrhage was noted in the pericardium. The liver was tan and soft.

HEMANGIOSARCOMA. This 12.5-year-old female burrowing owl had been clinically normal the previous day but eating less normally for the past week or so. It was found dead in the exhibit. Necropsy revealed good body condition fly eggs around the right eye a small amount of blood found in the mouth and trachea discolored lungs and the right lung slightly smaller than the left. Dark nodules were in the lungs. A pellet was found in the gizzard. The right kidney was slightly darker than the left. Adequate adipose stores were noted.

MESOTHELIOMA BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS VERTEBRAL CHONDROSARCOMA. This 8-year-old corn snake was found dead. It had a history of scent gland abscesses but no recent problems. Necropsy revealed a scar on the left side of the cloaca reddened lungs an undigested mouse in the caudal esophagus hyperemic small intestine enlarged liver and a series of nodes along the caudal gastrointestinal tract with vesicles on them that contain yolk colored substance. These are irregularly shaped and possibly early follicles.
adult. Weight: 30000.0 g.  Euthanased.  Multiple bite wounds.  Hepatitis.  Chronic nephritis.  Thickened left AV valve and nodules on aortic valve.  Tooth problems.  Pulmonary oedema +/- pneumonia?.

EUTHANASIA GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS PANCREATIC ADENOCARCINOMA. This 19-year-old female tiger was humanely euthanized. It had a 4+ year history of chronic renal failure. Prior to euthanasia the tiger’s food consumption decreased and water consumption decreased. The tiger developed pronounced hind limb weakness. At necropsy the tiger was very thin. There were minimal fat stores and there was muscle wasting. There were areas of fibrous tissue proliferation along both elbows in the point of the right shoulder. There was approximately 100 cc. of dark red fluid within the pericardial sac. The serosal surface of the heart was granular and irregular in appearance. It circumferentially surrounded the heart. The inner pericardial surface was ecchymotic. The pericardial membrane was thickened. There was a soft fleshy mass that extended from the pericardial surface. There were multiple small pale white to yellow foci scattered over the pulmonary surface and within the parenchyma. There was a 1 x 2 in. focal ulcerative area along the hard palate. There was moderate gingivitis. The mucosal surface of the stomach was diffusely hemorrhagic. The descending lobe of the pancreas appeared mottled. The ascending lobe was normal. Both adrenals appeared slightly hemorrhagic. The right lobe of the thyroid contained a small pale yellow focus along the ventral surface. Both popliteal lymph nodes appeared enlarged as did the left prescapular lymph node. There were multiple enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes. The bladder appeared uniformly thickened. There was a small fleshy raised red mass at the cranial aspect of the bladder mucosa. Both kidneys appeared small firm and pale with pale pitted cortices and irregular corticomedullary junctions. There were pale medullae with streaking of redness. There were bilateral cataracts.

EUTHANASIA MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA NEPHROLITHS STRESS. This 20-year/3-month-old female leopard was humanely euthanized. It had a left mammary mass that had enlarged and metastasized locally. It became ulcerated centrally leaving a draining open wound. This leopard also had several chronic conditions. At necropsy the left inguinal mammary gland had a large firm pink centrally ulcerated mass that measured 12 x 6 x 4 cm. There were several smaller masses palpated in the left mammary chain. The left and right inguinal lymph nodes and left popliteal lymph nodes were also enlarged. The mass was surrounded by fat and had a central core of firm irregular tissue with cystic areas containing tan/brown fluid. The mass was adhered to the left abdominal fascia. Another smaller softer mass (lipoma) was noted on the right hip within the subcutaneous tissue. The liver appeared pale tan to copper and had several fluid filled cysts within the parenchyma. There was a firm round mass (1.5 x 2 cm.) adhered to the greater omentum. There were renal calculi within the renal pelvis of the left kidney. There were cystic areas in the region between the cortex and medulla. The left renal pelvis appeared thickened and fibrotic. The right kidney was smaller than the left kidney. On cross section the kidney was pale and fibrous. Several calculi were noted. The right ureter contained a large stone at the level approximately 2 cm. from the renal pelvis. There was also a firm irregular mass adhered to the dorsal body wall at the pelvic inlet. The caudal lungs appeared dark and congested.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE DEGENEARATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE RENOLITH. This 18.5-year-old male Rodriguez flying fox had a digit amputation in June 2015 with a diagnosis of spindle cell sarcoma and complete excision (G15-3179). The patient was clinically normal and was found unable to use its hind limbs the day of death. Radiographs revealed lysis of the pelvis and proximal femurs bilaterally and destruction of both hip joints. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the liver had multifocal white pinpoint nodules. The kidneys were subjectively pale and enlarged.

Haired skin (x2): See comments Comments The histopathologic findings for both masses in this case are suggestive of soft tissue spindle cell sarcomas; for which the top differential for both masses is a fibrosarcoma. While the neoplastic cells were well-differentiated; they were noted to be densely cellular and dissecting between collagen and skeletal muscle bundles (suggestive of more infiltrative behavior; thus the malignant diagnosis). Soft tissue sarcomas have been reported in Capybaras; although it would appear that cutaneous soft tissue sarcomas have not; however; soft tissue sarcomas have been frequently reported in rodents in general. Complete excision could not be confirmed for either mass; as neoplastic cells extended to the examined margins. Stephanie French; DVM; MS

NEPHROSCLEROSIS GOUT MYELINIC EDEMA EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male milk snake had a progressive history of abnormal neurologic signs. The animal was frequently found upside-down or resting in odd positions but had a normal righting reflex good appetite and good weight maintenance. Eventually there was a decline in mentation friable scales dull skin weight loss and loss of righting reflex. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition enlarged heart a fluid-filled cyst in the caudal third of the coelom over the region of the spleen and gallbladder multiple pinpoint white spots in the kidney moderately thickened gastric and proximal intestinal mucosa edematous colon and two foci of urate accumulation in the kidney.

TRAUMA HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE INTRAMUSCULAR HEMORRHAGE. This 6-year-old female tern was found dead. At necropsy a large area of hemorrhage was present in the muscle of the left shoulder and thigh. A large quantity of hemorrhage was present in the abdominal cavity liver and adjacent to the kidneys. A small hematoma was noted on the right liver lobe.

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE ADRENAL CORTICAL ATROPHY (STEROIDS) CALCINOSIS CUTIS AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male red wolf was being treated for inflammatory bowel disease and more recently had developed pressure sores with fly strike. The animal had been inappetent for five days. Supportive care was administered but with poor response. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed numerous round to irregularly shaped malodorous cutaneous ulcers on all four limbs the ventral abdomen ventral thorax and the right caudal dorsum immediately cranial to the base of the tail. Diffuse subcutaneous edema was noted on the ventral caudal thorax and ventral abdomen. Numerous hyperemic superficial ulcers surrounded by a white/tan halo were present on the tongue especially on the ventral cranial aspect. A complete partially healed fracture is present in the midbody of the caudal aspect of the left patella. The corresponding capsule is markedly thickened and fibrotic and adhered to the cranial aspect of the patellar bone. The adrenal glands were bilaterally decreased in size. Numerous indented round to irregularly shaped dark red to black areas of superficial mucosal ulceration were noted in the pylorus and numerous dark brown to black nodules were embedded in the gastric mucosa. Several areas of white/tan parenchymal discoloration were noted in the hepatic lobes. The cranial lung lobes had several irregularly shaped foci of dark red to dark brown indentation and consolidation and the right caudal lung lobe was dark red to black. Multiple pinpoint foci of adhesions between the dura mater and the dorsal lateral aspect of the cerebral parietal lobes were noted. The leptomeninges adjacent to the adhesions had white/gray discoloration. The aortic valve had endocardiosis.

HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE LYMPH NODE HEMOSIDEROSIS ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 6-year-old male river otter was anesthetized for a preshipment examination. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy frank blood was noted in the abdomen. The liver was fractured and friable. Spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged.

SARCOCYSTOSIS PANCREATIC NECROSIS. This approximately 11.5-year-old male lorikeet was slow to come in for the evening and quickly became progressively weaker and began vocalizing. It died within 15 min. of onset of clinical signs. Necropsy revealed hepatomegaly abundant adipose tissue abnormal coloration in the pancreas and bilateral pulmonary congestion.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE THYROID CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female Thomson’s gazelle had severe progressive degenerative arthritis and inability to walk intermittently over the last two days. The animal had become unable to rise or ambulate in spite of increasing doses of various medications and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe arthritis in the joints and no gross lesions in the viscera.

EUTHANASIA SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC OOPHORITIS INANITION. This 13-year-old female snake had a history of periodic inappetence. The neck showed an area of deviation of the vertebrae. The animal was humanely euthanized. Areas of spondylosis were noted radiographically.

INTRACOELOMIC BIMORPHIC NEOPLASM BACTERIAL ABSCESS. This 5-year-old female chicken was found down outside the run with external wounds. Necropsy revealed thin body condition subcutaneous hemorrhage around the neck torn skin above the thigh. The keel was bent in an S-shape with lateral deviations. The coelom had a fluid wave and was distended 300 ml. of amber-tinged fluid was in the coelomic cavity and a 2-3 cm. tan plaque with a cystic appearance was on the coelomic surface of the body wall. Fluid was in the air sacs. The liver was small and mottled. A large cystic structure approximately the size of a large sweet potato was in the coelomic cavity. The structure was pedunculated and contained 200 ml. of serous fluid. A large mass was noted within the mesentery adjacent to the oviduct. The mass was 3-4 cm round with irregular/cystic margins and was hemorrhagic on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 15-month-old neutered male ferret presented with tachypnea and weight loss. The animal was euthanized after a diagnosis of lymphoma or thymoma was made based on cytology and radiology. At necropsy a large mass occupying approximately 85% of the thoracic cavity was present anterior to the heart. The liver also appeared enlarged and there was a 1 cm. in diameter mass at the cranial pole of both kidneys.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE BILIARY CYSTS. This captive bred 19-year-old male leopard was humanely euthanized. It had progressive weight loss and increasing BUN and creatinine over two years. The BUN was 126 mg/dl and the creatinine was 2.7 mg/dl. The leopard’s mentation began to depress. At necropsy both kidneys were very small (4x3 cm.). The liver was covered with fluid filled cysts 1-4 cm. in diameter.
INANITION SHOCK. This 5.5-year-old female wallaby was found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin with non discernable fat depots. The lungs were moderately congested.
