YOLK COELOMITIS RUPTURED FOLLICLE. This 7.5-year-old female Inca tern was found dead in its enclosure and had no prior clinical signs. It had been treated for malaria in October 2014. Necropsy revealed thin body condition subjectively everted cloaca a moderate amount of hemorrhagic or purulent material in the region of the cloaca and throughout the coelom. A blood clot to 4 cm. in diameter was associated with a ruptured follicle. The liver was pale feces were in the large intestine the kidneys were pale and no other gross abnormalities were noted.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC DERMATITIS BRONCHIOLOALVEOLAR HYPERPLASIA PNEUMONIA. This 2-year-old male opossum was euthanized due to deteriorating condition. The animal had a history of pelvic fracture. A mass developed on the right arm. Recently blindness and inability to use the left forelimb developed. At necropsy an ulcerated round mass was present on the ventrum of the right forelimb. Lungs contained multiple brown to white nodules.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 8-year-old gecko had a history of lethargy and weight loss. Radiographs revealed poor skeletal quality. Although clinical response was noted to calcium treatments skeletal density did not improve. The animal was found dead. At necropsy no coelomic fat depots were identified. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE AND EDEMA SUSPECT TRAUMA. This female 5-year-old fruit bat died. It was recently trapped and transferred to holding pen for physical exam. The animals were observed to be eating and drinking well. At necropsy the right caudal lung lobe appeared adhered to the rib cage. The lungs appeared enlarged and firm suggesting pulmonary edema. The heart appeared enlarged relative to body size and the left ventricular wall appeared hypertrophied. The intestines appeared slightly distended and discolored. There was an area of hemorrhage along the caudal base of the skull that extended onto the surface of the brain.

PROLIFERATIVE UROCYSTITIS URETERITIS AND DUODENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female gerenuk had been treated for chronic bilateral tarsal arthritis receiving steroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug therapy and more recently also treated regularly with laser applications. The animal developed muscle wasting commensurate with the age and bilateral hind limb instability of the stifles or tarsi causing the animal to walk with a twist to each leg the stifles rotating inward. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a dry rough haircoat with patches of barbering of varying chronicity over the face neck and back. Fat stores are minimal marked degenerative change was in the hip joints and some mild degenerative change was in the cartilage of the stifles. Both tarsi had marked cartilaginous erosions down to underlying bone and synovial fluid was thin and blood-tinged. Both tarsi had lateral and dorsal bulging or distention of the joint capsules. Spondylosis involved the ventral aspects of the lumbar and lumbosacral areas and a few costal vertebral joints were mildly enlarged and irregular. Some areas of previous bone trauma without displacement were in the left ribcage. Multiple areas of marked ventricular fibrosis with surface depression were noted in the heart and moderate endocardiosis and edema were in the left atrioventricular valve. Thyroids were mildly enlarged and finely cystic. Marked polypoid mucosal hyperplasia was in the duodenum. Moderate numbers of whipworms were noted in the colon. Both ureters were markedly enlarged and dilated with severe submucosal edema especially in portions closer to the kidney. The ureteral papillae at the trigone of the bladder were prominent but with no apparent obstructions. The urinary bladder has mildly irregular thickened and congested mucosa. A few small clear fluid-filled cysts were on the serosa of the uterus. Both kidneys had mild scattered fibrous scarring and irregular indentations in the cortex with some granular appearance to the cortex on cut surface. No uroliths were seen and the pelvises were not dilated.

ENCEPHALITIS AND GANGLIONEURITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 6.5-year-old male red panda had a history of chronic inflammatory bowel disease which has improved since arrival at the current institution one year earlier. The animal now has a two-month history of pelage disease beginning on the tail and progressing towards the pelvis. This animal was found dead unexpectedly in its exhibit and a review of the exhibit found one small piece of toxic nightshade plant. Necropsy revealed good body condition with fur disease on the tail and multifocal over the pelvis and lateral hind limbs. The dense fur undercoat was matted and reddened and the upper fur coat was missing in affected areas. Numerous lymph nodes are found throughout the abdomen and most are prominently associated with stomach and mesentery. No other abnormalities were noted.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GASTRIC MINERALIZATION BILIARY CYSTS. This 12-year-old male lion had a history of anorexia and abnormal behavior. Severe azotemia was diagnosed. The animal was given supportive care and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy one lobe of the liver contained a multilobulated cyst. The kidneys appeared to be of normal size and contour and were pale.

GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA SPLENITIS HEPATITIS PANCRATITIS. This 14-year-old tree boa was under treatment for respiratory disease. The animal was found dead. At necropsy marked hemorrhage was present in the lung. Marked exudate was present in the stomach.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTEROSIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ATHEROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS METASTATIC MINERALZATION. This 9-year/9-month-old male cockatiel was humanely euthanized due to poor quality of life. It had a history of hepatomegaly and decreased liver function that was responding well to supportive care. At necropsy the bird was very thin. There was a healing keel wound. The liver had large areas of firm white tissue on either side.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY COLITIS WITH BACTERIAL OVERGROWTH. This 3-year-old male pygmy marmoset had been off feed sleeping a lot and had dyspnea. Examination revealed severe pleural effusion and the animal arrested while thoracocentesis was being performed. Necropsy revealed pale dilated heart enlarged firm liver and pale tan kidneys.

HEARTWORM DISEASE MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 7-year/4-month-old male red panda was found dead. It had a history of decreased food consumption. At necropsy the animal was in good body condition. There were large fat pads within the abdominal cavity. There were 6-7 adult heartworms within the right ventricle that were wrapped around the valves. The liver was engorged and hemorrhagic in appearance. The renal cortices were somewhat hemorrhagic.

SHOCK. This 7-year/5-month-old female motmot was found dead. It had no prior medical problems and was in an outdoor enclosure. At necropsy the bird was fat. There was no evidence of trauma. There was subcutaneous edema present in the ventral coelomic area and in the body wall. The liver had several small pinpoint 1-2 mm. nonraised white to tan foci on the surface. The gall bladder was large full and difficult to express. There was food present in the gastrointestinal tract. The lungs were bright red to pink. The kidneys were pale pink and friable. The pancreas was firm.

PROBABLE HYPERTHERMIA. This 3-year-old male Flemish giant rabbit was found dead acutely on July 1 2011. The patient had been normal the previous day. Gross necropsy revealed abundant adipose blood around both nares and marked autolysis.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS C-CELL TUMOR MUSCULAR SARCOCYSTOSIS. This approximately 11-year-old female sheep was humanely euthanized due to poor quality of life as a result of chronic degenerative arthritis that was unresponsive to medication. At necropsy there was large irregular focal pale region associated with the right thyroid gland. There was evidence of arthritis in both stifles and irregularity to the edge of the femoral head. Tarsal joints appeared fine. There were pale streaks visible in the epicardium of the right ventricle. Liver heart kidney spleen brain and lung were frozen for future use if needed. Lung was submitted for culture.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE PULMONARY ATELECTASIS ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS. This 9-year-old male rabbit had been diagnosed with a collapsed right lung in December 2013 and had mildly abnormal respiratory pattern. The animal otherwise had a good appetite until two weeks prior to death when body condition declined and the animal became inappetent with progressively worsening respiratory efforts. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed atrophy of the pulmonary lobes on the right side with associated pleural adhesions and consolidation of the pulmonary parenchyma. The left lungs were hypertrophic with bullae at the medial aspect.

1) Heart: chronic multifocal myocarditis 2) Stomach: perigastric mass Comments The myocardial masses are believed to be infectious in origin; either abscesses or granulomas; however; neoplasia is alos in the differential. The mass observed adjecent the stomach may also indicate infection in the abdominal cavity or neoplastic process. Histopathology and bacterial culture are pending; and the results will be included in the final report. 1) Lung: Moderate chronic caseogranulomatous pneumonia 2) Kidney: Focal chronic caseogranulomatous nephritis 3) Heart: Severe multifocal caseogranulomatous and fibrosing myocarditis Bacterial septicemia resulting in caseogranulomatous myocarditis; pneumonia and nephritis Comments: The histologic findings confirm our suspicions on gross necropsy of bacterial infection affecting the myocardium and other tissues. Acinetobacter; a gram negative rod; is the most likely agent to be causing the caseogranulomatous lesions seen. Staphylococcus infection is likely secondary. This completes the outstanding testing for this case.

INTRACOELOMIC FIBROSIS AND ADHESIONS. This approximately 4-year-old female budgerigar died and necropsy revealed fatty liver cartilaginous neoplasia in the abdominal cavity and massive unilateral hemorrhage.

GASTRIC IMPACTION. This 2.5-year-old male silver rabbit was lethargic became laterally recumbent and died. At necropsy there was streaking on the serosal surface of the stomach. There was a trichobezoar lodged in the distal pylorus that was associated with an annular band of erythema hemorrhage and ulceration.

SUSPECT SHOCK ARTERIOSCLEROSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS SUSPECT HYPERTENSION RENAL ADENOMA HEPATITIS. This approximately 14.5-year-old male spoonbill was found dead in aviary. At necropsy there were broken blood feathers on the right wing. There was a small amount of blood on the feathers. The bird seemed wet under the right wing. There was thin feather coverage on the left dorsal back. The left leg had scabs on the anterior hock. There was a small abrasion just below the lateral hock on the left leg. The right lateral leg had a small abrasion on the lower thigh and below the hock. The medial right leg had a small abrasion just below the hock. There were missing feathers around the anterior neck. There were good muscle tone and fat stores.

PYELONEPHRITIS PATHOLOGIC FRACTURES PROBABLE FIBROUS OSTEODYSTROPHY. This 8-year-old female golden lion tamarin had a three month history of fractured femurs which were repaired with plates. Bone cortices were radiographically within normal limits but radiographs revealed evidence of previously healed fractures. The plated fractures healed slowly and subsequently refractured necessitating euthanasia for humane and diagnostic purposes. Blood work for this animal was within normal limits. An MGA implant had been placed two years earlier and was removed at the time of orthopedic surgery.

ACUTE SHOCK PROBABLE ENTEROTOXEMIA; MILD NONSUPPURATIVE ENCEPHALOMYELITIS. This 4.5-year-old male kangaroo had a two day history of lethargy and died spontaneously despite therapy. Necropsy revealed a large amount of melena congestion in the small intestine and no other significant findings.

BUMBLEFOOT GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS. This 16-year-old female American flamingo was treated for joint lameness and died suddenly the next day. Necropsy revealed uric acid deposits on the pericardium and pale tan kidneys. Some orange plaques were in the brachial arteries.

EARLY CIRRHOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EMACIATION COLLOID GOITER EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL GRANULOMAS. This 18-year-old female rattlesnake underwent esophagostomy four months prior to death for suspect esophageal obstruction. At surgery a mass effect in the proximal esophagus was noted. The animal had gradual weight decline postsurgery despite a good appetite. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy there was a red mass cranial to the heart that was solid to gel-like on cut section. The liver was prominent and there was a mass-like effect in the region of the gallbladder with pockets of fluid. The kidneys were unilaterally small.

TRICHOBEZOAR OBSTRUCTION SHOCK. This 19-day-old elephant shrew was one of twins. There have been recent issues with gastric trichobezoars in the neonates. This animal was reared by the dam for the first 10 days and then removed for hand and supplement feeding. Supportive care for dehydration was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed reduced bone density trichobezoar in the ileocecocolic junction obstructing the intestinal tract and gastric bloat.

MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS IN MULTIPLE TISSUES SUSPECTED PULMONARY HYERTENSION AND CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY WITH CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION CHRONIC HEMORRHAGE IN ADIPOSE TISSUE EUTHANASIA. This approximately 12-year-old female white-fronted wallaby had a history of mammary masses and pulmonary metastases found four months ago. The animal also had poor eyesight and nuclear sclerosis. The animal presented in respiratory distress and radiographs revealed extensive progression of pulmonary metastases. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Gross necropsy confirmed a mass associated with the right caudal mammary gland with ulceration and crusting in the pouch and regions of necrosis in the mass. The right lateral thigh had an irregular lobulated subcutaneous mass that was roughly 1 x 6 cm. The lungs contained numerous irregular marginated umbilicated and pale tan nodules with red discoloration effacing over 75% of the parenchyma. The tracheobronchial lymph nodes were subjectively enlarged. The kidneys contained a few renal cysts. No epicardial fat was present.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK CHRONIC DERMATITIS. This 18-year-old female squirrel monkey was found dead. The animal had recently arrived from another institution. At necropsy the heart was pale and rounded with white streaks.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA LEIOMYOSARCOMA. This 13-year-old female gazelle has a history of debilitating arthritis and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal had developed aggressive arthropathies in the carpi and left hock and mobility had become compromised. The gazelle was having getting up from a laying position. Necropsy revealed osteophyte formation in both carpi and the left tarsus with minimal cartilaginous erosion on the joint surfaces. Ligaments were stiff and appeared to be mineralized. Thyroids were firm on sectioning. Sunken yellow fibrous foci were noted on the epicardial surface of the right ventricle. The left kidney and an infarct in the cortical region and the right kidney were irregular on its capsular surface with many sunken areas. Medullary areas appeared ischemic and pale or tan and mottled suggesting a proliferative process. An oblong smooth tan colored nodule was in the right adrenal gland. Small round swellings were noted in the walls of the uterine horns. Several tan fluid filled translucent cysts were present in the ovaries. Some mesenteric lymph nodes appear larger than expected. A 4 in. irregular purple round mass was in the abdomen with a 7 in. long vascular stalk. The stalk communicated with the dorsal abdominal veins caudal to the left kidney. The mass was tan and bulged on cut surface. Fluid filled cysts were within the mass and these contain cloudy yellow fluid.

ASPIRATION POSTSURGICAL COMPLICATIONS. This 10-year-old lemur has been recovering slowly from a tonsillectomy one week earlier. The animal presented as an emergency with dyspnea lethargy and discharge from the nostrils then aspirated and died during anesthetic induction. Necropsy revealed food material and purulent discharge in the nasal cavity and sinuses. The lungs were reddened and a bulla was in one lobe.

CLOSTRIDIOSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 2-year-old female coconut lorikeet was found lethargic and fluffed in the aviary in the morning is isolated and treated but died shortly thereafter. The bird had dried fecal and urate debris around the vent. Necropsy revealed lean body condition watery tan-colored fluid in the trachea diffusely edematous lungs watery brown fluid in the coelomic cavity a white focus on the serosal surface of the liver petechiae throughout the serosa of the alimentary tract watery brown fluid in the crop empty proventriculus and ventriculus and a segment of firm jejunum with thickened fibrinous debris on the mucosal surface. Firm fecal material was also present in the ileum and colon. The kidneys were diffusely mildly pale and the ovary had numerous small follicles. Multiple areas of hemorrhage were noted in the skull bones.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 24-year-old female California sea lion had a history of swallowing a 15 ml. plastic dropper bottle of hypertonic saline which it regurgitated nine days later. Following the episode of regurgitation the animal became inappetent and lethargic. Supportive care was administered but the animal died three days later. This sea lion had a history of chronic eye problems. It had been treated with meloxicam intermittently for the last two years. Necropsy revealed aortic distention keratitis cataracts gingival recession flaccid heart endocardiosis multiple vacuolar cystic structures in the kidneys alopecia of the ventral skin dark stomach and tracheal congestion.

CARCINOMA (LIVER HEART KIDNEY LUNG) GRANULOMATOUS GASTRITIS COELOMITIS BACTERIAL GASTRITIS. This 16-year-old female boa was seen biting itself and later died. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted in the cloaca. A large mass was present adherent to the base of the heart. The mass consisted of adipose tissue clotted blood and inspissated material. Lungs were edematous. Multiple firm white masses were present in the liver. The coelomic cavity contained numerous red cyst-like masses containing blood.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS. This 16-year-old female ibex was humanely euthanized due to chronic progressive arthritis. At necropsy there was fluid filled enlargement of the left carpal joint and moderate valgus deformity at the carpus. There were numerous pinpoint nodules present along the cervical mucosa and rings. The left prescapular lymph node was slightly larger than the right but not mineralized. There were three small masses in the fascia along the left costal sternal border of the thorax. On section they were mineralized. A small less than 1 cm. parasite-like cyst was found in the axillary space. The lateral aspect of the carpal metacarpal joint of the right and left carpus had distinct roughening and cartilage deterioration and fibrocartilaginous growth. Sections of heart liver kidney spleen lung and lymph node were frozen for future use if needed.

INTRASPECIES TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) PULMONARY EDEMA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA SHOCK. This 1.5-year-old female gazelle suffered trauma from another gazelle with fracture of the right pelvis. Surgery was attempted to repair the fracture but was not possible. Anesthetic recovery was uneventful and the animal was placed in a small stall for strict stall rest. The animal was later found dead. At necropsy the trachea contained frothy blood tinged fluid. Bronchi and caudal lung lobes also contained frothy blood tinged fluid. A large area of hemorrhage was present on the mesentery in the caudal right abdomen. Areas of hemorrhage were also identified adjacent to the duodenum and pancreas. The right kidney contained a hemorrhagic infarct. The right uterine horn contained a 1 cm. fetus.

MYOPATHY ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS PERITONITIS. This 14-year/1-month-old male pig died. It had a history of hyperesthesia following anesthesia. The following day the pig could not ambulate even with assistance. Supportive care was initiated. The pig declined in neurologic function. At necropsy the pig was obese with abundant fat stores. The peritoneum was diffusely hemorrhagic and appeared thickened. The serosal surface of the heart was mottled dark red/black and the cardiac vasculature appeared enlarged. On cut surface the myocardium contained pinpoint hemorrhages. The lungs were enlarged heavy and mottled dark red/black. Dark blood oozed on cut surface. The spleen was greatly enlarged dark black and oozed dark black fluid on cut surface. The serosa of the entire gastrointestinal tract was diffusely hemorrhagic. The stomach contained multiple ulcerations of varying size. Some of the ulcers coalesced. The liver was mottled dark red/black. The cranial dorsal border contained multiple small raised pale nodules that felt like emphysematous nodules. The liver oozed dark brown frothy fluid on cut surface. The gall bladder was distended and hard. Bile could not be expressed from the bile ducts. Both kidneys were generally pale both exteriorly and on cut surface. The right kidney contained a 0.5 x 1 cm. cyst that extended above the capsular surface externally and effaced the normal architecture of the cortex medulla and corticomedullary junction internally. The cyst extended almost to the renal pelvis. Both adrenals were diffusely enlarged and contained multiple pinpoint hemorrhages along the serosa. The bladder was distended with urine and the mucosa was diffusely reddened. There was a small area of hemorrhage observed in the musculature ventral to the L3-4 vertebral space. Similar hemorrhage was noted in the muscle dorsal to the space. The hemorrhage extended into the overlying fat layer.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL DERMATITIS RUMINORETICULOMASITIS ULCERATIVE COLITIS MANDIBULAR OSTEOMYELITIS. This 3-year/3-month-old female gazelle was found down and was humanely euthanized. It did not respond to treatment for shock. At necropsy there was meningitis. There was severe osteomyelitis of the caudal sinus (cribriform) that extended into the skull. There was osteomyelitis of the rostral mandible. There were dark serosal striations on the cecum. The spleen was small. There were some fat stores present.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male tiger had been showing signs of moderate to severe right forelimb lameness and bilateral hind limb lameness. It responded initially to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug therapy but the animal became increasingly lame and bloodwork revealed severe azotemia and hyperphosphatemia consistent with renal failure. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed the arthritis of the hips and lesions in both kidneys.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS AND AIR SACCULITIS BILIARY ADENOMA. This 12-year-old female rock dove was an education animal and had been a long-term captive (12 years). Necropsy revealed a 6 x 5 cm. hepatic mass.

INANITION. This 6-year-old male tentacled snake was found at the bottom of the tank. One of this snake’s teeth was hooked on the skin of its neck. At necropsy the lungs were hyperemic and a large quantity of fluid was present in the distal colon.

\_ Skeletal muscle; heart: Moderate to severe multifocal myodegeneration; necrosis; and fibrosis with intralesional protozoal cysts (presumptive Toxoplasma sp.) Lung: Severe diffuse alveolar edema and mild multifocal acute interstitial pneumonia Liver: Moderate multifocal chronic suppurative periportal hepatitis Pancreas: Moderate multifocal acute pancreatitis with necrosis Kidney: Mild multifocal lymphoplasmacytic nephritis with tubular degeneration Salivary gland: Acute suppurative ductular sialadenitis Comment: The likely cause of death was the severe protozoal myocarditis and resultant pulmonary decompensation. The other changes are likely a result of the metabolic and immunocompromising changes that followed. TRAUMA DROWNED. This 10.5-year-old male river otter was found dead in the pool drain. It had been stressed from separation and had developed scuffed footpads. It refused food when introduced to conspecifics and was found dead shortly thereafter. It had no other signs of illness prior to death. Necropsy revealed a fractured sternum and several cranial ribs blood in the thorax froth in the trachea and upper airway and possibly thickened intestinal walls.

YOLK COELOMITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7-year-old female rock dove was found dead in its enclosure in the morning. Necropsy revealed bilateral enophthalmos and thin body condition. Food was in the crop and white diffuse nodular plaque-like infiltrates were noted throughout the air sacs and liver. White nodular lesions were at the apex of the heart and multiple cysts were in the reproductive tract.

EUTHANASIA CLOACITIS COELOMITIS ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old female lory had necrosis of the cloaca which communicated with the coelomic cavity and air sacs. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy the cloacal mucosa was thickened and perforated at the colon.

ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS INANITION. This 7-year-old male wallaroo had a history of gastric dilatation and volvulus secondary to a gastric foreign body in December of 2001. Since that time the stomach remained distended and the animal had an inability to completely digest the food since that time. Recently the animal had begun to lose condition and become weak. The animal was hospitalized and its condition deteriorated despite supportive care. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the stomach was distended with fluid and gas but was otherwise normal. The musculature over the back and hips was thin and wasted.

AMYLOIDOSIS. This ferret has a 3- to 4-month history of renal failure and a one day history of intussusception and colonic prolapse. Necropsy revealed mottled and enlarged kidneys mild hepatomegaly and intussusception with rectal prolapse.

INTERVERTEBRAL DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE INTRACOELOMIC SARCOMA BACTERIAL AND EGG YOLK COELOMITIS TRACHAEL RING FRACTURE. This 17-year-old female timber rattlesnake had a history of Salmonella septicemia. This did not resolve despite numerous and prolonged antibiotic therapy. Three days prior to death the animal had lethargy and swelling of the caudal third of the body. Ultrasound revealed fluid in the reproductive tract and the animal was euthanized. At necropsy there was mild ventral erythema. There was marked distention of the caudal third of the body. Surrounding the oviducts and ovary was a large fluid-filled sac the capsule of which was caseous and the cranial aspect was nodular and firm. The kidney had multifocal white streaking. One vertebral body was irregular.

MYCOTIC BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ASPERGILLOSIS INANITION. This 14-year-old female spoonbill was found segregated from the flock and very weak. Examination revealed extreme cachexia. Supportive care including intravenous fluids antibiotics and anti-inflammatory medications were provided for several days. The animal was anesthetized for radiographs which revealed opacities in the lung fields. Anesthetic recovery was uneventful; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy the right lung was nearly completely effaced by two large granulomas containing green fungal hyphae.

PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS ENTERITIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA SARCOCYSTOSIS. This greater than 4-year-old lorikeet presented one week earlier due to weight loss and lethargy and continued to lose weight despite aggressive supportive care. The animal became severely dyspneic after tube feeding and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed congestion of the left lung with multiple pinpoint tan-colored foci resembling feeding formula. The right lung was congested. The gastrointestinal tract proximal to midjejunum was markedly enlarged with gas and ingesta and a caseous plug was present within the jejunum. The intestinal tract distal to the plug was devoid of ingesta. The spleen was diffusely congested. The right thyroid gland was larger and more congested than the left. Muscle was atrophied.

HISTORICAL DIABETES ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA FOCAL HEPATIC LIPOMA. This 12-year-old female lemur has been managed for diabetes for years and occasionally crashes. The animal had recently started self-mutilating its right arm. The animal presented acutely with hypoglycemia (glucose 20) and was treated orally and intravenously but remained drowsy. The animal died spontaneously. Gross necropsy revealed a thin animal with healing chronic wounds on the forearm and hand food in the oropharynx and trachea hemorrhage in the lungs serous fluid in the thoracic cavity and gas in the stomach. The right auricle also appeared enlarged.

MYOSITIS INTRASPECIES TRAUMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PROTEINOSIS GLOMERULOSIS COLITIS PERITONITIS. This 17-year-old female lemur had been under treatment for infection due to bite wounds. The animal’s condition dramatically deteriorated and it was found dead. At necropsy body condition was fair to poor. A wound on the left hip was present which had extensive areas of necrosis. The urinary bladder was present within an abdominal hernia.  The thoracic cavity contained a large quantity of hemorrhagic fluid. Lungs were congested and atelectatic. A large lymph node was present within the mesentery.

SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL GOUT HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATITIS. This 24-year-old male flamingo was found dead. Whole body: Emaciation Kidneys: Mild to moderate; chronic interstitial nephritis Uterus: Endometrial cyst (incidental finding) Liver: Mild; multifocal; white foci. Comments: The underlying cause of the reported clinical signs was not evident from gross examination. The gross lesions in the kidney are most suggestive of chronic interstitial nephritis which may represent an aging change. Multiple organs contained foci of suspected calcification which may be an incidental lesion or may represent an underlying chronic disease process. The white foci within the liver were very small and nonspecific. Histopathology to further characterize these gross lesions is in progress; along with fecal analysis. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAMAnatomic pathology resident Cerebrum: Focal glial nodule with neutrophilic inflammation Lungs: 1. Multifocal subpleural and parenchymal foam cell foci 2. Mild; multifocal anthracosis Liver 1. Multifocal hepatic lipidosis 2. Multifocal; centrilobular to random; acute hepatocellular degeneration and necrosis Kidney (unilateral): Severe; locally extensive; suppurative nephritis with intralesional bacteria Kidney (unilateral): Moderate; multifocal; chronic interstitial nephritis with fibrosis and multifocal glomerulosclerosis Intestine: Mild coccidiasis Uterus: Focal endometrial hemorrhagic cyst Kidney: Unilateral severe bacterial nephritis Kidney: Moderate chronic interstitial nephritis Liver: 1. Multifocal hepatic lipidosis; 2. Multifocal; moderate hepatocellular degeneration Lung: 1. Multifocal; subpleural foam cell foci; 2. Multifocal anthracosis Intestine: Mild coccidiasis Comments: This animal has several significant lesions that are difficult to relate to one another and may represent concurrent but unconnected processes. Most significantly; there is a severe bacterial nephritis in one kidney. It could not be determined whether this arose by an ascending (from the urinary tract) or hematogenous (from the blood) route. No other tissue appears affected and there is no evidence of infection in the uterus. Although this renal infection appears severe enough to have some clinical impact; there still appears to be a fair amount of unaffected renal tissue remaining. Additionally; it is difficult to correlate this lesion with the clinical history of abdominal effusion. The opposite kidney has chronic changes supportive of chronic interstitial nephritis. The liver lesion is unusual. Hepatic lipidosis is not uncommon in post-parturition ruminants; however the distribution is often more diffuse. The cause for the liver degeneration is unknown. The foam cell foci in the lung are likely incidental findings possibly related to previous parasite migration. Coccidia are identified histologically and by fecal evaluation. Coccidiasis in adult alpacas is rarely clinically significant unless present in high numbers. Special stains are in process on the liver and kidney sections to determine if bacteria are present in small numbers in the liver and to attempt identification of the bacteria in the kidney. These results will be released as an addendum report. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAM Anatomic pathology reside See previous reports Comments: Although kidney was not available for culture; the bacteria observed in kidney tissue sections were gram negative rods and could be coliforms; which were isolated in high numbers from other tissues (liver; abdominal fluid; lungs). Although cultures must be interpreted with caution due to the state of the animal at necropsy; it is possible that bacterial septicemia (bacterial infection spread through the blood) could account for the lesion in the kidney; the abdominal fluid; and the poor general state of the animal. The types of bacteria isolated from tissues in this animal are all considered commensals (normal inhabitants of body sites such as the intestinal tract and skin) or are ubiquitous in the environment. Bacterial septicemia with these types of bacteria is usually secondary to other processes such as post-partum infections; wound infections/abscess; or opportunistic spread from a local site of infection (mastitis; pneumonia; etc...). A precise pathogenesis and definitive confirmation of bacterial septicemia is not possible in this case. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAMAnatomic pathology resident

SEMINOMA MACRORHABDIOSIS EMACIATION. This 9-year-old male budgerigar has a one month history of increased respiratory rate higher than normal body weight sharp keel and a possible mass effect. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a tumor in the liver.

HEPATITIS COELOMITIS SHOCK. This 21-year-old male owl was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy clear fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA AIR SACCULITIS AND HEPATITIS. This 2-year-old male lory was found dead. There is a history of lead poisoning in the exhibit. This bird lost 10% of its body weight over 10 weeks. GONGYLONEMA GINGIVAL EMACIATION ASPIRATION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 7-year-old female saki monkey presented two months earlier with a history of nasal discharge with minimal response to supportive care. The monkey became dyspneic and apneic during anesthesia but responded to emergency treatment. Blood work revealed elevated white blood cell count and bacterial cultures grew Pseudomonas and Klebsiella. Despite treatment the monkey developed intermittent bilateral nasal discharge. A CT scan revealed complete occlusion of the maxillary and sphenoid sinuses. The monkey became apneic during attempts to intubate for nasal flush and the procedure was aborted. A tracheostomy was performed the maxillary sinuses were flushed and the monkey improved but was found dyspneic the next day. During a maxillary perforation and sinus flush procedure the animal did not recover or respond to CPR attempts. Necropsy revealed caseous material in the sphenoid sinus and pinpoint white foci in the left cranial lung lobe. The heart appeared slightly enlarged.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 28-year-old male pale-headed saki was found recumbent and barely responsive. It was hospitalized and supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead a few hours later. Necropsy revealed thin body condition orange subcutaneous and omental tissues pale kidneys enlarged spleen erythematous stomach thickened pancreas stool in the colon and three cysts on the right testicle.

EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CATARACTS RENAL FIBROSIS SUSPECT VITAMIN A DEFICIENCY. This greater than 9-year-old female frog was humanely euthanized. It had a chronic history of squamous cell carcinoma of the left rear foot (G01-3050). The animal has had recurrent masses removed surgically but borders were always dirty. The frog also had coelomic fluid accumulation and bilateral cataracts. At necropsy the animal was thin with a prominent vertebral column. Approximately 3 cc. of straw colored fluid was obtained and submitted for cytology culture and fluid evaluation. Bilaterally the lenses were opaque. There was a protruding red hemorrhagic mass present along the plantar aspect of the left rear foot. The mass was friable and bled easily. The liver was dark black.
SPLENITIS INANITION. This 1-year-old toad was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the body was thin. The GI tract was devoid of ingesta.

COLONIC ADENOCARCINOMA ENTEROCOLITIS INANITION MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 8-year-old female tamarin died. It was in thin body condition. It had uncontrollable diarrhea for approximately 3-4 weeks with progressive weight loss. It had heat seeking behavior and lethargy. It was treated with metronidazole and Baytril for 10 days with no response to therapy. At necropsy the tamarin was desiccated. There was thickening of the bowel several centimeters from the ileocecal junction including the cecum. There were fluid feces throughout. There were raised plaques near the cecum that were firm. There were enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes. There was whole body muscle atrophy.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS PERITONITIS ATYPICAL LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA. This approximately 20-year-old female monkey was found dead in its enclosure. It had no external abnormalities. At necropsy it was thin. There was gas within the upper gastrointestinal tract. There were two 1 cm. in diameter nodules attached to the serosal surface of the jejunum and cecum. The nodules were dark red on cut surface. There was scant stool within the colon.

INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA OVARIAN ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 4-year-old female chicken presented to the zoo hospital with lethargy and a distended crop. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 4 cm. mass on the serosal surface of the intestine at the duodenal/jejunal junction. Air sacs were thickened and had numerous white foci. Inspissated yolk material was present in the fibrosed mesentery.
CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS. This 3.5-year-old female ferret had a history of chronic renal failure and was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy the kidneys were pale and pitted.

RENAL GOUT RENAL MINERALIZATION INANITION. This 8-year-old female lorikeet had a history of weight loss. The bird was found dead. At necropsy minimal adipose tissue stores were noted. Visceral gout was present on the capsule of the liver.

CHRONIC ARTHRITIS CHRONIC ABOMASITIS AND ENTEROCOLITIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS WITH PAPILLARY ATROPHY IMMOBILIZATION COMPLICATIONS. This 17.5-year-old male giraffe has had chronic intermittent right fetlock/pastern problems for years following an observed injury with possible fracture of lateral P1 in 2009. The giraffe had responded well to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for short periods of time when lame and also to laser therapy applied to the leg. Recently the animal developed hyperflexion of the fetlock with instability of the joint in a dorsal/palmar direction but did not seem to be able to extend the fetlock joint even to a fully upright position. Additionally a chronic malformation and overgrowth of the hooves on that leg of gradual onset had accentuated a varus deformity across the fetlock and distal digits. Lameness continued to respond to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and laser therapy but the joint remained hyperflexed and somewhat unstable. An attempt at standing sedation for hoof trim resulted in resistance to ropes on the legs but the animal became more sedated in a short time and slumped into belly bands and shortly after that developed respiratory arrest and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed good nutritional status with moderate muscle mass and adequate body fat. A few small gaps between some of the cheek teeth were noted with associated food packing and gingival recession but no teeth were loose and wear was uniform. Incisors were heavily worn but with good alignment. Some mild chronic blunting of the caudal buccal papillae was noted. The pericardium contained less than 500 ml. of serous fluid with mild villous fibrosis over portions of the epicardium. Endocardial petechiae were noted in the left ventricle and some mild fibrosis was in the left atrioventricular valve. The pulmonic and aortic valves were irregularly thinned in some places and scarred and stretched in others. The adrenals are mildly congested. Some depressions were noted in the parenchyma of the kidneys corresponding to areas of pallor on cut surface. A small herniated diverticulum at the apex of the bladder into the region of the urachus was noted. Some fibrous tags and weak adhesions were found over the serosa of the spiral colon and mesentery and over the dorsal/cranial surface of the urinary bladder. Similar fibrosis was noted over a small portion of the caudal ruminal wall. The right front foot had freshly trimmed hooves and the lateral digits abaxial wall was underrun the axial wall and sole were fragmented and cavitated and overgrown to abut against the medial digit hoof wall. Similar but less severe changes were in the left front foot. The right front fetlock was overflexed and could not be extended even after the flexor tendons were severed. The flexor joint was markedly thickened with fibrosis and synovial fat proliferation especially dorsal over the joint. Marked irregularity fragmentation and wear was noted on the dorsal aspects of the distal metacarpal condyles where the extensor tendons extended across the joint. The articular cartilage of the actual weight-bearing aspects of the metacarpal and P1’s was slightly grooved and thinned. All four of the sesamoid bones facing the joint from the flexor tendon surface were disintegrated or fractured and covered with irregular fibrosis and synovial tissue. Similar but milder changes were in the left fetlock joint. Mild roughening of the articular surfaces was noted in a carpal joint.

PITUITARY ADENOMA BILATERAL THYROID HYPERPLASIA ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female pygmy goat had a history of lactation without pregnancy and gradual weight loss resulting in emaciation over a six month period. The animal occasionally circled to the right or left and had hyperthyroidism. Udder fluid became serous and proteinaceous over the last two months of life and the animal became weak but was still bright alert and responsive. Necropsy revealed a serous yellow mammary discharge enlarged submandibular and mesenteric lymph nodes enlarged right thyroid endocardiosis involving the left atrioventricular valve hemorrhagic mucosa in the small intestine inflamed pancreas pale renal cortices numerous follicles on both ovaries and a 1 cm. hemorrhagic mass on the ventral aspect of the brain attached to or replacing the pituitary gland.

BLOAT (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ACUTE PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE RENAL MINERALIZATION HEPATITIS. This 13-year-old female sheep had a history of acute collapse and bloat. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy lungs were frothy.

A chain of dark red nodules is present along the neck.

PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE RIGHT-SIDED HEART FAILURE CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA. This 20.5-year-old male Madagascar boa was noted to have urates and liquid feces in the cage in the morning. Necropsy revealed a wound consistent with the entrapped leg history and the wound was several days old with a purulent discharge. The rabbit was emaciated and had no fat storage. Food was in the stomach and normal feces were in the colon. An abrasion was on the nose and a tear was in the upper lip.

SEPTIC VERTEBRAL OSTEOMYELITIS WITH PATHOLOGIC FRACTURE AND DEGENERATIVE LEUKOMYELOPATHY MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NARIS RHINITIS SUPERFICIAL EPIDERMITIS EUTHANASIA. Lung: Mild to moderate diffuse pulmonary edema with multifocal pulmonary hemorrhages Colon: multifocal necrotizing ulcerative colitis Stomach: Moderate locally extensive hemorrhage. Comment(s) The cause of the clinical signs and death of this animal is not known following gross necropsy. A final report will be issued following histopathologic examination; bacterial culture and parasitiologic examination of feces. Tanit Kasantikul; DVM Sections of brain; lung; heart; liver; kidney; spleen; pancreas; stomach; ileum; large intestine; adrenal gland; bone marrow; tongue; and eye; are examined. Within the sections of brain; there are multifocal small aggregates of glial cells scattered throughout the neuropil. The meninges are mildly expanded by minimal numbers of lymphocytes. Diffusely; pulmonary alveoli are markedly expanded by numerous erythrocytes. Multifocally; there are aggregates of macrophages plus lymphocytes and plasma cells within the alveolar interstitium. Within the section of heart; there are multifocal areas of devitalization and the cardiomyocytes occasionally contain scant amount of deep basophilic granular materials (mineralization) and the cardiac myofibers are often separated and replaced by mild to moderate numbers of lymphocytes and plasma cells. There are intracytoplasmic oval to elongate pseudocysts containing numerous round to oval protozoal trachyzoites surrounded by thin clear ring. The section of liver revealed multifocal aggregates of lymphocytes and plasma cells at the portal veins. The sinusoidal spaces are expanded by moderate numbers of erythrocytes and numerous hematopoietic cells. The splenic red pulp is markedly expanded by numerous erythrocytes. The remaining lymphoid follicles contain variable degrees of karyorrhectic cellular debris at the germinal centers. The gastric mucosa is mildly disrupted and is multifocally effaced by moderate numbers of extravasated erythrocytes. Within the eye; the iris and ciliary bodies are mildly expanded by moderate numbers of lymphocytes and plasma cells and also extended to trabecular meshwork and scattered throughout the choroid. There are no other significant findings within the sections of small and large intestine; adrenal gland; bone marrow; and kidney.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONCONIOSIS CARDIOMYOPATHY GANGLIONEURITIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMAS THYROID ADENOMA. This greater than 20-year-old spoonbill had a chronic history of lameness and myopathy (possible vitamin E deficiency). The bird developed acute dyspnea following ingestion of two large fish and died en route to the hospital. Necropsy revealed good nutritional status small inactive masses on the plantar surfaces of the joints of the feet air in the subcutis of the head and neck refluxed food in the mouth congested lungs yellow/tan streaks and hemorrhages in the heart muscle thickened heart valves vascular congestion a partially digested fish in the mid esophageal region and a medium sized fish in the distal esophagus and proventriculus. The ventriculus is distended with a large amount of “bird of prey” diet. Large round masses are present at the cranial pole of both kidneys in which the renal architecture is absent. The stifle joints were swollen with eburnated surfaces. Marked periosteal proliferation was detected on the medial aspect of the distal left tibiotarsal bone (submitted for microscopy).

SEPTICEMIA BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS CAPILLARIASIS PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS. This 3-year-old female prairie chicken died. At necropsy it was thin. There was little to no ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract. The gastrointestinal tract contained blood tinged fluid throughout the mid small intestine to the large intestine. There were multifocal yellow plaques on the serosal surface of the large intestine.

NEMATODE ABSCESS (COLON) SYSTEMIC SHOCK (PROBABLE ENDOTOXEMIA). This 5-year-old female armadillo had been housed in a travel container overnight and was found dead in the morning. It had been used in an educational program the previous evening as was standard procedure for this animal. Necropsy identified a large amount of diarrhea with some blood present around the tail. The liver was dark and friable the gallbladder was moderately distended with normal appearing bile ingesta were in the stomach and hemorrhagic streaks were present along the entire surface of the pylorus. Ingesta were in the small intestine and the cecum had an abrupt focus of red/purple discoloration that extended throughout the large intestine and was associated with hemorrhage on the mucosa and diarrhea.

PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLY DROWNED. This 17-year-old female Jamaican fruit bat was found dead on the exhibit floor in a deep puddle of water. Necropsy revealed good postmortem condition and good body condition. Areas of patchy alopecia were present over the dorsal head and dorsal body. A scabbed wound was on the ventral chin. No other gross abnormalities were noted other than mottled pink/red pulmonary parenchyma.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS URATE STASIS. This 13-year-old female merganser was found lethargic and stiff in the morning with her head lying on her back and subsequently died before arrival at the veterinary hospital. Necropsy revealed thin body condition extra bone growth along the keel white mottling and nodules in the liver macerated left kidney associated with a large fluid-filled cyst and thickening of the wall of the small and large intestine with luminal attenuation.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOSARCOMA (PHARYNX) C-CELL HYPERPLASIA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 3-year-old male hedgehog was lethargic and weak. The animal has been under treatment for upper respiratory infection. The animal was humanely euthanized due to lack of response to antibiotic therapy. At necropsy a 1 cm. in diameter firm tan mass was present in the soft palate and oropharynx.

BACTERIAL PYOTHROAX RENAL COCCIDIOSIS. This 1-year/6-month-old female kangaroo was found dead. The keeper had scheduled a visual exam on the day of death due to concern over some hair loss. There was a history of severe anemia with hematocrit of 11 lethargy and periocular swelling around the right eye that spontaneously resolved. It had a recent molar extraction due to an abscess and was started on Baytril last week. Leukogram showed some signs of inflammation. Over the past two days the kangaroo developed some dermatological lesions that may have been due to trauma or bite wounds. At necropsy there were several small dermal ulcers present on the left dorsal flank region with hair surrounding the area appearing barbered. There was an abrasion just caudal to the left pectoral area on the ventrum. There was a firm subcutaneous mass that was not attached to underlying tissue and appeared fatty in texture. The mass was about 3 cm. in length 2 cm. in diameter and rounded. It was closely associated with inguinal lymph nodes. There was severe pyothorax in both pleural chambers. The caudal ventral portions of both lungs were adhered to the parietal pleura. The lungs were mottled and had several areas that felt like hard nodules within the stroma. The right lung was not as affected as the left lung. Upon cross section of the left lung there were multiple small to very large abscesses scattered throughout the parenchyma. The right lung was discolored and had exudate upon cross section but did not have visible abscesses. The airways were filled with purulent liquid and caseated debris that was easily expressed. The spleen appeared enlarged and had a sharp line of demarcation that could have been liver mortis.

SEMINOMA INTERSTITIAL CELL TUMOR PULMONARY EDEMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 11-year-old male chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. The animal had a previous history of respiratory distress and avascular necrosis of the digits. At necropsy lungs were edematous and the trachea contained small particles of food. A 5 mm. in diameter yellow mass was noted near the gall bladder in the hepatic parenchyma. Kidneys were pale and contained urates. A large mass was present adjacent to the left testicle.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 15-year-old male river otter was anesthetized for an annual examination and electroejaculation. Anesthesia had been discontinued and the animal died during recovery. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy there were white firm areas on the surface of the left ventricle. Cataracts were present in both eyes.

ACUTE TOXICOSIS INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS CYTOLOGY. This 2-year-old male tanager had a history of openmouthed breathing periodically after the enclosure was serviced. It was found at the bottom of the enclosure with its wings spread and died minutes prior to presentation. Necropsy revealed caudal displacement of the liver large heart pale spleen and kidneys unilateral dark discoloration of the testicle and pale right thyroid.

LYMPH NODE MICROGRANULOMAS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS. This 17-year-old female captive bred bighorn sheep was euthanized due to severe arthritis. It had a chronic high white blood cell count and labored breathing after mild exertion. A bony mass was seen on radiographs coming off the sternum. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and the aorta was thick. Pus was in the uterus.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA DEGENERATIVE RENAL AND CARDIAC DISEASE CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 21-year-old female squirrel monkey was found dead in its cage following a period of thin body condition and elevated renal serum chemistries. Necropsy revealed grossly normal appearing kidney lean body condition and consolidated lungs with suppurative exudate.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male rattlesnake was found dead on exhibit and had no significant medical history. Necropsy revealed adequate body condition with identifiable coelomic fat stores. Tissues were pale. Skeletal remains were in the esophagus (prey item) stomach was empty ingesta were in the lower gastrointestinal tract kidneys were markedly pale and male gonad was identified.

NEUROPIL NECROSIS PROBABLE OLD INFARCT CEREBRUM. This 25-year-old female Peruvian squirrel monkey had a history of blindness and failing health. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bilateral cataracts and a long dark streak in the caudal portion of the cerebral hemisphere. The monkey was in thin body condition.

NASAL ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male African hunting dog had a history of recent nasal bleeding with increased severity and frequency. A CT scan confirmed the presence of left-sided maxillary sinus density extending into the left frontal sinus suggesting neoplasia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed worn teeth with irritated gingiva perianal cutaneous masses a multilobular vascular mass occupying the left maxillary and frontal sinuses with near complete lysis of the associated ethmoid turbinate bones generalized decreased muscle mass abundant abdominal fat stores some intra-abdominal hemorrhage in one fat body a 0.5 cm. focus of white discoloration in the spleen a 1 cm. gallstone dark and possibly enlarged pituitary thickening of the entire length of the bowel dark red mucosal surface of the bowel and 1 cm. fluid filled cyst in the right kidney.
TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 3-year-old male wallaby was found dead in its nest box at first morning check and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed bilateral pulmonary congestion.

METASTIC UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female domestic rabbit had a one-week history of inappetence lethargy and reclusive behavior and a two-day history of labored breathing knuckling of the forelimbs and ataxia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed obesity and small round firm white nodules throughout the pulmonary parenchyma primarily on the left side and a large multilobulated mass of the uterine body. Focal firm areas were in the renal cortex.
EUTHANASIA CARCINOMA HEPATITIS. This 10-year-old male corn snake was euthanized with a history of midbody swelling.

PULMONARY SHOCK CAUSE UNDETERMINED CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS. This greater than 3-year-old male rattlesnake was coming out of torpor as usual but was very ataxic and would not eat. Euthanasia was planned but the snake was found dead. Necropsy revealed fair body condition infection involving the ventral scales and autolysis of the viscera.

BACTERIAL MENINGITIS ENCEPHALITIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 11-year-old male tamarin was found comatose but died shortly after presentation despite therapy. At necropsy the spleen was swollen and congested.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE. This 19-year-old male snow leopard was found dead in its exhibit. It had a history of chronic renal disease. Necropsy revealed good body condition atelectasis hyperemic gastric mucosa a 1 mm. mass on the mucosa of the fundic portion of the stomach two 0.5 mm. ulcerated areas in the mid duodenum two segments of yellow firm jejunal mucosa a 1 cm. mass free in the abdomen several 2 mm. calculi in the right kidney multiple cysts in the liver and bilaterally cloudy lenses.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old male lory was found dead. There had been a 10 gm. weight loss since October 2001. Necropsy revealed good body condition and a large amount of hemorrhage in the subdural region of the right caudal temporal area.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS INTESTINAL TORSION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK. This 8-year-old female kangaroo had a two week history of weight loss and poor condition. The animal was found dead. A pouch joey was present but was euthanized due to young age. At necropsy a large section of the intestine was congested and possibly torsed.

VACOULAR HEPATOPATHY POSSIBLE ENDOCRINE DISTURBANCE. This 3-year-old male prairie dog died. It had a history of obesity and periodic constipation. It had a workup under anesthesia with increased respiratory effort. It was very thin and had lost half of its body weight over one year. It was missing its front incisors. At necropsy it had very thin walled and gas distended intestines. The lungs were mottled bright red and pale pink.

ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS PERIARTICULAR FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 13-year-old male bat was found down and poorly responsive. The animal presented moribund and had an abrasion over the tarsus with exposure of the metatarsal bones. Desiccated bone ends were also present in the phalanges. Supportive care was instituted; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin and had foci of alopecia.
adult.  Euthanased.  Arthritis both elbows.  Aspiration pneumonia (cyonal).

HEPATITIS SPLENIC NECROSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 3-year-old female lorikeet was the fifth psittacine to die acutely in the same area of the zoo. All of the psittacines have shown similar but not exactly the same liver spleen and gastrointestinal tract changes grossly. Preliminary bacterial culture results of a cloacal swab revealed heavy gram negative growth. At necropsy the spleen was enlarged. The liver had a golden tinged appearance along its borders. The bird was 5-7% dehydrated. The animal was well muscled and feathered. The gastrointestinal tract was partially devoid of ingesta but a yellow tinged material was swabbed from the crop and esophagus. The abdominal fat was bright yellow.

INTERMEDIATE GRADE LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12.5-year-old male rabbit had a history of weight loss and lethargy and blood work revealed significant leukocytosis and severe lymphocytosis. All other parameters were within normal limits and lymphoma was suspected. The animal was treated with high doses of prednisolone but there was no change in blood work and the animal’s quality of life continued to deteriorate. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an old hernia of retroperitoneal fat through the diaphragm.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS HEPATITIS PNEUMONIA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 34-year-old female flamingo was found weak. A coelomic mass was identified. The animal died prior to treatment. At necropsy the bird was thin. A mass was arising from the liver with numerous adhesions to the adjacent viscera.

EUTHANASIA SPINDLE CELL SARCOMA (MUSCLE) MAMMARY ADENOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA SPLENIC HEMATOMA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATELECTASIS. This 14-year-old female wolf had a history of fibrosarcoma over the left hip. The animal’s condition was declining and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a 2 x 3 cm. lobulated mass was present in the mediastinum. Masses were also present in the spleen. The left kidney showed atrophy of the caudal pole. A mass was identified in the right kidney.

EUTHANASIA GLOMERULONEPHRITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 4-year-old ferret had a history of abnormal stool anorexia and weight loss. Renal azotemia and hyperphosphatemia were identified on serum biochemistries. The animal’s condition declined despite treatment with antimicrobial and fluid therapies. The animal was euthanized. At gross necropsy a bone of pallor was present at the corticomedullary junction of both kidneys.

SEPSIS MENINGOENCPHALITIS GASTRITIS COLITIS COLONIC FLAGELLATES EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female lizard had neurologic signs with its head turned to the right side. Radiographs revealed a possible density in the gastrointestinal tract. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed tan liver a 2 mm. firm nodule in the mesentery near the small intestine sand in the intestine corresponding to the radiographic image no evidence of obstruction and no other remarkable findings.

SEPSIS PNEUMONIA GOITER. This at least 12-year-old male Matamata had a one month history of inappetence and died. Blood work and radiographs were within normal limits although recent blood sample had not been acquired prior to death. The turtle was found deceased at the bottom of the tank. Yellow viscous and malodorous fluid was in the axillary region from which Elizabethkingia meningoseptica.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT AND SYSTEMIC MINERALIZATION. This female approximately 13-year-old black milksnake was found dead in its enclosure. This milksnake had no prior medical problems. At necropsy there was moderate to severe autolysis of the carcass. Whitish urate tophi were noted throughout all major organs including heart lung liver and kidney.

CIRRHOSIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA ATHEROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL-RENAL-PANCREATIC FIBROSIS SPLENITIS ENTERITIS. This 14-year-old female turkey had a one day history of weakness and reluctance to move but had eaten in the morning. Examination revealed depression weakness minimal response to stimulation thin body condition prominent keel palpably enlarged liver and a mass in the caudal abdomen. Radiographs revealed rocks in the ventriculus and enlarged liver with rounded borders and widened cardiac/hepatic waist. Decreased detail was in the caudal coelomic cavity. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dark yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity firm enlarged thickened mottled liver that was dark and green on cut surfaces. The ventriculus was enlarged and occupied a large portion of the caudal coelom. Several small rocks were in the ventriculus.

SEPTICEMIA. This 12-year-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy it was in thin body condition. There were fly larvae in the eyes. The heart was large (2.5 cm. long and 1.5 cm. wide). The vena cava and azygos vein also appeared enlarged. The right ventricular free wall was 1 mm. the central free wall was 5 mm. and the left ventricular free wall was 3 mm. The lung was dark red to brown and hemorrhagic bilaterally. The brain was friable. The testicles were large with red foci ventrally.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS AORTIC FIBROSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS. This 24-year-old female sea lion had a history of anorexia. The animal died despite supportive care and treatment. At necropsy mature cataracts were present in both eyes. Pale areas were noted in the skin with erosion of the epidermis. The liver was pale orange to tan and firm.

TRAUMA THYPHLITIS. This 10-year/4-month-old male gerenuk was found dead. There was a large amount of blood present at the head area. The blood seemed to be coming out of the nose and mouth. There was no history of a change in the environment or in his behavior. Recently the nights have been cooler. He had a heated barn to stay in. Postmortem blood work and urine were submitted and yielded a high calcium phosphorus and potassium. Urine was concentrated. At necropsy the gerenuk was in good body condition. There was dried blood around the nares. There was blood in the mouth. There was trauma to the right side of the face below the eye and eyelid. There is bruising to the right side of the neck below the skin surface in the muscle layer. The pancreas appeared softer than normal and friable. The heart had several white irregular nonraised plaque-like lesions throughout the serosal surface. Fecals were negative. The right testicle appeared slightly larger than the left. Brain heart kidney lung and liver were frozen for future use if needed.

MYCOTIC PNEUMONIA AIR SACCULITIS. This 3-year-old male tanager was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the body was markedly autolyzed. Postmortem trauma was identified in the skull. The caudal thoracic air sac showed evidence of air sacculitis and hemorrhage was present in the right lung.

EUTHANASIA FOLLICULOGENESIS FATTY LIVER. This female greater than 4-year-old iguana was agonal in its exhibit and was euthanized. It was gravid. It had preovulatory egg binding. No peritonitis was noted at necropsy.

SEMINOMA. This greater than 15-year-old smoky jungle frog was hospitalized for supportive care due to emaciated condition but was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and a 3 cm. pale firm yellow mass in the coelomic cavity adjacent to the pancreas. Adhesions of the mass to the gastrointestinal tract were noted.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PNEUMONIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 2-year-old male opossum had a history of hind limb lameness. The animal was found with hind limb paresis but normal pain and withdrawal reflexes. Treatment was initiated; however due to the lack of response to therapy the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the right lung was collapsed congested and sank in formalin. Liver was tan to yellow.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS SEPTICEMIA. This 5-year/6-month-old male toad was found dead in its enclosure. It was found with a lesion under its chin. It recently came out of a cool down period. It was housed with another male. At necropsy there were raised nodules on the skin. There was a 1 cm. diameter ulcerated lesion under the chin. There was an ulcerated necrotic lesion on the right inguinal region. There was necrosis of the skin distally on the toes of the rear feet. The ventricular myocardium was pale tan. The musculature was generally pale. There was moderate gas in the intestine. The liver was dark and congested. The lesion on the chin had inflammation into the muscle beneath it.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. MACRORHABDIOSIS CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS. This 2-year-old male budgerigar was found on the floor with a dirty vent and appeared to be in molt. Necropsy revealed a large dried fecal mass matted to the feathers around the cloaca a mite infestation around the cere decreased pectoral muscle mass and no other abnormalities.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 4-year-old snake was found with a broken back. At necropsy areas of thickening of the spinal column were noted. Three slugs were present in the oviduct. The liver was yellow.

BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS (MANDIBLE) EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old neutered male captive bred wallaby had a ten day history of illness and was euthanized. The bird was hospitalized for mandibular osteomyelitis of bacterial origin. It did not respond to antibiotic therapy and was euthanized following lytic fracture of the mandible. Necropsy revealed a suppurative exudate replacing much of the mandible and an enlarged heart with white streaks.

GRANULOMATOUS DERMATITIS CHRONIC STOMATITIS MUCOSAL HYPERPLASIA OSTEOMYELITIS URATES STASIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION. This 5-year-old female lizard had been under treatment for conjunctivitis. Abscessation and swelling were noted adjacent to the globe. The animal died despite treatment. At necropsy lungs were congested. Liver was pale.

CIRRHOSIS CARDIOMYOPATHY STRESS. This 5-year-old male capybara was found dead in pool during morning. The animal had been doing well. At necropsy there was foam in the trachea. The liver was mottled irregular in shape and had edges that were broken. The stomach had a small ulcer.

RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female ferret recently became inappetent but maintained a normal attitude until becoming lethargic a few days prior to death. Examination revealed renal asymmetry with the left kidney larger than the right. Blood work revealed lymphopenia and chemistry panel revealed marked elevations in blood urea nitrogen and creatinine hyperphosphatemia hypocalcemia and inverse calcium:phosphorus ratio with mild hyperglycemia and hypochloremia. Urinalysis revealed hyposthenuria acid urine and glucosuria. A sediment exam revealed a preponderance of transitional epithelial cells that had features of atypia suggesting neoplasia. Diuresis was attempted but the animal’s condition did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition worn canines moderate tartar symmetrical kidneys pale renal cortices empty urinary bladder and no other remarkable gross findings.

BACTERIAL ABSCESSES AND SEPSIS. This greater than 1-year-old male alligator lizard had a history of decreased alertness and supportive care was administered. There appeared to be some improvement over the past few days and then the animal was found dead. The species has a history of bacterial abscessation. Necropsy revealed moderate body condition fluid in the coelom a small amount of fibrinous debris on the serosal membranes empty gallbladder flaccid gallbladder wall a few white masses in the hepatic parenchyma a 7 mm. encapsulated mass in the cranial pole of the right kidney with caseous contents.

EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (HORN BASE). This 10-year-old male sheep had a squamous cell carcinoma on the right horn. The animal was humanely euthanized due to expansion of the tumor. At necropsy the ventral right horn was soft broken and scabbed. Adjacent soft tissue was expanded. The right submandibular lymph node was mottled. The ventral right horn was replaced by spongy tan soft tissue extending into the frontal sinus.
SYSTEMIC SHOCK RHINITIS TRACHEITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 5-year-old naked mole rat was found dead. At gross necropsy the lungs were diffusely dark red. The GI tract was distended with gas.

STEATITIS (PROBABLE PANCREATITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old male ring-tailed lemur had slowly progressive deterioration associated with increased renal serum chemistry values. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large fat pad with 2-4 mm. white patches on the surface in the subcutaneous tissue. The mesenteric tissue and most of the abdominal organs were speckled with 2-4 mm. white patches. The descending colon left kidney and surrounding tissue were encompassed by a 4 cm. in diameter mass that appeared to originate off of the left kidney. The attachment of the intestines at the pancreas/stomach and duodenal flexure was engulfed in apparent necrotic fat or a tumor.

EMACIATION SHOCK. This greater than 11-year-old cockatiel is one of a large group of budgerigars cockatiels and rosellas that were recently acquired for an interactive aviary. This bird was found dead in the quarantine cage at morning check. Necropsy revealed liquid gas and seeds throughout the alimentary tract absence of coronary fat thin body condition and friable lungs and kidneys.

RETICULOENDOTHELIOSIS VIRUS LYMPHOID NEOPLASIA (LIVER HEART). This 3-year-old male prairie chicken was found dead. The animal had been reticuloendotheliosis virus positive. At necropsy the animal was thin with a prominent keel. A large quantity of red tinged fluid was present in the coelom. Multiple white to pink masses were present on the liver ranging from 1-3 cm. in diameter. Similar masses were present adjacent to the duodenum.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDITIS SHOCK. This 2-year-old male fruit bat was found in the ocelot enclosure with multiple wing web lacerations and corneal trauma. The animal was treated for shock and its condition improved for three days and then was found cold wet and in shock. The animal died shortly thereafter. At necropsy three punctate ulcerations were identified in the left cornea. Multiple lacerations were present in the wing web.

TRAUMA ASPIRATION DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE PULMONARY ABSCESSES HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 15-year-old female gerenuk had a history of chronic dental disease recurrent pneumonia tarsal arthritis and hypocalcemia. Recent blood work indicated low ionized calcium and low plasma zinc levels. At necropsy there was a small amount of pericardial effusion thickening of the central leaflet of the mitral valve and multiple areas of pallor in the myocardium. Luminal papillae appeared blunted. Fibrin adhesions are present from the reticulum to the diaphragm. Extreme wear was on the dental arcades and only a few molars remain. Sludge was in the gallbladder and the liver was small. Marked hemorrhage was in the large muscle groups of the right hind limb extending into the metatarsal region and a small amount of hemorrhage is present on the caudal aspect of the tarsus of the left leg. Osteoarthritis was in the right tarsus and both hip joints. The left posterior lobe of the lung was adhered to the diaphragm caudally and to the body wall dorsally and both lungs had firm masses present in the parenchyma that contained cream-colored exudate on cut surface. The right lung was more affected than the left. Some nodules were in he cervix up to 4 mm. in diameter and extended into the lumen of the uterus.
INANITION. This 5.5-year-old female ratsnake was found dead. The animal has a history of chronic poor condition. At necropsy the central spinal column was stiff and the body was thin.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female chicken is from a collection of birds that have a history of leukosis. This animal had developed a subcutaneous mass on the wings and also in the ventral abdomen. Cytology confirmed lymphoma. Euthanasia was performed when quality of life deteriorated and the bird became dyspneic. Necropsy revealed average fat stores subcutaneous masses in the wings and ventral abdomen pale areas in the heart muscle hemorrhage in the lungs a mass adhered to the ventral spine that incorporated some of the lung esophagus and liver. The spleen was enlarged and mottled on cut surface. Petechiae were noted on the mucosa of the duodenum and proximal jejunum. A 1 cm. cyst was in the ovary. The caudal lobes of the kidney were pale.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 4-year-old female armadillo had a one-day history of lethargy and died overnight. It had a chronic history of hypocalcemia heart murmur seizure-like activity and at necropsy was in thin body condition with erythematous skin on the nose. Many teeth were missing and abrasions were on the pelvic toes. In the thoracic cavity there were 5 ml. of fluid and 5 ml. of tan foamy fluid was in the abdomen. The stomach was empty but felt thickened. Feces were in the cecum and colon. Urine was in the urinary bladder. The brain was gelatinous/liquefied.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MAST CELL TUMOR (LIP) FIBROMA (LIVER). This 11-year-old male capybara was anesthetized for examination of a corneal ulcer and lip mass. Anesthetic recovery was prolonged. Abdominal distention was noted the following day related to a gas filled viscus. Cardiopulmonary arrest ensued. At necropsy the cecum was dilated with gas. A firm white mass was present adjacent to the pancreatic duct. Smaller white masses were present in the liver.

PANCREATITIS GASTROENTERITIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA SEPSIS. This 4-year-old male prairie dog had a history of diarrhea weight loss inappetence hematochezia melena hematemesis and death. Necropsy identified bloody nasal discharge blood in the pulmonary parenchyma copious abdominal fat blood in the esophagus and stomach pale tan liver that floated in formalin white plaques on the pancreas and melena in the intestine.

BACTERIAL ABSCESSES WITH SEPSIS (PROBABLE BRUCELLOSIS) GOUT EMACIATION. This 2-year-old frog has a history of ongoing health problems and treated in the past for weight loss and inappetence. Examination revealed lethargy abnormal coloration and weight loss and is from a collection with a history of brucellosis and intestinal nematodiasis. Supportive care was administered and the animal appeared to respond but later died. Necropsy revealed a small amount of dark red fluid in the coelom some pale yellow nodules scattered over the renal surface extending into the parenchyma.
adult. Weight: 72000.0 g.  Euthanasia; chronic hindleg stiffness. Arthritis; chronic; suspect; right hip; right stifle. Obesity.

STRESS DEHYDRATION. This approximately 1-year-old timber rattlesnake was brought to the zoo as a juvenile last fall. It had eaten several times before being put into brumation. The animal had just finished the warming up process when it was found limp in the enclosure. The animal was moribund at examination and died two hours later. Necropsy revealed some weight loss absence of adipose stores in the coelomic cavity and no other gross abnormalities.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA BACTEREMIA ESOPHAGEAL STRICTURE. This 2-year-old wallaby was found dead. The animal has a history of esophageal stricture which was treated by feeding a soft diet. At necropsy the animal was thin with little internal fat identified. The esophagus had a localized area of swelling and internal stricture which effaced approximately 80% of the dorsal lumen. Ingesta was present near the stricture and contained a mixture of food and grit.

SALPINGITIS BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS URATE STASIS INANITION. This 6-year-old female rattlesnake presented with distention of the abdomen. A necrotic ovum was expressed from the cloaca. Treatment was initiated however the animal later died. At necropsy necrotic ova were present in the ova duct.

SLIGHTLY THIN WITH NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female Jamaican fruit bat presented with a one week history of staying on the ground.
