Possible right elbow arthritis was noted radiographically. The bat was treated with supportive care and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for possible soft tissue injury or arthritis for one week. The bat’s weight improved but it was still unable to hang or climb although it was able to fly. The bat was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed fair body condition a possibly enlarged liver and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHROSIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This greater than 10-year-old male duck was humanely euthanized due to disequilibrium and emaciation. This duck was found in dorsal recumbency unable to right itself on exhibit. It was found to be emaciated when examined. Additional heat was provided overnight. Blood collected at exam revealed moderately elevated white blood cell count. The barn has a history of mycobacteriosis. Radiographs demonstrated stiff severe arthritis hepatomegaly and renal enlargement. At necropsy the duck was emaciated without any fat reserves present. The pectoral and epaxial muscles were severely wasted. There were heavy bumble lesions present along all digits and central pad. No ingesta was present in the gastrointestinal tract. There were few stones in the ventriculus with heavy bile staining. The liver was twice as large as expected. The kidneys were mildly enlarged. The testes were reduced in size. The spleen could not be found. The right stifle joint was entirely collapsed and had heavy osteophyte proliferation laterally. Sections of liver and small intestine were frozen for future use if needed.

CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA OR STRESS. This 18.5-year-old male hyacinth macaw presented with weakness and labored breathing shortly after having its nails trimmed. A moderate amount of blood was found on the floor of the enclosure and emergency supportive care was initiated. The bird arrested and could not be resuscitated. Blood drawn after death revealed a packed cell volume of 26%. Necropsy revealed a prominent keel moderate pectoral musculature development blood present on both feet a 2 cm. irregularly shaped cystic structure containing yellow fluid in the left caudal coelom attached to the coelomic wall pale liver with a darkened region on the margin of the right hepatic lobe and no other remarkable findings.

INANITION ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 11-year-old male ibex was found recumbent and reluctant to stand. The animal had been anesthetized for a hoof trim two days previously. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy scant fat depots were noted. Moderate enteritis was noted.

COELOMIC ADENOCARCINOMA COELOMITIS PNEUMONIA CUTANEOUS XANTHOMATOSIS. This 5-year/4-month-old male junglefowl was found dead. It had no previous medical history. The keepers did note that the animal was not as aggressive or as visible as was usual. At necropsy the bird was in fair body condition with prominent keel. The feathers were of good quality. There was green discoloration in the cranial two-thirds of pectoral musculature extending into the musculature as focal areas of dark discoloration. There were small multiple petechia present under the skin along the area of discoloration. There was a moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid in the coelomic cavity. There was a dark brown to yellow fibrinous sheet present along the ventral aspect of the coelom just underneath the coelomic musculature and attached to the underlying organ structures. There was a 7 x 4 cm. mass present in the cranial dorsal aspect of the coelomic cavity. The mass attached at the cranial aspect of the ventral liver and on its dorsal aspect to the cranial pole of the left kidney and on its ventral aspect to the gastrointestinal tract. The mass was soft necrotic and varied in color from purple red black to yellow. On cut surface the mass was variably tan to dark red soft and had a nodular appearance. The liver was dark red and slightly enlarged. The regions of intestine overlying the coelomic mass appeared inflamed and were distended with gastrointestinal contents. There was a fibrinous covering present over the caudal ventral surface of both lung lobes. Both lobes were dark red and mottled. The gonads could not be identified.

BACTERIAL GASTROENTERITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This approximately 8-month-old boa was captive born and had been in quarantine for a month and reportedly had been a “bad eater” but ate on 4/27 and soaked on 4/29 possibly defecating. It was fine until the end of the day when it was found dead. Necropsy revealed slight distention near the cloaca a 2 mm. white soft plaque adjacent to the lung food in the large intestine fecal matter at the distal end of the large intestine gravid oviduct and no other remarkable findings.

ABDOMINAL HEMORRHAGE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 9-year-old female sugar glider was restrained for a nail trim and suffered cardiopulmonary arrest. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy the abdomen contained frank blood. Several masses were noted in the liver.

SCLEROSING PERITONITIS DUODENAL PERFORATION. This greater than 9-year-old male wallaby was found dead at morning check and reportedly was clinically normal the previous day. Necropsy revealed thin body condition absence of muscling over the spine and limbs absence of cavitary fat 50 ml. of hemorrhagic fluid in the abdominal cavity fibrin tags over the intestinal serosa missing upper incisors on the right upper arcade mildly enlarged and contracted spleen old tail amputation reactive and mildly enlarged lymph nodes a 2 cm. linear perforation of the duodenum numerous fibrinonecrotic zones adjacent to the perforation fluid and food material in the stomach and adhesions of the liver to the duodenal laceration on the diaphragmatic aspects of the hepatic lobes.

SHOCK RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 5-year-old female warthog had a history of intermittent seizures of undetermined cause. There have been no signs of illness or excessive seizure activity reported recently. The animal had been examined on December 14th and was determined to be pregnant. The animal was found dead in its den box on January 3rd. The body was warm due to a heat lamp in the den box. Necropsy revealed blood around a tusk from the oral cavity on the right side. Marked subcutaneous bruising and hemorrhage was present on the midline of the sternum and congestion and hemorrhage were present on the mammary chain. Marked bilateral axillary deep muscle hemorrhage was noted and synovial fluid was hemorrhagic. Deep muscle of the thighs and hind limbs also had evidence of hemorrhage. In the abdominal cavity there were 30-40 ml. of frank blood. The liver was markedly autolyzed. The spleen was small and lymph nodes were difficult to locate. Small dark foci were present on the mucosal surface of the stomach possibly representing ulcers. Kidneys were congested with increased congestion at the corticomedullary junction. The mucosal surface of the uterus was congested and five developing fetuses were noted. An erythematous ring was present around the umbilicus of each fetus. Thick foamy bloody fluid was in the nasal sinus the mucosal lining of the trachea was dark green with a thin layer of foamy mucus on the surface and 30-40 ml. of frank blood was in the right hemithorax. The lungs were markedly congested but floated in formalin. The meninges were congested and spinal fluid had a hemorrhagic appearance.
HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 14-year-old female whistling duck was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant lesions were noted at necropsy.

EMACIATION PANCREATIC FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS COLONIC MINERALIZATION IRON STORAGE DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male rock hyrax had a history of chronic weight loss and presented in agonal condition. Radiographs revealed severe pleural effusion and serosanguineous fluid was obtained by thoracocentesis. Severe pitting edema was in the hind limbs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified severely congested lungs that partially sank in formalin and the lungs had a rough rim of deep red tissue around the perimeter. The larger airways oozed broth on cut surface. Abundant ingesta were in the stomach and digesta was in the caeca. The liver had a cobblestone surface texture but normal parenchyma on cut surface. Mesenteric lymph nodes were thickened and enlarged. The pancreas was small with normal texture.

EUTHANASIA GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 27-year-old flamingo had a history of chronic pneumonia and had been under treatment however the animals condition continued to decline. Subcutaneous emphysema developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a mass was present adherent to the keel and ribs. Small yellow masses were present on the pericardium and throughout the lung. Similar foci were identified in the liver and spleen.

ENCEPHALITIS AND NEURITIS POSITIVE WEST NILE VIRUS SEROLOGY EUTHANASIA. This approximately 4-year-old crocodile monitor presented with acute whole body paresis on 10/15/03. The lizard had spent part of the 2003 summer outdoors and had been moved inside for the cold season a short while before presenting with clinical signs. West Nile virus serology revealed a negative antibody titer before the onset of clinical signs and a strongly positive titer after the onset of clinical signs. A presumptive diagnosis of West Nile virus encephalomyelitis was made. The lizard was treated with supportive care and slowly improved neurologically primarily in the caudal half of the body. Concurrent stomatitis unresponsive to antimicrobials developed (G04-0490). The lizard could not properly prehend and consume food but showed some interest. The forelimbs were fixed in a caudal position with the dorsal aspect of the front feet in contact with the ground. This led to secondary contracture and freezing up of the joint capsules in the shoulder. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed ulcers on the dorsal aspects of both carpi mild muscle atrophy of both forelimbs absence of claws on the digits #3 and 4 of the left forelimb and an absence of the claw on digit #4 of the right forelimb. Fat stores appeared adequate. A 2 cm. diameter tan object was found adhered to the mesentery in the caudal coelom and not associated with any organs. The oral mucosa was erythematous and several teeth were missing loose or exfoliated easily.

TRAUMA. This 5-year-old female African lion was attacked by male conspecifics and killed while on exhibit. Necropsy revealed puncture wounds on either side of the trachea at the level of the glottis subdermal bruising in this region fractured hyoid bones and crushed trachea. Multiple follicles in various stages of development were noted in the ovary. Claw marks were noted in the hindquarters and bruising was present in the medial musculature of the right rear leg.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 14.5-year-old doe had a history of chronic arthritis and hoof abnormalities. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy pale streaks were noted in the myocardium.

BENIGN LIPOMA OF ABDOMINAL FAT EUTHANASIA. This approximately 3-year and 11-month-old female Virginia opossum was euthanized for chronic arthritis and progressive rear limb instability. Gross necropsy revealed a small red mass in the abdominal fat.

XANTHOMATOSIS CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS DEGENERATIVE HEPATOPATHY EMACIATION. This 11-year-old female gecko has a history of severe weight loss despite voracious appetite. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation a focus of white discoloration in the skin and subcutis on the left proximal arm a 4 cm. white granular mass caudal to the heart and cranial to the liver and a small but similar mass caudal to the liver.

EUTHANASIA YOLK COELOMITIS SHOCK. This 5-year-old female chicken developed a cloacal prolapse. A crushed egg was palpable in the caudal coelomic cavity and a large quantity of clear viscous fluid was aspirated from the coelom. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was yellow mottled and friable. The coelomic cavity contained a large quantity of fluid and necrotic yolk material was present adherent to the coelomic surfaces. A large cystic mass was present in the coelomic cavity.

EUTHANASIA ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA. This 4-year-old male hedgehog presented with an ulcerated mandibular swelling. Cytology was suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a firm white to tan mass was present infiltrating the right mandible and extending into the right maxilla.

LYMPHOMA. This approximately 9-year-old female snake was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed empty stomach normal feces in the colon inspissated material with hemorrhage and liquefaction in the large intestine and oviduct edematous and blotchy lung with mucoid frothy or clear fluid in the lumen hemorrhage liquefaction and some inspissated masses in the ovaries with associated adhesions.

ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS PYELONEPHRITIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 13-year-old male fruit bat presented with a degloving injury of the mandible and an open fracture of #3 digit on the left wing. The digit was amputated and the chin injury was repaired. The bat did well for a day but then became lethargic and died. No significant lesions were noted at necropsy.

No diagnostic lesions. Comments: The ultimate cause of death in this frog was undetermined. There was no evidence of infectious; marked inflammatory; or neoplastic disease noted within the examined tissue sections. Karla Fenton DVM; MS; PhD Liver: 1. Adenocarcinoma 2. Marked multifocal pyogranulomatous hepatitis with increased melanomacrophages Spleen: 1. Adenocarcinoma 2. Marked multifocal pyogranulomatous splenitis with increased melanomacrophages Kidney: Marked membranous glomerulopathy with glomerular sclerosis and pigmentary nephrosis Skin: Marked multifocal pyogranulomatous dermatitis Lung: Moderate multifocal pyogranulomatous pneumonia Heart: Moderate pyogranulomatous pericarditis Ovary: Moderate multifocal pyogranulomatous oophoritis Comments: The histopathologic findings are consistent with a highly invasive adenocarcinoma of the liver; spleen; and likely of the celomic cavity (based on the clinical history). Scattered throughout many organs including; the liver; spleen; skin; lung; pericardium; and ovaries were mulitfocal pyogranulomas. There was no evidence of an infectious agent noted on routine H&E stains; however; specials stains to aid in highlighting potential infectious agents is in progress. Karla Fenton DVM; MS; PhD Acid Fast: Negative Comments: The special stain failed to identify any infectious agents within the examined tissue sections. If fresh frozen tissues were saved; a macerated tissue culture maybe warranted. Please refer to the previous report comments for additional information. Karla Fenton DVM; MS; PhD

CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE. This 8-year-old female ibis was found dead in a planter on the rubber roof of the TF building. At necropsy the feathers beak and feet were in good condition. The keel was palpable. There was some hemorrhage present in the brain. Sections of brain and kidney were frozen for West Nile virus testing.

TRAUMA SARCOCYSTIS OR BESNOITIA MESENTERIC CESTODIASIS. This 1-year-old New England cottontail rabbit had been housed at the zoo one week after being trapped in the wild to augment captive breeding efforts. The rabbit was found dead in its cage with major degloving wounds along the lateral and dorsal body. The cage divider was disturbed and entrapment overnight was suspected. Necropsy revealed good body and postmortem condition and a 5 cm. full-thickness wound present on the left cervical region. The skin was degloved over the lateral and dorsal body beginning from the midlumbar region and extending over the lateral surface of the hind limbs. Normal ingesta was in the gastrointestinal tract and several mesenteric parasitic cysts were present. All other systems were within normal limits.

EUTHANASIA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA THYMOMA THYMIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYCOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS RUMENITIS MYOCARDIAL SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 16-year-old female sheep was euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy fat depots in the thoracic inlet were discolored yellow and were chalky. The heart was discolored brown and streaked with white. Kidneys were firm and had hard calculi in the pelvis. A large abscess was present in one kidney. Round masses up to 6 cm. in diameter were present anterior to the kidney.

THYROID CARCINOMA MELANOMA EUTHANASIA. This 41-year-old male Mexican beaded lizard had a four month history of progressive weight loss and inappetence with inactivity. Blood work and radiographs were unremarkable. The animal’s body condition continued to deteriorate and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 2 cm. beige focus on the surface and within the parenchyma of one hepatic lobe. A 2 cm. spherical mass was adjacent to the trachea and thoracic inlet that had friable luminal contents. Multiple nodular crunchy masses were present throughout the pulmonary parenchyma and a moderate amount of semimoist feces was in the colon.

BACTERIAL PLACENTITIS. This 4-year-old female squirrel monkey was pregnant and due to give birth. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a large fully developed female fetus was present in the uterus. A second placenta and short umbilical cord were also identified within the uterus attached to a small firm dark brown tissue mass presumed to represent in utero death of fraternal twin. The skull of the fetus appeared to be too large to fit through the pelvic canal of the dam.

RENAL AND HEPATIC CARCINOMAS PITUITARY NODULAR HYPERPLASIA METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA TO BRAIN. This 14-year-old male Pueblan milksnake died and necropsy revealed irregular kidneys and liver with yellow areas that had poor demarcation of the internal hepatic structures.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male hedgehog had a several month history of swollen eyelid enlarged lymph nodes that did not respond to supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME WHITE MATTER VACUOLIZATION. This 5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy fat depots were markedly reduced. Several teeth were loose. Kidneys were mottled with white plaques.
LYMPHOMA AND LYMPHOID LEUKEMIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This greater than 2-year-old Norway rat died. Necropsy revealed a markedly enlarged spleen mottled liver and atelectatic lung.

EUTHANASIA INTERVERTEBRAL DISK DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) NEPHRITIS RENAL CALCULI SHOCK. This 18-year-old male lion had a history of intervertebral disk disease which has been slowly progressive. Marked hind limb paresis and paralysis developed. The animal was anesthetized. Lumbar spinal spondylosis and kyphosis were noted. Narrowing of disk spaces from L1 thru L6 was identified radiographically. Despite steroid therapy the animal remained pruritic in the hind limbs and was humanely euthanized due to grave prognosis. The animal also has a history of repeated seropositivity for FIV. At necropsy kyphosis was noted over the lumbar spine. The right renal pelvis contained several calculi and a white mass was present in the right renal cortex.

POSTANESTHETIC DEATH COMMISSURE STOMATITIS AND GLOSSITIS WITH INTRALESIONAL BACTERIA AND FUNGI. This 23-year-old male hyacinth macaw had a one month history of lesions in the corners of the mouth. The bird had been treated with antibiotics but the lesions did not resolve. The bird was anesthetized for further workup and biopsy of the lesions but died during recovery from anesthesia. Gross necropsy revealed swelling and crusting of the soft tissues of the corners of the mouth and inside the mouth and crusting on the lateral aspects of the tongue possible dehydration hemorrhage in the right lung related to intracardiac injection during attempted resuscitation an irregular whitish appearance to the surface of the heart congestion of a 15 cm. segment of the intestine and congestion of meninges on the dorsal brain.

ECTOPIC EGG YOLK COELOMITIS HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female Java hen had a five-month history of coelomic distention of unknown origin with no other clinical signs. Recently the keeper reported lethargy and inappetence with increased respiratory effort and straining to defecate. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition some ingesta in the proximal trachea a 1-2 cm. in diameter round dark gray mass within the coelom with some fibrinous attachments to the serosal surface of the oviduct ingesta in the crop mottled orange/yellow liver and a 10 cm. yellow laminated mass in the lumen of the oviduct.

CHRONIC CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE CARDIAC FIBROSIS BRONCHIECTASIS TESTICULAR ATROPHY. This 8-year-old cheetah had a history of dyspnea and radiographs revealed pleural effusion and 1.5 liters of fluid were drained from the thoracic cavity. The fluid was chylous. Additional diagnostic examination revealed a mass in the stomach and endoscopy revealed that the mass was an accumulation of sand and plant matter. The animal developed additional thoracic fluid and 500 ml. of straw-colored fluid was drawn from the thoracic cavity. After the anesthetic event the animal was still dyspneic and still agitated and died in respiratory distress. Necropsy revealed abdominal distention some bruising over the right saphenous vein and right thorax ventral thoracic petechiae a liter of straw-colored fluid in the thoracic cavity moderate fibrin deposition on pleural and diaphragmatic surfaces serosanguineous foam in the trachea and main stem bronchi grossly consolidated lungs that were mottled dark red and tan and dark red hemorrhagic fluid and foam were on the cut surface of the pulmonary parenchyma. Mild valvular endocardiosis was noted in the left and right atrioventricular valves. A large amount of intra-abdominal fat was observed. A fresh fracture of the right mandibular canine had exposed pulp. Mild erosions were on the mucosal surface of the stomach. The liver had moderately rounded edges. The spleen was small but of normal contour. Moderate erythema was noted on the mucosal surface of the duodenum and jejunum. The ileum and cecum were filled with clay-like fecal material and had dry mucosal surfaces. The colon had hard fecal material and dry mucosal surface. The kidneys had a moderate number of small irregular depressions on the surfaces.

VERTEBRAL HEMANGIOSARCOMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female California kingsnake has a history of a firm swelling on the cranial dorsal region with associated osteolysis of spine and ribs. Scent glands are swollen. The animal is otherwise in good body condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed “carpet-like” lesions in the cornea a firm mass surrounded by a blood filled soft tissue on the dorsal spine a hard mass at the midbody ventral spine a 3x4 cm. mass distending the cranial pole of the kidney and multiple eggs in the shell gland some of which were inspissated.

EDEMA AND GLIAL CELL NECROSIS OF MIDBRAIN LOW-GRADE SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female goat had a four-month history of weight loss elevated renal parameters and a two-day history of recumbency that partially responded to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large amount of fat around the heart grayish liver and slightly small kidneys.

STRESS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS AMYLOIDOSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 18-year-old female black-necked swan had a one day history of lethargy and was found dead in the water approximately 10 minutes after a keeper observed the bird in the water with its mate and apparently not in distress. Necropsy revealed no external abnormalities white translucent fluid in the coelomic cavity wet lungs friable liver multiple foci of discoloration in the liver active ovaries three undeveloped eggs and multiple fat stores.

TRAUMA RENAL TUBULAR MINERALIZATION AND NEPHROLITHIASIS. This 8-month-old female naked mole rat was accidentally closed in the door of the mole rat room because it was on the floor. Necropsy revealed good body condition and good postmortem condition. A moderate amount of blood was from the nostrils. A large clot of blood extended the length of the trachea. Severe hemorrhage was present from the caudal half of the skull to the area between the scapulae and a clot of blood was present in the scapular region superficial to the muscle.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY WITH ADHESIONS STRESS CATARACTS HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMAS CHOLELITHIASIS DISSECTING ANEURYSM EUTHANASIA. This 47-year-old female gorilla collapsed suddenly on exhibit soon after the keeper staff observed the animal acting and moving normally. The animal was transported to the hospital but never regained consciousness. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal had been found face down in sternal recumbency with no response to tactile or audible stimulation and had a stable respiratory rate and heart rate with murmur but otherwise was nonresponsive. This gorilla has a history of partial nephrectomy constipation substantial lumbar and coxofemoral arthritis and lipomas. There is also a recent history of right forearm and right mammary bite wounds associated with conspecific aggression. Necropsy revealed slightly overweight body condition palpable lipomas worn teeth (especially the incisors) and recent bite wounds in the right forearm and right mammary gland that had healed with no swelling. Both hips had reduced range of motion. Abundant subcutaneous and cavitary fat stores were noted. Lungs were congested. The left atrioventricular and aortic valve valves were fibrotic. The left cranial and caudal hepatic lobes were greatly enlarged and infiltrated with tan friable tissue and loose aggregates that efface normal hepatic tissue. Smaller aggregates were identified in other lobes on cut surface. Multiple white to yellow stones of variable size were in the gallbladder. The right kidney was hypertrophied (compensatory for partial left nephrectomy) and adhesions or fibrosis were present in the area of the remnant left kidney colon and uterine horn. The left renal remnant was small and thickened. The uterus was thickened and enlarged with a small lumen on cut surface but with homogeneous features in the uterine wall. The right ovary was small but firm with few cystic structures. The left ovary was not identified due to adhesions. The right mammary gland was enlarged firm and contained aggregates of tan firm tissues with scattered areas of hemorrhage throughout the gland. The left mammary gland was small and normal on cut surface. Dark speckling was in the gastric mucosa. Multiple joint mice of variable size were removed from the coxofemoral joints and the articular surfaces of these joints were eroded. The intact head was donated to the Burke Museum.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA THERMAL BURN CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female squirrel monkey had a one-week history of lethargy and head pressing and had some burn wounds. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed three burn wounds on the left hip left shoulder and armpit right shoulder and back some mild petechiation of the gastric mucosa minimal feces worn teeth and moderate dental calculi.

ISLET CELL TUMOR DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old male rat presented with acute respiratory distress and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. It had no prior clinical abnormalities. Necropsy revealed obesity dark red and consolidated lungs and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA SPINDLE CELL SARCOMA (RIB) HISTIOCYTIC LYMPHADENITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 10-year-old spayed female rabbit has a history of chronic weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy spondylosis was noted in the lumbar spine. Firm raised tan to white nodules were present on the ribs.

1. Pharynx: Severe necrotizing pharyngitis with peripharyngeal abscess formation and associated lymphadenitis 2. Lung: Severe focally extensive bilateral bronchopneumonia 3. Adrenal: Enlarged adrenal medulla - pending histologic evaluation Comment The gross findings indicated severe pharyngitis and bronchopneumonia. Such pharyngeal lesions are most commonly associated with trauma from foreign objects. The pattern of findings suggested extension of infection from the pharynx to the lung by inhalation. Bacterial cultures on both pharynx and lung are underway; suspected agents include Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes and Fusobacterium necrophorum infection. Qualitative fecal culture has also been submitted for screening. Results of ancillary tests and complete histologic examination will be included in the final report. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Patholog Pharynx: Severe regionally extensive chronic pharyngeal/peripharyngeal abscess Lymph node: Severe chronic granulating and granulomatous lymphadenitis with multifocal necrosis/suppuration Lung: Severe multifocal aspiration pneumonia Adrenal gland: Multifocal cortical hyperplasia Severe chronic pharyngitis and peripharyngeal abscess formation with associated lymphadenitis and severe secondary aspiration pneumonia Comment The gross and histologic findings indicated severe pharyngeal inflammation with abscess formation; regional lymphadenitis; and aspiration pneumonia. Bacterial cultures indicated Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes as the primary infectious agent with the other isolates being likely secondary contaminants. Focal trauma likely contributed to development of the pharyngeal lesion which progressed to aspiration pneumonia. Bacterial culture of the lung is pending and those results will be released in an addendum report. Intestinal parasitism appeared incidental in this case; but evaluation of the antihelminthic regiment may be warranted and ongoing parasitism may herald antihelminthic resistance. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology) Isolation of Trueperella (Arcanobacterium) pyogenes from the lung further supported extension of infection from the pharyngeal lesion to the lung. The other isolated agents may represent contaminants; although some; such as Pasteurella species; may also have contributed to pulmonary pathology. This report concludes diagnostic testing in this case; tissues will be held for at least three weeks from the day of necropsy should further investigation be desired. Please refer to the final necropsy report for diagnosis and complete case comments. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology)

BACTERIAL PODODERMATITIS WITH SEPSIS RENAL GOUT. This 8-year-old male gecko was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed absence of digits #4-5 from the front left leg and abnormal conformation of the fourth digit of the right front leg (thinner) compared to the surrounding digits. Mottled white kidneys were noted and female reproductive tract was identified.

PULMONARY ASPERGILLOSIS. This 7-year-old female sun bittern was unwilling to stand was examined at which point it started openmouthed breathing. At examination it had two lipomas palpated along the ventrum and the animal became apneic and died. At necropsy there were plaques along the thoracic and cranial aspect of the coelomic cavity. There were granulomas around the right kidney. The oviduct was slightly enlarged and two lipomas were evident.

AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 23-year-old male Chilean flamingo was found moribund in the exhibit pool. The animal was hypothermic and hypoglycemia and was wet. The bird did not stand or eat overnight feces were matted around the vent and the patient died the following day while in a sling. Necropsy revealed necrotic edematous breast muscle and food and gruel were in the crop esophagus and gizzard. The left lung had areas congestion but was mostly normal. A moderate amount of pericardial fluid was present. The pericardium had some uric acid deposits and the heart valves were moderately thickened. The liver was enlarged and slightly pale. Severe renomegaly and pale tan discoloration was noted. The spleen was enlarged pale and appeared to be necrotic.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE LEIOMYOMA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 20-year-old female ibex was euthanized due to obstipation and respiratory difficulties. At necropsy large fat stores were noted. The left lung was consolidated and sank in formalin. An 8 cm. in diameter mass was present in the uterus adjacent to the bladder.

INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA WITH MESENTERIC AND LYMPH NODE METASTASIS. This 12-year-old female jaguar had an intestinal resection of a large mass previously diagnosed as an adenocarcinoma. Exploratory surgery revealed metastatic disease to lymph nodes and gastrointestinal tract and the animal was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed small white nodules in the pulmonary parenchyma a large mesenteric mass enlarged adrenals several large mesenteric lymph nodes pale liver polycystic left ovary with cyst in proximal horn large single cyst in right ovary several small nodules in the mucosa of the duodenum jejunum colon and rectum and annular thickening in the jejunum.

BACTERIAL/MYCOTIC PODODERMATITIS AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 26-year-old male flamingo was found depressed received supportive care but died within a few minutes. Necropsy revealed blood in the lungs a dark liver conical thick-walled heart mottled tan kidneys and pododermatitis.
INANITION CHRONIC ENTERITIS CHRONIC OMASITIS. This 10-year-old female eland was found dead. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the abdomen. Serous atrophy of fat was noted.

\_Morphologic diagnosis Hyperplasia of the Thyroid gland(suspect) (Cause of death undetermined) Comment The cause of death in this bird was not determined on gross examination. The lesion observed in the thyroid gland may be attributable to the exposure of the bird to the anesthesia. The lesion on the skull is a common finding of post mortem changes in the bird. Benjamin Adu-Addai; DVM \_ Body as a whole: Moderate congestion \_ No significant lesions Comment: The congestion noted histologically is a non-specific lesion; and likely associated with agonal changes in blood pressure. A specific cause of death or any significant pre-existing diseases could not be identified grossly or histologically. This concludes testing in this cas

CARDIOMYOPATHY ARTERIOSCLEROSIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE INANITION STOMATITIS GLOSSITIS STRESS. This captive bred approximately 5-year-old female marmoset died. It had lost weight since its arrival to the zoo in 1998. It had a history of inactivity. The tongue and gingiva were covered with white fungus that cultured positive for Candida on 10/29/01. It did not respond to nystatin. At necropsy the liver was brown/white with multifocal spots (0.5 mm.) on the surface on cut section. The edges were blunt. There was no fat in any body cavity. There were formed feces in the colon.

FACIAL CELLULITIS WITH SEPSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS IRON STORAGE NEPHRITIS COLITIS. This 4-year-old female squirrel monkey was apparently and was found comatose at midday and died shortly thereafter. The animal is housed in an outdoor exhibit with five other apparently healthy squirrel monkeys. She received an MGA implant last year and appeared to have gained a significant amount of weight in the last six months. Necropsy revealed obesity prominent thyroids large thymus and possible left ventricular hypertrophy.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENDOGENOUS LIPID PNEUMONIA. This 2-year-old female opossum was euthanized. At necropsy small foci of possible abscessation were noted in the lung. The uterine body contained a large quantity of purulent material. Small yellow nodules were present within the uterus.

YOLK COELOMITIS SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 7-year-old falcon historically lays 2-3 eggs per month and was due for an egg laying cycle. She was found on the nest with lethargy received supportive care but died a few hours after presentation. Necropsy revealed a grossly distended coelom good feather condition excessive adipose stores a large amount of yolk and fibrin in the coelomic cavity with associated adhesions to the viscera and normal appearing ovary.

EMACIATION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS CHRONIC ABOMASITIS AND RUMINORETICULITIS. This 3.5-year-old female addra gazelle had a history of endoparasitism and was treated accordingly. The animal was recently attacked by a male and sustained gore wounds to the right cervical and pectoral areas. The animal had continued to have high strongyle egg counts had a 3-month-old calf and appeared a bit thin with marked anemia. The animal was isolated for supportive care and was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed mildly overgrown hooves healed gore wound possible reduced bone density in the ribs mild serosanguineous and abdominal effusion congested lungs serous atrophy of fat numerous small mucosal defects were in the abomasum but no evidence of ulceration or petechiae and no nematodes were seen. The kidneys were markedly pale and several tortuous or thrombosed vessels were present along the uterine body.

RENAL GOUT COELOMITIS ENTERITIS. This 37-year-old male eagle had a history of panophthalmitis which was resistant to treatment. Enucleation was performed and the bird did well for several months. Weight loss and declining activity were noted and examination revealed renal failure. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy large dark calculi were present in the coelomic cavity.

ACUTE AND CHRONIC HEMORRHAGE MULTIPLE TISSUES ATHEROSCLEROSIS HYPERTENSION. This approximately 30-year-old male Chilean flamingo was found dead in holding in the morning. No previous abnormalities were noted. There has been a history of intermittent pools of blood found on the exhibit for approximately six months and the source and bird are unknown. The bird of this report had an annual exam and West Nile vaccination on 3/21. West Nile virus vaccine was administered in the left pectoral muscle. At that time the packed cell volume was 46%. Necropsy of the bird revealed a 12 cm. mass in the left pectoral muscle and skin and the mass had several cavities filled with clotted blood some more organized than others. A moderate amount of clotted blood was also in the left side of the thorax surrounding the heart and great vessels extending towards the clavicular air sac. A small amount of blood was in the left lung. Fresh food was in the crop and stomach and the liver and pancreas had generalized pallor.
adult. Weight: 950 g.  Neck haemorrhages; suspect rodenticide poisoning.

ARTERIOSCLEROSIS RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male Barbados sheep had a history of weight loss and had been unthrifty. It had persistent hypocalcemia hypomagnesemia and hyperphosphatemia. It had unresolving ataxia in the hind limbs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition some scaling of the skin diffuse reddening of the intestine small kidneys and scarce cavitary fat stores.

INTESTINAL AND COLONIC PERFORATIONS CHRONIC PERITONITIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE SYSTEMIC MINERALIZATION. This 17-year-old female gorilla had a purulent perineal discharge daily during the fall of 1999. This decreased in frequency and disappeared over the following 6-8 weeks. Weight loss was then retrospectively observed over the next two months. The animal had a 2-year-old infant that is largely weaned but still bonded. Multiple biopsies of intra-abdominal masses were detected to be bacterial abscesses and the source could not be identified from these biopsies. The animal subsequently developed Yersinia associated diarrhea and hypokalemia. Contrast studies revealed a urinary bladder leak and possible colonic leakage. Surgical intervention repaired the urinary tract problem but no gastrointestinal involvement was detected. Despite supportive therapy hypokalemia worsened and the animal developed abdominal signs again. The gorilla succumbed while sleeping. Detailed necropsy findings are included in the record.

CUTANEOUS VASCULITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male goat had a history of chronic dermatitis that had recently flared again and did not respond to various forms of treatment. Lesions consisted of alopecia and crusts. Underlying skin was pigmented. The goat was in poor body condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a full rumen and no other remarkable gross findings.

DEGENERATIVE RENAL AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 4-year-old marmoset had a tooth excised two weeks earlier. The animal became depressed and lethargic while on exhibit. Three more teeth were removed the animal became dehydrated with weight loss received supportive care but died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed periodontal disease dehydration decreased muscle mass pale lungs stool in the distal gut active ovaries bilaterally enlarged and white kidneys with slightly granular texture and enlarged pelvic spaces on cut surface. Tissues in general were pale and blood was thin.

ULCERATIVE ESOPHAGITIS EMACIATION SEPSIS. This 6-year-old male chameleon was noted to have lethargy and presented in agonal condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed black distal gastrointestinal tract and thin body condition.

PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS HEPATIC AND CEREBRAL MICROGRANULOMAS. This approximately 1-year-old male lory is from a flock with a history of salmonellosis and proventricular nematodiasis. This individual was treated for and recovered from salmonellosis and was admitted to the hospital for observation and treatment due to lethargy and minor dyspnea. It died the following day. Necropsy revealed good body condition nectar in the crop black material in the stomach two areas of gastric mucosa with nests of worms attached yellow liver pale spleen and kidneys small bruise on external surface of the calvarium and a 3 mm. dark streak on the ventral surface of the heart. Bacterial culture is pending.

VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS CERVICAL HEMORRHAGE (VENIPUNCTURE HEMATOMA). This 15-year-old male Inca tern was caught for annual examination and vaccination and developed a large hematoma at the site of the right jugular vein then weakened received supportive care but arrested and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed reduced internal fat stores large hematoma on the side of the neck slightly reddened intestines and no other abnormalities.

RUNGAL RHINITIS AND STOMATITIS CYSTIC UROLITHIASIS CHRONIC RENAL DIEEASE COELOMITIS. This greater than 2-year-old male tree frog was found dead. It had a previous history of cystotomy for a urinary bladder stone. It was also recently treated for strongyloidiasis. At necropsy the frog appeared thin. The skin was pale. There was a very large urolith in the bladder. The bladder wall appeared distended.

RUMINAL FISTULA WITH PERITONITIS. This approximately 13-year-old female kudu had a history of chronic weight loss with soft watery feces in the months leading up to death. Initial fecal examinations revealed high levels of coccidia. Supportive care was administered with no improvement. The animal was found acutely lethargic progressing to sternal recumbency. Supportive care was administered with initial improvement in attitude but the animal was later found dead. Blood work at the time revealed marked hypoglycemia. Necropsy revealed poor body condition purulent material in the subcutis of the caudal abdominal region overlying the abdominal musculature a fistula between the right lateral rumen and the body wall with purulent fluid in the tract. Multiple encapsulated abscesses were present in the regions of the tracts. Adhesions were present throughout the abdominal cavity. Numerous foci of erythema and ulceration were present on the mucosal surface of the cecum. A fluid-filled lumen was noted in the uterus and the fluid was serous with flocculent material. A fistula was present between the uterus and the urinary bladder. A mass was in the region of the left adrenal gland and the gland was significantly larger than the right adrenal gland. Three bands of thickened fibrous adhesions were present between the caudal and left lateral pericardial sac and body wall. A large region of ulceration was also present on the dorsal oral cavity exposing the hard palate. A fractured tooth was noted and the remainder of the dentition was in fair condition.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA WITH ATYPIA. This 16-year-old male tiger had a history of chronic renal failure of two years duration and a neuropathy in the rear limbs. The tiger recently had become inappetent not wanting to drink and had lethargy for at least two days. The animal was anesthetized for treatment and diagnostic procedures and arrested during recovery. Resuscitation was not successful. Necropsy revealed adequate adipose stores pinpoint mineralization in all pulmonary lobes arteriosclerosis in the great vessels erosions and hemorrhage along the rugae of the stomach and frank blood in the stomach and small amounts of blood intermittently encountered in the duodenum and jejunum. The heart had some apparent infarcts and flabbiness in the right ventricle. The kidneys had pale grainy cortices and a few subcapsular cysts were present in both kidneys. Infarction was in both kidneys and both kidneys were swollen and globoid. The spleen was mineralized.

INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA INANITION SEPTICEMIA. This approximately 19-year-old male milk snake was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy the carcass was dehydrated. There was a hemorrhagic ulcer in the small intestine.

AORTIC ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 37-year-old male two-toed sloth was found dead in the water of its exhibit on March 21 2011. The animal exhibited no clinical signs prior to death. Gross necropsy revealed poor body condition pulmonary congestion froth in the trachea bronchi and bronchioles a pale heart an irregular aortic intima yellow fluid in the thorax gastric bezoar and several foreign bodies in the stomach mottled kidneys and an impacted left scent gland.

RENAL GOUT AND TUBULAR NECROSIS KIDNEY. This greater than 8-year-old leiothrix was in a free flight exhibit and was found dead. Necropsy revealed a dark friable and possibly fractured liver pale granular kidneys and no other abnormalities.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS OF STIFLE EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female duck presented for shuffling bilateral lameness and possible poor hock flexibility three weeks prior to euthanasia. Radiographs revealed severe osteoarthritis of the stifles. Necropsy revealed thin body condition “knotty” stifles and hocks and luxated healed digital joints. The left stifle joint was submitted for culture. The right stifle joint was submitted for histopathology.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE PYOMETRA. This 6-year-old female meerkat was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed bloated abdominal cavity filled with frothy serous fluid congested and infarcted lungs and a few small raised white foci in the liver.

LEG AMPUTATION AMYLOIDOSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS (KETOPROFEN). This 4-year-old Speke’s gazelle broke its leg in early September and repair was attempted with external fixation but the distal leg had poor blood supply and became necrotic. The leg was amputated at mid femur the animal recovered uneventfully and stood on the afternoon of the surgery. The animal was recovering very well receiving supportive care. The herd was treated for strongyle infection and this animal had the heaviest worm burden. Low level coccidian infection was also noted. This animal became lethargic two days after being treated for parasitism was not passing feces and lost its appetite. Supportive care was administered but the animal died overnight. Necropsy revealed thin body condition ventral edema between the front legs healed amputation site tan muscle at the suture site (attributed to cautery) edematous and hyperemic abomasal mucosa hemorrhage in the mucosa of the distal cecum and frank blood in the caecal contents. One nematode was noted in the caecal contents.

TRAUMATIC DERMATITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS PANCREATIC ACINAR CELL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old black tree monitor had a history of weight loss and inappetence and would not eat on its own. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an ulcerative lesion on the right side of the dorsolateral thorax and a similar ulcerative lesion on the left side. The liver was yellow. An 8 mm. in diameter pale nodular lesion was in the pancreas that on cut surface was soft and friable and white foci were found multifocally in the caudal aspect of the intestinal tract.

OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female chicken had one episode of diarrhea and the condition resolved when the bird was treated with a wormer. One month later the bird developed lethargy and radiographs revealed a fluid-filled coelom. Aspiration yielded much yellow thick fluid. Supportive care was administered but the bird’s condition declined and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed yellow fluid in the coelom thickened intestines and white foci in the coelom on surfaces of all organs.
INANITION BACTERIAL GLOSSITIS AND ESOPHAGITIS. This 10-year/11-month-old male merganser died. At necropsy it was thin with no body fat. The liver was large and congested.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS LISTERIOSIS. This 17-year-old male golden lion tamarin had a one day history of ataxia and head tremors. The animal could not grasp with its hands or feet became minimally responsive improved with supportive care throughout the day but continued with neurologic deficits that included scratching at its face and mouth with its hands. The tamarin was noted to have consumed large amounts of pothos leaves when placed in a new exhibit. Treatment was continued throughout the night but the animal subsequently died. Necropsy revealed multiple white spots in the liver pale lumpy kidneys with large cystic cavitations on cut surface and some white viscous material in the stomach. Hepatic culture identified Listeria monocytogenes and Enterococcus sp.

ENTERITIS. This approximately 4-month-old female captive bred rattlesnake died. It was eating and defecating well. It was shedding well. At necropsy there was no food in the gastrointestinal tract. There was a mass palpable from the outside that was approximately 16.5 cm. distal to the head. It appeared to be a clear fluid filled structure (gall bladder). The entire coelomic cavity contained a significant amount of clear watery fluid (ascites-like). The kidneys were pale.

PANCREATIC ACINAR CELL ADENOCARCINOMA SMALL CELL LYMPHOMA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 8.5-year-old female domestic ferret had a history of multiple medical problems including adrenal disease a deslorelin implant insulinoma managed with prednisolone and diazoxide. The ferret gradually lost all hair and muscle mass and was difficult to manage the hypoglycemia. The ferret’s activity level was declining. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe muscle wasting a large amount of coelomic adipose tissue thin haircoat and easily epilated hair enlarged right ventricle a few white to tan nodules in multiple hepatic lobes enlarged spleen a 3 cm. irregular and round mass with a cavitated center in the right lobe of the pancreas that was mottled red and white. The right adrenal gland had a 1 cm. cystic mass. A 0.5 cm. mass was embedded in the adipose tissue of the mesentery separate from other organs and located in the right cranial quadrant.

BACTERIAL PYELONEPHRITIS TRAUMA. This 4-year-old female wallaroo was found dead. A small joey was in the pouch and was euthanized for humane purposes. Prior to death the wallaroo had been observed that morning apparently behaving normally. Necropsy revealed abundant body fat petechiation in the epaxial muscles congested lungs petechiae in the heart and pericardial fluid slightly enlarged left kidney and blood at the cloaca.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC COELOMITIS SALPINGITIS OOPHORITIS INANITION GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This 12-year-old corn snake was euthanized under anesthesia due to a nonresectable coelomic cavity mass. At necropsy all tissues were pale. A fibrinous mass was adherent to the muscle wall and small intestine.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS LOBAR GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 14-year-old female red kangaroo underwent routine physical examination and cataracts were noted. During recovery she developed cardiac arrest and resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed multiple adhesions congestion and little normal lung tissue in the right lung fields. The upper left premolar was loose and points were on the furthest molar on the left side. Teeth on the right side were normal. No adipose stores were noted.

SEPSIS UROLITHIASIS. This greater than 1-year-old female waxy tree frog was found dead in its enclosure. This tree frog had a recent history of recurring urolithiasis and treatments with manually administered baking soda enemas as well as soaking were administered. Analysis of the uroliths revealed ammonium acid urate. At necropsy the bladder had three large irregular square-like uroliths which appeared to be embedded within an irritated mucosa.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 4-year-old male meerkat had a history of marked global enlargement of all chambers of the heart with decreased ejection fraction. The animal was placed on heart medication and appeared to stabilize for months was eating and had taken medications in the morning was active normally in early afternoon and was found dead two hours later in the exhibit with no evidence of trauma. Necropsy revealed good body condition with symmetric adequate musculature healthy skin coat mild dental calculus slight increase in clear pericardial fluid enlarged heart thin left ventricular free wall a 10 mm. ovoid structure thought to be jejunal lymph node in the mesentery moderate amount of ingesta in the alimentary tract symmetrical testicles and no other abnormalities.

PNEUMONIA TRACHEITIS INANTION. This 8-year-old female snake was found with fluid at the nares and openmouthed breathing. The snake was found dead the following morning. There were no significant gross lesions found at necropsy.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS CUTANEOUS XANTHOMA (WING) CEREBRAL AND PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 35-year-old male cockatoo died spontaneously. The bird died several hours following amputation of a wing. The bird had problems with xanthomatosis and mutilation of the wing. Necropsy revealed pigmentation of the air sacs a large aorta large liver a cystic mass in the liver bilateral pulmonary congestion and pigmentation a mesenteric mass muscle necrosis and an ulcer on the tongue.

MYOPATHY DIC. This 4-year-old male addax had a history of ataxia hind limb weakness and required assistance to stand on its hind limbs for more than a short time. It is the third addax in the collection to present with neurologic disease and the first to develop paresis in the back legs. The animal did not develop the head wobble seen in the first two nor did resolution start to occur with supportive care. The animal was found dead in the evening and necropsy revealed ventral edema around the larynx a liter of yellow-tinged fluid in the peritoneal cavity 500 ml. of yellow-tinged fluid in the pleural space petechiae over the pleural surfaces congested lungs consolidated left lung foam in the airways streaking in the heart resembling infarcts arteriosclerosis in the aorta much fat in the coronary grooves digesta throughout the alimentary tract multiple erosions in the abomasum and jejunum possible glomerulonephritis and congested muscles in the rear legs with pale red coloration juxtaposed with dark gray coloration in some of the muscle bundles.

SPINAL HEMORRHAGE RENAL GOUT HISTIOCYTIC PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS. This 11-year-old female owl was emaciated anemic and had flaccid paralysis of the hind limbs. The animal died despite treatment. At necropsy mucous membranes were pale. Marked hemorrhage was present in the cervical region. The liver was friable golden color and with whitish nodules in the parenchyma. Sand was present in the distal colon and cloaca.

EUTHANASIA HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This 7-year/11-month-old female mole rat was humanely euthanized. It had a history of not doing right. It was not using its left hind leg well. There was mild muscle atrophy. The tail tip had been chewed on. At necropsy the mole rat was thin and dehydrated. There was a large amount of white to tan creamy material in the cecum. The gastrointestinal tract was filled with liquid and gas.

SCHISTOSOMIASIS. This 10-year/8-month-old male merganser died. At necropsy there was caseous material in the syrinx. The trachea had lateral flattening just proximal to the syrinx. There was a large clot in the right atrium.

ANESTHETIC DEATH HEPATIC CAPILLARIASIS CHRONIC CYSTITIS NEPHROLITHIASIS. This 14-year-old male river otter had a history of acute weight loss. Nephrolithiasis was diagnosed. The animal was taken to surgery for removal of the nephroliths and the animal died under anesthesia. At gross necropsy multiple small stones were present in the renal pelvis with dilation of the calices and ureters. Large areas of hilar atelectasis were identified. Many of the teeth were worn and there was prominent dental calculus. A firm yellow structure was present in the vertebral column. Adrenals were subjectively enlarged.

LYMPHOMA. This 1-year-old female domestic house mouse was found dead. At necropsy the animal was slightly overconditioned numerous subcutaneous masses were present throughout the body the liver was mildly enlarged and had pinpoint 2 mm. in diameter white lesions six dark red masses were present in the abdominal fat the left horn of the uterus was swollen and dark the pancreas was severely enlarged and dark red and the spleen was mildly enlarged. Small numbers of adhesions were throughout the small and large intestines.

VENTRICULAR SEPTAL DEFECT VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 2.5-year-old female agouti was found dead on exhibit in the morning. It had been previously diagnosed with a ventricular septal defect by ultrasonography. Necropsy revealed blood clots between the lobes of the liver substantially enlarged heart and a ventricular septal defect cranial and adjacent to the papillary muscle of the left ventricle and extending to the right ventricle beneath the right atrioventricular valve. The left AV valve had endocardiosis. Pulmonary edema was noted and white foam was in the tracheal lumen.

OBSTRUCTIVE BILIARY TRACT DISEASE CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS COELOMITIS RENAL GOUT. This approximately 16-year-old male pygmy falcon was clinically normal the previous day presented with labored breathing and was agonal upon arrival at the hospital. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed mucoid brown material in the duodenum normal digesta in the large intestine empty proventriculus and ventriculus enlarged and marbled liver containing several white nodules enlarged and friable pancreas and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA SPINDLE CELL SARCOMA (BODY WALL). This 20-year-old female boa had a four month history of a progressively enlarging coelomic mass. The animal was humanely euthanized due to continued weight loss and enlargement of the mass. At necropsy a large mass incorporating the ribs and invading the coelomic cavity was identified.

EUTHANSIA LYMPHOSARCOMA STRESS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL FIBROSIS. This approximately 12-year-old male otter was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed with lymphoma last year and went through a course of Adriamycin chemotherapy. The otter had been doing well until recently. At necropsy it was in thin body condition. The hips were visible. There were over 60 cc. of serous fluid in the abdomen. All lymph nodes were enlarged. The prostate measured over 6 cm. wide.

TRAUMA RENAL TREMATODIASIS. This 5-year-old female cockatiel was found on the floor of its enclosure in the morning and had no prior history of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition ant predation scant serosanguineous discharge from the nares full crop and no other abnormalities.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS ATYPICAL HISTIOCYTIC INFILTRATE LUNGS. This 13-year-old male rabbit died with no priori signs of illness. Necropsy revealed an emphysematous and consolidated right lung and consolidated left lung. No other lesions were seen.

ENDOCARDIOSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS ESOPHAGITIS. This approximately 6-year-old male turkey was found dead in wild turkey exhibit. The turkey was reported to be eating and appeared clinically normal prior to death. At necropsy there were moderate amounts of mesenteric fat. The spleen appeared spheroid and measured 5 cm. in diameter. There was a raised white focal nodule at the tracheal bifurcation (1 mm. x 1 mm.). There was moderate thickening of the mitral valve. There was also a raised firm plaque associated with the aorta at the level of the left ventricle. There were multifocal raised red plaques on the mucosal surface of the crop. The crop was moderately distended. The ventriculus was distended with gravel and dirt. The duodenum and proximal jejunum contained pasty gray/black material. A thread-like parasitic worm was found in the jejunum.

DERMATITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA SPLENITIS OOPHORITIS INANITION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 9-year-old female chicken was lethargic and inappetent. On examination the animal was emaciated. The animal died several days later. At necropsy marked muscle wasting was noted. Several masses within the dermis were noted over the body. A small fluid filled nodule was present in the esophagus. The liver was mottled and pale.

BACTERIAL PYELONEPHRITIS METABOLIC BONE DISEASE. This captive bred male greater than 1-year-old frog was one of three frogs that died acutely on 5/27. This is the only one of these three suitable for necropsy. These frogs had been maintained with dechlorinated water during their entire time at the zoo and no new husbandry changes were made prior to their death. The curator reported these frogs had been showing very mild twitching behavior over that time and that was not identified as pathologic until after their death. At necropsy the frog was in adequate nutritional condition. The kidneys were swollen and hemorrhagic. The tissues surrounding the kidneys were edematous. The bladder was mildly distended with urine. The lungs were dark and collapsed.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This greater than 7-year-old female python had been less active over the last few months possibly due to being gravid. One day prior to death this snake was reported to have wheezing and gurgling sounds. A cosmetic necropsy was performed and revealed adequate nutritional status a blood clot in the left naris purulent fluid in the trachea and main stem bronchi and red consolidated lungs with a perforated membrane on the mucosal surface. Ovaries were within normal limits and no eggs were present in the oviduct. The liver kidney splenopancreas and gastrointestinal tract had a normal gross appearance. The gastrointestinal tract was empty with the exception of large fecal balls containing an excessive amount of hair. Culture of the trachea was obtained. Tissues were frozen for viral isolation.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS. This 1-year-old lorikeet of undetermined gender was found dead with no prior signs of illness. It is one of several lorikeets in the exhibit that had been found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition no gross lesions and undetermined gender.

CNS DISEASE STEROID HEPATOPATHY. This 10-year-old male fennec fox was given a modified live canine distemper virus combination vaccine on 3/31/99 and developed conjunctivitis on 4/16/99 which had resolved by 4/22. The animal became dysphagic on 5/2 to 5/27 and had right corneal opacity. The animal eventually developed abnormal gait and behavior and died spontaneously on 7/10 despite supportive therapy. The animal had developed icterus the evening prior to death. Necropsy revealed hepatomegaly with pale friable appearance and numerous mottled white areas throughout the parenchyma renomegaly with icteric pelvises icteric urine but normal urinary bladder congested lung pale myocardium with white streaks in the left ventricle inflamed duodenal mucosa smaller than normal thyroid glands and white corneal opacity.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ANAL SAC PAPILOMA SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA EUTHANASIA. This 16.5-year-old male cheetah was euthanized after a prolonged history of renal disease. The cheetah had not been eating well for the past month. It had weight loss and decreasing appetite and was off of feed for several days prior to euthanasia. At necropsy there was evidence of loss of muscle mass that was done approximately 25 lbs. from normal weight. There was a lot of fat within the abdominal cavity. There was tartar/calculus on teeth. There were several 1-2 mm. in diameter white nodules on the surface of the lungs. The kidneys were pale yellow to white. On cut section they were fibrotic. Adrenal glands were gray in color and mushy. Pancreas had multiple cysts that contained clear fluid and measured approximately 5-10 mm. in diameter. The liver had areas of copper discoloration and the edges were somewhat rounded. The spleen had multiple white 5 mm. to 3 cm. in diameter nodules scattered throughout the parenchyma. The anal sacs were thickened and contained areas of granulation-like tissues. A complete set of almost all body organs has been sent to Dr. Linda Munson as part of the cheetah SSP protocol.

DEGENERATIVE LEUKOENCEPHALOMYELOPATHY CONSISTENT WITH WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME PASSIVE PULMONARY CONGESTION SPLENIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA. This approximately 3-year-old male hedgehog presented with ataxia characterized by dragging the rear limbs and a stiff-legged gait in the front limbs. The animal also had mites. The animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed spinal scoliosis a 1 cm. fluid-filled cyst in the liver and mites in the skin.

SHOCK BLOAT SUSPECT HEAT STRESS. This 12-year-old male lemur died. It presented morbid and was transported to the hospital and placed on oxygen. His temperature was 104.3°F. He became apneic and shortly after went into cardiac arrest. CPR was performed but the animal never recovered. At necropsy the lemur was in good body condition with considerable fat deposits. The stomach was gas filled but also contained about 200 cc. of runny ingesta. The gastric wall was dilated and the mucosa was hyperemic. The proximal duodenum appeared light purple on the serosa and mucosa. The liver was somewhat friable. Sections of heart lung liver kidney and spleen were submitted for culture. Sections of heart liver skeletal muscle lung kidney and spleen were frozen for future use if needed.

RENAL ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL GOUT. This approximately 9-year-old female milk snake died one day following exploratory surgery for lump in renal region. Exploratory surgery revealed lesions resembling gout within a kidney. Most of the kidney was surgically removed. At necropsy there were granular white lesions all along the kidneys.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ARTHRITIS STEROID HEPATOPATHY MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 31-year-old male polar bear was euthanized for humane reasons. It had been having trouble standing and walking on its rear legs. Physical examination revealed a decubital lesion on the right elbow that was nearly completely healed. There was crepitation upon palpation within the right stifle joint. The fur had been worn off of the dorsal surfaces of the rear feet as the bear has been dragging them while trying to ambulate. At necropsy the kidneys were pale. There was no defined corticomedullary junction. There was a small nodule on the spleen. The right lobes of the lung were partially atelectatic hemorrhagic and edematous. The pleural cavity contained some blood. The stomach was full of water and two mango seeds. The intestines were empty. The gall bladder was markedly distended with inspissated bile. There were scattered superficial mucosal hemorrhages on the small and large intestine. Samples of liver spleen heart and kidney were frozen for future use if needed.

SYSTEMIC HEMORRHAGE VASCULAR DEGENERATION POSSIBLE EHD OR BT. This 3-month-old female captive bred antelope had a less than one day history of illness died spontaneously and was maintained at environmental temperature a few hours prior to necropsy. The animal was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed hemorrhagic proximal duodenitis. Jejunal petechial hemorrhages were noted and the pancreas was hemorrhagic. A small amount of feces and blood was matted to the perineum. The liver felt firm. This animal’s sibling is currently doing poorly and has an elevated SDH and white blood cell count but does not show gastrointestinal tract signs. Liver biopsies are planned on the live animal.

PNEUMONIA PROBABLE DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 4-year-old male African four-toed hedgehog has been losing weight for several months. Blood work revealed elevated serum ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Blood spots were noticed on paper towels after handling for an education program one night earlier. The following morning the hedgehog was lethargic with a shaky gait and was circling. A large amount of bloody liquid presumed to be stool was present on the substrate and hemorrhagic feces were noted. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed ecchymoses on the ventral abdomen chin and right front leg tan mottled liver slightly enlarged spleen and enlarged adrenals.
PULMONARY EDEMA MILD MYOCARDITIS AND COELOMITIS. This approximately 33-year-old male American flamingo was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed dehydration and no other gross lesions.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS SHOCK. This 5-year-old female prairie dog was found dead. Significant trauma was noted on the face eye and chest. No significant gross lesions were noted at necropsy.
