BACTERIAL COLITIS OSTEOMYELITIS HEPATITIS MYOCARDITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GASTRIC MINERALIZATION. This 7-year-old cobra recently regurgitated after feeding. The animal passed a large urate concretion and a large quantity of liquid feces. A bony mass was present on the spinal column. Blood work revealed severe heterophilic leukocytosis and monocytosis with uric academia hypercalcemia and hyperphosphatemia. The animal’s condition did not improve with treatment and it was humanely euthanized. A necropsy bony masses were present on the vertebrae. A firm white mineralized mass was present on the serosal surface of the jejunum. The colon and cecum are severely distended with light brown fluid feces.

INTESTINAL LYMPHOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This captive bred 19-year-old spayed female jaguar was diagnosed ten months ago with inflammatory bowel disease and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency. One month later the animal was diagnosed with small round cell lymphoma. The animal was treated with both dietary and medical management including CCNU. Clinical signs improved but one month ago anorexia and diarrhea worsened and the animal developed ascites. The jaguar was euthanized on July 9 2014.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA OBESITY. This 5-year-old rabbit presented with respiratory signs. Bridging spondylosis and arthritis were identified. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy the animal was obese. Lungs were dark and wet.

MYCOTIC BRONCHOPNEUMONIA SEPSIS EMACIATION ATHEROSCLEROSIS EUTHANSIA. This 25-year-old female saki monkey had a tail amputation due to a bite wound two months earlier. It had developed an intermittent nasal discharge that did not respond to antibiotics three weeks ago. It has had two episodes of being knocked down and attacked by a cagemate. It has a 10-day history of being separated from its cagemate with lethargy and intermittent ataxia. It had a three-day history of lethargy ataxia weight loss and decreased appetite and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed three calcified foci in the left hepatic lobe and multiple foci of pale discoloration. Lungs were frothy and pale and the cecum was distended.

COELOMIC SARCOMA BACTERIAL VENTRICULITIS COELOMITIS. This approximately 11-year/11-month-old female mallard was found dead. It had a history of chronic right leg flaccid paralysis since November 2001. The paralysis was acute in onset. The animal responded partially to symptomatic treatment and hydrotherapy and was able to learn to ambulate with the dysfunctional limb. It had no difficulty using the leg for swimming. There was a possible mass noted on radiographic films that was suspected to be renal or other coelomic mass that impinged on nerves. Over time the animal was able to compensate sufficiently to be placed in an off exhibit holding facility. It had been losing weight but was eating well and maintaining a vigorous demeanor. At necropsy there was a large mass in the coelomic cavity that had a necrotic sac. There were organized blood clots present throughout the coelom. The mass was tightly adhered to the ventral surface of the liver and right vertebral fossa. It contained blood filled pockets on cut and exterior surface. Ovarian follicles were identified at the cranial extent of the mass. There was a large fresh blood clot loosely adhered to the ventral left portion of the mass. The mass palpated firm and rubbery. The liver was very friable. The distal colon was distended. The proventriculus contained abundant feed material. The lungs were pale and foamy. The kidneys were difficult to identify.

TRAUMA INTRAMUSCULAR HEMORRHAGE ATELECTASIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS TUBULAR MINERALIZATION. This 9-year-old mole rat was under treatment following trauma to the face and head. The animal later died. At necropsy an area of hemorrhage was noted beneath the skin over the skull. Minimal adipose tissue stores were present.

CHRONIC PYELONEPHRITIS HEPATIC TORSION EUTHANASIA. This 4.5-year-old female captive bred domestic rabbit had a history of urinary tract infections. The animal was anorectic and lab work revealed the possibility of renal failure. The animal was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed dark purple/green circular lesions on the serosal surface of the liver and a tan vascularized mass in the central lobe. The mass was attached to the liver but apparently not a part of it. Both kidneys had one or two purple circular areas 1 to 2 cm. in greatest dimension on the serosal surface. Occasional red streaks extended from the cortex to the medulla. The right kidney was mottled with brown dots over a tan surface and the right kidney had a thickened semiopaque capsule. The urinary bladder was thickened at its cranial tip. The adrenals seemed enlarged.

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR OSTEOMYELITIS ABSCESS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 3-year-old female rat presented with progressive posterior paresis and abscessation of the mandible. The animal’s condition continued to decline despite treatment and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. A large abscess was present adjacent to the right mandible. Caseous material was present in the distal urethra.

STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 20.5-year-old female tree boa had a history of listlessness and abnormal behavior in the morning and presented with bradycardia at the health center. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a dark green mottled liver and no other gross abnormalities.

COELOMIC CARCINOMA COELOMITIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE BACTERIAL VENTRICULITIS. This 14-year/1-month-old male duck died. At necropsy it had an abdominal mass of unknown origin. There was yellow plaque-like material within the thoracic cavity. The left stifle joint was swollen. There were lesions on the bill and mouth. There was a coelomitis with adhesions.

ENTERITIS GASTRITIS NEPHROPATHY. This 2-year-old ferret had a recent history of partial anorexia. The animal was found dead. At necropsy mesenteric lymph nodes appeared enlarged. The heart was round and flaccid. The duodenum contained clotted blood. The remainder of the GI tract was within normal limits. Kidneys contained uniform white streaks. One kidney contained a wedge of hemorrhage extending from the medulla to the cortex.

DENTAL DISEASE EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 7.5-year-old male African pygmy goat was standing and alert in the morning but by late morning was depressed and weak. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond developed what appeared to be partial airway obstruction and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal had a history of chronic dental disease and progressive hind limb weakness. Necropsy revealed atrophied muscles absence of subcutaneous fat stores approximately 5 ml. of straw-colored fluid in the thoracic cavity foam in the distal airways and a small amount of food in the distal airways wet congested lungs that floated in formalin serous atrophy at the base of the heart ulceration of the dental pad a wave form in the mandibular premolars and molars and worn or missing maxillary cheek teeth dry ruminal contents blunting or loss of the ruminal papillae distal distention of the abomasal outflow tract associated with a firm bolus of digesta thickened right adrenal cortex a small cyst on the serosal surface of the right thyroid urine in the urinary bladder and possibly some blood in the distal urethra. No stones were noted in the urinary tract.

GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This 11-year-old captive bred ratsnake had a history of intermittent regurgitation and inappetence of 2-3 years duration. PCR has been negative for cryptosporidiosis and Pseudomonas has been cultured from the stomach. The animal responded to antibiotics but the condition returned and radiographs revealed gastric obstruction associated with a prey item. Supportive care was administered the ingesta passed and the snake ate well thereafter but was found dead unexpectedly one week later. Necropsy revealed yellowish discoloration in the liver involuted ovarian follicles dark yellow discoloration in the fat bodies and no other gross abnormalities. A previous endoscopic biopsy of the stomach (G14-5513) revealed normal fundic mucosa.

ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old quail was unable to ambulate. Radiographs showed arthritis in the tarsi and stifles. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy decreased range of motion was noted in the tarsi and right stifle. A yellow/white nodule was present in the right lung.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL COLITIS SUSPECT SEPTICEMIA. This 9-year-old female viper was humanely euthanized. It had a history of dramatic weight loss over the last six months and refused food over the last month. Radiographs revealed severe proliferative lesions of the vertebrae at the level of the heart with some fusion and loss of flexibility. At necropsy there were no internal fat stores. There were uric acid deposits throughout the coelom.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA. This 11-year-old male agouti was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the kidneys were effaced by numerous masses some of which were cystic. A urinary calculus was present in the bladder.

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR OSTEOMYELITIS ULCERATIVE GASTROENTERITIS PERITONITIS. This captive bred 3-year/9-month-old male gazelle was humanely euthanized. This gazelle had a history of an abscess in the subcutaneous tissues of the right mandibular area as well as coronary abscess that appeared to have resulted from foot rot. The gazelle was treated but began to lose weight and became depressed. The gazelle was noted to have an ulcerative stomatitis including abscessation at the original site. At necropsy there was a severe large necrotic ulcer approximately 6 cm. in length within the right mandibular buccal and gingival mucosa. There appeared to be some mandibular involvement with softening of the bone. There were multiple severe chronic ulcerations on the mucosal surface of the rumen. Three of the ulcers had perforated to the serosa. There were serosal adhesions covering the perforations.

NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION SPINAL CORD EUTHANASIA. This approximately 3-year-old male giant eland had a gradual onset of dragging its hind toes and knuckling from time-to-time on its hind feet with a somewhat wide based stance. This condition progressed over one month’s time and then seemed to become more-or-less static. Only the hind limbs were recognized to have neurologic deficit and the animal remained alert active and ambulatory. Supportive care was administered but no improvement was noted. No improvement was noted in a treatment protocol for protozoa. The animal’s appetite decreased over time and significant atrophy of the hindquarter muscles occurred with subsequent overextension of the hocks. Gradual weight loss occurred and the eland developed a decubital sore over the right elbow and appeared to be having troubles arising from a sternal position. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized edema in the region of the hocks involving the tendon sheaths and joint but not associated with osteoarthritic changes. The animal was in thin body condition with minimal body fat and a single old fracture of a rib on the left side was noted. Both lungs had marked mineralization of the parenchyma and their caudal dorsal peripheries. The hepatic/gastric lymph nodes were enlarged.

HEPATITIS. This 1-year-old male lory was found down and lethargic. The animal was treated with fluid and placed in an oxygen incubator pending further treatment once the animal’s condition stabilized. The animal was found dead approximately one hour later. No significant gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

ENCEPHALITIS ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CALCINOSIS CIRCUMSCRIPTA. This 8-year-old male rabbit had a history of anorexia weight loss and paraparesis. The animal’s condition continued to decline with evidence of renal failure. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy pitting edema was noted in the hind limbs. A cavitated subcutaneous mass was present in the inguinal region.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL INFARCT OBESITY EUTHANASIA (CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS). This 13-year-old male raccoon presented for acute ataxia disorientation and left forefoot trauma. Historically this raccoon had a urinary obstruction resulting in perineal urethrostomy that was managed well despite chronic cystitis. Examination revealed partial amputation of the left forelimb digits #1-3 with exposed bone. Digit #4 was also damaged and would require partial amputation. Blood work revealed elevated serum ALT. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed obesity abundant subcutaneous and interrenal fat stores toenails were avulsed on digits #4-5 of the left forefoot all toenails were missing on the right forefoot and nail beds were exposed. The perineal urethrostomy site was clean and intact. The fur along the abdomen was soaked in urine. The heart and small portion of the left lung were discolored (euthanized artifact) the liver was diffusely firm and small and mesenteric lymph nodes were subjectively larger than normal.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS ABDOMINAL ADHESIONS. This 5-year-old female kangaroo was found on exhibit unable to rise one day prior to death. It was producing foul smelling liquid diarrhea. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead in the morning. A well developed if not completely weaned orphaned joey was present. Necropsy revealed necrosis of approximately 60% of the jejunum and a small amount of foul smelling peritoneal fluid.

PULMONARY EDEMA HEPATITIS SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 3-year-old lorikeet was found down in the exhibit being attacked by the cagemates. Respiratory distress was evident and the bird died before treatment could be initiated. At necropsy the liver contained multiple greenish foci within the parenchyma. The spleen was enlarged. Lungs were firm edematous and discolored brown.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA LYMPHADENITIS SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 15-year-old male warthog was found dead. The animal had been immobilized one day prior to death for treatment of dental disease. At necropsy the left lung had foci of consolidation.

INANITION INTESTINAL ULCER INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION. This approximately 18-year-old female pintail was found dead. It had a history of visual problems. At necropsy the pintail was very thin at the keel. The lower intestinal loops were greatly distended all proximal to an obstruction that was present in the colon. The obstruction consisted of some white caseous tissue-like material that was wedged in the lumen of the intestine. The duodenum had a large amount of grit/sand in it. The gastrointestinal tract appeared somewhat autolyzed. In the midcoelom attached to the serosal surfaces of adjacent small and large intestine was a greenish caseous firm gritty tissue-like mass (3 x 5 mm.). The right ventricle was enlarged thin walled and saccular. There was very little muscle mass.

TRACHEAL DYSPLASIA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA POLYCYSTIC KIDNEYS ENDOMETRIAL DYSPLASIA. This 15-year-old female Nubian ibex has a history of intermittent dyspnea of one month’s duration. Clinical signs are suggestive of upper airway obstruction. The condition acutely worsened seven days ago two days following an examination which revealed no obvious abnormalities. The animal was treated for suspected aspiration pneumonia and blood work at that time revealed azotemia. The animal became completely anorectic with worsening dyspnea. Bronchoscopy and repeat radiographs on 12/19 revealed a tracheal mass and a soft tissue mass in the cranioventral thorax. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed poor body condition a tracheal mass associated with dorsal deviation of a malformed tracheal ring consolidation of the entire cranial right lung lobe hydronephrotic right kidney multiple cysts in both kidneys and some broken incisors.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CHOLELITHIASIS. This 8.5-year-old screech owl had mature cataracts and died while anesthetized to have the cataracts emulsified. The animal had a loud arrhythmia prior to death. Necropsy revealed good body condition dark liver and possibly soft right ventricle.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 1-year-old male California sea lion has a history of inappetence and intermittent regurgitation following move to a new exhibit. The animal had a one day history of lethargy and physical examination revealed dehydration and icterus. Supportive care was administered but the sea lion died. Necropsy revealed generalized icterus enlarged pale yellow liver that floated in formalin an 8 cm. consolidated mass in the right caudal lung lobe and a 3 cm. consolidated mass in the left cranial lung lobe. The right eye had a large corneal ulcer.

ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 2-year-old female lorikeet was removed from the exhibit due to anorexia. The animal was later found dead. At necropsy feathers were missing from the dorsal cranium. Dark digesta was present in the proventriculus ventriculus and distal duodenum.

PROVENTRICULAR NRMATODIASIS PROVENTRICULITIS ENTERITIS PNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 7-year-old male lorikeet had a history of labored breathing and weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy air sacs were thickened and opaque. Digested blood was noted in the ventriculus. A small nematode was also present in the proventriculus.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PAPILLARY ADENOMA (OVARY) ENDOMETRIAL FIBROSIS. This 26-year-old female jaguar had been treated for chronic renal failure for approximately one year. Osteoarthritis was also present. Decreasing motility was noted despite increasing medications for arthritis. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy the animal was obese. Marked articular cartilage erosion and eburnation was noted over the elbows with osteophyte proliferation. Kidneys were small and pale. Multiple cysts were present in the ovaries and firm nodules were present in the uterine wall.

PULOMNARY AND PLEURAL HEMORRHAGE. This captive bred 8-year-old male reindeer was found dead in the barn. It had no recent history of problems. Radiographs of the right and left carpus were taken. Cultures of pleural fluid were performed. At necropsy the lungs were diffusely hemorrhagic. The trachea contained a large amount of blood adhered to the mucosa. The pleural cavity contained a large amount of bloody fluid. There were ample fat stores. The pericardial fluid was hemorrhagic. There was a small amount of bloody fluid in the abdominal cavity. The rumen was bloated. The liver was friable and autolytic. There were some areas of hemorrhage in the perirenal fat and capsule. The kidneys appeared pitted and autolyzed. The brain was submitted for chronic wasting disease to NVSL. Heart and kidney were submitted to Cornell for West Nile virus testing.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 10-year-old female rabbit had a history of chronic renal failure based on blood work. The rabbit was on a modified diet and was receiving subcutaneous fluids. The rabbit died unexpectedly overnight. Necropsy revealed pinpoint white nodules in the lungs white firm descending aorta small white nodules on the edge of one lobe of the liver pale and mottled kidneys and no other abnormalities.

ATRIAL HEMANGIOSARCOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA CUTANEOUS APOCRINE GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSES) EUTHANASIA. This 13.5-year-old male African hunting dog was being monitored for quality of life due to progressive hind limb paresis. The dog also had severe periodontal disease enlarged prostate chronic osteoarthritis in the coxofemoral and stifle joints bridging vertebral spondylosis multiple subcutaneous masses along the dorsum and irregularly shaped kidneys. Blood work had revealed mild azotemia and hypercalcemia. Over the past several days the animal had been unable to stand or move and was ataxic in the rear limbs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition fly strike in both pinna an 8.5 cm. raised firm nodule in the left lateral cervical region multiple 1-2 cm. firm subcutaneous masses in the dorsal thoracic area marked gingival hyperplasia dental wear and calculus over all arcades a 0.5 cm. pocket rostral to the right maxillary canine tooth filled with purulent debris markedly thickened prepuce abundant internal fat stores marked muscle atrophy in the rear legs multiple raised dark red nodules up to 1 cm. throughout the parenchyma of both lungs with diffuse pulmonary congestion a 2.5 cm. dark red mass and multiple smaller black masses on the surface of the right atrium nodular thickening of the free edge of both atrioventricular valves rounded hepatic margins and multiple tan masses extending into the parenchyma on all lobes and fibrosis on the margins of the right medial and lateral and left lateral lobes. Both kidneys had markedly irregular and multinodular appearance with cortical thinning and the distal aspect of the renal pelvis was firm. A 2 cm. pedunculated pink masses on the mucosal wall of the urinary bladder proximal to the trigone. The prostate gland was markedly enlarged.

EUTHANASIA ORAL FIBROSARCOMA. This 7-year-old female capybara was humanely euthanized due to oral tumor. It had a history of salivating blood. At necropsy there was a 4.5 cm. in diameter firm white homogeneous smooth spherical mass protruding from the right side of the oral cavity of the lower jaw just rostral to and involving the ventral aspect of the tongue and lingual frenulum. There was a 1 cm. ulceration on the surface of the mass. The left adrenal gland was approximately twice the size of the right adrenal gland.

IDIOPATHIC CHYLOTHORAX EUTHANASIA. This approximately 8-year-old female ring-tailed lemur had a four month history of chronic idiopathic chylothorax. Radiographs thoracic ultrasound and echocardiography failed to reveal a cause for the effusion. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal’s sibling died of a similar chronic pleural effusion/chylothorax. Necropsy revealed good body condition a single fibrous adhesion between the parietal and visceral pleura in the left thorax. In the left hemithorax there were 90 ml. of chylous effusion and 30 ml. in the right thorax. Moderate adipose tissue was present in the mediastinum and a single thoracic lymph node was identified but did not appear to be enlarged. The heart appeared normal in size and shape. All lung lobes were atelectatic and shrunken to barely recognizable. Edema is present on cut surface of the right lungs.

AMYLOIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male greater kudu had a history of overgrown hooves multiple lameness issues and a near fatal bout of hyperthermia. The animal had been anesthetized for hoof trim and to evaluate for lameness and towards the end of the procedure he regurgitated but recovered okay. Since then the animal has developed “snowshoes” on the front feet and is rocked back on the heels with intermittent lameness and stiffness in the hind limbs and loss of body condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed radiographic evidence of mild pedal osteitis and osteophytosis associated with the overgrown hooves but no evidence of arthritis in the distal joints and osteoarthritis in most of the remaining joints. All affected joints have irregular thinning and thickening of the cartilage surfaces with marked softening and fibrillation of the thicker cartilage areas and irregularities of the underlying bone on palpation. There is some grooving and wear almost down to subchondral bone in the shoulders and stifles and the right hock is slightly swollen. Fibrous adhesions are noted in the region of the right cranial lung to the costal surfaces. The right lung cranial to the heart is consolidated with fibrous thickening between the lobes and numerous small abscess pockets filled with light greenish to white creamy exudate. The caudal right lung and the entire left lung are otherwise congested. The heart has a few small depressed foci of fibrosis and scarring in the left ventricular myocardium. Some thickening and reddening of the scleral conjunctiva in the lateral canthus regions of both eyes is also noted. Segmental hyperemia or congestion of the small intestine and some hemorrhage on the serosal surfaces around blood vessels are noted. The rumen contains somewhat dry ingesta and there is moderate variation in villous development from the ventral sacs to the dorsal sacs with pedunculated nodules of mucosal hyperplasia. The medullary crests are normal with no evidence of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory induced necrosis. Both adrenals are congested and have bulging somewhat prominent cortices.

Kidney: Severe chronic interstitial nephritis and glomerulosclerosis (End stage kidney) Body as a whole: Severe arterio- and arterioloslerosis with mineralization and fibrinoid necrosis Liver: Capsular gout (Visceral gout) Heart: Mild multifocal myofiber mineralization Stomach: Severe laminar mucosal mineralization Heart: Myxosarcoma (presumptive) Comment: The cause of death and the multi-organ metastatic mineralization in this animal is kidney failure; a common finding in iguanas. This is a multifactorial disease; likely related to diet; hydration status; stress; and other factors. The tumor in the wall of the heart was interesting; but not likely clinically relevant.

PERITONITIS HEMORRHAGIC GASTRITIS BACTERIAL GASTRITIS SHOCK. This 8-month-old female ferret presented with acute onset of weakness. The animal was dehydrated. A soft tissue mass was identified on abdominal radiographs. Cloudy brown fluid was obtained from abdominocentesis. Exploratory laparotomy revealed perforation in the gastric wall. The animal later died. At necropsy a perforation was identified in the jejunum.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE THYROID ATROPHY POSSIBLE AMYLOIDOSIS ORAL VIRAL PAPILLOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male lion had a history of hepatoma cervical trauma chronic renal disease bilateral cataracts a tail mass and ulcerative dermatitis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an abrasion on the left lateral tarsus deep ulceration on the right tarsus proliferative tissue adhered to the lateral joint capsule in the tarsal region multiple foci of alopecia and mild erosive dermatitis over the rear limbs and scrotum a focal mass on the dorsal aspect of the tail that had a dark crust and on cut surface the mass was pigmented. The lion had a history of retinopathy and bilateral cataracts were observed at necropsy. Mild proliferation was noted on the distal humeral condyle of the right elbow. Mild proliferation was seen in the mitral valves. A 0.5 cm. raised nodule was on the lingual mucosa of the left cheek and a small proliferative mass was at the base of the tooth of the upper left first molar. A 2 cm. raised coalescing pale plaque was on the left ventrolateral tongue. Gas distention was in the stomach. Hyperemia was in the rugal folds. The small intestine had hyperemia in the mucosa. Large multiple fluid-filled cystic structures were in all hepatic lobes most of which contain serosanguineous exudate and one was pedunculated and arose from the caudal most margin. The gallbladder was distended and had a tortuous distended bile duct with a 0.5 cm. stone present in the bile duct. A 2-3 cm. cyst was in the left limb of the pancreas. Possible small enlargement of the right parathyroid gland was noted compared to the left side. The left adrenal gland was larger in shape and size than the right and had loss of corticomedullary architecture. Both renal pelvises were filled with flocculent greenish-colored material and the cortices were light tan and slightly more friable than normal. In some areas the cortex appeared thickened and the capsules were tightly adherent.

MYOCARDITIS AND VASCULITIS POSSIBLE VIRAL ETIOLOGY. This 5-year-old male/neutered captive bred reindeer had an approximately one month history of illness and died spontaneously. The animal had a history of weight loss with acute onset of depression and weakness and mild elevations in temperature and white blood cell count. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of pericardial fluid hemorrhagic abomasum and duodenum petechial hemorrhages in the skeletal and heart muscles. A malignant catarrhal fever titer is pending and a near-complete set of tissues has been frozen for future reference if needed.

EUTHANASIA DIABETES MELLITUS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS INANITION. This 8-year-old female capybara had a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus. Glucosuria and weight loss persisted despite treatment. The animal developed ataxia and ketosis and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. Several white streaks were noted in the myocardium. Several erosions were noted in the stomach. The liver was firm and nodular and contained an 8 cm. in diameter round nodule in the right lateral liver lobe. The left kidney contained a tan nodular area near the cranial pole.

ENDOCARDIOSIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION ARTERIOSCLEROSIS FAT ATROPHY BUMBLEFOOT HEPATITIS. This 20-year-old male spoonbill was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic arthritis and bumblefoot. It was not able to walk well on its legs and its feet were swollen. At necropsy the spoonbill was in fair to poor nutritional condition at time of death with minimal adipose tissue storages. There were multiple abrasions on the medial aspect of the wings. There were multiple large bumblefoot lesions on both feet. There appeared to be a pathologic fracture of the underlying phalange of the left fourth toe. Both legs were swollen with subcutaneous fluid from the stifles down to the toes. There was a large scab covering the length of the keel bone. All tissues examined had a dry tacky texture. There were multiple black foci covering the surface of both lungs. The lungs appeared congested. There was approximately 6 ml. of clear red fluid in the pericardial sac. The heart was grossly enlarged with a thickened left ventricle and dilated right ventricle. There were multiple nodules present on the left atrioventricular valve and aortic valve. There were multiple orange plaques present on the surface of the aorta. There was a large raised plaque at the proximal aorta. The liver was enlarged. The kidneys were congested. The spleen and adrenals appeared enlarged. The medial thigh muscles were pale.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HISTIOCYTIC PNEUMONITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 13-year-old male hunting dog had a history of progressive hind limb lameness. The animal was anesthetized for exam and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy lungs were edematous. The mitral valve was irregular and firm deposits were noted in the aortic valve and aortic wall.

RENAL GOUT GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS AND PNEUMONIA. This animal was found dead. The animal has been laying eggs every month for approximately 16 months. At necropsy a large quantity of fat was present in the lower abdomen. Two eggs were present in the oviducts. Liver was light tan.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS DIABETES MELLITUS. This 4-year-old male rock hyrax presented in recumbency with hypothermia. Blood work revealed severe hyperglycemia hyperkalemia elevated CK insulin and fructosamine. Glucosuria was also present. The animal was dehydrated and intravenous fluids were administered. The animal developed cardiopulmonary arrest upon recovery from immobilization and did not respond to the resuscitative attempts. This hyrax’s bloodline is distinct from those with pancreatic fibrosis previously documented in this collection. Necropsy revealed good nutritional status small lacerations from cardiac puncture in the heart (from CPR) fluid and ingesta in the stomach and no evidence of gastric outflow obstruction.

TRAUMA PYODERMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMAS. This approximately 34-year-old female spoonbill was found dead in the weather shelter with obvious external trauma. Necropsy revealed wet carcass ulcerative dermatitis on the skin particularly along the dorsum and on the inside and underside of the bill. A small yellow nodule was found on the liver. Numerous puncture wounds were on both sides of the skull and much bruising on the neck with associated neck fracture. Puncture wounds were also in the left abdomen caudal to the left wing with a small area where musculature was absent.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA OSTEOMYELITIS WITH DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male copperhead had a wound 6-7 in. caudal to the head that received supportive care but then another wound developed on the cranial third of the ventral thorax. Later an additional skin wound developed and the snake was not able to right itself. Radiographs revealed osteopathy and culture identified Pseudomonas sp. Supportive care was administered but a mass was identified in the cranial third of the body. Ultrasound revealed mass around the heart and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a yellow firm oblong mass in the liver enlarged pericardial sac thickened stomach and masses in the liver.

SEPSIS. This 1- to 2-year-old female gecko was found dead with several bite marks over its body. This animal was housed with a male and several other females and may have incurred breeding/courtship trauma. The group of geckos has a history of metabolic bone disease and poor bone density/calcium stores. Necropsy revealed adequate body condition with small fat depots. Despite the history no external skin damage or bite wounds were observed on the animal and no trauma was found over the cranium or brain. No calcium stores were detected in the endolymphatic glands. The femur seemed splintery-rubbery. Little or no ingesta was present in the gastrointestinal tract.

EUTHANASIA FEMORAL FRACTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ANESTHETIC COMPLICATION CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 18.5-year-old male tiger had a chronic history of liver and kidney disease. An attempt was made to immobilize the animal for examination and treatment; however the immobilization dart struck the femur. The femur was fractured. Euthanasia was elected due to overall poor prognosis. At necropsy there was a proximal spiral fracture of the right femur. The liver was enlarged with a thickened capsule. Kidneys were small with thinning of the cortex.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ASPERGILLOSIS INANITION. This 20-year-old female mynah was found with a fracture of the right carpus and tibiotarsus and was humanely euthanized. In addition to the fractures there were possible contusions in the right lung.

SUSPECT DROWNING HEMOSIDEROSIS. This female approximately 6.5-year-old mynah was found dead floating in the water in the Jungle River exhibit. It had no previous medical problems. At necropsy the bird was well muscled. There was no external evidence of trauma. There was mild serosanguineous discharge from the mouth. There was a small amount of serosanguineous pericardial fluid. There was mild serosanguineous fluid in the lungs on cut section. Sections of lung floated. There was mild serosanguineous fluid within the trachea. The colonic tissue was dark. The liver was grossly enlarged. The spleen was also grossly enlarged and mottled. Sections of liver heart brain lung and skeletal muscle were frozen for future use if needed. Culture of pericardial fluid and feces was performed.

CARCINOMATOSIS PROBABLE UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA. This 12-year-old female goat has a three-week history of decreased appetite and mobility dysuria in the past few days and subsequently became unable to rise bloated and died. Necropsy revealed 10 liters of straw-colored intra-abdominal fluid brown creamy fluid in the uterus multiple smooth creamy white nodules up to 3 cm. in greatest dimension covering serosal viscera some fibrinous tags throughout the abdominal cavity and multiple white nodules in the liver. Approximately 250 ml. of fluid was in the thorax.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC PANCREATITIS. This 1-year-old male hedgehog developed breathing difficulties and radiographs revealed congestion in the lungs. The animal eventually developed a loss of mobility in the rear legs. Necropsy revealed irregular kidneys mottled liver thickened lungs and irregular heart.

Lung: Severe diffuse acute hemorrhagic pneumonia Adrenal gland: Bilateral adrenal hyperplasia Skin: Moderate focally extensive alopecia Comments A definitive cause of death was not observed on gross examination. The lesions within the lung suggest a bacterial infection. The adrenal hyperplasia and alopecia suggests Cushing's syndrome; however; alopecia in guinea pigs can be a result of several disease entities including bacterial skin infection; ectoparasites; systemic salmonellosis; and vitamin C deficiency. Histopathology; bacteriology; and parasitology are pending and the results will be issued in the final report. Erin B. Howey; D Haired skin; flank: Moderate diffuse epidermal hyperkeratosis with multiple intralesional mites (consistent with Trixacaris caviae). Haired skin; prepuce: Marked diffuse epidermal hyperkeratosis; and sebaceous hyperplasia with multiple intrafollicular nematodes (consistent with Pelodera sp.). Adrenal gland: Bilateral cortical hyperplasia Stomach: Mild multifocal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate Ectoparasitism Comments The main findings are the ectoparasite infestations. Trixacaris caviae causes sarcoptic mange in guinea pigs and results in severe pruritus and; in severe cases; seizures and death. Pelodera sp. is a free living nematode that can be found in soil and damp bedding. The nematode larvae invade hair follicles resulting in pruritus and secondary bacterial infection. Infestation of both parasites; especially pelodera; suggests immunosuppression or underlying stress in this guinea pig. The adrenocortical hyperplasia also suggests increased cortisol release; consistent with stress. An underlying cause of immunosuppression was not observed. Husbandry of the animals should be evaluated to rule out external causes of stress (overcrowding; etc.). Erin B. Howey; D

HEAD TRAUMA PERIOPHTHALMITIS PERIOPTIC NEURITIS. This 4-year-old female meerkat died. It had acute injury to the left eye and suddenly became lethargic. Examination under anesthesia was performed. After the procedure the meerkat had ataxia and neurologic signs including a stiff abnormal gait and abnormal proprioception. At necropsy there was hemorrhage on the left side of the skull in the muscle. The left eye had hemorrhage. There was mild hemorrhage over the brain.

ULCERATIVE BACTERIAL COLITIS SEPTIC SALPINGITIS SEPSIS PERITONITIS URATE NEPHROPATHY LIPOFUSCINOSIS. This 6-year-old female eyelash palm pitviper had been anorectic for several months. Keepers had been force feeding the snake and performing regular soaks. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition a foul odor from the distal carcass anisocoria a moderately enlarged spleen inactive ovarian tissue caseous material in the oviducts mixed bacteria and leukocytes in cytologic specimens of the oviduct material fat bodies present a thickened intestine caseous debris in the colon and rounded kidneys with uric acid buildup.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 10-year-old male whistling duck had recently entered the collection. It was observed openmouthed breathing following each dive on the pond. Radiographs revealed a mass in the right lung and endoscopy identified granulomatous plaques and masses from which acid-fast bacteria were identified. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed numerous small tan plaques on the air sacs and serosal surfaces a few small tan nodules in the liver consolidation of the right lung by a dense granulomatous mass and similar smaller masses in the left lung.

Leukemic hemic neoplasia Comment The complete necropsy findings indicated a disseminated hemic neoplasia with blood and bone marrow involvement (leukemia). Features of the neoplastic cells were most suggestive of lymphocyte lineage; thus; leukemic lymphoma or lymphocytic leukemia. With disseminated disease; as in this case; distinguishing between these two hemic malignancies is challenging and may be unreliable and of little clinical value. The nematode organisms identified in the large intestine were most suggestive of Oxyuris sp. (pinworms). Immunohistochemical testing for lymphocyte markers is pending and those results will be released in an addendum report. Otherwise; necropsy evaluation is complete; tissues are held for at least three weeks from the date of gross necropsy should additional investigation be desired. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology)

BACTERIAL CELLULITIS AND OSTEOARTHRITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND HEPATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 18.5-year-old male Chilean flamingo had a two week history of severe inflammation in the right hock. Multiple treatments were attempted with little improvement. Necropsy revealed a swollen reddened right hock. Severe inflammation and fibrosis were noted in the joint and tendon above and below the joint and the joint space was filled with caseous material. The articular surfaces of the joint were slightly softened. The right ventricle of the heart had a noncommunicating open flap on the right side of the ventricular septum that drained towards the bottom of the ventricle. The rest of the necropsy was unremarkable.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS RENAL GOUT. This 8-year-old lizard was being treated for suspected gout and was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed an enlarged pale heart dilated vena cava fibrotic and enlarged liver limited range of motion in the stifles subcutaneous cream deposits around most joints especially in the tarsi and stifles and small and slightly pale kidneys.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male rat had a history of dyspnea received supportive care but the condition worsened and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified multiple large areas of induration in the lungs and a possibly enlarged and globoid heart.
adult.  Aspergillosis.

PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS COLITIS SEPSIS. This approximately 5-year-old Mexican tiger ratsnake was found dead on exhibit and had been partially traumatized after death by a musk turtle. Necropsy revealed white chalky deposits on the pericardium mottled myocardium hemorrhagic lungs white chalky deposits on the hepatic capsule mottled liver and necrosis and distention of the distal colon.

BOID INCLUSION BODY DISEASE BACTERIAL VERTEBRAL OSTEOMYELITIS EUTHANASIA. This captive bred 12-year-old female red-tailed boa has had mild head tremors for approximately two years and anorexia for the last two months. Radiographs showed abnormal spinal vertebrae in the midbody with three broken ribs in the same area. Ventral erythema was also present and has worsened. Buffy coat and esophageal swab from the snake were positive for inclusion body disease by PCR and the snake was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Gross necropsy revealed a thickened vertebra at the midbody with apparent instability.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION DEGENERATION OF PARS NERVOSA C-CELL TUMOR CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 26.5-year-old male California sea lion had been sedated for physical examination on 11/6 and since that time had been off exhibit in a holding pool due to inappetence and inability to administer drugs for seizure condition. The animal developed a minor recurrent penile prolapse muscle weakness with tremors in the pectoral flippers and difficulty using the rear flippers when ambulating on land or trying to get out of the pool. The animal did not respond to treatment so treatments were discontinued until the animal began having difficulty swimming openmouthed breathing and lethargy. The animal subsequently died. Necropsy revealed good body condition with adequate adipose stores and blubber mild skin abrasions on the rostral nares chin and ventral aspect of the pectoral flippers and pelvic flippers. Hematomas in areas of adipose necrosis were noted along the dorsal body wall in areas of injections. No visceral adipose tissue was observed. Both corneas had scars and a cloudy appearance and both eyes had cataracts. The caudal trachea and bronchi were filled with foam and the cranial trachea was filled with water. The lungs were wet dark purple and firm. Two 1 mm. nodules were on the mitral valve. The liver was moderately enlarged and half the hepatic lobes had rounded edges. The liver was firm and difficult to cut through the parenchyma. The coxofemoral joint/acetabulum had a rough surface with mild flattening of the femoral head.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE ERYTHROPHAGOCYTOSIS THYROID ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male cougar had a history of chronic cholangiohepatitis that was managed with medical support for 18 months with occasional waxing and waning of clinical signs. Over the last week the animal had become inappetent and lethargic without response to supportive care and with substantial weight loss. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The animal was severely anemic at the time of euthanasia. Necropsy revealed thin body condition pale mucous membranes thickened small intestine with scant thick mucoid rust-colored intestinal contents. A 3 mm. in diameter cyst was in the right kidney. A few cysts were also in the thyroid.

\_ Kidneys: Severe diffuse chronic interstitial lymphoplasmacytic nephritis with membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis; glomeruloslerosis; tubular atrophy; and proteinosis Stomach; tongue: Multifocal mild mineralization (uremic gastritis/glossitis) Intestines: Moderate bacterial overgrowth (dysbiosis) and mild erosive enteritis Adrenal gland: Mild cortical hypertrophy Pancreas: Mild exocrine nodular hyperplasia Spleen: Moderate hemosiderosis Eye: Preiridal fibrovascular membrane; Ectropion uvea Ovary; uterus: Immaturity Comment: Severe interstitial nephritis was the likely cause of death in this sea lion; leptospirosis would be a likely cause and can be ruled out by immunohistochemistry on histologic tissues (blocks L; O; or Z) or PCR on fresh or frozen tissue. The subtle mineralization seen in the tongue and stomach are compatible with renal failure and uremia. Dysbiosis and bacterial overgrowth in the intestines is likely due to anorexia. The other lesions are likely subclinical; though the ocular lesions and splenic hemosiderosis seem greater than expected in so young an animal. This animal would like be in puberty at this age; so immaturity of the reproductive tract is not unusual.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS AND ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This greater than 12-year-old male dwarf caiman had its right hind limb amputated due to extensive conspecific trauma and had been receiving antibiotic and fluid therapy. It was found dead. Necropsy revealed ecchymoses on the ventral scutes and no evidence of inflammation or infection at the surgical site.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 13-year-old male arctic wolf developed hind limb weakness or ataxia and osteoarthritis was suspected due to geriatric age and bilateral muscle wasting over the hips and lumbar spine. The animal became lethargic a few days later retreated to its den and was not seen again. The body was excavated from the den on 12/19. Necropsy revealed thin body condition calcified nodules in the lung fields thickened and meaty lungs foul smelling necrotic material in the stomach mottled and pitted kidneys oval plaques and nodules on the serosal surface extending into the parenchyma of the liver and mild to moderate arthritic changes in both tarsi.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL FRACTURE CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 10-year-old female bighorn suffered a fracture of the sacrum and neurologic deficits. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy pale streaking was noted in the left kidney. Callous formation was present over the sacral fracture.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA. This 5.5-year-old male hedgehog was diagnosed with congestive heart failure one year earlier and was receiving supportive care. Over the past few weeks the animal had become more lethargic with polydipsia and partial inappetence. The animal was anesthetized for examination and developed cardiac arrest during the procedure. Resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed icteric subcutaneous fat enlarged globoid heart mottled lungs that sank in formalin a large amount of serohemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity and a small amount of clotted blood. The liver and kidneys were pale.

BUMBLEFOOT AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION EMACIATION PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS. This 24-year-old male American flamingo had a history of trauma and bleeding from chronic bumblefoot but no recent problems. It was found dead in the pool and may have been trapped in the waterfall area and drowned. Necropsy revealed thin body condition firm tissue around the base of the heart possible necrosis or embolic foci in the upper small intestine thick pancreas and large friable tan/pink kidneys.

CHRONIC CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE CHOLECYSTITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 13-year-old female red panda has a greater than six month history of renal failure with partial recovery in July. The animal stopped eating five days ago was immobilized for evaluation and blood work indicated renal disease. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

NEPHRITIS. This 3-year-old male rat was found dead. The animal has been receiving Cosequin treatments for chronic lameness. At necropsy the lungs were congested. The right kidney was enlarged and had multifocal white foci.

Thoracic cavity: Moderate hydrothorax Lung: Diffuse; severe pulmonary edema C3: Locally extensive mucosal hyperplasia with multifocal granulomas Liver: Solid biliary adenoma Comments This animal had severe pulmonary edema and thoracic effusion. These lesions can be caused by left side heart failure; hypoproteinemia; and infection; however; they are also commonly seen in euthanized animals. The lesions found in the C3 are most likely associated with parasite infection. Samples were collected for fecal analysis as well as histopathology. The result will be included as a final report. Misa Komine DVM; PhD C3: Multifocal granulomas Liver: Bilicary cystic adenoma; Diffuse; moderate passive congestion with centrilobular fibrosis and bridging fibrosis Lung: Pulmonary congestion and edema Heart: Mild lymphocytic myocarditis Tongue: Moderate; multifocal; lymphocytic glossitis Third eyelid: Sebaceous hyperplasia; mild lymphocytic conjunctivitis Endoparasitism Comments The histological findings in the stomach (C3) are most consistent with parasitic granulomas; and Trichostrongylus spp were detected with fecal analysis. Intestinal parasite infection causes diarrhea and weight loss; resulting in hypoproteinemia. Thoracic effusion and pulmonary edema seen in this case may be associated with hypoproteinemia. Lesions seen in heart; liver and tongue are overall mild and non-specific; and are considered to be incidental findings often seen in aged animals. Misa Komine DVM; PhD

CAUDAL COELOMITIS SHOCK. This 40-year-old male hyacinth macaw was hospitalized for elevated uric acids and was being treated with subcutaneous fluids. The animal died spontaneously. At necropsy there was a small amount of blood around the vent. Kidneys were mottled dark and light purple. The thyroids were small. The meninges were erythematous.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female prairie dog had a history of small cell lymphoma diagnosed via skin biopsy in May 2013. The animal also has a history of hair loss and erythema since juvenile age. The animal was treated with prednisolone. The prairie dog had multiple self-inflicted lacerations that required surgical intervention and subsequently had been off of steroidal therapy for two months. One week prior to euthanasia the animal’s condition deteriorated and it was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition patchy alopecia with new hair growth on the dorsum a small skin excoriation swelling in the left submandibular region a soft 1 cm. mass noted in the swollen region purulent white material in the mass on cut surface multiple masses of various size throughout the hepatic parenchyma one affecting approximately half of the hepatic lobe. Multiple similar nodules were in the spleen.

HEMOCHROMATOSIS PULMONARY EDEMA AND HEMORRHAGE. This 2-year/3-month-old female lory was found dead in its enclosure. It had no premonitory clinical signs. At necropsy the liver was mottled. The spleen had a large pale area. Bilaterally there was possible hemorrhage/aspiration within the lungs.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA EMACIATION. This 6-year-old female gerenuk had appeared normal in the morning although all animals had been inside more than usual due to cold temperatures. It was found in the early afternoon dead with bloating and rigor. The animal had an intermandibular swelling that resolved with antibiotics three weeks prior to death. It had a chronic history of alopecia and hyperpigmentation of the skin presumably familial based on genealogy. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with absence of fat alopecia in patchy distribution with hyperpigmentation mostly on the neck and trunk and one lesion that was full thickness with loss of dermis and subcutis. Two focal areas of depot penicillin were present in the hindquarters. Trachea contained white frothy liquid. Lungs were darker in some areas with edema. A small amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the thoracic and abdominal cavity. Approximately 30 ml. of pericardial effusion was noted and the apex of the heart had full thickness pallor and a distorted shape. The heart was adhered to the ventral pleura. A large thrombus was present with a necrotic center. Several other smaller streaks of pallor were present on the surface of both ventricles and apparent vegetative lesions were on the mitral valves. The peritoneal surface of the diaphragm had a fine coating of fibrinous exudate also visible on the surface of the reticulum and to a lesser extent on the rumen and abomasum. All lymph nodes were melanotic and prominent. The liver seemed smaller than usual and edges were darker in color. The left kidney was smaller than the right but on cut surface no morphologic abnormalities were noted. The gastrointestinal tract was moderately autolyzed. The left adrenal was abnormal in shape and blackened. The pancreas appeared necrotic.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA PERIRENAL CYST RETINAL DEGENERATION HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA. This aged female Texas cougar is the last surviving female Texas cougar used in the Florida panther genetic restoration program. For the last 2-3 years her vision and hearing had been poor. Over the last month appetite had decreased. The cat was immobilized for examination and evaluation revealed dehydration anemia cloudy corneas hyperglobulinemia markedly elevated blood urea nitrogen creatinine and phosphorus a large irregular mass in the right cranial quadrant of the abdomen associated with the right kidney and liver and cystic kidneys. Supportive care was administered she improved slightly but then was found dead. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting adequate adipose stores dehydration fatty marrow multiple cystic structures in the spleen with luminal serosanguineous fluid and an indented focus in the middle of the splenic body. The lungs were dark red and oozed blood and foam on cut surface. The right heart was flabby and thin walled. Marked dental calculus and some mild to severe periodontal disease were noted. The liver was congested and the left middle lobe had a 4.5 cm. mass at the apex that was pale multilobulated and heterogeneous on cut surface. The left kidney was small and slightly irregular and one small cyst was present. The right kidney was associated with a large mass at the cranial pole that appeared to be originating from the right adrenal gland. The renal parenchyma was compressed. The mass was 10 cm. in dimension somewhat laminar with cysts containing either clear fluid or blood clots. The cranial portion of the mass had the embedded right adrenal gland. Parathyroids were hyperplastic and a cyst was in the right thyroid gland. The left adrenal gland had a 5 cm. nodular mass in the caudal two-thirds of the organ. Both corneas were cloudy.

SEPSIS. This 9-year-old male wolf had been missing for one day and was found dead in an adjacent pen. This animal had a seizure 10 days earlier. Necropsy revealed two bite wounds on the neck and a blood clot on the left side of the brain.

TRAUMA. This greater than 2-year-old female lory was found dead. At necropsy there was multiple bruising around the face head and neck. The lower beak was missing. There were lacerations on the face. The carpus of the right wing was fractured.

EUTHANASIA ABNORMAL DENTITION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BRONCHOPNEUMONIA INANITION ADRENAL FIBROSIS. This 4-year-old male degu has a history of ocular and nasal discharge weight loss and tachypnea. Radiographs revealed abnormal orientation of the molars with extension into the nasal passages. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. A firm white nodular mass was present in the left nasal passage associated with numerous molar roots.
AMYLOIDOSIS. This 15-year-old male swan was found dead. At necropsy bumblefoot lesions were identified on both feet. The liver was enlarged with rounded margins. The spleen was also enlarged.

DEGENERATIVE CADIAC DISEASE WITH CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA PRESUMED NEUROENDOCRINE ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS. This 18-year-old female snow leopard had an approximate four-week history of lethargy and hyporexia that became anorexia approximately 10 days before death. Four weeks prior to death examination on radiographs ultrasound and blood work was unremarkable. Following that the animal was anesthetized again and ultrasound showed evidence of pancreatitis neutrophilia with leukocytosis of 25000 mild azotemia and bacteria in the urine. The animal was immobilized several days later and had neutrophilia with leukocytosis of 35000. The animal began receiving IV medications and fluids. The animal was immobilized again several days later and the leukocytosis had decreased to 25000. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the animal was in excellent body condition. There was a small amount of blood around the oral cavity. The lungs were diffusely congested. The right side of the heart was thickened. The liver was mottled. The body of the stomach had multiple masses in the muscular layers without associated ulceration. The kidneys were subjectively small but otherwise normal. The frontal bone on the left side was thickened and the surface of the skull was bumpy in this region. There were several large masses in the submandibular region.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 20.5-year-old male red-tailed boa has a chronic history of spondylosis that did not respond to antibiotic therapy. The animal presented with flaccid paresis of the caudal third of the body a radiograph identified a spinal fracture and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed many areas of bone swelling and expansion along the length of the spine palpable laxity in the area of the spinal fracture and crepitus on flexion of the spine. On cut surface hemorrhage and roughened surfaces of bone were noted on either side of the fracture site.

GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 12-year-old fox had a several day history of inappetence. Elevations in BUN and phosphorus were noted. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized.

ASPERGILLOSIS. This 12-year-old female parrot had a history of weight loss and thin body condition received supportive care while hospitalized for four days but subsequently died. Necropsy revealed emaciation good plumage food in the crop dark pectoral muscles yellow firm caseous debris in the thoracic air sacs adhesions of the proventriculus and air sac caseous granulomas in the lung numerous plaques throughout the cranial coelom and no other abnormalities.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 8-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead and had no prior signs of illness although it may not have eaten last time the food was offered. A cosmetic necropsy was performed and the animal appeared to be in good body condition with ample fat bodies some free hemorrhage within the coelom and over organ surfaces active folliculogenesis pale yellowish liver crystalline reddened lungs and slightly enlarged kidneys.

UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA TRAUMA (CLINICAL) EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female opossum was found on the ground at opening rounds unable to use its pelvic limbs. It had no deep vein in the feet or tail bruising was present over the caudal thoracic spine region and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA METABOLIC BONE DISEASE INANITION HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY. This 4-year/4-month-old female gecko was humanely euthanized. It had a history of significant weight loss. It had been managed for irregular deposition of calcium in the chalk glands for several months without improvement. It was also noted to have broken ribs on the right side. At necropsy the chalk glands were filled with white fluid material bilaterally and were approximately 6 mm. in diameter. There were five broken ribs on the right side. All bones appeared more opaque than usual as there was less calcium. The nose was shortened.

TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE RENAL CARDIAC AND JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 12.5-year-old female slender-tailed meerkat has a history of chronic osteoarthritis and progressive right-sided paresis. The animal had several episodes in which it had fallen onto its side and was unable to right itself without assistance. The animal also had a persistent firm swelling and ovoid lytic lesion on its left rostral mandible that had been slowly progressing for three years. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition the previously mentioned swelling on the rostral aspect of the ventral mandible adequate internal fat stores enlarged heart with decreased thickness of the left ventricular wall enlargement of the left thyroid gland compared to the right enlarged and congested spleen thickened urinary bladder wall and a 3-4 mm. firm nodule adhered to the mucosa at the neck of the bladder.

ACUTE RENAL AND MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS IMMOBILIZATION COMPLICATIONS. This 8-year-old female African hunting dog had a history of septic arthritis involving the left carpus following a bite wound at a previous institution. A prostatic ligament was subsequently placed in the joint in 2007. The animal developed an opaque vaginal discharge in April 2013 that responded to antibiotic therapy. The dog presented with severe lethargy in August 2013 and had pyometra. Ovariohysterectomy was performed (G13-3446). The uterus had ruptured resulting in peritonitis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa was isolated from the uterus. The animal became inappetent following immobilization and started limping on the left front leg. This progressed over the next few weeks and did not improve with supportive care. Blood work indicated leukopenia and urinalysis showed white blood cells and bacteria. The dog developed prolonged periods of inappetence became disoriented with high stepping in the rear legs and circling behavior. The dog was immobilized the following day and became bradycardic. Supportive care was administered but the dog developed a seizure that did not respond to anticonvulsants and the dog subsequently died. Blood work at the time revealed elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine and hyposthenuria. Necropsy revealed fractured right maxillary incisor all bottom incisors worn tartar along the premolars and molars enlarged left carpus with restricted flexion and adhesion between the jejunum and previous incision site white streaking along the epicardium and pericardium enlarged papillary muscles in the left ventricular wall flaccid right ventricle atelectasis in the right pulmonary lobes and congestion along the caudal part of the left cranial pulmonary lobe hemorrhage and bile staining on the mucosal surface of the stomach and duodenum multiple white foci throughout the pancreas reddened colonic mucosa petechiae along the serosal surface of the kidneys reddened renal parenchyma and empty urinary bladder.
adult. Weight: 3764 g.  Pulmonary oedema; congestion and suspect pneumonia.  Splenitis.  Hepatomegaly.  Suspect malaria.

SUSPECT RHABODOMYOSARCOMA XANTHOMATOSIS HEPATOPATHY. This 11-year-old male gecko died. It had a six month history of progressive weight loss ataxia and anorexia. At necropsy there was a white oval firm mass (4 x 2 cm.) dorsal to the heart that extended from the heart base area to the cranial portion of the liver. It was adhered to both lungs. There were white nodules in the liver and on the serosal surface of the pericardium.

HEAD TRAUMA SYSTEMIC NONSUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION WITH NEUROTROPISM CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND PROVENTRICULITIS. This 12-year-old finch was released into the main aviary in the morning. Keepers observed the finch being chased by other birds and was later found dead floating in a pond. Necropsy revealed good body condition crush trauma to the head and no other abnormalities.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS. This 6-year-old female impala presented with ataxia which progressed to deterioration and recumbency and the animal was found dead the following day. Necropsy revealed abrasions in the skin subcutaneous hemorrhage ample fat smaller than expected liver petechiae on the spleen lymph nodes and thymus pulmonary congestion and a bezoar in the rumen containing abraded cord and several foci of entangled fibrous strands. Kidneys were mildly swollen and cortices were hemorrhagic. The right cerebellum seemed slightly asymmetrical.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 7-month-old male lory presented weak and lethargic with blood from the cloaca. The animal was treated with antibiotics but died shortly after the examination. At necropsy marked hemorrhage was present within the jejunum and colon.

HYDROCEPHALUS NEPHROSCLEROSIS POSSIBLE HYPERVISCOSITY. This 5-year-old female Gray’s monitor had a chronic intermittent history of lethargy weakness and inappetence. The animal had responded previously to supportive care. The current episode of illness persisted over one month. Blood work revealed renal disease. The animal did not respond well to therapy declined developed marked whole body rigidity and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition a small amount of retained shed on the neck and ventrum a focus of white discoloration on the ventral neck approximately 8 cm. in diameter thickening of the skin in this region prominent fat pads in the coelomic cavity slightly rounded and friable liver empty stomach and intestines small amount of fecal material in colon 12 ml. of urine a soft white chalky structure in the urinary bladder tan firm kidneys and inactive ovaries.

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE SMALL CELL LYMPHOMA ISLET CELL VACUOLAR DEGENERATION DIABETES MELLITUS. This 6.5-year-old female domestic ferret was hospitalized two months earlier for weight loss and was mildly hypoglycemic with thin body condition. Supportive care was administered but the animal began losing weight again and was hospitalized. Blood work revealed hypoglycemia and supportive care was administered. The animal’s appetite improved and it was discharged. The animal became hyperglycemic and prednisolone was slowly discontinued. The ferret remained hyperglycemic following discontinuation of the prednisolone and developed severe lethargy and inappetence of one week’s duration. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation and thin haircoat enlarged and thickened proximal limb of the pancreas irregularly shaped spleen consolidated left pulmonary lobe and intermittent reddening of the mucosa of the intestines. A fibrous peritoneal effusion was noted. The right adrenal gland was not located and the left adrenal gland was grossly normal. The left kidney was adhered to the body wall and on cut surface some white discoloration and pelvic dilatation were noted.

PAPILLARY NECROSIS VASCULAR DEGENERATION/HYPERTENSION TRANSMURAL ENTERITIS ABOMASAL ULCER CHRONIC RUMINORETICULITIS. This 12-year-old female eland has a history of chronic arthritis and has been treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The animal had recently become inappetent and depressed and stopped defecating. The animal was sedated for exam but began regurgitating flooded the airways and resuscitation was not attempted. Necropsy revealed muscle atrophy adequate fat stores enlargement of the bones of the coronary regions of the hind feet ruminal contents throughout the mouth nose pharynx larynx trachea and pulmonary parenchyma atelectasis and congestion or edema in the lungs a jet lesion above the left atrioventricular valve an old fracture of the central rib on the left side of the thorax a corresponding scar in the left pulmonary lobe fibrosis in the cortex of the kidneys a large cyst in the left thyroid and a large healed ulcer in the antrum of the abomasum.

MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY WITH PROTEIN LOSS ERYTHROPHAGOCYSTOSIS. This 27-year-old female sea lion was acting lethargic with possible abdominal pain and died two days later. Necropsy revealed severe periodontal disease mesenteric lymphadenomegaly mild pancreatitis thin walled right heart cataracts with right lenticular luxation adrenomegaly and dark colored urine.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIMYOPATHY CHRONIC AND RENAL DISEASE WOBBLY HEDEGEHOG SYNDROME NEUTROPHILIC EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female hedgehog has been ataxic and developed decreased conscious proprioception in both pelvic limbs and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The necropsy was unremarkable.

RENAL GOUT URATE STASIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION GLOMERULAR MINERALIZATION ARTERIOSCLEROSIS INTESTINAL HEMORRHAGE INANITION GRANULOMATOUS COELOMITIS. This 12-year-old female monitor had a recent history of lethargy and inappetence. The animal was found dead. At necropsy adhesions were present between the outer body wall and peritoneum. Numerous masses were present in the coelomic cavity. A large mass possibly a blood clot was present in the lower GI tract. Miliary white foci were present on the serosa of the liver. Kidneys were pale.

EUTHANASIA SUSPECT CAPRINE ARTHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS. This 12-year-old female goat was humanely euthanized due to poor condition. It had severe degenerative joint disease and caprine arthritis encephalitis (CAE). At necropsy the synovium was thickened.

INTERVERTEBRAL DISK DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS DEGENERATIVE MYELOPATHY MALIGNANT SPINAL CORD NEOPLASM OF UNCERTAIN ORIGIN THYROID C-CELL CARCINOMA. This captive bred 5-year-old male African hedgehog had a history of chronic obesity and a possible abdominal mass effect noted in January of 2011. Ear mites and bacterial otitis were noted in January of 2012. The animal had mild pelvic limb weakness noted in June that progressed and was consistent with a T3 to L3 myelopathy in August 2012. The animal was euthanized due to quality of life concerns. Gross necropsy revealed pelvic limb paresis with dragging of the limbs flaccid quills caudal to the T9-10 area overweight condition hyperpigmentation over the ventral surfaces of the metatarsal pads congestion of the right cranial pulmonary lobe gingival hyperplasia multiple enlarged lymph nodes including the mandibular retropharyngeal and cervical nodes splenic congestion enlarged seminal vesicles bright yellow adipose and possible spondylosis of vertebral bodies T6-8 and T11-12.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA PLEURAL EFFUSION. This 11.5-year-old female sheep had been down for two days and was thin. The animal had a distended abdomen. Approximately 10 liters of cloudy yellow fluid was removed from the abdomen. Cytology was suggestive of carcinoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the thorax and abdomen. Multifocal to coalescing tan/white plaques were present on the diaphragm. The liver was small firm and pale. One segment of GI tract was dark red. Moderate hydrometra was noted in the uterus.

RENAL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 7-year-old male budgerigar was euthanized for bilateral rear limb paresis weight loss lethargy and a pasty vent. Gross necropsy revealed poor body condition a scab on the proximal keel a pasted vent seed in the crop a bright blue cere and a dark yellow/brown friable mass in the cranial dorsal coelomic cavity along the midline.

AMYLOIDOSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS PANCREATIC NECROSIS. This 20-year/4-month-old male flamingo was found dead in pool. At necropsy the flamingo was in good body condition. The right lung was yellow to tan and somewhat firmer than normal. The heart appeared large. The right ventricular free wall was 1 mm. the left was 10 mm. and the central free wall was 7 mm.

EUTHANASIA EMACIATION. This 3-month-old Mexican lance-headed rattlesnake of undetermined sex received fluids which was a normal procedure to enhance hydration. Shortly thereafter the animal had loss of righting reflex segmentally in the body and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Prior to euthanasia the animal attempted to regurgitate prey. No lesions were identified at necropsy.

METASTATIC MELANOMA BACTERIAL COELOMITIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS CATARACT. This 20-year-old female python had a history of chronic illness reproductive tract problems intermittent inappetence and dehydration. The python died and necropsy revealed a suture line over the ovariohysterectomy site dysecdysis thin body condition distended caudal coelom fibrinous material throughout the coelom and on surfaces of the viscera black lung that floated in formalin a cyst at the juncture of the ventricle and atria some possible lymphonodular hyperplasia in the fascia at midbody thickened gallbladder and a hard linear tan structure to 4 cm. in length near the stomach resembling a walled off abscess.

CHRONIC ABOMASITIS RUMENITIS AND ENTERITIS ENDOTOXEMIA/SHOCK. This 7-year-old female ibex was found dead and an orphaned kid was pulled for hand rearing. Necropsy revealed full abomasum with partially digested dry ingesta possibly representing an impaction. Some areas of dark red small bowel are also noted. Involution of the uterus with luminal blood clots was noted.

EUTHANASIA DIABETES MELLITUS EOSINOPHILIC GASTRITIS. This captive bred 5.5-year-old female lemur was humanely euthanized. It had a one year treatment with insulin for diabetes. The blood glucose had been reduced from 900 to a range of 100-300 mg/dl. The lemur continued to lose weight.

Hypoxic damage was also evidenced in the kidney (tubular necrosis) and liver (centrolobular necrosis). No specific etiology for the underlying heart disease was apparent. Underlying chronic kidney disease also likely affected the overall health of this animal and may have been complicated by concurrent dehydration. The subcutaneous proliferative epithelial lesion was surrounded by fibroplasia; consistent with scarring from previous surgery. Although cellular deterioration interfered with classification of the lesion; the findings were most suggestive of a glandular neoplasm of apocrine gland origin. TTF-1 immunolabeling was performed and did not support a bronchogenic epithelial origin. Apocrine gland neoplasms may arise from adnexa of the haired skin or mammary glands; and according to a retrospective study in African hedgehogs; mammary gland adenocarcinomas are the most common tumor of the integumentary system; occurring along the ventral thorax as well as abdomen. In this case; cellular features did not clearly indicate malignancy; therefore an adenoma or a well-differentiated adenocarcinoma were considered.
