THYMOMA ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male goat has a history of a thoracic mass varus angulation of both forelimbs at the level of the carpi and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized muscle wasting a 10 cm. in diameter irregular mediastinal mass cranial to the heart that was mottled tan on cut surface and had areas of necrosis hemorrhage and possible mineralization and 10 ml. of yellow pericardial fluid was noted. Adipose stores were excessive. Some erosion was noted in the articular surface of the left carpus and on both medial and lateral aspects.

PLEURAL EFFUSION ATELECTASIS ALVEOLAR HISTIOCYTOSIS SHOCK HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 8-year-old male tamarin was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy minimal fat depots were present. The thoracic cavity contained a large quantity of fluid. A 3 cm. in diameter fluid filled bulla was present in the left caudal lung.

INTESTINAL TORSION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SYSTEMIC SHOCK BRONCHOPNEUMONIA CRYPTOCOCCOSIS. This 3-year-old female hunting dog had a history of intermittent cough. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the abdomen was markedly distended. Numerous small pale nodules containing purulent material were present in all lung lobes. The stomach was distended markedly with gas and was torsed 360*. The mucosal surface was sloughing near the pylorus. The stomach contained digested food bone fragments and undigested meat. A sharp line of demarcation was noted in the anterior duodenum and necrotic bowel continued to the ileum. Jejunum was hemorrhagic with necrosis of the mucosa. The left kidney had a 1.5 cm. raised red area.

GOUT NEPHROSCLEROSIS UROLITHIASIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BACTERIAL GRANULOMA METASTATIC MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male chuckwalla has had four surgeries for urolithiasis and recovered poorly from the last surgery. Kidneys were enlarged and phosphate levels were elevated. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed a small white nodule in the liver and grossly enlarged and irregular kidneys.

MYCOTIC DERMATITIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS PULMONARY FIBROSIS STEATITIS. This 18-year-old male gecko had been on treatment for chronic dermatitis. Severe ulcerative dermatitis recently developed and the animal later died. At necropsy numerous erythematous raised areas and tan plaques were present on the ventrum. The liver was enlarged with pale streaks. Several 2-3 mm. in diameter white masses were present on the liver and heart base.

MEXICAN BEADED LIZARD. This 13-year-old female Mexican beaded lizard had a three month history of anorexia and a one week history of marked anemia (PCV=8%) and pale mucous membranes. The animal died and necropsy revealed thin body condition with decreased tail thickness but adequate coelomic fat bodies. A small amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the coelomic cavity and all organs appeared generally pale. A 2 x 3 cm. pale pink mass was noted in the mesentery and exuded soft pink material on cut surface. The liver was pale yellow and friable and appeared to be enlarged and rounded with sharp borders. A 5 cm. cecolith was present and the stomach contained a 7 x 4 cm. mass that occupied approximately 70% of the gastric lumen.

INGUINAL HERNIA OF BOWEL INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This approximately 15-year-old female squirrel monkey was found dead in its enclosure. It had no recent medical problems. At necropsy blood was noted at the anus. There was herniation of bowel loops found in the subcutis of the left inner thigh through rupture of the inguinal canal. There was gaseous distention and gross enlargement of the stomach. The liver was pale tan with dark red to black parenchyma.

EUTHANASIA LUMPY JAW RENAL COCCIDIOSIS. This approximately 4.5-year-old male wallaby was humanely euthanized. It had a history of cagemate aggression and had sustained a neck wound from fighting. Despite aggressive therapy and supportive care the neck wound became progressively worse and involved mandibular and oral tissues.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS DERMATITIS ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA. This 10-year-old female rabbit had a history of degenerative joint disease and spondylosis. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy osteophytes and thickening of the joint capsule were noted in the stifle and spondylosis was present throughout the thoracolumbar spine. A nodular mass was present in the left adrenal gland.

HEAD TRAUMA. This greater than 11-year-old female chuckwalla was found dead. At necropsy there was a laceration and blood on the right skull right ear mandible forearm and lower forelegs. The medial right toe was missing. There was blood in the stomach. There was ingesta in the rest of the gastrointestinal tract. The liver appeared firm and mottled. The lungs were congested. There was food in the coelom.

ESOPHAGEAL FIBROSIS (POSSIBLE MEGA ESOPHAGUS) BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA RENAL TUBULAR MINERALIZATION. This approximately 6-year-old female agouti presented with acute moribund condition and lethargy crackles in the lungs and radiographic evidence of consolidated lungs. The animal was stabilized but then died a few hours later. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and absence of fat consolidation of the left pulmonary lobes and accumulations of white purulent fluid in the lung. The adrenal glands were large. Food and feces were in the alimentary tract.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This approximately 47-year-old male gorilla was noted to cough six times shortly after eating then collapsed on its back and developed convulsions. Resuscitative efforts were not successful. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. in diameter subcutaneous mass in the skin over the left bicep.

OBESITY MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CUTANEOUS VASCULITIS ADRENAL CORTICAL ATROPHY VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY. This 15.5-year-old male fruit bat was found dead on exhibit in the morning and was clinically normal the previous day. Necropsy revealed healed lesions on the nose ears and patagium due to previously diagnosed cutaneous vasculitis. Several months earlier septate fungal elements were noted in skin biopsies of the left ear. Necropsy revealed obesity pulmonary congestion mild left ventricular enlargement numerous areas of myocardial pallor clear urine in the urinary bladder copious adipose tissue in the cavities mild hepatic congestion ingesta in the stomach and smaller than expected adrenal glands. The cranial pole of the left kidney was pale.

HEPATIC HEMANGIOPERICYTOMA SUBCUTANEOUS HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA GINGIVAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CHRONIC PASSIVE PULMONARY CONGESTION EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female hedgehog had a history of not using its hind legs well and an abdominal mass. It was euthanized on February 3 2011. Gross necropsy revealed a skin mass on the right side of the ventral abdomen a mass along the hard palate of the upper left arcade an abdominal mass that was partly adhered to the liver and two firm masses in the liver. The adrenal glands also appeared enlarged and the heart was globoid.

EUTHANASIA POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PERITONITIS. This 9-year-old female hunting dog had a history of decreased appetite. The animal showed difficulty opening its mouth. The animal was treated with antibiotics and anti-inflammatories with no clinical improvement. Immobilization and radiographs revealed possible lucent alveolar bone adjacent to the mandibular premolars. A 10 cm. in diameter mass was present in the cranial abdomen. Laparotomy was performed and revealed polycystic kidneys. Azotemia was noted on blood work which progressed over several days. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis and poor response to treatment. At necropsy a 0.75 cm. dark cystic lesion was present in the spleen. The pancreas contained numerous firm white nodules. Foci of erosion were noted in the gastric mucosa and intestine. Kidneys were enlarged with numerous cysts throughout the cortices.

ADENOCARCINOMA (OVIDUCT SPLEEN LIVER COELOM). This 8-year-old female junglefowl was found dead. At necropsy the caudal coelom was distended with yellow fluid. A 5 cm. nodular white mass was present in the thorax.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 6.5-year-old male lemur presented with lethargy and inappetence and evaluation the following day revealed left shift elevated serum bilirubin and ALT elevated BUN and normal creatinine lethargy and partial inappetence. Supportive care was administered but the animal died overnight. Serology had been negative for Toxoplasma. Necropsy revealed dark red lungs. There is a possibility that the lemur may have eaten one snake root plant.

ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL CYSTS SUSPECT HYPERESTROGENISM CYSTIC PROSTATITIS WITH SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA. This 8-year-old male ferret was found dead. It had a history of hair loss and weight loss consistent with adrenal tumor. At necropsy there were bilateral adrenal tumors. There was cystic prostatitis and prostatic hyperplasia with urethral obstruction. The urine was dark and contained flocculent debris.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS WING TRAUMA HYPERPLASTIC GOITER AIR SAC SARCOMA. This 12-year-old male pelican presented as an emergency with a compound fracture of the right radius and ulna. A second fracture was palpated along the proximal aspect of the wing. The bird’s mucous membranes were pale and the animal was in shock. Supportive care was administered and the animal appeared to have stabilized and was standing the following morning. A surgical procedure was performed to amputate the distal wing at the level of the fracture but the animal did not recover from the anesthetic procedure could not be resuscitated and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed hypertrophied left ventricle some nodules on the mitral valve yellow plaques in the aorta displacement of the syrinx male reproductive tract and enlarged spleen.

TRAUMA LOW-GRADE SYSTEMIC ANTIGENIC STIMULATION (POSSIBLE ATOXOPLASMOSIS) IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 10-year-old female Bali mynah died and necropsy revealed a 2 cm. hematoma involving the right femoral region. Ingesta were present throughout the alimentary tract.

COLONIC IMPACTION. This female greater than 6-year-old mantella was found dead in enclosure pool. At necropsy there was a significant region of red discoloration of the skin on the ventral surface of both rear legs. The cloaca was prolapsed. The coelomic cavity was edematous with hemorrhage caudally. There was a large amount of ingesta on the proximal large intestine. The material was firm and gritty. Culture of the hyperemic skin was performed.

LYMPHOMA. This 2-year-old captive bred female pygmy goat had a ten day history of illness and was euthanized. The animal had severe hemorrhage pancytopenia a mass and fluid in the thorax and firm masses in the prescapular region.

HEPATIC SPOROZOANOSIS INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS (EIMERIA SP.). This 3-year-old male tanager was recently introduced to the aviary and was found dead. At necropsy there was extensive trauma with skull fractures and fracture of the right carpal joint. No hemorrhage was associated with these fractures however. A large area of acute hemorrhage was present in the right pectoral region. The coelomic cavity was filled with frank blood. The liver was friable and contained small foci of hemorrhage.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA TRACHEITIS. This 13-year-old male boa was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy several 3 mm. diameter soft masses were present in the tracheal lumen. The lung contained multiple white soft foci.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 3-year-old male lorikeet was found down in its pen and poorly responsive and was transferred to the veterinary hospital where it died two hours later. It is the third lorikeet to die in a similar manner in two days. Necropsy revealed contusions and abrasions on the scalp no gross lesions in the viscera and male reproductive tract.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 5.5-year-old female falcon was found dead in the morning soaking wet and covered in ants. It had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed green/black discoloration of the left lung and similar but less severe discoloration of the right lung. The liver was dark. Food was in the ventriculus and melena was in the gastrointestinal tract. Pink-colored opaque fluid was within the oviduct and the oviduct contained an unshelled yolk.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 23-year-old male cottontop tamarin had a one day history of illness prior to death. Keeper staff has had some respiratory disease. This animal developed lethargy labored breathing and was found sitting in a urine soaked corner of its paper box. The tamarin died and necropsy revealed generalized edema in the subcutis watery blood in the thoracic and abdominal cavities absence of fat stores swollen and roughened appearance to the liver a milky white covering on the hepatic capsule enlarged heart with thickened muscle thin-walled gas-filled large intestine and thickened small intestinal wall atelectasis in the caudal aspects of the lungs and advanced dental wear.

PULMONARY ABSCESSES NEPHROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 12-year-old female goat had a history of degenerative joint disease and spondylosis and had received supportive care that included phenylbutazone tramadol and gabapentin. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a nodule in the right caudal pulmonary lobe.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS SPLENIC LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 6-year/6-month-old male ferret was found dead. At necropsy there was foam in the trachea. The spleen had numerous multifocal pale to red circular areas that were throughout. The left kidney had a portion of the pelvis that appeared pink. The right kidney appeared somewhat degenerate on cut surface. The liver was very dark and friable. The lungs were mottled with ecchymoses. The urine had substantial debris that was analyzed and was cellular mixed with nondescript debris.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS. This approximately 17-year-old male mangrove snake presented acutely moribund had eaten two days prior to presentation and remained in good body condition. Supportive care was administered but the snake did not respond and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 0.75 cm. subcutaneous mass to the right of the dorsal midline in the caudal third of the body. Eyes were mildly exophthalmic. Cataracts were noted in both eyes. Congestion and edema were noted in the lungs and a small amount of clotted blood was in the tracheal lumen. Multiple small tan nodules were within the pulmonary parenchyma. A small amount of straw-colored pericardial fluid was noted. The liver had multiple small tan masses along the serosal surface and pale discolorations on the cut surface. A partially digested rodent was in the esophagus. Kidneys were pale and had some streaking. The left testicle was smaller than the right testicle. A large amount of coelomic adipose tissue was noted and a small amount of clear free fluid was in the coelom. Multiple nodules were on the ventricular valve of the heart.

ORAL GRANULOMA ENTERITIS FATTY LIVER. This 2-year/2-month-old boa of undetermined gender died. This snake was a stunted chronic poor doer that was being assist fed. It had a black scar on its head. This was one of four juveniles that came out of one shipment in November 2000. All were poor doers and only one is still alive. At necropsy the body condition seemed a bit thin. Coelomic fat bodies were dry and hemorrhagic. The lung was pale. The liver was very pale greasy and floated in formalin.
SHOCK ATROPHY OF FAT. This 1-year-old female ibex was being treated with intravenous fluids and was found dead. Necropsy revealed pericardial effusion and erythema in the small intestine.

AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC GASTRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female black footed ferret presented with weakness lethargy and dehydration. Physical examined revealed marked renal azotemia hypercholesterolemia hyperglobulinemia hyperglycemia inappropriately dilute urine and proteinuria. Glomerular renal failure and amyloidosis were suspected and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bilateral enlargement of the kidneys renal pallor and excoriations of the skin.

BACTERIAL/SPERM-ASSOCIATED GRANULOMATOSIS REPRODUCTIVE TRACT PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS GOUT. This 10-year-old male rattlesnake was found in the hibernation room with lots of substrate stuck in the mouth. The animal was warmed the mouth was rinsed and the snake appeared normal and alert when examined. Later in the afternoon it became lethargic and was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed emaciation pale green to white gallbladder and pale kidneys with white specks throughout the parenchyma.
EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ADENOMA. This 13-year-old hen was euthanized. Biliary cysts were noted in the liver. Arthritic changes were noted in the tarsometatarsal and phalangeal joints.

FRACTURE BACTERIAL CELLULITIS SEPSIS INTRACOELOMIC HEMORRHAGE ATHEROSCLEROSIS TRACHEAL STENOSIS (INTUBATION) ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 23-year-old male scarlet ibis died during sedation for cast removal due to a fracture of the left tarsometatarsal bone. The fracture was healing well but the bird developed a tracheal stricture 48 hours after the procedure which was treated with an air sac cannula. Necropsy revealed thin body condition black discoloration to the skin over the fracture site a fibrotic region in the trachea associated with stricture approximately 7-8 cm. from the glottis clotted blood oozing from the atrium/aorta and clotted blood around the cannula and free in the coelomic cavity and a fracture of the liver at the level of the tip of the cannula.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BILIARY CYSTADENOCARCINOMA AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male ferret had a history of chronic severe dental disease and an apocrine gland cystadenoma was removed from the tail in 2010. Keepers reported sudden lethargy and reduced appetite of several days duration and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed geriatric appearance mildly thin body condition enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes round pale clear to white lesions over the surface of the right caudal pulmonary lobe oligodontia with gingivitis numerous coalescing cysts in the right lobe of the liver associated with hepatic necrosis pale kidneys with irregular surfaces and some cortical cysts with a red focal subcapsular nodule in the right kidney and nuclear sclerosis and early cataract formation.

CHRONIC PASSIVE PULMONARY CONGESTION ACUTE FIBRINOPURULENT ;INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This approximately 2-year-old male rock hyrax presented obtunded and agonal. Radiographs revealed mild heart enlargement and interstitial edema in all pulmonary fields. The animal was electively euthanized. Gross necropsy confirmed serosanguineous fluid in the pleural cavity and pericardial sac right-sided heart enlargement a small right kidney and many cecal liths present in the cecum.
EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL PERISTOMATITIS. This 4-year/4-month-old female rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic neurologic problems. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

TRAUMA; PLASMACYTIC ENTERITIS. This greater than 3-year-old female prairie dog was attacked and killed on exhibit by a feral cat. At necropsy there were abundant fat stores. There was a small amount of bright red blood along the dorsal aspect of the cervical region just caudal to the skull. There was crepitus palpated in this region. The vertebrae palpated unstable. There was considerable hemorrhage in the dorsal cervical region with tearing of muscle bellies. The hemorrhage extended caudally to approximately T5. There were 4-5 small full thickness puncture wounds visible in the skin. The muscles tendons and vertebral ligaments were traumatized. Cervical vertebrae C3-C5 appeared fractured and were displaced. The spinal cord was almost fully severed at the level of C3-C5. The right lung lobes appeared collapsed. There were several small white pinpoint nodules scattered along the surface of the spleen.

CERVICAL TRAUMA. This 7-year-old male giraffe was found dead with its head twisted through the lower bars of a fence. The animal’s head was protruding through the second space and back in through the first space. It appeared to have died suddenly as there were no signs of a struggle. Necropsy revealed pulmonary atelectasis and congestion possible blunting of the heart valves rounded and congested liver congested spleen with fibrous material fracture of the right lateral transverse process of the second cervical vertebra with associated hemorrhage.

ATRIAL THROMBOSIS EUTHANASIA NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 2-year-old male rat had a history of progressive respiratory disease and keepers were having a difficult time medicating the rat due to stress resulting in worsening of the clinical condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed markedly enlarged right auricle and a solid mass occupying the entire lumen. No gross lesions were noted in the respiratory tract.

MALARIA. This 25-year-oldl male Humboldt penguin was found dead with no prior signs of illness other than a chronic history of left scapulohumeral osteomyelitis and arthrodesis. Necropsy revealed good body condition vascular congestion on the serosal surfaces some irregular cobblestone-like mural surfaces on the base of the outflow vessels edematous air sacs small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the cranial abdominal air sacs moderately congested lungs a few 1-2 mm. discrete pale lesions in the hepatic parenchyma associated with the hepatic surface and arthrodesis from bone remodeling in the left humeral scapular joint.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL FIBROSIS. This 16-year-old male tiger had been treated for chronic renal failure since March had been doing well eating and maintaining weight. In July the tiger became lethargic and inappetent and was found dead. Necropsy revealed large adrenal glands small but swollen kidneys with adhesive capsule dark tan serosal surface and poor cortical-medullary distinction. The pelvis was yellow. Multiple firm yellow splinter-like fragments were noted in the renal parenchyma. Two foci of orange discoloration 1-2 mm. in diameter were noted on the serosal surface of the liver which was otherwise grossly unremarkable. The lungs were diffusely reddened and had raised 1-2 mm. nodules on serosal and cut surfaces.

AMYLOIDOSIS. This 5-year/7-month-old male ferret was found dead. It had acute onset of lethargy anorexia and dehydration. CBC and chemistry panel revealed marked azotemia. At necropsy the stomach was dilated and contained reddened mucosa. The left adrenal appeared slightly enlarged. The kidneys were slightly enlarged.

BACTERIAL INFECTION WITH ULCERATION LOWER URINARY TRACT ABDOMINAL HEMORRHAGE MELENA. This 5-year-old domestic ferret was found obtunded pale and had melena. Supportive care was administered but the animal remained comatose and died. Necropsy revealed hypertrophic heart with fibrosis and blood around the great vessels. A fragile mass was noted adjacent to the pylorus with possible neoplastic involvement of the pancreas or intestine. The liver was mottled and had apparent fatty change. Bruising and hemorrhage were noted near the prostate.

HEPATITIS VENTRICULITIS COELOMITIS PANCREATITIS PANCREATIC DEGENERATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INTRAMUSCULAR SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 8-year-old male falcon had gross necropsy findings of an enlarged yellow and mottled liver and marked muscle wasting.

MESOTHELIOMA EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old female lion was recently euthanized due to declining quality of life and body condition. Necropsy revealed 800 ml. of clear straw-colored fluid and fibrin in the thoracic cavity numerous firm white coalescing plaques on the pericardial surface fibrous adhesions of the apex of the heart and the left ventricle to the pericardium few other fibrous pericardial attachments 30 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the pericardial sac clear cysts on the surface of the left ventricle plaques on the thoracic surface of the diaphragm and on the pleural surfaces of the lungs lymphatic dilatation on the serosal surfaces of the stomach omentum and mesentery and a tortuous common bile duct. Degenerative joint disease was in both stifles the ventral aspect of vertebral body T4 was thickened and had nodular bony proliferation bridging to T5 and T6 and the disk material from T3 through T8 had varying degrees of degeneration with associated narrowing of the intervertebral disk space.

INTESTINAL ULCER WITH INTUSSUSCEPTION. This 30-year-old female colobus monkey had a five-day history of gastrointestinal discomfort and one day prior to death was found recumbent hypothermic anemic hypoproteinemic and had regurgitation. The animal had respiratory arrest on one occasion and was recovered. An abdominal mass was detected and was identified surgically as an intestinal intussusception with hypoperfused bowel. Resection and anastomosis was performed but the animal died overnight after surgery. Necropsy revealed gas dilatation in the large intestine and cecum congestion in the small intestine with bloody content mineralized bone density in the tissues near the distal trachea that on cut surface was cream colored and granular bilateral cataracts some green gastric contents in the distal trachea some pinpoint black foci in the lungs and some dark purple discoloration of portions of the pulmonary parenchyma a 1 cm. round structure was lateral to the distal trachea in the surrounding soft tissues that was mineralized and gritty on cut surface (present several years identified radiographically) some yellow streaks in the heart and small spleen. The alimentary tract had dark purple discoloration in the gastric lining intact anastomosis site congested and distended cecum and dark brown or bloody luminal contents in the gut. The uterus was small the urinary bladder was devoid of urine and had normal mucosa and kidneys were pale tan with some pinpoint congestion on the surface.
MYCOTIC BALANITIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 3-year-old male panther chameleon had been off-feed for 2-3 days and died. Necropsy revealed cachexia and prominent white tubules in the kidneys.

ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 2-year-old male lory was pulled from the flight cage for breeding and was found dead in the holding area. At necropsy there were adhesions and small yellow foci in the thorax adjacent to the ribs. The intestines were congested with small yellow foci on the surface of the colon.
OSTEOMYELITIS. This 2-year-old female rattlesnake died. It was observed with a peculiar head tilt the day prior to death. At necropsy the liver was slightly pale and friable.
adult. Weight: 389 g.  Euthanased.  Poor condition.  Poor gut-fill.  Cataract.  Spinal deviations.  Distended scent glands.  Cystic testis.
EUTHANASIA PITUITARY ADENOMA RESPIRATORY MYCOPLASMOSIS. This 2-year-old female rat was euthanized.

ULCERATIVE BACTERIAL DERMATITIS BACTERIAL COLONIZATION OF LUNG. This 4-year-old male rattlesnake had been in hibernation since December 2 2010. It was found dead on January 31 2011. Gross necropsy revealed two areas of bruising on the ventrum with ulceration also present in one area and pale kidneys.

FRRACTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) RENAL GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS ENTERITIS. This 23-year-old flamingo fractured its leg and died under anesthesia. At necropsy there was a comminuted fracture of the proximal left tibiotarsus. The intestinal tract appeared moderately autolyzed.
YOLK COELOMITIS. No history is submitted for this 4-year-old female captive bred pintail duck. Necropsy revealed cloacal prolapse and thick tan/yellow free fluid in the coelomic cavity.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female fruit bat presented for respiratory distress and examination revealed right-sided pneumothorax and atelectatic left lung. Thoracocentesis was performed and air was removed. The animal’s condition continued to deteriorate and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed diffusely dark red to purple lung and 0.5 cc. of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity. Mild congestion was in the liver and a 1 mm. firm nodule was in the distal colon.

EMACIATION SPLENIC MICROGRANULOMA STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old male Burmese python has a one year history of anorexia despite forced feeding and medical treatments. Possible buphthalmia was noted in spring 2007. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed no abdominal fat thin muscle layers small lymphatic nodules along the entire length of the abdominal cavity large pocket of fluid next to the liver a large amount of hard feces in the colon and a “fur-like” appearance on the lining of the stomach that could not be removed with the flat edge of a knife.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE BRONCHIOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of neurologic signs with bilateral progressive ataxia of the pelvic limbs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed orange fat multiple coalescing areas of pallor in the capsule a generalized reticular pattern in the parenchyma of the liver a 3 mm. focus of gray/blue pigmentation in the pelvis and limited to the capsule of one kidney multiple coalescing foci of pallor and hemorrhage in the lungs and female reproductive tract.

EUTHANASIA RENAL CARCINOMA CARCINOMATOSIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS URATE STASIS INANITION. This 18-year-old female kingsnake had a history of multiple surgeries for renal masses. Regurgitation developed along with weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a firm mass was present near the liver and adjacent to the ovary. The left kidney was small tan and soft. The right kidney was enlarged and dark red.

CIRRHOSIS BILATERAL CATARACTS WITH PHACOCLASTIC UVEITIS ACUTE PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 20-year-old male Madagascar day gecko was found unresponsive on 4/1. It had no signs of illness prior to that. Necropsy findings revealed a large dark liver blackened intestines with normal mucosa dark testes clots above the heart and no other abnormalities. The gecko had refused food one day prior to death but this has not been uncommon in this animal.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 1-year-old female rainbow lorikeet was found dead in its cage. It had presented a few months earlier with ataxia which developed shortly after a fight with conspecifics and the CNS signs were believed to be due to head trauma. Blood work had revealed elevations in the serum AST and CPK. A conspecific recently died due to pulmonary sarcocystosis. Necropsy of this bird revealed possible ascites bilaterally congested lungs thin distended proventriculus and possibly enlarged heart.

ACUTE SHOCK. This approximately 2-year-old female lory was found dead and had been partially predated. Necropsy revealed anemia pink to tan liver large gastrointestinal tract full of ingesta large spleen and female gonad.

ENCEPHALITIS TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female pygmy goat had a one week history of severe hematuria with no evidence of infection based on urinalysis. Blood work revealed mild hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia. Ultrasound of the caudal abdomen was within normal limits and cystoscopy was within normal limits. The urine eventually returned to normal appearance and the goat became lethargic with head pressing and circling eventually becoming blind. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed malacia in the white matter of the brain.

METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA GASTRITIS ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 9-year-old female kangaroo was anesthetized for an annual exam. Recovery was normal. Three days later the animal was lethargic and inappetent with abdominal distention. Azotemia was identified. Exploratory surgery revealed a fluid distended stomach. Recovery was uneventful; however the animal was found dead. At necropsy a 1 cm. in diameter soft mass was present in the skin of the abdomen. The stomach was distended with fluid. Firm irregular pale masses were present in the cardia of the stomach. Smaller masses were present throughout the fundus and lumen. Masses were also present in the pancreas uterus and throughout the lung. The GI tract contained scant ingesta.
BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 8-month-old male lorikeet was found down and was humanely euthanized. The bird was thin.

INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 28-year-old sea lion was found dead. It had a history of inactivity anemia and hypoproteinemia. At necropsy there were multifocal confluent firm masses on the surface and cut section of the lung. The masses were 2-3 cm. in diameter and exuded purulent liquid on cut section. The right kidney had a black depressed area that was approximately 3 cm. in diameter.

EUTHANASIA FAT ATROPHY INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This approximately 11-year-old male wallaroo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of weight loss decreased alertness anemia and suspected gastroenteritis and coccidiosis. Endoscopic biopsy revealed lymphoplasmacytic gastritis and enteritis (inflammatory bowel disease). At necropsy some of the areas of the bowel wall appeared thickened. The kidneys appeared somewhat shrunken and pale. The right kidney had focal black spots. The lungs were congested. There was black granular material in some airways. There was one pea-sized abscess.

CHOLECYSTITIS FROTHY FLOAT EMACIATION PULMONARY ABSCESS. This 9-month-old female gerenuk was small for her age and began exhibiting diarrhea three weeks prior to death. Fecal culture was negative for pathogens and fecal EM was negative for viruses. No fecal parasites were seen in an exam. Shortly after treatment was initiated the gerenuk exhibited severe ruminal tympany that was nonresponsive to treatment. The animal died and necropsy revealed fair body condition marked abdominal gas distention moderate muscle wasting ruminal tympany absence of fat stores dark red lungs frothy ruminal fluid shortened ruminal papillae minimal ingestion in the small intestine and no formed pellets in the large intestine.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ISCHEMIC NECROSIS OF LONG BONE EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male stork had been previously diagnosed with a prominent heart murmur and enlarged cardiac silhouette. One week prior to death the animal developed right leg lameness that did not respond to treatment and continued to progress to nonweight bearing. No swelling or external trauma was noted and radiographs were within normal limits. Discoloration of the limb became apparent and suggested devitalization in the distal third of the femoral region and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition good postmortem condition dark purple discoloration of the left hind limb starting approximately 5 cm. proximal to the hock and involving the entirety of the distal limb. Incised tissues were dry firm had no hemorrhage or fluid and no swelling was noted. Moderate diffuse cardiac enlargement was noted and approximately 10-15 smooth firm discrete spherical white nodules up to 2 mm. in diameter were present in the mitral valve. Multiple regions of pale pink discoloration of the pectoral muscle were noted and a 2 cm. region was noted on the right pectoral musculature. A 4 cm. in diameter region was noted in the left pectoral muscle. These lesions were demarcated sharply by normal muscle.

BACTERIAL AND MYCOTIC RUMENITIS WITH ENDOTOXEMIA/ENTEROTOXEMIA. This 12-year-old female gazelle appeared lethargic and shaky on her feet in the afternoon and was found in lateral recumbency that night. She died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed good body condition congestion in the lungs erythema in the rumen and abomasum dry rumen contents congested small and large intestines necrotic liver and five variably sized stones in the gall bladder.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female duck was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes when severe degenerative joint disease no longer responded to supportive care. Necropsy revealed diminished range of motion in the stifles mineralization of the joint capsules of the stifles and small liver with pink discoloration of the distal right lobe.

EUTHANASIA AMYLOIDOSIS GASTROENTERITIS INANITION. This 6-year-old female pochard was humanely euthanized. It presented to the hospital rolling over and having difficulty walking. It was passing loose stool. The keel was visible without palpation. The eyes were slightly sunken. The bird was lame on the right foot with swelling at the tarsometatarsus. Treatment was started. At necropsy there was no body fat. The muscle mass was small. The heart was slightly enlarged with the right ventricle being thickened. There was watery clay-like material in the intestine cecum and rectum. The kidneys were friable on excision. Premortem cultures are pending. Brain and kidney were frozen for West Nile virus surveillance.

GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS MYCOTIC PROVENTRICULITIS EMACIATION. This 9-year-old male sun bittern presented in moribund condition with ataxia and had no prior recent medical history. Examination revealed emaciation. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. This bird tested negative for avian bornavirus. Necropsy revealed emaciation fecal material around the vent markedly enlarged liver with coalescing white firm lesions male reproductive tract and pectoral muscle atrophy.

GRANULOMATOSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS RENAL ADENOCARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male turkey has a history of advanced bilateral pododermatitis and osteoarthritis and has also had positive fecal exams for ascarids and Capillaria sp. The bird’s quality of life deteriorated in association with the bumblefoot and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified chewing lice in the skin cachexia small white granuloma-like mass on the right hepatic lobe similar masses in the spleen and kidney ingesta throughout the alimentary tract and thickened joint capsule of the left hip.

ACUTE SHOCK CHRONIC NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 18-year-old male Nubian ibex had received an excessive amount of banamine three days earlier. It developed a two day history of lethargy and on the morning of death was found with its head hanging. The animal seizured and was dead within five minutes. Necropsy revealed autolysis pulmonary hemorrhages cobblestone liver irritation on the mucosa of the abomasum foul smelling liquid in the jejunum and colon cystic kidneys and necrosis of the adrenal glands.

TRAUMA. This greater than 22-year-old male flamingo was found dead in exhibit. At necropsy the left side of the neck and distal cervical area contained abundant subcutaneous blood that was clotted. There was a puncture wound in the left side of the neck through the skin. The hemorrhage continued dorsally and ventrally to the interscapular area. There were good fat stores present. There was very mild pododermatitis.

EUTHANASIA ENCEPHALITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 7-year-old female rabbit had a history of chronic dental disease and neurologic signs. The animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy urine scald was noted in the perineum. Kidneys were enlarged and irregular.

MAMMARY CARCINOMA WITH MULTIORGAN METASTASIS. This 14-year-old female meerkat has been managed for progressive mobility issues secondary to degenerative joint disease. Her mobility declined severely and on examination she was noted to have a mass in the right first mammary gland and the right axillary lymph node was greatly enlarged. Given her mobility issues and advanced age she was euthanized. The most significant findings at necropsy were extensive metastatic lesions to the lungs liver spleen kidneys and pericardium.

EUTHANASIA CELLULITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION SHOCK. This 21-year-old female guanaco had severe cellulitis and maggot infestation. The animal was humanely euthanized. In addition to the foci of cellulitis and fly strike a large mineralized mass was present in the abomasum.

SEMINOMAS. This 13-year-old male duck had cataracts and impaired vision. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed active testicles and the testicles had irregular consistency with firm and hard regions.
HEPATITIS AIR SACCULITIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 10-year-old female pochard was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the liver was irregular and lobulated.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 17-year-old male cattle egret is in a group that lives outside during warmer weather but was recently moved inside. It is the third animal in the group to be found dead in the past week. It had no signs of illness nor have any of the other animals from the current flock. Necropsy revealed thin body condition no signs of trauma no abnormalities in the choana or nares and male reproductive tract.

OSMOREGULATORY DISTURBANCE MELANOSIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS CHOLELITHIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female axolotl had a history of blunted gills and coelomic effusion but had been eating and had normal behavior. It was subsequently found moribund and nonresponsive but still had withdrawal reflexes. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed blunted gill plumes and a large volume of serous coelomic effusion. The liver was dark red/brown and friable.

SHOCK HEPATITIS. This 19-year-old female spoonbill died approximately three days after being put into an outdoor aviary. No external signs of trauma or illness were noted. At necropsy mild erythema was noted in the GI tract.

GALLBLADDER CARCINOMA GOUT BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female Dumeril’s ground boa had a history of lethargy genetic deformities and decreased clinical health. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a markedly enlarged gallbladder with possible displacement and blockage of the gastrointestinal tract and stomach. The gallbladder was 8 cm. in greatest dimension and contained 30 ml. of viscous bile. A nodular-like structure was on the inside surface of the gallbladder’s wall and several hard white crystallized structures were noted in the lung liver and kidneys. Multiple variably-sized cysts were in the ovaries.

BACTERIAL YOLK COELOMITIS PROLIFERATIVE PNEUMONIA NEPHROSIS. This 15-year/4-month-old female python died. The animal had a history of doing poorly and had unresponsive dehydration. The python was noted to be lethargic. There were areas of shedding noted but the skin underneath was black. Radiographs were not diagnostic. The python was treated with piperacillin. The packed cell volume was 9. The uric acid was 36 and total protein was 13.5. At necropsy there was a large extensive encasement of the left reproductive tract. The encasement was enclosed by coelomic fat and appeared to contain six follicles/eggs from the right side that appeared to be normal as well as the left tract that appeared necrotic and contained numerous small necrotic follicles. The liver appeared slightly grainy on the surface but was normal on cut surface. The heart had hemorrhage. There were dark areas beneath the areas of recently shed skin.

VISCERAL GOUT. This approximately 7-year-old female viper died. It had a history of lethargy and decreased alertness. It had not eaten for the past two feedings. At necropsy the snake was in good body condition. There were small white foci scattered throughout the subcutaneous tissues. The soft tissue over the ventral ends of many of the ribs appeared to contain large accumulations of white granular material. There was a single large yellow/white structure on the ventral body wall just cranial to the heart that appeared to be an encysted larval stage of a parasite. There was blood tinged fluid in the coelomic cavity. The pericoelomic tissues were edematous. The liver seemed enlarged. The left ventral side of the liver was very hard. Incising the capsule of the liver revealed the hard area was caused by a thin layer of dark green/black calcified material that partially wrapped around the left side of the liver. The remaining hepatic parenchyma was filled with many small white foci. There was extensive pericardial fluid that appeared slightly cloudy. The pericardium was partially attached to the heart muscle by fibrinous adhesions. Culture of the pericardial fluid was performed. The aorta was extremely rigid through the entire length of the body. The stomach and upper small intestine were filled with thick green tinged mucus. The wall of the upper small intestine was thickened and congested. The kidneys were firm and filled with urates.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS SHOCK SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMAS. This 7-year-old female cheetah was immobilized for a root canal. Induction and maintenance anesthesia was smooth except for mild to moderate hypertension. The root canal procedure was routine and the cheetah was transported on oxygen back to its den for recovery. The cat arrested shortly after extubation despite signs of routine recovery that included blinking breathing well and gagging on the tube. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation was unsuccessful. A moderate amount of foamy fluid was suctioned from the endotracheal tube during CPR. Necropsy revealed good body condition scant amount of hemorrhagic pleural fluid patchy atelectasis hemorrhagic fluid from the parenchyma of the lung on cut surface foamy fluid in the trachea moderate amount of pericardial fat a few ecchymoses on the endocardium slightly palpable irregularities in the mitral valve a small amount of hemorrhage in the abdominal cavity subjectively dilated and tortuous bile duct small gallbladder that was easily expressed multiple white nodules throughout the splenic parenchyma a 2 cm. cyst on the surface of the kidneys and adrenal asymmetry with the right adrenal approximately 50% larger than the left and mottled on cut surface. The left adrenal had pinpoint tan spots in the parenchyma on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA MALIGNANT THYMOMA. This 103 kg. 10.5-year-old male domestic goat was examined due to bloating and difficulty breathing. Radiographs showed an extremely large heart with tracheal deviation dorsally and a probable mass/abscess in the mediastinum. The animal was euthanized.

RENAL GOUT PODODERMATITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 41-year-old flamingo was weak and depressed with marked bumblefoot lesions. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition declined and it later died. At necropsy the liver was enlarged with blood filled spaces. The spleen was enlarged. Urates were noted in the kidneys.

INANITION SHOCK. This male 7-month-old parrot died before supportive treatment could be given. It presented to the hospital in shock after two days of being chased and harassed by two other birds. It was being chased first by the male parent and then a lorikeet. At necropsy the keel was prominent. The pectoral muscles were very soft. The heart appeared to be larger than normal. The liver was very dark and friable. The intestines were dark. The kidneys were very dark and slightly friable.

VISCERAL GOUT. This 9.5-year-old male duck was found dead in holding pen. At necropsy there were some gouty tophi present in the subcutaneous tissues. There were white slightly gritty deposits of material in and around examined joints. The liver was pale and mottled with pale red areas. The liver appeared enlarged and had rounded edges. The tissue was friable. The spleen was very small and triangular in shape. There were small gouty tophi on the pericardium. There were small amounts of ingesta along the length of the gastrointestinal tract. The kidneys appeared very small and had a distinct separation between the cranial and middle portions.

HEMORRHAGIC DIAPHYSIS GANGLIONEURITIS. This 2-year-old scarlet ibis was noted to have fallen from a tree and may have been dead before it hit the ground. Necropsy revealed adequate fat stores and blood clots in the liver lung and kidney. The liver was friable and had dark black pinpoint lesions on the surface. Small blood clots were in the trachea. The caudal area of the right lung was dark.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 21-year-old female otter had a history of facial swelling and dental disease of eight months duration and had been treated accordingly. The animal died and necropsy revealed multiple white spots on the surface of the lungs diffuse pulmonary congestion intimal roughening of the aorta a cyst in the right ovary pale liver pale kidneys with lots of spaces between the lobules absence of body fat and some dark areas along the wall of the small intestine.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS URATE STASIS. This 10.5-year-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy marked pododermatitis was noted. Pinpoint white foci were present on the surface of the heart. A red consolidated area was present in the lung.

HEPATIC TORSION. This 2-year-old male captive bred rabbit had an acute onset of illness and died spontaneously. The rabbit was hospitalized for heat stress one week prior to death. Treatment appeared to be successful but four hours prior to death the rabbit was found weak and depressed with pale mucous membranes and an enlarged abdomen. Supportive therapy was unsuccessful. Problems with gastric obstruction due to low fiber diet had been encountered in the rabbit’s historically. The rabbit had been switched to a high fiber reduced concentrate diet one month prior to death. Necropsy revealed good body and coat condition with adequate fat stores and a mildly distended firm abdomen. The lungs were diffusely mottled with areas of dark hemorrhage and excessive amounts of blood on cut surface. Normal ingesta was present in the stomach (no evidence of trichobezoar) and the cecum was diffusely dark red. The right caudal liver lobe was displaced 180° from its normal position. The lobe was enlarged with rounded margins and was diffusely black/red. The remainder of the liver was normal. The pancreas and kidneys were diffusely darkened.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old female tiger was euthanized due to poor mobility and poor quality of life. Necropsy identified thin body condition pale tan and firm kidneys a 1 cm. in diameter cyst in the right kidney some erosions on the mucosal surface spondylosis deformans of the ventral aspect of the spine and no other gross lesions.

Compartment 3: C3 Impaction Esophagus: Multifocal mucosal ulcers Peritoneal; thoracic; and pericardial cavities: Tricavitary effusion Liver: Hepatic lipidosis Subcutis of neck; dorsal thorax: Petechial hemorrhage Pericardium; endocardium; mediastinum: Petechial hemorrhage Lungs: Focal pulmonary consolidation Lip commissures: Bilateral proliferative dermatitis Comment The most striking gross findings were impacted ingesta in C3 and contraction of the aboral small intestine with nearly no intestinal content. The pathogenesis of this lesion is unknown. Negative energy balance likely contributed to hepatic lipid accumulation. The body cavitary effusions appeared transudative. Hemorrhages in the thorax and neck regions may represent terminal (agonal) changes. Lesions will be further evaluated histologically and ancillary testing for parasitology as well as bacterial cultures of the lung and liver are underway. The results of complete histologic evaluation and ancillary tests will be included in the final report. Charlotte Hollinger; VMD; MS; DACVP (Clinical Pathology) Lung: Mild multifocal suppurative bronchopneumonia with intralesional plant material Liver: Marked diffuse hepatic lipidosis and mild suppurative peridochitis Glandular stomach (C3): Small inestine: Mild lymphocytic and eosinophilic enteritis Skin: Moderate regional epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis with multifocal epidermal erosion; serocellular crusting; and mild superficial perivascular dermatitis C3 impaction with mild gastritis and enteritis; marked hepatic lipidosis; and perimortem aspiration pneumonia Comment The complete necropsy findings revealed C3 impaction; severe hepatic lipidosis; multifocal hemorrhage; and evidence of perimortem aspiration. A combination of factors likely contributed to the animals' illness; and perimortem aspiration may have contributed to worsening clinical picture and demise. The cutaneous lesions reported clinically consisted of proliferative epidermis with multifocal erosion and crusting. In addition to the clinically suspected differential of Orf (Contagious Ecthyma; Contagious Viral Pustular Dermatitis); another top differential is Idiopathic Nasal/Perioral Hyperkeratotic Dermatosis (also known as Munge); a relatively common condition in young alpacas and llamas for which the inciting cause is unknown. If desired based on herd or human health concerns; PCR testing for parapoxvirus (the inciting agent of Orf) could be pursued to further investigate the cutaneous lesion. Otherwise; this report concludes diagnostic testing in this case. Tissues will be retained for at least three weeks from the date of necropsy should further investigation be desired.
