SEPSIS. This 13.5-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed ecdysis a 1 cm. mass caudal to the cloaca in the area of the scent gland and inspissated material present within the mass. A moderate amount of ascites was in the coelom the right lung was hemorrhagic multiple pale nodules of various size were noted throughout the liver hydropericardium was noted a moderate amount of petechiation was in the myocardium and two firm nodules are in the spleen.

NERVE SHEATH TUMOR LYMPHOMA. This 5-year-old male hedgehog died two hours after excision of an axillary mass. Necropsy revealed possible induration of the fat pads in the inguinal areas possibly some cellulitis in this region.

BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS WING TRAUMA ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male lorikeet fell from its perch and a large scab was noted on the left shoulder when the bird was examined. The bird has had a history of flying problems due to left wing trauma. Wounds on the shoulder have been treated with antibiotics with resolution of wounds although the shoulder wound has recurred. Radiographs revealed bone masses over the left shoulder and left phalanges and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a hard mineralized granular mass that incorporated the proximal left humerus coracoid and scapula corresponding to the scar in the skin. Thickened irregular and mineralized material surrounded the left phalanges.

RENAL GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION MYCOTIC GRANULOMATOSIS. This greater than 12-year-old female cobra had a history of sepsis associated with dermatitis and stomatitis. The animal appeared to respond to supportive care but then deteriorated and was found dead. Necropsy revealed generalized ecdysis granulomas in a number of different tissues and urates in the renal tubules including a large urate-like stone in the cranial pole of one kidney.

ISLET HYPERPLASIA WITH FIBROSIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 3-year-old male rock hyrax has lost 1 lb. over a course of four weeks. Blood work revealed elevated amylase BUN and creatinine. The animal eventually became moribund with open mouth breathing and died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed poor body condition with patchy alopecia attributed to penmate overgrooming (vulturine guineafowl) pulmonary congestion prominent cardiac vasculature and pericardial fat grainy kidneys with discolored cortex shrunken pancreas oral ulcers and maggots in the visceral cavity.

HEAD TRAUMA (COLLISION) EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old male motmot was a high strung anxious bird that was recently acquired by the zoo and several trial releases were attempted but the bird kept flying into the mesh and injuring itself. Following one of these episodes severe bilateral open fractures of the mandibles were noted and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good nutritional status good pectoral mass minor trauma to the face in addition to the mandibular fractures and apparent gross mineralization of the right ventricle and pericardium.

ENCEPHALITIS MENINGITIS MYOCARDIAL MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 4-month-old female meerkat had a prior history of neurologic signs and the animal’s condition rapidly declined. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy pasty green material was present throughout the GI tract.

EMACIATION INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS ASPIRATION. This approximately 2-year-old pigeon of undetermined gender was found recumbent and lethargic in the morning. When struggling the bird flipped into dorsal recumbency and was stargazing had gaping respirations and intermittently had poor control of the head. The animal died prior to initiation of treatment. This bird had completed two training flights the previous day and had no clinical abnormalities at that time. Necropsy revealed fair body condition but good postmortem condition. The liver was homogeneously congested. Multiple white parasites resembling nematodes approximately 2 cm. in length and 2 mm. in diameter were present in the proximal and mid intestinal tract. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

SEIZURES EMACIATION MEDIASTINITIS EUTHANSIA. This 2-year-old male cottontail rabbit had a one-week history of inappetence and diarrhea and examination identified a wound on the scrotum and associated purulent discharge. Supportive care was administered and the diarrhea resolved over a four-day interval. The animal’s appetite returned but nine days after original presentation the animal developed an apparent seizure and subsequently seizured at least once per day for the subsequent four days. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachexia hard small stools slightly enlarged prostate and prostatic pallor some possible liquefactive necrosis in the cerebrum food in the stomach and no other remarkable gross findings.

YOLK COELOMITIS BCATERIAL COELOMITIS. This 4-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy swelling was noted in the caudal coelomic cavity. Caseous yellow material was present in this area adherent to the kidney and small intestine.

Body cavity: Tri-cavity effusion Lung: Marked pulmonary edema Heart: Moderate; multifocal; subintimal hemorrhage Abomasum: Moderate; multifocal; gastric ulcers Liver: Moderate multifocal hepatic necrosis (presumptive); Mild hepatic congestion Comments: No obvious cause of death was observed on gross examination. Due to subintimal hemorrhage and hepatic congestion; tissue samples were submitted for epizootic hemorrhagic disease. A final report is pending histopathological examination; virology; CWD testing; and parasitology. Samples of fresh tissues were saved for further testing if necessary. Tuddow Thaiwong; DVM; PhD Heart: Marked; locally-extensive; subintimal hemorrhage Spleen: Marked; diffuse splenic congestion Lung: Marked; diffuse pulmonary congestion and edema Lymph node: Moderate to marked; hyperplastic lymph node with neutrophilic infiltrates (draining) with mild lymphoid depletion and moderate medullary histiocytosis Liver: Diffuse; hepatic congestion Abomasum: Moderate; multifocal gastric ulceration with intralesional nematode worms and eggs Kidney: Mild; multifocal; interstitial lymphoplasmacytic nephritis

OVARIAN CARCINOMA COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE CHRONIC AIR SACCULITIS. This 8-year-old duck was found to be lethargic and died before examination. At necropsy the animal was thin. A large quantity of serosanguineous fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Multiple plaques were present in the air sacs. Sections of lung were friable and hemorrhagic. The ovary contained a large cystic mass of follicles and serosanguineous fluid. The distal reproductive tract was hemorrhagic and friable.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS. This 26-year-old female chimpanzee died under anesthesia. Necropsy revealed good body condition. A drain and several sutures are present at the site of amputation of the left rear toe and beneath this area much soft tissue necrosis was surrounding the distal portion of the fourth metatarsal bone. Adipose stores were copious and bright yellow. Lungs were edematous. Numerous adhesions were noted in the abdominal cavity. The liver appeared enlarged. The pancreas was edematous and reddened.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 16-year-old female squirrel monkey was found on the ground at morning check. The monkey died en route to the hospital. Necropsy revealed purulent fluid in the abdominal cavity. The lungs were congested. Some mild ventricular thickening was noted in the heart.
adult. Weight: 506 g.  Euthanasia. Poor condition. Abdominal haermorrhage. Pulmonary emphysema.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS SPLENITIS SHOCK. This 10-year-old female pochard was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy adhesions were present within the coelomic cavity. A fluid filled mass was present adjacent to the liver. A crushed shelled egg was present in the cloaca.

SYSTEMIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This approximately 22-year-old male flamingo was noted to not be using one of his legs. The bird was found dead in its exhibit. Gross necropsy revealed abundant depot adipose dilation of the left atrium small white deposits inside the right ventricle thickening of the mitral and aortic valves small deposits on the surface of the liver biliary cysts on the apex of the hepatic lobes multiple small white nodules in the kidneys enlarged kidneys and unremarkable testes. Antemortem blood work showed elevated urea uric acid and CK.

CUTANEOUS MELANOMA WITH VISCERAL METASTASIS. This 17-year-old female green tree python had a history of cutaneous melanoma that was partially excised on two different occasions. The animal died and necropsy revealed swelling just caudal to the old incision site where the melanoma was debulked multifocal white masses in the lung liver and kidney.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female duck was examined five days earlier for everted cloaca and examination revealed minimal mucosal exposure. Radiographs identified subjectively thickened intestines and a coelomic mass in the lower cavity. Blood work three days after initial hospitalization suggested sepsis and hepatic disease. Supportive care was administered but the bird continued to decline over the following 24 hours developing severe lethargy inappetence weakness and moribund condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had a history of testing positive in a group fecal for Mycobacterium genavense in 2011. Necropsy revealed good body condition mildly everted cloaca small amount of fecal material adhered to the mucosal surface of the cloaca multiple 2-5 mm. round white firm masses noted bilaterally in the pectoral muscles and some bead-like masses were also identified. White/tan material was in the esophagus and crop. The liver was enlarged and had multiple 1-1.5 cm. irregular off white masses throughout the parenchyma and some small bead-like masses. Multiple round yellow masses up to 5 mm. in greatest dimension were present throughout the mesentery. The spleen was enlarged dark and had multiple bead-like granulomas on the cut surface. Two large masses were found within the lung both of which were yellow and firm.

SERTOLI CELL TUMOR CHRONIC COELOMITIS. This 7-year-old male chicken was found weak lethargic and dyspneic and in thin body condition. Supportive care was administered but the bird died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed no external abnormalities yellow translucent gel in the coelomic cavity cloudy white pericardium hemorrhagic lungs with gray/white to yellow material in the parenchyma enlarged mottled liver with few areas of pallor fibrinous membrane encapsulating the gastrointestinal tract large round irregular firm and vascularized mass in the region of the left testicle that weighed 40 gm. and was firm on cut surface and was yellow.

METASTIC ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 18-year-old female California sea lion had a several-day history of inappetence and lethargy received supportive care with suboptimal response and the animal died abruptly and unexpectedly in the pool and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed good body condition moderate abdominal distention copious amounts of hemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic and abdominal cavities congested lungs that exuded blood on cut surface segmental marked hyperemia with erosion or ulceration in the jejunum generalized lymphadenopathy and no other remarkable findings.

GASTRIC DILATATION/VOLVULUS DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CEREBELLAR DYSPLASIA PERIANAL GLAND ADENOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male African painted dog had a history of chronic mild head tilt occasional seizures and dilated cardiomyopathy and also had multiple 1-2 cm. nodular masses in the perianal region. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a slab fracture of the upper right premolar #3 gingival and periosteal hyperplasia surrounding the dental arcade a large amount of dark debris in the middle and inner ear canals gas distention and rotation of the stomach on its axis and multiple gas distended loops of bowel. The lumen of the stomach was filled with ingesta and multiple areas of red discoloration were in the gastric mucosa. The proximal duodenum was dark and congested and mesenteric vessels were enlarged. Hemorrhage was present in the mesentery. The spleen was filled with blood. The liver was congested and 50 ml. of pleural effusion was noted. The left lung was small and congested and the right lung was grossly normal. All pulmonary lobes floated in formalin. The heart was diffusely dilated and all chamber walls were thin. The myocardium was pale with full thickness streaks.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 10-year-old female chinchilla had a history of thin body condition. Following examination while anesthetized the animal became listless received supportive care but was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed a mottled liver congested lungs with consolidation in the middle right pulmonary lobe gas in the alimentary tract prominent vessels and erythema in the uterus.

ATOPY DISC DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS PANCREATITIS LOW-GRADE SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 12.5-year-old male African hunting dog was euthanized due to concerns for disc disease and severe spondylosis. This dog also had a history of atopy. Necropsy identified several areas of erythema and ulceration on skin surfaces throughout the body. Disc compression was noted at L3-L4. No other remarkable findings were noted.

INTRASPECIES TRAUMA. This 2-year-old female tamarin suffered intraspecies trauma and was found dead. At necropsy lacerations were noted on all four feet and extensive bruising was noted on the forearms and thigh.

POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE. This approximately 7-year-old dwarf Surinam toad of undetermined sex was found dead. At necropsy there was a mass dorsal and cranial to the heart to which the heart attached bilaterally. The mass was bilobed white and smooth.

OOPHORITIS. This 1-year/9-month-old female snake was found dead on exhibit. It had no previous signs of illness. Several other snakes from the same enclosure have died recently some with skin lesions. At necropsy the snake appeared to be in good body condition. The lungs were mottled red/purple. There was a small amount of clear foam in the trachea. There were numerous ovarian follicles with the largest measuring 2.5-3 cm. in diameter.

CARCINOMA LUNG UTERUS; CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA HEPATIC ABSCESS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 14-year-old female sheep began coughing became anorexic and failed to show improvement with therapy. At necropsy a large abscess was present on the colon containing greenish necrotic material. The uterus was enlarged and contained a large quantity of flocculent yellow fluid. The liver contained firm white to yellow nodules. Firm white nodules were present in the lung. Large firm white masses were present at the thoracic inlet extending to the pericardium.

SUSPECT NEPHROTOXICITY DUE TO CISPLATIN EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old spayed female black-footed ferret had hepatic carcinoma with surgical removal in the right hepatic lobe. This animal received a regimen of chemotherapy which was stopped due to worsening renal values. The animal was euthanized six months later for humane and diagnostic purposes.

INTESTINAL HEMORRHAGE POSSIBLE ENTEROTOXEMIA HYPERPLASTIC GOITER. This approximately 10-year-old female pelican had been sitting on a nest and was not eating well for some time. It was reportedly found floating nonresponsive in the water. A heartbeat was detectable but the bird was not responsive to handling. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed adequate adipose stores brown/orange vomit in the pouch and oropharynx thin fragile and malleable keel multiple broken ribs that are poorly mineralized and easily bent or snapped firm long bones marked congestion and hemorrhage in the connective tissues on the interior keel overlying the heart and lungs and apparent fibrinous pleuritis congested and wet lungs white streaking of the ventricles dark brown/black fluid in the esophagus proventriculus and gizzard and numerous coiled white nematodes in the proventriculus and gizzard.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISESE. This greater than 10-year-old male boa constrictor has a four-month history of lying in a lateral position with the middle third of its body. Radiographs revealed osseous proliferation. The animal was not responsive to analgesics and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA INANITION GRANULOMATOUS COELOMITIS. This 20-year-old corn snake has a history of chronic anorexia and retained shed. The animal was humanely euthanized. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA MALIGNANT ROUND CELL NEOPLASM CARDIOMYOPATHY MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 6-year/3-month-old female meerkat was humanely euthanized. It had a history of a mass that involved the right kidney. At necropsy the liver was copper colored and mottled. The left kidney was copper colored. There were yellow plaque-like nodules noted throughout the mesentery and diaphragm. There was a white rubbery mass (2.5 x 3.5 cm.) infiltrating the right kidney in the right cranial lobe.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC GASTRITIS LOCALIZED COLITIS/PERITONITIS MYELOLIPOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11.5-year-old male cheetah has a history of severe azotemia that has not responded to treatment and was progressively worsening. The animal was not eating. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dehydration and emaciation white hard masses throughout the spleen and a red/hemorrhagic mass approximately 3 cm. in greatest dimension perpendicular to the colon located on the mesenteric border of the colonic serosa. No evidence of ulcers was noted within the gastrointestinal tract. The liver had several small black circular areas throughout the surface. Kidneys were small firm and had irregular corticomedullary architecture.

URETERITIS GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 6-year-old female cockatiel presented for poor body condition and abnormal behavior isolating itself from the flock. Examination revealed severe hyperuricemia hypercalcemia and elevated CK. The bird became apneic during recovery from anesthesia and died despite resuscitation attempts. Necropsy revealed poor body condition alopecia on the head cervical region and cranial dorsum elongated heart with pinpoint white foci in the epicardial surface diffusely pale kidneys and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE. This 11-year-old female goat was humanely euthanized due to nonresponsive lameness associated with arthritis of the right carpal joint. The arthritis was unresponsive despite treatment. At necropsy there were mild erosive lesions on the articular cartilage of the left carpus. The right carpus had many roughened irregular edges on the articular surface of both portions of the joint. The mucosal surface of the uterine body and horns were covered with small nodular growths.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS URATE STASIS ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 14-year-old female merganser was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the bird was thin with a prominent keel. The right kidney was enlarged and pale tan.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE AXONAL DEGENERATION PHACOCLASTIC UVEITIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male pintail had a history of difficulty walking and was unstable and thin. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. It had permanent loss of vision in the right eye due to trauma. Necropsy revealed white apex of the heart with occasional white striations throughout the cardiac muscle primarily in the atria and the heart appears subjectively enlarged. Liver had a small cyst with clear fluid in one lobe. A small amount of yellow-tinged fluid was in the caudal cervical region and some minor erosions were associated with joint surfaces on the coxofemoral joints. The right femoral tibiotarsal joint had a moderate amount of sanguineous fluid with mild osteoproliferative change. No other abnormalities were noted.

EUTHANASIA XANTHOMA (MENINGES) ENCEPHALITIS INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 12-year-old gecko had a history of neurologic signs including stargazing. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition declined and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were enlarged and pale.

ACUTE SKELETAL MUSCLE NECROSIS AND HEMORRHAGE UTERINE FIBROLEIOMYOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female greater kudu initially presented for a dental abscess that was treated surgically. Following anesthesia the animal was unable to rise and was holding its rear limbs in a splay-legged position. The animal was also tachypneic and dyspneic. The animal’s clinical condition rapidly deteriorated and it was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition bruising and abrasions along the limbs gritty material within the tooth socket of the extracted molar pulmonary congestion hepatic and splenic congestion two small cysts within the vaginal mucosa waxy and tarry concretions within the cervix and right uterine horn a mass on the right uterine horn a cyst in the left uterine horn and within the right ovary and reddish-purple tissue within the lateral ventricles of the brain.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME MYOCARDITIS RENAL INFRACTS. This 2-year-old female hedgehog had a history of slowly progressive weight loss head tilt and mild ataxia and wobbly hedgehog syndrome was suspected. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition and excellent postmortem condition. No gross lesions were seen.

NONSUPPURATIVE ENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male banded rock rattlesnake left quarantine in November 2011 was treated for dysecdysis and a degloving rattle injury in February 2012 and has been reported to have chronic progressive abnormal behavior that includes rigid movements no defense behavior and recent head bobbing and slow righting reflex. The snake has always had a good appetite and growth rate. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a small regrown rattle yellow kidneys with only a small amount of normal parenchyma apparent in the right kidney a single tan round thyroid cyst and adequate adipose stores.

PNEUMONITIS EPIDERMITIS. This approximately 8-year-old male snake died. It had a history of inactiveness and absence of any righting reflex. A cagemate had recently died. At necropsy the pericardium was filled with blood.

OBSTRUCTIVE CHOLELITHIASIS WITH CHOLECYSTITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female tamarin had been losing weight despite good appetite and had elevated hepatic enzymes including total bilirubin and GGT. Ultrasound revealed an area in the liver suspected to be a gallbladder impaction or neoplasm. An aspirate from this area identified bacteria. The animal had been pregnant but aborted one month prior to death. Despite supportive care the animal declined and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hard dry bile in the gallbladder and bile duct. The liver was yellow tinged and pale. Dark yellow/gray hard foci were in the right and left uterine horns.

LYMPHOID LEUKEMIA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year/10-month-old male koala was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed with lymphoid leukemia. At necropsy clotted blood was found in the abdomen. The spleen appeared normal. There were 1 mm. white foci uniformly dispersed throughout the liver. The right side of the heart was somewhat dilated. The left ventricular free wall thickness was 0.8 cm. and the right was 0.2 cm. At the thoracic inlet bilaterally along the trachea there was a 2 cm. long by 5 mm. thick whitish-yellow almost rough textured tissue.

EMACIATION PROVENTRICULAR MACRORHABDIOSIS. This 7-year-old budgerigar was isolated 10 days earlier for weight loss and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed a hard mass between the intestines and the liver.

SUSPECT PULMONARY FIBROSIS SUSPECT INTESTINAL ADENOVIRUS. This 7-year-old male cockatiel was having breathing issues lethargy and both nares were variably occluded. The animal was found dead. At necropsy there was a decrease in pectoral muscling. The left lung was pale and firmly adhered to the underlying tissues.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL CYST CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 28-year-old female mandrill was euthanized due to severe degenerative joint disease and possible mammary neoplasia. Kyphosis was noted in the thoracolumbar spine. Stifles were enlarged due to bony proliferation. Firm ulcerated masses were identified in the mammary tissue.

AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT. This 41-year-old male American flamingo was found dead in the morning after a very cold night. Necropsy revealed enlarged kidneys prominent liver some scarring in the lungs and air sacs and possibly some fibrin deposition in the pericardium.

LOW GRADE SEPSIS. This 9-year-old male emerald tree boa was recently being medicated for bacterial infection and died on exhibit. Necropsy revealed good body condition. A lesion in the last third of the body was believed to be associated with rodent predation postmortem.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS OSTEOMYELITIS. This 11-year-old male lion was found dead. The lion’s recent appetite and behavior had been normal. The lion has a history of seasonal allergy hemolytic anemia presumed to have been related to trimethoprim sulfa therapy and a self-inflicted wound to the tail tip. The animal had been treated with long-term tricyclic antidepressant therapy (amitriptyline). At gross necropsy the body was markedly autolyzed. The myocardium was mottled and the left ventricle contained aberrant chordae tendinea.

METASTATIC BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 27-year-old male baboon showed signs of weight loss inappetence and depression of several days duration prior to death. Antemortem examination revealed moderate dehydration mild to moderate anemia mild icterus and metallic densities in the stomach. The animal did not recover from anesthesia. Necropsy revealed diffuse caseous lesions 0.5 to 3 cm. in diameter throughout the liver. Large granulomas were adhered to the sternum in the serosa of the lower esophagus. A focal enlargement was in the bile duct and contained a small concretion 0.5 cm. in diameter. Multiple diffuse caseous lesions 2-8 mm. in diameter were found in the lungs. Three coins were found in the stomach (1980 & 1971 pennies and a quarter). Mucosa of the stomach was irregular and hyperemic.
INANITION. This 1-year-old female viper had recently shed. The animal was found dead. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL OSTEOARTHROSIS. This female 18-year-old boa was humanely euthanized. It had a history of depression anorexia dehydration abdominal swelling anemia and osteopathy of one-third of the vertebrae. It was positive for cryptosporidia. Treatment was done. At necropsy the body condition was good. There was ventral dermatitis with the caudal two-thirds of the body affected. The scales were flaky and cracked. There was hyperemia and swelling between the scales. The caudal one-half to two-thirds of the body was flaccid and did not maintain a normal oval cross sectional shape. The boa had a history of not moving well in the cage. It would allow the caudal third to be placed in ventral dorsal position without attempts to right itself. The pericardium was filled with clear fluid. Bilaterally the lungs were hyperemic wet and erythematous. The esophagus was dilated and thin walled and filled with gelatinous sticky whitish material. The stomach was diffusely thickened with a cartilaginous texture. The mucosa was tan/brown and peeled off the underlying tissue easily. The small intestinal mucosa was thickened irregular and tan with a granular appearance. The large intestine was gas distended. The pancreas had multifocal circular areas of hemorrhage. The coelomic cavity contained a large amount of yellow fluid. There was radiographic evidence of vertebral changes in the mid one-third of the body.

NECROULCERATIVE DERMATITIS (POSSIBLE BURNS) SEPSIS. This 4-year-old female black tree monitor was found dead. This monitor had a lead level of 11 µg/dl several months earlier. It had a history of superficial ulcerative dermatitis over the paralumbar region. Necropsy revealed skin lesions adjacent to the spine and three eggs in the oviduct.

DISSEMINATED ROUND CELL TUMOR BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS. This 12.5-year-old female Gaboon viper was found dead following a several week history of inappetence. The animal had been restrained one day earlier for venipuncture and radiographs. Necropsy revealed mildly thin body condition and no major lesions in the skin or scales. A moderate amount of clotted blood was apparent within the pericardial sac and hemorrhage was in the wall of the left ventricle attributed to venipuncture. The ventricle otherwise was markedly pale. The muscular and submucosal tunics of the stomach appeared thickened. The liver was diffusely mottled with occasional firm pale foci. The colonic mucosa was congested. The serosal surfaces of the alimentary tract were pale. The splenopancreas was hemorrhagic. White urate accumulations were noted in the kidneys and hemorrhage was also noted in both kidneys. Musculature was markedly pale.

CLOACITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS SHOCK. This 11-year-old male sun bittern was found dead. At necropsy severe urate and fecal accumulation was present around the cloaca which completely occluded the cloaca. The large intestine and colon were markedly dilated with feces.

IRON STORAGE DISEASE MYOCARDIAL AND HEPATIC FIBROSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS LYMPHOHISTIOCYTIC LYMPHADENITIS. This 7.5-year-old male harbor seal had a few week history of swelling under the mandible attributed to a tooth root abscess. While anesthetized the animal developed anesthetic complications with associated pulmonary edema and could not be revived. Necropsy revealed overconditioning a 2 cm. area of fibrosis in the right ventricle and congestion of the brain.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL HYPEROSTOSIS INANITION. This 2-year-old female viper was euthanized due to multiple foci of spinal fusion. At necropsy the central one-half of the body is nearly completely fused with multiple foci of malalignment. The colon and jejunum were impacted with feces.

HEMORRHAGIC SALPINGITIS BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS SHOCK. This 4-year-old female lorikeet suffered a uterine prolapse which was reduced. The animal was found dead two days later. At necropsy gouty tophi were present on the serosal surfaces of the liver and other coelomic organs. The spleen was pale. The distal one-third of the uterus was prolapsed into the cloaca and was edematous and hemorrhagic.

NEPHROLITHIASIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION YOLK COELOMITIS. This 22-year-old female beaded lizard was reported as lethargic and barely responsive in the morning and examination did not identify a heartbeat. Necropsy revealed yolk coelomitis associated with numerous variably sized eggs in the coelom. The liver was firm.
WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female hedgehog was submitted with no history.

ENTRAPMENT FRACTURED CERVICAL VERTEBRA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ASPIRATION. This 14-year-old female tammar wallaby was found dead in the morning with its head lodged in a small opening under a metal gate. It had been dead at least several hours and had evidence of abdominal bloating and the presence of insects in the pouch and in the oral and anal cavities. This animal was clinically normal the previous day. Necropsy revealed good body condition postmortem gas distention in the abdomen splintered and broken hind medial claws empty and clean pouch no mammary development pelleted feces in the colon and normal ingesta in the stomach markedly congested lungs with frothy white material on cut surface possible hypertrophy in the ventricles of the heart a fracture at the atlantooccipital junction with associated hemorrhage into the surrounding soft tissues and caudal ventral portion of the cranial vault and surrounding brainstem.

PORTAL HEPATITIS MYOCARDITIS MYOSITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA MUSCULAR SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 8-year-old male teal was found dead. It had some wing abrasions in the spring. It was moved to a new exhibit in May. It had no clinical problems. It had been vaccinated for West Nile virus. At necropsy it was in good body condition. There were several clumps of fly eggs in the neck feathers. The pectoral musculature had thin red streaks running throughout. The serosal surface of the myocardium had very prominent vasculature. The cranial lungs seemed dark purple and gel-like in texture. The caudal lungs were normal. The caudal margins of the liver extended well past the sternal margins. The kidneys were pale with a slight mottled appearance.

INCLUSION BODY DISEASE VASCULITIS AND GANGLIONEURITIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female red-tailed boa had refused food for three weeks and had a two week history of stargazing and gaping. A blood film evaluation noted inclusions and multiple lymphocytes suggestive of inclusion body disease. Endoscopic biopsies were obtained but the snake developed severe arrhythmia and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition a large amount of fat in the coelomic cavity severely hypertrophied ventricle amber pericardial fluid congested small vessels near the stomach pancreas and spleen forming a streak pattern. The stomach had multiple erosions throughout the mucosa that were more severe in the pyloric region. Multiple small erosions were also noted in the esophagus near the stomach. The liver was slightly pale.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 1-year-old female lory was found lethargic and died. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the jejunum and parts of the duodenum and some mild bruising around the calvarium. The liver was enlarged.

ADENOCARCINOMA (SPLEEN LIVER LUNG) HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 2-year-old female hedgehog had a large subcutaneous mass removed. Two days later the animal was hypothermic and lethargic. The animal later died. At necropsy the animal was moderately obese. The spleen was enlarged and contained numerous white masses. Melena was noted in the distal GI tract. The liver was pale and floated in formalin.
EDEMA SUSPECT INANITION. This female 10-month/9-day-old tree frog was found dead. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION RUMINORETICULITIS. This 7.5-year-old male greater kudu had a several month history of decreased appetite and progressive weight loss starting in December 2012 after an incident of abdominal trauma with herniation of the omentum. The hernia was repaired surgically. A young female kudu that died in December also had a similar history of progressive weight loss but had no history of trauma (G13-0094). Necropsy of the animal of this report revealed emaciation pulmonary congestion multiple linear ulcerations on the ventral abomasum petechiae in the pylorus enlarged gallbladder flaccid spleen enlarged lymph node adjacent to the rumen petechiae in the urinary bladder marked muscle wasting and marked atrophy of fat.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PNEUMOTHORAX. This 1-year-old female naked mole rat has a history of respiratory distress and died before treatment could be initiated. Necropsy revealed bilaterally congested lungs and no other gross lesions.

HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA ATHEROSCLEROSIS LYMPHANGIECTASIA EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female meerkat has a history of ataxia and thromboembolism is suspected. It had a two-year history of severe lipemia and acute onset of ataxia with knuckling of both left limbs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified 1 mm. white plaques on the aortic valve globoid heart multiple thin white bands extending the entire circumference of the serosal surface of the small intestine and these do not extend to the mucosa. The stomach was corrugated. Two subcutaneous masses are on the dorsum of the left hind foot the largest is 3 mm. in diameter and yellow on cut surface. The left adrenal gland was larger than the right.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY ACUTE HEPATIC NECROSIS CEPHALIC SHOCK EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female giraffe was anesthetized for routine hoof trim but was unable to stand following anesthetic recovery developed dull mentation and muscle fasciculations did not respond with supportive care and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple stones in the left renal pelvis pale streaks on the capsular surface of the liver gritty hepatic parenchyma on cut surface focal petechiae in the dorsal subcutis of the midcervical region thinning of the articular cartilage of the coxofemoral joints and ample fat stores.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK CHRONIC NEPHRITIS SPLENIC EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS. This 1.5-year-old male hedgehog developed difficulty breathing following an education program. The animal was dead on presentation to the hospital. At necropsy hemorrhagic fluid was identified in the oral cavity. Lungs contained frothy fluid and bruising.

SHOCK. This approximately 5-month-old female toad is from a collection that was captive reared at the zoo. This frog is from a group of 10 in which there have been no losses since metamorphosis and the toads have been eating well with no signs of illness. This toad was found dead at the morning check. Necropsy revealed moderate anasarca and ascites. Fat stores were noted and the sternum and ribs appeared soft when cut.

BUMBLEFOOT (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH SEPSIS STRESS MYCOTIC GLOSSITIS ESOPHAGEAL ABSCESSES. This 20-year-old male flamingo had a history of depression and ataxia. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed bumblefoot on both feet orange fat in the coelomic cavity bruising and lacerations of the epithelia of the tongue hemorrhage inside the mouth an abscess inside the tongue mottled tan liver a pale tan spot in the spleen and no other gross abnormalities.

MALARIA ATHEROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA (UROPYGIAL GLAND) POSSIBLE GOITER. This 19-year-old female penguin developed a gradual worsening onset of weakness decreased appetite and ataxia with difficulty swimming and swallowing fish. Blood work revealed a marked elevation in packed cell volume and lymphocytic leukocytosis. Mucosal proventricular biopsies were histologically within normal limits. Supportive care was administered and the bird appeared to show transient improvement before declining and was found dead prior to the afternoon feeding. Necropsy revealed fair to good nutritional status and good hydration. Numerous 1-5 mm. in diameter discrete but coalescing cream to tan colored raised lesions were adherent to the air sac membranes on all surfaces of both cranial air sacs but especially more prominent in the caudal air sacs. The lungs were congested.

Ovary (left): Carcinoma with metastases to the kidney; uterus; lymph node; lung; adrenal; urethra; skeletal muscle; mammary gland; and large blood vessels Uterus: Mild cystic endometrial hyperplasia Vagina; uterus: Leiomyomas Kidney: Severe chronic interstitial nephritis Intestine: Moderate chronic lymphoplasmacytic enteritis Liver: Mild multifocal cholangitis Lymph node; other organs : Mild sinusoidal and perivascular hemosiderosis Tongue: Moderate hemorrhage Comment: The cause of death in this Indian rhinoceros was clearly the multiorgan dysfunction precipitated by the widely metastasizing carcinoma. Based on the most severe and largest mass; the neoplasm is most likley ovarian in origin; though it is possible that it had originated as a ductal carcinoma from the mammary gland or elsewhere and metastasized early to the ovary. The kidney changes may be secondary at least in part to the neoplastic disease; but could also have been pre-existing and contributed to this animal's debilitation (including the clinically reported edema and the hemorrhage noted in the tongue). Enteritis and cholangitis are likely related and are probably unrelated to the carcinoma

HYPERTENSION GOUT PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS DOUBLE LENS. This 2.5-year-old male gecko was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed pale liver with pinpoint light foci over the hepatic capsule and on cut surface. No fat stores were noted.

EUTHANASIA POSTOPERATIVE COMPLICATIONS NERVE TRAUMA. This 13-year-old Ibex underwent a cesarean section and ovariohysterectomy. The animal failed to recover and suffered nerve damage with splay leg. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the pericardium.

DISSEMINATED ROUND CELL MALIGNANCY CELL OF ORIGIN UNDETERMINED. This 18-year-old female Madagascar tree boa presented for swelling of the throat and examination revealed lethargy and limp body condition. The snake died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed a large amount of blood in the body condition and ten undeveloped fetuses showing signs of hemorrhage. This snake had been gravid approximately two years earlier and all offspring were stillborn.

UTERINE AND MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old female peccary was found laterally recumbent on exhibit was immobilized for examination and a mass was identified in the caudal abdomen possibly associated with the reproductive tract. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed round nodules throughout the pulmonary lobes up to 1 cm. in greatest dimension and the nodules were firm and tan. Four or five rounded light yellow nodules resembling cysts were present in the middle hepatic lobe. Some reddening was in the small intestine. Multiple cysts were present in both ovaries and an 8 cm. mass was present in the right uterine horn extending into the bifurcation of the uterine body. The mass also appeared to infiltrate the left uterine horn to a lesser extent. A nodule was associated with the distal right mammary gland.

TRAUMA. This 7-month-old female parrot died during a preshipment examination. It had an overgrown beak and the bird died while the beak was being trimmed. The bird had been handled before. It had no prior clinical signs of illness and weight appeared to be adequate. Necropsy revealed good body condition seeds in the crop inactive ovary and good abdominal fat stores.
adult. Weight: 249 g.  Euth. Fracture/luxation R wing tip. Skin damage; L wing tip & caudal wing membrane.

INTESTINAL LYMPHOMA SEPSIS. This 7-year-old female common marmoset was found dead in its nest box and had lost approximately 100 gm. Necropsy revealed infected left lower molar and bile in the intestines associated with hemorrhage.

METABOLIC BONE DISEASE PULMONARY CONGESTION TRAUMA. This less than 1-year-old male leaf nosed bat was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy there was bruising on the right side of the jaw. The adrenal glands were enlarged.

Biliary Tree: Severe biliary ectasia and possible hypertrophy Liver: Moderate focal adhesion of the left caudal liver lobe to the stomach and omentum; Multifocal; white discolorations on the serosal surface of the left lateral liver lobe Kidney: Multifocal cortico-medullary cysts Spine: Traumatic fracture at the level of L4 and L5 Comment The brain appeared grossly normal. There is evidence of a disease process in the liver and biliary tracts; the tortuous bile duct seen via MRI was visualized on necropsy. The adhesions of the left caudal liver lobe and the white discolorations may be due to migrating parasites. A more definitive diagnosis may be possible when additional results from histopathology are available. Stephanie French; DVM; MS

ANESTHETIC DEATH FIBROSARCOMA (SKIN) WITH LYMPH NODE METASTASIS MYOCARDIAL FIRBOSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 13-year-old male giraffe had a chronic infection of the left carpus. The animal died during standing sedation for cast removal and wound treatment. Marked hemorrhage occurred from the wound cavity. At necropsy a large hygroma containing malodorous fibrinopurulent debris was noted adjacent to the carpus. Petechial hemorrhages were noted over the heart. A small globoid mass was present on the right AV valve.

PARALYSIS CAUSE UNDETERMINED EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female tiger became acutely and unexpectedly recumbent. The cat appeared to have rapidly progressing ascending paralysis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed congestion of the kidney liver and lung some nodules in the spleen mild valvular endocardiosis and few cysts in the right kidney.

RENAL GOUT VISCERAL GOUT INANITION. This 12-year-old female gecko had a history of urate impaction with a firm immoveable mass in the caudal abdomen. Surgery was performed to remove a mass of urate material from the bladder. White nodular material was present on the mucosa and serosal surface of the bladder. Anesthetic recovery was prolonged and the animal was euthanized. Urate deposits were identified throughout the bladder and left kidney. Fluid was present in the trachea and lungs sank in formalin.

ANESTHETIC RELATED DEATH TOXOPLASMOSIS. This approximately 2-year/6-month-old male kangaroo died. It was immobilized with isoflurane for treatment. It was undergoing bandage changes on both feet and left hip. Dead tissue was debrided from the left hip lesion. The right hock lesion appeared to have improved. There was a new opening in the abscessed pocket on the medial aspect of the foot and there was much less purulent drainage. The left hock lesion appeared unchanged. The kangaroo went into respiratory and cardiac arrest within a few minutes during the procedure. The kangaroo was intubated and ventilated with oxygen. The heart was restarted with intracardiac epinephrine and Doxapram. It was unable to be resuscitated. At necropsy both feet were bandaged and the bandages covered a 10 cm. in diameter ulcerated area over both hips. There were a number of smaller ulcers and abrasions on the front feet and front limbs that were not bandaged. Tissues along the ventral abdomen were edematous with a small amount of fluid seeping from the skin lesions along the ventral abdominal wall. There were some pale muscle bundles in the hind limbs. The abdominal cavity contained 200-300 ml. of clear straw colored fluid. There were a few fibrin strands present. The free edges of the liver were slightly rounded and the parenchyma showed mottling typical of chronic passive congestion. Both lungs were very edematous and barely floated in formalin. The down lung (right) during the procedure was congested. There was substantial clotted blood in the pericardial sac from repeated intracardiac injections. The left ventricular wall was about twice the thickness of the right.

ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS PYELONEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS WITH ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 17-year-old female snow leopard had a one month history of illness characterized by osteoarthritis urinary tract infection and generalized malaise. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Blood work prior to death revealed marked anemia slightly elevated white blood cell count with increased band cells and elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine. Necropsy revealed atrophy of the muscle over the hindquarters and top of the head tacky fascial planes slightly yellow skin over the abdomen yellow fat rough haircoat 40 ml. of pericardial clear fluid several 1-2 mm. tan nodules in the lungs unilateral asymmetry in the thyroid glands with the left 1.5 times larger than the right petechiae in the parathyroids mottled red/tan liver with numerous tan foci throughout the hepatic lobes and fibrous texture when cut rancid ingesta in the stomach including items fed one week earlier greasy fecal material in the colon and some areas of frank blood bilateral medullary abscesses in the kidneys purulent material in the urinary bladder and depletion of the medullary regions of the adrenal gland.

ANESTHETIC DEATH SYSTEMIC SHOCK PULMONARY EDEMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS LYMPHOSARCOMA. This 8.5-year-old female capybara was restrained for chemotherapeutic treatment of lymphoma. The animal suffered cardiopulmonary arrest during recovery and died. At necropsy a large ventral cervical mask was present. Lungs were mottled dark red to purple. Cervical lymph nodes were enlarged.

ACUTE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS. This 25-year-old female dwarf caiman was being treated for a skin lesion on the ventral thorax of several weeks duration had been isolated two weeks earlier to facilitate treatment had been inappetent for several weeks and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy identified a 2 cm. ulcerative skin lesion on the ventral thorax and a slightly smaller ulcerated skin lesion on the ventral neck copious adipose stores some serous atrophy of fat in the cranial coelomic cavity pale liver active follicles and some inspissated follicles with associated congestion gastric congestion much clear fluid in the gastric lumen dark liquid ingesta in the intestine and pale lumbosacral musculature.
adult. Weight: 223.2 g.  Euth. Mandibular abscess.

ADVANCED NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male African dog was identified with renal disease in September 2015. It also had a history of alopecia with reddened skin that responded to treatment. The animal declined in condition with loose stool unkempt appearance lethargy inappetence unstable gait and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed ulceration of the gingiva along the maxillary and mandibular arcades tan circular lesions in the lymph nodes fluid in the prostate. Erosion in the skin of the preputial sheath irregular thickness of the renal cortices with tan coloration and on cut surface marked reduction of normal renal structure with loss of distinction in the papillae and calyces. White striations were present in the parenchyma.

UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female addra gazelle was depressed and off feed for a few days. The animal had a swelling on the right side of the mandible. Abdominocentesis revealed atypical cells. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the caudal abdomen encompassing the uterus. A multilobulated hemorrhagic mass was inside the uterus and had cystic areas that contained brown translucent fluid. The lungs had apparent metastatic disease. A mass in the brisket was 3 x 3 x 3 cm. and firm.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS OSTEOMYELITIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This greater than 7-year-old female lizard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of no improvement in ability to move or show interest in anything. At necropsy there was a section of mandible with caseous material present. There was a yellow round structure present in the coelom.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) AMYLOIDOSIS ABDOMINAL ABSCESS WITH BACTERIA EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old oryx has a history of left forelimb hoof abscess (12 years ago) trauma to the thoracic wall (7 years ago) calved in 2003 2007 and 2009 and in 2010 began to lose body condition in spite of increased caloric intake. In April 2012 the animal developed a left head tilt with head and neck in lowered extended position and osteoarthritic changes were suspected rather than neurologic deficits. Supportive care was administered but the animal eventually was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Blood work revealed hypoalbuminemia elevated blood urea nitrogen and mild hypocalcemia. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting and thin body condition dermatopathy with scaling and alopecia over the distal limbs and tail head fibrosis involving the caudal portion of the right caudal pulmonary field an omental mass attached to the left ruminal wall firm small kidneys with areas of pallor resembling infarcts granular texture in the medulla of the adrenal a hematoma between the cerebellum and brainstem and degenerative joint disease.

TRAUMA. This 1.5-year-old female gerenuk was found dead in its exhibit area. This animal had been housed with another female gerenuk. Both had been hand raised. The two were placed out on exhibit and both had been in this exhibit before with no complications. The keepers checked the animals every 5-10 minutes. The keepers noted this gerenuk down and found dead. It was transported to the clinic where radiographs determined the cause of death could be trauma-related. At necropsy the gerenuk was in good body condition. There was partial luxation of the atlanto-occipital joint. The intestines appeared congested and attenuated. The first premolar on the left maxillary arcade was loose. There was a 5 mm. in diameter follicle on the right ovary and a 7-8 mm. diameter corpus hemorrhagicum on the left ovary. Sections of heart liver lung kidney and lymph node were frozen for future use if needed.

GASTRITIS PERITONITIS ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 16-year-old female red panda had a history of lethargy and chronic hair loss. Treatment was initiated; however there was little response to therapy and the animal later died. At necropsy the liver was yellow. A moderate quantity of serous fluid was present in the abdomen along with fibrin tags. Three trichobezoars were present in the stomach and a defect was present in the gastric wall covered by omentum.
adult. Weight: 85.9 g.  Euthanased.  Fractured leg.  Cranial haemorrhages.  Splenomegaly .  Pulmonary congestion.

BACTERIAL PLEURITIS WITH SEPSIS CHRONIC ENTEROTYPHLOCOLITIS. This 15.5-year-old male mustached tamarin was recently moved to a new enclosure along with a female. The female died two days ago of undetermined cause and the male appeared normal until being found moribund in mid morning and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed purulent material covering the entire left side of the inner ribcage and lung surface with associated pulmonary emboli and edema. The heart was enlarged pale and had thickened ventricular walls. The mucosa was thickened throughout the gastrointestinal tract and large lymphoid aggregates were noted in the intestine. The cecum was corrugated and had erosions. The mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Multiple white pinpoint foci were on the surface of the liver. The gallbladder was enlarged. The spleen was small with rounded edges and multiple white spots. The adrenals were friable. No retroperitoneal fat was seen.

GRANULOMATOUS STOMATITIS AND OSTEOMYELITIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female blue spiny lizard had a two-day history of inappetence and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed normal fat pads mottled pale liver gravid reproductive tract and osteolysis in the right mandible.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMAS AMYLOIDOSIS SARCOCYSTIS PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS TETRAMERES SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION. This 10-year-old male northern pintail died spontaneously. At necropsy the ventriculus was very thin. The proventriculus had multiple cyst-like structures within the mucosa. There were multiple pinpoint foci in the spleen.

MYELOLIPOMA ATHEROSCLEROSIS URATE STASIS HEPATITIS. This 11-year-old male lovebird was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a large mass was present in the left kidney and extended across the midline to the right kidney.

ACUTE COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE PROBABLE TRAUMA ATHEROSCLEROSIS ESOPHAGEAL/INGLUVIAL NEMATODIASIS (CAPILLARIA). This 4-year-old male prairie chicken died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed no significant lesions and good body condition.

EUTHANASIA SARCOMA (ABDOMEN STOMACH) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 16-year-old male tiger had a history of abdominal distention and inappetence. The animal was anesthetized. A large mass was identified in the abdomen. Exploratory laparotomy revealed disseminated masses throughout the abdomen. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple firm raised nodules were present in the esophagus thoracic wall and on the serosal surface of multiple abdominal organs.

DROWNED CHRONIC COLITIS. This 5-year-old male basilisk was found dead in the pool within its enclosure. It had been found previously in the pool but has survived past episodes. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of serosanguineous fluid in the coelom and three white up to 10 cm. long nematodes in the mouth stomach and coelom.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This approximately 10-month-old lizard was found dead. It was the smallest in the collection and was being raised separately in the hospital after an episode of dehydration and anorexia. It doubled its weight in the hospital so it was returned to the biome two days prior to death. At necropsy there was bile staining on the ventrum. There was purple staining on the ventral neck. The liver was slightly mottled tan/red.

VALVULAR DYSPLASIA CARDIAC FAILURE MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY. This 13-year-old male cottontop tamarin had a normal chest evaluation in July 2013. In late October the animal displayed signs of right arm lameness that did not resolve with supportive care and at that time a heart murmur was noted with cardiac enlargement detected. Ultrasound revealed severe mitral regurgitation and mild tricuspid regurgitation. Supportive care was administered but the animal was subsequently found with openmouthed breathing and died during a brief episode of manual restraint. Necropsy revealed approximately 20 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity. No other gross lesions were seen.

TRAUMA. This 8-year-old male wood duck was reported to have been limping on its right leg. Physical exam revealed bruising of the right wing and luxation of the right knee. The animal was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed displacement of the tibiotarsus and a wound 1 cm. from the femur. Hemorrhage of the skin and muscle was detected in the affected area and also in the cervical region.

TRAUMA PERIRENAL HEMORRHAGE. This 1.5-year-old female kangaroo was found unable to stand with ataxia. Treatment was initiated; however no improvement was noted and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large area of hemorrhage was noted adjacent to the left kidney.

PYELONEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS TRAUMATIC SPINAL CORD LESION ADRENAL MYELOLIPOMA VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female tamarin developed a sudden onset of partial paralysis in both hind limbs with no deep pain to either hind leg and bilateral hyperreflexion. The tail was paralyzed and there was no anal or bladder tone. The animal was euthanized. Necropsy revealed softening of the spinal cord in the thoracolumbar region with possible malacia. The base of the tail was necrotic with periosteal proliferation and periostitis. The colon was flaccid and full of hard fecal balls.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA. This 28-year-old bear had a history of anorexia and renal failure. Clinical response to treatment for renal failure was not seen and the animal was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy there was a large area of dermatitis adjacent to the perineum. Approximately 60% of the liver was effaced by a white firm lobulated mass approximately 20 x 20 cm. in size. Kidneys were bilaterally firm but were of normal size.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female gazelle had a one month history of pneumonia. Pseudomonas aeruginosa was isolated from tracheal washes. The animal was euthanized. Necropsy revealed adhesion in the right lung to the diaphragm and thoracic wall and abscesses present in the left lung. A transudate was present in the uterus.

ALIMENTARY LYMPHOSARCOMA. This female approximately 12-year-old tamarin died. It presented in lateral recumbency. Mucous membranes were very pale. There was severe melena. Treatment was initiated. The tamarin stopped breathing and CPR was performed but she did not recover. A partially eaten dead mouse was found in the exhibit. At necropsy the tamarin was thin. Ribs were prominent. The hair was matted down with bloody fluid. Mucous membranes were pale and tacky. The spleen had some multifocal white plaques. The entire gastrointestinal tract from the stomach to the colon had petechial hemorrhage present with severe deep ulcerations in the mucosa and submucosa of the upper and lower gastrointestinal tract including the jejunum and multiple areas of the colon. Bloody fluid was present throughout the intestines. Kidneys appeared slightly enlarged. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged.

BRONCHIECTASIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA WITH ABSCESSES CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male rabbit has a history of chronic nasal discharge attributed to pasteurellosis and had developed acute dyspnea. Examination identified a thoracic mass and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified thin body condition numerous fibrinous adhesions around the liver kidney and stomach 6 ml. of straw-colored fluid in the abdomen a thick-walled abscess obliterating most of the left lung with adhesion to the ribs diaphragm and pericardium. The right lung was edematous.

SUSPECT MALARIA SUSPECT ASPERGILLOSIS. This 6-year/4-month-old male tern was found dead below lower pool. It seemed fine the day before. The other tern found dead was too autolyzed for submission. At necropsy it was in good nutritional condition. The abdominal air sac was mildly thickened with 6-8 small pinpoint white foci on the surface along the liver. The liver was mildly enlarged. The gall bladder was full. The left thyroid was larger than the right. The lungs were off color and pale tan instead of bright pink. There were bilateral symmetrical friable yellowish nodules externally at the bifurcation of the syrinx. The atria were mottled (dark purple). The adrenals appeared bilaterally enlarged. The kidneys were diffuse pale tan with granular and pitted appearance. The gastrointestinal tract was completely empty. The pancreas was pale white. The muscles of the leg were pale. There was a small 1.5 mm. dark firm nodule in the coelomic membrane on the right side of the body wall.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE WITH PULMONARY MINERALIZATION. This 7-year-old male pigeon had an eight day history of illness and died spontaneously. The bird had been lethargic thin and not flying. The bird during venipuncture. Necropsy revealed thin body condition hemorrhagic lungs that sank in formalin and markedly enlarged pale kidneys.

SHOCK POSSIBLE HYPERTHERMIA BLADDER NEMATODES TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS BRONCHIOLITIS. This 1-year-old female/spayed dumbo rat had been transported with two conspecifics in the same crate to a program. When the staff at the program arrived one hour later all rats were dead. No urine or feces were found in the crate suggesting that the rats died shortly after the trip had started. The rats may have been put too close to a heat duct. Necropsy revealed normal ingesta in the stomach congested lungs that oozed blood on cut surface and advanced autolysis.

CLOACAL POLYP WITH ASSOCIATED PROLAPSE AND SEPSIS. This greater than 7-year-old timber rattlesnake had repeated cloacal prolapse that was reduced surgically but the animal died eight days later. Necropsy revealed a 2 cm. round mass in the wall of the cloaca/rectum and several smaller masses also in the area. The distal colonic mucosa was reddened. The kidneys had tan/white striations.
ACUTE INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This greater than 7-year-old corn snake was found dead. Necropsy revealed numerous ovarian follicles.

PANCREATITIS AND STEATITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male tamarin presented with acute lethargy and weakness with a wound on the dorsal head. The animal was suspected to have fallen when climbing on exhibit. Blood work revealed elevations in renal and hepatic values and a possible irregular mass had been palpated in the abdomen. Supportive care was administered but over the course of treatment appetite and behavior declined. Exploratory surgery was performed and euthanasia was elected prior to recovery. Necropsy revealed dark red lungs a portion of which sank in formalin. The root of the mesentery in the retroperitoneal space was expanded by white/cream firm irregular and lobulated mass that enveloped both kidneys mesentery and the pancreas. Adrenal glands were not identified. The spleen was firmly adhered to the mass. On cut surface the mass was white/tan and firm although in some areas more friable and lamellar.

SEVERE NEPHROSCLEROSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION EUTHANASIA ULCERATIVE ESOPHAGITIS. This 16-year-old female golden lion tamarin had a history of chronic renal failure and was euthanized for declining condition and collapse. At necropsy the animal was thin with muscle wasting. The lungs were moderately nodular. The heart was slightly enlarged. The urinary bladder was distended with chalky urine and both kidneys were small pale tan and pitted. The stomach was slightly erythematous. The pancreas was firm.

XANTHOMATOSIS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEMANGIOMA WITH OSSEOUS METAPLASIA COELOMIC CAVITY. This 13-year-old female copperhead died. It had a history of being fed regurgitating two days later and was found dead the following day. Necropsy suggested fatty liver and a mass of unknown origin cranial to the heart. Intestinal vessels were hyperemic kidneys were dark and there was a slight increase in the rugal folds of the stomach.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This female 16-year-old whistling duck was found dead. There had been an acute onset of aggression from exhibitmates 24 hours earlier although no signs of trauma were noted. Necropsy revealed pale tan kidneys white powdery urate crystals on the pericardium and 30 ml. of clear fluid in the caudal coelomic air sacs.

UROLITHIASIS URINARY BLADDER RUPTURE. This 2-year-old male warthog died two hours after being found recumbent in shock and having bloody urine dripping from the prepuce. At necropsy there was a large amount of fluid and clotted blood in the abdominal cavity. The bladder wall was thickened hemorrhagic and had a large rent with several small uroliths.

SPLENIC HEMATOMA. This 10-year-old teal had a history of cataracts and poor vision. The animal was found dead. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

ENVENOMATION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EPICARDIAL HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 11-year-old male boa constrictor was found dead and may have been envenomated by a pit viper. At necropsy a 10 cm. length of hemorrhage was present in the coelomic cavity extending in both directions from the heart.

MACROHABDUS INFECTION PROVENTRICULAR DYSPLASIA GRANULOMATIOUS ENTERITIS. This approximately 3-year-old male budgie was being treated for chronic macrorhabdiosis. Other budgies in the collection have macrorhabdiosis and intestinal acid-fast bacteria. It is not indicated if the animal died or was euthanized.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE LYMPHOMA. This 15-year-old female chinchilla had been ill for two days and was found dead. Necropsy revealed possible hepatic enlargement and a small mass in the omentum.

DIC GASTROENTERITIS GASTRIC ULCERS SEPSIS HEMOGLOBIN NEPHROSIS GALACTORRHEA UTERINE DYSPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female pygmy goat had a four day history of illness that included hematuria subsequent acute azotemia and renal failure. Radiographs revealed an enlarged vagina and uterus. Abdominal exploratory revealed a small urinary bladder small uterus and ovaries and an enlarged vaginal canal filled with viscous yellow/brown cellular fluid. Ovariohysterectomy was performed but the animal was eventually euthanized due to anuria and worsening renal values. Necropsy revealed mild edema and a mild amount of free fluid in the abdomen attributed to fluid overload associated with anuria. Lungs were edematous and pink foam was in the trachea. The kidneys had marked differences in color contrast between the medulla and cortex. The uterus had a few mildly cystic regions. The vagina had 250 cc. of viscous yellow/brown cellular fluid and the hymen may have been intact (the goat was never bred). The goat had mammary development and thin milk-like substance in the udders since the previous summer although this condition never progressed or resolved.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 4.5-year-old male prairie dog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of weight loss. Blood work revealed renal disease. Laparoscopic examination revealed gray kidneys and pale liver. There were no fat stores.

CLOACAL IMPACTION WITH COLITIS CHRONIC RESPIRATORY DISEASE. This 12-year-old boa was being treated for presumptive pneumonia and was found dead in the morning. The snake had appeared to improve with treatment prior to being found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition desiccated fecal material in the distal colon and no other gross lesions including lung.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 16-year-old female wallaroo suffered a femoral fracture and later died. At necropsy severe dental wear was noted. Multiple cysts were present in the kidneys. A compound fracture was present in the femur.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This greater than 7-year-old chicken presented in mid-March for ataxia abnormal mentation received supportive care but steadily declined over the next four days was unable to stand feed itself or right itself. After being extubated the tip of the tube was noted to be bloody. Due to the declining condition of the bird euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition good postmortem condition bruising over the left inner humerus pulmonary contusions mainly in the right cranial area a mass assumed to be a blood clot in the right ventricle of the heart and a grossly thickened left ventricular wall.

EUTHANASIA MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA PULMONARY METASTASIS SPLENIC INFARCT MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS GASTRIC MUCOSAL HYPERPLASIA. This 19-year-old female lion has a one week history of inappetence and regurgitation. An irregular mass was identified in the mammary gland. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy miliary masses were present in the lung and lymph nodes as well as the liver. A pedunculated mass was present in the stomach.

SCHISTOSOMIASIS NEPHRITIS MYOCARDITIS AND ESOPHAGITIS. This 6-year-old female raccoon was found unresponsive and moribund in its exhibit late in the day. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed firm thick organs and a hard brown grainy liver.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 7-year-old male bat was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a large hematoma was present within the cranium filling the caudal cranial fossa.

Liver (necropsy specimen): Well differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma; biliary cystadenoma; glycogen accumulation Liver (surgical specimen): Pelioid hepatocellular carcinoma; glycogen accumulation Adrenal gland: Cortical hyperplasia Kidney: Moderate multifocal membranous glomerulonephritis; multifocal glomerulosclerosis; multifocal interstitial nephritis Pancreas: Nodular hyperplasia Barbie J. Gadsden; DVM Adrenal gland: Moderate cortical hyperplasia Pancreas: Islet cell vacuolation Comment: No distinct adrenal mass was observed within sections of adrenal gland. Islet cell vacuolation may be seen in cases of diabetes; however; the presence of this lesion alone is not sufficient for a definitive diagnosis of diabetes. Histologic findings must be interpreted with clinical data for a definitive diagnosis. Barbie J. Gadsden; D

EUTHANASIA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS INANITION. This 5-year/6-month-old male gerenuk was humanely euthanized. It had acute renal failure based on azotemia with isosthenuric urine. There was also mild increase in hepatic enzymes. Supportive therapy was given but the gerenuk’s condition rapidly worsened over 72 hours. At necropsy the liver was small and dark purple. It was nodular on the serosal surface. On cut section it appeared mottled and dark. The right kidney was smaller than the left and was irregular in shape. There was approximately 200 ml. of orange tinged fluid in the peritoneal cavity. There was approximately 50 ml of clear yellow pericardial fluid. The lungs were firm and red on cut surface. There was pink frothy material that oozed from the lower airways. The pancreas was dark purple.

EMACIATION NECROULCERATIVE COLITIS EDEMA RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 27-year-old male desert tortoise had multiple limb paresis and was found dead. At necropsy the eyes were sunken no adipose stores were noted the muscles were markedly edematous the atria were distended the liver was dark and congested the walls of the cecum and large intestine were extremely thickened with edema and the mucosa was possibly overlain by a diphtheritic membrane. Kidneys were slightly granular and there was a large amount of free fluid within the coelom.

EUTHANASIA ENDOCARDIOSIS INTERVERTEBRAL DISC DISEASE CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE PAPILLARY NECROSIS BILIARY CYSTADENOMA. This approximately 26-year-old female tiger was humanely euthanized. It was an older cat with long-term intervertebral disc disease. It had a history of right tibial fracture with multiple repairs. It had a recent exacerbation of hind limb ataxia and lameness in the right and left hind legs and also forelimb ataxia. The signs improved with therapy but suddenly worsened again on 3/5/03 in the evening. Radiographs of the spine and right tibia were taken after euthanasia and revealed multiple collapsed intervertebral spaces present in the lumbar thoracic and cervical regions. The tibial fracture site appeared remodeled and stable. At necropsy the mucosa of the stomach was somewhat irregular. The liver was somewhat mottled. One area had cystic degenerative changes present. The mitral and aortic valves had small knob lesions. Both renal cortices were pale yellow/gray. The junction was dark liver colored and the pelvises were full of creamy thick fluid and green debris. Culture was taken of the material. The bladder was full of clear urine.

EUTHANASIA GERIATRIC. This 27-year-old male boa had chronic inappetence weight loss and anemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed yellow 4 mm. nodules in the parenchyma of the pancreas.

BACTERIAL HEPATITIS LYMPHADENITIS PNEUMONIA SHOCK. This 2-year-old male squirrel monkey was found dead. At necropsy the heart was rounded with enlargement of the ventriculus. Fluid was present in the thorax.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS. This greater than 50-year-old flamingo was found dead in the pool. The animal had been examined along with the rest of the flock three days earlier and was clinically normal. Necropsy revealed good body condition no evidence of trauma arteriosclerosis in the great vessels pale kidneys and no other abnormalities.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 4-year-old male cheetah was housed alone and had tested positive for herpes (PCR) and Helicobacter (biopsy). Most recent biopsy results (1/21/99) indicated a grade II chronic lymphoplasmacytic gastritis with fibrosis mucosal atrophy and intralesional Helicobacter sp. The appetite has been inconsistent during the month of June. One day prior to death he came off exhibit and acted alarmed when approaching the bottom of the holding ramp. The cat appeared to develop acute respiratory distress and did not respond to supportive care. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed hemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity splenic capsular fibrosis mucus in the nostrils hemorrhagic fluid in the right lung consolidation of the left lung with multiple areas of firm white nodules foci of pale streaking in the left ventricle lacerations on the lip and tongue ingesta in the esophagus and stomach and caudal enlargement of the esophagus mucosal ulcers in the stomach. A mixed population of bacteria was isolated from the trachea pericardium and stomach.

EMACIATION IRON STORAGE CHRONIC ENTERITIS PARATHYROID CARCINOMA. This 13-year-old male ruddy duck had an acute presentation of lethargy and anorexia and blood work revealed marked anemia and leukocytosis and mild panhypoproteinemia. Supportive care was administered but the bird was eventually euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition.

TRAUMA (FRACTURED VERTEBRAL COLUMN) EUTHANASIA. This 1.5-year-old male wallaby was found near a fence alive but partially paralyzed and radiographs revealed fractured vertebrae. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA HEPATIC ABSCESS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 7-year-old female fruit bat had a history of progressive weakness and was found down. Examination revealed elevation of hepatic values. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin with scant fat depots. An encapsulated mass was present in the right liver. The mass contained a large quantity of thick yellow material.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS FIBRINOUS COELOMITIS AND MENINGITIS. This 21-year-old female Gila monster had a history of coelomitis and transudate/ascites. A retained egg was diagnosed and exploratory surgery for ovariectomy revealed fluid-filled ovaries and degenerative egg yolk masses. Blood work at the time of surgery revealed leukocytosis and anemia. Ovarian and coelomic anaerobic and aerobic cultures revealed no growth. Supportive care was administered postsurgically but the animal did not respond and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 14.5-year-old female false water cobra had been active and eating well. It was found with its head wedged between the water pan and the enclosure wall. Necropsy revealed opaque eyes and brown liver with a nodular pattern throughout the parenchyma with associated adhesions to both pulmonary lobes and the esophagus. Multiple tan nodules were also in the mesentery. Fat deposits were irregular. The spleen was pink/red with a bumpy irregular surface. A small focus of red discoloration was at the apex of the heart. Two mice were in the alimentary tract.

EUTHANASIA CERVICAL TRAUMA. This 9-year-old male gerenuk was humanely euthanized. It was pulled off exhibit the day prior to death due to lameness in left leg. It was suspected of having crashed into a fence. The gerenuk was found recumbent but responsive. Radiographs revealed potential lateral avulsion of C5-C6 causing visible lateral deviation of the cranial cervical area. There was ventral cervical edema and cellulitis. Recovery from anesthesia was very slow and the gerenuk never regained full consciousness despite several unsuccessful attempts to stand. At necropsy the gerenuk was in good body condition.
