There was extensive bruising of the subcutaneous tissues of the cervical area. There was visible lateral left deviation of the cranial cervical area at C5-C6. There was marked thickening of the skin and subcutaneous edema of the ventral cervical mandibular areas. There was moderate congestion and edema of the lungs. The pericardial sac contained approximately 25 ml. of serous fluid. There was mild congestion of cerebral blood vessels. There was no hemorrhage within the brain case or surrounding the spinal cord.

BACTERIAL ORCHITIS AMYLOIDOSIS TRAUMA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 7-year-old male duck presented with depression and regurgitation and was dead upon arrival at the hospital. Necropsy revealed good body condition prominent vasculature and some hemorrhage in the subcutis mild red streaking in the epicardium some possible hemorrhage in the liver prominent mesenteric vasculature moderately enlarged right testicle and some red streaking in the muscle of the legs.

ABDOMINAL ADHESIONS MYOGLOBIN NEPHROSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female pygmy goat had a four-day history of bloating and azotemia and knuckling of the right hind foot. Exploratory laparotomy was performed to check for obstruction and the animal did not regain consciousness following the surgical procedure appeared to be neurologic with muscle twitching and mydriasis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild hyperemia of the luminal mucosa distended abomasum a 2 cm. plaque in the pulmonary artery cranial to the heart empty urinary bladder despite 14 hours of intravascular fluid therapy heavy and wet lungs froth in the airways and edematous kidneys. This animal also had chronic mild to moderate bloat for several years with poor dentition.

EUTHANASIA AMYLOIDOSIS BACTERIAL PODODERMATITIS MINERALIZATION OF BLOOD VESSELS IN BRAIN PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA RENAL GOUT DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE. This 14-year-old male white faced whistling duck had chronic severe right coxofemoral degenerative joint disease resulting in debilitating lameness. Additionally the right distal phalanges were shortened for unknown reasons and affected by proliferative fibrotic tissue causing placement abnormalities. Despite corrective foot surgery involving resection of the foot webbing the use of the right limb worsened and the animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition/nutritional status. Sutures were present in digits #2 3 and 4 and a lack of webbing was noted between these digits corresponding to the described surgical procedure. The distal most phalanx of these three digits was missing and the terminal portions of the existing phalanges are enlarged and fibrotic in appearance. The liver was uniformly large and pale with imprecise large mottled areas of darker discoloration. The kidneys were bilaterally and symmetrically enlarged and pale. The spleen was spherical and 1.5 cm. in diameter. The coxofemoral joints with the associated pelvic region were submitted intact. The affected digits of the right foot are submitted intact as well.

PODODERMATITIS AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This greater than 30-year-old female flamingo was found dead in the flamingo pool. Necropsy revealed bumblefoot lesions on each foot thickened and yellowed right caudal thoracic air sac distention of the gall bladder with normal appearing fluid bilaterally enlarged kidneys necrotic and friable ovary and hemorrhage in the oviduct.
ENTERITIS. This 4-year-old male marmoset was in quarantine. The animal was lethargic and was treated with antibiotics. The animal was found dead. At necropsy fat depots were absent.

CEREBRAL ARTERIOSCLEROSIS THYROID FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA THYROID AMYLOIDOSIS. This 17-year-old female peccary had a history of seizures and severe neurologic disease. At necropsy arteriosclerosis was noted in the great vessels. Kidneys showed evidence of glomerular disease. A mass was identified at the base of the brain. Severe dental disease was present.

XANTHOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female gecko had a history of progressive neurologic disease including right-sided head tilt and ataxia first identified in November 2011. The animal’s neurologic status has been in decline with intention tremors when feeding progressive ataxia and weight loss. Several exams have failed to identify a definitive cause for the neurologic disease which is believed to be central in origin. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a nutmeg appearance in the liver fair body condition and markedly thickened gallbladder wall containing caseated green-gray material.

ASPERGILLOSIS. This 9-month-old rainbow lorikeet was noted to have a one day history of walking more than the other birds rather than flying. It was found on the floor after a crashing noise was heard assuming it had run into a wall. It was treated for head trauma and shock but died. Necropsy revealed a 2 mm. white mass in the left thoracic wall a 1 cm. mass at the heart base enclosing the great vessels consolidated left lung an asymmetrical mass in the distal thorax and an enlarged pale liver.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE SHOCK EMACIATION CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS EROSIVE VENTRICULUS. This 5-year-old domestic chicken has a history of mild neurologic signs that included ataxia but was maintained with medication. The chicken accidentally was left outside overnight and the following morning was slow and shivering but appeared to improve with time. It was found dead in the morning a few days later. Necropsy identified emaciation severe feather mite infestation clear fluid in the pericardial sac subjectively enlarged spleen congested lungs that oozed blood on cut surface dark red to brown fluid within the gastrointestinal tract thin mottled liver that bled on cut surface and subjectively enlarged kidneys.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ENTEROCOLITIS WITH BACTERIAL OVERGROWTH BILATERAL GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS EUTHANASIA. This 27-year-old female squirrel monkey presented with acute respiratory distress and radiographs revealed heart failure. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition (although the animal had good appetite) large amount of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity purple lung that was heavy and sank in formalin mottled purple right lungs that floated in formalin and no other gross abnormalities.

MYCOTIC DERMATITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS CATARACT. This approximately 14-year-old tiger salamander had a several day history of inappetence and bloat and a transudate was aspirated from the coelom. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead. The two other tiger salamanders in the collection are also ill and have different presenting signs but all are approximately 13 years old. Necropsy of this salamander revealed generalized reddening bloody fluid near the cloaca adequate intracoelomic fat stores congested lungs free fluid in a blood clot around the heart mottled liver mucoid fluid in the stomach partially pigmented caudal aspect of the intestine with luminal undigested crickets.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS PULMONARY SHOCK TRAUMA (CONSPECIFIC AGGRESSION). This 5-year-old female capybara had been fighting on previous days was separated with a few facial lacerations collapsed in the yard and died on its return to the zoo. There is a history of baylisascariasis on the zoo grounds. Necropsy revealed abrasions around the face and nose calluses on both elbows froth in the lungs dark purple right lung large adrenal glands with pale cortex and dark purple medulla dark purple spleen and no other abnormalities.

CHRONIC PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS AND CHRONIC PROVENTRICULITIS ADENOMATOUS HYPERPLASIA WITH SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA OF UROPYGIAL GLAND EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old ibis has a chronic history of impacted uropygial gland. Numerous surgical procedures were performed but the bird continued to decline. The bird achieved a point of emaciation with poor feathering condition and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with poor feathering and enlargement with hyperemia of both bulbs of the preening gland.

MENINGOENCEPHALITIS PNEUMONIA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 12-year-old male meerkat presented with lethargy and inappetence with progressive neurologic deficits. Elevations in cholesterol were noted on blood work. The animal was humanely euthanized. Multiple pinpoint white foci were present throughout the liver.

GRANULOMATOUS TRACHEITIS. This 13-year-old male Humboldt penguin has a six month history of inflamed nodular tracheitis and is currently being treated accordingly. A conspecific had similar but more severe lesions and was diagnosed with mycobacteriosis at necropsy. A biopsy from the penguin of this report was obtained from the swollen mucosa just distal to the tracheal bifurcation and this tissue appeared to be infected.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE CIRRHOSIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old hedgehog had a history of congestive heart failure inappetence and lethargy with marked weight loss and exercise intolerance. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged heart with irregular muscle consolidated lungs multiple white masses in the hepatic parenchyma two symmetrical multilobulated masses within the urogenital system and pale kidneys with loss of corticomedullary architecture.

GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA. This 18-year-old female desert tortoise had severe dermatitis with sloughing of the nails skin and beak two years ago. Biopsies at the time suggested vasculitis. The condition improved following intensive therapy. The animal was found dead with recent medical history. At necropsy the lungs were hard and dark. Multiple 1 cm. in diameter pale yellow nodules were scattered throughout the lung effacing approximately 70% of the pulmonary tissue. The coelomic cavity also contained approximately 60 cc. of clear straw colored fluid.

DUCK VIRAL ENTERITIS HEPATITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS BACTEREMIA. This 6-year-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy the body was in good nutritional condition and had generalized vascular congestion. The esophagus intestine and colon contained foul smelling brown fluid. The liver had petechial hemorrhages.

INANITION DERAMTITIS. This approximately 2-month-old male naked mole rat died. The whole litter had died off over time. All were too autolyzed for histopathology except for this animal. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.
adult. Weight: 4200.0 g.  Euthanased.  Osteoarthritis left stifle.  Hepatomegaly with chronic granulomas?  Renal nodules.

TRAUMA ENTRAPMENT EUTHANASIA. While being trapped this 2-month-old female rabbit severed its flexor tendons at the tarsus was dragging the distal limb and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Aside from the leg injury multiple tick nymphs were present in the integument. No visceral lesions were seen.

HEPATIC SINUSOIDAL AMYLOID ACCUMULATION FOCAL HETEROPHILIC KERATITIS. This greater than 10-year-old male hooded merganser previously had a left eye enucleation and chronic orbital infection that appeared to resolve after several weeks of treatment. Prior to death suspected choroidal ulceration was noted on the right eye. Two weeks after treatment acute respiratory abnormalities were noted. The animal died during restraint for treatment. Gross necropsy revealed excellent body condition minimal ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract increased thickness of the gastrointestinal tract a healed left orbit and a small piece of suspected food material lodged in the trachea at the midpoint.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS SHOCK. This 2-year-old female rat was under treatment for dyspnea and weight loss. The animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin.

COAGULOPATHY/DIC POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS VASCULAR DEGENERATION. This 12-year-old male addax presented with signs of abdominal discomfort lethargy and anorexia with decreased fecal output. Evaluation revealed azotemia elevated hepatic enzymes and bilirubin and with hematuria. The animal responded partially to supportive care but presented again a week later with neurologic signs and hypoglycemia with hyperthermia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed inspissated material in the gall bladder and hemorrhage of the serosal surface of the gall bladder endocardiosis and myocardial hemorrhage pulmonary congestion and edema generalized icterus oral ulcer and aspirated material in the trachea.

THYMOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old neutered male pygmy goat had a two-month history of weight loss despite normal appetite lameness in the left front leg of a year’s duration and a several month history of progressive lameness. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified muscle wasting over the spine bridging spondylosis in the thoracic and lumbar spine one liter of serosanguineous fluid in the thorax and a 10 cm. round cavitated mass in the mediastinum.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA BILIARY CYSTADENOMA CYSTITIS EUTHANASIA. This 31-year-old male polar bear had a previously diagnosed hepatocellular adenoma two months before death. He was progressively hyporexic and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. He also had a history of urethral blockage and stranguria. At necropsy there was a large tumor on the liver and scattered tumors throughout other hepatic lobes. Multiple gallbladder stones were present. Additionally there was a firm mass to 4 cm. in diameter in the caudal edge of one hepatic lobe. There was minor arthritis. There is corneal lipidosis bilaterally.

PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA CATARACTS EUTHANASIA. This 27-year-old female guanaco had a history of recent loss of site and disorientation and also had a history of inappetence and muscle wasting in the hind limbs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed points on the teeth gingival erosions and alveolar bone erosions on the molars mild focal eburnation of the stifle joint and a small point of erosion on the joint surface of the patella tan/red mottled liver and a 5 mm. soft mass on the cut surface of the adrenal gland.

GASTRIC PERFORATION. This 11-month-old male zebra was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed a large amount of thick white froth in the nostrils bloated abdomen moderate amount of serosanguineous pleural effusion thick white foamy discharge in the lumen of the upper airways and moderately congested and edematous lungs especially the left lung (animal in right lateral recumbency). A small amount of straw-colored mildly serosanguineous pericardial effusion was noted. Much greenish-tinged straw-colored ascitic fluid was in the caudal abdomen and a large amount of green fluid with food particles was present in the more cranial aspects of the abdomen. All intestines were distended with gas. A rupture was in the caudal third of the stomach associated with thinning of the wall bruising and discoloration of the tissue in this region and a large amount of dry compact food material in the lumen. Multiple foci of superficial erosion or ulceration with erythema were present on serosal surfaces of remaining sections of the stomach. Lesions are limited to the glandular portion of the stomach. Variations in color of the muscle were present especially in the hind limbs with some bundles pale. Some slightly elongated spherical cartilaginous erosions that extend to the bone are present on the medial aspect of both tarsal joints on the metatarsal bone with a compensatory mirror lesion on the opposing tibial bone.

CHRONIC ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS CHRONIC DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA. This 16-year-old male corn snake had a four month history of weight loss and regurgitation with dysecdysis. Necropsy revealed fluid in the lungs. The thyroid was enlarged and there was a 90° kink in the trachea.

CARDIOMYOPATHY STRESS LEUKEMOID REACTION. This greater than 2-year-old male hedgehog died. It was brought to the health center on 1/3 for lethargy dyspnea and covered with Sarcoptes mites. It had a severe crusting dermatitis. Pyrethrins were applied causing a severe comatose condition. The pyrethrins were washed off the skin and the hedgehog was given subcutaneous LRS Lasix dexamethasone thiamin and atropine. It was kept in an oxygen mask for two hours. It was improved on 1/4 but still dyspneic. It ate very little. At necropsy there was congestion in the spleen and liver. Dilated cardiomyopathy was suspected.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA VACUOLAR LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old fennec fox was euthanized due to chronic renal failure. Necropsy revealed pale tan and atrophied kidneys good body condition adequate fat stores and areas of pulmonary edema. Mucosal ulcerations were in the body of the stomach. The liver was mottled with areas of apparent necrosis. Some hyperplasia was noted in the lymph nodes. The cecum was full of ingesta. The kidneys lacked corticomedullary junction and were irregular and tan/brown.

THORACIC HEMORRHAGE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS URATE STASIS INANITION. This 13-year-old male copperhead was found dead. At necropsy a mass was present in the coelomic cavity just caudal to the heart. A large clot of blood was present adjacent to this area. Liver and kidneys were pale.

CARDIAC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 5-year-old male sun bittern was found dead floating in its pool. Necropsy revealed a wet carcass in good nutritional status with an enlarged liver clear fluid in the coelomic cavity edematous purple/red lungs firm lumpy kidneys and firm pale intestinal walls and thickened left ventricular wall.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE PANCREATIC ISLET FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 10-year-old female rock hyrax developed acute respiratory distress and was treated with Lasix. Physical examination was performed two days later and the animal was continued on treatment with Lasix and antibiotics. The animal was found dead approximately one hour following treatment. At necropsy the left lung had foci of emphysema with acute hemorrhage. The heart was enlarged with thickening of the left ventricular free wall.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE ATRIAL THROMBOSIS. This 14-year-old male screech owl fell from its perch after being brought inside in the afternoon. The animal had recovered within a half an hour and was taking food by hand and looked normal at evening check. Necropsy identified slightly thin body condition moderate to severe coelomic distention severe fibrinous coelomitis with pseudomembrane formation thickened membranes and multiple organ adhesions. Approximately 4 ml. of straw-colored fluid was in the coelomic cavity. The heart was slightly enlarged and flaccid. The lungs were dark pink to red and mottled. The liver was firm enlarged and pitted on serosal surfaces with several firm white nodules scattered throughout the parenchyma. White indistinct focal areas of discoloration were along the ventricular surface where it contacted the liver. The intestines were diffusely reddened firm and rigid and mostly devoid of intestinal contents. The kidneys were diffusely darkened. A firm white nodule to 4 mm. in greatest dimension was present in the cranial ventral portion of the left kidney.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA AMYLOIDOSIS. This 6-year-old male black footed ferret had a one day history of neurologic signs that included lethargy and inappetence. Examination revealed dehydration renal failure and leukopenia. The animal was found dead the following day. Necropsy revealed good body condition a moderate amount of tan/red opaque pleural effusion large soft pink mediastinal mass extending from the thoracic inlet to the base of the heart small amount of pericardial effusion moderate amount of tan/red translucent peritoneal effusion and multiple areas of petechiation on the serosal surfaces of the abdominal organs and within the mesenteric and omental fat. The basilar artery of the brain was congested.

CAECAL IMPACTION EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female greater kudu had a history of dystocia in which the calf was easily extracted but did not survive. The dam appeared extremely thin postparturition. The dam was separated for monitoring and was noted to have decreased grain consumption but good hay/browse consumption. The animal became severely dehydrated requiring immobilization three weeks after parturition. Blood work revealed hypocalcemia and anemia. The dam failed to improve substantially so was immobilized again one week later for fluid therapy and diagnostic examination. The animal remained anemic but was normocalcemic. Over the next month the animal was offered various types of grain with intermittent consumption and was observed drinking and appeared to maintain hydration status. Body weight however continued to decline. The animal was immobilized again for diagnostic examination due to muscle wasting and intermittent appetite and was noted to have severe mineral and electrolyte abnormalities and marked hypoglycemia. Supportive care was administered and blood values improved within the next six hours but the animal became unable to stand after reversing the immobilization agent. Blood values returned to pretreatment values the following morning and the animal’s condition had declined further so humane euthanasia was performed. Necropsy identified emaciation subcutaneous fluid accumulation along the ventral abdomen and within the udder a 3 cm. wound on the cranial aspect of the left stifle minor fresh abrasions on the caudal aspects of the elbow and hair epilated easily over the entire body. The trachea contained a large amount of fluid with froth and the lungs were diffusely wet and heavy with marked congestion and edema. A large amount of serous pericardial fluid was present. The liver had diffuse mild congestion. The gallbladder was mildly enlarged but contained normal appearing bile. A few small rocks and sand were in the rumen caudal abomasum and proximal duodenum. The omasum was filled with fibrous ingesta and granular particulates. The jejunum contained thick white mucus. The entire caecal lumen was impacted with hard fibrous food material. These hard contents were coated with a fibrinous and mucoid film. The mucosal surface of the cecum was diffusely injected and mottled. The mucosa of the spiral colon had intermittent bands of congestion. Normal fecal material was noted within the colon and vasculature of the small intestinal tract appeared diffusely congested. The urinary bladder was distended with urine and the uterus was contracted. Severe muscle wasting was noted and mild hemorrhaging was in the thigh musculature in areas of injections. A small amount of serous fluid was noted within the abdominal cavity and marked atrophy of cavitary fat was noted.

EMACIATION. This 11-year-old female ruddy duck was examined two days prior to death and determined to have multiple swellings and ulcerations over the joints of several digits with weight loss and poor body condition. It had a history of decline during its initial period in quarantine and supplemental tube feeding and antibiotics were initiated. The bird regained lost weight and treatment was discontinued. At quarantine exam there was significant weight loss again. Supplemental tube feeding was scheduled to start but the bird was found dead. Necropsy revealed a wet carcass (found dead in pool).

PROBABLE MYCOBACTERIOSIS GRANULOMATOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 4-year-old male saki monkey was being treated for a large wound on the right thigh was having trouble ambulating incurred multiple injuries was thin and had evidence of a large liver lung lesions and moth-eaten tarsi. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple white masses of varying size on the serosal surfaces of the parenchyma in all pulmonary fields in all hepatic lobes in the left kidney and absence of fat.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA COLLOID GOITER. This 14-year-old male pygmy goat developed severe neurologic signs and inability to stand. The animal has a history of anemia a ventral neck mass and weight loss. At necropsy the liver contained a 5 x 3 x 1 cm. area with white to tan streaks within the parenchyma. The left lung had an area of hemorrhage and atelectasis. Numerous adhesions were present in the pleural cavity. The right kidney contained two large infarcts extending from the pelvis to the capsule. Cartilage erosion and osteophyte formation were identified in the hips and stifles. The right thyroid was replaced by a homogeneous gelatinous substance. An 8 x 5 x 4 cm. mass was present in the ventral mediastinum. The mass was firm to gritty with several foci of caseous material.

Oral cavity/lip: Suspected neoplasm COMMENTS: While the oral mass; attached to the upper right lip; is suspected to be a neoplasm; the gross appearance is suggestive of an oral papilloma. To confirm this mass as a neoplasm and to determine its histogenesis; tissues for histopathologic examination are under process. The microscopic findings will be included in the final report. Vinicius S. Carreira; DVM See previous report. Lip: Papilloma Liver: Moderate centrilobular to midzonal hepatic lipidosis Papilloma Hepatic lipidosis COMMENTS: Histopathology confirmed the impression at necropsy that the tumor at the lip was a papilloma; i.e.; a benign tumor that stems from keratinocytes. Hepatic lipidosis is likely due to increased mobilication of fat stores. Vinicius S. Carreira; DVM

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This greater than 10-year-old male Indian peacock died unexpectedly following a brief period of lethargy and drooling. Necropsy revealed petechiae and inflammation at the cecum and colon but no evidence of a foreign body. The liver was small and the heart seemed thickened.

Avian; whole body: Disseminated lymphoma (suspected); Emaciation Comments: The most likely cause for the severe emaciation in this animal was the disseminated neoplastic process observed; most consistent with lymphoma. Microscopic examination of tissues is pending. Various tissues are on hold for additional diagnostic testing (bacteriology; virology; etc.) if warranted. Michael C. Boyle; DVM Spleen; Liver; Bone Marrow; Lung; Kidney; Feathered skin; Right eye: Lymphosarcoma Myocardium: Mild; multifocal and random necrosis Thyroid: Severe; multifocal and coalescing necrotizing thyroiditis Disseminated lymphosarcoma Comments: The various zones and foci of necrosis observed in numerous organs associated with nodules or sheets of neoplastic cells were most likely neoplastic foci which underwent hypoxia and devitalization; or as a result of radiation therapy. Radiation therapy may also have been responsible for the random crypt abscesses in the absence of other gastrointestinal lesions. Infectious causes for the myocardial necrosis are under investigation. No definitive cause for the inflammatory thyroid lesion could be determined. Michael C. Boyle; D Disseminated lymphosarcoma Comments: WNV antigen was not detected in the myocardial lesions. Please see the necropsy final report for more information. Michael C. Boyle; DVM

AMYLOIDOSIS BACTERIAL MYOCARDITIS NEPHRITIS AND HEPATITIS BILIARY CYSTADENOMA MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 6-year-old male ferret was found dead in night enclosure. It had a history of lethargy weight loss shaking and rear limb paralysis. At necropsy the ferret was thin with slight emaciation. There was straw in the oral cavity. The teeth were worn. There was mild to moderate tartar. There were chronic renal changes. The left adrenal gland was plump. There was a cystic mass in the right lateral hepatic lobe and several cystic masses in the left lobe. The lungs were collapsed. Seven different lymph nodes were bilaterally enlarged.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PULMONARY GRANULOMAS. This 5-year-old male African hunting dog died while anesthetized for a root canal dental procedure. Necropsy revealed blood extending from the larynx into the lung filling the upper and lower airways. Kidneys were dark red to purple and the heart was streaked white. The entire small intestine was dark red to purple.

EMACIATION AND DEHYDRATION COLONIC IMPACTION WITH BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 9-month-old female tree boa was in quarantine. It was found moribund and died despite supportive efforts. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and no food in the gastrointestinal tract. A small amount of urates were in the cloaca. The liver was tan and the gall bladder was distended with bile. Ovaries were identified. The pancreas was mildly erythematous.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS ARTICULAR GOUT XANTHOMATOSIS. This 8-year-old male cockatiel had a history of multiple periarticular changes and swelling of the left foot. Uric acid levels were elevated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed decreased pectoral muscle mass and swollen joints.
COELOMITIS AIR SACCULITIS HEPATITIS SALPINGITIS. This 7-year-old female Bali mynah was found dead on the exhibit. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

CARDIOMYOPATHY PNEUMONIA. This 17-year-old male tamarin was found recumbent in its cage after eliciting a loud scream. This tamarin had a history of being hospitalized for presumed liver failure and was diagnosed with probable congestive heart failure. It had been recently started on furosemide and digoxin. At necropsy the heart was somewhat enlarged and occupied 50% of the thoracic cavity. Both auricles were filled with gray/brown masses. Similar masses were present within the right ventricle. There was extreme hypertrophy of the heart muscle. The caudal right lung lobe was brown grayish-red with several white foci. The liver was enlarged and swollen with an uneven surface.

ANESTHETIC DEATH FATTY LIVER HEPATITIS. This female greater than 1-year-old leiothrix died during transfer back into OB187. It had been immobilized for exam and blood collection and never completely recovered. At necropsy the body was slightly autolyzed. There were no significant findings.
EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS SHOCK. This 14-year-old male sheep was humanely euthanized. It had a history of arthritis and problems getting up. At necropsy the small intestine was hemorrhagic.

EUTHANASIA SYSTEMIC ANTIGENIC STIMULATION TRAUMA (PREDATION). This 1-year-old male lory was found injured in the flight cage in the morning with severe trauma to the left leg. Examination revealed that the leg had been chewed off to the level of the body wall likely by a raccoon. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed no other gross lesions and the bird appeared to be in good nutritional status.

PANCREATIC FIBROSIS PROBABLE DIABETES MELLITUS AMYLOIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 7-year-old female rock hyrax had a one day history of illness characterized by thin body condition hypothermia and agonal condition. Resuscitation was not successful. Necropsy revealed multiple retained calcified nodules in the uterus resembling fetal mummies or teratomas serous atrophy of fat gastric ulceration and deep dental caries.
NEPHROSCLEROSIS HEMATOMAS EUTHANSIA. This 12.5-year-old male wolf developed acute renal failure and did not respond to supportive care.

ISLET AND INTERSITITAL FIBROSIS DIABETES MELLITUS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 8-year-old female rock hyrax has a history of cardiac murmur cataracts hepatic enlargement and pulmonary edema. It had a melengestrol acetate implant in December 2001 and had been treated with atropine doxapram and furosemide. The patient died approximately one month after treatment was initiated. Necropsy revealed a large amount of yellow fluid in the abdominal cavity and thoracic cavity. Multiple firm yellow/white irregular ovoid masses were attached to the omentum and mesentery. The liver had rounded edges and a “nutmeg” appearance on cut surface. The spleen contained a smooth round mass protruding from the surface 1.5 cm. in diameter. On cut surface the mass was slightly paler than the spleen. The lungs were slightly firm and consolidated cranially. A large amount of fluid was in the pericardial sac and the heart appeared slightly enlarged. The valve leaflets were thickened. Plaques of white material were detected on the intimal surfaces of the great vessels. The pancreas was smaller than expected.

Kidney: focal cortical cyst Ovary: paraovarian cyst Thoracic cavity: moderate pleural effusion Comments: Overall findings were highly suggestive of hypoproteinemia and poor body condition. Hypoproteinemia is often associated with severe parasitism; however parasites were not observed during the necropsy. Histopathology; virology; bacteriology; nutrition; and parasitology is in progress. Cyst found in the kidney and adjacent to the ovary were incidental findings and were unassociated with the cause of this animal's demise. Schantel A. Hayes; DVM Liver: severe; centrilobular to midzonal necrosis Heart: minimal myofiber degeneration with numerous intracellular protozoa (Sarcocyst) Kidney: multifocal mild interstitial fibrosis with multifocal tubular mineralization Stomach: moderate crypt hyperplasia Comments: The primary cause for hepatic lesions could not be determined histologically however; lesions may represent anemia or acute cardiovascular collapse (heart failure). Another differential is vitamin E and selenium deficiency. To rule out this etiology; liver has been submitted to nutrition. A supplemental report will be released when results are available. Changes in the heart were minimal. There were large numbers of Sarcocyst within myofibers. This finding is generally incidental however; large numbers may impede cardiac conduction and cause cardiovascular compromise. There was no evidence of parasites in sections of stomach or intestine examined however; many coccidial oocyst and trichostrongyles were found in feces submitted to parasitology. The parasite load may have contributed to the long history of diarrhea. Schantel A. Hayes; DVM

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA. This greater than 2-year-old male rat is one of three rats currently being treated for wheezing and respiratory disease. The rat was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed tan firm lungs a 2 cm. hemorrhagic mass in the right cranial lung lobe and no other abnormalities.

MALIGNANT MELANOMA INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 15-year-old female ring-tailed lemur had prior surgeries to remove masses from the thorax. Radiographs revealed pulmonary metastasis. The animal developed progressive labored breathing and weakness. At necropsy the kidneys were irregular. Nodular masses were present on the pericardium and throughout the lung fields. The thoracic cavity contained a large quantity of serous fluid.

SEPSIS HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMAS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 6-year-old male sugar glider had been recently implanted with a microchip. An abscess was noted at the site of the injection. Antibiotics were administered but the lesion became necrotic quickly and skin separated from the underlying tissues. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed grossly enlarged and light tan liver with three parenchymal masses one of which was associated with the gallbladder.
FUNGAL TRACHEITIS INANITION. This captive bred 11-year-old male milksnake was found dead. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

TRAUMA HEMOCHROMATOSIS. This greater than 1-year-old male lory was found on the ground lethargic with heavy breathing mouth gaping and a slight head twitch before dying. At necropsy there was hemorrhage over the caudal cranium and dorsal neck. The bird was in good flesh. There was severe hemorrhage in the neck musculature extending to the vertebrae. The heart had multifocal 1-2 mm. white foci on the pericardium.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 6-year-old male chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the animal was in good condition. Trauma and hemorrhage were present in the cervical region adjacent to C2-C4.

SUPPURATIVE MYOSITIS WITH HEMORRHAGE DROWNED SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 21-year-old female sea lion had a history of bilateral lens removal 2.5 weeks earlier. Postoperatively the animal did not eat well. Supportive care was administered but the animal became increasingly more depressed and inappetent and was found dead in its pool. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a 3.5 cm. round focus of alopecia on the left caudal dorsum a 1 cm. round raised nodule with purulent debris on the left hip fluid exudate on cut surface of the subcutaneous tissue of the ventral abdomen hematoma in the right pectoral muscle containing two liters of blood 5 cm. swelling on the cranial border of the right sixth rib corresponding to a hematoma within the intercostal muscles diffuse serous atrophy of fat congested lungs tiger-striped gallbladder a 15 cm. focus of thickened gray gastric mucosa a 2 cm. mass in the left kidney several small firm nodules around the adrenal glands congested right adrenal medulla a serous fluid-filled cyst in the center of the right ovary and no other abnormalities.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE CEPHALIC THROMBOSIS WITH CEREBELLAR THROMBOSIS (OLD INFRACT) RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 21-year-old male peccary presented with a seizure and had a history of neurologic disease over the past year. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed good body condition adequate adipose stores no external wounds some pulmonary contusions and some emphysematous changes arteriosclerosis in the great vessels food in the alimentary tract mild degenerative changes in the kidneys and no gross lesions in remaining tissues including brain.

MYCOTIC PODODERMATITIS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS BACTERIAL PODODERMATITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND HEPATITIS. This greater than 31-year-old female Chilean flamingo had been segregated due to behavior problems and abnormal feces and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed shrunken white kidneys and uremic frosting of the epicardium hepatic capsule and serosa of the intestine. A 2 cm. thick scab was on the sternum. Bilateral pododermatitis was also noted.

EUTHANASIA PULMONARY EDEMA GLOMERULOSCELROSIS ENTERITIS. This 3-year-old female rock hyrax has never reached normal size. The animal has a history of conjunctivitis. The animal became lethargic and was treated with Baytril for a sinus infection. The condition declined and the animal could no longer right itself and was euthanized. At gross necropsy bilateral lobar pneumonia was diagnosed.

MENINGOENCEPHALITIS TOXOPLASMA IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY. This 2-year-old male sea lion has been off food for approximately 1.5 weeks and was lethargic. A diagnostic workup revealed hyponatremia. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to refuse food and developed a mild head tremor. The animal died and necropsy revealed good body condition. The lungs were dark purple. A small amount of clear yellow abdominal fluid was noted. The brain was congested. The lymph nodes were enlarged in the abdomen.

AMYLOIDOSIS CHOLELITHIASIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 8-year-old male quail was found dead in the morning and had no prior medical history. Necropsy revealed mild feather loss on the dorsal surface of the head consolidated lungs dark friable liver large amount of yellow fluid in the coelom pale kidneys and otherwise good body condition.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) FIBROIDS CATARACT EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female karakul sheep had a history of chronic arthritis and severe decline in overall status over the last few days to weeks with inappetence increased lameness minimal response to therapy increased respiratory effort and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed atrophied muscle but adequate adipose stores severe arthritis in all limbs (particularly the hind limbs) mild amount of fluid in the pericardium all incisors broken or missing and a mild abrasion on the interior aspect of the bottom lip multiple fibroids in the uterus and a moderate amount of gray purulent material within the uterine body and horns.

EMACIATION. This 7.5-year-old female giant eland had been anemic and in poor condition for several months. Supportive care was administered with temporary improvement but the condition then worsened when the treatments were discontinued. The patient had a good appetite despite loss of condition. The eland subsequently died. Necropsy revealed a healed rib fracture in the costochondral region a small amount of serous atrophy of fat congestion in the lungs foam in the distal trachea and large bronchi some thickening of the abomasal outflow tract (possibly normal) mild blunting of the ruminal papillae petechiae in the mucosa of the small intestine large numbers of Trichuris worms in the cecum associated with a single focus of mucosal reddening and a small black raised firm nodule on the surface of one ovary.

EUTHANASIA HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA HEPATIC NECROSIS CHRONIC COLITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 22-year-old male polar bear had a history of weight loss and diarrhea. A suspected abdominal mass was present and biopsies were suggestive of hepatocellular carcinoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large quantity of brown colored pleural effusion was present. An abscess was present in the left canine. Minimal fat depots were present in the abdomen. Foci of necrotic tumor were present throughout the liver.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS MESENTERIC NEMATODE GRANULOMAS RUPTURED OVUM. This approximately 5-year-old female toad developed a swollen coelom three days prior to death. The toad died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed serosanguineous coelomic effusion with numerous miliary white foci in the liver. The ovaries had numerous follicles none of which appeared to be reaching maturity.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC CARCINOMA PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 18-year/5-month-old male leopard was humanely euthanized. It had not eaten since 10/20. It lost 5 lb. since 10/01. It had a history of renal disease and testicular cancer. He was treated with calcitriol. At necropsy the left kidney weighed 67.6 gm. and was 6.5 x 4 cm and the right kidney weighed 59.1 gm. and was 7 x 4.5 cm. There were calculi in the left kidney. The right kidney was smaller in size and paler. The renal pelvis also had calculi. There was no evidence of hydronephrosis. There was white streaking of the cortex of the right kidney. There was a small area of pale discoloration in the center of the left testis. There was 3.25 x 2.5 cm. mass in the liver. The mass was irregular tan round and was in the caudal right liver lobe. The spleen had slightly rounded edges. The right thyroid on the surface had tan discoloration and a circular 2 mm. mass. The lungs had miliary firm nodules that felt calcified and were in a linear pattern. The right side of the heart was slightly dilated. The left ventricular wall measured 1.5 cm. thick. The right ventricular wall was 0.2 cm. thick. The leopard was in generally thin body condition with an unthrifty appearance. Renal concretions were submitted for analysis.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL ABSCESSES AMYLOIDOSIS. This 6-year-old female pintail was found dead. It had a history of intermittent mild lameness. Necropsy revealed an enlarged and obstructed left cecum approximately 10x larger than the right cecum. The liver was friable. The head of the right femur was eroded and an abscess was observed in the cranial pole of the right kidney possibly pressing on the sacral nerve plexus.

EMACIATION VENTRICULAR AND ESOPHAGEAL CANDIDIASIS EGG YOLK COELOMITIS VALVULAR MINERALIZATION PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 13-year-old female wild turkey was lethargic for approximately five days. Blood work revealed dehydration anemia and leukocytosis. The animal also had a heart murmur. The animal was given supportive care and was found dead. At necropsy there was severe muscle wasting. The coelomic cavity contained abundant white to yellow fibrous material that adhered numerous coelomic organs to each other. Cardiac valve leaflets had pinpoint white nodules. The ovary had many large follicles.

EMACIATION DROWNED. This 5-year-old male ruddy duck was in quarantine and had lost approximately 10% of its body weight over a ten day period and also has moderate bumblefoot lesions that started less than seven days earlier. The bird was bright alert and observed eating the evening prior to being found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed congested liver and lungs mottled intestines with thin walls and dark segments.

UNDIFFERENTIATED SARCOMA (LUNG) HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS INANITION. This 18-year-old female mynah has a history of blindness and weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy feathers were missing from the dorsal skull and cervical region. The keel was prominent. The right lung contained a well circumscribed soft pink homogeneous mass.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS. This 13-year/6-month-old neutered male impala was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic arthritis. It had a hunched back and was dropped down in its back legs. It was emaciated. It had some improvement on Flunixin. At necropsy the front hooves were slightly overgrown. There was malocclusion of the right cheek teeth. There was erosion of the articular cartilage of the left hip and both carpi. The left carpus would flex only half the normal range of motion. Both carpi had severe osteophyte formation and partial ankylosis. There was a 3 cm. walled off abscess in the liver that contained dry yellow/green material.

SEPTICEMIA NEPHRITIS MYOCARDITIS HEPATITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA SPLENIC INFARCT SUSPECT SPLENIC HEMANGIOMA. This 1.5-year-old female hedgehog was found dead in enclosure. At necropsy there was a large splenic mass adhered to the adjoining intestine. There was visible intestinal necrosis. The kidneys were mottled. The adrenals were large. There were ecchymotic lesions found scattered about the lungs. There were hepatic masses. There was adequate body condition. The heart was enlarged.

CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 7-year-old female meerkat was found dead at morning check and had no prior signs of illness. It had access to heat and shelter overnight and was housed with one female meerkat that appears normal. Necropsy revealed a large quantity of intra-abdominal fat a small cystic lesion on the right capsule of the kidney two small clear cysts at the apex of the urinary bladder and a 5 cm. focus of large intestinal congestion.

ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male panda developed progressive central nervous system disease with ileus and an inability to stand and raise its head. It appeared aggressive which was unusual for this animal. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed impacted anal glands hepatic fibrosis and necrosis pulmonary atelectasis and congestion congestion in the meninges of the brain and two small round brown masses near the pancreas and mesentery and one at the base of the aorta. The large colon had ileus.

EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS SEIZURE DISORDER. This 15-year-old female tiger developed spontaneous seizure activity while on exhibit especially when waking up from sleeping. The cat would turn in circles and then lay on her side and paddle. The animal arrested and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed well hydrated and good body condition some nodular lesions on the edges on the atrioventricular valves a small amount of blood in the pericardium linear congestion in the lungs corresponding to the arrangement of the ribs gastric distention with gas and the colon and rectum were intermittently distended with gas. The pancreas and liver were diffusely congested. Subcapsular hemorrhage was in the right kidney and the left renal pelvis was moderately dilated. A 5 mm. cream-colored soft mass was in the right uterine horn. The right occipital lobe of the brain was reddened especially in the sulci and associated with a white/tan exudate in some of the sulci. The right occipital lobe was palpably firmer than the contralateral lobe.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA HEPATIC FIBROSIS RENAL MINERALIZATION STEATITIS. This 8.5-year-old male hyrax had been under treatment for congestive heart failure. The animal’s condition rapidly declined and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy thoracic lymph nodes were prominent and edematous. Edema and congestion were noted in the lungs. The left ventricle was dilated with thinning of the free wall. AV and aortic valve cusps were thickened and a raised white plaque was present in the aorta. Marked thinning is noted in the apex of the right ventricular free wall. Cataracts were noted bilaterally.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY THROMBOSIS RENAL FIBROSIS. This 18-year-old male river otter had a history of intervertebral disk disease with paresis of the hind limbs. The paresis worsened and a seizure-like episode was noted and the animal was euthanized. At necropsy abrasions were noted on the hind limbs and tail secondary to the paresis. The elbow joints had severe periarticular osteophytes with roughening of the articular surface. Gross examination of the heart by Dr. Garner revealed moderate left ventricular dilatative cardiomyopathy.

TRAUMA DERMATITIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION. This 2.5-year-old lizard was trapped behind a rock on the exhibit for approximately 24 hours. The animal was treated with fluids steroids and antibiotics but continued to do poorly. Several digits were injured. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor condition. At necropsy lungs were collapsed and congested. Trauma was noted in the rear limb.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE THYROID FOLLICULAR TUMOR. This 10-year-old male agouti had a one month history of hair loss over the dorsum progressively worsening. It was immobilized for castration and died during the anesthetic procedure. Necropsy revealed large adrenal glands congested lungs lobulated appearance to both kidneys the right worse than the left.

BACTERIAL VASCULITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 10-year-old male tiger ratsnake had a 3-4 month history of tail lesions that responded to supportive care although one lesion persisted. The lesion was periodically infected with maggots but would resolve with treatment. A prolapsed hemipene was amputated on 10/25 and microscopic examination of the amputated hemipene suggested vasculitis (G10-5610). Shortly thereafter the snake died. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the cranial third of the body and a large blood clot along the cranial aspect of the body.

RENAL NEMATODIASIS COELOMIC NEMATODIASIS INANITION. This 13-year-old bullfrog was found dead. The animal had a recent history of lacerations on the bottom of both forelimbs. At necropsy petechial hemorrhages were present in the ventral caudal abdomen and ventral hind limbs. There was a large quantity of edema over the entire body and large amount of ascites. The spleen contained a 5 mm. round lobulated mass. A cyst was present on the serosa of the stomach with numerous hard black objects embedded in the serosa. A 1.5 cm. round mass was present in the anterior right kidney.

HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE HEPATITIS GRANULOMATOUS SPLENITIS PROVENTRICULAR ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK. This 5-year-old male rhea had a one week history of an abscess in the wall of the proventriculus. The animal had been under treatment and clinical improvement was noted; however the animal was found dead. At necropsy kidneys were friable.

Right eye: Narrowing and descemetization of the ciliary cleft Segmental pre-iridal fibrovascular membrane with inferior ectropion uvea Lens luxation and moderate cortical cataractous change Inner to full thickness retinal atrophy; and segmental detachment Marked optic nerve atrophy; rarefaction; and gliosis Corneal edema; epithelial hyperplasia; parakeratosis; and fibrosis Focal staphyloma and fibrosis Comment Overall; the described histologic findings are consistent with chronic severe glaucoma; however; the exact cause of glaucoma is difficult to determine based on histologic findings. The ciliary cleft was diffusely narrowed; and endothelium and associated Descemet's membrane extended deep within the ciliary cleft. While it could be speculated that this contributed to glaucoma; this cannot be definitively confirmed as the singular cause of glaucoma. The ciliary cleft was otherwise not obstructed and there was no overt neoplastic population; evidence of active inflammatory process; or infectious agent within the examined sections. The focal peripheral area of corneal epithelial disruption and fibrosis dissecting under Descemet's membrane is of unknown significance; but likely represents a focus of scarring possibly related to prior corneal disease or trauma. Katie Barnes; DVM

ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male corn snake had a history of cataracts and arthritis and had recently become inappetent. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed striated fragile kidneys and good body condition.

LYMPHOMA. This male 8.5-year-old teal was found dead under bush on side of shelter #2. It had no previous clinical signs. At necropsy the duck was in fair to good nutritional condition. Skin on the feet was white. All internal organs were pale. The caudal aspect of the lung lobes were red/purple and wet. They oozed blood. The caudal thoracic air sacs and abdominal air sacs were filled with blood clots. There was no food present in the proventriculus and ventriculus. There was a small amount of digested food present in the remainder of the gastrointestinal tract. The liver was pale and grossly enlarged. The right kidney was surrounded by blood clots. The spleen was surrounded by a blood clot. Sections of heart kidney and brain were submitted for West Nile virus testing.

CERVICAL FRACTURE RENAL MYXOSPORIDIOSIS. This 2-year-old female wallaby jumped up and fractured its cervical (atlas) vertebra and died despite CPR. At necropsy there was extensive hemorrhage in the muscles and subcutaneous tissues in the cervical region. Segmental portions of small intestine were black and friable. The kidneys appeared dark brown. The body of the atlas was fractured. There was hemorrhage in the surrounding muscles. Sections of heart lung mesenteric lymph node kidney liver and spleen were frozen for future use if needed.

SHOCK. This female 6-year-old wallaroo was found dead. At necropsy the left lung was very congested and the right lung was mildly congested. The trachea and lungs were hyperemic. The left kidney had a shrunken surface and it was irregular. On cut section there were infarcts. There was a gritty texture to the kidney. There was at least one calcium nodule in the renal pelvis. The thymus appeared large for an animal of this age and size (4 cm. in diameter). There was hemorrhage and edema fluid in the left chest wall.

SYSTEMIC ACARIASIS RENAL TREMATODIASIS. This 8-year-old male ocellated turkey presented as an emergency was unable to walk upright had gurgly pulmonary sounds and fluid from its mouth as well as diarrhea. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed a prominent keel food in the oral cavity and feces/urates along the tail. The serosal surface of the heart had white striations. The ventriculus was empty. Male reproductive tract was identified.

EUTHANASIA MYOSITIS MYOCARDITIS. This approximately 6-month-old female sheep was humanely euthanized. It was suspect positive on TB test on caudal fold. Sections of lymph node were submitted for tuberculosis screening. At necropsy there were no gross lesions.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE THYROID FOLLICULAR ADENOMA. This 14-year-old female arctic wolf has a three day history of progressive ataxia and incoordination to the point of falling and has become progressively inactive since the exhibitmate was euthanized due to heart failure four weeks earlier. Euthanasia of the female was subsequently performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

RENAL FIBROSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 9-year/6-month-old female chinchilla died. It had mild renal failure. It presented lethargic. At necropsy there was a small amount of dark bloody fluid within the abdominal cavity. Mesenteric adipose tissue was bright yellow. The liver was pale tan and friable. The right lung was very congested. The ventricular wall of the heart seemed thicker than normal. Both kidneys were smaller than normal and had an irregular capsular surface. On cut section the cortices were very thin.
juvenile. Weight: 8.1 g.  Euthanaised; ranial haemorrhge linear (focal). Fighting injury; suspect.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 16-year-old female tree kangaroo had a history of pyelonephritis and peritonitis. The animal recovered however persistent elevations of BUN and creatinine were noted. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the kidneys were irregular and cystic. The animal had also previously been diagnosed with mycobacteriosis (M. avium).

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE AXONAL DEGENERATION STRESS EUTHANASIA CRANIAL COELOMIC TUMOR (RESEMBLING GANGLIONEUROMA). This 19-year-old male boa had a history of poor husbandry hypothermia lack of proper lighting and inappropriate diet. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified blistered skin with clear green serous fluid thick lung with few white foci a whitish-tan irregular mass cranial to the thyroid a small amount of dark fluid inside the mass atrophied testicles thickened and irregular vertebral bodies in several segments of the caudal spine and no other gross abnormalities.

SYSTEMIC ABSCESSES. This approximately 8-year-old male sheep has had a cough for approximately three years. Tracheal culture and sensitivity and blood work in 1998 were within normal limits. The animal was euthanized for humane reasons following radiographic evidence of multiple lung masses. Necropsy revealed masses throughout the lungs spleen pericardial sac liver exudate in the airways serosanguineous fluid in the peritoneum serous fluid in the pericardium white plaques in the epicardium and petechiae on the epicardium thickening of the AV valves osteoarthrosis of the coxofemoral joints and an ulcer on the prepuce. Lung cultures were obtained. Analysis of pericardial fluid revealed a possible mesothelioma based on cytologic evaluation.

PARASITE TRACT PROBABLE BAYLISASCARIASIS BRAIN EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female lorikeet had a one month history of neurologic signs and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed loss of feathers on the body good body condition and male reproductive tract.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 5-year-old female burrowing owl had a prolonged history of intermittent weight loss a coelomic wall hernia that was surgically repaired two months earlier improvement in weight gain following the surgery but in the last two weeks the bird had dropped 15% of its body weight. Blood work identified heterophilia with toxic changes. Supportive care was administered and appetite remained adequate but weight loss persisted. The bird was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition subcutaneous bruising in the inguinal area an adhesion between the ventriculus loops of the small intestine and the previous hernia site multiple wispy white lesions on the surface of the liver slightly gritty white material on the surfaces of the pericardium and epicardium bilaterally enlarged pale and irregular kidneys and subjectively thin walled ventriculus.

GASTRIC ADENOCARCINOMA. This 11-year-old female darma wallaby was found dead and had no prior medical problems. Necropsy revealed enlarged adrenal glands a mild infarct in the right kidney congested lungs a large left thyroid and petechiae throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

Body as a whole (both mice): Marked to severe autolysis Comments Gross postmortem examination of the submitted mice did not reveal any significant lesions to provide a clear cause for the described clinical illness; however; critical gross examination was impaired by advanced autolytic changes in both animals. Due to the extensive diagnostic testing already performed on this colony and the lack of significant gross lesions; further diagnostic testing (i.e.; virology & bacteriology) is not being pursued at this time. However; select frozen specimens have been saved if additional testing is warranted. Histopathologic evaluation of the submitted specimens will be sent in a final report. Heather Tillman; DVM Middle ear (one mouse): Mild suppurative otitis media Oral tissue; gingival sulcus (both mice): Moderate; multifocal; suppurative periodontitis; with intralesional foreign material (impacted hair) Stomach; non-glandular portion: Moderate squamous hyperplasia Cause of death undetermined based on gross and histopathologic examination Periodonitis with hair impaction Otitis media Comments Both gross and histopathologic examination of the submitted mice did not provide a cause for the described clinical illness and death. The otitis media; periodontitis; and gastric squamous mucosal hyperplasia are relatively mild and considered incidental findings. There is no overt evidence of a neoplastic or infectious process within these animals; however; advanced autolysis of both mice may have precluded identification of subtle alterations. If losses in the colony continue; submission of these animals is warranted. Heather Tillman; DVM

HEPATIC ADENOMA HEMATOMA (LIVER) SHOCK. This 19-year-old male owl has a chronic history of elevated hepatic enzymes. The animal has been losing weight despite a good appetite. The animal was found in sternal recumbency and died that same day. At necropsy the bird was thin with marked muscle wasting. Multiple white plaque-like lesions were present in the caudal thoracic and abdominal air sacs. The liver was markedly enlarged and contained a 2.5 cm. white mass. The mass contained multiple cavitated areas filled with blood. Bilateral cataracts were present.

ENTERITIS INANITION. This 1-year-old male snake was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy moderate edema was present adjacent to the heart and lung. A mass of ingesta within the ileum contains a small bone which appears to perforate through the intestine. Two small nodular lesions are present in the distal coelom which contain tan caseous material.

RETINAL DEGENERATION RENAL PAPILLARY NECROSIS PULMONARY AND MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 19-year-old male tiger had a long history of intermittent vomiting retinal atrophy lymphocytic/plasmacytic gastritis loss of muscle mass intermittent ataxia recent weight loss and vomiting. The animal was anesthetized for examination and a hiatal hernia was identified as well as some mild renal cysts. The animal was being returned to its building for recovery and developed cardiopulmonary arrest. It could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed thin to good body condition multiple firm nodules firmly adhered to the pleural wall of the chest and caudal lobe of the left lung large area of emphysema and possible consolidation of the edges of the lungs. Mild valvular thickening was noted in both chambers of the heart. The entire gastrointestinal tract from esophagus to colon demonstrates varying degrees of severity of chronic inflammation with thickening of the walls congestion and reddening and a diphtheritic membrane in the walls of the jejunum. On cut surface the kidneys had a grainy appearance in the cortex and some small renal cysts were noted. The liver was swollen along the capsular edges and the adrenal glands were firm.

GRANULOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old turkey is one of a group of eight specimens. Two have died due to mycobacteriosis. The remaining birds were euthanized. White granulomas were observed in multiple internal organs.

INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA SCLEROSING PERITONITIS. This 16-year-old female African lion has a two-year history of intermittent bouts of lethargy and inappetence with reduced appetite nausea and vomiting and refusal to ship normally between exhibit and night house. Endoscopic biopsies of stomach were histologically within normal limits (G16-0720). Since the time of the biopsy the cat continued to lose weight and had bouts of inappetence. Ultrasound and radiographs identified a mass in the small intestine and exploratory surgery revealed an 8 cm. mass in the duodenum associated with partial obstruction. Surrounding lymph nodes were enlarged and structures resembling metastatic foci were in the surrounding mesentery. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA CAPRINE ARTHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 12-year-old female goat was humanely euthanized due to crippling arthritis. It had caprine arthritis encephalitis (CAE). At necropsy there was a ventral nodular patchy consolidation of both lungs.

DENTAL OSTEOMYELITIS AND PULPITIS WITH SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old silver fox rabbit developed ileus after it moved to a new enclosure. Examination was unremarkable and supportive care was administered but during the course of hospitalization the rabbit developed increased respiratory effort and severe facial swelling attributed to abscess formation. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition and good postmortem condition the left side of the face was markedly swollen extending from the orbit to the ventral mandible. No external wounds were noted. No dental or gingival lesions were noted although a focus of ecchymoses was on the left side of the soft palate. Internal examination revealed deep pockets of purulent material extending into the temporomandibular joint and ventral to the mandible. Both lungs were mottled dark red/pink and some sections did not float in formalin. The left cranial lung had a focus of gray/tan firm parenchyma. The liver had a 3-4 mm. white firm and somewhat cystic mass.
adult. Weight: 70000.0 g.  Open; Dental Attrition; poor gastro intestinal content - low fibre.

PULMONARY ABSCESS NEPHROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ABOMASITIS NECROTIZING STEATITIS EUTHANSIA. This 12-year-old female gazelle initially was treated for facial swelling and weight loss had a tooth extraction with follow-up supportive care but its weight continued to decline and respirations became labored. Chronic pneumonia was suspected and the animal received supportive care for this condition. The animal’s condition continued to decline and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachectic body condition uremic odor to the carcass multiple small white linear streaks in the abdominal membranes adhesion of the left lung to the thoracic wall a 10 cm. gray to black abscess in the region of the adhesion with a liquefied center and a foul odor and firm dark red parenchyma in the left and right cranial pulmonary lobes with multiple 1-2 mm. white to yellow foci. The renal cortex was pale yellow to tan and the capsular surfaces of the kidneys were irregular.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 5-year-old female greater kudu had a several week history of bloody mucous diarrhea head tremors reduced activity level and possibly opisthotonos. Necropsy revealed a bloody discharge from the rectum hyperemic mucous membranes thin body condition congested lungs one adluminal and reticular papilla reddened gastrointestinal tract bloody diarrhea in the small intestine and proliferative/granulomatous lesions along the mucosa of the alimentary tract. Bacterial cultures were obtained of the cecal contents liver and lung.

STRESS MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE STEATOSIS INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS LEG TRAUMA. This 28-year-old male Chilean flamingo developed a sudden onset of leg weakness and lameness and could not stand. It was managed in a sling for 10 days and otherwise appeared clinically normal until the last three days when it became depressed. It died overnight. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no external lesions other than minor abrasions to the carpi on the right proximal tibia. Raised orange plaques were present on the thoracic and abdominal aorta and in the left branch of the iliac bifurcation. The dorsal portions of the lungs were congested a 5 mm. raised mass was present in the left caudal thoracic air sac and no gross abnormalities were noted in the joints or muscles of the left leg.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS MINERALIZATION OF GREAT VESSELS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 6-year-old male green crested basilisk had a history of blindness associated with cloudy corneas. The condition did not respond to treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS SPLENIC LIPIDOSIS. This greater than 5-year-old female lorikeet has a history of conspecific trauma and blood work revealed hypoalbuminemia and increased serum AST. The bird was unable to use its rear legs. Exploratory surgery was performed and revealed clear yellow fluid in the air sacs and coelomic cavity pale liver with circular and irregular patches of discoloration and with irregular surface. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed marked renomegaly and cysts masses and patches of discoloration in the liver. The spleen also appeared enlarged and the lung was congested.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS. This 16-year-old female ibex was humanely euthanized. It was a geriatric animal that had a history of progressive lameness in the left rear limb. Over the past two months the ibex was favoring the right front limb. At necropsy the ibex was in fair body condition with adequate fat stores. There was a 1 cm. round cyst in the right kidney. The hock and stifle joints of the hind limbs had significant erosions and deterioration of the cartilage and irregular fibrocartilaginous growths.

PULMONARY GRANULOMATOSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS AMYLOIDOSIS OVIDUCT CYSTS. This 28.5-year-old female Humboldt penguin became inappetent and lethargic over a two-day interval and examination revealed multiple foci of consolidation in the pulmonary fields and air sacs with associated leukocytosis. Supportive care was administered but the patient was found dead on day #3. Necropsy identified plaques on the air sacs nodules in the lungs mucus in the stomach enlarged pale kidneys and inactive ovary.

ANEMIA. This 2-year-old male lory was found dead on the ground. At necropsy there were maggots present. There was no evidence of trauma. The liver was pale. The lungs were white. The lory appeared anemic but there was no evidence of acute blood loss. The kidneys were pale tan. There was a large amount of gas and dark black substance in the gastrointestinal tract.

Liver: Severe chronic necrotizing and suppurative hepatitis with granulation tissue and bile duct hyperplasia Ovaries: Bilateral cystic rete ovarii Uterus: Cystic endometrial hyperplasia; Endometrial carcinoma Comment: A cause of the hepatitis is not evident in the sections examined; however; bacterial culture of liver would be recommended if tissue is still in hand. A possible hepatic carcinoma underlying the inflammation cannot be ruled out in this case either; though this seems less likely. The ovarian tumors are common in guinea pigs; however; the uterine tumor is more unusual. This neoplasm does not appear to have metastasized at the time of necropsy.

GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 15-year-old female eastern screech owl had a five-day history of labored breathing received antifungal therapy and improved with medication. The bird also had a markedly elevated white blood cell count. The bird then developed a one-day history of inappetence and died. Necropsy revealed pulmonary edema ascites hepatomegaly cardiomegaly and enlarged kidneys.

BACTERIAL SPLENITIS BACTEREMIA. This 3-year-old female monitor was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a small quantity of foul smelling fluid was present in the oral cavity. The peritoneal cavity was distended with gas. Gas bubbles were present in the serosa of most internal organs. The ovaries contained numerous developing ova.

adult. Weight: 3900.0 g.  Euth. Hepato and Splenomegaly. Generalised congestion. Avian malaria; chronic; suspect. Mild nodular thickening; left AV valve and aortic valve. Air sacculitits and coelomitis; chronic; suspect. Focal air sac nodule (granuloma).

HEPATOCELLULAR IRON STORAGE DISEASE. This 24-year-old male lemur became acutely lethargic in the morning and examination while anesthetized revealed yellow sclera a large abdominal mass with palpable fluid wave elevated packed cell volume and ultrasonographic evidence of a large irregular hepatic mass. Numerous large cystic structures containing fluid were in the right hepatic lobe and free fluid was noted throughout the abdomen. Abdominocentesis revealed frank blood. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed severe dental attrition hemorrhage and light brown fluid within the pulmonary tissue and pericardial sac a large amount of unclotted frank blood in the abdominal cavity a large irregular multinodular and multicavitated mass that was present throughout the hepatic lobes encompassing approximately 95% of the liver and 12 cm. in greatest dimension. A loop of small intestine appeared to enter and communicate with the hepatic mass and an intussusception was noted within a different portion of the small intestine. The small intestines were thickened and had injected serosal vessels. Two small nodules were on the longitudinal surface of the spleen.

AUTOLYZED TISSUE (POSSIBLE ABSENCE OF FIXATIVE) EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male rat had a history of dyspnea that did not respond to antibiotics and had become inappetent. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple focal scars and nodules in the lung.

SEPSIS. This approximately 1-year-old blue spiny lizard was found lethargic in the enclosure. It had been seen eating recently. The animal was moribund upon presentation. The animal did not respond to supportive care or to resuscitation attempts. Necropsy revealed good body condition and mild fatty change in the liver.

GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS HEPATIC MELANOSIS. This 16-year-old male gecko was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the animal was thin and bilateral cataracts were noted. The GI tract was dark brown to black and had a strong odor. Tissues were friable and autolyzed. Three distinct nodules were identified within the liver.

NASAL ADENDOCARCINOMA. Periodic seizures for 3 years. At gross necropsy there was a large multilobulated fibrous mass in the frontal sinus/olfactory area of the cranium possibly penetrating the cribiform plate.

ISLET ADENOMA PARATHYROID ADENOMA METASTATIC ROUND CELL TUMOR TO BRAIN NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male cheetah had a history of hiatal hernia and chronic renal failure with enucleation of one eye. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dried urine on the hindquarters hard dry black feces in the stall areas of consolidation and mineralization in the lungs globoid heart with thickened left ventricular wall and arteriosclerosis hiatal hernia with one-quarter of the total gastric volume within the thoracic cavity fibrosis around the hiatal opening inability to reduce the hernia normal gastric mucosa with one small fibrotic area possibly representing healed gastric ulcer diphtheritic membrane on the mucosal surfaces of the duodenum and ileum markedly thickened bladder wall and rounded small kidneys. Multiple white nodules are present throughout the spleen and both thyroid glands are reduced in size and cystic. The remaining eye was grossly unremarkable. The cat also had a history of intermittent seizures of 1-2 months duration but the brain was grossly normal.

AMYLOIDOSIS CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY DIC COLLOID GOITER CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE. This 10-year-old male pygmy marmoset had a history of liver disease and hepatomegaly. It developed a less than eight hour duration of posterior paresis and one episode of spontaneous tail movement. No reflexes pain or anal tone were noted. Necropsy revealed enlarged cervical and left axillary lymph nodes containing white foci. The mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and dark brown. The lungs had ecchymoses. The heart was enlarged and the pericardium was adhered to the left thorax. Foci of white discoloration were in the ileum and cecum. Adrenals were enlarged. The liver was enlarged with a reticulated appearance and multiple white foci. The urinary bladder was distended.

CARDIOMYOPATHY ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male meerkat had a one day history of vomiting whimpering ataxic behavior and separating itself from the group. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not recover from anesthesia and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a thin flaccid right ventricle and petechiae on the cranial third of the gastric mucosa. A large amount of intra-abdominal fat was noted.

FATTY LIVER. This 3-year/3-month-old female degu was found lethargic and was taken to the clinic and treated with fluids B vitamins vitamin C and antibiotics and died overnight in incubator. At necropsy there was one area of bruising on the inside surface of the skin near the chest on the right side. The liver was extremely pale enlarged and friable. The right kidney was friable.

LEUKOENCEPHALOMALACIA EROSIVE TYPHLITIS WITH HEMORRHAGE AND PROBABLE ENTEROTOXEMIA. This 1-year-old male cottontail rabbit was found dead with no history of illness. It had been housed in an outdoor pen for breeding purposes and was found dead with evidence of hemorrhagic diarrhea. Fecal parasite exam revealed rare coccidia and tapeworm ova. Necropsy revealed hemorrhagic diarrhea around the perineum. Lungs were pink to dark red. The duodenum contained an adult tapeworm. The cecum and colon had dark brown/red liquid fecal material with no formed fecal balls present. The serosal surface of the proximal cecum and colon were dark red.

CERVICAL ABSCESS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 2-year-old female bat had metabolic bone disease as a juvenile with associated curled wing bones. There is no history of metabolic bone disease in the rest of the colony. The bat had an inverted calcium/phosphorus ratio with severely elevated phosphorus but normal PTH when clinical. Supportive care was administered and the bat recovered but the wings remained curled. The bat had been housed in an incubator with one other handicapped bat.
