It was found with a ruptured abscess on the neck and died while anesthetized to remove the abscess. It had lost 35 gm. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a 2 cm. abscess in the front of the neck with associated ulceration curling of P2-P3 involving all digits possible slight splenic enlargement absence of mandibular canines associated with a chronic chin lesion and prominent adrenals.

HEPATITIS COELOMITIS ENTERITIS AIR SACCULITIS. This 3-year/1-month-old female lory was found dead. The bird was found on the ground cold and depressed and was treated. At necropsy there was mild erythema of the pancreas.

ENCEPHALITIS (BAYLISASCARIS-LIKE) EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female lorikeet had a two-week history of neurologic signs that included ataxia and unsteadiness on its perch. It had tested positive for avian bornavirus from blood and choanal/cloacal swabs one month earlier. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition hemorrhage on the right side of the pleural cavity female reproductive tract and a few foci of hemorrhage in the calvarium.

RIGHT ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA SMALL CELL LYMPHOMA GASTROENTERITIS POSSIBLE AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7-year-old male ferret was being treated for presumptive dilated cardiomyopathy and had a recent history of progressive weight gain with polyuria and polydipsia and increased respiratory effort. Physical examination revealed a large abdominal mass and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed obesity dermatitis over the dorsum right adrenal gland tumor right renal infarct metastatic tumor in the liver nodules in the lung and apparent metastatic tumor in the lymph node.

MAMMARY GLAND AND HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMAS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY AND RENAL DISEASE PULMONARY TREMATODE GRANULOMA EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female sugar glider was found recumbent on the bottom of the enclosure and minimally responsive. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1.5 cm. multilobulated mass associated with the right mammary gland that expressed thick fluid when cut. Multiple masses were in the liver and a firm yellow mass was in the sublumbar region that exuded white fluid on cut surface.
CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS. This 1-year-old female lory presented for regurgitation and was treated for one day but died. Necropsy revealed multiple foci of hemorrhage in the gastrointestinal tract.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA AND PERITONITIS. This 10-year-old female cotton-headed tamarin was found dead. It had a history of transmural ulcerative typhlitis attributed to bacterial infection (G10-6164) and was being treated for Campylobacter infection. It had recovered in the hospital and was doing well but was found dead. Necropsy revealed fibrin on the heart thickened pericardium white streaks in the heart muscle gray/brown discoloration of the pancreas adhesions in the abdominal cavity enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes large and yellow/tan adrenal dark purple kidneys that were granular on cut surfaces and well healed cecal surgical site.
INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS MYOCARDIAL MINERALIZATION ATELECTASIS SHOCK. This 2-month-old female ferret was found dead. Dehydration and diarrhea were noted at necropsy.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS MICROGRANULOMATOSIS. This 6-year-old male corn snake was emaciated and did not respond to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a yellow/tan liver with brown circular areas to 3 mm. in diameter throughout the parenchyma. Ulceration was noted sporadically throughout the stomach and intestinal tract.
adult. Weight: 15.7 g.  Euth. Spondylosis; thor & lumb spine.

BLASTOMYCOSIS. This 29-year-old male Sea Lion had a two week history of upper respiratory tract infection inappetence and mucoid stool. The animal died spontaneously and necropsy revealed spherical nodules in the skin nodules in the lungs and on the pleural surface and a nodule in mesenteric lymph node. EUTHANASIA SPINAL TRAUMA SHOCK. This 14-year-old male flying fox was found on the ground. Loss of paralysis was noted on the hind limbs. Liver: Severe acute massive hepatopathy and focal necrosis. Lung: Mild pulmonary fibrosis Massive hepatopathy (please see comments) Comments: Pulmonary findings are not significant in the cause of death and are likely related to aging. Aeromonas veronii biovar sobria is a ubiquitous pathogen found in aquatic environments and is implicated in cases of diarrhea in humans and diseases of fish. The pathogenesis; pathogenic mechanism; and virulence factors responsible for infection in different species are not well understood; and the significance of the bacteria in this case without microscopic pathology is questionable. Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) cause hepatotoxicity by disorganization of hepatocytes leading to necrosis; apoptosis; and perisinusoidal hemorrhage; frequently; individual or small groups of hepatocytes are affected; rather than zonal necrosis. The hepatopathy as demonstrated in this case likely preceeded massive hepatic necrosis. Cyanobacteria toxicosis is a primarily differential; however; definitive diagnosis is pending additional diagnostic testing to be completed at another diagnostic laboratory. Additional results will be addressed in a future addendum. Kristy A. Mietelka; DVM Negative for cyanide toxicity Comments:The toxicologic assay for cyanide did not detect this chemical in submitted liver samples. Stomach contents and liver have been sent to the California Animal Health and Food Safety Laboratory System for Anatoxin-A and Microcystins (for microscopic algae detection; i.e. Blue Green Algae). Additional results will be sent to you directly from CAHFS. Kristy A. Mietelka; DVM Negative for cyanobacteria toxins Comments: While the toxicology analysis performed at California Animal Health and Food Safety Laboratory System did not detect microcystins or anatoxin-a in the submitted sample of stomach contents; the hepatopathy as demonstrated in this case is consistent with cyanobacteria toxicosis. Degradation of the toxins or very low content of toxins within the sample may lead to no detection. Death due to anatoxin-a fast-death factor found in some blooms is also a consideration in this case; however; these deaths usually follow collapse; prostration; and hyperesthesia; and are typically devoid of any specific lesions. This concludes diagnostic testing for this case. Kristy A. Mietelka; D

Small intestine: Locally extensive chronic mucosal proliferation Small and large intestine: Diffuse serosal hyperemia with diarrhea Kidney: Focal cortical cyst Comments: The gross findings are most suggestive of underlying enteritis; of which; a definitive cause can not be determined at this time. Differentials for this mass include malignant lymphoma and plasma cell tumor. Immunohistochemical staining to further characterize the cell line of origin is in progress and results will be released in an addendum. The mass resulted in perforation of the jejunum with secondary peritonitis; which is the likely cause of death of this ferret. Overall; the changes in the renal glomeruli were mild; and likely were not causing any functional problems at the time of death. There was no evidence of any underlying infectious disease process in any of the tissues examined. Fecal examination was negative for enteric parasites Intestinal mass: B cell lymphosarcoma

INANITION. This 2-year/8-month-old snake of undetermined gender died. At necropsy the carcass was in good condition. There were fat stores present but were not large. There were nematodes in the gastrointestinal tract.

EUTHANASIA PANCREATITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL CYST ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 15-year-old female red panda has a several day history of respiratory difficulties inappetence and weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining condition and chronic arthritis. At necropsy muscle atrophy was noted in the spine with prominent kyphosis. Urine scalding was noted on the hind limbs. Severe degenerative joint disease was noted in the stifle. The heart was rounded with thinning of the left ventricle.

EUTHANASIA ECTOPIC NECROTIC EGG YOLK COELOMITIS. This captive bred 4-year-old female chicken was humanely euthanized. It had a two week duration of illness. It had a large abdominal mass that was visible and palpable. Radiographs were inconclusive. Ultrasound revealed fluid but was inconclusive. Exploratory surgery revealed a mass that extended from the keel to the pelvis. The abdominal organs were adhered. At necropsy there was a large ectopic egg mass. The oviduct was not obstructed.

CIRRHOSIS. This 8-year-old female lory was noted to have lethargy and labored breathing during the morning check. Examination revealed a mass effect in the coelomic cavity. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed some dried urates around the cloaca congestion within the ventral lungs 2 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the coelomic cavity pale red/orange liver with enlargement of the distal right lobe and a white firm nodule at the peripheral aspect of the distal left lobe. An additional raised firm nodule was on the medial aspect of the middle half of the left lobe approximately 1 mm. in diameter.

HEMOPHAGOCYTIC SYNDROME SEPSIS RENAL TREMATODIASIS. This 10-year-old female spoonbill presented in comatose condition. The animal was treated for shock but died within minutes. At necropsy feathers were missing from the mid to upper neck with evidence of feather regrowth. Small foci of hemorrhage were present in the pectoral muscle (injection sites). Scant adipose tissue depots were identified. The spleen was oval and enlarged. Minimal ingesta was present within the GI tract. Adrenal glands appeared to be enlarged.

SHOCK MILD CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND MESENTERIC LYMPH NODE EDEMA. This 9-year-old male red panda had a history of weight loss despite good appetite and exploratory surgery was performed. A biopsy specimen (G15-3615) identified mild enteritis and lymph node hyperplasia. The animal died four days later and necropsy revealed multifocal reddening of the intestinal tract a small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity and mild thickening of the intestinal walls.

EMACIATION LYMPH NODE HYPERPLASIA. This 2-month-old female cottontail rabbit had recently been released to a hardening pen and there is a previous history of bacterial enterocolitis in the group. This rabbit had been found dead by staff inside the grain storage area. Necropsy revealed thin body condition autolysis and no external or internal abnormalities other than lack of ingesta in the stomach.

UROLITHIASIS URETHRAL OBSTRUCTION RUPTURED URINARY BLADDER PERITONITIS. This 3-year-old male capybara has a three day history of inappetence and separating itself from the group. It has been inactive and mildly obtunded in the morning and a urethral obstruction was diagnosed at the distal penis where a large firm mass was palpable. When flushed the mass dissolved into grit and copious frank bloody dark fluid. The animal was catheterized and two liters of the same fluid and grit was extracted. The animal recovered poorly from anesthesia and became agonal several hours later and did not respond to resuscitation. Necropsy revealed blood in the preputial region adequate subcutaneous adipose stores 500 ml. of frank blood in the coelom dark purple urinary bladder with a straight focal laceration leaking bloody red fluid and 100 ml. of blood red fluid is present in the lumen of the urinary bladder. The ureters were red and dilated. The kidneys were purple with blood tinge to the pelvis. The liver appeared congested. Some hemorrhage was noted on the serosal surface of the cecum. Aspirated food material was present in the trachea and a bronchiole.
EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 18-year-old male puma was humanely euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy there were cysts on the liver. The spleen was large.

MYOPATHY PROBABLE EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY. This greater than 12-year-old brown pelican had been inappetent for two days and seemed unable to stand so was moved to a holding cage and received supportive care. The bird was alert and able to hold its head up but unable to stand and was weak and poorly responsive. The bird died shortly thereafter. Blood work revealed leukocytosis with heterophilia elevated serum AST and CK and hypoproteinemia. A young female conspecific died approximately two months earlier with similar presenting signs and necropsy revealed skeletal muscle necrosis (G12-5955) although vitamin E levels in the liver were judged to be adequate. Necropsy of the bird for this report revealed pale pectoral muscles that were streaked and orange tinted. Leg muscles were pale and tinted. Adequate intracoelomic fat was noted. Moderate to large foci of congestion and hemorrhage were present throughout both lungs. Small hemorrhages were on the myocardium and some mild pale streaking was noted. Petechial hemorrhages of the mucosa were noted along most of the intestine which contained a small amount of liquid ingesta.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE PYELONEPHRITIS CHOLECYSTITIS AND CHOLELITHIASIS. This 23-year-old female squirrel monkey presented for acute lethargy. For 1-2 years the animal has been thin with a scruffy coat. Examination revealed azotemia gastric distention and mineral opacities in the hepatic region. Supportive care was administered but the animal declined and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous lipomas over the limbs enlarged heart with thin-walled large atria a small amount of food in the stomach gastric distention a 2 mm. green firm cholelith in the gallbladder admixed with creamy white liquid pale right renal cortex and knobby external surface of the right kidney.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS FIBROSARCOMA (UTERUS). This 17-year-old female guinea hog had a history of decreased appetite. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a large mass was present in the uterus and smaller masses were present in the liver.
INANITION BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 3-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead with its head in the water bowl. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

BUMBLEFOOT TRACHEAL TRAUMA (INTUBATION-LIKE) CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK. This 19.5-year-old male roseate spoonbill had a bumblefoot lesion on the right foot that was surgically excised. The bird had been nonweight bearing on this foot. A few days prior to death the bird appeared to have increased respiratory effort that would resolve spontaneously. Eventually respiratory effort did not resolve and supplemental oxygen was administered but the bird died shortly thereafter. Radiographs had identified a small soft tissue opacity in the cranial trachea. Necropsy revealed a 1.5 cm. mass nearly occluding the lumen of the trachea. The ventriculus was full of partially digested food. The heart was mildly thickened and the proventriculus was empty.

MACRORHABDIOSIS WITH ATYPIA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA ATYPICAL ESOPHAGEAL MUCOSAL PROLIFERATION. This 6-year-old male budgerigar is being monitored for regurgitation with heavy breathing and fluctuating weight. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed decreased pectoral muscle mass and no other abnormalities.

Thoracic cavity: Moderate hydrothorax Lung: Diffuse; severe pulmonary edema C3: Locally extensive mucosal hyperplasia with multifocal granulomas Liver: Solid biliary adenoma Comments This animal had severe pulmonary edema and thoracic effusion. These lesions can be caused by left side heart failure; hypoproteinemia; and infection; however; they are also commonly seen in euthanized animals. The lesions found in the C3 are most likely associated with parasite infection. Samples were collected for fecal analysis as well as histopathology. The result will be included as a final report. Misa Komine DVM; PhD C3: Multifocal granulomas Liver: Bilicary cystic adenoma; Diffuse; moderate passive congestion with centrilobular fibrosis and bridging fibrosis Lung: Pulmonary congestion and edema Heart: Mild lymphocytic myocarditis Tongue: Moderate; multifocal; lymphocytic glossitis Third eyelid: Sebaceous hyperplasia; mild lymphocytic conjunctivitis Endoparasitism Comments The histological findings in the stomach (C3) are most consistent with parasitic granulomas; and Trichostrongylus spp were detected with fecal analysis. Intestinal parasite infection causes diarrhea and weight loss; resulting in hypoproteinemia. Thoracic effusion and pulmonary edema seen in this case may be associated with hypoproteinemia. Lesions seen in heart; liver and tongue are overall mild and non-specific; and are considered to be incidental findings often seen in aged animals. Misa Komine DVM; PhD

CERVICAL FRACTURE. This 4-year-old male impala was startled and ran into a fence followed by immediate recumbency and inability to stand. The animal died shortly thereafter. It had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed excellent body condition a 30 cm. section of jejunum with hemorrhagic contents bone fragments within the C3-C4 intervertebral disk space and fractures of both end plates a comminuted fracture of the C4 vertebra and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS VENTRICULITIS. This 7-month/2-day-old female lory died during treatment. It had a history of regurgitation and pasty bloody vent. The bird was thin. At necropsy the brain appeared edematous. The gastrointestinal tract was devoid of ingesta. In the proventriculus there were two small pieces (2-3 mm.) of black semirigid material. The duodenum and upper jejunum were thickened with multifocal areas of hemorrhage in the mucosa and muscularis. The lower bowel was dark red to black with frank hemorrhage throughout. The cloaca was hemorrhagic. Fecal smear did not reveal any parasites. Cloacal and duodenal cultures were performed.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND JOIN DISEASE CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY (METACAM TOXICOSIS-LIKE) EUTHANASIA. This approximately 20-year-old male flying fox had a 2-3 day history of progressive lethargy and inappetence and a chronic history of arthritis for which it was receiving supportive care. The left hind foot had severe arthritis and dislocation and the right stifle was chronically displaced. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed absence of the right eye previously described skeletal lesions small amount of hemorrhage in the pericardial sac red/brown mottling of the liver and small yellow kidneys.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC CIRRHOSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS ENTERITIS. This 16-year-old male tamarin was found dead at the morning check without premonitory signs. At necropsy the liver was enlarged with numerous nodules within the parenchyma. The heart appeared dilated. No clinical diagnosis was provided.

AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION GOUT IRON STORAGE PODODERMATITIS EMACIATION. This 31-year-old male American flamingo had unusual behavior noted approximately two days before death. Possible neurologic signs were noted. The bird died and necropsy revealed good body condition scoliosis between C2-C8 a pinioned right wing moderate to severe pododermatitis at the interphalangeal joints on each digit of the feet and smaller lesions on webbing between the digits hyperpigmentation in the connective tissue around the trachea and air sacs mild to moderate endocardiosis in the left atrioventricular valve multiple firm nodules up to 1 cm. in greatest dimension in the lungs diffusely pale kidneys with enlarged cranial poles and small testes.

AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA. This 12-year-old female cheetah fractured a leg five weeks prior to death during an immobilization. The animal developed cystitis during the postoperative period resulting in renal failure. Euthanasia was scheduled; however the animal died spontaneously. At necropsy tissues were icteric and minimal adipose tissues were identified. The caudal end of the spleen contained small clusters of raised dark masses. The liver was enlarged with rounded edges. The left kidney was very small with an irregular contour. Several large pale depressions were present in the cortical surface and pale streaks extended through the cortex into the medulla. The right kidney had a finely granular surface with pale streaks extending into the parenchyma. A 2 x 1 cm. ovoid swelling was present in the wall of the uterine horn.

CHRONIC TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS WITH PROTEINURIA MA MAMMARY FIBROADENOMAS LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC TRACHEITIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female roof rat was euthanized due to quality of life concerns. The animal had two large masses located in the inguinal region and on the axillary region that were interfering with ambulation. In addition to the masses gross necropsy revealed bilateral pleural adhesions and a dark red area on the left ventricle interpreted as resulting from intracardiac euthanasia.

GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old male mandrill had a history of spondylosis renal disease inappetence bladder stone and cardiac insufficiency. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed loss of body condition infarcts in the heart thickening of the cardiac valves especially in the atrioventricular valves severe arteriosclerosis in the great vessels a 1.5 cm. stone in the urinary bladder and thickened bladder wall dilated ureters shrunken left kidney granular renal parenchyma markedly dilated right renal pelvis with loss of medulla and generalized arthritis in most joints including osteophytes in the stifles and bridging spondylosis.

GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS OOPHORITIS ENTERITIS BACTERIAL HEPATITIS INANITION. This 14-year-old female adder was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy fat depots were absent. A mass was noted at the anterior end of the liver appearing as an organizing hematoma.

SEPSIS. This 9-year-old female Parma wallaby was found dead in the morning with no prior history of illness. Necropsy revealed hair loss over the entire tail an anterior lens luxation in the left eye no evidence of corneal damage no obvious trauma noted female reproductive tract a cyst on the right ovary pale yellow liver irregular pale kidneys especially in the medulla two areas of hemorrhage in the colon and all pulmonary lobes reddened.

PULMONARY ABSCESS PNEUMONIA. This 7-month-old male rabbit was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the animal was thin. Fat depots were absent. The left lung was firm and friable with consolidating white to tan foci. A cavitary mass containing purulent material was present in the right lung.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE. This 15-year-old female Jamaican fruit bat was euthanized for declining quality of life. It had been unable to fly and was housed off exhibit. Necropsy revealed decreased range of motion in the wing joints.

MYCOTIC DERMATITIS RENAL GOUT HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INANITION. This 16-year-old corn snake survived a building fire approximately eight months previously. Azurophilia was noted with no response to antibiotic or antifungal therapy. Diffuse dermatitis developed and the animal later died. At necropsy severe dysecdysis was noted. Lungs were edematous and sank in formalin. Hemorrhage was noted within the coelomic cavity.

CARCINOMATOSIS ASPIRATION. This 5-year-old female chicken had been hospitalized for decreased activity and appetite with weight loss and died the following morning. Necropsy revealed aspirated food material in the lungs engorged alimentary tract containing ingesta and thickened intestinal walls and active ovary with areas of folliculostasis and decomposition.

EUTHANASIA MALIGNANT MELANOMA. This 12-year-old male snow leopard was humanely euthanized. It had acute onset of weight loss. Biopsy of an elbow mass confirmed melanoma. At necropsy there were black spots (2x2 mm.) throughout the parenchyma and surfaces of all lung lobes pancreas and adrenal.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS EMACIATION MUSCLE HEMORRHAGE AND NECROSIS. This 14-year-old male Guam rail was found dead in its enclosure laying on its side. The animal had a long history of bilateral lameness which responded to long-term treatment although the rail was recently slowing down. Necropsy revealed fair body condition some cracks in the skin bilaterally over the tarsometatarsus serous fluid in the coelomic cavity small firm irregular liver enlarged kidneys and no other abnormalities.

TRAUMATIC FORELEG MUSCLE AND NERVE DAMAGE CHRONIC RUMENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-month-old female addra gazelle had a one month history of nonweight bearing lameness on the right front leg attributed to radial nerve or brachioplexus injury. Hair loss was present over the shoulder. A conspecific in the herd was also lame on the right front leg with dropped shoulder suggesting suprascapular nerve injury. Examination revealed localized swelling and bruising over the right shoulder and lateral radius and radiographs of the leg did not show any bone or joint abnormalities. The lesions were attributed to trauma; the animal was confined and received supportive care. The condition did not improve over the next few weeks and minimal pain could be elicited in the distal portions of the leg. Range of motion of the right elbow was severely impaired. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition with minimal subcutaneous fat stores muscle atrophy in the right scapular muscles and muscles of the right forelimb decreased range of motion in the right elbow healing fractures of ribs #4-6 on the right thoracic wall and rib #10 on the left thoracic wall. The right prescapular lymph node was markedly enlarged reddened and had pockets of purulent exudate (attributed to subcutaneous injections in the region). The spleen was enlarged and markedly engorged with blood. An old healing contusion or tears to the right lung from the rib fractures was noted. The ventral most portion of the left cranial pulmonary lobe was brownish-green and consolidated. The lungs otherwise were congested especially on the down side. The liver was congested. The nerves of the right brachioplexus were grossly normal. The right suprascapular nerve was discolored yellow/brown and somewhat atrophied. The right radial nerve where it passed laterally over the distal radius was focally narrowed and nearly severed and also discolored yellow/brown. Surrounding soft tissue was fibrotic.

SUSPECT ENTERIC FOREIGN BODY RENAL INFARCTS. This 3-year-old male domestic rabbit had a one-day history of depression and lethargy. The animal was also falling over. Radiographs were attempted but the animal went into cardiac arrest and could not be resuscitated. At necropsy the animal had fleas the lungs were congested there was a trichobezoar obstructing the pylorus with surrounding hemorrhage there were generalized diffuse white nodules on the gastric mucosa the small intestine was regionally thickened and the kidneys had petechiation.

MYCOTIC DERMATITIS. This approximately 8-year-old male timber rattlesnake was collected as part of a health survey of timber rattlesnakes. During sampling it was noted that the snake was weak in the rear but not paralyzed and seemed lethargic. Initial blood work was unremarkable and radiographs showed no abnormalities. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to decline and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. A small amount of amber fluid was in the coelomic cavity and no other gross lesions were seen.

EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 12-year-old female ibis has a history of chronic shedding of Campylobacter despite repeated treatment. The animal was euthanized. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

Kidney: Severe chronic interstitial nephritis and glomerulosclerosis (End stage kidney) Body as a whole: Severe arterio- and arterioloslerosis with mineralization and fibrinoid necrosis Liver: Capsular gout (Visceral gout) Heart: Mild multifocal myofiber mineralization Stomach: Severe laminar mucosal mineralization Heart: Myxosarcoma (presumptive) Comment: The cause of death and the multi-organ metastatic mineralization in this animal is kidney failure; a common finding in iguanas. This is a multifactorial disease; likely related to diet; hydration status; stress; and other factors. The tumor in the wall of the heart was interesting; but not likely clinically relevant.

COELOMIC NEMATODIASIS WITH HEMATOMA FORMATION. This 4-year-old lorikeet was noted to be lethargic and separated from the flock. It had been showing some signs of respiratory distress. It was captured for transport to the hospital but died prior to arrival. Necropsy revealed hematomas throughout the coelomic cavity.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC CARCINOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS. This 17-year-old female mandrill has been under treatment for acute renal failure. Although the animal’s clinical condition responded to therapy the electrolyte parameters remained extremely high. The animal developed pitting edema of the rear limbs and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple pale nodules were present in the diaphragm and ventral thoracic wall. Similar nodular masses efface the pancreas and are present adjacent to the liver and kidney.

HEPATIC SPOROZOANOSIS ENTERITIS. This 3-year-old female tanager was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the abdominal and thoracic air sacs were filled with frank blood. The liver was soft and friable with foci of hemorrhage.

PULMONARY MINERALIZATION RENAL GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male captive bred pigeon had a three day history of illness and was euthanized for humane reasons. It is the second pigeon from the flock to be euthanized due to severe respiratory disease. Necropsy revealed free and clotted blood in the coelomic cavity and extensive ecchymoses in the cervical region. Lungs were heavy red to purple and did not float in formalin. Culture is pending. The bird was in thin body condition.

PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA THYMOMA EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This approximately 15-year-old male goat had a history of progressive loss of muscle mass and body condition attributed to severe dental disease but had been reportedly eating and acting normally the evening prior to death. It was found down in the morning unable to rise but was responsive. Some regurgitation was on the ground in front of the animal and ptyalism was noted. Supportive care was administered but the animal developed heart arrhythmias vertical nystagmus and mydriasis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Moderate amounts of straw-colored fluid were in the abdomen and thorax all fat was gelatinous numerous tan spherical infiltrates were in the adrenals the kidneys were pale and soft the liver was small and dark but congested on cut surface the heart was mildly pale the cranial mediastinal lymph node was markedly enlarged and tan and scant digesta was noted from the pylorus to the colon.

HEPATITIS SEPTICEMIA URATE STASIS CHRONIC GASTRITIS. This 4.5-year-old male alligator lizard had a one day history of lethargy and was found dead. At necropsy multiple foci of hemorrhage and necrosis were identified in the liver. Urate stasis was present in the kidney. The coelomic cavity contained a scant quantity of fluid. Culture of this fluid revealed moderate growth of Enterobacter and Klebsiella along with Candida and coagulase negative Staphylococcus.

GRANULOMATOUS FACIAL CELLULITIS SALPINGITIS SEPSIS. This 16-year-old female boa has a history that suggests past neurological condition although this was not confirmed. The animal may have become dehydrated several years earlier but no recent dehydration has been noted. The animal ate and drank regularly.  Defecation intervals became longer as the animal grew older although the animal did have normal defecation a few days ago. The snake has been clinically normal the past several months. The snake was found dead and necropsy identified two large desiccated ova in the reproductive tract and no other abnormalities.

VISCERAL AND ARTICULAR GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female day gecko was found dead. This animal had a two-day history of joint swelling around the right elbow. The animal had become lethargic and died later in the day. Necropsy revealed a swollen left hock and right elbow some shedding of the skin at the toe tips and no other gross abnormalities.

MANDIBULAR OSTEOSARCOMA BRONCHIOLOALVEOLAR ADENOMAS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2-year-old female opossum was euthanized for an oral mass of unknown duration. Radiographically the oral mass was associated with severe lysis of the left rostral mandible and was interpreted to be neoplastic. Gross necropsy confirmed the presence of an oral mass involving soft tissue but also with invasion into the mandibular symphysis and down the rami. Pinpoint spherical nodules were also visible within the lungs. The distal right uterine horn was dilated and filled with clear fluid.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT FOLLICULAR ATRESIA AND OOPHORITIS. This 13-year-old female Gaboon viper was noted to be rolling over several times and appeared to be agonal. This snake was dead on arrival at the hospital. Necropsy revealed moderate skin tent food throughout the gastrointestinal tract 3 cc. of pericardial yellowish clear fluid adequate fat deposits eight large egg yolks and approximately 20 inspissated exudative lesions in the mid and lower abdomen up to 2 cm. in greatest dimension.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS BILATERAL SEMINOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male banded rail previously fractured its femur in 2006. It developed lameness in 2012 with some bone proliferation attributed to degenerative osteoarthritis. Supportive care was administered until the bird’s quality of life deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bone proliferation at the previous fracture site fair body condition and a moderate amount of dark-colored fibrinonecrotic debris within the right stifle. Proliferative changes were noted in both stifle joints and tarsi. The great vessels were firm food was in the ventriculus both testes were enlarged and a core of debris was in the right testis.

HEPATIC FIBROSIS AND MELANOSIS WITH LIPIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 15-year-old male captive bred boa constrictor had a 16 month history of illness. The snake presented with respiratory disease and was treated with a variety of antibiotics with an associated increase in uric acid level. The animal appeared septic lethargic and weak with anorexia. Paramyxovirus serology and inclusion body disease testing were negative. The animal developed a hemipene prolapse which was treated with amputation. The snake’s condition continued to deteriorate and it was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed opaque eyes thickened ventricle viscous fluid in the ileum urates in the distal colon dark kidneys and liver.

CARCINOMA. This 11-year/9-month-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy there was 4.2x6.4 cm. nodular mass in the coelomic cavity. The mass was firmly adhered to the proximal kidney bilaterally and ventral aspect of the adjacent vertebral column. There was a focus of white discoloration present on the left lobe of the liver (0.25 cm. diameter). The heart had several pale red to white streaks along the ventricular epicardium.

LEIOMYOSARCOMA COELOMIC CAVITY (PROBABLY GUT). This 7-year-old female corn snake had a history of a mass near the stomach that was detected radiographically. The animal was thin. Surgical exploratory revealed a 15 cm. long 6 cm. wide mass in the region of the stomach incorporating the wall of the stomach and the cranial and caudal loops of bowel. The mass was highly vascular. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA NEUROENDOCRINE TUMOR HEPATITIS SHOCK. This 6-year-old female ferret had a chronic history of an insulinoma. Hypoglycemic episodes were becoming more severe and frequent and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple small nodules were present in the pancreas liver and lungs. Lymph nodes were uniformly enlarged and firm.

NECROTIZING ENTERITIS. This 4-year/1-month-old male kudu was found dead. It was noted to be in sternal recumbency that morning. It had a preshipment examination with immobilization 10 days prior to death. It slightly reacted to TB test. It was immobilized again five days ago for the state veterinarian to do a comparative TB. The kudu was immobilized two days prior to death to read the TB test and it was negative. The kudu had decreased stool production during this time. At necropsy the kudu appeared to have lost approximately 50 lb. The small intestine cecum and colon were hemorrhagic and dark red to purple.

ITO CELL HYPERTROPHY ANEMIA INFLAMMATORY SKIN DISEASE POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS OR DIETARY IMBALANCE. This 2-year-old male Swainson’s lorikeet has a history of acute lethargy and bilateral gold colored iris. It is showing the same signs as two previously deceased lorikeets in the same flock. The birds were treated with fluids and antibiotics and blood sample was obtained. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed golden orange subcutaneous fat and intracoelomic fat. Some blunting of the choanal papillae was noted. The liver appeared enlarged and was pale. The kidneys were pale and friable. The adrenals appeared bilaterally enlarged.

FIP. This 4.5-year-old female cheetah had a one month history of partial inappetence and weight loss that progressed to diarrhea inactivity ataxia dyspnea and abdominal distention. Supportive care was administered but the cat died. Necropsy revealed a large amount of fluid in the abdominal cavity mucosal hyperplasia in the esophagus ulcers on the lips fluid accumulation in the pericardium and pleural space and icterus.

DART IMMOBILIZATION SEROMA EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female addax developed seromas following dart immobilization with subsequent draining tracts and contamination with bedding material. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 2 cm. dark firm nodule in the left subcutaneous thoracolumbar region. Large fat pads were present over the thoracolumbar dorsum. A large seroma pocket was present on the left dorsocaudal rump extending ventromedially within the subcutaneous tissues of the left rear leg. The left thyroid had a long caudal extension at least twice as long as the right thyroid. Periodontal pockets with gum recession were noted around molars and impacted plant material was present. Two areas in the lumbar vertebrae were where vertebral bodies expanded into spherical nodular regions.

GASTRIC DILATION/VOLVULUS ISLET CELL CARCINOMA MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA CUTANEOUS APOCRINE GLAND ADENOMAS POSSIBLE ESOPHAGEAL AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female African hunting dog was found bloated and vomiting bile in the morning became recumbent and comatose and arrested but was successfully resuscitated with chest compressions and supportive care. Radiographs identified a gastric dilatation and volvulus and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed marked nuclear sclerosis in both eyes marked dental wear and calculus fly strike on both pinna a 5 cm. oval shaped firm dermal mass on the ventral aspect of the distal portion of the tumor and numerous multinodular and well encapsulated dermal masses on the dorsal spine. A moderate amount of hemorrhagic fluid and free clots were in the peritoneal cavity. The stomach was gas distended and rotated 180° and approximately 25% of the serosal surface of the stomach was discolored dark red to purple. A large amount of undigested meat was in the stomach and multiple 1 mm. blister-like nodules were on the mucosa of the caudal two-thirds of the esophagus. The bladder wall was diffusely thickened and both kidneys were pale. Multiple 4 mm. cystic structures were in the left ovary and two firm masses were within the left uterine horn up to 2 cm. in greatest dimension. A 2 cm. firm mass was on the caudal mammary gland and a 4.5 cm. multinodular firm mass was in the second most caudal mammary gland. The left adrenal gland was lobulated dark red on the caudal pole.

ANEMIA AUTOLYZED TISSUE. This 2-year-old Rosenberg’s lorikeet was admitted to the animal clinic with anemia (PCV=19%). Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed brown uniform matter thought to be degenerative blood cells in the proventriculus and ventriculus. Organs were pale.

INANITION VISCERAL GOUT. This 5-year/4-month-old female duck was found dead. It was noted to be sleeping the day prior to death on the water. At necropsy the bird was in fair condition. There was no evidence of trauma. The body condition score was 2. The air sacs were cloudy (translucent). The oral cavity was pale. The ovaries had small follicles. The pericardial sac was thickened and contained multiple diffuse white streaking throughout. The duodenal area was dark. The pancreas appeared thickened. There were large amounts of urates in the cloaca. The feces were positive for coccidia (2+). Air sac cytology is pending. The kidneys were slightly pale and firm.
adult. Weight: 100.4 g.  Open.  Splenomegaly.  Possible enteritis.  Pulmonary congestion.  Hyperkeratosis on legs and feet.  Possible trauma.

GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS WITH THROMBI ASCARID MIGRATION. This 14-year-old female emerald tree boa has a long history of ascarid infection. The snake died. Suspected fat necrosis was noted at necropsy. Two white nodular areas were noted in a portion of the lung and intracoelomic nodules were present adjacent to the liver.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 30-year-old male gorilla was humanely euthanized due to progressive signs of severe congestive heart failure diagnosed in July 2005. The animal had been diagnosed with dilatative cardiomyopathy and was being treated with various drugs. After a protracted course of treatment and continual decline the animal became refractory to medical management and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Ascites dependent edema lethargy weight loss partial anorexia and exercise were noted clinically prior to death. Cardiac ultrasound prior to euthanasia showed adequate movement of the valves but very poor ventricular free wall contractility. Necropsy revealed dependent edema in both feet and legs several gallons of serosanguineous fluid in the abdomen adhesion of the omentum to the right lobe of the liver cysts in the left lobes that contain transparent yellow fluid multiple adhesions of the colon and body wall pulmonary edema enlarged and rounded heart with blunted apex pinpoint ulcers in the fundic region of the stomach and proximal duodenum and no other significant gross abnormalities.

HEPATIC FIBROSIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMOSIDEROSIS MALASSEZIA DERMATITIS DERMAL MELANOCYTOMA. This 5-year-old male hedgehog was treated for chronic otitis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a raised pigmented lesion was present at the right ear tip. The ear canal contained purulent material. Miliary white foci were present in the liver and lung.

TRAUMA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 15-year-old female ibis had a history of arthritis and chronic renal disease. The bird was found dead. THYMOMA CHRONIC RUMENITIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS HEPATIC ABSCESS EUTHANASIA. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition with muscle wasting in the rear absence of some incisors and molars and a large amount of ingesta in the omasum and rumen.

DEGENERATIVE DISK DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male tiger had a history of kyphosis and mild forelimb lameness six months earlier. The condition responded minimally to supportive care and an MRI identified compressed myelopathy at T2-T3 from disk protrusion. A number of additional noncompressive disk protrusions were present throughout the cervical thoracic and lumbar vertebrae. The animal initially responded to a new treatment protocol but in the weeks prior to death moderate decline was observed with increase in discomfort and chronic skin abrasions on the limbs. The animal was found in the morning parapruritic and unable to stand could move the cranial portion of the body into sternal recumbency and drag the body but was unable to manipulate or bear weight on the hind limbs. Kicking and movement of the hind limbs was noted but no ability to manipulate the limbs under the body. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE OBESITY EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old female turkey had developed acute weakness and examination revealed pallor faintly audible heart sounds and radiographic and electrocardiographic evidence of cardiac disease. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of serosanguineous coelomic fluid edema and hemorrhage in the lungs cardiomegaly with enlarged left ventricle and areas of suspected fibrosis at the base of the heart. Yellow fibrin plaques were on the serosal surface of the large intestine. The liver was enlarged.

FRACTURED FEMUR GAS EMBOLI HYPERKERATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female basilisk was noted to have an open fracture of the left femur and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed female reproductive tract and no other abnormalities other than the fracture.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female colobus monkey has a history of lymphoma that was not responding to prednisolone. The animal developed progressive inappetence and lethargy with severe decline in attention and interactions. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed marked hypertrophy of lymph nodes throughout the body hypertrophy of the tonsils a mass in the left lacrimal gland pyloric hypertrophy nodules in the pancreas punctate nodules in the liver a uterine mass possible ovarian mass possible pituitary hypertrophy nodularity in effacement of normal architecture in the spleen and both kidneys and a small amount of ascites.

SEPSIS. This approximately 2-year-old male squirrel monkey was hospitalized for progressive weakness. A cagemate has been hospitalized for similar presentation. Laboratory values reveal Giardia in stool samples dehydration and elevated white blood cell count. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with unkempt haircoat petechial hemorrhages on the serosal surfaces of the duodenum and cecum frank blood on the mucosa of the duodenum thickening of the ileum and cecum melena in the cecum enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes with petechiae hemorrhage throughout the lungs swollen and pale kidneys rounded and swollen liver with petechiae on the serosal surfaces.

EMACIATION CHRONIC HEPATITIS EARLY CIRROSIS INTESTINAL ULCERATION. This approximately 7-year-old male reunion chameleon has a several month history of hyporexia. Recently the animal would not swallow and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the animal was cachectic with undigested food in the lower gastrointestinal tract and dark discoloration of the gastrointestinal tract.
PULMONARY BACTERIAL GRANULOMA. This 12-year/4-month-old male owl died. At necropsy there was a 1.5 x 1 cm. gray mass attached to the caudal dorsal portion of the left lung.

SHOCK. This approximately 4-year-old female snake died. It had a recent history of abnormal coiling represented by opisthotonic-like posturing in the cranial third of the body. On admission to the hospital for examination the snake presented BAR and lacking neurologic signs. Blood was collected via cardiac puncture without apparent complications. During radiography the snake became very limp. Heart rate and respirations were within normal limits. At necropsy the snake was in very good body condition. The heart appeared slightly enlarged and elongated with mild bleeding into the pericardium.
CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 9-month-old female was found dead. At necropsy the intestines were dark red and contained red to black ingesta.

HEPATIC LACERATION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS ENTERITIS HEPATITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS URATE STASIS RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS. This 11-year-old male turkey was found dead. BACTERIAL PLEURITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 11-year-old male panda had a waxing and waning history of anorexia and panting and died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed good body condition with moderate dental disease and approximately 300 ml. of yellow cloudy fluid in the thorax. No normal lung tissue was noted. Possible generalized icterus was noted and the liver was mottled. A yellow exudate was in the left renal cortex.

POLIONCEPHALOMALACIA (RESOLVED) BILATERAL RETINAL DEGENERATION DIGITAL TRAUMA GANGLIONIC INCLUSIONS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female meerkat has a history of cellulitis and uterine leiomyomas (G11-5729). Ovariohysterectomy was performed at that time. In the past six months the meerkat and two other conspecifics had decreased appetite. The animals were transferred to the hospital while their holding pen was worked on and while their holding pen was worked on and while another troop member was recovering from a pancreatic mass removal. The meerkat of this report had a mature cataract and had episodes of circling or wandering aimlessly in April 2013. Blood work revealed moderate leukocytosis and antibiotic therapy was administered. The animal did not respond. There is a recent history of polioencephalomalacia in another meerkat from this troop and the animal of this report was treated accordingly. The animal developed cognitive dysfunction and presented two weeks ago with macerated right rear foot necessitating partial digital amputation. The animal did not respond well following surgery and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mature cataract in the right eye and opacity in the lens of the left eye. The amputation site remained swollen as did the adjacent digit #4. The spleen has several round nonraised slightly pale discolored foci that did not extend into the parenchyma. Focal areas of enlargement on ribs #9 and 10 on the right thoracic wall were noted.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS HEMANGIOSARCOMA ISLET CELL TUMOR INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 5-year-old male ferret has a history of hypoglycemia and presented with pallor and was unresponsive. CHYTRIDIOMYCOSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANASIA. This 7-month-old ornate horn frog tested positive for chytridiomycosis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

HIND LIMB PARESIS AND ATAXIA INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIAL MINERALIZATION. This 5-year-old male giant Flemish rabbit was humanely euthanized after a long history of hind limb ataxia and paresis unresponsive to pulse steroid therapy that progressed to loss of righting reflex and inability to use hind limbs. Necropsy revealed left pulmonary atelectasis and consolidation mild capsular fibrosis in the kidneys pale musculature in both hind limbs and no evidence of disc protrusion or compression of the spinal cord.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA EMACIATION INTESTINAL PARASITISM CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY AND DEGENERATIVE RENAL DISEASE. This 6-year-old male kudu was found dead. It had been locked in a barn during the night. There were no health problems other than parasitism. Necropsy revealed lesions suggestive of encephalomyocarditis virus infection. The heart was enlarged the lungs were hemorrhagic and airways were filled with foam and blood.

EUTHANASIA COLITIS INANITION SHOCK CEREBRAL EDEMA. This 15-year-old male tamarin has a history of severe weight loss. The animal was found lethargic. Treatment was initiated; however the animal developed neurologic signs and was euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. Liquid feces were present in the colon.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL DERMATITIS RENAL ADENOMA GRANULOMTOUS ESOPHAGITIS. This 9-year-old female python has a history of recurrent egg impaction cataracts and weight loss. Crusted skin lesions were noted which were positive for Pseudomonas and Morganella. The animal was humanely euthanized.

Liver: Mild; multifocal; granulomatous hepatitis (suspected; pending histopathology) Skin: Multifocal abscesses Stomach (C3): Mild; multifocal hemorrhage Right lung and kidney: Marked; diffuse hypostatic congestion Spleen: Moderate diffuse congestion Comments The above described and listed gross findings are not pathognomonic for any specific disease entity and may require further ancillary tests to determine the ultimate demise of this animal. Histopathology is pending and will be described in the final report; together with the results of the pending parasitology test on the feces. Samples of selected tissues were saved for additional tests if indicated by histopathology. Karla Fenton DVM; MS Skin: Moderate; focal; granulomatous dermatitis with intralesional foreign material Liver: Mild multifocal hepatitis; Locally extensive fatty degeneration (tension lipidosis) Intestine: Mild neutrophilic enteritis Spinal Cord: Mild myelin degeneration Open Comments Gross; histologic; and laboratory findings were largely nonspecific and were unable to identify a specific etiologic agent to explain the chronic weight loss and weakness. Parasitology identified few coccidial oocysts in the submitted well formed feces; however; these parasites were not identified in the sections of intestine examined microscopically. This may have been at least in part because of post-mortem loss of the lining epithelium. Diagnosis of clinically significant coccidiosis is based on clinical signs of diarrhea and often the demonstration of very large numbers of oocysts in the feces. These features were not present in this case. There was instead histologic evidence of mild neutrophilic enteritis; but the cause of it was not apparent. Advanced autolysis within the intestine greatly hampered critical evaluation of this tissue. There was histologic evidence of hepatitis; however; based on the mildness and very scattered distribution of this lesion; the significance towards the clinical signs of this animal is questionable. It is suspected that the focal area of fatty degeneration likely represents an area of ligament attachment to the liver and subsequent fatty change due to localized tension. As noted grossly; there was histologic evidence of a locally extensive area of dermatitis. These lesions likely formed in response to traumatically inoculated foreign material. Mild degenerative changes were noted within sections of the short segments of cranial cervical and lumbar spinal cord collected at necropsy. Although mild; these lesions could potentially explain the clinical signs of weakness.There was no gross or histologic evidence of the meningeal worm (Parelaphostrongylus tenuis); but lesions due to this parasite are focal and may not have been represented in the sections examined. Karla Fenton DVM; Open Comments The selenium (Se) level was slightly elevated in this animal. Several veterinary laboratories are reportedly finding significantly higher concentrations of Se (>12 ug/g dry weight) in llama and alpaca liver samples with no associated definable pathologic lesions. Use of newer feed supplements may result in higher liver and tissue Se concentrations. Further investigation is required to better define camelid Se requirements and toxicity levels. The Vitamin E level was slightly elevated in this animal; however; excess vitamin E is not considered harmful. Liver vitamin E concentration is a good indicator of dietary vitamin E intake. Nevertheless; hepatic vitamin E concentration is dynamic and the liver should be viewed as a very short-term vitamin E storage pool. There has been one documented report of vitamin E-related muscular disease in a llama; with musculoskeletal lesions similar to what is seen in other species; however; these lesions were related to a deficiency of vitamin E; which is the opposite of the result in this case. The copper (Cu) level was slightly decreased in this alpaca. Cu is often associated with anemia; altered hair coloration; impaired immune response; and poor growth; but usually in these cases the Cu levels are much lower than that observed in this animal. The iron (Fe) level was increased in this animal. The significance of this finding is undetermined because there is no report of iron toxicity in new world camelids. Karla Fenton DVM; MS

Skin; rectum; lip; scrotum: Severe multifocal traumatic lacerations with secondary necrosis Digits: Severe lacerations and traumatic amputation Heart: Moderate myocardial fibrosis (presumptive; pending histopathology) Urinary bladder: Distention and possible neurogenic distention Abdominal cavity: Chronic mild peritonitis with adhesions Lungs: Moderate hilar hemorrhage (likely due to CPR) Prostate: Mild prostatic hyperplasia Testicle (left): Moderate atrophy Epdididymi: Bilateral granulomatous epididymitis (sperm granulomas - secondary to vasectomy) Stifle; hip (bilaterally): Moderate degenerative arthropathy Vertebra (L1; L2): Focal nodular osseous proliferation Comment: At this point; a clear cause of death is not evident. The wounds did not appear to cause peritonitis (the changes in the abdomen are too chronic and low-grade); nor did the chimp appear septic at the time of death. The appearance of fibrosis in the heart is of concern; as heart disease is common in aged male chimps. The cause for the retention of urine in the bladder is not clear - neurogenic causes are most likely and so the spinal cord has been removed to the point of the cauda equina for microscopic inspection. The reproductive and musculoskeletal changes are expected in an animal of this age; and the lung lesions were likely secondary to CPR. Additional data and photographs are on file with the recorded weights of organs and the Great Ape Heart Project protocol data on the heart. These will be held on file at the DCPAH and sent to the zoo and the SSP pathologist for chimps. Histopathology is pending and a final report will give these results. Multiple frozen tissues are on file as well and will not be discarded without the zoo's notice so that they may be retrieved if desired Examined are sections of eye (block 1); left and right trigeminal; pituitary gland (2); left and right testicle; epididymi (3-6); heart apex (7); apex; left outflow tract (7); left ventricle (9-10); right ventricle (11); aorta (arch); left ventricle (12); hemorrhoid (13); prostatic urethra (14); liver (15); skin (16); adrenal glands (17); tongue; intestine (18); intestines; salivary gland (19-20); kidney (21); kidney; spleen (22); trachea; airsac (23); bone marrow (24); thyroid gland (25); stomach; pancreas (26-27); urethra; trigone; seminal vesicle (28); prostate; seminal vesicle (29); lung (30-31); brain (32-36); spinal cord (caudal cord L3-S) (37); spinal cord (cranial T; C); brachial plexus (39); and bone (vertebral mass)(40). In almost all areas of the heart; there are multifocal bands of mature fibrosis separating bundles of cardiac myocytes and sometimes isolating individual fibers. In many areas; the myocytes are shrunken; vacuolated; and sometimes pale staining. There is marked anisokaryosis and pleomorphism among nuclei; and in some muscle fibers; there are aggregated bundles of nuclei. In the aorta; there is a single focus of mineralization which disrupts the contour of the intima and projects into the lumen. In the lung; there is some peripheral consolidation and collapse. Throughout the lung; there are marked congestion and frequent individal and small aggregates of hemosiderin laden alveolar macrophages. In one bronchiole; there is abundant mucus and many large vacuolated macrophages. In the liver; there is marked congestion and degeneration of central hepatocytes; as well as abundant agggregates of hemosiderin within Kupffer cells concentrated in the centrilobular areas. In some areas; there is frank necrosis and fibrin plaques lining sinusoids. In the adrenal gland; there are several nodular foci of cortical cell hyperplasia within and beyond the capsule. In the cortex; the fasciulata and reticularis cells have abundant lipofuscin within Additional diagnoses: Spinal cord: Mild arterial hyaline degeneration Vertebral body (L1-2): Osteochondroma Comment: The arterial changes in the spinal cord are likely incidental and age-related. Osteochondromas are benign developmental abnormalites that arise along growth plates in a variety of locations and have been reported in many species. Usually they are reported when they are intraspinal and cause compression of the spinal cord. In this case; the tumor was extraspinal and unlikely to have caused any clinical signs. This completes testing on this case. Frozen archived tissues will be held in the Agnew research laboratory unless the zoo would prefer to hold these in their facility

INTRA-ABDOMINAL AND CUTANEOUS ABSCESSES SEPSIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS HYPERPLASTIC PYLORIC GASRITIS. This 17-year-old male cottontop tamarin died following an episode of weakness. Necropsy revealed depleted fat pale liver no free fluid a 1 cm. mass on the apex of the urinary bladder a thick pylorus and no other gross abnormalities.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATIC NECROSIS ENTERITIS. This 21-year-old male duck was unable to stand and had limited range of motion in the coxofemoral joints. The animal was later found dead. At necropsy a 5 mm. in diameter brown area was present in the left hepatic lobe.

INGLUVITIS PNEUMONITIS PROVENTRICULITIS. This 3-year/3-month-old female parrot. It was noted to be fluffed during the past few days prior to death. It was negative for polyomavirus. At necropsy there was brown liquid in the oral cavity and trachea. There was food and bile in the gastrointestinal tract.

SOFT TISSUE MINERALIZATION ACUTE MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS. This 4-year-old captive bred male sloth had a 10 day history of lethargy and progressive anorexia and depression. The animal had an intra-abdominal abscess secondary to porcupine quill migration removed surgically last fall.  The animal has also been drinking more water than normal since last fall. Prior to death the animal had mild neutrophilia hypoalbuminemia elevations in AST and GGT dehydration periodic bloat and a nephrolith in the right kidney detected by ultrasound. The animal died spontaneously. Gross necropsy revealed a larger than expected left ventricular lumen. The surgical site in the abdomen was completely healed. No nephrolith was found.

ENDOMETRIAL MUCOSAL AND STROMAL HYPERPLASIA MESENTERIC ADENOCARCINOMA (METASTASIS). This greater than 5-year-old bat was found dead on exhibit and had no prior medical history. Necropsy revealed a 2 mm. diameter nodule on the caudal lobe of the right lung. The uterus was large and filled with dark mucosanguineous fluid. The luminal surface had an undulating appearance.

TRAUMA CRANIAL SWELLING PODODERMATITIS SHOCK. This 37-year-old male flamingo was found dead with blood coming from the mouth. The bird was noted to be limping in the afternoon of the previous day. Necropsy revealed fair body condition frank blood in the nares and mouth wet feathers edema in the head and proximal aspects of the neck nodular pododermatitis on multiple digits these lesions up to 3 cm. in greatest dimension. No subcutaneous adipose stores were identified. Eyes were reddened. Lungs were congested but floated in formalin. Very little intracoelomic fat was identified. Male reproductive tract was present.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 1-year/8-month-old male scarlet-chested parrot was found dead in its exhibit with no prior clinical signs. Gross necropsy revealed scabs and feather loss on the dorsum erythema on the dorsum feather loss on the right caudal wing dried blood on the left nostril worms in the duodenum and jejunum and good body condition.

SKIN ABSCESS NEPHRITIS. This 8-year-old female turtle had a history of a chronic abscess on the foot. The animal’s condition declined despite treatment. At necropsy multiple abscesses were noted in the front foot and the pancreas was unusually firm.

YOLK COELOMITIS BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This 4-year-old lizard underwent celiotomy to remove yellow firm material from the coelomic cavity. The animal later died. At necropsy fibrous adhesions were present in the caudal coelom. Masses of hard yellow material were present in the coelomic cavity.

SPONGIFORM ENCEPHALOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old female opossum developed acute hind end weakness that did not respond to supportive care. Signs progressed from the hind to the front legs and brain with knuckling of the forelimbs and ataxia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed splenomegaly some pinpoint 1 cm. mineralized foci in both lungs prominent submandibular lymph nodes and prominent left adrenal gland.

WEST NILE VIRUS STRESS GOITER. This approximately 18-year/8-month-old male seal died. It presented with acute dyspnea two days prior to death. It was anesthetized and taken to MVS for a nasal CAT scan. It did well during the procedure but died in recovery. It had no response to CPR. At necropsy the seal was in thin body condition. There was a 1 cm. blubber layer ventrally. There was generalized lymphadenopathy. The trachea contained a moderate amount of yellow mucopurulent discharge. The main stem bronchi contained over 20 cc. of mucopurulent discharge. Cultures were taken. The lungs were wet and did not float in formalin. Mucopurulent discharge was expressed from most areas of the lungs. There was a large fibrin tag in the right atrium and on the valves of the right ventricle. Heart kidney and brain were frozen for West Nile virus testing.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION NEPHROCALCINOSIS POSSIBLE HYPERVITAMINOSIS D. This 5-year-old male agouti was noted to have sudden apathy and depression and did not avoid capture. Physical exam revealed weight loss and transparent blood. The animal developed respiratory arrest during anesthetic induction initially responded to CPR but arrest twice more and died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and pale mucous membranes empty small intestine full cecum fecal pellets and full stomach. The capsular surface of the spleen was roughened kidneys were mottled and contained numerous medullary cysts the gall bladder was full and the lungs were mottled.

METASTATIC CARCINOMA YOLK COELOMITIS RENAL GOUT EPICARDIAL GOUT BACTERIAL ESOPHAGITIS. This 5-year-old female chicken was under treatment with crop stasis and was found dead. At necropsy pectoral muscle atrophy was noted and coelomic fat depots were absent. Multiple white foci were present on the epicardium. The serosal surfaces of the GI tract were adherent and contained a firm white irregular mass. Kidneys were pale tan.

HEPATITIS TRAUMA SUSPECT PREDATION. This 3 year old rabbit was found dead on exhibit. It appeared to have been predated. At necropsy there were excessive body fat stores. There was extensive trauma to the neck region with complete cervical dislocation. The head was attached to the body by a small strip of skin. The right humerus was dislocated from the scapula. There was extensive muscle tearing. The lungs were congested and red with mottling of all lobes. The left side was darker than the right side. There were multiple plaque-like foci over the serosal surface of the liver. The stomach had multiple small erosions.

MACRORHABDUS ORNITHOGASTER PROVENTRICULAR DYSPLASIA GRANULOMAS. This 2-year-old male budgie was reported to not be doing well and was found dead. At necropsy there was free and clotted blood within the coelomic cavity as well as reddening in both lungs.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PYOMETRA CYSTITIS INANITION. This 18-year-old female squirrel monkey had marked weight loss and was under treatment. The animal was head pressing and shaking following anesthesia which failed to respond to further treatment. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. The uterus contained a large quantity of purulent material. A small calculus was present in the urinary bladder. The left kidney showed dilation of the pelvis.

XANTHOMATOSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 21-year-old female gecko was found dead. The animal had a recent history of ataxia and head tilt. At necropsy a large white mass was present in the liver. Similar material was adherent to the pericardium. A large granuloma was noted adjacent to the auditory bulla.
adult. Weight: 2300.0 g.  Euthanised; lymphosarcoma; lymphadenopathy; poor condition; pulmonary oedema; nodular left av and aortic valves; collapse/atelectasis right apical and cardiac lobes.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old wild turkey initially was admitted for ataxia and weight loss and tested negative for West Nile virus and heavy metals. Supportive care was administered and the turkey improved over several months but when returned to the area again began to lose weight. Conspecific trauma resulted in recumbency and the bird continued to decline despite supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 3 cm. in diameter smooth light tan left renal mass entrapping the left sciatic nerve.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS STRESS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old rattlesnake was brought into captivity approximately six months ago and did not adapt well. The snake never fed voluntarily. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a single ascarid-like nematode in the upper small intestine.

DISSEMINATED BACTERIAL INFECTION EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female caribou had a history of draining fistulous tracts on the ventral abdomen and biopsies demonstrated inflammation with filamentous bacteria. Exploratory surgery revealed similar intra-abdominal abscesses and the animal was euthanized. Aerobic anaerobic and mycobacterial cultures were obtained. Necropsy revealed multiple abscesses throughout the omentum and on the serosal surface of the rumen within the spleen and on the placental membranes. Numerous adhesions were in the abdominal cavity. Sublumbar and tracheobronchial lymph nodes were slightly enlarged. A 1 cm. dark nodule was in the left cranial lung lobe and a large abscess adhered the right caudal thorax to the diaphragm. Multiple abscesses were also detected throughout the placental and fetal membranes of the female fetus.

CORNEAL LIPIDOSIS EMACIATION. This 6-year-old basilisk had a history of blindness and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed clouded eyes emaciation melanistic and atrophied fat pads four pinky mice in the stomach dark liver digesta in the intestines dark kidneys and male reproductive tract.

PITUITARY CARCINOMA EMACIATION. This 26.5-year-old female zebra was reluctant to get up had blood coming from the mouth and when examined appeared to have bitten its tongue suggesting previous seizure activity. The animal was subsequently found dead in the enclosure the following morning. This patient had a history of intermittent blindness following immobilization a few years earlier and somewhat inappropriate herd interaction for the last few years. Currently the animal was separated from the herd and a companion for a female that was the target for stallion harassment. Necropsy revealed good body condition poor hoof quality a chronic cutaneous lesion over the left lateral stifle and bilateral cutaneous abrasions dorsal to the eyes. Some chronic lesions were in the costochondral junction of the left ribs #7-8. Minimal fat stores were noted and one liter of clear yellow fluid was in the abdomen. In the pericardial sac there were 50 ml. of clear fluid. An 8 mm. dark nodule was noted in the body of the spleen. Some hemorrhage was in the right ventricular free wall tricuspid valve and in the interventricular septum. Similar hemorrhage was noted in the right atrium. Some small nodules were on the leaflets of the aortic and left atrioventricular valves. Ulceration and laceration were noted on the base of the tongue. Wavemouth was noted in the dental arcades. Multiple areas of ulceration were in the stomach primarily at the margo plicatus but extending into the glandular and nonglandular portions of the stomach. A large amount of fluid was in the jejunum. A 1.5 cm. nodule was attached to the caudal aspect of the right medial cerebral hemisphere. Some darkened material was present ventral to the cerebellum and dorsal to the brainstem.

BACTERIAL CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS AND CHOLELITHIASIS OBESITY. This 21-year-old female lemur had a history of lethargy and decreased appetite and examination revealed hyperglycemia with mildly elevated renal values and hypocalcemia. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy identified obesity dental wear dark lungs subjectively thickened left ventricular free wall and a coalescing mass in the right middle hepatic lobe up to 5 cm. in greatest dimension that oozed yellow mucoid material on cut surface.

EUTHANASIA BRONCHIOLOALVEOLAR CARCINOMA. PNEUMONIA PERITONITIS. This 4-month-old female opossum developed hind limb paresis and urinary incontinence. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple fatty masses were present in the abdomen.

SHOCK ENTERITIS. This male 1.5-year-old capybara was found dead lying on right side in a large exhibit pool. At necropsy there was bruising on the inside of both rear legs. There were two small bald patches on each side of the shoulder blades. The lung lobes were mottled red with patchy discoloration. The bronchi contained red frothy foam. Similar foam was in the esophagus. The lungs were red throughout.

ANAPLASTIC SARCOMA SITE NOT SPECIFIED. This 18-year-old intact female Burmese python has a history of bacterial stomatitis and initial biopsies were consistent with inflammation (G09-3357). Progressive development of mandibular masses was noted the snake declined became weak was subsequently diagnosed by biopsy with a poorly-differentiated sarcoma and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

HEMANGIOSARCOMA ABDOMINAL CAVITY PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA EUTHANSIA. This 10-year-old African hunting dog had a history of previously excised oral osteoma and presented acutely with severe weakness and lethargy. Examination revealed a bleeding abdominal mass and anemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 10 cm. cavitated hemorrhagic mass adhered to tissue surrounding the ventral surface of the urinary bladder but not intimately associated with the bladder wall. A 1 cm. area of rupture with associated clot formation was present on the cranial ventral mass. No evidence of metastasis was in other tissues. A few small foci of ulceration were in the gastric mucosa.

DECUBITAL ULCER HISTORICAL TOXOPLASMA. This approximately 9-year-old male red kangaroo had a history of unilateral progressing to bilateral paresis approximately six months prior to death. The animal was confirmed to have toxoplasmosis and responded positively to treatment and supportive care over the next four months; however over the right hip the animal developed an infected progressive deep cubital ulcer. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the animal was in thin body condition there was a large ulceration with purulent debris over the right hip that extended into the musculature the right ventricle contained an irregular pale pink mass that was tightly adhered to all valves the caudal vena cava was narrowed submitted lymph nodes were enlarged the gastric mucosa was brown to purple the blood vessels of the left hemisphere were congested and the ulcer over the right lateral hip extended to the proximal femur periosteum.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 23-year-old female python developed respiratory disease of two days duration and died. Necropsy revealed mucus or pus in the lungs a mottled liver fluid in the pericardium white streaks in the heart discolored ovaries empty stomach petechiae in the trachea and hemorrhagic/bruised lungs.
HEPATIC FRACTURE HEMOPERITONEUM. This male approximately 1-year-old capybara died. At necropsy it had a fissure at the base of the gall bladder and left middle liver lobe.

SUSPECTED COLONIC ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS. This captive bred 25-year-old male baboon had a history of an abnormal gait for several months. Recent trauma from the other baboons was also present. The animal had a recent development of edema near the ischial callosity. The animal also had muscle atrophy most prominent in the rear legs. The animal was anesthetized for examination but arrested approximately 20 min. after initial sedation. Necropsy revealed masses that involved the liver bowel gallbladder vena cava and lungs. Masses had multiple green flecks and produced cream-colored pus. Masses were also present in the diaphragm. The pleural space was filled with fluid bilaterally. Lungs were dark and deflated. Atrioventricular valves had tiny pebble-like bumps bilaterally. The stifle joint was roughened with not a lot of synovial fluid. On radiographs the spine appeared fused.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE UTERINE HEMANGIOMA STRESS. This 8-year/10-month-old female rabbit was humanely euthanized. This rabbit had a mammary tumor removed in July that was diagnosed as a papillary cystadenoma. This rabbit also has a history of progressive cataracts. The rabbit started to lose weight and was not as active as usual. At necropsy the rabbit was emaciated and 6% dehydrated. The mucous membranes were pale. There was a suppurative material subcutaneously around the mammary area as well as in the cervical region ventrally in the subcutaneous space. The right lung was diffusely congested. The uterus was thickened and had areas that were firm ranging from 5 mm. to 1 cm. in diameter. The color ranged from red/black like a hematoma but was firmly adhered and involved the entire uterine section. The kidneys were diffusely pale tan.
ENTERITIS OOPHORITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 23-year-old female desert tortoise was found dead. At gross necropsy the liver was mottled and the heart muscle was friable and soft.

Alopecic and ulcerative dermatitis with occasional mites Comments: No definitive cause for the alopecia in this animal could be determined based on gross necropsy. Attempts to identify the mite observed in the skin scrapings are in progress. Microscopic examination of tissues is in progress. Michael C. ENDOCARDITIS VALVULAR FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VASCULAR THROMBOSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 11/2-year-old female rat had broken a nail and was bleeding. An attempt was made to bandage the foot; however the animal became dyspneic was placed in an oxygen cage but died shortly thereafter. At necropsy the right lung was consolidated. The left lung was mottled. One segment of jejunum appeared hemorrhagic. A 2 mm. dark mass was identified in the left oviduct.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ARTHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 18-year-old male ibex was euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Abnormal hoof wall growth was present on all four feet.
