Consolidation was noted in the lung lobes. Atherosclerosis was noted in the great vessels. Marked tooth wear was also present.
ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female agouti had a history of swelling on the face and a mammary mass. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE INANITION HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 3-year-old dove was flying poorly and presented with opisthotonos and weakness. The animal died immediately following examination. At necropsy the bird was thin.

SPONDYLOSIS LOW GRADE SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male timber rattlesnake had a history of chronic progressive intervertebral arthritis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fused vertebrae in the middle third of the body.

MALIGNANT SERTOLI CELL TUMOR METASTATIC INTESTINAL ADENOCARCINOMA COELOMITIS. This 5-year-old male chicken seizured and died while cleaning fecal matter from the feathers around the vent. This chicken had a recent history of weight loss and a heart arrhythmia. At necropsy the chicken was in fair to poor nutritional condition. There was significant muscle atrophy around the keel. There were small amounts of subcutaneous cavitary and cardiac adipose tissue. The skin of both feet was hyperkeratotic. Almost all of the tissues examined had some black pigmentation present. The lungs were congested with blood and wet but floated in 10% formalin. The mesentery and air sacs were thickened and adhered to the heart and gastrointestinal tract. There were multiple small black spots over the tissues. The left side of the heart was enlarged and flaccid. The left atrioventricular valves were thickened and had multiple small nodules. There was a large amount of necrotic food present in the crop and no food in the proventriculus or ventriculus. One surface of the ventriculus was covered with pink/white masses. The masses were present on the surface of the remainder of the gastrointestinal tract. The masses had very soft interiors. The outer surface of the intestinal tract was covered with masses ranging from 2-8 mm. in diameter. Impression smears of one of the masses showed predominantly mononuclear cells of different sizes with large nucleoli. There were also multiple yellow cystic structures ranging from 5-20 mm. in diameter. Some of these appeared to be multiloculated. The liver was enlarged and adhered to the masses. The kidneys were congested. A large mass with adhesions in the area of the gonad precluded evaluation of the gender. There was a large green mass approximately 25 mm. in diameter in the area of the gonad. On section part of the mass was composed of concentric layers of necrotic tissue. The muscles had multiple black spots. The meninges were black. A swab of the purulent exudate was submitted for culture. Liver kidney and brain were frozen for future use if needed.
adult. Weight: 1700.0 g.  Euthanased.  Chronic peritonitis/serositis.  Suspect intestinal leakage due to foreign body.
FUNGAL PNEUMONIA FOREIGN BODY GRANULOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female buff-banded rail had weight loss neurologic behavior and was euthanized due to lack of response to treatment.

FUNGAL AND PARASITIC DERMATITIS INTRSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 5-year-old male banded Gila monster was four months into a five-month brumation and was found dead. Culture of the liver grew large numbers of Serratia proteamaculans and heavy growth of Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumoniae. Necropsy was unremarkable.
adult. Weight: 1696 g.  Euthanasia.Pulmonary congestions plus/minus collapaes; suspect aganol.

CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE COAGULOPATHY THYROID ADENOMA. This 11-year/9-month-old female warthog was found dead. The sow presented with vulvar swelling and a red crusty discharge on 2/14. The male warthog was found dead on 2/19 after acute onset of lethargy and anorexia. Gross necropsy in that case revealed large numbers of free blood in the abdominal cavity and pericardial sac. Liver from the dead male was submitted for toxicology and this sow was started on oral vitamin K. No anticoagulant compounds were found in the liver of the boar. On the morning of 3/2 the sow was reluctant to rise looked depressed refused food and was heard coughing. At necropsy the bone marrow appeared pale and fatty. There were ample fat stores. There were several 100 ml. of bloody fluid free in the abdominal cavity. There were some hematomas in the abdominal cavity. There was free yellow fluid in the pleural space. There was white froth in the trachea and bronchi. The pericardial sac was distended with frank blood and a large clot that surrounded the entire heart. The left atrioventricular valve was somewhat shrunken and nodular. The liver was dark purple and had a reticular pattern. On cut surface liver was congested and friable. One liver lobe had a subcapsular hematoma. At the proximal duodenum there was a 1 cm. diameter red mucosal mass. The vaginal vault contained a small amount of thick yellow mucoid material. The mucosa of both uterine horns appeared irregular with multiple 2 x 2 mm. raised yellow/tan nodules along with polypoid cystic structures that contained clear fluid. There was a firm 4 x 4 x 4 cm. mass in the thyroid gland.

EUTHANASIA PANCREATIC CARCINOMA ENDOMETRIAL CARCINOMA ADRENAL CARCINOMA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 13-year-old female impala was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic intermittent seizures since 6/8/02. Workup showed no specific findings. West Nile virus serology was negative. At necropsy the impala was in fair to good nutritional condition. The lungs were congested. The liver appeared grossly enlarged. There was a firm approximately 5 cm. in diameter white mass in the mesentery. There were multiple cysts in the kidneys. The largest was 2 cm. in diameter. The blood vessels of the brain were congested. Sections of mesenteric mass liver kidney brain and heart were frozen for future use if needed. West Nile virus tissue PCR was negative.

MYOCARDIA FIBROSIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old male meerkat had a history of chronic lameness that was not responding to medication and the animal did not recover from anesthesia. The meerkat became cyanotic with irregular heartbeat and agonal respirations. Normal cardiac rhythm was retrieved mucous membranes were suffused but the animal did not recover beyond paddling and sternal recumbency. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed obesity and possibly enlarged spleen.

INTESTINAL PERFORATION POSSIBLE INTESTINAL LYMPHOMA SEPSIS. This 9-year-old male wolf was clinically normal in the morning and was found dead in the afternoon. Necropsy revealed brown liquid droplets on the fur of the front limbs a hemorrhagic peritoneal effusion multiple petechiae on the serosal surfaces of the intestine and kidneys reddened pyloric mucosa and erosion of the mucosa through the duodenum to midjejunum a healed perforation to 7 cm. in greatest dimension in midjejunum associated with omental adhesions and suppurative exudate a trichobezoar in the distal jejunum a prominent sternal lymph node and mildly prominent mesenteric lymph node.

GASTRIC BLOAT POSTANESTHETIC RECOVERY. This 10-year-old female gray wolf was immobilized to determine the cause of a 30% weight loss. Immobilization and recovery were uneventful but the animal later bloated and was reimmobilized. The stomach was decompressed the wolf stabilized but died overnight. Necropsy revealed a significantly thickened left ventricular wall 300-700 cc. of serosanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity free blood and clots in the stomach moderate bruising of the stomach at the lesser curvature and proximal one-third of the greater curvature uniformly small liver dark red gastric mucosa.

DUCK VIRAL ENTERITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE SPLENIC NECROSIS. This 7-year-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy the body was in good nutritional condition and approximately 5 ml. of serosanguineous fluid were present in the coelomic cavity. Generalized vascular congestion was noted. The esophagus intestine and colon contained foul smelling brown fluid.

HEPATIC CIRRHOSIS WITH CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS IRON STORAGE. This 8-year-old rainbow lorikeet presented three days ago with tachypnea and an enlarged abdomen. The heart and liver were radiographically determined to be enlarged. White blood cell count was elevated and the animal was anemic and hypoproteinemic. Fecal occult blood was positive and cultures are pending. The animal initially improved with supportive care and antibiotic treatment and then deteriorated rapidly developing ascites. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition and bright yellow skin. In the coelom there were 3-4 ml. of watery straw colored fluid. The air sacs were thickened and milky especially around the right lobe of the liver. The liver spleen and kidneys were bright orange/yellow. The liver was enlarged firm and had rounded edges. Watery feces were in the intestine and frank blood was in the duodenum. The proventriculus was grossly normal and the ventriculus seemed thin walled. The heart was approximately 2x normal size with a flabby right ventricle. Considerable pericardial fluid was present.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA WITH SEPSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This 12-year-old male tamarin had a one-day history of lethargy and weakness with ataxia and arrested shortly after anesthesia for examination. The animal could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed dehydration some crusts on the nares multiple areas of hair loss on the tail slightly thickened pericardium and multiple fibrin strands adhered to the pleural surfaces. There were 2 ml. of pericardial fluid present and was yellow/orange. A small amount of fat was present around the great vessels. The lungs were congested and discolored contained foamy fluid on cut surface and a substantial amount of pleural fluid was in the thoracic cavity. Multiple fibrinous adhesions were in the chest cavity. Yellow fluid was in the trachea. Calculus was present over all teeth. A pinpoint white plaque was on the dorsum of the tongue near the base. Spleen was enlarged and fibrin was on the surface of the tail of the spleen. A small amount of congealed urine was in the urinary bladder.

ENTERITIS SHOCK PULMONARY EDEMA. This 1-year-old lory was found acutely down and passing watery stools. The animal was treated but later died. At necropsy the margins of the liver were dark black. A 2 cm. section of jejunum was thin walled green and filled with feces.

YOLK COELOMITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 5-year-old female teal was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy thick tan colored fluid was present between the heart and liver. The liver was friable. Air sacs were thickened and opaque. Scant ingesta was present in the GI tract.

EUTHANASIA. This male greater than 10-year-old bat was humanely euthanized. It was unable to hang and had difficulty eating for the past four days. It had no response to anti-inflammatories including dexamethasone. At necropsy there were no gross lesions.

OVARIAN TORSION WITH YOLK COELOMITIS SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA AND PAPILLIFORM HYPERPLASIA OF THE OVIDUCT. This 5-year-old female leopard gecko was found dead. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage and torsion of the ovary and generalized pallor.

Liver: Moderately severe; centrilobular to diffuse hepatic lipidosis Subcutaneous mass: Mammary adenoma Hepatic lipidosis Mammary adenoma Comments The exact cause of death was not identified histologically. Marked post mortem autolysis may have precluded diagnosis of gastrointestinal disease in this case. E.coli were isolated by bacterial culture of the intestine; however; these organisms likely represent normal GI flora. PAS stain is pending on sections of kidney to determine the significance of the described renal alterations. The results will be described in an addendum report. Jennifer Lamoureux; DVM

LEIOMYOMA (VAGINA) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY FIBROSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS ENTERITIS ESOPHAGEAL HEMORRHAGE. This 13-year-old female pygmy goat was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the body appeared bloated and straw-colored fluid was present in the thorax. A trichobezoar was found in the rumen. An 8 x 6 cm. irregular lobulated mass was present in the reproductive tract. Scattered smaller masses were also present in the vaginal wall.

DUODENAL ULCERATION SEPSIS. This approximately 1-year-old male North American river otter developed peracute hematemesis on exhibit was inappetent and died while anesthetized for endoscopic exam. Necropsy revealed frank blood in the proximal half of the small intestine and tan pasty ingesta in the distal small intestine. The left lung was multifocally red and firm and bled when incised. The liver was congested.

CEREBRAL CORTICAL ATROPHY CORTICAL LAMINAR NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 13-year-old female monkey presented for dystocia and underwent cesarean section and ovariohysterectomy. The animal was treated for sepsis and disseminated intravascular coagulation during the following week after surgery. The animal became acutely nonvisual five days after surgery and required assisted feeding. The animal was euthanized due to quality of life concerns.

PANCREATIC CARCINOMA MYOCARDITIS SEPTICEMIA RENAL GOUT HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 7-year-old alligator lizard was inappetent and later died. At necropsy the liver was dark. A white firm mass was adherent to the spleen and pancreas. Marked coelomic effusion was also present.

TRAUMA SHOCK CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 4.5-year-old male kangaroo was being transferred to another exhibit. The animal collapsed and died during transport. At necropsy a moderate quantity of clear yellow fluid was present in the abdomen. A possible fracture of C3 was identified radiographically.

ANESTHETIC RELATED EATH INANITION COLONIC IMPACTION. This 1-year/1-month-old male warthog died during anesthesia. Immediate resuscitation attempts were made. At necropsy the warthog was thin and had a prominent spine. There was white crusty skin over the bridge of the rostrum. The musculature of the caudal aspect of the rear legs was pale. There was 65 ml. of slightly cloudy serosanguineous fluid free in the abdomen. There was little fat in the abdomen and thorax. Both lungs were red and appeared to be collapsed. The tracheal mucosa was red where the endotracheal tube likely ended. Some areas of duodenal mucosa were red. The jejunum was red throughout its length and was empty. There was redness in the serosa. The last 1.5-2 turns of the centrifugal turns of the ascending colon and the transverse colon were distended (7 cm. in diameter) and contained very hard green ingesta admixed with a mat of hay fragments cut into various lengths and other unidentified material. The descending colon was empty and was only 3 cm. in diameter. One lobe of the thyroid was deep red and the other was rather friable and smaller.
YOLK COELOMITIS HEMOSIDEROSIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 22-year-old female flamingo was found dead. Necropsy revealed eggs in various stages of development and darkened inflamed and friable ovaries.

ARTERIOSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS THYROID SARCOMA SUPBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA. This 17-year-old female tiger ratsnake was euthanized for progressive spondylosis and deteriorating quality of life. At necropsy there were minimal fat stores. The thyroid gland was enlarged and contained mostly yellowish gelatinous material with a small firm white nodule present at its center. Small nodules were present throughout the lungs. Hepatic lobes were variably encased in a white membrane. Pinpoint black spots are present throughout hepatic lobes. A small cyst was at the distal pole of the left kidney. Large nodular bony proliferations were along the ventral aspect of the spine. There were bilateral cataracts.

SEPSIS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 14-year-old male tamarin was examined for lethargy and poor body condition. Examination revealed an enlarged liver and hypothermia with loose feces around the rectum. The animal was slow to recover from anesthesia and died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed moderate to severe mottling of the entire surface and cut surface of the liver a possible mass in the left adrenal gland roughened pancreas numerous nodules in the mesentery (probably lymph nodes) and no other abnormalities.

ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA INTESTINAL MICROABSCESSES EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female armadillo presented obtunded in appetent and bleeding from the mouth. An exophytic growth was in the floor of the mouth and alveolar ridge and breeched the mandibular ramus. Gas was in the intestine and cecum and the animal had a heart murmur. The animal partially recovered from anesthesia but was never able to stay upright for lengthy intervals and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin heart muscle possible adrenal enlargement cachexia and involuted reproductive tract.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male rat had a history of chronic recurrent pneumonia and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed consolidation of the caudal dorsal aspect of both lungs the right middle and lower pulmonary lobes more severely affected than the others and covered in small raised bumps. Numerous coalescing abscesses with mucopurulent material were in both caudal lungs.

TRAUMA ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 29-year-old male bald eagle was found dead. At necropsy there was abundant evidence of predation including detachment of the head soft tissue loss over the cervical region keel and dorsal scapular region and penetrating wound in the cranial coelomic cavity. There were abundant fly larvae on the carcass.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PULMONARY EDEMA ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 22-year-old female addax was immobilized for dental exam and dentistry. Anesthetic recovery was normal; however the animal collapsed and died shortly after anesthesia. At necropsy firm areas were present in the right lung along with ruminal contents.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE POLYURIA/POLYDIPSIA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 4.5-year-old male pig had a history of chronic polyuria and polydyspnea with hyposthenuria and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of serous fluid in the abdominal cavity greatly distended urinary bladder and no other gross abnormalities.

CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE HEMOSIDEROSIS INANITION GASTRITIS HEPATITIS. This 21-year-old female monkey died. It had a positive reaction to TB test. At necropsy there was no evidence of tuberculosis. There was fluid in the abdomen and chest. There was a large amount of pericardial fluid. The lungs were clear. The liver was mottled. The spleen was pale brown. The heart valves were compromised. The adrenal gland seemed enlarged.
EXTRAVASCULAR HEMOLYSIS. This greater than 1-year-old lory of unknown gender was found dead. It was otherwise healthy the day prior to death. No lesions were noted at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS (GROSS DIAGNOSIS) INANITION COLITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS TESTICULAR MINERALIZATION. This 13-year-old male gazelle had a history of weight loss and lameness. The animal was euthanized due to the debilitated condition. At gross necropsy the animal was emaciated and had severe osteoarthritis of the coxofemoral joints and moderate spondylosis.
NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 6-year-old female gecko was under treatment with calcium and force feedings. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the animal was thin.

BONE FRACTURES EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male red kangaroo had a history of bilateral tibia and fibular fractures and a right tarsal fracture that were repaired with bone plates screws and pins. When a new fracture occurred above the bone plate on the right side euthanasia was performed. Necropsy revealed reddening of the duodenal mucosa and serosa and no other abnormalities other than the bone fractures.

MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION PULMONARY ATELECTASIS SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 5.5-year-old female sheep has a history of weight loss. Ketonuria and proteinuria were noted on a urine sample. The animal died despite treatment. At necropsy the omasum contained very dry impacted material. A 2 ft. section of jejunum was filled with red/brown fluid.

ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2-year-old female hedgehog had a two month history of weight loss mite infestation proptosis and bleeding mouth loose teeth and apparent squamous cell carcinoma involving the sinuses and maxilla. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA OSTEITIS DEFORMANS GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS. This 19-year-old male python was euthanized due to severe spondylosis and deteriorating condition. A moderate quantity of clear yellow fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. The vertebral bodies show marked irregular proliferation.

CATARACTS CHRONIC KERATITIS SCLEROSING PERITONITIS BILIARY CYSTIC HYPERPLASIA. This 10-year-old male domestic rabbit had a history of chronic cataracts mild head tilt and slow loss of condition. Ultrasound revealed severe hepatic disease with multiple cystic structures containing some “sulfur granules”. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male marine toad has a history of poor bone development. A dilated loop of bowel was diagnosed by celiotomy in November 2012 and the animal presented with substantial weight loss (approximately 20%) inappetence and no fecal production. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 1-2 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the coelomic cavity some small punctate white foci were in the lungs and kidneys were firmly adhered to each other and to nearby loops of intestine although intestines appeared otherwise normal except for previously diagnosed megacolon. A coelomic membrane near the cloaca was thickened.

COLONIC MYXOSARCOMA URATE STASIS INANITION. This 27-year-old male Gila monster was found moribund and dehydrated. The animal was found dead despite treatment. At necropsy a large quantity of fecal material was present in the distal colon. Adjacent tissue was thickened firm and white. Kidneys were enlarged pale and filled with urates.

BACTERIAL/FLAGELLATE ENTEROCOLITIS PERITONITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 10-year-old male squirrel monkey had multiple surgeries over a three year period for removal of large lipomas that developed on the left leg abdominal wall and neck. The animal was apparently healthy at the time of death. Necropsy revealed 1.5 cc. of fluid in the pericardial sac and cytology suggested a transudate and possible heart failure.

METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 13-year-old female sheep had a history of chronic weight loss inappetence and lack of response to treatment. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large white to yellow mass in the left thoracic inlet in the area of the thyroid or thymus. Three more masses were noted at the heart base. Two 1 cm. masses were in each pulmonary lobe and a small white spot was in the liver. Ruminal papillae were stunted or short. Mammary glands had milk and tan/brown clear substance.

Lung: Severe diffuse acute hemorrhagic pneumonia Adrenal gland: Bilateral adrenal hyperplasia Skin: Moderate focally extensive alopecia Comments A definitive cause of death was not observed on gross examination. The lesions within the lung suggest a bacterial infection. The adrenal hyperplasia and alopecia suggests Cushing's syndrome; however; alopecia in guinea pigs can be a result of several disease entities including bacterial skin infection; ectoparasites; systemic salmonellosis; and vitamin C deficiency. Histopathology; bacteriology; and parasitology are pending and the results will be issued in the final report. Erin B. Howey; D Haired skin; flank: Moderate diffuse epidermal hyperkeratosis with multiple intralesional mites (consistent with Trixacaris caviae). Haired skin; prepuce: Marked diffuse epidermal hyperkeratosis; and sebaceous hyperplasia with multiple intrafollicular nematodes (consistent with Pelodera sp.). Adrenal gland: Bilateral cortical hyperplasia Stomach: Mild multifocal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate Ectoparasitism Comments The main findings are the ectoparasite infestations. Trixacaris caviae causes sarcoptic mange in guinea pigs and results in severe pruritus and; in severe cases; seizures and death. Pelodera sp. is a free living nematode that can be found in soil and damp bedding. The nematode larvae invade hair follicles resulting in pruritus and secondary bacterial infection. Infestation of both parasites; especially pelodera; suggests immunosuppression or underlying stress in this guinea pig. The adrenocortical hyperplasia also suggests increased cortisol release; consistent with stress. An underlying cause of immunosuppression was not observed. Husbandry of the animals should be evaluated to rule out external causes of stress (overcrowding; etc.). Erin B. Howey; D
BACTERIAL STOMATITIS HEPATITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 8-year-old alligator lizard was found dead. At necropsy caseous stomatitis was noted in the maxilla. The liver was enlarged yellow and firm.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS POSSIBLE SELENIUM DEFICIENCY ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC SEGMENTAL ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male/castrated domestic goat had a greater than two year history of weight loss anemia eosinophilia intermittent inappetence and intermittent diarrhea. The goat had been doing well until placed on a reducing diet for obesity. As the energy level of the diet was increased the animal continued to lose weight. About this time the amount of pelleted feed was reduced to a problem with cystic calculi in the herd and the goats lived mostly on hay trace mineral salt and browse. The goat herd developed selenium deficiency based on serum levels but no clinical signs and selenium was given via rumen boluses. Biopsies of muscle gut and liver did not show significant abnormalities. The goat was sedated for ultrasound of the cranial abdomen to look for cysticerci in the cranial abdomen that may have been missed during one of the exploratory surgeries. Shortly after sedation the goat regurgitated and aspirated. The goat was treated for the aspiration for four days but eventually was euthanized due to complex and manifold problems. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting serous atrophy of fat and fatty bone marrow. The liver was mildly swollen especially the left caudal lobe which was previously biopsied. Bacillus sp. was cultured from gallbladder aspirate.

METASTATIC SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA PLEURAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 25-year-old female llama had a recent history of poor condition and decreased appetite. The animal was found dead. At necropsy moderate ventral edema was noted. A large quantity of straw colored fluid was present in the pleural cavity.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This approximately 3-year-old male wallaby died. It was found shocky the day prior to death and emergency treatment resulted in 24 hour recovery. At necropsy there was a large (4 in. mass) found near the mesenteric root. There were multiple small (0.5 cm.) nodules spread throughout the mesentery. The wallaby was emaciated.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS HEPATOCELLULAR TOXIC CHANGE OCULAR TRAUMA. This approximately 8-year-old male sugar glider was found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition ruptured left globe associated with dried and crusted tissue and no other abnormalities noted.

ULCERATIVE PODODERMATITIS AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old male Chilean flamingo had a one day history of lethargy and bilateral paresis suggesting sciatic impingement. The bird also had chronic pododermatitis. Blood work revealed elevated uric acid levels and electrolyte abnormalities and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed keel ulceration bilaterally severe pododermatitis visceral gout and bilateral renomegaly with urate deposits.

AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL GOUT CAECAL FIBROSARCOMA. This greater than 35-year-old male flamingo died. It was thin weak and was treated with antibiotics fluids and heat. The bird was breathing heavy. At necropsy there was no fat present in the coelomic cavity. The gastrointestinal tract was empty. The ventriculus contained some vegetative material and rocks. The tissue around the heart and on the serosal surface of viscera contained white chalky foci. The kidneys were bright yellow to tan with specks of white chalky material diffusely throughout. There was a small mass approximately 3 mm. in diameter present on the most proximal serosal aspect of one of the caeca at the entrance into the small intestine. The mass was smooth pink and firm on palpation.

INANITION VENTRICULITIS SUSPECT INTESTINAL AMYLOIDOSIS. This 13-year-old male ibis was found dead. It appeared weak and had its wings drooping. It was treated. At necropsy there was acute hemorrhagic enteritis.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 6-year-old male sloth was found during the morning check hooked onto the front of the cage mesh with the left claws and sunken between the cage mesh and branching. The sloth was unresponsive and was not breathing. It had eaten the previous day. Necropsy revealed thickenings in the walls of the major arteries pale areas towards the periphery of the major hepatic lobe gray discoloration of the glandular portion of the pylorus large amount of ingesta in the stomach and no other remarkable findings.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS. This 2-year-old female California sea lion was admitted as a yearling with bilateral cataracts and was nonvisual. She was in captivity at Fort MacArthur for over one year to facilitate placement approval and cataract surgery. Surgery was performed on September 10th and the sea lion was found dead on September 14th. She did not eat the day prior to surgery when she was moved to a new enclosure nor did she eat in the days following surgery. She passed thick tan mucus from the rectum the day before she died. Necropsy revealed icterus in the blubber layer ecchymoses in the neck adjacent to the jugular vein bruising in the musculature over the right shoulder and right hip atelectatic cranial lung lobes that were dark red enlarged and reddened gastric lymph nodes approximately 100 ml. of clear bloody fluid in the abdomen reddening of the distal small intestine and colon and thick mucus adhered to the mucosa of the colon.

EUTHANASIA HYDROCEPHALY CEREBRAL INFARCTION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE CHRONIC GASTRITIS. This 18-year-old female tiger has a history of declining condition including altered mentation and decreased mobility. The animal presented with seizures and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple collapsed disk spaces were noted. Dilation of the lateral ventricles was noted in the brain.

EUTHANASIA MYOSITIS ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS INANITION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 25-year-old female tortoise had a two month history of lethargy and inappetence. The animal presented with fly strike and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy maggots were identified in the oral cavity and adjacent to the forelimb. Adipose tissue depots were absent and generalized muscle atrophy was noted. Dark foci were noted in the gastric mucosa. Calculi were present in the urinary bladder.

ACUTE PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 2-year-old female impala was gored by a male that was housed with the herd overnight. Gross necropsy revealed good body condition a 2 cm. wound in the left lateral thoracic wall a puncture of the adjacent lung that extended through the diaphragm multiple large blood clots in the thoracic and abdominal cavities and pregnancy with an approximately 2-month-old fetus.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male hedgehog has a history of chronic progressive weakness with unilateral front leg eventually becoming proprioceptive deficits in the rear legs. The animal had a good appetite. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA ADENOCARCINOMA (LIVER LUNG) RENAL MINERALIZATION FEATHER CYST. This 41-year-old penguin presented with weight loss and dyspnea. Elevations in white cells and uric acid were noted. The animal failed to respond to treatment and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy multiple white nodules were noted in the liver and lung.

AMYLOIDOSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 18-year/2-month-old male flamingo died. It was found down in its enclosure. It was given supportive care fluids and steroids. It had some improvement but was still flaccid in the legs. The muscles were soft. There was moderate bumblefoot. At necropsy the kidneys were bilaterally pale. There was myocardial streaking and necrosis. The liver was pale and friable. There was lipofuscin pigment within the lungs.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK PULMONARY HEMANGIOSARCOMA. This 11-year-old male chicken was on medication for ear and nose infections. It was found dead in the morning upside down with fluid coming from its nose and mouth. Necropsy revealed a large amount of food in the crop food in the nares choanal slit and oral cavity regurgitated brown fluid material in the trachea a single dark lesion on the serosal surface of the right distal hepatic lobe red wet lungs bilaterally chronic pododermatitis lesions and roughened skin over the ventral coelomic cavity.

ACUTE INTESTINAL TORSION CHRONIC UVEITIS (LIKELY GLAUCOMA). This greater than 32-year-old female harbor seal had a few day history of lethargy following an episode in which it fell into the moat. Physical examination revealed chronic eye lesions but the eyes appeared to be visual. Following the episode of falling in the moat the animal became lethargic developed respiratory distress and died. Necropsy revealed an intestinal torsion.

BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS WITH COELOMITIS. This greater than 8-year-old lorikeet was found fluffed and dyspneic on the ground in the morning and died en route to the hospital. Necropsy revealed coelomitis cachexia splenomegaly atherosclerosis hemorrhage in the skull bones hepatomegaly and generalized cardiomegaly.

TOXOPLASMOSIS ESOPHAGEAL CANDIDIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old red-necked wallaby presented with ataxia and neurologic signs. Serology identified a strong positive titer at presentation consistent with acute toxoplasmosis. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to decline and was euthanized one week after presentation. Clotting times had been elevated prior to death. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and no other external abnormalities. Prominent inguinal lymph nodes were noted and the lungs were mottled dark red to pink and some portions sank in formalin. On cut surface the spleen had numerous pale 1-2 mm. nodules.

EUTHANASIA HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA HEPATITIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 15-year/4-month-old female red kangaroo was humanely euthanized. It had been immobilized for workup and had severe degenerative joint disease declining health and a tooth root abscess. At necropsy there was a 10 x 1-2 cm. firm scab on the lateral aspect of the rear leg. There was crepitus evident on the left rear limb at the stifle joint. The joint and capsule revealed a large amount of thick dark yellow flocculent fluid. The patella-like structure appeared calcified and not as smooth as on the other leg. There were erosions of the surface of the bone and bony proliferation along the distal end of the femur at the lateral and medial condyles. The tibial plate showed similar changes. There was a 3 cm. in diameter irregular red structure found near the craniodorsal aspect of the liver. On cut surface there were pockets of black fluid in the mass. The right globe was excised from the skull and there was a large amount of tan/yellow caseous material found retrobulbar. The caseous material was continuous with the abscess in the upper right molar.

SQUAMOUS PAPILLOMA (SKIN) CLOACITIS HEPATITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 27-year-old male flamingo was found dead. At necropsy a feather cyst was present on the abdomen. The keel was prominent. Great vessels appeared larger than normal. Hemorrhage was noted adjacent to the kidney.

CEREBRAL ABSCESS OSTEOMYELITIS HEPATITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS BACTERIAL ENCEPHALITIS. This 11-year-old male meerkat was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a draining tract was present in the right mandible related to a canine tooth root abscess. Other teeth are fractured. Bones were soft and easily fractured. A firm dark lesion was found in the cerebrum dorsal to the left lateral ventricle.

HOOF OVERGROWTH ABOMASITIS AND COLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female Grévy’s zebra arrived in quarantine 1.5 years earlier with chronic hoof overgrowth pertaining to both front feet. The animal received supportive care for the problem but an additional problem developed in the left front foot and quality of life was declining so euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an open wound on the bottom of the left front foot near the tip of the toe resembling a bruise. Approximately 500 ml. of clear straw-colored fluid was in the abdomen. Moderate valvular thickening was noted in the left and right heart and a depression was in the proximal aorta in the location that the ductus arteriosus had been. The stomach had extensive ulceration. Approximately 75% of the proximal small intestine contains submucosal hemorrhage and was thickened. A cyst was in one ovary.

FATTY LIVER. This approximately 8-year-old female pit viper died. It had a history of swelling in the caudal one-third of the body that was evident about three weeks priori to death. The snake was started on antibiotics and fluid therapy. Blood work was unremarkable. At necropsy there were adequate fat bodies in the coelom. There were two large firm irregularly shaped structures in the coelom that appeared to be ovaries. They contained several inspissated follicles. They measured 6 x 8 cm. in length. The terminal colon was thickened and edematous. It was purple and had a small amount of fecal material.

GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS PROTEIN LOSING NEPHROPATHY CHRONIC BRONCHOSPASMS (POSSIBLE ANESTHESIA-RELATED). This approximately 3-year-old female black footed ferret was being treated for anorexia and dehydration. Recovery from anesthesia was typically prolonged. The animal died spontaneously and necropsy revealed a small necrotic mass on a stalk in the lower right abdominal quadrant thin body condition and large multicolored and streaked kidneys.

SOFT TISSUE SARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male white-faced whistling duck had been noted to be lame on the right leg for a few days was found lying on its side in the planter by the lake where it lives and was noted to have a large soft tissue mass involving the right femur. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed that the mass did not appear to involve the bone.

MULTIORGAN INFLAMMATORY DISEASE. This 3-year/2-month-old male parrot was found dead in public area of exhibit. It was moved off exhibit in October due to labored breathing and was released back into exhibit on 11/1. It was negative for polyomavirus. At necropsy there was hemorrhage on the cere. There was hemorrhage throughout the neck beneath the skin. There was hemorrhage within the cranial lungs throughout the liver and in the coelomic cavity. The spleen was 1.5 cm. in diameter.

EUTHANASIA INANITION UNDIFFERENTIATED SARCOMA (CLOACA) HEPATITIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 17-year-old female boa presented with a mass proximal to the cloaca. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the snake was thin. A 2 x 1.5 cm. soft tissue mass was present beneath the skin proximal to the vent.

EUTHANASIA GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA NEPHRITIS HEPATITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 22-year-old female boa was found unresponsive with its head in the water bowl. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy clear fluid was present in the trachea and lung. Small firm white nodules were present on the serosa of the coelomic viscera. A large fluid filled space was present in the caudal coelom.

CERVICAL FRACTURE TRAUMA ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 34-year-old male flamingo was found acutely down. The animal died prior to treatment. At necropsy a cervical dislocation with hemorrhage in the adjacent muscle was noted. Midcervical fracture was present in the vertebrae. Minimal fat depots were present.
HEPATITIS AIR SACCULITIS. This 7-year-old budgie had difficulty perching and was euthanized.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS TO LUNG DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS. This greater than 23-year-old female addax had increasingly thin body condition in the months prior to euthanasia despite large quantities of feed. The animal also had difficulty standing and ambulating. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and good postmortem condition with normal ingesta throughout the alimentary tract. The uterine body was diffusely thickened.

BROAD LIGAMENT LEIOMYOMA. This approximately 2-year-old female Wyandotte chicken presented for lethargy. A mass was palpated in the coelom and presumed to be an egg. The chicken was anesthetized for workup but died under anesthesia. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition dehydration possible pulmonary hemorrhage from CPR dried feces and urates around the vent a friable and pale liver inactive ovary a thickened oviduct with inspissated egg material in the lumen and a 3 cm. pale tan oval mass adjacent to the shell gland.

CHRONIC YOLK COELOMITIS. This female approximately 8-year-old chuckwalla died postoperatively. There were several hard masses within the abdomen and had not laid eggs since 1998. Surgery revealed extensive diffuse fibrosis and three large black masses were removed and identified as being eggs. Numerous granulomas were also removed. The ovaries and several developing follicles were also surgically removed. At necropsy there was a mass palpated within the subcutaneous area in the right lateral abdomen. The area was an aggregate of granulomas located between the muscle wall and the skin. There was diffuse fibrosis to numerous organs including the lung stomach and intestine. There were scant adipose stores present. There were several granulomas free within the coelomic cavity. The liver was diffusely mottled.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS INANITION THYROID FOLLICULAR CYST ENTERITIS. This 16-year-old female llama was euthanized due to progressive renal disease. At necropsy diffuse subcutaneous edema was noted. A small fluid-filled cyst was present in the thyroid. Marked edema was noted within the stomach.
COELOMITIS ENTERITIS. This 3-year-old budgie was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy abdominal air sacs contained a large quantity of fluid and urates.

PRESUMED TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 18-year-old male ring-tailed lemur had a three-week history of inappetence. The animal had exploratory surgery three days prior to death. At necropsy the right ventricular wall was subjectively thickened. The small intestinal mucosa was reddened and there was a small nodular mass in the mid small intestines. The liver had mild adhesions with hemorrhage. A pale yellow mass was in the liver with distinct margins. Urinary bladder was distended large and difficult to express. Thick white material was in the proximal urethra. The right kidney had a pale surface and a small cyst in the medulla. The left kidney was firm.

ACUTE SEPSIS. This 7-year-old male golden lion tamarin was admitted hypothermic and moribund and radiographs revealed spondylosis at T10-11. Initial blood work was within normal limits. The animal died while trying to warm it up. Necropsy revealed overconditioning with fat present around the pectoral muscles and a short tail from previous amputation. The cecum appeared slightly thickened. The pancreas was hemorrhagic. The liver had a nutmeg appearance. Intra-abdominal fat was copious. Gelatinous urine was in the bladder. Culture was obtained of the jejunal contents.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2-year-old female house mouse recently developed rapid respiration had a rough haircoat and a rounded appearance. Examination revealed possible hepatomegaly or abdominal mass and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition decreased muscling rough haircoat abdominal enlargement diffusely enlarged liver and spleen and a 9 mm. flat white plaque on the greater curvature of the stomach corresponding to the splenic attachment. The right lung was effaced by firm tan homogenous tissue.

EMACIATION CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 7-year-old rainbow lorikeet is the second of this species to die in four days. Necropsy revealed thin body condition. A few white spots were noted on the outside of the intestine.

EUTHANASIA MALIGNANT SEMINOMA. This approximately 13-year-old male duck was humanely euthanized. It had been lame on the left leg for nearly two weeks. A large abdominal mass was noted on examination and radiographs. Fine needle aspirate indicated possible carcinoma. At necropsy there were two large firm white abdominal masses that were suspected to be testicular tissue. The left measured 12 x 5 cm. and was lumpy. The right measured 9 x 4 cm. and was smooth. The left kidney was also infiltrated with abnormal tissue. There was cataract in the right eye. There was food in the proventriculus.

RENAL ADENOMA URATE STASIS PNEUMONIA AIR SACCULITIS SHOCK. This 22-year-old female spoonbill was found down. The animal had a recent history of weight loss. At necropsy the body was thin. A large quantity of fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. A large mass was present adjacent to the ovary. Foci of necrosis were present deep within the mass. Kidneys were not identified and may have contributed to the formation of the mass.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR SPINAL CORD AND RENAL DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS (CLINCAL DIAGNOSIS) CATARACTS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old Malayan tiger had a history of ataxia in the rear legs loss of body condition and had been treated for chronic renal disease of 19 months duration. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed several areas of scar tissue on pressure points some inactive cracks in the front foot pads atrophy of muscle over the pelvic and shoulder area bony protuberances on the ventral aspect of the spine in the cervical area and thoracolumbar area multiple white foci were in the pulmonary parenchyma that were firm on cut surface and the left lung had a firm parenchyma. The left lung was moderately congested (left lateral recumbency). Congestion was mild in the duodenal mucosa and moderate in the jejunal mucosa. The adrenal glands were firm and difficult to cut and were dark on cut surface. The wall of the urinary bladder was thickened. Urine appeared grossly normal and kidneys were firm when sectioned.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 5-year-old male crocodile monitor presented with lethargy difficulty moving the hind legs and decreased appetite. Necropsy revealed enlargement of the right femur humerus and left tibia. The animal received supportive care but subsequently died. Necropsy revealed loss of definition in the kidneys and soft renal parenchyma. Cortical medullary distinction was present in the bone but with very thick uniform proliferation surrounding the cortex of the bone. Male reproductive tract was identified.

LYMPHOMA COLONIC NEMATODIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old male rat had a history of chronic recurrent pneumonia that was unresponsive to treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified chronic scarring and consolidation of the lungs.
juvenile. Weight: 5.3 g.  Open. Suspect trauma to distal limbs. Possible haemopericardium.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PLEURITIS EPICARDITIS SEPSIS. This 9-year-old female kangaroo had a seizure four days prior to death. In the following three days she was noted to be exhibiting some odd behaviors and possible respiratory distress. The animal had been anesthetized 2-3 weeks earlier for some pouch edema similar to an episode that was seen the previous year. The kangaroo died and necropsy revealed a dilated cardiac sac with pericardial effusion severe thickening of the pericardium with visible fibrinous and fibrous adhesions in multiple areas between the pericardium and the cardiac musculature. The heart was adhered to the body wall on the left side and it was difficult to separate the pericardium from the pleura. A single roundworm was found in the stomach and 60 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was in the peritoneal cavity. A mammary vein was dilated and may have contained a thrombus. The left adrenal gland was pale at the periphery and reddened at the center. A 5 cm. area on the internal thoracic wall at approximately the sixth intercostal space was dark but no fractures were seen. A focal hard mass was on the left mandible two-thirds the length of the ramus approximately 1 cm. in length and green/brown. Multiple abscesses were present along the bronchial tree with complete consolidation of the middle and caudal pulmonary lobes and severe adhesions on both sides worse on the right side. Only the left dorsal pulmonary lobe appeared close to normal in appearance and architecture. A small amount of mucoid material was in the uterine body and horns.

PANCREATIC ACINAR ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female guanaco had a two month history of poor appetite azotemia and elevated hepatic values. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed peritonitis and a mass at the root of the mesentery.

ENTERITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 1-year-old lory was found dead without premonitory signs. Marked weight loss was noted at necropsy. Extensive hemorrhage was present over the cervical vertebrae which extended into the skull. A large bruised area was present over the right humerus and ulna.

BACTERIAL MENINGITIS WITH SEPSIS CHRONIC ENTEROTYPHLOCOLITIS. This 11-year-old female tamarin presented for a swollen right eye was immobilized for examination and the following day appeared ill and not doing well. Blood work revealed hypoglycemia hypokalemia and supportive care was administered. The tamarin died later and necropsy revealed hemorrhage involving the right caudal lung lobe edematous lungs pinpoint lesions on the surface of the liver enlarged kidneys and adrenals prominent mesenteric lymph nodes splenomegaly with irregular shape prominent lymphoid tissue in the colon and some petechiae on the serosa.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 2.5-year-old female lorikeet was found dead on exhibit with no prior signs of illness. It is from a group in which there has been abrupt mortality in the last few days in several birds. Necropsy revealed some abrasions and contusions of the head and no gross lesions. Female reproductive tract was identified.

ENTERITIS PNEUMONIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 14-year-old male wallaby was examined under anesthesia for lethargy and inappetence. Periodontal disease was noted. The animal was found seizuring the following day and died en route to the hospital. At necropsy atherosclerosis was present in the aortic root. A length of rope was identified in the stomach; however the foreign body did not appear to be obstructing the pylorus. A segment of the distal jejunum was dark red to purple and contained blood.

CERVICAL FRACTURE. This 25-year-old female flamingo would not stand after being examined and was treated for myopathy. The bird developed cardiac arrest shortly after the exam and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous and muscular hematomas in the caudal cervical region hemorrhages in the ventral aspect of the trachea hemorrhage in the abdominal muscles joint laxity and crepitus in the last cervical intervertebral joint hematoma at the thoracic inlet miliary pale pattern with mild regional hemorrhage in the liver mildly darkened kidneys pale apex of the heart.

CALCINOSIS CIRCUMSCRIPTA RENAL TUBULAR MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old naked mole rat had a subcutaneous white mass in the left neck region. A fine needle aspirate identified calcium crystals. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

TRAUMA GASTRIC PERFORATION. This 2-year-old boa was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy frothy blood-tinged fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. The lining of the stomach was thinned with a small hole associated with a puncture from an ingested rat bone.

ABSCESS COELOMITIS. This 8-year-old male axolotl was under treatment for ascites and an abscess on the left side. The animal died after a few days of treatment. At necropsy a 4 mm. white area was identified on the left side corresponding to a subcutaneous abscess. The lesion did not appear to penetrate the body wall. The caudal half of the coelomic cavity was occupied by a 3 cm. in diameter thick walled fluid filled structure. The mass was filled with cloudy fluid and flocculent material.

EUTHANSIA ENCEPHALITIS. This greater than 13-year-old female boa was humanely euthanized. It had a chronic history of neurologic disease characterized by major head and body tilt. At necropsy the boa had abnormal flexion of the head and neck. There was food in the colon. There was a very small amount of fat present.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CEREBRAL VASCULAR MINERALIZATION CEREBRAL EDEMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 12-year-old male tamarin had a history of diabetes mellitus and cardiomegaly due to right heart enlargement. The animal was found weak and seizures followed by cardiopulmonary arrest ensued. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy the liver spleen and heart were moderately enlarged.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RUMENITIS. This 17-year-old female ibex was acting blind and crashed into the walls. The animal was sedated and euthanized. At necropsy bruising and hemorrhage were noted over the head. Marked dental attrition was present. Erosion of articular cartilage of joints was present. Mature cataracts were present in both eyes.

HEPATITIS SPLENITIS NEPHRITIS MENINGITIS. This 8-year-old male marmoset was found seizuring. Treatment was initiated; however the animal remained minimally responsive and later died. At necropsy a large mass was present on the spleen.

AMYLOIDOSIS ARTICULAR GOUT BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male duck was found dead. It had been pulled off exhibit the day prior to death due to lameness in the left leg. At necropsy the duck was in good body condition. The liver was enlarged and discolored. It was friable when manipulated. The kidneys were discolored. The heart valves appeared to be calcified. The left tibiotarsal/tarsometatarsal joint was enlarged and contained caseous material that extended distally down the tendon sheaths.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA COLONIC HEMORRHAGE INANITION. This 19-year-old female rattlesnake had a recent exploratory celiotomy for a colonic impaction. The colon was resected and anastomosed. Anesthetic recovery was uneventful; however the following day the animal was found dead. At necropsy hemorrhagic fluid was present in the coelomic cavity. Other organs had no significant histologic changes.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE. This 4-year-old female marmoset presented for severe lethargy and respiratory distress. Severe abdominal effusion was noted on radiographs. Treatment was initiated; however the animal died a short time later. At necropsy the thorax and abdomen contained straw-colored fluid. Lungs sank in formalin. The heart was rounded and there was marked pericardial effusion. Multiple nodular masses were noted in the mesentery.

EUTHANASIA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 9-month-old peccary developed acute respiratory distress. Purulent discharge was noted in the lungs. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the pulmonary lobes were effaced by miliary white material with purulent discharge in the trachea.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS INTERSTITIAL AMYLOIDOSIS. This 16-year-old female sea lion presented with lethargy and marked weight loss. The animal’s condition initially improved with treatment but rapidly deteriorated. Blood work revealed elevations of BUN creatinine and phosphorus. The animal died during recovery from anesthesia. At necropsy the kidneys were enlarged and edematous.

METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA (LUNG LIVER ADRENAL SPLEEN) APOCRINE ADENOMA (SKIN) LEIOMYOMA (UTERUS) CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 12-year-old female hunting dog had a recent history of lethargy and was found dead the following day. At necropsy the animal was thin. Glandular proliferations were noted along the dorsum. A large quantity of serosanguineous fluid was present in the abdomen. Numerous white nodules were present in the lung and spleen. Cysts were present in the kidneys. Masses were present in the liver and right uterine horn.

METABOLIC BONE DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) COELOMITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old female frog was found dead. The animal has a prior history of metabolic bone disease. At necropsy legs and jaw were abnormal in appearance.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This greater than 9-year-old male dwarf caiman had diminished righting reflex periodically after being moved to a new facility on 8/26/08. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead in an 85° pool on its back. Necropsy revealed moderate loss of body condition darkened areas in the left lung and pericardial effusion.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS STEATOSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE. This 11-year-old female snow leopard had a history of progressive respiratory difficulties which were nonresponsive to antibiotic therapy. At gross necropsy foci of pallor were identified on the myocardial surface and lungs were mottled with pale pink and dark pink areas.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 15-year-old male rattlesnake is geriatric and has been moving slower in the past few months. It was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed some pinpoint white foci throughout the hepatic parenchyma pale kidneys with white foci throughout the parenchyma a rodent in the distal esophagus that was malodorous subjectively thickened and reddened mucosa of the stomach and no other abnormalities.

ENTRAPMENT DROWNED. This 16-year-old male flamingo was found dead in the pool with its feet caught in the metal leg band. This male currently was raising a chick. Necropsy revealed moderate intracoelomic fat a small amount of clear fluid in the thoracic air sacs a moderate amount of frothy fluid in the distal trachea copious amounts of water in the lungs full gallbladder small grit and pebbles in the ventriculus and a small amount of yellowish ingesta in the intestines.

COLONIC ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC COLITIS SHOCK. This 7-year-old female tamarin has a history of weakness and emaciation. The animal was manually restrained for treatment collapsed and died. At necropsy areas of alopecia and skin abrasions were noted on the tail feet and face. Fat depots were absent. Liquid ingesta was present throughout the GI tract.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 9-year-old male cattle egret was found dead by keepers in the aviary. A pintail was also found dead on the same day. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a pale liver and male reproductive tract.

CERVICAL HEMORRHAGE PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 18-year-old male scarlet ibis had a history of an old injury to the mandibular beak breaking off a portion of the beak. The animal has done well with the shorter beak. The bird was found dead and necropsy revealed a large clot in the caudal vena cava resembling a ruptured vessel or aneurysm.

EUTHANASIA CHOLECYSTITIS CHOLANGITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS HISTIOCYTIC LYMPHADENITIS. This 5.5-year-old male ferret has a history of melena and declining quality of life. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were pale. Adipose tissue depots were icteric. The liver was large and friable.

ISLET CELL TURMO ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA LYMPHOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE ENTERIC CRYPT LOSS EUTHANASIA. This male 6-year-old ferret was euthanized. This ferret had its annual physical exam at the beginning of November. Its body condition was sparse with splenomegaly tail alopecia and apparent skin tumors. It additionally had heavy cerumen accumulations that were cleaned away from both ears. Within 48 hours it was pruritic and ataxic with a right head tilt. A tympanic rupture was suspected. At hospitalization it was found to have a tympanum tear but additional diagnostics were suggestive of a pancreatic tumor. Medical attempts were made to stabilize the animal to allow surgical intervention but after an initial brief response the ferret began to decline in body weight condition appetite and overall demeanor. Euthanasia was elected. At necropsy the ferret was in thin body condition with abnormal fat reserves. The fat bodies remained present subcutaneously and within the abdominal cavity but they were attenuated and inflamed with abnormal consistency. On the left thoracic body wall a skin lesion of 1 cm. diameter was found that was crateriform and inflamed. Alopecia was present over the tail tip with some speckled hyperpigmentation in the skin also observed. The lungs appeared somewhat attached to the cranial parietal pleura but no visible adhesions were observed. All lung lobes were brightly reddened and did not ooze blood on cut surface. The heart seemed somewhat globoid with streaks of fibrosis present in the ventricular myocardium. The gastric lumen was devoid of contents except for some fine grains of coffee ground appearing debris which suggested bleeding gastric ulceration. The intestines contained abnormal chyme with increased mucus that was yellow to green. There was no evidence of enteric hemorrhage. The liver was mottled and congested. The gall bladder was mildly enlarged with bile but appeared normal. The pancreas was hyperemic and two nodules (1 cm. in diameter) were found in the arm of the lobe that appeared actually hemorrhagic and engorged. The spleen was greatly enlarged nearly 6 cm. long and 4 cm. wide but did not appear congested. Both salivary glands were at least 1 cm. x 0.5 cm. with hemorrhagic centers on cut section. Adrenal glands could not be identified. Testes were missing because the animal was previously neutered. Several of the joints were opened and appeared eburnated but without arthritic changes grossly. The brain was found particularly deteriorated (malacia). The right ear canal was opened to and through the osseous bulla. No hemorrhage exudate or tympanic debris were found in the canal or in the bulla. An actual tympanum remnant could not be found.

SUPPURATIVE MYOSITIS ENCEPHALITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS SPLENIC INFARCT BRANCHIAL CYST HEPATOCELLULAR HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 10-year-old female tamarin had a two week history of rear leg stiffness. A deep puncture wound was present in the medial thigh. The animal was treated with antibiotics and appeared to be recovering but was found dead. At necropsy a small quantity of purulent material was present in the thigh wound. A fluid filled cyst was present adjacent to the left thyroid gland. The liver was enlarged firm and orange.

LEG TRAUMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female Nubian ibex was found unable to stand in the moat of its exhibit and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition with excessive adipose stores arteriosclerosis in the great vessels of the heart dislocation of the fore and rear fetlocks and completely torn joint capsule.

EUTHANASIA PERITONITIS PANCREATITIS MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA. This female 16-year/2-month-old red kangaroo was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis after successful surgical management of bloat and peritonitis three weeks ago. The kangaroo became bloated and lethargic again the day prior to death. At exploratory surgery there was severe peritonitis. At necropsy there was a 2 cm. firm mass on one mammary gland. There were several abscesses at skin suture sites and two at abdominal suture sites. The uterus was very edematous and had a small amount of fluid. There were many 1-2 mm. white plaques on the peritoneum and serosal surfaces of intestines and kidneys. Cytology showed neutrophils with bacteria. The stomach appeared to be twisted about 90° on the root of the mesentery. There were several small ulcers that may have occurred during suction at surgery. There are two areas of stomach mucosa that are quite edematous and mildly hyperemic. Mesenteric lymph nodes were edematous and multifocally hemorrhagic. Cultures of plaques and abdomen are pending.
SHOCK POSSIBLE TOXIN. This 9-month/30-day-old male horned frog was found dead in its enclosure. At necropsy the liver was mottled. The testes were hypertrophied.

INTRACOELOMIC CARCINOMA AMEBIASIS VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS. This 14-year-old male whistling duck presented on July 12th for reduced activity separation from the flock and 20% weight loss. Blood work revealed markedly elevated white blood cell count a fecal acid-fast stain was negative and a PCR probe for Chlamydophila was also negative. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed severe emaciation and a large adhesion of the coelomic air sacs to the viscera.

ANAPLASTIC CEPHALIC MALIGNANCY RESEMBLING ASTROCYTOMA GOUT RHABDOMYOLYSIS CATARACTS. This 14-year-old female burrowing owl had a one week history of illness that included moribund presentation renal compromise improvement with treatment but then decline sharp elevation in renal analytes and also had a prior history of granuloma removal from the left eye in the epibulbar region that cultured positive for Mycobacterium intracellulare. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed cachexia pale kidneys flaccid heart pinpoint deposits or infiltrates on the left side of the coelomic membranes and bilateral cataracts. The left eye had uveitis.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE LIPOMA (SKIN) CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 3-year-old male ferret was found dead. At necropsy the heart was enlarged with thickening of the left ventricle. A multinodular mass was noted near the prepuce.

NECROTIZING GASTRITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 9-year-old male rattlesnake presented in the spring for poor condition and occasional regurgitation. Its mate died several months earlier of disseminated granulomatous disease. This snake was euthanized and necropsy revealed moderate fat depots and empty alimentary tract. The kidneys were pale and engorged with urates.

CHOLESTASIS WITH HEPATIC NECROSIS CEREBRAL INFARCTS FRACTURED WING. This 4-month-old male fruit bat was being introduced into a new exhibit and was kept in a large kennel with possibly no room for wingspan. Necropsy revealed discoloration of the liver enlarged heart small amount of food in the gut and a compound fracture of the left wing.

EUTHANASIA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS RESPIRATORY PROBLEMS. This 26-year-old male ring-tailed lemur has had difficulty breathing for a number of months and historically has had a mass in the right caudal lung field and possibly a mass pushing the trachea cranial lateral on the right above the heart. Two palpable masses were cranial to the scapulohumeral joint and the arytenoid cartilage appeared to be paralyzed. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cataracts worn teeth impacted scent glands atelectasis of the distal end of the right lung two masses 1 and 2 cm. in diameter respectively overlying the heart that on cut surface resemble lymph nodes and no other abnormalities.
EUTHANASIA LIPOMA INANITION. This 14-year-old female corn snake was euthanized due to numerous coelomic masses.

SHOCK SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS SPLENIC EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS CUTANEOUS ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 1-year-old female rat presented with lethargy and dehydration. The animal responded to supportive care but became dehydrated two days later. The animal died following treatment. At necropsy a thin walled abscess containing purulent material was present in the inguinal area. A smaller abscess was present in the right thoracic body wall.

BACTERIAL GASTRITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 2.5-year-old male chameleon was found dead unexpectedly and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed dark liver mottled kidneys and possible gastrointestinal bleed out.
INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS PULMONARY EDEMA SHOCK. This 2-month-old female ferret was found dead. At necropsy intestines were pale. Lungs were congested.

DEGENERATIVE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM LESIONS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female bighorn sheep has a one month history of a progressive hind limb weakness progressing to forelimb and hind limb ataxia and muscle atrophy. An 8-month-old male bighorn sheep from the same dam has neurologic signs as well. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed muscle atrophy pregnancy with deformed (headless) fetus and multiple thickened annular lesions in the uterus resembling implantation sites.

EUTHANASIA NEPHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS NEMATODIASIS TOXOPLASMOSIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 12.5-year-old female wallaroo developed neurologic sign on 1/25/04 with depression and intention tremors. The animal previously had elevated Toxoplasma titer. Treatment was initiated with trimethoprim sulfa and vitamin E. The animal’s condition improved with periodic treatment. In January of 2005 the symptoms recurred and progressed to whole body tremors. Valium was used to treat the tremors; however the animal remained recumbent and when the Valium was reversed the tremors recurred. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy a large smooth dark black mass was present within the lumen at the ileocecocolic junction. The colon contained many foci of hemorrhage. The kidneys contained numerous irregular cortical nodules.

LYMPHOMA. This 18-year-old male wallaroo was found dead on exhibit with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed hemoabdomen mild points on the buccal aspect of both maxillary arcades a loose right mandibular cheek tooth and multiple masses attached to the serosal surface of the jejunum that were cream-colored and appeared to invade the intestinal mucosa. The largest mass was 42 cm. in greatest dimension. Several smaller cream-colored masses were in the mesentery. Adhesions were noted between the urinary bladder and intestine. Multiple cysts were in the renal cortices and two of the cysts contained green/yellow fluid.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA. This 8-year-old male fruit bat was found down. The animal was hypothermic. Treatment was initiated; however cardiopulmonary arrest developed and the animal later died. At necropsy the liver was swollen dark black and friable. Several masses were present in the gallbladder.

BLADDER DYSPLASIA PROBABLE TRANSITIONAL CELL CARCINOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS PELIOSIS. This 18.5-year-old male snow leopard was found dead on exhibit. It had a recent history of probable injury to the back and some neurologic issues involving the urinary bladder and hind legs. The animal appeared to be responding to treatment and death was unexpected. Necropsy revealed markedly enlarged urinary bladder with normal urine slightly thickened bladder wall blood tinged fluid in the abdomen petechiae in the pancreas serosal and mucosal petechiae in the stomach but no ulcers and mottled purple red and black liver.

NEUTROPHILIC CHONANGIOHEPATITIS WITH BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 11-year-old chimpanzee had a history of green serum noted eight months prior to biopsy. The animal’s half-brother had green serum and hepatic amyloidosis at necropsy. As part of a preshipment exam a hepatic biopsy was obtained on this chimpanzee.
DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE. This 6-year-old male pygmy falcon was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed congested lungs and pale kidneys. The animal was obese.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS. This 6-year-old scarlet ibis was housed in the same area as an egret that was diagnosed with mycobacteriosis (G15-0888) in which PCR identification is still pending. The bird of this report was found dead in the morning with no signs of illness. Necropsy revealed emaciation small liver with pinpoint white to yellow dots large spleen covered in thick white material white thickened material throughout the left lung and cranial air space slightly pale kidney and food throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

CHRONIC RUMENITIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female gerenuk had a history of weight loss poor body condition and waxing and waning diarrhea. The animal had episodes of varying severity including seemingly normal feces at times. The gerenuk recently developed intractable weight loss with liquid feces and presented unable to move with dehydration. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed absence of adipose stores emaciation muscle wasting enlarged mesenteric lymph node congested spleen multiple round brown lesions on the luminal surface of the trachea associated with the rings (possible chronic hemorrhage) 15 ml. of straw-colored transparent fluid in the pericardial sac ingesta throughout the gastrointestinal tract with the exception of the colon which was distended with gas and contained a small amount of liquid fecal material. The ruminal papillae were subjectively blunted. The liver was small and multiple foci of white discoloration and indentation were in the capsule. The gallbladder was filled with gold to light green transparent fluid and the bile duct was patent. Approximately 30 ml. of dark gold urine was in the urinary bladder. Some white streaks and grit were in the right renal medulla. The right eye had a 1.8 cm. ulcer in the middle of the cornea.

EPITHELIAL INCLUSION CYST GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS AND AIR SACCULITIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 5-year-old quail had a 16 month history of recurrent sinusitis and a palpable mass in the left supraorbital region. Progressive dyspnea was noted over the past several weeks with occlusion of the nares by caseous material. The animal was anesthetized to flush the sinuses. The animal suffered cardiopulmonary arrest under anesthesia and died. At necropsy the left nasal and supraorbital sinus is effaced by a firm fibrous and cystic growth.
adult. Weight: 2488 g.  Euthanased - multiple skin wounds; suspect bites. Broken canine.
adult. Weight: 40 g.  Euthanased.  Poor condition.  Poor teeth.  Nop fibre in GIT.  Pulmonary congestion.  Ovarian nodules.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS MYOCARDITIS PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS GASTRITIS. This 5.5-year-old female African wild dog died while anesthetized for routine exam 25 min. into the procedure. A large amount of dark blood and froth poured forth from the trachea prior to death and the dog could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed an enlarged right ventricle. Both lungs were congested. The spleen was congested and lymph nodes were pale and mildly enlarged. This dog was noted to have a short seizure 11 min. after induction with midazolam.

CEREBRAL PLAQUES CHRONIC CARDIAC HEPATIC AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 28.5-year-old male lemur has a history of intermittent normal mentation nasal congestion and sneezing loss of body condition decreased appetite and increased sleeping behavior. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed absence of subcutaneous adipose tissue lenticular sclerosis in both eyes clear free fluid in the abdomen and thorax froth in the trachea dark purple oblong spleen multiple large raised areas in the liver multiple cysts in the parenchyma on cut surface thick dark green sludge in the gallbladder small cysts in the kidneys prominent seminal vesicles in prostate and no other remarkable findings.

UROLITHIASIS RUPTURED URINARY BLADDER PERITONITIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male chinchilla had a two-week history of lethargy and abdominal pain and stones were identified radiographically. Laboratory values identified renal disease and uroabdomen. Exploratory surgery identified severe urinary bladder damage and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Both kidneys appeared enlarged as did the adrenal glands.

EUTHANASIA SEIZURE DISORDER DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 13-year-old female Leicester longwool sheep had a history of degenerative joint disease poor gait and limping for three years. The sheep had been treated every other day with an anti-inflammatory drug for two years. It had a one-day history of limping after being knocked over by other sheep. Later in the day the sheep was recumbent and had developed persistent seizuring that did not respond to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hyperemic and frothy lungs and an apparent loss of vasculature on the right side of the cerebrum.

EMACIATION INTESTINAL TREMATODIASIS AND NEMATODIASIS INTRACOELOMIC ABSCESSES. This 11-year-old male black-necked swan was found moribund in a mixed waterfowl exhibit. Supportive care was administered but the bird died shortly thereafter was resuscitated but then arrested again and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed an arrowhead-like object adjacent to the ventriculus emaciation absence of adipose stores some pinpoint black specks in the lateral aspects of the lungs egg white-like material in the pulmonary parenchyma on cut surface sand in the proventriculus and ventriculus (no sand in the exhibit) and pale ventral tips of the liver.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS SPONDYLOSIS SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (LUNG) RENAL CYST. This 21-year-old male otter had a history of muscle wasting in the hind limbs. Renal failure was identified on blood work. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy the right lung was consolidated. Marked spondylosis and arthritis were noted in the thoracolumbar spine.

FATTY LIVER. This greater than 10-year-old female owl was found dead in exhibit. It was obese and had no other clinical signs. At necropsy the liver was very pale and enlarged. Sections floated in formalin. No other gross lesions were noted.

SPINAL FRACTURE OSTEOMYELITIS SPLENITIS AXONAL DEGENERATION (SPINAL CORD) INANITION. This 2.5-year-old female cobra developed neurologic signs and abnormal movement in the caudal body distal to an old scarred area. Bony proliferations were noted along the spine and a complete fracture of the spine was identified. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition continued to decline and it was humanely euthanized.

EUTHANASIA ODONTOMA. This approximately 6-year-old spayed female prairie dog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of difficulty respiratory efforts. A mineral dense round mass was seen arising from the dorsal tooth root base and extended into the nasal cavity on radiographs.
