At necropsy there was a remnant of the right incisor present within the nasal passage. There was a large round bony mass protruding into the nasal passage.
EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS INANITION. This 8-year-old male emerald tree boa was humanely euthanized. This snake was a poor doer and never ate well despite many attempts by the keepers.

PYELOLONEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 14-year-old female wallaroo had a 3-day history of lethargy was easily approached and had multiple instances of head shaking. The animal was found dead later in the afternoon. Necropsy revealed white streaks in the myocardium a 2 cm. full thickness ulcer and a 1 cm. full thickness ulcer in the stomach with associated gut contents in the abdominal cavity. Multiple adhesions were present between the ulcerated regions and the mesentery. Yellow particulate debris was packed into both ear canals. The liver was diffusely mottled light yellow and pale and a lesion corresponding to the gastric ulceration was present on the ventral surface of one hepatic lobe. Mild roughening of the lateral aspect of the left distal femur at the stifle joint was noted.

COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS PERFORATED BOWEL OPTIC NERVE GLIOSIS WITH INTRANUCLEAR INCLUSIONS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male wallaby had a history of inappetence and swelling of the right jaw. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a focal area of alopecia on the base of the tail and some scaly skin. The haircoat was dull. Multiple white nodules were in the lungs. Moderate endocardiosis was in the heart valves and 3 ml. of serosanguineous pericardial effusion was noted. The right mandible was swollen and multiple adhesions were present throughout the intestines and stomach. The stomach was enlarged and filled with gas. The pancreas was enlarged and reddened. The liver had three focal white raised firm nodules. Multiple hilar lymph nodes were markedly enlarged and irregularly shaped. Numerous erosions and ulcers were present in the stomach.

HYDRONEPHROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 11-year-old female karakul sheep had an approximately one year history of slowly progressive weight loss and inability to keep up with the herd. The animal was removed to a retirement paddock with other elderly animals seven days earlier and was subsequently found acutely dyspneic and weak. The animal died a few minutes later. Necropsy revealed mild dependent edema in the subcutis of the thorax large volumes of bloody pleural effusion and mild straw-colored abdominal effusion. The right side of the heart was enlarged and thin walled and a mild straw-colored pericardial effusion was noted. Frothy foam was in the oral cavity and the distal trachea. A 5 mm. section of firm ingesta was noted in the esophagus at the thoracic inlet. The right kidney contained multiple variably sized nephroliths and the left kidney had severe hydronephrosis and hydroureter. The urinary bladder contained approximately 60 cc. of grossly normal urine. Blood work obtained from this animal two months prior to death had normal renal values.

EUTHANASIA NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 23-year-old female lemur had a history of renal disease and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed white cystic kidneys with firm lumps and no normal tissue. The uterus was enlarged and had cysts. Small white infiltrates were scattered throughout the hepatic lobes.

OSTEOMYELITIS TENOSYNOVITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 9-year-old female duck had a lesion in the stifle which appeared to be progressive with osteolysis of the distal femur and proximal tibiotarsus. Cardiopulmonary arrest developed under anesthesia and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted in the right lung.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 2.5-year-old male Virginia opossum was noted to have decreased appetite and increased respiratory effort and evaluation revealed pleural effusion. The animal was treated for congestive heart failure initially responded but subsequently decompensated and died. Necropsy revealed 100-200 cc. of pink tinged free thoracic fluid globoid enlarged and thin walled heart and swollen/enlarged liver.

BOID INCLUSION BODY DISEASE DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 10-year-old male boa constrictor had an approximately one year history of osteosclerosis associated with the vertebrae. The snake had been eating poorly over the last three to four months. Euthanasia was performed.

EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 10-year-old male ibis was part of a quarantined group with chronic shedding of Campylobacter sp. despite repeated treatment. The animal was humanely euthanized to protect the collection. At necropsy no significant gross lesions were identified.

SHOCK HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 7-year-old female bat was restrained to place a transponder chip. The animal was found dead a few minutes later. At necropsy the lungs were markedly congested. No other gross abnormalities were identified.

COLONIC IMPACTION BACTERIAL COLITIS COELOMITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL GOUT INANITION. This 9-year-old female snake has a history of large mass in the caudal abdomen. The animal was found dead. At necropsy several masses were noted beneath the skin and a firm mass in the caudal abdomen corresponded to a large fecalith in the terminal GI tract.

ACUTE PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SYSTEMIC SHOCK OSTEOMYELITIS. This 5-year-old fruit bat was found down in the exhibit. There was evidence of trauma and a possible clavicular fracture. The animal’s condition declined and it developed hemiparesis. The animal died before treatment could be initiated. No significant lesions were identified at gross necropsy.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA (FRACTURED WING) HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS BILE STASIS CYSTIC BILIARY HYPERPLASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 11-year-old male fruit bat was found down on the exhibit floor. The left proximal radius was fractured. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy marked tooth wear was noted. Open fractures were noted in the digits of the right wing.

COELOMITIS. This 3-year-old female lory was found dead in the exhibit. At gross necropsy the lower mandible was missing and there was hemorrhage on the right pectoral muscle. Intestines were hemorrhagic and the lungs were congested.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This approximately 13-year-old female python was found dead. An exhibitmate (#S01903) died on 1/25/02 and was positive for mycobacteriosis (G02-1507). At necropsy random ventral scutes were hemorrhagic. The trachea and bronchi were filled with mucus along with the lungs. There were excessive amounts of clear green fluid in the coelomic cavity. There was no ingesta in the stomach and no digesta in the intestines. Liver spleen and kidneys had disseminated pinpoint white masses. There was one bruised area within the skeletal muscles. There were small fat pads present. Sections of liver kidney spleen lung and heart were frozen for future use if needed.

CHRONIC RENAL AND CARDIAC DISEASE. This 36-year-old male Gila monster presented with decreased reactivity and no righting reflex. It had been found on its side or back and unresponsive. He had his usual warm water soak one-half hour earlier. The lizard had eaten one week earlier. This lizard had been removed from aestivation prematurely due to exhibit renovations. Necropsy revealed 4 cc. of clear yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity reduced fat body size multiple dark spots over the scattered over the serosal surface of the lungs mottled liver dark mottled small kidneys and abundant milky fluid in the ovaries.

POSTANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS PULMONARY SHOCK POSSIBLE ASPIRATION. This 12.5-year-old addax had a one day history of illness and died. A tree had fallen on the animal’s head and broke its jaw. The animal died after surgery to fix the fracture. The animal did well during anesthesia but bloated regurgitated and aspirated in the recovery stall. Necropsy revealed shavings and food particles in the trachea and lung and no other abnormalities.

FIBROSARCOMA INTERRENAL CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old male timber rattlesnake was noted to have a mass on the dorsal midline approximately 10 in. caudal to the head. The mass was previously diagnosed as a fibrosarcoma (Antech). As the tumor enlarged euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

ISLET AND INTERSITITAL FIBROSIS DIABETES MELLITUS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY GLOMERULONEPHRITIS. This 8-year-old female rock hyrax had a history of glycosuria and a cataract at the time of melengestrol acetate implant. The patient was found dead one month later and had been alive that morning. Necropsy revealed a 5 cm. flattened lobulated mass in the right dorsal aspect of the abdominal cavity. No other abnormalities were detected.
juvenile. Weight: 9.3 g.  Euth; deformed beak. Cran.haems; trauma v hypertens'n.

LYMPHOCYTIC DERMATITIS AND DERMAL VASCULITIS VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male Egyptian fruit bat had a few week history of ulcerative ventral cervical dermatitis that responded moderately but transiently to conservative topical treatment. Biopsies identified an atypical lymphoid infiltrate suggestive of lymphoma and the bat was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair nutritional condition moderate dehydration and a 3.5 cm. area of alopecia with ulceration and thickened skin overlying the ventral mandible and ventral cervical region.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 2-year-old female opossum had acute onset of dyspnea that was unresponsive to Lasix and subsequently died. At necropsy there was pulmonary edema. The body condition was good.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC ABOMASITIS ENTERITIS NEPHRITIS. This 15-year-old male goat had a history of forelimb lameness. The condition failed to improve despite treatment and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy adhesion of the rumen and jejunum was noted adjacent to the body wall.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS ABOMASITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 12-year-old male goat had a history of renal disease and anemia. Significant weight loss has been noted with progression of the renal disease. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Consolidation was noted in the right lung. Small circular raised lesions were noted in the abomasal mucosa. Kidneys were pale and contained small cysts.

LYMPHOSARCOMA. This approximately 3-year-old female polecat was found dead. It had no history of problems or illness and was fine that morning. At necropsy the abdominal cavity contained a large amount of nonclotted blood. The spleen had a golf ball-sized mass on the cranial end that was fibrous on cut surface. There were small areas of darkened condensed areas throughout the rest of the spleen.
adult.  Euth. Dermatitis. Lymphadenopathy. Splenitis.

PULMONARY BACTERIAL ABSCESSES (NOCARDIA OR ACTINOMYCES-LIKE) GLOMERULONEPHRITIS. This approximately 4-year-old male hedgehog had a history of possible mite infestation based on fecal exam. Carbaryl was applied topically in two doses seven days apart. The animal was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed white swollen lung fields with pale yellow exudate ingesta in the mouth digesta in the small and large intestines and fair overall body condition.

INTRATHORACIC MESOTHELIOMA. This 6-year-old female wolf was introduced to another female on 11/16 and was started on antibiotics on 11/17 for multiple bite wounds that did not appear to be life-threatening. Keepers had noted recent weight gain and the animal appeared to be adjusting well to its cagemate. The animal developed a one day history of dyspnea and was found dead. Necropsy revealed bloated abdomen containing straw colored to serosanguineous fluid large mesenteric lymph nodes enlarged mediastinal lymph node pulmonary atelectasis small hard white foci in the lung fields bloody fluid in the pericardial sac with marked pericardial thickening and multiple raised nodular foci on the pericardial surface. The liver was firm with rounded edges and areas of tan discoloration. The omentum was icteric and emboli were seen in the mesentery.

FIBROUS OSTEODYSTROPHY/METABOLIC BONE DISEASE ACTIVE REPRODUCTIVE STATUS. This greater than 2-year-old gecko had a history of rubber jaw due to constant egg laying. The animal was treated accordingly but died. Necropsy revealed emaciation demineralization of the long bones and fatty liver.

PERITONITIS METRITIS WITH TRACT FORMATION (GRASS AWN) ULCERATIVE COLITIS DISECTING AORTIC ANEURYSM. This approximately 45-year-old female western lowland gorilla was found dead in her enclosure in the morning. The gorilla was in a normal sleeping position lying with her right side down right arm extended and one arm bent and resting on her chest. Necropsy revealed a walled off abscess lined between the colon and the uterus. The abscess appeared to be associated with a perforation of the pelvic organs including sigmoid colon rectosigmoid colon uterus and urinary bladder. A colouterine fistula was noted. Multiple ulcers were noted in the pyloric antrum the body and the cardiac area of the stomach. A plant on lies in the anterior most end of the uterine lumen.

GASTRIC GRANULOMA ENTEROCOLITIS. This approximately 11-year-old male lizard was humanely euthanized. It had intermittent anorexia over the past several months and progressive declining body condition. At necropsy there were multiple 0.5 mm. raised white plaques along the entire gastrointestinal tract. Similar plaques were found on the spleen.

INANITION. This 10-year-old female merganser was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the heart appeared enlarged and straw colored fluid was present distending the pericardial sac. The liver was enlarged and firm.
SUPPURATIVE PERITONTITIS AND SEPTICEMIA. This female 2-month-old tamarin had been apparently healthy and was found dead. Necropsy revealed gaseous distention of the bowel and generalized pallor.

RENAL TUBULAR ECTASIA WITH PROTEINURIA PULMONARY VASCULAR MINERALIZATION. This captive bred over 25-year-old female Inca tern had a two day history of severe lethargy and anorexia. Exam showed severe weight loss. The bird was humanely euthanized due to age and its poor condition. Gross necropsy revealed possible renal gout and white material below the serosa on the body wall.

SHOCK. This approximately 10-year-old female copperhead was found dead in the enclosure. It had a previous squamous cell carcinoma removed from the tail. At necropsy there was a small amount of internal body fat stores. There were two round raised approximately 2 mm. in diameter lesions on the hepatic capsular surface. The gastrointestinal tract was empty except for foaming mucus within the stomach. The proximal small intestine was dilated and dark purple.

EMACIATION HEAD AND NECK TRAUMA. This 8-month-old female oryx was released from quarantine in mid November. She was found down by a fence on 12/23 comatose and agonal with hypothermia. Head trauma was suspected. Necropsy revealed mandibular subluxation and cervical instability thin body condition no external wounds foam in the trachea and bronchi plant material in the right bronchus right cranial pulmonary lobe thickening congestion of remaining lobes yellow-colored pericardial effusion bruising over the lateral aspect of the rumen irregular and firm hepatic surface congestion and hemorrhage in the pancreas hemorrhage surrounding the spinal cord between C1 and C2 edema around the pharynx and atlantooccipital area hemorrhage and bruising of the muscles in the region of C1-C2 mandibular luxation to the right and possible luxation of the atlantooccipital-atlantoaxial joint spaces.

FOLLICULAR ATRESIA WITH YOLK EMBOLI HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 6-year-old female beaded lizard was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed prominent ovarian follicles with prominent vasculature this tissue displacing the coelomic viscera. The liver was pale yellow and fat stores appeared adequate.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 3-year/9-month-old female toad was humanely euthanized. The entire group of five animals was culled to screen for mycobacteriosis. Historically they were in contact with an animal that was suspect for tuberculosis based on histopathology. Tissues were submitted for mycobacterial culture.

PULMONARY SHOCK (ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED). This 3-year-old female lorikeet was being treated for weakness and respiratory distress and died shortly after the second day’s treatments. Necropsy revealed good body condition enlarged liver with rounded edges and pale tan discoloration dark purple lungs that sank in formalin a dark purple exudate in the proximal trachea near the syrinx nectar in the crop and digesta in the ventriculus and intestines.

ENTEROCOLITIS SYSPECT COLONIC CARCINOMA IN SITU. This 5-year/1-month-old male tamarin died. It had been recently diagnosed with lymphoblastic lymphoma from fine needle aspirate of an abdominal mass. Surgery was performed and the mass was successfully removed. A mesenteric lymph node was also removed at that time. The surgery was uneventful and recovery was normal. The tamarin did well postsurgery for 48 hours and then was noted to have some vomiting. On the morning of the third day postsurgery the tamarin vomited again overnight and was treated with fluids and antinausea medication as well as antibiotics. At necropsy there was an intussusception of the entire jejunum into the colon. The cecum did not appear to be involved. The intussusception could not be reduced without dissection. The jejunum was dark and appeared necrotic. The areas where the mass and the lymph node were identified were normal. The sutures were present and there were no signs of hemorrhage. The tamarin was in thin body condition with no fat stores noted.

HYDRONEPHROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS EUTHANASIA (CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS). This 9-year-old female wallaroo had a history of neurologic signs and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes when the signs progressed to seizures.

RETINAL DEGENERATION EUTHANASIA. This greater than 9-year-old female owl had a several day history of stargazing and depression. The bird was euthanized and necropsy revealed a friable liver irregularly shaped kidneys entropion of the ventral right eyelid and feather loss on the head.

Additional fresh tissues are being held should further laboratory testing be required. Erin B. EUTHANASIA LEIOMYOMA (COLON) URATE STASIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA DERMATITIS INANITION. This 25-year-old female corn snake was euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy the liver was dark and nodular. An oval mass was adherent to the colon.

TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS SUSPECT DROWNING. This 7-year/6-month-old female bat was found dead in bottom of exhibit pond. There was no previous clinical history. At necropsy the animal appeared in good condition. The body was wet. Both lungs floated in formalin.

EUTHANASIA PORTAL HEPATITIS HEPATOPATHY. This female approximately 13-year-old ibex was humanely euthanized. It had a history of lethargy and left head tilt. It initially responded to supportive care. It subsequently fractured MC3-4 in the carpus resulting in lateral deviation of the lower limb. Blood work revealed slight hypokalemia and hypophosphatemia. At necropsy the heart musculature appeared dark brown. The lungs had some areas of atelectasis. The cranial mediastinal lymph node appeared enlarged nodular and hard. All other lymph nodes appeared normal. The rumen appeared distended and flaccid with an area of hemorrhage around the ventral rumen groove. The abomasum also had multiple areas of petechiation in the serosa and mucosal surfaces. The liver was slightly harder in consistency than expected. The gall bladder was distended. The uterus appeared enlarged and was full of a thick tan substance and had a central core of dark brown hard material. The substance easily peeled out of the uterine horns but filled both horns in the body of the uterus. The ovaries were small and inactive. The bladder wall was thickened and had multiple areas of petechiation on the mucosal surface. There was complete fracture of metacarpal 3 and 4. The head was removed with the brain intact for arboviral and rabies testing at the state lab.

SEPTICEMIA GRANULOMATOUS MYOCARDITIS GASTRITIS AND HEPATITIS. This 6-year/9-month-old male snake was found dead on exhibit. At necropsy the lung was bright pink. The gastrointestinal tract was empty except for some liquid in the small intestine and colon. The gall bladder was distended and firm.

FOLLICULAR RUPTURE YOLK COELOMITIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION BACTERIAL GASTROENTERITIS INTESTINAL INTUSSUSCEPTION VENOM GLAND ADENITIS. This 7.5-year-old female rattlesnake died. Necropsy revealed no external lesions reddening of the cardiac region of the stomach a possible tear or trauma in the stomach with associated infection an area of redness and inflammation with white scarring or suppurative exudate in the body wall adjacent to the affected section of stomach a thick white fibrous firm mass inside the stomach yellow to green to tan fluid in the ovaries large full gallbladder and no other abnormalities.
BACTERIAL HEPATITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 18-year-old male python had a history of anorexia and spondylosis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the liver was mottled and friable.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS METAZOAN PARASITE MICROGRANULOMAS EMACIATION. This greater than 8-year-old male dwarf caiman has a history of chronic weight loss and on presentation was emaciated. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed multiple pale lesions throughout the lungs and serosal aspects of the intestine. Some thickening was present in segments of the intestine. An encysted nematode was noted in the coelomic wall.

MYOSITIS COELOMITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA NODULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 7-year-old male rattlesnake had a mass on the left side of the body. A soft tissue mass was also identified radiographically at the level of the stomach. A fine needle aspirate revealed heterophilic inflammation. The animal was found dead two days later. At necropsy a firm cutaneous mass approximately 4 mm. in diameter was present in the right anterior body. The mass was white on section. The liver was markedly enlarged pale and friable and had a large hematoma at the caudal extent. Multiple 5 mm. in diameter masses extended into the parenchyma which were white to gray on section. The stomach and small intestine were thickened with prominent rugal folds. White striations were present within the ureters and kidneys.

TRAUMA PREDATION. This 2.5-year-old neutered male rabbit was found dead on exhibit. It had extensive bruising on the neck. At necropsy there was bruising on the neck. All other systems were normal. Another exhibitmate died in a similar fashion the previous day.

EUTHANASIA COPD INANITION. This 5-year-old female bighorn sheep was humanely euthanized due to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. This sheep had a chronic history of respiratory disease including dyspnea and tachypnea that seemed to be especially worse in hot weather and under restraint. This summer she was particularly tachypneic and lost condition since the spring. Keepers reported that she seemed to be handling the hot weather even worse than prior summers. At necropsy this sheep had little fat reserve. The pelage was scruffy and not completely shed out from the winter coat. There was a mild thoracic effusion that was clear and colorless. The pulmonary parenchyma was mildly congested but substantially emphysematous. There was mild pulmonary edema. Lymph nodes within the thoracic cavity inguinal area and prescapular region were enlarged and edematous. Lung was submitted for caprine arthritis encephalitis PCR testing. Sections of lung brain lymph node joint capsule and synovium were frozen for future use if needed.

BACTERIAL PLACENTITIS AND ENDOMETRITIS EMACIATION STRESS. This 11-year-old female ibex died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed urine on the legs a cyst on the dorsum of the cervix a retained placenta and no other lesions. One of the herd is seropositive for leptospirosis.

BACTERIAL/MYCOTIC CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS WITH PROTOZOA HEPATIC GRANULOMATOSIS. This 3-year-old male chameleon was found dead and had no prior signs of illness for the last year although had a previous episode of weight loss and weakness that responded to treatment. The animal also had coccidia at one time. Necropsy revealed multiple cyst-like lesions in the liver. Urate crystals were in the kidney.

ACUTE PULMONARY SHOCK CAUSE UNDETERMINED. This 15-month-old male cheetah had a three day history of partial inappetence and mild behavior abnormalities and was found dead. Necropsy revealed congestion of all lung fields. No other abnormalities were noted.

INTRACOELOMIC SARCOMA. This 13-year-old male California kingsnake was anesthetized for coelomic swelling. A large mass was identified at surgery. The mass was excised and there was substantial bleeding during surgery. The snake began to breathe on its own following surgery but then became apneic and died. At necropsy there multiple granulomas in the liver and firm lesions along the kidneys. The splenopancreas was not identified.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA SPONGIFORM CHANGE IN BRAIN EUTHANASIA. This 5.5-year-old male hedgehog had a five week history of an oral mass which has continued to enlarge. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 2 cm. expansile mass in the left maxillary region extending from ventral to the orbit to just medial dental arcade. The associated dentition was mobile. The right eye had a mature cataract. Moderate subcutaneous and internal fat stores were noted. The lung had several 1-2 mm. soft white foci in both lobes. The lungs were dark red and some sections sank in formalin. The liver was slightly mottled. The kidneys were irregular and had several dark 1 mm. foci on the capsular surfaces.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS TRANSMURAL ENTERITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 29-year-old male colobus had a history of inappetence. The animal was anesthetized for examination but later died. At necropsy severe peritonitis with perforation of the small intestine was noted.

INTERVERTEBRAL DISC DISEASE SPONDYLOSIS AXONAL DEGENERATION OCULAR TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old male African hedgehog has a one-week history of progressive lower motor signs to the rear limbs anus and urinary bladder. The animal was minimally responsive to treatment and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the bladder was severely distended but was easily expressed. Additionally the lumbar vertebrae were ankylosed.

Peritoneal cavity: ascites Stomach (C3): ulceration; mucosal; multifocal Aorta: multifocal intimal mineralization Lung: emphysematous bullae Comments A definitive cause of reported clinical signs was not identified grossly. It is very possible that the mucosal ulcerations in C3 may be a contributing factor. Changes in the aorta are interesting; but a definitive cause is uncertain. The kidneys did not appear to have significant gross changes. Histopathology is in progress to identify underlying disease which may have contributed to this llama's clinical signs. Daven N. Jackson; DVM Lung: multifocal pulmonary emphysema Intestine: mild suppurative enteritis (suspected) Pericardial fat: mineralization; mild; multifocal Stomach (C3): ulceration; mucosal; multifocal (gross) Aorta: multifocal intimal mineralization (gross) Peritoneal cavity: ascites (gross) Cause of death undetermined. Comments Microscopic examination did not reveal any underlying disease. There was no evidence of neoplasia or significant inflammation. Due to the presence of inflammatory cells and edema within the submucosa and tunica muscularis; an enteritis is suspected but could not be confirmed because of severe mucosal autolysis. The cause of this llama's clinical signs and gross lesions could not be identified. The lack of renal or hepatic disease suggests that this animal may have suffered from a metabolic disturbance. Daven N. Jackson; DVM

FACIAL ABSCESS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA SEPSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 10-year-old male red-necked wallaby presented with a swollen face and Fusobacterium was cultured from the lesion. The condition recurred 10 months later and the animal presented with depression reluctance to move tearing at the eyes diffuse swelling on the left side of the face buphthalmia and conjunctivitis. The animal died during recovery following examination. No other abnormalities were noted at necropsy aside from some petechiation in the lungs.

HEPATIC ABSCESS CIRRHOSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE IRON STORAGE. This 23.5-year-old male lemur had a history of a hepatic mass received supportive care but died. Necropsy revealed a 10 cm. mass in the liver that contained a large abscess.

INANITION MYOSITIS. This female greater than 1-year-old leiothrix was found dead outside of its enclosure. It had been held in quarantine and escaped overnight into an empty adjacent bird pen where it was found dead the next morning. At necropsy there was a 0.25 cm. region of feather loss on the cranial aspect of the left femur. There was also a pinpoint area of dry blood on the medial aspect of the left wing in the radius-ulnar region. There was mild hemorrhage within the lungs. The liver and intestines were somewhat autolyzed.

RENAL DYSPLASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 2.5-year-old female African painted dog was euthanized due to acute and chronic renal failure. The animal was diagnosed with renal dysplasia approximately one year prior to death. The animal had been losing weight and began to be hyporexic despite treatment. All littermates have died from suspected renal failure. At necropsy there were small ulcers along the oral commissures. The small intestinal mucosa was multifocally red. The kidneys were small.
