AMEBIASIS LUNGWORMS. This approximately 7-year-old male Gaboon viper died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed large adipose stores circumferential thickening of the colon and necrotic material in the lumen of the colon mottled liver fluid in the lungs and no other remarkable gross findings.

BACTERIAL DEMATITIS AND CELLULITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE TRAUMA HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY RENAL GOUT. This 7-year/1-month-old female motmot was found dead in cage. It had chicks in a ground nest and was apparently beaten up by male motmot. She was treated symptomatically. At necropsy there were no down feathers and large numbers of feathers were missing over the caudal half of the body. There were no tail feathers. There was a large wound over the left hip backbone and pelvis that extended to the tail tip. The lungs were slightly congested. The liver was enlarged with a few white foci. The spleen was extremely small. The pectoral muscles were very pale. No body fat was present.

OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA COELOMIC METASTASIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VALVULAR MINERALIZATION INANITION. This 11-year-old female chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the bird was emaciated. The coelomic cavity contained a large quantity of fluid. A yellow irregular mass was present on the aortic valve. The GI tract was covered with thick fibrous tissue. Fibrous nodules were present in the oviduct.

ENTERITIS INANITION. This 17-year-old female llama had a three day history of anorexia abdominal distention and constipation. The animal died despite supportive care. At necropsy superficial ulcers and congestion were noted in the forestomachs. The jejunum was dilated and thin walled.

EUTHANASIA CHONIC NEPHRITIS ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA. This 17-year-old female tiger was inappetent and lethargic. Examination revealed elevation of BUN creatinine and phosphorus. Fluid therapy was provided; however no change was noted in blood values and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys appeared swollen and pale. Other tissues had no significant gross lesions.

FATTY LIVER BACTERIAL STOMATITIS SEPTICEMIA. This greater than 9-year-old male monitor was found dead. It was recently treated for chronic mouth rot. At necropsy there were bilateral erosions of the mid maxilla and mid mandible. The erosions appeared to encompass the dental arcade and penetrated into the sinus. There was ingesta present in the stomach. There was digesta present in the small and large intestine. The liver was significantly enlarged and mottled throughout. It was very firm.

VACUOLAR LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY (WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME). This 6.5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of chronic wobbler syndrome and a recent onset of respiratory wheeze that did not respond to empirical care. The hedgehog also was losing weight and was found recumbent. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS CHRONIC DERMATITIS RENAL GOUT GASTRITIS INANITION BACTERIAL DERMATITIS. This 5-year-old male snake was found dead. The animal has a history of cachexia and skin disease. At necropsy a snake was emaciated. Circular white foci were noted in the skin. The gastric mucosa was hyperemic to hemorrhagic.

TRAUMA (PENMATE AGGRESSION) GERIATRIC. This 11.5-year-old male wild turkey had recently been released from the clinic after supportive care for weight loss. The turkey was reintroduced to the exhibit one day earlier and then found dead in the exhibit after being attacked by a javelina. Necropsy revealed a prominent keel a large open wound on the right side of the body extending from the axilla to the vent a large amount of hemorrhage surrounding the area exposed organs protruding from the wound erosion of cartilage on the head of the femurs and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS SEROUS ATROPHY OF FAT. This 24-year/11-month-old male giraffe was humanely euthanized. The giraffe was found down with rear limbs spread eagle in the night house. All attempts to get the giraffe to stand were unsuccessful. Supportive treatment was initiated but the giraffe could not rise. At necropsy there was multifocal abomasal mucosal hemorrhage. There was severe urinary bladder distention. There was mitral valve hypertrophy. There was osteoarthritis within the carpal joints stifle joints scapulohumeral joints and coxofemoral joints. The lungs were congested.

EUTHANASIA MALIGNANT MELANOMA (MAMMARY GLAND LYMPH NODE) HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA BILIARY CYSTADENOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA VALVULAR FIBROSIS CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This 15-year-old female red wolf has marked abdominal distention and rapidly declining condition. The white blood cell count declined rapidly to near zero. The animal became comatose and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy haircoat was thin. The abdomen was markedly distended. Masses were palpable in the right mammary gland. Tissues were icteric. The urinary bladder was distended with urine. A smooth raised mass was present in the liver along with a cluster of 2-3 cm. in diameter cysts. Excessive pericardial fluid and fibrin were noted in the pericardial sac. The medial leaflet of the right AV valve is contracted and hard. Kidneys had fibrosis with irregular thin cortices.

ACUTE PULMONARY NECROSIS AND EDEMA ERYTHROPHAGOCYTOSIS HEPATIC LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC INFLAMMATION. This 4-year-old male lorikeet weighed 183 g and was in good body condition. The bird was found dead without previous clinical signs. Severe pulmonary edema (lungs like wet sponges) was seen at necropsy. No other lesions were observed.

PODODERMATITIS EUTHANASIA. This 35-year-old female American flamingo had chronic intermittent lameness that did not improve with treatment and the animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was chronic pododermatitis on the right foot. The left thyroid gland was mildly enlarged and the right thyroid gland was not identified. There was some abnormal dark tissue at the proximal aspect of the proventriculus. The left oviduct was adhered to the jejunum and did not apparently connect to the uterus. The left intertarsal joint had mild arthritis.

CARDIAC TAMPONADE DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE OBESITY. This 17-year-old male skink was found dead. Necropsy revealed good body condition good hydration adhesions to the ventral thoracic wall and pericardium and the pericardium is markedly enlarged and contains approximately 5 ml. of blood surrounding the heart (which is very small). Areas of irregular tan/black mottling were in the caudal lobes of the liver. A 1.5 cm. in diameter thin-walled cyst containing serous fluid was adhered to and replacing some of the hepatic parenchyma at the caudal extent of the left caudal lobe. A 1 cm. in diameter area of white deposition was in the mesentery overlying the liver. A 1.5 cm. in diameter spherical abscess was in the left caudal coelomic cavity attached to the pelvic inlet by a thin vascular stalk.

EUTHANASIA MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA OVARIAN CYSTADENOMA. This 14-year-old female jaguar was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. It had a history of mammary neoplasia of approximately one year duration. The masses were enlarging. The body condition started to decline. At necropsy there were multiple bilateral mammary masses. Some of the masses were firm and multinodular. Some were cystic with clear fluid. There were minute white masses in the omentum. The uterus had an infiltrative mass in the wall. There was purulent material in the lumen. The ovaries were cystic and irregular. The surface of the liver was pitted. There were areas of the pancreas that were red.

ZINC TOXICOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE) HEMOGLOBINURIA ENTERITIS ANESTHETIC DEATH SHOCK. This 5-year-old female harbor seal had a six day history of lethargy and anorexia. Coins were regurgitated and many more were present radiographically within the stomach. The animal had severe azotemia and mild hematuria. The animal later died. At necropsy severe gastritis with ulceration was present. At the pylorus 32 coins were present. Severe duodenal hemorrhage was present. Kidneys were diffusely enlarged. Hemorrhage was present within the lung. Hematuria was present in the urinary bladder.

ENTEROTOXEMIA INTRA-ABDOMINAL GRANULATION TISSUE AND ACUTE HEMORRHAGE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS. This 5-year-old male capybara had a history of reluctance to walk and wobbly gait and was clinically normal the previous day. It had been housed on its own for one month prior to presentation. Blood work revealed elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine acidosis and the animal was in thin body condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This is the third capybara mortality in the last two months at this facility. Necropsy revealed minimal body fat hemorrhagic cecal wall with bloody luminal contents and lots of ingesta in the alimentary tract. The small intestinal wall was hemorrhagic and contained bloody contents. Much food was in the stomach. A large gelatinous blood clot was in the mesentery around a portion of the pancreas. The parenchyma of the pancreas appeared thickened and a semifirm mass was adjacent to the pancreas.

CRYTOSPORIDIOSIS BACTERIAL COLITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 7-year-old female corn snake was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed multiple cysts in the gastric mucosa that were light yellow. Another cyst-like structure was present at the base of the heart. A section of the distal colon was dark purple with multiple plaque-like lesions on the mucosal surface. Some pinpoint spots were in the kidneys.

PULMONARY ABSCESSES BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This 5-year-old desert tortoise was alive at the end of the day but was found dead the following morning in the same location it was last seen the evening before. A black widow spider was also seen in holding but three feet from where the tortoises rest. Necropsy revealed thin body condition malodorous carcass fluid in the coelom that was malodorous a large hard mass of uric acid in the urinary bladder malodorous and darkly discolored coelomic contents absence of adipose tissue female reproductive tract with active folliculogenesis and eggs in the ovaries adhesions of the heart and lungs to the gastrointestinal tract gravel in the gastrointestinal tract and consolidated lungs that sink in formalin. A previously noted shell lesion had healed.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC HEPATITIS CIRRHOSIS HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 22-year-old male lemur had a history of chronic hepatopathy renal disease and cardiac disease. The animal presented in moribund condition and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the heart was enlarged with thinning of the ventricular walls. The liver was small and firm. A cavitated mass was present associated with the gallbladder. Kidneys were irregular.

SYSTEMIC MELANOSIS NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 1-year-old female eyelash palm-pit viper had been showing central nervous system signs and had flaccid body tone. Pseudomonas was cultured from the mouth. The animal did not respond to appropriate antibiotic therapy. Euthanasia was elected for humane reasons.

MAREKS DISEASE WITH VISCERAL AND NERVE LYMPHOSARCOMA EGG COELOMITIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old hen had a history of weight loss poor appetite and left leg lameness. Radiographs revealed a speckled appearance to the long bones. Lameness did not respond to anti-inflammatories. The hen was euthanized on 9/18/15. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition many abdominal adhesions bright yellow fat a mildly mottled appearance to the liver an enlarged spleen egg material in the coelom enlargement of the left kidney with effacement of the parenchyma by abnormal white tissue and decreased muscle mass of the left pectorals.
LYMPHOMA THYROID TUMOR. This 5-year-old male hedgehog had been slow moving and was found dead at morning rounds. Necropsy revealed an intestinal tumor with lymph node involvement.

MYXOSARCOMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SURGICAL DEHISCENCE CYSTIC BILIARY HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 13-year-old female wolf had an axillary mass infiltrating the triceps. Biopsy revealed myxosarcoma. The surgical wound dehisced and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy thickening of the triceps and infraspinatus muscles was noted. Necrosis and thickening of the surgical margins was noted. Adjacent lymph nodes were markedly enlarged. No other lesions were noted at necropsy.

PITUITARY TUMOR EUTHANASIA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 2-year-old male rat presented several months ago with severe degenerative joint disease in both knees and obesity. Attempts to control pain were unsuccessful and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed poor body condition a 4 mm. round object resembling thyroid or parathyroid neoplasia or possible lymph node abscess in the cervical region. Purulent material was present on cut surface of the mass. The mass appeared to be firmly attached to the trachea but did not penetrate the lumen. A large dark mass was noted in the location of the pituitary gland protruding upward into the cranium.

PANCREATIC ACINAR CELL ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASES EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male milksnake has a history of intracoelomic mass and surgery revealed an extensive mass involving the gastrointestinal tract and bile duct. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed that the mass appeared to be in the caudal portion of the stomach and liver. Perforation appears to be present throughout several sections of the alimentary tract and splenopancreas is not identified. The lungs had purulent tan multifocal nodules and a smaller mass was present proximal to the larger mass adhered to the mucosa of the stomach. White nodules were present throughout the kidneys.
HEMOCHROMATOSIS MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS. This 5-year-old male lory developed sneezing and labored open mouth breathing and died the same day. Necropsy revealed pale kidneys and no other abnormalities.

PULMONARY AND HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE ASPIRATION HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA. This 23-year-old Humboldt penguin was found dead on exhibit without history of illness. The penguin appeared to have stumbled several times and then fell and struggled approximately one minute before it died (video camera review). Necropsy revealed good body condition a large amount of opaque red fluid in the coelom numerous large blood clots present in the abdominal cavity pale mottled liver with a single 1 cm. white firm lesion extending into the parenchyma and surrounded by hemorrhage. Several areas of the liver contain pockets of blood but no obvious lesions were present. The reproductive tract was adhered to the dorsal body wall and many follicles were in various stages of development. A few small foci of intraluminal hyperemia were noted in the small intestine. The stomach was filled with ingesta.

LYMPHOSARCOMA CHRONIC COLITIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 7-year-old male capybara was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy an 8 cm. in diameter multilobular mass was present in the area of the jejunum. Retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes were markedly enlarged.

EMACIATION EUTHANASIA CHRONIC KERATITS ANTERIOR UVEITIS. This 12-year-old male southern black-bellied whistling duct had a history of a cloudy left eye with distortion of the pupil. The animal was examined and had a heart murmur thickening of the cloacal ring with a tubular soft tissue structure on the left side of the coelomic cavity observed on radiographs. Additionally the left tarsal joint was ill defined suggestive of osteoarthritis. Due to underlying cardiac disease and intermittent lameness the animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was a tube-like structure on the left side of the coelomic cavity and enlargement of tissue on the tricuspid valve.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE. This 15-year-old male tamarin was found dead on exhibit. Necropsy revealed a moderate to severely enlarged heart congested lungs dark kidneys food throughout the gastrointestinal tract mild dehydration and good body condition.

PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS TRAUMA. This 10-year-old male rail was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage under the calvarium multiple fissures within the liver petechial hemorrhages along the kidneys thickened left abdominal air sac a focal white nonraised lesion in the spleen and no other gross abnormalities.

WING TRAUMA LOW-GRADE SYSTEMIC ANTIGENIC STIMULATION EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female Bali mynah had a history of a chronic ulcerative wound on the right wing with self-mutilation poor feather condition and large areas of skin without feathers for many years. The bird had been treated for skin loss of many weeks duration and was stable until the morning of euthanasia when it was found bleeding where it had opened crossing vessels at the elbow. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large ulcerated area under the right wing crossing the elbow and up to the propatagium and caudal patagium and extending from the elbow to the body wall. No other abnormalities were noted.

EUTHANASIA CATARACT KERATITIS ANTERIOR SYNECHIAE. This 13-year-old male pintail had a history of a cataract and recently presented with exophthalmos in the affected eye. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a mature cataract was present in the left eye. The right eye had severe exposure keratitis and exophthalmos. The lens could not be identified.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHRONIC CYSTITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATELECTASIS INSULINOMA. This 8-year-old female ferret has a recent history of weight loss and stranguria. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy tan to white foci were present in the lungs. Kidneys were irregular and contained fluid filled cysts.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA GASRIC ADENOCARCNOMA ENDOCARDIOSIS. This 32-year-old female mandrill was found dead. It was found the day prior to death with both eyelids swollen and lacerations over the left eye. Trauma may have been from the result of conspecific interaction or a fall. The next day sedation was performed for physical exam. The mandrill had altered mental status prior to sedation. There were multiple age-related problems. The trauma appeared to have been the result of a fall. Recovery from sedation was prolonged. At necropsy the body of the mandrill was in good nutritional condition. There was bruising around both eyes with a laceration of the left eye. The lungs were mottled purple/red. There were multiple small black specks in and on the surface of the lungs. The mucosal surface of the trachea was mottled red/brown and thickened. Changes appeared to extend into bronchi. The heart appeared grossly enlarged. All valves appeared thickened. Some had small masses present. There were jet lesions present on the surface of the aorta. There was a slightly raised area on the proximal surface of the aorta. There was moderate to severe chronic periodontal disease. There was a small firm mass palpable on the inside of the lower lip. There was an ulcer present in the esophageal mucosa near the gastroesophageal sphincter. There were what appeared to be chronic ulcers on the mucosal surface of the stomach. The liver appeared grossly enlarged. There were occasional small cysts in the kidneys. The cervix and uterine walls were both thickened. The lumen of the uterus was filled with a mass that appeared to be attached to the endometrium in two locations. The mass had a fluid filled center. Ovaries appeared small and inactive. The spleen appeared grossly enlarged. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes appeared enlarged and dark. There was severe spondylosis and kyphosis of the spine. There was moderate eburnation of the bone at both elbow joints. There were mature cataracts present in both eyes. Lung was submitted for culture.

VEGETATIVE VALVULAR ENDOCARDITIS BACTERIAL SPLENITIS NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 3-year-old male turkey was ataxic and reluctant to move. The skin on the head was pale. Anesthesia was induced for physical exam but the animal died. At necropsy a large quantity of pale straw colored fluid was present in the pericardium. The heart had pale foci in the apex. The aortic valve was thickened and irregular.

BILIRUBIN CHOLELITHIASIS MYOCARDIAL SARCOCYSTOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 18-year-old neutered male sheep was found down and unable to stand. The sheep was electively euthanized due to advancing age and arthritis. Gross necropsy revealed bruising on the face from thrashing on the concrete floor gallstones a congested appearance to multiple segments of gastrointestinal tract chronic osteoarthritis of the left hip missing teeth and uneven tooth wear and some intra-abdominal fat.

EMACIATION PITUITARY ADENOMA. This 14-year-old female milksnake was found dead. Necropsy revealed thin epaxial musculature thickened red lungs thickened thyroid and old remnant necrotic ova. Skin was in shed cycle. Eyes had cataracts.

XANTHOMATOSIS CIRRHOSIS. This 10.5-year-old male gecko had a two week history of progressive weight loss and inappetence. The gecko sloughed its tail while being restrained for examination and the procedure was discontinued. Supportive care was administered but the gecko died overnight. Necropsy revealed a tan 2 cm. bilobed mass between the liver and the heart and a similar but smaller mass to the left of this mass.

AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION PODODERMATITIS EMACIATION. This 21-year-old female Caribbean flamingo was weak and emaciated. On examination the animal had minor abrasions overlying both carpi severe pododermatitis and severe dehydration. The animal died spontaneously. Perimortem blood work revealed leukocytosis hyperphosphatemia and hyperuricemia. At necropsy there was dark blood in the lumina of the airways and sections of lung sank in formalin. Both kidneys were enlarged.

SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS AND GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS PANCREATIC CYST CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE CARDIA LIPOMATOSIS CHRONIC GASTROENTERITIS STRESS RESPONSE OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 15-year and 9-month-old male cheetah has a history of osteoarthritis chronic renal failure and possible seizure-like episodes. The animal was receiving enalapril gabapentin tramadol and Cosaquin. One day prior to death the animal was outside for an extended period of time during a heat wave greater than 100°F. Upon coming inside the animal was tremoring lethargic and dehydrated. The animal did not eat that night or the following morning. The next day the animal was weak lethargic and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the animal was emaciated and had dental calculus multiple canine fractures an enlarged left thyroid gland approximately 1.5 times the size of the right mottled liver a moderate amount of effusion in the peritoneal cavity multiple firm tan masses in the spleen a pancreatic cyst pale and firm kidneys and pulmonary congestion. The left and right ventricular walls of the heart appeared thickened.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS CARDIAC FIBROSIS AND MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female African hedgehog had a history of abnormal gait and hind end ataxia similar to that seen with wobbly hedgehog syndrome. The animal’s appetite had declined recently and skin abrasions were noted on the right posterior hock and tail tip. A large volume of abdominal fluid was noted radiographically and pleural edema with loss of cardiac silhouette was also noted. A focus of mineralization in the abdominal cavity possibly in the reproductive tract was also noted and some mild vertebral spondylosis was seen. Numerous irregular masses were noted in the region of the kidney by ultrasound and the lung had poor contractility.

ENTERITIS PULMONARY NEMATODIASIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 6-year-old toad was found dead following a history of anorexia and weight loss. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. Otherwise no significant gross lesions were identified.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION GOUT GRANULOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male chameleon had lost its ability to extend its tongue to capture prey. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed poor body condition and minimal postmortem autolysis. The animal was thin and the ribs could be visualized. The kidneys were dark tan with some areas of light purple discoloration. A tan waxy plug 2.5 cm. long was in the cloaca.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS MESENTERIC ABSCESS ENTERITIS RENAL COCCIDIOSIS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY INANITION. This 6-year/2-month-old male wallaby was humanely euthanized. It had a history of weight loss and loss of body condition over the last few months. It was also noted to have increased ocular discharge over the past few days and had slowed down in its activity. It was known to be positive for wallaby retrovirus. A large round abdominal mass was palpated. It was moveable firm and could not be associated with any particular organ. Radiographs revealed some radiopaque material in the stomach and abdomen. The mass was of soft tissue density. At necropsy the wallaby was in very poor body condition. There was whole body muscle atrophy. There was a large palpable mass midway in the abdomen. Upon entering the abdominal cavity there was a large amount of straw colored fluid free in the abdomen. There was a large mesenteric abscess that was 570 gm. well encapsulated well vascularized and within the mesentery of the jejunum close to the cranial mesenteric artery. There were enlarged mesenteric inguinal mediastinal and cervical lymph nodes. The liver seemed somewhat mottled and had few swollen edges. There were hepatic areas where the edges were white and the capsule was thickened. The spleen was small. Upon cross section there were several bulging tan nodules evenly dispersed throughout the parenchyma. The kidneys were pale. The mediastinal space was enlarged and had enlarged lymph nodes. The heart appeared enlarged. The right ventricular wall measured 3 mm. and the left ventricular wall width was 12 mm. The right wall seemed flaccid and excessive. Aerobic and anaerobic cultures of the abscess and mediastinal lymph nodes were performed.

UTERINE LEIOMYOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC MASTITIS. This 8-year-old female pygmy goat had mammary gland enlargement without evidence of mastitis. A draining tract developed and a bilateral mastectomy was performed. The animal died during anesthetic recovery. At necropsy abundant fat depots were identified within the subcutis and abdomen. Marked edema was present in the pharynx and laryngeal tissue. Aspiration of rumen contents was not identified in the respiratory tree. The right mammary gland was firm and contained a fistulous tract leading to a cavitated area within the gland lined by thick firm fibrous tissue. A small quantity of turbulent yellow/brown fluid was present within the cavitated mass. The body of the uterus was markedly enlarged and very firm. The wall of the uterus contained a firm pale tan to white mass extending into the lumen as a large papillary and expansile mass within the lumen of the uterus.
MULTICENTRIC LYMPHOSARCOMA. This approximately 9-year-old male African pygmy falcon was found dead. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition and enlarged cranial lobes of both kidneys.

EUTHANASIA EPIMYOCARDITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 12-year/11-month-old male falcon was humanely euthanized. It had been hospitalized for several weeks due to weight loss and poor appearance. It was treated with antibiotics and antifungals. On radiographs the liver looked enlarged. At necropsy the liver was enlarged and friable. There was edema around the heart.

OVARIAN SARCOMA EUTHANASIA SUSPECT TRAUMA. This 18-year-old female blue mountain lorikeet was attacked by cagemates in the morning and subsequently had difficulty breathing. At examination the animal was dyspneic with bilateral mydriasis and obtunded. The animal was in respiratory distress with an elevated heart rate increased pulmonary and air sac sounds and remained obtunded. The animal had seizure-like activity during radiographs which revealed an enlarged cardiac silhouette. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy there was a fluid-filled renal cyst of the left kidney the right atrium was white and the great vessels were thickened with possible mineralization.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE TRAUMA. This 17-year-old male straw-colored fruit bat was euthanized for progressive decreased mobility. At necropsy there were multiple fractures of the ribs bilaterally changes to the wing digits including swelling and healed fractures and anisocoria which was clinically noted.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION URATE STASIS. This 9-year-old male junglefowl was found dead. At necropsy the right kidney was enlarged and friable. Straw colored fluid was present in the coelom.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ATELECTASIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 17-year-old male red panda presented with abdominal distention. Ascites and enlarged heart were noted. Treatment was initiated; however cardiac signs progressed and pulmonary edema developed. The animal was humanely euthanized due to progression of the cardiac signs. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the abdomen. The liver was small and firm. Lungs were firm and mottled. White to gray foci were noted in the myocardium.

HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOCARCINOMA. This greater than 10-year-old female axolotl was found dead with no previous medical history. At necropsy the coelomic cavity was very turgid and contained at least 6 cc. of hemorrhagic fluid and one large blood clot attached to the liver. There was a ruptured 1.5 x 1.5 cm. hepatic mass on the most caudal ventral section. This was the site of the attached blood clot. The liver was tan in this area with the normal coloration being gray/black.
adult.  Decapitation.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS PYODERMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old female African hedgehog had a history of a maxillary growth that was getting progressively larger. Cytology suggested squamous cell carcinoma and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition swollen right maxilla involving the upper premolar and molar tooth. The skin around the tail and vulva was hyperemic and moist. The lungs were hemorrhagic but floated in formalin. A few pale areas were in the liver.

BACTERIAL STOMATITIS AND FACIAL CELLULITIS. This 10-year-old female panda was found recumbent and had agonal respirations. It had been normal the previous evening. Necropsy revealed hemorrhagic edematous lungs particularly on the left side. An oral fistula with bruised swollen buccal mucosa was noted caudal to the last maxillary molar on the left side. A firm thick walled large intestine was present. Renal cysts and infarcts were noted. Hemorrhagic nasal sinuses with frank blood were present in the left nares. Good fat reserves were noted and food contents were in the stomach.

RHABDOMYOLYSIS STRESS COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE ASSOCIATED WITH ORGANIZED HEMATOMA. This 23-year-old female ibis was found dead. No clinical abnormalities had been observed. Necropsy revealed pooling of blood around the right hepatic lobe. Two discolored foci in the right hepatic lobe a large number of rocks in the gizzard and adequate adipose stores.

VENTRICULITIS NEPHROSIS. This male 18-year-old tern was found dead in the water. This was the second of two Inca terns to die without previous signs of illness. Both were found in the water. Several other birds nearby have died acutely but with different lesions. At necropsy the condition of the carcass was poor with loss of body condition. The gastrointestinal tract contained no ingesta.
SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED. This 4-year-old female motmot was found dead. Necropsy revealed an apparent ruptured gall bladder and spleen.

ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC GASTRITIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 16-year-old male macaque had a chronic history of inflammatory bowel disease for several years and also had been on insulin beginning in July 2010. The animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy findings were not included with the submitted paperwork.

ACUTE BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old male wallaroo entered the collection on 10/93 with no remarkable history and subsequently died on 6/9/95. Necropsy revealed absence of fat deposits and hemorrhagic enteritis.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE NEPHROSCLEROSIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE COLONIC NEMATODIASIS. This 6.5-year-old female rock hyrax was found dead. At necropsy there was a large amount of effusion within the coelom and abdomen. All pulmonary lobes were congested. The heart walls were thin and overall there was cardiomegaly.

LYMPHOMA VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS AND BACTERIA. This approximately 3-year-old female ringed teal was found dead in its enclosure. It was seen being attacked by a male duck. At necropsy there was a large mass of subcutaneous fat-like material within the body cavity cranial to the heart and lungs. The kidneys were pale. Several pinpoint white foci were noted over the serosal surface of the spleen.

IRON STORAGE INTRACOELOMIC HEMORRHAGE CHRONIC ENTERITIS AND HEPATITIS. This 5.5-year-old male black-capped lory had a one-day history of fluffed appearance and stargazing behavior received supportive care but was found later lying in sternal recumbency and unable to stand and died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed thin body condition hemorrhage in the lungs enlarged golden yellow liver normal ingesta throughout the alimentary tract diffusely pale kidneys and a mild amount of straw-colored coelomic fluid.

VEGETATIVE VALVULAR ENDOCARDITIS PULMONARY INFARCTS LYMPHADENITIS LUMPY JAW. This 8-year-old female wallaby was found dead after treatment of fly strike and mandibular osteomyelitis. At necropsy the wallaby was in fair nutritional state with minimal adipose tissue storage. There are multiple old infarcts present on the periphery of multiple lung lobes. The heart appeared grossly enlarged. There were two masses present on the right atrioventricular valves. The right ventricle appeared dilated. The left atrioventricular valves appeared thickened. All the teeth of the left mandible were absent. There was a small amount of food in the stomach. There were multiple erosions and ulcer on the mucosal surface of the glandular part of the stomach.

CIRRHOSIS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 14-year-old female rainbow lorikeet has a history of abnormal abdominal palpation and had been stepped on by a patron one year earlier. The bird had difficulty perching with its right foot. Physical examination revealed a grossly distended abdomen with a palpable mass extending caudal to the ribcage. The animal developed respiratory distress and died while anesthetized for exploratory surgery. Necropsy revealed a tan liver and a 2 cm. rounded mass attached to the caudal surface of the right hepatic lobe.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 17-year-old female Oryx was euthanized due to chronic degenerative joint disease severe lameness and reluctance to move. Marked degenerative joint disease was present in both stifles. At necropsy the animal was in thin body condition and had marked decrease in range of motion of both stifles with crepitus. Severe osteophyte proliferation and erosion of the articular cartilage was noted in the stifles. Similar changes were present in the humeral heads and carpi. A tapeworm cyst was identified in the left ventral thoracic cavity.

EUTHANASIA RENAL GOUT RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS VASCULAR AMYLOIDOSIS METASTIC MINERALIZATION. This 35-year-old female Chilean flamingo had recurrent swelling of the right hock. The animal responded variably to treatment and was found down did not respond to supportive care and was euthanized. At necropsy there was a proliferative wound on the right hock with central ulceration. There were multiple fibrous adhesions between the small intestine and the body wall. Multiple air sacs were thickened with large areas of opacity. The pulmonary parenchyma was consolidated with multiple firm nodules. The distal portion of the left oviduct was dilated. The kidneys were mildly enlarged and on cut surface were gritty. The right tibial plateau contained white grainy nodules.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEMORRHAGIC ENTERITIS COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE. This 10-year-old snake was found dead. At necropsy the caudal body was dark red and a mass of consolidated or clotted material was present adjacent to the kidneys.

INANITION HEPATITIS. This 6-year-old female lorikeet was lethargic and fluffed. The bird was found dead the following day. At necropsy the animal was thin. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE. This 1-year-old opossum was found dead in the enclosure. At gross necropsy there were loose feces around the peritoneum and a small amount of straw colored fluid in the peritoneum and thoracic cavity. The right ventricle of the heart was enlarged and there was thinning of the right ventricular free wall. The tricuspid valve did not appear to be fully formed.

EUTHANASIA HEMATOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL GOUT HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INANITION. This 15-year-old male kingsnake had a previous history of renal adenocarcinoma. Recently the animal has lost weight and begun regurgitating. Masses were noted consistent with a hematoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy minimal body fat was identified. A 2 x 3 cm. in diameter mass was present near the splenopancreas and a smaller mass was adjacent to the pancreas. The kidney contained gouty deposits.

HYPERKERATOSIS POSSIBLE HYPOVITAMINOSIS A EUTHANSIA. This 1.5-year-old female green basilisk presented for dysecdysis with yellow thickening of the skin and poor body condition. The lizard also seemed lethargic when examined. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. In addition to the skin lesions necropsy identified absence of digit #5 on the left forefoot and digit #4 disarticulated on the right forefoot. The distal few centimeters of the tail were dry and had dark discoloration. Yellow/gray discoloration with hyperkeratosis was noted on the ventral abdomen feet and digits. Hyperkeratosis was also present on the dorsum. The liver was mottled pale tan to red. Female reproductive tract was identified. The cranial pole of both kidneys was pale.

YOLK COELOMITIS AIR EMBOLI EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female chicken has a history of complete inappetence toxic heterophils with left shift and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The bird also had crop stasis. Necropsy revealed adhesions in the coelomic cavity crop dilatation impacted ventriculus ascites and inspissated eggs.

TETROBULBAR ABSCESS SEPSIS ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS. This 6-year-old male rabbit presented with prolapsed right third eyelid and marked conjunctivitis. Supportive care was administered but the animal worsened and became lethargic and inappetent. Blood work revealed an inflammatory hemogram. The rabbit died and necropsy revealed congested lungs a purulent exudate in the calvarium associated with the right ventral bulbar region and some pitting of the subcapsular parenchyma of the right kidney. The third eyelid was erythematous and edematous and a purulent and malodorous exudate was identified in the retrobulbar space.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY METASTATIC MINERALIZATION (STOMACH). This 5-year-old male polar bear had a one day history of illness and died. The animal had been inappetent and lethargic on the previous day. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no gross lesions externally. Positional pulmonary congestion was noted but the rest of the lungs appeared normal. Minor hemorrhagic streaking was noted in a 2 x 2 cm. area of the epicardium. A large amount of dark red fluid was in the stomach and no food contents were present. The mucosa of the lower body and pylorus of the stomach had multiple purple/red patches. The mucosa of the duodenum and jejunum was uniformly dark brown. No evidence of a torsion or foreign body was noted.

GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS MYOCARDITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA INANITION. This 3-year-old female ratsnake presented with acute swelling in the cardiac region. Radiographs reveal an enlarged cardiac silhouette. The animal died during the examination. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the coelom. The lungs kidneys intestinal tract and spleen were edematous. The liver contained a single 3-4 mm. in diameter abscess. The myocardium had three 1-2 mm. raised tan nodules.

LYMPHOMA. SPONGIFORM ENCEPHALOPATHY. This 2-year-old female hedgehog had a one day history of lethargy and inappetence and died when placed in an oxygen cage for rewarming. The hedgehog had chronic hematuria chronic left cataract and phthisis of the globe. Necropsy revealed pinpoint areas of hemorrhage on the mucous membranes of the stomach and small intestines a mixture of hemorrhagic mucoid ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract atrophy of the left globe and two firm white round small structures that exfoliate easily from the mucosa of each uterine horn.

EMACIATION STRESS MILD CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 5-year-old female ibis is part of a group that had tested positive for chlamydiosis several years earlier. The animal was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed a wet carcass with fire ant predation thin body condition orange friable liver slightly enlarged heart and no other abnormalities.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 4-year-old female frilled leaf-tailed gecko was evaluated for lethargy and abnormal shed. At examination multiple nematodes were identified within the oral cavity. The animal was treated with subcutaneous fluids and ivermectin and was found dead. At necropsy there are large fat bodies present in the coelomic cavity. The kidneys were pale tan.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS FRACTURED FEMUR PORTAL HEPATITIS AND ENTERITIS. This 11.5-year-old female duck presented for lameness on the right leg was immobilized for radiographs and a closed complete fracture was noted along the proximal right femur. Osteoarthritis was noted in both stifles. The bird was immobilized a second time for fracture repair several hours later and arrested during recovery from fracture repair. Necropsy revealed good body condition mild bumbles on both metatarsal footpads bruising along the right thigh some white linear streaking along the epicardium cysts on both kidneys prominent oviduct and a blood clot and bruising within the tissue along the medial aspect of the right thigh.

THYMOMA BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS. This approximately 41-year-old boa had previously been ill in 2006 but responded well to antibiotics. Necropsy revealed a subcutaneous granulomatous mass over the splenopancreas region watery fluid and gelatinous clumps in the coelomic cavity engorged jugular veins particularly on the right enlarged splenopancreas multiple firm masses in the lungs markedly enlarged thyroid and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA THYROID CARCINOMA. This 10-year-old female duck was euthanized due to a prolonged history of openmouthed breathing which was nonresponsive to treatment. At necropsy an irregular was present adjacent to the heart.

ACUTE PSEUDOMEMBRANOUS COLITIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 11-year-old male Gila monster had been inappetent the previous night and was found moribund. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hyperemic intestines and no other abnormalities.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 2-year-old male dog has a history of chronic renal disease and was found dead in its enclosure in the morning. A sibling of this animal at the Gladys Porter Zoo and at the origin of this animal at the Sedgwick County Zoo have evidence of renal disease and congenital anomaly is suspected. Necropsy identified a thickened right ventricle a gray jejunal lymph node markedly distended stomach containing partially digested food renal asymmetry with the left kidney slightly larger than the right kidney and on cut surface reduced architectural structure in the renal papillae columns and calices.

INCLUSION DISORDER EUTHANASIA. This 11.5-year-old male kingsnake has been in quarantine for approximately five months. In quarantine blood work inclusions were noted in the nuclei of lymphocytes. The snake has not been eating well and intermittently exhibited unusual behavior such as rolling on its back submerging itself in water for several minutes coming up gasping. The snake also was slithering with the caudal portion of its body not moving properly. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed light tan kidneys with patchy areas of brown pigmentation. No other remarkable findings were seen.

COELOMITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 17-year-old male ratsnake has a history of inappetence and weight loss. Masses were identified on radiographs. The animal was found dead. At necropsy foci of hemorrhage were noted beneath the skin. Severe postmortem autolysis was noted.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 18-year-old male kingsnake had a history of abnormal behavior was self-injurious at times and had neurologic deficits. Prior to euthanasia the snake had a delayed righting reflex. Necropsy identified thin body condition but abundant intracoelomic fat cloudiness around the periphery of the spectacles and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA CADIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 12-year-old male meerkat was humanely euthanized. It had a history of arthritis and recently started to not eat. It was treated with subcutaneous fluids antibiotics and steroids.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This male approximately 2-year-old opossum was humanely euthanized. It had a history of hind limb ataxia and muscle atrophy. It had labored breathing and paleness noted on 2/24. Physical examination revealed a heart rate of 60 respiratory rate of 16 with increased effort ataxia dehydration thinness and bilateral pinnae with lacerations. At necropsy the distal pinnae were necrotic. There was a small amount of clear froth in the trachea. The lung lobes were firm with multiple areas of dark red/purple discoloration. The liver was dark brown mottled with multifocal yellow/brown spots. The gall bladder was filled with bile. The stomach was filled with food material. The duodenum and jejunum contained yellowish-brown mucous material. The large intestine contained large amounts of dark brown firm fecal material. Degenerative joint disease was noted in both acetabular joints.

POSTANESTHETIC DEATH ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 8-year-old female warthog died about 10 hours after anesthesia to replace contraceptive implant. It did not recover normally but seemed to slowly become more responsive until it was found dead at last check. At necropsy there were adequate adipose tissue stores. The liver had a finely granular surface. There was a bile stone. The left lung was congested. There was white foam in bronchioles. The gastric contents were composed of milky lime green liquid. There were congested vessels in the stomach. The urinary bladder was full with clear 1 liter light yellow urine.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 8-year-old male rat walked slower than expected since arrival was falling over and hypothermic. It presented moribund received supportive care but died overnight. Necropsy revealed edematous lungs pale left kidney and some cystic lesions noted in the kidney.

ACUTE SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 15-year-old male colobus died. The animal was fine the previous day and had no recent medical problems. Necropsy revealed clear white areas on the epicardium resembling fibrosis.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS AND ENTERITIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS SEPSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION DYSTOCIA. This 4-year-old female iguana has a 10 day history of inappetence and cachexia. Supportive care was administered and dystocia was diagnosed. Eggs were removed surgically. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed collapse of the right globe and debris accumulation between the globe and the palpebrum. A yellow nasal discharge was noted from the left naris. The liver has a normal reticulated pattern and color is yellow/gray. Numerous thin nematodes were in the colon and the colonic junction and cloacal mucosa were adhered with yellow fibrinous material. Ovaries were atretic and kidneys were pale to yellow and enlarged.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 5-year-old male lory was found dead in the incubator. It had been hospitalized the previous day in thin body condition with dried urates around the vent appeared to respond well to treatment and was found dead unexpectedly in the morning. It is the eighth lorikeet from the collection that has died in the last two weeks. Necropsy revealed lean body condition diffuse edema and hemorrhage in the lungs watery contents in the alimentary tract dilated duodenum and jejunum injected serosal surfaces of the intestine thickened mucosal surfaces pale kidneys areas of hemorrhage in the dorsal skull bone and a small amount of brown/yellow fluid in the coelomic cavity.

TRAUMA (FRACTURED LEG) EUTHANASIA. This 6-month-old male sheep was found in the barn with a broken left leg and had been fine at early morning checks. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a comminuted closed proximal tibial fracture and no other gross lesions.

SEPSIS IRON STORAGE. This greater than 4-year-old female Egyptian fruit bat died while being treated for shock. Necropsy revealed good body condition. The animal was well muscled but no adipose was noted.

EUTHANASIA HEPATITIS ENTERITIS GASTRITIS INANITION ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHROSIS. This 15-year-old male captive bred macaque was humanely euthanized. It had approximately a less than six month duration of illness. It had a history of subacute weight loss and appeared uncomfortable. A CAT scan suggested an abdominal tumor. On 8/2 it was unable to stand and had near total paralysis of the right arm. It had a prior history of long-term lead exposure. It was treated with prednisone. Sections of liver kidney bone and urine were collected for toxicology. Urinalysis revealed a specific gravity 1.015 large amounts of blood trace leukocytes and pH 6.0. Cultures of liver colon and joint were performed. At necropsy the gastric mucosa appeared hyperemic. There was an adhesion of the gastrosplenic ligament to the abdominal wall. There was an adhesion of the descending colon to the right lower abdominal wall. A previous colopexy was performed in 1988 because of a rectal prolapse. One side of the prostate was larger than the other. There was an overall lack of body fat. There was significant loss of the skeletal muscle mass. The omentum/mesentery appeared dark orange. The peritoneal lining also was dark orange. The kidneys were pale and slightly enlarged. The renal pelvis appeared slightly dilated. The spleen was small and meaty in texture.

EUTHANASIA FIBROSARCOMA NEPHRITIS THRUSH CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS COLITIS HEPATOPATHY. This 12-year/5-month-old male tamarin was humanely euthanized due to facial fibrosarcoma associated with the left parotid salivary gland. The fibrosarcoma was diagnosed by surgical biopsy. The tamarin presented with left-sided facial swelling in May 2002 and workup included physical exam blood collection fine needle aspirate cytology bacterial culture MRI and finally exploratory incisional biopsy/debulking surgery. Complete resection was not possible and adjunct treatments were not pursued. At necropsy the tamarin was in lean body condition. There was chronic alopecia and hyperpigmentation of the dorsal aspect of the tail. The tail tip was bloody. The left side of the face was obliterated by a neoplasm that exposed subcutaneous tissues. The left lip commissure was absent. Some of the cervical lymph nodes were possibly enlarged. There were peritracheal nodular structures. The liver was mottled and had a slightly lumpy almost granular serosa. Liver margins were sharp. The left adrenal seemed enlarged.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA SARCOCYSTIS. This 22-year-old male salmon-crested cockatoo had oral gavages for several weeks due to chronic weight loss and was being treated with enrofloxacin amikacin metronidazole and ponazuril. The animal had a moderately positive result for Sarcocystis and was PCR negative for chlamydiosis. The animal also had a bacterial culture of the crop and cloaca which grew a resistant E. coli species. Radiographs revealed aspiration. The animal died spontaneously. At necropsy there was tan fluid in the cranial thoracic and cervical air sacs granulomas in the lungs and purulent fluid that oozed from the lung on cut section.

INTESTINAL VOLVULUS. This 10-year/6-month-old female seal was found dead. She had a short history of not eating and floating on the surface with the right side more dorsal than the left the day prior to death. There may have been some possible regurgitation. At necropsy there was serosanguineous discharge coming from the mouth and covering the cranial third of the body. A large amount of gas was expelled upon opening the abdomen. The jejunum was entrapped in portions of torn hepatomesenteric ligament. There was a minimum of three perforations noted in the ligament into which the small bowel had become entrapped. A total of 3 ft. of proximal jejunum and 9 ft. of distal jejunum were caught and twisted in ligament openings. The sections of bowel were congested and necrotic. There was diffuse congestion of visceral vessels. The spleen and liver were both enlarged. The lungs were heavy wet and congested but floated in formalin. The right ventricle had eccentric hypertrophy.

EUTHANASIA BILIARY CYSTADENOMAS HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY AMYLOIDOSIS. This 8-year/7-month-old male marmoset was humanely euthanized. It had a history of abdominal distention. Physical exam revealed a very large multilobular structure in the abdomen. Radiographs revealed a large abdominal mass that was cystic and filled the entire abdomen. At necropsy the marmoset was thin. There was mild consolidation in both lungs. The liver was very large and had multiple cysts that were within and congruent (2-3 mm. to 4 cm.). The hepatic parenchyma appeared dark.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 19-year-old female Gila monster has a history of left upper coelomic mass and died at the completion of left hepatic lobectomy. Necropsy revealed apparent metastasis of the hepatic tumor with associated ascites and pericardial effusion. Cloacal tissue was pale. The heart base had apparent metastatic disease. Urates were in the ureters and a neoplastic lesion was distorting the right kidney.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VALVULAR FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS PERITONITIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 10-year-old female tamarin recently delivered twins. The animal was found dead. At necropsy subcutaneous edema was noted over the thorax and abdomen. A large quantity of fluid was present in the thorax. Fat depots were atrophied. The left ventricle was thickened.

MYCOBACTERIUM OR OTHER ACID-FAST ORGANISM IN LYMPH NODE NEPHROSCLEROSIS GRANULOMATOUS LYMPHADENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female ferret had a history of progressive weight loss lethargy and inappetence suspected to be associated with chronic renal disease. The ferret also has a history of barbering. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin condition barbering over the flanks mild generalized dental disease 2-3 mm. wide round plaque-like flat lesions over the caudal dorsal lungs possible enlarged perihilar lymph node soft pale irregular kidneys cortical cyst in the right kidney and scant adipose tissue. The liver had a few cysts noted in the left lateral lobe.

CAUSE OF DEATH UNDETERMINED PROBABLE TRAUMA. This 1-year-old male river otter had recently been released from quarantine. It showed no signs of illness but was found dead at the bottom of the exhibit pool. A pile of vomit was found in the exhibit and contained a large amount of plant material from a bush in the exhibit. The bush is presumed to be a false indigo shrub. This otter had been noted to chew on items in its habitat. Necropsy revealed hemorrhagic fluid from the oral cavity adequate adipose stores that were pink or orange. The lungs were congested and had coalescing hemorrhage on the serosal surface tan froth was in all the airways and the duodenum was filled with thick white mucoid material. A large amount of plant material consistent with leaves seedpods and bark of the false indigo shrub were in the jejunum some clear fluid was in the stomach and soft fecal material was in the colon.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This greater than 5-year-old ferret has clinical signs consistent with adrenal disease. Bilateral adrenalectomy was performed and the ferret developed Addisonian crisis that initially responded to therapy but less so over time. The animal declined significantly and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of alopecia on the dorsum between the shoulder blades and along the ventral chest area and on the top of the head. Some hair loss was also noted on the distal third of the tail. A hairball oriented around some coated metal wire with crimped plastic was present in the pylorus. Some foci of red discoloration were noted in the gastric wall.

GRANULOMATOUS COELOMITIS ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 11-year-old female rainbow lorikeet was examined for weakness and dyspnea. The animal had increased radiodensity to the lungs and died during anesthetic recovery. At necropsy the lungs were dark purple. The liver was enlarged and tan with white foci. There was a 1 x 2 x 3 cm. white soft tissue mass in the left ovary.

LOW GRADE SEPSIS. This 9-month-old female slender-tailed meerkat was found dead under a large log that appeared to have fallen on it at the end of the day. Necropsy revealed sand in the oral cavity and eye sockets and no evidence of external injuries or fractures.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (NASAL PASSAGES LUNG) MELANOMA (THYROID STIFLE) HEPATITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 5-year-old male hedgehog had a previously diagnosed carcinoma. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a mass was present in the left neck extending into the thoracic cavity.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 5-year-old male green tree python was noted to have lack of appetite and loss of body condition and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed thick white mucous in the mouth. The snake had been treated 10 days with antibiotics. Necropsy revealed multiple small 1 mm. white foci throughout the liver.

BACTERIAL RHINITIS AND STOMATITIS GOUT STRESS. This 10-year-old female green tree python was found dead. It had laid eggs one week earlier. Necropsy revealed thin body condition but some coelomic fat stores were present. Tissues were dehydrated. Some yellow debris was in the oral cavity but not adhered to the mucosal surface and no oral lesions were seen. Tan material was adhered to the mucosa of the stomach. Multiple firm yellow to white concretions were in the distal gastrointestinal tract and cloaca. The ovary appeared inactive.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA NEMATODIASIS OF COLON AND URINARY BLADDER BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 3-month-old female captive bred rat is in a group from which multiple rats have died after anesthesia. Underlying respiratory disease is suspected. Necropsy revealed blood in the trachea.

SARCOCYSTIS MYOCARDITIS HEPATIC SPLENIC AND RENAL PIGMENT. This 20-year-old female California sea lion had a four day history of inappetence and lethargy. The animal arrested 45 minutes into an immobilization procedure and diagnostic workup. Necropsy revealed pale streaks in the pectoral muscles congestion of the left lung and generalized lymphadenopathy.

RENAL GOUT. This 4-year-old male tree frog had a recent history of color change. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a stripe of dark skin was identified on the head and a smaller patch of dark skin was present on the right forelimb. Fat bodies were depleted. Kidneys were light tan with pale streaks.

CHRONIC PYOGRANULOMATOUS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 7.5-year-old African hunting dog had a one day history of dry heaving and coughing and was diagnosed with bronchitis mucus in the lungs and minimal air movement. This condition progressed overnight despite treatment and the animal died in the morning while being treated. Resuscitation was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed obesity a 3 mm. pigmented skin tag in the left axilla fractured upper right canine tooth with exposed pulp moderate dental calculus mild subcutaneous edema in the ventral neck prominent inguinal lymph nodes some chronic abdominal adhesions attributed to previous surgery several years earlier some newer adhesions of the pancreas to the greater curvature of the stomach and right hepatic lobe thickened mottled pancreas rounded hepatic lobes moderately distended gallbladder but with typical fluid slight reddening of the mucosa of one section of the small intestine prominent lymph nodes in the mediastinum and thorax possible enlarged thymus or lymph node in the cranial thorax 15 ml. of clear fluid in the pericardial sac slightly rounded and larger than expected heart possible enlargement of the right side of the heart antemortem thrombi in both ventricles and no other abnormalities.

PROVENTRICULAR MACRORHABDIOSIS WITH DYSPLASIA RENAL ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male budgerigar was found by an attendant unable to use its right foot or leg and the legs had turned blue. The bird had a good appetite and no history of trauma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a cyst-like mass in the coelom that ruptured when the viscera were extracted.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS UTERINE LEIOMYOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female sheep had a history of severe arthritis and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fair body condition overgrown hooves despite hoof trims abnormal hoof conformation in the left rear sharp points on all teeth slightly enlarged and yellowish mammary glands that expressed yellowish fluid multiple degenerative joint lesions multiple firm homogeneous nodules throughout the uterine body one of which had areas of calcification on cut surface and uterine horns were filled with thick yellow-tinged fluid.

LYMPHOSARCOMA GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS. This 21-year-old female boa had a history of inappetence and weight loss. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a mass of tissue was present adherent to the ventral surface of the spinal column extending approximately two-thirds of the length down the body. A mass of tissue was present in the caudal coelom which encompassed all organs. Numerous round white masses were present scattered throughout the parenchyma of the liver and attached to the lobules of the kidney.

SUSPECT YOLK COELOMITIS VACOULAR HEPATOPATHY SPLENITIS. This 8-year/10-month-old female toad was found dead in lobby tank. It had no prior clinical signs or problems. At necropsy it had severe generalized edema. There was cloudy yellow/red fluid in the coelom. There were large numbers of 2-4 mm. yellow eggs filling the coelom. Several eggs appeared inspissated. The liver appeared rounded and mottled tan with blotchy red areas. The gall bladder was distended and contained flocculated gelatinous red material. Portions of oviduct appeared red and edematous. There was 1.3 x 0.7 cm. ovoid spiny concretion within the urodeum. There was a 2 x 4 cm. smooth ovoid concretion found in the proctodeum surrounded by normal fecal material. No impaction or obstruction was evident at either site.

Please see comments. Comment: The cause of this bird's unstable balance was not evident upon gross necropsy. The hip joints and feet were normal; and there was no evidence of arthritis. The testicles were of normal size; and there was no evidence of neoplasia observed. Histologic examination of tissues and microbiologic testing are in progress to identify/rule out any infectious etiologies and further investigate the cause of this bird's death. Results will be issued in an addendum report. Kidney: Severe diffuse interstitial fibrosis with tubular mineralization Kidney: Diffuse glomerulosclerosis Sciatic nerve (bilateral): Mild multifocal axonal degeneration Spinal cord and ganglia: Moderate neuronal lipofuscinosis Muscle: Mild myodegeneration Tibiotarsal-tarsometatarsal joint: Mild degenerative arthropathy Heart: Mild myocardial degeneration Bone: Mild degenerative arthropathy with intra-articular osteophyte Intestine; crop: Gram-negative bacterial overgrowth (Dysbiosis) Severe chronic interstitial nephritis Neuronal and nerve degeneration Muscle atrophy and degeneration Dysbiosis Comment: Severe chronic interstitial nephritis was most likely a major factor in this bird's death. The cause of this bird's reported instability and difficulty perching was probably related to the changes described within the nerves; muscles; and bone. While some degree of lipofuscin is expected in neurons as an animal ages; the quanitity noted in the neurons of this animal appeared excessive and may have contributed to its neurologic signs. In addition; there was axonal degeneration noted in both sciatic nerves; degenerative arthropathy; and muscle atrophy; all of which may have contributed to its difficulty in perching. All of the above described lesions are often age-related. No significant bacterial pathogens or Chlamydophila sp. were isolated from this bird; and it was free of intestinal parasites.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 1.5- to 2-year-old female degu had a greater than two week history of lower respiratory tract disease that was not responsive to antibiotics. The condition improved with oxygen therapy but the animal died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed an enlarged friable liver pale kidneys bilateral adrenal enlargement a foamy exudate in the trachea and bronchi good fat stores and body condition and no other abnormalities.

MESENTERIC VOLVULUS. This 9-year-old male red kangaroo was noted to have vomited once one day prior to death. Necropsy revealed extensive serosal hemorrhage of the gastrointestinal tract and pulmonary congestion.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS WITH SEPSIS CONSPECIFIC AGGRESSION. This less than 1-year-old chameleon that is one of a group that were found dead. Conspecific aggression and stress are considered possible. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and possibly enlarged liver. Some possible trauma was noted to the dorsum and neck.

PULMONARY BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS PULMONARY MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 9-year-old male emerald tree boa was found dead. Keepers had noted blood draining from the mouth. The snake had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed good body condition with blood in the oral cavity. The lungs were congested and hemorrhagic and contained multifocal tan lesions ranging in morphology from solitary nodules to lesions that appeared to follow the faveolar architecture. Adequate fat bodies were present and no other gross lesions were noted.

SALPINGITIS URATE STASIS RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 5-year-old female rattlesnake had numerous infertile ova identified one week prior to death. Although the animal had been treated medically it was scheduled for surgical removal of the eggs. Unfortunately the animal was found dead. At necropsy the oviduct was hemorrhagic with bruising near the cloaca. A large irregularly shaped egg with a rough adherent surface was present in the distal oviduct associated with caseated material.

BACTERIAL MENINGOENCEPHALITIS AND CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA. This greater than 2-year-old female rat presented with lethargy respiratory distress and shaking its head frequently. Supportive care was administered but the rat died. Necropsy revealed consolidated lungs with lobulated yellow masses. Both ears were filled with thick greenish-yellow purulent material that extended to the base of the brain.

CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR. This approximately 22-year-old female squirrel monkey was found down on the bottom of its cage and died while being treated. Necropsy revealed marked dental calculus and some fractured teeth globose heart pitting on the serosal surface of the liver and kidney two renal cysts containing dark fluid and apparent blood in the lumen of the stomach.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA COELOMITIS INANITION. This 20-year-old male boa had a history of anorexia which was unresponsive to treatment. The animal became lethargic and was found dead. At necropsy kidneys were dark black to purple. Granular yellow foci were present throughout the mesentery and stomach.

Brain: Severe diffuse spongiosis of the brain white matter with presence of Alzheimer type II astrocytes Spinal cord: Diffuse Wallerian degeneration of the spinal cord with focal necrotizing myelitis Kidney: Severe chronic diffuse interstitial nephritis Heart: Mild chronic multifocal fibrosing myocarditis Lung: Multifocal bronchiolar adenoma Liver: Multifocal biliary cysts Euthanasia Uremic encephalopathy Diffuse Wallerian degeneration of the spinal cord with focal necrotizing myelitis Spondylosis and degenerative intervertebral disk disease Mild chronic multifocal fibrosing myocarditis Multifocal bronchiolar adenoma Multifocal biliary cysts Comments: Histologically; the lesions found at the brain and kidneys are suggestive for uremic encephalopathy. Focal necrosis of the spinal cord is suspected to be due to compression. The brain and spinal cord lesions are undoubtedly accounted for the animal's lameness and ataxia; which lead to poor quality of life. The pulmonary masses; bronchiolar adenoma; and hepatic biliary cysts are benign lesions. Katriya Chankow; DVM

ABDOMINAL EFFUSION WITH ADHESIONS PORTAL HYPERTENSION SHOCK. This 9-year-old male Sumatran tiger has a three day history of inappetence and lethargy but appeared to improve over the last 24 hours. Urinalysis revealed bilirubinuria. Supportive care was administered but the animal deteriorated rapidly and died. Necropsy revealed marked icterus thickened gall bladder with thick gelatinous green-tinged material tortuous bile duct pale swollen kidneys that bulge on cut surface and some mucoid material in the urinary bladder.
