TRAUMA HEPATIC LIPIDFOSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This 18-year-old male flying fox was found down with a severe fracture of the stifle. The limb was amputated and the animal’s condition was improving. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the liver was yellow and friable.

INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE WITH TRANSFORMATION TO LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male domestic ferret has a greater than two year history of adrenal disease and the left adrenal gland had been previously excised. The ferret also has a history of hypoglycemia that responded to prednisolone therapy. The animal has a two week history of weight loss despite supplemental feeding but maintained normal appetite and behavior. Blood work revealed mild hemoconcentration with dehydration and hypoglycemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large amount of cavitary adipose tissue. Some dark granular material was in the stomach accompanied by pinpoint hemorrhage in the mucosa and some thickened areas were noted in the intestine. The kidneys had mild to moderate pitting on the serosal surface. The spleen was contracted and had some scarring from a previous fracture. A cystic structure was lateral to the trachea and distal to the hyoid structure and the thyroid and parathyroid could not be located.

EMACIATION. This 12-year-old female ringed teal was found dead in big lake. The teal had been in B-2 and had no veterinary care while in the collection. Necropsy revealed no food in the alimentary tract.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATIC METASTASIS. This 7-year-old rabbit was euthanized due to declining quality of life. The animal had a prior history of uterine tumors and chronic dental disease. At necropsy the body was thin. The liver contained a 0.5 cm. diameter spherical mass near the margin. Multiple to coalescing masses were present in the uterine horns.

SARCOCYSTOSIS BACTERIAL COLITIS CHRONIC PROVENTRICULITIS. This 7-year-old lorikeet was noted to be unable to fly in the morning. The bird’s legs and wings were stiff and extended and it developed cardiac arrest when captured. This bird also had a history of getting caught in the netting and attacked by cagemates approximately three weeks earlier but did not suffer any apparent trauma. Necropsy revealed dark red lungs some pale foci near the apex of the heart several areas of pale thickened small intestine enlarged liver with rounded borders and numerous pale tan areas and a 4 mm. mass in the spleen.
AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATITIS. This 17-year-old female swan was found dead. At necropsy large foci of pododermatitis were present on both feet. The liver was friable.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE URATE STASIS. This 20-year-old Inca tern was found in the exhibit poorly responsive and was dead within one hour of presentation. The bird had been hospitalized for a month up until three days prior to death due to lethargy and suspected urate stasis. Heterophilia hyperglobulinemia and mildly increased plasma uric acid concentration were also noted. Necropsy revealed pale tan swollen kidneys. The bird also had a callus associated with pododermatitis on the major pad of the left foot of several years duration. A previous biopsy from this bird revealed mild perivascular dermatitis around the uropygial gland. A conspecific was suspected of hypovitaminosis E based on steatitis on the uropygial gland.

ATYPICAL LYMPHOID INFILTRATE EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male African lion was diagnosed with small cell lymphoma from a splenic biopsy ten weeks earlier. It was treated palliatively with prednisolone until its condition deteriorated when it was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition ulcerative wounds on the left foreleg hind limbs and scrotum alopecia near a healed wound at the lateral canthus of both eyes dried blood around the upper incisors ulceration to 5 cm. in greatest dimension on the hard palate several cysts with gelatinous material in the left thyroid splenic enlargement with occasional white nodules yellow/green renal cortices with hemorrhage at the corticomedullary interface and a central area of hemorrhage in the middle of the medulla and erythematous small intestinal mucosa.

CHRONIC ENTEROCLOITIS BACTERIAL OVERGRWOTH SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 15-year-old female pygmy marmoset was found dead on exhibit. The animal had lost approximately 30 gm. since last weighed several months earlier. Necropsy revealed globoid cardiac shape and a 1 mm. translucent mass in the hepatic parenchyma.

SYSTEMIC MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male hedgehog has a history of chronic weight loss since February despite good appetite. The animal was euthanized for humane reasons. Necropsy revealed bilateral corneal opacities congested lungs a dark area on the cranial aspect of the left cranial lung lobe congested enlarged spleen with raised gray nodule at the center bilateral adrenomegaly pale kidneys thin body condition enlarged liver with multiple nodules in the right lobe mineralization of the seminal vesicles with adhesions of the urinary bladder to the right seminal vesicle.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION GOUT YOLK COELOMITIS. This 22-year-old female sun bittern was found acutely obtunded and gasping on the ground. The animal was administered supportive care but died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed pale friable kidneys mottled liver and coelomic adhesions.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male fox was under treatment for renal failure and intestinal obstruction. An enterotomy had been performed to relieve the intestinal obstruction with removal of inspissated fecal material. The splenic mass was noted at that time. The animal later developed ataxia and apparent blindness. Due to lack of clinical response to therapy and progression of renal failure the animal was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy the animal was in poor body condition with marked wear of teeth. The right kidney was markedly shrunken. The left kidney contained a depressed area corresponding to an area of cortical hemorrhage.

PNEUMONIA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 5-week-old rabbit was born in a captive breeding program was transferred to a “hardening pen” to acclimate the rabbit to natural temperature and life cycles and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed mucus in the stomach a few pinpoint gastric ulcers absence of intra-abdominal fat and poor body condition. Another rabbit from the same group died within a day of this rabbit.

EXHIBIT ENTRAPMENT EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 1.5-year-old female bighorn sheep had become entangled in the fence hanging from its right hind limb. The patient was subsequently unable to stand in the rear despite two days of supportive care. Capture myopathy was suspected and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed extended right hind leg with limited or no mobility subcutaneous edema in the right inguinal region a few abrasions on the rump and hind limbs small adhesion between the right cranial pulmonary lobe and right thoracic wall mild ventral consolidation of the right cranial pulmonary lobe pale streaks in the papillary muscles of the left ventricle brown to yellow mottled discoloration on the surface of the liver extending into the parenchyma and multiple 1-2 mm. white nodules surrounding pancreatic tissue in the parenchyma minimal to no urine in the urinary bladder healed corneal graft on the right eye multiple areas of pale discoloration throughout the right thigh lumbar and ventral abdominal muscles as well as the diaphragm severe hemorrhage and edema around affected muscles extending cranially along the ventral body wall and incorporating approximately 40% of the evaluated body musculature possible partial avulsive fracture of the greater trochanter of the femur with possible rupture of the ligament of the head of the femur and a puncture wound on lateral aspect of P1 on the right hind extending through the periosteum through the cortical bone approximately 1-2 cm. in width at the location where the fence edge had punctured through the skin.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION HEMOSIDEROSIS COLITIS GASTRITIS. This 7.5-year-old female hyrax was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy there were minimal fat stores and the heart was rounded and enlarged with left ventricular thickening.

PERIANAL ADENOCARCINOMA CHRONIC GASTROENTERITIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male ferret had a two week history of intermittent inappetence responded well to supportive care and then decompensated with recurrent impacted anal glands. A fine needle aspirate of the right anal gland region revealed pleomorphic cells with inflammation and was suspicious for neoplasia. The ferret had marked loss of body condition with each examination and progression of the perianal mass. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. yellow/translucent cyst on the liver. Kidneys had an irregular surface with dull cortices and loss of proportion of the cortex and medulla. Yellow deposits were in the cortex. The right anal gland was abnormal and extended around the circumference of the anus but is especially prominent in the right side.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS SEPSIS HEPATIC PARASITE GRANULOMA (AGENT UNIDENTIFIED). This greater than 1-year-old male gecko was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed thin body condition erythematous skin on the left hind leg and reddish-brown kidneys.

URATE STASIS RENAL GOUT GRANULOMATOUS NEPHRITIS ORCHITIS. This 13-year-old male pit viper presented in moribund condition and was humanely euthanized. At necropsy several rocks were noted in the esophagus and stomach. The liver was discolored green. Kidneys showed urate stasis.

INCLUSION BODY HEPATPATHY. This 7-year-old male swan has a history of anemia and was administered a blood transfusion from a conspecific. The animal was ataxic prior to death and resuscitation was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed petechiae on the feet fluid in the pericardial sac hemorrhage in the cardiac muscles of both ventricles and on the epicardial surface petechiae on the surfaces of the gastrointestinal tract and dark feces around the vent.

OSTEOMYELITIS. This 7-year-old male rattlesnake had a history of a mass on the dorsum with proliferation of bone along the vertebrae. Loss of neurologic function to the caudal body developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a hard mass was present on the spinal column.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 19-year-old female mot mot was found unresponsive on the floor of the Rain Forest and brought to the hospital. It was sedated for physical examination and a large abdominal mass was palpated. The mass filled the entire abdominal cavity. The bird was found dead approximately two hours later. Necropsy revealed poor nutritional status with no adipose stores muscle atrophy and no food in the digestive tract. Urates were focally around the cloaca and the abdomen was distended by a large firm mass. The mass was an enlarged firm and lobulated liver that compressed the gastrointestinal tract heart and lungs. No normal appearing liver was present. The bulk of the mass was tan/pink with some areas of central necrosis. Kidneys were pale tan and the ovary was small and inactive. Approximately 2 ml. of clear yellow fluid was in the abdominal cavity.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male hedgehog had chronic central nervous system signs and was falling to the left. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed consolidated lungs.

SCLEROSING PERITONITIS GASTRIC DEHISCENCE SEPSIS. This 15-year-old female colobus monkey had a history of gastrotomy due to hay impaction in January 06. Subsequently the monkey had variable inappetence lethargy and diarrhea and became extremely weak was hospitalized and treated but died the following morning. Necropsy revealed straw colored fluid in the peritoneal cavity and some serosanguineous fluid in the pleural cavity. Multiple adhesions were noted in the abdominal cavity involving the liver stomach and peritoneal body wall. Lungs were consolidated and oozed fluid and foam on cut surface. The gastric surgical incision was dehisced with a 5 mm. perforation and focal thickening of the incision edges. The perforation corresponded with a 5 mm. opening into an enclosed sacculation between the diaphragm and peritoneal membrane. The stomach was adhered to the affected portion of the peritoneum. Direct leakage of gastric contents was noted. A similar sacculation was also noted between the diaphragm and the peritoneal membrane with a 5 mm. opening into the peritoneal cavity to the right of the stomach and liver. Mucosa in all areas of the stomach and proximal small intestine had multifocally and densely distributed petechiae. A 4 mm. fracture of the acetabular rim was also noted.

EUTHANASIA GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 17-year-old female rattlesnake was euthanized due to a positive gastric biopsy for cryptosporidiosis. Ovaries contained developing follicles containing flocculent or purulent material. Ovaries were contained within fluid filled sacs.

PREDATION SHOCK. This 14-year-old female pronghorn was attacked by feral dogs. At necropsy puncture wounds were present over the forelimbs and flank as well as over the nasal area. Crepitus was noted in the nasal sinuses. Extensive hemorrhage was noted in the forelimbs and thigh. Lungs and trachea contained frank hemorrhage.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHROSIS. This female greater than 16-year-old addax was humanely euthanized due to chronic osteoarthritis. She was separated from the herd in 1998 due to loss in her status and general decline in mobility. She was managed with stall rest nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and stall adjustments. The day prior to death she was unable to rise without substantial difficulty and had little movement. There was substantial muscle wasting over the shoulder and thighs. At necropsy there was mild erosive osteoarthritis within the cubital and carpal joints. There was substantial neck erosion and head eburnation bilaterally at the coxofemoral joint. The stifle joints had mild erosive osteoarthritis. The fetlocks and pasterns were grossly normal. The left tibiotarsal joint had excessive but grossly normal joint fluid and moderate osteoarthritis without periarticular mineralization. The right tibiotarsal joint had grossly thickened and caramel colored joint fluid with numerous mineralized pieces of debris. The medial collateral ligament of the right tibiotarsus was mineralized and somewhat bonded to the tibia. The right gastrocnemius tendon was also mineralized. The abomasal mucosa had very slight congestion and there were erosions present on some rugae. Only the prescapular lymph nodes appeared enlarged. Cultures of lymph nodes were performed. Sections of liver lung kidney heart and spleen were frozen for future use if needed.

MICROGRANULOMATOSIS CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS EOSINOPHILIC ENTEROCOLITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE SEVERE DIGITAL OSTEOATHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old female black and white ruffed lemur has a several year history of renal disease and arthritis and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a vulvar cyst mild pulmonary edema thickened left ventricle white nodules throughout the parenchyma of the spleen small lobulated kidneys with multiple cysts.

BUMBLEFOOT AMYLOIDOSIS METASTATIC MINERALIATION PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE RENAL GOUT. This 26.5-year-old male Caribbean flamingo was found down on exhibit following collision with another bird. Necropsy revealed thin body condition rounded hepatic margins and firm hepatic parenchyma enlarged kidneys with prominent speckling of the parenchyma enlarged spleen and no other gross abnormalities. Bumblefoot lesions were noted on all six forward toes.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL ENTERITIS LYMPHADENITIS SIALOADENITIS MYOSITIS INANITION. This 6-year-old female red panda had a chronic history of colitis. Recently the animal became inappetent and was found dead. At necropsy marked weight loss was noted. Teeth of the right mandible were loose. Muscles of the temporomandibular area were hyperemic. GI contents appeared hemorrhagic.

CARDIOMYOPATHY HYPERTENSION WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME CUTANEOUS HEMANGIOSARCOMA. This 2.5-year-old male hedgehog had a brief episode of inappetence and then returned to clinically normal. The animal then had a one-month history of moderate weight loss and decreased appetite. Weight loss and decreased appetite were attributed to breeding behavior. The animal then presented 36 hours prior to death with inappetence lethargy stiff gait and reluctance to move its hind limbs. Clinical evaluation identified a large mass in the caudal abdomen and skin mass. Increased pulmonary opacity was noted radiographically. Supportive care was administered but the animal was found dead in the morning. Necropsy identified thin body condition a 1 cm. firm dark purple mass on the right side of the body within a quilled area diffusely pale tan and firm right lung congested caudal left lung a 5 mm. hematoma at the thoracic inlet and a 10 mm. hematoma along the cranial vena cava 1 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the thoracic cavity generalized cardiomegaly petechiae on the serosal surface of the colon pale red renal cortices red serosal surface of the urinary bladder patent urinary tract enlarged prostate that oozed thick white fluid on cut surface and an enlarged sublumbar lymph node with similar parenchymal appearance to that of prostatic tissue a 2 mm. dark purple lesion within the parenchyma of the spleen and enlarged popliteal lymph nodes.

ARTICULAR GOUT HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female frilled lizard has swollen joints and high uric acid with inability to move noted several weeks ago. It appeared to be responding to allopurinol therapy and recovered some mobility but became inappetent and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes when it developed acute respiratory signs. Blood was noted from the inner canthal area of the left eye and a possible mass was seen in the rear oropharynx at the base of the skull.

DUCK VIRUS ENTERITIS. This approximately 6-year-old male fulvous whistling duck was found dead in the afternoon and appeared normal in the morning. It is one of six fulvous whistling ducks that presented from the river exhibit. Mortality due to duck virus enteritis has reached 90% in this species. This bird was vaccinated for duck virus enteritis three days prior to death. Necropsy revealed good body condition some bumblefoot lesions on both feet hemorrhage on the surface of the left ventricle hemorrhage in the wall of the crop dark red fluid in the lumen of the small and large intestine hemorrhages on the surface of enlarged liver enlarged spleen petechiae on the surfaces of the pancreas and congested meninges.

EUTHANASIA BESNOITIA AXONAL DEGENERATION. This 11-month-old male opossum has a 2- to 3-week history of lethargy and ataxia. Radiograph revealed an abnormal thoracic vertebra. This animal additionally has a history of Besnoitia. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy Besnoitia lesions were frequent on the skin. An area of compression was noted in the thoracic spinal canal.
SHOCK. This 11-year-old female fruit bat was found dead in the exhibit pool. At necropsy the teeth were severely worn.
