RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS POSSIBLE NEPHROTOXICOSIS. This 16-year-old male sheep had a one-day history of lethargy and inappetence and was found agonal at morning check. The animal died and necropsy identified bilateral cataracts muscle wasting along the topline and hips reddened lungs abundant adipose tissue thin right ventricle black discoloration of the ruminal papillae mottled pale tan liver with adhesions on the caudal aspect near the gallbladder and adhesions of this area to the duodenum and omentum reddening of the pancreas with adhesions some white/yellow raised lesions on the serosal surface of the duodenum a firm irregular object within the lumen of the duodenum and no other abnormalities.

BACTERIAL /MYCOTIC ABSCESS PULMONARY TREMATODE-LIKE GRANULOMA RIGHT-SIDED CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HYPERTENSION STROKE PULMONARY ABSCESSES DIGITAL TRAUMA (BITE WOUNDS) EUTHANASIA. This 20-year-old female colobus monkey had a 10 day history for progressive inappetence depression and diarrhea. Blood work indicated dehydration. Serum leptospirosis titers were somewhat elevated and the animal had not been recently vaccinated. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed 35 cc. of blood-tinged fluid in the abdominal cavity yellow fat multiple pulmonary adhesions to the thoracic walls a discrete firm white nodule in one pulmonary lobe fluid ingesta in the alimentary tract with no formed feces multiple reactive lymph nodes in the mesentery and bilaterally firm pale kidneys with congestion in the cortex. A dark red focus was present on the surface of the cerebellum.

INTRA-ABDOMINAL HEMORRHAGE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) PROBABLE TRAUMA. This approximately 25-year-old female chimpanzee was clinically normal in the morning then within an hour of observation became ataxic and depressed with no interest in food became recumbent within minutes with abnormal deep erratic respirations and poor gingival color. The animal subsequently arrested and resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. The time between initial presentation and cardiac arrest was approximately 20 minutes. Postmortem thoracic abdominal and skull radiographs were within normal limits. Blood work obtained after death revealed moderate anemia leukopenia and no other abnormalities. This animal was low in the group hierarchy. Necropsy revealed good body condition and excellent postmortem condition with minimal hair present on the dorsal portion of both forelimbs along the entire length as well as the dorsal cranium attributed to self-trauma and hair plucking. The abdominal cavity was filled with blood and no source of hemorrhage was noted. Moderately diffuse thickening of the mucosa of the colon was noted affecting approximately 90% of the tissue. Multiple regions of hemorrhage and petechiae were present in the cecum and colon sharply demarcated from areas of clinically normal mucosa. Multiple clots were present in the wall of the colon and did not extend into the lumen. Severe erythema and hemorrhage were noted in an approximately 20 cm. segment of the jejunum and hemorrhagic mucus was in the lumen and adhered to the wall of the intestine. A 1.5 cm. cyst was present in the uterus. The left elbow joint was fused at approximately 90° with no motion or laxity present representing an arthrodesis secondary to a previous injury. No other joint abnormalities were noted.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA RHABDOMYOLYSIS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS AND RUMENITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 10-year-old female gerenuk died after immobilization for treatment of hypocalcemia and hypothermia. Necropsy revealed multiple 1-2 cm. white foci on the myocardium on the left side of the heart that extended into the myocardium. Moderate atrophy of fat was also noted. Omental blood vessels were tortuous and congested. A 5 cm. bezoar was in the abomasum. Intestines had congested serosa and mucosa. Multiple mesenteric lymph nodes had moderate to severe congestion. Intestinal content appeared to be normal digesta. Subcutaneous adipose stores were absent and vertebrae and pelvis were prominent. Hematomas were in the intercostal muscles. Marked congestion was in the right lung. Eyes were cloudy.

EUTHANASIA SELF-TRAUMA. This 7-year-old female tamarin presented with a fracture of the left femur with extensive bite wounds. The animal had a previously amputated limb and trauma was noted at this site as well.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 3-year-old red kangaroo was found dead in the morning without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy there was a small joey in the pouch approximately 7 cm. in length. The liver was mottled tan red and black. The pericardial sac contained a small quantity of red tinged fluid.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATONS COELOMIC GRANULOMAS CHRONIC COELOMITIS CUTANEOUS VIRAL PAPILLOMA EMACIATION. This 18-year-old male salmon crested cockatoo appeared clinically healthy but had a history of high serum zinc levels. The bird also had feather loss on the legs and pectoral areas from self-trauma and feather loss on the caudal cervical area considered likely from mate trauma. During annual vaccinations in early May 2004 the bird was found to have a possible mass on the right foot. The bird was anesthetized for radiographs and examination but developed respiratory arrest during anesthesia and did not respond to resuscitative attempts. Necropsy revealed slight obesity hyperkeratosis of the skin involving the right plantar region mild pallor in the liver a discrete white mass on the cranial aspect of the liver that contained caseous material on cut surface and pulmonary congestion.

TRAUMA MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE CHRONIC ENTERITIS EUTHANASIA STRESS RESPONSE. This 2.5-year-old male budgerigar was euthanized for chronic weight loss. Recently the animal also had left leg paralysis and increased respiratory rate.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA ATYPICAL ADENOMYOSIS BRONCHOALVEOLAR ADENOCARCINOMA. This 15-year-old female Jamaican fruit bat was euthanized due to declining quality of life and had been unable to fly and was housed off exhibit. Necropsy revealed decreased range of motion in the wing joints. A 0.5 cm. smooth white firm uterine mass was noted and some 1-2 mm. white foci were in both lungs.

EUTHANASIA ENCEPHALITIS MYELIN VACUOLIZATION MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 3-year-old male hedgehog had a history of cardiomyopathy weight loss and poor condition. The animal was humanely euthanized. Lungs were heavy and wet and a white nodule was present in the left lung. The left kidney showed dilation of the pelvis and hydronephrosis. The liver was enlarged and mottled. The heart was markedly dilated. The prostate was enlarged and firm to nodular.

EUTHANASIA MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY PYELONEPHRITIS CYSTITIS ENTERITIS. This 12-year/2-month-old neutered male tiger was humanely euthanized. The tiger had a history of chronic gastritis and had marginal renal function for several years. It was found down the day before and was immobilized and treated for severe dehydration and probable renal failure. The tiger had very little improvement despite treatment. At necropsy there was some discoloration of the lungs (dark purple). The gastric mucosa had a large number of pinpoint areas of red discoloration. The stomach was full of thick green bile. The mucosa of the small intestine was dark red to purple and very rough. The mucosal surface of the large intestine was dark red to purple and very rough. The hepatic margins were very rounded. The urinary bladder contained a small amount of very cloudy urine. The mucosal surface of the bladder was discolored red/pink. Neither of the kidneys had a recognizable medullary cavity. The renal pelvises was filled with a yellow/green grainy material.

PYELITIS SEPSIS CHRONIC CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE ADRENAL CORTICAL HYPERPLASIA EOSINOPHILIC GRANULOMA EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female tiger had a history of chronic azotemia and chronic renal disease of several years duration. Over the past month the tiger had been vomiting more frequently and had erratic appetite and was being treated with Cerenia and more recently with famotidine in an attempt to relieve nausea and gastritis. Over the past week she had also begun passing some blood in her urine and was prescribed antibiotics but due to poor appetite had not been getting regular doses. On the day of euthanasia the cat had been lethargic and progressively less interested in her environment with some glassy-eyed staring. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed adequate fat stores but generalized muscle wasting and a rough haircoat. Fat and subcutaneous tissues were slightly yellow. An irregular raised soft grayish-pink granulation type lesion or ulcer was in the caudal hard palate. Some minor recent chips were present in the canine teeth and moderate to severe tartar buildup was on the molars and premolars with mild gingival reaction. A small reddened polyp was on the mucosa under the tip of the tongue. The thyroids were multifocally cystic with prominent parathyroids. The lungs were moderately atelectatic. The gallbladder was distended with bile and had tiny granular dark green sand. The spleen was large and congested with some serosal fibrous plaques marbling the surface. The uterine stump was small well healed and had a few fibrous adhesions to the rectum and urinary bladder. The urinary bladder contained clear and grossly normal urine and no mucosal lesions were noted. The adrenals had cobbled surfaces with a few small pale yellow nodules noted on cut surface in the cortices. Both kidneys had marked hemorrhagic necrosis with tissue loss renal crests/medullas with few soft blobs of pale greenish-yellow material suggesting pus mucous sludge or necrotic tissue and no uroliths were found. Both renal cortices were granular in appearance on section with tiny cysts and/or one or two bloody fluid-filled larger cystic lesions in each. Streaks of white and red discoloration were in the renal medullas. The mucosa of the stomach was cobbled or thickened but no hemorrhage or ulcers were noted. The intestines were mostly empty.

OSSEOUS METAPLASIA ARTERIAL MINERALIZATION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 4-year-old male agouti was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy there was focal mineralization of the muscles of the hind limb and epaxial muscles. The GI tract was devoid of ingesta. Other organs had no significant gross lesions.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA LIPOSARCOMA. This female 22-year-old leopard was humanely euthanized. It had a history of urinary tract infections and ingrown nails. It had a substantial tumor on her caudal right side that had been diagnosed as a lipoma from an aspiration in 1998. At necropsy there was a tumor on the right caudal side of the body that extended laterally from approximately the last rib to the femoral head and dorsally along the epaxial muscles and caudally along the entire ventrum almost to the other side. The tumor measured 91 x 42.8 x 33.5 cm. When excised the tumor had a fatty appearance but was more vascular than expected with areas of necrosis. Approximately one-third of the tumor extended into the body. It was encapsulated but did not break through the body wall. The tumor weighed 7.4 kg. Submandibular axillary and popliteal lymph nodes were enlarged. The heart was very small (approximately 5 cm. in diameter). The left ventricular walls were thickened and there was very little lumen. The right ventricular wall was very thin and flabby. All lung lobes were mottled and emphysema was present. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were enlarged and reactive. The duodenal mucosa was thickened and the lumen was very small. The stomach was devoid of ingesta. The liver had numerous cysts filled with serosanguineous fluid ranging in size from 0.5 to 1.5 cm. It had a mottled appearance roughened edges and the surface had a roughened appearance. The spleen also had rounded edges and a roughened surface. All loops of small and large intestine have petechiae. All mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. There was megacolon in the caudal portion of the colon. There were large numbers of hard fecal balls present. All body fat appeared to be jaundiced. The kidneys were not uniform in appearance. Both kidneys had numerous stones and lots of grit present. The renal pelvis of the left kidney was abnormal in appearance. There was hydronephrosis. Both ureters and the bladder also had numerous stones and grit. The bladder was full of urine. There was a kidney shaped tumor in the uterus about 10.5 x 11 cm. in size. The right ovary was enlarged.

INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA RHABDOMYOLYSIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 3.5-year-old female bighorn sheep had a three-day history of bloat and two days of suspected inappetence. Conspecific aggression was noted and the animal was immobilized for examination which revealed severe dehydration with severely elevated lactate level and decreased calcium chloride and sodium with severe azotemia and suspected pneumonia. The sheep arrested during recovery. Necropsy revealed enophthalmic globes obese body condition a moderate amount of ruminal fluid and hay in the trachea with bruising of the tracheal mucosa consolidation of the right cranial pulmonary lobe with food material in the bronchi possible thickening of the left atrioventricular valve leaflets a moderate amount of free serohemorrhagic fluid in the abdominal cavity a large amount of ingesta in the rumen and reticulum with areas of reddening in the mucosa of the omasum and abomasum and a possible ulcer in the pylorus. The liver had rounded margins yellow discoloration and granular texture on cut surface. Some hyperemia was noted in the proximal duodenal mucosa and full thickness bruising was noted around a 2 cm. circular intraluminal foreign body that on cut surface is composed of fibers. Petechiae were present throughout the gastrointestinal tract. Dry small fecal pellets were in the rectum. Brown mucoid fluid was in both uterine horns. The uterine mucosa was covered with multiple circular raised lesions and the kidneys were bilaterally symmetrical but small.

PROLIFERATIVE OSTEOARTHRITIS AND OSTEOARTHROSIS. This 11-year-old male rattlesnake died overnight following recovery from anesthesia. There was a chronic history of anorexia with associated cachexia. The day prior to death diagnostic workup revealed significant hyperostosis spondylosis and fusion of the middle 50% of the vertebral column. Bone biopsy and culture were submitted. At necropsy it was in poor body condition with advanced cachexia. There was a small amount of red watery fluid in the distal coelom. Fat bodies were present throughout the distal coelom. Few scales were raised and slightly erythemic. The ventral scales were slightly erythemic. Both kidneys appeared firm. There was fusion and hyperostosis of the vertebral column.

MYXOSARCOMA FACIAL SOFT TISSUES. This 23-year-old male flamingo has a mass in the left facial sinuses previously diagnosed as a myxosarcoma. The animal had been doing well clinically with normal behavior and maintaining its weight but with persistent air distention of the sinus. A second debulking surgery was performed. Sharp and blunt dissection of mass material was performed through an incision to enlarge the right naris. Multiple pieces of mass material were removed and submitted.
CAGEMATE TRAUMA CHRONIC CYSTITIS. This 2-year-old female prairie dog was found dead in the cage with apparent cagemate trauma. At gross necropsy the bladder mucosa was hemorrhagic.
adult. Weight: 293 g.  Euthanased.  Focal pneumonia.  Splenomegaly.  Liver nodule/necrosis.

PNEUMONIA COELOMITIS NEPHRITIS INANITION CATARACTS MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 4-year-old female tentacled snake recently had surgery. The animal was found dead. The surgical site showed no signs of healing. At necropsy serosanguineous fluid was present in the trachea. Multiple pinpoint white foci were present throughout the liver. The anterior lung was thickened and nodular.

1) Heart: chronic multifocal myocarditis 2) Stomach: perigastric mass Comments The myocardial masses are believed to be infectious in origin; either abscesses or granulomas; however; neoplasia is alos in the differential. The mass observed adjecent the stomach may also indicate infection in the abdominal cavity or neoplastic process. Histopathology and bacterial culture are pending; and the results will be included in the final report. 1) Lung: Moderate chronic caseogranulomatous pneumonia 2) Kidney: Focal chronic caseogranulomatous nephritis 3) Heart: Severe multifocal caseogranulomatous and fibrosing myocarditis Bacterial septicemia resulting in caseogranulomatous myocarditis; pneumonia and nephritis Comments: The histologic findings confirm our suspicions on gross necropsy of bacterial infection affecting the myocardium and other tissues. Acinetobacter; a gram negative rod; is the most likely agent to be causing the caseogranulomatous lesions seen. Staphylococcus infection is likely secondary. This completes the outstanding testing for this case.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK RENAL GOUT PNEUMOCONIOSIS FUNGAL PNEUMONIA CHRONIC OOPHORITIS ENTERITIS. This 33-year-old female flamingo had been lethargic for a few days prior to death. The bird was found dead. At necropsy large foci of pododermatitis were identified on the feet. No other significant gross findings were noted.

LYMPHOMA EMACIATION. This 17-year-old female milk snake presented for inappetence and reluctance to shed and examination revealed a mass in the coelom. The animal was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed a 5 cm. soft circumscribed mass in the region of the stomach. A second 4 cm. mass was seen close to the intestine but separated from the intestine and contained dark brown material.

DEGENERATIVE DISEASE METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 15.5-year-old red panda fell four feet out of a tree was breathing rapid and shallow and was weak. The animal subsequently decompensated received supportive care but had an unsteady gait and labored breathing and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had previous episodes of difficult breathing. Necropsy revealed loss of muscle mass blood-tinged frothy fluid from the nares and oral cavity no appreciable subcutaneous fat stores extensive subcutaneous edema and possibly some emphysema 70 ml. of red fluid in the abdominal cavity and 40 ml. of dark red fluid in the thoracic cavity. Some clear yellow fluid was in the pericardial sac. Multiple enlarged lymph nodes were identified in the cranial mediastinum and around the heart the largest between trachea and an auricle. The heart appeared generally enlarged and the right ventricle was especially flabby. The lungs were enlarged edematous wet heavy and oozed red fluid on cut surface. Clear frothy fluid was in the trachea. Multiple white nodules were scattered throughout the surface of the lung most of which extended into the parenchyma and on cut surface the nodules were homogeneous and some had hemorrhagic borders with the lung. The gastric mucosa appeared slightly hemorrhagic. Both ovarian bursas appeared dark red and hemorrhagic and both contained a small firm round tan structure that was homogeneous on cut surface. The uterine body was enlarged firm and contained dense tan firm homogeneous tissue on cut surface. The liver was diffusely mottled and slightly rounded.

BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS MALARIA EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female Inca tern had a history of lysis in the left tibiotarsal/metatarsal joint that was not responding to treatment the bird was losing weight and Plasmodium was seen in red blood cells and confirmed by PCR. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed absence of adipose stores inactive ovary and swollen left tibiotarsal/metatarsal joint.

PYOMETRITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 3-year-old female tamarin died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed significant hemorrhage over the rear legs and perineum and a 1 mm. laceration at the dorsal aspect of the vulva. Severely hemorrhagic pancreas pale mushy kidneys and intrauterine hemorrhage were also detected.

Kidney: focal cortical cyst Ovary: paraovarian cyst Thoracic cavity: moderate pleural effusion Comments: Overall findings were highly suggestive of hypoproteinemia and poor body condition. Hypoproteinemia is often associated with severe parasitism; however parasites were not observed during the necropsy. Histopathology; virology; bacteriology; nutrition; and parasitology is in progress. Cyst found in the kidney and adjacent to the ovary were incidental findings and were unassociated with the cause of this animal's demise. Schantel A. Hayes; DVM Liver: severe; centrilobular to midzonal necrosis Heart: minimal myofiber degeneration with numerous intracellular protozoa (Sarcocyst) Kidney: multifocal mild interstitial fibrosis with multifocal tubular mineralization Stomach: moderate crypt hyperplasia Comments: The primary cause for hepatic lesions could not be determined histologically however; lesions may represent anemia or acute cardiovascular collapse (heart failure). Another differential is vitamin E and selenium deficiency. To rule out this etiology; liver has been submitted to nutrition. A supplemental report will be released when results are available. Changes in the heart were minimal. There were large numbers of Sarcocyst within myofibers. This finding is generally incidental however; large numbers may impede cardiac conduction and cause cardiovascular compromise. There was no evidence of parasites in sections of stomach or intestine examined however; many coccidial oocyst and trichostrongyles were found in feces submitted to parasitology. The parasite load may have contributed to the long history of diarrhea. Schantel A. Hayes; DVM

NEPHROSCLEROSIS ASPIRATION PANCREATIC FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old ring-tailed lemur had a previous history of renal disease and retroperitoneal cysts (G12-0973). The animal had been clinically normal with good appetite and weight gain until one week prior to presentation. The animal subsequently developed several days of mild shifting limb lameness that appeared to resolve without treatment. Signs progressed to lethargy hunched posture and possibly hind limb weakness. Examination revealed gas distended stomach and intestinal loops and the morning after anesthesia it had severe dyspnea. Radiographic pattern suggested pulmonary thromboembolism in the right middle pulmonary lobe. Heparin therapy and supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed diffusely abnormal right pulmonary fields with discolored tan/brown parenchyma and large amounts of foamy white fluid on cut surface. The left lungs were partially atelectatic and congested. The left ventricle was diffusely thickened and the right atrium possibly enlarged. Gas was in the alimentary tract no ingesta was in the stomach and the colon was grossly distended for approximately 6 cm. a few centimeters proximal to the rectum. Kidneys were diffusely pale with multiple 1.2 mm. depressions throughout the cortex. Mild degenerative changes were in the stifles.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE STRESS PARATHYROID ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male spoonbill had recurrent bouts of weakness and lameness of a few months duration that appeared to alternate between the right and left leg. The bird also had moderate bumblefoot that did not seem severe enough or to have changed in recent years to have explained the signs. An interphalangeal subluxation of digit #4 of the left foot was also present. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed flaccid right ventricular wall hemorrhage on the left anterior tibiotarsus extending into the musculature of the stifle orange and possibly enlarged urogenital system.

DISSEMINATED INFECTIOUS PROCESS SERTOLI CELL TUMOR. This 4-year-old male bobwhite quail was found dead. Necropsy revealed overgrown beak blood in the mouth hemorrhagic lungs clear fluid in the trachea and enlarged irregular testicles with white patches.

EUTHANASIA INANITION CHOLESTASIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ATELECTASIS. This 18-year-old female tamarin was euthanized due to declining condition and chronic hepatopathy. At necropsy the right tibia and fibula were fractured. Inspissated bile was present in the gall bladder. A hard tan nodule was present at the base of the gall bladder. The left kidney contained a triangular cyst-like structure.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 11-year-old female reindeer has a history of weight loss. Cough and nasal discharge recently developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. Adhesions were present between the pericardium and lungs. The caudal ventral lobe of the left lung was consolidated and dark. Remaining lung was also consolidated and dark. Granulomatous foci were present throughout the lung. Similar lesions were present within the liver. An ulcer was present in the abomasum.

EUTHANASIA SPLENIC LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA PORTAL HEPATITIS. This captive bred female 4-year-old chicken was humanely euthanized. It was part of an education department. It had bumblefoot lesions that were nonresponsive to conservative and surgical treatment. At necropsy there were bilateral bumblefoot lesions. The spleen was enlarged and had white spots on the surface that were also present on cross section throughout the parenchyma. The kidneys appeared swollen and very dark. There were some white areas on the surface. The reproductive tract was active. The gizzard contained broken eggshells.

BILIARY CYSTS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION CUTANEOUS PAPILLOMA ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS ENTERITIS. This 23-year-old female river otter had a history of intermittent hind limb lameness and paresis. The animal was anesthetized for physical exam. Radiographs revealed bridging spondylosis and increased fluid in the peritoneal cavity. The animal began seizuring during anesthetic recovered which recurred despite repeated doses of diazepam. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a large quantity of fibrin was present in the anterior abdominal cavity. Peritoneal fluid was yellowish and cloudy. The pericardium had a 3 cm. red tissue mass. The right ventricle was thin walled and flaccid. A large quantity of fibrin was present in the thoracic cavity. The liver was mottled and contained a tortuous cyst approximately 3-4 cm. in length. A cystic yellow mass was present adjacent to the gall bladder.

EUTHANASIA PANCREATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS SHOCK. This 22-year-old female lemur had a chronic history of degenerative joint disease and was found recumbent and seizuring. The animal was humanely euthanized. Two other lemurs have died in this group with lesions of toxoplasmosis.
adult. Weight: 164.8 g.  Cranial haemorrhage; trauma; flew into object.

PNEUMONIAPERITONITIS KLEBSIELLA. This 14-year-old male lemur had intermittent periods of anorexia lameness and abscess formation following quarantine. The lemur died spontaneously and necropsy revealed good nutritional status puncture wound over the rib cage pleural adhesions mottled lungs abdominal adhesions hepatomegaly and hemorrhagic mesenteric fat.

ASTROCYTOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 5-year-old hedgehog had a history of progressive ataxia weakness inappetence and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mature cataract in the right eye and early cataract in the left eye. Some mild bruising was in the ventral cervical area (venipuncture site) adipose stores were abundant two round symmetrical masses were on either side of the trachea in the ventral midcervical region. The masses were beige and homogeneous. Thyroid glands were subjectively enlarged and pale tan. The left pleural cavity was filled with cloudy fluid and the left lung was diffusely dark red and consolidated. The right pleural cavity contained a large blood clot (intracardiac euthanasia). The right lung was diffusely dark red and consolidated. The heart was subjectively enlarged and the left ventricle was subjectively thickened. The liver was diffusely pale brown. The stomach contained feed material and the intestines were basically empty. The kidneys were diffusely pale and the right kidney contained a large fluid-filled cyst in the cranial pole.

EUTHANASIA ADENOCARCINOMA HERNIA. This captive bred greater than 10-year-old female sheep was humanely euthanized. It had a history of partial anorexia for three days and staying separate from the herd. It was lethargic and preferred to lie down. An abdominal wall hernia (reducible) was palpated to contain intestinal loops. At necropsy there was an approximate 3 in. diameter reducible abdominal wall hernia. It contained mesentery and a loop of jejunum. On the serosal surface of the mesentery there were several raised tan plaques which felt firm. On cut surface these plaques had a black layer. The right cranial lung lobe had a 1 cm. area of fibrosis. The heart was firmly attached to the sternum. There were hard nodules of pericardial fat. The uterus contained approximately 300 ml. of clear fluid. There was one corpus hemorrhagicum in the ovary. The splenic capsule had a grainy/sandy texture. The capsule was speckled with tan blotchy areas and diffuse black 1 mm. foci. There were several raised pink nodules 2-3 mm. in diameter.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE DEGENERATIVE RENAL DISEASE PANCREATIC FIRBROSIS IRON STORAGE DISEASE COLONIC NEMATODIASIS NECROTIC LIPOMA. This 14.5-year-old female rock hyrax was found dead. The animal had an examination approximately one year prior and had a mammary mass that was histologically consistent with a suspect carcinoma. At necropsy the right uterine horn was enlarged with clear fluid. The liver was firm and mottled. Pulmonary lobes are dark red. The left side of the heart was slightly thin. There are a few white firm regions along the gastric wall.

LYMPHOMA. This 1.5-year-old female cottontail rabbit had a two week history of illness that included onset of bilateral hind limb paresis with no evidence of a spinal fracture. The animal was treated for spinal cord trauma and encephalitozoonosis with initial improvement but then declined. Necropsy revealed multiple pinpoint white nodules in the spleen white solid multifocal discrete masses in both kidneys and white multiple nodules in one lobe of the liver.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GRANULOMATOUS PNEUMONIA LYMPHADENITIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This 7-year-old female gazelle had a chronic history of poor condition. Recently the animal developed a mandibular abscess. Blood work revealed azotemia and hypocalcemia. The animal did not recover from anesthesia and was found dead. At necropsy caseous nodules were present in the lung. Pinpoint white foci were present in the liver. Calculi were present in the right kidney.

EUTHANASIA CARDIOMYOPATHY PLASMACYTIC ENTERITIS. This approximately 11-year-old female captive bred chinchilla was humanely euthanized. It had a five month duration of illness with chronic wasting. Exploratory surgery with intestinal biopsy was done. The chinchilla declined two days later.

SEPSIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female emerald tree boa was humanely euthanized due to declining condition over several months. The snake had chronic inappetence dehydration dysecdysis anemia and weight loss. The snake developed openmouthed breathing and gaping one day prior to euthanasia. It had regurgitated a mouse two days prior to euthanasia. Necropsy revealed multiple discolored scales thin body condition absence of fat stores a desiccated mouse adhered to the mucosa of the colon coconut shell substrate in the stomach multiple degenerative ovarian follicles with apparent abscessation multiple 3 mm. white foci in the liver and some cystic foci in the liver.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS MACRORHABDIOSIS. This 3-year-old male budgerigar had been treated several times for Macrorhabdus infection. The bird often had feces on the vent and spent more than average time on the floor. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed stained vent feathers and no other gross lesions.

RECTAL PROLAPSE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS LOW GRADE SEPSIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female chinchilla has a history of severe rectal prolapse on 10/12 and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION BILIARY CYSTADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female/spayed cougar has an approximate six-month history of mild renal disease. Six months ago ultrasound revealed some cardiomegaly ascites and edema that were thought to be related to medetomidine. Three months prior to death the animal had progressive weight loss intermittent anorexia vomiting and progressively worsening mental status (confusion disorientation). One week prior to death the animal was lethargic with loss of appetite vomiting and tarry stool. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the kidneys were small. There was a 1 cm. pancreatic nodule and a cystic lesion at the center of the liver.

EUTHANASIA DYSTOCIA UTERINE RUPTURE. This 15-year-old female addax presented with dystocia with a dead fetus. Manual extraction of the calf was unsuccessful. Laparotomy revealed a large quantity of blood in the peritoneal cavity and rupture of the uterus. The animal was humanely euthanized.

TRAUMATIC FRACTURE DIGITAL OSTEOMYELITIS COLONIC ULCERATION DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female wallaroo incurred a traumatic fracture of the left femur which was repaired surgically. Following stabilization digital amputation of the right hind leg was performed surgically and at that time the animal was noted to be anemic. During a subsequent bandage change it was noted that the left femur had been refractured. Hematocrit continued to decline and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple fracture fragments in the left femoral region with associated severe hemorrhage and bruising. This animal had dilated pupils during its entire hospitalization and prior to hospitalization.

EUTHANASIA ATHEROSCLEROSIS SEMINOMA HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS TRACHEITIS AIR SACCULITIS PORTAL HEPATITIS. This 32-year-old male flamingo was humanely euthanized. It had a history of ataxia and was unable to stand or walk normally. At necropsy the left testis was 5 x 4.5 cm. The liver was dark brown and friable. The aorta was thickened and irregular near the kidneys.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS RUMINORETICULITIS. This 11-year-old male/neutered sheep was clinically normal other than mature bilateral cataracts that developed over the past year resulting in 90% blindness. Cataract surgery was planned the animal received preanesthetic drugs and anesthetic induction. The animal died during the induction procedure and could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed 15 cc. of straw-colored effusion in the cranial abdomen consolidation and reddening of 60% of the pulmonary mass thin walled and dilated right ventricle with multiple pinpoint areas of hemorrhage on the surface and mature cataracts on both eyes. Partial phacoemulsification was performed after death. The left eye was submitted.

MYOCARDIAL HEPATIC AND RENAL FIBROSIS PINEAL GLAND HYPERPLASIA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS CATARACTS. This 15-year-old male ratsnake has a history of chronic cataract with loss of visual acuity had abnormal behavior that included flattening the body and actively defensive behavior on exhibit last week. The animal ate two weeks earlier but had been eating less. A large amount of feces was noted one week earlier. It was found dead in its cage unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed cachexia a focal tan raised 2 mm. lesion on the ventral proximal trachea 3 cm. caudal to the glottis. The thyroid was firm and tan. Some areas of pallor were present in the ventricular myocardium the liver was firm and the gallbladder was engorged. The stomach was empty and the rugae were prominent and tan. The spleen was small and the pancreas was firm. A focal cyst to 5 mm. in greatest dimension was in the cranial aspect of the testicle and contained luminal clear fluid. The kidneys were tan. A 15 cm. tract of tan fat was noted distal to the kidneys.

EUTHANASIA INANITION METABOLIC BONE DISEASE CHROMOMYCOSIS. This 3-year/7-month-old female frog was humanely euthanized. It had a history of ulcerate right wrist. The frog was not eating on its own. Its overall condition was poor.

CHRONIC COELOMITIS FOLLICULOSTASIS (CLINICAL) EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female rhea had a hysterectomy on the first of January for retained egg. Yolk coelomitis was evident at surgery and an inspissated egg was in the fimbria two ova were in the oviduct and one broken egg was in the shell gland. The bird also had coins in the ventriculus based on radiographs. The bird was standing and apparently doing well for four days after the surgical procedure but was not eating and being tube fed under manual restraint. The bird subsequently became recumbent necessitating a sling. The bird was not producing feces and had an obstructive pattern with ileus. Surgery revealed intestinal adhesions and devitalization of the caeca with coelomitis and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed markedly distended caeca filled with gas and green digesta seeds plastic bottle caps two quarters a dime and two pennies from 1964 and 1973 and several pieces of glass from the ventriculus. The spleen was oblong. The kidneys were pale tan. An irregular large clot was present at the transected shell gland and a scalpel handle could be passed through the coprodeum.

PRIMARY REMAL SARCOMA PROBABLE NEPHROBLASTOMA. This 6.5-year-old female captive bred lemur died spontaneously. It had a one month history of abdominal distention. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the abdominal cavity associated with adhesions to the diaphragm and serosanguineous exudate. The left kidney was not identified.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA PLEURITIS. This 3-year-old male kangaroo was under treatment for pleural effusion and lethargy. The animal collapsed and died. At necropsy the thoracic cavity contained a large quantity of yellow tinged fluid. Lungs were thickened firm and contained several larger firm granulomas. An impression smear of the pulmonary granuloma was negative for mycobacteria.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 17-year-old female squirrel monkey was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous masses in the region of the forearm and right distal tibia fluid filled chest enlarged heart mottled lungs roughened firm liver and thin body condition.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS. This 1-year-old red panda had a historical injury to the left hind leg as a neonate that resulted in an ataxic gait in the hind limbs. It recently presented with inability to raise its head and with ataxia. The animal was alert and responding to visual stimuli. Radiographs of the cervical spine were unremarkable. The animal’s condition deteriorated through the day and neurologic exam revealed possible encephalitis. Supportive care was administered and almost complete resolution of neurologic signs was noted the following morning but signs returned when medication was switched to oral formulations. An MRI revealed subtle lesions in the brain and brainstem. Recovery from anesthesia was prolonged and the animal’s condition deteriorated rapidly. Its temperature was elevated and did not respond to supportive care. The animal became ventilator dependent and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA ENTEROCOLITIS INANITION. This 1-year-old female addax presented with neurologic signs including opisthotonos. The animal was lethargic reluctant to stand and was euthanized. At necropsy the only significant gross lesion was serous atrophy of fat depots.

AUTOLYZED TISSUE. This 8-year-old male bighorn sheep had a two day history of laying down a lot and no other signs of illness. The sheep died and necropsy revealed blood dripping from the nose fluid filled frothy lungs and thickened heart muscle.

SPLENITIS PANCREATITIS NEMATODE LARVAL GRANULOMAS PNEUMONIA NEPHRITIS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY. This greater than 2-year-old female lizard was found dead on the ground of its cage. A large spider was found in the cage. There was a bite wound apparent on the left front leg. At necropsy there was an ulcerated and necrotic wound over the left cubital joint with an apparent double puncture wound 3 mm. apart. The liver was large and gray/brown. It was very dense/thick on cut section. The stomach had 0.5-1 mm. pale diffuse foci.

SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA WITH ASSOCIATED BACTERIAL CELLULITIS FACIAL SOFT TISSUES EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old lizard had a greater than two year history of mandibular swelling with recurrent stomatitis and ocular disease. It was treated repeatedly oral vitamin A topical ocular treatments and systemic antibiotics responded to therapy but would relapse 3-4 weeks after discontinuation of treatment. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. An oral biopsy of swollen mandibular tissue obtained in August 2011 revealed mucosal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis with probable squamous metaplasia (G11-4424). Necropsy revealed good body condition swollen conjunctiva and closed eyes mandibular swelling of soft tissue with erythema and bleeding large fat bodies and multiple digital abnormalities.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This greater than 8-year-old male mantella was found dead in enclosure pool. It had no signs of illness present. The water quality was fine. There was another animal in the group that died recently. At necropsy there were no notable lesions.

NORMAL EYE AND BRAIN. This 18.5-year-old male Sumatran tiger has been declining over several months and renal failure was diagnosed in November 2008. A nail is growing into a front footpad and the cat has rapidly declined over the past week. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed absence of the right kidney and mildly enlarged left kidney with dilated pelvis. Previous histologic diagnosis (G08-6531) is chronic renal disease. Sections of eye and brain are submitted.

LYMPHOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE PANCREATIC ADENOCARCINOMA OVARIAN ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female Sebright domestic chicken was previously diagnosed with lymphoma secondary to Marek’s disease. The animal had weight loss over two weeks and was found weak lethargic and ataxic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the keel was prominent. There was abundant sand packed within the crop and ventriculus. The pancreas was thickened firm and mottled. Kidneys were large and friable. A large ovarian mass was present over the caudal dorsal coelom that was white to tan on cut section.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS. This approximately 43-year-old male Matamata was found upside-down in the pool acted normally when righted and was found upside-down again the following morning dead. Necropsy revealed algae on the surface of the shell deeply pitted plastron irregular carapace with pyramiding numerous variably sized white/opaque firm nodules in the cervical soft tissues in the mid caudal neck region fat pads present a single 1.5 cm. well circumscribed mass in the hepatic parenchyma which has the same color as the adjacent parenchyma erythema in the stomach white round firm nodules in the renal parenchyma and pale foci in the parenchyma.

OBESITY HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHRONIC YOLK COELOMITIS WITH ADHESIONS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female chicken presented with acute dyspnea that did not respond to supportive care. Radiographs revealed compression of all air sacs associated with a coelomic mass and alveolar densities in the hilar region of the lungs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed obesity hemorrhage in the left lung hemorrhage in the syrinx firm great vessels prominent spleen and mottled yellow/gold/brown and slightly enlarged liver. The ovary was active but without signs of vitellogenesis. The aortic valves were thickened and yellow.

EUTHANASIA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE ISLET CELL VACUOLATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 5-year-old female domestic ferret had adrenal disease diagnosed in early 2014 that was treated with deslorelin. An insulinoma was removed in 2014 with resolution of hypoglycemia; however clinical signs of insulinoma returned in 2016. The animal has an approximate two-year history of progressive diarrhea anorexia and weight loss. The animal has been treated supportively with prednisone metronidazole and famotidine. The animal became increasingly lethargic with weight loss and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was an approximately 1 mm. raised mass on the visceral surface of the liver. There were several pinpoint areas throughout the pancreas that were firm.

POSTPARTUM SEPTIC ENDOMETRITIS HYPERKERATOTIC AND BACTERIAL RUMENITIS AND POSSIBLE OSTEOGENESIS IMPERFECTA. This approximately 7-year-old captive bred female gerenuk calved on August 14 2013 but had dystocia and required assistance. The animal was treated with antibiotics but became increasingly lethargic with leukopenia left shift and marked toxicity. The animal was found dead on August 16 2013. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition an odd odor coming from the patient brittle ribs that broke easily diffuse fibrin tags on the abdominal cavity a possible abomasal ulcer ten Trichuris in the cecum and an unremarkable reproductive system with no evidence of retained placenta. The liver was very firm and appeared rounded.

TOXOPLASMOSIS CILIATE GASTRITIS MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA PYLORIC ADENOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 14-year-old female wallaroo presented with labored breathing and died while being restrained for medications and blood collection. Necropsy revealed dark red lungs apparent cardiomegaly some white streaking in the ventricular epicardium hemorrhage on the descending aorta and multiple foci of white discoloration on the serosal surface of the liver and spleen.

SALMONELLOSIS VACCINE REACTION. This 6-year-old male captive bred lorikeet died spontaneously. It is one of six birds in the flock that have died suddenly in the past five days. The bird was admitted with lethargy and dyspnea and improved slightly throughout the day and ate well but died overnight. Necropsy revealed good body condition with areas of hemorrhage on the external surface of the skull. The liver was huge with rounded margins and yellow mottling. The spleen was enlarged and friable. Hemorrhage was noted in both lungs.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS VERTEBRAL SPONDYLOSIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SUPPURATIVE BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 22-year-old female tree kangaroo had a chronic history of mycobacteriosis and has been on long-term therapy (12 years). The animal was humanely euthanized due to geriatric condition and difficulty in locomotion. At necropsy muscle wasting was noted over the hind limbs. Erosion of articular cartilage was noted in the stifles. Roughening of the coxofemoral joints was also present. Bony proliferations were present along the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae. The intervertebral disk at L2-3 protruded into the spinal canal with compression of the adjacent cord. The left lung was contracted and covered by a thick capsule of fibrous tissue. Adhesions were present between the visceral and parietal pleura. Pulmonary parenchyma was gray to brown with cavitations containing yellow mucoid material.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY AND NEPHROPATHY. This 6-year/5-month-old male axolotl was humanely euthanized. It had a history of poor body condition and weakness. Its appetite was sporadic. The animal had a history of problems. At necropsy the axolotl was in thin body condition. The spleen was large and elongated. The liver appeared slightly gray/black. There were rocks in the stomach.

BACTERIAL OSTEOMYELITIS EROSIVE GASTRITIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 18-year-old female rattlesnake had a history of progressive spondylitis and cultured positive for Salmonella arizonae. The snake had severe weight loss in past several months with loss of mobility and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cachexia with severe spondylitis and several dark old slugs in follicles in the reproductive tract.

GRANULOMATOUS SYNOVITIS (GOUT-LIKE) DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS. This 3-year-old male Virginia opossum was found dead. This animal had a history of proliferative lesions involving the left front paw primarily granulation tissue and granulomatous inflammation with some foreign material (G11-6319 G11-1892). The opossum had become progressively thinner over the past year although was eating well. The opossum also had some mild spinal ataxia of the hind limbs in recent months. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a small amount of coagulated blood in the left nostril left side of the mouth and left ear canal 100 ml. of dark yellow clear fluid in the thoracic cavity multiple similarly-sized yellow firm raised nodules on the medial surface of both lungs and diffuse transmural circular areas of yellow discoloration on the dorsal surfaces. The pharynx contained large white worms 2.5 in. in length. These were also in the esophagus and in the proximal trachea. Numerous large worms were also present in the stomach. The mucosa of the stomach was hyperemic. The urinary bladder had proliferative mucosal lesions resembling papillomas. The liver was firm dark and mottled.

VISCERAL GOUT. This 24-year-old female dwarf caiman was either euthanized or died spontaneously. At necropsy skeletal muscle and kidneys were pale. Deposits were noted throughout the coelomic cavity. The liver was brown with white deposits and the spleen was tan.

EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA CONJUNCTIVITIS. This 5-year-old male chicken had apparent difficulty in swallowing. A large mass was identified in the oropharynx. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the oropharynx contained a fibrous mass approximately 1 cm. in diameter arising from the right dorsal pharynx and obliterating the choana. On section the mass was pale and firm.

PNEUMONIA GASTRITIS. This 9-year-old male rattlesnake was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy kidneys were pale. The lung was dark and hemorrhage was noted in the air sac. Hemorrhagic material was present in the stomach.

BACTERIAL TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS ASCITES MELANOMA CHOLELITHIASIS. This 8-year-old female toad presented with bloat and was spending an unusual amount of time at the surface of the tank. The toad subsequently died and necropsy revealed moderate ascites a 5 mm. raised soft tissue nodule on the right dorsal forelimb consolidated lungs that sank in formalin rounded hepatic margins a lobe-like appendage to the gallbladder with firm bile-stained material in the center three rocks in the pyloric region of the stomach a thin-walled dilated sac distal to the stomach containing luminal brown fluid empty urinary bladder mild follicular development and a cone-shaped structure in the oviduct. Adipose stores were atrophic.

RENAL GOUT COELOMITIS BACTEREMIA SHOCK. This 1-year-old female teal was found in the nest box. At necropsy white gouty deposits were present on the serosa of most thoracic and coelomic organs. Purulent exudate was noted in the right caudal coelomic cavity. Urates were present within renal tubules.

ENCEPHALITIS WITH NEURONAL INCLUSIONS HELICOBACTER GASTRITIS. This 9-year-old female fennec fox had an acute onset of ptyalism “gum chewing” behavior depression and tongue ulceration. Blood work revealed elevated serum ALP hypoproteinemia hypoalbuminemia and mild anemia. The animal recently had delivered one pup which it cannibalized on 3/22. The animal was vaccinated with routine canine vaccines and a killed rabies vaccine on 3/31. It was treated with supportive care following onset of clinical signs and partially responded. It was found dead on 4/17. The animal was housed with a male fox and there is some concern for contagious disease. Necropsy revealed hepatosplenomegaly aspirated food material in the airways and dark brown digesta in the small intestine. A mucopurulent discharge was detected in the left eye and ventral alopecia with seborrhea was detected.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK RHABDOMYOLYSIS POSSIBLE HYPERTHERMIA. This 2-year-old male capybara had been in a fight several days earlier and had an open wound in the cranial left elbow that is being treated with oral antibiotics. The animal developed acute diarrhea the treatment protocol was changed and the animal did not respond. The animal’s condition deteriorated and it was anesthetized again for treatment and diagnostic work but was unable to stand after recovering and died overnight. Necropsy revealed congestion and atelectasis in a dependent lung frothy fluid in the trachea reddened liver hemorrhage in the caudal half of the spleen pulpy kidneys inflamed caecal wall with associated hemorrhage and blood liquid contents similar findings in the large intestine and inflamed mesentery.

HEMOPERICARDIUM CARDIAC TAMPONADE. This approximately 7-year-old male wallaroo died. It had short-term lethargy and recent history of moving into a new exhibit. At necropsy there was severe cardiac involvement (necrosis? infarcts?). The pericardial sac was thickened. There were nodules in the liver.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS SHOCK STRESS. This 5-year/3-month-old female gazelle was found dead in its enclosure. It was pregnant and the unborn calf was delivered by C-section. The male calf was nearly term and alive but obtunded and could not be revived. The dam had been very weak for approximately a week. She was showing evidence of renal failure and had been recumbent for three days. At necropsy there were scrapes present on both carpi and elbows. The left lung was approximately 90% collapsed. There was approximately 20 ml. of clear yellow fluid within the thoracic cavity. The right cranial lung lobe was collapsed. The ruminal papillae were blunted and there was a gray discoloration to the mucosa. There was homogeneous reddish-purple discoloration of the mucosa and serosa of the omasum and abomasum. There was similar discoloration of the mucosa and serosa of the small and large intestine.

PULMONARY ABSCESS WITH HEMORRHAGE RUMINAL PARAKERATOSIS. This 3-year-old female gazelle was being treated for a thoracic mass of six months duration presumed to be an abscess. The animal developed a one day history of epistaxis with respiratory distress and died. This animal had a four month-old male calf. Necropsy of the dam revealed a chronic pulmonary abscess that eroded through the pulmonary artery and was associated with hemorrhage into the pericardium and thoracic cavity.

TRAUMA GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 3.5-year-old female motmot was found on the bottom of the enclosure being attacked by a Pionus parrot. Injury was noted to the upper beak. Nasal turbinates were exposed and nares were no longer patent. Supportive care was administered but the animal continued to decline and did not fully recover from anesthesia five days into the treatment protocol. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed white material in the cranial air sacs pale right ventricle white crystalline material on the surfaces of the great vessels multiple white lesions throughout the hepatic lobes pale small kidneys and no other abnormalities.

DEGENERATIVE CERVICAL ARTHRITIS ASPERGILLOSIS AMYLOIDOSIS GOITER EUTHANASIA. This 10.5-year-old female penguin has a few month history of bilateral limb paresis evidence of discospondylosis of thoracic vertebrae lethargy regurgitation and kyphosis (the latter since birth). Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a slight right dorsal lateral valgus deformity in the thoraco-synsacrum region. No spinal cord compression was noted. Mycotic granulomas associated with the cranial air sacs and tracheal bifurcation were noted. The liver was slightly enlarged with rounded edges and the spleen was moderately enlarged.

BACTERIAL ENDOMETRITIS UROCYSTITIS AND PERITONITIS. This 4-year-old female sugar glider was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed an enlarged abdomen with several firm swellings. Purulent material was expressed from the vaginal tract when the abdomen was palpated. The urinary bladder was filled with urine and angled to the left due to adhesions and purulent masses. Urine was clear and yellow. Multiple adhesions and abscesses were present throughout the abdominal cavity and abdominal organs.

MALIGNANT ROUND CELL TUMOR PROBABLE LYMPHOMA MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male fruit bat has a mass extending from the region of the left mandible ventrally across the midline with an ulcerated ventral aspect the size of a quarter oozing serous fluid. At surgery the mass was determined to be unresectable and the animal was humanely euthanized. On cut surface the mass was not firm and had no visible blood vessels.

Adenocarcinoma; pancreatic origin (suspected) Comment: The gross alterations within this hen were morphologically suggestive of adenocarcinoma. The most likely source of the adenocarcinoma in this case; based upon presentation; would be pancreas. Additional testing is being performed and a final report will be generated when that testing is completed. If you have any questions or concerns; feel free to contact me at 517-353-3701. Microscopic examination of specimens taken at necropsy revealed the presence of pancreatic acinar cell adenocarcinoma. The adenocarcinoma expanded and replaced the normal pancreatic stroma and was found in nests and islets on the serosa of the intestines. The adenocarcinoma was characterized by cuboidal cells arranged in acini and supported by an abundant and well developed fibrovascular stroma. Some acini contained small amounts of eosinophilic hyaline material. Pancreatic acinar cell adenocarcinoma Comment: The gross and microscopic alterations within this chicken were morphologically consistent with pancreatic acinar cell adenocarcinoma. This report concludes our formal communication about this submission. If you have additional questions or concerns; feel free to contact me at 517-353-3701.

GUNSHOT TRAUMA AORTIC DEGENERATION HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 13-year-old male western lowland gorilla was shot and killed by police when it escaped from its exhibit. Necropsy revealed very good physical condition with heavy muscling over the entire body and small adipose tissue stores. Multiple wounds and abrasions were present on the body particularly in the right chest and right facial region. Entry wounds of bullets were in the right facial region mid cervical region and thoracic inlet. No exit wounds were noted. Radiographs revealed multiple metal densities throughout the thoracic cavity extending into the cranial left abdomen. Coagulated blood was in the right hemithorax. The left hemithorax was filled with food and partially herniated stomach. The right lung lobes were partially macerated. The right atrium of the heart was lacerated and food and granular blood clots were present in the right and left ventricles. The stomach had herniated through the diaphragm of the left hemithorax through what appeared to be a traumatic tear in the diaphragm. A small perforation of the large bowel associated with a small metal fragment was noted.

EUTHANASIA GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS ENTERITIS INANITION. This 9-year-old male ratsnake was thin and inappetent. The animal has a recent history of regurgitation and previous exposure to Cryptosporidium sp. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the body was emaciated with no fat stores. The stomach was thickened.
PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE TRAUMA SHOCK. This 12-year-old male duck was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy there was marked pulmonary hemorrhage.

LINEAR FOREIGN BODY POSTOPERATIVE DEATH PULMONARY ABSCESS. This 8-year-old male tree kangaroo had a two-day history of lethargy inappetence and abdominal discomfort and had a history of bloating and intussusception earlier in the year that was treated surgically. Follow-up exploratory surgery identified a string foreign body in the stomach and duodenum dark red/purple discoloration of the duodenum and areas of near perforation along the mesenteric border that required resection and anastomosis. The animal had a slow incomplete recovery from anesthesia and was found dead later in the day. Necropsy identified a 1 cm. nodule in the right caudal pulmonary lobe. The nodule had a capsule and thick white contents. A 1 cm. focus of pleural adhesion to the body wall was noted. Fluid ingesta were in the stomach. The margins of the resection site were dark red although the surgical sites were intact. Mesenteric lymph nodes were dark red.

SMALL CELL LYMPHOMA RIGHT ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 6-year-old male ferret has a three year history of enlarged abdominal lymph nodes and a three month history of peripheral lymphadenopathy. Small cell lymphoma was diagnosed in lymph node biopsies in 2011. Islet cell carcinoma and adenoma are also diagnoses (G11-4331). The ferret improved following exploratory surgery and was maintained on a low dose of prednisolone. In January 2013 the animal was observed defecating in abnormal places and had grainy feces. The animal was treated with azathioprine that resulted in a dramatic drop in platelet count necessitating a 25% decrease in the dose. One week later the animal presented in shock nonresponsive and died despite supportive care. Necropsy revealed severe generalized lymphadenopathy involving the mediastinal mesenteric and peripheral lymph nodes.

EUTHANASIA CEREBRAL EDEMA HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 15-year-old female sheep had a history of chronic arthritis. The animal was found acutely down in a rocky area showing neurological symptoms. The animal was humanely euthanized. Marked fluid accumulation was noted beneath the meninges.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS SHOCK. This 11-year-old female wallaroo had a history of ataxia and coccidiosis. Treatment was initiated with trimethoprim sulfa resulting in mild improvement. Complete recovery never occurred and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the cecum contained a large quantity of shavings. No other gross lesions were identified.

INANITION TRAUMATIC TARSAL DERMATITIS STRESS. This 2-year/8-month-old female pigeon was found dead in its enclosure. It was kept in a flock with 20 members. It was actively performing up to the time of death. White plaques were seen in the throat in April. At necropsy there was minimal fat reserves. There was an oral plaque on the hard palate. There was left tarsal joint inflammation. The crop was mildly distended and full of food.

THYMOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female goat was found recumbent and could not get up. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large multilobulated mass in the cranial thorax filled with thick yellow/tan purulent material and several adhesions and multiple nodules in the larger mass. The heart was dark and streaked with fat. Much fat was present elsewhere. One portion of the lung appeared consolidated.

GOUT POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS (CARPROFEN) BUMBLEFOOT ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) PULMONARY SHOCK POSSIBLE TRAUMA. This 26-year-old female has a history of degenerative joint disease involving the left stifle was doing well on nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs although the lameness eventually progressed. The animal regurgitated when a new anti-inflammatory drug was added to the protocol and was found dead two days later. Necropsy revealed partial flipper amputations (previously done) some fresh ulcerated lesions on the tip of the left flipper a chronic scabbed callus on the right foot absence of adipose tissue some pigmentation in both lungs and somewhat rubbery and dark right lung moderate urate accumulation around the heart under the pericardium which was thickened and coelomic mesentery was thickened and dark with some adhesions. The hepatic capsule was thick. The esophagus and stomach were empty. Some liquid ingesta were in the intestines. The ovary was inactive. Both kidneys had pallor and urate stasis.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS VERTEBRAL FRACTURE STRESS PHTHISIS BULBI GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 17-year-old python had been examined two weeks earlier due to perching problems and decreased appetite. Radiographs revealed multiple foci of proliferative osteopathy especially in the cervical region and blood work revealed elevated white blood cell count. The snake subsequently died and necropsy revealed a vertebral fracture 21 cm. from the nose. The fracture was displaced and the spinal cord was severed. A second fracture was also noted distally to this fracture but was nondisplaced and the spinal cord was intact at this location.

PNEUMONIA PRENATAL DEATH (TERM FETUS). This 3.5-year-old bat was found dead. Necropsy revealed a distended abdomen female reproductive tract near term or full term fetus within the uterus heavy lungs melena in the gastrointestinal tract and congestion along the calvarium.

MANDIBULAR OSTEOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female/spayed had a one week history of lethargy and a three day history of inappetence and generalized weakness. The animal was immobilized and a mandibular mass with miliary pulmonary pattern was identified. The wolf’s condition deteriorated and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed excellent carcass condition some atrophy in the hindquarters and an 8 cm. raised soft to firm mass in the right rostral ventral mandible that was mottled white and red on cut surface and associated with bone lysis. A 10 cm. smooth irregular mass was present in the thorax between the right caudal and accessory pulmonary lobes and on cut surface it was mottled red white and yellow and had bone consistency in other areas. The mitral valve was subjectively thickened. Miliary calculi were present throughout the pulmonary lobes.

OSTEOARTHRITIS CELLULITIS INANITION INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 6-year/8-month-old female frog died. It was found with its right rear leg swollen approximately two weeks ago. Surgical exploration of the leg was performed. It was not eating since surgery and had lost significant weight. At necropsy the frog was thin. The right rear leg had two surgical incisions. The proximal 2 mm. incision had some increased vasculature but minimal gross inflammation or healing. The large incision along the tibia had five sutures in place. The sutures were in good condition and there was no swelling around them. There was moderate inflammation and healing reaction around the sutures. The surrounding musculature appeared healthy. The stifle joint was completely luxated. Underneath the joint capsule there was purulent exudate and no attachments between the femur and tibia. The distal femur and proximal tibia appeared yellow with very roughened lytic edges and no obvious vasculature. There was a callus present within the mid diaphysis of the tibia. The purulent exudate from the joint capsule extended one-third of the way down the tibia and at least half the way up the femur between muscles planes close to the bone. The lungs appeared hyperinflated and diffusely reddened. The heart muscle appeared diffusely pale. The stomach was enlarged and contained completely undigested cricket pieces.

BACTERIAL PYOMETRITIS CERVICAL TRAUMA. This 1-year-old female sheep was found dead in the barn. Radiographs revealed cervical trauma. The animal had had a recent C-section. Necropsy revealed depleted body fat possible cataract in the left eye and trauma to the right eye and a mild amount of serosanguineous pericardial fluid. Mild petechiae were noted on the surface of the cerebrum and instability was noted at the atlantoaxial joint with protrusion of soft tissues through the dorsal space.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DIESASE PROCESS. This greater than 3-year-old male lory was found fluffed in the morning and was subsequently killed by conspecifics. Necropsy revealed conspecific external trauma including absence of feathers on the head no left eye absence of half of the tongue and absence of some of the muscle on the left wing. The right wing had a hemorrhagic area on the dorsum. Lungs were hemorrhagic. Kidneys appear congested.
EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC HEPATITIS. This 11-year-old male sugar glider had a history of weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized.
adult. Weight: 372 g.  Emaciated; hypothermia (presumed). Hypothermia; emaciation.
INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS. This 20-year-old male rat had a history of progressive weight loss. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was tan to yellow.

INANITION MYCOTIC DERMATITIS OSTEOMYELITIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 7-year-old female snake had a history of dermatitis and was under treatment. The animal was inappetent and was tube fed. The animal was found dead. At necropsy scant adipose tissue depots were present.

SHOCK UTERINE STROMAL PROLIFERATION WITH EROSION AND ADENOMYOSIS. This greater than 5-year-old was found dead clinging to the door of the exhibit. No previous medical problems were noted. Necropsy revealed no evidence of injuries other than some abrasions on the rostral mandible and nasal planum. The uterus was very large and firm and on cut surface the uterine wall was thickened and luminal contents were hemorrhagic and polypoid. Digital photographs of the uterus were obtained and submitted. Kidneys appeared enlarged and gray.

HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS WITH MELANOMACROPHAGE HYPERPLASIA. This 8-year-old frog was found dead with no previous abnormalities noted. Gross necropsy revealed a single 2 x 1.5 cm. urinary calculus within the bladder. No other abnormalities were found.

VISCERAL GOUT. This 8-year-old male monitor was found dead. It was noted to be bloated the morning before death. It was found dead the same morning. Postmortem radiographs showed reduced coelomic detail. At necropsy the monitor was in good nutritional condition. It appeared to have been dehydrated prior to death. There were bilateral white discolorations of the lower eyelids. There was a moderate subacute rostral abrasion. There was approximately 5 ml. of straw colored coelomic fluid. The coelomic cavity membrane was thickened with multifocal white plaques. The lungs were diffusely hemorrhagic and edematous. The pericardial sac was diffusely thickened and fibrotic. It was covered with white friable diphtheric membrane. The tongue had multifocal pinpoint white lesions on the ventral surface. The liver was pale and irregularly discolored. The kidneys were bilaterally swollen and enlarged.
EUTHANASIA VERTEBRAL SPONDYLOSIS OSTEOMYELITIS INANITION. This 4.5-year-old male snake was euthanized due to chronic spinal disease. At necropsy multiple areas of spinal fusion were identified.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS ORAL AND ESOPHAGEAL CANDIDIASIS. This 34-year-old female western lowland gorilla was anesthetized for emergency examination and was found to have substantial abdominal peritonitis with several suppurative tracts. The animal never recovered fully from anesthesia and was found dead. At necropsy there was abundant abdominal effusion and petechial hemorrhages noted on multiple serosal organs. Additionally the intestines were adhered to the abdominal wall.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS. This 16-year-old wood duck was found dead in the aviary with no prior signs of illness. This bird had previously been exposed to a bird diagnosed with mycobacteriosis. Necropsy revealed numerous nodular white lesions throughout the viscera and air sacs some food in the gastrointestinal tract and pale brown kidneys.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA RETROVIRUS. This 5-year-old female koala has a history of testing positive for retrovirus has been treated with antiretroviral drugs for four weeks had a very high viral load throughout treatment and profound lymphocytosis was noted (252000) with associated anemia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with pale mucous membranes and no other abnormalities.

YOLK EMBOLISM HYPERPROTEINEMIA. This 21.5-year-old male Dumeril’s ground boa was found dead at mid-day rounds. It had passed normal feces overnight. Necropsy revealed obesity wood shavings in the mouth a palpable mass in the area of the stomach a large volume of free blood in the coelomic cavity firm esophagus and stomach a 19 cm. mass associated with the left testis that is encapsulated multilobulated and composed of firm white solid tissue with a large amount of free blood within.

HEPATIC CARCINOMA CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 31-year-old female chimpanzee was found dead. It had a two week history of progressive cough and dyspnea that was unresponsive to antibiotics and expectorants. At necropsy the liver was enlarged and contained numerous firm nodules ranging in size from a few millimeters to several centimeters. The right side of the thorax contained several liters of straw colored fluid. This caused the diaphragm to bulge when viewed from the abdominal cavity. The lung was completely collapsed and the tissue appeared dark and necrotic. The pleural surface of the ribcage was covered by a thick adherent layer of yellow tissue (fibrin?). The pericardium was thickened.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This 40-year-old female hyacinth macaw has a history of acute hind limb paresis/paralysis with lethargy and weakness and radiographic evidence of renal enlargement. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition cataract in both eyes chalky material on the serosal surface of the viscera markedly enlarged pale tan kidneys and gritty texture to the kidneys on cut surface.

SUSPECT BAYLISASCARIASIS SUSPECT ENCEPHALITOZOONOSIS SUSPECT SPINAL CORD TRAUMA. This 4-year-old female rabbit had a five month history of hind limb ataxia progressing to recumbency and inability to properly void feces from the perianal region. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This rabbit lived in an exhibit where wallabies and an emu died due to baylisascariasis.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 1-year-old female saki monkey was found on the cage floor with evidence of vomiting nystagmus and rhythmic eyelid movements. Supportive care was administered but the monkey died overnight. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the right ventral brain shell on the floor of the cranium.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS PROBABLE SALMONELLOSIS. This approximately 10-year-old female copperhead had no prior medical history was normal in the morning and was found dead in the afternoon. Necropsy revealed moderate blood tinged pericardial effusion and severe discoloration and patchy appearance to the liver. Other organs appeared normal.

1) Liver: focal hematoma or infarcted gall bladder. 2) Lung: diffuse pulmonary congestion and edema Comments: The liver lesion appears most likely to be a resolving hematoma; although I cannot rule out an infarcted/necrotic gall bladder; perhaps you remember if the gall bladder was present/intact at necropsy or not? Certainly; if this is an infarcted gall bladder; it could have caused the inappetance reported; while a hematoma indicates trauma and is less likely the cause of this otters clinical signs. No microscopic evidence of infectious or inflammatory disease; including Canine Distemper or Toxoplasmosis; was found in any of the tissues examined.
