Comment: While no evidence of Toxoplasma gondii cysts or associated inflammation was found microscopically; the titers indicate exposure to this organism. This completes the outstanding testing on this case.\_
ULCERATIVE GLOSSITIS SHOCK. This 11-month-old tern was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

SCHISTOSOMIASIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE THYROID HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female raccoon had a history of increased respiratory effort of one day’s duration with worsening condition inappetence recent increase in water intake and signs of early renal insufficiency. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA. This 13-year neutered female tiger was humanely euthanized. It had a history of vomiting green liquid and anorexia. Exploratory surgery revealed a spleen containing suspicious tumors. Splenectomy was done. The liver was also full of tumors. Bile had been vomited during induction. The uterus had been removed two years ago due to pyometra and adenocarcinoma. The tiger did well until recently when it developed vomiting of bile anorexia and lethargy. At necropsy the stomach was full of a large amount of green liquid and white mucus. There was one small ulcer. The liver was covered with small white raised irregular nodules that were encapsulated on cut surface. There was a small mass in the mammary tissue.

DIC DISSEMINATED FIBRINOUS INFLAMMATION AND NECROSIS ASPIRATION. This 14-month-old female lemur presented for lethargy inappetence and facial swelling. Examination revealed that the animal was febrile with harsh pulmonary sounds edema along the ventral mandible and a live Cuterebra was extracted from the left clavicular region. Blood work and radiographs were unremarkable. The animal received supportive care but its condition declined despite treatment and it was found dead within 72 hours of treatment. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a 1 cm. wound over the left clavicle (previous Cuterebra site). Edema was present along the ventral mandible. A large amount of clear foamy fluid was noted within the trachea and primary bronchi. The lungs were mottled with patchy areas of congestion and hemorrhage. A large firm clump of fruit was in the esophagus proximal to the heart and the outer surface of the esophagus in this region was dark red to purple. The stomach and intestinal tract had normal ingesta and formed stool was within the colon. The duodenum and proximal jejunal mucosa were diffusely reddened. The liver was pale and congested. Both kidneys were pale.

UTERINE ADENOSARCOMA. This 4-year-old female African hedgehog had acute weight loss and incoordination. It is not stated if the animal was euthanized or died spontaneously. At necropsy there was a mass associated with the uterus that had a friable center.

AMYLOIDOSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EMACIATION. This 7-year-old male pygmy marmoset had been lethargic in the morning somewhat inappetent and died after arriving at the clinic for examination. Necropsy revealed an enlarged liver and possibly enlarged heart.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA INANITION. This 25-year-old male rock python was found dead. Necropsy revealed severe muscle wasting and atrophy of the fat bodies. The oral cavity had evidence of stomatitis. Marked amounts of yellow fluid were present in the caudal coelomic cavity.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL DERMATITIS OSTEOMYELITIS RHINITIS CHRONIC OOPHORITIS. This 9-year-old female Gila monster had marked muscle atrophy and weight loss following hibernation. Discharge was also noted in the oral cavity with difficulty breathing. Ascites was present in the coelomic cavity. Numerous bacteria were present in the coelomic fluid. The animal was treated with antibiotics and supportive care. The condition gradually improved; however ulceration of the right eye and mycotic ophthalmitis developed. The animal was eventually euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy a large area of skin maxilla and right eye were necrotic and sloughing. Green cystic masses were present in the liver.

SCROTAL MELANOMA EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old male lemur was diagnosed in July with a scrotal melanoma. The animal was treated with surgery and a melanoma vaccine but when the tumor recurred for a third time the animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. No foci of metastasis were seen.

PULMONARY ABSCESSES RUMINORETICULITIS AND ENTERITIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS NEPHROLITHIASIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 14-year-old male sheep was geriatric and had arthritis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed consolidated left lung with firm hard nodules. Stones were noted in the kidney.

ENDOCARDIOSIS GOUT INTESTINAL MUCOSAL AND HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA/ATYPIA. This approximately 4-year-old blue spiny lizard developed a sudden onset of lethargy unwillingness to move and dehydration. Examination revealed stomatitis and supportive care was administered. Radiodense material was noted in the dilated lower bowel. Radiographs also revealed spondylosis in the spine suggesting advanced age. Partial paresis of the limbs was noted although the lizard could ambulate short distances. No significant improvement was noted and the animal was euthanized due to poor prognosis and for diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed sand particular material and food in a dilated portion of the colon to 4 cm. in length. A waxworm head was noted in the colon and may have been the radiodense material. The bowel was constricted tightly anterior to the dilatation but not associated with discoloration or other lesions and the bowel was not occluded. The stomach was full had three worms present and some formulated food. The liver was small and a scar was present on the ventral cranial end. The gallbladder was filled with light green bile. A significant amount of clear fluid was present in the coelomic cavity particularly pooled around the lungs.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This 10-year-old neutered male addax died. It had a recent history of swollen scrotal sac and had been separated from the herd due to severe wounds suffered during fights in spring 2001 that required extensive surgical interventions. On 10/17 the addax was immobilized for elective castration and scrotal sac resection. It had respiratory arrest and atrial fibrillation upon induction. It was stabilized and surgery proceeded uneventfully. The animal was hypothermic during the procedure. At necropsy the addax had thin body condition and a rough haircoat. The surgical sites appeared intact. There were multifocal petechiae and ecchymoses along the ventral surface of the lumbar musculature. Overall the muscles appeared dark. There was regurgitated feed in the nose and mouth. The right ventricular wall appeared slightly thin and the left ventricular wall appeared slightly thickened. The pericardial sac was thickened and firmly adhered to the heart. The surface of the heart appeared very dark with multiple areas of ecchymoses. There was approximately 1-2 liters of straw colored pleural effusion in the thoracic cavity. There were petechiae and ecchymoses along the visceral surface of ribs. The lungs appeared frothy with bilateral areas of cranial atelectasis. There was a large amount of digesta in the trachea. Both kidneys appeared smaller than expected and were moderately cobbled in appearance on the surface. The renal capsules were firmly attached. Both adrenals were enlarged and hyperemic.

CHOLECYSTITIS CHOLANGITIS ENTERITIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 9-year-old female lemur had a prior history of diabetes. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the bile duct appeared abnormal. Kidneys were enlarged and pale. Urine was orange.

LYMPHOMA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male gazelle was found in sternal recumbency in an outdoor exhibit and was unwilling to stand. The animal was eventually coaxed to a small corral and euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal had a lengthy history of lameness. Necropsy revealed poor haircoat a laceration over the rostral mandibular gingiva a 9 cm. mass in the region of the prescapular lymph node cartilaginous erosions and osteophytes in the scapulohumeral and coxofemoral joints generalized lymphadenopathy an infiltrate in the right lung a caseous abscess in the thoracic cavity internal to the manubrium enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes multiple foci of thickened small intestine a mixed bezoar in the rumen worn rostral incisors black flecks on the internal surface of the urinary bladder and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA. This captive bred 6-year-old female marmoset was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic weight loss. It preferred to lie on its back. It had a history of radiographic idiopathic osteolytic disease. There were no other abnormalities noted at necropsy.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 27-year-old female thick-billed parrot was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed absence of feathers over the keel intact skin both legs missing no visible fat stores and some mild streaking of the liver.

PRENATAL DEATH (DAM EUTHANIZED FOR TRAUMA). This 10.5-year-old female gazelle became acutely lame in its left rear limb and examination revealed dislocation of the left stifle with destruction of both cruciates. Surgical repair was performed but the animal was found recumbent the next morning with a fractured left tibia and destruction of the stifle repair. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed marked swelling and bruising at the surgical site swelling of the limb distal to the incision site crepitus in the joint marked bilateral pulmonary congestion and adhesion of the right lung to the thoracic wall in two different locations much adipose tissue in the mediastinum ecchymoses in the mediastinum and the liver was congested. Ruminal villi seemed less dense than expected congested duodenum and surrounding soft tissues congested pancreas slight thyroid asymmetry with the left larger than the right reddish-orange urine mildly congested urinary bladder mucosa enlarged uterine horns with the right larger than the left and a small fetus with associated placenta in the right horn. Marked bruising and swelling of the musculature was present near the left stifle.
ENTERIC TREMATODIASIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION. This 14-year-old female blue-tongued skink was found dead. Necropsy was unremarkable.

SHOCK MYOSITIS. This 10.5-year-old male wallaby had a swollen jaw and rapidly developing edema. The animal died during the physical exam. Necropsy revealed marked pneumonia cardiomegaly abscessation of a tooth root and a large quantity of necrotic tissue within the subcutis and muscle of the head and forelimbs.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS EMACIATION ABSCESS. This 9.5-year-old male giant eland was examined for a 30 cm. raised subcutaneous mass on the ventral midline cranial to the prepuce. The patient regurgitated and aspirated ruminal contents prior to tracheal intubation. The mass was diagnosed as an abscess lanced and drained and the patient was treated with antibiotics and anti-inflammatory drugs. The patient made attempts to stand but did not succeed after anesthetic reversal remained sternal and was found deceased three hours after the anesthetic reversal. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with generalized loss of muscle mass no communication of the abscess to the prepuce or abdominal cavity mild bruising in the right rear leg and petechia distal to the hip generalized serous atrophy of fat 3 liters of serosanguineous peritoneal fluid and 1 liter of serosanguineous pleural fluid foam throughout the trachea regurgitated ruminal contents in the trachea from the glottis to the thoracic inlet extremely small amount of aspirated ruminal contents at the tracheal bifurcation a large ball of feed at the larynx grossly normal lungs endocardiosis on the right and left atrioventricular valves erythema on the serosal surfaces of the ventral rumen and blunting of the ruminal papillae most severe in the ventral rumen and associated with ruminal dilatation reddening of the spiral colon and mucoid bile in the bile ducts of the liver. Blood work obtained on the day of death was consistent with sepsis.

EUTHANASIA WHITE MATTER VACUOLIZATION (WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME PRESUMPTIVE) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHRONIC CHOLECYSTITIS. This 3-year-old female hedgehog had a history of weight loss and was euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy many tissues were tan to gold. Kidneys were yellow to tan and firm.

HYDROCEPHALUS EUTHANASIA EMACIATION. This 2-year-old desert tortoise of undetermined gender has always been smaller than its clutch mates and had developed a very soft cell with no improvement following husbandry changes and treatment. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition friable skin that easily separated from the carapace and plastron edematous lungs mild gas distention 10 ml. of clear coelomic fluid fecal material and small stones in the colon white granular material consistent with urates in the urinary bladder and extremely soft and pliable plastron and carapace.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS GASTRITIS. This 6-year-old male polecat had a history of a soft tissue swelling adjacent to the mandible. The presumptive diagnosis was lymphosarcoma. Treatment was initiated; however weight loss and condition rapidly declined and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. Miliary white foci were present throughout the lungs. Two small trichobezoars were present in the stomach. The right mandibular gastric and retroperitoneal lymph nodes were markedly enlarged.

TRAUMA STRESS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 39-year-old female flamingo was found dead in the afternoon with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy identified good body condition no external signs of trauma a large amount of food in the crop and no gross coelomic lesions.

EMC NECROTIZING MYOCARDITIS GRANULOMATOSIS ENTEROCOLITIS. This approximately 25-year-old female ring-tailed lemur has a history of suspected cardiac disease in a mammary mass. It was reported to develop acute lethargy with dilated pupils and died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed bilateral mammary masses hypertrophy of the thyroid glands hemorrhage in the duodenum hypertrophy of the left ventricle of the heart hepatomegaly a pedunculated mass in the right lobe of the pancreas and bilaterally small kidneys.

Gall bladder: Mild cystic mucosal hyperplasia Kidney: Mild membranous glomerulonephritis Lung: Mild multifocal atelectasis Lung: Multifocal ectopic ossification Lung: Moderate anthracosis Comment: The cause of death based on the gross findings; the history; and the histologic findings was most likely shock; exhaustion; and the metabolic derangements secondary to urinary bladder obstruction and post-renal azotemia due to urinary bladder prolapse. Liver congestion and a shrunken depleted spleen suggest shunting of blood away from vital organs with subsequent hypoxic damage (compatible with shock). Cortical hyperplasia in the adrenal gland is usually compatible with longterm environmental or metabolic stress.The urate crystals suggestive of gouty tophi are a ique finding; suggesting poor perfusion; dehydration; and simultaneous high uricemia; though other metabolic derangements cannot be ruled out due to the unusual nature of this lesion. It is unlikely that the Helicobacter sp. noted are clinically significant; they typically are not in most species; but there is some minimal to mild gastritis which might be a result of their presence. ANESTHETIC COMPLICATION OBESITY NEPHROSCLEROSIS TAIL TRAUMA. This 17.5-year-old male African lion had a history of self-mutilation of the tail necessitating vasectomy and surgical debridement of the tail. The animal had chewed off several inches of the tail. While anesthetized for tail amputation the cat developed a few brief episodes of apnea but then stabilized and was returned to its enclosure. The animal developed respiratory arrest and subsequently could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed overconditioning some firm small white nodules in the pulmonary parenchyma brittle bronchi some hemorrhage and hematomas on the inner surface of the distal trachea some small nodules in the heart valve leaflets dark red gastric mucosa with areas of petechiation and ulceration and no other remarkable findings.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY PULMONARY ADENOMA LOBAR CIRRHOSIS. This 4-year-old Virginia opossum had intermittent episodes of constipation that responded to enemas fluids and lactulose. It had a one-day history of dyspnea with pleural effusion and thoracocentesis yielded serosanguineous fluid and gas. Supportive care was administered but the animal died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed a pedunculated vascular mass attached to the mesentery that was 8 cm. in greatest dimension. Serosanguineous fluid was present throughout the thorax and yellow firm masses up to 1.5 cm. in greatest dimension are present throughout the lungs.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA DENTAL ABSCESSES AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION. This 6.5-year-old male gerenuk developed an acute episode of lateral recumbency with dull mentation following a cold night. Examination revealed depression severe dehydration and thin body condition. Blood work revealed moderate leukocytosis with marked azotemia hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia. Supportive care was administered but the patient did not respond and died. Necropsy revealed unilateral granulomatous pneumonia multiple bilateral tooth abscesses and a large amount of straw colored fluid in the peritoneal cavity.

METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA. This 7-year-old male black footed ferret had a history of anorexia and rear leg paresis and a palpable mass in the abdominal cavity. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed masses throughout the abdominal cavity.

EMACIATION GOUT. This 20-year-old male scarlet ibis has an approximately two week history of trauma to the eye and leg. Supportive care was administered but the bird’s appetite decreased but improved when the animal was moved to an area near the exhibit. Following this observation the animal then became inappetent with weight loss and died. Necropsy revealed a large amount of food throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

Spleen - Mild; multifocal extramedullary hematopoiesis Pancreas - Islet cell adenoma Lymph node - Sinus histiocytosis and erythrocytosis; with intrasinusoidal poorly differentiated cell colonization Comments The splenic tissue is histologically unremarkable. The pancreatic neoplasm is a benign neuroendocrine neoplasm arising from the islet of Langerhans. The designation of an adenoma in the ferret is made based on small size; and lack of perceived invasion. The majority of islet cell tumors in ferrets are beta cell tumors that can secrete insulin. Such neoplasms are most commonly diagnosed between 4 and 5 years of age; though they are often seen as incidental findings during necropsy. Distant metastasis is rare. The findings in the lymph node are notable; but not specific. The population of cells within the sinusoids is poorly differentiated. Differential diagnoses include mast cells; lymphocytes; and epithelial cells. Further histochemical testing is in progress; the results of which will be released in an addendum report. David Needle; D

PERFORATING INTESTINAL ULCERS WITH ADHESIONS AND PERITONITIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female tamarin presented for ongoing diarrhea and lethargy of three weeks duration. The patient had maintained a good appetite and was receiving supportive care initially showing some improvement. Diagnostic tests identified substantial anemia hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia. Body condition was poor and the animal appeared cachectic. Exploratory surgery was performed for a suspected mass in the abdomen and the animal was euthanized during this procedure. Necropsy revealed a pale yellow liver with cyst-like features on the margins of the lobe firm enlarged and distended gallbladder with tortuous bile duct ingesta in the stomach a perforation with smooth margins at the duodenum with associated leakage of gut contents into the abdomen gas distended small intestine brown fragile ileocecocolic junction distended cecum adhered to the peritoneum a perforation at the level of the adhesion marked thickening of the cecum and fibrous texture on cut surface pale kidneys enlarged adrenal glands and mahogany colored round-like masses proximal to each kidney approximately 4-5 on each side. Several mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and firm.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA TESTICLE ROUND CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male budgerigar had a small mass noted on the right clavicle two years earlier. It otherwise has had an unremarkable recent history.

NECROBACILLOSIS FOOT; LEIOMYOMA RUMEN PAPILLOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female captive bred gazelle had a five day history of illness and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The right hind medial claw had been amputated nine years earlier due to necrobacillosis and associated osteomyelitis. The animal was subsequently vaccinated against Fusobacterium and Bacteroides. Two days prior to death the animal presented with lameness and swelling in both front limbs with increased lameness in the right hind limb accompanied by anorexia. The patient did not respond to antibiotic and anti-inflammatory drug therapy and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

PULMONARY AND CERVICAL ABSCESSATION CHRONIC ABOMASITIS EMACIATION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This female 7-year-old Speke’s gazelle was found dead four hours after an anesthetic procedure to treat a cervical abscess. At the time of treatment radiographic signs of pneumonia were noted. Bacteroides sp. and Fusobacterium sp. were isolated from the abscess. In addition to these organisms Actinomyces sp. was isolated from mucus on the endotracheal tube. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not fully awaken from anesthesia following reexamination and radiographs. This animal along with the other hoof stock in the exhibit have received supportive care for Haemonchus infections. Necropsy of the Speke’s gazelle identified multiple scars in the skin around the right shoulder and right thigh attributed to sedation and antibiotic delivery healed scars surrounding the left cervical region a well-demarcated abscess in the deep tissues to this area mucus in the trachea multiple well demarcated abscesses in the parenchyma of the caudal right pulmonary lobe normal ruminal and omasal contents rust-colored ingesta in the abomasum and no other abnormalities.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 8-year-old female tamarin is from a group that entered quarantine 55 hours earlier after traveling 50 hours by van from the East Coast. The animal from this report is the matriarch of the group and was currently nursing a five-week-old juvenile. Necropsy revealed adequate intra-abdominal fat monkey chow in the stomach gas-filled intestinal tract containing ingesta pale liver congested lungs and a small amount of serohemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity.

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATOCELLULAR HYPERPLASIA SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PERITONITIS. This 12-year-old male pig was euthanized due to chronic mandibular abscesses and osteomyelitis. At necropsy a draining tract was identified in the lower jaw. An abscess pocket was present in the left mandibular bone. The liver was enlarged with multiple tissue masses and cysts. Smaller masses were identified in the spleen.

ARTHRITIS THYROID TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This 18.5-year-old female Thomson’s gazelle had progressively become more and more arthritic in the hind limbs with enlarged and laterally rotated stifles. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed some muscle atrophy over the pelvic region adequate fat stores markedly enlarged stifles with limited range of motion some mild thickening of the hip joints osseous and cartilaginous replacement of the joint capsules in the stifles contracture of the digital flexures across the backs of the carpi slightly swollen seroma/hematoma over the right tuber ischium with associated cellulitis and fibrosis. Some regional lymph nodes are enlarged. Some congestion and enlargement of the left mandibular lymph node is noted. The left thyroid is markedly enlarged by a spherical red/gray soft mass and the right thyroid is firm irregularly cystic and mildly enlarged. The liver has several variably-sized white nodules in the parenchyma and some sludge is in the gallbladder. The left adrenal has a small pink nodule in the medulla. Variably-sized cysts are in the renal parenchyma and some yellow/white streaking is in the renal crest. The uterus has few white semi-firm nodules in the walls of each horn and some cystic dilatation of oviduct or other structures near the ovary and the cervix has some cyst-like nodularity of the mucosa. A few Haemonchus sp. are in the abomasum. A mild to moderate load of Trichuris sp. is in the cecum.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS PULMONARY ABSCESS MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE EMACIATION. This 4-year-old male hedgehog had a history of chronic steady weight loss of several months duration. It was treated for a high white blood cell count but continued to lose weight and was found dead. Necropsy revealed fair body condition with red irritated skin around the perineum and rectum. The right pulmonary lobe was consolidated and had caseous material throughout the entire lobe and did not float in formalin.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 15.5-year-old male monkey had a three-day history of lethargy. An abdominal effusion was identified on day #2 and an exploratory celiotomy revealed markedly reddened pancreas with reddened and friable spleen. Splenectomy was performed and recovery was uneventful but the animal arrested the following day. Necropsy revealed 30-40 ml. of pleural effusion generalized edema and a mottled liver.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 2-year-old female cottontop tamarin is from a group that entered quarantine after traveling 50 hours by van from the East Coast. Necropsy revealed a partially amputated tail adequate amount of intra-abdominal fat minimal gastric contents minimal ingesta or feces in the lower gastrointestinal tract congested lungs and a small amount of serohemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity.

TOXOPLASMOSIS SUSPECT VIRAL INFECTION. This approximately 1-year/8-month-old male kangaroo was found dead in holding pen. It had been under treatment for pneumonia and presumptive toxoplasmosis infection. It had a titer greater than 1600 for Toxoplasma gondii. The animal was in declining condition. At necropsy there were mild amounts of subcutaneous fat. There was some dried liquid fecal material present on the left hip/thigh region. The surface of the liver had tan foci 1-2 mm. in diameter extending into the parenchyma. The liver was red/brown. The mesenteric lymph node appeared enlarged and inflamed. The central portion of the lymph node was slightly softer in consistency and redder in color than normal. The lungs were bilaterally erythematous. The parenchyma was deep red to deep red/purple. The surface of both lungs had gray foci evenly distributed and extending 1-2 mm. into the parenchyma. The anterior aspect of the ventricular myocardium had an irregular shape poorly defined erythematous focus 1-2 cm. in diameter in it. Sections of heart lung liver spleen lymph node and brain were frozen for future use if needed.

MANAGEMENT EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 10-year-old copperhead was in contact with Cryptosporidium sp. positive animal and was humanely euthanized. No significant gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

CARDIAC FIBROSIS ULCERATIVE GLOSSITIS. This 5-year-old female pygmy marmoset presented for cyanosis and dyspnea. Pulmonary congestion and cardiomegaly were noted radiographically. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed a thick white pericardium and pale thick myocardium with severe uniform bilateral reddening of the pulmonary tissue. Pulmonary parenchyma was firm.
ENCEPHALITIS. This 8-month-old female tamarin presented with vestibular signs and nystagmus. At necropsy the tympanic bulla was discolored and thickening was noted over the meninges.

EMACIATION CECAL NEMATODIASIS (WHIPWORMS) CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 2-year-old gerenuk appeared thin and when examined was determined to have lost 25% of its body weight in the last three months. The animal was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed gray/green intestines and thin body condition.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SARCOMA (CERVIX) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 14-year-old ewe was euthanized due to lameness and anorexia. Erosion of articular cartilage and marked osteophyte proliferation was noted in the digital joints and carpi.

EUTHANASIA MYCOTIC DERMATITIS PULMONARY NEMATODIASIS INANITION. This 16-year-old boa was hospitalized for several weeks for weight loss and anorexia. The animal sustained skin lacerations from the cage while hospitalized and progressive necrosis of the skin occurred adjacent to the wounds. The animal was humanely euthanized due to poor response to therapy. At necropsy the proximal lung contained three small raised white lesions. Foci of necrosis were identified within the skin with underlying fluid filled pockets within the subcutis.

SEPSIS OOPHORITIS AND YOLK COELOMITIS. This 9-year-old female lizard was found dead on exhibit. There was a short history of illness of unknown origin. Necropsy revealed thin body condition with minimal fat stores pinpoint full-thickness lesions observed throughout the liver and one ectopic yolk body.

RENAL DISEASE MYOCARDIAL EDEMA. This 14-year-old female oryx died. It was immobilized four days prior to death. Examination and blood work at that time were normal. At necropsy there was a moderate amount of discoloration of all internal organs (probably postmortem). The kidneys were soft and puffy. The fat surrounding the kidneys had areas that were hard (calcified). The left ventricle may have had a thin wall.

BACTERIAL ENDOMETRITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 7-year-old golden lion tamarin became moribund two days after delivering one live and one dead neonate. The animal was hypothermic and although supportive care was administered the animal died approximately an hour after presentation. Necropsy revealed gray/brown lining of the uterine mucosa from which E. coli and Proteus were cultured.

RENAL CARCINOMA RENAL GOUT GASTRIC MINERALIZATION AORTIC MINERALIZATION INANITION. This 10-year-old male viper had a history of inability to defecate for the past few months. The animal was found dead. At necropsy white plaque-like lesions were present along the great vessels. The vessels were stiff. The GI tract from the small intestine to the colon is packed with fecal material. The kidney contained a large pale yellow lobular mass.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS SEPTICEMIA PULMONARY EDEMA AND HEMORRHAGE FATTY LIVER. This greater than 3-year-old female frilled lizard was found dead in its enclosure. It had a history of refusal of food water and was lethargic. At necropsy there was a preovulatory egg rupture with possible septicemia. The lungs were dark and congested. There was possible hepatitis. There was hemorrhage within the distal colonic mucosa. There were large abdominal fat pads.

BLOAT SEPSIS. This 14-year-old female squirrel money arrived in quarantine in mid-October. Quarantine examination revealed good health status but dental disease. The animal had some trauma to an ear in November which healed without issue. The animal was found unexpectedly dead on exhibit in the morning. Necropsy revealed some possible purulent material in the vulvar region. Some signs of trauma were noted. The abdomen appeared bloated and the stomach was noted to be bloated with gas and rotated 90°. No splenic entrapment or mesenteric congestion was noted. The right and left broad ligaments of the uterus had a firm white rounded mass associated with the tissues.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS GRANULOMATOUS MYOSITIS HEPATITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 10-year-old female duck had a history of severe lameness with mineralized material in the joint space. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy minimal coelomic fat was noted. Swelling was present adjacent to the tibiotarsus. Marked pododermatitis was present on the feet.

EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 14-year-old female sea lion had been anesthetized for transfer and recovery was uneventful. The animal was found dead a few hours thereafter. Necropsy revealed warm tissues a dead fetus some thin white streaks in the heart absence of clotted blood and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL STOMATITIS OOPHORITIS AND COELOMITIS. This 1-year-old female tentacled snake was observed swimming erratically with its mouth open at the bottom of the aquarium. The snake was listless and unresponsive when examined was intubated and manually ventilated but fluid was noted in the trachea during manual ventilation the animal did not respond and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition diffuse edema in the lungs congestion of the adrenal gland a large amount of yellow colored fluid in the right ovary much thickened material in the left ovary and mild serosal congestion involving the distal aspects. Adipose stores appeared adequate. A curled nematode was noted on the serosal surface of the stomach.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS EOSINOPHILIC ENTEROCOLITIS ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This approximately 36-year-old female mandrill had a history of severe spondylosis arthritis hyporexia and weight loss. The animal was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the animal had decreased body condition dry skin an abdominal hernia kyphosis fused sternal and vertebral segments fused metatarsal/phalangeal joints adhesions between the accessory and hepatic lobe of the gastric wall enlargement of adrenal glands brownish mucoid discharge from the uterus cystic lesions in the kidneys and small cysts in the left ovary.
EUTHANASIA SPINAL TRAUMA. This 2-year-old male prairie dog sustained a spinal injury from climbing and falling. Due to the poor prognosis the animal was humanely euthanized.

TRAUMA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 11-year-old male straw-colored fruit bat was found dead on the ground near the exhibit wall mesh in the morning. Necropsy revealed some clear fluid in the pericardial sac multiple black foci in the liver tan pale enlarged kidneys luxated left D3 enlarged distal interphalangeal joint enlarged right D3 joint multiple raised irregular black skin masses on the ventral chin and neck a small skin avulsion over the rostral mandible and reddening of the skin along the brachii and antebrachii with associated subcutaneous hemorrhage. Some subdural hemorrhage was noted on the dorsal aspect of the left hemisphere.

YOLLK COELOMITIS GRANULOMATOSIS YOLK EMBOLISM MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 13-year-old female boa died en route to the hospital. The keeper reported a mass cranial to the cloaca that had been present for some time and was associated with constipation. Necropsy revealed good postmortem condition but emaciated body condition and a firm mass cranial to the cloaca. The mass was a 5 cm. caseous yellow mass in the oviduct. The oviduct had ruptured ventrally and caseous material was in the coelomic cavity. Copious fecal material was present in the colon cranial to the mass. Two large follicles containing caseous yellow material were present in the ovary. The lungs contained multiple white nodules up to 3 mm. in diameter that were hemorrhagic and did not float in formalin. The gastric wall was subjectively thickened.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This greater than 11-year-old male thick-billed parrot had been ill for three days and in thin body condition. The bird was perching when it fell over and had what appeared to be a seizure. Supportive care was administered and the bird appeared to stabilize although eventually developed another seizure and died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition slightly enlarged liver and a hematoma involving the head.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS CHOLELITHIASIS INTERSTITIAL CELL TUMOR (TESTIS). This 17-year-old male golden lion tamarin was found dead. At necropsy bruising was noted over the lips nose and tongue. The gallbladder was enlarged and contained multiple small calculi.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS BACTERIAL BRONCHIOLITIS. This 19-year-old male sea lion was anesthetized for preshipment blood collection and exam but died 10 minutes into the procedure. A purulent discharge was noted in the tracheal tube when extubated. Cytology showed many neutrophils with intracellular cocci. Necropsy revealed a green purulent discharge at the tracheal bifurcation that lines the entire right primary bronchus. The left primary bronchus had foamy white material. Lungs were wet and heavy with normal tissue present only at the caudal dorsal lobes.

CHRONIC ANTERIOR GASTROENTERITIS WITH HELICOBACTER-LIKE BACTERIA CHRONIC ADHESIONS ACUTE BACTERIAL ENTERITIS POSTSURGICAL COMPLICATIONS. This 23-year-old female captive bred mandrill had a one week history of illness died spontaneously and was refrigerated 16 hours prior to necropsy. The animal had a one week history of lethargy and inappetence and appeared to be bloating. Surgical exploration revealed a loop of jejunum trapped in a ventral abdominal mass (present greater than two years) with adhesions of the mesentery to the mass. The mesenteric root was twisted and corrected at surgery but the animal died following recovery from surgery. Necropsy revealed nodules on the buccal mucosa degeneration of cartilage at articulations of both legs and femoral neck thickening of the right hip mucoid discharge in the major airways thickened heart valves enlarged left thyroid with cystic nodule pale liver with rounded edges bile and flocculent material in distended gall bladder inflamed pancreas weak adhesions of the small intestine large amount of partially digested food in the stomach inflammation of the pyloric mucosa multiple green/gray plaques in the proximal duodenum bruising of the serosal surface of the small intestine hemorrhage in the colon granular kidneys with capsular adhesions cyst in the cranial pole of the right kidney and two smaller cysts in the left kidney thick black exudate in the cervix and uterine body and three or four small cystic nodules in the cervix. Ovaries were not readily identified. The fourth digit of the right hand had a soft tissue mass at P2 on the palmar surface spanning the P1-P2 joint.

LEG FRACTURE ISCHEMIC NECROSIS OF LEG AND FOOT DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male scarlet ibis had a history of fractured tarsometatarsal bone. A splint was applied but the bird luxated digit #3 on the left foot necessitating partial amputation. Digits on the right foot became progressively more discolored and rigid throughout treatment and the bird lost weight. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition yellow colored fat mottled appearance to the heart large liver prominent cranial lobes of both kidneys male reproductive tract possible bruising on the surface of the skull and healing at the amputation site of the digit and healing of the fracture but purple/black discoloration of the leg and digit distal to the fracture site.

STOMATITIS AND BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA. This male 16-year-old green tree python was found dead in its enclosure. It had a history of infectious stomatitis that appeared to have resolved. At necropsy there was ingesta present within the stomach small intestine and large intestine. The python was thin and had no evidence of adipose tissue.
VENTRICULITIS HEAD TRAUMA DROWNING. This 11-year-old female ibis was found dead in water. At necropsy there is hemorrhage around the dorsal calvaria. There was evidence of water in the airways.

ANESTHETIC-RELATED DEATH INANITION GASTROENTEROCOLITIS CHOLECYSTITIS. This 9-year/4-month-old female saki died during anesthesia. It had a history of depression. Treatment was initiated during anesthesia. CPR had been attempted. At necropsy the saki was in thin body condition (body condition = 1). The lungs were pale pink. There were approximately 30 cc. of clear fluid within the abdomen. The pancreas was pink and thin. There was no digesta within the stomach or colon. The kidneys were small and firm. The bladder was empty.

SYSTEMIC AMYLOIDOSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female Siberian tiger was euthanized due to progressive decline in health status. Necropsy revealed petechiae in the tracheal mucosa liters of serosanguineous peritoneal and pleural fluid dark red to black kidneys dense lungs pericardial effusion and edematous pericardial fat lobulated irregular liver lipoma-like lesion in the occipital region and a dark focus in the right caudal cerebellum. One ovary was enlarged and cystic. Adhesions were noted on the surfaces of the lungs and kidneys.

EUTHANASIA CAPRINE ARTHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS VIRAL INFECTION CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This approximately 7-year-old female goat was humanely euthanized due to severe joint pain that was nonresponsive to pain medication. The goat was positive for caprine arthritis encephalitis virus. It also had a history of carpal swelling and periodic lameness which largely resolved with oral banamine. At necropsy there was a large 4 x 6 in. subcutaneous fluctuant swelling on the central ventral brisket area. When incised it was found to be a pocket containing approximately 100 cc. of reddish-tan clear fluid. The lungs were congested. There was foam in the trachea and main stem bronchi. Both kidneys had multifocal white areas ranging from 0.2 to 1 cm. in diameter that were visible on the serosal surface and extended into the renal parenchyma on cut surface. The left carpal joint had large diffuse soft tissue swelling on the anterior aspect. On cut surface the articular surfaces were covered with gritty white material and the joint space exuded approximately 1 cc. of pink purulent material when flexed and squeezed from the sides. The right carpal joint and right hock joint had mild roughness on the articular surface but contained purulent material. Sections of left carpal joint were submitted for aerobic and anaerobic culture. The fluid and material from the sternum was also submitted for culture.

CATARACTS INANITION BILIARY CYSTS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 17-year-old female tree boa had a history of a cataract in the left eye. The animal was found dead. At necropsy firm tan nodules were present throughout the hepatic parenchyma. The liver was very firm.
NA

BACTERIAL PLEUROPNEUMONIA SEPSIS. This approximately 5-year-old female captive bred squirrel monkey was found down laying over a branch. No problems had been noted in previous days. Necropsy revealed opaque fluid in the left side of the thorax and flocculent material within the fluid and attached to the lung. The lung was congested. Culture was obtained.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS FIBRINOUS PERITONITIS SUPPURATIVE LYMPHADENITIS ADENOMYOSIS CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 15.5-year-old female Vietnamese potbellied pig had been gradually losing condition and developed an enlarged abdomen. The pig also had a history of scruffy scaly dermatitis that had been particularly bad in the last year. Examination revealed a large solid mass filling the abdominal cavity. This seemed to be associated with the liver and more abnormal masses and cystic lesions were noted throughout the abdominal cavity associated with visceral compression. Mediastinal and sternal lymph nodes were enlarged. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large mass arose from one uterine horn and was associated with displacement and compression of the viscera. The uterus was also enlarged and somewhat twisted with both horns intertwined. The mucosa of the uterus had a polycystic lining and numerous cysts were also noted in one ovary. Sublumbar lymph nodes were enlarged both kidneys had variably sized cysts and the liver was atrophic. The gallbladder contained thick yellow sludge and a few waxy firm stones. The pancreatic duct appeared dilated. Numerous pinpoint raised white foci were on the pleural surfaces of the lung and approximately 100 ml. of serous pericardial effusion was noted. Several enlarged cranial mediastinal lymph nodes were noted.

CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE ENCEPHALITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS THYROID FOLLICULAR HYPERPLASIA LYMPH NODE HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 15-year-old female panda was found down with seizure activity. Treatment was initiated; however the animal’s condition failed to improve and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a firm dark mass was present in the caudal lung. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were black. Multiple cysts were present in the renal cortex. A large hematoma was identified in the left cerebral hemisphere.

HEPATIC FIBROSIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY OXALATE NEPHROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female Amur leopard had a three week history of hind leg lameness that responded to supportive care but then the animal became inappetent with a wobbly stance was reluctant to enter the exhibit and appeared to be “gazing” at the floor and walls. Blood work revealed elevated total bilirubin and neutrophilia and no other abnormalities. Supportive care was continued and the cat’s appetite and activity level waxed and waned between nearly normal behavior and lethargy. Hematuria then developed. The animal remained inappetent and all medications were eventually discontinued. Two days prior to death the animal had epistaxis and became dehydrated. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a large amount of intra-abdominal fat congested caudal pulmonary lobes dark purple bruise in the superficial tissue in a cranial spinal cord segment and hemorrhagic fluid around the brain. Blood filled cavities were in the nasal passages and both maxillary sinuses were packed with blood clots and fibrinous friable material.

POLIOENCEPHALOMALACIA CAE POSITIVE EUTHANASIA. This 8-month-old female goat became acutely ataxic and this progressed to recumbency. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed lice in the haircoat enlargement of mesenteric gastrohepatic and mediastinal lymph nodes pallor in the right atrium and a bumpy surface on the ventricular septum venous congestion in the right half of the cerebrum and a glow under black light and no other gross findings. This animal is positive for CAE.
EUTHANASIA. This 6-year/3-month-old female rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic neurologic problems. At necropsy there were no gross findings.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MAMMARY ABSCESS FIBROMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 3-year-old female Norway rat has a history of neoplasia with abscess and leg fracture and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a subcutaneous mass in the right thoracic and left inguinal regions a healed left tibial fracture with callus and no other abnormalities.
SYSTEMIC SHOCK RENAL GOUT. This 3-year-old lorikeet was found dead. No significant gross abnormalities were noted at necropsy.

AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION CLOACAL PROLAPSE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 16-year-old pochard was found dead in its enclosure and had been doing well with improved lameness until it was found dead. Necropsy revealed dark segment of intestine fragile kidneys and a prolapsed cloaca.

BACERIAL CELLULITIS AND SEPSIS ASPIRATION ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 2-year/4-month-old male white faced saki died while undergoing an anesthetic procedure. It had been manually restrained and immobilized with isoflurane via face mask for evaluation of left hand trauma. Physical exam findings noted moderate depression and cellulitis of the left arm up to the level of the elbow. The bones were exposed with copious amounts of pus present. During induction the saki began vomiting first water then food. Aspiration of food occurred prior to intubation leading to cyanosis and death. It was unresponsive to emergency resuscitation efforts. At necropsy the left hand was swollen with bones of P4/P5 exposed. The distal parts of the digits were absent. There was obvious cellulitis of the left forearm. The pulmonary pleura were orange. The trachea and bronchi contained aspirated food. The lungs were emphysematous with some atelectasis and hemorrhage. Ingesta was present in the stomach. The mesentery was orange. There was digesta present within the small and large intestine. Hilar lymph nodes were enlarged. Sections of liver lung and salivary gland have been frozen for future use if needed. Cultures of left carpal joint were done.

ATYPICAL VASCULAR PROLIFERATION VERTEBRAE. This approximately 9.5-year-old male corn snake has a history of a recurrent mass on the tail suspicious for neoplasia. The tail was amputated and dissection of the tail revealed a large blood clot originating off of the ventral tail vein on the right side with adherence to the right hemipene.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE BLADDER TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old male squirrel monkey has a history of dilated cardiomyopathy with associated ventricular and supraventricular tachycardia. The animal presented with acute collapse therapy was ineffective and the animal became paraplegic with no apparent conscious proprioception. Hematuria was present. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed several subcutaneous lipomas markedly enlarged heart thin-walled left ventricle and left atrium atelectatic lungs and a clot in the descending aorta proximal to the bifurcation and extending into the right side of the bifurcation. One-half of the bladder wall was hemorrhagic and hematuria was present with several jelly-like clots in the lumen of the bladder. A 2 mm. cyst was in the left kidney. This animal also had a history of possible seizure activity.

BRAIN ABSCESS. This 13-year-old male llama was euthanized due to progressive neurological signs that included head tilt eye droop etc. The condition was nonresponsive to therapy. At necropsy an abscess and fistulous tract extended along cranial nerves V-VII to the brain stem on the left side.

DROWNED. This 4-year-old female meerkat was found dead in a drain of the enclosure and is believed to have drowned. Necropsy revealed a firm and rounded liver and congestion in the lungs. The animal appeared to be obese.

SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION RENAL GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 5.5-year-old male lizard had been housed off exhibit for three years due to marked corneal opacity in both eyes. The animal had been doing well until November 2013 at which time it presented with bilateral conjunctivitis and received numerous medications with continued progression of ocular disease. The animal was not able to visualize prey and to be force-fed daily. The animal’s eyes would become stuck shut without daily topical therapy. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition marked bilateral conjunctival swelling chronic corneal opacity in the right eye and abnormal pupil shape and focal corneal opacity in the left eye. Multiple digital malformations were noted. Mild bilateral congestion was noted in the lungs. Pinpoint white foci were in the parenchyma of the kidneys the left kidney more affected than the right.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION FAT ATROPHY. This approximately 11-year-old female tortoise was found dead four days after presentation. It presented with anorexia weight loss lethargy and swollen eyelids. During handling the skin over the tail tip degloved and spontaneous lacerations occurred on the forelimbs. CBC revealed marked leukocytosis characterized by lymphocytosis and basophilia. Chemistries revealed significant elevations of CPK moderate panhypoproteinemia and hypocalcemia. Radiographs revealed large cystic calculi or retained ova. The tortoise was started on empirical therapy. At necropsy the tortoise was underweight. There appeared to be diffuse subcutaneous edema. The carcass was moderately autolyzed. The skeletal muscles were diffusely tough and pale. There was edema and fibrosis intermixed with the muscles. The shell broke easily along the suture lines. There was blood tinged fluid free within the coelomic cavity. There were minimal fat stores evident. The entire gastrointestinal tract was multifocally hyperemic on the serosal and mucosal aspects. The liver appeared gritty and small. The urinary bladder contained urine and some mineralized sand-like uroliths.

ASPERGILLOSIS ENTERITIS CLOACITIS INANITION. This male greater than 35-year-old scarlet ibis died after extensive treatment and supportive care for a broken mandibular beak. During this period it was being tube fed with difficulty eating. At necropsy the ibis had poor feather condition. There were numerous nodular growths throughout the lungs and on the air sacs some with obvious fungal spores. The ibis was emaciated. There was frank blood within the small intestine. The kidneys appeared enlarged.

RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS VASCULAR AMYLOIDOSIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA ENTERITIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 25-year-old female flamingo had a wing amputation two weeks prior to death. The animal was lethargic weak and developed neurologic signs. The animal’s condition continued to decline despite treatment and progressed to regurgitation cardiopulmonary arrest and death. At necropsy gray tinged fluid was present in the nares. The pericardium was thickened and opaque and covered by white material (visceral gout).

METASTATIC SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male antelope was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the right mandible (G14-0432). Supportive care was administered which necessitated a second debulking procedure but progressive necrosis developed at the site. The animal did well until 24 hours prior to death when it became inappetent and the wound was noted to be infested with maggots. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good to fair body condition a 6 cm. deep cavernous necrotic area in the caudal right mandible full of maggots enlargement of the right mandibular lymph node sclerosis in both eyes and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA UNDIFFERENTIATED SARCOMA CELLULITIS INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS INANITION. This 14-year-old rattlesnake had a spindle cell neoplasia diagnosed by fine needle aspirate one year prior to death. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining quality of life. At necropsy a raised soft to firm subcutaneous mass was present on the right side adjacent to the vertebrae. On section the mass contained areas of hemorrhage and friable necrotic material. The GI tract contained numerous cestodes in the stomach. Numerous 2 x 1 cm. flattened cream colored objects were free within the coelom within the musculature and in the GI tract presumed to represent parasites. The kidneys were uniformly white.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL GRANULOMA HEPATOPATHY. This 18-year/8-month-old female skink was humanely euthanized. It had an abscess in the scent gland area that was very necrotic and extended into the vertebral column area. At necropsy there was clear serous fluid in the coelomic cavity. The abscess moved down to the vertebral column and was close to penetrating the coelomic cavity.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 27-year-old female parrot was found dead in its cage. The animal is housed with a conspecific female. This bird was acquired from another institution one year earlier and had a history of mobility and stability issues for several years. A crop biopsy did not identify proventricular dilatation disease although bornavirus test was positive in feces. Follow-up testing was negative for bornavirus. Necropsy revealed poor body condition retained sheaths around primary blood feathers hemocoelom enlarged thyroid pale mottled liver a cyst-like structure in the liver (possible gallbladder) enlarged spleen enlarged pale kidneys mildly cystic ovarian duct and no other findings.

INTESTINAL PERFORATION TRAUMA PANCREATITIS. This 10-year-old female pale-headed saki had a history of bloating. This animal became lethargic and bloated a few days prior to death. The animal did not improve with medical treatment and was found dead. At necropsy there were two punctures of the left body wall with intestinal herniation and perforation. There was a right inguinal puncture with a small amount of surrounding blood. The adrenal glands and uterine body were discolored green to yellow. The intestines were severely inflamed. Ulcers were within the colon and duodenum. The pancreas was inflamed. Subdural and cerebral hemorrhage was present.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS BACTERIAL COLITIS SHOCK. This 20-year-old female chinchilla had a history of inappetence. The animal’s condition acutely declined and it died despite supportive care. At necropsy moderate effusion was noted in the pleural cavity. Kidneys were pale and finely nodular.

EUTHANASIA PROLIFERATIVE AND HYPERKERATOTIC DERMATITIS EPICARDITIS. This 8-year/6-month-old male milksnake was humanely euthanized. It had a previous diagnosis of dysecdysis. Skin biopsy in November revealed hyperkeratotic dermatitis with superficial colonization and dysecdysis. Vitamin A therapy was instituted on 11/20. There was no change in condition several months later. At necropsy the skin was very thickened and stiff. The scales were flaking readily. There was a 4x2 cm. clear fluid filled sac noted near the vent. It was lightly attached to the mesentery. There was also a 2x2 cm. sac filled with clear tan fluid and small particulate matter just cranial to the large mass and was free floating in the coelom. There was a 2 mm. mass just cranial to the heart.

ACUTE SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This greater than 8-year-old female cobra was found dead in its exhibit with no prior signs of illness. The body was refrigerated approximately 48 hours prior to necropsy. Necropsy revealed erythema of the epidermis along the lower left jaw paintbrush hemorrhages on the mucosal surface of the trachea reddened lungs blood in the oral cavity congested liver and no other abnormalities.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS RENAL GOUT BACTERIAL/AMOEBIC COLITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 26-year-old male Gila monster had a history of inappetence regurgitation and thin body condition. The animal did not respond to supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a pseudomembrane on the mucosal surface of the colon.

SEPTIC PULMONARY ABSCESSATION ACUTE INTERSTITIAL PULMONARY DISEASE UREMIC GASTRITIS. This 3-year-old captive bred male black-footed ferret was found deceased on August 11 2016. The patient had severe azotemia hyperphosphatemia and hyperkalemia. It had a one-day history of anorexia lethargy and diarrhea. Chronic renal disease and renal failure are suspected. The animal was treated with fluids penicillin maropitant and famotidine. Urine specific gravity was greater than 1.050 and 1+ protein was present. BUN was 123 and creatinine was 0.9. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition severe dehydration patchy alopecia on the thighs a dark purple left cranial pulmonary lobe with multifocal purulent foci throughout white foci with purulent material in other pulmonary lobes and symmetrical smooth kidneys.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS RENAL GOUT ENTERITIS ENCEPHALITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 8-year-old female chicken had a history of weight loss. The animal was found down with a large fecal mass at the vent. Ulcerative dermatitis was noted adjacent to the vent. The following day the animal was dyspneic and was later found dead. At necropsy pectoral muscle mass was reduced; however extensive deposits of adipose tissue were present within the coelomic cavity and subcutaneous tissues. The mucosa of the distal colon was dark red. A small raised reddened mass was present ventral to the cloaca. Lungs were markedly congested. The liver was mottled red and black and was friable. The right AV valve was irregular with multiple raised 1 mm. foci.

EUTHANASIA BACTERIAL AND FUNGAL DERMATITIS AND CONJUNCTIVITIS. This 2-year/5-month-old male milksnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of bilateral conjunctivitis and diffuse dermatitis of chronic duration. At necropsy there was massive diffuse dermatitis with chronic conjunctivitis. The pancreas was enlarged.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA AMYLOIDOSIS. This 7-year-old black footed ferret had a two day history of lethargy and did not respond to supportive care. Blood work revealed markedly elevated renal values. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a firm mass in the cranial liver lobe pale kidneys and petechiae on the right kidney.

SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS WITH FIBROSIS (POSSIBLE OLD INFARCT) EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old spayed female gray wolf had a previous episode of diarrhea six weeks earlier and a two-day history of lethargy possible neurologic signs and apparent hemoabdomen. Surgery identified a 5 cm. solid mass in the spleen and a 6 cm. mass in the left middle pulmonary lobe. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified areas of atelectasis and mineralization in the lungs in addition to the masses described previously.

ANESTHETIC RELATED DEATH ARTERIOSCLEROSIS CYSTITIS ABOMASITIS. This 11-year-old female impala died during anesthesia. It had demonstrated a chronic quidding problem and was sedated for further diagnostic testing. It did not respond to resuscitation attempts and went into cardiac arrest. At necropsy it was in good nutritional condition. There was a small white mass present subcutaneously over the mid lateral left rib area. There was pink foam present in the trachea. The lungs were mottled pink/tan. The left side of the cranial lung lobe had an area of hemorrhage. There was approximately 60 ml. of clear pink fluid in the pericardial sac. The surface of the proximal pulmonary artery was roughened with multiple narrow fissures. There was a circular small depression present on the surface of the medial wall of the pulmonary artery as it exited the right ventricle. There was severe chronic periodontal disease with gingival erosions. There was malocclusion. The right uterine horn was approximately twice the size of the left but appeared normal grossly. There was an area of the proximal left uterine horn that was mottled tan/red. The spleen was enlarged. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were dark red and appeared enlarged. Meningeal blood vessels were congested.

CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE SHOCK PERINATAL DEATH (2 DAYS). This 3-year-old lorikeet was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy feather loss was noted over the skull and neck with discoloration of the skin.

ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 30-year-old male Chilean flamingo had a 10 month history of arthritic hock with associated hospitalization with treatment. An attempt to arthrodese the joint was performed in February 2012 with several complications that eventually necessitated euthanasia for humane and diagnostic purposes.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION RENAL GOUT. This greater than 10-year-old male chuckwalla died. It had a history of emaciation and dehydration. Blood work revealed normal uric acid but an inverse calcium/phosphorus ratio (15:9). Supportive care was initiated. At necropsy there was a slight reticular appearance to the liver. There were white deposits in the kidney.

SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS PULMONARY SHOCK. This 20-year-old female duck was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed scant ingesta in the alimentary tract several white plaques throughout the air sacs foamy white/tan liquid in the lungs inactive left ovary and muscle atrophy.

EUTHANASIA GRANULOMATOUS DISEASE SEPTICEMIA GOITER DIC STRESS. This approximately 30-year-old male rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It presented extremely lethargic and depressed. There was an obvious mid coelomic mass. The rattlesnake became apneic during physical examination. At necropsy there was edema fluid and an abscess within the coelomic cavity. There were abscesses within the liver.
EUTHANASIA SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (ORAL CAVITY) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 3-year-old female elephant shrew had swelling on the face. The animal was humanely euthanized.

MANGEMENT EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 14-year-old male copperhead was euthanized due to contact with Cryptosporidium positive cagemates. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

RENAL AND PULMONARY MINERALIZATION YOLK COELOMITIS. This 11-year-old dove of undetermined gender was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed fair body condition and good postmortem condition some bruising on the dorsal cranium distended crop with ingesta white discoloration of the right caudal pulmonary lobe and no other gross abnormalities.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA WITH OTITIS MEDIA INTRATHORACIC NEOPLASM (BRONCHOGENIC OR MESOTHELIOMA). This greater than 2-year-old male domestic rat was found dead. Necropsy revealed a thick caseating infiltrate in the lungs congested meninges and no other abnormalities. This animal periodically had nose bleeds head tilt and a long history of respiratory problems. Head tilt was severe one day prior to death.

RENAL INTERSTITIAL FIBROSIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION PANCREATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA BILIARY CYSTS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 12-year-old male black tree monitor had a history of lead detected in the peripheral blood and treatment with calcium EDTA. The animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed a white focus on the spleen a small amount of fluid in the pericardial sac multifocal white foci in the pancreas two cystic structures within the liver and multifocal yellow to white lesions on the gallbladder with inspissated bile in the gallbladder.

EUTHANASIA SKULL DEFECT CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS STRESS. This 9-year-old female burrowing owl was humanely euthanized due to poor quality of life. It had a history of severe head tilt and a CT scan identified a possible skeletal deformity in the right cranium causing pressure on the right side of the brain. Necropsy revealed that the right eye socket was covered by skin and feather a phthisical ocular structure was still present within the socket. The left eye was normal. Some keratinaceous debris was in the right ear canal. Some white iridescent streaking was over the left atrium on the epicardial surface. The right cerebral hemisphere was darker than the left and a defined indentation was present along the lateral margin. Some abnormal bone growth was noted along the inside of the right cranium pressing on the right side of the brain. All viscera were grossly normal and female reproductive tract was identified.

BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This 5.5-year-old male quail had not been located for two days after which it was found dead in some tall grasses of the exhibit. It had a history of abnormal beak shape and growth and had recently lost a small amount of weight and was being monitored. Necropsy revealed thin body condition right eye crusted shut clear fluid in the eyelids food material crusted to the upper and lower beak autolyzed intestinal tract a layer of thick fibrinous material covering the serosal surface of the left hepatic lobe and ventriculus and male reproductive tract.

LYMPHOMA SPLEEN AND LIVER; ECTOPIC ADRENAL CORTICAL TISSUE INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 6-year-old female ferret had a bilateral adrenalectomy in 2001. Acute hind limb paresis developed and an abdominal mass and irregularly enlarged spleen were palpated. Medical workup revealed generalized lymphadenopathy splenomegaly and a 2 cm. mass near the right kidney. Blood glucose was within normal limits. The ferret died at the end of the anesthetic recovery after apparent intravascular overhydration. Necropsy revealed 100 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the peritoneal cavity a 2 cm. mass associated with the pancreas congested intestinal vessels enlarged popliteal prescapular femoral and mediastinal lymph nodes enlarged spleen with multiple white lesions throughout the capsule and apparent masses present in both caudal and cranial poles. The adrenal glands were absent.
RENAL GOUT GASTRIC MINERALIZATION INANITION. This 10-year-old snake presented with neurologic signs and regurgitation. The animal later died. At necropsy the animal was thin.

ENTERITIS VACUOLAR DEGENERATION MENINGEAL EDEMA. This 4.5-year-old male lemur had a history of lethargy and was found dead. At necropsy the liver contained multifocal 1 mm. tan to yellow lesions in multiple lobes. The stomach had foci of ulceration. Ulcerated foci were also identified within the cecum.
SHOCK PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 1-year-old male bat was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

SHOCK HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 18-year-old female Bali mynah was trapped between rocks in the enclosure. The animal was weak and died despite treatment. At necropsy the bird was thin. White foci were noted in the lung. The liver was brown and friable.

Immunohistochemistry; Canine distemper virus: Canine distemper virus antigen not detected Warthin-Starry staining; Stomach: Moderate numbers of spirochetes; consistent with Helicobacter sp. Comments: Although the immunohistochemistry failed to identify canine distemper virus within the tissue; given the histopathologic lesions of interstitial pneumonia and syncytial formation of transitional epithelium of the urinary bladder; canine distemper virus infection is still concerned. Therefore; PCRs for generic paramyxovirus and canine distemper virus are pending. The results will be included in the addendum. In addition; Warthin-Starry special stain highlighted moderate numbers of small spirochete bacteria in the stomach. These bacteria were consistent with Helicobacter sp.; which is a common cause of gastritis in ferrets that have been stressed or have other concurrent disease. Tuddow Thaiwong; DVM; PhD Lung: Marked interstitial pneumonia Urinary bladder: Multifocal syncytial cell formation Stomach: Marked multifocal lymphoplasmacytic gastritis Small and large intestine: Moderate to marked lymphoplasmacytic enteritis Uterus: Mild suppurative endometritis Haired skin: Marked secondary follicle atrophy Comments The most striking lesion in this animal was marked interstitial pneumonia. In combination with the presence of syncytial cells within the urinary bladder; this lesion could represent a canine distemper virus infection. Immunohistochemistry for canine distemper virus is in progress. In the sections of haired skin; there was a mild secondary hair follicle atrophy; and there was no evidence of immune-mediated disease; neoplasm; and inflammation. The ovary contained multiple developing follicles; supportive non-pregnancy status. Mild endometritis was seen on the uterus; but the degree of inflammation was mild and likely represented a normal involuting uterus. Inflammation of the stomach and intestine may reflect the response to stress; however; infection of Helicobacter sp. may also contribute to gastritis in this case. Therefore; detection of Helicobacter sp. using immunohistochemistry is pending. Results of additional testing will be included in the addendum. This case was reviewed by Dr. Matti Kiupel. Tuddow Thaiwong; DVM; PhD Please see comments Comments: Concern remains regarding infection of canine distemper viral infection; although PCRs for both canine distemper virus and generic paramyxovirus were negative. Therefore; submission of any sickened animal for full necropsy is highly recommended. Tuddow Thaiwong; DVM; P

SUSPECT TRAUMA SUSPECT DROWNING. This greater than 1-year-old male tanager was found dead in the filter basket of one of the NACC’s emersion gallery pools. There is a possible history of conspecific aggression. At necropsy the body was wet and had moderate autolysis of internal organs. The tanager was in good body condition as determined by the pectoral muscle mass. Reproductive activity was evident by the testicular size. There were diffuse subcutaneous hemorrhages on the dorsal aspect of the body and over the midproximal wings.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS URATE STASIS. This 13-year-old male egret was attacked by cagemates and suffered a laceration of the wing. The animal was treated but was found dead several days later. At necropsy a large amount of bruising was present over the head and neck. No significant internal lesions were noted.

SPONDYLOSIS VERTEBRAL FRATURE GOITER. This 11-year/7-month-old female python was found dead in its enclosure. It had been scheduled for humane euthanasia due to chronic poor health primarily musculoskeletal problems. It had a history of listlessness and absent righting response. There were several palpable lumps within the coelom. At necropsy there was chronic vertebral osteomyelitis.

ARTICULAR AMYLOIDOSIS DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female ringed teal was diagnosed with right coxofemoral degenerative joint disease 1.5 years ago and this was associated with severe debilitating lameness. There were repeated episodes of neurologic disease (ataxia). One year ago uric acid levels were elevated and the teal responded to fluid therapy. Recently neurologic disease has recurred involving ataxia and incoordination with potential visual deficits. Due to the grave prognosis euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed moderately good nutritional status a small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the lungs congestion of blood vessels in the serosa of the intestine.

RENAL GOUT VASCULAR MINERALIZATION INTRAMUSCULAR HEMORRHAGE CATARACTS INANITION. This 7-year-old male lizard was under treatment for anorexia and lethargy. Respiratory arrest developed during examination and a large quantity of mucoid hemorrhagic material was present in the oral cavity. Resuscitation was successful but then the animal was found dead with hemorrhage in the oral cavity. At necropsy hemorrhagic and mucoid material was present in the oral cavity and esophagus. Multiple round white nodules were present in the intestinal wall. Pinpoint white foci were present in the kidneys.

SKELETAL GOUT OVARIAN ABSCESSES. This 5-year-old female frilled lizard was treated for abscesses in both limbs. In September the animal was attacked by another reptile and incurred a fractured left maxilla with loss of several teeth and associated corneal ulceration. The animal recovered from this episode but over the last few weeks the condition has declined and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition abnormal scales where abscesses had previously been several eggs present in the coelom with a few adhered to the liver and thick white material in the limbs.

PULMONARY ABSCESSES ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male/neutered dumbo rat presented with lethargy and inappetence and had lost a significant amount of weight in the last 4-6 weeks. Radiographs revealed a large pulmonary mass and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed little to no fat stores an area of alopecia over the left hip and two large firm yellow/tan masses in the right and left caudal pulmonary fields that oozed purulent debris on cut surface. Caseous debris was in both inner ears.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATC MYELOLIPOMA. This 25-year-old neutered male guanaco had a history of severe degenerative joint disease. A wound with maggot infection was noted. The animal was humanely euthanized.

CHOLESTASIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS CHOLELITHIASIS ADRENAL FIBROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male mountain lion had been lethargic and inappetent for five days and had orange urine and marked bilirubinuria. The cat responded to supportive care but a mass was detected in the upper abdomen and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized hepatomegaly and a 5 cm. brown focal mass between the pancreas and liver along the portal veins. The gallbladder was distended and had an enlarged tortuous bile duct. Dark black pin-sized stones were within the lumen of the gallbladder. The spleen was enlarged and congested. Lungs were atelectatic and a nodular firm lesion was associated with the primary bronchioles. The trachea was jaundiced. The left auricle was thickened and appeared to be fibrotic and the mitral and tricuspid valves were thickened.
DROWNING (PRESUMPTIVE SHOCK). This 8-year-old male motmot was recently introduced into the aviary. The bird was found dead. At necropsy the lungs were edematous and hemorrhagic.

BRAIN ABSCESS PROVENTRICULAR NEMATODIASIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS ANEMIA. This 4-year-old female rainbow lorikeet had a recent history of anemia hypoproteinemia weight loss and severe ataxia. A blood transfusion was administered four days earlier. Several birds in the flock have died with visceral larval migrans. This bird was found dead in the morning and necropsy revealed a pale liver and viscera pale muscles many small worms within the proventriculus and no other abnormalities.

EMACIATION CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE LOW-GRADE SEPSIS. This greater than 7-year-old frog had an episode of metabolic bone disease in 2005 with subsequent deformities in the skeletal system. The frog has had multiple gastric impactions one of which was treated with surgical correction. The frog tested positive for chytridiomycosis in 2010 was treated and has since tested negative. In 2011 a cystic mass was detected with a muscle belly of the left pelvic limb and cytology suggested a spindle cell or connective tissue tumor although histopathology results were consistent with inflammation. The frog has chronic mild bloating and subcutaneous edema and recent inappetence was noted by the keepers. The frog was found dead. Necropsy revealed deformities in the skeletal system bloat thin body condition excess shed over the dorsum ventral abdomen and left medial thigh papillomatous cutaneous lesions at healed sites of previous surgery subcutaneous edema at the level of the pelvic limbs marked cardiac pallor minimal fat stores 30 ml. of transparent fluid in the coelom dark liver nodular and irregular kidneys and a thickened diaphysis in the left femur compared to the right.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male black-tailed prairie dog has a chronic history of moderate weight loss although is still in good body condition. It was found acutely moribund and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes.
