Three other animals in the colony have been euthanized in the past few months two with confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma and one with gross lesions consistent with hepatic neoplasia. Necropsy findings in this prairie dog revealed good body condition and two large masses in the cranial left quadrant of the abdomen associated with the left hepatic lobe. The masses were dark liver colored and approximately 4 cm. in greatest dimension. On cut surface the masses were red/tan and firm. A 1 cm. liver colored mass was adhered to the pelvic surface of the right kidney. No other abnormalities were noted.
SHOCK SMOKE INHALATION. This 6-year-old male chinchilla was found dead following an electrical fire in the enclosure. At necropsy lungs were fluid filled and hemorrhagic.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female hedgehog had a history of weight loss and ataxia and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mottled lungs pale foci in the left ventricle of the heart which appeared to be thickened and adhesion of the liver to the abdominal wall.

GOUT NEPHROSCLEROSIS BACTERIAL FOLLICULITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 5-year-old frilled lizard had a long history of gout and had become progressively less mobile. It recently received prey-inflected trauma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition depleted fat stores friable mottled liver pale cream deposits in multiple soft tissue locations such as the forelimb musculature and left thoracic inlet pale small kidneys several free-floating concretions of inspissated yolk material in the coelomic cavity and a few follicles.

EUTHANASIA ADRENAL MEDULLARY PROLIFERATION POSSIBLE PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. This approximately 14-year-old female red kangaroo has had continued problems moving with minimal control of the right leg recumbency and inability to right itself easily. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition congestion in the viscera and a hemorrhagic appearance to the mucosal lining at the base of the stomach and renal parenchyma.

BACTERIAL DERMATITIS AND SAPROLEGNIOSIS. This greater than 2-year-old toad was being treated with antibiotics for flesh eating infection of the distal digits and nose. One other Surinam toad had less severe but similar lesions. The toad died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed fair body condition but a prominent pelvis loss of skin muscle and bone on all digits of the front feet exposing an average of 4 mm. of phalanges on each digit. The edge of these lesions is discolored yellow with a fuzzy appearance. More proximal on each toe is an area of redness and two digits appear to have fissures in the skin at this level. There is a similar appearance to the nose tip. When the nose is depressed fluid comes from both nostrils that is blood tinged and slightly yellow. There is blushing of the skin on the rear feet. Gross exam with internal organs reveals no abnormalities except in the small bowel where there is an area of red discoloration.

CHRONIC ENTERITIS INANITION. This 1.5-year-old male saki was behaving abnormally and was examined. Marked weight loss and muscle wasting were noted. The animal died overnight. At necropsy marked muscle wasting and lack of adipose tissue stores were noted.

BILIARY CARCINOMA BRONCHIOLOALVEOLAR CARCINOMA BASAL CELL CARCINOMA BRANCHIAL CLEFT CYST MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 19-year-old male lion had a history of hind limb paresis. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy nodular lesions were noted in the lung and liver. Erosion was noted in the femoral articular cartilage. Nodular foci were present adjacent to the heart base. Bridging spondylosis was present within the vertebral bodies.

SEPSIS ETIOLOGY UNDETERMINED. This 5-year-old male greater kudu had a one day history of progressive neurologic signs that included ataxia generalized weakness and seizures. The animal continued to eat and drink. Between suspected seizure activities mentation appeared normal. The animal subsequently died during recovery from an anesthetic procedure. Necropsy revealed multiple abrasions in the skin overgrown hooves fibrinous and cloudy cerebrospinal fluid foamy red-tinged fluid in the trachea effaced right pulmonary lobe contusion in the dorsal left middle pulmonary lobe red-tinged fluid in the pericardium hemorrhage in the endocardium of both ventricles a calculus in the right kidney with no associated dilatation of the pelvis two medium-sized trichobezoars in the rumen urine in the urinary bladder and hemorrhage within the connective tissue ventral to the pelvis and within the musculature around the pelvis. Lymph nodes are prominent in the area of hemorrhage and multiple fractures of the pelvis are noted. Severe erosion on the head of the femur is noted in the right hip joint.
SHOCK PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEPATITIS. This 18-year-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy brown material was present in the proventriculus. The animal was thin.

PROLIFERATIVE COLITIS WITH ATYPIA BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female beaded lizard had persistent mucoid material that was bright green in the feces. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mature ovarian follicles a white nodular mass in the parenchyma of the liver approximately 3 mm. in greatest dimension. Inspissated bile was in the gallbladder and the gallbladder was irregularly shaped. A large amount of green mucoid material was in the digestive tract. Inspissated yolk was present in one ovary.

GASTRIC DILATATION/ VOLVULUS. This 12-year-old female wallaroo was found down in the moat and died during exam. Blood work revealed renal disease. Necropsy revealed pulmonary and cardiac congestion gas distended stomach fatty liver right unilateral mammary gland enlargement bruised kidneys marked splenomegaly and edema in the ventral abdominal muscles.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PYELONEPHRITIS CYSTITIS. This 20-year-old puma has a history of chronic renal disease. The animal’s condition declined and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy kidneys were small with cavitated areas. Generalized muscle atrophy was also noted.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 7.5-year-old male meerkat was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy one year earlier received supportive care but developed episodes of increased respiration isolated behavior and possibly some lack of awareness. Symptoms persisted and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed muscle atrophy moderate dehydration and severe cardiomegaly with enlargement of the left ventricle right ventricle and left atrium. Both lungs were enlarged and oozed fluid on cut surface. The liver was enlarged with rounded borders and a slightly pitted serosal surface and oozed fluid on cut surface. Both kidneys were slightly small with an irregular serosal surface and some hemorrhage was noted at the corticomedullary junctions.

HEPATIC PASSIVE CONGESTION POSSIBLE CARDIOMYOPATHY EUTHANASIA (HIND LIMB PARALYSIS). This 2-year-old male opossum had a four week history of hind limb paresis and had been dragging its rear legs for the last two weeks. Appetite and orientation have remained normal. The animal was euthanized for humane reasons. Lungs were mottled with numerous white foci resembling gout and a small area of erythema was in the mucosa of the cardiac region of the stomach. Abrasions were detected on the digits.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 17-month-old male Virginia opossum had a 24 hour onset of inappetence and was found dead. Necropsy revealed clear light brown-tinged fluid in the thoracic cavity enlarged and thin walled left ventricle whitish-yellow thickened foci on the pleural surfaces and no other gross lesions.

UTERINE LEIOMYOMA UTERINE CARCINOMA RENAL ADENOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 18-year-old female warthog had a history of chronic degenerative joint disease. Dark vaginal discharge was also noted recently. The animal’s condition was declining and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy areas of erosion were noted in the articular cartilage of the femur and patella. Large areas of hemorrhage and blood clots were noted in the abdomen. Kidneys were enlarged. A white to tan firm mass was present in the pelvis of the left kidney. An irregularly sized mass was present in the uterus.

RENAL HEMATOMA WITH HEMOCOELOM. This 11-year-old male rainbow lorikeet had been completely normal and was found dead on its exhibit in the middle of the day. Necropsy revealed a 2 cm. cavitated lesion on the caudal pole of the left kidney a large amount of clotted blood in the caudal region of the coelom.

POSTANESTHETIC DEATH ENDOCARDIOSIS MYOCARDIAL DEGENERATION GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 17-year/8-month-old male polar bear died. The polar bear was presented for evaluation of a wooden foreign body stuck in the upper incisors that was there for over one week. Anesthesia was performed to retrieve the object stuck on a split incisor and a tooth was also extracted. Hyperthermia was evident throughout the procedure and alcohol was used to help with this condition. After the procedure was done reversal agents were given. The animal was observed until alert sternal and several attempts to stand were performed. Around 20 min. later the animal was reported to be breathing heavily and in lateral recumbency. It stopped breathing. Several attempts were made to resuscitate the polar bear without any success. At necropsy there was moist dermatitis on all paws. The left axillary lymph node was enlarged with a generalized mottled appearance. Thoracic lymph nodes were hemorrhagic. Tracheobronchial lymph nodes were hemorrhagic. The right inguinal lymph node was hyperemic and had a very mottled appearance. The right adrenal gland had some acute hemorrhage. There was an area of emphysema cranial to the trachea. There was localized hemorrhage on the serosal and mucosal surfaces. There were bullae noted in some lung lobes. The heart had some areas of petechia on the serosal surface. There was vegetative endocarditis evident in the mitral valves. The right ventricular wall had an increased thickness toward the coronary vessels and septum with a 2 cm. versus 1 cm. difference. The left ventricle was 2.8 cm. thick. The esophagus contained foam and mucus. The stomach contained food. The duodenum had thickened mucosa and generalized areas of ulceration. The spleen had a black/red mottled appearance in the serosal surface. Both kidneys had some medullary congestion and pale cortices.

XANTHOMATOSIS FIBROSIS OR AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old male corn snake had declining body condition with bilateral cataracts atrophy and a persistent caudal swelling suggestive of neoplasia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed minimal fat stores enlarged firm testicles containing cystic structures and small firm kidneys.

EUTHANASIA LYMPHOSARCOMA (LYMPHOID LEUKOSIS PRESUMPTIVE). This 1-year-old hen had a history of weight loss. Treatment was initiated; however neurologic signs developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was emaciated. Small irregular tan nodules were present adherent to the proventriculus and ovary as well as the serosa of the distal GI tract. Frontal bones of the cranium were malformed with protrusion of the cerebrum.

OSTEOMYELITIS RHINITIS PERORBITAL ABSCESS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year/6-month-old female wallaby was humanely euthanized due to poor prognosis. It had a history of chronic rhinitis and dental abscesses with osteomyelitis. It recently developed exophthalmos with a retrobulbar abscess. At necropsy the left eye was exophthalmic and had a corneal ulcer. There was an abscess that filled the left eye socket and extended to the third maxillary molar. The left nasal turbinates were nonexistent and the mucosa was hemorrhagic. There was a suspected sequestrum found at the mandibular symphysis. There were smooth white foci on the liver. The wallaby was thin.

INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK PERINATAL DEATH (2 MONTHS). This 2-month-old ferret was anesthetized for a preshipment examination. The animal was found dead two days after the anesthesia. At necropsy the large intestine contained pasty cream colored feces. Fecal exam at the time of necropsy revealed abundant coccidia.

INTESTINAL DISPLACEMENT ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA POSTSURGICAL COMPLICATIONS CHRONIC RUMENITIS EMACIATION. This 7-year-old male gerenuk has a history of doing poorly with loss of 4 lb. over a five day interval. Blood work as within normal limits the animal tested negative for Johne’s disease and was dewormed for whipworms. Examination revealed three large bezoars in the rumen that were surgically excised. The animal recovered well but was found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition darkened lungs arteriosclerosis in the heart and great vessels no leakage from the surgical sites an erosion in the abomasum multiple Trichuris worms in the cecum dark cobblestone liver gritty hepatic parenchyma and no other abnormalities.

CARDIOMYOPATHY. This 7-year-old male fruit bat was found dead on the floor of exhibit. At necropsy there was some bruising on the left wing. The bat was slightly thin. An appendage was missing from the right wing and appeared to be a fairly recent injury. The heart muscle had a roughened almost cobblestone appearance. It was slightly flabby and misshapen. The liver appeared larger than normal.
GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 8-year-old female golden lion tamarin had a history of weight loss. At necropsy focal pale areas were present in the kidneys.

Thoracic cavity: Moderate hydrothorax Lung: Diffuse; severe pulmonary edema C3: Locally extensive mucosal hyperplasia with multifocal granulomas Liver: Solid biliary adenoma Comments This animal had severe pulmonary edema and thoracic effusion. These lesions can be caused by left side heart failure; hypoproteinemia; and infection; however; they are also commonly seen in euthanized animals. The lesions found in the C3 are most likely associated with parasite infection. Samples were collected for fecal analysis as well as histopathology. The result will be included as a final report. Misa Komine DVM; PhD C3: Multifocal granulomas Liver: Bilicary cystic adenoma; Diffuse; moderate passive congestion with centrilobular fibrosis and bridging fibrosis Lung: Pulmonary congestion and edema Heart: Mild lymphocytic myocarditis Tongue: Moderate; multifocal; lymphocytic glossitis Third eyelid: Sebaceous hyperplasia; mild lymphocytic conjunctivitis Endoparasitism Comments The histological findings in the stomach (C3) are most consistent with parasitic granulomas; and Trichostrongylus spp were detected with fecal analysis. Intestinal parasite infection causes diarrhea and weight loss; resulting in hypoproteinemia. Thoracic effusion and pulmonary edema seen in this case may be associated with hypoproteinemia. Lesions seen in heart; liver and tongue are overall mild and non-specific; and are considered to be incidental findings often seen in aged animals. Misa Komine DVM; PhD

DROWNING. This 16-year/3-month-old male flamingo was found dead in his water bucket. It may have fallen into the bucket and could not get out. It recently had its wing amputated. At necropsy the bird was wet. The right carpus was abraded. The amputation site musculature was bruised. There was approximately 3 cc. of orange tinged fluid present in the pericardial sac. There was ingesta in the gastrointestinal tract.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS WITH OSTEOARTHRITIS. This 12-year-old male palm viper has a history of chronic proliferative spinal disease with decreased movement in the caudal portion of the body inappetence of several months duration and was being tube fed monthly for supportive care. It recently developed dermatitis and was noted on the bottom of the enclosure more frequently. It was subsequently found dead and had been fed four days prior to being found dead. Necropsy revealed fair to good postmortem condition fair body condition dull thickened skin with grayish-tan discoloration that was generalized. A 10 cm. long pale tan soft multilobulated mass was present between the fat bodies caudal to the gallbladder and cranial to the kidneys. The kidneys were slightly pale. The midbody vertebral column was stiff and thickened in a 3 cm. length.

SMALL INTESTINAL CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This approximately 12-year-old Gila Monster has a 1-year history of weight loss and regurgitation with occasional blood in the stool. A conspecific was euthanized 2 years ago due to cryptosporidiosis. Gastric and small intestinal biopsies were obtained. The stomach was grossly normal but the small intestine appeared hyperemic hypervascular edematous and distended.
SHOCK PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE. This 11-year-old female ibis was captured for feather collection. The animal was found dead shortly thereafter. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

MYONECROSIS DERMATITIS. This 6-year-old female ibis was found dead soaking wet. At necropsy the wound had granulated nicely over the dorsal sacral area. There was a large thickened uropygial gland that contained thick gray material. The body condition was good. The liver was pale tan to light brown and mottled. The kidneys were pale brown to dark brown.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS CHOLECYSTITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS SHOCK. This 6-year-old male ferret was found dead. At necropsy blood was present in the oral cavity. Hemorrhage was noted in the GI tract. Spleen was enlarged.

SYSTEMIC NONSUPPURATIVE INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS POSSIBLY VIRAL. This 1-year-old male captive bred junglefowl had a two week history of illness characterized by torticollis and difficulty standing. The bird was euthanized for humane reasons.

BRONCHIECTASIS LIPID PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 3-year-old rat presented in an obtunded condition and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed coalescing white plaques on the dorsal surfaces of both lungs and congestion in the left lung.

TYPHLITIS OR COLITIS WITH BACTERIAL OVERGROWTH MESENTERIC CESTODIASIS. This approximately 2-year-old female cottontail rabbit was found dead with no obvious antemortem signs of illness. Necropsy revealed watery diarrhea around the perineum dark caeca with red/black liquid and no normal fecal material noted past the ileocecal junction.

THYMOMA. This 12-year-old female goat had a three day history of dyspnea was febrile developed a bloated abdomen and had no stool. The animal subsequently died and necropsy revealed multiple nodules in the mediastinum above the heart hyperemic and edematous lungs pericardial effusion minimal ascites food in the stomach and bloated stomach.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS TOOTH ROOT ABSCESS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male rabbit has a history of chronic nasal discharge and a history of a mass in the right nasal cavity and right sinus cavity. The right maxillary incisor had become reabsorbed and the tooth never grew. This animal had a previous right nephrectomy and did well afterwards. Over the past week this animal’s appetite and activity levels have decreased and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified cysts in the right thyroid gland and the right caudal pulmonary lobe cataracts in both eyes mottled and slightly rounded liver and two raised nodules on the surface of the kidney at opposing poles.

STOMATITIS BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA COELOMITIS INANITION. This 33-year-old female tortoise had a defect in the oral cavity and had been under treatment. The animal was found flaccid and recovered with supportive care but was found in similar condition the following week. Caseous material was noted in the trachea. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was pale and friable. A firm tan mass was adjacent caudal to the esophagus and adjacent to the bronchus. Smaller masses were noted in the coelomic cavity. Multiple abscesses were present in the lung.

GASTRIC FOREIGN BODY (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) COELOMIC HEMORRHAGE INANITION. This 27-year-old female turtle was doing poorly and died before physical examination was possible. The animal has a prior history of anemia and anorexia. At necropsy petechiae were present on the bridges of the shell. The coelomic cavity was filled with hemorrhagic fluid. A 2 x 1 cm. fibrin clot was present in the coelomic cavity. Present in the pericardial sac were 30 cc. of yellow fluid. A foreign body (wire) was present on the serosa of the stomach which appeared well encapsulated. A small dark nodule was present in the distal small intestine.

HISTOPLASMOSIS. This 12-year-old female wallaby was reported to have diarrhea in its enclosure and was lethargic in the morning. Examination revealed poor general condition and bilateral horizontal nystagmus. The animal died during transfer to a referral ophthalmologist. There is a history of retinal disease in a similar animal. Necropsy revealed thin body condition small focus of congestion in the left lung small white lesions throughout all lobes of the liver small amount of frank blood admixed with ingesta in the stomach multiple hyperemic erosions in the stomach small dark/black intraluminal and mucosal lesions in the small intestine liquid contents in the distal small intestine and marked bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy with large lymphoid aggregate deep to the pouch region that appears firm and contains areas of purulent discharge. A small amount of intracranial hemorrhage is present. Bilateral cataracts are noted.

HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA. This 23-year-old male green tree python was found at the bottom of its enclosure for the past few days. Temperature has been suboptimal. The snake ate two weeks earlier. Examination revealed caudal paresis flaccid muscle tone and lack of a righting reflex. Radiographs revealed opacities in the gastrointestinal tract consistent with fecal material and this material was manually extracted. The animal was found dead the next morning on the exhibit floor. This snake had been housed alone and had no history of other disease processes. Necropsy revealed multiple dark staining nodules in the lungs and the these tissues sank in formalin. Some bile staining around the gallbladder was noted a partially digested mouse was in the stomach a 2 cm. irregular mass surrounded the proximal small intestine and formed feces was in the colon.
EUTHANASIA SARCOMA SKULL MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 8-year-old female degu had a history of sarcoma over the skull. The animal recently became inappetent and inactive and was euthanized.

SEPTIC SALPINGITIS ACUTE SEPSIS. This approximately 3-year-old female forest dragon was found dead in its tank. Gross necropsy revealed thin body condition inspissated yolk adjacent to the spleen and liver a ruptured hole in the dorsal oviduct with yellow fibrinous membranes on the interior mucosa two nonshelled ova in the left oviduct tan kidneys with adherent yellow fibrin on their cranial poles adjacent to the ruptured oviduct and multifocal yellow masses within the liver.

CAPRINE ARTHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS. This approximately 9-year-old female goat was humanely euthanized. It was diagnosed with CAE after concern about months of enlarged and firm udder as well as lethargy and stiff ambulation. CBC demonstrated moderate leukopenia and lymphopenia along with anemia. At necropsy there were bilaterally enlarged mammary glands and swollen teat canals. There was marked mottling of most lung lobes except for the left caudal with mottling more pronounced in the right middle lung lobe. The lungs were wet to frothy and occasionally hemorrhagic on cut section. All sections of lung floated in formalin. The trachea contained much froth and aspirated rumen contents cranially. There was a very small amount of calculi within one area of the renal pelvis of one kidney.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS. This 8-year-old male whistling duck had a history of lameness. Severe periosteal bone formation and bony lysis were present in the distal femur and proximal tibiotarsus. Treatment was initiated; however the animal failed to respond and it was found dead. At necropsy ankylosis of the right stifle was present with severe periosteal proliferation and irregular joint surface.
DROWNING SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 5-year-old female duck was found dead floating in the pool. At necropsy the lungs were pale edematous and free water was present within the air sacs.

XANTHOMATOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female leopard gecko recently was noted to have weight loss but was still eating. Physical exam revealed a space occupying coelomic mass. Xanthomatosis was suspected and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed tissue that displaced the heart lungs and liver and the liver had multiple small white masses throughout the parenchyma. Female reproductive tract was identified and no coelomic fat stores were seen.
PULMONARY SHOCK. This 3-year-old female tanager was found dead in the exhibit pool. At necropsy the body was severely autolyzed and no gross lesions were identified.

YOLK COELOMITIS INTESTINAL PERFORATION. This 4-year-old female whistling duck was noted to be depressed and died when it was captured for examination. Necropsy revealed good body condition distended coelomic cavity multiple adhesions in the coelomic viscera purulent/hemorrhagic fluid throughout the coelomic cavity congested lungs a perforation of the intestine active folliculogenesis and hypertrophied uterus.

TRAUMA RENAL AND METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 12-year-old female scarlet ibis presented with acute recumbency weakness and a distended coelom. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Blood work prior to death revealed anemia elevated AST and CK hypoproteinemia and elevated calcium phosphorus and uric acid. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage in the right lung blood clot in the right caudal hepatic lobe large amounts of yellow coelomic fat and active folliculogenesis.

According to the history provided; this 9-year-old female alpaca was found down the evening of 10/15/17 and was taken to MSU VMC after failing to respond to treatment with banamine; baytril; ivermectin; and dexamethasone. On presentation at MSU; she was recumbent; unresponsive; hypothermic; tachycardic; and was breathing agonally. Ocular examination revealed an absent pupillary light response OS and positional nystagmus. Supportive treatment was unsuccessful; and she died on 10/17/17 and was submitted for necropsy and rabies testing the same day. An 87-kg female alpaca was necropsied 10/17/17. Autolysis was mild. An indwelling venous catheter was present in the right jugular vein. There was scant subcutaneous and visceral fat; and the animal had an overall body condition score of 3/9. The subcutaneous tissues over the mandible; inner thighs; and ventral abdomen were expanded by pale yellow gelatinous edema. There was red-tinged serous fluid in the peritoneum (300 mL) and thoracic cavity (80 mL). The pericardium contained approximately 5 mL of clear yellow thin fluid admixed with few white strands of fibrin. There were 10-15 0.3-0.5-cm irregular white foci in the left ventricular myocardium in the region of the aortic outflow tract. The lungs were mottled pink to dark red; wet; and oozed red serous fluid on cut section. Clusters of pinpoint to 1-mm diameter white round foci were scattered throughout the pleural surface of the right and left caudal lung lobes; consistent with endogenous lipid pneumonia. The cortex of the right kidney contained a focal 1-cm cyst. The jejunum contained dark red watery fluid digesta. There were formed fecal pellets in the colon. There were no other significant gross lesions. Body as a whole: Ventral subcutaneous edema Peritoneum; Thoracic cavity; Pericardium: Tricavitary effusion Lungs: Pulmonary edema; Multifocal subpleural lipogranulomas Kidney: Focal renal cortical cyst Open Comments: This alpaca had significant tricavitary effusion and edema for which the inciting cause was unclear. Such effusion and edema commonly form secondary to endoparasitism in alpacas and other small ruminants; however; no parasites were seen on gross examination. The endogenous lipid pneumonia and renal cyst are considered incidental findings in this case. Histopathologic examination of tissues and results will be released in a final report. Rabies testing results will be released in a separate report. Michelle Magagna; DVM Brain: rabies negative Comments: Histopathologic examination of tissues and additional diagnostic testing is pending. Results will be released in a final report. Michelle Magagna; DVM Representative sections of brain; trachea; lung; tongue; heart; thymus; spleen; liver; kidney; adrenal gland; pituitary gland; pancreas; thyroid gland; urinary bladder; skeletal muscle; esophagus; stomach; small intestine; and large intestine were examined. Autolysis was mild. The myocardium of the left ventricle contained multifocal locally extensive areas of myofiber necrosis and mineralization. Necrotic myofibers were characterized by hypereosinophilia; sarcolemmic clumping; loss of cross-striations; fragmentation; and nuclear pyknosis. Additionally within this region; there were occasional foci of fibrosis that variably separated and individualized myofibers. In sections of liver; the majority of centrilobular and midzonal hepatocytes contained a single large discrete lipid vacuole or multiple smaller lipid vacuoles; consistent with macro- and microvacuolar degeneration. Within the renal cortex; there were few focal aggregates of dilated tubules lined by attenuated cuboidal epithelium with increased cytoplasmic basophilia; consistent with tubular regeneration. Dilated tubules occasionally contained intraluminal eosinophilic proteinaceous fluid; and were variably surrounded by increased amounts of interstitial fibrosis. In one section; the renal cortex and medulla were regionally compressed by an expansile; well-demarcated cyst lined by flattened rectangular epithelial cells and surrounded by a thin fibrous capsule. Few tubules in the cortex and medulla were focally mineralized. In the lung; bronchiole-associated lymphoid tissue was multifocally mildly prominent and occasionally contained aggregates of foamy; vacuolated macrophages with intracytoplasmic brown; crystalline pigment. Few small aggregates of similar macrophages were scattered throughout the subpleural pulmonary interstitium. Alveolar septa were diffusely congested. Moderate numbers of eosinophils were scattered throughout the superficial and deep lamina propria of the small intestine. There were Heart; left ventricle: Multifocal myocardial necrosis; mineralization; and fibrosis Liver: Centrilobular to midzonal vacuolar degeneration Kidney: Multifocal tubular regeneration; Focal renal cyst; Mild multifocal tubular mineralization Lung: Mild BALT hyperplasia and pneumoconiosis Suspect nutritional cardiomyopathy Comments: The histologic lesions in the heart are most suggestive of a nutritional myopathy; such as is commonly seen with vitamin E/selenium deficiency. The grossly observed effusion and edema likely developed secondary to heart failure. The vacuolar degeneration in the liver was thought to represent hypoxic change resulting from terminal cardiac shock. The remainder of the lesions represent subclinical processes or incidental findings. Qualitative fecal analysis and liver vitamin E levels and trace mineral analysis are pending. Results will be reported as an addendum. Michelle Magagna; DVM Liver trace mineral analysis : Mildly elevated selenium (3.83 ug/g; reference interval 1-3 ug/g) Liver vitamin E levels: 316.18 ug/g Comments: While vitamin E and selenium appeared to be mildly elevated; these values are most suggestive of recent supplementation and likely do not reflect long-standing; established vitamin E/selenium levels in this alpaca. The histologic the histologic lesions in the heart remain consistent with white muscle disease; caused by vitamin E/selenium deficiency. This completes all diagnostic testing for this case. Michelle Magagna; DVM

EUTHANASIA PITUITARY ADENOMA MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY RHINITIS KERATITIS STRESS. This 2-year/8-month-old male rat was humanely euthanized. It had a history of gradual deterioration chronic disease and nasal exudate. At necropsy the rat had adequate body muscling and fat reserves. The haircoat was roughened and somewhat thinned. There were slight amounts of dry nasal exudate present bilaterally. The nasal conchae were yellow to green. The lungs were collapsed and mildly congested dorsally. The liver contained an adult cestode in a cyst on the left lateral hepatic lobe. The cestode was submitted for identification. The pituitary gland seemed quite large (2-4 mm. in diameter) and was hemorrhagic.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male meerkat had a one-year history of suspected hepatic tumor and more recently has developed a facial swelling and weight loss. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified thin body condition a small wound on the left caudal muzzle area in the area of a previously treated abscess 10 ml. of hemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity dark red left lungs compared to right lungs a moderate amount of hemorrhagic pericardial fluid a 10 cm. in diameter tumor in the left hepatic lobe and three smaller tumors up to 2 cm. in greatest dimension in the right and middle lobes. The quadrate lobe had a cystic green colored mass that appeared to be filled with bile. Muscles were atrophic. A mucoid discharge was from the left eye.

CHRONIC SALPINGITIS RETAINED OVA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old chicken had marked weight loss. There was myiasis adjacent to the vent. The coelom was distended with a left-sided caudal coelomic mass. The animal was humanely euthanized. At gross necropsy a large mass arising from the oviduct was found. This contained numerous inspissated ova.

UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA OBSTRUCTIVE UROCYSTITIS DUODENAL PERFORATION WITH PERITONITIS CHOLEMIC NEPHROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female goat had been hospitalized for lethargy and recurrent urinary tract infection from which Corynebacterium was isolated. It initially responded but then decompensated in the hospital had hypophosphatemia and anemia leukocytosis hyperglobulinemia and elevated fibrinogen. Supportive care was administered but the goat did not respond and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation a soiled coat and skin on the rear legs and perianal region. The lungs were mottled. Mild accumulation of yellow pericardial fluid was noted and the aortic valve had some endocardiosis. An adhesion of the gallbladder to the stomach and liver was noted. No fluid was in the uterine stump (previous hydrometra). The urinary bladder was muddy thickened hyperemic and no stones or masses were noted.

SEPTICEMIA COLITIS FATTY LIVER. This approximately 4-year-old male monitor was found dead in pool. The female was found dead two days previously. There was no previous indication of illness. This exhibit was next to an exhibit where three sanzinia died within one week of another. At necropsy there was a scar over the left stifle. There was adequate fat. The liver was long and elongate. It was slightly pale and had a pronounced dark variegated pattern. The heart was pale pink and had red petechiae primarily over the base region. The kidneys were yellow and had small pinpoint white foci present in several areas. There was ingesta present in the colon but none in the upper gastrointestinal tract. Both lungs were edematous and had frothy liquid. There may have been a small amount of foreign material present in the lungs. There were arthritic type lesions in the left stifle.

LOBAR BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 18-year-old female beaded lizard was found dead in its enclosure and had no prior medical problems. Necropsy revealed moderate amounts of adipose tissue in the coelom some yellow/red tissue with a reticulate pattern near the heart interpreted as lung and the tissue contained yellow nodules on the cranial portion. Multiple 1 mm. clear gelatinous soft nodules associated with blood vessels were in the pectoral girdle near the heart base. One segment of the small intestine has deeply hyperemic mucosa. Multiple well-developed yellow follicles were in each ovary. The liver was pink and friable.

EYELID MELANOMA WITH METASTASIS BILIARY CYST ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 10-year-old male rabbit died while anesthetized for removal of a mass under the right eye. Necropsy revealed scarring on the hocks from previous episodes of “sore hock” a cluster of many cystic structures surrounding the liver and adhered to the lobes blood filled trachea wet lungs that oozed blood on cut surface and no other abnormalities other than a mass on the lower palpebra.

PARVOVIRAL ENTERITIS. This 12-week-old female captive bred Mexican wolf had a 2-3 day history of illness and died. It is from a litter of 10 pups. All pups were vaccinated at eight weeks of age and treated for parasites (ivermectin and topical flea prevention product). The pups were revaccinated at 12 weeks of age with the same products. The pups then developed loose stool/diarrhea with depression and two died. All pups were lethargic dehydrated and most had profuse hemorrhagic diarrhea. Blood work revealed profound leukopenia with toxic change. Fecal exams revealed coccidia. Necropsy of this pup revealed thin body condition watery pale green colored liquid in the intestine hemorrhage on the serosal surfaces of the intestines sections of sloughing mucosa throughout the intestine and an accentuated lobular pattern in the liver.

EUTHANASIA MYCOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL STEATOSIS SHOCK. This 10-year-old male kangaroo had been treated for an abscess in the paw. Paraparesis developed progressing to recumbency. The animal’s condition continued to deteriorate and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a small wound on the left forelimb appeared to be healing. Marked edema was noted in the right hind limb. The left axillary lymph node was enlarged. The spleen contained numerous 1-3 mm. round white lesions.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS COELOMITIS SPONDYLOSIS OSTEITIS DEFORMANS. This 18-year-old female viper was found dead. The animal has a recent history of poor condition. At necropsy moderate cachexia was noted. Bony enlargements were present on the proximal ribs and ventral spine. Adipose tissue stores were atrophic. The large bowel contained watery feces and the colonic mucosa was hyperemic. The uterus contained foul smelling fluid and necrotic debris.

INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS ATELECTASIS SHOCK. This 2-month-old ferret was found dead. The litter had been treated for coccidiosis. At necropsy the animal was dehydrated. Lymph nodes were enlarged. The GI tract contained minimal ingesta.

MYOCARDITIS SPLENITIS HEPATITIS SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 4-year-old female falcon was found lethargic and was treated with fluids and antibiotics; however the animal died shortly after an exam. CPR was attempted but was unsuccessful. At gross necropsy the liver was enlarged and dark red.

AMYLOIDOSIS EMACIATION. This 10-year-old male Speke’s gazelle was examined due to weight loss of 60 days duration with partial inappetence of several days duration. Blood work reveled renal failure and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed small misshapen kidneys and possibly a thickened or inflamed pancreas. The animal ha d a very high titer for Toxoplasma.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE LEIOMYOSARCOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 2-year-old female hedgehog had a history of hematuria. A large mass was identified in the uterus. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was pale. Multiple solid white masses were present in the uterus.

SUPPURATIVE OSTEOARTHRITIS AND TENOSYNOVITIS FRACTURES MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS SHOCK. This approximately 22-year-old male bat was diagnosed with a fractured left tibia and fibula and returned to exhibit where it seemed to do well. It was subsequently found on the floor of the exhibit upside-down and died. Necropsy revealed swelling at the fracture site (right tibia). No sign of bone healing was noted radiographically. Various luxations and calluses were noted in the phalanges (typical of the species in this enclosure). Cataract was noted in the left eye.

EUTHANASIA PREGNANCY TOXEMIA HEPATOPATHY ENDOMETRITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This female 7-year/4-month-old pygmy goat was humanely euthanized. It had a recent history of serosanguineous vaginal discharge and restlessness. It was pregnant and had a kid positioned at the pelvic inlet but the cervix was not dilated. CBC showed a mild leukocytosis with a left shift. Chemistry showed hypocalcemia. A c-section was performed and two dead feti were removed. The goat was treated with intravenous and subcutaneous calcium gluconate. Twelve hours postoperative the goat became progressively lethargic anorexic hypoglycemic and hypothermic. The skin over the udder turned purple. Sections of lymph node were frozen for tuberculosis test if necessary. At necropsy there was serosanguineous fluid within the pleural cavity. There was excessive body fat. There were 40-50 ml. of yellow translucent fluid within the abdominal cavity. The lungs were mottled purple/red. The rumen was full of ingesta. The uterine incision was intact. The uterine lining was covered with what appeared to be necrotic placental material. The udder was purple and filled with foul smelling milk. Sections of liver and lymph node were frozen for future use if needed.

PARAMYXOVIRUS-LIKE LESIONS PROLIFERATIVE ENTERITIS. This approximately 20-year-old gopher snake had a history of chronic bilateral cataract formation and corneal opacities and had been in an enclosure that housed several rattlesnakes that had recently died due to paramyxovirus infection. It was recently examined after laying multiple eggs and thin body condition was noted with worn rostral maxilla chronic ocular opacities a focal mass effect in the caudal coelom and hemorrhagic mucoid diarrhea with numerous flagellates. Blood work revealed hyperproteinemia hyperglobulinemia and hypercholesterolemia and radiographs were unremarkable. Supportive care was administered and the diarrhea resolved and the snake appeared to have an improved appetite and energy level but then refused its last three feedings and was found dead. Necropsy revealed flocculent white material in the lung and the parenchyma was congested. Suspected thrombi were present in blood vessels to the pancreas and gastrointestinal tract. A mild amount of serous effusion was in the caudal coelom. Gray viscous mucus was in the oral cavity and pyloric region of the stomach. The liver was congested. The pancreas was mottled white yellow and tan. The spleen was pale. A large amount of sludge was in the gallbladder. Desiccated yolks were in the right oviduct and multiple cystic and firm round nodules were in the left oviduct. Several foci of yellow granular material were noted in the kidneys. The thyroid was multilobulated and had a cystic appearance. Bilateral pinpoint white corneal opacities were noted centrally and cataracts were present. Muscles were atrophic.

DROWNED. This greater than 5-year-old male fruit bat was found dead in a pond at the Tropical Forest. Its only medical history is fracture of the left humerus in February 1997. Necropsy revealed good body condition and a small hard swelling on the distal left radius. Postmortem radiographs revealed a 0.5 cm. incomplete oblique fracture in this region. A moderate amount of red fluid was in the thoracic cavity. All lung lobes were dark and mottled but did not appear edematous. The liver appeared abnormally enlarged but with normal color and morphology. The kidneys appeared bilaterally enlarged. Enlarged tubular structures were detected in the coelomic cavity and were possibly normal structures.

EMACIATION. This greater than 10-year-old Jamaican fruit bat had a one week history of presenting on the ground in body condition and appeared to respond to supportive care. The animal was transferred back to the group but was found dead. There was no history of evidence or evidence of trauma at necropsy. The animal had lost 8 gm. after being reunited with the group and necropsy revealed apparent emaciation.

ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) TRAUMATIC CELLULITIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female duck had a history of chronic arthritis was lying on its keel and a pressure sore developed. The sore progressively worsened despite medical management and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

TRAUMA (HBC) ATRIAL SEPTAL DEFECT (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS AND TREMATODIASIS VISCERAL LARVAL MIGRANS CHRONIC INTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS. This approximately 6-month-old Florida panther cub was hit by a car on 6/17. The animal was easily immobilized was triaged at an animal specialty hospital and examination revealed moderate to severe pulmonary contusions ischial and pubic pelvic fractures that were considered nonsurgical. The cub was tachypneic with moderate respiratory effort depending on level of stress. Following stabilization the animal was transferred to White Oak for further care. The cub was weak did not resist shifting had rapid respirations with moderate effort and a serosanguineous drainage from the right nostril. The animal was monitored throughout the night and was alive at morning check but found dead one hour later. Necropsy revealed good body condition adequate hydration and pink mucous membranes abrasions and excoriations were on the left medial stifle area right flank fold and right ventral perineal region. Superficial lacerations were on the right tail base. No palpable fractures of long bones were identified. A moderate serosanguineous discharge was from both nostrils and in the oral cavity. Subcutaneous and muscular hemorrhage was present in the perineal and caudal pelvic region especially on the right side and associated with a displaced fracture of the right ischium. Hemorrhage was in the right coxofemoral joint. A small amount of serosanguineous fluid was in the pleural cavity. Adipose stores were present. The spleen was dark substantial serosanguineous fluid and foam were in the major bronchi and trachea and when palpated flood fluid into the trachea. The right pulmonary lobe was uniformly dark red and multiple areas of hemorrhage were noted. The right pulmonary lobes oozed flood and foam. The left middle and cranial pulmonary lobes were firm consolidated and appeared hepatified in texture. On cut surface these lobes oozed fluid and airways contained purulent exudate. Sections of the left middle and cranial pulmonary lobes sank in formalin. A 4-5 mm. atrial septal defect was present in the foramen ovale. Food was in the stomach (deer skin and muscle with bone fragments) and the entire intestinal tract was full of digesta 20 ml. of clear golden urine was in the urinary bladder and ovaries were immature. Pseudomonas flourescens and Klebsiella pneumoniae were isolated from lung.

SEPSIS. This 14-year-old female green tree python had a history of abrasions on the mandible and possible bubbling from the nares. Supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed a small scab at the rostral mandible adequate fat stores consolidation of the cranial aspect of the lung and no other gross abnormalities.

TRAUMA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 1-year-old male parrot was found in wobbly condition unable to fly but would crash land and appeared to be ataxic and unable to perch. No obvious abnormalities other than a 2 mm. bald spot on the head were noted during physical examination. Supportive care was administered but the bird died. Necropsy revealed a linear full thickness laceration in the skull and the caudal abdominal skin and subcutis on the left side were reddened. Hemorrhage was noted in the coelomic cavity deep to this region.

EMACIATION LYMPHOID DEPLETION MESENTERIC TORSION HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 17-year-old koala presented with loose stool 10 days earlier received supportive care but developed watery stool was treated aggressively for suspected typhlocolitis and initially responded with pelleted stool and increase in appetite but then slowly developed lethargy lack of appetite and no stool. A barium study revealed no blockages. The animal had no overt signs of discomfort but would sit in a ball instead of in a tree and upright. It developed substantial depression in the late afternoon and was found dead the following morning. This animal had a history of advanced degenerative joint disease involving the left elbow and right femoral head. Necropsy revealed subcutaneous edema between the shoulder blades (fluid administration) a moderate volume of yellow fluid in the peritoneal and pericardial cavities emphysema on the edges of the pulmonary lobes and some edema in the lungs. The left lung was congested. Some foci of green discoloration were present within the pulmonary parenchyma. The pancreas was reddened. A 1 cm. transmural lesion was present in the gastric wall. Two mesenteric torsions were identified one at the ileocecocolic junction associated with hemorrhage and gas accumulation in the intestine proximal to the torsion and deflated cecum with minimal food material. An additional lesion in the cecum was suspected to be residual typhlocolitis (second torsion not described). The eyes had opacification of the lenses.

MAXILLARY OSTEOMYELITIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old female southern gerenuk had been receiving treatment for nasal discharge vaginal discharge depression and inappetence. The patient’s condition declined and purulent right-sided nasal discharge and right mandibular swelling were noted. The animal became ataxic did not respond to supportive care was found in lateral recumbency with open-mouth breathing and muscle rigidity and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed purulent exudate in the right maxillary sinus originating from the premolar #3 and molars #1-2. The exudate extended caudally into the sinus to the orbit and was associated with osteolysis of the rostral orbit. Some endocardiosis was noted in the left atrioventricular valve and aortic valve. Gingival recession and pocketing consistent with periodontal disease was noted in the right maxillary arcade.

NECROTIZING GLOSSITIS LOW-GRADE SEPSIS EMACIATION CHRONIC RUMENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female greater kudu has given birth to several viable calves. The animal developed a “rough” looking appearance in the past year and was in thin body condition. The kudu subsequently gave birth to a calf that presented for having a swollen face and difficulty nursing. Necrotizing stomatitis is identified in the calf and euthanasia was performed. The adult was observed to have a swollen face two days ago and an immobilization revealed a mass-like lesion at the base of the tongue. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. No adipose stores were identified. A pedunculated growth was noted at the pole of the left adrenal gland and a 1 cm. yellow-colored well-encapsulated region was in the left renal cortex. Whipworms were identified in the cecum.

SUPPURATIVE MENINGITIS THYROID ADENOCARCINOMAS NEPHROSCLEROSIS. This 14.5-year-old female agouti had been acting abnormally in the evening at closing time but did not appear critical. It was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed bruising and hair loss on the left knee bruising under the mandible hair loss and thinning over the right hip inactive ovaries small kidneys with indentations and round red cysts or clots. Small red cysts filled with blood were present throughout both kidneys and on the surface. The spleen had small white spots protruding from the surface. Both thyroids were enlarged and the right thyroid had a white “cortex”. A firm white nodule was present in the lungs. Meninges over the cerebellum and cerebrum were dark red.

ENDOCARDIOSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA COLONIC CARCINOMA IN SITU CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HEPATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 16-year-old female potbelly pig was euthanized due to hyporexia weight loss lethargy and a recent seizure-like episode. Additionally the animal had a systolic heart murmur. At necropsy multiple masses were identified including papillomatous masses extending from the colonic mucosa masses associated with the right adrenal gland and enlarged pituitary.

EUTHANASIA SEPTIC PERITONITIS SUSPECT LEFT-SIDED HEART FAILURE TRAUMA. This 1-year and 8-month-old male black-tailed prairie dog was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was a puncture wound through the left abdomen with prolapse of abdominal organs. There are multiple firm structures in the abdomen one was free floating and one was embedded in the omentum. Urinary bladder had mild hemorrhage on the mucosa. The secondary sex glands appeared abnormal. The heart was subjectively enlarged.

EUTHANASIA GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDITIS BILIARY CYST. This 16-year-old male leopard had been under treatment for renal disease. Anorexia developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy cysts were present in the liver. Kidney was yellow and firm.

CARDIOMYOPATHY TRAUMA. This 17-year-old male fruit bat was found dead in incubator. It was found in the exhibit on the wall low to the ground and was brought to the hospital. It was placed on antibiotics (Baytril) and put in an incubator. It seemed very active and eating well for four days. At necropsy the left wing was bloody and the joint was swollen. The skin peeled off the wing. The liver was very yellow.
EUTHANASIA ENCEPHALITIS. This 1-year/10-month-old female rattlesnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of neurologic disease of chronic duration.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 7-year-old male rainbow lorikeet is one of multiple birds from this group that have died in the past two weeks. Necropsy revealed ulcers in the gut and associated coelomitis.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA. This 12-year-old male Guam rail had a history of elevated bile acids a few weeks prior to being found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition absence of the right eye from a previous traumatic injury and associated enucleation full gallbladder empty alimentary tract and male reproductive tract.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL GOUT VISCERAL GOUT GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 30-year-old male flamingo was found dead. At necropsy white material was present on the air sacs and pericardium as well as the serosa of the liver. The feet contained several large calluses.

HEMANGIOSARCOMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS THYROID TUMORS CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY RENA TUBULAR NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4.5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of weight loss and lethargy and examination identified an enlarged multinodular left kidney. Exploratory surgery revealed multiple dark purple masses in the kidneys a similar nodule in the middle of the spleen and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

BACTERIAL HEPATITIS RUMENITIS PYELONEPHRITIS PNEUMONIA. This 8-month-old female gerenuk had a history of deep wound in the caudal thigh which had apparently healed. Recently diarrhea and weight loss developed. Serum phosphorus and calcium were low. The animal was found dead. At necropsy a white caseous lesion was present in the right and left hepatic lobes. A similar lesion was also present in the diaphragm.

FOLLICULAR DEGENERATION WITH LOCALIZED YOLK COELOMITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 9-year-old female frilled lizard was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed free yolk in the coelomic cavity and mature follicles.

EUTHANASIA FRACTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYCOTIC BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 3-year-old male gazelle had a prior history of pleuropneumonia that responded to long-term antimicrobial therapy. The animal’s condition had been improving but recently was found with a fracture of the radius and ulna. The fracture was surgically repaired; however vascular supply to the distal limb was compromised and the repair was unsuccessful. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a transverse fracture of the proximal radius and ulna with associated soft tissue hemorrhaging was identified. Numerous adhesions were present between the left lung pericardium and left body wall. A single abscess was present in the dorsal right lung. The tissues examined were grossly normal.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS YOLK COELOMITIS RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMATOUS HYPERPLASIA. This 24-year-old male African spoonbill presented with weakness and emaciation associated with a retained egg and died a few minutes after the egg was removed. Necropsy revealed atrophied pectoral muscles and prominent keel protrusion with partial prolapse of the cloaca small spleen dark pigmentation throughout the lungs ingesta in the gizzard congested and thickened uterus with brown fluid and clumps of white material (caseous exudate?). Eggshell fragments are in the distal uterus/proximal cloaca. Some partially developed and atretic follicles are noted in the ovary.

TRACHEAL TREMATODIASIS PULMONARY TREMATODIASIS HEPATITIS ENTERITIS. This 6-year-old female motmot had a history of air sac trematodiasis. The animal presented with marked dyspnea. Endoscopy revealed a mucoid mass in the trachea containing trematode ova. The animal was found dead the following day. At necropsy two mucoid masses were identified in the trachea. The right main stem bronchus was completely occluded by flukes. Flukes were also noted in lung tissue.

YOLK COELOMITIS ECTOPIC EGG CARDIAC XANTHOMATOSIS. This 19-year-old female python refused its last few feedings. The temperature in the exhibit had dropped recently but no other changes were noted. The animal was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed fair body condition no skin abnormalities and normal eyes and oral cavity. Both oviducts were filled with a large amount of purulent material that appeared to be resorbing eggs and the cranial aspects of both lungs were very red. A ping pong ball-sized mass was located on the serosal side of the stomach near the pylorus and the mucosa in this area was slightly reddened and possibly ulcerated. The heart valves appeared possibly thickened.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL MINERALIZATION PULMONARY MINERALIZATION BRONCHOPNEUMONIA INANITION. This 11-year-old female sheep presented with chronic weight loss and emaciation. At necropsy ascites was noted. Caseous abscesses were present in the cranial lung lobes.

Abdominal mass: Traumatized adipose (Granulomatous panniculitis) Urinary bladder: Chronic cystitis with urolithiasis Comment: The cause of the abdominal distension was not apparent; however; the mass was most likely the nodule of adipose tissue dissected by macrophages and fibrous connective tissue; most compatible with traumatic insult to the adipose. The urinary bladder appeared chronically irritated based on the degree of squamous metaplasia of the lining and the chronic inflammation. While very unlikely; an acid fast stain is pending to rule out a mycobacterial infection of the adipose tissue.

DISSEMINATED MICROGRANULOMATOSIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 8-year-old female tanager was found dead in exhibit. Necropsy revealed white speckles throughout the liver enlarged ventricular walls large gall bladder and empty stomach.

METASTATIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA. This 17-year-old female lizard had a distal limb amputation eight years earlier for a localized vascular anomaly probable benign hemangioma (G07-0339) causing anatomical deformity and ulcerations. Recently it had begun passing frank blood in its stool. Imaging revealed a large fluid-filled mass in the coelomic cavity. A small dermal mass with associated scale separation was on the right flank with a similar appearance to the hemangioma identified in previous years. Blood work identified severe anemia (PCV=4%). The animal was subsequently found dead. At necropsy the dermal mass ruptured when manipulated and was filled with blood. A 7 mm. mass was attached to the ventral coelomic wall and multiple apparent metastases were in both lungs. The liver spleen and pancreas were adhered into an indistinguishable mass in the mid coelomic cavity. Pinpoint tan foci were present on the serosal surface of the right hepatic lobe. The adhered foci appeared to be associated with an organized hematoma. A firm globoid mass was in the left hepatic lobe that was tan on cut surface and bulged on cut surface. A gelatinous brown mass was present in the bladder that resembled a blood clot.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 7-year-old female wallaby had a sudden onset of seizures progressing to a comatose state. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was mottled. Cream colored tissue replaced the normal hepatic tissue. The distal jejunum was dark and contained green or hemorrhagic contents. Dark hemorrhagic material was also present in the colon and cecum. Lungs were congested to hemorrhagic with large blood clots in the bronchi. A large calculus was present in the renal pelvis of the right kidney.

ANEMIA ERYTHROID ANOMALY CEPHALIC HEMORRHAGE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-year-old male duck developed an acute onset of weakness and was separated from the group. Examination revealed anemia and weakness with no evidence of metallic foreign body or sign of blood loss. The bird developed a coelomic effusion 48 hours into supportive care and 50 ml. of fluid was removed by coelomocentesis with material resembling uric acid crystals in the fluid. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition and a moderate amount of straw-colored coelomic fluid in the pericardial region and cranial thoracic air sacs. Hemorrhage was present in the right hepatic lobe on the surface (coelomocentesis) the heart was subjectively enlarged and flaccid with thin-walled atria and auricles and two irregular multilobulated tan cystic masses were within the cranial thoracic/cervical air sacs.

MYOCARDIAL HEMORRHAGE CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE HEMORRHAGIC ENTERITIS RENAL TUBULAR MINERALIZATION. This 5-year-old lory presented in distress and unable to stand. The animal died overnight. At necropsy feather loss and bruising were noted over the head. The right pectoral muscle was paler than the left and contained white streaks. Foci of hemorrhage were noted in the muscle of the cranial neck at the base of the skull. The liver was pale tan. The spleen was enlarged with focal areas of hemorrhage. Hemorrhage was noted on the pericardium of the heart and adjacent to the great vessels. Some segments of bowel were dark and contained dark red to black contents.

ENCEPHALITIS PROBABLE BAYLISASCARIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old male rabbit had been trapped in the wild and transported to the zoo to augment captive breeding efforts. The rabbit developed neurologic signs (ataxia) 24 hours after arrival but was eating and defecating normally. Examination revealed no abnormalities although acute phase protein was elevated. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed adequate fat stores normal ingesta throughout the alimentary tract and good body condition.
PNEUMONIA BACTERIAL HEPATITIS INTRAMUSCULAR SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 13-year-old male falcon was found dead. At necropsy the heart and liver were mildly enlarged.

NONSUPPURATIVE MENINGOENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 9-month-old female captive bred lion had a six month history of illness and was euthanized for humane reasons. The animal presented with acute blindness comatose and hyperthermic on 8/25/98. The lion improved significantly within 24 hours but remained blind and ataxic. It had bouts of pyrexia and leukocytosis over the following week but subsequently remained clinically normal other than blindness and occasional ataxia of three months duration. Due to lack of improvement the animal was euthanized. An MRI confirmed lesions of the cerebral cortex in the caudal suprasylvian sulcus and marginal sulcus bilaterally. The animal had a fourfold increase in canine distemper titers and negative titers for toxoplasmosis FeLV FIV and FIP.

CUTANEOUS ULCERATION WITH MIXED INTRALESIONAL BACTERIA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 6-year-old female black tree monitor had a history of a 3-4 cm. ulcerative skin lesion on the left dorsum and previous biopsy of the ventral abdominal skin. Culture of the skin lesion on the left dorsum recovered Stenotrophomonas maltophilia a coagulase negative Staphylococcus sp. and no fungal growth. The animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy confirmed extensive coelomic fat pads and a diffusely pale liver.

BRAIN TUMOR TESTICULAR HAMARTOMA CHRONIC UROGENITAL INFLAMMATION CATARACT EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male captive bred hedgehog was euthanized following a one month period of weight loss loss of right hind limb function and a brief period of lateral recumbency and thrashing behavior.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA SPLENIC METASTASIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 4-year-old female hedgehog was found dead without premonitory signs. At gross necropsy the internal organs were moderately autolyzed. The liver was mottled and swollen and contained three firm tan 2-5 mm. diameter masses. The lungs and intestine were dark purple.

ATHEROSCLEROSIS EGG BOUND PULMONARY SHOCK. This 1-year-old female parakeet was examined for acute egg binding and a 1 cm. egg was found in the caudal coelom. Supportive care was administered but the bird died 10 minutes later. Necropsy identified some feather loss over the back of the neck a 1 cm. firm egg in the shell gland pale liver active folliculogenesis and no other abnormalities. The egg fractured during manual manipulation.

BACTERIAL/AMOEBIC COLITIS DROWNED. This greater than 4-year-old female basilisk had been transferred into the anaconda exhibit one day earlier was observed swimming in the exhibit pool while it was filling in the morning and was found dead on the bottom of the pool later. Necropsy revealed some chronic scabbing and scarring over the rostrum and complete obstruction of both nares. Body mass and adipose stores appeared adequate. Numerous active ovarian follicles were noted as well as a few chronic granulomas with thick capsules and laminated core coagulums. Clear colorless froth was in the lungs. The liver had brown/tan lobular parenchyma. The stomach was empty. A large area of irregular raised proliferative mucosa with hemorrhage and ulcers was noted in the colon.

HISTIOCYTIC ILEOTYPHILITIS FIBRINOUS SPLENITIS. This 2-year-old rabbit had been inappetent and clinically normal the previous day. It was found dead in the morning. It had a history of being off its pellets a few months before but that had resolved without incident. Necropsy revealed obesity congestion of the dependent lung fatty liver fecal pellets in the distal colon and a small granuloma in the caudal intra-abdominal fat.
ABSCESSES SKIN. This 1-year-old female opossum was euthanized due to extensive walled off abscessation of the pouch and mammary tissue.

MINERALIZATION STOMACH AND SECONDARY SEX GLAND. This greater than 3-year-old male hedgehog had a history of reduced appetite and ongoing weight loss. The animal died spontaneously and was refrigerated 72 hours prior to necropsy. Necropsy revealed apparent gastric ulcers and enlarged prostates.

LYMPHOMA RUMINORETICULITIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male Speke’s gazelle developed acute severe lymphadenopathy and inappetence received supportive care with no response to treatment and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Lymph node aspirates had been consistent with lymphoma. Necropsy revealed enlargement of all peripheral lymph nodes and cavitary lymph nodes and mottled tan circular lesions in the spleen.

EUTHANASIA ARTHRITIS ENTERITIS HEPATITIS MYOSITIS CHRONIC PODODERMATITIS. This 17-year-old flamingo had a history of lameness which did not respond to treatment. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver was moderately friable.
OVARIAN HEMORRHAGE YOLK COELOMITIS ENTERITIS. This 2-year-old female skink was found dead. At necropsy a hemorrhagic mass was present in the coelomic cavity possibly arising from the ovary.

ARTICULAR GOUT DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE STRESS EUTHANASIA. This approximately 6-year-old male lizard has a two month history of mild lethargy and decreased mobility with mild joint swelling. Evaluation identified some old bone lesions and low vitamin D level when compared to conspecifics. Uric acid was also judged to be slightly high. Supportive care was administered with no improvement and aspirates suggested calcinosis circumscripta or calcinosis cutis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hyperemic skin in areas of prior aspiration necrosis of digits multiple subcutaneous tophi full urinary bladder chalky material lining the wall of the urinary bladder and male reproductive tract.

ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS WITH BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA MYCOTIC ENTERITIS. This 4.5-year-old frilled lizard had been clamped on by an armadillo several weeks earlier. The enclosure has also experienced cold temperatures in the last week. Supportive care was administered the animal responded but then died. Necropsy revealed blood on the top of the head bruised musculature of the ribs dark internal viscera discolored vent mucous membrane and evidence of friction from cage rubbing on the dorsal mouth.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA ESOPHAGEAL RHABDOMYOSARCOMA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL CONDITION BRONCHOALVEOLAR ADENOMA. This 14-year-old female Egyptian fruit bat had an approximately one-week history of weight loss and polyuria. The animal was diffusely icteric with hepatomegaly. The animal died spontaneously and perimortem blood work revealed hyperbilirubinemia regenerative anemia thrombocytopenia and mild elevations in ALP ALT and AST. At necropsy the animal was diffusely icteric with decreased muscling. There was bruising of the patagium. The lungs were pale the liver was severely enlarged and mottled and there is a soft tissue mass approximately 7 mm. in greatest dimension adjacent to the gallbladder.

EUTHANASIA ESOPHAGITIS. This 10-year-old female boa was humanely euthanized. It had a history of anorexia and bloody discharge from the mouth two weeks prior to euthanasia. There was no response to supportive care and antibiotic therapy. At necropsy the lungs appeared diffusely hemorrhagic.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA VASCULITIS MYOCARDITIS ENCEPHALITIS CESTODIASIS INANITION. This 20-year-old kingsnake was found dead. At necropsy thick yellow fluid was present in the pericardium. Kidneys were diffusely white. The spleen was enlarged and had a large white mass caudal to the spleen.

EUTHANASIA CATARACT ADENOMYOSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS GINGIVAL HYPERPLASIA. This 6.5-year-old female hedgehog had a history of cataracts uterine mass and paresis. The animal was humanely euthanized.

INTESTINAL ROUND CELL TUMOR ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA ENDOMETRIAL STROMAL CELL SARCOMA NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4.5-year-old female hedgehog had a six-month history of hematuria and ultrasound identified renoliths in both kidneys and ureteroliths in both ureters. An abdominal mass was in the caudal abdomen of at least one month’s duration. Hematuria persisted and weight loss was identified. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a 2 cm. mass in the mesentery adjacent to the pancreas. The duodenum had a 1 cm. area of thickening adjacent to the mesenteric mass. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy two firm white masses were present in the uterine body and the right uterine horn. The liver was diffusely pale. Multiple 2-3 mm. pale areas were in the spleen. The kidneys were pale and had areas of hyperemia and the left pelvis was enlarged.

This parakeet presented for breathing hard.  There is a mass identified that appears to be part of the preen gland.  The bird was euthanized.  The mass is a fibrosarcoma with an extremely high mitotic rate of >20 per high-power field.  It has effaced bone sections.

EMACIATION FOLLICULAR DEGENERATION WITH BACTERIAL COLONIZATION AND LOW-GRADE SEPSIS. This 3-year-old female chameleon was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed emaciation old follicles or slugs in the coelom atrophied dark liver. The chameleon had a recent history of trauma and predation with loss of the eye and portions of the tail several weeks prior to death and never recovered well enough to maintain although recently had started to eat.

PANCREATIC ADENOCARCINOMA ATHROSCLEROSIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 50-year-old female gorilla died unexpectedly five days after oral surgery. The animal had been acting normal following surgery and appeared to be normal one hour prior to death. Necropsy revealed marked gaseous distention of the stomach and intestines and prolapse of the intestine through the rectum (possibly postmortem).

PULMONARY MINERALIZATION RENAL GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female captive bred pigeon had a one day history of illness and was euthanized for humane reasons. The animal had an acute onset of dyspnea. Necropsy revealed red discoloration of approximately 90% of the lungs and representative sections sank in formalin. No other abnormalities were detected other than thin body condition.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS OBESITY DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE CHRONIC ENTERITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS. This 5-year-old female chicken had a history of respiratory distress and died while being examined. Necropsy revealed black discoloration of the dorsal surface of the right tarsometatarsal/phalangeal joint hemorrhage in the liver indentations in the hepatic parenchyma flaccid left and right atria atrial enlargement dark red/purple lungs filled with blood dark colored left ovary a large thrombus in the trachea at the level of the syrinx and a 6 cm. long cystic structure filled with clear fluid and white particles attached near the cloaca.

ACUTE SYSTEM SHOCK MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS FIBROUS OSTEODYSTROPHY. This greater than 1-year-old male nine-banded armadillo is one of two animals under treatment for presumed hypovitaminosis D and hypocalcemia. There has been concern for malabsorption in both animals and Salmonella was cultured from feces associated with intermittent episodes of soft stool. The animal of this report had a malformation of the right forelimb and hind limb but this condition had not progressed. This animal had been receiving vitamin D supplementation and had been stable the last seven days with no overt signs of illness and was found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and several areas of cutaneous congestion in the right forelimb and right anterior portion of the armor. Bones appear to but more easily than expected. A small amount of clear fluid was in the thoracic cavity and pericardial sac. The pericardium was adhered to the costal pleura caudoventrally and in an area resembling thymus. Myocardium and skeletal muscle seem paler than normal and liver was more friable than expected. Adrenal glands seemed large but were symmetrical. The duodenum was darker than the remainder of the small intestinal tract and possibly more friable.

ENTERITIS SEPTICEMIA INTESTINAL TORSION INTUSSUSCEPTION. This 2-year-old female tamarin died. It presented with acute onset of extreme lethargy and foaming at the mouth. It appeared unable to stay awake. Blood work revealed extreme hypoglycemia and dehydration. Fluids and dextrose were administered under anesthesia and the tamarin went into cardiac arrest and died shortly following recovery. At necropsy there were adequate body fat stores and muscling. Both ovaries appeared enlarged light tan with dark brown speckling scattered across the serosal surface. The central area of both ovaries appeared dark red on cut surface. The uterine body was swollen. There was evidence of early pregnancy. There was a small focal area of hemorrhage noted along the right cardiac side (postmortem cardiocentesis). The stomach and intestines were empty. There were petechiae at the mucosal and serosal surfaces of the duodenum. There was an intussusception of the small intestine at approximately 0.2 in. proximal to the cecum. When the intestine was withdrawn from the intussusception there was a 180° intestinal torsion present. The affected bowel was only slightly edematous and was pink to dark red. There was congestion of the associated vasculature.
ENTERITIS NEPHRITIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 8-year-old male pochard was found dead. No significant lesions were identified at gross necropsy.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) RENAL NECROSIS (RESEMBLING PAPILLARY NECROSIS) INTESTINAL MASS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female tiger had a one-year history of difficulty eating and also had been having problems walking and getting traction as well as having difficulty rising. The cat recently fell in the moat and her head was submerged several times. The cat had a difficult time getting out of the moat. The tiger experienced signs of cognitive dysfunction with anxiety confusion and aggression towards perceived objects that were not there. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a few fractured teeth some dental calculus and gingivitis atrophied epaxial muscles worn nails on all paws and some hemorrhage on the left rear digit #3 nail. The left ventricular wall seemed somewhat thickened. Some bullae were noted at the tips of the lung. A follicular cyst was in the left ovary and a small amount of fluid was in both uterine horns. Adipose stores were abundant. The adrenal glands appeared small. A 3-4 cm. intramural abscess was found in the jejunum that contained yellow nonodorous purulent material.
COLITIS SHOCK. This 12.5-year-old duck was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a large quantity of feces was present in the cloaca.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ABOMASITIS ENTEROCOLITIS AND RUMINORETICULITIS EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old female impala had a history of bilateral tarsal infusion weight loss and lameness and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified swelling of both tarsi associated with excessive joint fluid accumulation. Body condition was thin. The right lung had congestion attributed to penmate trauma (kicked by zebra). Cysts were in both ovaries. The left uterine horn was swollen and had clear fluid. An omental hernia was in the intercostal space between T11-12 on the right side attributed to a gore wound three years earlier. Some lingual points were on the rear molars. Well-digested foodstuffs were throughout the alimentary tract. There was loss of articular cartilage on both tarsal joints with osteophyte formation and possible joint mouse in the left tarsus.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC ENTEROCOLITIS WITH LYMPHANGIECTASIA. This 44-year-old male gorilla was euthanized due to immobility and severity of chronic arthritis that did not respond to treatment.
