Necropsy revealed severe generalized osteoarthritis fluid accumulation and adhesions in the abdominal cavity multiple missing teeth gingival hyperplasia multiple masses in the appendix and cecum a melanotic mass in the urinary bladder bilateral testicular adhesions and a unilateral testicular mass.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) NEPHROSCLEROSIS AND TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS RETINAL DEGENERATION EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female leopard had been slightly off the last few months with variable appetite and was less willing to interact with keepers. It had increased drinking in the last 4-5 months. The cat became depressed moved little and had a poor appetite the last three days which appeared to improve with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The cat had been treated for dilated cardiomyopathy and this condition responded well to cardiac medications. Follow-up blood work identified very high blood urea nitrogen and creatinine acidosis and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed abundant adipose stores heavy calculus on the teeth areas of irregular reddening in the lungs 8 ml. of blood-tinged pericardial fluid whitish epicardium several small areas of fluid-filled cystic lesions in hepatic lobes congested pancreas pale kidneys with scattered white pinpoint foci on the surfaces mild to moderate congestion of the mucosa of the small intestine cataracts in both eyes and no other gross remarkable findings.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA RENAL MINERALIZATION THYROID FOLLICULAR CYST. This 11-year-old female goat was found dead. At necropsy follicular cysts were noted in the thyroid. Serous atrophy of fat was noted in the pericardium. Lungs were heavy and wet.

ANESTHETIC RELATED DEATH ENDOCARDIOSIS CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA VENTRICULITIS. This approximately 13-year-old female duck died under anesthesia. It was diagnosed with a cardiac murmur in March. It presented on July 2nd weak dyspneic tachypneic and probably in shock. At necropsy there was severe consolidation of the left lung with an abscess. There was a large firm pink mass in the right lung extending caudally to the cranial aspect of the kidney and appeared to engulf the kidney. The cranial abdominal air sac on the right side was filled with dark yellow thick material. An impression smear revealed mononuclear cell proliferation. Liver was enlarged and pale. The mitral valve was thickened. This duck had a history of chronic pododermatitis.

THYMOMA CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA THYROID FOLLICULAR TUMOR. This 2.5-year-old female rat has a history of chronic lower airway disease has positive Mycoplasma serology and has developed a mediastinal mass associated with worsening of the respiratory rate. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a 3.5 cm. mediastinal mass and compressed pulmonary lobes. Some multifocal black pinpointed lesions were on the serosal and cut surfaces of the lungs. The rat also had muscle wasting.

HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOCARCINOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 11-year-old female meerkat had a hepatocellular carcinoma removed on 10/20. The meerkat recovered well from surgery and was acting normal until 11/14 when a suspected seizure was observed. The meerkat recovered well on its own and seemed back to normal but was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed fair to good body condition but with some autolysis. A few small nodules were noted in the parenchyma of the left lateral hepatic lobe and the caudate lobe had a 1 cm. spherical pale pink nodule.

HEAD TRAUMA. This 5-year-old male Jamaican fruit bat was found dead with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed no external abnormalities male reproductive tract some hemorrhage around the calvarium and no other abnormalities.

ADENOCARCINOMA (LIVER OVARY KIDNEY). This 7-year-old female toad presented with discoloration of the ventral skin and legs. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy superficial skin was peeling from the ventrum and legs. A small quantity of serous fluid was present in the coelom. An irregular 2 mm. mass was noted on the epicardium. A large irregular mass was present in the ovaries adherent to the liver.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK URATE STASIS. This 2-year-old female mot mot was hospitalized and under treatment. The animal was found dead. Blood work suggested trauma with elevations of CPK and AST. At necropsy tan/white foci were present in the cranial dorsal lungs. Kidneys were enlarged and finely nodular.

Stomach: Marked lymphoplasmacytic gastritis and Helicobacter spp colonization Kidney: Moderate chronic multifocal to global membranous glomerulopathy; Moderate multifocal lymphoplasmacytic glomerulonephritis with interstitial fibrosis; Mild multifocal tubular degeneration and proteinosis Spleen: Feline systemic mastocytosis Anal sac: Modified sebaceous epithelioma Lung: Multifocal foam cell foci Skeletal muscle: Multifocal intramuscular sarcosystosis Liver: Locally-extensive hepatic telangiectasia Comments: The most significant lesions in this animal were severe gastritis and chronic renal disease. In captive cheetah populations; a severe gastritis associated with Helicobacter spp. infection is a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Given the severity of the lesion in the stomach; this lesion could be a main contributor to the clinical presentation of this animal. The changes in the kidney including the membranous changes in the glomeruli and the interstitial lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates are suggestive of chronic renal disease; however; the clinical significance of these changes is unclear based on histologic examination alone as there no obvious histologic evidence of chronic uremic changes observed in other tissues. There were multiple studies showed that many cheetahs develop glomerulopathy secondary to gastritis that can progress to renal failure; a leading cause of death among captive cheetahs. There was no microscopic lesion in the brain that could explain multiple episodes of seizure; however; given the poor body condition and chronic renal disease; there was a possibility of hypoglycemic seizure or uremic encephalopathy in this case. The histopathologic findings of the mass over the anal sac were consistent with modified sebaceous epithelioma; resembling hepatoid gland epithelioma in dogs. The spleen contained neoplastic mast cell proliferation; similar to described in domestic cats. The foam cell foci in the lung likely represent an incide

DISSECTING AORTIC ANEURYSM HYPERTENSION DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 36-year-old male western gorilla was diagnosed with fibrosing cardiomyopathy in 2010. The gorilla acutely collapsed and developed cardiac arrest in the morning. Resuscitation was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed fair to poor body condition with only a few fat stores present subcutaneously and in the abdomen. Both hips had severely reduced range of motion and could not be extended. The hips were in a permanently flexed position. A large amount of clotted blood filled the pericardial sac. The myocardium of the left ventricle is markedly thickened with associated significant reduction in the left ventricular filling volume. The left atrium was markedly enlarged and firm. An irregular round hole was found in the ventral aspect of the left atrium. The atrium was filled with gray/brown material that was firm and friable. The material was adhered to the endocardial surface of the atrium and the walls of the left atrium were thickened and firm. All other thoracic cavity contents were grossly normal. The entire omentum was adhered to the peritoneal body wall throughout the abdomen and all abdominal organs were grossly normal.

POSTANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS HEMOSIDEROSIS RENAL ADENOMA. This greater than 11-year-old female red billed leiothrix died during recovery from anesthesia. It was noted to not be doing right and was picked up off of a branch out of the exhibit. Cataracts were developing in the eyes. The bird became apneic approximately 5 minutes after turning off anesthesia. It did not respond to Dopram or cardiac massage. At necropsy the liver was small and copper colored. The kidney appeared enlarged. There was a small amount of hemorrhage in the right jugular vein.

OSTEOFIBROSIS. This 6-year-old rabbit has a history of respiratory difficulties. The animal was found dead. At necropsy there was overgrowth of the teeth of the lower mandible. The stomach contained an ulcer and the GI tract contained melena.

MESOTHELIOMA. This 12-year-old goat had a recent episode of dyspnea and hyperthermia following a hoof trim. The animal was found dead a few days later. At gross necropsy the abdominal cavity contained a large amount of cloudy fluid with white flocculent material. There were also numerous slightly raised masses on the omentum and severe serous atrophy of all adipose tissue.

GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS VISCERAL GOUT RENAL GOUT INTESTINAL MINERALIZATION OSTEITIS DEFORMANS. This 17-year-old male kingsnake had a swelling noted in the midbody approximately one week prior to death. A cystic hepatic mass was identified via ultrasound. Exploratory surgery was performed; however a large amount of intraoperative hemorrhage occurred and the animal did not recover from anesthesia. At necropsy a large firm tan mass was present in the anterior third of the liver. Numerous small cysts were present throughout the mass containing clear mucoid fluid. A similar mass with granular white mineralized material was present in the kidney.

This 5-year-old male alpaca presented to MSU VMC on 4/15/2015 for pain and labored breathing after being found lateral that morning. Physical exam indicated decreased lung sounds ventrally on the left side; no gut sounds; and a firm; bloated abdomen. Exploratory abdominal surgery revealed a large gas- and ingesta-filled C1 compartment of the stomach. Excessive ingesta was removed surgically. Postoperatively; the animal's condition deteriorated; with the development of significant bilateral pleural effusion and diarrhea. The animal died on the evening of 4/15; and was submitted for necropsy on 4/17. Additional history is on file at DCPAH. An 81-kg male alpaca was examined on 4/17/2015. Autolysis was moderate. The animal had adequate subcutaneous and visceral fat stores and an overall body condition of 5/9. There were bilateral chest tubes and nasal cannulas. A closed ventral midline abdominal surgical incision extended 13 cm cranial and 7 cm caudal to the umbilicus. There was 1L of watery; translucent; serosanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity that had a urine-like smell; but the urogenital tract was intact. The thoracic cavity contained 500 mL of similar fluid with strands of free-floating fibrin. There were multifocal; random; pinpoint to 5-mm diameter petechiae and ecchymoses on the parietal pleura; visceral pleura; and epicardial surface along the coronary groove and the interventricular septum. The C1 compartment of the stomach was gas distended and had a 10-cm; linear; closed surgical incision along the left ventrolateral wall. The mucosal surface of C3 had numerous 2- to 5-mm diameter; white to tan; firm nodules and multifocal random petechia and ecchymoses; of which the largest measured 1 cm in diameter. The liver had an enhanced lobular pattern; and multiple (approximately 10) white to tan; firm nodules were multifocally randomly scattered throughout the liver parenchyma. The mucosal surface of the larynx was diffusely dark red. The esophagus contained a green to brown; 10-cm long; fairly formed but moist; dark green brown trichobezoar at the level of the tracheal carina. The esophageal mucosa in this region was diffusely dark red. No other significant lesions were observed. Whole body: hydroabdomen and hydrothorax/pleuritis; multifocal pleural and epicardial hemorrhages C3 stomach: multifocal mucosal nodules liver: multifocal nodules esophagus: trichobezoar; with associated mucosal hyperemia and hemorrhage Comments The hemorrhages and pleuritis are suggestive of septicemia. The noted firm nodules in the C3 stomach and liver are likely due to parasites. A final report is pending complete histologic evaluation; fecal parasite analysis; and aerobic culture of the liver and lungs. Erica Noland; DVM; MS Sections of brain; lung; trachea; thyroid gland; heart; spleen; liver; kidney; adrenal gland; stomach; intestine; and tongue are examined. There are multifocal; large organizing fibrin thrombi within hepatic; pulmonary; and esophageal blood vessels. In the liver; there is regionally extensive capsular and parenchymal fibrosis; with scattered multifocal hemorrhage. Thrombosed vessels are surrounded by variably dense rims of fibrosis. There are abundant intracytoplasmic accumulations of rhodanine- positive; coarse granular material within large numbers of primarily centrilobular to midzonal hepatocytes. There are multifocal centrilobular to random foci of hepatocellular necrosis admixed with small to moderate numbers of histiocytes containing rhodanine-positive granular material; lymphocytes; plasma cells; and fewer neutrophils. Perioportal and centrilobular regions are multifocally mildly expanded by similar cellular infiltrates. There is mild bile duct hyperplasia. The hepatic parenchyma is focally expanded by a region of mineralization associated with varying amounts of fibrosis and moderate numbers of macrophages. Similar foci of dystrophic mineralization are focally to multifocally present within the splenic parenchyma; the submucosa of C3; and the intestines; associated with various amounts of fibrosis and small to moderate numbers of macrophages. In the kidney; there are multifocal wedge-shaped areas of renal cortical coagulative necrosis characterized by hypereosinophilic tubular epithelial cells with fragmented nuclei (karyorrhexis). These regions are outlined peripherally by moderate congestion. Adjacent intact tubules multifocally contain bright eosinophilic proteinaceous material. The capsular surface is focally lined by plump reactive mesothelial cells and there are moderate aggregates of infiltrating lymphocytes. The lungs are mildly diffusely congested and alveolar spaces multifocally contain small numbers of histiocytes. The pleural surface is lined by Liver: Chronic fibrosing hepatitis; marked centrilobular to midzonal copper accumulation; mild bile duct hyperplasia; hepatic thrombosis; and multifocal dystrophic mineralization Kidney: Acute to peracute renal infarctions; multifocal tubular proteinosis; and lymphocytic serositis/peritonitis Lung: Focal pulmonary thrombus; mild alveolar histiocytosis; and pleural fibrosis Esophagus: Locally extensive transmural hemorrhage and edema Spleen/C3/Intestines: Multifocal dystrophic mineralization Chronic fibrosing hepatocellular necrosis and hepatitis; and multiorgan fibrin thrombi Comments The multifocal thrombosis is suggestive of disseminated intravascular coagulation; which may be related to chronic liver disease. The findings in the liver are both severe and chronic; and may be due to copper toxicosis; as suggested by excessive staining for copper in histologic sections. Quantification of the hepatic copper level is pending to confirm this; and an addendum report will be issued when results are available. The noted ischemic changes (i.e.; infarcts) in the kidney are likely due to thrombi not captured in the planes of sections examined. Thus; these renal lesions may also be associated with DIC. Effusions in both the thoracic and abdominal cavities may have been due to hypoproteinemia associated with liver disease; although total solids were apparently not low until after intravenous fluids administration. The multifocal dystrophic mineralization is consistent with old parasitic cysts. These foci are all similar in terms of chronicity--i.e.; similar degrees of fibrosis; mineralization; and mild macrophage infiltration; but with a lack of apparent parasites; suggesting the animal was treated for an infestation at one time. The locally extensive hemorrhage seen in the esophagus grossly and histologically was possibly associated with the trichobezoar identified at necropsy. Erica Noland; DVM; MS Copper-associated hepatitis Comments The quantitative copper amount of 525.05 ug/g dw in this case is consistent with copper toxicosis . A level this high is consistent with excessive dietary intake. Consultation with a veterinary nutritionist is recommended to address appropriate feeding for the remaining animals in the herd. There are several references to copper toxicosis in camelids in the published literature; including: Copper poisoning in four llamas. 1989. J Am Vet Med Assoc 195(7): 987-989. Erica Noland; DVM; MS

BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS WITH YOLK/BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This 9-year-old female ibis died spontaneously with no recent medical history. Necropsy revealed severe chronic peritonitis/coelomitis and a perforated region in the jejunum. The intestines had diffuse mucosal thickening. Lungs were hemorrhagic and pale areas were detected in the heart. The liver was pale and friable. A large amount of intra-abdominal fat was detected and ovaries were active.

EUTHANASIA RENAL GOUT RENAL FIBROSIS HEPATIC FIBROSIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA HEPATITIS. This 13-year-old male iguana had a history of elevated phosphorus and uric acid. The animal was humanely euthanized with a diagnosis of renal failure. At necropsy the kidneys were enlarged. There was evidence of stomatitis.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOMYELITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 19-year-old female golden lion tamarin had a history of lower right mandibular swelling. The animal was recently found down. Radiographs revealed lysis of the right mandible with granulation tissue or a possible mass involving the incisors and premolars. Due to age and poor prognosis the animal was humanely euthanized.

EUTHANASIA SRTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 10-year-old female sheep has a history of chronic forelimb lameness. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy cartilage erosion was noted in the left shoulder and elbow with marked osteophyte proliferation in both elbows. Severe lumbar and thoracic spondylosis were also noted.

TOXOPLASMOSIS ACUTE BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS. This 5-year-old male red kangaroo had a two day history of diarrhea and lethargy. A female conspecific in the same enclosure died one day earlier. Necropsy revealed loose stool in the colon two liters of opaque thick fluid in the peritoneal cavity similar fluid in the thoracic cavity petechiae and ecchymoses on all serosal surfaces apparent hemorrhage in two segments of the large intestine numerous white foci in the liver and a similar white focus in the kidney gastric erosions and petechiae in the brain.

EUTHANASIA HEPATOCELLULAR ADENOMA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PNEUMONIA INANITION. This 13-year-old male sugar glider has a history of hepatic and renal failure. The animal was humanely euthanized. Generalized icterus was noted. The liver was enlarged mottled and irregularly nodular. Masses were seen in the cross sections.

AMYLOIDOSIS PODODERMATITIS ENTERITIS. This 41-year-old female Caribbean flamingo died suddenly with no clinical signs. At necropsy there was a presumably necrotic egg in the coelom moderate to severe pododermatitis swelling of the joint capsule and accumulation of white material within both hock joints.

DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOUS DISEASE. This approximately 14-year-old male crocodile monitor was found dead. Necropsy revealed small white granules similar to uncooked rice on the outside of the mouth and on the serosal surface of the intestines.

PROLAPSE EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male green tree python presented with a large swollen hyperemic prolapse. Sepsis was considered likely and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A frog in the same exhibit was previously diagnosed with mycobacteriosis. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no other abnormalities aside from the prolapse.

BACTERIAL PYELONEPHRITIS DERMATITIS METABOLIC BONE DISEASE. This female greater than 1-year-old captive bred frog was one of three frogs that died acutely on 5/27. This is the cagemate of one of those frogs. This frog was exhibiting neurologic signs about 30 minutes prior to death. The frog was flipping upside-down on its back and was unable to right itself. The only husbandry changes made recently involved a change from dechlorinated water to regular tap water after the first three animals died. Two of the original three animals were housed together in a separate location from this animal and its cagemate. Another frog died four days later. Only three of these carcasses were suitable for necropsy. At necropsy the whole body was bloated and fluid filled. The skin of the ventral rear legs was reddened and blotchy. There were normal fat bodies. There was a large amount of fluid within the abdomen that appeared to be a greatly distended urinary bladder. In-house evaluation showed specific gravity=1.003 pH=6.0 protein=10 and blood=3+. Cytology showed amorphous crystals and numerous bacteria with occasional renal epithelial cells. The lungs were dark and collapsed. The heart was pale. The kidneys appeared swollen and severely hemorrhagic. The surrounding tissues were edematous.

AMYLOIDOSIS LYMPHADENITIS HEPATITIS. This approximately 10-year/5-month-old female sheep died during recovery from anesthesia. She had been worked up and had skull radiographs for dental abnormalities. The oral cavity was explored and preparations were made to remove a loose tooth and to address the left upper molars that were overgrown laterally and the left lower molar which also appeared to be overgrown on the lateral side. An abscess associated on the side of the face was clipped and scrubbed. An incision was made and a significant amount of pus was expressed. She was transferred back to her enclosure and was given yohimbine IM. It was noted she was not breathing although she had a pulse. While administering Dopram it was noted that the pulse had stopped. CPR was initiated. At necropsy the liver contained numerous multifocal abscesses of various size on the surface and throughout the parenchyma. There also appeared to be areas of scarring in the liver. The lungs had some areas of what appeared to be abscesses or scarring. Due to concerns of Johne’s disease the mesenteric lymph nodes were collected as were two pieces of ileum. Ileum was submitted for culture. Culture of abscess was performed. There was a long tubular structure in the mesentery and jejunum that appeared to be lymphoid grossly. There was a large blood clot in the thoracic cavity. There was edema of the pleura surrounding the accessory lung lobe. There was a clot in the trachea. There was severe gingival recession on the left side. There was severe molar overgrowth on the left side. There was tooth root degeneration and periodontal disease. The right kidney had an area of possible hemorrhage along the line between the cortex and medulla.

LYMPHOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE. This 7.5-year-old female/spayed ferret was euthanized following a one month history of progressive inappetence and weight loss. Necropsy revealed a pancreatic mass that extended circumferentially around the duodenum. Both adrenals had 1 mm. nodules.

BACTERIAL HEPATITIS PANCREATITIS PERITONITIS. This 6-year-old male meerkat was found dead with no previous clinical signs. At necropsy the liver contained multifocal areas of either tumor or abscess. The pancreas appeared hemorrhagic.

NECROTIZING STEATITIS. This 9-year-old male African painted dog was found laterally recumbent and stuporous on exhibit. Examination revealed serosanguineous peritoneal effusion moderate acidosis elevated heart rate and coma following anesthesia. The animal was found dead in the morning and had no urine production since administration of intravascular fluids. The animal had received prednisolone daily for suspected pannus for two years. A recent ocular flare-up 3-4 days earlier had self-resolved. Necropsy revealed moderate atelectasis and mottling of the lungs mildly rounded hepatic margins with some moderate diffuse yellow mottling of the parenchyma dark purple firm pancreas adhered to the mesentery and duodenum dilated dark purple duodenum multiple patches of erythema in the small intestinal mucosa and diffuse thickening of the intestinal wall few yellow smooth deposits in the right kidney and small urinary bladder with no urine production. The meninges of the brain were thickened and a possible mass was near the optic chiasm. The corneas had melanosis.

ASPERGILLOSIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ENCEPHALITIS HEPATITIS. This 7-month-old male teal had been under treatment for weight loss anorexia and anemia. Initial response to therapy was noted; however the animal’s condition declined. The animal later died despite therapy. At necropsy the bird was emaciated. All tissues were pale. Numerous granulomas were present in the left thoracic air sac abdominal air sacs and within both lungs.
adult. Weight: 3450.0 g.  Aspergilosis.

EUTHANASIA OSTOEARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 14-year-old male goat had a history of chronic osteoarthritis. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining condition.

COLITIS INANITION ADRENAL NECROSIS. This 6-year-old male tamarin presented very weak with possible diarrhea. The animal was treated with antibiotics fluids and dextrose and immediate improvement was noted. The animal died several days later. At necropsy marked megacolon was noted. The right parathyroid gland was markedly enlarged.

ENDOTOXIC SHOCK. This 2-year-old male rat died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed a ruptured stomach with gastric contents within the peritoneal cavity. Yellow/white plaque-like adhesions were on the dorsal surface of the liver. No other evidence of peritonitis was observed. Stomach rupture may have been postmortem. Paired gray gonads were present (testes?).

DIABETES MELLITUS EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old female mynah had been managed for several months for diabetes mellitus using insulin injections and dietary modification. The bird seemed stable for several months but recently developed severe hypoglycemia and inappetence. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition some alopecia on the neck and back of the head and over the keel several pinpoint white spots in the pectoral muscles adequate fat stores slightly enlarged right ventricle and thickened myocardium a yellow translucent spot approximately 5 mm. in greatest dimension in the duodenal loop of the pancreas mild enlargement of the right hepatic lobe and no other remarkable abnormalities.

AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATIC HEMATOMA. This 13-year/10-month-old female kudu was found dead in the stall. It had not eaten since immobilization in mid November. It had an elevated creatinine and BUN and decreasing serum calcium levels. It was being treated with fluids steroids and furosemide. The kudu started grinding its molars the day prior to death. At necropsy there was bruising hair loss and minor abrasions in the left thorax and on the left side of the head particularly around the left eye. There was some subcutaneous edema along the left abdominal wall. There was bloody fluid (about 1 liter) in the abdomen. The entire right lobe of the liver was greatly enlarged swollen and almost spherical in shape. On cut surface enlargement was due to a subcapsular hematoma. The hematoma seemed to be somewhat organized and the total volume was approximately 1-2 liters. There were large 4-5 mm. in diameter petechiae scattered over the entire spleen. There were multiple petechiae over the serosal surface of the abomasum. There were some small erosions of the mucosal surface. There were mineralized bezoars in the rumen. There was an extremely firm almost hard mass of fecal material in the small intestine. Both kidneys seemed slightly small. The capsule on the left kidney seemed thicker than normal and was more tightly adhered to the cortex. The medulla had an unusual yellow/tan discoloration. The left lobe of the thyroid was 2-3 times larger than the right lobe. There was a large cyst present in the left lobe.

SEPSIS. This 18-year-old male Rodriguez fruit bat presented with bloody wingtips and a history of roosting in an atypical location. Blood work revealed left shift anemia renal azotemia and hyponatremia. Subcutaneous fluids and antibiotics were administered and the animal was isolated for observation and was found dead a few days later. Necropsy revealed alopecia on the head and patagia. The nasal philtrum was deviated to the left and the left eye opening was small compared to the right. The bat had a history of conspecific aggression and facial asymmetry was believed to be secondary to traumatic episodes and possible facial nerve paralysis and soft tissue contracture. Wingtips were disfigured with multiple luxations of the interphalangeal joints and patagial tears. The lower canine teeth and the maxillary left canine tooth were broken at the gum level and other teeth showed variable wear.

HEPATIC AND COELOMIC BACTERIAL ABSCESSES CHRONIC PROVENTRICULITIS AND ENTERITIS. This 4.5-year-old male green-naped lory was recently treated for a respiratory infection using nebulized antibiotics. The bird’s attitude seemed to improve but it was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed fair body condition congested lungs and hepatomegaly with several distinct 1 mm. foci that were yellow. Adhesions of the liver to the ventral body wall by thick yellow tissue was also noted. Male gonads were identified.

BACTERIAL/MYCOTIC CELLULITIS SEPSIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS EUTHANSIA. This 7-year-old female pit viper has a 3-month history of inappetence weight loss and presence of cryptosporidia DNA in a cloacal swab. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed empty gastrointestinal tract irregular and firm ovaries resembling saponified fat bodies and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA (POSSIBLE ASPRIATION) CARDIAC MINERALIZATION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female captive bred wallaby had an approximately one month history of pulmonary consolidation and pneumonia with adhesions and was euthanized.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA METABOLIC BONE DISESE. This 4-year/4-month-old male frog died. It had been losing weight despite hand feeding. It had a rub lesion on the lower jaw. At necropsy there was an abrasion along the rostral mandible. There were multiorgan granulomas. Culture was submitted. The colon was full of feces. The stomach was full of food.

COLONIC ADENOCARCINOMA WITH SQUAMOUS DIFFERENTATION MULTIFOCAL THROMBOSIS SEPTIC PERITONITIS. This 1.5-year-old female great basin gopher snake had a recent diagnosis of a cloacal mass as squamous cell carcinoma. The animal was euthanized. At necropsy the pericardium was thickened with trauma to the myocardium (euthanasia artifact). The distal aspect of the colon is expanded by a mass throughout the entire circumference. The left kidney was subjectively small and the adrenal congested.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EPICARDIAL ADHESIONS COELOMIC ADHESIONS EMACIATION RENAL AND HEPATIC FIBROSIS. This 35-year-old female desert tortoise had been inappetent for several weeks received supportive care for constipation but died. Necropsy revealed ants on the carcass erythematous cloaca fresh blood under the chin emphysema of the chin and ventral neck blood on the left back inner thigh serous discharge from the nares edema in the subcutis of the chin and ventral neck gas filled small colon large amount of soft feces in the colon reddening of the mucosa of the small intestine and colon renal asymmetry with the right kidney smaller than the left a large amount of digested food in the stomach and no other remarkable gross findings.

PYELONEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS OLD CEREBELLAR INFRACT. This animal had intention tremors of 12 years duration tested negative for West Nile virus infection and was being managed with anticonvulsant therapy. An MRI in 2007 showed lesions in the cerebral cortex and right hemisphere near the hypothalamus. Baylisascaris migration was suspected. The animal also had a history of whipworms and was treated accordingly. Recently this animal had been acting abnormally in the afternoon of the previous day and was drooling. By the end of the day the colobus was sitting on the floor in the back of the holding area and the following day became recumbent and minimally responsive. Blood work revealed hypoglycemia hyperkalemia hyponatremia elevated hepatic enzymes and elevated renal values. Supportive care was administered but the animal never fully recovered. Bacterial rods were identified in a blood film. The animal died and necropsy revealed gas-filled stomach and intestines petechiae in the mucosa of the bladder renal asymmetry with the right smaller than the left cystic right ovary pale mottled liver and congested and mottled lungs.

CLOSTRIDIAL ENTERITIS HEPATITIS COELOMITIS. This 3-year-old female lory was found dead. At necropsy a segment of intestine measuring approximately 2 to 2.5 cm. is necrotic and friable. Other sections of intestine were hyperemic and filled with blood.
OVIDUCT ADENOCARCINOMA. This 7-year-old female chicken became depressed and was experiencing conspecific aggression. Necropsy revealed neoplasia in several tissues.

Kidney: Moderate membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis; nonsuppurative interstitial nephritis with fibrosis Adrenal gland: Severe cortical hyperplasia Lung: Anthracosis Heart: Mild multifocal myocardial degeneration and fibrosis Liver: Moderate diffuse hepatic lipidosis Comment: A specific cause of death was not apparent upon histologic evaluation of the tissues. The lesions observed are fairly nonspecific; and common findings in older animals; but in sum may have debilitated it. The severe adrenal cortical hyperplasia suggests that this animal may have been undergoing chronic physiologic stress. Hepatic lipidosis indicates that this animal was anorexic for a few days before death. There was no evidence of neoplasia or an infectious agents within the examined tissue sections. Barbie J. Gadsden; DV

CHRONIC ENTERITIS (POSSIBLY CORONAVIRUS ASSOCIATED RUMENITIS ABOMASITIS SIALOADENITIS EMACIATION. This 5-year-old female gerenuk had a history of chronic intermittent diarrhea poor body condition and inflammatory leukogram of undetermined cause. Its condition continued to decline over the last month and the animal was subsequently found dead while being monitored in the hospital. This animal’s first episode of diarrhea occurred at two weeks of age and it was suspected to have developed acute renal failure. It again developed diarrhea at four and ten months of age and was examined subsequently on several occasions for weight loss and weakness. The animal had been treated with supportive care on all occasions and had been dewormed on multiple occasions. The gerenuk also received monthly copper boluses. The animal delivered a stillborn calf one day after being handled for a vaccine booster in March 2015. Two months later she was examined for weight loss and diarrhea. Supportive care again was administered and the animal responded but then again developed periodic diarrhea. The animal again developed periodic diarrhea. The animal was being closely monitored and treated for diarrhea at the time of death. Fecal examination revealed strongyles Campylobacter sp. and coronavirus particles in electron microscopic examination. On the day of death the animal was noted to have a large amount of liquid diarrhea. Necropsy revealed emaciation alopecia in the distal pelvic limbs dull coat with easily epilated hair mild to moderate overgrowth of the hoof walls possible decreased bone density (transparent marrow in the ribs) absence of adipose tissue and associated serous atrophy mild amount of clear pericardial effusion small amount of serosanguineous fluid in the gallbladder numerous 0.5 to 1.0 cm. round pale/white depressions in the capsule of the liver purple atrophic pancreas frothy green feed stuffs in the rumen diffusely thickened rugae in the abomasum multiple areas of jejunal mucosal hyperemia a focal apparent stricture at the free end of the cecum dilated colon with thin walls and brown liquid stool a 3 mm. round cyst at the corticomedullary junction of the right kidney mildly edematous vulva and no other remarkable findings.

THYMOMA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA RUMINAL ACIDOSIS. This 8-year-old male Nigerian dwarf goat was normal in the morning and was found dead one hour later. At necropsy ruminal papillae were blunted. The abomasum was erythematous. The left adrenal gland was larger than the right. The right pulmonary lobe was consolidated and the thymus was prominent. The gallbladder was full.

EUTHANASIA MYOCARDIAL FIRBOAIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS ULCERATIVE GASTRITIS STEATITIS. This 13-year-old female capybara had a history of chronic arthritis and blindness. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining condition. At necropsy the liver was friable. Ulcers and petechial hemorrhages were noted in the stomach. Multiple cysts were present in the kidney.

ACUTE PULMONARY SHOCK BILIARY ADENOCARCINOMA. This 18-year-old female puma was found dead. It had possible exercise intolerance over the past week but appeared to be bright and alert and interactive three hours prior to being found dead. A sibling died three years earlier with marked myocardial degeneration (G09-0706). Necropsy of the puma in this report revealed dark reddened pulmonary lobes filled with red-tinged fluid and a nodular surface to the liver.

ANESTHETIC DEATH PNEUMOMEDIASTINUM (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATIC CESTODIASIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE OBESITY SHOCK. This 9-year-old female pig was anesthetized for dental treatment and hoof trim. Severe crepitus was noted in the elbows. Severe degenerative joint disease with osteophyte proliferation was noted radiographically. Respiratory arrest developed during anesthetic recovery and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy the animal was obese. Marked subcutaneous emphysema was noted over the forelimbs and thorax. The pharynx was edematous and hyperemic. A 1 cm. tear was present in the junction of the pharynx and trachea. Lungs were collapsed and deep red. A cyst containing opaque fluid was present in the liver.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 8-year-old female meerkat was found unexpectedly in the morning with unsteady gait and shaking. Supportive care was administered but the animal died shortly after being treated. Necropsy revealed enlarged left kidney.

CARDIOMYOPATHY HYDROPIC HEPATOPATHY ENDOMETRITIS. This approximately 2-year/5-month-old female bat was found dead at the base of the tree in the exhibit. At necropsy there are multiple small areas of hemorrhage on the left and right forearms and wing webs. The nipples were enlarged and flattened suggesting previous lactation. There were small areas of hemorrhage over the thorax neck and head. The hemorrhage on the right side of the head was most severe. Many veins were extremely congested especially caudal to the kidneys. There is severe congestion of the meninges covering the brain.

INANITION MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 6-year/4-month-old female tamarin died. It had a history of diabetes mellitus. At necropsy the tamarin was very thin. The gall bladder was large and full. The pancreas appeared tan and enlarged. The spleen was small. The urinary bladder was small. The kidneys appeared larger than normal and pale pink (1.8 x 1 cm.). The uterus appeared very hemorrhagic. The adrenal gland was very large (4 x 5 mm.).

FLAGELLATED PROTOZOAN ENTERITIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This approximately 1-year-old blue spiny lizard was found dead and was being treated for weight loss. It had been observed frequently on exhibit with its eyes closed and not acting normally. Necropsy revealed hyperemic lungs a friable liver and a gas distended intestinal tract.

BACTERIAL CELLUITIS (LUMPY JAW) SEPTICEMIA SEPTIC SHOCK. This 5-year-old male wallaby arrested after approximately 1 min. of anesthesia. It was unable to be resuscitated. The day prior to death the wallaby was noted to have a swollen jaw and was found the next day ataxic on exhibit. It had serous putrid discharge from the oral cavity. At necropsy the right mandible was thickened and irregular along its entire length. There was a firm mass associated with the mandibular-ramus area. When incised the muscle and subcutaneous tissues appeared thickened hemorrhagic and necrotic. There was a pocket (2-3 cm.) of thick brown purulent fluid incised in this area. The right submandibular lymph node appeared enlarged and hemorrhagic. The upper molars were discolored gray and had marked gingival recession. There were pinpoint hemorrhages in the tissues over all ribs. The pericardium was thickened. The lungs had large areas of hemorrhage. The bladder had petechia and approximately 10 cc. of hemorrhagic urine. Cultures of mandibular abscess were performed.

EUTHANASIA INTESTINAL CESTODIASIS HEPATITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS PULMONARY SHOCK. This 7-year-old female chicken had a history of weight loss and inappetence. A coelomic mass was identified. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy marked muscle wasting was identified; however extensive adipose deposits were present subcutaneously and intracoelomically. The lungs were hemorrhagic. The liver was enlarged and pale.
RENAL GOUT STRESS. This 5-year-old male rattlesnake was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition empty alimentary tract and no other abnormalities.

OVIDUCTAL RUPTURE BACTERIAL COELOMITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This female greater than 7-year-old rattlesnake was found dead in its enclosure. It had an approximately one week history of swollen body from the midbody to the vent. At necropsy there was partial rupture of the left oviduct. There was moderate to severe autolysis. There was rat fur within the stomach.

EMACIATION. This 3-year-old male leiothrix was found weak and may have hit a cage as there was a small scrape at the cere and the bird had neurologic signs and was gasping. Supportive care was administered but the bird died in the oxygen cage. Necropsy revealed a deformity in the calvarium. No other gross lesions were noted.

DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old female meerkat had degenerative arthritis involving the left stifle and right elbow with associated weight loss. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1 mm. punctate red focus on the spleen a 3 mm. yellow focus on one lobe of the liver corpora lutea in the ovaries and no other remarkable findings.

INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATIC GRANULOMAS FATTY LIVER. This 5.5-year-old male gecko was found dead. It had no previous abnormalities noted. At necropsy the gecko was in good nutritional condition with adequate muscling and large abdominal fat bodies. The lungs appeared congested and edematous. The liver was moderately enlarged with multifocal to coalescing pale yellow foci throughout the parenchyma. There also were multiple pinpoint dark foci throughout the parenchyma.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS COLITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS SPONDYLOSIS. This 7-year-old male meerkat had a two day history of vomiting and lethargy. GI distention was noted by palpation. An enema was performed. Supportive care was instituted; however the animal was later found dead. At necropsy cystic foci were identified in the oral mucosa. Gastric contents were greenish-brown and fetid. Discoloration was noted in the colonic mucosa and serosa.

RENAL AND ARTICULAR GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 7-year-old female cockatiel presented with right hind limb lameness and thin body condition. Multiple firm white swellings were noted around the right tarsus. Radiographs revealed articular gout. The bird’s condition declined despite treatment and blood work revealed renal failure and possible hepatic disease. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified emaciation multiple firm white nodules containing thick white/yellow material in the joint of the right tarsus mottled liver pale kidneys with pinpoint white foci and crystalline white material on the surface of the proventriculus.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PROBABLE ASPIRATION. This 15-year-old male cottontop tamarin died and had no clinical signs of illness prior to death. There is a history of toxoplasmosis in squirrel monkeys housed in close proximity to this tamarin. Necropsy revealed good body condition fly strike in the skin hemorrhage in the lungs and a red/brown oral nasal discharge.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS INTRACOELOMIC ABSCESS SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION EUTHANASIA. This 10.5-year-old male snake was submitted with no history. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified good body condition several foci of spinal fusion and a 4 cm. oval white mass in the middle of the coelom cranial to the gallbladder that on cut surface had multiple concentric circles. The mass is adhered to the surface of the stomach intestine liver and body wall. The kidneys had a white to yellow appearance consistent with gout. A few gout tophi were seen in the coelom.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSISBRONCHOPNEUMONIA COELOMITIS COELOMIC CESTODIASIS INANITION URATE STASIS. This 9-year-old male python was restrained for radiographs. Audible respirations were noted at the time. A mixed interstitial and miliary pattern was present in the lung fields. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the snake was in poor condition with inflammation adjacent to the glottis. The trachea contained yellow mucus. The lungs contained similar material and white caseous nodules. Similar caseous nodules were present throughout the coelom and anterior to the heart.

ARTERIOVENOUS FISTULAS UNKNOWN GREAT VESSEL. This approximately 18-year-old female Caribbean flamingo was found dead on June 4 2014. Gross necropsy revealed hemorrhages on the serosal surfaces of the respiratory tract large hemorrhagic follicles present in the ovary a dilated oviduct with a partially shelled ovum in the vagina and greater than 20 ml. of frank hemorrhage within the coelom.

NODULAR ACINAR CELL HYPERPLASIA PANCREAS. This 5-year-old male captive bred ferret has a history of insulinoma obese body condition thin haircoat and thin skin possibly due to prednisolone therapy. Surgical palpation of the pancreas revealed two small hard nodules 2 mm. in diameter that were bluntly dissected and submitted.

YOLK COELOMITIS. This 10-year-old female blue-crowned lory was found dead. Necropsy revealed pericloacal contour feathers matted markedly overgrown toenails moderately distended distal coelom fibrous adhesions in the coelomic cavity associated with dilatation of the distal 4 cm. of the large intestine brick red granular exudate in the dilated colon and multiple ova of varying sizes in the ovary.

Euthanasia Spondylosis Degenerative intervetebral disk disease Comments: Histopathologic examination of tissues is in progress. Results will be stated in the final report. Katriya Chankow; DVM Brain: Severe diffuse spongiosis of the brain white matter with presence of Alzheimer type II astrocytes Spinal cord: Diffuse Wallerian degeneration of the spinal cord with focal necrotizing myelitis Kidney: Severe chronic diffuse interstitial nephritis Heart: Mild chronic multifocal fibrosing myocarditis Lung: Multifocal bronchiolar adenoma Liver: Multifocal biliary cysts Euthanasia Uremic encephalopathy Diffuse Wallerian degeneration of the spinal cord with focal necrotizing myelitis Spondylosis and degenerative intervertebral disk disease Mild chronic multifocal fibrosing myocarditis Multifocal bronchiolar adenoma Multifocal biliary cysts Comments: Histologically; the lesions found at the brain and kidneys are suggestive for uremic encephalopathy. Focal necrosis of the spinal cord is suspected to be due to compression. The brain and spinal cord lesions are undoubtedly accounted for the animal's lameness and ataxia; which lead to poor quality of life. The pulmonary masses; bronchiolar adenoma; and hepatic biliary cysts are benign lesions. Katriya Chankow; DVM

RHABDOMYOLYSIS CNS SIGNS EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old male meerkat developed acute onset of lethargy on July 9th with possible mild ataxia. Blood work and radiographs were unremarkable. Supportive care was administered but the patient became increasingly ataxic and appeared to be blind. Symptoms improve with dexamethasone therapy as the animal was able to ambulate better but still was ataxic. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed mild enlargement of the heart and slightly larger left adrenal gland than right adrenal gland.

SEPSIS RHABDOMYOLYSIS CONSPECIFIC AGGRESSION. This 11-year-old male meerkat had recently been introduced to new female conspecifics accompanied by significant aggression during the first 24 hours. The animal sustained multiple bite wounds to its rear limbs and facial region and became inappetent. The meerkat was separated and received supportive care but developed hematuria became weak and dyspneic and died during transport to the hospital. Necropsy revealed good body condition and multiple pinpoint puncture and bite wounds to the nose and left naris left elbow right hind limb left hind limb and left side of the scrotum. The left carpus was swollen maxillary incisor and left mandibular incisors #1-2 were missing viscous dark brown fluid was in the oral cavity the lungs were congested dark brown liquid material was in the esophagus multiple pinpoint ulcers were in the gastric mucosa a 0.5 cm. area of dark purple discoloration was on the surface of the right kidney the adrenals were bilaterally enlarged and two 3 mm. semicircular areas of pallor were in the tail of the spleen. Spondylosis was noted on the ventral aspect of thoracic vertebrae.

NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 9-year/11-month-old male duck died. It had a history of head tilt to the left and right leg lameness in early June. It resolved with supportive care and antibiotics. At necropsy there was autolysis.

BILATERAL PHEOCHROMOCYTOMAS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This approximately 6-year-old female prairie dog was found dead in its enclosure and had no prior signs of illness other than a chronic head tilt to the right and obesity. Necropsy revealed no external wounds good teeth 30 ml. of pleural fluid rounded heart deflated left cranial lung lobe bruising of the remaining lungs thin aorta enlarged right thyroid gland prominent adrenals pale kidneys hyperemic thick uterine horns and quiescent ovaries.

HISTIOCYTIC INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA METASTATIC ENDOCRINE CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL) EUTHANASIA. This 24-year-old male peccary had a history of osteoarthritis bilateral nuclear sclerosis oligodontia and marked dental disease and bilateral medial patellar luxation. In the last three months it had decreased activity and mobility decreased range of motion in the joints and was found in lateral recumbency on exhibit with obtunded mentation one day after being anesthetized for exam. Radiographs revealed an interstitial pattern in the caudal dorsal pulmonary fields moderate hyperglycemia and possible recent infarction in the cortex thalamus midbrain and cerebellum. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed diffuse pulmonary congestion pale ventricles petechiae in the glandular portion of the stomach purple discoloration of the liver mildly enlarged spleen and hilar lymph nodes bilateral renal pallor pallor in the limb muscles and degenerative joint disease in multiple joints.

SHOCK PULMONARY ADENOCARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE CATARACT MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 3.5-year-old male opossum had been used in a demonstration in the morning and was clinically normal but then found dead in the evening. Necropsy revealed good body condition extensive dental wear with severe periodontal disease mottled pink/red lungs firm raised sessile nodular lesions throughout each pulmonary lobe up to 1 cm. in greatest dimension and no other abnormalities.

SEPSIS BILIARY CYSTADENOMA EXUBERANT HEPATIC HEMATOPOIESIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female chicken was humanely euthanized. It had a one day history of depressed weakness and distended crop that was full of foul smelling fluid plant material and gravel. The chicken had continued deterioration. At necropsy the chicken was thin and emaciated. The skin had multiple ecchymotic areas and mites. There were multiple pinpoint white foci in the epicardium and on the ventral aspect between atria. The air sacs were cloudy. There was a 1 cm. white plaque on the cranial thoracic air sac. The liver weighed 30 gm. and had diffuse patchy tan/yellow discoloration. There were 0.5 cm. white/yellow nodules in one lobe. The crop was severely impacted with fermented grass gravel and sand. The ventriculus contained ingesta and grit. Culture of oral cavity submitted.
adult. Weight: 83500.0 g.  # larynx; asphyxiation. Wounds ++. Fighting injuries. Myopathy?.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS AORTIC THROMBOSIS INFRACTED SALIVARY GLAND NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old female tamarin presented with acute paralysis of both rear legs in the tail. Three wounds were present one of which was nearly full thickness through the tail. No deep pain response was noted in either rear foot or the tail. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a thrombus in the caudal aorta near the bifurcation of the iliac arteries. White streaks were noted in the capsular surface of the liver and some renal cysts were noted. A multilobulated pale mass 3 cm. in greatest dimension was present on the left side of the face which had widened and deformed the area of the zygomatic arch over time producing a cavitated area on the left side of the skull. No other gross lesions were noted.
EMACIATION PULMONARY SHOCK PROBABLE TRAUMA AMYLOIDOSIS. This 9-year-old male white-faced whistling duck was found dead. Necropsy was unremarkable.
NA
NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 9-month-old lizard was found dead with no premonitory signs. At necropsy a large piece of carrot was present in the stomach.

HEAD TRAUMA. This 2-year-old female motmot was introduced to a male and injuries were then noted around the face of the female. The bird was separated but was found dead in its cage the following morning. Necropsy revealed ants on the carcass good body condition and feather quality a loss of feathers on the dorsal head around the eyes and around the beak superficial abrasions in these regions bleeding around the dorsal spinal cord at C1 multiple 1.5 cm. brown oval objects within the coelomic cavity attached to the air sac membranes the epicardium between hepatic lobes the esophagus the syrinx and within the choana.

SEPTECEMIA EMACIATION. This greater than 16-year-old female frog was found dead on 4/12. Necropsy revealed a large hemorrhagic mass with multifocal circular gray nodules throughout the reproductive tract. Hemorrhagic mucosa was noted in the proximal small intestine. The liver was enlarged and congested.

OSSEOUS METAPLASIA WITH CHRONIC TRACHEITIS CORTICAL ADENOMA. This 11-year-old peafowl had been treated for tracheal aspergillosis and died. Necropsy revealed extensive muscle necrosis in the left pectoral region attributed to injections. The trachea had a 10 cm. section of greatly thickened granulomatous wall with reduced luminal diameter.

GRANULOMATOSIS EMACIATION ARTERIOSCLEROSIS STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 21-year-old male monitor had fallen off its perch and was found biting its foot was limp and minimally responsive. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dry and dull skin pale mucous membranes absence of fat stores small black spots in the cranial lung dark tan liver with rounded edges several small masses throughout the liver ingesta in the stomach and several mucosal ulcers in the stomach a 2 cm. dark mass in the mesentery cranial to the colon that on cut surface had numerous hard white nodules. The colon was discolored and distended. A small amount of blood-tinged clear fluid was in the pericardium.

PULMONARY SHOCK HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 6-year-old green tree monitor was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed adequate body condition good fat stores some scabs on the left lower side of the gums and reddening of the right lower gums.  The liver was pale brown and possibly had areas of necrosis.

EUTHANASIA BUMBLEFOOT. This 5-year-old female chicken was humanely euthanized. It had a history of bumblefoot lesions with hemorrhage. Radiographs revealed bone involvement. At necropsy there were bumblefoot lesions on both feet. The bird was obese. Air sacs were clear. There was food in the crop. The liver was friable and yellow with hemorrhagic-like areas.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC DERMATITIS PERIARTICULAR FIBROSIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 9-year-old male fruit bat had a history of chronic dermatitis of the wing. The animal was humanely euthanized. Severe contraction of the left wing with ulcerative dermatitis was present.

DISSEMINATED BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA POSSIBLE DYSTOCIA. This 1-year-old female capybara died spontaneously with no prior medical history. Necropsy revealed good body condition and five full-term fetuses in the uterus. The liver contained whitish foci approximately 1 mm. in diameter centered around the diaphragmatic border of the central lobe. The right adrenal gland was enlarged with cavitation.

CARDIOMYOPATHY CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE METASTATIC HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA UTERINE LEIOMYOMA CHRONIC REAL DISEASE. This female approximately 42-year-old chimpanzee acutely collapsed and died during treatment. This chimpanzee was a geriatric animal that had been at The Toledo Zoo since 1959. In February 2000 the chimpanzee developed chronic illness including lethargy decreased appetite and a productive cough. Workup indicated possible pneumonia and heart disease. Treatments were administered with some improvement. At necropsy there was gross evidence of congestive heart failure. There were emboli within both the right and left lung. There was a thrombus within the right side of the heart. There were thrombi in the right and left lung. There was a fibrinonecrotic pneumonia. There was a fibrous neoplasm within the uterus. There was an epicardial lipoma.

SPLENITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 31-year-old swan has a history of chronic elevated renal indices on serum chemistry. The bird was recently found with its head in the water weak and semiconscious. The bird was euthanized. At necropsy the serosa of the liver was mottled. Kidneys were dark red and firm.

BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS AMYLOIDOSIS ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA. This 7-year-old male black footed ferret had blood work suggestive of hemolytic disorder and urinalysis suggestive of renal disease. The animal was found dead and necropsy revealed a 0.5 cm. mass in the lower lumbar epaxial area hemorrhagic lungs cysts in the liver hemorrhage on the serosal surfaces of the urinary bladder and stomach hemorrhage in the subcutis near the prepuce and hemorrhage in the spleen.
FATTY LIVER. This approximately 35-year-old male lizard was found dead. At necropsy there was ingesta present in the stomach and digesta present in the small and large intestine.

HEPATOCELLULAR NODULAR HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) UTERINE LEIOMYOMA CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 12-year-old female meerkat was euthanized with wounds over the hind limbs and tail. Masses were noted in the uterine horns.

PNEUMONIA COLITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 10.5-year-old female boa had a recent history of inappetence and was found dead. At necropsy the lung had severe effusion and proliferative lesions with foci of erosion of the lining epithelium.

ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CHRONIC PARABRONCHITIS AND PNEUMONOCONIOSIS FLAVUS. This 2-year-old female chicken had a swollen region above the left eyelid associated with some feather loss. The animal died during isoflurane anesthesia while the eyelid swelling was being biopsied. Necropsy revealed good body condition cloudy pericardium bilaterally congested lungs and friable liver with palpable nodules. Several regions of the bowel had a darkened appearance and the mucosa seemed to be sloughing.

PITUITARY TUMOR THYROID ADENOCARCINOMA PROLAPSED AORTIC VALVE CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 29-year-old female giraffe has lost condition rapidly over the past several months and became recumbent in the exhibit after a fall over a barrier in early February. The animal developed mild lameness after being recovered but this resolved over the next several days. The animal never was felt to have returned to normal behavior. The animal had recently been a target of aggression and harassment from the male conspecifics sustaining multiple wounds and marked swelling over the right vulvar lip. Supportive care was administered and the animal was returned to the herd but was again attacked by the male and subsequently separated. The giraffe was found dead unexpectedly in her pen the following morning lying on her side with no sign of struggling. Necropsy revealed moderate generalized muscle atrophy scant fat stores many scabbed abrasions and lacerations over the body and legs markedly swollen right vulvar lip large subcutaneous hematoma associated with the lip lesion bruising and hematoma formation in the epaxial muscles behind the scapula and over the lumbar region. Marked bruising also was noted over the caudal pelvis and thighs especially in the region of the left ischium and hemorrhage is present in the muscles of the cranial third of the neck. Moderate chronic degenerative joint disease was in most of the major joints and an old chip fracture was in the medial aspect of the left carpus with apparent synovitis and hemorrhage into the joint fluid. Teeth were unevenly worn. The brain had unexpectedly thickened opaque meninges with congestion of the vessels. Food material was in the esophagus and trachea. Parathyroids are prominent. Mild serous pleural and peritoneal effusions were noted. A few small subpleural foci of fibrosis are noted. The atrioventricular valves have mild endocardiosis the aortic valves have marked thickening attributed to edema and fibrosis and the septal leaflet is partially prolapsed along the lip. The liver appeared fibrotic on section. A few scattered small cysts were in the kidneys. Some clear slightly yellowed crystalline grit-like uroliths were in the urine although the bladder mucosa was grossly normal. A fluid-filled cyst or follicle was in the left ovary. An old metal hair clip was in the rumen. The rumen also contained a small amount of sand. The mucosa had diffuse thick villous lining with normal but small variation in size of the villi. The abomasum had some mild nodular cobbling of the mucosa.

BUMBLEFOOT LUXATED STIFLE EMACIATION TRAUMA. This 3.5-year-old female duck has a one-month history of left-legged lameness and was subsequently found dead. Necropsy revealed contusions of the muscles of the caudal skull and cranial cervical region a chronic luxation of the right stifle an abscess on digit #4 of the right foot and numerous bacteria identified in a smear of synovial fluid.

CHRONIC MYOCARDITIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This captive bred 5-year-old male white-faced whistling duck presented with neurologic signs in April of 2010. The patient was diagnosed with aspergillosis and had been treated with itraconazole since that time. The patient died acutely on March 23 2011. Gross necropsy revealed pink fluid in the coelom thin body condition a blood clot in the proximal trachea wet mottled lungs with pinpoint light yellow foci throughout some areas yellowish opacities within the right caudal thoracic air sac a possible yellowish nodular growth adjacent to the mitral valve and possibly enlarged liver and kidneys. The heart also appeared enlarged.

ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS VACUOLAR HEPATOPATHY CHRONIC GASTROENTEROCOLITIS ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 26.5-year-old female macaque had recently been acting more arthritic and was receiving nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug therapy. In the past week it was acting dull and had a runny nose eventually became lethargic and shaky in the evening and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed yellow body fat ulceration on the ischial pads hepatomegaly with rounded edges some pulmonary bullae in the cranial lobe a substantial but not excessive amount of hard fecal material in the colon small spleen and food in the stomach.

LYMPHOMA. This 8-year-old female rhea had a history of recent diarrhea lethargy and weakness and developed respiratory arrest during manual restraint. Necropsy revealed anemia and a thoracic inlet mass. The heart was encased in a thick viscous clear to pink colored gelatinous material. Small white nodules were on the surface of the left atrioventricular valve. The ventriculus was filled with digesta and rocks and was mildly to moderately distended. A mass-like structure was present at the pyloric opening that was 4 cm. thick and pale cream-colored on cut surface. A small nodule was in the hepatic lobe and was encapsulated and pink on cut surface. The spleen was elongated narrow and pale pink. A large thick mass obstructed the lumen of the caeca at midbody and was white on cut surface. Ovaries were inactive. The mass at the thoracic inlet had a fatty texture and was 15 cm. in greatest dimension. A small pocket of clear yellow fluid was cranial to the mass.

EMACIATION EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY CHRONIC ABOMASITIS AND COLITIS. This 1-year-old female eland had been treated for mandibular edema weight loss and diarrhea and had a strongyle infection with associated leukocytosis received supportive care and was isolated for further supportive care. Edema resolved quickly but a recheck fecal exam identified a higher strongyle count than the initial exam and the animal continued to lose weight. The animal was returned to the herd to limit stress and improved feed intake subsequently developed mandibular edema and the strongyle count continued to increase. Edema resolved with treatment but strongyle count remained high. The animal was again isolated for treatment but escaped into the herd and was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed scant brown ceruminous debris in both ears a pocked of serous fluid deep to the left biceps femoris that contained free-floating fibrinous material and the surrounding muscle was pale. A mild amount of serous bilateral pleural effusion and a moderate amount of serous pericardial fusion were noted. The lungs were heavy and wet and the dependent lung was congested. Cardiac muscle was pale and serous atrophy was in the adipose of the cardiac groove. A pocket of impacted hay and grass was on the buccal surface of the left maxillary cheek tooth. The rumen was gas distended and contained mostly hay and grass. The ruminal lining sloughed easily (autolysis). The abomasal mucosa had multiple linear areas of hyperemia. The majority of the small and large bowel was filled with watery green stool and pelleted feces were in the colon. Serous atrophy of mesenteric fat was noted. The kidneys seemed bilaterally small for the age and species but had no additional gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA RENAL ADENOMA ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 8-year-old male quail presented with left hind limb lameness. Marked leukocytosis was noted. The animal’s condition worsened despite treatment and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the bird was thin. An off-white mass was present on the right kidney containing straw-colored fluid and caseous debris. A similar smaller mass was present in the left kidney.

CHRONIC HEPATITIS SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 13-year-old male roseate spoonbill was found obtunded. There was a strong storm the night before. The animal was hospitalized and continued to decline despite treatment and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy there was slight pulmonary edema.

EUTHANASIA PERITONAL FIBROSIS PLEURAL FIBROSIS HEPATITIS ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA MYOCARDIAL SARCOCYSTOSIS. This 20-year-old female sheep was euthanized due to a history of lethargy and weight loss. Thoracic and lumbar intervertebral disk disease and pleural effusion were noted radiographically. At necropsy clear yellow pleural and abdominal fluid was present. Thick firm white tissue with areas of hemorrhage was adherent to the stomach and small intestine. Uterine horns were filled with cloudy yellow fluid.

MILD CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA (DISEASE SCREEN FOR ENCEPHALITIS). This 15.5-year-old male coconut lorikeet was one of several birds that had previously developed signs of lethargy and neurologic disease. This bird presented to the hospital for lethargy and was treated accordingly failed to respond and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition male reproductive tract possible edema in the brain and no other gross abnormalities.

BACTERIAL GRANULOMAS. This approximately 1-year-old eyelash palm pitviper of undetermined sex was not doing well per the curator and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. There was a blister-like lesion along the skin that was cultured and grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

TRAUMA. This 4-year-old male mynah was found dead. At necropsy the beak was damaged; however no hemorrhage was identified. A small puncture wound was present near the left kidney with areas of hemorrhage.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE CATARACT MULTICENTRIC RENAL CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male wood duck had a four month history of intermittent right leg lameness and previous radiographs had revealed periosteal new bone on the lateral and anterior surfaces of the right tarsus calcification in the extensor tendon and lysis of the underlying periosteal new bone. Multiple triangular osteophytes were noted extending from the lateral surface of the distal tibiotarsal bone. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed yellow fibrinous cartilage surrounding and within the right tarsal joint two focal white circular well-circumscribed raised lesions to 1 cm. in diameter protruding from the cortex of the caudal pole of the right kidney and a 3 cm. focal nodular white infiltrative mass protruding from the cortex of the caudal pole of the left kidney. All renal masses were firm.
INANITION. This 7-year-old male snake had a several week history of anorexia and was being force fed. The animal was found dead. At necropsy dark material was present in the hemipenes.

PREDATORY TRAUMA. This 11-year-old female Speke’s gazelle was found dead along with a cagemate and signs of predation were noted. Necropsy revealed caudal an inguinal areas torn open to the bone skinning of the tail with bone exposure superficial bite marks on the right flank a single intramuscular puncture wound on the left flank blood around the nose and mouth no abnormalities in the cervical area or thorax a full-term fetus in the abdomen two large cysts on the kidneys a 6 cm. gaping hole in the abdomen outside at the level of the colon and no other abnormalities.

PLACENTITIS ENDOMETRITIS VASCULAR THROMBOSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS INANITION. This 8-year-old female kudu had a recent history of inappetence loose stool and hemorrhagic urine. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the epicardium had areas of dark discoloration. A large quantity of serosanguineous fluid was present in the abdominal cavity. A large area of discoloration was present in the rumen corresponding with a large knotted rope in the rumen. The uterus contained a full-term male calf. No fat depots were identified.

MYOCARDITIS (PROBABLE EMC) PYODERMA GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS. This 30-year-old female mandrill has a history of chronic intermittent moist dermatitis and severe spondylosis. The mandrill had a relatively acute onset of anorexia with mild intermittent vomiting lethargy and inappetence. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes and necropsy revealed streaks in the heart.

LYMPHOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDER. This 1-year/8-month-old female lory died 30 min. after presentation. It was found on the ground lethargic and cold. It was taken to AHC and given fluids vitamin B and Baytril. At necropsy the spleen was very enlarged. The liver was enlarged rounded and friable.

EUTHANASIA APOCRINE ADENOCARCINOMA (SKIN LYMPH NODE) UTERINE LEIOMYOMA GLOSSITIS PULMONARY MINERALIZATION AORTIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC INTERSTITAL NEPHRITIS ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old female hunting dog presented recumbent and weak. The animal has a history of skin masses. Purulent discharge was noted from the vulva. The animal was treated with fluids and antibiotics; however its condition declined and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy numerous coalescing masses were present in the skin and dermis along the dorsum axilla and on the fourth digit of the right hind limb. Kidneys were irregular and pale. Several cysts were present in the left cortex. A firm red mass was present in the primary bronchus of the right lung. Multiple gritty foci were present in the left lung. GI tract was congested.

TRAUMA CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY RUMINORETICULITIS. This 11-year-old female addra gazelle was found dead in its exhibit with no prior signs of illness or injury. A male was introduced to this group a few weeks earlier. Necropsy revealed no external signs of trauma. The lungs had dark purple serosa and ecchymoses or hematomas were present throughout the lung lobes. A laceration was in the left cranial lobe of liver and a large blood clot was present between the capsule and serosal surface on the dorsal side of the left cranial lobe. The other lobes were mottled brown/purple. A focus of dark purple discoloration was present in the cortex and medulla of one kidney. A serosal surface of the rumen had a hematoma approximately 16 cm. in greatest dimension.

AMYLOIDOSIS GOUT METASTATIC MINERALIZATION BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 25-year-old male flamingo is the parent of a 2.5-week-old chick and was observed to be isolating himself from the flock. Examination revealed thin body condition swelling of the left hock joint and metatarsal phalangeal joint but no active bumblefoot lesions. Urate precipitates were noted in the hock joint. Supportive care was administered but the bird died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed urate deposition on the pericardium and epicardium possible thinning of the left ventricular wall thickening of the aortic valves swollen kidneys that are speckled tan and white with retained urates congested surface vasculature in the brain and no other abnormalities.
adult. Weight: 274 g.  Otitis media. Rat respiratory disease complex; otitis media.

THYMOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS. This 17-year-old female Amur tiger was noted to have a slight wheezing sound the past few days when being removed from its exhibit but not at other times. The animal was otherwise completely normal. The animal was then found gasping for air in its exhibit and died before it could be immobilized for examination. Necropsy revealed dark purple tongue and a large mediastinal mass 5.5 cm. in greatest dimension that was smooth and bulged on cross sectioning. Both kidneys had uniformly pale cortices. Both ovaries had multiple diffuse bright orange spots on the surface.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS PANCREATITIS INANITION COLLOID GOITER CYSTIC BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 21-year-old female lemur had a history of chronic renal failure. The animal’s condition was declining and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was markedly thin. A large quantity of serosanguineous fluid was present in the peritoneal cavity. Foci of hemorrhage and cortical cysts were present in the kidneys. Lungs were consolidated and sank in formalin. A 2 cm. in diameter soft white mass was present in the anterior mediastinum.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE HEMOSIDEROSIS ENTERITIS. This 1.5-year-old female rat was extremely lethargic and dehydrated. The animal had dark green watery feces. The animal was treated with fluids and supportive care but was found dead the following day. CBC revealed leukopenia with lymphocytopenia and neutrophilia. At necropsy the lungs were dark and the GI tract appeared autolyzed.

ADRENAL CORTICAL ADENOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old female ferret has been treated for insulinoma but eventually euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified multiple small white nodules in the pancreas and liver. Lungs were dark with white spots. A cyst was found on the liver.
adult. Weight: 3022 g.  Open.  Pulmonary congestion.  Stomatitis.

INTRA-ABDOMINAL ABSCESS CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE EMACIATION. This 25-year-old female Bennett’s wallaby was found in lateral recumbency but when stimulated the animal stood and ambulated within normal limits. The following morning the animal was depressed and inappetent. Evaluation revealed hypothermia and hypoglycemia. Supportive care was administered but the animal became recumbent could not stand developed moderate ataxia when assisted and could not maintain normal body temperature. The animal’s condition declined it developed tremors dyspnea and complete recumbency and was found dead shortly thereafter. This wallaby had a history of dental abnormalities with previous removal of all of the right mandibular dentition and treatment of chronic draining mandibular abscess. Necropsy revealed multiple adhesions of the abdominal cavity most of the intestine had adhered to a firm sphere. One region of the jejunum was discolored dark purple. No perforations were seen. A raised roughened region of bone was present on the lateral aspect of the right mandible.

INFECTIOUS SYSTEMIC DISEASE PROCESS POSSIBLY VIRAL. This 13-year-old female duck was found dead after capture for routine yearly exam. No trauma was reported during the capture although the bird was found dead 15 min. later at a transport crate. It had no prior signs of illness although in 2011 had an elevated white blood cell count and elevated hepatic enzymes that did not appear to be associated with clinical disease. Necropsy of the bird revealed good body condition mild bilateral pododermatitis adequate adipose stores mottled and friable liver and prominent and mildly enlarged spleen.

DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 5-year-old male meerkat has a history of heart murmur and occasional fainting spells. Cardiac treatment resulted in some improvement but several recent episodes had been seen. The animal was found dead. Necropsy revealed a possibly enlarged heart.

INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA TRAUMA SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This 6-year-old prairie dog was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed good body condition two vertical full-thickness lacerations on both lateral sides of the face and no other gross abnormalities.
