Euthanized (for soft tissue sarcoma previously diagnosed) Kidney: Multifocal severe glomerulosclerosis; proteinosis; and mild glomerulonephritis Liver: Mild hemosiderosis Lung: Mild multifocal granulomatous pneumonia with lipid (endogenous lipid pneumonia) Small intestine: Mild multifocal crypt ectasia Ovary: Cystic rete ovarii; ovarian lipidosis; follicular exhaustion Uterus: Moderate endometrial atrophy; arteriolar hyalinization Comment: These changes are all common in geriatric patients and none were clinically significant; though the renal lesions were likely progressive and would have continued to develop leading to decreased renal function. The reproductive organs have been archived in the Reproductive Health Surveillance program.

EMACIATION CHRONIC ABOMASITIS DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE. This 12-year-old female gerenuk died. Necropsy revealed thin body condition multiple firm white possibly calcified lesions on the serosal surface of the lungs pink pulmonary parenchyma possible accessory spleens up to 2 cm. in greatest dimension throughout the omentum fibrous tissue in the pelvic region of both kidneys enlarged right adrenal gland and no other remarkable findings.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS GI FOREIGN BODY (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 19-year-old polar bear had a three day history of decreased appetite and activity. The animal died during recovery from physical exam. At necropsy peritonitis with inflammation and fibrinous tags was noted over the small intestine and mesentery. The jejunum contained clotted blood. A small folded piece of plastic was noted in the duodenum.

COPROSTASIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA NECROTIZING HEPATITIS SHOCK. This 13-year-old male owl was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the bird was thin. A uric acid concretion was adhered to the vent. The cloaca was distended with feces. Friable pale foci were present throughout the liver. An abscessed area was noted in the liver and adjacent kidney.

PULMONARY SHOCK ATHEROSCLEROSIS WITH ANEURYSM EMACIATION PROVENTRICULAR MINERALIZATION. This 12.5-year-old female cockatiel had a one-day history of illness that included abnormal perching behavior was found in its pan with its beak in the mesh and was dead upon admission to the hospital. Necropsy revealed thin body condition muscle atrophy white precipitate on the pericardium pale and swollen kidneys and no other gross lesions.

AMYLOIDOSIS BACTERIAL MYOCARDITIS. This 4-year-old male ringed teal was found caught in the fence. Necropsy revealed good body condition and no signs of external trauma. A frostbite lesion with necrosis on the right lateral toe was noted. Also missing were the left lateral and middle toes on the 2nd and 3rd phalanges probably secondary to frostbite. The liver was enlarged and hard with mottling and the spleen was enlarged and firm. The kidneys were enlarged. Large amounts of ascites were in the coelomic cavity. The pancreas and small intestines appeared inflamed.

1. Abomasum: Haemonchosis 2. Body as a whole: Anemia 3. Head; haired skin: Cellulitis; chronic; focally extensive; necrotizing and suppurative; severe 4. Kidneys: Bilateral cortical cysts; multifocal; chronic; mild Comments The exact cause of death in this animal is unclear from the gross necropsy alone. The anemia seen in this animal is severe enough to cause clincial signs. The finding of numerous abomasal worms (Haemonchus contortus) suggests chronic parasitism as the most likely cause blood loss. The cellulitis present on the head represents a severe; chronic; infection. Due to its suppurative nature a bacterial infection is likely. It is unclear if this infection is related to the neurologic signs described. No gross lesions are observed on examination of the brain. The renal cysts do not appear to significantly affect renal function and are considered an incidental finding. A final report is pending histopathologic evaluation and fecal examination for gastrointestinal parasites. Heather Tilllman; D Small intestine: Moderate; chronic-active; eosinophilic enteritis; with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate Large intestine: Moderate; chronic-active; eosinophilic colitis; with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate Abomasum: Mild; chronic-active; lymphoplasmacytic abomasitis with rare eosinophils Bone marrow: Moderate hypercellularity Spleen: Extramedullary hematopoeisis Chronic intestinal parasitism Active bone marrow Comments The large numbers of eosinophils; along with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates; found in all abomasal and intestinal sections suggests chronic parasitism. Hypercellular bone marrow indicates a regenerative response to the profound anemia noted on gross examination. No lesions were noted in the brain to explain the reported neurologic signs. CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This greater than 3-year-old female iguana presented with thin body condition elevated serum phosphorus and anemia. Necropsy revealed no significant findings.

ULCERATIVE COLITIS WITH SEPSIS RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA. This 36-year-old Gila monster was found dead. It had no recent clinical problems. Necropsy revealed two erosions on the tongue ruptured distal colon enlarged liver with multiple 0.25 cm. in diameter nodules that are palpable but not grossly evident enlarged and semifirm pancreas and a white irregular firm gritty nodule 1.5 cm. in diameter on the surface of the right kidney.
BACTERIAL PERITONITIS. This 8-year-old female naked mole rat was found dead. At necropsy discoloration was noted on the mandible and shoulder.

ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA DEGENERATIVE HEPATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This approximately 5-year-old male African hedgehog presented two weeks earlier with ocular discharge that resolved with supportive care. The animal subsequently developed a one day history of exophthalmia involving the left eye with left facial swelling and a 1 cm. maxillary mass was found in the oral cavity. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. The mass extended from the second premolar to the temporal mandibular joint medial to the midline palate and dorsally to the left globe. The right maxilla had an area of gingival proliferation on the third premolar. Fat stores were adequate. The right lateral and quadrate hepatic lobes were irregular and slightly firm. The left lateral lobe was pale tan/cream on serosal and cut surfaces. The left tail of the spleen had a 2 mm. circular pale focus on serosal and cut surfaces. The adrenal glands were bilaterally prominent. The left seminal vesicle had a 2 mm. firm nodule at the most lateral aspect. A smaller unidentified accessory sex gland had a similar nodule on the left lobe.

MYCOTIC FACIAL CELLULITIS AND PNEUMONIA. This 13-year-old female Inca tern presented one week earlier with swelling of the right side of the head and proptosis of the right eye. Swelling was also noted on the inside of the upper right oral mucous membranes. The right pupil was dilated and fixed. Supportive care was administered but the bird’s condition deteriorated it developed labored wheezing and breathing and subsequently died. Necropsy revealed pale kidneys pericarditis pale spleen hemorrhage in the gizzard with possible ulceration hemorrhagic material in the small intestine and a retrobulbar mass associated with a purulent discharge involving the right eye.

TRAUMA (CERVICAL) CHRONIC ABOMASITIS ENTERITIS AND CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS RUMENITIS. This 10-month-old male gerenuk was hand raised and had a history of intermittent diarrhea the last episode one month earlier. Diarrhea was associated with coccidiosis and resolved with appropriate treatment. This animal was found dead unexpectedly and postmortem radiographs revealed a fracture at C2-C3. This finding was confirmed at necropsy.

MICROGRANULOMATOSIS CHLAMYDIOSIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This 10-year-old female bullsnake was treated for cholestasis that never resolved. The snake continued to eat and was active prior to being found dead. Necropsy revealed a mass at the bile duct and an enlarged gall bladder. This snake had thin body condition.

EUTHANASIA TIBIAL FRACTURE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 2.5-year-old male rat had been under treatment for degenerative joint disease. Cataracts were identified in both eyes. The animal had a fracture of the tibia after entangling its foot. The animal was humanely euthanized.
RENAL GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS HEPATITIS ENTERITIS. This 17-year-old flamingo was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy pinpoint white foci were noted in the liver and kidney.

CIRRHOSIS HISTIOCYTIC COLITIS AND LYMPHADENITIS. This 1-year-old female capybara was seizuring. Supportive care was administered but with minimal improvement and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed that the animal was half the size expected for its age. Body condition was good. Lungs were congested. The colon and cecum were dark and contents appeared hemorrhagic and malodorous. Adrenal glands were larger than expected and possibly necrotic on cut surface. The liver was shrunken and multiple lobes appeared cirrhotic. Yellowish fluid was in the gallbladder.

BUMBLEFOOT AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC HEPATITIS AND ENTERITIS STRESS POLYPOID RHINITIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 30-year-old female Chilean flamingo was euthanized for chronic weakness dyspnea and elevated uric acid levels. Necropsy revealed a thin walled and dilated right ventricle thin orange plaques on the intima of the aortic arches and around the semilunar valves kidneys were multinodular and mottled pink and brown mucus was in the nares and the turbinates had multiple white to pink nodules on their surfaces. The liver was pale tan to dark brown and multiple typical bumblefoot type lesions were on the footpads of both feet.

BILATERAL ADRENAL TUMORS PROSTATIC SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA AND PROSTATITIS LOW GRADE SEPSIS INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 4.5-year-old ferret had a history of inability to urinate increased alopecia over the ventral neck and dorsal thorax and at the tail base and rump splenomegaly and painful urinary bladder. The animal had not responded to melatonin therapy and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an enlarged spleen multiple pale foci in the capsule of the liver right adrenomegaly irregular nodular yellow structures in the omentum multiple cysts in the right kidney asymmetrical prostate yellow flocculent material in the urinary bladder viscous material in the pelvic urethra and prostate and red discoloration in the pelvic urethra and associated prostate.

EUTHANASIA GASTRIC ULCER PANCREATIC NODULAR HYPERPLASIA. This 17-year-old male leopard was humanely euthanized due to chronic lameness. At necropsy the pancreas was firm and mottled. The middle portion of the stomach was thickened with healed ulcers.
CIRRHOSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 16-year-old female iguana died. Necropsy revealed emaciation minimal renal tissue and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA PITUITARY ADENOMA. This 2-year-old female rat had a mass in the left axilla which was surgically removed. Postsurgical recovery was poor and neurologic signs including rolling developed. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the animal was thin. A large dark purple mass was present in the region of the pituitary gland.

TRAUMA EXERTIONAL MYOPATHY RENAL GOUT. This 13-year/5-month-old female rhea died. It had a history of lameness on 11/29/01. There was severe joint luxation with evidence of healing skin abrasions identified on physical exam and radiographs. The stifle was stable with callous formation. Blood work at this time demonstrated elevated uric acid. The male had been observed chasing this female for several days prior to death. On the day of death the staff found the animal severely beaten and lying in ventral recumbency on exhibit. Presumed that the male conspecific attacked this animal. There was severe trauma to the head neck eyes and extremities. The animal was placed in a sling and treated with fluids dextrose antibiotics steroids vitamin A & B and thermal support. The animal responded slightly to treatment and then worsened. At necropsy the rhea was in thin to fair body condition with no subcutaneous and minimal coelomic fat stores. There were two leathery dry collapsed white structures floating free in the coelom. There was severe hemorrhage and bruising noted over the head neck proximal limb musculature pectoral and coelomic musculature muscles of the dorsum and proximal wings. There was moderate to severe edema noted subcutaneously over the skull. There was hemorrhage in both aural cavities. There was bruising over the skull. The major muscle groups appeared dark red. The liver was dark red and oozed blood on cut surface. Both kidneys appeared pale and were firm on cut surface. The renal vasculature appeared distended. The tissue surrounding the eyes was severely traumatized and lacerated. There were petechia over the intestinal tract. Mesenteric vessels were enlarged and distended.

PROLIFERATIVE INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA LIKELY VIRAL. This 20-year-old male captive bred green tree python had a chronic history of illness and was euthanized for humane reasons. The right eye was enucleated following an episode of trauma one year ago. The snake has a history of chronic respiratory disease prior to arriving at the zoo in 1998. A paramyxovirus titer was performed in June 1000 (10) and the snake developed lethargy anorexia neurological signs and difficulty controlling head movement. The snake also had respiratory difficulty. Minimal improvement was noted with antibiotic therapy. Culture result revealed Enterobacter sp. Necropsy revealed a foamy exudate in the lungs thickened pericardial sac pale myocardium small firm spleen thickened mucosa in the small intestine enlarged liver with serous fluid under the capsule and congested kidneys.

BACTERIAL OVARIOSALPINGITIS. This 13-year-old female rattlesnake was found dead on exhibit with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed no external lesions and abundant intracoelomic adipose stores. A round firm structure is cranial to the heart but without the typical thyroid parenchymal experience. The gastrointestinal tract is empty and the gastric mucosa is grossly normal. From mid to caudal coelom are seven large firm masses with a substantial amount of adhesions to the surrounding tissues. Several other masses that are smaller are also present. The structures appear to represent inspissated ovarian follicles. The masses were generally white and contained thick gray purulent material. The kidneys were slightly pale.

NORMAL EYE. This 16-year-old male cheetah had a history of cystitis and progressive neurologic signs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 3 cm. cyst in the pancreas filled with fluid a cobblestone appearance to the urinary bladder with a 3 cm. portion that was red and raised.

CHRONIC YOLK COELOMITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS BILIARY CYST. This 6-year-old female duck was euthanized due to chronic yolk coelomitis. At necropsy the air sac was thickened with marked deposits of yellow material. Similar material was present within the left air sac and adherent to all serosal surfaces. Multifocal raised fluid filled foci were scattered throughout the liver. Egg yolk and shell were present adherent to the left lung.

RENAL TUBULAR ADENOMA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA HEPATIC FIBROSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 13.5-year-old male warthog was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a small quantity of bloody feces was present in the perineum. The liver was firm and contained numerous small white foci. The gall bladder was enlarged with a thickened wall and contained clumped yellow contents. Petechial to ecchymotic hemorrhages were present on the heart ventricles. Thickening of the left AV valve was noted. A 3 cm. in diameter mass was present in the left kidney.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA HEMOLYSIS AORTIC MINERALIZATION. This 7-year-old male pygmy goat became inappetent five days following a dental prophylaxis and auscultation was consistent with right-sided cranial pneumonia. Azotemia developed and the animal was hospitalized for supportive care. The goat subsequently developed gastrointestinal stasis severe anemia and exploratory laparotomy was performed. The gastrointestinal tract was unremarkable but the goat died during the surgical procedure. Necropsy revealed multiple 2-3 cm. hard white plaques in the aorta at the level of the base of the heart and descending aorta at the level just cranial to the diaphragm. Ulceration and hemorrhage were in the cecum. The right cranial and middle pulmonary lobes were consolidated gray and firm. Multiple firm nodules were noted on the right side of the lungs. The right cranial and middle pulmonary lobes were adhered to the thoracic wall and pericardium.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS RHINITIS AND NEPHRITIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA. This greater than 9-year-old male mottled rock rattlesnake had a recent history of regurgitation and inappetence and gastric biopsies have been negative for Cryptosporidium sp. The snake was found dead in its cage. Necropsy revealed some tan round lesions 1-3 mm. in diameter extending into the parenchyma of the liver and some miliary white spots in the kidneys.

INANITION GASTROPATHY SUSPECT GASTRIC CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS. This approximately 18-year-old female milk snake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of regurgitation and cataracts. No gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

ACUTE ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 15-year-old male addax had been immobilized five days earlier to collect semen and had a normal recovery. Blood work at the time revealed elevated red blood cell count normal blood urea nitrogen creatinine protein low albumin and hypoglycemia. The animal had been slightly ill one day prior to being found dead. Necropsy revealed dark red lungs foam in the bronchi fresh ingesta in the downed lung dark red gallbladder with inspissated bile pale tan renal cortices and hemorrhage in the adrenal and duodenal mucosa.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS CEREBRAL ARTERIOSCLEROSIS VASCULAR MINERALIZATION BRAINSTEM HEMORRHAGE SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (MAMMARY GLAND) LYMPHOBLASTIC LYMPHOSARCOMA (SPLEEN LIVER) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 18-year-old female otter had central nervous system signs and cardiac enlargement. The animal died during anesthetic recovery. At necropsy fluid filled cysts were present within the dermis and subcutis. Pale foci were noted in the liver. The left heart was markedly dilated and thin walled. A dark spherical area was present in the right ventral brainstem.

HEPATOCELLULAR VACUOLAR DEGENERATION HEPATITIS WITH MICROGRANULOMAS EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old male captive bred cotton topped tamarin has a history of Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and Campylobacter infection and a chronic draining submandibular lymph node. Alopecia was also noted. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy all tissues appeared within normal limits except for an enlarged submandibular lymph node.

BACTERIAL NEPHRITIS CHRONIC HEPATITIS PULMONARY SHOCK. This 9-year-old lorikeet developed acute onset of neurologic signs including right head tilt and weakness. Marked weight loss was noted. Treatment was initiated; however the animal died shortly thereafter. At necropsy internal fat depots were present. The liver had rounded margins and was mottled. A firm round mass was present in the right hepatic lobe. A 1 mm. in diameter area of hemorrhage was present beneath the dura on the right cerebral hemisphere.

INANITION SUSPECT SEPTECEMIA. This 7-year/2-month-old female snake was found dead. It was reported to be thin three days prior to death. At necropsy the snake was in thin body condition. There were fish in the stomach. There were no body fat stores.

SEPSIS. This 7-month-old tamarin had a one day history of seizures. Blood work revealed extremely elevated hepatic enzymes and white blood cell count. It was found dead in the afternoon. Necropsy revealed large mesenteric lymph nodes mottled lungs and black discoloration around the edges of the liver and spleen.

EUTHANASIA CARDIOMYOPATHY PERITONITIS. This 9-year/16-day-old male wallaby was humanely euthanized. It had a history of dilated cardiomyopathy and valvular insufficiency of three valves. It had weakness that progressively got worse. On the day of death the wallaby was found down when it was easily picked up and transported to the hospital. It had diminished heart sounds on the right side and arrhythmia with a gallop murmur suspected. At necropsy there was dilated cardiomyopathy with the left side predominating. There was severe right lung edema with hemorrhage. There was adrenomegaly. There was no evidence of trichobezoar. There was enteritis and mild serositis.
SHOCK. This 3-year-old bat was found dead after escaping from its cage. No gross abnormalities were noted at necropsy.

SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA MYELINIC EDEMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female hedgehog had a two-week history of swelling in the left mandible and an aspirate was suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma (G15-4206). Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed pathologic fracture of the left mandible and firm swelling extending into the oral cavity. Two lacerations were on the left rear foot and the cervix was prominent. The uterus was turgid and a cystic follicle was in the left ovary.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE BRONCHIOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male rabbit has a history of chronic degenerative joint disease of several months duration and was leaning to its left side. Over the last 2-3 weeks this has progressed to being unable to right itself when laid on its side including an inability to right its hind limbs when its forelimbs are placed upright. The rabbit had a 1-2 week history of crossing of the forelimbs and lack of conscious proprioception. The rabbit also has a prolonged history of upper respiratory tract disease. At the time of euthanasia matting was noted on the medial aspects of the forelimbs and mild crusting ocular nasal discharge was present. Necropsy revealed brown coloration on the surface of the cranial and caudal one-third of the cerebrum with pigment extending through the surface of the cerebrum. The middle third of the cerebral surface was pink. One renal surface had 3-5 areas of depressing ranging from 1-5 mm. in diameter and darker coloration extended through the parenchyma. In the cranial lumbar spine at L1-L3 three vertebral bodies had marked bony prominences on the ventral surface extending a short distance into the abdominal cavity at the level of the kidney.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR METASTATIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC CARDIOPULMONARY DISEASE CONSPECIFIC AGGRESSION. This 14-year-old female agouti died following aggression by an anteater on exhibit. Necropsy revealed a comminuted and flaccid skull. The animal had a history of an abscess in the left facial area and cytology suggested an underlying malignancy. The animal had been doing well prior to being traumatized by a penmate.

BACTERIAL MYOSITIS HEPATITIS SPLENITIS MYCOTIC RHINITIS URATE STASIS. This 4-year-old female rattlesnake was found lethargic and unable to right itself. Edema was noted over the head. The animal was humanely euthanized due to rapid decline in condition. At necropsy multiple nodules were noted in the spleen. These were pale tan. The GI tract showed marked edema.

SEPSIS. This 2-year-old female opossum was found moribund in the morning and died shortly thereafter. It had been clinically normal the night before. Necropsy revealed fat pads protruding around the eyes petechiae in the mouth a dry pouch petechiae in the small intestines mottled liver dark gallbladder enlarged left adrenal gland dark kidneys enlarged dark pancreas thickened pericardium and enlarged perihilar lymph node.

BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA PROBABLE SALMONELLOSIS. This 2.5-year-old basilisk was found dead on exhibit. One other female had been found dead in a similar manner a few weeks earlier. Necropsy of that animal revealed egg binding and coelomitis with sepsis. A hepatic culture revealed Salmonella. The animal of this report had a small superficial abrasion over the head and neck the tail tip was black and necrotic with blackened scales extending halfway up the tail. Female reproductive tract was identified. Adhesions were noted throughout the coelomic cavity associated with a matte of thick light yellow debris and a small amount of opaque yellow-tinged fluid. The coelomic wall was inflamed. The liver was darker than expected. The kidneys were pale and had thin thread-like lesions running through them. A large C-shaped firm mass was in the coelom that contained five eggs. The lungs were inflamed. The heart had pale white patches and numerous streaks ventricle and in the atria.

CHRONIC TUBULOINTERSTITIAL NEPHRITIS CHRONIC PULMONARY AND ABSCESSATION WITHIN THE ACCESSORY LUNG LOBE EUTHANASIA. This approximately 10-year-old female warthog was euthanized due to renal failure. Gross necropsy revealed pale muscles abundant adipose in the body cavities a mottled dark and firm accessory lung lobe abundant white foam in the trachea a mottled liver small and firm kidneys an impacted stomach hemorrhagic mucosa in the duodenum and spiral colon and a left uterine mass.
TRAUMA. This captive bred 2-year-old male tanager was found dead. At necropsy there was hemorrhage at the cerebellar medullary junction.

INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This approximately 1-year-old female captive bred prairie dog died spontaneously and was refrigerated 50 hours prior to necropsy. Necropsy results revealed dark wet lungs and good body condition with no evidence of trauma or bite wounds. The lungs are submitted for microscopic examination.

NECROTIZING MYOSITIS TETANIC SEIZURES RHABDOMYOLYSIS NEPHRITIS UROCYSTITIS. This 1-year-old female agouti was found in its enclosure in the afternoon in an unresponsive state. Severe muscle spasming was noted while it was in its enclosure with its head tilted back and its arm stretched forward (opisthotonos). The patient died in transit to the hospital. Necropsy revealed good body condition a 3 cm. long superficial skin scrape on the right cranial tibia hemorrhage in the inguinal regions and a 2 mm. pale depression in the right kidney corresponding with a conical shaped fibrous structure extending towards the pelvis. No other gross lesions were seen.

SPINAL TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old male naked mole rat presented in moribund condition and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. The rat had a skin wound and contusions running obliquely across the ventral abdomen and a hematoma beneath the lumbar epaxial muscles and skin. The abdominal cavity contained free blood and adherent clots were associated with the greater omentum.

SPLENIC MYCOBACTERIOSIS RENAL FIBROSIS CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA GRANULOMATOUS SPLENITIS. This approximately 8-year-old female Rex rabbit had a history of severe weight loss dehydration poor body condition glucosuria azotemia hyperglycemia and elevated creatinine. The rabbit died spontaneously. Gross necropsy revealed straw-colored fluid in the abdominal cavity blood-tinged fluid in the thoracic cavity cortical streaking and firmness in both kidneys with the right kidney approximately 50% larger than the left and a soft 8 mm. round mass within the uterine stump.

TRACHEAL NEMATODIASIS TRACHEITIS SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 7.5-year-old male falcon was found gaping at the bottom of the exhibit. The animal was treated but later died. At necropsy inflammation was identified within the trachea. Numerous nematodes were identified in the tracheal lumen.

MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY DERMATITIS. This 8-year-old female chinchilla died. It had a history of chronic dental disease. At necropsy the left adrenal gland was enlarged. There was alopecia.

LYMPHOSARCOMA LYMPHOID LEUKOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE). This 1-year-old female chicken had a one week history of weight loss. A mass was identified in the coelomic cavity. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the bird was emaciated. The coelomic cavity contained soft solid yellow material.

TRAUMA FRACTURED TIBIA EUTHANASIA. This 7-month-old male gazelle was injured on exhibit after being chased by a zebra and fractured its tibia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified good body condition multiple abrasions on the front legs severely swollen left rear leg a closed oblique fracture at the proximal diaphysis of the tibia with multiple splintered pieces of proximal fracture segment. No other gross abnormalities were noted.

EOSINOPHILIC ENTERITIS CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM SIGNS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female wallaroo had developed an acute onset of central nervous system signs and had tested positive for Toxoplasma gondii. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal also had a positive retrovirus titer. Necropsy revealed a dead fetus in the pouch (G11-4492) bilateral consolidation in the lungs multiple foci of white discoloration on the serosal surface of the liver enlarged mammary tissue enlarged and hypertrophied duodenal wall and pinpoint foci of apparent hemorrhage in the ventricles and white matter of the brain.

EUTHANASIA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE. This 25-year-old female ruddy duck has a recent history of apparent age-related decrease in mobility that included trouble getting around flipping on its back and needing assistance to right itself. The animal otherwise had good appetite but there was recent body weight loss recorded. On examination the animal had osteoarthritis confirmed in both legs as well as the right wing. The animal was euthanized.
adult. Weight: 127 g.  Open.  Emaciation.
adult. Weight: 7.9 g.  Open. Leg trauma.

INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 9-year-old gecko died suddenly while the keeper was working in the exhibit. At necropsy areas of pallor were noted in the liver. An area of hemorrhage was present adjacent to the heart.

BACTERIAL PODODERMATITIS AND VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS. This 6-year-old scarlet ibis had been spending most of its time on the ground and apparently had a broken toe. The bird was the outcast of the group. During physical examination the bird developed respiratory distress and died. Necropsy revealed an enlarged heart with endocarditis hepatomegaly friable spleen and pododermatitis.

MELANOMA GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR EUTHANASIA. This approximately 12-year-old carpet python was donated from Ringling. It had a history of recurrent neoplasia involving the skin. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a mass on the left lateral body wall to 67 cm. from the rostrum that was firm and in the skin and subcutis. The mass was 9 cm. long 7 cm. wide and 4 cm. in depth. A granulomatous or collagenous mass surrounded a firmer layer of necrotic tissue near the ovaries.

BACTERIAL CELLULITIS. This approximately 6-year-old female lemur was found dead. The lemur had a swollen muzzle and jaw. This resulted in inspiratory difficulty. Emergency treatment was performed. At necropsy there was a large amount of mucopurulent green/brown discharge present within the left sinus. There was bilateral mammary enlargement. There is a large fat pad in the ventral abdomen. The lungs appeared consolidated with hemorrhagic dark regions. There was tan froth within the bronchi and trachea. The heart appeared large. There was a 0.5 x 0.2 cm. mineralized cream colored mass at the great vessels in the area of the heart. The right ventricle appeared large and somewhat flabby. The left ventricular wall appeared hypertrophied. The right to left ventricular wall ratio was 1:5. The liver had a nutmeg pattern and one small pale area. The pharynx was inflamed which extended around and into the glottis.

MENINGEAL HEMORRHAGE EPICARDIAL HEMORRHAGE PULMONARY EDEMA SHOCK. This 9-year-old male wallaroo was sedated for a physical exam. The animal was later found dead. Hemorrhage was noted in the oral cavity nose and one ear with an injury to the hard palate. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted over the cerebral hemispheres and brainstem.

AORTIC MINERALIZATION AGONAL BACTEREMIA NEPHRITIS ARTICULAR GOUT. This 6-year-old male iguana was lethargic and died within 24 hours. At necropsy a 1 x 2 cm. nodular mass was present at the heart base.

SUSPECT HERPESVIRUS. This male 2.75-year-old teal was found dead in wetlands exhibit. At necropsy there was mild lice infestation. There was a 1 cm. diameter patch of broken contoured feathers noted in the mid caudal cervical area. The gastrointestinal tract was largely devoid of ingesta. The spleen was large black and spherical. There was mild vascular congestion of the meningeal vessels in the rostral half of the cerebrum. Sections of brain kidney and pancreas were frozen for future use if needed.

HEPATOCELLULAR NECROSIS DUE TO SUSPECTED HEPATOTOXICITY DEGENERATIVE OSTEOARTHRITIS. This approximately 11-year-old male hooded merganser was receiving meloxicam and tramadol orally as treatment for arthritis in the left leg. The merganser was hiding for most of the day prior to death. The animal was found dead in the water. Necropsy revealed good body condition and swollen joints on the left leg. No food was present in the digestive tract. A fluid filled cyst was found in tissue near the right shoulder joint.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 20-year-old female ibex was euthanized due to severe arthritis and abnormal hoof growth. At necropsy the body was in poor condition with minimal adipose tissue depots. Hooves were misshapen with excessive growth of the hoof wall. Arteriosclerosis was noted in the great vessels. Severe arthritis with erosion of the articular cartilage and numerous osteophytes were present in the joints.

EUTHANASIA SEIZURE DISORDER NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION. This 22-year-old male mandrill was anesthetized for a dental procedure recovered normally and had blood work consistent with leukocytosis and left shift. Three days later the animal developed lethargy inappetence and watery diarrhea followed by several seizures. Anticonvulsant therapy was administered and blood work revealed mild hypokalemia and hypocalcemia. The animal’s condition deteriorated seizures continued and the mandrill did not respond to any drug therapy. An MRI revealed severe cephalic edema and material in the left auditory conduct. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a small amount of serous fluid in the laryngeal air sacs several white scars 5-10 cm. long on the superficial diaphragmatic lower part of the liver and yellow/brown discoloration of the diaphragmatic side of the liver. The pancreas was hemorrhagic the adrenal glands had hemorrhage in the parenchyma the left epididymis was filled with a suppurative exudate and material resembling stones and similar material was in the right epididymis. Much spondylosis was noted in the thoracic vertebrae. A suppurative exudate was present over the left meninges.

INTRAMUSCULAR HEMORRHAGE BACTERIAL MYOSITIS CHRONIC RUMENITIS. This 5-year-old female impala was found with facial swelling and later collapsed. The animal died despite treatment. At necropsy muscles of the jaw and neck were necrotic and foul smelling.

DERMATITIS WITH BACTERIA AND FUNGI STOMATITIS WITH BACTERIA AND FUNGI. This approximately 3.5-year-old male rhinoceros snake was found dead. The animal had chronic skin issues that were variably responsive to treatment. At necropsy there were white flecks in the oral mucosa and abnormally retained shed along the head and body. There was bright red vasculature along the kidneys.

LYMPHOMA. This 9-year-old female Bali mynah had a long history of neurological problems involving the digits of the right foot. The signs were intermittent and seemed to respond to supportive care. Recently the bird had a two week history of weight loss despite healthy appetite and normal behavior and was found dead. Necropsy revealed thin body condition diffusely enlarged liver and gallbladder pale liver and thin body condition.

ENTERITIS INANITION ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 3-year-old male reindeer was immobilized but never fully recovered from anesthesia. It was in a herd of three and was always thin despite preventative dewormings. It was on a good diet. This animal had maggots on its head and was cleaned and started antibiotics. Sections of tissues were submitted for Johne’s culture. At necropsy the spleen appeared atrophied. The heart had hypertrophy of the left and right ventricular walls.

HODGKINS-LIKE LYMPHOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old domestic ferret has a history of chronic adrenal gland disease and had been managed with a deslorelin implant. It had been diagnosed recently with malignant lymphoma and was being treated with prednisolone. It developed rapid decline in weight and energy over a 72 hour course and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation thin skin and coat condition subjectively thin right ventricle a 3 cm. round gastric lymph node adhered to the serosal surface of the stomach with disruption of the mucosal surface rounded and enlarged diffusely mottled hepatic lobes enlarged spleen enlarged and abnormally appearing lymph node chains some of which appeared hemorrhagic on cut surface thickened colon irregular renal cortices and unidentified adrenals in areas of abnormal lymph nodes.

EUTHANASIA GLOSSITIS ARTHRITIS SPONDYLOSIS. This 9-year/11-month-old male flying fox was humanely euthanized. It presented on the floor of the exhibit hypoglycemic and hypothermic. The bat had a dull mentation and poor use of its tongue and limbs. Blood work revealed left shift anemia elevated ALT AST and CPK hypoalbuminemia and hyperphosphatemia. The bat did not respond to supportive care and treatment. At necropsy the body condition was good. There were superficial wounds on the wings. Some of the interphalangeal joints were swollen. The spleen appeared small. The lungs were mottled and edematous. The tongue was traumatized. There were small lacerations and crushing injuries. The liver had a single pale focus within the parenchyma. The adrenal glands appeared enlarged.

SYNCYTIAL CELL PNEUMONIA DIC. This 22-year-old female gorilla had been inappetent for 2-3 days and had some vomiting. The gorilla was immobilized for examination and determined to be severely anemic hypoglycemic and icteric with possible hepatomegaly and decreased cardiac contractility. The animal had also been cycling early the past few months. It was found dead at morning check. Necropsy revealed icterus approximately 100 ml. of serosanguineous fluid in the thorax swollen mottled liver thick bile that appeared hemorrhagic firm and tight spleen mottled pale pink and congested lung and adhesions in the abdomen with adhesions of 5-7 cm. involving the colonic wall. The urinary bladder was full multiple cysts were on the left ovary a 5 cm. focus of small intestine was thin walled and distended mucoid discharge was present around both eyes and all lymph nodes throughout the body were enlarged and prominent.

ASPERGILLOSIS. This 35-year-old bald eagle was found with its leg caught hanging in its exhibit three weeks earlier. It was hospitalized and treated for injury to the right leg which had been severely bruised and swollen. Initial response to treatment was good but the bird deteriorated over the last 10 days of treatment and died. Necropsy revealed lesions consistent with aspergillosis in the air sacs.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE PULMONARY FIBROSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS LEIOMYOMA (UTERUS). This 50-year-old female chimpanzee had a history of weakness and ataxia and died acutely. At necropsy the mitral valve was nodular and irregular. A small white nodule was noted on the cerebrum and the brainstem was asymmetrical. Some thickening of the cerebral artery was identified.

GLOMERULONEPHRITIS. This 7-year-old male parrot was found dead in the aviary with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed missing feathers over the head good body condition slightly pale myocardium male gonads and slightly pale kidneys with some possible mineralization.

VISCERAL GOUT METASTATIC CARCINOMA. This approximately 12-year-old female python was found dead. It had a history of dysecdysis and slight weight loss six months prior to death that resolved four months prior to death. At necropsy the animal was in good body condition with adequate muscling and body fat stores. The distal one-third of the coelomic cavity had a thickened coelomic membrane that was opaque with prominent vasculature in some areas. There was clear yellow fluid present in the serosal surface of the organs and this area appeared hyperemic. The heart appeared flabby and the right atrium was almost twice the size of the left atrium. The lungs contained a small amount of white frothy fluid. The liver contained multiple small white pinpoint foci scattered over the serosal surface and within the parenchyma. There were some raised pale white to pale red firm nodules present. Ovarian tissue appeared lobulated on cut surface with small pale yellow pinpoint foci scattered over the cut surface of the parenchyma. The kidneys were difficult to identify and they appeared very pale friable and had necrotic areas of tissue but remained the normal lobulated appearance. On cut surface both kidneys appeared as lobulated areas of pale firm tissue with streaking areas of hemorrhage. Thick cream white/yellow material exuded from the cut surface. There was a necrotic mass which contained the right kidney to a portion of the colon and partially invaded the colon and was visible from within the lumen of the colon. A partial obstruction was present at this location.

SEPSIS. This 2-year-old female lemur was found dead in the incubator. It had presented with facial swelling anisocoria and labored breathing. Necropsy revealed icteric subcutaneous fluid in the head and thorax amber colored pleural effusion pulmonary atelectasis with hemorrhage yellow liver distended bile duct and gallbladder yellow discoloration and pallor in the kidneys fair body condition ecchymoses on the serosa of the cecum and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA ARHTRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CHRONIC NEPHRITIS RENAL AMYLOIDOSIS ABOMASITIS PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. This 18-year-old female gazelle was lame in the forelimb. Permanent flexion of the elbow was identified on exam and the animal was humanely euthanized due to geriatric age and declining quality of life. At necropsy the animal was thin. Mild degenerative changes were noted in the elbow. A large mass was present in the abdomen.

CONSPECIFIC TRAUMA. This 13-year-old female Swainson’s lorikeet was brought to the hospital after being found minimally responsive in a nest box. Supportive care was administered but it was found dead 30 minutes later. Necropsy revealed bruising over the cranium and extremities feather loss over the cranium and dorsum and bruising with multiple puncture wounds. No other abnormalities were noted.

PANCREATITIS. This approximately 9-month/19-day-old male lizard was found dead underneath basking site. All other individuals in the group appear normal. At necropsy the lizard’s body appeared flattened dorsoventrally.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL OSTEOMYELITIS CHRONIC DERMATITIS. This 17-year-old female boa had a history of ulcerative dermatitis and spinal osteopathy. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy skin ulcers were present over the length of the body. Marked bony proliferations were present over the distal third of the spine.

AMYLOIDOSIS CLOSTRIDIAL GASTRITIS. This 6-year-old male black-footed ferret had been under treatment for a tooth root abscess and inappetence and had poor recovery from anesthesia on 2/27. It was found dead on the cage floor the following morning. Necropsy revealed a large amount of fluid in the pleural cavity serous atrophy of fat mottled and consolidated lungs moderate amount of fluid in the peritoneal cavity possible tooth root infection multiple black/brown nodules in the liver pale enlarged kidneys and thin body wall in the area of a hernia repair on the ventral midline.

CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION INTESTINAL LYMPHOMA DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA. This 19-year-old male Siberian tiger has a history of chronic rear limb ataxia arthritis and pain and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed no abnormalities other than roughened femoral heads.

EUTHANASIA ELBOW FRACTURE MYONECROSIS MYOSITIS LYMPHADENITIS. This 1.5-year-old female gazelle suffered a fracture of the olecranon. Surgical attempts failed and marked wound dehiscence was noted. Marked weight loss was also seen and the animal was humanely euthanized due to grave prognosis. At necropsy an open wound was present over the elbow with foreign material fetid necrotic debris and exposure of the underlying bone.

EMACIATION SEPSIS INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS. This 1-year-old frog had been thin and inappetent had been isolated from the group and fed free choice and had been force fed one day prior to being found dead. Necropsy revealed decreased body condition with prominent skeletal structures 0.5 ml. of dark red fluid in the coelomic cavity focal dark discoloration of the proximal intestine and a sharp demarcation between this tissue and the stomach. The heart was pale.

EMACIATION ANEMIA CHRONIC RUMENITIS AND ABOMASITIS. This 9-year-old female gazelle was noted to be in thin body condition which had worsened after the animal calved two months earlier. The gazelle had a history of endoparasitism (strongyles) and had received treatment three weeks prior to death. Attempts to isolate this animal and its calf to increase food access were unsuccessful and this animal was found dead in the morning with no signs of external history. Necropsy revealed mildly overgrown hoof walls a deep vertical crack in the lateral claw of the right thoracic limb with splitting of the toe but no exposed bone or vital tissue generalized muscle atrophy a 4 cm. thick irregular firm pale to white mass dorsal to the aorta and possibly in the thoracic duct. The mass had a gritty texture on cut surface. Mild congestion was in the dependent lung. Serous atrophy of fat was present around the coronary vessels and what appeared to be an aneurysm was noted in the right uterine artery or vein but with no evidence of rupture. A firm clot was in the dilated vessel. Fluid and frothy digesta were in the rumen but no fiber matte was seen. Papillae sloughed easily with gentle digital manipulation. Kidneys were subjectively small. The right uterine horn was moderately larger than the left and the mucosal surface was yellow to green or purple (recent parturition).

NECROTIZING MYOCARDITIS EMC. This 18-year-old male black and white ruffed lemur is one of several lemurs at this facility to have died recently. The animal presented 24 hours prior to death with anorexia and mild lethargy but is otherwise normal in appearance. It was found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed ischemia at the apex of the left ventricle.

SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE. This 1-year-old hedgehog had a history of chronic gross hematuria although the cause could not be identified. The animal also has a history of an angiolipoma on the neck which apparently resolved on its own. It had been treated several times for mite infestation. The hedgehog was found down unexpectedly in her cage. Necropsy revealed marked gingival hyperplasia abundant adipose tissue clotted and unclotted blood in the peritoneum a large ruptured tumor in the spleen pale yellow liver some possibly displaced pancreatic tissue adhered to the serosa of the duodenum large depressed scars in the cortices of the kidneys clefts in the parenchyma of the left kidney on cut surface white coloration of the renal crests mottled green/yellow/red pulmonary parenchyma and few areas of pulmonary consolidation.

UTERINE CARCINOSARCOMA UTERINE CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA MAMMARY DUCT ECTASIA HEPATIC EOSINOPHILIC FOCI EUTHANASIA. This approximately 6-year-old female captive bred dwarf rabbit was euthanized due to progressive hind limb incoordination and difficulty getting up from a lateral position. Radiographs revealed severe spondylosis and vertebral abnormalities. The animal was electively euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed trauma around the right eye numerous cystic structures in the subcutaneous tissue along the ventral body a dark red right lung that did not float in fixative and a cystic uterine wall with a large irregular mass present.

MACRORHABDIOSIS CUTANEOUS ACARIASIS CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK. This 2-year-old male budgerigar had been removed from the exhibit due to weight loss regurgitated in its crate on the way to the veterinary clinic and was dead upon arrival. This is one of three budgerigars that were isolated for weight loss. Necropsy revealed brownish fluid dried around the beak and face thin to good body condition possible cyanosis in the legs and feet mild splenomegaly and seed in the crop and extending into the oral cavity and proventriculus/ventriculus. An area of erythema is noted along the inner lining of the proventriculus.

EPIDERMAL ULCERATION SUBOPTIMAL NUTRITIONAL STATUS. This approximately 5-year-old newt was noted one day earlier to have eye problems and was in thin body condition. Supportive care was administered and the newt was separated from the group did not eat overnight and was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition corneal fibrosis and hypopyon and corneal neovascularization and hyphema.

EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 14-year-old female ibis was euthanized due to chronic shedding of Campylobacter sp. despite repeated treatment. No significant abnormalities were identified at necropsy.

EUTHANASIA HEMANGIOSARCOMA (LIVER) INANITION RETINAL DEGENERATION. This 10-year-old chicken had severe cataracts bilaterally chronic weight loss and inappetence. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy moderate edema was noted in the lungs. The left AV valve and aortic valve were nodular. The liver was enlarged and contained numerous variably sized nodules. Some contained tan caseous material.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE PERFORATING GASTRIC ULCERS CHRONIC BRONCHITIS WITH GLANDULAR PROLIFERATION. This 13-year-old male chinchilla had a history of uremia. Supportive care had been administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed full thickness ulcers of the stomach and mottled corrugated kidneys.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC CARCINOMA CARDIOMYOPATHY ENDOCARDIOSIS STRESS. This female 17-year-old chinchilla was humanely euthanized. It had a recent history of blepharospasms inappetence and weight loss. It had been seen at the zoo hospital for tooth trims ocular exams and weight stabilization. The weight loss had stabilized although the animal remained thin. She was found agonal in her cage late on the day of euthanasia. At necropsy the animal was extremely thin. There was fur matted around the mouth. There was urine staining on the ventral side of the tail. The incisors appeared moderately overgrown but not interfering with food apprehension and chewing. The molars were worn down. The right ventricle appeared thin walled while the left appeared thickened. The lungs appeared hemorrhagic. The liver appeared enlarged with multiple tan nodules throughout. The spleen appeared enlarged and fibrous. There was a large multiloculated firm mass in the region of the stomach and right kidney. The cecum was distended. The left kidney and left adrenal appeared enlarged. The gall bladder was distended with dark colored bile.

EUTHANASIA WHITE MATTER VACUOLIZATION PITUITARY ENLARGEMENT ENTERITIS ASTROCYTOMA. This 3.5-year-old male hedgehog presented with central blindness and dilated pupils. Ocular lesions were not identified. The animal was ataxic and was euthanized.

EUTHANASIA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA THYMOMA ADENOCARCINOAM CARCINOMATOSIS. This 20-year-old female sheep was euthanized due to decrease in quality of life and chronic inappetence. At necropsy a large quantity of fluid was present in the abdomen. The uterus and thorax also contained fluid. A mass was present on the heart and adjacent to the bladder. The left adrenal was markedly enlarged.

CHRONIC HEPATOPATHY BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 17-year-old male gecko had become progressively debilitated and had difficulty ambulating requiring assisted feeding to maintain its weight. It had become increasingly inappetent and dehydrated and died despite supportive care. Necropsy revealed decreased fat stores and multiple pale circular areas in the liver.

CARDIOMYOPATHY CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE INANITION EUTHANASIA. This 13-year/6-month-old male Guam rail was humanely euthanized due to liver pathology and poor prognosis. The liver appeared very large and was covered with fibrin. There was about 30 ml. of watery-like fluid and blood tinged straw colored fluid within the coelomic cavity. There was a mass near the right testis. The spleen was small (4 mm. x 2 mm.). The lungs were wet and congested. Sections of lung liver and intestine were frozen for future use if needed.

MILD GASTRITIS RIGHT-SIDED CONGESTIVE HEART FAILUE ATRIOVENTRICULAR BLOCK (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This spayed female 7.5-year-old domestic ferret had a history of third degree atrioventricular block with intermittent syncopal episodes. The episodes had become more frequent and the animal was found dead. At necropsy there are approximately 10 ml. of serous fluid in the thoracic cavity the lungs were mottled the heart was generally enlarged the liver was mottled and the right adrenal gland was enlarged.

SHOCK STRESS PORTAL HEPATITIS. This 1-year-old female cottontop tamarin is one of several that died while in quarantine shortly after a long road trip. Necropsy revealed minimal intra-abdominal fat empty stomach minimal ingesta or feces in the intestine congested lungs and a small amount of serohemorrhagic fluid in the thoracic cavity.

HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This greater than 1-year-old male leaf-tailed gecko was found dead unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed snails present on the surface of the skin. The liver was speckled light and dark brown and the kidneys were speckled light brown and tan. Ingesta were present throughout the stomach and intestinal tract. The heart was pale pink/white and the lungs were pale.

DUCK VIRUS ENTERITIS BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA STRESS. This 8-year-old male fulvous whistling duck died after a blood sample was obtained and treatment was administered. It is one of seven fulvous whistling ducks presented from the river exhibit one morning. Four were dead and three were alive. All three live birds died either en route to the hospital or shortly after treatment. Five birds were dead in the same exhibit the previous day. These deaths constitute approximately one-third of the fulvous whistling duck population in the large outdoor exhibit that contains multiple bird species. No other bird species are affected at this time. Necropsy of this bird revealed good nutritional status and moderate adipose with little food or digested food in the gastrointestinal tract. Bumblefoot lesions were present on both feet. Clear fluid was in the mouth and air sacs and a moderate amount of clear fluid distended the crop esophagus proventriculus and ventriculus. Hemorrhages were on the serosal surface of the caeca and distal small intestine. The lumina of the small and large intestine were filled with opaque red/brown fluid. The liver was enlarged and hemorrhages were on the surface. The kidneys were pale. The testes were large consistent with seasonal reproductive hypertrophy. Multiple petechial hemorrhages were on the surface of the pancreas. Meningeal blood vessels were mildly congested.

CORONARY ARTERIOSCLEROSIS ENDOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENTERITIS ANESTHETIC DEATH. This 4-year-old male tiger died during anesthetic recovery. Serosanguineous fluid was noted in the endotracheal tube. Resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy lungs showed moderate to severe edema. The proximal duodenum was hyperemic.

MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old male budgerigar fell off its feed stick and blood was seen on the stick. The bird was easily caught off of the ground was wobbly with blood in the nares and could not grip with its left foot. Legs were blue the bird was breathing fast and shallow and pupils were dilated. The bird was in thin body condition. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a small amount of dark red fluid in the coelomic cavity numerous adhesions between the abdominal wall and coelomic organs and a soft oblong dark red mass adhered to multiple coelomic organs.

MYOPATHY WITH HEMORRHAGE (POSSIBLE CLOSTRIDIUM) PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. This 12-year-old female gazelle was found dead on exhibit and appeared to be “resting peacefully”. All three gazelles appeared to be alive five hours earlier and no recent medical problems had been noted. The last Mhorr gazelle that died died of protozoan encephalitis. Necropsy of the gazelle of this report revealed generalized autolysis endocardiosis pulmonary congestion generalized muscle pallor subcutaneous hemorrhage and no other abnormalities.
EUTHANASIA SPINAL TRAUMA. This 2-year-old male prairie dog was euthanized due to hind limb paralysis secondary to spinal cord trauma.

POSSIBLE ORAL POXVIRUS RENAL ADENOCARCINOMA AMYLOIDOSIS TRAUMA. This male approximately 25-year-old wild turkey was found dead. It was suspected to have been killed by a predator within the bison exhibit. It had housed in the bison exhibit with other turkeys bison and pronghorn. Parasitology and virology were performed. At necropsy the turkey was missing a portion of the breast muscle. There were open lacerations in the neck exposing the trachea. The skin around the neck was absent. There was a large amount of feathers absent on the back. There was a 5 cm. round laceration on the cranial left back and a larger 10 cm. laceration on the caudal right back area. There were several scrapes on the skin on the back. The trachea was severed. There were slight decreases in fat stores. The left lung was severely hemorrhagic. The trachea contained blood. Air sacs were clear. The oral mucosa on the roof of the mouth had yellow diffuse plaques. The kidneys had many white lesions 1-3 mm. in diameter with diffuse distribution throughout the medulla as well as on the surface. Sections of kidney have been frozen for future use if needed.

CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE. This approximately 12-year-old male agouti went into respiratory arrest and despite efforts to revive it died. It had been doing well since its arrival in 1999. It was housed with a female that died of bronchoalveolar carcinoma. This animal was moved to a new enclosure two weeks ago and seemed to be doing well. It was found the day of death on its side in extensor rigidity and gasping for breath. At necropsy there was blood coming out of the nostrils and copious amounts of foamy material in the oral cavity. The muscles were congested. The kidneys were swollen and grainy on the capsular surface. The pulmonary airways contained hemorrhage. The lungs had the appearance of hyperinflation. The heart was globoid and cardiac vessels were injected. There were some plaques on the leaflets of the mitral valve. There was a normal penis but no testis could be found. A structure shaped similar to a uterus but without the musculature was discovered dorsal to the bladder. The brain had some petechia.

SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA AMYLOIDOSIS. This 28-year-old male flamingo was found dead in the holding area in the morning. A coyote had been observed outside the enclosure and birds had been frightened the previous night. Necropsy revealed good body condition ant infestation good plumage bloody mucus at the choanal orifice trace blood in the lumen of the trachea abundant adipose stores and a 5 cm. mass in the coelom adhered to the valve and mesentery. Clotted hemorrhage is also associated with the adhesions. Several nodular firm lesions resembling abscesses on cut surface were present throughout the hepatic parenchyma. On cut surface the mass had texture similar to spleen and the spleen could not be located. The mass had variable areas of clotted blood or multiloculated nodules with necrotic centers. Minimal bone proliferation was in the joints.

RENAL AND ARTICULAR GOUT AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male whistling duck was euthanized due to severe lameness that was unresponsive to painkillers. Necropsy revealed good body condition and good postmortem condition. The tarsal and hock joints and surrounding tissue contain white gritty material resembling urates. The liver was small and firm and a patch of the capsule was thickened and white. The kidneys were small and dark red.

PERIBRONCHIOLITIS PROBABLE CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This 2.5-year-old domestic rat had a history of pneumonia and had been on antibiotics for several weeks. Signs progressed despite treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed congestion in both lungs.

ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA MILD CHRONIC RENAL FIBROSIS AND TUBULAR ATROPHY EUTHANASIA. This approximately 10-year- and 8-month-old female slender-tailed meerkat had a mass on the mandible resulting in difficulty eating and bleeding from the mouth. Radiographs revealed lytic lesions in the mandible. The animal was euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed slightly thin body condition and a pronounced mass invading the entire mandible. The mass involved muscle tissue and bone and extended caudally into the oropharynx. The mass involved the entire rostral section of the mandible. The lungs were congested. A single focal pinpoint white lesion was present in the liver.

EUTHANASIA CATARACT DEGENERATIVE MYELOPATHY VERTEBRAL OSTEOARTHROSIS. This greater than 19-year-old male milksnake was humanely euthanized. It had a history of difficulty moving and had a poor quality of life. Radiographs revealed a large amount of callous formation throughout the vertebral column. There were urates in the kidneys. The milksnake was thin.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS MACRORHABDIOSIS EMACIATION. This 3-year-old male budgerigar incurred a possible injury while on exhibit and was noted to have some regurgitation and tail quivering when returned to the flock. The bird subsequently died and necropsy revealed no external abnormalities or visceral gross abnormalities.
INANITION SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 6-year-old male fruit bat was found dead. At necropsy the body was thin. The heart was subjectively enlarged. There was no external evidence of trauma.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 6-year-old female kangaroo was seen lying in the pool and was found dead the following day. At necropsy lungs were hemorrhagic. The GI tract was congested.

EUTHANASIA HUMERAL FRACTURE AORTIC MINERALIZATION RENAL CYST. This 18-year-old male tamarin suffered a fracture of the distal humerus. The animal was blind and had a history of mineralization of the aorta and heart failure. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the right kidney contained a large cyst on the cranial pole. The aortic arch was mineralized.

CIRRHOSIS. This greater than 5-year-old rainbow lorikeet is from a large aviary of rainbow lorikeets. Multiple birds from this flock have died in the past year due to liver disease. This bird initially presented in December 2005 with ascites and lethargy. A liver biopsy revealed cirrhosis with pigment deposition. The bird responded to supportive care and was returned to the aviary. It represented in August 2006 for dyspnea ascites and a palpable liver had a suboptimal response to treatment and died during handling. Necropsy revealed ascites enlarged rounded multicystic liver with multiple adhesions to the ventral body wall and pericardial sac a large pale cyst in the right caudal liver lobe with white/yellow liquid and multiple smaller cysts throughout the parenchyma. The lungs were congested but floated in formalin.

HELICOBACTER GASTRITIS CERVICAL APOCRINE ADENOMAS SUBCUTANEOUS HEMANGIOSARCOMA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 12-year-old male hunting dog was depressed and unable to rise. The animal was thin and anemic with elevated BUN and was electively euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed abundant fat stores thickened and hyperpigmented skin on the legs subcutaneous masses in the dorsal cervical region a possible abscess at the ventral tail base thickened and edematous gastric rugae hyperemic thickened and edematous pylorus and small intestine and an old healed fracture of the spleen. A 2 cm. black mass was present at the cranial pole of the right kidney and was presumed to be the adrenal gland.

PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS BILIARY HYPERPLASIA SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA TOXOPLASMOSIS (PRESUMPTIVE) ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old male kangaroo has a history of anorexia and regurgitation. Elevations of BUN and creatinine were noted on blood work. A left shift with toxic changes was present on CBC. Exploratory surgery revealed a gas filled stomach with little GI motility. The animal had poor anesthetic recovery and its condition declined over the next several days with continued severe hypoglycemia. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the distal intestine contained red gelatinous material. Fluid and gas were present throughout the intestine. Pale yellow nodules were present throughout the cecum and mesentery. Lungs were consolidated and contained thick blood. Yellow nodules were present throughout the pulmonary parenchyma.

ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS SPINAL CORD NEURAXONAL DEGENERATION. This 10-year-old female meerkat had a history of chronic spinal left shoulder and stifle joint disease. The animal developed acute partial hind limb paresis with no improvement following supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed cervical and thoracic spondylosis and a narrow disc space at T6-7.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPSIS TAPEWORM CYST PNEUMOTHORAX (TRAUMA). This 4-year-old female New England cottontail rabbit was part of a captive breeding program and had given birth to a litter on 5/31/14 all of which died shortly thereafter. When placed back in the breeding pen with the male severe skin wounds and difficult breathing were identified the animal received supportive care but died shortly thereafter. Necropsy revealed bruising and several small skin wounds in the thoracic region a large full thickness skin wound over the dorsal hindquarters and a 2-3 mm. area of hyperinflated lung in the right caudal region. This rabbit was the dam of two recent neonatal submissions (G14-2678/400200-rhinitis and head trauma; G14-2679/400201-hepatic necrosis and emaciation).
BACTEREMIA. This is a 2.5-year-old female glider which was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the viscera were autolyzed but no obvious gross lesions were identified.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA BACTERIAL DERMATITIS. This 16-year-old female/spayed red wolf was humanely euthanized. The wolf had a history of intermittent soft stools until 1.5 weeks prior to death when the stools became liquid. The wolf became inappetent and cachectic. It had thoracic miliary lung pattern noted previously on radiographs. Hysterectomy was performed due to pyometra approximately three years ago. A large fibrosarcoma was excised from the left foreleg approximately four months ago. A mammary gland adenocarcinoma was also diagnosed at that time. An axillary lymph node was aspirated at that time and was found to contain adenocarcinoma. At necropsy the wolf’s body condition was thin. Both carpi had raised thickened areas with ulcerative centers. The right tarsus had a 2 cm. thickened area with large ulcerative center. The distal tip of the left pinna was thickened with fur loss. All ribs were enlarged with beaded thickening of the costochondral junctions. There was a pink bilobed cystic mass located on the right thorax immediately caudal to the elbow and was located within the muscle layer. There was a white 1.5 cm. nodule associated with the pericardium near the ventral aspect of the aorta. When incised there were inner dark layers immediately beneath the outer white surface and a cavity filled with white liquid. The right ventricle appeared thin walled. There was a 4 cm. nodular mass associated with the bronchus and the cranial aspect of the right lung lobe. The external mass was brown and when incised it had a thick grainy gray liquid. The medial aspect of the left caudal lung lobe had a bilobed mass. The parenchyma of the lung tissue appeared congested. There were glandular-looking nodules distributed throughout all of the lobes. There was a dark red 8 cm. mass within the descending aorta adhered to the thoracic surface of the diaphragm and to the quadrant and right medial liver lobes. The mass was lobulated and located primarily within the thoracic cavity. The right axillary lymph node was bilobed and gritty on cut surface. The mediastinal lymph nodes varied in appearance. The spleen had a firm white stellate scar. The kidneys had small raised plaques. The left adrenal gland was enlarged. The tongue had a 3 cm. healed laceration at the tip. The duodenum had areas of frank blood. The jejunum had raised areas of linear ulcerations.

PULMONARY SHOCK PNEUMOCONIOSIS THYMITIS HEPATITIS URATE STASIS. This 9-year-old chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the lungs were dark red and congested. The coelomic cavity contained 5-6 ml. of red to orange fluid.
TRAUMA SHOCK. This 3-year-old male teal was found dead. At necropsy a fracture of the pubis with associated hemorrhage was noted. A large blood clot was present between the lobes of the liver.

Ovary (left): Carcinoma with metastases to the kidney; uterus; lymph node; lung; adrenal; urethra; skeletal muscle; mammary gland; and large blood vessels Uterus: Mild cystic endometrial hyperplasia Vagina; uterus: Leiomyomas Kidney: Severe chronic interstitial nephritis Intestine: Moderate chronic lymphoplasmacytic enteritis Liver: Mild multifocal cholangitis Lymph node; other organs : Mild sinusoidal and perivascular hemosiderosis Tongue: Moderate hemorrhage Comment: The cause of death in this Indian rhinoceros was clearly the multiorgan dysfunction precipitated by the widely metastasizing carcinoma. Based on the most severe and largest mass; the neoplasm is most likley ovarian in origin; though it is possible that it had originated as a ductal carcinoma from the mammary gland or elsewhere and metastasized early to the ovary. The kidney changes may be secondary at least in part to the neoplastic disease; but could also have been pre-existing and contributed to this animal's debilitation (including the clinically reported edema and the hemorrhage noted in the tongue). Enteritis and cholangitis are likely related and are probably unrelated to the carcinoma

HEMOGLOBIN CRYSTALLIZATION POSSIBLE TOXICOSIS. This 5-year-old tentacled snake was found dead on exhibit along with a tankmate. Necropsy revealed autolysis darkened pulmonary surface adjacent to the liver and no other gross abnormalities.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 2.5-year-old female hedgehog was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. A recent annual exam revealed no abnormalities. Necropsy revealed good body condition frank blood on the mouth and on the vulva subjectively enlarged heart white striations in the left ventricle and in the diaphragm multiple petechiae on the mucosa of the stomach thick bile in the gallbladder and a white spot on the epiglottis.

THYMOMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female pygmy goat had a chronic history of arthritis and was being treated long-term with anti-inflammatory drugs. It had a 1-2 week history of inappetence and occasional cough progressing to weakness and unsteadiness of two days duration and some facial swelling. A mediastinal mass was identified by ultrasonography and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a mediastinal mass and generalized cellulitis in the head and neck.

GASTROENTERTIIS AMYLOIDOSIS MEMBRANOUS GLOMERULONEPHRITIS/CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE. This 6- to 7-year-old male captive bred pygmy marmoset was found dead. At necropsy the cecum contained small 1 mm. in diameter white raised firm nodule. The kidneys were irregular and mottled. The liver was slightly mottled.

RENAL ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL GOUT INANITION NEPHRITIS. This 24-year-old female Gila monster had a history of anorexia. The animal presented emaciated and dehydrated. A renal mass was identified on palpation and radiographs. The animal died despite treatment. At necropsy coelomic fat depots were absent and marked muscle loss was noted over the pelvis and vertebrae. Lungs were hyperemic. Small areas of ischemia were noted on the surface of the myocardium. A 5 cm. in diameter mass extended from the cranial pole of the left kidney. The mass impinged on the colon and bladder. The mass was filled with urate crystals.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOPULMONARY AND RENAL DISEASE. This 17-year-old male chinchilla had a history of weight loss and had been diagnosed with chronic renal failure. It developed signs of upper respiratory tract infection received supportive care but developed a short seizure and then died. Necropsy revealed an incidental ribcage deformity a mild amount of yellow-tinged slightly opaque fluid in the thorax pale lungs and pale kidneys with rough surfaces.

BRONCHOPNEUMONIA DIC HEPATIC AND RENAL NECROSIS. This 8-year-old female goat presented on August 3rd with fever anorexia coughing and depression. Blood work revealed leukopenia and supportive care was administered. The following day the goat developed bilateral nasal and ocular discharge and harsh lung sounds. Repeated blood work revealed increasing total bilirubin and serum AST. Fever eventually diminished but the animal became more depressed with mucopurulent nasal discharge with apparent pain and was found dead on the morning of 8/9. Necropsy revealed generalized lymphadenomegaly thin body condition moderate amount of yellow fluid in the thoracic cavity small nodules in each lung lobe mottled liver edematous and soft kidneys.

EMACIATION EUTHANASIA GRANULOCYTIC HEPATITIS. This 3-year-old male domestic chicken had a seven-day history of progressive weight loss with openmouthed breathing and was nonresponsive to supportive care. Blood work and radiographs did not reveal a diagnosis and the animal was euthanized. At necropsy there were no gross lesions.
SEPTIC. This 1-year-old male captive bred mole rat died spontaneously with no prior signs of illness. No gross lesions were detected at necropsy.
GASTRIC NEMATODIASIS ENTERITIS INANITION. This 12-year-old female snake was found dead without premonitory signs. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy.

BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ENCEPHALITIS CHRONIC DERMATITIS CATARACT (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 10-year-old male wallaby had a history of progressive weight loss. The animal had been under treatment for a nonhealing pressure sore on the right foot. The animal was found dead. At necropsy luxation of the lens and a hypermature cataract was noted. The animal was emaciated.

CARDIOMYOPATHY ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 10-year/8-month-old male turkey was found dead. Keepers reported a male sandhill crane chased the animal approximately 10 days ago. Previous conspecifics have died several years ago to what collection staff referred to as a mysterious virus. Several turkeys were positive for reticuloendotheliosis by ELISA testing. At necropsy the turkey had a prominent keel. There was a healing scab over the dorsal head. Several muscle bellies in the medial thigh appeared light in color bilaterally. There was diffuse mucosal erythema along the proximal aspect of the small intestine. There were focal black areas along the mucosa of the ventriculus. There were focal areas of nodular pallor in the apex of the heart.

Thymus: Moderate multifocal thymic hemorrhage Lung: Mild diffuse congestion and alveolar histiocytosis. Comments A definitive cause of death was not observed on histologic examination. Evidence of infectious disease or neoplasia was not observed. Erin B. Howey; DVM
adult. Weight: 1200.0 g.  Open; trauma. Tentative rodenticide toxicity.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA EMACIATION ABDOMINAL ADHESIONS. This approximately 15-year-old male black and white colobus monkey was undergoing treatment for weakness and dental disease when it died. Necropsy revealed gingivitis periodontal disease missing incisors and a hemorrhagic ulcerated area in the small intestine.

PREDATION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK HEPATITIS PNEUMOCONIOSIS. This 22-year-old stork was found in the woods in very thick vegetation apparently chased there by a predator. At necropsy the animal was in good body condition. Large bite wound was present across the ventral body with two punctures into the pectoral muscles and crushing injuries to the keel. Other punctures entered the caudal coelomic cavity and lacerated the lower GI tract. Lungs and air sacs contained clotted blood.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL TRAUMA HEMORRHAGIC CYSTITIS SHOCK. This 2-year-old male prairie dog was euthanized for hind limb paralysis secondary to spinal trauma. At gross necropsy the urinary bladder had a hemorrhagic mucosa and was ruptured with hemorrhage into the peritoneal cavity.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA HEPATOPATHY. This 5-year-old male fruit bat was humanely euthanized. It had a left proximal radial ulnar fracture that was repaired but was self-mutilated overnight. There was a fresh wound on the medial aspect of the left humeroulnar joint that exposed the underlying bones ligaments and tendons. An intramedullary pin was found exiting the dorsal aspect of the left radial metacarpal joint. There was minimal fat. The left cranial lung was consolidated and dark gray to black. Rabies testing was negative.

ADRENAL CORTICAL CARCINOMA LYMPHOMA HEPATOPATHY GASTRITIS. This approximately 7-year-old female ferret was humanely euthanized. This ferret had a history of weight loss for approximately 2.5 months. It also had a history of ear mites and was treated appropriately. Approximately one week prior to death the ferret became lethargic and minimally responsive to stimuli. The heart rate was 20 beats/minute. Radiographs revealed cardiomegaly. The ferret was treated symptomatically. The ferret showed some clinical improvement for approximately one week but then became unresponsive and limp. At necropsy there were multifocal yellow plaques on the serosal surface of the lungs. The mucous membranes were pale. The heart was enlarged with dilation of the ventricles. The spleen was congested and enlarged. The left adrenal gland had a nodular appearance. The right adrenal gland was slightly enlarged. The pancreas was very pale thin and had a nodule on the right arm. The liver was pale and enlarged. Kidneys were pale. The left kidney had cystic structures at the corticomedullary junction that contained brown serous exudate.
