INTRACOELOMIC BACTERIAL GRANULOMA AMYLOIDOSIS. This 3-year-old male turkey presented with lethargy but stable weight and with elevated white blood cell count and left shift. The animal responded partially to antibiotics then relapsed and died. Necropsy revealed a granuloma in the spleen.

EUTHANASIA ANEMIA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION MARROW HYPOPLASIA ERYTHROPHAGOCYTOSIS HEPATITIS. This 8.5-year-old male pygmy goat was under treatment for low hematocrit. The source of the problem was not determined but autoimmune hemolytic anemia was suspected. The animal’s condition declined and was euthanized. At gross necropsy fluid was present within the pleural and peritoneal cavities and the lungs were heavy and wet. Bone marrow was pale orange and gelatinous.

PULMONARY MINERALIZATION WITH HEMORRHAGE ARTICULAR GOUT FOLLICULAR DEGENERATION WITH BACTERIAL OOPHORITIS. This 4-year-old female frilled lizard had a history of inappetence of several days duration and presented in comatose condition with dehydration and agonal breathing. Necropsy revealed firm irregular preovulatory follicles and an enlarged darkly colored liver. The gastrointestinal tract was empty.

ESOPHAGEAL PERFORATION PERIORBITAL ABSCESS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 5-year-old female had been treated for a periorbital abscess but developed gastrointestinal stasis. The animal became stiff when tubed to be fed but returned to normal when the tube was removed. The animal was subsequently found dead the following morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition approximately 2 ml. of food in the thorax and a perforation in the esophagus near the heart. An ulcerated region was present distal to the perforation. Lungs were red and collapsed. Adrenal glands were large. Normal feces were in part of the gastrointestinal tract. Food was in the stomach. Gastric walls were thin. The colon was reddened and full of mucus. Pancreas was small. Both uterine horns were distended with clear to white liquid. A few pieces of semifirm dark tissue were in the uterine horns.

ENDOCARDIOSIS PORTAL HEPATITIS. This 14-year/9-month-old female ibis died 20 min. after it was moved to brooder for recovery. It developed stress after physical exam. It had a prominent heart murmur. It was given fluids enrofloxacin and dexamethasone. At necropsy the bird was obese. The left ventricular lumen was very small. The mitral valve appeared dysplastic. The liver was pale green/brown enlarged and had rounded margins.

ENTERITIS GASTRIC ULCER (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) INANITION. This 8-year-old male otter was lethargic and had severe weight loss. Examination revealed anemia and hypoglycemia. Pyloric ulcers were noted on gastroscopy. Treatment was initiated; however the animal was found dead. At necropsy ulcers were present in the stomach. Dark tarry feces were present in the distal GI tract.

CARDIOMYOPATHY HEMOSIDEROSIS ENTERITIS. This 12-year-old female fruit bat was found dead in gorilla exhibit. It had no recent history of problems. At necropsy there were fly eggs noted. There was a piece of melon with juice already strained out of it in the oral cavity. The heart was darkly discolored. The lungs had emphysematous bulla along the margins of all lung lobes. The liver was very dark.

PULMONARY MINERALIZATION BILIARY CYST INANITION. This 14-year-old female chuckwalla has a recent history of weight loss and exploratory surgery. At necropsy a deformity of the rostral maxilla was identified. The liver was mottled with cystic structures on the caudal margin.

PROVENTRICULAR ADENOCARCINOMA WITH METASTASIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male wild turkey had a several month history of inappetence and weight loss with recent decline and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed dark blood-like fluid draining from the esophagus thin body condition a 3 cm. in diameter mass located at the point of the liver and isthmus adhesions were noted along the left coelomic wall with collapse of the cranial and caudal thoracic air sacs. The left lung was partially collapsed and diffusely necrotic. Multiple white 1 cm. lesions were present throughout the myocardium including a perforating mass within the ventricular septum and right ventricle. Hemorrhagic dark fluid is present in the crop. The wall of the crop was thickened. The isthmus of the proventriculus was irritated and a diverticulum had formed where the 3 cm. in diameter mass was attached. Normal proventricular tissue was present distally. Small white plaques were present along the serosal wall of the small intestine. The kidneys were pale and irregular.

ASPIRATION. This 4-year/5-month-old male wild dog was found down on the ground blue with dilated pupils and was unable to be resuscitated with CPR. Food was lodged in the mouth and trachea. At necropsy the dog was in good body condition with ample fat stores. There was a small 0.5 cm. brown oval structure attached to the surface of the lung on the left side. There was over 1 lb. of diet in the stomach and some in the esophagus. The mucosal lining of the stomach appeared red over half of its surface. The proximal duodenum was red and inflamed looking with mucus adhered to the mucosal lining. A small segment of the jejunum had similar appearance.

CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA GASTRITIS PANCREATITIS HEPATITIS THYROID HYPERPLASIA. This 17-year-old male red panda had a history of chronic weight loss and muscle atrophy. Exam revealed elevated BUN and creatinine. The animal was humanely euthanized due to declining condition and geriatric age. At necropsy generalized muscle wasting was noted. Brown/tan lesions were noted throughout the lungs. Erosions and ulcers were noted in the GI tract. Kidneys were irregular and contained small cysts.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK (PROBABLE ENTEROTOXEMIA) GASTRIC HEMORRHAGE GASTRIC BLOAT. This 3-month-old male ferret was normal the previous day and found dead unexpectedly in its cage the following morning. Its cagemate is clinically normal but possibly a bit quiet. Necropsy revealed good body condition markedly distended abdomen due to gas and fluid accumulation in the gastrointestinal tract. Mild to moderate mural petechiation is noted in some segments of the intestine. A few hairballs are in the stomach. Mild atelectasis and a few areas of compression or congestion are noted in the lungs. The heart is large round and firm and the left ventricular wall is thicker than expected.

CONSPECIFIC TRAUMA. This 1-year-old female rabbit was part of a captive breeding colony and was found dead in the breeding pen with external wounds the day after introduction to a male. Necropsy revealed good body condition some autolysis some postmortem insect scavenging extensive trauma in the right hind limb around the lateral thigh with associated exposure of the femur and avulsion of several muscle bellies with associated bruising. Degloving injuries and deep lacerations were present in the ventral cervical region. Normal gut contents were noted and no visceral gross lesions were seen.

EUTHANASIA CATARACTS BODY WALL ROUND CELL TUMOR (PRESUMPTIVE LYMPHOMA). This 19-year-old male Madagascar day gecko was geriatric and had a previous diagnosis of cataracts. This animal had an enlarging subcutaneous tissue mass that was previously diagnosed as a round cell tumor and was euthanized.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old female rattlesnake had a several month history of inappetence and several episodes of regurgitation. A gastric wash was negative for cryptosporidia. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a distended gallbladder and no other abnormalities.

CHRONIC ENTERITIS SPLENIC EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS VACUOLAR DEGENERATION. This 2.5-year-old male ferret presented with lethargy and weight loss. Severe anemia and marked leukopenia were noted. The animal’s condition continued to decline despite treatment and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy mucous membranes were pale and icteric. Serosanguineous oral and nasal discharge was present. The heart was enlarged and rounded. The liver was large pale and contained multiple punctate white foci. The spleen was enlarged and firm. A large quantity of digested blood was present in the stomach and duodenum.

ISLET CELL CARCINOMA INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE SHOCK ASSOCIATED WITH PRIOR SURGERY. This 4-year-old male/castrated ferret was examined for abdominal distention and alopecia and found to have marked splenomegaly a pancreatic mass and bilaterally slightly enlarged adrenal glands. Exploratory laparotomy was performed and several biopsies were obtained. Recovery was uneventful but the animal was found dead 10 hours later. Necropsy revealed bruising cellulitis and subcuticular hemorrhage and edema at the abdominal incision site. A small amount of free blood was in the abdomen. The lungs had serosanguineous fluid on cut surface. The gastrointestinal blood vessels were moderately congested. Multiple 1 mm. foci were present in all lobes of the liver. The spleen was markedly enlarged. A 4 mm. nodule was in the pancreas. The left adrenal gland was slightly large. The right adrenal gland was also slightly enlarged.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY PULMONARY ADENOMA. This 6-year-old female opossum developed sudden acute collapse with cyanosis. Necropsy revealed serosanguineous fluid in the chest a 1 cm. raised white nodule in the right lung lobe edematous trachea and larynx and no other abnormalities.

LYMPHOMA EUTHANASIA. This 12-year-old female cottontop tamarin has a several year history of colitis which was treated symptomatically. It recently developed an acute loss of body condition over a 2-3 week period and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes when intra-abdominal surgery revealed masses in the alimentary tract and lymph nodes.

EGG IMPACTION (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) BRONCHOPNEUMONIA HEPATITIS. This 3-year-old lory was examined for possible egg binding. An egg was palpable in the coelomic cavity. Cardiac arrest ensued and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy the jejunum and right kidney were hemorrhagic. An egg was present in the oviduct and scar tissue was present in the cloaca.

EUTHANASIA ADRENAL CARCINOMA HEMANGIOSARCOMA GASTROENTERITIS. This 5-year-old female ferret had adrenal cortical disease approximately one year ago. The animal was euthanized due to deteriorating quality of life. At necropsy a 3-4 cm. red friable mass was present in the left inguinal area just beneath the skin. A large tan mass approximately 6 x 8 x 5 cm. was present attached to the right kidney and adherent to the right lobe of the liver. A 3 cm. cortical cyst was present in the left kidney.

SERTOLI CELL TUMOR. This greater than 9-year-old zebra finch was found on the ground in the exhibit. The bird had a coelomic mass and was breathing heavily. Supportive care was administered but the bird was found dead the next morning. Necropsy revealed a large mass in the coelomic cavity in the region of the testis. Normal testis was not visible. A small amount of clotted blood was in the coelomic cavity and lungs were congested.

BRONCHOINTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 9-year-old female corn snake was observed to have blood at the back of its mouth but no other signs of illness. It was found dead in its cage the following day with a profuse amount of blood on the cage floor. This snake had been housed next to three Dumeril’s boas suspected of having a primary infectious event involving the esophagus and respiratory tract. Necropsy revealed good body condition with dehydration generalized pallor hemorrhage in the lung and possibly thickened parenchyma blood throughout the gastrointestinal tract severely distended colon filled with ingesta firm urates in the urodeum dark brown kidneys incompletely formed eggs in the oviduct empty stomach small gallbladder and no source for the blood in the intestine.

COAGULOPATHY FRACTURED CORACOID ISCHEMIC WINGTIP NECROSIS. This 40-year-old male Chilean flamingo developed sudden onset of wing droop in late April and radiographs revealed a fractured coracoid bone. Blood work revealed elevated serum AST and CK consistent with muscle trauma. The animal did not improve with three weeks of wing immobilization. The wings subsequently began oozing and became cold at the tip just above the carpus with associated swelling and oozing from the skin. Supportive care was administered but the bird was found dead the next day. Necropsy revealed much blood in the mouth and around the head blood in the lumen of the trachea mild congestion of the tracheal wall and severe hemorrhage of the esophageal wall along its entire length with blood present in the lumen. A small amount of bloody mucoid fluid was in the proventriculus. Sand was in the ventriculus admixed with a small amount of blood. The entire length of the small intestine was reddened and had bloody luminal contents. The distal colon contained fecal material and was grossly normal in appearance.
SHOCK RENAL GOUT CHRONIC ENTERITIS HEPATITIS. This 2-year-old rooster was found dead. At necropsy petechial hemorrhages were noted in the GI tract. An irregular pale area was noted in the kidney.

UROLITHIASIS URINARY OBSTRUCTION. This 2-year-old male warthog died. It had hematuria noted three days prior to death. It was treated with antibiotics Flumexin meglumine and intravenous fluids. This warthog died three weeks after another warthog died. At necropsy the bladder wall was thickened and had some hemorrhage. There was a single urolith found in the pelvic urethra. Analysis of the urolith revealed 100% calcium carbonate.

INTERVERTEBRAL DISK DEGENERATION HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old captive bred female lemur was euthanized on July 7 2011 due to chronic spinal arthritis and neurologic deficits to the rear limbs. The animal also had chronic weight loss and muscle loss. Gross necropsy revealed no fat stores severe muscle wasting loss of mobility in lumbar sacral and coccygeal spinal column and a mass within the caudate lobe of the liver.
juvenile. Weight: 42.4 g.  Lung pathology.

LEFT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY WITH CHRONIC PASSIVE CONGESTION. This 2-year-old male chinchilla was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed a moderately enlarged right ventricle and thin right ventricular free wall. The left ventricular wall was subjectively thickened. Kidneys were slightly pale with a dark red medulla.

DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE NECROULCERATIVE CELLULITIS SEPSIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 28-year-old male saki monkey had a necrotic wound extending from the shoulder blades to the pelvis incorporating skin muscle and dorsal spinal processes. The animal also had two episodes of necrotic tail tip in 1998 and again in 2014. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed that the wound extended into the vertebrae. The animal was in poor body condition heart had a rounded apex the left atrioventricular valve was thickened and rough minimal fat stores were noted the liver was slightly enlarged spleen was prominent and the urinary bladder was distended.

Kidney: Severe chronic interstitial nephritis and glomerulosclerosis (End stage kidney) Body as a whole: Severe arterio- and arterioloslerosis with mineralization and fibrinoid necrosis Liver: Capsular gout (Visceral gout) Heart: Mild multifocal myofiber mineralization Stomach: Severe laminar mucosal mineralization Heart: Myxosarcoma (presumptive) Comment: The cause of death and the multi-organ metastatic mineralization in this animal is kidney failure; a common finding in iguanas. This is a multifactorial disease; likely related to diet; hydration status; stress; and other factors. The tumor in the wall of the heart was interesting; but not likely clinically relevant.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE GASTRIC MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male agouti was found in left lateral recumbency and unresponsive. It was unable to get up or move. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. It had a history of chronic renal disease. Necropsy revealed yellow bumpy and shrunken kidneys with scarring and indentations and areas of black to blue discoloration in the parenchyma. Adrenal glands were enlarged and had yellow coloration. The spleen contained tiny white infiltrates.

AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 6.5-year-old female/spayed ferret had a three-day history of lethargy and decreased appetite with vomiting and diarrhea and elevated renal values. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified cardiomegaly gastric ulceration a cyst in the liver irregular and pitted kidneys and reddened pancreas and lungs.

COLITIS INANITION SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 13-year-old female colobus had a three month history of colitis and diarrhea unresponsive to antibiotics and anti-inflammatories. No significant gross lesions were identified at necropsy. Blood work revealed hypoproteinemia elevations of BUN CPK and plasma T4. Hematocrit hemoglobin and serum potassium were low.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS DISSEMINATED HISTIOCYTIC INFILTRATE ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 29-year-old male baboon had a history of chronic central nervous system disease characterized by left-sided hemiparesis and dysphagia. An MRI revealed numerous microabscesses and cystic lesions in the cerebrum and left thalamus. glucose in september was mildly increased (he was anesthetized with an alpha-2) and urine was negative for glucose. The baboon tested for SIV (neg) and SA-6 (pos) in 2006. In 2008 he was tested for SIV SA-8 HSV-1 HSV-2 HVZ CHIMP CMV EBV-VCA and SA-6; he was positive for EBV-VCA and SA-6. In May 2012 he was negative for STLV-1.  Supportive care was administered but the condition progressed when medications were discontinued. The baboon also had osteoarthritis and lumbar spondylosis particularly in the cervical thoracic spine. Supportive care for the osteoarthritis was also administered. Eventually the baboon had difficulty prehending food and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed muscle wasting multiple superficial abrasions over the ischial pads and tail hair loss 6-10 black nodules up to 1 cm. in greatest dimension on the mucosal surface of the tracheal bifurcation and the nodules oozed black liquid on cut surface. Numerous gray to black pinpoint discolorations were noted in all pulmonary lobes. A mild globoid appearance to the heart was noted and the right ventricular free wall was subjectively thin. Mild generalized periodontal disease was noted. The liver was congested with rounded borders and a reticular pattern. The spleen was congested and two small nodules were present in the perisplenic fat resembling accessory spleens. A few shallow cortical defects were noted in the kidneys and the adrenal glands were pale and gritty. Muscles of the right limb were contracted and the stifle and hip could not be extended. Cortical bone of the vertebral column was thin and weak and the spinal column was easily transected.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS CARDIAC FIBROSIS ANKYLOSING SPONDYLOSIS SEPTATE GALLBLADDER EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female tamarin had a one week history of decreased appetite and mobility that progressively worsened and the animal was subsequently euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed generalized muscle atrophy lumbar spondylosis slight pericardial effusion distended and tortuous gallbladder and bilateral renal pallor with pitted surfaces.

RENAL AND ARTICULAR GOUT EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male frilled lizard had an inability to use its rear limbs especially the right leg and had swollen joints was inappetent and lethargic. A conspecific had a similar course with evidence of severe goat. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed fat pad asymmetry with one normal and one enlarged and possibly central calcifications or tophi. The joints were swollen and the kidneys were small. An obstructive stone was in the cloaca. The lungs and liver were abnormal.

DEGENERATIVE RENAL AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. This 20.5-year-old male common marmoset had a history of chronic renal failure with cachexia and weakness fell off its perch onto its head was obtunded and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a subdural hematoma renal fibrosis aortic sclerosis and rigidity hepatic lesions enlargement of one adrenal possible thyroid enlargement and severe cachexia.
AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC ENTERITIS CHRONIC HEPATITIS. This approximately 33-year-old male flamingo died during transport to its exhibit. At necropsy the kidneys were swollen and pale.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS EUTHANASIA. This 7-year-old male budgerigar presented for euthanasia due to chronic regurgitation issues and failure to respond to treatment. Necropsy revealed inflammation in the lower esophagus and possibly in the pancreas. Pinpoint hemorrhages were noted on the back of the skull.

VOLVULUS. This approximately 3-year/8-month-old female rabbit presented as an emergency gastric dilatation and died while being prepped for surgery. At necropsy there was severe gastric dilatation. There was gas distended duodenum. There were petechial hemorrhages on the serosal surfaces. There was a severely congested section of jejunum with a distinct line of demarcation between the duodenum and jejunum associated with a twist in the bowel loop near the cranial mesenteric artery.

GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL GOUT BACTERIAL ABSCESS. This 5-year-old female snake had intermittent periods of regurgitation for several years duration especially severe over the last month. Radiographs identified a mass in the proximal third of the body in the area of the liver and a mass in the kidney associated with calcification. Blood work identified severely elevated uric acid and calcium levels. This snake was related to another snake that was diagnosed with gout and renal carcinoma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Postmortem findings included distention in portions of the gastrointestinal tract two raised masses in the liver mineralization and enlargement of the renal parenchyma and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC NEPHRITIS GLOMERULSCLEROSIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS VENO-OCCLUSIVE DISEASE IRIDOCYCITIS CATARACT CYSTIC ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA. This 18-year-old female leopard had a history of renal disease. The animal was found dead. At necropsy multifocal and coalescing firm foci were noted throughout the lungs. Multifocal firm lesions were also noted in the spleen. Kidneys were firm and pale.

ENTERITIS HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS. This is a 25-year-old hyacinth macaw. The bird was found dead and no additional clinical information was provided. At gross necropsy a mass was present in the coelomic cavity near the sacral area approximately 18 x 22 x 10 mm. Also there was a foreign body and obstruction present within the ileum grossly identified as a pine nut. Scattered pinpoint yellow to tan foci were scattered throughout the liver. Foci of hemorrhage were also noted beneath the koilin layer in the ventriculus.

PANCREATIC FIBROSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male black tailed prairie dog is from a colony diagnosed with Giardia and coccidiosis. Treatment was commenced but this animal did not improve with treatment. The animal became weaker and more lethargic and continued to lose weight despite supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a globoid heart congested lungs and a 3 mm. white plaque adhered to the serosal surface of the bowel.

ASPERGILLOSIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA TRACHEITIS HEPATITIS INANITION. This 30-year-old female flamingo was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the right lung was infiltrated by multiple yellow to white caseous masses extending to the bronchi and nearly occluding the syrinx. The animal was identified as a male at necropsy.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 25-year-old male squirrel monkey had a history of chronic weight loss and poor body condition ataxia falling from the perches and associated trauma. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition bruising on the lateral side of the right eye and bruises and associated ischemia under the left eye. No visible fat stores were seen and muscles were atrophied. The aorta was prominent and white. Darkened corticomedullary junctions were in the kidneys.

RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT. This approximately 6-year-old female budgerigar was found dead. No prior medical history was noted. Necropsy revealed bruising on the pectoral muscle mottled friable kidneys and white mottled pericardium.

DISSEMINATED INFECTIOUS DISEASE PROCESS POSSIBLE WEST NILE VIRUS. This 6-year-old female rainbow lory was apparently healthy and was found dead unexpectedly during the morning check. Five of ten lories have died in the last 2-3 weeks. The birds are housed in a large outdoor free flight aviary. Necropsy revealed an enlarged liver and spleen with mild hyperemia of the serosal surfaces of the small intestine. A moderately sized brain hemorrhage was noted at the base of the skull. There is a recent history of hepatitis and enteritis in lories from this facility.

CYSTIC CALCULI (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) CYSTIC PERITONITIS HEPATIC NECROSIS. This 2-year-old male rabbit was found dead. At necropsy the bladder was markedly distended with brown firm sand-like material. The mucosa was hemorrhagic. White foci were present throughout the liver.

SEMINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old male chicken developed a voice change in October 2015. Radiography identified a large mass that occupied the mid to caudal coelomic cavity. The bird’s weight remained stable until December when it developed mild ascites. The bird presented in February agonal and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified a 5 cm. mass in the caudal coelom and an 8 mm. cystic necrotic pocket within the mass. A few 1 cm. pink masses were disseminated throughout the body cavity.

HEAD TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SYSTEMIC SHOCK. This 4-year-old female wallaby hit the chain link fence surrounding the exhibit and died. At necropsy bruising was present on the skull and hemorrhage was within the brain.

EUTHANASIA ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA AMYLOIDOSIS GASTRITIS. This 11-year/1-month-old male pig was humanely euthanized due to hind limb ataxia. At necropsy both kidneys were cystic. A portion of the jejunum appeared hyperemic. There was a 3 cm. hard dry blood clot adhered to the right ventricular wall. The stomach was full of ingesta. There was normal stool in the colon. The right femoral head had a few erosions.

WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME ASTROCYTOMA CHRONIC UROCYSTITIS WITH SEPSIS PAPILLARY NECROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 1-year-old male hedgehog had a history of intermittent and mild leaning to the right which progressed to weakness ataxia and dull mentation loss of appetite and weight loss. The animal did not respond to a five day trial of meloxicam and omega-3. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

HEPATITIS ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 10-year-old egret had a history of poor feather condition and was found dead. At necropsy sparse feathering was present over the breast and abdomen. A large clot of blood was present over the keel.

BACTERIAL PERITONITIS WITH ABSCESSES. This approximately 1-year-old female rat was found dead. Necropsy revealed a 5 cm. intra-abdominal mass that communicated with the body wall in the inguinal region. Walled off abscesses were adhered to the liver and spleen.

BACTERIAL ENDOMETRITIS HISTIOCYTIC SARCOMA (LUNG). This 2-year-old female rat had a three week history of vaginal bleeding and rapid respirations. Treatment was unsuccessful and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy five 0.5-1 cm. in diameter firm nodular masses were present in the left uterine horn. The lung was 75% consolidated and firm with tan to yellow tissue on section.

SEPSIS EMACIATION POSTPARTURIENT STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old female colobus has a six week history of illness that included unkempt appearance although appetite and behavior were mostly normal. A conspecific had a baby six weeks earlier. On two occasions mild incoordination was noted in this animal. It has been unsuccessfully treated for Capillaria infection four weeks earlier and then received fenbendazole 10 days prior to death. The animal delivered a term normal appearing stillborn infant two days prior to death and passed normal appearing placenta 24 hours later with no hemorrhage noted. Mild postparturient lethargy was attributed to parturition but the animal was found moribund with seizure activity the next morning. Examination revealed distended abdomen severe hypoglycemia and hypocalcemia liquid diarrhea moderate ascites and a thickened and empty uterus. Supportive care was administered but the animal arrested during the procedure was resuscitated but then arrested again and resuscitation was not attempted. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of straw-colored clear fluid in the abdomen similar fluid in the thorax purple right lung and normal left lung hyperemic omentum devoid of fat a serosal scar associated with purple vessels on the serosa of the stomach fibrous and hemorrhagic digesta adhered to the mucosal surface at this site liquid digesta in the small and large intestine and some hemorrhage noted distally markedly thickened but intact uterus with sloughing endometrium mild renal pallor pale thyroids injected meninges and cataracts. E. coli was cultured from the liver and spleen.

MANDIBULAR OSTEOMYLETIS EMACIATION NEPHROSCLEROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male kangaroo had a two month history of osteomyelitis involving the right mandible that was unresponsive to treatment. The condition was accompanied by severe weight loss and the animal was euthanized.
EUTHANASIA FEMORAL FRACTURE SHOCK ENTERITIS. This 18-year-old female addax was euthanized due to a fracture of the right femur.

MAST CELL TUMORS SKIN. This 10-year-old male African hunting dog was anesthetized to evaluate acute onset of nonweight bearing rear limb lameness inappetence and facial wounds associated with conspecific aggression. A conspecific recently was euthanized due to gastric rupture. During the anesthetic procedure some small skin growths on the right hip and flank were removed.
adult. Weight: 248.3 g.  Euthanasia. Poor body condition. Neoplasia; multilobular; mesocolon. Fighting injuries.
MYCOBACTERIOSIS GRANULOMATOSIS. This 4-year-old tentacled snake was found dead in its enclosure. Necropsy revealed generalized autolysis of tissues and no gross lesions.

BACTERIAL/YOLK/FOREIGN BODY COELOMITIS BACTERIAL SEPTICEMIA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA ESOPHAGEAL GLANDULAR ABSCESSES. This 2-year-old female chicken died on exhibit. Necropsy revealed thick yellow viscous fluid consistent with yolk material throughout the coelomic cavity. The spleen was pale pink. The oviduct was dark red and diffusely thickened. Two desiccated empty leathery shells were found within the oviduct.

CHRONIC BACTERIAL INFECTION WITH PNEUMONIA VENTRICULAR THROMBOSIS STEATITIS HEPATITIS AND VERTEBRAL OSTEOMYELITIS. This approximately 7-year-old male palm pit viper was removed from the exhibit on June 12th because of a cut on the neck. The wound appeared to be healing but the snake refused to eat on June 18th and was found dead on June 21 2014. Gross necropsy revealed swelling and red discoloration on the dorsal right neck with proliferation of tissue and/or exudate in the subcutis adequate body fat stores red and white discoloration of the adipose a thickened lung a prominent thyroid gland a swollen liver mild pinpoint raised foci in the liver scant feces in the distal intestines and petechial hemorrhage in the cloaca.

PERIRENAL HEMATOMA ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 10-year/2-month-old female junglefowl was humanely euthanized. It was unable to use its right leg. The leg was cold. At necropsy the body condition score was 2. The tarsi were swollen bilaterally with the right greater than the left. The right leg was rotated outward. The liver was soft friable and tan to light brown. The caudal pole of the right kidney was large 2 x 1 cm. and green to black firm and round. The mass was present in layers. Fecals were positive for coccidia.

SHOCK TRAUMA MACRORHABDIOSIS CHRONIC COLITIS. This 3.5-year-old male budgerigar was found dead at morning check and had no prior medical history other than being a poor flyer as a juvenile. Necropsy identified no gross lesions.

INTESTINAL NEMATODIASIS WITH SEPSIS (PARASTRONGYLUS). This 6-year-old tamarin presented for loose stool and vocalizing while defecating in the morning. Examination identified a firm mass palpable in the right caudal abdomen. Supportive care was administered and exploratory surgery was performed that afternoon. The intestines were erythematous the cecum was firm and thickened and a granuloma extended through the mucosal wall. A second firm granulomatous-like mass was palpated in the jejunum and appeared to be causing at least partial obstruction. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A conspecific was euthanized for gastrointestinal problems a few months earlier and was diagnosed with perforating ulcers of the duodenum and cecum.

CAPILLARIASIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA YOLK COELOMITIS. This 1-year-old female chicken was found dead in the holding area in the morning. The animal had been treated for lice over the past several weeks but had not received an ivermectin injection for two weeks. Necropsy revealed bilateral pododermatitis and lice.

ENTERITIS INTERSTITIAL PNEUMONIA. This 4.5-year-old male lory was under treatment and was found dead. At gross necropsy the feathers were missing over the head and neck. There were foci of bruising and edema beneath the skin of the pectoral and abdominal muscles.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS FIBROMATOSIS EMACIATION EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female Burmese python has a one year history of moderate progressive weight loss and a four week history of a mass on the maxillary arcade previously diagnosed as a polyp (G14-0827). Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. mass on the maxilla multiple erythematous round flat nodules in the coelom marked thickening of the gastric mucosa and multiple raised bullous nodules up to 3 cm. in greatest dimension throughout the small intestine and large intestine with associated intussusception.

INANITION PODODERMATITIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 10-year/4-month-old male scarlet ibis was found dead in its enclosure. It had presented several days previous for emaciation with chronic bumblefoot lesions. The ibis was treated symptomatically. At necropsy there were numerous pinpoint white spots within the liver. The keel muscles were extremely atrophied. The heart was somewhat flaccid. Sections of liver were frozen for future use if needed.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA RENAL ADENOMA RENAL MINERALIZATION. This 15-year-old male gazelle presented with nonweight bearing rear leg lameness. A compound fracture of the proximal femur was identified and the animal was humanely euthanized.

TRAUMA CAPILLARIASIS EUTHANASIA. This 6-year-old male quail was euthanized following trauma to the head and osteomyelitis of the foot. Necropsy revealed a 2.5 cm. circular abrasion on the back of the skull that was completely denuded and the skull bone was visible. The plantar surface of the left digit #2 was swollen and had an open granulomatous wound. The lungs had a dark mottled appearance and a 0.5 cm. dark cream-colored mass was in the spleen.

LYMPHOSARCOMA EUTHANASIA. This approximately 2-year-old female chicken was losing weight despite having a good appetite. Celiotomy revealed a pale liver thickened intestinal loops and a small mass on the serosa of the small intestine. The chicken was electively euthanized. Gross necropsy revealed multifocal round masses throughout the liver numerous gastrointestinal nematodes and a small intestinal serosal mass.

NECROTIZING MYOCARDITIS PROBABLE EMC. This 20-year-old female/spayed mandrill had a one day history of anorexia and intermittent vomiting with depression. It was immobilized and determined to be dehydrated and had a severe infection in the inguinal area attributed to bacteria and yeast infection. Necropsy revealed pulmonary edema pericardial effusion and pale streaking throughout the heart muscle. The animal also had severe spondylosis and degenerative arthritis in the stifles and other major joints.

ENCEPHALITIS (BAYLISASCARIS-LIKE) CESTODIASIS NEMATODIASIS FOREIGN BODY PERITONITIS EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old female New England cottontail rabbit is part of a captive breeding program of New England cottontails. It presented with ataxia after recently weaning a litter but was eating and defecating normally. Examination was unremarkable. The rabbit’s condition deteriorated in spite of supportive care and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. A conspecific with similar but less substantial signs tested negative for encephalitozoonosis and pasteurellosis although an antibody titer for Pasteurella was positive. Necropsy revealed a serosanguineous bilateral nasal discharge bilateral dark mottled lungs that floated in formalin six or seven 3-4 mm. cystic structures in the abdominal cavity caudal to the liver and along the gastric border and no other abnormalities.

DISSEMINATED INFLAMMATION AND NECROSIS HERPESVIRUS-LIKE INCLUSIONS. This 19-year-old male Madagascar tree boa was found dead on display with no prior signs of illness. Necropsy revealed erythema in the gums adequate fat stores bilateral pulmonary hemorrhage hemorrhage in the mucosa of the stomach and small intestine few areas of dark purple discoloration of the intestine thickening of the mucosa of the stomach firm and white pancreas and firm spleen.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA STRESS GOUT. This approximately 12-year-old male tree monitor was found dead in its enclosure. It was received from another institution approximately one month ago and had been in quarantine since that time. While in quarantine the monitor showed typical stress response behaviors and refusal to eat. At necropsy the monitor was in good body condition. There were large abdominal fat pads. The spleen had a focal white lesion at the cortical edge. The lungs were congested and spongy. There were irregular deposits of chalky white substance over the serosal surface of the pericardium and on the epicardial surface. There were small hemorrhages around several teeth. There were ulcers on the gastric mucosa. The intestinal mucosa appeared generally erythematous. There was mild rectal prolapse. Liver was enlarged and spotted black and yellow.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA HEMOCHROMATOSIS. This 9-year/9-month-old male fox died several hours postoperative for removal of a large liver tumor. At necropsy there were multiple tan nodules on all liver lobes ranging from 3-10 cm. The repaired vena cava was visualized and seemed secure. There was no evidence of postoperative bleeding other than that soaked up by the gel foam and collagen pad.

EUTHANASIA DERMATITIS SUBCUTANEOUS FISTULA WITH FOREIGN BODY. On September 30 2010 keepers reported that the dorsal side of the right toes of this 14-year-old male fruit bat were abraded and blistered and that the ankle joint was swollen. Tissue on the medial and distal portion of the right leg was necrotic. There was hard dead tissue running from a wound near the dorsal aspect of the tail region to the right foot. This animal was housed side-by-side with other Rodriguez fruit bats. At the time of examination the body weight was 0.297 kg which is down 7.1% compared to a previous average weight of 0.334 kg. The bat continued to have chronic decreased activity and appetite and was euthanized.

ARTHRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 18-year-old female addax has a history of increased stiffness and lameness over the past few weeks and was found recumbent and unable to stand. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bruising along the facial region attributed to impacts with the ground. Moderate hemorrhagic fluid was present in the cerebral ventricles and the remainder of the brain was grossly within normal limits. Mild to moderate arthritis and cartilaginous erosion were present in multiple joints including both coxofemoral joints and stifles. The left stifle was most severely affected. Moderate mucosal hemorrhage was noted throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

DISSEMINATED PROTOZOAN INFECTION PROBABLE MALARIA. This 1-year-old female tern died. Necropsy revealed good body condition a small amount of clear to serosanguineous fluid in the coelomic cavity and no other abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ENTERITIS. This 19-year-old peacock had been under treatment for aspergillosis. Severe arthritis was present in the hind limb. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the stifle joint was dry and contained orange dried material. Marked erosion of articular cartilage was noted.

CERVICAL TRAUMA SHOCK. This 1.5-year-old female gerenuk ran into a fence and died. At necropsy a large hematoma was present over the cervical region with fracture of C2 and severance of the spinal cord between C1 and C2.

BACTERIAL SALPINGITIS WITH SEPSIS NONSUPPURATIVE MYOCARDITIS SARCOCYSTIS (SKELETAL MUSCLE). This 8-year/10-month-old female crocodile monitor was found dead. It was being bled monthly for a research project. The packed cell volume had dropped from low 30’s in January and February to 15 in March. At necropsy there was marked pericardial effusion. The heart was contracted. There was small amount of ingesta present within the stomach. There was digesta present within the small intestine. The intestines appeared thickened and nodular. There was digesta present within the large intestine. The liver was mottled yellow and dark red with a reticular pattern. The spleen was markedly contracted. Areas along the oviduct were dark red/brown. There was little follicular activity. The fat bodies appeared to be subcutaneous and pushed the peritoneum away from the body wall. There was marked hemorrhage into the subcutaneous fat along the left ventrolateral body wall. Samples of small intestine liver kidney and cloaca with oviduct were frozen for future use if needed.

MEMBRANOPROLIFERATIVE GLOMERULOPATHY SERTOLI CELL TUMOR. This 16-year/6-month-old male lemur died. It was a geriatric animal with a long history of medical problems. This lemur had seasonal allergic dermatitis and associated pyoderma. It also had dental disease including tooth root abscesses and worn teeth. A liver biopsy confirmed hemosiderosis and a recent kidney biopsy 16 days prior to death confirmed glomerulonephropathy. In addition this lemur had routinely low blood glucose levels during immobilizations and often elevated insulin values suggesting possible insulinoma. Surgery did not find an insulinoma but medical management was initiated. This lemur was treated empirically with diazoxide for suspected insulinoma. Liver/kidney iron levels are pending. At necropsy the lemur was in good body condition. Cartilage on the left femoral head appeared thin. There was free blood within the peritoneal cavity. There were adhesions from the spleen to the capsule of the left kidney. There were free hematomas within the peritoneal cavity. The pancreas was difficult to locate given the hemorrhage and adhesions in the peritoneal cavity. The liver was tan and had sharp edges. The left kidney measured 7.5 x 7.5 x 7.5 cm. On cut surface there was a subcapsular hematoma surrounding the kidney. The left ureter seemed enlarged. The right kidney was 2.8 x 5.4 x 2 cm. The subcapsular surface was tan and pitted. Sections of liver spleen lung and kidney were frozen for future use if needed.

HISTIOCYTIC COELOMITIS ENTERITIS PNEUMONIA HEPATITIS NEPHRITIS SPLENITIS BACTERIAL COELOMITIS. This 10-year-old female chicken was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy moderate pulmonary edema was present. Nodular changes were noted in the aortic and left AV valves. The liver was pale and friable. The spleen was markedly enlarged and friable. Frank blood was present in the coelomic cavity.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL GRANULOMATOSIS. This approximately 17-year-old female monitor had been monitored the past month or so for quality of life. The animal had become monitored the past month or so for quality of life. The animal had become very thin was slow to eat although appeared interested and would fall asleep while eating. Supportive care was administered but blood work revealed leukocytosis and suspected renal problems. Blood work improved with fluid therapy but the animal’s overall condition did not improve despite attempts to feed daily. The monitor was found in a seizuring condition and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dry skin some scarring over the rostrum and dorsal cranium slightly more than expected pericardial fluid brown to maroon discoloration of the liver and spleen pale kidneys cyst-like cream-colored protrusions 3-4 mm. in diameter on the surface of both testicles and reddened lungs.
INANITION SPLENITIS PANCREATITIS. This 12-year-old male viper was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy the pancreas was enlarged and firm.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE THYROID CARCINOMA UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA OVIDUCT ADENOMAS HEPATIC ABSCESS DIABETES MELLITUS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 30-year-old female lemur had a two day history of depression and was moving slowly but still eating and interacting with two other lemurs. It was found dead. It had a long history of diabetes that was controlled with oral medication. Necropsy revealed a yellow hue to both ocular lenses a small amount of free fluid in the abdominal cavity absence of intra-abdominal fat yellow and necrotic omentum multiple adhesions of the omentum liver and intestines in the cranial right abdominal quadrant a few small green firm irregular stones in the caudal abdomen a few flat dark 1 mm. foci were in the spleen indistinct pancreas caseous necrosis of the right hepatic lobe with associated accumulation of yellow liquid in the core of the lesion several 1 cm. white nodules with caseous material on the capsular surface of the liver worn dentition multiple cysts in both ovaries a pink/white structure in the lumen of the uterus and a 2 cm. cyst in the cranial pole of the left kidney.

SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMAS SEX CORD STROMAL TUMOR BILIARY CYSTADENOMA EXOCRINE PANCREATIC HYPERPLASIA MILD CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE HELICOBACTER-ASSOCIATED GASTRITIS UROCYSTITIS NUCLEAR SCLEROSIS EOSINOPHILIC ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 17.5-year-old female cheetah was euthanized. At necropsy there was lenticular sclerosis crusting of the ear tips thickened cardiac wall multifocal hemorrhage of the lungs palatine erosions reddening of the esophagus an abnormal lobule at the cranial aspect of the stomach reactive mesenteric lymph nodes lobular appearance to the spleen and a thickened bladder wall.

TRAUMA. This 7-year-old female stork was found dead. Several puncture wounds were noted in the carcass. A second stork was also found in moribund condition and recumbent with wounds. Necropsy of the dead stork revealed good nutritional status and several puncture wounds on the dorsum and lateral right thigh. The lungs were bilaterally hemorrhagic. A focus of subcutaneous hemorrhage was noted over the caudal cranium. Severe hemorrhage and contusion was noted in the caudal cerebrum and cerebellum.
NA

TENOSYNOVITIS AND OSTEOARTHRITIS ENCEPHALITIS EUTHANASIA. This 7.5-year-old female banded rail had a few day history of intermittent ataxia swollen feet and elevated uric acid levels. Supportive care was administered and the foot swelling improved but the ataxia persisted. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition adequate adipose stores some mild hemorrhages in the tibiotarsal muscles of both legs and in the thigh muscles. Some swelling of tissues was noted at the left base of the foot and in the distal flexor tendon proximal to the hallux. Some congestion or hemorrhage was in the lungs. The ovary was inactive. Some possible swelling was in the cranial lobes of the kidneys.

PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE HYPERTENSION EUTHANSIA. This 26-year-old female polar bear had a two-week history of inappetence and lethargy with decreased awareness and had been examined twice in a 14-day interval while anesthetized. Blood work and other diagnostic aids were noncontributory. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not improve and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed hair loss at bony prominences sebaceous gland cyst over the neck a zone of circumferential reddened mucosa in the duodenum blunt hepatic margins no clear corticomedullary demarcation in the adrenal glands and markedly enlarged spleen with rounded edges.

FATTY LIVER UTERINE ADENOCARCINOMA HYDRONEPHROSIS. This 5-year/10-month-old female shrew was found dead. At necropsy there was pallor to the musculature. There was some sand adhered to the skin and hair around the mouth. The liver was pale pink and mottled dark red. The liver seemed large. The lungs seemed slightly consolidated and barely floated in 10% formalin. The left ventricle appeared thick and the muscle was pale. There was ingesta in the stomach. The kidneys were very irregular and pale. The right kidney was small. There was a large dark red swelling in the right uterine horn.

EUTHANASIA INANITION. This 13-year/3-month-old female stork was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic weight loss lethargy and being unable to stand. At necropsy both hocks were eroded and ulcerated through to the joints. The stork was very emaciated. There were no fat stores evident within the coelomic cavity.

NECROSUPPURATIVE RHINITIS EMACIATION. This 15-year-old male straw-colored fruit bat was noted to have signs of facial trauma four years earlier that included shortening of the maxilla with flattening of the planum nasale partial degloving of the rostral mandible and loss of all canine teeth. The bat had been noted by keepers to be lethargic and was scheduled for an examination but was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed occluded nares due to scar tissue and possible old hemorrhage in both nasal cavities. The distal phalanges of the wings had multiple malunion fractures. No other abnormalities were noted.

NEMATODE LARVAL MIGRATION PROBABLE BAYLISASCARIS SP. TRAUMA ENTRAPMENT. This 8-month-old female rabbit had been trapped by biologists and transported to the zoo for entry into a captive breeding program. Upon arrival it was noted that the rabbit had facial wounds had dyspnea and was in lateral recumbency. Nondisplaced skull fractures were palpable and air was escaping in the subcutaneous tissues over the nasal passages. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified fur loss and ecchymoses over the dorsal nasal region adequate adipose stores ingesta in the alimentary tract pink frothy fluid in the trachea multiple areas of red coloration in the lungs bruising over the right dorsal head region and left ventral mandible fractured dorsal rim at the right orbit and fracture of the nasal bones.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA CHRONIC ENTERITIS ISLET CELL HYPERPLASIA EUTHANASIA. This 2-year-old male rat has a history of chronic dyspnea and had been treated for chronic pneumonia on several occasions with relapse each time. It was admitted with respiratory distress and improved only when at rest in the oxygen chamber. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed chronic lesions with thickening and scarring of the lungs and possibly hypertrophied adrenal glands.

HODGKINS LYMPHOMA UROTHELIAL PAPILLOMA VENTRICULAR MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 8-year-old female rock hyrax was found dead. Gross necropsy revealed a thorax full of a white mass or large abscess with oily yellow fluid and thick white purulent material. The mass encompassed the left lung and pericardium with severe adhesions and thickening of the pericardium. The heart was discolored white. The right lung was unremarkable. Adrenal glands were enlarged. Firm nodules were present in the center of the intestinal pluck with a cyst in the middle filled with whitish fluid. A 1 cm. spherical white nodule was present in the liver. The animal was pregnant. A 1 cm. cauliflower-shaped mass was present in the bladder at the trigone.

YOLK COELOMITIS MINERALIZATION. This 1.5-year-old female chicken was found dead at evening rounds. The bird had been caught up for a physical examination earlier in the day although no procedures had been done. At the time of the physical exam the keeper noted that the bird did not like people and would become stressed with openmouthed breathing. The bird was leaner than the others in the group. Necropsy revealed lean body condition but adequate internal fat stores food in the gastrointestinal tract sand and fibrous material in the gizzard multiple mature follicles in the ovaries and throughout the uterus a normally sized and shaped egg in the uterus deep red/purple lungs and no other remarkable findings.

INTRASPECIES TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) HEMANGIOSARCOMA INSULAR AMYLOIDOSIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS MYOCARDIAL STEATOSIS PULMONARY EDEMA. This 19-year-old female baboon was found dead without premonitory signs. An increase in aggression and fighting in the group has been noted. At necropsy bite wounds to the upper arms were identified. The abdominal cavity contained approximately 2 liters of serosanguineous fluid.

TRAUMATIC RUMINORETICULITIS WITH FOREIGN BODY MIGRATION PULMONARY ABSCESSES ACUTE ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 18-year-old female pronghorn antelope had a seven day history of mild colic. The antelope was anesthetized and blood work revealed elevated bilirubin and mild azotemia. Radiographs revealed increased pulmonary opacities. Supportive care was administered and recovery from anesthesia was uneventful. The antelope was found dead in its stall the following morning. This is one of four hand reared young born in 2007. All four animals were inbred. This is the only animal that has lived beyond 1.5 years of age. Two died during routine castration and one died following mild gastrointestinal colic. Necropsy of the antelope of this report revealed mildly thin body condition with superficial abrasions on the neck and fibrinous adhesions throughout the thoracic cavity. Lungs were completely consolidated and contained purulent debris within the airways on cut surface. A large abscessed area 3 cm. in diameter was in the caudal right lung lobe directly adjacent to adhesions formed between the lung lobe diaphragm and an old puncture wound in the reticulum. Lungs were adhered to the pericardium and to the thoracic wall. A small amount of serous pericardial effusion was noted and the pericardium was adhered to the lung. A moderate amount of yellow tinged abdominal fluid with adhesions was in the abdomen. The reticulum had what appeared to be a partially healed puncture wound associated with a fibrous adhesion between the reticulum diaphragm and left caudal lung lobe. The gallbladder is filled with bile and the wall is thick. The liver has a slightly mottled appearance. Areas of hemorrhage and discoloration were on serosal surfaces of the intestine and adhesions were present throughout the gut. Kidneys appeared congested.
NA

PROLIFERATIVE GINGIVITIS AND SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA HERPESVIRUS DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male tree monitor has a 5.5 month history of squamous cell carcinoma associated with black tree monitor herpesvirus (G13-3691) and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. No additional information is available (necropsy report to follow).

EUTHANASIA BODY WALL SARCOMA PRESUMPTIVE FIBROSARCOMA METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 15-year-old female corn snake had a biopsy in March 2016 that was consistent with cellulitis. The animal also had a cloacal culture that was positive for Salmonella. In August 2016 the animal was rebiopsied and revealed probable sarcoma. The animal also had an enlarged hepatic silhouette on radiographs. The animal was euthanized.
NA

INANITION ENTERITIS. This male greater than 5-year-old mynah was found dead in outdoor flight cage stream bed. It had no previous clinical history. At necropsy there was no evidence of trauma. The testes appeared large.

CHRONIC SPINAL FRACTURE DEGENERATIVE MYELOPATHY COELOMIC MYCOBACTERIOSIS PANCREATIC INTERSTITIAL MINERALIZATION. This captive bred 11-year-old female corn snake had a history of spinal fracture in 2016 likely related to trauma. The snake had mild paresis and occasional constipation. Exploratory surgery was performed three weeks ago including an enterotomy to remove a fecal plug that was adhered to the mucosal surface. Biopsy results of abnormal tissue at surgery indicated mycobacteria (#G16-2574). The snake was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Gross necropsy revealed a firm nodule in the spine at the fracture site distention of the distal coelom at previous surgical site small black and white foci on the hepatic surface an abnormal distal 8 cm. of bowel that had dilation and green staining with dark green material in the lumen mottled and edematous adipose pinpoint foci on the surface of the left proximal oviduct a congested lung with small pinpoint pale foci on the serosa and a cystic appearance to the spine and spinal cord radiographically at the site of the fracture.

HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA BACTERIAL TRACHEITIS VENTRICULAR CANDIDIASIS. This 14.5-year-old female mynah had been hospitalized in early November for being found on the ground unable to fly well with distended abdomen and muscle wasting. The bird was shedding coccidia in its feces and atoxoplasmosis was considered possible. Supportive care was administered radiographs revealed hepatomegaly and the bird appeared to improve with treatment. The bird subsequently deteriorated again was shedding yeast and pseudohyphae in the feces was treated for candidiasis and improved briefly but then deteriorated again. An exploratory surgery was performed and hepatomegaly was apparent but no other abnormalities were seen. A biopsy of the liver revealed hepatitis suggestive of atoxoplasmosis and the bird was treated again but continued to worsen and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed scruffy plumage and areas of alopecia and scarring over the head fecal soiling around the vent yellow skull focal corneal lesion in the right eye with associated white material in the anterior chamber or adhered to the iris associated with an old eyelid fissure a thick yellow plaque running the length of the cervical portion of the trachea moderately congested and edematous lungs multilobular tan soft masses throughout the left pulmonary lobe and cranial two-thirds of the right pulmonary lobe healed previous biopsy site and some blotchy discoloration and swelling. The proventriculus and gizzard are enveloped by hepatic masses that are invading the serosal wall of the gizzard. The intestines are gnarled the small intestine is erythematous the pancreas is obscured or effaced by tan nodules which are confluent with the hepatic nodules and the ovary is difficult to separate from the hepatic masses. The spleen is pale small and stuck between the hepatic masses. A moderate amount of internal fat is noted.

YOLK COELOMITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS INANITION. This 9-year-old female anole suffered trauma to the tail and had been under treatment. The animal was found dead. At necropsy the distal portion of the tail was necrotic and underlying bone was exposed. A large opening was present at the cloaca with exposure of soft tissue underneath. A large quantity of inspissated yolk was present in the coelomic cavity.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE PITUITARY HYPERPLASIA SUSPECT PARATHYROID ADENOMA ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS CARDIOPULMONARY SHOCK. This 35-year-old gorilla was acquired by the zoo in 1983 as a juvenile along with a family group. As a young animal the gorilla had a few medical problems with the exception of fight-related injuries and a few bouts of diarrhea. The father was diagnosed with hypertension and succumbed at 30 years of age to cardiac fibrosis and heart failure. The animal of this report developed hypertension and mild left ventricular thickening in 1998 and had been controlled since then with blood pressure medications. Five days prior to death this animal refused food and laid down refusing its medications. A problem was suspected based on signs in a conspecific and some soft stool development overnight. The gorilla continued to eat only select items over the next few days and inconsistently consumed cardiac medications. Lethargy continued although fecal consistency returned to near normal. No enteric pathogens were cultured or identified in fecal parasite exams. Due to persistent lethargy the animal was anesthetized for examination and cardiac evaluation and cardiac parameters were within normal limits. Blood work identified marked azotemia. Examination revealed periodontal disease and an infected loose premolar. Supportive care was administered but the gorilla had problems with anesthetic recovery developing apnea that required reintubation. The gorilla appeared to stabilize and over the next eight hours respirations were stable although no signs of arousal occurred. The animal subsequently arrested and resuscitation was unsuccessful. Necropsy revealed obesity a lipoma in the subcutaneous tissues over the left costal arch moderate periodontal disease with gingival recession and hyperplasia and some pockets around the premolars and molars. Bloody mucus was present around the premolar extraction site. Two areas of granulation tissue were present between the molars on the right mandibular arcade and purulent exudate from what appeared to be a fistulous tract was deep between the right upper first and second molars. Pharyngeal soft tissues appeared hyperplastic and mild congestion was in the larynx. Some cystic enlargement of the thyroid follicles was noted and the isthmus was large. The left axillary lymph nodes were enlarged and edematous. The scrotum was edematous with multifocal adhesions of the testicles to the vaginal tunics. A few small whitish nodules were in the peritesticular tissues on the right side. Mild softening and wear of the articular cartilage around the acetabular rim of the left hip joint was noted. Both stifle joints had thinning and irregular wear with softening and fibrillation of the left lateral femoral condyle and tibial plateau and the right medial femoral condyle. Joint mice were in the left stifle joint space. In the thoracic cavity there were 100 ml. of slightly yellow serous fluid. Marked multifocal hemorrhage mucous exudate and erosions or ulcerations extended from just distal to the larynx well past the hilus and both major bronchi and the bronchial lymph nodes are congested. Mild to moderate thickening of the left ventricle is noted and some patchy pallor is present in the myocardium compared to the right ventricle. The pulmonary valve leaflets had mild granular texture around the attachment sites and a few small nodules were noted in the left atrioventricular valves. Some mild subvalvular endocardial thickening was noted beneath the aortic valves and a small fibrotic shelf of tissue extended from the central septal valve onto the septal ventricular wall. The gallbladder was distended with normal bile. The spleen was congested. The appendix was mildly congested and the adrenals were congested. Patchy hemorrhage was found the  Page 2 G14-5189 Western Lowland Gorilla #M00109/14-325 Zoo Miami  right kidney and the renal medullary regions were congested at the corticomedullary junction especially the left kidney. A few scattered small cystic areas were in the cortex and medulla and some tan creamy thick liquid material was expressed from the medulla and pelvic recesses of the right kidney.

CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS POSTSURGICAL COELOMITIS. This 13-year-old male Gila monster has a history of cryptosporidiosis and coelomitis diagnosed with biopsy. The lizard recovered well from the surgical procedure but did poorly despite supportive care thereafter and was found dead. Necropsy revealed serosanguineous fluid in the coelomic cavity and fibrin adhesions present throughout the coelomic cavity especially at one of the intestinal biopsy sites.

MUSCLE TRAUMA AND RHABDOMYOLYSIS VASCULAR DEGENERATION AND URINARY BLADDER. This 14-year-old female impala was noted to be knuckled over on her left rear fetlock four days prior to euthanasia. She was suspected to have a rupture of the digital extensor tendon and was treated with anti-inflammatory drugs and placed in a splint which was effective. Blood work revealed elevated AST CPK and leukocytosis. Necropsy revealed lean to normal body condition fair tooth condition enlarged retropharyngeal lymph nodes a focus of discoloration and consolidation at the dorsal aspect of the left middle lung lobe a 3 cm. mineralized trichobezoar in the reticulum and some mineralized braided twine in the reticulum pallor of both femoral muscle bundles and laxity of the left hind digital extensor associated with complete disruption of the muscle belly of the left cranial tibial muscle.

SYNCYTIAL CELL PNEUMONIA AND VASCULITIS PROBABLY VIRAL GRANULOMATOUS VASCULITIS CARDITIS. This 13-year-old female cottontop tamarin has a history of loose or bloody stools of several months duration sometimes associated with weight loss. The monkey’s condition eventually deteriorated and she was found dead. Necropsy revealed dark red clotted blood on organs just under the skin of the abdominal area no normal lung tissue excess fluid in the pericardial sac rounded heart with possible scarring of the heart muscle complete absence of fat and multiple nodules clumping the bladder and reproductive organs together.

MAMMARY GLAND ADENOCARCINOMA ENDOMETRIAL STROMAL CELL SARCOMA WOBBLY HEDGEHOG SYNDROME ESOPHAGITIS EUTHANASIA. This 5-year-old female hedgehog was diagnosed with a possible sarcoma by biopsy in 2009 was found moribund and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 0.5 cm. firm round subcutaneous mass in the ventral midline of the thoracic region. Another smaller firm mass was found subcutaneously in the left axillary region. Multiple pale cream circular nodules were on the hepatic surface and the liver was pale red. The left adrenal gland was slightly larger than the right. The uterine wall was thickened and slightly firm on palpation with multiple endometrial cysts. A mediastinal lymph node was enlarged to 1 cm. in greatest dimension.

OBESITY HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This greater than 10-year-old screech owl became inappetent approximately 18 days ago and started to have yellow urates in the stool. The animal was found dead following 24 hours of neurologic signs. Necropsy revealed a tan markedly enlarged liver that floated in formalin. A large amount of pericardial fat was noted. The left eye had no discernible iris (old injury).

UROLITHIASIS NEPHROSCLEROSIS METASTATIC MINERALIZATION EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female prairie dog is one of several that were examined. This animal was noted to be thin and the upper incisors were missing. The lower incisors were severely overgrown. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition rough haircoat with areas of alopecia irregular renal surfaces a large smooth urolith in the urinary bladder and reddened bladder mucosa.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS ENDOCRINE DERMATOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 11.5-year-old female meerkat was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure two days earlier responded poorly to treatment and became debilitated. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. This animal also had a history of chronic degenerative joint disease in the right carpus. Necropsy revealed some “scolding” on the ventral tail adjacent to the rectum fair body condition absence of most teeth edematous lungs a moderate amount of free fluid in the thoracic cavity enlarged heart with dilated left ventricle and thin left ventricular walls dilation of the right ventricle and a small amount of pericardial fluid. The left kidney had a cavitated lesion and pallor in the medulla below the cavitated region. Ovaries were inactive. A small amount of dark ingesta was in the small intestine.

BACTERIAL PYOMETRITIS WITH SEPSIS/DIC OVARIAN/OVIDUCT ADENOMA FIBROLEIOMYOMA. This 11-year-old female pot-bellied pig died spontaneously and was refrigerated eight hours prior to necropsy. Clinical signs included feed refusal elevated white blood cell count cloudy gelatinous urine. The animal partially responded to antibiotic therapy but then deteriorated and was found dead. Necropsy revealed an 8 cm. mass near the left ovary and adhesions between the left ovary and large intestine.
