LYMPHOMA AMYLOIDOSIS GRANULOMATOUS LYMPHADENITIS EUTHANASIA. This 8-year-old female black-footed ferret had a history of weight loss lethargy and inappetence and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed poor body condition but adequate adipose stores in body cavities. Teeth were worn the stomach was empty a 2 cm. firm mass was in the wall of the proximal jejunum that was uniformly pink on cut surface and jejunum adjacent to the mass was firm on both sides. A few small cysts were in the liver. The distal end of the pancreas had two masses that were white to gray on cut surface and 1.5 cm. in greatest dimension. The smaller mass also had a small amount of blood on cut surface. The pancreas was contiguous with the masses but they did not appear to be part of the pancreatic parenchyma. The left kidney contained an infarct. Some foci of brown/gray discoloration were on the underside of the brainstem. A Deslorelin implant was present and female reproductive tract was identified.

ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS SUPPURATIVE SPINAL OSTEOARTHRITIS WITH MENINGITIS. This 27-year-old female baboon had a history of lying on the bottom of the enclosure one day and a three day history of inappetence and reluctance to take phenobarbital. This animal has a lifelong history of seizures which recently had become more frequent. The animal also has a history of mild arthritis. Necropsy revealed periodontal disease with missing incisors and premolars and alopecia was on the dorsum tail and head. An abscess was noted on the tail from a previous bite wound. Mild crepitus was in the wrists elbows and knees. Multiple fatty masses were in the subcutis. A small amount of clear yellow fluid was in the chest. The lungs were mottled firm and dark red. Fibrin strands were noted within the thoracic cavity. White thick material was found along the thoracic vertebra. Severe osteolysis of vertebral segments was noted. A small hole in the lytic portion of the vertebra discharged clear fluid. The right kidney was rounded and two-thirds the size of the left kidney.
NA

INTESTINAL COCCIDIOSIS ATELECTASIS SHOCK. This 2-month-old ferret is from a litter which has been treated for coccidiosis. This animal presented weak and dehydrated and later died. At necropsy feces were pasted on the inguinal region. Mediastinal lymph nodes were enlarged. GI tract was devoid of ingesta.

EUTHANASIA UTERINE LEIOMYOMA LUTEOMA CHRONIC ENTERITIS RETICULATES. This 22-year-old female antelope was immobilized on 10/28 for hoof work and a horn trim. Keepers reported that the antelope was lethargic on 10/31 and 11/1 with apparent visual impairment tremors and poor renal values on blood work. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed an irregular mass associated with the vasculature of the right ovary slight thickening of the left atrioventricular valve a longitudinal fracture through the crown of the right mandibular molar #3 and hyperkeratotic change in the perianal region.
juvenile. Weight: 4103 g.  Rectum empty.  Lymphadenitis; especially mesenteric.  Poor condition.  Hydrothorax; pericardium and peritoneum.  Toxoplasmosis?.

VISCERAL GOUT AND METASTATIC MINERALIZATION PULMONARY FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 17-year-old female skink had a three-week history of lethargy and inappetence. Examination identified renal failure and injury to the distal tongue incurred during the exam. Supportive care was administered but the animal did not respond to treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified hyperemia in the ventral scales white creamy plaques present along the ribs within the pectoral girdle and on the serosal surfaces of the pericardium intestine and coelom. Adipose stores were adequate. The tongue was missing the distal tip and thin dark tissue was present at the amputation site. Cloacal mucosa was pale or white. The liver had a mottled tan pattern and white crystalline flakes were noted in bile. The spleen was enlarged and pink. The pancreas was white and firm. A 2.8 cm. cystic structure was associated with the pole of the left kidney. A flat tan structure was located caudal to the kidney and also 2.8 cm. in greatest dimension. Gonads were firmly adhered to the caudal vena cava.

DUCK VIRAL ENTERITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS BACTEREMIA. This 8-year-old male duck was found dead. At necropsy the body was in good nutritional condition with marked vascular congestion throughout all organs. The esophagus intestine and colon contained foul smelling brown liquid. Petechial hemorrhages were noted in the liver.

TRAUMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male whistling duck was found lethargic and ataxic and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed numerous blood clots in the coelomic cavity and in the subcutis of the medial aspect of the femoral region of the left leg. Contusions were also in the musculature of the femoral region of the left leg.

POSSIBLE ENCEPHALOMYOCARDITIS VIRUS INFECTION. This 4-year-old male tamarin presented with lethargy and did not respond to supportive therapy. Necropsy revealed free blood in the abdominal cavity and no other lesions. Gut stomach and liver were frozen.

FACIAL SOFT TISSUE SARCOMA DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE DEGENERATIVE RENAL DISEASE FLAGELLATE COLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old male degu was diagnosed with a soft tissue sarcoma involving the facial soft tissues and also had degenerative joint disease for which it was receiving nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy identified good body condition a 2 cm. firm ulcerated mass on the left side of the face ventral to the eye that was uniformly tan/white on cut surface. Abnormal tan tissue was also identified in the cranial mediastinum. A small pinpoint white structure was within the gallbladder. The kidney was pale. The mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged. Both adrenal glands were prominent. Both kidneys were irregular on serosal surfaces and had few small cysts in the parenchyma. Degenerative joint disease was severe in the stifles and stifle range of motion was decreased.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) ADRENAL HEMORRHAGE. This 18-year-old peccary was euthanized due to severe chronic degenerative joint disease. At necropsy a small renal cyst was present in the left kidney. No other gross lesions were noted.
AIR SACCULITIS PULMONARY EDEMA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 13-year-old female parrot was found dead. At necropsy the left atrium was dilated. Great vessels were thickened.

CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 3-year-old rat had abnormal posture in the front legs dyspnea hyperpnea decreased pulmonary sounds inappetence and only partial response to supportive care. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed nodular atelectasis in the left lung hemorrhagic fluid in the right lung and partial atelectasis of the right lung.

EUTHANASIA TIBIOTARSAL FRACTURE BACTERIAL MYOSITIS PROVENTRICULITIS TYPHLOCOLITIS. This approximately 7-year-old male turkey was humanely euthanized. It had fractured its right tibiotarsus that was repaired using a type II external KE method but after two days the bird traumatized itself again refracturing the tibiotarsus and therefore was humanely euthanized. A metallic foreign body was also noted within the ventriculus and one was noted in the exterior portion of the ventriculus radiographically. At necropsy the turkey was in good nutritional body condition. The lungs were hemorrhagic. The air sacs were moderately cloudy. The gastrointestinal tract vasculature was congested. There was a 3.5 cm. linear metallic foreign body adjacent to and adhered to the right serosal surface of the ventriculus. The ventriculus contained a curved metallic foreign body. There was a comminuted fracture of the right tibiotarsus with eight fragments ranging in size from 2-30 mm. There was severe muscle trauma.

ENDOMETRIOSIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS EUTHANASIA. This 22-year-old female mandrill had a history of arthritis generalized pallor a large abdomen and radiographic evidence of fluid in the abdomen. Abdominocentesis revealed blood and exploratory surgery could not find the source. Adhesions were noted between the uterus colon and bladder. The liver appeared swollen. A few small firm free-floating masses were observed and a few similar masses were noted on the serosal surface of the colon. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a 1 cm. ulcer in the mucosa of the uterus several cystic structures on the serosal surface of the urinary bladder swollen liver with rounded edges slightly hemorrhagic adrenals and numerous small firm masses adhered to the serosal surface of the colon. Petechial hemorrhages were also noted on the serosal surface of the colon.

PYOGRANULOMATOUS ENTERITIS AND LYMPHADENITIS AMYLOIDOSIS. This 6-year-old black-footed ferret had a several day history of inappetence and green mucoid feces and was more lethargic than usual with some weight loss. Blood work revealed elevated renal values elevated total protein and globulin and elevated potassium level. The animal developed cardiac arrest while an intravenous catheter was being placed. A fecal culture was negative for enteric pathogens. Necropsy revealed presumptive hemorrhage in the intestine hepatopathy hemorrhage in the lung larger than expected lymph nodes and dark red/brown kidneys with several indentations in the cortex and capsule.

EUTHANASIA SELF-TRAUMA HEPATITIS. This approximately 4-year-old male lovebird was humanely euthanized. It had protracted unsuccessful treatment for self-mutilation of the left axillary area. At necropsy there was a full thickness circumferential skin wound of the left axilla and proximal humerus that was concentrated at the anterior aspect of the proximal humerus. There was a large area of ulcerated skin surrounding the wound. There was alopecia of the left axilla and the left breast and cervical area. The lungs were diffusely and moderately congested. The liver was moderately pale.
BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA PERIPORTAL HEPATITIS URETERITIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 14-year-old male eagle was found dead. At necropsy marked pulmonary edema was noted.

ANAPLASTIC SARCOMA (LEG) WITH VISCERAL METASTASIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 3-year-old male budgerigar has a history of massive swelling and lameness involving the right leg at the stifle. The condition has not responded to treatment. Amputation was performed but the bird did not recover from the procedure. Necropsy revealed a large intracoelomic mass.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENTERITIS. This 10-year-old chinchilla had a history of abnormal tooth growth with impaired ability to eat and weight loss. The tooth was trimmed; however the animal died nine days later while being force fed. At necropsy the lungs were edematous and the liver was mottled.

ANESTHETIC DEATH MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS ENDOCARDITIS PULMONARY HISTIOCYTOSIS PULMONARY THROMBOSIS GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS HEPATIC HEMORRHAGE. This 8-year-old male polar bear was anesthetized to examine for a source of oral cavity bleeding. Anesthetic recovery was prolonged and the animal began struggling and became unable to use its hind legs. The animal later died. At necropsy a large quantity of straw colored fluid was present in the abdominal cavity. A large quantity of hemorrhagic fluid was present in the thorax.

PROLIFERATIVE COLITIS COLONIC MUCOID ADENOCARCINOMA PROLAPSED COLON EUTHANASIA. This 23.5-year-old Gila monster has a history of chronic prolapse which recently was nonreducible and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a mass in the colon urates on serosal surfaces of the viscera and fibrous liver.

EUTHANASIA NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS BARBITURATE ARTIFACT. This greater than 8-year-old male blue spiny lizard had been eating well the past three months. It developed a three week episode of decreased appetite and lethargy became obtunded and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition dull skin with urates adhered to the vent dilated cecum filled with thick brown material full gallbladder dark liver with few tan spots on the edges and hyperpigmentation of the body wall and one kidney. This group of lizards has a history of lymphoma.

EUTHANASIA TRAUMA METACARPAL FRACTURE. This 2-year/10-month-old male gerenuk was found with its leg trapped in a fence and the leg was fractured so it was euthanized. At necropsy the right metacarpal was fractured about 8 cm. above the fetlock joint. The fracture was compound with extensive bone exposure. The distal portion of the leg remained attached by a small strip of skin and the flexor tendons. There was congestion in the left lung that was down during the anesthesia prior to euthanasia. There was some white foam in the trachea. There were small pale white slightly raised plaques on the surface of both caudal lobes. The plaques were thin and did not extend into the parenchyma. There was a small amount of food around the right testis. Only the left adrenal gland was located. The adrenal had an unusual gray/tan discoloration to the medulla.

SEMINOMA DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY EUTHANASIA. This 16-year-old male duck has a history of lameness ataxia and elevated uric acid levels. The bird was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed bilateral multilobular cystic structures in the testes. The heart was enlarged and the epicardium had an irregular surface.

ACUTE RENAL TUBULAR NECROSIS COLITIS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male ibex had a chronic history of abnormal hoof wear and lameness. The animal developed lethargy decreased fecal production and pitting edema of the limbs and brisket. Serum biochemistry suggested renal failure (creatinine 4.5) and protein loss (albumin 0.9). The animal was euthanized. At gross necropsy there was marked dependent edema and a large quantity of sanguineous fluid in the abdominal cavity. Kidneys had multifocal depressed pale foci. A 5 mm. cyst was present in the medulla of the left kidney.

SALPINGITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK. This 21-year-old female rhea was found weak and died during the exam. A large soft mass was present in the coelomic cavity. Necropsy revealed masses in the oviduct and a large granuloma. Mummified eggs were present in the oviduct.

BACTERIAL ABSCESSES AND OSTOEMYELITIS DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE POSSIBLE CARDIAC DISEASE EUTHANASIA. This 13-year-old male kangaroo presented several times for substantial medical problems including tendosynovitis periodontal disease and sialoadenitis. This spring he presented with a 3 cm. diameter swelling of the left forearm tentatively diagnosed as neoplasia by cytology. The lesion was excised and the animal was returned to its group. It did not do well thereafter and workup revealed probable renal disease potential cardiac enlargements and two areas of vertebral change in the thoracic and lumbar regions that were initially interpreted as spondylosis but also had areas of lysis. The animal eventually became recumbent with paretic hind limbs. Euthanasia was performed for suspected spinal cord compromise in the thoracic region. Necropsy revealed pulmonary edema enlarged heart 750 ml. of sanguineous fluid with fibrinous tags in the abdominal cavity hepatic cyst eroded pyloric mucosa hemorrhagic intestine edematous lymph nodes pale and fibrotic kidneys with small renoliths in the pelvis seromas in the area of the previous surgical procedure on the forearm and mild eburnation of the scapulohumeral joint. The thoracic vertebral mass was dissected from the surrounding costae. The right costae of this caudal thoracic vertebra was luxated with a small amount of yellow debris and hemorrhage. Once removed a 5 mm. thick bone slab fell loose from the caudal surface of the vertebra and was freely movable in a vertical fashion. The lumbar vertebral mass was more solid and difficult to dislodge.

FRACTURED TIBIA FAILED SURGICAL REDUCTION EUTHANASIA. This 5-month-old male gazelle incurred a tibial fracture that was repaired with a plate two weeks earlier. The gazelle had been doing well was calm and eating in the confined bedded hallway space. Eventually increased laxity and movement was noted at the fracture site and radiographs identified a failed fracture repair. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed good body condition some healed incisions on the medial and lateral aspect of the distal right tibia. The distal right tibia hock and metatarsal areas are enlarged compared to the left. The lung had some areas of atelectasis. Some dark red streaking and thinning of the mucosa was noted in the abomasum. The ruminal papillae were relatively short. Sublumbar lymph nodes were moderately enlarged. Pink and mottled red firm tissue proliferation was present over the bone plate on the medial aspect of the tibia. The distal fragment of the tibia was severely comminuted and bone screws were loose.

PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE ENTERITIS HEPATIC NECROSIS. This approximately 1-year-old female lory was found dead in incubator. It was found on the ground with two other lorikeets pecking at its head. It was brought to the hospital. It had no external wounds. It was placed in the incubator for observation and seemed to be doing well. It was offered food and nectar which it ate. In the afternoon the lorikeet fluffed and was sitting quietly. It was administered 0.5 cc. subcutaneous fluids. At necropsy there was slight icteric appearance to the liver. The crop was distended but there was no food.

1. Hock: Chronic active; focal; ulcerative dermatitis with underlying bony lysis; locally extensive reactive bone formation; and possibly focal lymphoplasmacytic synovitis (2/2) 2. Right popliteal lymph node: Reactive lymph node (1/2) 3. Lung: Mild; multifocal; granulomatous pneumonia (1/2); marked diffuse congestion (2/2); moderate BALT hyperplasia (2/2) 4. Heart: Mild; multifocal; myocardial degeneration and fibrosis (2/2) 5. Kidney: Mild to moderate; multifocal; membranous glomerulopathy with mild tubular proteinosis (2/2) Locally-extensive; chronic lymphoplasmacytic synovitis with reactive new bone formation Moderate lymphoplasmacytic dermatitis with focal epidermal ulceration Membranous glomerulopathy with intratubular protein cast Myocardial degeneration and fibrosis Granulomatous pneumonia with diffuse pulmonary congestion and BALT hyperplasia Comments The major histologic findings suggest a chronic inflammatory process within the digit. There was no evidence of an underlying cause; histologically. The reactive new bone formation and fibrosis associated with the epidermal ulceration and chronic dermatitis was most suggestive of an outside-in inflammatory response. The causes may include trauma from irregular cage surfaces or roughly textured bedding materials; and obesity (increased pressure on the feet). This leads to a wound with chronic inflammation; abscesses; or secondary infection to the joint and new bone formation. The lesions observed in the kidney and heart were most likely from age-related alteration. Inhalation of foreign body; such as bedding particles may contribute to granulomatous pneumonia; and diffuse congestion and edema may result from euthanasia method using CO2 inhalation. Tuddow Thaiwong; DVM; PhD

EUTHANASIA MANDIBULAR SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA OVARIAN GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS VACUOLAR MYELINOPATHY. This 2-year-old female hedgehog had a mass on the thorax and mandible. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the left mandible contained a 3x3x1 cm. firm tan mass which effaced the underlying bone. The subcutis contained a 3x3x2 cm. encapsulated firm mass.

PYOMETRA SEPSIS PULMONARY ADENOMA. This 1-year-old female Virginia opossum was found dead and had no prior signs of illness. Some mild bruising was noted at the base of the right ear. Necropsy revealed no abnormalities and the animal appeared to be in good nutritional status.

EUTHANASIA TETANUS BACTERIAL THORACIC ABSCESS GLOMERULONEPHROPATHY. This 14-year/2-month-old male giraffe was humanely euthanized. It had sustained a gore wound in the right side behind the elbow from an adult male greater kudu while in mixed exhibit approximately three weeks prior to death. The wound appeared to heal normally and the giraffe exhibited no clinical signs until approximately two weeks later when he became lethargic and began to develop a sawhorse stance at rest. The giraffe had difficulty eating and opening its mouth. Tetanus was diagnosed and intensive treatment with antibiotics tetanus antitoxin and supportive fluids were given over the course of the last 10 days. He did not respond to treatment. While in the chute being treated he collapsed went down and began regurgitating profusely. At necropsy the entrance of the gore wound was approximately 10 cm. caudal to the point of the right elbow. There was a healing granulation tract extending dorsally into subcutaneous tissue which then traveled throughout the ribcage and into the chest cavity 9 inches dorsal to the entrance wound (approximately shoulder level). At this level in the pleural cavity there was a large pocket (6 in. diameter) of caseous necrotic material. There were adhesions of the pericardium and cranial medial right lung lobe to the abscessed area. The affected lung lobes were also dark gray and firm. There was white foam in the trachea admixed with green feed material. There were minimal fat stores in the abdomen. All major joints of the limbs were examined and were within normal limits. The heart weighed 0.47% of the carcass weight.

CUTANEOUS VASCULITIS PROBABLE PROTOZOAN ETIOLOGY ANESTHETIC COMPLICATION. This 4-year-old female quail developed digital necrosis and died while anesthetized for toe amputation. Necropsy revealed a small focus of alopecia on the dorsum of the head a thickened region just left of the keel approximately 0.5 cm. in greatest dimension a small amount of red fluid in the trachea food in the crop slightly mottled liver and pancreas some hemorrhage in the pectoral muscle to the right of the keel and no other abnormalities.

ASPIRATION RUMENITIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 7-month-old male kudu had been immobilized for routine vasectomy regurgitated and aspirated severely during the procedure and was unable to breathe. The animal died despite emergency intubation and CPR. Necropsy revealed good body condition a large amount of liquid ingesta in the trachea major airways and deeper small airways in both lungs occluded by green fibrous material patchy pink and red lungs a few red patches in the abomasum and no other gross abnormalities.

EUTHANASIA HEMANGIOSARCOMA (ORAL CAVITY) AORTIC MINERALIZATION. This 12-year-old female mynah had a mass in the oral cavity suspected to represent a vascular sarcoma. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy dark exudate was present at the commissure of the mouth. Radiographically lysis of the right mandible was present. The right ventricle was enlarged and the myocardium was irregularly thickened.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY EDEMA THYMOMA. This 5-year-old domestic ferret was under treatment for cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure; however its condition declined and it was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a moderate quantity of fluid was present in the thorax. White foci were present in the liver. A large tan mass was present in the anterior thoracic cavity. The heart was enlarged with dilation of the left ventricle.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC DISEASE PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA EUTHANASIA. This 4-year-old female opossum had a history of mild erythema on the left side attributed to postmortem recumbency. An anal gland discharge was noted around the perianal region. The animal had bilateral cataracts and anisocoria with the right larger than the left. Mild bilateral exophthalmia was noted. Nodules were on the tricuspid and mitral valves the right ventricular wall was thin and loose and 0.7 ml. of serosanguineous pericardial fluid was collected. Some liquid was in the trachea and multiple caseous nodes were in two lobes. Moderate emphysema was noted and the parenchyma was congested. A moderate quantity of dental tartar and some broken teeth were noted. Five ulcers were next to the gastroduodenal papillae. Mesenteric lymph nodes were enlarged and the intestines were congested. Mild fibrin deposition was between the left ventral and dorsal lobes of the liver related to a caseous node. Four yellow soft nodes were associated with the pancreas. Heterogeneous mass 0.7 cm. was in the left uterine wall cysts were in the right uterine lumen 35 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was in the abdomen and 80 ml. of serosanguineous liquid was in the thorax.

EUTHANSIA BRONCHOPNEUMONIA TRACHEITIS. This greater than 2-year-old female rat was humanely euthanized. It had a recent episode of dyspnea that did not respond to antibiotic treatment. It also had a history of weight loss. Bacterial culture of the lung was performed.

TRAUMA (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) SHOCK CHRONIC NEPHRITIS. This 15-year-old female duck had a long history of arthritis. The animal was found dead. At necropsy hemorrhage was noted in the breast muscle and ventrum.

EUTHANASIA MYCOBACTERIOSIS GLOMERULAR LIPIDOSIS. This greater than 5-year -old male toad was humanely euthanized. The entire group of five animals was culled to screen for mycobacteriosis. Historically they were in contact with an animal that was suspect for tuberculosis based on histopathology but no cultures were done to confirm this. At necropsy the liver had 5-10 pinpoint foci that were slightly paler than the rest of the hepatic tissue and were raised. The fat stores were yellow and the tissue bled more than the other four specimens. Liver was submitted for mycobacterial culture.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS PULMONARY SHOCK HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 13-year-old Egyptian fruit bat was found on the bottom of the exhibit floor with no prior evidence of illness. Necropsy revealed poor body condition and excellent postmortem condition. The liver appeared to be enlarged but no other changes were noted.

VEGETATIVE ENDOCARDITIS CASEOUS ABSCESSES DIGITAL OSTEOMYELITIS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old male tree kangaroo had a one-month history of nonweight bearing lameness of the left hind lateral foot. A previous exam revealed paronychia on the left hind toe. Supportive care was administered but examination four weeks later revealed intermittent lameness and swelling of the left mandible. Radiographs of the toe revealed severe bone loss of P3 and some bone remodeling of P3-P2 joint. The toe was surgically amputated and follow-up treatment was ineffective. Further decline was noted and ultrasound identified abdominal and thoracic effusions possible hypertrophied cardiomyopathy and a 4 cm. mass in the left ventricle. Blood work revealed moderate to severe renal failure received therapeutic abdominal and thoracocentesis and fluid therapy while anesthetized recovered initially but then continued to decline and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed thin body condition a full thickness bite wound on the lateral surface of the tongue well healed lateral hind toe amputation site moderate subcutaneous edema throughout the body and head 300 ml. of transudative fluid with fibrinous strands throughout the abdominal cavity dark purple/mottled liver dilated gallbladder with pale white edges white/fibrinous-like material within the hepatic parenchyma thickened reddened mucosal surface of the intestine and colon bilaterally enlarged prostate multiple areas of reddening on cut surface of the prostate 800 ml. of transudate in the thoracic cavity containing fibrinous material mottled purple/pink lungs with white edges consolidation of the caudal ventral pulmonary lobes pale cardiac muscle with abnormal striations hard gritty calcified material on cut surface of the left auricle corresponding to a central focus of pallor on the external surface and two large masses adhered to the lateral wall of the left ventricle which could be freed with manipulation from the surface of the ventricle. A second mass was on the lateral wall of the apex. The right ventricular wall was subjectively thin.

Whole body: Emaciation Kidneys: Mild to moderate; chronic interstitial nephritis Uterus: Endometrial cyst (incidental finding) Liver: Mild; multifocal; white foci. Comments: The underlying cause of the reported clinical signs was not evident from gross examination. The gross lesions in the kidney are most suggestive of chronic interstitial nephritis which may represent an aging change. Multiple organs contained foci of suspected calcification which may be an incidental lesion or may represent an underlying chronic disease process. The white foci within the liver were very small and nonspecific. Histopathology to further characterize these gross lesions is in progress; along with fecal analysis. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAMAnatomic pathology resident Cerebrum: Focal glial nodule with neutrophilic inflammation Lungs: 1. Multifocal subpleural and parenchymal foam cell foci 2. Mild; multifocal anthracosis Liver 1. Multifocal hepatic lipidosis 2. Multifocal; centrilobular to random; acute hepatocellular degeneration and necrosis Kidney (unilateral): Severe; locally extensive; suppurative nephritis with intralesional bacteria Kidney (unilateral): Moderate; multifocal; chronic interstitial nephritis with fibrosis and multifocal glomerulosclerosis Intestine: Mild coccidiasis Uterus: Focal endometrial hemorrhagic cyst Kidney: Unilateral severe bacterial nephritis Kidney: Moderate chronic interstitial nephritis Liver: 1. Multifocal hepatic lipidosis; 2. Multifocal; moderate hepatocellular degeneration Lung: 1. Multifocal; subpleural foam cell foci; 2. Multifocal anthracosis Intestine: Mild coccidiasis Comments: This animal has several significant lesions that are difficult to relate to one another and may represent concurrent but unconnected processes. Most significantly; there is a severe bacterial nephritis in one kidney. It could not be determined whether this arose by an ascending (from the urinary tract) or hematogenous (from the blood) route. No other tissue appears affected and there is no evidence of infection in the uterus. Although this renal infection appears severe enough to have some clinical impact; there still appears to be a fair amount of unaffected renal tissue remaining. Additionally; it is difficult to correlate this lesion with the clinical history of abdominal effusion. The opposite kidney has chronic changes supportive of chronic interstitial nephritis. The liver lesion is unusual. Hepatic lipidosis is not uncommon in post-parturition ruminants; however the distribution is often more diffuse. The cause for the liver degeneration is unknown. The foam cell foci in the lung are likely incidental findings possibly related to previous parasite migration. Coccidia are identified histologically and by fecal evaluation. Coccidiasis in adult alpacas is rarely clinically significant unless present in high numbers. Special stains are in process on the liver and kidney sections to determine if bacteria are present in small numbers in the liver and to attempt identification of the bacteria in the kidney. These results will be released as an addendum report. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAM Anatomic pathology reside See previous reports Comments: Although kidney was not available for culture; the bacteria observed in kidney tissue sections were gram negative rods and could be coliforms; which were isolated in high numbers from other tissues (liver; abdominal fluid; lungs). Although cultures must be interpreted with caution due to the state of the animal at necropsy; it is possible that bacterial septicemia (bacterial infection spread through the blood) could account for the lesion in the kidney; the abdominal fluid; and the poor general state of the animal. The types of bacteria isolated from tissues in this animal are all considered commensals (normal inhabitants of body sites such as the intestinal tract and skin) or are ubiquitous in the environment. Bacterial septicemia with these types of bacteria is usually secondary to other processes such as post-partum infections; wound infections/abscess; or opportunistic spread from a local site of infection (mastitis; pneumonia; etc...). A precise pathogenesis and definitive confirmation of bacterial septicemia is not possible in this case. Ingrid L. Bergin; VMD; MS; DACLAMAnatomic pathology resident

DUCK VIRUS ENTERITIS YOLK COELOMITIS. This approximately 6-year-old female duck presented to the hospital in moribund lethargic condition and died shortly after presentation. It is one of seven fulvous whistling ducks presented on 5/21 from the river exhibit four of which were found dead. On 5/20 five ducks of the same species were found dead or dying in the exhibit. Necropsy of this bird revealed good nutritional status. The coelomic cavity had blood tinged fluid and the liver was mottled with petechial hemorrhages along the capsular surface and a single ecchymotic hemorrhage at the base of the liver. The gastrointestinal tract was filled with fluid. The esophagus was full of digesta associated with regurgitation prior to death. The jejunum was filled with necrohemorrhagic fluid and the serosal surface of the jejunum was reddened and inflamed. The caeca contained foul smelling fluid. The ovaries were dark and congested and the oviduct was thickened. The spleen was congested and oozed on cut surface.

CRYPTOSPORIDIOSIS SEPTICEMIA. This 3-year-old female gerenuk developed progressive neurological disease with rotating nystagmus on the left side and vertical nystagmus on the right side. Subtle dyspnea was also detected prior to euthanasia. Necropsy revealed hemorrhage around the brain and cervical spinal cord renal congestion serosal and mucosal hemorrhages in the urinary bladder and extensive hemorrhage and edema in the lungs. Mild peritonitis and pancreatic necrosis were noted. Mesenteric lymph nodes were prominent and the small intestine appeared inflamed. The omasum was congested.

GRANULOMATOUS HEPATITIS COELOMITIS BRONCHOPNEUMONIA. This 14-year-old female chuckwalla has a history of weakness lethargy and inappetence for approximately one week. The animal was under treatment with tube feeding and antibiotics and was found dead. At necropsy the anterior lungs were congested. The liver contained multifocal white foci.

CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY JOINT DISEASE. This 10-year-old male captive bred otter was euthanized due to arthritis and a history of heart disease. Necropsy revealed severe degenerative joint disease of both stifles dilated cardiomyopathy involving the left ventricle and six stones to 1 mm. in greatest dimension within the left kidney. The dorsal lung fields were dark red and wet on cut surface.
PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA. This approximately 9-year-old female merganser died during catch-up and weighing. At necropsy it was thin. The air sacs appeared cloudy.

EUTHANASIA CHRONIC KERATITIS HEPATITIS. This 10.5-year-old falcon was due to deterioration of condition and poor vision in the left eye. At gross necropsy there was an opaque white area in the cornea of the left eye.

ENCEPHALITIS HEMOSIDEROSIS WEST NILE VIRUS. This 2-year-old female lory had a history of lethargy inappetence and weight loss. The bird was found dead. No significant gross findings were noted at necropsy.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASSE LINGUAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA BACTERIAL CHOLANGIOHEPATITIS AND CHOLECYSTITIS ENTERITIS WITH FLAGELLATED PROTOZOA ARTERIOSCLEROSIS. This 32-year-old male golden lion tamarin presented with hypothermia and in moribund condition. It died despite fluid and emergency therapy. Bile culture was obtained. Necropsy revealed emaciation and dehydration with generalized alopecia a fluid filled cyst in the subcutis of the right cervical region discospondylosis of most vertebrae thin femoral cortex depleted fat stores atrophic skeletal muscle enlarged liver two 1 mm. diameter black semifirm nodules in the pancreas and severe enlargement and inspissation of bile in the gall bladder. Kidneys were polycystic and the adrenal was dark red to black.

DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE ULCERATIVE DERMATITIS/PODODERMATITIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 14-year-old male turkey had a history of lameness in the right leg bilateral wing droop absence of the right superior palpebra (chronic) and had a history of head and neck trauma from conspecific aggression six months earlier. The bird was eventually returned to the avian department and subsequently found in lateral recumbency and unable to stand. Supportive care was administered during which time openmouthed breathing appeared to resolve. The bird was noted to have a deep wound over the skull and developed bilateral pressure sores along the posterior aspect of both tarsi. In spite of supportive care that included bandaging antibiotics and laser therapy the bird continued to lose weight responded poorly to treatment and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed poor body condition minimal pectoral musculature a callus over the keel absence of feathers on the cervical and pectoral regions tattered wing and tail feathers enlarged tarsi with the right larger than the left pressure sores on the posterior aspects of the tarsi a 1 cm. scab along the distal aspect of digit #3 on the right foot a 1 cm. open wound on the dorsal aspect of the skull with visible calvarium in this region serous atrophy of fat in cardiovascular grooves thickened mitral valves a small yellow raised plaque at the level of the abdominal aorta a granuloma in the left lung darkened pulmonary tissues food and a smooth piece of glass in the ventriculus bilaterally distended ceca small spleen inactive testicles mottled cranial renal lobes a green granuloma on the ventral aspect of the left kidney moderate bone proliferation along the internal aspect of the left coxofemoral joint and marked proliferation to the level of the right coxofemoral joint and yellow fibrinous material along the side of the pressure wound within the right tarsus/tarsometatarsus.

BACTERIAL ENTERITIS GASTRITIS BACTEREMIA. This 14-year-old female boa presented with acute onset of lethargy and paresis. The animal’s condition declined rapidly and it later died. At necropsy lungs were hyperemic and thickened. The small intestine was also hyperemic and thickened with marked serosal edema.

CHIN TRAUMA IRON STORAGE DISEASE DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS. This 9-year-old male bat had a seven day history of illness and died while anesthetized for examination. The bat could not be resuscitated. Necropsy revealed a lobulated liver with multiple pale brown areas that extended into the parenchyma on cut surface and had a necrotic texture. Some liquid was also present in one of the lesions. Lungs were pale pink. The inguinal lymph nodes were bilaterally enlarged. The right testicle was half the size of the left testicle and had no normal architecture on cut surface.

ULCERATIVE CELLULITIS STRESS EUTHANASIA. This 15-year-old female mangrove snake was noted to have a wound on the ventral surface of the skin from which several bacteria were isolated. Supportive care was administered and biopsy identified bacterial abscess with chronic cellulitis. An acid-fast stain was negative. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a healthy appearing granulation bed at the site of the wound absence of food in the alimentary tract a retained ovum in the uterus and no other abnormalities.

NECROTIZING STOMATITIS CHRONIC ABOMASITIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female addra gazelle has a history of chronic recurrent stomatitis elevated fecal strongyle egg counts and weight loss. Multiple necrotic oral lesions have been debulked with associated supportive care. Fusobacterium necrophorum has been isolated from the oral lesions. More recently this animal displayed abnormal chewing behavior despite the absence of active oral lesions. The right cheek had palpated thick and firm and biopsies revealed fibrosis and granulation tissue. The animal continued to lose weight with recurrence of oral lesions. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation some round oral lesions on the left maxilla corresponding to the necrotic lesion in the left cheek hyperplasia of the mucosa over the epiglottis and arytenoids reddened fluid in the abomasum hypertrophy of the mucosal folds in the abomasum ulcers in the pylorus and duodenum milk in the mammary glands and no other remarkable findings.
MYOCARDITIS MYXOMATOUS DEGENERATION ENTERITIS. This 10-year-old female ibis had been treated for chronic pododermatitis and a fractured beak. At necropsy the heart and liver were enlarged.

CHRONIC MALNUTRITION AND STARVATION. This approximately 12-year-old male desert tortoise had a history of possible pneumonia and chronic malnutrition. The animal presented minimally responsive severely anemic and severely hypoglycemic. In addition the animal had swollen eyelids and was unable to open its eyes. The animal died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed very poor body condition easily removed scutes clear fluid in the nares and trachea thickened caudal lungs a 3 cm. in diameter bladder stone small and yellowish kidneys and weak bones.

AMYLOIDOSIS RENAL AND VISCERAL GOUT BUMBLEFOOT PORTAL HEPATITIS. This greater than 38-year-old male flamingo was found morbid and died shortly after. At necropsy it was in good body condition with fat stores present on the heart surface and in the coelomic cavity. There were mites moving on the feathers. There were multiple pinpoint white flecks present on the air sacs and surfaces of the liver kidney and intestines. The heart appeared enlarged. All the valves appeared thickened at the corner edges and particularly the right atrioventricular valves. The aorta had jet lesions on its exit from the heart as well as plaques along the endothelium. The liver was enlarged with blunted lobes. The gall bladder was distended and had viscid bile. The proventriculus appeared edematous. The mucosa of the large bowel had multiple congested blood vessels. The spleen was not identified. The kidneys were yellow/brown and swollen. The hock and carpal joints were smooth and appeared free of gout. Cerebral vessels were congested. Sections of brain liver kidney and heart were collected for West Nile virus testing.

COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS BACTERIAL ENTEROCOLITIS EUTHANASIA. This greater than 20-year-old female squirrel monkey developed weight loss lethargy and lameness in the left leg of 1-2 months duration. Radiographs had identified a femoral neck lesion in the right leg. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed emaciation absence of fat stores numerous small white nodules throughout the hepatic parenchyma rounded hepatic margins sludge in the gallbladder multiple white raised firm nodules throughout the spleen adherence of the bladder to the uterus numerous white nodules throughout the kidneys possibly enlarged adrenal glands minimal muscle mass and roughened abnormal femoral neck that ruptured during prosection.

PERFORATING INTESTINAL ULCERS SEPSIS DIC. This 17-year-old female llama had a two day history of decreased appetite one day of lethargy and watery diarrhea and decompensated quickly was rolling and kicking at its abdomen developed tachycardia and dyspnea and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed a moderate amount of abdominal fluid and multiple adhesions in the gastrointestinal tract. Most of the jejunum was hemorrhagic and a firm mass 6 in. in diameter spanned several loops of intestine. Multiple full thickness necrotic perforations were in the intestinal wall. Two large thrombi were in the vasculature adjacent to the spleen one of which was mineralized. Compartment #1 of the stomach was full of hay and all of the gastrointestinal tract aboral to C1 was empty. Thoracic viscera were within normal limits.

EMACIATION OLD RIB FRACTURES COLONIC PERFORATION. This 1-year-old male python arrived from Indonesia with no preshipment examination. Upon entry into quarantine a heavy mite infestation was noted and supportive care was administered. During this time all of the snakes in the shipment developed pyrethrin intoxication but survived with no apparent sequela. Three months later this snake became bloated and skin ripped easily when the snake was handled in the area of the bloat and examination revealed that the bloated area was due to edema in the muscle and subcutaneous tissue. Contrast radiography revealed intestinal obstruction with partial improvement following treatment although surgery was elected to evacuate the intestine. Firm pasty material was removed from the distal colon. The animal was subsequently found dead at morning check five days after the surgical procedure. Necropsy revealed fragile skin multiple bead-shaped lesions on the ribs especially in the second half of the body empty alimentary tract absence of fat bodies and no other remarkable abnormalities.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA CHRONIC GASTRITIS AND COLITIS DEGENERATIVE ARTHRITIS (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS). This 24-year-old male mandrill had a recent history of weight loss and abnormal gait especially in the right leg and had not been feeling well. It had been receiving prednisolone Rimadyl and gabapentin. The animal was observed to fall from its perch and died a few minutes later. Necropsy revealed multiple foci of gingival hyperplasia arthritis in the knees and elbows consolidation of the ventral aspect of the left lung thickened pericardium with petechiae and numerous prominent lymph nodes in the mesentery. The liver was red with multiple nodular thickenings in all lobes. The gastrointestinal tract was adhered to the liver and diaphragm. On cut surface the hepatic nodules had the same appearance as adjacent hepatic parenchyma.

Lymphoma Comments: The enlarged lymph nodes and thymus seen both in this mouse and in the previous colony member are consistent with a neoplastic lymphoid tissue proliferation. This particular strain may be more susceptible to lymphoma development due to their unique knockout nature. Systemic lymphoma Comment: The cause of death of this mouse is due to advance stage lymphoma. Please refer to the preliminary report comments. Benjamin Adu-Addai; DVM

EUTHANASIA ORAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA PULMONARY METASTISIS CHRONIC NEPHRITIS SPLENIC EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS. This 15-year-old female wolf had a history of maxillary facial swelling. A mass was identified invading bone and soft tissue with foci of abscessation. The animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy a mass was present invading the maxilla and nasal sinuses. The right adrenal was enlarged.

EUTHANASIA SPINAL FRACTURE SHOCK. This 2-year-old male prairie dog was found paralyzed in the hind end. A compression fracture was identified at the lumbosacral junction and the animal was euthanized.

RENAL GOUT BACTERRIAL ENTERITIS WITH SEPTICEMIA DEGENERATIVE OSTEOARTHRITIS. This 12-year-old female whistling duck had a limp on the left leg since October 1994. Its weight has ranged from 476 gm. to 601 gm. The limp has slowly gotten worse over time. The animal died spontaneously. Necropsy revealed white gritty material within the renal parenchyma.

HISTORICAL SPONDYLOSIS AT L1-L2 SLIGHT MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MILD AORTIC ARTERIOSCLEROSIS HEPATIC HEMOSIDEROSIS INTESTINAL ARTERIOLAR FIBRINOID DEGENERATION. This 41-year- and 4-month-old male western lowland gorilla was exhibiting lethargy and reduced appetite on April 28th. Examination on May 5th revealed some signs of infection on blood work dental disease and lumbar spondylosis with bridging of L1-L2. Supportive care resulted in no improvement. A dental surgery was performed May 8th and two molars were extracted and a root canal was performed on a fractured canine tooth. Slightly improvement was noted following the dental surgery but the patient never returned to normal and remained markedly depressed. Acute hyaline paresis developed on June 16th. An MRI revealed compression of the lumbar spine at the L1-L2 area with spinal stenosis caudally. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Gross necropsy revealed thin nutritional condition approximately 5 ml. of clear yellow pericardial fluid red to purple discoloration of the gastric mucosa and lumbar vertebrae that were markedly irregular in size and shape.

INANITION HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 6-year-old male rattlesnake was found dead. At necropsy brown and white mineralized material was present in the coelomic cavity. A perforation was noted in the colon anterior to the cloaca. A stick was identified in the area of the stomach and liver.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOVASCULAR AND RENAL DISEASE THYROID ADENOMA CHROMAFFIN CELL HYPERPLASIA COCCIDIOIDOMYCOSIS EMPHYSEMATOUS GASTRITIS EUTHANASIA. This 23-year-old mandrill had a history of chronic hepatic disease and chronic coccidioidomycosis involving the lung and thoracic vertebrae. The animal developed hind limb paralysis necessitating a hemilaminectomy for granulomatous inflammation in the spinal column but eventually developed lower urinary tract infection became markedly depressed and was euthanized for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed multiple abrasions in the skin atrophy of pelvic limb musculature and edema in the hind limbs. The accessory lobe of the lung was consolidated and firm. Mild diffuse mottling was noted in the liver. The spleen was small but had normal appearing parenchyma. Muscle wasting was present throughout the body. Hemorrhage was present in the spinal canal at T10-11 and narrowing of the vertebral canal was noted at T10.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS UREMIC VASCULOPATHY PARATHYROID ADENOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male cheetah had been anorectic and vomiting intermittently since early July and was hospitalized for severe azotemia hypercalcemia and hyperphosphatemia with suspected ileus or intestinal blockage. A rapid decline occurred and exploratory laparotomy revealed an ileal mass that perforated the serosa and was associated with hemoabdomen. Multiple splenic masses were also noted. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. At necropsy the parathyroid glands appeared bilaterally enlarged measuring 2 x 1.5 x 0.5 cm. each. The peritoneal cavity contained approximately two liters of frank blood. Approximately 500 ml. of serous fluid was in the pleural cavity and approximately 50 ml. of serosanguineous fluid was in the pericardial sac.

ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA. This 8-month-old male giraffe died a few hours following anesthetic procedure to retrieve a retained testicle. The animal may have aspirated ruminal contents during the actual anesthetic procedure and again during agonal throws. The animal was given several vaccinations during the procedure prior to the clinical signs. At necropsy there were ruminal contents in the lungs. The lungs were dark red and glistening.

PERIDONTITIS BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE MEDIASTINITIS. This 2-year-old female prairie dog was found dead. At necropsy dried blood was noted in the nares and on the tongue. Patchy areas of alopecia were present on the head and body. Lungs were congested and sank in formalin. A small mass was identified in the right palate.

MYCOBACTERIOSIS BACTERIAL BRONCHOPNEUMONIA BILIARY HYPERPLASIA. This 14-year-old female Matschie’s tree kangaroo has a history of intermittent dyspnea and nasal discharge. Thoracic radiographs and nasal culture in November 2010 revealed no abnormalities and PCR/DNA probes on nasal swabs for Mycobacterium avium were negative. The kangaroo responded briefly to empirical treatment but then died unexpectedly. Necropsy revealed a thickened trachea firm thickened caudal pulmonary tissue and miliary granulomatous white foci scattered throughout the lungs.
BACTERIAL SPLENITIS SPLENIC AMYLOIDOSIS GLOMERULAR AMYLOIDOSIS. This 1-year-old female marmoset was found dead. No significant gross lesions were noted at necropsy.

ESOPHAGEAL ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL TUBULAR ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 9.5-year-old female kingsnake had a history of renal adenocarcinoma. Two separate surgeries were performed to remove renal masses. The animal had become inappetent for three months and was intermittently tube fed. A mid cranial mass was apparent and fine needle aspirates suggested infection. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Serum uric acid level was twice the normal value at the time of euthanasia. Necropsy revealed dark red lungs dark purple heart a 2.5 cm. mass in the esophageal lumen white pinpoint foci within the remaining portions of the kidney and some clear cysts in one of the kidneys.

EUTHANASIA PELVIC FRACTURE SPLENIC MYELOLIPOMA HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 10.5-year-old male cheetah had a fracture of the ischial tuberosity and evidence of renal failure and was euthanized. At gross necropsy there was a fracture of the left ischial tuberosity and the right pelvis anterior to the acetabulum. The spleen contained multifocal pale nodules.

DIC SEPSIS HEMOLYTIC EVENT UROLITHIASIS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This male 8-year-old harbor seal died after approximately a three week period of irregular inappetence. This seal had a positive heartworm antigen test but negative Knott’s test and had been receiving ciprofloxacin orally for four days. Cultures of liver and kidney were performed and results are pending. At necropsy the carcass was underweight and there was a 3 x 1.5 cm. ovoid rock within the stomach. There appeared to be an enterocolitis. Multiple gray-green to white nephroliths were present. No Dirofilaria were noted.

TOXOPLASMOSIS. This 15-year-old male cottontop tamarin was found dead in its nesting box. It had no prior history of illness and was in excellent body condition. Necropsy revealed a mottled liver and a prominent vessel in the cerebral cortex associated with a small hematoma.

EUTHANASIA YOLK COELOMITIS ENTERITIS SHOCK. This 1-year-old female teal developed neurologic signs and fetid watery feces. The animal was humanely euthanized due to progression of the clinical signs. At necropsy the distal GI tract and cloaca contained watery feces.

ACUTE SHOCK RESTRAINT COMPLICATIONS. This approximately 5-year-old female budgerigar died while being weighed. Necropsy revealed good body condition enlarged opening of the left naris small streak of hemorrhage on the epicardium of the left ventricle and no other abnormalities.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIOMYOPATHY WITH CARDIAC INSUFFICIENCY. This 13-year-old male scarlet ibis was found dead. Necropsy revealed yellow fluid in the cranial coelomic cavity yellow tenacious fluid in the caudal coelomic cavity firm heart firm hemorrhagic intestines digesta in the small intestine and ingesta in the stomach and numerous white petechiae in the liver. The pancreas had foci of red discoloration. Body condition was thin.

NEPHROSCLEROSIS UROLITHIASIS ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 11-year-old male river otter was found by a keeper in its exhibit and was extremely lethargic anorexic and thin. The animal arrested several times during anesthesia for blood work and radiographs developed seizures and died in recovery. Necropsy revealed renal calculi throughout the kidneys.

VASCULOPATHY CARDIAC NECROSIS AND HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 8-year/9-month-old female kudu was found dead in sternal recumbency in its stall with its head tucked back along the right side of the body. It had some seizures prior to death. It was not able to get up after the seizures on 5/21. It was treated with antibiotics vitamin E selenium Banamine calcium and Ivomec. At necropsy there were multiple abrasions on the entire right side of the body. Some were completely through the skin. There was clear yellow fluid in the mammary gland. The lungs were not consolidated but very congested bilaterally. The abomasal mucosa was congested. There was copious clear serous pericardial fluid. There were petechia over the epicardium. The veins on the dorsal aspect of the brain were engorged.

DEGENERATIVE CARDIAC AND RENAL DISEASE PERFORATING PYLORIC ULCER DEGENERATIVE JOINT DISEASE (CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS) EUTHANASIA ISLET AMYLOIDOSIS. This 32-year-old female colobus was euthanized due to advanced age-related problems. Necropsy revealed cachexia congested lungs larger than expected ventricles and bridging spondylosis.

PROLIFERATIVE CATARRHAL ENTERITIS ARTERIOSCLEROSIS PAPILLARY INFARCT. This 10-year-old male African hunting dog recently developed inappetence vomiting dehydration and weight loss. Supportive care was administered but the response to treatment was suboptimal and euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

ENTERITIS PNEUMONIA SPLENIC HEMOSIDEROSIS. This 5-year-old neutered male rabbit had acute onset of lethargy. The animal suffered cardiopulmonary arrest and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. At necropsy the pleural cavity contained a small quantity of fluid. Foci of ulceration were noted in the stomach and duodenum.

SYSTEMIC INFECTIOUS DISEASEPROCESS PROBABLY VIRAL. This approximately 19-year-old male Humboldt penguin had a chronic history of intermittent lameness but otherwise uneventful history. The bird appeared otherwise normal in the morning and was found floating and unresponsive by late morning. Necropsy revealed moderate thickening of the cranial coelomic air sacs. No other lesions were noted.

EMACIATION. This 7-year-old male Parma wallaby was being treated for a cheek tooth abscess for four weeks prior to death. It had presented with weight loss severe lethargy and dull mentation hypothermia dehydration and hypoglycemia. Supportive care was administered and the animal improved slightly the next day and was standing but severely depressed. Supportive care was continued but the animal died overnight. Blood work had showed marked elevation in CK. IgM and IgG titers to Toxoplasma gondii were negative. There is a history of a rabid raccoon on the zoo grounds recently but no known contact with this animal and no wounds of unknown origin. Necropsy revealed thin body condition and resolved dental abscess. Meningeal vessels were congested and meninges were firmly attached to the underlying brain in some areas.

EUTHANASIA OSTEOARTHROSIS ENTERITIS LYMPHADENITIS LUTEOMA. This 17-year/4-month-old female Oryx was humanely euthanized. It had a history of chronic lameness of the right front and cachexia. At necropsy its body condition was 1. There was arthritis of the right front foot. On cut surface the joint surfaces were irregular and worn. The hip joints had similar changes. The uterus was large and flaccid. The right ovary was large and had a red 2 cm. dark red firm mass. The kidneys appeared small.

METASTATIC MINERALIZATION NEPHROSCLEROSIS PULMONARY ABSCESS. This greater than 15-year-old female sloth had a few day history of being found lying on the ground. It was moved to an off-exhibit area for closer monitoring and supportive care and seemed to be doing a little better but was found dead one morning. Necropsy revealed thin body condition hyperostosis of the last rib on the right side firm vena cava and aorta and an abscess in the cranial aspect of the right lung. A 0.5 cm. nodule was on the mucosal surface of the bladder wall. The urinary bladder contained 120 ml. of clear light yellow urine and no casts or crystals were noted. The kidneys had poor delineation between the cortex and medulla.

INANITION MELANOSIS. This approximately 11-year-old female toad died. Breeding has been seen in the rain forest in which they are living in. There have been no apparent problems seen with any of the toads. This toad was found dead in the middle of the rain forest. It was just brought over from HMLR where it lived in a 10 gal. tank for five years. At necropsy there were small fat bodies. There was a small amount of free fluid within the coelomic cavity. There were a few 0.5-1 mm. white nodules on the lungs bilaterally. The stomach was full of clear viscous fluid. There was a very large egg mass taking up a large portion of the body cavity. The total egg mass weighed 116 gm.

CHRONIC RENAL DISEASE METASTATIC MINERALIZATION. This 7-year-old female lizard had a recent history of eye problems that included closed eyes and a crusty exudate. Supportive care was administered but the lizard was found dead in the morning. Necropsy revealed blood in the mouth reduced fat pad density reddened lungs that bled on cut surface and did not float in formalin a large spleen two free-floating brown masses in the coelom bloody dark semi-thick fluid in the alimentary tract and pale enlarged kidneys.

BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA NEPHRITIS HEPATIC AMYLOIDOSIS. This 10-year/11-month-old male kudu died. It had a history of chronic renal failure over the last few years. It was noted to be vomiting and dehydrated two days ago. It was being darted with ketofen and antibiotics the last few days. At necropsy the kudu was thin. The lungs were severely consolidated throughout the ventral aspect of both lungs cranially and caudally. There were numerous adhesions from the lungs to the thoracic walls and between the lung lobes. There were numerous hardened white masses of varying size throughout the consolidated lung tissue. Both kidneys were enlarged and flocculent. There was minimal normal tissue remaining in either kidney.

RESPIRATORY AND DISSEMINATED GRANULOMATOSIS MYCOBACTERIOSIS. This 14-year-old male penguin was diagnosed with tracheal aspergillosis in 2008 and had recently presented for wheezing. Tan plaques and severe inflammation were noted in the distal trachea visible by endoscopy. The lesions were debrided and the bird was treated accordingly. Symptoms progressed and the bird died presumably due to asphyxiation associated with the tracheal inflammation and mucous production. Necropsy revealed nodules in the distal larynx and trachea with complete obstruction of the left side of the trachea and increased density to the caudal half of the left lung. Nodular inflammation was present around the lung within the air sacs. Two small granulomas were noted in the oropharynx. Pinpoint white lesions were noted on the surface of the liver.

Liver: suggestive of mild; multifocal hepatopathy Open COMMENTS: The pale foci within the liver may be caused by uneven blood pooling postmortem; and will require histopathology to confirm. A cause for the neurologic signs was not determined on gross examination. Previous clinical pathology from 12/13/08 indicated a calcium: phosphorus ratio imbalance (0.9:1.0). Nutritional inadequacies; such as seen with all seed diets; should be considered as a cause for hypocalcemia and neurologic signs in this case. Selective tissue have been placed on hold; and histopathology is pending. A final report will follow. Danielle Desjardins; D Testicular atrophy; bilateral; diffuse. Moderate; bilateral parathyroid hyperplasia. Mild; multifocal pulmonary anthrocosis? mild heterophilic tracheitis and bronchitis. Mild to moderate; multifocal random hepatocellular necrosis with mild heterophilic hepatitis and vacuolar degeneration. \_ Adrenal lesions have been described in a high percentage of birds on postmortem examination; however a clinical diagnosis of naturally occuring hypoadrenocorticism has not been documented in birds. It is possible the adrenal cortical degeneration may have contributed to anorexia; weakness and lethargy secondary to decreased glucocorticoid production. In addition; the cerebral edema identified within the brain may have been caused by electrolyte abnormalities; which may have been related to a deficiency in mineralcoritcoids from the adrenal cortex. The parathyroid gland hyperplasia in combination with the calcium:phosporous imbalance may be secondary to a diet which was high in phosphrous and low in calcium and vitamin D. All seed diets; fruits and most vegtables are low in calcium. High fat seeds; such as sunflowers; may interfere with calcium uptake. It is important to note that in nutritional secodnary hyperparathyroidism; serum caclium levels may be low to normal; despite clinical signs of weakness; seizures; etc. Ultimately; the proximate cause of death in this bird was most likely acute liver failure. A culture of the liver has been submitted to investigate the possibility of a terminal bacterial septicemia. An association between these findings and the findings in the brain and adrenal gland has not been determined. EUTHANASIA CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA HEMOCHROMATOSIS. This 25-year-old male sea lion was humanely euthanized after acute onset of lethargy and nonresponsiveness. It had a history of corneal edema opacity and intermittent blepharospasm. At necropsy all liver lobes were firm on palpation. There were 1-2 mm. elevated firm nodules throughout the hepatic surface and on cut section. The gall bladder was replaced by a firm brown mass that was elevated approximately 2 cm. above the hepatic surface.

SPLENIC HEMANGIOSARCOMA WITH METASTASIS EUTHANASIA. This 10-year-old female dog presented approximately eight days earlier with serosanguineous discharge from the mouth and a swollen left soft tissue on the underside of the mandible. The animal responded partially to antibiotic therapy. Examination had evidence of hypovolemic shock with pale mucous membranes and two palpable masses were in the abdomen with an associated fluid wave. Ultrasound revealed an enlarged splenic mass that was cavitated and had fluid. Blood work revealed disseminated intravascular coagulation. Radiographs revealed pulmonary metastasis. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed approximately two liters of blood in the abdomen and some associated blood clots multifocal random black blood-filled nodules throughout the pulmonary parenchyma up to 2 cm. in diameter and enlarged cavitated lymph nodes with luminal blood in the thoracic cavity. A large mass was noted at the level of the subiliac lymph node the spleen had an 8 cm. circular cavitary black mass on the tail and a lymph node at the base of the aorta was black cavitated and filled with blood. Prominent dental disease with multiple fractured teeth and pulp canal exposure and gingival recession was noted in the dental arcades. Multiple random small black masses up to 8 mm. in size were within the mesentery. The liver had multiple raised black cavity blood-filled masses. Small raised nodules were on the surfaces of the kidneys.

PANCREATIC NECROSIS ENTERITIS. This 3-year-old adult male lorikeet was found dead. It had no premonitory clinical signs. Preliminary bacterial culture results of crop and cloacal swabs revealed heavy gram negative growth. The bird may have been passing watery stool. At necropsy the crop was empty. The lower gastrointestinal tract was dark pink. The spleen was slightly enlarged and very pale. The brain was dark pink. The liver was mottled with light tan mixed with a normal colored liver. The liver appeared slightly enlarged.

LYMPHOMA CHRONIC MURINE PNEUMONIA EUTHANASIA. This greater than 3-year-old female rat had a history of consistent weight loss over the last several months and problems with ambulating due to paresis in the right pelvic limb. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes.

MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS MALARIA (PRESUMPTIVE). This 27-year-old female squirrel monkey was found acutely down. Treatment was initiated; however the animal later died. At necropsy lungs were mottled and firm. Blood work revealed azotemia and hyponatremia.

DUODENAL NEMATODIASIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS HEPATIC GRANULOMATOSIS HISTIOCYTIC HEPATITIS. This 7-year-old pigeon died. It had been admitted to the hospital for inappetence and blood work identified anemia. Necropsy revealed thin body condition fecal staining around the cloacal opening hemorrhage in the left pectoral muscle adjacent to the keel bone muscle atrophy and absence of adipose stores full proventriculus hemorrhage in the right hepatic lobe some pale yellow flat lesions in the left cranial hepatic lobe gravel in the ventriculus firm and enlarged duodenum associated with a 1 cm. focus of ulceration and necrosis on the duodenal flexure luminal round worm impaction in the duodenum and digested blood admixed with the roundworms.

HEPATITIS ENTERITIS PERICARDIAL HEMORRHAGE SHOCK. This 14-year-old male lory was found dead without premonitory signs. At necropsy a small quantity of hemorrhagic fluid was present in the coelom. The liver was enlarged with scattered pale foci. Hemorrhage was noted over the left cerebral hemisphere.

FUNGAL PNEUMONIA AND AIR SACCULITIS BACTERIAL AND FUNGAL DERMATITIS BACTERIAL ENTERITIS. This approximately 9-year-old male macaw underwent respiratory arrest within 10 min. of induction for anesthesia. It had a history of lethargy and anorexia. There was blood in the feces. Despite resuscitation attempts the macaw died. Thoracic radiographs revealed large patchy infiltrates in the lungs and the cardiac silhouette was increased. At necropsy there was regurgitated fluid in the oral cavity. There was severe crusted regional dermatitis in the left and right axilla. The superficial myocardium had multifocal indistinct white streaking that was not apparent on the endocardial surface or deeper myocardium. White plaques covered the pulmonary trunk on the ventral surface. The connective tissue around and between the great vessels seemed thickened by firm fibrous material. There was approximately 5 ml. of yellow slightly viscous pericardial fluid. Bilaterally there were severe dark red areas in the lungs usually surrounding firm brown to green regions. The intestinal loops were distended and fluid filled. There was blood in the lumen. The liver was mildly enlarged tan to brown and had rounded edges. The kidneys were generally enlarged friable and pale tan.

AMYLOIDOSIS PYELONEPHRITIS WITH SEPSIS ATHEROSCLEROSIS. This 7-year-old female marmoset had an acute onset of bloody nose followed by lethargy. The animal died. Necropsy revealed biliary lesions in the kidney.

GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS NEPHRITIS HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS. This 5.5-year-old corn snake was found dead. At necropsy the heart was enlarged and surrounded by clots. The spleen contained a 0.5 x 0.5 x 0.75 in. firm nodular mass.

GASTRIC BLOAT/VOLVULUS. This 6-year-old spayed female straw-colored fruit bat was found thrashing on the exhibit floor and was hypothermic. It was transferred to the hospital and supportive care was administered but the animal died. Necropsy revealed severe gastric ulceration involving three-quarters of the mucosal surfaces.

HEMANGIOSARCOMA ADNEXAL ADENOMA AND ADENOCARCINOMA EUTHANASIA. This 11-year-old male hunting dog had a history of dyspnea and radiographs revealed apparent metastatic lesions in the lungs. Euthanasia was performed for humane and diagnostic purposes. Necropsy revealed two skin masses in the dorsal caudal cervical region one of which was flat and the other proliferative. Numerous nodular masses up to 3 cm. in greatest dimension were in the lungs and the masses appear to represent clotted blood on cut surface. Mixed blood and mucus were in the trachea. A 3 cm. friable mass was in the lumen of the right auricle. Intervertebral disc protrusions were noted in the first three thoracic intervertebral disc spaces and spinal cord from this region was collected. This dog has a history of adnexal adenomas and adenocarcinomas that had been previously excised (G15-5668).

PERIOSTEAL FIBROSIS PERIOSTEAL HYPERPLASIA MYOCARDIAL FIBROSIS. This 10-year-old female peafowl had a history of chronic lameness. Osteolysis was noted in the distal tibiotarsus joint. Rupture of the tarsal flexor and digital extensor tendons developed and the animal was humanely euthanized. At necropsy the liver contained a 5 mm. thick walled cyst.
ERYTHROID CONSUMPTIVE ANOMALY. This 4-month-old female ringed teal was in quarantine. Another bird in quarantine had died one week earlier. Necropsy revealed no gross lesions.

SYSTEMIC SHOCK NO PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS. This 7-year-old male sea lion was being transported from another institution to the Buffalo Zoo. The temperature in the trailer was maintained at 60°. The animal was found dead on the first night of transport. At necropsy a large quantity of blood was present in the oral cavity and the left incisor was fractured. A large quantity of blood was present within the abdomen. The trachea was filled with blood and the bronchi were dark red.

EUTHANASIA CONJUNCTIVITIS METABOLIC BONE DISEASE. This 9-month-old knight anole of undetermined gender was humanely euthanized. It was found with bilateral eye infection and was very lethargic and dehydrated. It was given supportive care and antibiotics for nine days with no improvement. At necropsy there was thick purulent material removed from the surface of the globe. The anole was in thin body condition.

EUTHANASIA METASTATIC MAMMARY ADENOCARCINOMA RENAL INCLUSION BODIES. This approximately 12-year-old female fox was humanely euthanized. It had poor prognosis and deterioration. It had a history of chronic weight loss. There were multiple cutaneous soft tissue masses identified. Thoracic radiographs showed metastasis to the cranial thorax. At necropsy there were multiple subcutaneous soft tissue masses in the ventral thoracic region and a single mass on the abdominal skin. The lungs were pink soft and spongy. The cranial lung lobes were adhered to the pleural cavity wall. There were multiple small soft tissue masses on the pericardium and masses of variable size invading the thoracic cavity. There were multifocal coalescing masses in the dorsal portion of the thoracic cavity.
